Let them weigh the benefit of Christ, who redeemed us, and who, having overcome the devil, asserted us into liberty (Matt. 12; John 8; Gen. 3; 1 Pet. 2, etc.). 3. Let them consider their duty, which is to stand in liberty (Gal. 5). Let them not turn this into licence, but give place to God, that he may reign in them (Rom. 6:12; Matt. 6). Let them edify one another with such talk, and flee wicked conversations (1 Cor. 5). But here men almost always sin. Most people do not know themselves, and so they do not recognise the benefit of Christ. And although they are called Christians, they serve the devil. Hence the wrath of God, which grows heavier every day; and there is no hope of salvation unless we are converted (Col. 3; Isa. 9; Amos 4).

units.la: HOMILIA III.
units.tr: HOMILY III.

units.la: 4 Et congregatis illis, præcepit, ne discedrent Hierosolymis, sed expe-ctarent promissum patris. De quo, inquit, audiuistis ex me.
units.tr: 4 And when he had gathered them together, he commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, which, he said, you have heard from me.

units.la: 5 Quia Iohannes quidem baptizauit aqua: Vos autem baptizabimini Spiritu sancto post dies hosce non multos.
units.tr: 5 For John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days hence.

units.la: Quo
units.tr: Wherefore

units.la: OVoniam Christus Apostolos elegerat,vt per ipsos Euangelium toti orbi prædicaretur,necesse fuit,vt probè instituerentur in omnibus, quæ ad ipsorum munus faciebant. Fecit hoc diligenter Christus. 1. Quia resurrectio eius nostræ salutis fundamentum est , hanc multis argumentis per dies 40. asseruit. 2. Disseruit illis de regno suo,cum, vt falsam de hoc opinionem animis eorum exi meret, tum vt scirent, quis illis prædicationis finis esse deberet.His tertium subijcitur,spiritus sancti promissio,quam repetit & confirmat, simulque de loco & tempore,& alijs hic obseruatu necessarijs admoneet.
units.tr: Since Christ had chosen the apostles so that the Gospel might be preached through them to the whole world, it was necessary that they be thoroughly instructed in everything that pertained to their office. Christ did this carefully. (1) Since his resurrection is the foundation of our salvation, he established it by many proofs over forty days. (2) He taught them about his kingdom, both to drive out of their minds a false opinion about it and so that they might know what the goal of their preaching ought to be. To these is added a third point, the promise of the Holy Spirit, which he repeats and confirms, and at the same time he admonishes them about the place and the time and other matters here to be observed.

units.la: I. Locum indicat, iubens ne Hierosolyma discedant. Sic Luc.24, Voluit obedientiæ assuescere eos,qui debebant fidei obedientiam docere.At mirum videri potest, Hierosolymam destinari negotio omnium saluberrimo & excellentissimo. Quia enim fuerit,habes Matth.23. Luc. 13.19 &c. Quæ ergo causa fuit , &c? Non alia quàm Dei veritas , qui sic olim promiserat. Psalm. 2 10. Isaiæ secundo Mich. quarto.
units.tr: I. He indicates the place, commanding that they not depart from Jerusalem. So Luke 24. He wished those who were to teach obedience to faith to be accustomed to obedience themselves. But it may seem strange that Jerusalem was appointed for a business most salutary and most excellent. Why it was so, you have in Matt. 23, Luke 13, 19, etc. What then was the cause? None other than the truth of God, who had promised this long ago. Psalm 2, 10; Isaiah 2; Micah 4.

units.la: NOT. 1.Dei promissiones non fieri irritas, etsi aliqui non credant,&c.Rom 3.
units.tr: NOTE 1. God's promises are not made void even if some do not believe, etc. Rom. 3.

units.la: Soletur hoc, quando propter vniuersa- lem fere impietatem terremur, ne ea no- bis etiam fraudi fit, & proinde ipsi quoq; remissiores fumus. Cogita Deum nouisse suos,neque eorum obliuisci. 2. Tim.2. Ifa. 49.Et quia iustus est,no perdit pium cum impio.Gen.18. Qui item sapientissimus & omnipotens est, facilè potest inter illos discernere. Sic factum cum Noa, Gen.6 Lotho,Gen.19. In Babylon.Dan.5.6. Ita hic factum de reliquijs piorum. Id verò generale est.Mal.3.Mat 3.Id ergo nos sole tur.
units.tr: This is a consolation when we are terrified by the almost universal impiety, lest we too be harmed by it and therefore become more lax ourselves. Consider that God knows his own and does not forget them. 2 Tim. 2; Isaiah 49. And since he is just, he does not destroy the godly along with the wicked. Gen. 18. He who is also most wise and almighty can easily distinguish between them. So it happened with Noah, Gen. 6; with Lot, Gen. 19; in Babylon, Dan. 5, 6. So it happens here with the remnant of the godly. This is indeed a general rule. Mal. 3; Matt. 3. Let us therefore be comforted by this.

units.la: ¶ 2.Nullis praerogatiuis defendi eos, qui pergunt in impietate. Nulla vrbs vn- quam Hierosolyma praestantior fuit. Ve- tuftate, Gen.14.Sedes regni & sacerdotij per annos 477.Potentissima. Habuit Re- ges,Sacerdotes,prophetas. Et quod om- nia superat,typus Ecclesiae. Hinc illa prae- conia, Pfalm.48. 132.Matth.5.Et nunc ibi Spiritum sanctum accipiunt Apostoli, & regni fui exordiu facit Christus.Sed quia ingrata fuit & rebellis,omnia haec non iu- uerunt,sed intra annos 40.perijt. Sic fa- ctum cum Gal.vrbibus.Matth.11. Frustra ergo hodie gloriamur maiorum virtute, Euangelij praedicatione, &c. nisi mores nostri respondeant. II.Quid
units.tr: 2. The impious are defended by no prerogatives when they persist in wickedness. Jerusalem was never a more outstanding city. For antiquity, Gen. 14; it was the seat of the kingdom and priesthood for 477 years; it was most powerful. It had kings, priests, prophets. And, which surpasses all, it was a type of the Church. Hence those praises, Psalm 48, 132; Matt. 5. And now the apostles receive the Holy Spirit there, and Christ makes the beginning of his kingdom there. But because it was ungrateful and rebellious, none of these things helped it, and within forty years it perished. So it happened with the Galatian cities. Matt. 11. Therefore it is in vain for us today to boast of the virtue of our ancestors, of the preaching of the Gospel, etc., unless our morals correspond to it.

units.la: Multorum impietas Dei promissa non fa- cit irrita. Impios nul la iniuria gloria vel praeregatiua.
units.tr: The impiety of many does not make God's promises void. No honour or prerogative is any injury to the impious.

units.la: II.Quid illic faciant, docet: Expeftent promissionem patris. Sic dicit Spiritum sanctum: quia olim illum Deus promise- rat,Ioel.2.Ifa.59. Et simul suas promissio- nes eis in mentem reuocat, Ioh. 7.14. 15. 16.&c.
units.tr: II. He teaches what they are to do there: they are to await the promise of the Father. So he calls the Holy Spirit, because God had promised him long before, Joel 2; Isaiah 59. And at the same time he recalls to their minds his own promises, John 7, 14, 15, 16, etc.

units.la: In his autem Nota ¶Ministris Ver- bi Spiritu sancto opus esse. Sine hoc enim ipsi nihil proficient in cordib. hominum 1.Cor.3.Idem dici potest de iis, qui volunt in Republica cum laude versari. Vidit hoc Solomon,1.Reg.3.Precibus ergo opus est Psal.51.72.&c.
units.tr: In these words note that the ministers of the Word need the Holy Spirit. For without him they accomplish nothing in the hearts of men. 1 Cor. 3. The same can be said of those who wish to live with credit in the commonwealth. Solomon saw this, 1 Kings 3. There is need, therefore, of prayer. Psalm 51, 72, etc.

units.la: ¶2. Apostolorum doctrinam non humanam,sed diuinam esse. Hinc illud Christi Luc.10.11. Ideo Paulus tam confiden- ter pronuntiat.Gal.2 2.Cor.13. Obseruan dum propter eos, qui Apostolos quoque homines fuisse dicunt,vt ita humanis traditionibus locum faciant. At fuerunt Dei homines, & quidem Christi legati. 2. Corinth.5.
units.tr: 2. The doctrine of the apostles is not human but divine. Hence that saying of Christ, Luke 10, 11. Therefore Paul pronounces so confidently, Gal. 2; 2 Cor. 13. We must take care on account of those who say that the apostles too were merely men, so that they may thus make room for human traditions. But they were men of God, and indeed legates of Christ. 2 Cor. 5.

units.la: III.Promissionem confirmat, nimirum ne mora offenderentur. Repetit ergo priores promissiones, & simul Iohannis Baptistæ testimonium illis in mentem re- uocat, eo quod maxima esset huius autho- ritas Quasi diceret. Scitis quid sæpè pro- miserim, quid item olim Ioannes dixerit,
units.tr: III. He confirms the promise, namely so that they might not be offended by the delay. He therefore repeats the earlier promises and at the same time recalls to their minds the testimony of John the Baptist, because the authority of that testimony was very great. As if he said: You know what I have often promised, and what John also said long ago,

units.la: ¶ Nota: Euangelij minifri ipi ritu sancto opus abent. fore vt ego meos baptizem in Spiritu sancto & igne Matth. 3. Itaque huius symbolum fuit baptismus. Hunc ergo quia à Iohanne accepistis, ne dubitetis de me, quin ipse etiam meo officio fungar.
units.tr: Note: the ministers of the Gospel need the Holy Spirit. that I will baptize mine in the Holy Spirit and in fire, Matt. 3. Therefore baptism was the sign of this. Since you have received it from John, do not doubt about me, that I too will carry out my office.

units.la: NOT. 1. Christum interse & Iohannem distinguere, vt huic quidem administrationem signi externi tribuat, sibi vero vendicet id, quod illo adumbratur. Ob seruandum hoc in toto ministerio. Ministri circa sola externa occupantur, docendo, hortando, orando, Sacramenta dispensando. In animos autem soli Christus est. Vide 1.Cor.3 Act.10.16 Eph.2. Quod interdum ministri dicuntur regenerare, seruare, &c. (1.Cor.4 Gal.4 Actor.16. Ab die 1.) propter Christum fit, qui cum suo ministerio coniunctus est.
units.tr: NOTE 1. Christ distinguishes himself from John, so that he assigns to John the administration of the outward sign, but claims for himself what that sign foreshadows. This must be observed throughout the whole ministry. Ministers are occupied only with outward things: teaching, exhorting, praying, dispensing the sacraments. But Christ alone is the one who acts upon the minds. See 1 Cor. 3; Acts 10, 16; Eph. 2. That ministers are sometimes said to regenerate, to save, etc. (1 Cor. 4; Gal. 4; Acts 16, from the first day), happens on account of Christ, who is joined with their ministry.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quod à baptismo argumentumducit, quo suae promissioni fidem facit. Sunt ergo Sacramenta signa promissionis Dei. Sic de Circumcisione, Rom.4. Sic Euangelium permittit ablutionem à peccatis, & spiritum adoptionis, 1.Iohan. 1 Roman.8. Sigillum promissionis huius est Baptismus, Tit.3. Quàm igitur certò hunc accepimus, tam certum est, nos Christi sanguine ablutos, & Dei filios factos esse, &c. Euangelium docet, Christum se pro nobis in mortem tradidisse, & panem vitæ esse factum, Iohan. 6. Memoria & sigillum huius est Cœna, 1. Corinth. 11. 10. Quisquis igitur Euangelio credit, Christo frui turpe per fidem, perinde vt ore panem & vinum percipit. Et hac ratione Sacramenta fidem confirmare dicuntur, &c. Nos in omnibus his Dei bonitatem agnoscamus, & vt suo nos Spiritu regat. Oremus.
units.tr: 2. He draws an argument from baptism, by which he gives assurance of his promise. Sacraments are therefore signs of God's promise. So with circumcision, Rom. 4. So the Gospel grants cleansing from sins and the spirit of adoption, 1 John 1; Rom. 8. Baptism is the seal of this promise, Titus 3. Therefore, as surely as we have received this, it is equally certain that we have been washed in the blood of Christ and made sons of God, etc. The Gospel teaches that Christ delivered himself to death for us and became the bread of life, John 6. The Supper is the memorial and seal of this, 1 Cor. 11, 10. Whoever therefore believes the Gospel feeds on Christ through faith, just as he receives bread and wine with the mouth. And in this way the sacraments are said to confirm faith, etc. Let us in all these things acknowledge the goodness of God, and pray that he rule us by his Spirit. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA IV.
units.tr: HOMILIA IV.

units.la: 6 Illi igitur quum conuenissent, interrogarunt illum, dicentes: Domine, num hoc tempore restitues regnum Israel?
units.tr: 6 When they therefore had come together, they asked him, saying: Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?

units.la: 7 Dixit autem illis: Non est vestrum nosse tempora, & articulos temporum, quos pater, &c. Vsq; adversum 9.
units.tr: 7 But he said to them: It is not for you to know the times and seasons, which the Father has, etc. Down to verse 9.

units.la: POstquam exposuit Lucas, vt Christus discipulos suos abunde instruxerit in omnibus, quæ quoad munus illorum ipsis cognitu necessaria erant, transit modo, ad eius Ascensionem. Huic autem præmit tit postremum colloquium, quo illos am plius admonet de officio suo, &c. Et quia hic simul illustratur tota regni Christi ratio, proderit singula diligentius inspexisse.
units.tr: After Luke has set out how Christ fully instructed his disciples in all those matters which were necessary for them to know concerning their office, he passes over to his Ascension. But before it he places the last conversation, in which he admonishes them more fully about their duty, etc. And since the whole reasoning of Christ's kingdom is illuminated here at the same time, it will be useful to examine each part more carefully.

units.la: ¶ Colloquio occasionem dederunt discipuli, qui quaerunt: Domine an hoc tempore, &c Quaerunt autem de regno terreno, quale Iudae somniabant ex prophetijs perperam intellectis. 2. Sam. 7. Psal. 89. Ierem. 23. Idem error discipulos tenuit, ex quo infiniti nascebantur. 1. De regno quae runt, qui toties de cruce admoniti erant, Mat. 16. 10. Ioh. 15. 16. Luc. 21. Voluntergo regnare priusquam pugnarint. Itahodie multi: In primis spirituales Patres 2. De solo Israele quaerunt, de aliis gentib. nihil soliciti. Atqui Christus Rex catholicus de scribitur, Psal. 2. 72. If. 60. Zach. 9. Itavero in Christum simul & gentes iniurij sunt 3. Curiosi quaerunt de articulo temporis. Atqui potius quaesiuissent de suo officio, & operam suam obtulissent. Est ergo insigne exemplum, quid eueniat ijs, qui in Scriptura oscitanter versantur.
units.tr: The disciples gave the occasion for the conversation, asking: Lord, is it at this time, etc.? They ask about an earthly kingdom, such as the Jews dreamed of from the prophecies wrongly understood (2 Sam. 7; Ps. 89; Jer. 23). The same error held the disciples, from which countless others arose. (1) They ask about a kingdom, though they had so often been warned about the cross (Matt. 16; John 15:16; Luke 21). They wish to reign before they have fought. So many today do likewise, especially the spiritual Fathers. (2) They ask about Israel alone, caring nothing for the other nations. Yet Christ is described as the universal King (Ps. 2; 72; Isa. 60; Zech. 9). Thus they wrong Christ and the Gentiles alike. (3) The curious ask about the moment of time. Yet they ought rather to have asked about their own office and offered their own labour. This is therefore a notable example of what happens to those who handle Scripture carelessly.

units.la: Et NOTA ¶ Hominem facile labi, errores autem inueteratos aegre tolli, maxi mefi publico exemplo confirmentur. Talis fuit iste. Et Christus circa hunc maximé laborauit. Vide Mat. 18. 20. Io. 6. Lu. 22. Ioh. 18. Luc 24. Et nunc per dies 40. Vnde ergo quod rursus impingunt? Quia haec est naturae corruptio, vt semper recurrant errores. Sic Israel. Exod. 32. Hinc ex-celsocelsorum superstitio. In nobis experimur. Pauci norunt, quid fit Papat. Attamen in dictis, & factis superstitionem spirant. Ita in moribus fit. Necesse ergo superstitionu reliquias radicitus euellere in Reformationibus, vt Ezechias fecit, 2. Reg 18. Et ferendi patienter, qui talia arguunt. Nulla diligentia potest superuacanea esse. Sequitur Christi responsio bipertita.
units.tr: And NOTE: that a man easily slips, and that long-entrenched errors are hard to remove, is confirmed by a public example. Such was this one, and Christ laboured especially hard over him (see Matt. 18:20; John 6; Luke 22; John 18; Luke 24), and now for forty days. Why then do they stumble again? Because it is the corruption of nature that errors always recur. So Israel (Exod. 32). Hence the superstition of the great ones. We experience this in ourselves. Few know what the Papacy is, yet in their words and deeds they breathe superstition. So it is in morals. It is necessary, therefore, in the Reformations to root out the remnants of superstition completely, as Hezekiah did (2 Kings 18), and to bear patiently with those who point such things out. No diligence can be superfluous. Christ's reply follows, in two parts.

units.la: I. Reijcit quaestionem vt ineptam & indignam responso: Non est vestrum, &c. Non confutat ipsorum opinionem: quia non opus erat, cum breui Spiritum fandum acceptur essent. Sensus: Esto, regnum habeam quale vos somniatis, tamen reprehendi meretur vestra curiositas, qui de articulo temporis quaeritis, de quo nihil vnquam dixi, & plus scire vultis quam Deus reuelarit.
units.tr: I. He rejects the question as foolish and unworthy of an answer: "It is not for you," etc. He does not refute their opinion, because there was no need, since they were soon to receive the Holy Spirit. The sense is: Grant that I have a kingdom such as you dream of; still your curiosity deserves reproof, you who ask about the moment of time, about which I have never said anything, and wish to know more than God has revealed.

units.la: No T. ¶ Sapientiae Christianae limites. Quia enim reprehenduntur discipuli hoc nomine, &c. hic nobis modulus sapientiae fit, vt ea cognoscamus diligenter, quae De us in Scripturis manifestauit. Reliqua fi- namus vsque in illum diem, &c. 1. Cor. 13. Vide Eccles. 3. Prou. 25.
units.tr: NOTE: The limits of Christian wisdom. For since the disciples are reproved on this account, etc., here we have a measure of wisdom: that we diligently learn those things which God has made manifest in the Scriptures. Let us leave the rest until that day, etc. (1 Cor. 13). See Eccles. 3; Prov. 25.

units.la: 1. Arguuntur fatidici, & imprimis Astro logi. Prohibet Christus inquirire tempo- rum articulum. At hic praecipuus Astro-
units.tr: 1. Prophesiers are rebuked, and above all the astrologers. Christ forbids us to inquire into the moment of the times. Yet this is the chief use of the astrologers, in nativities and prognostications.

units.la: logorum vsus est in Natiuit.& Prog. Imò discipuli reprehenduntur, qui Christum interrogant. Illi adaftra recurrunt contra illa Leuit.20. Deut.18. Ier.10. Mich.5 If 8.
units.tr: Indeed the disciples are reproved who question Christ. The astrologers resort to the stars, against which see Lev. 20; Deut. 18; Jer. 10; Mic. 5; Isa. 8.

units.la: 2. Qui præde stinationis mysterium inquirunt.Contenti simus ijs,quæ Deus reuelauit.Nos electos esse ex gratia in Christo,Rom.9. Eph.1. Electionem hanc esse stabilem,Rom.11.Signum eius esse fidem, quæ Christū apprehendit, Act.14. Finem esse, vt inculpati simus,& Deum glorificemus;Eph.1.1.Pet.2. In his exerceamur.
units.tr: 2. Those who inquire into the mystery of predestination. Let us be content with what God has revealed: that we are elect in Christ from grace (Rom. 9; Eph. 1); that this election is stable (Rom. 11); that its sign is faith, which lays hold of Christ (Acts 14); that its end is that we be blameless and glorify God (Eph. 1; 1 Pet. 2). Let us exercise ourselves in these things.

units.la: II.Repetit de regno suo, quæ ipsis ser-uiebant.Accipietis, &c. NOT. ¶ Promissionem spiritus sancti repeti, qua & solatur, & regni sui conditionem exprimit: Quasi dicat: Ne terreamini, quod regno meo propagando estis destinati. Nec enim humana,sed Dei virtute hoc fiet,quæ non deerit,&c. Itaq; regnum Christi non est ex mundo,Ioh.18. Ideo non armis pro pagatur,sed verbi prædicatione,2.Cor.10. Econtra etiam nihil proficient,qui illud armis oppugnant:Psalm.2 Zach 12. &c.
units.tr: II. He repeats concerning his kingdom, which served them: "You shall receive," etc. NOTE: The promise of the Holy Spirit is repeated, by which he both comforts them and expresses the condition of his kingdom, as if to say: Do not be terrified that you are destined to spread my kingdom. For this will be done not by human but by God's power, which will not fail, etc. Therefore the kingdom of Christ is not of this world (John 18). For this reason it is not propagated by arms but by the preaching of the Word (2 Cor. 10). On the other hand, those who assail it with arms will also accomplish nothing (Ps. 2; Zech. 12; etc.).

units.la: ¶ Officium illorum tradit: Eritis mihi testes.Quasi dicat:Vestrum munus erit te-stari de omnib. quæ vidistis & audiuistis, &c. vt ita me omnes agnoscant suum esse seruatorem, &c. Et sane testes eiusmodi fuerunt Apostoli,vt patebit ex tota historia Act.2.3.4.5.&c.Confirmârunt proprio exemplo,(Phil.3.) imò suo sanguine.
units.tr: He sets out their office: "You shall be my witnesses." As if to say: It will be your task to bear witness to all that you have seen and heard, so that all may thus acknowledge me as their Saviour, etc. And indeed the Apostles were such witnesses, as will be clear from the whole history in Acts 2, 3, 4, 5, etc. They confirmed it by their own example (Phil. 3), and indeed by their blood.

units.la: Obseruandum, quæ sit Euangelij digni tas,& quàm graue scelus sit, ei contradicere.Non tutum est iuratis testibus fidem derogare.Quid ergo fiet illis,qui Apostolis fidem derogant? Redundat hæc iniuria in ipsum Deum,1.Ioh.5.Matth.17. At quid hodie tam est vulgare? Quid ergo miramur iram Dei vndique se exerentem Ioh.3.
units.tr: It is to be observed how worthy of the Gospel it is, and how grave a crime it is to contradict it. It is not safe to detract from the faith of sworn witnesses. What then will become of those who derogate from the faith of the Apostles? This injury overflows upon God himself (1 John 5; Matt. 17). But what is so common today? Why then do we wonder at the wrath of God breaking out on every side (John 3)?

units.la: ¶3. Fines regni Christi Hierofol. consultò nominat,ne indignam putarent, & propter Pf.110.Ifa.2. Mich.4. Samar.propter odium gentis,Ioh.4.8. item : quia ab illis omnibus abhorrebant, Act. 10.11. Et hos fines etiam Prophetæ constituunt, Psal.2.72.Ifa.49.&c.
units.tr: 3. He deliberately names the bounds of Christ's kingdom as Jerusalem, lest they think it unworthy, and on account of Ps. 110; Isa. 2; Mic. 4; Samaria, on account of hatred of the nation (John 4; 8); likewise because they shrank from all those (Acts 10; 11). The prophets too set these same bounds (Ps. 2; 72; Isa. 49; etc.).

units.la: Est ergo Christus vniuersalis omnium Seruator,& arguuntur, qui vnumquenq; in sua religione seruari dicunt, Col 3.Ro. 1.&c. Agnoscamus hanc Dei bonitatem, & sanguine Christi partam salutem amplexi, perpetuo simus in statione, vigilemus & Oremus.
units.tr: Christ is therefore the universal Saviour of all, and those are refuted who say that each is saved in his own religion (Col. 3; Rom. 1; etc.). Let us acknowledge this goodness of God, and, embracing the salvation won by the blood of Christ, let us always be at our post, watch and pray.

units.la: HOMILIA V.
units.tr: HOMILY V.

units.la: 9 Et cùm hæc dixisset,aspicientibus B 2 illis elevatus est, & nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum,
units.tr: 9 And when he had said these things, while they looked on, he was lifted up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.

units.la: 10 Et cum esset intentus in caelum oculis, eo proficiscente, &c. ad verf.12.
units.tr: 10 And while they were gazing up to heaven as he went, etc., to verse 12.

units.la: Quoniam Lucas ex Spiritus S. suggestione Apostolorum acta narrat reinstituit, non incommodè ab ijs ordinatur, quae Christus iam terras reliquerat cum illis egit. Ex ijs enim patet, illos nihil priuata temeritate fecisse, sed eorum executores fuisse, quae Dei Filius iniunxerat: ideoque ipsorum doctrinam pro ipsius Christi doctrina recipi debere, Luc.10. 1. Thes. 2. Sequitur nunc ipsa Ascensio, in qua tres insignes fidei nostrae articuli continentur, in quibus species nostra potissimum funda data est, &c. Partes historiae sunt duae.
units.tr: Since Luke, under the prompting of the Holy Spirit, relates the acts of the Apostles, it is not inappropriately ordered by what Christ did with them after he had left the earth. From these things it is clear that they did nothing from private rashness but were the carriers out of what the Son of God had enjoined. Therefore their teaching ought to be received as the teaching of Christ himself, Luke 10; 1 Thess. 2. Next follows the Ascension itself, in which three notable articles of our faith are contained, and on which our hope is chiefly founded, etc. The history has two parts.

units.la: I. Ascensionem paucis absoluit, cum quod Angeli testimonium subijciet, tum quod aliqua iam scripserat, Luc. 24. Quibus adde Mar. 16. Sunt haec simplicissima, & conueniunt cum prophetijs, Psalm. 68. 110. Sunt tamen propter nouatores aliquos singula propius consideranda.
units.tr: I. He finishes the account of the Ascension briefly, both by adding the testimony of the angels and by what he had already written, Luke 24. Add Mark 16. These things are very simple and agree with the prophecies, Ps. 68, 110. Nevertheless, because of certain innovators, each point must be considered more closely.

units.la: I. Quis ascenderit? Iesus Christus, de quo tota Euangelica historia loquitur. At qui est is in vna eademque persona Deus & Homo. Quia vero quoad Deitatem non opus habuit Ascensione: Hæc de assumta Humanitate debet intelligi, vt etiam quæ de eius morte & resurrectione dicuntur. Non ergo audiendi, qui illum adhuc in terris monstrant contra Matt.24.
units.tr: I. Who ascended? Jesus Christ, of whom the whole evangelical history speaks. He is one and the same person, God and man. But since as regards his Deity he had no need of an ascension, this must be understood of the assumed humanity, as also what is said of his death and resurrection. Therefore those are not to be heard who still show him on earth, contrary to Matt. 24.

units.la: Interim Notat. Quod qui tam indigna passus erat, ascendit. Ergo quæ in terris patimur non obstant, quò minus suo tempore cœlesti gloria fruamur. Huc pro misericordiis faciunt, Ioh.12.14.17 Luc.22. Ne minem ergo offendant afflictiones 2.Tim.2 Roman.8. II Quo? In altum, vt Psal.68. Angeli postea cœlum nominant, vt & Mar cus, qui addit, Et sedit à dextertis Dei.
units.tr: Meanwhile note that he who had suffered such indignities ascended. Therefore what we suffer on earth does not stand in the way of our enjoying heavenly glory in its time. Here belong John 12, 14, 17; Luke 22. Let afflictions therefore give offence to no one: 2 Tim. 2; Rom. 8. II. Whither? On high, as in Ps. 68. The angels afterwards call it heaven, as does Mark, who adds, "and sat at the right hand of God."

units.la: Vbi Nota 1 Locum, quò abijt. Cœlum scilicet. Sic autem dicitur beatitudinis æternæ sedes, quæ super omnes cœlorum orbes & corruptibilem mundum est: quò nos quoque transferemur. Patet hoc ex promissionib. citatis, & Phil.3.1.Thes. 4.1 2. Conditionem. A Dexteris Dei. Significatur consortium diuinæ gloriæ & potestatis, vt prædictum Psalm.110. Matth. 20. Et ita exponitur Ephes.1. Id verò consolationi seruiat in omni tentatione, Mar. 28. Rom 8.
units.tr: Here note: 1. The place to which he went: heaven, namely. This is called the seat of eternal blessedness, which lies above all the spheres of the heavens and the corruptible world, and to which we also shall be transferred. This is clear from the promises cited, and Phil. 3; 1 Thess. 4. 2. The condition: at the right hand of God. This signifies a sharing in divine glory and power, as in the aforesaid Ps. 110, and Matt. 20. And so it is explained in Eph. 1. This serves for consolation in every temptation, Mark 28; Rom. 8.

units.la: III. Quomodo? Benedixit discipulis, & ita protectioni Dei commisit. Deinde ip- sis videntibus subuectus est, Psalm. 104.
units.tr: III. How? He blessed the disciples and thus committed them to the protection of God. Then, while they watched, he was carried up, Ps. 104.

units.la: Exod.13.14.16.40.Num.9.1.Reg.9. Accedunt & Angeli.
units.tr: Exod. 13, 14, 16, 40; Num. 9; 1 Kings 9. The angels also join in.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Christi seruatoris maiestatem & potentiam. Nubium ministerio vtitur, quibus nemo praeter Deum imperat, & quibus nihil mirabilius, &c. Iob.36.37.38. Angelis item Dan.7.Psal.97.Heb.1. Quid ergo timemus? Quin cum Dauide dicimus,Psalm.27.118.Item ad Romanos 8.
units.tr: NOTE: the majesty and power of Christ the Saviour. He makes use of the service of clouds, which no one commands except God, and nothing is more wonderful than these, etc. Job 36, 37, 38; likewise the angels, Dan. 7; Ps. 97; Heb. 1. Why then do we fear? Rather let us say with David, Ps. 27, 118; likewise Romans 8.

units.la: IV.Fructum,qui multiplex est.1.De salute certos facit. Quia enim propter nos in mundum venit, & carnem assumpsit, (Matth.12.) & in ea triumphans caelos conscendit, docet hostes omnes iam deuictos,nec quicquam in terris porro agendum fuisse,&c.Psalm.68.Ephes.4.Ioh.14.16. 2. Coelos nobis quoque aperuit, qui propter peccatum clausi erant,Gen.3.Iohan.14. 3.Illic pro nobis intercedit,Rom.8.1.Iohan.2.Heb.9. Ista vt nos consolantur:ita officij admonent, vt nimirum hoc vno contenti simus,&c.Iohan.6.4.Isa.46. &c. Deinde vt ipsi etiam reliquis terrenis studijs caelestia sectemur,Vide Col.3.Matthaei 6.1.Tim.6.&c.
units.tr: IV. The fruit, which is manifold. 1. He makes us certain of salvation. For since he came into the world on our account and assumed flesh (Matt. 12), and ascending triumphant into the heavens, he teaches that all enemies are now conquered and that nothing further was to be done on earth, etc. Ps. 68; Eph. 4; John 14, 16. 2. He has also opened the heavens for us, which had been closed on account of sin, Gen. 3; John 14. 3. There he intercedes for us, Rom. 8; 1 John 2; Heb. 9. As these things console us, so they also admonish us of our duty, namely that we should be content with this one thing alone, etc. John 6; Isa. 46, etc. Then, that we ourselves, besides our other earthly pursuits, should also seek heavenly things. See Col. 3; Matt. 6; 1 Tim. 6, etc.

units.la: II.Quia haec nondum intelligunt discipuli, & ideo obstupefacti suspiciunt, apparent Angeli, & illos plenius instituunt. Exordiuntur autem à reprehensione, non quod Christum visu fcquerentur,sed quod obliti promissionum, eum carnis affectu requirerent. Seruit eadem reprehensio nostris hodie, &c, Iohan.6. Inde consolationem subijciunt, dum de eius reditu differunt: Hic ipse veniet, quomodo videbitis, &c. Ergo visibiliter veniet. Loquuntur autem de eius aduentu ad iudicium, quae in Symbolo profitemur. Hunc omnis Scriptura praedicat. Dan.7. Matth. 24.25. Rom.14. 1.Thess.4. 1.Cor.15. &c. Ita vero discipulos excitare voluerunt ad officium faciendum, & simul consolari in periculis, Luc.12. 2.Cor 5. 1.Tim.4.
units.tr: II. Because the disciples do not yet understand these things, and so look up in astonishment, angels appear and instruct them more fully. They begin with a rebuke, not because the disciples were seeking Christ with their eyes, but because, having forgotten the promises, they sought him with fleshly affection. The same rebuke serves us today, etc. John 6. Then they add consolation, while they speak of his return: "This same Jesus, who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him go into heaven." Therefore he will come visibly. They speak of his coming to judgement, which we profess in the Creed. All Scripture preaches this: Dan. 7; Matt. 24, 25; Rom. 14; 1 Thess. 4; 1 Cor. 15, etc. They wished indeed to stir the disciples up to do their duty, and at the same time to console them in dangers, Luke 12; 2 Cor. 5; 1 Tim. 4.

units.la: Vbi similiter NOTA ¶ Eundem vsum aduentus Domini nobis etiam esse debere. Vt huius memores non cessemus in officio. Quid enim tunc iuuabunt opes, honores, delitiae? Matth.16. 2.Pet.3. Idem ille consoletur etiam nos. In Christo enim ostendit Deus magnitudinem suae virtutis, qua erga omnes credentes vult vti. Ve niet item ille redemptor suorum &c. Luc. 21. Phil.3. Vidit hoc Iob. Cap.19. Item.1. Thess.4 Eadem nobis applicemus in mor bis, egestate, persecutionibus, conscientiae tentationibus. In summa, hac spe animati, calcemus terram, & aspiremus ad coelos, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: Here likewise note: the same use of the Lord's coming ought to be ours also, so that, mindful of it, we may not cease in our duty. For what will riches, honours and pleasures avail then? Matt. 16; 2 Pet. 3. May that same One console us too. For in Christ God shows the greatness of his power, which he wills to use towards all believers. The Redeemer of his own will also come, etc. Luke 21; Phil. 3. Job saw this, chap. 19. Likewise 1 Thess. 4. Let us apply the same in sicknesses, want, persecutions and the temptations of conscience. In sum, animated by this hope, let us tread the earth underfoot and aspire to heaven, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA VI.
units.tr: Homily VI.

units.la: 12 Tunc reuersi sunt in Hierusalem à monte qui vocatur Oliveti, qui est prope Hierusalem, distans itinere Sabbathi.
units.tr: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a sabbath day's journey away.

units.la: 13 Et cum introissent ascenderunt in cœnaculum vbi commorabantur & Petrus & Iacobus & Ioannes & Andreas, Philippus & Thomas, Bartholomæus et Matthæus, Iacobus filius Alphæi, & c. ad ver. 15.
units.tr: And when they had gone in, they went up to the upper room where Peter, James, John and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and so on, were staying, as far as verse 15.

units.la: ETsi Christus corpus suum in cœlos euexerit, non tamen deposuit suæ Ecclesiæ curam. Patet hoc ex eo, quòd aliturus discipulis mandata dedit, quòd item Angeli eosdem consolantur. Et efficacem fuisse consolationem docent quæ sequuntur. Incipit enim narrare Lucas, quid porrò Apostoli fecerint: vbi egregia fidei argumenta concurrunt.
units.tr: Although Christ has raised his body into heaven, he has not laid down the care of his Church. This is clear from the fact that he gave his disciples commands, as one who would sustain them, and that angels likewise comfort them. The things that follow show that this consolation was effective. For Luke begins to relate what the apostles then did, and in it outstanding arguments of faith come together.

units.la: I. Redeunt in vrbe postquam orassent (Luc.24.) & illic manent, vtSpiritum sanctum exspectent.
units.tr: I. They return to the city after they had prayed (Luke 24), and remain there so that they may await the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Not. ¶ Obedientia fidei. Ita enim Christus iusserat. Atqui multa poterant absterrere. Periculum. Incommoditas loci & inopia. Quòd item Spiritus non alligatus loco, Ioh.3. Nec est dubium cogitatiogitationes has omnes illis obrepsisse pro carnis ingenio,&c. At vincunt omnia ista per fidem: Neq; deest successus. Peratur hinc generalis regula, vt Deo aliquid iubenti obediamus simpliciter. Quia enim bonus & pater est, nihil quàm bonũ & iuTare iubet,i.Tim.2.Pf.119. Quia item fidelis & omnipotens est, tuetur in sua vocatione ambulantes,neq; finit supra vires &c.1 Cor.10 2 Cor.1. Exempla sunt passim.Abraham,Gen.12 &c.Pfal.105.Transferant hæc singuli ad fe, ne in Dei mandatis carnem in consilium adhibeant. Hæc præfentifsima pestis est. Vide Saulem,1. Sam.13.15. Econtra sapientia vera est,Deum timere & huic obedire,Prou.1. Deut. 4.Num,15. At hic feré offendimus.
units.tr: Note: the obedience of faith. For Christ had so commanded. Yet many things could terrify them: danger, the inconvenience of the place and want. Likewise, that the Spirit is not bound to a place (John 3). Nor is there any doubt that all these thoughts crept upon them according to the nature of the flesh, and so on. But they overcome all these things through faith, and success is not lacking. From this a general rule is drawn: that we obey God simply when he commands something. For because he is good and a father, he commands nothing but what is good and useful (1 Tim. 2; Ps. 119). Because he is also faithful and almighty, he protects those who walk in their calling, and does not allow them to be tempted beyond their strength, and so on (1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1). Examples are everywhere: Abraham (Gen. 12), and so on; Ps. 105. Let each one apply these things to himself, lest in God's commands he take counsel from the flesh. This is the most present plague. See Saul (1 Sam. 13, 15). On the contrary, true wisdom is to fear God and obey him (Prov. 1; Deut. 4; Num. 15). But here we nearly stumble.

units.la: II. Nomina recensentur, nimirum vt sciremus in gratiam esse receptos. Poterat enim de eo dubitari propter ea quæ fe cerant,Matt.26.&c.Ne ergo illorum vitia doctrinæ fraudi effent, ijdé recensentur qui prius Mat.10.Luc. 9. Vno Iuda excepto.
units.tr: II. The names are listed, namely so that we may know they had been received back into favour. For doubt could have arisen about them because of what they had done (Matt. 26, and so on). So that their faults might not be a cause of harm to the doctrine, the same men are listed who were named before (Matt. 10; Luke 9), with Judas alone excepted.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ 1. Bonitatem Dei,non igno-scentis modó,sed etiam restituentis.Vide Ioh.21.Sic gratia abundat,vbi delicta, &c. Rom 5.Pfalm. 130. Nemo igitur desperet, Zach.1,Ezech.18.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The goodness of God, which not only forgives but also restores. See John 21. Thus grace abounds where sins abound (Rom. 5). Ps. 130. Let no one therefore despair (Zech. 1; Ezek. 18).

units.la: § 2. Viles & ignobiles modò recenseri. Piscatores, Publicanos. Atqui poterat quosuis alios vocare Christus. Sed docet partim se neminem fastidire (Pf. 113. Luc. 1.) partim de fide & religione non ex hominum authoritate, sed verbo Dei esse iu dicandum. Ohsceruandum hoc propter eos, qui nobis aduersariorum potentiam, gloriam, opes, obijciunt, & nostrorum hominum tenuitatem exprobrant. Sic olim Sacerdotes, Ioh.7. Nihil ergo hoc nouum est. Vide i.Reg.18.22. Nos in his consilium agnoscamus, 1.Cor.1. Et dum illi haec tonant, nos cum Christo praedicemus Dei bonitatem, Mat.11.&c.
units.tr: § 2. They are listed as humble and lowly men: fishermen, tax collectors. Yet Christ could have called any others. But he teaches, partly, that he despises no one (Ps. 113; Luke 1), and partly that in matters of faith and religion one must judge not by human authority but by the word of God. This is to be observed on account of those who throw in our faces the power, glory and wealth of our adversaries, and reproach our men for their lowliness. So the priests of old did (John 7). Nothing therefore is new in this. See 1 Kings 18:22. In these matters let us acknowledge the counsel (of God) (1 Cor. 1). And while they thunder these things, let us, with Christ, proclaim the goodness of God (Matt. 11, and so on).

units.la: III. Mulierum fit mentio. Fuerunt ex Galilaea, Luc.23.24. Item vxores Apostolorum, de quibus 1 Cor.9. Quia ergo laborum sociae futurae erant, iplas etiam Spiritu sancto praeparari & confirmari oportuit. Additur his Maria virgo cum fratribus, id est, cognatis Christi, Mar.6.
units.tr: III. Mention is made of women. They were from Galilee (Luke 23, 24), and likewise the wives of the apostles, of whom 1 Cor. 9 speaks. Since therefore they were to be companions in their labours, it was fitting that they too be prepared and strengthened by the Holy Spirit. To these is added Mary the virgin with the brothers, that is, the kinsmen of Christ (Mark 6).

units.la: NOTA.§1. Hic postremam fieri Mariae mentionem, cum Apostolorum res diligentissimè describantur. Voluit ergo Deus superstitionibus occurrere, quæ postea exortæ sunt, & nos ad Apostolorum doctrinam remittere.
units.tr: NOTE. § 1. Here Mary is mentioned for the last time, although the affairs of the apostles are described very carefully. God therefore wished to forestall the superstitions that arose afterwards, and to refer us back to the doctrine of the apostles.

units.la: § 2. Christum matri suæ & fratribus præ-
units.tr: § 2. That Christ gave to his mother and brothers

units.la: præsidium dedisse tam infirmum, Ioh.19. Atqui Regi alicui illos committere poterat, vt Dauid 1.Sam.22. Sed qui in animos ius habet, contra quosuis tueri poterit. Et hæc tutela fuit sufficies. Interim fuit hic typus Ecclesiæ, quæ fere deserta videtur. Sed sem per cogita quid Christus promiserit, Ioh. 14. Matt.28. Dic quod Dauid Psal.27.118.
units.tr: such a weak protection (John 19). Yet he could have committed them to some king, as David did (1 Sam. 22). But he who has right over minds will be able to protect them against anyone. And this protection was sufficient. Meanwhile, here was a type of the Church, which seems almost deserted. But always consider what Christ has promised (John 14; Matt. 28). Say with David what he says (Ps. 27, 118).

units.la: IIII. Quid interea fecerunt? Perseuerā runt vnanimiter in precatione: Nimirum vt spiritum Deus mitteret, &c.
units.tr: IV. What did they do meanwhile? They persevered unanimously in prayer, namely that God would send the Spirit, and so on.

units.la: NOTA. 1.Hoc de iis dici, qui promiserunt. Fides non fiones acceperant, & illis credebant. Fides obstat, quia ergo non obstat precibus & operibus bonis. Imo nisi credamus, non poterimus orare, Mar.11 Iac.1. Psal.116. Similiter qui Deo fidunt per Christum, ij eundem amant, seq; totos illi consecrant (Rom.12.) qui bonorum operum fons est, Ioh.15.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. This is said of those who had been promised. They had received the promise and believed those who gave it. Faith does not hinder prayers; rather, unless we believe we cannot pray (Mark 11; James 1; Ps. 116). Similarly, those who trust God through Christ love him and consecrate themselves wholly to him (Rom. 12), which is the source of good works (John 15).

units.la: 2. Quales in precibus fuerint? 1.Vna- nimes. Opus eo, quia eiusdem Patris filij sumus qui cum charitas sit, dissidentes no fert. Hinc illud Matthæi 5. Et in oratione Dominica eiusdem admonemur. 2.Per seuerarunt Opus etiam isto, quia Deus sæpius opem promissam differt, &c. Tunc illæ voces etiam pijs excidunt, Psalm.13. 22.Hab.1. Sed non potest eorum obliuisci Deus, quos Filij sanguine redemit, Isa.49.
units.tr: 2. What were they like in their prayers? 1. Unanimous. This is needed, because we are sons of the same Father, and since charity is the bond, it does not tolerate dissent. Hence that saying of Matthew 5, and in the Lord's Prayer we are admonished of the same. 2. They persevered. This too is needed, because God often defers the help he has promised, and so on. Then those cries escape even the pious (Ps. 13, 22; Hab. 1). But God cannot forget those whom he redeemed with the blood of his Son (Isa. 49).

units.la: Psal.56.Differt autem interdum, vt fidem nostram exerceat, & quia adhuc castigatio ne opus habemus, Heb.12. Tunc ergo neruos fidei intendere oportet, & quodammodo luctari cum Deo, vt de Iacobo scribitur Gen.32.Hos.12. Sic iubet Christus, Luc.18.Matth 8.Obseruemus hodie. Instant vndique pericula. Multi tentantur, languent. Multi toti deprauati sunt. Opus Spiritu Dei. Vigilemus vnanimes & assiduè Oremus.
units.tr: Ps. 56. He sometimes defers in order to exercise our faith, and because we still have need of chastisement (Heb. 12). Then therefore one must strain the sinews of faith and in some way wrestle with God, as is written of Jacob (Gen. 32; Hos. 12). So Christ commands (Luke 18; Matt. 8). Let us observe this today. Dangers press in from every side. Many are tempted and languish; many are utterly corrupted. This work belongs to the Spirit of God. Let us watch unanimously and pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA VII.
units.tr: HOMILY VII.

units.la: 15 Et per eos dies assurgens Petrus in medio discipulorum, dixit (erat autem turba nominum simul ferè centum viginti.)
units.tr: 15 And in those days Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples and said (and there was a crowd of about one hundred and twenty names together).

units.la: 16 Viri fratres, oportuit impleri scripturam hanc, quam prædixit Spiritus sanctus per os Dauidis, de Iuda, qui fuit dux eorum qui comprehenderunt Iesum, &c. Act. 1.
units.tr: 16 Men, brothers, this Scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit foretold by the mouth of David, concerning Judas, who was the guide of those who seized Jesus, etc. Acts 1.

units.la: EXposuit Luc. quid Apostoli fecerint post Christi ascensionem, interea dum Spiritus sancti missionem expectarunt. Manserunt Hierosolymis vt ille iusserat. Vnanimes fuerunt, atque perseuerarunt in precibus, Hæc sunt Christianorum exerexercitia, quibus nos quoq; intentos esse decet. Sequitur modo, quid primum sece rint inter ea, quae ad ipsorum munus pertinebant: Vt nimirum Matth. furrogârint in locum Iudae. Quia enim Christus xii. elegerat propter iz Israel. Matth. 19. numerum hunc impleri oportuit, ne Iudae impietas Christi instituto aliquid derogasse videretur.
units.tr: Luke has set out what the apostles did after Christ's ascension, while they waited for the sending of the Holy Spirit. They remained in Jerusalem as he had commanded. They were of one accord and persevered in prayers. These are the exercises of Christians, and we too ought to be devoted to them. Next he relates what they first did, among those things that belonged to their office: namely, that they substituted someone in the place of Judas. For since Christ had chosen twelve, for the twelve tribes of Israel (Matt. 19), this number had to be filled, lest the impiety of Judas seem to have detracted something from Christ's institution.

units.la: Discimus, in Ecclesia primam curam esse debere, vt doctores sint idonei. Etsi enim Deus solus fidem donet (Ioh. 6. Isa. 54.) id tamen facit per verbi praedicatio-nem, Rom. 10. 1. Cor. 3. Ideo hoc inter Dei beneficia maxima praedicatur semper, Mi-chae 6. Eph. 4. &c. Huius ergo memine-rint, quibus Ecclesiae cura credita est, &c. vt vero eligi debeant, hic discemus.
units.tr: We learn that in the Church the first care must be that the teachers are fit. For although God alone gives faith (John 6; Isa. 54), he does so through the preaching of the Word (Rom. 10; 1 Cor. 3). Therefore this is always proclaimed among God's greatest benefits (Micah 6; Eph. 4, etc.). Let those to whom the care of the Church has been entrusted remember this, etc. How they ought to be chosen, we shall learn here.

units.la: I. Qui nam elegerint? Tota nimirum Ecclesia, quae fuit izo. hominum, ad quos hanc causam Petrus, &c.
units.tr: I. Who then chose them? Surely the whole Church, which was about one hundred and twenty men, to whom Peter addressed this matter, etc.

units.la: NOTA. Paucitatem credentium in vrbe populosissima. Atqui nihil in ea intentatum reliquit Deus. Dedit prophetas. Sequutus Baptista, Isa. 4o. Mal. 4. Ipse Dei Filius, qui & docuit & doctrinam mi raculis confirmauit, Ioh. 3, 7. Prodigia in morte, Mat. 27. At his omnibus tam pauci lucri facti sunt, & hi quidem plerique ex
units.tr: NOTE. The small number of believers in a very populous city. Yet God left nothing untried in it. He gave prophets. John the Baptist followed (Isa. 40; Mal. 4). The Son of God himself, who both taught and confirmed his teaching by miracles (John 3, 7). Portents at his death (Matt. 27). Yet despite all these, so few were gained, and most of these were foreigners.

units.la: peregrinis.Hoc illud est, de quo Ifa.53.24. Discimus de fide & religione non iudicandum esse ex feftatorum numero,digni tate.Semper enim pauciores veritatem fe cuti sunt.Noe,Loth,Patriarchæ.Prophetarum tempora,1.Reg.18 22.Ifa.8.&c. Et Christus hoc prædixit,Luc.12.18.Dei ver bum respiciatur,&c.
units.tr: This is what Isa. 53.24 speaks of. We learn that judgment about faith and religion is not to be made from the number of adherents, but from their worth. For the truth has always been followed by fewer. Noah, Lot, the patriarchs. The times of the prophets (1 Kings 18, 22; Isa. 8, etc.). And Christ foretold this (Luke 12.18). Let regard be had to the word of God, etc.

units.la: II. Petrus surgit & hanc causam refert adEcclefiam.Id vero no fecit vt princeps, sed ex spiritus suggestione, qui exemplû gratiæ in illo propositum sic illustrari voluit. Alioqui ratum manet,quod Christus pronuntiauit Luc.22. Et hoc ipse Petrus agnouit, vt eius verba de Iuda testantur, & 2.Pet.5.Paulus item Gal.2.1.Cor.3.
units.tr: II. Peter stands up and refers this matter to the Church. He did this not as a prince, but at the prompting of the Spirit, who wished the example of grace set forth in him to be thus illustrated. Otherwise what Christ pronounced in Luke 22 remains valid. Peter himself acknowledged this, as his words about Judas bear witness; see also 2 Pet. 5; likewise Paul, Gal. 2; 1 Cor. 3.

units.la: Quoad orationem, duæ sunt partes: 1. Medetur scandalo, quod Iudas dederat. 2. Iubet alium surrogari,ne Christi institu to quid defit. Nunc priorem partem videamus.
units.tr: As to the speech, it has two parts: 1. He remedies the scandal that Judas had given. 2. He bids that another be substituted, lest anything be lacking to Christ's institution. Let us now look at the first part.

units.la: 2. Orditur à scriptura testimonio,quo ita à Deo decretum fuisse docet. Quasi di cat:Nolo vos offendi,quasi hæc temerè fa cтa sint,vel Dei filius à Iuda fit circumuen tus. Aut quod huius scelus nostræ functioni derogari debeat. Ita enim olim fuit decretum, & scitis quid prædictum Pfal. 41. cuius ipse Dominus meminit in Cœna,Ioh.13.
units.tr: 2. He begins from the testimony of Scripture, by which he shows that it was so decreed by God. As if he said: "I do not want you to be offended, as if these things were done rashly, or as if the Son of God had been circumvented by Judas, or as if the wickedness of this man ought to detract from our office. For so it was decreed of old, and you know what was foretold in Ps. 41, which the Lord himself recalled at the Supper (John 13)."

units.la: Vbi Nota.¶ Petrum hoc non ideo di cere,vt scelus Iudæ in Deu reijciat. Quan do enim impij peccant,id propria malitia faciunt. Quòd Deus ipsorum opera benè vtitur ad suorum decretorum executionem,id ipsius sapientiæ & bonitati debet tribui,&c. Oportuit Christum pati, &c. Luc.24. Sed Iudas motus est auaritia,&c. Iohannis 12. Vide Matthæi 26. Eadem ratio Sacerdotum,Pilati, &c. Simile exemplum in Iosepho & fratribus,Psal.105. Ge. 50 Ita hodie multa,&c. Vsus istorum,ne offendamur impiorum succesiuus, consolationem verò habeamus ex Dei proui dentia,Iob.1.2.&c.
units.tr: Here note: Peter does not say this so as to throw the crime of Judas back upon God. For when the wicked sin, they do so by their own malice. That God makes good use of their works for the execution of his decrees must be attributed to his wisdom and goodness, etc. "It behoved Christ to suffer" (Luke 24). But Judas was moved by avarice, etc. (John 12). See Matt. 26. The same reasoning applies to the priests, to Pilate, etc. A similar example is found in Joseph and his brothers (Ps. 105; Gen. 50). So today many things, etc. The use of these things is that we should not be offended by the continued success of the wicked, but rather have consolation from God's providence (Job 1, 2, etc.).

units.la: 2. Iudæ dignitatem priorem exponit, ne quis eum propter numerum modo,co optatum putaret. Itaque partem ministerij eum habuisse dicit. Vide Matth.10. Luc 6.} Mar.14.&c. Obseruandum hoc, ne quis Dei instituta damnet, si qui in illis peccant. Faciunt hoc Anabaptistæ, quoad magistratum. Qui item matrimonium reijciunt.
units.tr: 2. He sets forth Judas's former dignity, lest anyone think he had been counted in only for the sake of the number. Therefore he says that Judas had a share in the ministry. See Matt. 10; Luke 6; Mark 14, etc. This must be observed, lest anyone condemn God's institutions because some sin within them. The Anabaptists do this with regard to the magistracy, and likewise they reject marriage.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Sortem fidelium. Fe- rè suos sibi inimicos esse sentiunt. Abel, Ge.4.Isaac,Ge.21 Gal.4 Iacob,Ge 27.28. Iosepf,Ge.37.Dauid,Psal.41.55 Ita nobis Christus prædixit, Matthæi 10. Lucæ 12.
units.tr: Meanwhile note the lot of the faithful: they almost always find their own kin to be their enemies. Abel (Gen. 4), Isaac (Gen. 21; Gal. 4), Jacob (Gen. 27, 28), Joseph (Gen. 37), David (Ps. 41, 55). So Christ foretold to us (Matt. 10; Luke 12).

units.la: Causa notatur,Ioh.3. Offendunt hæc multos,ut vel de doctrina dubitent,vel fidelium morositati hoc tribuant. Sed quid fiat nobis, quando idem Christo accidit, Ioh.1. Interim piorum est, pacem sectari cum omnibus,Rom.12. Oremus.
units.tr: The cause is noted (John 3). These things offend many, so that they either doubt the doctrine or ascribe this to the peevishness of the faithful. But what happens to us when the same thing happened to Christ (John 1)? Meanwhile it is the mark of the godly to seek peace with all (Rom. 12). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA VIII.
units.tr: HOMILY VIII.

units.la: 18 Is igitur acquisiuit agrum ex mercede iniustitiæ, & præcipitatus cre puit medius, & effusa sunt omnia viscera eius.
units.tr: Now this man acquired a field with the reward of his iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst open in the middle, and all his bowels gushed out.

units.la: 10 Innotuit omnibus habitantibus Hierosolymæ, adeo ut vocetur ager ille proprius ipsorum lingua, Acceldama, hoc est, ager sanguinis, &c. ad ver. 23.
units.tr: It became known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their own language Aceldama, that is, the field of blood, etc. To verse 23.

units.la: OVoniam Apostoli nostræ redemptionis, quæ per Christum facta est, testes esse debuerunt, vtile & necessarium est, vt illos legitime ad hoc ordinatos fuisse sciamus. Alioqui nulla erit testimonium ipsorum authoritas. Ideo multa de illis dicuntur, Matt. 4.9.10. Luc.9. Ioh.15. 20.&c. At quia de Matthia dubitari poterat, huius quoque ordinationem Lucas describit. In hac præcipuum est, quod Petrus hanc rem ad Ecclesiam retulit, quæ vnanimi consensu cum precibus Dei suf-fragium fragium quæsiuit. Vnde colligitur, quod quicquid fecerunt, Dei auspicijs factum sit,secundum illud Psal.133.Matth. 18. & ideo Matthiam germanum esse Christi Apostolum.
units.tr: Since the Apostles were to be witnesses of our redemption, which was accomplished through Christ, it is useful and necessary that we know they were lawfully appointed to this office. Otherwise their testimony would have no authority. So much is said about them at Matthew 4:9-10, Luke 9, John 15:20, etc. But because Matthias' appointment could be doubted, Luke also describes his ordination. The chief point here is that Peter referred the matter to the Church, which, with one accord, sought the suffrage of God with prayers. From this it is gathered that whatever they did was done under God's auspices, according to that of Psalm 133 and Matthew 18; and therefore Matthias is a true Apostle of Christ.

units.la: ¶ Discimus pro Dei seruis habendos esse, quotquot etiam hodie legitimè ab Ecclesia ordinantur. Quoad vero Petri orationem, constat ea duabus partibus. Prima scandalum remouet quod ex Iudæis nascebatur, idque argumentis duob. 1. Quòd nihil temere sit factum, sed ex Dei decreto. 2. Quòd Iudas poenas dederit, similiter à Deo ipsi decretas. Id nunc explicat, nimirum vt Dei timorem omnibus commendet.
units.tr: We learn that all who are now lawfully ordained by the Church are to be regarded as servants of God. As for Peter's speech, it consists of two parts. The first removes the scandal arising among the Jews, and does so by two arguments: (1) that nothing was done rashly, but by the decree of God; (2) that Judas has paid the penalty, likewise decreed for him by God. He now explains this, namely in order to commend the fear of God to all.

units.la: Et is quidem possedit, &c. Paucis comprehendit historiam Matth. 27. Concur. runt multa, quæ docent, quam horribiliter Deus vltus sit Filij sui mortem indignam. 1. Domestici hostis excitat conscientiam. Huius terrores pecuniæ odium pariunt, confessione peccati extorquent, & vitæ tædium ferunt. 2. Ipse sibi mortem consciscit. 3. Crepat medius, &c. 4. Emitur ager, ex quo æterna infamia. Hunc posse diffe dicitur, quia eius pecunia emptus, ipsum in primis diffamauit. Omnibus enim res innotuit, &c. Matt. 10. His additur
units.tr: And he indeed possessed a field, etc. He briefly sums up the history of Matthew 27. Many things combine to teach how dreadfully God avenged the unworthy death of his Son. (1) An enemy from within stirs up his conscience. Its terrors produce hatred of the money, extort a confession of sin, and bring weariness of life. (2) He takes his own death. (3) He burst open in the middle, etc. (4) The field is bought, from which comes eternal infamy. It is said that he himself made it known, because, having been bought with his money, he first of all spread the infamy of it. For the matter became known to all, etc., Matthew 10. To this is added

units.la: C
units.tr: C

units.la: testimonium ex Psalm. 69 & 109.
units.tr: the testimony from Psalms 69 and 109.

units.la: NOTA. Figuratum hic fuisse quid eorum venturum sit vniuersis Christi hostibus, qui suis commodis consulunt piorum fan guine. Prouocant Christi iudicium, qui id non ferre potest, Zach. 1. Act 9. Hinc conscientiæ terrores, incertitudo consiliorum, & quod omnia sibi infelta sentiunt, Ila. 48. 57. Crepant medij, & ipsi sibi perditionis authores sunt, Psal. 33. 2. Zach. 12. Et quia Christum abijciunt, vnà vita æterna spo liantur, Ioh. 3. Mar. 16. Domus excinditur, vt vel memoria intereat, vel fœtida sit, & de illorum impietate teftan ur opes, ædifi cia, &c. Ioel. 2. Acciderunt hæc omnia Sacerdotibus & toti Iudæorum genti, sicuti Christus prædixerat, Mat. 23 21 24. Luc. 19. Postea Imperatoribus quoq; Romanis, & ipsi Romæ. Et nostro tempore huius generis multa vidimus publicè & priuatim in ijs, qui ex sanguine ditescunt, Habac. 2. Mich. 6. Transferuntur ad alios quæ habent, (Luc. 12.) in primis vero nihil præter infamem memoriam remanet.
units.tr: NOTE. Here it was foreshadowed what will come upon all of Christ's enemies, who look to their own advantage at the cost of the blood of the godly. They provoke the judgment of Christ, which he cannot bear, Zechariah 1; Acts 9. Hence come terrors of conscience, uncertainty of counsels, and the sense that all things turn out unfavourably for them, Isaiah 48 and 57. They burst open in the middle, and they themselves are the authors of their own destruction, Psalm 33; Zechariah 12. And because they reject Christ, they are at once deprived of eternal life, John 3; Mark 16. Their house is laid waste, so that either its memory perishes or it becomes foul; and their wealth, buildings, etc., bear witness to their impiety, Joel 2. All these things happened to the priests and to the whole Jewish nation, just as Christ had foretold, Matthew 23:21-24; Luke 19. Afterwards it happened to the Roman emperors too, and to Rome itself. And in our own time we have seen many things of this kind, both publicly and privately, in those who grow rich from blood, Habakkuk 2; Micah 6. What they have is transferred to others (Luke 12), and above all nothing remains but an infamous memory.

units.la: § 2. Quæ ratio sit tutissima retinendi suam authoritatem? Necessaria doctrina hodie, &c. Sed audi Christū Matt. 25. 1. Sa. 2. Impletum in Iudaicis Sacerdotibus. Hodie in Ecclesiasticis & politicis. Paretibus item. Qui ergo suæ existimatiōni consultū volunt, Deo fideles sint, officium faciant.
units.tr: § 2. What is the safest way of keeping one's authority? "A necessary doctrine today," etc. But hear Christ at Matthew 25; 1 Samuel 2, fulfilled in the Jewish priests. Today it is fulfilled in ecclesiastical and civil officials, and likewise in parents. Therefore those who want to look after their reputation should be faithful to God and do their duty.

units.la: Quia autem prædistum de Iuda fuit. Et Omnis Episcopatum eius, &c. ex eo Petrus alte-ram partem infert, qua hortatur, vt alium surrogent: Oportet ergo, &c. Argumenti vis ex eo dependet, quod ipsis Ecclesiæ suæ curam Christus commiserat, Luc. 12. Matth. 24. Ioh. 20. 21.
units.tr: But because what was foretold about Judas, "And let his bishopric," etc., Peter draws from this the second part, in which he urges that another be appointed in his place: "It is necessary therefore," etc. The force of the argument depends on the fact that Christ had committed the care of his Church to them, Luke 12; Matthew 24; John 20 and 21.

units.la: ¶ Discimus vt ipsi quoq; debeamus in Scripturis versari. Sic nimirum, vt in no stram vocationem intenti ad nos transfe-ramus quicquid ad eam pertinet. Este-nim Scriptura propter nos data, Rom. 15. 2. Tim. 3. Obseruent ministri, quæ de Prophetis & Apostolis dicuntur, Ezech. 3. Ie-rem. 1. Magistratus item &c. Psalm. 72. 82. Singuli item.
units.tr: We learn that we too ought to occupy ourselves with the Scriptures, in such a way that, attentive to our own calling, we apply to ourselves whatever pertains to it. For Scripture was given for our sake, Romans 15; 2 Timothy 3. Let ministers observe what is said of the Prophets and Apostles, Ezekiel 3; Jeremiah 1. Likewise the magistrates, etc., Psalms 72 and 82. Likewise each individual.

units.la: Interim NOTA. ¶ 1. Qualem velit eli-gi: Ex ijs qui nobiscum fuerunt, &c. Duo re quirit. 1. Cognitionem solidam Christi & omnium quæ fecit, &c. Ne quis tamen cu risiūs hæc latiūs extenderet, terminos ponit, Baptismum & Ascensionem. In Baptismo demum initiatus est, Matt. 3. Quo ad puerilem ætatem, sufficiunt quę haben tur Luc. 1. 2. Matt. 1. 2. Arguuntur Monachi fabulatores. 2. Perseuerantiam. Nec enim vult aliquem eligi ex ijs, qui defecerant.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE. (1) What sort of person he wishes to be chosen: "from those who have been with us," etc. He requires two things. (1) A solid knowledge of Christ and of all that he did, etc. Yet lest anyone extend this too broadly, he sets limits: Baptism and the Ascension. He was initiated only at Baptism, Matthew 3. As for childhood, what is recorded in Luke 1 and 2 and Matthew 1 and 2 is sufficient. The fabulous monks are refuted. (2) Perseverance. For he does not want anyone chosen from among those who had fallen away.

units.la: (Ioh.6.)aut nouitium. Obseruanda hæc etiam hodie. Primas hic tenet doctrina, Mal.2.Mat.28.Opus ergo cognitione cer ta.Deinde docendi facultate i.Tim.3.Tit. 1.2.Tim.3. Quia item functio hæc laboris & periculi plena est, perseuerantia requiritur,Luc.9.lere.1.Ideo neophyti reijciun tur,1.Tim.3.
units.tr: (John 6) or a novice. These things are to be observed today as well. Doctrine holds the first place here, Malachi 2; Matthew 28. Therefore sure knowledge is needed. Then the capacity to teach, 1 Timothy 3; Titus 1 and 2; 2 Timothy 3. Since this office is also full of toil and danger, perseverance is required, Luke 9; Jeremiah 1. Therefore neophytes are rejected, 1 Timothy 3.

units.la: Officium: Vt sit nobis cum testis resurrectionis. A Nobis cum Collegam ergo vult habere,non seruum. Sic 1.Pet.5. B Testis, Id ad Euangelij certitudinem facit,& eos arguit qui contradicunt. C Resurrectionis Huius in primis meminit, quia vt nostræ redemptionis complementum habet; Ita eam Iudæi maxime negabant, Acto.3.4.5. &c.Obseruanda hæc ministris. Se mutuo agnoscant pro collegis,& iuuent. Testes sint fideles & fortes etiam in ijs,quæ mun do minus arridēt, Gal.1. Reliqui omnes agnoscant Dei beneficium in filio suo nobis exhibitum, & quod per Euangelium quotidie nobis offert.Grati simus,obedia-mus,Oremus.
units.tr: Office: that he may be with us a witness of the resurrection. A: "with us": he therefore wants a colleague, not a servant. So 1 Peter 5. B: "witness": this contributes to the certainty of the Gospel and refutes those who contradict it. C: he mentions especially the resurrection, because it is the completion of our redemption; and the Jews above all denied it, Acts 3, 4 and 5, etc. These points are to be observed by ministers: let them acknowledge one another as colleagues and help one another. Let them be faithful and brave as witnesses, even in matters that please the world less, Galatians 1. Let all the rest acknowledge God's benefit exhibited to us in his Son, and which he offers to us daily through the Gospel. Let us be thankful and obedient. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA IX.
units.tr: HOMILIA IX.

units.la: 23 Statuerunt igitur duos, Ioseph qui vocabatur Barsabas,qui cognominatus est Iustus, & Matthiam.
units.tr: 23 So they put forward two men, Joseph, called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

units.la: 24 Et precantes dixerunt, Tu Domine, qui corda omnium nouisti, ostende de vtrum elegeris ex his duobus.
units.tr: 24 And praying, they said, "You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which of these two you have chosen,

units.la: 25 Vt accipiat sortem ministerij huius & Apostolatus, a quo aberrauit Iudas, vt abiret in locum suum.
units.tr: 25 to take up the lot of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas turned aside, to go to his own place."

units.la: 26 Lecerunt igitur sortes eorum: et cecidit sors super Matthiam, qui communibus calculis allectus est cum vndecim Apostolis.
units.tr: 26 And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

units.la: VT Ecclesia verbi ministris opus habet, per quos colligatur & in fide vera conseruetur: Ita eosdem legitimè oportet, vt ipsos diuinitus missos esse constet. Quae causa est, quod in Matthiae electione tam religiose egit primitiua Ecclesia. Et voluit historiam hanc describi Deus, vt formulam habeamus, quae semper obseruetur. In hac primum occurrit quod Petrus hanc causam ad totam Ecclesiam refert. Admonemur, nihil in Ecclesia cuiusquam authoritate priuata debere statui. Est enim hęc sponsa Dei, Psal. 45. & ideo ei nihil inuitæ, nihil contra Dei voluntate obtrudi debet. Hoc enim non fert Deus, qui Zelotes est, Exod. 20. Nah. 1. Sequitur.
units.tr: Just as the Church needs ministers of the Word, through whom it is gathered and preserved in the true faith, so these men ought to be lawfully called, so that it is evident they have been sent by God. This is why the early Church acted so scrupulously in the election of Matthias. God also willed this history to be recorded, so that we might have a pattern that is always to be observed. In it we see first that Peter refers this matter to the whole Church. We are reminded that nothing should be decided in the Church by anyone's private authority. The Church is God's bride (Ps. 45), and so nothing should be forced upon her against her will, nothing against the will of God. For God, who is a jealous God (Exod. 20; Nah. 1), does not bear this. It follows.

units.la: I. Statuerunt duos, & c. Factum hoc viri- tim dictis sententijs, & ita in his duobus consenserunt,qui reliquis erant præstan-tiores, &c. Hos deinde produxerunt in medium.
units.tr: I. "They put forward two," and so on. This was done by the votes of individuals, and in this way they agreed on these two, who were superior to the rest, and so on. Then they brought them forward into the midst.

units.la: II.Rem omnem ad Deum referunt,nec adhuc quisquam sibi ius eligendi vendi-cat.Sed ad preces conuertuntur; Tu Do-mine, mine,qui nouisti,&c.Ergo ministrorum ec-lectio ad Deum vnum debet referri. {1}. Ecclesia Dei domus est, in qua illi seruiunt,Matth.24.1.Cor.4.Quis vero tam insolens est, vt alienæ domui ipse velit obtrudere œconomum. {2}.Animus maxime spectandus. At hunc solus Deus nouit,Iere.17.Psal.7.Iere.11.20.&c.Falluntur hic etiam occulatissimi,vt apparet in Apostolis quoad ludam. Interim meminerint omnes improbi, Deum nihil latere, nec falli posse,&c. {3}. Authoritatem hoc consiliat ministris. Nemo enim potest suspectum habere eum,qui sic eligitur. Ita nec contemnere aut odisse. Similiter hoc ministris animum addit,& excitat ne segnescant,Ezech.3.Iere.1.Matt.10 Luc.21.Hinc illa prophetarum animositas,Amos 3.7. &c. Apostolorum,Act.4.5.2.Cor.5. &c. Qui ipsi currunt,aut ab hominum fauore pendent,quouis periculo terrentur,& hominibus placere volunt,Gal.1. Potest idem de Magistratibus dici.Vide Dauidem, Ps. 2. &c. Singuli ergo vocationem suam exspectent,& in ea fideles sint & fortes.
units.tr: II. They refer the whole matter to God, and no one yet claims for himself the right of choosing. Instead they turn to prayer: "You, Lord, who know the hearts of all," and so on. Therefore the choice of ministers ought to be referred to the one God. (1) The Church is God's house, in which these men serve (Matt. 24; 1 Cor. 4). Who would be so insolent as to thrust a steward on another man's house? (2) The disposition of the heart is above all to be considered. But God alone knows it (Jer. 17; Ps. 7; Jer. 11.20, etc.). Even the most sharp-sighted are deceived here, as appears in the apostles with regard to Judas. Meanwhile, let all wicked men remember that nothing is hidden from God, and that he cannot be deceived, etc. (3) This lends authority to ministers. For no one can hold in suspicion, or despise or hate, one who is chosen in this way. Likewise it gives courage to ministers and rouses them so that they do not grow slack (Ezek. 3; Jer. 1; Matt. 10; Luke 21). Hence the boldness of the prophets (Amos 3.7, etc.) and of the apostles (Acts 4, 5; 2 Cor. 5, etc.). Those who run of their own accord, or depend on the favour of men, are terrified by every danger and want to please men (Gal. 1). The same can be said of magistrates. See David, Ps. 2, etc. Let each therefore await his own calling, and be faithful and brave in it.

units.la: III. Sortes iaciunt.Vbi No T. {4} Sortes esse diuersi generis.1. Sunt illicitæ,quando artibus curiosis & superstitiosis scruta mur quæ nihil ad nos pertinent.Huc refer
units.tr: III. They cast lots. Here NOTE: (4) lots are of different kinds. (1) Some are unlawful, when by curious and superstitious arts we pry into things that do not concern us. Refer here

units.la: {4} Sors mini-steri & apostolatus geomantes,ariolos,Meonenim.Hi omnes damnantur,Deut.18.Mich.5.Isa.8. 2.Lici-tæ,quibus rei necessariæ cognitu euentus absque omni superstitione ad Dei iudici-um refertur,vt vel authoritas maior fit eo rum,qui rei alicui destinantur,vel vt lites caueantur. De his Prou.18. Vsus harum antiquissimus. Vide Ioh.i.Romani pro-uincias sortiebantur, vt hodie quidam. Sortibus item terra diuisa,Num.33.Et ho-die ijsdem pij vtuntur. Non ergo pecca-runt isti,&c.
units.tr: (4) the lot of the ministry and of the apostleship. Here belong geomancers, soothsayers, and observers of times (Meonenim). All of these are condemned (Deut. 18; Mic. 5; Isa. 8). (2) Lawful lots are those by which the outcome of a matter that needs to be known is referred to God's judgment, without any superstition, either so that the authority of those designated for some task is greater, or so that disputes are avoided. On these see Prov. 18. The use of them is most ancient; see John 1. The Romans allotted provinces, as some still do today. Land was also divided by lot (Num. 33), and godly people use the same means today. Therefore those men did not sin, etc.

units.la: ¶ Prouidentia Dei, quæ has gubernat, Prou.16. Hinc colligenihil fieri fortuito, Mat.10.Luc.12. Huc etiam tempestates & prouentus frugum pertinet,Psal.104.147. Discamus ergo rectè iudicare de omni-bus.Vide Deut.18.Leuit 26.
units.tr: ¶ The providence of God, which governs these, is taught in Prov. 16. From this we gather that nothing happens by chance (Matt. 10; Luke 12). To this also belong storms and the yield of crops (Ps. 104, 147). Let us learn therefore to judge rightly of all things. See Deut. 18; Lev. 26.

units.la: IIII. Matthias designatur. At videtur hominū iudicio præstare Iosephus,quem Barsab.id est,iurisiurandi filium dixerunt & cognomine Iustum. Et primus videtur nominatus fuisse.Sed non statim Deo pro-batur quod hominibus,1.Sam.16.&c.
units.tr: IV. Matthias is designated. But in human judgement Joseph seems to be preferable, whom they called Barsabbas, that is, son of the oath, and surnamed Justus. And he seems to have been named first. But what pleases men is not at once approved by God (1 Sam. 16, and so on).

units.la: Nota. ¶ 1. Nemo hominum existima-tione superbiat.Falluntur hi sæpe. Vel a-lioqui mutant sententiam, Psal.116. Cura fit,vt Deo probemur,qui humilibus gau-det,Psal.113.1.Cor.1. ¶ 2 Barsabas non murmurat, nec etiam illi, quiab eius parte steterant. Sciebat vtique se in alijs posse seruire. Ita nos no-stra sorte contenti simus, nec ægre fera-mus interdum alios nobis præferri. Vide exemplum Spartani cuiusdam.Qui alti o-ra affectant modis illicitis, ferè grauiter ruunt.Prouer.16 Habent singulì abundè quod agant in sua vocatione. In ea ergo seduli simus, vigilemus, & vt Deus nos regat,Oremus.
units.tr: Note. 1. No one should be puffed up by the esteem of men. They are often deceived; or else they change their opinion (Ps. 116). Care must be taken that we be approved by God, who delights in the humble (Ps. 113; 1 Cor. 1). 2. Barsabbas does not complain, nor do those who had stood on his side. He knew that he could serve in other ways. So let us be content with our own lot, and not bear it with resentment when others are sometimes set before us. See the example of a certain Spartan, who, aspiring to high honours by unlawful means, generally falls headlong (Prov. 16). Each one has enough to do in his own calling. Let us therefore be diligent in it and watchful, and let us pray that God may rule us. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: Homilia x.
units.tr: Homily x.

units.la: CVm autem aduenisset dies Pen-tecostes,erant omnes concorditer eodem loci.
units.tr: When the day of Pentecost had come, they were all together in one place with one accord.

units.la: 2 Tunc extitit repente è cœlo so-nitus, tanquam ruentis flatus violenti, qui replerunt totam domum,vbi erant se dentes,
units.tr: 2 Suddenly there came from heaven a sound, as of a violent rushing wind, which filled the whole house where they were sitting.

units.la: 3 Et visæ sunt eis dispertitæ linguæ instar ignis, qui etiam sedit per vnum-quenque eorum.
units.tr: 3 And there appeared to them divided tongues, like fire, which also sat upon each one of them.

units.la: Tsi Christus perasta redemptio-ne nostra corpus suo in cœlum subuexerit, non deposuit tamen curam suæ Ecclesiæ, Matth. 28.
units.tr: Although Christ, having accomplished our redemption, carried his body up into heaven, he did not lay down the care of his Church, Matt. 28.

units.la: Patet hoc ex missione Spiritus S. quem sæpius promisit, ne se relictos putent. Iohan.14.16. Actorum quinto. Vt vero hoc oportuit Apostolos instrui: ita nos quoque de eo oportuit certiores fieri, vt illorum doctrinam sciremus ex Deo prodiisse. Luc decimo. Ideo non occultè est illis datus, nec sine visibili miraculo.
units.tr: This is evident from the sending of the Holy Spirit, whom he promised often, so that they should not think they had been left behind. John 14:16. Acts 5. As it was necessary for the Apostles to be instructed in this way, so it was also necessary for us to be made certain of it, so that we might know that their teaching came forth from God. Luke 10. Therefore the Spirit was given to them not secretly, nor without a visible miracle.

units.la: I. Quando Die 50 à Pascha te, qui alias festum hebdomadarum & nouarum frugum, Leuit.23. Deuter. 16. Præcipuum erat memoria legis datæ, Exod.19. Itaque electus hic dies: Propter populi frequentiam, &c. Vult enim Deus notissima fieri, quæ salutis sunt, 1. ad Timotheum fecundo. Ideo Christus etiam dies festos & celebriora loca ad jt.
units.tr: I. When: on the fiftieth day after Passover, which was otherwise the feast of weeks and of the new fruits, Lev. 23. Deut. 16. It was chiefly a memorial of the giving of the law, Exod. 19. Therefore this day was chosen: because of the crowd of people, etc. For God wishes the things that pertain to salvation to be made most widely known, 1 Tim. 2. Therefore Christ also [went] to festal days and more celebrated places.

units.la: NOTA ¶ Bonitatem Dei, quia nos colemur, quando Satan suggerit, redemptionem in Christo non pertinere ad nos. Tunc promissiones generales repetetur, Mat. 11. Iohan. 7.5.6. Item præsens hoc. 11. Propter legis memoriam. Conuenit typus cum historia. Ergo Christus legis interpres & finis, Matth 5. Gal 4.
units.tr: NOTE: The goodness of God, because we are comforted when Satan suggests that redemption in Christ does not pertain to us. Then the general promises are repeated, Matt. 11. John 7:5, 6. Likewise this present passage. 11. On account of the memory of the law. The type agrees with the history. Therefore Christ is the interpreter and the end of the law, Matt. 5. Gal. 4.

units.la: NOTA ¶ Vnum & eundem esse vete-ris & Noui Testamenti spiritum, & illius sensum in solo Christo disci, 2. Corinth.3. Obseruemus hoc propter eos, qui legebatur, butunbutuntur ad tuendam iuftititiam operum Gal.3. Item qui libros veteris Testamenti reijciunt. Eadem Dei voluntas. Idem author.Idem vsus legis qui olim,quod nimirum peccata arguit, & vitæ officia tradit,ad Christum ducit.Rom.7.
units.tr: NOTE: That the spirit of the Old and New Testament is one and the same, and that its sense is learned in Christ alone, 2 Cor. 3. Let us observe this on account of those who abuse the law to defend the righteousness of works, Gal. 3. Likewise those who reject the books of the Old Testament. The same will of God. The same author. The same use of the law as in former times, which indeed convicts of sins and hands down the duties of life, leads to Christ. Rom. 7.

units.la: II.Quid Apostoli Repete, quod manse runt lerofol.vnanimes, & orârunt. Actorum 1.
units.tr: II. What the Apostles did: recall that they remained at Jerusalem with one accord, and prayed. Acts 1.

units.la: NoT. ¶ Quid faciant, qui volunt spiritus capaces esse. Necessaria doctrina, quia eo opus est omnibus propter regenerationem, Ioh.3. Mundi exemplum & carnis desideria. Vt item in tentationibus fit arrhabo salutis,2.Cor.1.5.Rom.8. Præparari ergo nos oportet. Hic ante omnia requiritur Obedientia : quia non possunt spiritum Dei accipere,quifuo ducuntur. Ordo precationis Dominicæ. Psal.25.51. 119. Concordia : eo quod charitas mutua Christianorum nota est. Ioh.13.15. Precibus, quia Deus orari vult: & hoc proprium fidei opus est. Psal.11.18. Mar.11. Quid ergo mirum,si multi spiritu careant?
units.tr: NOTE: What those should do who want to be capable of the Spirit. The teaching is necessary, because everyone needs it on account of regeneration, John 3. The example of the world and the desires of the flesh. Likewise in temptations it is a pledge of salvation, 2 Cor. 1:5. Rom. 8. We must therefore prepare ourselves. Here above all obedience is required, because those who are led by their own will cannot receive the Spirit of God. The order of the Lord's Prayer. Ps. 25, 51, 119.
