Concord: because the mutual love of Christians is a mark of them, John 13:15. By prayers, because God wishes to be prayed to, and this is a proper work of faith. Ps. 11, 18. Mark 11. What wonder, then, if many lack the Spirit?

units.la: ¶ Spiritum Christi, qui ex Euangelio hauritur, sanctimoniæ & concordiæ spiritum esse,non licentiæ & dissidiorum. Nos enim Deo & nobis inuicem obstringit. Quod aliqui abutuntur Euangelio, nō de
units.tr: The Spirit of Christ, which is drawn from the Gospel, is the spirit of holiness and concord, not of licence and dissension. For it binds us to God and to one another. That some abuse the Gospel

units.la: Spiritus Christi aut thorconcordiæ sanctimo-nia. bet huic fraudi efle,vt nec alijs rebus,quæ in abusum veniunt. Imo non alia Concordia potest placere Deo, quam quæ inter pios in Christo coalescit. Nec vera est sanctimonia, quàm cuius author est Christus. I.Cor.1.6. Reliqua omnia sunt hypocrisis mera.
units.tr: The spirit of Christ, of concord and holiness, ought to be no cause for this fraud, any more than for other things that come to be abused. Indeed no other concord can please God than that which coalesces among the godly in Christ. Nor is holiness true if Christ is not its author. 1 Cor. 1:6. All the rest is mere hypocrisy.

units.la: III. Quomodo verò Visibiliter, cum propter Apostolos, tum propter nos, vt confirmemur in fidei promissis. Iohan. 14. Luc. 21, Matth.10.28. ¶ 1. Repente sonat e cælo. Deus promittat quando spes nulla. Sic Exod. 2 3. Dan.5. Ita in Christi natiuitate. Luc.2. Exspectemus ergo illum, nec ei temere præscribamus, Psalm.27 62.65. Hab.2. Obseruandum imprimis, Apostolorum doctrinam ex cœlo esse. Arguuntur, qui doctores ex alio mundo requirunt. Luc.16. Atqui Christum habent Iohan.1.7. Nunc Spiritum sanctum. Sed velint nouum quid audire. Gal.1.
units.tr: III. But how visibly: both on account of the Apostles and on account of us, so that we might be confirmed in the promises of faith. John 14. Luke 21. Matt. 10:28. 1. It sounds suddenly from heaven. God promises when there is no hope. Thus Exod. 2 3. Dan. 5. So also at Christ's birth, Luke 2. Let us therefore await him, and not rashly prescribe to him, Ps. 27, 62, 65. Hab. 2. This must be observed above all: that the teaching of the Apostles is from heaven. Those are rebuked who demand teachers from another world. Luke 16. And yet they have Christ, John 1:7. Now the Holy Spirit. But they want to hear something new. Gal. 1.

units.la: ¶ 2 Flatus vehemens replet domum. Sym
units.tr: 2 A violent blast fills the house. The emblem

units.la: bolum spiritus, qui venti instar omnia penetrat, & seruat Ioh.3. Est ergo operatio Spiritus per Euangelium incomprehensibilis & inuisibilis, vt venti. Ridiculi fiunt, qui vento obluctantur. Vide Apostolos & horum Rom.15.Col.1. nos soletur hodie.
units.tr: of the Spirit, which penetrates all things like the wind and preserves them, John 3. The operation of the Spirit through the Gospel is therefore incomprehensible and invisible, like the wind. Those who struggle against the wind make themselves ridiculous. See the Apostles and their followers, Rom. 15. Col. 1. Let us be comforted by this today.

units.la: ¶ 3 Lin.
units.tr: 3 Tongues.

units.la: ¶ 3 Liguæ igneæ diffɛ̈ꝛæ illis insident, &c. Additur visibile etiam signum, ne quid dubitent. Est autem Sacramentalis locutio,quod Spiritus dicitur insedisse.
units.tr: Tongues of fire, divided, sit upon them, etc. A visible sign is added, so that they should doubt nothing. But it is a sacramental way of speaking, that the Spirit is said to have sat upon them.

units.la: Interim omnia probè conueniunt. Linguæ necessariæ totius orbis preconibus. Ideo dissectæ,vt sarciretur vitium diuisionis linguarum. Gen.11. Ignis doctrinæ efficacitatem notat. Consumit. Accendit. Calefacit. Ita verbum Dei. Ierem.25. Lucæ 13.
units.tr: Meanwhile all things agree well. Tongues are necessary for the preachers of the whole world. Therefore they were divided, so that the defect of the division of tongues might be made good, Gen. 11. Fire denotes the efficacy of doctrine. It consumes. It kindles. It warms. So does the Word of God, Jer. 25. Luke 13.

units.la: Ex his notis eos agnoscito, qui Christi Spiritu ducuntur. Hodie plerique frigent, aut tepidi sunt, Apoc.3. Ardent in cupiditatibus. Consumitur paulatim fides, charitas, &c. Luc.18. Matth.24. Regnat impuritas in distis, factis, &c. Ista emendemus, & vt Spiritu ambulare (Gal.5.) nobis detur, Oremus.
units.tr: From these marks recognise those who are led by the Spirit of Christ. Today most are cold, or lukewarm, Rev. 3. They burn with desires. Faith and charity are gradually consumed, etc. Luke 18. Matt. 24. Impurity reigns in words, deeds, etc. Let us amend these things, and pray that we may be given to walk in the Spirit (Gal. 5.).

units.la: HOMILIA XI.
units.tr: HOMILIA XI.

units.la: 4 Repleti sunt autem omnes Spiritu sancto cœperunt̨ loqui aliis linguis prout Spiritus ille dabat eis loqui.
units.tr: 4 Now they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

units.la: 5 Erant verò Hierosolymis commorantes Judæi, viri religiosi ex omnibus nationibus eorum, qui sub cœlo sunt, &c. ad vers.14.
units.tr: 5 Now there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, from every nation under heaven, etc., to verse 14.

units.la: VTt Apostolis spiritu sancto opus fuit propter omnis generis vitia.
units.tr: Just as the Apostles needed the Holy Spirit because of every kind of vice,

units.la: vt munus suum possent obire: ita nobis ille non minus necessarius est,quia fine illo nec Christiane viuere, nec inter tentationes fidei certitudinem retinere possumus,1. Cor. 12. Est ergo dignißima confideratu hæc historia, quæ & Apostolicæ doctrinæ authoritatem asserit,& simul docet, vt nos quoque ad Spiritum sanctum præparari, quibus item iudicijs istum declarare, & spiritus omnes dijudicare debeamus. De primo nuper, sequentur reliqua, quæ in Apostolis & auditoribus proponuntur. De illis duo dicuntur.
units.tr: so that they could discharge their office, so he is no less necessary to us, since without him we can neither live as Christians nor keep the certainty of faith amid temptations (1 Cor. 12). This history is therefore most worthy of consideration: it both asserts the authority of apostolic doctrine and at the same time teaches us how we too must be prepared for the Holy Spirit, and by what judgements we ought to recognise him and test all spirits. Of the first point we spoke recently; what follows concerns the things set before the Apostles and the hearers. Two things are said about them.

units.la: I. Alijs linguis locuti sunt. Ingens minus culum, in quo nihil potest tribui industriæ humanæ. Seruiuit autem non ostentationi,sed necessitati. Obstabat Apostolis linguæ diuersitas. Gen. 11. Sed subito tollitur hoc obstaculum. Vnde generalis consolatio debet peti, ne diffidant qui ambulant in vocatione Dei. Obijciuntur multa, quibus Deus illos non impedire vult,sed fidem eorū exercere. Tunc fortitudine opus est & obedientia, nec deerit Deus. Moses Exo. 3.4. Israel Exo. 14. Ps. 114.
units.tr: I. They spoke in other tongues. This is a great miracle, in which nothing can be ascribed to human industry. It served not display but necessity. The diversity of languages stood in the Apostles' way (Gen. 11). But this obstacle is suddenly removed. Hence a general consolation should be sought, so that those who walk in the calling of God may not lose heart. Many obstacles are put in their way, by which God does not wish to hinder them but to exercise their faith. Then there is need of courage and obedience, and God will not be lacking. Moses (Exod. 3, 4), Israel (Exod. 14), Ps. 114.

units.la: Interim No T. 1. Quod qui rudes vocauit,non nisi instructissimos emisit,quo- ad linguarum & scripturæ cognitionem. Arguuntur Anabaptistæ,qui cum nihil no- rint sint,currunt,Ier.23. Abutuntur Apostolo-rum exemplo.Sed per hos conuincuntur hic &c. 1.Tim 3. Tit 1.Etsi enim miraculo hac linguarum omnium cognitione non fit omnibus opus, attame aliqua opus est, vt & artibus dicendi.Et quia haec non om nibus miraculosè obtingunt, studio & scholis est opus. Curarunt has olim prophetae 1.Sam.io. 2. Reg.2.4. Ecclesia item primitiua, Act 13. Christiani item principes, vt collegiorum fundationes testantur. Hic magistratus est curare, ne quid corrumpatur. Accusauit olim Dauidem Amos 2.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note 1: he who called them untutored sent them forth only most fully equipped, as regards knowledge of languages and of Scripture. The Anabaptists are refuted, who, knowing nothing, run about (Jer. 23); they abuse the example of the Apostles. But they are convicted here by these passages: 1 Tim. 3, Titus 1. For although by miracle this knowledge of all languages is not needed by everyone, nevertheless some training is needed, as also in the arts of speaking; and since these things do not come to all by miracle, study and schools are needed. The prophets once took care of these matters (1 Sam. 10; 2 Kings 2, 4). So too the primitive Church (Acts 13), and Christian princes likewise, as the foundations of colleges bear witness. It is the magistrate's task here to see that nothing is corrupted. Amos once accused David (Amos 2).

units.la: ¶ 2 Effectum Spiritus sancti commu- nem omnibus credentibus. Quod nimi-rum linguam mutat. Ex nobis ipsis non possumus loqui de diuinis, 1.Cor.2. Ro.1. Delectamur itcm vanitate & turpiloquio. Imo ne preces quide fundere possumus, quia aut conscientiae terroribus impedimur, aut cogitationib. vanis abstrahimur. Imo nescimus feré quid petamus,Mat.zo. Roman.8. Istis vitijs omnibus medetur Spiritus. Illustrat animos cognitione dis-uinorum.Facit vt honestis deleCtemur,& loquamur quaedificationi seruiunt,Col. 3.4.Fiducia replet fimulq;,quid petamus, suggerit.Rom.8.Zach.12.Cogitationibus
units.tr: ¶ 2. The effect of the Holy Spirit is common to all believers: namely, that he changes the tongue. Of ourselves we cannot speak of divine things (1 Cor. 2; Rom. 1). We also delight in vanity and foul speech. Indeed we cannot even pour out prayers, since we are either hindered by terrors of conscience or drawn away by vain thoughts. Indeed we scarcely know what we should ask for (Matt. 20; Rom. 8). The Spirit heals all these vices. He enlightens minds with the knowledge of divine things; he makes us delight in honest things and speak what serves for edification (Col. 3, 4). Confidence fills us and at the same time suggests what we should ask (Rom. 8; Zech. 12). Thoughts

units.la: obftar.Denique facit, vt omnium linguæ consentiant, &c. Ifa.19. Arguunt ista illu- fores diuinorum,blasphemos, maledicos, turpiloquos, &c. Ex abundantia cordis, &c.Mat.15.Pfal.110.
units.tr: are hindered. Finally, he makes the tongues of all agree, etc. (Isa. 19). Those who mock divine things, blasphemers, revilers, foul-mouthed men, etc., are refuted by these things: "Out of the abundance of the heart," etc. (Matt. 15; Ps. 110).

units.la: II.Fortes & intrepidi prædicant magnifica Dei. Ita dicitur prædicatio Christi, quia Dei maiestas in eo magis quàm vllo alio opere elucet. Est hoc argumentum magnæ mutationis, si quales ante fuerint consideres, Luc.24. Ioh.20.
units.tr: II. Bold and fearless, they proclaim the magnificent works of God. Thus the preaching of Christ is called so, because the majesty of God shines forth in it more than in any other work. This is a proof of a great change, if you consider what sort they were before (Luke 24; John 20).

units.la: Interim Notr. Spiritum sanctum in fidei confessione potissimum exercere. Vt enim fidem in nobis gignit, ita etiam amore Christi accendit, quo fit, vt nos eius non pudeat, neque ab eius confessione nos patiamur absterreri. Vide Rom.1. Arguuntur, qui hanc inter ἀδιαφορα nu merant. Falsi Christum insimulant, Matt. 10. Mar. 8. Martyres stultitiæ damnant & impostura. Quin eo ipso se alienos à fide esse produnt, Apoc.2. Vide Rom 10.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: the Holy Spirit chiefly exercises himself in the confession of faith. For as he begets faith in us, so he also kindles it with the love of Christ, so that we are not ashamed of him and do not allow ourselves to be frightened away from confessing him. See Rom. 1. Those who number this among things indifferent are refuted. They falsely accuse Christ (Matt. 10; Mark 8). Martyrs they condemn as folly and imposture. Indeed by this very thing they show themselves to be strangers to the faith (Rev. 2). See Rom. 10.

units.la: Sequuntur auditores, quorum duo genera fuerunt.
units.tr: There follow the hearers, of whom there were two kinds.

units.la: 1.Pij & religiosi, qui vndique conuenerant. Fuerunt enim Iudæi à tempore exilij Babilonici varie dispersi. Pleriq; manserunt in Oriente. Reduces dispersi sub Antiocho & aliás. Qui vero religiosiores erant, solebant diebus festis ire Hierosolymam, vt sacris, &c. Deut.16. Tales isti, qui nunc miraculum agnoscunt, praedicant, &c. Quaerunt, &c.
units.tr: 1. The pious and devout, who had gathered from every quarter. For the Jews had been variously scattered since the time of the Babylonian exile. Most remained in the East; others, returning, were dispersed under Antiochus and elsewhere. Those who were more devout were accustomed to go to Jerusalem on the festival days, for the sacred rites (Deut. 16). Such were these men, who now acknowledge the miracle, proclaim it, etc. They seek, etc.

units.la: Not. ¶1. Bonitatem Dei, qui sicuti promiserat (Isa.1.10. Joel.2.) seruauit sibi reliquias ex quibus Ecclesia instaurare-tur. Sic i. Reg. 19. Ita semper fiet. Hinc ergo petamus consolationem.
units.tr: Note ¶1. The goodness of God, who, as he had promised (Isa. 1; Joel 2), kept for himself remnants from whom the Church might be restored. So 1 Kings 19. So it will always be. Hence let us seek consolation here.

units.la: ¶2. Qui sint auditores idonei? Qui ad Dei opera contremiscunt (Isa 66.) & quae runt diligenter. Hi nō frustrantur, i. Tim. 2. Matt. 7. Prou.2. Hodie pauci ferio quae-runt. Plerique faciunt, vt, &c. Iohan.3.
units.tr: ¶2. Who are the fit hearers? Those who tremble at the works of God (Isa. 66) and seek diligently. These are not disappointed (1 Tim. 2; Matt. 7; Prov. 2). Today few seek earnestly. Most act so that, etc. (John 3).

units.la: 2. Prophani illusores, quos Christus porcos & canes dicit, Matth.7. Hi ebrios dicunt, & turpissimo vitio acceptum fe-runt opus spiritus sancti.
units.tr: 2. Profane mockers, whom Christ calls swine and dogs (Matt. 7). These say the men are drunk, and attribute the work of the Holy Spirit to the most shameful vice.

units.la: Not. ¶Quousque progrediantur, qui Verbum Dei deuota mente persequuntur. Incurabiles quotidie in peius proficiunt. Ita istis accidit, Act.3.4.5 6.7.8.&c. Talis Pharao, Achab. Quid ergo hodie sper es de illis, qui dicunt, Diabolo pleni sunt isti doctores? Ita vero Euangelium est allijs odor mortis. 2. Cor.2. Ne ergo offenda-mur, sed relinquamus hos iusto Dei iudicio, mentes vero nostras accommodemus Deo, & locum demus verbo eius, & spiritus fanêti testimonio. Vt verò id fiat, indesinenter, Oremus.
units.tr: Note ¶ How far those progress who with devoted mind persecute the Word of God. The incurable grow worse every day. So it happened to these (Acts 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, etc.). Such was Pharaoh, Ahab. What then do you hope for today from those who say, "These teachers are full of the devil"? Indeed the Gospel is to some a savour of death (2 Cor. 2). Let us therefore not be offended, but leave these men to the just judgement of God, and accommodate our minds to God, and give place to his word and to the testimony of the Holy Spirit. And so that this may be done, let us pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA XII.
units.tr: HOMILY XII.

units.la: 14 Stans autem Petrus cum vn-decim, sustulit vocem suam, & locutus eis est, dicens: Viri Iudæi, vosque omnes qui habitatis Hierosolymis, hoc vobis notum esto, auribus percipite verba mea.
units.tr: Peter stood up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and spoke to them, saying: Men of Judea, and all you who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my words.

units.la: ETsi Euangelium Christi per se lætis-simum sit nuntium, & omnem falu-tis rationem tradat, plures tamé sunt sem-per qui contradicunt, aut saltem contem-nunt. Sic prædictum Isa.53. Luc.2. Causa in-dicatur Iohan.3.15. Exempla passim sunt, quorum vsus est, ne hodie similibus offen-damur. Facit huc imprimis, quod accidit in Pentecoste. Moxscifma fit. Religiosi-ores agnoscunt opus Dei, mirantur, quæ-runt, postea credunt. Alij scurriliter ri-dent, dicunt ebrios.
units.tr: Although the gospel of Christ is in itself the most joyful news and sets out every way of salvation, there are always many who contradict it, or at least despise it. So it was foretold, Isa. 53; Luke 2. The cause is indicated in John 3:15. Examples are everywhere, and we use them so that we may not be offended by similar things today. What chiefly bears on this is what happened at Pentecost. Straightway there is division. The more religious recognise the work of God, marvel, inquire, and afterwards believe. Others mock scornfully and say they are drunk.

units.la: 2. Sequitur quid fecerint Apostoli, vbi primam illorum concionem audiemus.
units.tr: 2. Next follows what the apostles did, where we shall hear their first sermon.

units.la: Petrus constitit cum XI. Papistæ hinc colligunt, Petrum fuisse principem Apo-stolorum, vt Pontificum primatum stabi-liant. Sed illud repugnat Christi verbis, Mat.18.20. Luc.22. Ioh.13. Et hic nulla fit primaprimatus mentio. Nec enim Petrus conse dit aut stetit, alijs instar feruorum ipsum stipantibus,sed vt vnus ex illis stetit. Et licet solus loquatur,tamen causam commu nem agit,adeoq; omnibus feruit,vt Christus iusserat,Luc.22. Ita agant omnes ministri, Phil.2.
units.tr: Peter stood up with the eleven. The Papists gather from this that Peter was the prince of the apostles, in order to establish the primacy of the popes. But this contradicts the words of Christ, Matt. 18:20; Luke 22; John 13. Nor is any primacy mentioned here at all. For Peter neither sat nor stood as though the others were servants crowding around him, but he stood as one of them. And although he alone speaks, he nonetheless pleads the common cause, and so serves all, as Christ had commanded, Luke 22. So should all ministers act, Phil. 2.

units.la: Hic potiùs Not. ¶1. Exemplum bonitatis Dei peccatores recipientis.Promiserat hanc Petro, Luc.22. Prœftitit,quando lapsum non passus est excidere, sed respexit. Matt.26. In resurrectione.Mar.16. Luc.24. Solenni restitutione, Ioh.21. &c. Et ne quis dubitaret,nunc alijs animofio rem & zelofiorem facit, vt & postea,Act. 3.4.5. Sic cum Paulo actum, 1.Tim.1.; Corinth.15.Hinc consolationem petant peccatores in conscientiæ tentationib. Sunt enim alia etiam exempla, quæ omnia vniuersalibus promissionibus confirmantur, Ezech.18.Matt.9.11.Ioh.6.
units.tr: Here it is rather to be noted: (1) an example of the goodness of God in receiving sinners. He had promised this to Peter, Luke 22. He fulfilled it when he did not allow the fallen man to fall away, but looked upon him, Matt. 26; in the resurrection, Mark 16; Luke 24; by a solemn restoration, John 21, etc. And lest anyone should doubt it, he now makes Peter more lively and zealous than the others, as also afterwards, Acts 3, 4, 5. So it was with Paul, 1 Tim. 1; 1 Cor. 15. Hence let sinners seek consolation in the temptations of conscience. For there are other examples too, all of which are confirmed by universal promises, Ezek. 18; Matt. 9, 11; John 6.

units.la: ¶ 2.Efficaciam Spiritus sancti. Apostoli rudes erant,&c. Hinc contentiones de primatu,&c. Actor.1. Latuerunt meticulofi. Nunc Spiritu accepto, sciunt quale regnū Christi,& quod suū in eo officium. In eo consentiunt,& iunctis viribus prodeunt. Nec verentur multitudine aut scuras.Imo non requisiti,agunt causam Christi.
units.tr: (2) The efficacy of the Holy Spirit. The apostles were rude, etc. Hence contentions about primacy, etc., Acts 1. They lay hidden, timid. Now, having received the Spirit, they know what sort of kingdom Christ has and what their office in it is. In this they agree, and with united strength they come forward. Nor do they fear the crowd or the mockers. Indeed, though not asked, they plead the cause of Christ.

units.la: sti. His argumentis ipsi quoque tstemur Christi spiritum. Cœlcstiam illo quæramus, zelo accensi asseramus eius gloriam & Euangelium veritatis. Rom.1. Iohan.6. Simile filij. Arguuntur nostri seculi mores. Fatentur multi Christum,vbi nihil pe riculi. In periculis dissimulant, vt Petrus, Matth 26. conuitia patienter ferunt. Imo si qui respondeant, indignantur. Causa, quia mundi pacem & gloriam quæruntur. Ideo non possunt esse Christi serui,Ioh.5. Gal.1.Iacob.4. Meminerimus qualem pacem Christus promittat. Ioh. 14. 15. Luc. 12. Quoad nos,pacem sectemur, &c.Rom. 12. In causa Christi locum habeat, Matth. 10. Luc.14. Mar.9.
units.tr: By these arguments we too may prove the Spirit of Christ. Kindled with heavenly zeal, let us assert his glory and the gospel of truth, Rom. 1; John 6. Like children. Here the manners of our own age are exposed. Many confess Christ when there is no danger. In dangers they dissemble, like Peter, Matt. 26; they bear insults patiently. Indeed if some answer back, they become indignant. The reason is that they seek the peace and glory of the world. Therefore they cannot be servants of Christ, John 5; Gal. 1; James 4. Let us remember what peace Christ promises, John 14, 15; Luke 12. As far as we are concerned, let us seek peace, etc., Rom. 12. Let it have its place in the cause of Christ, Matt. 10; Luke 14; Mark 9.

units.la: Quoad concionem, exordio breui ex- citat omnes, vt ostendat, Euangelium ad omnes pertinere Mar.16.Matth.11. Col.3. Gal.3. Titulis autem vtitur, qui illos admoneant veteris promissionis & officij, Exod.19.Psal.76.132.&c. Et hic olim erat titulorum vsus. Hodie omnia manibus strepunt, strepunt quod in instrumentis & tabulis publicis.
units.tr: As for the sermon, with a brief opening he rouses all, to show that the gospel pertains to everyone, Mark 16; Matt. 11; Col. 3; Gal. 3. He uses titles which remind them of the old promise and of their office, Exod. 19; Ps. 76, 132, etc. And this was once the custom with titles. Today everything is noisy with hands; it clatters with titles in deeds and public records.

units.la: Concionis partes dug.1.Diluit conuitiū quia sic opus erat.2.Christū prædicat &c.
units.tr: The parts of the sermon are two: (1) he refutes the insult, because it was necessary; (2) he preaches Christ, etc.

units.la: Licet ergo respondere conuitijs, & fa- mam tueri,Prou.22.Nececsse hoc in aliquo officio publico constitutis. Hinc illud,i· Tim.3. Quia verò multi crimina falsa intentant, defensione opus est, qua Christus etiam vsus,Matt.9.15.Ioh.5 8 18.Paulus sæpè.2.Cor.1.2.10.11.12.Gal.1.2.
units.tr: It is therefore lawful to answer insults and to defend one's reputation, Prov. 22. This is necessary for those placed in some public office. Hence that passage, 1 Tim. 3. But since many bring false charges, a defence is needed, which Christ also used, Matt. 9:15; John 5, 8, 18; Paul often, 2 Cor. 1, 2, 10, 11, 12; Gal. 1, 2.

units.la: Interim imprimis Not. ¶ 1.Quodebrietatis crimen publice putauit diluendum.Hodie hoc superuacuum videretur: quia plerique leuiculum putant,imò excusant non sine abusu Scripturæ.Psal 104. Iud.9. Vetustate item, Gen.9.19 Amicitijs.Sed Petrum mouit,partim quod illud pseudoprophetis tribuitur.Isa.56.Matth. 24. partim quod per se est scelus grauissimum,quo varie peccatur.1.Abusu donorum Dei, vbi concurrunt, Ingratitudo cum Dei contemptu.Negleƈtum charitatis officium,Amos 6 Luc.12.16. 2.Seipsos perdunt quoad corpus. Fortunas,Prou. 21.Animum,Hoseæ 4.Nō obseruant opus Dei.Isa.5.Suos negligunt,1.Tim 5 Pudorem exuunt,vt Noa,Gen.9 Loth.Gen.19. 3. Alijs nocent. Ad inopiam redacti fallunt creditores varijs dolis. Alij molesti sunt omnibus propinando. Simile canis. Alij mordent linguis & conuitiantur. Alij obscena loquuntur & canunt. Alij pugnant. Hinc cædes,&c.Prou.23.Et hæc quidem in priuatis hominibus. 4 Qui verò alijs præsunt,ij prostituunt suam authori‑tatem.Ita leges eneruantur & verbũ Do‑mini. Scandalum multiplex præbent, & suo exemplo abducunt alios.Hinc religio interit,&honestatis studium extinguitur. Egestas publica inuehitur.Socordia pub‑lica, & tandem exitium. Vide Ecclef. 10. Exempla sunt. Ante diluuium & tempo‑re Noe,Matth.24.Ezech. 16.Ægypt. Iuda & Ifr.Amos 6.If.5.28.Mich.2. Babyl.Hab. 2.Dan.5.Hinc nouissimis quoque tempo‑ribus malum prædicit Christus, Matt.24. Luc.21. Experimur publicè & priuatim. Non temerè ergo Petrus. Sic Apostoli o‑mnes, Gal.5.Eph.5. 1.Cor.5.Carent com‑muni sensu,qui hodie ebrietate gloriatur.
units.tr: Here first note: (1) that Peter thought the charge of drunkenness should be publicly refuted. Today this would seem superfluous, because most think it a trifling fault and even excuse it, not without abuse of Scripture, Ps. 104; Judg. 9. Likewise by appeal to antiquity, Gen. 9:19, and by friendships. But Peter was moved partly because it is attributed to false prophets, Isa. 56; Matt. 24, and partly because drunkenness is in itself a most grievous crime, by which people sin in various ways. (a) By abuse of God's gifts, where ingratitude combines with contempt of God; neglect of the duty of charity, Amos 6; Luke 12:16. (b) They destroy themselves in body, fortunes (Prov. 21), and mind (Hosea 4); they do not observe the work of God, Isa. 5; they neglect their own, 1 Tim. 5; they cast off shame, as Noah, Gen. 9, and Lot, Gen. 19. (c) They harm others. Reduced to poverty, they cheat their creditors by various tricks. Others are a nuisance to everyone by pressing drink upon them, like a dog. Others bite with their tongues and revile. Others speak and sing obscenities. Others fight; hence slaughters, etc., Prov. 23. These things happen in private persons. (d) But those who preside over others prostitute their authority. Thus laws are weakened and the word of the Lord. They give manifold scandal and by their example lead others astray. Hence religion perishes and the zeal for honesty is extinguished. Public want is brought in, public sloth, and at last ruin. See Eccl. 10. There are examples: before the flood, and in the time of Noah, Matt. 24; Ezek. 16; Egypt, Judah and Israel, Amos 6; Isa. 5:28; Mic. 2; Babylon, Hab. 2; Dan. 5. Hence Christ also foretells this evil for the last times, Matt. 24; Luke 21. We experience it publicly and privately. Peter did not speak rashly, therefore. So did all the apostles, Gal. 5; Eph. 5; 1 Cor. 5. They lack common sense who today glory in drunkenness.

units.la: ¶ 2.Argumentum Petri:Est hora dei ter tia.Sumitur ex more communi,1.Thef.5. At hodie apud multos non valeret argu‑mentū:qui faciunt quod est If.5.56. Quid ergo speres aliud quàm interitum? Eccl. 10. De his discamus omnes ferió cogitare, vtq; hoc malum emendetur, Oremus.
units.tr: (2) Peter's argument: it is the third hour of the day. It is taken from common custom, 1 Thess. 5. But today the argument would not carry weight with many, who do what is said in Isa. 5:56. What else, then, can you hope for but ruin? Eccl. 10. Let us all learn from these things to think on them diligently, and so that this evil may be amended. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XIII.

units.la: 16 Sed hoc illud est, quod dictum est per prophetam Ioel.
units.tr: 16 But this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel.

units.la: 17 Et erit vltimis temporibus (dicit Dominus) effundam exspiritu meo in quamuis carnem : & prophetabunt filij vestri,& filiæ vestræ, & iuuenes vestri visionem videbunt, & seniores vestri somnia somniabunt.
units.tr: 17 "And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith the Lord, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams."

units.la: 18 Et quidem super seruos meos & super ancillas meas, in diebus illis effundam de spiritu meo, & prophetabunt.
units.tr: 18 And indeed upon my servants and upon my handmaids in those days I will pour out my Spirit, and they shall prophesy.

units.la: CHristus discipulos suos passim ad patientiam hortatur, & huius exemplum perfectum in seipso præbuit, Isa. 53.1.Pet.2.Sed non obstat hoc, quò minùs Christiani interdum calumnijs responde-ant, & honorem suum tueantur. Imò hoc necesse est, quando in ipsis veritas & Dei gloria periclitatur.Obseruârunt hoc Apostoli in prima concione. Cùm enim mira-culosum hoc Dei opus quidam ebrietati tribuerent, ab eo Petrus orditur,&c. Nec enim de illis, sed de fidei doctrina agebatur,&c. Didicimus nuper quàm turpis sit ebrietas, & quantoperè ijs cauenda, qui publicam functionem sustinent,Prou.20. Quia verò non sufficit calumniam depulse, nisi de rei veritate constet, nunc ad rem ipsam Petrus accedit.
units.tr: Christ exhorts his disciples to patience everywhere and set a perfect example of it in himself (Isa. 53; 1 Pet. 2). Yet this does not prevent Christians from sometimes answering slanders and defending their honour. Indeed it is necessary when the truth and the glory of God are in danger. The Apostles observed this in their first sermon. When some attributed this miraculous work of God to drunkenness, Peter begins from that point, etc. For it was not about those men but about the doctrine of faith, etc. We have recently learned how shameful drunkenness is, and how much those who bear public office must avoid it (Prov. 20). But because it is not enough to repel a slander unless the truth of the matter is established, Peter now comes to the matter itself.

units.la: Respondet enim religiosioribus, qui quæreb ant,Quid hoc,&c.Et ostendit, Spiritus sancti opus esse, olim à Deo promissum:idq; probat ex Ioel.2. Vbi obferuan-dum,non fatis esse, fi qui Spiritu sanctum iactent (vt hodie pontifices in Concilijs) sed hoc probari oportet, 1.Ioh.4. 1.Theff. 5.Id vero per Scripturas fiat, in quibus il-le loquitur (2.Pet.2.1.2.Tim.2.) & sibi fem per constat.
units.tr: For he answers the more devout, who were asking What is this, etc. and he shows that it is a work of the Spirit of God, promised long ago by God; and he proves this from Joel 2. Here it must be observed that it is not enough for men to boast of having the Holy Spirit (as the Pontiffs do today in their councils); this must be proved (1 John 4; 1 Thess. 5). Moreover, this must be done through the Scriptures, in which the Spirit speaks (2 Pet. 2; 2 Tim. 2), and is always consistent with himself.

units.la: ¶ Quoad vero Ioelem, prophetauit is sub Ezechia, quando Deus post varias ad monitiones bellum affyricum immisit, de quo Isa.36.37. Hortatur ad poenitentiam, & formam huius praescribit, insuper con-uersis optima quaeque pollicetur. Vt vero confirmaret fidem trepidorum, ad pro-missionem de Christo & foedus Dei eos remmittit,quod ratum fit futurum,Ier.33. Eaque occasione vaticinium de Christo interserit,quod Petrus adducit,tum vt o-fcitantiam iplorum arguat, tum quod to-tum mysterium Christi comprehendit. Nam huius tres partes sunt. 1. De Spiri-tus sancti missione vaticinatur, vt doceat, quale regnum hic habiturus sit,& quid in illo debeat quaeri, 2. Quae tunc futura re-rum conditio,&c 3. Vt in turbis medijs sa-lus retineri quaeat. In praesenti prima par-tem audiemus, cuius verba plana sunt. Qnare res ipsas obseruemus.
units.tr: Concerning Joel: he prophesied under Hezekiah, when God, after various warnings, sent the Assyrian war, of which see Isa. 36–37. He exhorts them to repentance and prescribes its form, and moreover promises all good things to those who are converted. But in order to strengthen the faith of the trembling, he sends them back to the promise concerning Christ and the covenant of God, which will surely be ratified (Jer. 33). On this occasion he inserts the prophecy about Christ which Peter quotes, both to convict their indifference and because it embraces the whole mystery of Christ. For it has three parts: (1) he prophesies of the sending of the Holy Spirit, to teach what kind of kingdom Christ will have here and what ought to be sought in it; (2) what the condition of things will then be, etc.; (3) that salvation may be retained in the midst of troubles. At present we shall hear the first part, whose words are plain. Let us therefore observe the matters themselves.

units.la: 1. Quod omissis alijs Christi beneficijs, de Spiritus sanêti donis agit. Causa, quòd vt Apostoli illo in primis opus habuerũt, ita nobis nihil magis necessarium, &c. Licet enim in Christo nobis offeratur pecca torum remissio, gratia Dei, regeneratio, hæreditas regni Dei: nullo tamen horum frui possumus absq; Spiritu sancto, i. Cor. 2. Rom. 7. Iohan. 3. Imò nemo potest, &c. 1. Corinth. 2. Hinc illud ad Romanos 8. Imò ex eo patet, Deum totum nostrum esse, &c.
units.tr: 1. That, setting aside other benefits of Christ, he speaks of the gifts of the Holy Spirit. The reason is that, just as the Apostles especially needed this, so nothing is more necessary for us, etc. For although the remission of sins, the grace of God, regeneration, and the inheritance of the kingdom of God are offered to us in Christ, we can enjoy none of these without the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 2; Rom. 7; John 3). Indeed no one can, etc. (1 Cor. 2). Hence that saying in Romans 8. Indeed from this it is clear that God is wholly ours, etc.

units.la: NOTA. Quid in Christi regno quæri debeat? Necessarium obseruatu. Quia plerique terrena quærunt, licenter viuunt, & tandem deficiunt in cruce, Luc, 8. Obseruemus ergo regnum eius non esse de hoc mundo, (Ioh. 18.) sed totum spiritu constare, ad Rom. 14. Quæramus ergo spiritualia. Iustitiam quæ Deo placeat, 2. Cor. 5. 1. Cor. 1. Pacem cum Deo, Mat. 3. Gaudium solidum in aduersis, Phil. 3. 4. Hæc omnia in vno Christo habentur, cuius spiritus nos securos facit, Rom 8. 5. Interim meminerimus, hoc etiam nobis esse incedendum. Est enim regenerationis & innouationis Spiritus, Iohan. 3. 2. Cor. 5 Itaque hunc ducem secuti non perficiamus carnis desideria, Rom. 1. Galat. 5. Huc faciunt, quæcunq; de nostri abnegatione, mortificatione carnis traduntur,Matth. 19. Col. 3. Ad hanc regenerationem examina mores nostros,& videbis,quid nobis defit.
units.tr: NOTE. What ought to be sought in the kingdom of Christ? This is necessary to observe, because most people seek earthly things, live licentiously, and at last fail at the cross (Luke 8). Let us observe, therefore, that his kingdom is not of this world (John 18) but consists entirely in the Spirit (Rom. 14). Let us seek therefore spiritual things: the righteousness that pleases God (2 Cor. 5; 1 Cor. 1); peace with God (Matt. 3); solid joy in adversities (Phil. 3; 4). All these are found in Christ alone, whose Spirit makes us secure (Rom. 8). Meanwhile let us remember that we must also walk in this Spirit. For it is the Spirit of regeneration and renewal (John 3; 2 Cor. 5). Therefore, following this guide, let us not fulfil the desires of the flesh (Rom. 1; Gal. 5). To this purpose belong all the things that are taught about our self-denial and the mortification of the flesh (Matt. 19; Col. 3). Examine your manners by this regeneration, and you will see what is lacking in you.

units.la: II. Quid promittatur,& quomodo? Ef fundam,&c. Largissimam gratiam promit tit Psal. 45. Ioh 1. & 7. Deinde omnem carnem dicit pro omnibus electis ex diuersis gentibus. Ideo subijcit species, vt omnem discrimen tollat, Act. 10. Gal. 3. Col. 3.
units.tr: II. What is promised, and how? I will pour out, etc. He promises a most abundant grace (Ps. 45; John 1 and 7). Then he says "all flesh", meaning all the elect from the various nations. Therefore he adds the species, so as to remove every distinction (Acts 10; Gal. 3; Col. 3).

units.la: Vbi NOT. 1. Discrimen veteris & novi Testamenti. Idem vtrobiq; Christus, Heb. 13. Eadem fides, & eadem ratio salutis, 1. Cor. 10. Heb. 11. Ioh. 8. Differentia est: 1. In numero credentium. Olim Iudaei foli peculium Dei, Exod. 19. Amos 3. Ps. 76. 146. In nouo Testamento disrupta maceria. Ite in orbem, &c. Eph. 2. Marc 16. Mat. 28. Iohan. 19. 2. In modo tradendi. Veteres habuerunt promissiones, typos, vaticinia de futuris, & ideo omnia illis obscuriora fuerunt, Heb. 1. Nunc velo sublato omnia patent, Iohan. 19. Matt. 13. 3. Olim pauci ad mittebantur ad sacerdotium: Nunc omnes credentes, Apoc. 1. 5.
units.tr: Here NOTE 1. The difference between the Old and the New Testament. Christ is the same in both (Heb. 13). The faith and the manner of salvation are the same (1 Cor. 10; Heb. 11; John 8). The difference is: (1) in the number of believers: formerly the Jews alone were God's peculiar people (Exod. 19; Amos 3; Ps. 76; 146); in the New Testament the wall of partition has been broken down: "Go into all the world," etc. (Eph. 2; Mark 16; Matt. 28; John 19). (2) In the mode of delivery: the ancients had promises, types, and prophecies of future things, and therefore all those things were more obscure to them (Heb. 1). Now, with the veil removed, all things are open (John 19; Matt. 13). (3) Formerly few were sent to the priesthood; now all believers are (Rev. 1; 5).

units.la: ¶ 2. Neminem excipi, quo minus propter vitae genus & conditionem debeat Deo consecratus viuere, seq; ipsum Deo viuentem hostiam sistere, ad Romanos 12. Sibi ergo singuli haec applicent.
units.tr: ¶ 2. No one is excluded from living as one consecrated to God, on account of the kind of life or condition he has, and from presenting himself as a living sacrifice to God living (Rom. 12). Let each one therefore apply these things to himself.

units.la: III. Effecta. Omissa alijs prophetiam ponit, in qua vberior gratia Dei elucet, secundum illud Iohan. 15. Meminit autem visionum & somniorum, quia his medijs olim Deus vtebatur, Num.12. Comprehendit autem prophetia cognitionē mysteriorum salutis & linguas: 1. Cor. 12. Sensus est, Cognitionem regni Dei communem fore, & ex omni genere hominum oriturus, &c. Isa. 11.54. Impletum primo in Apostolis. Vide Act. 19. 21. 8. Et adhuc impletur hodie, Eph. 4.
units.tr: III. The effect. Setting aside the rest, he sets forth a prophecy in which the more abundant grace of God shines forth, according to that saying in John 15. He mentions visions and dreams because God formerly used these means (Num. 12). The prophecy, moreover, includes knowledge of the mysteries of salvation and tongues (1 Cor. 12). The sense is that the knowledge of the kingdom of God would be common, and would arise from every kind of people, etc. (Isa. 11; 54). It was first fulfilled in the Apostles (see Acts 19; 21; 8), and it is still fulfilled today (Eph. 4).

units.la: Nota. ¶ 1. Curam Dei pro Ecclesia, quādo de futuris quoq; admonet. Vide 2. Thes. 5.2. Ti.3.1. Ti.4. 2. Pet. 2. & 3.1 The. 5. Matt. 24. &c. Meminerimus horum, & nobis cauteamus.
units.tr: Note. ¶ 1. God's care for the Church, since he also warns about future things. See 2 Thess. 2; 1 Tim. 3; 1 Tim. 4; 2 Pet. 2 and 3; 1 Thess. 5; Matt. 24, etc. Let us remember these things and take heed to ourselves.

units.la: ¶ 2. Cognitionem Scripturæ ad omnis generis homines pertinere. Tyranni Ecclesiæ sunt qui laicos arcent, &c. Interim memineris, non sufficere nudam cognitio nem, sed πράξιν requiri. Iacob. 2. Mat. 5. In his sedulis simus, & Oremus.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The knowledge of Scripture pertains to men of every kind. Those are tyrants of the Church who keep the laity away, etc. Meanwhile remember that bare knowledge is not sufficient, but practice [πράξιν] is required (James 2; Matt. 5). Let us be diligent in these things. And let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XIIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XIIII.

units.la: 19 Et edam miracula in cœlo sursum, & signa in terra deorsum & sanguinem & ignem & vaporem fumi.
units.tr: 19 And I will also show wonders in heaven above, and signs on earth beneath: blood and fire and a vapour of smoke.

units.la: 20 Sol convertetur in tenebras. {a}bras,& luna in sanguinem, priusquam veniat dies ille Domini magnus & illustris.
units.tr: 20 The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord come.

units.la: 21 Et futurum est vt quicunque inuocauerit nomen Domini, saluus erit.
units.tr: 21 And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

units.la: QVONIAM Christus Euangelium id deo praedicare iusit, vt homines ipsi credant & seruentur. Petrus primam quoque concionem eo dirigit, & ideo diligenter ijs occurrit, quae negotium hoc suspectum facere, & fidem auditorum poterant impedire. Erant inter hos aliqui religiosi, sed ignorantes. Deinde impij scurrae, &c. Vt ergo vtrisque medeatur, loel. adducit, ita docens nihil hic fortuitum fieri, sed ex Dei decreto, qui ita olim praedixerit. Citat autem locum totum, quia totus huic negotio seruit. Nam prima pars habet promissionem spiritus sancti, quae docet quid in Christi regno quaeri debeat, & quam liberaliter Deus gratias suas thesauros sit effusurus.
units.tr: Since Christ commanded that the Gospel be preached to God, so that men may themselves believe and be saved, Peter likewise directs his first sermon to this end, and so he carefully meets those objections which could make this business suspect and hinder the faith of the hearers. Some of these were devout but ignorant; then there were the impious mockers, etc. So that he may heal both kinds of hearers, he adduces Joel, teaching that nothing here happens by chance, but by the decree of God, who long ago foretold it. He cites the whole passage, because the whole of it serves this matter. For the first part contains the promise of the Holy Spirit, which teaches what is to be sought in the kingdom of Christ, and how generously God is about to pour out his graces and treasures.

units.la: I. Ne quis sub Christi regno sibi omnia laeta promittat, vt olim Iudaei & hodie etiam qui Chiliastes sequuntur, docet quam horribilis futura sit rerum huius seculi facies, partim vt fide commendet, quae tunc sola seruabit, partim vt Christi contemptores terreat. Dabo prodigia, &c. Debet hoc
units.tr: I. Lest anyone promise himself all joyful things under the kingdom of Christ, as the Jews did long ago and as those who follow the Chiliasts still do, he teaches how dreadful the face of the things of this age will be, partly so that he may commend by faith what alone will then save, and partly so that he may terrify the despisers of Christ. "I will give prodigies," etc. This ought to be extended over the whole time

units.la: Nouissimi seculi statum turbulentius. ad tempus omne extendi vfq; ad nouisi‑mum Christi aduentum, quo is regnum suum complebit. Et sensus est, in omnibus mundi partibus apparitura irae Dei signa, eamq; fore rerum facie, vt omnia elemen‑ta contra genus humanum confpirasse vi deantur. Sic Christus Mat.24. Luc.21. Et coeperunt haec impleri inter Iudaeos statim à Christi ascensione. Deinde in Ro‑mano imperio. Et hodie fiunt ista omnia, &c.
units.tr: of the last age, which will be more turbulent, right up to the final coming of Christ, by which he will complete his kingdom. The sense is that signs of the wrath of God will appear in all parts of the world, and the face of things will be such that all the elements seem to have conspired against the human race. So Christ says in Matthew 24 and Luke 21. And these things began to be fulfilled among the Jews immediately after Christ's ascension, then in the Roman empire. And today all these things are happening, etc.

units.la: ¶ At miretur quis, cur Deus post exhi‑bitum Filium suum tam atrociter iram su-lorum in eam exerat. Videtur enim hoc pugnare cum iniquis, qui habentur Ifa.11. Psal. 72. &c. Item Luc.2. Mat.3. 17. Necessaria quaestio: quia hoc olim calumniati sunt hostes Christi, Act 24. 16. 17. &c. Symmachus postea. Hodie item: & ideo infirmiores tentantur & labascunt. At causa est non in doctrina de Christo, quae pacem & charitatem commendat (Ioh.14.15. Rom.12. &c.) sed in hominibus. Inter hos pars maior est impio-rum (Matt.7.) qui aut superstitiosi sunt, aut Epicurei illusores, 2.Pet.3. Vtrique ode runt lucem (Ioh.3) & ideo credentes per sequuntur, Ioh.15.16. Digni ergo qui pu‑niantur. Ideo certè excisi sunt Iudaei, Luc.21.Mat.21.23. Hinc clades Rom. Imp. apud
units.tr: ¶ But someone may wonder why God, after sending his Son, should so terribly vent his wrath upon the people. For this seems to conflict with the righteous, who are described in Isaiah 11, Psalm 72, etc., and also in Luke 2 and Matthew 3:17. This is a necessary question, because Christ's enemies used to slander this, Acts 24:16-17, etc. Symmachus later did the same, and so today too; and therefore the weaker are tempted and totter. But the cause lies not in the doctrine about Christ, which commends peace and charity (John 14:15; Romans 12, etc.), but in men. Among these the greater part are impious (Matthew 7), who are either superstitious or Epicurean scoffers (2 Peter 3). Both hate the light (John 3), and so they persecute the believers (John 15:16). They are worthy, then, to be punished. Certainly the Jews were cut off for this reason (Luke 21; Matthew 21, 23). Hence the calamities of the Roman empire, among Orosius

units.la: Causa mis-
units.tr: The cause of the mis-

units.la: nō-
units.tr: no-

units.la: culi
units.tr: culi

units.la: Orofium. Quid ergo hodie miramur, quando inaudita crudelitate furit mundus?
units.tr: Orosius. Why then do we wonder today, when the world rages with unheard-of cruelty?

units.la: Quoad pios,recte quidem illi credunt: at alij seculo addicti quaerunt opes,honores,res,mundi amicitiá,&c.Alij fecuriores car ni indulgent. Vtriq; ergo disciplina opus habent,i.Cor.ii.Pfal.119. Et postulat hoc Dei iustitia, vt à domo sua incipiat, &c.i. Pet.4.No habemus ergo quod queramur.
units.tr: As for the pious, they indeed believe rightly; but others, given over to the age, seek wealth, honours, possessions, friendship with the world, etc. Others, more careless, indulge in the flesh. Both therefore need discipline (1 Corinthians 11; Psalm 119). And the justice of God requires this, that judgment begin at his own house, etc. (1 Peter 4). We have therefore nothing to complain of.

units.la: ¶ Imò bonitatem Dei agnoscamus,qui nos propter nomen suum,&c. Mat.5.Act. 5.Quod præmonet,quod Spiritum dat pa racletum,Ioh.14.2.Cor.i.Pf.94. i.Cor.10. quod deniq; erit dies redemptionis, Luc. 21.i.Theff.4.&c.
units.tr: ¶ Rather, let us acknowledge the goodness of God, who for his name's sake [suffers us] etc. (Matthew 5; Acts 5). In that he forewarns us, in that he gives the Paraclete, the Spirit (John 14:2; 1 Corinthians 1; Psalm 94; 1 Corinthians 10), and in that finally there will be a day of redemption (Luke 21; 1 Thessalonians 4, etc.).

units.la: II. Docet quid tunc fieri debeat:Et ex rit; omnis qui,&c. Quasi dicat:Vt tut tumul tuetur orbis, pij tamen non desperent. Quisquis enim nomen Domini invocaue rit, tunc redemptorem suum experietur. Et voluit hanc quoque partem adducere Petrus,vt intelligant,prophetas quoque eandem salutis rationem tradidisse. Nam ad regnum Christi hoc dictum pertinere, apparet ex Rom.10.
units.tr: II. He teaches what ought then to be done, and from this: "And it shall come to pass; whosoever," etc. As if to say: however much the world rages in tumult, the godly should nevertheless not despair. For whoever shall call on the name of the Lord will then experience his Redeemer. Peter also wished to adduce this part, so that they might understand that the prophets too had handed down the same way of salvation. For that this saying pertains to the kingdom of Christ appears from Romans 10.

units.la: Sed Not. ¶ 1. Quibus hoc promittitur? Omnibus,abfq; discrimine gentis,sexus,&c.Sic exponitur, Rom.10.2.Act.10.
units.tr: But note: ¶ 1. To whom is this promised? To all, without distinction of nation, sex, etc. It is explained thus in Romans 10:2 and Acts 10.

units.la: Gal.3.5.Col.3. Et passim vniuersaliter enuntiantur salutis promissiones, vt quibus eas sibi applicet, Matth.11. Mar.16. Ioh. 3.4.5. &c. Est haec efficacisima consolatio in tentationibus.
units.tr: Galatians 3:5; Colossians 3. And the promises of salvation are everywhere announced universally, so that one may apply them to oneself: Matthew 11; Mark 16; John 3, 4, 5, etc. This is the most effective consolation in temptations.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quid debet fieri? Qui innocauerit. Sub inuocatione fides comprehenditur. Quomodo enim invocabunt, &c. Ro.10. Et est inuocatio proprium fidei opus: & ideo paísim praecipitur, Pf.50.145.34. &c. Debemus ergo Deo fidere, & fidem inuocatione testari. Hoc vt testatur salutem in nobis nullam esse,sed extra nos quaeri debere, ita arguit Diuorum inuocatores, Exod.30.
units.tr: ¶ 2. What ought to be done? "Whoever shall call." Faith is comprehended under invocation. "For how shall they call," etc. (Romans 10). Invocation is a proper work of faith, and therefore it is commanded throughout (Psalm 50; Psalm 145; Psalm 34, etc.). We ought therefore to trust in God and to bear witness to our faith by invocation. As this testifies that there is no salvation in us but that it must be sought outside us, so it also refutes those who invoke the saints (Exodus 30).

units.la: ¶ 3. Modum inuocationis: Nomen Domini. Sic dicitur quicquid de illo praedicatur, Exod.34. Misericordia, luftitia, Veritas, Sapientia, Omnipotentia, &c. Elucent haec in singulis operibus eius: maximè autem in Christo. In hoc Deus manifestatus in carne, 1.Timo.3. Idem hic Mediator est, Ioh.14.1. Tim.2. Inuocant ergo nomè Domini, qui per Christum inuocant. Sic ipse docet, Matth.18. Ioh.14,16. Heb.13. Hinc vetus mos Ecclesiae. Obseruandum autem includi hic poenitentiae & obedientiae votum. Ideo manus attollimus, &c. Vide If 1.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The manner of invocation: "the name of the Lord." Whatever is proclaimed about him is so called, Exodus 34: mercy, justice, truth, wisdom, omnipotence, etc. These shine forth in each of his works, but chiefly in Christ. In him God was manifested in the flesh (1 Timothy 3). He is also here the Mediator (John 14:6; 1 Timothy 2). Those therefore call on the name of the Lord who call through Christ. So he himself teaches (Matthew 18; John 14, 16; Hebrews 13). Hence the ancient custom of the Church. It must be observed, however, that a vow of repentance and obedience is included here. Therefore we lift up our hands, etc. See Isaiah 1.

units.la: ¶ 4. Effectum inuocationis ex fide: Ser. uabitur. Absolutè promittitur salus, vt diŭ- scamus, inuocantibus nomen Domini ni- hil defuturum. Dat enim Deus quæ hic il- lis sunt necessaria, Psal. 37. 112. 128. Deut. 28. Matth. 6. Luc. 12. Si quid aduersi incidit, id quoq; bono cedit illorum, Rom. 8. & vt ita fiat opus est. Interim ijdem in Christo habent peccatorum remissionē certam & perfectam, Ioh. 1. 2. Cor. 5. 1. Cor. 1. Isa. 53. At his sublatis, Dei ira quoq; placatur, Psal. 32. Isa. 59. Nulla ergo condemnatio, &c. Ro. 8. Ad omnes pertinet, quod habetur Mat. 3. 17. Ioh. 3. Rom. 5. Ita verò Petrus Iudæos docet, quid faciant, si Dei iram velint effu- gere.
units.tr: ¶ 4. The effect of invocation, from faith: "shall be saved." Salvation is promised absolutely, so that we may learn that nothing will be lacking to those who call on the name of the Lord. For God gives in this life what is necessary for them (Psalm 37, 112, 128; Deuteronomy 28; Matthew 6; Luke 12). If anything adverse befalls, that too turns to their good (Romans 8), and so it must be. Meanwhile they have in Christ a certain and perfect remission of sins (John 1; 2 Corinthians 5; 1 Corinthians 1; Isaiah 53). When these are taken away, the wrath of God too is appeased (Psalm 32; Isaiah 59). "There is therefore no condemnation," etc. (Romans 8). What is found in Matthew 3:17 and John 3 and Romans 5 pertains to all. Thus Peter teaches the Jews what they should do if they wish to escape the wrath of God.

units.la: Ista ergo nobis etiam applicemus. Fiunt omnia quę prædicta sunt olim, Mar. 13. Luc. 18. 21. Consultatur à multis, & huma- nis rationibus agitur. Sed hinc nihil quā consiliorum incertitudo, molestia, pericu- la. Conuersione, patientia, & fidei obedi- entia opus est, Isa. 30. Pf. 121. 123. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us therefore apply these things to ourselves as well. All the things foretold long ago come to pass (Mark 13; Luke 18, 21). Many consult and act by human reasons. But from this nothing comes except uncertainty of counsels, trouble, and dangers. Conversion, patience, and obedient faith are needed (Isaiah 30; Psalms 121, 123). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XV.
units.tr: HOMILIA XV.

units.la: Viri Israelitæ audite sermo- nes istos: Iesum illum Nazarenum, vi- rum à Deo approbatum apud vos præ- stantibus factis & miraculis & signis, quæ edidit per eum Deus in medio vestri, sicut & ipsinostis:
units.tr: Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God among you by mighty works, wonders and signs, which God did through him in the midst of you, as you yourselves know.

units.la: 2 Hunc inquam definito consilio, & prouidentia Dei deditum, cum acceptissetis, manibus sceleratis, cruci affixum interemistis.
units.tr: 2 Him, I say, delivered up by the set purpose and foreknowledge of God, you took and, with wicked hands, fastened to the cross and killed.

units.la: POstquam Petrus prima suæ concionis parte ijs respondit, qui Apostolos ebrios dicebant, & ex Ioele docuit, hoc omne Spiritus sancti opus esse: transfit mo do ad a teram partem, quaillis Christum prædicat, & vt hunc amplestantur monet. Vt vero magis moueat, illos sceleris in hunc commissi argui, vt intra conscientiam suam conuictos cogat, &c. Argumentum: Iesus hic, quem vos crucifixistis, seruator est, quem Deus misit, & talem esse multis operibus ostendit, in primis resurrectione. Continentur ergo hic præcipui fidei articuli. Quis Christus quoad personam, Passio vel mors: Resurrectio, &c.
units.tr: After Peter, in the first part of his sermon, answered those who said the apostles were drunk, and taught from Joel that all this was the work of the Holy Spirit, he now turns to the other part, in which he preaches Christ and urges them to embrace him. He means to move them more strongly, so he charges them with their crime against him, to convict them from their own conscience, etc. The argument is this: Jesus, whom you crucified, is the Saviour whom God sent, and that he is such he showed by many works, above all by the resurrection. Here, therefore, the chief articles of faith are contained: who Christ is as to his person, his passion or death, his resurrection, etc.

units.la: I. Christi personam describit, id vero caute admodum, ne infirmos offendat. Iesu persona, sum Nazarenum, &c. Duo dei lo prædicat. i. Hominem verum fuisse docet. Nazarenum dicit à loco, Iohan. i. Mar. 6. Deinde virum, quod soli homini conuenit.
units.tr: I. He describes Christ's person, and does so very cautiously, so as not to offend the weak. Of Jesus' person he says, "of Nazareth," etc. He teaches two things. First, he shows that he was a true man. He calls him "of Nazareth" from his place of origin (John 1; Mark 6). Then "a man," which belongs only to a human being.

units.la: 2. Ne quis vulgarem hominem putaret, distinguit eum ab aliis quoad opera, quæ illum simul Deum esse probant. Quasi di-
units.tr: 2. Lest anyone think him an ordinary man, he distinguishes him from others by his works, which prove at the same time that he is God. As if he said:

units.la: cat: Iesum Nazarenū prædicamus, quem pleriq; hominem nudum putatis: sed ope ra erant obseruanda, quibus de illo Deus testatus est. A. Virtutes ei tribuit, ne quis præstigiatorem putet. Verè enim fecit omnia, &c. Luc.6.8. Mat.6.Ioh 7. B. Prodigia, quia præter naturam facta. C. Signa, quia in certum finem facta, Ifa. 35. Iohan. 20. Sic ipse docet, Iohannis 5.15. Quo sensu Petrus quoque inter ipsos edita dicit, ne possint negare, Ioh.3.7.
units.tr: "We preach Jesus of Nazareth, whom many of you think a mere man; but there were works to be observed by which God bore witness to him. A. He ascribes powers to him, lest anyone think him a juggler: for he truly did all things, etc. (Luke 6, 8; Matt. 6; John 7). B. Wonders, because they were done beyond nature. C. Signs, because they were done for a certain end (Isa. 35; John 20). So he himself teaches (John 5, 15). In this sense Peter also says that these things were done among them themselves, so that they could not deny them (John 3, 7)."

units.la: NOTA. Qualis Christus agnosci debeat quoad personam. Verus Deus & Homo, &c. Talis prædicatur à Prophetis, Ifa. 11.9 35.33. Pfal.110. Ierem.23. Mich 5. Zach. 12. &c. Sic Paulus ad Romanos 19. Heb.12 &c. Hic consentiunt articuli Symboli Apostolici, Item quæcunq; de incarnatione illius dicuntur, Iohannis 1. Luc.1. & 2. Mat thæi 1.
units.tr: NOTE. What sort of Christ must be acknowledged as to his person: true God and man, etc. Such is he preached by the prophets (Isa. 11, 9; 35, 33; Ps. 110; Jer. 23; Mic. 5; Zech. 12, etc.). So Paul in Romans 1, 9; Heb. 12, etc. Here the articles of the Apostles' Creed agree, and likewise whatever is said of his incarnation (John 1; Luke 1 and 2; Matthew 1).

units.la: 2. Vsum horum: Vt eius officium & salutis nostræ certitudinem discamus: Quia enim talis est, Mediatorem poteftagere, Heb 4 2. Vide Matth.3 7. Et priori ad Timoth.2.
units.tr: 2. The use of these things: that we may learn his office and the certainty of our salvation. For since he is such, he can act as Mediator (Heb. 4, 2). See Matt. 3, 7, and 1 Tim. 2.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui de salute sua dubitant, & ideo hinc inde discurrentes quærunt alios Mediatores, similes eorum, de quibus lere.2. Audi Ioh.14 4. II. Passionem & mortem Christi prædi cat, sic vt terrere velit ipsorum confcien- tias.Tria autem dicit: 1. Totum populum accusat:Vos affixum cruci,&c. Atsciebat à militibus esse crucifixum.Sed toti popu lo hoc tribuit, quia sic voluerant, Luc.23. Iohan.18.19.Peccant ergo non modo, qui scelera designant, sed quiista probant,& ijsdem delectantur, vel etiam non impe- diunt.
units.tr: Those are rebuked who doubt their own salvation and therefore run hither and thither seeking other mediators, like those of whom Jeremiah speaks (Jer. 2). Hear John 14, 4. II. He preaches the passion and death of Christ in such a way that he wishes to terrify their consciences. He says three things. 1. He accuses the whole people: You fastened him to the cross, etc. Yet he knew that he had been crucified by soldiers. But he ascribes it to the whole people, because they had so willed it (Luke 23; John 18, 19). Therefore not only those who devise crimes sin, but also those who approve them, delight in them, or even do not prevent them.

units.la: NOTA.¶ Vnde debeat fieri initiũ præ dicationis Euangelicæ. A peccatorum re. dargutione,Lucæ24 Nili enim illa homi- nes agnoscant, Christo non putant sibi opus esse.Simile ægroti. Vide Pharifæos & nostros Monachos.Hinc illa Matt.9.11.5. Iohannis 16. Rectè ergo hinc orditur Petrus, & hodie sic prædicari debet: vt omnes se reos mortis Christi esse intelli- gant.
units.tr: NOTE. Whence the beginning of evangelical preaching should be made: from the rebuke of sins (Luke 24). For unless men acknowledge these, they do not think they need Christ, as with the sick. See the Pharisees and our own monks. Hence those words of Matthew 9, 11, 5; John 16. Rightly, therefore, Peter begins here, and today it ought to be preached in such a way that all understand themselves to be guilty of Christ's death.

units.la: II. Authores præcipuos arguit. Per mu nus miquorum.Qui illi? Iudas,Sacerdotes, Scribæ,Seniores,Matt.26.Iohannis 11.Pilatus & Herodes. Fuit hoc dicere periculosissimum. Dicit tamen Petrus palàm, &c. Vide quàm fortes faciat Spiritus san stus.
units.tr: II. He accuses the chief authors. By the hands of the wicked. Who were they? Judas, the priests, the scribes, the elders (Matt. 26; John 11), Pilate and Herod. It was a most dangerous thing to say. Yet Peter says it openly, etc. See how bold the Holy Spirit makes men.

units.la: NOT.¶ Qua libertate dicendi vti debe ant ministri? Putant aliqui multa difsimulanda vel extenuanda. Atqui peccata per se blandiuntur nobis,Pfalm.36.Nec debet haberi personarum respectus ijs, qui Dei ministri sunt,2.Paral.19. Actor.10. Et quo maior aliquorum authoritas, eo grauius scandalum. Deniq; publica persona est mi nifter,Icre.1.Ezech.33.Matt.24. Itaq; ferant correptionem, qui volunt esse ex do mo Domini,2.Tim.4.
units.tr: NOTE. With what freedom of speech ministers ought to use. Some think many things should be concealed or softened. But sins flatter us of themselves (Ps. 36). Nor should any respect of persons be shown to those who are ministers of God (2 Chron. 19; Acts 10). And the greater the authority of some, the graver the scandal. Finally, the minister is a public person (Jer. 1; Ezek. 33; Matt. 24). Therefore let those who wish to be of the household of the Lord bear correction (2 Tim. 4).

units.la: III. Ne quis offenderetur,quasi non effet Dei Filius, quem potuissent homines occidere,addit: Definito consilio,etc.Quasi dicat: Nemo putet,tantum hominibus exfelicuiffe. Dei prouidentia & decreto haec factafunt. Sic 1. Pet.1. Faciunt huc Promisiones,Ge.3 Typi,Sacrificia, Exo. 12.Leuit.4.6 & 16.Prophetiæ,Isa.53.
units.tr: III. Lest anyone be offended, as if he were not the Son of God, since men could kill him, he adds: "by the set purpose," etc. As if he said: let no one think that these things happened by mere human chance. They were done by the providence and decree of God. So 1 Peter 1. To this belong the promises (Gen. 3), the types, the sacrifices (Exod. 12; Lev. 4, 6 and 16), and the prophecies (Isa. 53).

units.la: Sed NOTA. Quod non præscientiæ modo,sed decreti quoq; Dei meminit.In fra manus etiam,Actor. 5. Deus ergo non est otiosus spectator rerum,qui permittat modo. Vide ad Roman.11.Actor. 17. OBIECT. Ergo author peccati? RESPON. Minimè : quia sponte peccant homines, Deus autem peccata regit, & illis bene vtitur.Applica.
units.tr: But NOTE that he mentions not only God's foreknowledge but also his decree. "By the hands," too (Acts 5). God therefore is not an idle spectator of things who merely permits them. See on Romans 11; Acts 17. OBJECTION: Then is God the author of sin? ANSWER: By no means. For men sin willingly, but God governs sins and makes good use of them. Apply it.

units.la: 2.Vsum huius doctrinæ.1.Salutis certitudinem asserit, quæ in æterno Dei decreto fundata est Eph.1.1.Pet.1.Rom.9.11.
units.tr: 2. The use of this doctrine. 1. It asserts the certainty of salvation, which is founded in God's eternal decree (Eph. 1; 1 Pet. 1; Rom. 9, 11).

units.la: II. Officij admonet,ne nos illum putemus latere, Psal.13.94 Zach.4. III. Solatur,ne impiorum successibus offendamur, quasi illos Deus ignoret, Psal.73.37. IIII. Patientes facit. Vide Dauidem, 2. Sam.15.16. Psalm. 139. Ideo nos huc remittit Christus, Luc. 12. Matt.6.10. His Christi resurrectionem subijciet; de qua in sequenti Sermone, Oremus.
units.tr: II. It admonishes us not to think that he is hidden from us (Ps. 13, 94; Zech. 4). III. It comforts us, lest we be offended by the success of the wicked, as if God did not know them (Ps. 73, 37). IV. It makes us patient. See David, 2 Sam. 15, 16; Ps. 139. Therefore Christ sends us back here (Luke 12; Matt. 6, 10). To these he will subjoin Christ's resurrection, of which in the following sermon. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XVI.
units.tr: HOMILY XVI.

units.la: 24 Quem Deus excitauit solutis doloribus mortis, eo quod impossibile erat ipsum ab ea retineri.
units.tr: 24 Whom God raised up, having loosed the pains of death, because it was impossible for him to be held by it.

units.la: 25 Dauid enim dicit de eo, Prospiciebam Dominum coram me semper, quoniam est mihi ad dextram, ne concutiar.
units.tr: 25 For David says of him: I have always set the Lord before me, because he is at my right hand, so that I shall not be moved.

units.la: 26 Propterea oblectatum est cor meum, et exultauit lingua mea, atque adeo caro mea requiescit in spe.
units.tr: 26 Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced, and moreover my flesh rests in hope.

units.la: 27 Quoniam non derelinques animam meam apud inferos: nec sinies sanctum tuum sentire corruptionem.
units.tr: 27 For you will not leave my soul among the dead, nor will you suffer your Holy One to see corruption.

units.la: 28 Notas mihi fecisti vias vitae: replebis me iucunditate in tui conspectu.
units.tr: 28 You have made known to me the ways of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence.

units.la: PEtrus prima hac concione hoc agit, vt doceat Iesum esse promissum Seruatorem,quem omnes debeant ampleƈti, qui perire nolunt. Id sic tradit,vt omnes fere articulos fidei comprehendat.1.Quis fit quoad personam: Deus nimirum & homo. Et ideo miraculorum eius meminit.
units.tr: In this first sermon Peter aims to teach that Jesus is the promised Saviour, whom all who do not wish to perish ought to embrace. He hands this down in such a way that he comprehends almost all the articles of faith. (1) As to his person, he is God and man. Therefore he mentions his miracles.

units.la: 2.Mortis meminit, quod hanc subierit ex decreto Patris, nimirum vt peccata nostra expiaret,Ifa.53. Vbi obseruandum, quod Iudæos huius reos agit,partim vt territos conscientia sceleris cogat ampleƈti Christum,partim vt doceat mortem eius sic debere considerari,vt singuli fe huius autho res esse cogitent.
units.tr: (2) He mentions his death, that he underwent it by the decree of the Father, namely to expiate our sins (Isa. 53). Here it is to be observed that he charges the Jews as guilty of it, partly so that, terrified in conscience over the crime, they would be compelled to embrace Christ, and partly so that he teaches that the death of Christ should be considered in such a way that each one thinks himself its author.

units.la: At quia mors Christi Iudæis scandalo erat,(1.Cor.1.) Nunc resurrectionem quo que subijcit,vt hanc mortem deuiƈtam,& non amplius timendam esse doceat.
units.tr: But because the death of Christ was a stumbling block to the Jews (1 Cor. 1), he now adds the resurrection also, so that he may teach that this death has been overcome and is no longer to be feared.

units.la: I. Summatim comprehendit quicquid poterat dici.Hunc Deus suscitauit. Tria di cit. 1. Quod Deus ipsum fufcitârit. Quia autem ipse Deus est,propria virtute refur rexit,vt prædixerat,Ioh.2. 2. Quod mortis dolores soluerit.Metaphora àparturi entibus,eo quod nos mors quasi pariebat ad æternos cruciatus. 3. Quod non potuerit his teneri: partim quia in ipso vita, &c.Iohan.1.partim quia ita Deus decreue rat:quod mox probabit.
units.tr: I. He briefly comprehends whatever could be said. God raised this one up. He says three things. (1) That God raised him up. But because he is himself God, he rose by his own power, as he had foretold (John 2). (2) That he loosed the pains of death. This is a metaphor from women in labour, because death was, as it were, bringing us forth to eternal torments. (3) That he could not be held by these: partly because life is in him (John 1), and partly because God had so decreed, which he will soon prove.

units.la: Not. In Christo haberi salutem per festam.Duo infestant nos. 1.Peccatum,If. 53 59.Rom.3.&c.Athoc ille expiauit suæ mortis merito. II. Mors pœna peccati. Hanc vicit,imo soluit eius dolores, vt nihil in nos iuris habeat,Hebr. 2. Sentimus quidem adhuc dolores,& hos voluit Deus manere, ad arguendam peccati atrociratem,Eccle.7. Interim non habet mors vim nos detinendi,&c.Vide Ioh. 5' Licet ergo omnibus dicere quod habetur Hofeæ 13 1.Cor.15.Rom.8.
units.tr: Note: in Christ salvation is had through faith. Two things harass us. (1) Sin (Isa. 53, 59; Rom. 3, etc.), and this he expiated by the merit of his death. (2) Death is the punishment of sin. He has conquered this, indeed loosed its pains, so that it has no right over us (Heb. 2). We still indeed feel pains, and God willed these to remain, to demonstrate the atrocity of sin (Eccl. 7). Meanwhile death does not have the power to detain us, etc. See John 5. It is therefore lawful to say to all what is found in Hosea 13, 1 Cor. 15, and Rom. 8.

units.la: II.Non omnib.coftabat de Resurrectio ne vt de morte,imo incredibil.videbatur.
units.tr: II. The resurrection was not as universally agreed upon as death; indeed it seemed incredible.

units.la: 1. Propter Saddu.Matt.22.Act 23.
units.tr: (1) On account of the Sadducees (Matt. 22; Acts 23).

units.la: 2. Propter rumorem,de quo Matt.28.
units.tr: (2) On account of the rumour, of which Matt. 28 speaks.

units.la: 3. Quia Christus non omnibus fe manifeftârat,sed solis discipulis,Act 10.Ideo aducit testimonium,Pf.16.quo docet,illam quoq; non esse nouam,sed olim prædicta. Argumentu Psalmi est,quod Dauid summum bonum describit,quod ipse quærat, & quo seipsum sustentet. Quia aute Christi typus fuit, ita hoc facit vt pleraq; huic pofsintraccommodari,&c.
units.tr: (3) Because Christ had not manifested himself to everyone, but only to the disciples (Acts 10). Therefore he adduces testimony from Psalm 16, by which he teaches that this too is not new, but was predicted long ago. The argument of the Psalm is that David describes the highest good, which he himself seeks and by which he sustains himself. But since he was a type of Christ, he does this in such a way that most of what is said can be applied to Christ, etc.

units.la: Habes hic summam salutis.
units.tr: Here you have the sum of salvation.

units.la: I. Summam verę pietatis explicat, In qua No.q 1.Quid fecerit? Posui Domino, &c. Semper ob oculos habui Deum,nec vnquam mihi excidit,me coram illo viuere.Est hæc summa eorum, quæ Deus å hobis requirit,Gen.17. Ex hoc enim nasci tur obedientia & illi placendi studiû.Deinde fides, quæ in hunc vnum respicit, (Psal.123.) & in aduersis sustentat. Vtriq; studuit Christus,Phil 2.Iohan.12.17. Luc. 22.Ad hoc exemplum singuli se accommodent. Ita vitijs resistent, & virtuti studebunt. q 1. Causam: Quia mihi à dextris, etc. Quasi dicat: Si obseruo eum, adest mihi Seruator.Sin minus, adest inspector, &c. Hæc causa omnes sanctos mouit,&c. Iofephum,Ge.39.In hoc ergo fimus assidui. Vide Matt.28.Ioh.10. Qui hoc negligunt, ruunt in omne scelus,Psal.13.
units.tr: I. He explains the sum of true piety, in which note: (1) What did he do? "I have set the Lord before me," etc. I always had God before my eyes, and it never slipped from my mind that I live in his presence. This is the sum of what God requires of us (Gen. 17). For from this arises obedience and zeal to please him. Then comes faith, which looks to this one thing (Ps. 123) and sustains us in adversities. Christ strove for both (Phil. 2; John 12, 17; Luke 22). Let each one conform himself to this example. Thus they will resist vices and strive for virtue. (2) The cause: because he is at my right hand, etc. As if he said: if I observe him, a Saviour is present to me; if not, an inspector is present, etc. This cause moved all the saints, etc., such as Joseph (Gen. 39). Therefore let us be diligent in this. See Matt. 28; John 10. Those who neglect this rush into every crime (Ps. 13).

units.la: 2.Fructus huius studij. q 1. Lætatus est, &c. De gaudio loquitur, quod non animo solû sentitur,sed lingua quoq; sepródit.Hoc sensit Christus,Luc.10. Promittit & suis,Iohan.16.Oritur ex sensu gratiæ Dei,Rom.14.&c. Et ideo solidum est, & semper durat,Rom.5.1.Theff.5.Phil.4. Aliafors impiorum.
units.tr: (2) The fruit of this zeal. (1) He rejoiced, etc. He speaks of joy, which is not felt in the mind alone, but is also betrayed by the tongue. Christ felt this (Luke 10), and he promises it to his own (John 16). It arises from a sense of the grace of God (Rom. 14, etc.), and therefore it is solid and always endures (Rom. 5; 1 Thess. 5; Phil. 4). Otherwise it may be the joy of the impious.

units.la: 2. Caro mea requiescet,&c. Mortem in telligit lætam, quæ summæ felicitatis nota est,Impiorum gaudia mors turbat,immo mentio mortis,Lucæ 12,&16. At pij hac gaudent. 1. Quia ad solam carnem spectat, in animam nihil potest, Iohannis 5. 2. Hæc quiescit à laboribus, quorum vita hæc plena est, Psal. 90. Iob. 5. Vide Apoc. 14. 3. Quomodo? Num vt iumenta? Mini- me. Sed in specie. Resurrectione nimirum 1. Cor. 15. Phil. 3. Hæc sola confirmat, &c. Iob. 19. 2. Tim. 4.
units.tr: (2) "My flesh will rest," etc. He understands death as joyful, which is a mark of highest happiness. Death disturbs the joys of the impious; indeed even the mention of death does (Luke 12 and 16). But the pious rejoice in this. (1) Because it looks only to the flesh; it can do nothing against the soul (John 5). (2) The flesh rests from labours, of which this life is full (Ps. 90; Job 5). See Rev. 14. (3) How? Surely not as beasts do? By no means, but in its proper form, namely by the resurrection (1 Cor. 15; Phil. 3). This alone confirms, etc. (Job 19; 2 Tim. 4).

units.la: ¶ 3. Non relinquesanimam, &c. Inferi pro sepulchro, Gen. 44. Sensus, Anima mea nō erit diu separata à corpore. Quod de descensu Christi ad inferos dicitur, non ad animam pertinet, (Luc. 23. Iob. 19.) sed de merito & prædicatione Christi, 1. Pet. 4. Soletur nos, quod animæ nostræ sunt in manu Dei, Sap. 3.
units.tr: (3) "You will not leave my soul," etc. Hell is taken for the grave (Gen. 44). The sense is: my soul will not be separated from the body for long. What is said of Christ's descent to hell does not pertain to the soul (Luke 23; Job 19), but to the merit and preaching of Christ (1 Pet. 4). Let us be comforted that our souls are in the hand of God (Wis. 3).

units.la: ¶ 4. Non dabis, vt corruptionem, &c. Hoc proprié de solo Christo dicitur. Nostra corpora oportet corrumpi, 1. Cor. 15. At ne hæc quidem corruptio erit perpetua, 1. Cor. 15. Phil. 3.
units.tr: (4) "You will not give," etc. This is said properly of Christ alone. Our bodies must be corrupted (1 Cor. 15). But not even this corruption will be perpetual (1 Cor. 15; Phil. 3).

units.la: ¶ 5. Notas fecisti, &c. Id est in viam veram adduxisti me. Ita nobis fiet in resurrectione. At via hæc in solo Christo est, Ioh. 14. 8.
units.tr: (5) "You have made known," etc. That is, you have led me into the true way. So it will happen to us in the resurrection. But this way is in Christ alone (John 14).

units.la: ¶ 6. Replebis, &c. Exprimitur conditio vitæ æternæ. Præsens hæc triftifsima. In illa abstergentur lachrymæ, Isa. 25. 64. Apocal. 7 21. Ideo gaudium & gloria dicitur Matth. 25 Iohan. 17. Eiusdem nos quoque participes erimus, Luc. 22. Iohan. 14. 15. &c.
units.tr: (6) "You will fill," etc. The condition of eternal life is expressed. The present life is most sorrowful. In that life tears will be wiped away (Isa. 25; 64; Rev. 7, 21). Therefore joy and glory are spoken of (Matt. 25; John 17). We too will be partakers of the same (Luke 22; John 14, 15, etc.).
12. etc.

units.la: Ostenditur autem hoc gaudium in vultu Dei. Vultus regis, &c. Prou.16.20. Est autem argumentum perpetuæ beatitatis & perfectæ quod coram Deo consistere poterimus. Gen.3. Vsus horum, vt Iesum agnoscamus esse Christum. Deinde vt ipsi quoq; Deum nobis ob oculos ponamus. Ita pie viuemus in hoc seculo, & æternum viuemus atque gaudebimus, Oremus.
units.tr: This joy, moreover, is shown in the countenance of God. The countenance of the king, etc. (Prov. 16:20). The argument for perpetual and perfect blessedness is that we will be able to stand before God (Gen. 3). The use of these things is that we may acknowledge Jesus to be the Christ, and then that we also set God before our eyes. Thus we will live piously in this age, and will live and rejoice eternally. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XVII.
units.tr: HOMILY XVII.

units.la: 29 Viri fratres, licet liberè dicere apud vos de Patriarch. Dauid, eum et obijsse & sepultum esse, & monumen-tum eius esse apud nos in hunc vfq; diem
units.tr: 29 Men and brethren, I may speak freely to you of the Patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.

units.la: 30 Propheta igitur cum effet, & sciret Deu iure iurando sibi iurasse, fa-re vt ex fructu lumbi ipsius, quod car-nem attinet, Christum excitaret, &c. ad ver. 37
units.tr: 30 Since he was a prophet, and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath that he would raise up Christ from the fruit of his loins according to the flesh, etc. to verse 37.

units.la: VT Christus suam resurrectionem multis probauit: Ita Apostoli eandem in suis concionibus maximè vrgent. Causa, quòd in ea fundatur nostræ salutis certitudo. 1. Peccatum sublatum esse do-cet, 1. Cor. 15. Rom. 4. 2. Animarum immor-talitatem & corporum resurrectione asse-rit. rit,Iohan.12.14.17. Phil.3. 3. Crucis scan-dalo medetur. Ideo Petrus de hac diligen tissimè agit:& quia incredibilis videba-tur, adducit testimonium, Psal.16. Obijci poterat:Dauid de seipso, &c. Docet ergo nunc de solo Christo exponi posse. Inde colligit, hunc esse Seruatore promissum, quem omnes amplecti debeant.
units.tr: As Christ proved his resurrection by many means, so the Apostles above all press it in their sermons. The reason is that the certainty of our salvation is founded on it. (1) It shows that sin has been taken away: 1 Cor. 15; Rom. 4. (2) It asserts the immortality of souls and the resurrection of bodies: John 12.14, 17; Phil. 3. (3) It heals the scandal of the cross. Therefore Peter treats this very diligently, and because it seemed incredible, he adduces testimony, Psalm 16. It could be objected that David said this of himself. He therefore teaches that it can now be explained of Christ alone, and from this he infers that this is the Saviour promised, whom all ought to embrace.

units.la: I. Docet testimonium hoc non posse de Dauide exponi: Licet liberé, &c. Argumen-tum, Dauid de quodam agit, qui non sit mansurus in morte: At ipse mortuus est, sepultus, denique iuit viam omnis terræ, 1 Reg.2. Ergo non de seipso hæc dixit.
units.tr: I. He teaches that this testimony cannot be explained of David. "Men and brethren, I may speak freely," etc. The argument: David speaks of one who was not going to remain in death; but David himself died, was buried, and at last went the way of all the earth, 1 Kings 2. Therefore he did not say these things of himself.

units.la: Not. ¶ Quòd hoc licuit dicere Petro de Dauide. Vt enim nota erant omnibus: ita etiam si magnus esset Dauid apud om-nes, nemo tamen tunc ex defunctis Deos faciebat. Simile Act.13. Imo sepulchra ferunt, ut de illis admonerentur. Discamus, vt nos quoque sentire debeamus de mortuis, Isa.36.
units.tr: Note: it was permissible for Peter to say this about David. For as his death and burial were known to all, so even if David was great among everyone, nobody then made gods of the dead. Similar in Acts 13. Indeed, they bear sepulchres so that men may be reminded of the dead. Let us learn that we too ought to think the same about the dead, Isa. 36.

units.la: II. Probat de Christo illum locutum esse. 1. Propheta cum esset, &c. Quasi dicat: Prophetæ de futuris vaticinantur, imprimis de Christo, 1. Petr. 1. Luc.24. Dauid fuit propheta: Ergo, &c.2. Cum sciret, &c. Addit hoc, ne quis illum de rebus ignotis putaret locutum. Imò sciuit. Necobiter, fedDei iure iurando confirmatus. Vide 2.Sam.7.Pfal.89.131.110.
units.tr: II. He proves that David spoke of Christ. (1) "Since he was a prophet," etc. As if to say: the prophets foretell future things, above all concerning Christ: 1 Pet. 1; Luke 24.
