David was a prophet; therefore, etc. (2) "Since he knew," etc. He adds this so that no one would think he spoke of things unknown. Indeed he knew them, and he was confirmed by God's oath. See 2 Sam. 7; Ps. 89, 131, 110.

units.la: {q} 2. Ergo Christi mysteria veteribus non ignota fuerunt. Etsi enim plenior cognitio seruata sit tempore praefinito, (Mat 13.Gal.4.) habuerunt tamen illi quoque quod satis fuit, Ioh 8. 1.Cor.10. Est ergo fides Christiana vetustissima.
units.tr: 2. Therefore the mysteries of Christ were not unknown to the ancients. For although a fuller knowledge was reserved for the appointed time (Matt. 13; Gal. 4), they too had what was enough: John 8; 1 Cor. 10. Therefore the Christian faith is very ancient.

units.la: Interim Nota {q} Salutem in Christo iureiurando Dei confirmatam esse. Sic fa ctum cum Abrahamo, Gen.15.22. Heb.6, Isaaco, Gen.26. Eodem pertinet Patris testimonium, Matth.3.17. Item, Amen dico &c. Ioh.3.5.6. &c. Obseruandum, quanti fieri debeat Christi praedicatio. Vide de le gis contemptoribus, Heb.10. Item 1.Ioh.5 Consolationi quoque seruiat hoc in tentationibus, ne de promissionibus salutis dubitemus, Isa.40.
units.tr: Meanwhile note that salvation in Christ has been confirmed by God's oath. So it was done with Abraham, Gen. 15.22; Heb. 6; and with Isaac, Gen. 26. To this belongs the Father's testimony, Matt. 3.17; likewise "Amen, I say to you," etc., John 3.5, 6, etc. It is to be observed how highly the preaching of Christ ought to be valued. See on the despisers of the law, Heb. 10; likewise 1 John 5. This also serves for consolation in temptations, so that we do not doubt the promises of salvation, Isa. 40.

units.la: III. Applicat Christo: Hunc Iesum, &c. Sensus: Mesiam ex mortuis excitari debere olim praedictum: At Iesum excitauit Deus. Ergo, &c. At quia minor negatur, confirmat publico testimonio.
units.tr: III. He applies it to Christ: "This Jesus," etc. The sense: it was foretold long ago that the Messiah must be raised from the dead; but God raised up Jesus. Therefore, etc. But because the minor premise is denied, he confirms it by public testimony.

units.la: Obseruemus fidem & integritatem Apostolorum. Fuerunt electi testes, Act.1. Ioh.5 Testantur ergo intrepidè, licet sci-rent aliud velle Sacerdotes & Seniores, qui milites conduxerant, Matt.28. Imitemur mur hodie, nec moueamur mundi minis & conatibus, Mar.8 Rom.1. 1.Tim.1.
units.tr: Let us observe the faith and integrity of the Apostles. They were chosen witnesses, Acts 1; John 5. They therefore testify fearlessly, although the chief priests and elders, who had hired the soldiers, wished otherwise, Matt. 28. Let us imitate them today, and not be moved by the threats and efforts of the world: Mark 8; Rom. 1; 1 Tim. 1.

units.la: IV. Præsenti actioni applicat omnia. Exaltatus ergo dextra Dei, & promissum spi ritum, &c. Ita vero remittit eos ad Psal.68. & hunc etiam de illo, non de Dauide exponi debere probat, Psal.110. Quasi dicat: Messias in cœlum ascendere, & spiritus sancti dona effundere debuit. Id non fecit Dauid, qui non ascendit, quoad corpus scilicet. Ergo Christus est Messias, &c.
units.tr: IV. He applies everything to the present action. "Therefore, exalted at the right hand of God, and having received the promised Spirit," etc. He sends them back to Psalm 68, and proves that this too must be explained of Christ, not of David, from Psalm 110. As if to say: the Messiah had to ascend into heaven and pour out the gifts of the Holy Spirit. David did not do this, for he did not ascend, that is, as to his body. Therefore Christ is the Messiah, etc.

units.la: NOT. Regni Christi conditionem.
units.tr: NOTE: the condition of Christ's kingdom.

units.la: 1. Dextra Dei exaltatus ascendit cœlum. Ergo non est de hoc mundo, nec mundi principis nititur, Ioh. 18. Spiritus virtute seruatur. Arguuntur, qui carnis præsentiam propugnant, Matt.24.2. Sedet ad dextram Dei, nimirum eiusdem essentiæ, potestatis & maiestatis. Sic Dan.7 Ipse Iohan.10.14.17. Est autem plenum consolationis, quod quoad carnem, potestatem omnem accepit, Ioh.3.5. Matth.11.28. &c. Potest ergo & vult seruare. 3. Donec ponam hostes, &c. Princeps horum Satan, Gen.3. Iohan.12.16. Peccatum, Roman.8. Ioh 1.Mors & inferi.Hof.13 1.Cor.15. Quid ergo mundum metuimus, qui his seruili- ter subijcitur? Psal.2. Interim nostri officij fuerit contra hos omnes constanter pugnare,&c.
units.tr: (1) Exalted at the right hand of God, he ascended into heaven. Therefore he is not of this world, nor does he rest on the prince of this world: John 18. He is preserved by the power of the Spirit. Those are refuted who defend the presence of the flesh: Matt. 24.2. (2) He sits at the right hand of God, that is, of the same essence, power and majesty; so Dan. 7. Indeed, John 10.14, 17. It is full of consolation that, as to the flesh, he has received all power: John 3.5; Matt. 11.28, etc. Therefore he can and will save. (3) "Until I make your enemies," etc. The chief of these is Satan: Gen. 3; John 12.16. Then sin: Rom. 8; John 1. Then death and hell: Hos. 13; 1 Cor. 15. Why then do we fear the world, which is slavishly subject to these? Ps. 2. Meanwhile it is our duty to fight constantly against all of these, etc.

units.la: V.Concludit: Sciat tota domus,&c. Do mum totam compellat, vt innuat Chri-ftum ad omnes pertinere Galat. 2. Col.3. Inest etiam his consolatio magna, &c. 2. Certò sciat. Ergo salus in Christo certa est,non dubia,Mat.16.Ioh.10. 2.Tim.2 ad Romanos 8 3. Quòd fiDeus hunc Iesum fecit Dominum & Christum. Dominum dicit propter redemptionis beneficium,Ifa.42. Christum,quia Rex & Sacerdos. Repetit autem ,quòd ipsi illum crucifixerint, vt sic aculeum relinquat in illorum cordibus.
units.tr: V. He concludes: Let the whole house of Israel know, etc. He addresses the whole house, to imply that Christ pertains to all: Gal. 2; Col. 3. There is also in these words great consolation, etc. (1) Let them know for certain. Therefore salvation in Christ is certain, not doubtful: Matt. 16; John 10; 2 Tim. 2; Rom. 8. (2) That God has made this Jesus both Lord and Christ. He calls him Lord on account of the benefit of redemption: Isa. 42. Christ, because he is King and Priest. He repeats that they themselves crucified him, so that he leaves a sting in their hearts.

units.la: ¶ Peccant ergo in Christianam religio nem qui alios dominos, reges, facerdo tes , id est, seruatores & mediatores sibi fingunt.Ista enim illi foli debentur,Ifa.42. Actor.4.1.Tim.2.Ioh.14.
units.tr: Therefore those sin against the Christian religion who feign for themselves other lords, kings, priests, that is, other saviours and mediators. For these titles are due to him alone: Isa. 42; Acts 4; 1 Tim. 2; John 14.

units.la: Hæc est prima Petri concio, quæ omnes Symboli articulos comprehendit. In qua obseruem.nihil hîc agi de Petri prima tu,cófeffione & absolutione priuata,fatis* factione,intercessione Diuorum,Purgato rio,Imaginibus,&c.Sed ad vnum Chriftu remittit. Quod fi hic illis sufficere potuit, cur non & nobis?Eo igitur contenti,in illo vno acquiescamus,Ioh.6.4. Oremus.
units.tr: This is Peter's first sermon, which comprehends all the articles of the Creed. In it I observe that nothing is said here of auricular confession, private absolution, satisfaction, the intercession of the saints, Purgatory, images, etc., but he refers them to Christ alone. If that was enough for them, why should it not be enough for us? Let us therefore be content with that, and rest in that one alone: John 6.4. Let us pray.

units.la: 37 His autem auditis compuncti sunt corde, & dixerunt ad Petrum ac reliquos Apostolos, Quid faciemus viri fratres?
units.tr: 37 Now when they heard this, they were pricked in heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, "Men and brethren, what shall we do?"

units.la: 38 Petrus autem ait ad eos, Resipiscite, & baptizetur vnusquisque vestrum in nomine Iesu Christi, in remissionem peccatorum: & accipietis donum Spiritus sancti, & c, ad ver. 41.
units.tr: 38 Then Peter said to them, "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit," etc., to verse 41.

units.la: EXposita est prima Petri concio, cuius status est, lefum esse Mefiam. Id autem sic docet, vt ludaeis grauiter expro birarit scelus in hunc commissum, no qui dem conuitiandi libidine, sed vt illos cogat ad eum confugere. Sequitur nunc effectus: Quod nimirum multi territi, conjilium petierint, quod illis Petrus dedit, &c. Vsus, vt discamus quid fieri debeat, fi quando scelerum conuicti, Deum nobis iratum esse sentimus. Necessaria doctrina, quia plerique hic errant, dum proxima quaeque arripiunt, & fere ea quae improbantur Deo, &c. Videamus ergo singula.
units.tr: Peter's first sermon has been expounded; its theme is that Jesus is the Messiah. He teaches this in such a way that he gravely upbraids the Jews for the crime committed against him, not indeed out of a desire to revile, but in order to compel them to flee to him. Now the effect follows: namely that many, terrified, sought counsel, which Peter gave them, etc. The use is that we learn what ought to be done if ever, convicted of our sins, we feel God angry with us. This doctrine is necessary, because many go astray here, seizing upon whatever is nearest at hand, and generally those things which are disapproved by God, etc. Let us look at each point then.

units.la: I. Qui consilium petant? ludaei, qui in Dei Filium impijfime peccarant, Luc.23. Ioh.18. & 19. &c. Quod fi istis profuit, vtiq; omnibus proderit, qui ferio salutem quaerunt.Ergo quid fecerint.Not. ¶ Compunt esse sunt corde. Intelliguntur conscientiae terrores, ex peccati agnitione & sensu irae Dei, &c. Est hoc initium salutis. Simile aegroti & medici. At quia peccati atrocitatem ex nobis ipsis non agnoscimus, verbo opus est, quod arguat. Id in iis est aeternitur. Sic in Dauide 2. Sam. 11.12. Imo singuli hoc experimur, Psalm. 36. Et in eo elucet Dei bonitas, qui ideo sic instituit verbi praedicationem, Isa. 58. Ioh. 16.2. Tim 3.4. Feramus ergo patienter, & tunc putemus ministros officiū fecisse, quando nos compungi sentimus.
units.tr: I. Who seek counsel? The Jews, who sinned most impiously against the Son of God: Luke 23; John 18 and 19, etc. If this profited them, it will surely profit all who seriously seek salvation. Consider therefore what they did. Note: they were pricked in heart. This is understood as terrors of conscience, arising from the recognition of sin and a sense of God's wrath, etc. This is the beginning of salvation, similar to a sick man and a doctor. But because we do not recognise the atrocity of sin from ourselves, we need the word, which convicts us. This is constantly so in them: so in David, 2 Sam. 11, 12. Indeed each of us experiences this, Ps. 36. And in this God's goodness shines forth, who therefore so ordained the preaching of the word: Isa. 58; John 16.2; Tim. 3.4. Let us therefore bear it patiently, and then think that the ministers have done their duty when we feel ourselves pricked.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quaerunt, Quid faciemus? Est hic alter gradus ad salutem. Nam impij quoque sentiunt se tangi, & conuincuntur intra animos suos, sed vel exasperati magis ferociunt, Gen. 4. Achab. 1. Reg. 21. Sacerdotes Ioh. 8. 10. &c. Vel desperant, ut rursus Cain & Iudas, Matth. 27. At ilti longius progressi, abijs consilium petunt, qui ipsos terruerant. Sic postea Paulus, Actor. 9 Ita nos ex eodem verbo, quo vulnerati sumus, consilium petamus & consolationem. Nec enim ideo terret Deus ut perdat, sed ut de salute cogitare cogat, & ipse met remedium adhibet. Vide Prophetarum conciones. Ita in praesenti Apostoli
units.tr: 2. They ask, "What shall we do?" This is a second step towards salvation. For the wicked too feel themselves touched and are convicted within their own minds, but either, exasperated, they grow fiercer: Gen. 4; Ahab, 1 Kings 21; the priests, John 8, 10, etc.; or they despair, like Cain and Judas, Matt. 27. But these, having advanced further, seek counsel from those very men who had terrified them. So afterwards Paul, Acts 9. Thus let us, from the same word by which we were wounded, seek counsel and consolation. For God does not terrify in order to destroy, but to make us think of salvation, and he himself supplies the remedy. See the sermons of the Prophets. So in the present case the Apostles...

units.la: Neminem ergo terreat peccatorum atrocitas. Semper enim ratum erit quod habetur Ezechiel.decimo octauo, Zachriæ 1. Isa.55. Et Christus tales inuitat, Matthæi vndecimo, Iohan.6. Hodie omne malum ex eo est, quod non accedimus: similes eorum, de quibus Isa.65. Zach.1.
units.tr: Let therefore no one be terrified by the atrocity of his sins. For what is stated in Ezekiel 18, Zechariah 1, and Isaiah 55 will always stand firm. And Christ invites such people in Matthew 11 and John 6. Today every evil arises from this, that we do not draw near: they are like those of whom Isaiah 65 and Zechariah 1 speak.

units.la: II. Consilium Petri narratur, quo tria iubentur: 1. Pœnitentiam agite. Scriptura. Christus ipse, Mar.1. Matth.4. Et sic iusserat, Luc.24. Est autem conuerso a peccatis ad Deum. Quia enim peccando a Deo recedimus (Isa.59) ad hunc redeamus oportet, Ier.3 & 4. Errant igitur, qui vel ad alios Deos, vel creaturas, aut etiam sua opera conuertuntur.
units.tr: II. Peter's counsel is related, in which three things are commanded: 1. Repent. Scripture: Christ himself, Mark 1 and Matthew 4. And he had so commanded in Luke 24. Now repentance is a turning from sins to God. For since by sinning we withdraw from God (Isaiah 59), we ought to return to him, Jeremiah 3 and 4. Therefore they err who turn to other gods, or to creatures, or even to their own works.

units.la: Exigitur autem hic: 1. Confessio peccatorum, non auricularis, sed quæ Deo fiat, cui peccauimus, &c. Pf.51.2. Inuocatio gratiæ Dei, Luc.18. 3. Vitæ totius mutatio cum perpetuo studio emendationis. Sic olim fecit Dauid, Psal.25.51.32. Petrus, Matt.26. Ioh.20.21. Ita docet Christus Mat.18. Et in filio prodigo. Luc.15.
units.tr: Here is required: 1. Confession of sins, not auricular but made to God, against whom we have sinned, etc. Psalm 51:2. Invocation of the grace of God, Luke 18. 3. A change of the whole life with constant zeal for amendment. So David once did, Psalm 25, 51, 32. Peter, Matthew 26; John 20, 21. Thus Christ teaches in Matthew 18, and in the prodigal son, Luke 15.

units.la: ¶ 2. Baptizetur quisque, &c. Ad Christum eos remittit, ne quid suis operibus tribuant, vt Pharisæi: aut in suis purificationibus salutem quærant. Mar.7. Vult ergo ad Ecclesiam accedant, in qua est peccatorum
units.tr: ¶ 2. Let each one be baptized, etc. He sends them to Christ, so that they may not ascribe anything to their own works, as the Pharisees did, or seek salvation in their own purifications. Mark 7. He wills therefore that they come to the Church, in which is the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: {y} Pœnitentiam agite.
units.tr: {y} Repent.

units.la: Ablutio.Intellexit hoc Dauid, Psal.51.Sic docemur 1.Ioh.1. Et in Symbolo de eo ad monemur. Obseruandum interim publi- ca confessione opus esse, ne nos pudeat nostrę pœnitentię.
units.tr: Washing. David understood this, Psalm 51. Thus we are taught in 1 John 1. And we are reminded of it in the Creed. Meanwhile it should be observed that there is need of public confession, lest we be ashamed of our repentance.

units.la: ¶3. Sernemini a generatione hæc prau a. Et hoc multis vrget : quia durum erat à recepta patrum religione deficere, vt patet Ioh.6. Vtitur autem Seruandi vocabulo, vt salutem eorum periclitari doceat, & ideo hoc necessarium esse. Ita ergo ad Christum accedamus, vt nihil cum nobis sit cum huius hostibus, Apo. 18 2 Cor.6.Isa.52. Erant hic omnia, quæ istos detinere poterant. Sed erant praua generatio,Iohan.8. Hoc ipsum de nostris quoque potest verissimè dici.
units.tr: ¶3. "Save yourselves from this perverse generation." And he presses this on many: because it was hard to fall away from the religion of the fathers that had been received, as is clear from John 6. He uses the word "save" so as to teach that their salvation was in danger, and therefore that this was necessary. Thus let us come to Christ so that we have nothing to do with his enemies, Revelation 18; 2 Corinthians 6; Isaiah 52. Here were all those things which could detain them. But they were a perverse generation, John 8. This very thing can most truly be said of our own people too.

units.la: 111.Vt dubios & infirmos soletur, duplicem promissionem interserit.1 Accipietis Spiritum sanctum. Quasi dicat:Non modo peccata vobis remittentur, sed eiusdem doni nobiscum participes eritis, si cut prom sum Ioel.2. Et poterat hoc pro mittere ex Christi verbis Ioh.14.
units.tr: 111. To comfort the doubting and weak, he adds a twofold promise. 1. "You shall receive the Holy Spirit." As if he said: not only will your sins be forgiven you, but you will also be partakers with us of the same gift, as was promised in Joel 2. And he could have drawn this promise from the words of Christ in John 14.

units.la: 2.Vobis enim facta est promissio, & filijs, & omnibus qui longè sunt, &c. In mentem reuocat fœdus, Gen.17 & quæ dicta de gentium vocatione, vtsic argumento à comparatis eos consoletur, &c. Et facit huc,quod de reliquijs Iudæorum dicitur, Ioel.2. Isa.10.
units.tr: 2. "For the promise is made to you and to your children, and to all who are afar off, etc." He recalls to mind the covenant, Genesis 17, and what was said about the calling of the Gentiles, so that by an argument from things compared he might comfort them, etc. And what is said of the remnant of the Jews, Joel 2 and Isaiah 10, pertains to this.

units.la: ¶ Bonitatis Dei argumentu, quine n vniuersali quidem repudio suorum obi uiscitur, licet pacucissimi sint. Sic in diluuio, & in Sodomis, &c. Gen.6.7.8.9.18.19. Sic nouissimo tempore propter electos abbreuiabuntur dies, &c. Mat.24.
units.tr: ¶ An argument of God's goodness, that he does not at all times wholly reject his own, although they are very few. So in the flood, and in Sodom, etc., Genesis 6, 7, 8, 9, 18, 19. So in the last time, for the sake of the elect the days will be shortened, etc., Matthew 24.

units.la: Vsus omnium horum sit, vt stos imitemur. Peccauimus omnes, & sentimus iratum Deum. Idem per verbum nos arguit, & intra conscientias proprias convincit. Accedamus ergo ad Deum. Fateamur nos peccasse, vt Dan.9. Imploremus eius misericordiam. Voueamus pœnitentiam & emendationem, neq; nos conuersionis pudeat. Ita salui erimus. Oremus.
units.tr: The use of all these things is that we should imitate them. We have all sinned, and we perceive God to be angry. The same God convicts us by his Word and convinces us within our own consciences. Let us therefore come to God. Let us confess that we have sinned, as Daniel 9. Let us implore his mercy. Let us vow repentance and amendment, and let us not be ashamed of conversion. So we shall be saved. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XIX.
units.tr: HOMILY XIX.

units.la: 41 Qui ergo libenter exceperunt sermonem eius, baptizati sunt: & addita sunt Ecclesiæ die illa circiter tria milia.
units.tr: 41 Those who therefore gladly received his word were baptized, and there were added to the Church that day about three thousand.

units.la: 42 Erant autem perdurantes in doctrina Apostolorum, & communicatione, & fractione panis & precibus.
units.tr: 42 And they continued steadfastly in the doctrine of the Apostles, in fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers.

units.la: 43 Obortus est autem omnibus timor, multaq; miracula & signa per Apostolos edebantur.
units.tr: 43 And fear came upon everyone, and many wonders and signs were done through the Apostles.

units.la: PEtrus prima sua concione Hierosolymitanis ita Christum prædicauit, vt illis simul scelus in hunc commissum exprobrârit. Id vero fecit, vt intra seipsos conuicti, salutis desiderio accenderentur, & ad Christum confugerent. Ideo compunctis consuluit etiam quid faciant. Vbi didicimus, quid hodie etiam faciant, quot quot iram Dei declinare, & salute in Christo asseqqui cupiunt. Sequitur exitus huius actionis, qui duo continet. 1. Quàm multi conuersi. 2. Quid fecerint? Vbi proponetur forma primitiuæ & veræ catholicæ Ecclesiæ, ad quam omnes Ecclesiæ reformari & componi oportet.
units.tr: In his first sermon, Peter preached Christ to the Jerusalemites in such a way that at the same time he rebuked them for the crime they had committed against him. He did this so that, convicted within themselves, they would be kindled with desire for salvation and would flee to Christ. For this reason he also advised the pricked-hearted what they should do. From this we learn what people today should also do, as many as desire to avoid God's wrath and to obtain salvation in Christ. There follows the outcome of this action, which contains two things: 1. how many were converted; 2. what they did. Here is set forth the form of the primitive and true catholic Church, to which all churches ought to be reformed and conformed.

units.la: I. Qui libenter amplexi, &c. Paucis comprehendit rem maximam, qua verè impletum illud Christi, Luc.5.
units.tr: I. "Those who gladly embraced," etc. In a few words he comprehends a very great matter, by which that saying of Christ, Luke 5, was truly fulfilled.

units.la: Not. 1. Bonitate Dei, qui ex Filij sui carnificib. tam multos seruari voluit. Fuerunt indignissimi, Ioh. 18.19. Sed orauit pro illis Christus, Luc.23. Idem in Paulo factum, Act.8.9. Hodie similia fiunt. Vsus ne desperemus in tentationibus, 1 Tim.1. Constat sibi Deus semper, nec fallent promissiones, Ezech.18.Isa.43.
units.tr: Note 1. The goodness of God, who willed that so many be saved from the executioners of his own Son. They were most unworthy, John 18:19. But Christ prayed for them, Luke 23. The same happened in Paul, Acts 8:9. Similar things happen today. Use: that we not despair in temptations, 1 Tim. 1. God is always consistent with himself, and his promises do not fail, Ezek. 18; Isa. 43.

units.la: 2. Vim verbi Dei, & quod nunquam
units.tr: 2. The power of the Word of God, and that it is never

units.la: absque fructu prædicetur. Simile pluuiæ & seminis, Isa.55. Mar.4. Sunt hic remoræ multæ. Populus duræ ceruicis Deut.31.32. Exod.32.33. Sacerdotes impij. Principes exacerbati. Vrbs assueta sanguine, Luc.13. Matth.32. Edicta, Ioh.9.12. Apostoli rudes, obscuri, &c. Sed non obstant hæc omnia, &c. Soletur hoc nos contra impiorum conatus. Habet Deus vbiq; suos electos, quos vocat, quando vult, nec aliquis ipsi resistere poterit.
units.tr: preached without fruit. It is like rain and seed, Isa. 55; Mark 4. There are many hindrances here: a people stiff-necked, Deut. 31, 32; Exod. 32, 33; impious priests; exasperated princes; a city accustomed to blood, Luke 13; Matt. 23; edicts, John 9, 12; the Apostles rude, obscure, etc. But all these things do not stand in the way. This should comfort us against the attempts of the impious. God has his elect everywhere, whom he calls when he wills, and no one will be able to resist him.

units.la: ¶ Arguuntur, qui multos annos audiunt verbum Dei, & non conuertuntur. Vide Bull.
units.tr: ¶ Those are rebuked who hear the Word of God for many years and are not converted. See Bullinger.

units.la: II. Quid fecerint? ¶ 1. Libenter amplexi sunt sermonem. Agnoscunt electi vocem fidei & eius pastoris, & quia Spiritus agit in cordibus ipsorum, sequuntur voluntarij Ps.110. Ioh.10. Ps.19.119. Et hoc est quod Paulus dicit de spiritu ὑοθεσίας, &c. Rom.8. Arguuntur, qui verbum oderunt, & aures obturant, Io.8. ¶ 2. Baptizati sunt, &c. Naaman. Ergo non puduit iam illos Christi & Euangelij sui. Imo voluerunt separari, &c. Rom.1. ¶ 3. Perseuerârunt in doctrina Apostolorum, non admiserunt aues, spinas, &c. Luc.8. In communicatione, id est, beneficentia mutua, de qua post. In fractione panis. Cœnam mysticam intelligit. In precibus publicis nimirum: quibus pri uatæ etiam accesserunt.
units.tr: II. What did they do? ¶ 1. They gladly embraced the word. The elect recognize the voice of faith and of its minister, and because the Spirit works in their hearts, they follow willingly, Ps. 110; John 10; Ps. 19, 119. And this is what Paul says of the spirit of adoption [υἱοθεσίας], etc., Rom. 8. Those are rebuked who hate the word and stop their ears, John 8. ¶ 2. They were baptized, etc. Naaman. Therefore they were not then ashamed of Christ and of his Gospel. Indeed they wished to be separated, etc., Rom. 1. ¶ 3. They persevered in the doctrine of the Apostles; they did not let the birds and thorns in, etc., Luke 8. In fellowship, that is, mutual beneficence, of which more later. In the breaking of bread: he means the mystical Supper. In prayers, namely public ones, to which private ones were also added.

units.la: Habes hic exercitia Ecclesiæ Catholi cæ.Vtile hoc scire hodie.
units.tr: Here you have the exercises of the Catholic Church. It is useful to know this today.

units.la: 1 Doctrina Apostolorum. Hanc primo loco ponit, quia per eam Ecclesia colligi-tur, fides traditur, & nos regeneramur, al-imur quoad animam, Rom.10.1 Pet.1.In ea autem in primis videre oportet, vt certa sit & stabilis: quia non poterunt colligi & in vnitate perfistere, qui incertis doctrinis agitantur, Eph.4. Atqui tales sunt hominum traditiones, quæ ideo damnantur, If 29 Mat 15. Apostolica ergo retineri debet, quæ Christi est (Luc.10.2.Cor.13.) & sola habet promissiones salutis, Ioh.17.
units.tr: 1. The doctrine of the Apostles. He puts this first, because through it the Church is gathered, faith is handed down, and we are regenerated and nourished as to the soul, Rom. 10; 1 Pet. 1. In it, however, one must chiefly see that it be certain and stable, because those who are tossed about by uncertain doctrines cannot be gathered or persevere in unity, Eph. 4. Yet such are the traditions of men, which are therefore condemned, Isa. 29; Matt. 15. Therefore the apostolic doctrine, which is Christ's (Luke 10; 2 Cor. 13), must be retained, and it alone has the promises of salvation, John 17.

units.la: Mar.16.Gal.1.Hæc duo tradit: 1. Salutis ratione. Ibi docet nos peccatores & mortis reos esse &c. Ro.1.2.7 Iustitia vero & vi-tam monstrat in gratia Dei per vnu Chri-stum,2.Cor.5.1.Cor.1.2.Act.4.1.Iohan.1.2. &c. Hunc fide apprehendi, & ideo hac nos iustificari & seruari, Ioh.3.4.5 Rom.3.Act.15.2. Officia vitæ Christianæ. Consistit hoc in dilectione Dei & proximi, Luc.10. ad Romanos decimotertio, ad Galatas quinto. Hinc obedientia fidei & innocentia vitæ, ad Romanos decimosexto. 1. Thessal.4. In hac doctrina perseueremus, Gal.1.2.Tim.3. Qui deficiunt,in fe&tas fcin duntur.
units.tr: Mark 16; Gal. 1. He hands down these two things: 1. with respect to salvation. There he teaches us that we are sinners and guilty of death, etc., Rom. 1, 2, 7. But he shows righteousness and life in the grace of God through the one Christ, 2 Cor. 5; 1 Cor. 1, 2; Acts 4; John 1, 2, etc. This is apprehended by faith, and therefore we are justified and saved by it, John 3, 4, 5; Rom. 3; Acts 15. 2. The duties of the Christian life. This consists in the love of God and neighbour, Luke 10; to the Romans chapter thirteen; to the Galatians chapter five. Hence obedience of faith and innocence of life, to the Romans chapter sixteen; 1 Thess. 4. Let us persevere in this doctrine, Gal. 1, 2; 2 Tim. 3. Those who fail are led astray into sects.

units.la: 2. Communicatio. Intelligitur mutua beneficentia,Heb.13.Subtexitur doctrinę, quia per hanc in vnū corpus colligimur. Debemus ergo omnia habere communia 1.Cor.12.
units.tr: 2. Fellowship. It is understood as mutual beneficence, Heb. 13. It is appended to the doctrine, because through this we are gathered into one body. We ought therefore to have all things in common, 1 Cor. 12.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Argui eos, qui nullius miserijs tanguntur, dummodo ipsis bene fit.Ila 5. Amos 6 Luc.16.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ Those are rebuked who are not moved by anyone's miseries, provided only that it goes well for themselves. Isa. 5; Amos 6; Luke 16.

units.la: 3. Coena Domini. Sub hac baptismus comprehenditur: de quo prius. Vocat panis fractionem: quia illic panis frangitur in memoriam mortis Christi, deinde in peccatorum confessionem,& vt communionis admoneamur.1.Cor.10.Vbi NOT. ¶ Simplicitatem primitiuæ Ecclesiæ,quæ ritum à Christo traditum retinuit: nihil ex se affinxit.Obseruandū hoc:quia vt pri mum receditur à prima institutione, non sunt amplius Sacramenta, Isa.1.Psalm 50. Ier.4.7 1.Corinth.11. Quid ergo de Missa iudicesi?De Lutherizantibus item.
units.tr: 3. The Lord's Supper. Under this the baptism is included, of which we spoke before. It calls it the breaking of bread, because there the bread is broken in memory of the death of Christ, then in confession of sins, and so that we may be reminded of communion, 1 Cor. 10. Here NOTE ¶ the simplicity of the primitive Church, which retained the rite handed down by Christ and added nothing of its own. This must be observed, because as soon as one departs from the first institution, these are no longer sacraments, Isa. 1; Ps. 50; Jer. 4, 7; 1 Cor. 11. What then do you judge of the Mass? And likewise of the Lutheranizers.

units.la: 4. Preces:Opus his,quia fine Deo nihil possumus, & commendantur promissione peculiari,Mat.18. Ideo semper in vsu fuerunt. Tempore prophetarum, Ioel. 2.Apostolorum 1. Tim.2.Vide Tertull.
units.tr: 4. Prayers. These are necessary, because without God we can do nothing, and they are commended by a special promise, Matt. 18. Therefore they have always been in use: in the time of the prophets, Joel 2; of the Apostles, 1 Tim. 2. See Tertullian.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Hæc olim satis fuisse cum Ecclesia essetfanctisima. Cur ergo haeretici dicuntur hodie,qui his solis contenti, nihil praeterea volunt respicere?
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ These things were once sufficient when the Church was most holy. Why, then, are those called heretics today who, content with these alone, wish to look at nothing beyond them?

units.la: III. Fructus istorum. 1. Obortus est timor & c. Innuit tutos fuisse & securos. Ingens miraculum. Sed Deus terruit hostes,ne quid auderent. Sic olim Psal.105 Gen.35.
units.tr: III. The fruits of these things. 1. Fear came upon them, etc. He hints that they were safe and secure. A great miracle. But God terrified their enemies, so that they would not dare anything. So of old, Ps. 105; Gen. 35.

units.la: II. Quotidie fiebant prodigia & signa per Apostolos, quae doctrinam confirmabant, & quibus plures alij attrahebantur.
units.tr: II. Daily prodigies and signs were done through the Apostles, which confirmed the doctrine and by which many others were drawn in.

units.la: Nota. Quae optima ratio pacis & securitatis obtinendae? Si nos Deo accom modemus,& eidem obediamus,Psalm.81. Isaiae 48 Potest is tueri, cum in sua manu sint corda omnium. Vultitem, Iohan.14. Matthaei 28 Hodie mundi amicitiam Deo praeferimus,& nostris consilijs circumferimur. Imo plerique ludunt cum Deo & verbo eius. Hinc omnia nobis infesta. Oremus.
units.tr: Note. What is the best way of obtaining peace and security? If we accommodate ourselves to God and obey him, Ps. 81; Isa. 48. He can protect us, since the hearts of all are in his hand. He wills it, John 14; Matt. 28. Today we prefer the friendship of the world to God, and we are carried about by our own counsels. Indeed, many play with God and his Word. Hence everything is hostile to us. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XX.
units.tr: HOMILY XX.

units.la: 44 Omnes autem qui credebant erant eodem loci, & habebant omnia communia.
units.tr: 44 And all who believed were in the same place, and had all things in common.

units.la: 45 Et possessiones & facultates vendebant, & dispertiebant ea omnibus,prout cuique opus erat, etc. ad finem Capitis.
units.tr: 45 And they sold their possessions and goods, and distributed them to all, as each had need, etc. to the end of the chapter.

units.la: VT omnis salus in vno Christo habe tur, ita illius nemo potest particeps efle,nisi qui Ecclesiae eius membrum fuerit. Illa enim ideo Christi corpus dicitur, quod per fidem vnita huic ceu capiti cohaeret, qui vitae spiritum in singulis membris diffundit; Ephe.1.4. Vide Symbolum Apostolicum. Quia autem sectae ferè omnes Ecclesia Dei dici volunt, Lucas primam Ecclesiam diligenter describit, vt ex ea de aliis omnibus iudicare posumus, & simul discamus,quid nobis opus sit facto. Faciunt huc quae praecesserunt, in quibus expofuitEcclesiae illius exercitia,&c.Quia autem quaedam diligentiori declaratione opus habebant, eam in praesenti subijcit, vnà cum felici eorum successu.
units.tr: As all salvation is had in the one Christ, so no one can be a partaker of him unless he is a member of his Church. For it is called the body of Christ because, united by faith, it clings to him as to its head, who pours the spirit of life into the individual members; Eph. 1.4. See the Apostles' Creed. But since almost all sects wish to be called the Church of God, Luke describes the first Church carefully, so that from it we may judge all others and at the same time learn what we need to do. What came before bears on this, where he set out the exercises of that Church, etc. But since some things needed a more careful explanation, he now adds them, together with their happy outcome.

units.la: I. De communicatione agit,Primò conjunctos fuisse dicit,animis nimirum. Id est, vt omnia haberent comunia,&c. NOTA.
units.tr: I. He treats of fellowship. First he says they were joined together in mind, namely, that they had all things in common, etc. NOTE.

units.la: {1}. Quae communicationis huius ratio fuerit? Sunt enim qui Platonicam fingunt,& rerum proprietatem tollunt. Errant, quod ex singulari exemplo legem faciunt,nec vident,quid Deus alibi statuat. 1. Oeconomiam praecipit, & diuitibus sua officia praescribit,1.Tim,5.6. 2.Furta pro hibet & fraudes, Exod.20.21. 3.Exempla plura sunt eorum,qui sua retinuerunt &c.
units.tr: {1}. What was the reason for this fellowship? For there are those who imagine a Platonic arrangement and abolish the ownership of property. They are mistaken, because they make a law out of a single example, and do not see what God establishes elsewhere. (1) He prescribes household management and prescribes their duties to the rich, 1 Tim. 5.6. (2) He forbids thefts and frauds, Exod. 20.21. (3) There are many examples of those who kept what was their own, etc.

units.la: {1} De communicatione.
units.tr: {1} On fellowship.

units.la: Iosephus Arimathæus, Matt.27.Lazarus, Ioh.11.16.Mulieres Luc.8.4.Ipse Christus nullius rem tractauit temere ipso inuito, Matt.21.26. Denique hic locus docet pro prietatem non esse prohibitam. Alioqui non licuisset his sua vendere. Deinde distributionis mentio fit,&c. Adhæc nemi-nem coegerunt,&c.Actor 5. Multos item sua retinuisse patet in domib. &c. In Cornelio,Lydia,Caio,Acto 10.12.16.Rom 16. Philem. Quod ergo hic factum, tempori seruiuit. Excommunicabantur Christi di icipuli,Ioh.9 12. Ne ergo egestas cogeret redire ad Iudaeos,ita rem ordinarunt. Et quia charitas regnabat, voluntate omnia habuerunt communia,&c.
units.tr: Joseph of Arimathea, Matt. 27. Lazarus, John 11.16. The women, Luke 8.4. Christ himself never touched anyone's property rashly, against the owner's will, Matt. 21.26. Finally, this passage teaches that ownership was not forbidden; otherwise they would not have been allowed to sell their goods. Next, mention is made of distribution, etc. Moreover, they compelled no one, etc., Acts 5. It is also clear that many kept their goods in their houses, etc. In Cornelius, Lydia, Gaius, Acts 10, 12, 16, Rom. 16, Philem. What was done here, therefore, served the circumstances of the time. The disciples of Christ were excommunicated, John 9.12. So, lest want force them to return to the Jews, they arranged things in this way. And because love reigned, they had all things in common by their own willing, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Officia Christianorum:vt ipsi quo-que pauperibus prospiciant. Monet Lex, Deut.15. Hanc collapsam sub Sacerdotib. instaurarunt Apostoli hic, &c. Acto 4.11. Gal.2 2.Corin.8 9.1.Cor.16.&c.Caulæ:1. Quia mendicatio aduersatur charitati,Lu-cæ 10. 2.Discipline officit, 2 Thess.3.&c liberis,&c.3.Diffamat professionem nomi-nis Christiani,&c. Imo qui negligunt, à Iudæis iudicabuntur.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The duties of Christians: that they should also provide for the poor. The Law admonishes this, Deut. 15. The apostles here restored what had fallen under the priests, etc., Acts 4.11, Gal. 2.2, 2 Cor. 8, 9, 1 Cor. 16, etc. Reasons: (1) because begging is opposed to charity, Luke 10; (2) it hinders discipline, 2 Thess. 3, etc.; (3) it brings disrepute on the profession of the Christian name, etc. Indeed, those who neglect this will be judged by the Jews.

units.la: ¶ 3.Quomodo prosppiciendum egenis? Num vt otientur? Minimè, sed vt labo-rent. Vide 2.Thess.3.Eph.4. Obseruarunt hoc in bene constitutis Rebuspub. Athe-nienses,Mafsilienses. Quanto æquius,vt illi cogantur ad laborem, qui volunt ex publico viuere? Exigit hoc çum Lege Adamo data,Gen.3.Pf 128.
units.tr: ¶ 3. How should the needy be provided for? Surely not so that they may be idle? By no means, but so that they may labour. See 2 Thess. 3, Eph. 4. The Athenians and Massilians observed this in their well-ordered commonwealths. How much more just is it that those be compelled to labour who wish to live at public expense? This is required by the Law given to Adam, Gen. 3, Ps. 128.

units.la: II. Coetus ipsorum describit, vt often- dat,eos non in occulto modò Christianos fuisse,sed publi è etiam, &c.Ro.1,Mar.8. Quotidie perseuerârunt vnanimiter in templo. Habuerunt ergo cœtus frequentes.Et quidem in templo,non vt sacris Iudæorum interessent(Ioh.17.Heb.9.Acto. 7.15.) sed vt plures lucrifacerent. Idem Christus obseruauit,Luc.22.Ioh.18.
units.tr: II. He describes their assembly, showing that they were Christians not only in secret but also openly, etc., Rom. 1, Mark 8. "They persevered daily with one accord in the temple." They therefore had frequent assemblies. And indeed in the temple, not so as to take part in the sacred rites of the Jews (John 17, Heb. 9, Acts 7.15), but so as to win more people. Christ himself observed the same, Luke 22, John 18.

units.la: Nota. 1. Cœtus sacros inter exercitia religionis esse præcipuum. In his fit publica professio fidei,1.Cor.10. In his prædicatur, oratur, Sacramenta vsurpantur. Ideo in Lege præcepti,Deut.6. Obseruâruntsanĉti diligêtissimè. Vide Dauidem. Veteres Christianos. Nostri sæculi vbi persecutiones seruent. Nos in eo prodimus teporem nostrû,quòd emanendi occasiones quærimus.
units.tr: Note. (1) Sacred assemblies are the chief of the exercises of religion. In these public profession of faith is made, 1 Cor. 10. In these preaching takes place, prayer is offered, and the sacraments are used. Therefore a precept is given in the Law, Deut. 6. The saints observed this most diligently; see David, the early Christians. In our age, where persecutions are absent, we betray our lukewarmness in this, that we seek occasions for staying away.

units.la: 2. Vnanimitatis toties fieri mentionem. Exigitur hæc semper à Christianis, Ioh.17.1.Cor.12.Eph.4. In primis autē in cœtibus hanc requirūt, Doctrina, Preces (Matth.5.18.) Sacramenta,1.Corinth.10.
units.tr: (2) That the mention of unanimity is made so often. This is always required of Christians, John 17, 1 Cor. 12, Eph. 4. Above all they require it in assemblies: in doctrine, in prayers (Matt. 5.18), and in the sacraments, 1 Cor. 10.

units.la: Hos adituri deponant,odium,fastum,pro ximi contemptum.
units.tr: Those who are about to enter these should put aside hatred, pride and contempt for their neighbour.

units.la: III. De priuata illorum vita: Frangebant panem, &c. Loquitur partim de coena my-stica, quam in priuatis ædibus egerunt, quod in téplo non liceret: partim de conuiuijs, vt ostendat, illos non modò in publico contulisse, sed priuatim quoq; ex ijs, quæ sibi feruârant, fuisse beneficos.
units.tr: III. On the private life of those people: "They broke bread, etc." He speaks partly of the mystical supper, which they celebrated in private houses because it was not allowed in the temple; partly of banquets, to show that they not only contributed in public but also, in private, were generous with what they had kept for themselves.

units.la: Vbi Nota. Conuiuiorum rationem. Vetus mos, vt honoris & amicitiæ ergo agantur, Gen. 18.21.26.43.&c. Ioh. 12. Sed in his semper habenda pauperum ratio, Deut. 16. Lu. 14. Deinde obseruentur quæ de his dicuntur. 1. Hilaritas sançta, ne pi-geat beneficentiæ, Rom. 12.2. Cor. 9.2. Simplicitas cordis, ne dolus subsit, &c. 3. Gratiarum actio. Commendat hanc Lex naturæ, cum Dei conuiuæ simus, Psal. 104. 147. Matt. 6. Eadem cibos sanctificat, 1. Tim. 4. Prohibet luxum & intemperantiam, If. 5. Ex his œconomiæ leges sibijpsis sanciant Christiani homines.
units.tr: Here note the manner of banquets. It is an old custom that they be held for the sake of honour and friendship, Gen. 18.21.26.43, etc., John 12. But in these a regard for the poor must always be had, Deut. 16, Luke 14. Next, the things said about them should be observed. (1) Holy cheerfulness, so that they do not grudge beneficence, Rom. 12.2 Cor. 9.2. (2) Simplicity of heart, so that no deceit lies beneath, etc. (3) Thanksgiving. The law of nature commends this, since we are guests of God, Ps. 104, 147, Matt. 6. The same sanctifies food, 1 Tim. 4. It forbids luxury and intemperance, Isa. 5. From these things Christians should lay down rules of household management for themselves.

units.la: Fructus omnium fuit duplex. 1. Gratiam habuerunt apud omnes cordatiores nimirû. Impijs enim terrori fuerunt. Obseruandum, quæ ratio sit acquirendæ gratiæ & authoritatis? Nimirum expietatis & gloriæ Dei studio, 1. Sam. 2. His studeant ministri & magistratus. Imo singuli. Hodie die fauorem hominum quaerimus licentia morum, & bonarum legum dissipatione.
units.tr: The fruit of all this was twofold. (1) They gained favour among all the more discerning, for among the impious they were a terror. What is the method of gaining favour and authority to be observed? Namely, by zeal for piety and the glory of God, 1 Sam. 2. Ministers and magistrates should strive for this, and indeed each individual. Today we seek the favour of men through licence of morals and the dissipation of good laws.

units.la: {q}2. Dominus quotidie addebat Ecclesiae. Incrementum ergo ex Deo est, 1. Corin 3. Accedit hoc si eius ordo seruetur. Imitemur ergo horum studia, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: {q}(2) The Lord added to the Church daily. The increase therefore comes from God, 1 Cor. 3. This happens if his order is kept. Let us therefore imitate their zeal, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPUT III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: HOMILIA XXI.
units.tr: HOMILY XXI.

units.la: CAeterum Petrus & Iohannes simul ascendebant in templum sub horam precationis nempe nonam.
units.tr: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, namely the ninth hour.

units.la: 2 Quidam autem vir claudus ab vtero matris suae portabatur: quem ponebant quotidie ad portam templi quae dicitur speciosa, vt peteret eleemosynam ab iis qui ingrediebantur in templum, &c. ad ver. 9.
units.tr: And a certain man who was lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms from those who entered the temple, etc., to verse 9.

units.la: Voniam Euangelium a seculo abscónditum (Rom. 16.) & proinde eius doctrina noua atq; insolens fuit, Christus illud non modo obiter praedicari voluit, sed Apostolos suos miraculis quoq; instruxit, quibus suam doctrinam confirmarent, Mar. 16. Nuper ergo de illis in genere locutus est Lucas. Vt autem costaret qualia illa fuerint, nunc vnum ex multis describit, quod vt totam salutis rationem adumbrat: ita occasionem dedit concioni nouæ,qua homi num aliquot millia conuersa sunt.
units.tr: Because the Gospel had been hidden from the world (Rom. 16), its teaching was new and unusual. Christ wished it to be preached not only in passing, but also equipped his apostles with miracles, by which they might confirm their doctrine (Mark 16). Luke had recently spoken of these in general terms. So that it might be clear what they were like, he now describes one of the many, which in a way sketches the whole account of salvation. Thus he gave occasion for a new sermon, by which some thousands of men were converted.

units.la: I. Occasio.Petrus & Iohannes hora no na precationis, &c. Fuerunt statæ horæ precationis,manè & vesperi,quando sacri ficabatur,Exod.29 Num.28. Accessit deinde meridiana quoq;, Dan.6 Act 10. Et necesse est ista publicè & priuatim obseruari, quando sine precibus nihil bene fit, & omnia nostra à Deo pendent, Prou.16. Quòd verò hodie pulsui nolarum alligantur preces, superstitiosum est,& vitandū, ne Papis communicemus,Apoc 18.
units.tr: I. The occasion. Peter and John at the ninth hour of prayer, etc. There were fixed hours of prayer, morning and evening, when the sacrifice was offered (Exod. 29; Num. 28). Then a midday hour was added as well (Dan. 6; Acts 10). These hours must be observed both publicly and privately, since nothing is done well without prayer, and all our affairs depend on God (Prov. 16). But that today prayers are tied to the ringing of bells is superstitious and to be avoided, lest we have fellowship with the Papists (Rev. 18).

units.la: Interim No T. ¶ Apostolorum sedulita tem, qui etiamsi multos haberent hostes, omnem tamen occasione captârunt propagandi regni Christi. Imitemur. Quia enim Christus idem fecit propter nos, in excusabiles erimus, si nos simus segnio res.Hoc obseruent tepidi illi,qui omnem occasionem negligunt,Ierc.48.
units.tr: Meanwhile note the diligence of the apostles, who, although they had many enemies, nevertheless seized every opportunity of spreading the kingdom of Christ. Let us imitate them. For since Christ did the same on our behalf, we will be inexcusable if we are slower. Let those lukewarm people observe this, who neglect every opportunity (Jer. 48).

units.la: II. Persona miraculi describitur,vt eluce at virtus Christi. Claudus ab vtero, vt ge stari eū oporteret.Quadragenarius,ideo que incurabilis. Accedit quòd mendicus.
units.tr: II. The person healed is described, so that the power of Christ may shine forth. Lame from the womb, so that he had to be carried. He was forty years old, and therefore incurable. Moreover, he was a beggar.

units.la: Et pulchrè hoc proponitur ijs, quę nuper audiuimus de Ecclesia. Hæc Dei lege seruauit, & licet haberet pauperes, tamen ita illis prospexit, ne mendicarent, Deutero-nodecimo quinto. Sacerdotes & Senio-res ècōtra suos neglexerunt. Arguuntur igitur exemplo primitiuæ Ecclesiæ, & eo dem nostri quoque seculi homines damnantur.
units.tr: This is set forth beautifully in view of what we heard recently about the Church. She kept the law of God, and although she had poor people, she so provided for them that they did not have to beg (Deut. 15). The priests and elders, on the contrary, neglected their own. They are therefore rebuked by the example of the primitive Church, and the men of our own age are condemned by the same example.

units.la: Nota. Mala, quibus premimur, nos nō arcere à gratia Dei, sed potiùs nos præparare, vt in nobis Dei gloria illustretur. Docet hoc Christus Iohan. 9. In præsenti idem cernitur. Sic in publicis calamitatibus. In Ægypto Exod. 1 2 3. 12. 14. In Babylone, Dan. 5. Ergo nemo temerè damnari debet propter aduersa. In hoc lobi amici offendunt. Hodie multi. Imò si constet aliquos meruisse, tamen ineunda ratio, quę docetur Luc. 13.
units.tr: Note. The evils by which we are pressed do not keep us from the grace of God, but rather prepare us, so that the glory of God may be displayed in us. Christ teaches this in John 9, and it is seen in the present case too. So it is in public calamities: in Egypt (Exod. 1, 2, 3, 12, 14), in Babylon (Dan. 5). Therefore no one should be rashly condemned on account of adversity. In this Job's friends went wrong, and many today do the same. Indeed, even if it were established that some had deserved their suffering, the principle taught in Luke 13 must still be borne in mind.

units.la: In primis soletur hoc nos, ne desperemus. Potest in extremis laborantes Deus iuuare, &c. Ifa. 28. Et si patienter feramus, plus dat quàm petamus. Factum hoc in præsenti, &c. Sic Abrahamo, Gen. 17. 18. 21. Israelitis, Exod. 12. Dauidi, 2. Sam. 7. Et ho die temporaria quærentibus, æterna ille offert, Matth. 6.
units.tr: Above all, let this console us, that we do not despair. God can help those who labour in extremity (Isa. 28). And if we bear our trouble patiently, he gives more than we ask. This has happened in the present case, etc. So it was with Abraham (Gen. 17, 18, 21), with the Israelites (Exod. 12), and with David (2 Sam. 7). And today he offers eternal things to those who seek temporal ones (Matt. 6).

units.la: III. Miraculum. Petrus iubet respicere:
units.tr: III. The miracle. Peter bids him look up:

units.la: nimirum vt attentu reddat,& maius quid sperare doceat. Ideo eximit spem pecuniae: Aurum & argentum,&c. Quibus vero bis primo paupertatem profitetur. Erat enim ex eorum numero, qui omnia reliquerant,Mar.10. Deinde animum benefi cum offert,Quasi dicat:Si aurum & argentum haberem,etiam hoc darem,&c. Itaq; in nomine Iesu,&c.Nec mora manu praehensum erigit,&c.
units.tr: clearly so as to make him attentive and to teach him to hope for something greater. Therefore he sets aside any hope of money: Silver and gold, etc. By these words he first professes his poverty, for he was one of those who had left everything (Mark 10). Then he offers a generous spirit, as if to say: If I had silver and gold, I would give you this as well, etc. And so, in the name of Jesus, etc. Without delay he takes him by the hand and raises him up, etc.

units.la: No T. ¶ 1.Apostolos non opum huius seculi,sed mysteriorum regni Dei dispensatores fuisse,1.Cor.4.Id ita obseruarunt, vt mensis pauperum noluerint ministrare,Act.6.
units.tr: Note 1. The apostles were dispensers not of the wealth of this age but of the mysteries of the kingdom of God (1 Cor. 4). They observed this so strictly that they were unwilling to serve tables for the poor (Acts 6).

units.la: Arguit hoc primum eos,qui sub Euangelij praetextu ditescunt:Deinde Pontifices,qui Petri patrimonium iactant,& hoc nomine omnia regna sibi vendicant. Id vero ne Christus quidem fecit, Iohan.18. Luc.2 Fecit autem Satan,Matt.4. Et Antichristo tribuuntur thesauri, Daniel.11. Itaq; illius vicarij &ἀντιχεἰμενοι illi sunt 2.Thess.2.Pet.2. Idq; eo clarius apparet, quod hisce Petri verbis improbè illudūt, dum creantur.
units.tr: This rebukes, first, those who grow rich under the pretext of the Gospel; then the Pontiffs, who boast of the patrimony of Peter and on this ground claim all kingdoms for themselves. Yet Christ himself did not do this (John 18; Luke 2). Satan did it (Matt. 4). And treasures are attributed to Antichrist (Dan. 11). Therefore his vicars and opponents [ἀντικείμενοι] are those (2 Thess. 2; 2 Pet. 2). And this appears all the more clearly because they shamefully mock us with these words of Peter, while they are being created.

units.la: ¶ 2. Typum nostrae restitutionis. Eadem omnium nostrum conditio,quae istius. Corrupti & peccatores ex vtero matris. Gen.5.Pfal.51.Et ex nobis ipsis nihil possumus,Gen.8.2.Corin.3. Quoad humanis praesidijs gestamur,mendici fumus.Vt ve rò hunc bonitate sua praeuenit Deus per Petrum: Ita nos omnes,&c. Gen.3.Act.14. Vt idem Christi nomine fanatur,quem illi Petrus praedicat, simulque praehensa manu erigit: Ita omnibus nobis Deus in Christo per Euangelium quasi manu por rigit,&c.Matth.3 17.11.Iohan 15.Qui hunc apprehendunt fide, ij fe renasci & instaurari sentiunt.
units.tr: 2. A type of our restoration. Our condition is the same as his: corrupt and sinners from the mother's womb (Gen. 5; Ps. 51). Of ourselves we can do nothing (Gen. 8; 2 Cor. 3). As far as human aids go, we are carried, we are beggars. Just as God anticipated him in his goodness through Peter, so he anticipates all of us (Gen. 3; Acts 14). Just as the man is healed in the name of Christ, whom Peter preaches to him, and at the same time is raised up by the hand, so God in Christ, through the Gospel, raises all of us, as it were by the hand (Matt. 3:17; 17:5; John 15). Those who grasp him by faith feel themselves reborn and restored.

units.la: ¶ 3.Officium eorum,qui restituti sunt.
units.tr: 3. The duty of those who have been restored.

units.la: 1. Exilit. Ita nos exiliamus è peccatorum luto. Idem docet exemplum Bartimaei, Mar.10.Roman.6. 2.Cum Apostolis templum ingreditur. Ecclesiae typus, in qua Christus reposuit thesauros suos,1.Tim.3. Huic ergo nos quoq; coniungamur,ducibus Apostolis,Ioh.17. Neq; nos detineat speciosa porta ceremoniarum. Symbolum.3.Exultauit laudans Deum.Gaudeamus ipsi quoq; in Dn.inter media certamina affliictionum,Phil.3.4.Ioh.16. Laudemus ite Dominu. Hoc illi sacrificium est gratisimum,Pfal.69.&116. Exigitur hic confessio fidei, ne nos Christi Seruatoris pudeat,Mar.8.Rom.10. Vbi tamen videndum, vt vita tota Christum referat, Iac.2.
units.tr: 1. He leaps up. So we leap up from the mire of sin. The example of Bartimaeus teaches the same (Mark 10; Rom. 6). 2. He enters the temple with the apostles. This is a type of the Church, in which Christ has laid up his treasures (1 Tim. 3). Let us therefore join ourselves to her, with the apostles as our leaders (John 17). Let not the beautiful gate of ceremonies hold us back. (Creed, art. 3.) He leapt and praised God. Let us also rejoice in the midst of the struggles of affliction (Phil. 3, 4; John 16). Let us praise the Lord. This is a most pleasing sacrifice to him (Ps. 69; 116). Here the confession of faith is required, lest we be ashamed of Christ our Saviour (Mark 8; Rom. 10). Yet here we must take care that our whole life refers to Christ (James 2).

units.la: Matth. 5. Tit. 1. In his fere hodie cessatur. Studeamus ergo emedationi & Oremus.
units.tr: (Matt. 5; Titus 1.) Nearly today people are idle in these things. Let us therefore labour at amendment. And let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXII.

units.la: 9 Viditq; eum totus populus ambulantem & laudantem Deum.
units.tr: 9 And all the people saw him walking and praising God.

units.la: 10 Et agnouerunt eum esse, qui ad petendum eleemosynam sedebat ad speciosam portam templi, & impleti sunt pauore & stupore super eo quod ei contig-rat, &c. ad ver. 13.
units.tr: 10 And they knew that he was the one who used to sit begging alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him, etc., to verse 13.

units.la: INter miracula Apostolorum primum narratur, quo claudus ab vtero matris lanatus est. Voluit eo illorum doctrinam de Christo Deo obsignare, vt cóstet hunc esse Seruatorem, qui vitiosi nostrae naturae medeatur, & a peccato simul atq; eius poena liberet. At quia is nemini salutaris est, nisi qui eum digne excipit, narratur quoque quid fecerit claudus. Imitentur hunc omnes. 1. Exiliant e luto peccatorum vocati. 2. Reliquis superstitionibus ad Ecclesiam accedant cum Apostolis. 3 Exulent in Christo, & Deum laudent. Deniq; ad huius gloriam omnia dirigant. Sequitur quid populus fecerit, vtq; Petro data nouae concionis occasio.
units.tr: Among the miracles of the Apostles, the first recorded is the one by which the man lame from his mother's womb was healed. Through it the Lord meant to confirm their teaching about Christ as God, so that it might be established that he is the Saviour who heals our faulty nature and frees us at once from sin and its punishment. But since he is of no benefit to anyone unless he is received worthily, the narrative also tells what the lame man did. Let all imitate him: (1) those called out of the mire of their sins should leap up; (2) they should come to the Church with the Apostles, leaving behind their other superstitions; (3) they should exult in Christ and praise God. Finally, they should direct everything to his glory. Next follows what the people did, and how an occasion for a new sermon was given to Peter.

units.la: I. Postquam vidit sanatum, & cognouit, quod is esset, &c. Ita asseritur rei veritas. tas. Ideo admirabundi confluunt ad A-poftolos,&c.
units.tr: I. After they saw him healed and learned who he was, etc. In this way the truth of the matter is asserted. Therefore, astonished, they flock to the Apostles, etc.

units.la: NOT. 1. Quòd miraculi nouitate ftu pent. Debent enim opera Dei non ofcitan ter considerari. Sabbathi vsus Exod. 20. Hac enim præparatione ad Dei cognitionem venitur. Reuelat quidem fe & volun tatem suam Deus in suo verbo, &c. Sed quia ofcitantiores fumus, ferè opera coniungit, quibus excitemur. Hic ergo fiat quod Ioh. 3.7. Et sic ipse monet, Ioh. 5.10. 25. At hic non solum miraculofa opera considerari debent, sed quæcunque is facit, vt vel puniat contumaces, vel suos tueatur. In eo plurimum peccatur. Audimus verbum. Confirmat Deus mirabili suæ Ecclesiæ defensione, & pœnarum exemplis. Sed quid fit? Qui optimi sunt, negligunt, vt fortuita. Alij ridentz. Pet. 3. Fit ergo quod prædictum Mat. 24.1. Thef. 5. Sed vel eo viso capita attollamus, Lucæ 21.
units.tr: NOTE 1. That they are struck by the novelty of the miracle. For the works of God ought not to be considered with indifference. The use of the Sabbath, Exod. 20. For through this preparation one comes to the knowledge of God. God indeed reveals himself and his will in his word, etc. But since we are rather sluggish, he often joins works to it by which we may be roused. Here, then, let what is said in John 3:7 be done, and so he himself admonishes, John 5:10, 25. But here not only miraculous works ought to be considered, but whatever he does, whether to punish the obstinate or to protect his own. Much sin is committed in this respect. We hear the word. God confirms his Church by a wonderful defence and by examples of punishment. But what happens? Those who are best neglect these things as if they were accidental; others mock. 2 Pet. 3. So what Matt. 24 foretold comes to pass. 1 Thess. 5. But even if we see this, let us lift up our heads, Luke 21.

units.la: ¶ 2. Errorem reprehensione dignum, quòd solos Apostolos respiciunt, &c. Est hoc carnis ingenium, præfentibus modò inhærere, &c. Hinc superstitiones natæ apud gentes, Rom. 1. Ita inter Christianos factum. Initium ex Legendis. Hinc inuocatio, vota, imagines, quæ Satan nouis miraculis nobilitauit.
units.tr: ¶ 2. An error worthy of reproof is that they look only to the Apostles, etc. It is the nature of the flesh to cling to what is present, etc. Hence superstitions arose among the nations, Rom. 1. So it happened among Christians too, beginning from the Legends. Hence invocation, vows, and images, which Satan has ennobled with new miracles.

units.la: {q}Ergo non debent illa abfq; verbo Dei considerari. Sunt enim vera & falsa. Vera, quæ verè fiunt, & quæ veritatem confirmant, vt Apostolorum, Matth.10. Mar.16. Falsa, quæ vel decipiunt præstigijs, vel à veritate auocant: vt Magorum, Exo.5. Antichristi, 2 Thess.2. Matt.24. Permittit hęc Deus ob duas causas, Deut.13. 2 Thessal.2. Ne ergo temere credas doctrinæ cuiuis, sed probemus omnia, 1 Thess.5. 1 Iohan.4. Id nisi fiat, per vera quoq; possumus edu-ci, vt hic & Lyftren. Act 14.
units.tr: {q} Therefore these ought not to be considered apart from the word of God. For there are true and false ones. True are those that truly happen and confirm the truth, such as those of the Apostles, Matt. 10, Mark 16. False are those that either deceive by illusions or draw us away from the truth, such as those of the magicians, Exod. 5, and of Antichrist, 2 Thess. 2, Matt. 24. God permits these for two reasons, Deut. 13, 2 Thess. 2. Therefore do not believe every teaching rashly, but let us test all things, 1 Thess. 5, 1 John 4. Unless this is done, we can be led astray even by true things, as here and at Lystra, Acts 14.

units.la: II. Petrus ex populi admiratione do-cendi occasionem arripit, vbi rursus appa-ret Apostolorum feruor. Num autem ab-utitur vulgi stupore? Minimè. Imo Chri-sti gloriam asserit, & horum saluti consu-lit. 1. Ignorantiæ eorum medetur. 2. Au-thorem indicat, & hic arguit scelus eorū. 3. Pœnitentiam suadet, & vt persuadeat, Christum in Mose & prophetis tradi-cet, &c. Et hunc ad ipsos etiam pertine-re affirmat.
units.tr: II. Peter seizes on the people's admiration as an occasion for teaching, where again the Apostles' fervour appears. Does he, however, take advantage of the crowd's amazement? By no means. Rather he asserts the glory of Christ and consults their salvation. (1) He heals their ignorance. (2) He indicates the author, and here he accuses their crime. (3) He urges repentance, and to persuade them he teaches that Christ is handed down in Moses and the prophets, etc., and he affirms that this pertains to them as well.

units.la: Ignorantiæ & errori medetur: qui ve-rus docendi ordo est. Eadem enim homi-nis conditio, quæ terræ. Hinc illud Vere. Grauiter autem agit Petrus & non sine re prehensione. Quasi dicat: Quid ita obtu-pescitis, cùm multa similia Christus sece-rit? rit? Cur non horum recordamini, & facilé pateret huius etiam author. Nec est quod nos inspiciatis, &c.
units.tr: He heals their ignorance and error, which is the true order of teaching. For the condition of man is the same as that of the earth. Hence that word "Truly." Peter speaks seriously, and not without reason in his rebuke, as if to say: Why are you so stunned, since Christ did many similar things? Why do you not remember these, so that the author of this would also be easily evident? Nor is there any reason for you to look at us, etc.

units.la: NOT. §1. Apostolorum modestiam & fidem, qui honore suum Christo ita vendicant, ut sibi nihil referuent eorum, quae ipsi debentur. Ita omnes sancti, ut qui non-runt illud Isa.42. Sic Baptista, Ioh.1. Matt.3. Ioh.3. Matt.11. Petrus iterum Actor.10. Paulus Act.14.1 Cor.1 3.15. Imo Angeli, Apoc.19.22 Vide Augusti. Hinc ergo regula petatur de omnibus doctrinis & spiritibus, qui apparent. Qui vni Deo fidere docent per Christum, boni sunt.1 Ioh.4. Qui secus, &c. Gal.1 In primis autem arguitur hic, qui vulgi simplicitate abutuntur, & eo argumento defendunt Imagines, Purgatorium, &c. Nullus in religione locus fraudi.
units.tr: NOTE §1. Observe the modesty and faith of the Apostles, who so claim the honour for Christ that they keep nothing back of those things which are due to themselves. So all the saints acted, refusing what Isa. 42 says. So the Baptist, John 1, Matt. 3, John 3, Matt. 11. Peter again, Acts 10; Paul, Acts 14, 1 Cor. 1, 3, 15. Indeed the angels too, Rev. 19, 22. See Augustine. Hence a rule should be sought concerning all doctrines and spirits that appear: those who teach that we trust in the one God through Christ are good, 1 John 4; those who teach otherwise, etc., Gal. 1. But in the first place this rebukes those who abuse the simplicity of the crowd and by this argument defend images, purgatory, etc. In religion nothing should be a cause for deceit.

units.la: §2. Ad quem miracula referri debeant? Spectantur fere potentia & sanctitas eorum, per quos fiunt. Sed hic vtrumque ne-gatur. Quia enim fiunt contra naturam, nihil possunt hic homines, qui ne in naturalibus quidem aliquid possunt, Matth.6.5. 1.Cor.3. Christo soli omnis potestas data, Ioh.3 Matt.28.11. Deinde sanctissimi quique hoc dono caruerunt, Patriarchae, Prophetae plerique. E contra impij saepe illud habuerunt,vt Iudas:Matth.10.Luc.9. Item Matth. 7. Vt ergo non sunt sanctitatis testimonium, ita neque huic debent tribui. Quid enim mereatur homo hic,qui in naturalibus nihil meretur? Deihaec opera sunt, qui ita non strae saluti consulit. Sunt enim doctrinae testimonium, & mentes excitant. Eadem illorum ratio, quae olim apud sepulchra sanctorum facta. Elisaeus, 2.Reg.13.
units.tr: §2. To whom should miracles be referred? Usually one looks at the power and holiness of those through whom they happen. But here both are denied. For since they happen contrary to nature, these men can do nothing, who cannot even do anything in natural things, Matt. 6, 1 Cor. 3. All power has been given to Christ alone, John 3, Matt. 28. Moreover, the most holy of all have lacked this gift, the Patriarchs and most of the Prophets. On the contrary, the impious have often had it, as Judas did, Matt. 10, Luke 9; likewise in Matt. 7. So just as these are no testimony of holiness, neither ought they to be attributed to this man. For what does a man deserve who deserves nothing even in natural things? These works are of God, who thus consults our salvation. For they are a testimony to the doctrine and rouse the minds of men. The reason is the same as that for the things formerly done at the tombs of the saints, Elisha, 2 Kings 13.

units.la: §3. Non ideo suum honorem Diuis debeatur trahi. Agnoscimus illos suo seculo deseruijsse, vt vasa gratiae, Acto.13. Nunc nobis seruire doctrina & exemplo, Luc.10.Mat. 13.1.Cor.11. Quoad animas, in coelis viuere omnis mali expertes, Ifa 63. &c. Mundi gubernationem vni Deo tribuamus, qui nemine opus habet, Psalm.104.113. &c. Salutem in vno Christo quaerimus, vt illi docuerunt, Act.4.1.Tim.2. Sic ipsa Maria, Iohan.2. Quid vero ille iubet? Venite ad me omnes, &c. Matt.11. Iohan.6.7.4. &c. Oremus.
units.tr: §3. Nor is their honour to be transferred to the saints. We acknowledge that they served their own age as vessels of grace, Acts 13. Now they serve us by doctrine and example, Luke 10, Matt. 13, 1 Cor. 11. As to their souls, they live in heaven free of all evil, Isa. 63, etc. Let us attribute the government of the world to the one God, who needs no one, Ps. 104, 113, etc. We seek salvation in the one Christ, as they taught, Acts 4, 1 Tim. 2. So too Mary herself, John 2. But what does he command? "Come to me, all of you," etc., Matt. 11, John 6, 7, 4, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXIII.

units.la: 13 Deus ille Abraham & Isaac & Iacob, Deus inquam, Patrum nostrorum glorificabit Filium suum Iesum sum, quem vos prodidistis, & abnegastis in consessu Pilati, quum ille iudicas- set esse absoluendum,
units.tr: 13 The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God, I say, of our fathers, has glorified his Son Jesus, whom you delivered up and denied in the presence of Pilate, when he had judged him to be released.

units.la: 14 Vos autem sanctum illum & in- stum abnegastis, & postulastis homi- dam condonari vobis, &c. ad Verf. 17.
units.tr: 14 But you denied the holy and just one, and asked that a murderer be granted to you, etc., to verse 17.

units.la: Ovamuis Apostoli claudum non alio, qua Christi nomine sanari, populus tamen admirabundus, in ipsos re- spexit, &c. Ideo Petrus prima sua concio- nis parte errorem istum remouit, & difer te testatus est, nihil vel potentiae vel sanctitati ipsorum tribui debere. Sequitur se- cunda pars, qua miraculi authorem Deum facit, & illos in Christum Mediato- rem respicere docet. Et quia haec praecipua est concionis pars, ordine commodis- simo rem tractat.
units.tr: Although the Apostles healed the lame man by no other power than the name of Christ, the people, astonished, looked upon them. Therefore Peter, in the first part of his sermon, removed this error and testified that nothing should be attributed to their power or holiness. There follows the second part, in which he makes God the author of the miracle and teaches them to look to Christ the Mediator. Because this is the chief part of the sermon, he treats the matter in a most suitable order.

units.la: I. Summa: Deus Abraham, etc. Compre hendit miraculi authorem, Deum & finem. Et vt prius nihil ibuit sibi, ita hic quoque omnia ad Deum refert per Christum.
units.tr: I. Summary: The God of Abraham, etc. It comprehends the author of the miracle, God, and its end. And as before he claimed nothing for himself, so here too he refers everything to God through Christ.

units.la: Not. 1. Dicit Deum Abrahami, &c. Sic ipse Deus de se loquitur, & est hoc ma- gnum bonitatis argumentum, &c. Petrus tamen altius quid spectat. 1. Promissio- nem in mentem reuocat, Gen. 17, 22, 28, 26. Oportebat repeti, quia illas negarant. Ioh. 19. Ne ergo se excidisse putarent, ostendit
units.tr: Note 1. He says "the God of Abraham, etc." Thus God himself speaks of himself, and this is a great argument of his goodness, etc. Yet Peter looks at something deeper. 1. He recalls the promise to mind, Gen. 17, 22, 28, 26. It was necessary to repeat it, because they had denied it, John 19. So that they might not think that he had fallen away, he shows

units.la: Deum illum adhuc viuere,nec patrum pi-gere,&c. 2.Suspicionem declinat. Puta-bantur Deum nouum prædicare, & ideo supplicio digni,Deut.13. Protestatur er-go,&c. 3.Docet quos patres in fide debe-ant imitari. Gloriabantur patribus nouis, & horum traditionibus,Mat.15 23. Et pro pter hos Christum oderant. Remittit er-go ad veteres patres,quorū fides in Scri-pturis commendatur. Inter hos primus Abraham,Gen 12.17.Rom.8.Ioh.8. Obser uandum hoc propter eos, qui hodie Pa-tres tonant,eos autē adducunt, quos con-stat erraffe. Quin virtutes horum refe-runt.
units.tr: that God still lives and is not ashamed of the fathers, etc. 2. He averts suspicion. They were thought to be preaching a new God, and therefore deserving of punishment, Deut. 13. He therefore protests, etc. 3. He teaches which fathers they ought to imitate in faith. They gloried in new fathers and their traditions, Matt. 15:2, and on account of these they hated Christ. He therefore refers them back to the ancient fathers, whose faith is commended in the Scriptures. Among these the first is Abraham, Gen. 12, 17, Rom. 8, John 8. This must be observed on account of those who today thunder about the Fathers, yet cite those who are known to have erred. Indeed, they attribute to them the virtues of these men.

units.la: ¶ 2. Glorificauit Filium suum, &c. Ergo omnium miraculorum finis est glorifica-tio Chr sti,Iohan.20.5 9 11.Arguuntur fi-gna,quibus homines à Christo auocantur Matt.24.2.Theff 2.
units.tr: ¶ 2. "He glorified his Son, etc." Therefore the end of all miracles is the glorification of Christ, John 20:5, 9, 11. The signs are refuted by which men are drawn away from Christ, Matt. 24:2, 2 Thess. 2.

units.la: II. Quia Christi meminit, sceleris in hunc commissi admonet. Grauiter agit, vt desiderium pœnitentię & salutis accen-dat. 1.Tradidistis, gentibus scilicet. Hor-rendum: quia Iudæi erant peculium Dei, Exod.19.Psal.76.147.Item quod commu-ni consensu,Luc. 23. 2. Neg stis coram Pi-lato,Mar.8. Et cum illo simul renuntiastis omnibus promissionibus patrum,Ioh.19. Et quidem non coacti, sed reluctante Pi-lato. Id·q; tanto odio, vt filios denoueritis 4. Collatione amplificat. Sanctum & ho-micidam, Sanctus, vel omnium testimonio Luc. 23. Author vitæ, Ioh. 11. Et hæc dicun-tur Hierosol.
units.tr: II. Since he mentions Christ, he reminds them of the crime committed against him. He acts severely, so that the desire for repentance and salvation may be kindled. 1. "You delivered up," namely to the Gentiles. A horrible thing, because the Jews were God's own people, Exod. 19, Ps. 76, 147; likewise that it was done by common consent, Luke 23. 2. "You denied him before Pilate," Mark 8. And together with him you renounced all the promises of the fathers, John 19. And indeed not compelled, but while Pilate resisted. And that with such hatred that you preferred a murderer, etc. 4. He amplifies by comparison. The holy and the murderer, holy, both by the testimony of all, Luke 23; the Author of life, John 11. And these things are said in Jerusalem.

units.la: Nota ¶ Qua libertate scelera accusa-ri debeant à ministris. Sunt hi publici ex-cubitores, Ezech. 3 & 33. Act. 20. Ira & gla-dius Dei ex sceleribus, Col. 3. Rom. 1. Hæc ergo arguantur, Isa. 58. Mich. 3. Nec est, quòd dicas, hæc hodie nemini obijci pos-se. Hodie etiam traditur Christus in Ver-bo & membris suis. Abnegatur propter mundum. In pretio habetur Barrabæ, qui communi patriæ exitio sunt. Quis ergo taceat? Amos 3. Imò multi hodie Iudæis peiores. Hi passi sunt ista accusari. Atho-die, qui Christiani dicuntur, ministris leges præscribunt, vt Isa. 28. 30. &c.
units.tr: Note ¶ With what freedom crimes ought to be accused by ministers. They are public watchmen, Ezek. 3 and 33, Acts 20. The wrath and sword of God is upon sins, Col. 3, Rom. 1. These therefore should be charged, Isa. 58, Mic. 3. Nor can you say that these things cannot today be objected to anyone. Today too Christ is betrayed in his Word and his members. He is denied for the sake of the world. Barabbas, who are a common ruin to the homeland, is held in esteem. Who then should keep silent? Amos 3. Indeed many today are worse than the Jews. They suffered these things to be charged against them. Today, those who are called Christians prescribe laws to the ministers, as in Isa. 28, 30, etc.

units.la: III. Ne quis morte Christi offendatur, de Resurrectione testatur, partim vt ostendat, hunc vitæ authorem esse, partim vt constet, ipsos se quidem scelere polluit se, nihil autem derogasse Christo, &c. Id de omnibus impijs debet intelligi, qui ni-hil proficiunt, Psal. 2. Cur ergo eos timeas, Matth. 10. Luc. 12. Id verò omne accommo-dat præsenti causæ, & ita reddit miraculi rationem, & Christi virtutem praedicat. Sensus: Christus per suum nomen, id est, potentiam & meritum huic subuenit: quia in eum credidit. Et Christi nomen subinde repetit, vt Christi gloria & virtus sit euidentior. Habes hic totam nostrae salutis rationem, in qua NOT. Prius omnem hominum potentiam & dignitatem exclusit. In praefen ti solius Christi nomen allegat. Ergo hic solus nos seruat. Vide Isa.42.43.45 7 Mat. 1. Actor.4. Arguuntur omnes, qui salutem alibi quaerunt, Isa.55. Ioh.4. Ier.2.
units.tr: III. Lest anyone be offended by the death of Christ, he bears witness to the Resurrection, partly to show that this one is the author of life, partly to establish that they indeed polluted themselves with a crime, but had taken nothing away from Christ, etc. This must be understood of all the impious, who accomplish nothing, Ps. 2. Why then fear them, Matt. 10, Luke 12? All this indeed suits the present case, and so gives the reason for the miracle and proclaims the power of Christ. The sense: Christ, through his name, that is, his power and merit, came to this man's aid, because he believed in him. And he repeats the name of Christ again and again, so that the glory and power of Christ may be more evident. You have here the whole reason of our salvation, in which NOTE: first he excluded all human power and dignity. In the present case he appeals to the name of Christ alone. Therefore he alone saves us. See Isa. 42, 43, 45, 7, Matt. 1, Acts 4. All are refuted who seek salvation elsewhere, Isa. 55, John 4, Jer. 2.

units.la: Hic Petrus fidem bis nominat. Hac sola enim Christus apprehenditur, vt qui corpore discessit, Ioh 6. Ideo haec seruare & iustificare dicitur, Matth.9. Mar.9. Luc.7. Rom.3.4 &c. Obseruemus autem fidei definitionem. Fides nominis ipsius, & Fides quae in ipsum est. Loquitur ergo de fide in Christum, quae talem agnoscit, qualis nomine suo describitur. Est hoc IESVS id est, seruator, Matth.1. Luc.2. CHRISTVS, id est, Rex & Sacerdos. Talis describitur Pf.2.110. Vt Rex Asserit, regit, tuetur, ditat, Psal.72. Zach 9. Vt Sacerdos docet, (Deut.18, Luc.5. Matt 17.) Heb.9 10.) intercedit (1. Tim 2.1. Ioh.2. Hec.4.5.) benedicit. nedicit, Gen.22. Eph.1. Qui talem agno-fcunt,ij in nomen eius credunt,& faciunt quod Deus exigit,Ioh.6.1.Ioh.3.
units.tr: Here Peter names faith twice. For by this alone Christ is apprehended, as one who has departed in the body, John 6. Therefore it is said to save and justify, Matt. 9, Mark 9, Luke 7, Rom. 3, 4, etc. Let us observe, moreover, the definition of faith: faith in the name itself, and faith which is in him. He speaks therefore of faith in Christ, which acknowledges him as he is described by his name. This is JESUS, that is, Saviour, Matt. 1, Luke 2. CHRIST, that is, King and Priest. He is so described in Ps. 2 and 110. As King he asserts, rules, protects, enriches, Ps. 72, Zech. 9. As Priest he teaches (Deut. 18, Luke 5, Matt. 17, Heb. 9, 10), intercedes (1 Tim. 2:1, John 2, Heb. 4, 5), blesses, Gen. 22, Eph. 1. Those who acknowledge him as such, believe in his name and do what God requires, John 6:1, John 3.

units.la: ¶ 3.Fructus ὁλοκληρία,id est,totius homiminis integritas. Hanc obtinuit claudus hic, vtpote anima & corpore sanatus. Ita Christus nos totos instaurat. Liberat a peccatis,morte,diabolo Isa.14.42.43.Ioh.14.15.Regenerat in filios Dei,Ro.4.Gal.4 Hinc possumus caelestia sapere,velle quae Deus vult,carni resistere,omnia denique, &c.1.Cor.1.Rom.8.Phil.4. Denique corporis vitia significat,ne nobis obsint, Roman.8.Est ergo salus haec perfectissima,vt quam caelestis & aeterna vita excipit, Ioh.5.12.14.17.1.Thes.4.Itaq; vno Christo contenti simus,hunc audiamus,&c.Oremus.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The fruit is soundness [ὁλοκληρία], that is, the integrity of the whole man. This the lame man obtained, being healed in both soul and body. So Christ restores us wholly. He frees us from sins, death, and the devil, Isa. 14, 42, 43, John 14, 15. He regenerates us into sons of God, Rom. 4, Gal. 4. Hence we can be wise in heavenly things, will what God wills, resist the flesh, and finally all things, etc., 1 Cor. 1, Rom. 8, Phil. 4. Lastly he signifies the defects of the body, so that they may not harm us, Rom. 8. This salvation is therefore most perfect, since heavenly and eternal life receives it, John 5:12, 14, 17, 1 Thess. 4. Therefore let us be content with Christ alone, let us hear him, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXIV.
units.tr: HOMILY XXIV.

units.la: 17 Sed nunc fratres, scio vos per ignorantiam ista fecisse, sicut & primo res vestras.
units.tr: 17 But now, brothers, I know that you did these things through ignorance, as your rulers also did.

units.la: 18 Deus autem quae pronuntiaue rat per os omnium prophetarū suorum, Christum passurum,ita impleuit.
units.tr: 18 But God fulfilled in this way what he had foretold through the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ would suffer.

units.la: 19 Resipiscite igitur, & conuerti mini, vt deleantur peccata vestra, post quam venerint tempora refrigerationis a confectu Domini.
units.tr: 19 Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out, after the times of refreshing shall have come from the presence of the Lord.

units.la: Cap.3. 20 Et miserit praenuntiatum vo bis Iesum Christum, &c. ad verf.22.
units.tr: Chapter 3. 20 And he shall send you Jesus Christ, who was preached to you, etc., to verse 22.

units.la: PEtrus nuper Iudaeos sceleris in Christum admissi accusauit. At quia nihil illo atrocius fingi poterat, haud dubie multorum conscientiae vehementer perculsae fuerunt: ideoque illis salutis viam monstrari oportuit. Id nunc facit hoc ordine.1. Docet spem veniae & salutis adhuc reliquam esse. Nisi enim hoc intelligant peccatores, frustra eos ad poenitentiam hortaberis. Aut enim praefractiores fiunt, vt Cain & Saul, aut desperant vt Iudas. Ideo prophetae etiam minis promissiones & oracula de Christo interserunt, quos Petrus imitatur. 2. Viam salutis monstrat, & vrget rationibus, vt hanc sequantur. Quoad primum, argumenta duo adducit:
units.tr: Peter has just accused the Jews of the crime committed against Christ.
