Since nothing more atrocious could be imagined, the consciences of many were no doubt deeply shaken, and so it was necessary to show them the way of salvation. He does this now in the following order. (1) He teaches that hope of pardon and salvation still remains. For unless sinners understand this, you will exhort them to repentance in vain. Otherwise they become more stubborn, like Cain and Saul, or they despair, like Judas. Therefore the prophets also interweave threats with promises and oracles about Christ, and Peter imitates them. (2) He shows the way of salvation and urges them with reasons to follow it. As to the first, he brings forward two arguments.

units.la: 1. Ignorantia mitigat scelus. Et nunc scio, &c. Si enim nouissent, &c. 1. Cor.2. Non autem ex leuitate nunc extenuat fce lus, quod prius amplificauit, &c. Et ignorantia per fe non excusat ea, quae contra Dei gloriam fiunt. Sed distinguit a peccato in Spiritum sanctum, quod est, quando quis Christum, qui animo eius illuxit, sciens & volens abijcit, imo oppugnat. Sic Iudas Ioh.6.12. Iulian. Hoc est irremissibile, le,Matth.12.1.Ioh.5. Rationem vide Heb. 6. Hac culpa istos liberat, respiciens ad preces Christi,Luc.23.
units.tr: 1. Ignorance lessens the crime. "And now I know," etc. "For if they had known," etc. (1 Cor. 2.). He does not now lessen the crime out of levity, which he had earlier magnified, etc. Ignorance in itself does not excuse those things that are done against the glory of God. But it is distinguished from the sin against the Holy Spirit, which is when someone, knowing and willing, casts off, or rather attacks, Christ, who has shone into his mind. So Judas (John 6.12). Julian. This is unforgivable (Matt. 12.1; John 5.). See the reasoning in Heb. 6. This fault frees these people, looking to the prayer of Christ (Luke 23.).

units.la: Not. Ignorantia,quæ mitiget fcele-ra.Duplex est,1.Impiorum & voluntaria, vt Pharaonis, Exod.5 8 9.14. Iudæorum, Ifa.6.Item Ier.44. Hodie multorum, qui fe non aliter edoctos esse dicunt, nolunt autem discere. Inexcusabiles, Iohan.3.9. 2.Nascitur ex gloriæ Dei zelo, sed absque scientia. Ita multi Iudæi Christum persecuti sunt, quod Mosis hostem esse putarent. Rom.10. Phil 3. Hæc veniam habet: institutionem admittit. Quam qui reijciunt, ad primum genus pertinent.
units.tr: Note. Ignorance that mitigates crimes. It is twofold: (1) that of the impious, which is voluntary, as of Pharaoh (Exod. 5.8, 9, 14); of the Jews (Isa. 6.); likewise (Jer. 44.). Today it belongs to many who say they have not been taught otherwise, yet are unwilling to learn. These are inexcusable (John 3.9). (2) It arises from zeal for the glory of God, but without knowledge. So many Jews persecuted Christ, because they thought he was an enemy of Moses (Rom. 10.; Phil. 3.). This has pardon, since it admits instruction. Those who reject instruction belong to the first kind.

units.la: 2. A Dei prouidentia. Isita impleuit, quæ prædixerat, & bene vsus est vestro peccato:ergo ne desperetis. Nota V. sum prouidentiæ. Non vtnoftris sceleribus patrocinemur,sed vt Dei bonitatem, sapientiam, & potentiam agnoscamus, & inde petamus consolationem. Item ne rigidiores fimus in alijs damnandis &c.Mat thæi 7. Sic Iofeph. Gen.45. &.50. Ita hic Petrus.
units.tr: 2. From the providence of God. He fulfilled what he had foretold, and he has made good use of your sin; therefore do not despair. Note the fivefold use of providence. Not that we should defend our wickedness, but that we should acknowledge the goodness, wisdom and power of God, and from that seek consolation. Likewise, so that we may not be too harsh in condemning others (Matt. 7.). So Joseph (Gen. 45. and 50.). So also Peter here.

units.la: Salutis consilium tradit, quod duobus partibus constat. 1. Præcepto, quod idem est cum eo quod habetur Act.2. Pœnitentiam agite, &c. Pœnitentia constat peccati agnitione & contritione. Et ab hac ordiuntur omnes,verbi precones,vtque sic fiat necesse est. Quia autem ista in impios quoque cadunt,addit: Et conuerti mini. Exigitur autem conuersio ad eum, a quo discessimus, Deo scilicet Ier. 3. 4. Requirit ea fidem in Christum,sine qua non venitur ad Patrem,Ioh.14. Matth.17. Ideo pœnitentiam quoque in suo nomine prædicare iussit,Luc 24.&c. Deinde vt eas emendationem, qua opus est, ne peccatis nostris Deus offensus oculos auertat,&c.If.59.1.&c.Ista singuli ad se transferant & videbunt quid priuatim ipsis,quid omnibus publicè sit faciendû hodie, &c.
units.tr: He gives the counsel of salvation, which consists of two parts. (1) A command, which is the same as what is found in Acts 2., "Repent," etc. Repentance consists of the recognition of sin and contrition. All preachers of the Word begin with this, and it must be so. But because these things also fall upon the impious, he adds: "And turn again." Conversion is required toward him from whom we have departed, namely God (Jer. 3.4). It requires faith in Christ, without which no one comes to the Father (John 14.; Matt. 17.). Therefore he also commanded repentance to be preached in his own name (Luke 24., etc.). Then, that we may have the amendment that is needed, so that God, offended by our sins, may not turn away his eyes (Isa. 59.1, etc.). Let each one apply these things to himself, and they will see what must be done today privately by themselves and publicly by all.

units.la: 2.Promissione : Vt deleantur peccata vestra. Non dicit, Vt ita deleatis peccata. Sed,Vt deleantur: Nimirum ab eo,qui illa delendi ius habet. Est is solus Deus. Huic enim peccamus, & peccando eius debitores efficimur.Psal 51. Simile creditoris & debitoris,Mat.18.6.. Agnouerunt hoc omnes sapientes,gentium & Iudæorum,Matt.9. Errârunt autem quoad causam.&c.Hanc ille monstrat,Ifa.43.Propter me,id est, quia misericors sum,& propter Filium meû,&c. Sic If.44 45.Hinc illa Ps. 130.&51. De his Petrus admonet Iudæos, ne in proprijs meritis acquiescant: quod nobis
units.tr: (2) The promise: "that your sins may be blotted out." He does not say, "that you may so blot out your sins," but "that they may be blotted out," namely by him who has the right to blot them out. This is God alone. For it is against him that we sin, and by sinning we become his debtors (Ps. 51.). It is like a creditor and debtor (Matt. 18.6). All the wise men, of the Gentiles and of the Jews, have acknowledged this (Matt. 9.). Yet they erred as to the cause, etc. God shows this cause (Isa. 43.): "For my own sake, that is, because I am merciful, and for the sake of my Son," etc. So also (Isa. 44 and 45.). Hence that Psalm 130 and Psalm 51. Peter warns the Jews about these things, that they should not rest in their own merits. This we also must beware of (Ps. 143.; 64.).

units.la: Cap. 3. nobis etiam est cauendum, Psal.143.64.
units.tr: Ch. 3. This we too must beware of (Ps. 143.; 64.).

units.la: {1}Quia caro feré cunctatur, argumen-tis vrget. Quasi dicat: Non semper dura-bit hæc facies mundi, se veniet aliquando nouissimus dies, quando Christus, qui nunc vobis prædicatur, veniet ad iudici-um, vt suis refrigerium ferat, & omnia re-stituat. Videte ergo, vt tunc possitis consistere, & vobis quoque sit dies refrigerij &c. Idem monet quod Christus Mat. 26.
units.tr: {1} Because the flesh almost always delays, he presses with arguments. As if he said: This face of the world will not last forever, but a last day will come at some time, when Christ, who is now preached to you, will come to judgment, to bring refreshment to his own and to restore all things. See to it, therefore, that you may then be able to stand, and that for you too there may be a day of refreshing, etc. He gives the same warning that Christ gave (Matt. 26.).

units.la: Sed NOTA {1}. Nouissimi diei condi-tionem. 1. Refrigerium feret. Id vero ad solos pios pertinet, Tunc abstergentur la-chrymæ, If.25. Apo.21. Fruentur bonis il-lis, de quibus If. 64. E carne sua videbunt Deū, Iob.19.Ps.16. Ideo iubentur capita at tollere, Lu.21. Ingens ergo bonū fidei, quę tunc beat, quando omnia fallunt, 2. Pet.3.
units.tr: But NOTE {1}: the condition of the last day. (1) It will bring refreshment. This indeed pertains only to the godly: "Then the tears will be wiped away" (Isa. 25.; Rev. 21.). They will enjoy those good things of which Isaiah speaks (Isa. 64.). "In my flesh they will see God" (Job 19.; Ps. 16.). Therefore they are commanded to lift up their heads (Luke 21.). Great, therefore, is the good of faith, which blesses us when all things deceive (2 Pet. 3.).

units.la: 2. Restitutionis dies: quia tunc reduce-tur stabilis mundi conditio. A corruptio-ne liberabitur tota hæc machina, Rom.8. Apo.21.2.Pet.2 Restituentur nobis corpo-ra, & in illis retribuetur, &c. Apoc.20.2. Cor.5 1.Cor.15 Tolletur deneque consu-sio, quæ nunc omnia turbat, & Christi re-gnum omnia obtinebit in pace illa verè aurea, &c. Isa.9.11. Ier.23. Ps.72.1. Cor.15.
units.tr: (2) The day of restitution: because then the stable condition of the world will be restored. This whole machine will be freed from corruption (Rom. 8.; Rev. 21.; 2 Pet. 2.). Our bodies will be restored to us, and rewards will be given in them, etc. (Rev. 20.; 2 Cor. 5.; 1 Cor. 15.). Finally, that confusion which now disturbs all things will be removed, and the kingdom of Christ will possess everything in that truly golden peace, etc. (Isa. 9.11.; Jer. 23.; Ps. 72.; 1 Cor. 15.).

units.la: {2}. Cur non nunc venit Christus? Præoccupat: Opertet illum cœlis capi, &c.
units.tr: {2} Why does Christ not come now? He anticipates the objection: "It is necessary that he be received by heaven," etc.

units.la: Quasi dicat: Peregit quæ in terris fuerunt agenda. Sed restant quædam, vt Euangelij per totum orbem prædicatio, Vocatio gentium, Antichrist.myst. & vt Mart. numerus impleatur, Ifa.2.42.49.60.&c.2. Thes.2.Apo.7.Quib. adde Mat.24. Luc.21 Istis ergo locù cessit in cœlos subuectus: non autem interea suos negligit, sed olim veniet, &c.Iohan.14. Matth.24.25. Actorum 2.
units.tr: As if he said: He has completed what had to be done on earth. But some things remain, such as the preaching of the gospel throughout the whole world, the calling of the Gentiles, the mystery of Antichrist, and that the number of the martyrs be completed (Isa. 2.; 42.; 49.; 60., etc.; 2 Thess. 2.; Rev. 7.). To these add Matt. 24.; Luke 21. Therefore he yielded a place to these things by being carried up into heaven. Yet he does not in the meantime neglect his own, but he will come at length (John 14.; Matt. 24.25.; Acts 2.).

units.la: Ista nos consolentur. Vtut hic mundus tumultuetur, habemus tamen vindicem, cui omnis potestas data est. Matt.28.Psal. 110. Ad hunc animos attollamus sursum. Interim præparemus nos ad eius aduentum, ne imparatos inueniat, Luc.12. Matt. 24.25.Mar.13. Oremus.
units.tr: These things should console us. However much this world may be in tumult, we have nevertheless an avenger, to whom all power has been given (Matt. 28.; Ps. 110.). Let us lift up our minds to him on high. In the meantime let us prepare ourselves for his coming, so that he may not find us unprepared (Luke 12.; Matt. 24.25.; Mark 13.). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXV.
units.tr: HOMILY XXV.

units.la: 22 Moses etenim ad Patres dixit, Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus Deus vester ex fratribus vestris, sicut me: audietis cum in omnibus quæ locutus fuerit vobis.
units.tr: 22 For Moses said to the fathers: "The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, as he raised me up. You shall hear him in all that he tells you."

units.la: 23 Futurum est autem, vt quisquis non auscultâuit Prophetam illum disperdatur a populo.
units.tr: 23 And it will come about that everyone who does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed from the people.

units.la: POst quàm Petrus Iudæis scelus in Filium Dei commissum exprobrauit, mox,ijsdem salutis consilium dedit, vt nimirum pœniteant & ad Deum conuertan tur. Vrgetur hoc passim in scripturis, Ier. 3.4.Ifa 55. Matth.3.4. &c. Requiriturau- tem pi i.nó conuersio apeccatis, quæ to† tius vitæ emendationem comprehendit, Ifa.1.Deinde fides in Christum, sine quo nemo ad Deum venit, Ioh.14. Matth.3.17. 1.Tim.2. At obstabat Iudæis, quod time- bant,ne Christum apprehendendo in Mo sem delinquerent,& graue erat cultum pa trium,& a Deo traditum relinquere, Ioh. 6.Occurrit ergo Petrus & docet tam Mo sem quàm Prophetas ad Christum rele- gare, ideoque his eos demum verè crede- re,qui Christum recipiunt.
units.tr: When Peter had reproached the Jews for the crime committed against the Son of God, he at once gave them the counsel of salvation: namely, that they should repent and turn to God. This is urged everywhere in Scripture (Jer. 3, 4; Isa. 55; Matt. 3, 4, etc.). Repentance requires conversion from sins, which includes the amendment of one's whole life (Isa. 1). Then comes faith in Christ, without whom no one comes to God (John 14; Matt. 3:17; 1 Tim. 2). But what stood in the way for the Jews was that they feared that by laying hold of Christ they would sin against Moses, and it was hard to abandon the worship of their fathers, which had been given by God (John 6). Peter therefore meets them and teaches that both Moses and the Prophets refer us to Christ, and that therefore only those truly believe them who receive Christ.

units.la: A Mose orditur, cuius summa erat au- thoritas: & docet,hunc tam abfuisse, vt in ipso hęrere voluerit patres,vt potius post traditam legem ostenderit, alium a Deo destinatum esse doctorem, quem omnes audire debeant. Locus habetur Deut.18. Prohibentur artes fatidicæ, & iubentur, vt ab vnius Dei verbo pendeant. Ne ve† rô hoc putarent incertū, promittit nun- quam defuturos prophetas,&c.Imo ven† turum aliquando Magnū illum prophe- tam, Christum, qui plenissimè omnia sit traditurus,&c,Itaq; hunc esse audiendum
units.tr: He begins with Moses, whose authority was supreme, and he teaches that Moses was so far from wanting the fathers to cling to himself that, rather, after the law was given, he showed that another teacher had been appointed by God, whom everyone ought to hear. The passage is Deut. 18. Magic arts are forbidden, and people are commanded to depend on the word of the one God alone. Lest they think this uncertain, Moses promises that prophets will never be lacking, etc. Indeed, he says that at some time that great prophet, Christ, would come, who would hand down all things most fully, etc. Therefore he is to be heard.

units.la: Moses Chri sto testimo nium dat. ¶ Sed proderit singula, quæ de illo dicit, inspexisse.
units.tr: Moses gives testimony to Christ. But it will be useful to have examined the individual things he says about him.

units.la: I. Vnde exoriturus sit, docet. Suscitabit illum Deus ex fratribus vestris. Ergo ex Iudæis nasci debuit, quod veræ incarnationis est argumentum. Heb 2. Rom.9. Idem innnunt promissiones, Ge.3 22. Psal. 89.132. &c. Interim ne quis vulgarem hominem putaret, Deum resuscitaturum dicit. Exponit Angelus, Luc.1. Matthæi primo.
units.tr: I. He teaches where he is to arise from: "God will raise him up from your brothers." Therefore he had to be born of the Jews, which is the proof of a true incarnation (Heb. 2; Rom. 9). The promises point to the same thing (Gen. 3:22; Ps. 89, 132, etc.). Meanwhile, lest anyone think he was an ordinary man, Moses says that God will raise him up. The angel explains this (Luke 1; Matt. 1).

units.la: Nota ¶ Bonitatem Dei, qui cum Filium nobis Seruatorem destinasset, eundem voluit hominem fieri, vt fidelis esset Pontifex, ad quem nobis liceret accedere. Heb.2.4. Idem sic ita nobis commendat, & ad se inuitat. Matth.11.12. Arguuntur Diuorum inuocatores.
units.tr: Note the goodness of God, who, having appointed his Son as our Saviour, willed that the same one should be made a man, so that he might be a faithful High Priest, to whom we may draw near (Heb. 2, 4). Thus he commends himself to us and invites us to himself (Matt. 11:12). The invokers of the saints are refuted by this.

units.la: II. Officium indicat dum Prophetam dicit. Id ei tribuit propter præsens argumentum. Heb 2. Dicuntur autem Prophetæ voluntatis Dei interpretes. Et quia Christus Sacerdos æternus esse debuit, (Psal.110.) nō potuit docendi munus omittere Mal 1. Hinc illa Is.61. Luc 4. Obserue mus hic ministerij dignitatem, quando Dei Filius illud obiuit. Ante hunc omnes homines selectissimi, Patriarchæ. Psalm.105. Genes. vigesimo. Postea Apostoli & quidem d: m ipsius nomine,2.Corinth.5.Damnan tur artes fatidicæ etiam hodie. Micheæ 5. Isa.8.
units.tr: II. He indicates the office when he calls him a Prophet. He ascribes this to him because of the present argument (Heb. 2). Prophets are called interpreters of the will of God. And since Christ had to be an eternal Priest (Ps. 110), he could not leave out the office of teaching (Mal. 1). Hence that passage of Isa. 61 and Luke 4. Let us observe here the dignity of the ministry, since the Son of God undertook it. Before him all men were most select, the patriarchs (Ps. 105; Gen. 20). Afterwards came the apostles, and indeed in his name (2 Cor. 5). Magic arts are condemned even today (Mic. 5; Isa. 8).

units.la: Sed No T. ¶ Qualis Propheta fit? Mosi similis. Debet hoc ad typü referri,quem Moses gessit. 1. Moses reliquit aulam,& cum fratribus affligi maluit, &c. Hebr.11. Idem affectus fuit in Christo.Phil.2. 2.Vt Mosem fratres reiecerunt, Exod.2 5. Ita Christum,&c.Ioh.1.19.Et adhuc reijcitur. 3.Moses populum ex Ægypto eduxit, & Pharaonem submersit: Ita Christus, &c. 4.Vt Moses per desertum duxit:Ita Christus suas oues per vmbram mortis, &c. Psal.23. Ioh.8. &10. 5.Moses dedit Manna & aquas:Sic Christus, Iohan.6.4.19.& 10.&c. 6.Moses interpres Dei fuit ad populum: Ita Christus, Ioh.1.15. 7 Ad Mosem referebantur causæ graviores, cuius sententia oportebat stare, Exod. 18. 33. Leuit.24. Numer.15. Ita Christus audiendus in omnibus, quæ nostrum captum superant,&c. 8. Moses intercessit pro populo,&se deleri voluit, &c. Numer.11.12. Exod.32 33.Ita Christus se interposuit,exe cratio pro nobis factus, Isa.53. Galat.3. Et adhuc intercedit 1.Iohan.2.
units.tr: But note: what sort of prophet is he? Like Moses. This must be referred to the type which Moses bore. 1. Moses left the court and chose rather to be afflicted with his brothers, etc. (Heb. 11). The same attitude was in Christ (Phil. 2). 2. As the brothers rejected Moses (Exod. 2), so they rejected Christ, etc. (John 1:19), and he is still rejected. 3. Moses led the people out of Egypt and drowned Pharaoh; so Christ, etc. 4. As Moses led them through the desert, so Christ leads his sheep through the shadow of death, etc. (Ps. 23; John 8, 10). 5. Moses gave manna and water; so Christ (John 6:4, 19; 10, etc.). 6. Moses was God's interpreter to the people; so Christ (John 1:15). 7. Weightier causes were referred to Moses, and his judgment had to be upheld (Exod. 18, 33; Lev. 24; Num. 15). So Christ is to be heard in all things that exceed our capacity, etc. 8. Moses interceded for the people and wished himself to be blotted out, etc. (Num. 11, 12; Exod. 32, 33). So Christ interposed himself, made a curse for us (Isa. 53; Gal. 3), and still intercedes (1 John 2).

units.la: III. Quid illi debemus? Ipsum audiendo. Sic Matth.17. Requiritur primo studii. um verbi diligens, Luc.10. Deinde fides, Ioh.5. Rom.10. Hinc obedientia. Rom.1. 16 Et hæc notæ sunt filiorum Dei, Iohan.8. 10.5.
units.tr: III. What do we owe him? To hear him. So Matt. 17. First, diligent study of the word is required (Luke 10). Then faith (John 5; Rom. 10). Hence obedience (Rom. 1:16). And these are the marks of the children of God (John 8; 10:5).

units.la: Interim Not. {q}1. Quod omnia audire iubemur. Sunt qui carni placentia audire volunt, (Ifo.Mich.2.) reliqua tali idiunt. Vt qui solam gratiam prædicari volunt, pœnitentiam non item. Sed utrumque præcipitur, Luc.24. Qui item nolunt argui Antichristum & eius satellites, 2. Thess.2. 1.Tim.4.2. Tim.3. Qui denique nihil quod crucem parit prædicari volunt. Atqui vt Christus nō scinditur aut mutatur. (Heb.13.) ita nec verbum eius, &c. Matth.24. Totum oportet edere & concoquere. Exod.12.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: 1. That we are bidden to hear everything. There are those who want to hear only what pleases the flesh (Isa.; Mic. 2) and pass over the rest. Like those who want only grace preached, and not repentance. But both are commanded (Luke 24). Likewise those who do not want Antichrist and his satellites exposed (2 Thess. 2; 1 Tim. 4; 2 Tim. 3). Finally, those who want nothing preached that brings a cross. Yet as Christ is not divided or changed (Heb. 13), neither is his word, etc. (Matt. 24). It is necessary to eat it all and digest it (Exod. 12).

units.la: {2}. Pœnam qua terret. Comprehendit totius hominis interitum. Exclusis a populo Dei nulla spes superest. At per Euangelium ad illius societatem colligimur. Et si olim moriebantur, &c. Heb.10. Hinc illæ minæ, Iohan.3. Mar.16. Causam habes, 1.Iohan.5. De eo admonet, ne Christi contemtum iusum putarent.
units.tr: 2. The punishment with which he terrifies. It comprises the destruction of the whole man. For those excluded from the people of God no hope remains. But through the Gospel we are gathered into his fellowship. And if formerly they died, etc. (Heb. 10). Hence those threats (John 3; Mark 16). You have the reason (1 John 5). He warns about this so that they would not think contempt for Christ goes unpunished.

units.la: Idem nobis dici putemus & in eo firmus constantes. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us think that the same is said to us as well, and let us be firm and constant in it. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY XXVI.

units.la: 24 Sed & omnes prophetæ a Samuele muele, & ijs qui deinceps secuti sunt, quo quot loquuti sunt etiam prænuntiarunt dies illos.
units.tr: 24 But also all the prophets, from Samuel onward and those who came after him, as many as have spoken, have foretold these days.

units.la: 25 Vos estis filij prophetarum, & pacti quod pepigit Deus erga Patres nostros, dicens ad Abraham: Et in semine tuo, &c. ad finem Cap.
units.tr: 25 You are the sons of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham: "And in your seed," etc., to the end of the chapter.

units.la: PEtrus fidem in Christum ita docet, ut simul omnibus occurrat, quæ ludaeos impediebant. Erat inter hæc præcipuum nimia Mosis & Legis obseruantia. Ioh. 6. Ostendit ergo Mosem ipsum ad Christum remittere suos (Deut. 18) ideoque eos dem um esse veros Mosis discipulos, qui illum amplectuntur. Ioh. 5.
units.tr: Peter teaches faith in Christ in such a way that he at the same time meets all the objections that hindered the Jews. Chief among these was an excessive observance of Moses and the Law. John 6. He shows, therefore, that Moses himself refers his people to Christ (Deut. 18), and so those are truly Moses' disciples who embrace him. John 5.

units.la: Et quamuis hoc sufficere posset, tamen confirmitat omnis loco Prophetas quoq; adjicit, quorum vaticinia aliquot haud dubie adduxit. A Samuele autem ordi-tur, quia primus est, cuius scripta extant, &c. Omnes autem de Christo vaticinantur. Nathan, 2. Sam. 7. Dauid Psal. 2 22.89. 72 110. 132. &c. Imo omnes hoc commune habent, quod hinc petunt consolationis argumenta. Isa. 2. 7 8 9 35.40.51. Amos 9. Mich. 4 5. Ier. 23. Ezech. el 34. Zach. 3 4 9. 15. Malach. 4. &c. In quibus Noter. Fidei Christianae anti-quitatem & certitudinem. Nullus anti-
units.tr: Although this might suffice, he nevertheless confirms it throughout and adds the Prophets too, some of whose prophecies he undoubtedly cited. He begins with Samuel, because he is the first whose writings are extant, etc. Yet all of them prophesy of Christ: Nathan, 2 Sam. 7; David, Ps. 2, 22, 89, 72, 110, 132, etc. Indeed, they all have this in common, that they draw from this source their arguments of consolation: Isa. 2, 7, 8, 9, 35, 40, 51; Amos 9; Mic. 4, 5; Jer. 23; Ezek. 34; Zech. 3, 4, 9, 15; Mal. 4, etc. In these, note the antiquity and certainty of the Christian faith. No writer is more ancient

units.la: quior scriptor Mose, qui idem fidelis, &c. Numer. 12. At hic fidei nostrae originem ex paradiso deducit, Genef 3. Nulla item religio tot testimonijs confirmata. Prophetarum, 1.Pet.1. 2. Pet. 1. Apostolorum & Martyrum. Nulla tot signis & prodigijs commendata. In natali Christi, &c. Nulla etiam diutius durauit, & adhuc durabit, Matth.28. Mar.13. Itaque nos quoque in ea fimus constantes. Matth 24. Luc.21.
units.tr: than Moses, who was also faithful, etc., Num. 12. Yet Moses derives the origin of our faith from paradise, Gen. 3. Likewise, no religion has been confirmed by so many testimonies: those of the prophets (1 Pet. 1; 2 Pet. 1), of the apostles and of the martyrs. No religion has been commended by so many signs and wonders: at the birth of Christ, etc. Nor has any lasted longer, and it will still last, Matt. 28; Mark 13. Therefore let us also be steadfast in it. Matt. 24; Luke 21.

units.la: Caeterum melioribus obstat sceleris in Christum admissi conscientia, de quo Petrus grauissimè pronuntiârat. Æquum esse videbant, vt quia ipsi Christum negarant, ab eo vicissim negarentur, Mar. 8. Matth. 10. Sciebant item illud Ifa.1. Ergo docet nunc Christum & quaecunque de hoc praedicata sunt, ad ipsos pertinere, ne que repulsam pafluros, &c.
units.tr: Moreover, the consciousness of the crime committed against Christ, of which Peter had spoken very gravely, stood in the way of the better sort. They thought it only fair that, since they had denied Christ, they in turn should be denied by him, Mark 8; Matt. 10. They also knew that passage in Isa. 1. Therefore he now teaches that Christ, and all that has been preached about him, pertains to them as well, so that they will not suffer rejection, etc.

units.la: Obseruandum, quae recta fit ratio praedicandi. Arguenda scelera, Iohan. 16. Sed conuersis non neganda spes salutis, &c. Ideo Petrus nunc ipsis applicat.
units.tr: Observe what is the right method of preaching: crimes must be rebuked, John 16; but to those who have been converted, the hope of salvation must not be denied, etc. For this reason Peter now applies it to them.

units.la: I. Vos estis filij Prophetarum, & teft. &c. I. Estis ex ea gente, quae prophetas genuit, & cum vestris patribus teftamentu fecit Deus, ideoq; ad vos ceu haeredes legitimos promissiones istae omnes pertinent. Cum enim gentes etiam benedici debeant. ant, multò magis vos? Interim obseruemus, hæc omnia conditionaliter dici, si nì mirùm credant. Nisi enim id fiat, earnis generatio nihil prodest, I h 1.
units.tr: I. "You are the sons of the prophets," etc. (1) You are of that nation which produced the prophets, and God made his covenant with your fathers; therefore all those promises pertain to you as lawful heirs. For since the Gentiles also ought to be blessed, how much more you? Meanwhile let us observe that all these things are said conditionally, if indeed they believe. For unless this happens, descent from the flesh profits nothing, John 1.

units.la: Sed Not. §1. Salutem nostram testamento Dei niti. Factum hoc cum Abrahamo, Gen 12.15 17. 22. Inde sæpe innoua-tum 2 Sam 7. Psal 89 1.2. Ier 31. Inde collige salutem nostram esse certissimam. Si enim hominis testamentum, &c. Gal 3. Rom 11. Adde quòd Deus hoc iureiurando confirmauit. Hebr 6. Vide Ier 33. Isa 49.
units.tr: But note first: our salvation rests on the covenant of God. This was made with Abraham, Gen. 12, 15, 17, 22, and often renewed afterwards, 2 Sam. 7; Ps. 89; Jer. 31. From this gather that our salvation is most certain. For if a man's covenant, etc., Gal. 3; Rom. 11. Add that God confirmed this with an oath, Heb. 6. See Jer. 33; Isa. 49.

units.la: § 2. Testamenti huius summam: In semine tuo, &c. Tria dicit. I. Benedictionem promittit. Opponitur maledictio, quæ per peccatum fuit ingressa, Deut 27. Gen 3. In telligitur Dei fauor, ex quo omnis salus dependet. Si enim Deus nobiscum, quis contra nos? Rom 8.
units.tr: §2. The sum of this covenant is: "In your seed," etc. It says three things. (1) It promises a blessing. Opposed to it is the curse, which entered through sin, Deut. 27; Gen. 3. The favour of God is understood, on which all salvation depends. For if God is with us, who is against us? Rom. 8.

units.la: II. Mediator huius indicatur. In semine tuo. Id solo de Christo exponi debere docet Paulus Gal 3. Quia enim omnes homines peccárant, nemo poterat benedictionem afferre Isa 43. Rom 3. Vnus Christus omnis peccati purus est. If 53. Et huic pater testimoniū fert, Mat 3.17. In huius sanguine testamentum nouū habetur. 1 Cor. 11. Vltimus deniq; eius actus in terris fuit benedictio, Luc 24.
units.tr: (2) The mediator of this is indicated: "In your seed." Paul teaches that this must be explained solely of Christ, Gal. 3. For since all men had sinned, no one could bring the blessing, Isa. 43; Rom. 3. Christ alone is free of all sin, Isa. 53. And the Father bears witness to him, Matt. 3:17. In his blood the new covenant is established, 1 Cor. 11. Finally, his last act on earth was a blessing, Luke 24.

units.la: III. Quorum est benedictio? Omnes familiae terrae.
units.tr: III. Who are the recipients of the blessing? All the families of the earth.

units.la: Quia nulla est personarum acceptio apud Deum. Act. 10. Rom. 3. Et ipse Christus hoc testatur, Actor. 1. Et hæc causa est, quod Abraham pater mulierum gentium dicitur. Gen. 17.
units.tr: Because there is no respect of persons with God, Acts 10; Rom. 3. Christ himself testifies to this, Acts 1. And this is the reason why Abraham is called the father of many nations, Gen. 17.

units.la: Ita nos officij admoneant, ne quem contemnamus. Solentur item in tentationibus.
units.tr: Thus let these things remind us of our duty not to despise anyone. They also console us in temptations.

units.la: Recenti beneficio confirmat: Vobis primum, &c. Quasi diceret. Praestitit Deus quod promisit, & suscitavit Prophetam illum, & eundem primum ad vos misit, idem inter vos docuit, miracula fecit (Mat. 15.) denique vobis obtulit seipsum & omnem benedictionem, Matth. 9. 11. Iohan. 5. 8. 7. Matthæi 10. Actor. 1. &c. Ne dubitetis ergo quin ad se conversos receptu rus sit in gratiam. Ideo enim misit hunc Deus, ut vobis benedicat, dum vos convertit ab iniquitatibus.
units.tr: He confirms it with a recent benefit: "To you first," etc. As if he were saying: God has done what he promised; he has raised up that Prophet and sent him first to you; he taught among you, worked miracles (Matt. 15), and finally offered to you himself and every blessing, Matt. 9, 11; John 5, 8, 7; Matt. 10; Acts 1, etc. Do not doubt, therefore, that he will receive into grace those converted to him. For God sent him for this purpose, that he might bless you, by turning you from your iniquities.

units.la: NOTA. 1. Quomodo nobis Christus benedicat? Non obiter modo & nudis verbis ut Sacerdotes, Num 6. Sed vere, dum primo peccata expiat, & maledictionem abolet. Deinde dum Spiritu suo regenerat, & conversionis veræ nobis author est. In ipso enim nova creatura effici mur. 2. Corinth. 5. Itaque qui Christo fruitur, volunt,credant oportet,& vita vel moribus fidem testentur,Rom. 12.
units.tr: NOTE 1. How does Christ bless us? Not merely in passing and with bare words, as priests do, Num. 6; but truly, since first he expiates sins and abolishes the curse, and then, since he regenerates us by his Spirit and is the author of true conversion in us. For in him we are made a new creature, 2 Cor. 5. Therefore whoever enjoys Christ ought to will and believe, and to bear witness to his faith by life and morals, Rom. 12.

units.la: 2. Arguuntur qui sub Euangelij præ-textu licentiam carnis quærunt. Hos non iuuant vllæ prærogatiue.Fient n ouisimi, & tandem illis dicetur quod est Matth. 7. 25.&c.Vigilemus & Oremus.
units.tr: 2. Those are rebuked who seek licence for the flesh under the pretext of the Gospel. No privileges help these people. They will become last, and at last it will be said to them what is written in Matt. 7; 25, etc. Let us watch and pray.

units.la: CAPVT IIII. HOMILIA XXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER 4. HOMILY 27.

units.la: Loquentibus autè ipsis ad populum fuerunt enerunt illis Sacerdotes & præfectus templi, & Sadducæi.
units.tr: And while they were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them.

units.la: 2 Molestè ferentes quod docerent populum, et annuntiarent in nomine Iesu resurrectionem ex mortuis,
units.tr: (2) Being greatly troubled that they taught the people and proclaimed in the name of Jesus the resurrection from the dead,

units.la: 3 Et iniecerunt eis manus, posuerunt eos in custodiam in posterum diem &c. ad verf. 5. v/q.
units.tr: (3) and they laid hands on them, put them in custody until the next day, etc., to verse 5.

units.la: Efcripfit Lucas Ecclesiæ primitiuæ initium & progressum. Vidimus quæ Apostolorum doctrina, quæ item primitiuæ Ecclesiæ fuerint exercitia. Sequitur vt hæc acceperit mundus: nimirum vt prædicstum, Ioh.15.Matth.10.Et hæc iam incipiunt sentire, quos Deus hactenus tutos fecerat,donec Ecclesia stabiliretur. Iam vero insurgunt hostes,capiunt, sistunt concilio,minantur. Vsus,ne hodie similibus offendamur.Nihil fit insoles.Est hoc mun di ingenium,Ioh.3.Imitemur nos Ecclefię primitiuę constantiam:nec dubitemus de ope Dei, 1 Cor.10.2.Cor.1.Matth.10. Sed videamus singula.
units.tr: Luke has written down the beginning and progress of the primitive Church. We have seen what the doctrine of the Apostles was, and likewise what the practices of the primitive Church were. It follows how the world received these things: namely, as was foretold (John 15; Matthew 10). And now those whom God had hitherto kept safe begin to feel it, until the Church should be established. Now indeed the enemies rise up, they seize, they bring them before the council, they threaten. Let us be prepared, so that we are not taken aback today by similar things. Nothing happens out of the ordinary. This is the nature of the world (John 3). Let us imitate the constancy of the primitive Church, and let us not doubt the help of God (1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1; Matthew 10). But let us look at the particulars one by one.

units.la: I. Hostium tria genera. 1. Sacerdotes, qui duces fuerunt. Atqui horū erat Christo populum adducere,Ioh.5.Sed qui fuerint,patet Matth.15 21.23 Luc.13.2. Præfectus templi,nimirum ex Trib. militum. 3. Sadducæi, qui religionem omnem habebant ludibrio,Matth.22 Act.23.Idem ergo hic fit,quod Luc.22.
units.tr: I. There are three kinds of enemies. (1) The priests, who were the leaders. Yet it was their task to bring the people to Christ (John 5). But who they were is plain from Matthew 15, 21, 23 and Luke 13. (2) The captain of the temple, namely from the tribune of the soldiers. (3) The Sadducees, who made mockery of all religion (Matthew 22; Acts 23). So here what happens is the same as in Luke 22.

units.la: NOT. Qui primi & acerrimi Ecclesiæ & veritatis hostes sint? Sacerdotes.Vt primum hi religionem quæstum faciunt, fieri nequit,quin primi fe opponant. Ita factum Prophetis.Bap.Iohan.1. Christo. Nunc Apostolis, quibus Pilatus & Herodes hucusq; pepercerant. Ne ergo offendamur hodie,si hostes sint, qui sibi Ecclesię primatum vendicant. Quia enim horū similes sunt,vt prædictum(2 Pet.3.2.Tim. 3.) prodigium est aliquos conuerti.
units.tr: NOTE. Who are the first and fiercest enemies of the Church and of the truth? The priests. As soon as they make religion a source of gain, it cannot be that they are not the first to set themselves against it. So it happened to the Prophets (Baptist John, chapter 1) and to Christ; now to the Apostles, whom Pilate and Herod had hitherto spared. Therefore let us not be offended today if those are enemies who claim for themselves the primacy of the Church. For since they are like those foretold (2 Pet. 3; 2 Tim. 3), it is a marvel that some are converted.

units.la: II.Vt negotium hoc egerint? 1. Non soli veniunt,nec causam priuatam agere putentur, tentur,aut populus concitetur. Sed præ- sectum sibi adiungunt, cuius erat in tem- plo turbas prohibere. Ita pacis studium fi- mulant,&c.Sadducęos item alienos ab o- mni religione,&c proinde huic rei maxim é idoneos,&c.Ex improuiso quoq;, vt ma- gis terreant. Vnde apparet;eos occasio- nem captauisse.Eadem astutia vtuntur o- mnes veritatis hostes, maximè falsi anti- stites,vt tunc suas res agant, quando nihil minus facere videntur. Habet Antichri- stus oculos hominis,Dan.7. Sic Bonifac. III. Phocam sibi demeretur. Sic contra Græcos vsi sunt Longobardis,Cōtra hos Francis.Deniq; ideo excitârunt imagines veteris beatiæ,&c.Apoc.13 Ita alienis viri- bus & opibus suas res perficiunt,& omnia sic instituunt, vt simplicioribus terrorem incutiant.Vigilemus ergo,Luc.16.
units.tr: II. How did they carry out this business? (1) They do not come alone, nor are they to be thought to be pursuing a private cause, nor is the people stirred up. But they join to themselves a captain, whose duty it was to restrain crowds in the temple. Thus they feign a zeal for peace, etc. Likewise the Sadducees, strangers to all religion, etc., and therefore most suited to this business, etc. Also unexpectedly, so that they may terrify more. Hence it appears that they seized the opportunity. All enemies of the truth use the same cunning, especially false bishops, so that they carry out their own affairs when they seem to be doing least of all. Antichrist has the eyes of a man (Daniel 7). So Boniface III won over Phocas to himself. So they used the Lombards against the Greeks, and against these the Franks. Finally, for this reason they have stirred up images of the old superstition, etc. (Revelation 13). Thus they accomplish their own affairs by the strength and resources of others, and arrange everything so as to strike terror into the simpler sort. Let us therefore be watchful (Luke 16).

units.la: 2.Quid mouit eos,& quid prætexunt? Dolet, quod ipsi doceant populum, &c, duobus criminibus illos grauant. Primò quod ipsi,rudes scilicet & illiterati(Matt. 4.) docerent. Id verò scilicet ut fama spirare videatur,Eò enim rem adduxerant,vt nemini nisi per ipsos ordinato liceret docere, Ioh.1.18.Sic in Pap.Apoc.13. Et hoc facit, quod Collationes omnium Ecclesiarum adsc rapuerunt, & immunitatem Ecclefiasticam constituerunt, ipsis Regibus ter ribilem. A terum,quod Iesum dicerent re surrexisse. Ridebant hoc Sadducæi: sed a- lijs hoc intolerabile videtur,partim quod ita afferebatur Christi Deitas (Rom. 1.) partim ipsorum arguebatur iniquitas. Id quod seditiosum poterat videri. Ista quidem praetexunt,sed aliud fpectârunt. Si enim oderunt scisma,cur ferunt Pharif. Esi- sen Sadduc. denique? Si seditiones detestantur, cur Barrab. sibi petierunt dari? At hæc sunt, quæ om ibus seculis intentantur Dei ferruis: quod nimirum scismata & seditiones moueant. Vide 1 Reg. 18 Amos 7. Ier 26 &c Lu. 23. Hodie eadem audiuntur. Sed potest responderi quod istis. Si Ecclesiam noluit scindi, cur sectas Monach. fouent contra illud Pauli, 1. Cor. 1. 3. Si pax eis cordi est, cur bella seminant, pacem violant? cur ad ipsos deferuntur per- fidæ cæsorum capita?
units.tr: 2. What moved them, and what do they pretend? They grieve that these men teach the people, and they burden them with two charges. First, that they, being of course unlearned and unskilled (Matthew 4), should teach. And indeed this, as it were, is to breathe out rumour, for they had brought the matter to such a point that no one was allowed to teach except those ordained by themselves (John 1:18). So it is in the Papacy (Revelation 13). And this they do, since they have seized all the collations of the churches for themselves and established ecclesiastical immunity, a thing terrible even to kings. Second, that they said Jesus had risen. The Sadducees laughed at this; but to others it seemed intolerable, partly because by this the divinity of Christ was asserted (Romans 1), and partly because their own iniquity was thereby exposed. This could seem seditious. These are the things they pretend, but they aimed at something else. For if they hate schism, why do they put up with the Pharisees and finally the Sadducees? If they detest seditions, why did they ask that Barabbas be given to them? But these are the charges that in every age are brought against the servants of God: that is, that they stir up schisms and seditions. See 1 Kings 18; Amos 7; Jeremiah 26; Luke 23. Today the same things are heard. But it may be answered to them as to those: if they did not want the Church to be divided, why do they foster the monastic sects, against that saying of Paul (1 Cor. 1)? If peace is dear to them, why do they sow wars and violate peace? Why are the heads of the slain treacherously brought to them?

units.la: § 3 Iniecta manu rapiunt in carcerem, nec priùs audiunt eos. Hoc imprimis agunt impij, vt omnis,cautam suam dicendi,facultas Deiferuis eripiatur. Sciunt enim quid possit veritas, & quod vulgi ignorantia regnum ipsorum maximè ltabilitur. Ido libros sacros quoq; prohibent. Ipsi autem loco Scripturæ faces & gladios exös expediunt.Sed est hæc tenebrarum po testas,Luc.22.Erit vindex Deus, Apoc 6. 14 15 16 17. & 18. Interea nos fimus constantes.
units.tr: 3. Seizing them by the hand, they drag them into prison, and do not hear them first. This the impious especially work to achieve, that every opportunity of speaking freely be snatched from the servants of God. For they know what truth can do, and that their own kingdom is most firmly established by the ignorance of the common people. Therefore they also forbid the holy books. But instead of Scripture they draw out torches and swords. Yet this is the power of darkness (Luke 22). God will be the avenger (Revelation 6:14, 15, 16, 17, 18). Meanwhile let us be steadfast.

units.la: III. Quàm parum enim proficiant,apparet, Multi credunt, vt iam virorum sint 5000. Voluntterrere, & ita prohibere Evangelij cursum, & ecce promouet hunc, & plures accedunt,&c. NOT. Quàm facile sit Christo dissipare suorum hostium conspiliam,Psal.33. Fit hic planè quod habetur Psal.2. Est autem hæc perpetua Ecclesiæ sors, quòd persecutionibus augetur. Sic factum in Ægypto,Exod.1.2. Sub Babyl.& Persis, Dan.3.6. Sub Rom. Hodie idem fit,& impletur,Psal.110.
units.tr: III. How little they profit is evident. Many believe, so that the number of men is now about 5000. They wanted to terrify, and so to hinder the course of the Gospel, and behold, this one advances, and more come forward, etc. NOTE. How easily Christ scatters the plots of his enemies (Psalm 33). Here what is found in Psalm 2 plainly comes to pass. Moreover this is the perpetual lot of the Church, that it is increased by persecutions. So it happened in Egypt (Exodus 1, 2); under Babylon and Persia (Daniel 3, 6); under Rome. Today the same thing happens and is fulfilled (Psalm 110).

units.la: ¶ Excitent nos ista,& confirment in fide, nehoftiū rabie nos superari sinamus. Non possunt illi nisi in corpora sæuire, Matth.10. Luc.12. Vinciunt ministros verbi,sed hoc non vincitur,2.Tim.2.Ioh.3 Et maior est,qui in nobis, quàm qui in mundo,1.Ioh.4.& 5.In mundo Satan agit, iam olim superatus,Ioh.12 16. In nobis Christus,cui omnis potestas data, Matth.28. & in quo possumus omnia,Phil 4. Idem vt hic tuetur,ita nobis in cœlis locum parauit, Luc.22. Iohannis 14 17.
units.tr: ¶ Let these things stir us up and confirm us in the faith, and let us not allow ourselves to be overcome by the rage of enemies. They can only rage against the bodies (Matthew 10; Luke 12). They bind the ministers of the Word, but the Word is not bound (2 Tim. 2; John 3). And greater is he who is in us than he who is in the world (1 John 4, 5). In the world Satan works, already long since conquered (John 12, 16). In us is Christ, to whom all power is given (Matthew 28), and in whom we can do all things (Philippians 4). The same Christ, as he defends us here, so has prepared a place for us in heaven (Luke 22; John 14, 17).

units.la: Oremus.
units.tr: Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XVIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XVIII.

units.la: 5 Factum est autem postero die, ut congregarentur primores eorum & Seniores, & Scribæ in Ierusalem.
units.tr: 5 It came to pass on the next day that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered together at Jerusalem.

units.la: 6 Et Annas Pontifex maximus et Caiaphas, & Iohannes & Alexander, & quotquot erant ex genere pontificio, & c. ad ver. 11.
units.tr: 6 And Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John and Alexander, and as many as were of the high-priestly family, etc., to verse 11.

units.la: CHristus se suis semper affuturum promittit, sequi pastorem fidum esse profitetur, qui oves sibi eripi non sinat, Matt. 10. Ioh. 10. Id semper praestat, maxime autem, quando hostes fidei instant, & nullum vspiam praesidium apparet. Tunc enim spiritu suo non modo consolatur, verumetiam docet quid faciant & loquantur, Matt. 10. Mar. 13. Luc. 21. Exemplum hic proponitur. Audiuimus enim Apostolos captos fuisse, eo quod praedicarent iniusi, &c. Seu quitur, ut causam suam egerint in Senatu magna etiam cum admiratione hostium & eorundem confusione. Estq; locus hic eo diligentius considerandus, quod typu com cilij Antichristiani continet.
units.tr: Christ promises that he will always be present with his own, and he declares that he is a faithful shepherd who does not allow his sheep to be snatched from him (Matt. 10; John 10). He always does this, and most of all when the enemies of the faith press hard and no help appears anywhere. For then he comforts them by his Spirit, and teaches them what to do and what to say (Matt. 10; Mark 13; Luke 21). An example is set before us here. For we have heard that the apostles were seized because they taught without authority, etc. It follows that they pleaded their cause in the Senate, to the great astonishment of the enemies and their confusion. This passage is to be considered all the more carefully because it contains a type of the Antichristian council.

units.la: 1. Orditur à Iudæcum consessu, ut often dat, qui & quales contra Apostolos conuenerint. Comprehendit autem tribus ordinibus omnes, qui apud Iudæos fuerunt eximij
units.tr: 1. He begins with the assembly of the Jews, as is his custom, and with who and what sort of men gathered against the apostles. He includes all the distinguished men among the Jews under three orders.

units.la: Concilij Pon. ... descriptio.
units.tr: Description of the Papal council.

units.la: eximij. 1.Principes,quibus per Romanos commissa fuit rerum administratio, & for tafsis praesidis loco aderant conuentibus. 2.Seniores, qui Senatum constituebant, sic di-cti, quod gravitate senili tales commendari decet. 3. Scribae,penes quos instrumenta publica asseruabantur, qui ijdem Scripturas profitebantur.His addun tur omnes ex ordine Pontifices, & quidé aliqui nominatim. Talis ergo fuit confef-sus hic,vt nihil eo posset fingi magnificen tius. Adsunt enim magistratus ordinarij, quos Rom. Imp. authoritas defendebat. Item qui eruditionis existimationem fusti nebant. Denique ad quos cura religionis pertinebat ex Dei instituto, Malachiae 2. Deutero.17. Et durarat iam ordo Sacerd. annis amplius 1500. Successores item e-rant sanctissimi hominû,qui omnes Chri-fti typum gesserunt.
units.tr: The distinguished men: (1) the princes, to whom the administration of affairs had been committed by the Romans, and who attended the assemblies in place of the proconsul; (2) the elders, who constituted the Senate, so called because such men ought to be commended for senile gravity; (3) the scribes, in whose keeping the public records were preserved, and who likewise professed the Scriptures. To these are added all the high priests in order, and some of them by name. So this assembly was such that nothing more splendid could be imagined. For here are present the ordinary magistrates, whom the authority of the Roman emperor protected; likewise those who held a reputation for learning; and finally those to whom the care of religion belonged by God's institution (Malachi 2; Deut. 17). The order of priesthood had also lasted now for more than 1500 years, and its successors were most holy men, who all bore the figure of Christ.

units.la: Vbi Not. ¶ Quod tales propter Apo-ftolos conueniunt, quibus nihil erat con-temptius & infirmius.Miretur quis. Sed irritauit eos quaestus & gloriae priuatę ftu dium,quod illorum doctrina labefactaba-tur. Et foletita Deus fastum suorum ho-ftiumvlcifci.Proprium his,quód in ipsum sibi ius sumunt,Pfal.12.& 49. Interim fe-rè homines vilifsimi fe illis opponunt, qui eis negotium faciunt, 1. Cor.1. Sic fit Ioh.9.Ita in præsenti. Sub Imperatoribus multa similia facta. Et hodie nihil frequentius fit. Olim Imperatores cum Pontificibus congresi succubuerunt. Nostro tem-pore obscuri homines vicerunt dicendo & scribendo. Hoc est quod prædictum, 2. Thess.2.
units.tr: Note: that such men assembled on account of the apostles, who were held in the greatest contempt and weakness. One may be astonished. But gain and zeal for private glory provoked them, because their teaching was weakening. God is accustomed to avenge the pride of his enemies in this way. It is characteristic of them that they claim for themselves a right against him (Ps. 12 and 49). Meanwhile, quite lowly men set themselves against them, who cause them trouble (1 Cor. 1). So it happens (John 9). So it is in the present case. Under the emperors many similar things were done. And today nothing happens more often. Formerly emperors who contended with the pontiffs were overcome. In our time obscure men have conquered by speaking and writing. This is what was foretold (2 Thess. 2).

units.la: ¶ 2. Hostium Christi authoritate & potentia neminem debere offendi, vt vel me tu succumbat, aut se illis subijciat. In diui-nis hominum dignitas nulla est, Isa.1.29. Matth.15. Vendicant hodie sibi & concilijs suis Pontifices quiduis statuendi au-thoritatem. Argumento vtuntur, quod Petri cathedram teneant & successores sint Apostolorum, de quibus dictum, Matthei 10. Luc.10. Ioh.13. Quod item Regum authoritate confirmati sint, Amos 7. At-qui omnia ista habuerunt isti, de quibus in præsenti. Non tamen illis cesserunt Apostoli, eò quòd degenerassent, Vt ergo nostris illis hæc omnia demus, nihil tamē his iuuabuntur, cùm etiam ipsi nihil Apostolicum referant: sed ea faciant, quæ olim Christus & Apostoli prædixerunt, Matt.24.1. Tim 4.2 Tim.3 2.Pet.3.2.Thess.2.
units.tr: 2. No one should be offended by the authority and power of Christ's enemies, so that he either gives way to them or submits himself to them. In divine matters there is no dignity of men, Isa. 1.29; Matth. 15. Today the pontiffs claim for themselves and their councils the authority to decide whatever they please. They argue that they hold Peter's chair and are the successors of the Apostles, of whom it is said in Matt. 10, Luke 10 and John 13. They argue likewise that they are confirmed by the authority of kings, Amos 7. Yet those men of whom we now speak had all these things. Still, the Apostles did not yield to them on the ground that they had degenerated. So even if we grant them all these things, they will gain nothing from them, since they themselves show nothing Apostolic, but do the very things which Christ and the Apostles foretold: Matt. 24; 1 Tim. 4; 2 Tim. 3; 2 Pet. 3; 2 Thess. 2.

units.la: II. Quæstio illorum fuit: In qua virtute &c. Cum imperio agunt, & prætexunt ze-li di-
units.tr: II. Their question was: "By what power, etc.?" They act with authority and pretend zeal...

units.la: Quæstio sex-ta- de certa ... concilij.
units.tr: Sixth question: concerning the certain ... of the council.

units.la: li diuini speciem, quasi ex officio hoc quae rant, ut quorum sit cauere ne populus sal sa doctrina aut signis seducatur. Sed calumniandi occasionem venantur, ut in Christo, Matth.21.12.22.Iohan.18.Luc.10. Quid enim opus erat quaerere id, de quo publice dixerant Apostoli.
units.tr: But they hunt for an occasion to slander, as against Christ (Matt. 21:12, 22; John 18; Luke 10). For what need was there to ask about that which the apostles had publicly declared?

units.la: Nota. Atqui dudum ad ista responsum est. Sed ansam captant ex verbis temere elapsis. Suspecta ergo nobis sint talium consilia, & serpentina prudentia utamur, Mat.10.
units.tr: Note: yet an answer has long since been given to these things. But they seize on an occasion from words rashly uttered. Therefore let us regard the counsels of such men with suspicion, and let us use serpent-like prudence (Matt. 10).

units.la: Interim Petrum imitemur, qui fortiter respondet. Praestatur promissio, Luc.21.
units.tr: Meanwhile let us imitate Peter, who answers boldly. The promise is given (Luke 21).

units.la: 1. Arguit illorum improbitatem, hono rifice tamen praefatur, ne ex affectu pute-tur agere. Quasi dicat: Mirabamur cur in carcerem adductifimus, vtpote nullius maleficij nobis conscij. At quantum video propter beneficium homini misero collatum hoc nobis accidit, &c.
units.tr: 1. He argues against their wickedness, yet first speaks with honour, lest it be thought that he acts out of passion. As if he were saying: We were wondering why we had been brought into prison, being conscious of no wrongdoing. But as far as I can see, this has happened to us on account of a benefit conferred on a wretched man, etc.

units.la: Habent ista singularem acrimoniam, in qua Nota. Perstringi communem in gratitudinem mundi, qui fere benefactores odit & insectatur. Sic Mosi accidit, Exod.2.14.16.Num.11.16.&c. Prophetis,1.
units.tr: These matters have a singular bitterness, and here note: the ingratitude common to the world is lashed, which almost always hates and persecutes its benefactors. So it happened to Moses, Exod. 2.14, 16; Num. 11.16, etc.; to the prophets, 1 Kings 18; Jer. 45, etc.

units.la: I
units.tr: I

units.la: Reg.i8.Iere.45. &c. In primis vide Mich. 6. Quàm multi tunc erant Hierosolymæ malefici omnis generis. At nullus horum iudicio sistitur. Soli Apoitoli,&c. Ita hodie fere fit. Fiunt omnia, quæ turbas parere possunt. Interim de nemine queritur mundus,quàm de verbi præconibus. Causa, quòd mauult mundus in peccatis commputrefcere, quàm pœnitere vt feruetur. Simile à mendicis, &c. Non ergo hodie offendamur. Vlciscetur Deus,&c.
units.tr: Especially see Mich. 6: how many evildoers of every kind there were then in Jerusalem, yet none of these is brought to judgement; only the Apostles, etc. So it is nearly the same today. Everything is done that can stir up tumults, yet the world complains of no one more than of the heralds of the Word. The cause is that the world prefers to rot in its sins rather than repent and be saved. Compare beggars, etc. Therefore let us not be offended today. God will avenge, etc.

units.la: 2. Adquæstionem transit: Notum sit vo bis omnibus & toti populo, &c. Ostendit hu-ius causæ cognitionem ad omnes pertine-re. Et idem dicit quod in templo, simulq; scelus eis in faciem exprobrat. Resurre-ctionem vero adjcit, vt innuat illos fru-stra cum Christo bellum suscepisse.
units.tr: 2. He moves on to the question: "Be it known to you all and to the whole people, etc." He shows that knowledge of this cause pertains to everyone, and he says the same thing as in the temple, while at the same time throwing their crime in their faces. But he adds the resurrection, to hint that they had waged war against Christ in vain.

units.la: Interim Not.q Vt agendum cum ho-stibus veritatis. Dignatur quidem titulis suis, interim non seruiliter adulatur, sed li-berè dicit, quæ ipsis arguendis & asseren-dæ gloriæ Dei seruiebant. Ita abstineant ministri à petulantibus conuitijs. Etsi e-nim aliqui digni contumelia, nos tamen indigni, &c. Interim non dissimulemus quæ veritatis sunt. Et semper in animo hç reat, Christum resurrexisse, & ideo vitę au-thorem esse, qui nos tueri pussit, Rom.14.
units.tr: Meanwhile note: how one ought to deal with the enemies of the truth. He does indeed respect their titles, yet he does not flatter them servilely, but speaks freely about those things which served to refute them and to assert the glory of God. So let ministers abstain from wanton reproaches. For although some are worthy of insult, we are not, etc. Meanwhile let us not dissemble the things that belong to the truth. And let this always remain in our mind: that Christ has risen, and that he is therefore the author of life, who is able to protect us (Rom. 14).

units.la: Oremus.
units.tr: Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY XXIX.

units.la: 11 Hic est lapis ille pro nihilo habi-tus a vobis aedificantibus, qui factus est caput anguli.
units.tr: 11 This is the stone which was set at nought by you builders, which is become the head of the corner.

units.la: 12 Nec est in alio quoquam salus: nec enim aliud nomen est sub caelo quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos salvari.
units.tr: 12 Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.

units.la: VT Christus discipulis praedixit, fore vt in concilijs & coram principibus sistantur ad reddendā suae fidei & doctrinae rationem: ita monet ne ideo solicit sint, quia non ipsi sint, qui causam hanc agant, sed, &c. Matt. 10. Luc. 21. Id quàm fideliter praestiterit, prima haec actio docet. Capiuntur Apostoli, quòd oblata per miraculū occasione Christum in templo praedicârunt. Inde sistuntur iudicio, ad quod consederunt quicunque tunc authoritate praestabant apud Iudaeos. Quaeritur, cuius virtute & nomine haec faciant? Hic ex tempore Petrus respondet tam fortiter & bene, vt ipsi hæreant. 1. Iniquitatem eorum arguit, &c. 2. Christū liberè fatetur, simulque scelus in hunc comissum exprobrat, & quae in templo dixit, nunc in facie, &c. Quo docemur adeo nō debere nos Christi pudere, vt hunc non modò profiteamur, verumetiá eius hostes corripiamus, Mar. 8.Rom.1 Quia autem præcipuum Apostolorum munus fuit,Christum prædicare,&in hoc salutem omnibus offerre (Luc 24.)idipsum nunc facit.Et quia in Christi mentionem incidit, ostendit quis ille sit.Fundamentum scilicet & caput Ecclesiæ,in quo vno omnis salus habeatur. Id autem tradit hoc ordine.
units.tr: As Christ foretold to his disciples that they would be brought before councils and before rulers to give an account of their faith and doctrine, so he warns them not to be anxious on that account, since it is not they themselves who conduct this cause, but... (Matt. 10; Luke 21). How faithfully he fulfilled this, the first action of the apostles shows. Peter and John are seized because, on the occasion of a miracle that had been performed, they preached Christ in the temple. Then they are brought before the court, in which sat whoever then held authority among the Jews. The question is asked: by whose power and in whose name do they do these things? Here Peter answers extempore, so boldly and well that his opponents are struck dumb. (1) He argues against their wickedness; (2) he freely confesses Christ, and at the same time reproaches them for the crime committed against him, and what he had said in the temple he now says to their face. From this we are taught that we ought not to be ashamed of Christ to such a degree that we merely profess him, but we should also rebuke his enemies (Mark 8; Rom. 1). Because the chief office of the apostles was to preach Christ and in him offer salvation to all (Luke 24), he now does the same. And since mention of Christ has come up, he shows who he is: namely the foundation and head of the Church, in whom alone all salvation is found. He sets this out in the following order.

units.la: I. Scandalo occurrit, quod inde obijciebatur,quód ij Christum reijcerent,qui religionis & doctrinæ erant præsides Sacerdotes nimirum,de quibus Mal.2.Deut er.17.Idem enim tunc multi patiebantur, quod hodie quidam.Id ergo Petrus remo uet Dauidis testimonio,ex Psalm.118.quo Christus quoq; vtitur Mat.21.Mar.12.Lucæ 20. Et de Sacerdotibus diserté expo-nens ait: Hic est lapis, &c. Sensus: Scio plerisq, mirum videri, nos Christo tantum tribuere, quem vos contumeliosissimè reiecistis.At hic meminisse oportebat, hoc à Domino factum,& vel hinc constare eum esse,de quo prophetæ sunt vaticinati.Num illud Dauidis excidit? Atqui vos estis architecti illi. Vos Iesum reiecistis vt prophanum,&c. At hunc refuscitastum Deus extulit,&c.
units.tr: I. He meets the scandal which was being raised from this, namely that those who were the presidents of religion and doctrine rejected Christ, that is, the priests, concerning whom Mal. 2 and Deut. 17. For many then suffered what some suffer today. Peter therefore removes this objection by the testimony of David from Psalm 118, which Christ also uses (Matt. 21; Mark 12; Luke 20). And, expounding explicitly concerning the priests, he says: This is the stone, etc. The sense: I know that many think it strange that we attribute so much to Christ, whom you rejected with the greatest contempt. But here one ought to remember that this was done by the Lord, and from this alone it is established that he is the one of whom the prophets prophesied. Has that saying of David slipped your minds? Yet you are those builders. You rejected Jesus as profane, etc. But God raised up this same man whom you had crucified, etc.

units.la: In quibus NOTA. §1. Christum lapidi conconferri. Sic Dan.2.Zach.3 12.If28. Ratio, quod hic sit Ecclesiæ fundamentum. Ita ipse exponit Matth.16 & ita intellexerunt Apostoli,1.Pet.2.Eph. 2. 1. Cor.3.Ergo nō sunt Ecclesia,qui non super hunc æd ficati sunt. Simul hoc consolationi seruit, ne de Ecclesiæ perpetuitate,aut nostræ salutis certitudine dubitemus. Licet enim illius membra aliquando vacillent,non mouetur tamen fundamentum,& qui huic nituntur non pereunt.Mat.7 Luc.22.
units.tr: On these points NOTE. §1. Christ is compared to a stone; so Dan. 2, Zech. 3, Isa. 28. The reason is that he is the foundation of the Church. He himself expounds this in Matt. 16, and the apostles understood it so (1 Pet. 2; Eph. 2; 1 Cor. 3). Therefore those who are not built upon him are not the Church. At the same time this serves for consolation, so that we need not doubt either the perpetuity of the Church or the certainty of our salvation. For although its members sometimes waver, the foundation is not moved, and those who rest upon it do not perish (Matt. 7; Luke 22).

units.la: ¶2. Quæ fors Christi inter homines? Reijcitur ferè,& quidem ab ædificantibus. Hi sunt Sacerdotes & qui ordinarij Ecclesiæ ministri sunt.Sic dicuntur,quia eorum est colligere & extruere Ecclesiam, quæ est domus Dei,1.Timo.3.1.Cor.2. Id fit,si ad Christum adducant,&c.1.Pet.2. Id olim fecerant prophetæ,1. Pet.1.2. Pet.1. At diuersum faciebant sacerdotes. Causa, quia suis intenti hoc quærebant, vt hæreditatem sibi vendicarent, Ioh.5 Matth.21. Perpetuum hoc. Obseruemus hoc propter eos, qui Pontificios errare posse negant.Vnde postea pleriq; offenduntur, si Christum ab eis reijci videant. Atqui isti cum in Mosis cathedra sederent(Mat.23.) errârunt tamen in capite salutis. Et quid nostris hodie tribui debeat, mores docet.
units.tr: ¶2. What is Christ's lot among men? He is almost always rejected, and indeed by the builders. These are the priests and those who are the ordinary ministers of the Church. They are so called because it is their task to gather and build up the Church, which is the house of God (1 Tim. 3; 1 Cor. 3). This is done if they bring people to Christ, etc. (1 Pet. 2). The prophets did this in former times (1 Pet. 1; 2 Pet. 1). But the priests did the opposite. The reason is that, intent on their own affairs, they sought this, that they might claim the inheritance for themselves (John 5; Matt. 21). This is perpetual. Let us observe this on account of those who deny that the Papists can err, and from which many afterwards take offence if they see Christ rejected by them. Yet these men, although they sat in Moses' seat (Matt. 23), nevertheless erred in the chief matter of salvation. And what ought to be attributed to our own men today, their conduct teaches.

units.la: Idem futurum nouisimis temporibus ostendum praedictum, Matt.24. Act.20.2. Thess.2. 1.Tim.3. 2.Pet.2.
units.tr: That the same will happen in the last times is shown by prophecy: Matt. 24; Acts 20; 2 Thess. 2; 1 Tim. 3; 2 Pet. 2.

units.la: Num autem ideo Christus reiectus apud Deum? Imò factus in caput anguli. Caput quia Rex & Sacerdos, Psal.2. & 110. Anguli, quia duos populos complectitur, Eph.2. Et hic honor ei semper integer manebit, ad Heb. 13. Vnde sequitur ipsi nihil decedere, eos autem multari, qui ad eum offendunt, &c. Vide Luc.20. Zach.12.
units.tr: But is Christ therefore rejected by God? On the contrary, he has been made the head of the corner. Head, because he is King and Priest (Ps. 2 and 110). Corner, because he embraces two peoples (Eph. 2). And this honour will remain whole for him always (Heb. 13). Whence it follows that nothing is taken away from him, but that those who stumble against him are punished, etc. See Luke 20; Zech. 12.

units.la: II. Applicat ista praesentiae causae, ne quis praeter hunc aliam salutis rationem excogitet, aut Christo aliquid coniungi posse arbitretur: ut fecerunt quidam, Act.15. & hodie in Papatu fit. Dicit ergo: Non est in alio salus. Et mox probat aeterno Dei decreto. Nec enim aliud nomen, id est nihil quod nominari possit, &c. Quasi dicat: Vt in rerum natura unam quamq; rem oportet ijs medijs confici, quę Deus ad eam decrevit: Ita etiam salus non aliter, quàm vt Deus statuit, acquiritur: At is illa in vno Christo conclusit. Ergo in nullo alio inuenietur. Est hoc argumentum firmissimum, quia Dei decreta sunt inuiolabilia, Isa.14. 40. Matt.24. Psa.33. Conueniunt his omnes Scripturae. Primae promissiones, Ge.3. 22. 26. 28. 49. Moses Deut.18. Prophetae, 1.
units.tr: II. He applies these things to the present cause, so that no one may devise any other way of salvation apart from this one, or think that anything can be joined to Christ, as some did (Acts 15), and as is done today in the Papacy. He therefore says: there is no salvation in another. And soon he proves it by God's eternal decree. For there is no other name, that is, nothing that can be named, etc. As if he said: just as in the nature of things each thing must be brought about by those means which God decreed for it, so salvation too is acquired in no other way than as God has ordained; but he has enclosed it in Christ alone. Therefore it will be found in no other. This is a most firm argument, because the decrees of God are inviolable (Isa. 14; 40; Matt. 24; Ps. 33). All Scripture agrees with these. The first promises (Gen. 3; 22; 26; 28; 49); Moses (Deut. 18); the prophets.

units.la: tç,i.Pet.i.If.42.53 35 Mich 4.5.Ier.23 Zac. 13.Bap.Ioh.1.3 Angeli Mat.i.Luc.2. Pater cælitus,Matt.3.17.Apostoli hîc, Act.13.15. Item 1.Pet 1.Eph.1 1 Cor.1.2.1 Ioh 1 2.Ipse Christus Ioh.14.4 10. Luc.24. Et res ipsa loquitur. Vt enim feruemur opus peccatorum expiatione,noua iustitia,regene ratione & viuificatione.Hæc omnia vnus Christus præstat,Ioh.1.Heb 9.10. Dan.9. 1.Cor.1.1.Pet.1.2.Cor.5.Ioh. 6. Nec gloriam dat alij,Ifa.42.
units.tr: ...(Isa. 42; 53; 35); Mic. 4, 5; Jer. 23; Zech. 13; John the Baptist (John 1, 3); the angels (Matt. 1; Luke 2); the Father from heaven (Matt. 3:17); the apostles here (Acts 13, 15). Likewise 1 Pet. 1; Eph. 1; 1 Cor. 1, 2; 1 John 1, 2. Christ himself (John 14; Luke 24). And the thing itself speaks. For we are delivered from the guilt of sins by expiation, and receive new righteousness, regeneration and quickening. All these things the one Christ alone bestows (John 1; Heb. 9, 10; Dan. 9; 1 Cor. 1; 1 Pet. 1; 2 Cor. 5; John 6). Nor does he give his glory to another (Isa. 42).

units.la: No T.¶ 1.Bonitatem Dei, qui cùm nobis nō alia ratione posset succurri, Filium dedit,idq; ex mera dileƈtione,Ioh.3 1.Ioh. 4. Id soletur in tentationibus.Quid enim porrò negaret? Rom.8.
units.tr: Note. 1. The goodness of God, who, since we could not be helped in any other way, gave his Son, and that out of mere love (John 3; 1 John 4). This consoles us in temptations. For what would he further deny us? (Rom. 8).

units.la: ¶ 2.Officij admonemur. 1. Quoad fidé, vno Christo contenti fimus. Hîç enim euertuntur omnes aliæ superstitiones & fe êtæ,eorum in primis, qui noua nomina sibi aflumunt,vt olim 1.Cor 1.Itaq; nó mo ueat nos quorumcunq; authoritas, quin nos faciamus quod habetur Mich.4. Sic Petrus Iohan.6. 2.Cor.5. Rom.9.12.Iac.2. &c. Qui his student, in illo reuera seruabuntur. Oremus.
units.tr: ¶2. We are reminded of our duty. 1. As to faith, let us be content with Christ alone. For here all other superstitions and sects are overturned, especially those of men who assume new names for themselves, as once happened (1 Cor. 1). Therefore let no one's authority move us from doing what is commanded (Mic. 4). So Peter (John 6); (2 Cor. 5; Rom. 9, 12; James 2), etc. Those who strive after these things will truly be saved in him. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXX.
units.tr: HOMILY XXX.

units.la: 13 Confpeƈta vero Petri in dicen- 14 do libertate, & Iohannis, compertoq; homines esse illiteratos et idiotas, admirabantur, & agnoscebant eos cum Iesu fuisse.
units.tr: 13 When they saw the boldness of Peter in speaking, and of John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and recognised that they had been with Jesus.

units.la: 14 Illum verò videntes stantem cum eis qui, &c. ad ver. 19. v/q.
units.tr: 14 But seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, etc., as far as verse 19.

units.la: LVcas diligenter narrat primam actio nem Apostolorum in Concilio, vt ea discamus, quid pij in simili casu faciant, & quibus armis impij veritatem oppugnent, & quàm nihil proficiant. Ad primum pertinet Petri responsio, qui nō mo dò ingenuè fatetur, de quo rogatus fuit, sed insuper salutem omnem in vno Christo contineri docet, nihil illos moratus, quos nihil iniquius ferre sciebat. Imitemur nos & fateamur liberè veritatem, neq; nos Christi & Euangelij pudeat, Ro. 8. Mar. 8. Sequitur alterum, quid Petro audito fecerint aduersarij. Vbi multa concurrunt, quæ ad nostram institutionem & consolationem faciunt.
units.tr: Luke relates carefully the first action of the Apostles before the Council, so that we may learn what the godly do in a similar case, with what weapons the ungodly attack the truth, and how little they accomplish. To the first point belongs Peter's answer, who not only frankly confesses what he was asked, but also teaches that all salvation is contained in Christ alone, and is not deterred by those whom he knew to be utterly unjust. Let us imitate him and freely confess the truth; let us not be ashamed of Christ and the Gospel, Rom. 8; Mark 8. Next comes what the adversaries did when they heard Peter. Here many things come together that serve for our instruction and consolation.

units.la: I. Stupent & mirantur, incerti quid faciant. Causæ sunt: 1. παρρησία inexspecta ta Apostolorum. Sciebant idiotas esse, & ideo sperabant eos facilè posse terreri, vel nō habituros quod responderent. Non possunt ergo non obstupescere, quando illos tam cordatos & fortes vident.
units.tr: I. They are stunned and amazed, uncertain what to do. The causes are: 1. the boldness (parrhesia) of the Apostles, which they did not expect. They knew them to be unlearned, and so they hoped they could easily be terrified, or that they would have no answer to give. They cannot therefore but be astonished when they see them so wise and brave.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶Impios nulla rema- gis confundi, quàm libera redargutione verbi Dei.Audaces enim fiunt,quòd Deum sua scelera latere putant, Pfalm. 94. Si ergo fe intra animos suos sentiant con uictos,stupent & timent.Sic Achab.1.Regum 21. Econtra fi ministros vel blandiri vel mutos canes esse videant(Ifa.56.)proficiunt in peius, & tandem cum his perevnt. Ideo παῤῥησία haec passim praecipitur,Ifa.58.Ezech.3.Ier.1.1.Tim.5.2.Tim.4. Et Paulus hanc sibi dari precabatur, Eph. 6. Vide infra 4. cap. Qui hanc ferre nolunt, cum propria salute pugnant. 11. Veritas signi euidens, quae negari non potest, nec magiae insimulari. Astabat enim ille discipulis. Haerent ergo, & qui vnica quaestione eos vinci posse speraue-rant, iam fe captos sentiunt. Tam vana sunt hominum consilia contra Deum, Pf. 94.Iob.5.Simile exemplum Ioh.9. Nemi-nem ergo terreat astutia vel potentia hominum.Dei causa,Matth.10.
units.tr: Note meanwhile that the wicked are confounded by nothing more than by the free rebuke of God's Word. For they grow bold because they think God does not see their crimes, Ps. 94. If, therefore, they feel themselves convicted within their own minds, they are stunned and afraid, as Ahab was, 1 Kings 21. On the contrary, if they see ministers either flattering them or acting like dumb dogs (Isa. 56), they grow worse and in the end perish along with them. Therefore this boldness (parrhesia) is commanded everywhere: Isa. 58; Ezek. 3; Jer. 1; 1 Tim. 5; 2 Tim. 4. Paul too asked that it be given to him, Eph. 6. See below, chapter 4. Those who are unwilling to bear it fight against their own salvation. 11. The truth of the sign is evident and cannot be denied, nor can it be charged with magic. For the man stood with the disciples. Those who had hoped to beat them with a single question now feel themselves caught. So vain are the counsels of men against God, Ps. 94; Job 5. A similar example is John 9. Let no one be terrified by the cunning or power of men; it is for God's cause, Matt. 10.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶1.Mirabile Dei con- filium, qui non alium Apostolis adiunxit patronum ex hominibus, quàm mendicum & prius claudum. Atqui quemuis alium darepoterat, vt prius Nicod.Ioh.7. Iofeph Luc,23.Sed ita ei visum est, vt suos hostes magis confunderet.i.Cor.i.Fuit enim hic sufficiens. Sic Mosi Aaronem dedit, Exod. 4. 5. Obler. hodie contra eos, qui nobis exprobrant nostrorum ignobilitatem,perinde vt Io. 7.Atqui isti hafte-nus inuisi fuerunt regibus & Papis, &c. Matthaei 11.
units.tr: Note meanwhile: 1. The wonderful counsel of God, who joined to the Apostles no human patron other than a beggar, and one who had formerly been lame. Yet he could have given any other, as before Nicodemus, John 7, and Joseph, Luke 23. But so it seemed good to him, that he might confound his enemies the more, 1 Cor. 1. For this man was sufficient. So to Moses he gave Aaron, Exod. 4–5. Observe today against those who reproach us with the lowliness of our people, just as in John 7. Yet these men have hitherto been hated by kings and Popes, etc., Matt. 11.

units.la: 2. Gratitudinem claudi.Poterat femul tis excusare, & deprecari culpam. Arguun tur, qui in Christo beneficio quidem salutis frui volunt,at pro eodem nolunt periclitari. Tales sunt,qui Euangelium praedicari sinunt, sed vt ea dicantur non ferunt, quae aliquos offendunt. Item qui cum impij furiunt contra ministros, omnem his opem negant: Imo confpeftum eorum declinant, ne veniant in suspicionem. Quales vero qui conuitiantur, & frigidi suffundunt. Sed memineris, Christum non diuidi.Per crucem ingressus est in gloriam,Luc.24.i.Pet.i. Eadem via nobis quoque eundum,Matt.16. 2.Timoth. 3.Imitemur nos ergo claudi fidem & fortitudinem.
units.tr: 2. The gratitude of the lame man. He could have excused himself and begged off the blame. Those are reproved who wish to enjoy the benefit of salvation in Christ, but are unwilling to be put in danger for the same cause. Such are those who allow the Gospel to be preached, but do not bear that things be said which offend some. Likewise those who, when the impious rage against ministers, deny them all help; indeed they turn their eyes away, lest they come under suspicion. And those who revile, and then blush coldly, are of the same kind. But remember that Christ is not divided. He entered into glory through the cross, Luke 24; 1 Pet. 1. By the same way we too must go, Matt. 16; 2 Tim. 3. Let us therefore imitate the faith and fortitude of the lame man.

units.la: II.Decretum exponitur,vbi mira confusio 1. Quid faciemus? An ergo nesciebant innocentes dimitti & beneficij authores remunerari debere?Sed occasionem quae runt;Fatentur miraculu.Impij ergo quod in eius authorem conspirant. 3. Produnt quid ipsos maximè vrat. Scilicet quòd populo innotuerit. Pluris ergo populum fa iunt quàm Deù, Io.h5.4. Coucludunt, Ne porrò diuulgetur, &c. Et hoc minis putant impetrari posse. Ideò accersunt Apostolos, minantur. Concurrunt impudentia, stultitia, impietas. Obliteratum vo lunt, quod ipsi fatentur. Tacitum, quod erat in ore omni populo. Nec verentur cum Christo adhuc pugnare, cuius vim in morte & resurrectione senserât, Mat. 27.28
units.tr: II. The decree is set out, where there is strange confusion. 1. What shall we do? Did they not know that the innocent must be released and that the authors of a benefit ought to be rewarded? But they seek an occasion. They confess the miracle; the wicked therefore conspire against its author. 3. They betray what most burns them: that it has become known to the people. They value the people more than God, John 12:43. They conclude that it must not be spread any further, etc., and they think this can be obtained by threats. Therefore they summon the Apostles and threaten them. Impudence, folly and impiety meet together. They want to wipe out what they themselves confess, and silence what was on every tongue. Nor do they fear to fight still against Christ, whose power they had felt in his death and resurrection, Matt. 27–28.

units.la: Vbi Not. 1. Quò erumpat semel conceptum diuinæ veritatis odiū. Non reftin guitur propriæ cófcientiæ teftimoniū. Sic Magi, Exo.8.Balaa, Nu 22.23 24. Ita hodie Pontificij cum suis. Ipsi non semel errores fassi sunt: hodie vident deteftos, feq; rideri ab omnib. vt prædictū Apo.18. Adhuc ta men sibi ius omne vendicat, negant (e ere re posse, filentiū mandant, & toties victi, adhuc pugnam contra Chriftū instaurant.
units.tr: Note here: 1. How far the hatred once conceived against divine truth bursts out. The testimony of one's own conscience does not restrain it. So the Magi, Exod. 8; Balaam, Num. 22–24. So today the Papists with their own. They themselves have more than once confessed their errors; today they see themselves exposed and mocked by all, as foretold in Rev. 18. Yet still they claim every right for themselves, deny that anything can be changed, order silence, and though often defeated, they renew the battle against Christ.

units.la: 2. Quàm periculosum fit potestatem in Repub. credere hominib. non timentibus Deū. Nulla in talibus sapientia, Prou. 1. Itaq; effunduntur in omnem licentiam. Imo eo superbiunt, quòd ipsi nullis legibus teneantur, Pf. 12 54. Quid hinc speres quàm naufragiū? Palli hocApoft. sub istis.
units.tr: 2. How dangerous it is to entrust power in the commonwealth to men who do not fear God. There is no wisdom in such men, Prov. 1. Therefore they pour themselves out into every licence. Indeed they grow proud because they are bound by no laws, Ps. 12; 54. What can you hope from this but shipwreck? Let the Apostle's warning be heeded under such men.

units.la: Obseruemus hodie magistratum electione. Ingens Dei beneficium. Sequere re ergo regulam, quæ extat. Exod. 18. Ex omni populo elige viros facultatum, mentes Dei, viros veraces, qui oderint auaritiam. Qui vero in magistratu iunt, minerint iudicium esse Dei, qui ipsis medius interfit, Deut. 1. 2. Paral. 19. Psa. 72. 82. Ita seipsos & Rempubl. cum seruabunt, Oremus.
units.tr: Let us observe today the election of magistrates, a huge benefit of God. Follow therefore the rule that is set out in Exod. 18: from all the people choose men of ability, who fear God, men of truth, who hate avarice.
