Those who hold office should remember that judgment is God's, who is present in the midst of them, Deut. 1; 2 Chron. 19; Ps. 72, 82. Thus they will preserve both themselves and the commonwealth. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXI.
units.tr: Homily XXXI.

units.la: 19 Petrus autem & Iohannes respondentes dixerunt eis: An apud Deum iustum sit vobis potius auscultare quàm Deo, indicate,
units.tr: 19 But Peter and John answered and said to them: Judge for yourselves whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God.

units.la: 20 Non enim possumus quæ vidimus & audiuimus non loqui.
units.tr: 20 For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

units.la: CHristus Apostolis suis & omnibus in se credentibus crebrò de cruce concionatur. Id vero non facit vt terreat, sed fidi Imperatoris instar, vt aduersus præuisa pericula fide & patientia armemur. Et ideo simul ope pollicetur, & omnibus periculis superiores fore dicit, Lu. 21. 12. Io. 16. &c. Exemplum huius rei euidēs hoc Cap. habetur. Cōspirarunt contra Apostolos, quicunq; authoritate & potentia valebant: Et per hos factum, vt primò in carcerem conijcerentur, deinde concilio cilio sisterentur,vt coram iniquissimis iudicibus fidei & doctrinæ suæ rationem redderent. Vincit tamen veritas,& ita vincit, vt hostes obstupescant, & rerum incerti nihil habeant quàm minas graues, &c.
units.tr: Christ often preaches to his Apostles and to all who believe in him about the cross. He does not do this to terrify them, but like a faithful commander, so that we may be armed with faith and patience against foreseen dangers. Therefore he promises help at the same time and says that they will be superior to all dangers (Luke 21:12; John 16, etc.). A clear example of this is found in this chapter. Those who held authority and power conspired against the Apostles, and through them it came about that they were first thrown into prison and then brought before the council, so that they might give an account of their faith and teaching before the most unjust judges. Yet the truth prevails, and prevails in such a way that the enemies are struck dumb, and, uncertain of their own position, have nothing left but serious threats, etc.

units.la: Ita solent Euangelij hostes. Initio ius prætexunt,& videri volunt iudicio agere. At quando vident se succumbere, tunc minis & vi apertâ agunt.
units.tr: So the enemies of the Gospel usually behave. At first they pretend to have the law on their side and want to seem to act by judgment. But when they see that they are giving way, then they act with threats and open force.

units.la: Sequitur quid Apostoli fecerint,& quid in simili casu fieri debeat.
units.tr: There follows what the Apostles did, and what ought to be done in a similar case.

units.la: Summa & propositio est,quòd se neq; posse, neque velle obedire respondent. Ne tamen proterui & impudentes videantur,rationibus agunt solidissimis. Obseruent hoc pij,vt constantes quidè sint, sed non præfracti vel audaces. Sed ita agant,vt qui curabiles sunt,posint discere & lucrifieri. Sic Christus passim.Rationes sunt duæ.
units.tr: The sum and proposition is this: they answer that they can neither obey nor are willing to obey. Lest they seem shameless and impudent, however, they argue from very solid reasons. Let the godly observe this: they should be steadfast, but not stubborn or reckless. They should act so that those who can be cured may be able to learn and be won over. So Christ does everywhere. There are two reasons.

units.la: I. Dei mandato se tuentur,cuius autho ritas maior est, quàm vt cuiquam cedere debeat.Argumentum: Deo magis est obediendum, quàm hominibus. Deus iussit prædicare(Mat.28.Luc.24.Mar.16.Act.1.) quod vos prohibetis:&c.Ergo, &c. Interim vtuntur Concessione,& ipsis iudicium deferunt, vt in re, quæ sit extra con-
units.tr: I. They defend themselves by the command of God, whose authority is too great to yield to anyone. The argument runs: we must obey God rather than men. God commanded preaching (Matt. 28; Luke 24; Mark 16; Acts 1), and you forbid it; therefore, etc. Meanwhile they make a concession and leave the judgment to their opponents, as in a matter beyond dispute.

units.la: trouerfiam. Etenim plus quàm diabolica effet confidentia, fi quis seipsum vellet Deo Præferre. Proponitur autem hic tota ratio veræ obedientiæ,quę doctrina vti liffima est Exigitur passim obedientia, & necessaria est priuatim & publicè,in re do meftica,militari, Repub. Sed feré vtrinq; érratur, abijs quiiubent, & ijs qui obe- diunt,&c.Nota ¶1.Qui iubendi ius ha- bent, ne quid iubeant quod Deo impro- betur. Etsi enim hic aliquos alijs præfece- rit,sibi tamen in omnes ius feruat, & omnes sibi parere & seruire vult.Ideo D.Do minantium dicitur,Deut.10.1.Tim.6.&c. Apoc.19.Vir vxoris caput,sed cum ratio- ne,ne cogat ad impia.Eph.5. Parentü po- testas magna in liberos, Deut.21. Sed habet hæc suos limites,Deut.6.Pfal.78 Leuit.20.2.Reg.21.&c.Sic doctorum munus a Deo est,Mal.2.Deut.17 2.Cor.5.Matt.16 Sed tunc ista rata sunt, fi Dei verbũ prædicent. Sic dictum prophetis, Ezech.3.33. Ier.1.Matth.28.Ita magistratus Dij dicuntur,Exod 22.Pfal.82. Et his obediendum, Rom.13.Sed ijdem ferui Dei sunt, quibus ille sua iudicia credidit,Deut.1.Pfalm.72. 2.Par.19. Illa ergo enuntient.
units.tr: For it would be more than diabolical presumption for anyone to set himself above God. Here is set out the whole doctrine of true obedience, which is most useful. Obedience is required everywhere, and it is necessary both privately and publicly, in the household, in the army, and in the commonwealth. But almost everywhere people err, both those who command and those who obey, etc. Note ¶1: those who have the right to command must take care not to command anything that is displeasing to God. For although he has set some over others, he nonetheless keeps authority over all, and wishes all to obey and serve him. Hence the Lord is called "the Lord of lords" (Deut. 10; 1 Tim. 6; Rev. 19). The husband is "the head of the wife," but with reason, so that he does not compel her to impious things (Eph. 5). The power of parents over children is great (Deut. 21), but it has its limits (Deut. 6; Ps. 78; Lev. 20; 2 Kings 21, etc.). So too the office of teachers is from God (Mal. 2; Deut. 17; 2 Cor. 5; Matt. 16). But their authority stands only if they preach the Word of God. So it was said to the prophets (Ezek. 3, 33; Jer. 1; Matt. 28). Thus magistrates are called gods (Exod. 22; Ps. 82), and they must be obeyed (Rom. 13). But they are the servants of God, to whom he entrusted his judgments (Deut. 1; Ps. 72; 2 Chron. 19). Let them therefore proclaim those things.

units.la: ¶2.Quæ obedientiæ ratio. Examinent singuli quid iubeantur.Si id cum Dei voluntate luntate cōuenit,obediant. Sin illi aduersa tur,dicant quod Apostoli.Obseruent host coniuges, Coloss.3. Liberi. In verbi mini- stris idem obseruetur.Si verbum Dei præ dicent, obediamus simpliciter. Luc. 10. Matth.21.2.Cor.10.Sin sua figmenta,anathema sint,Gal.2. Deut 13. Ita si magistratus edicta sint sanēta & ex Dei verbo desurpta, parendum propter conscientiam Rom.13.Alioqui locum habet illud 1. Sam. 12. Imo si per se iniqua imponat & agat quæ tamen salua conscientia possunt fieri, nihil seditiose agendum. Vide Dauidem 1.Sam.24.26. Sin vero iubeat quæ impia sunt & a Deo prohibita, tunc faciendum quod hic habetur. Ita Christus iubet Mat. 21.¶3.Peccant ergo grauissimè,qui superstitiones excusant regum & principum authoritate Item qui hodie bonis & sanctis legibus non obediunt, in quas iurarunt.Monachi item, qui vota sua prætexunt. Aliter Prophetæ, Apostoli, Martyres.
units.tr: ¶2: The rule of obedience. Let each person examine what he is commanded. If it agrees with the will of God, let him obey. But if it opposes that will, let him say what the apostles said. Let wives observe this (Col. 3), and children likewise. The same is to be observed in ministers of the Word. If they preach the Word of God, we should obey them without qualification (Luke 10; Matt. 21; 2 Cor. 10). But if they preach their own inventions, let them be anathema (Gal. 1; Deut. 13). So, too, if the edicts of magistrates are holy and drawn from the Word of God, they must be obeyed for conscience' sake (Rom. 13). Otherwise the saying of 1 Sam. 12 applies. Indeed, if a magistrate imposes things that are unjust in themselves, but which can be done with a clear conscience, nothing is to be done seditiously. See David (1 Sam. 24, 26). But if he commands things that are impious and forbidden by God, then one must do what is taught here. So Christ commands (Matt. 21). ¶3: They therefore sin most gravely who excuse superstitions by the authority of kings and princes. Likewise those who today refuse to obey good and holy laws, which they have sworn to keep. Monks too, who put forward their vows. The prophets, apostles, and martyrs acted otherwise.

units.la: II.Vidimus & audiuimus ista:ergo non possumus non loqui. Consequentiæ vis in eo,quòd vt testes viderant, Ioh.15.Act. 1. Deinde quòd ad communem salutem ista pertinent ,cuius ipsi debebant esse ministri,Matth. 28. Act. 11, 16. Itaque tacendo in Christi gloriam & homines peccassent, 2. Cor.5.
units.tr: II. "We have seen and heard these things; therefore we cannot but speak." The force of this consequence lies in the fact that, as witnesses, they had seen (John 15; Acts 1). Further, these things pertain to the common salvation, of which they ought to be ministers (Matt. 28; Acts 11, 16). Thus by keeping silent they would have sinned both against the glory of Christ and against men (2 Cor. 5).

units.la: Vbi NOTA ¶ Quibus armis ministri contra minas & conatus hostium fe confirmare debeant. 1. Cogitent Deum velle vt Euangelium prædicetur (Mar. 13.) & hoc ipsorum esse, 1. Cor.9. Væ mihi, &c. Huc refer Ionæ exemplum, Ioh. 1.3. Hinc illud Amos .3. Agitur hic de gloria Dei & salute publica. Vtiufque ergo prodito-res sunt,fi quid reticeant.3.Deo olim red-dendam esse rationem, &c. Matth.25. & 24.&c.Hæc animosos reddent.
units.tr: Here NOTE: With what weapons ministers ought to strengthen themselves against the threats and attempts of enemies. First, let them consider that God wills the Gospel to be preached (Mark 13), and that this is their duty (1 Cor. 9: Woe is me, etc.). Refer here the example of Jonah (Jonah 1:3), and hence that saying of Amos 3. The matter here concerns the glory of God and the public salvation. Therefore if they keep silent about anything, they are betrayers of both. Third, that an account will one day be required of them by God (Matt. 25 and 24, etc.). These considerations will make them bold.

units.la: ¶ At ista non minus pertinent ad magistratus. Vult Deus ius dici, asseri innocentes,pauperes,viduas,&c.Pfal.72.lac.1. Vult viui honestè & sanctè.Faciunt ista ad eius gloriam & publicam pacem. Olim item ex illorum manibus requiret populum.Ista animent pios Senatores, ne fegnefcant aut timeant.Aderit illis Deus, vt possint plus quàm putetur.Populus obe-diat.Oremus.
units.tr: But these things pertain no less to magistrates. God wills justice to be done, and the innocent, the poor and widows to be defended (Ps. 72; James 1). He wills them to live honestly and holily. These things serve his glory and public peace. Likewise, God will one day require the people at their hands. These things should encourage godly senators, so that they do not grow sluggish or afraid. God will be with them, so that they can do more than is thought. Let the people obey. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXII.

units.la: 21 Illi vero non inuenientes quomodo punirent eos,additis minis eos diminserunt,propter populum : quia omnes glorificabant Deum,super eo quod factum fuerat. 22 An-
units.tr: 21 But they, not finding how they might punish them, dismissed them with threats, because of the people, since everyone was glorifying God for what had been done. 22 An-

units.la: Quibus armis ministri contra minas Cauftri mundo se oppone-re debeant
units.tr: With what weapons ministers ought to arm themselves against the threats of the world

units.la: 22 Annorum enim erat quadragin ta homo ille, in quo editum erat signum istud sanationis.
units.tr: 22 For the man on whom this sign of healing had been wrought was forty years old.

units.la: 23 Dimissi autem illi venerunt ad suos, & annuntiauerunt quæ principes Sacerdotum & Seniores ipsis dixerant.
units.tr: 23 And when they were let go, they went to their own people and reported what the chief priests and elders had said to them.

units.la: Icuti Lucas diligenter narrat, quid Sacerdotes & Seniores Hierosol. aduersus fidem Christianam & huius præcones Apostolos tentarint: Ita horum quoque fortitudinem & constantiam describit. In illis nihil præter vim apertam & dolos videre licet. Nam Apostolos immerentes in carcerem ducunt, mox autem iudicio sistunt, vt suæ fidei & doctrinæ rationem reddant: & ita prętexunt iuris studium. Ita verò causam agentibus Apostolis, vt ipsi nō habeant quod contradicant, non cedunt, sed minantur & mandant silentium. Ita solent hostes Christi, & hodie exempla sunt. Quid verò Apostoli? Initio reddunt rationem modestè, & facit Petrus, quod posteà Christianis omnibus præcipit, 1. Pet. 3. At vbi istos vident minaciter agere, negant se obedire posse, & excusant se mandato Dei, qui diuersum iusserit, &c. Act. 5.
units.tr: Just as Luke carefully narrates what the chief priests and elders of Jerusalem attempted against the Christian faith and against its heralds, the apostles, so he also describes the courage and steadfastness of the apostles. In the priests and elders we can see nothing but open force and trickery. For they lead the innocent apostles into prison and soon bring them before a court, so that they may give an account of their faith and teaching, and they put forward the pretext of legal procedure. But when the apostles argue the case so well that their opponents have nothing to say in reply, the priests do not give way; instead they threaten and order silence. This is how the enemies of Christ usually behave, and today there are examples of it. What do the apostles do? At first they give their account calmly, and Peter does what he later commands all Christians to do (1 Pet. 3). But when they see these men acting threateningly, they say that they cannot obey, and they excuse themselves by the command of God, who has ordered otherwise, etc. (Acts 5).

units.la: Vbi Not. ¶ Obedientiæ rationem. Sunt qui simpliciter obediendum dicunt
units.tr: Note: the reason for obedience. There are some who say that one must simply obey the magistrate in all things, and they misuse 1 Pet. 2 and Rom. 13.

units.la: magistratui in omnibus, & abutuntur 1. Pet.2.Rom.13. Sed tenendum est, Deum ita aliquos aliis praestantiores facere, ut ipse suis ius in omnes feruet, & ideo Christus audiendus Matth. 17. Obseruarunt hoc Martyres. Vide Dan 3.6. Ita hic Apostoli, & postea omnes alij, quorum memoria hodie sancta est. Sed videamus quid porro factum.
units.tr: But it must be held that God makes some more excellent than others in such a way that he himself keeps his right over all, and therefore Christ is to be heard (Matt. 17). The martyrs observed this; see Dan. 3:6. So did the apostles here, and afterwards all others whose memory is holy today. But let us see what happened next.

units.la: I Apostoli additis minis dimittuntur. Iam ergo crescit audacia. Non possunt respondere ad propositam causam, minantur tamen. Quid hoc aliud erat quàm si dixissent: Quid ad nos, quid Deus vobis mandarit, &c. Qualescunque tamen sint, dimittunt eos, maximè propter populū, quòd tanta esset miraculi perspicuitas, ut omnes Deum glorificarent, &c.
units.tr: I. The apostles are dismissed with threats added. Now boldness grows. They cannot answer the case put to them, yet they threaten. What else was this than if they had said: "What is it to us what God has commanded you," etc.? Whatever they were, they dismissed the apostles, chiefly because of the people, since the miracle was so manifest that all glorified God, etc.

units.la: In quibus Not. §1. Impios veritatem implacabiliter odisse, nec admittere ratio nes. Imò ferè indignos putat Christi fer- uos, quibus respondeatur. Pergunt ergo conuiuiti licet. Sic cum Achabo factum, 1.Reg 18,19.20.22. Hodie idem multi faciunt non solum in religione, verumetiam quoad mores, quando ea tuentur, quae Ethnici improbarunt. Ne ergo securitati nos dedamus. Retinet ingenium suum mundus Ioh.3,14. Et ideo licet Veritas vincat, tamen
units.tr: Note here, first: the wicked hate the truth implacably and do not admit reasons. They think the servants of Christ are almost unworthy of being answered. So they go on, though they are reviled. Thus it happened with Ahab (1 Kings 18, 19, 20, 22). Today many do the same, not only in religion but also in morals, when they defend what even the heathen have condemned. Let us not, therefore, give ourselves over to complacency. The world keeps its nature (John 3:14). And so, although truth conquers,

units.la: mea men non nisi sub crucis vexillo triumphat. Vide Ioh.16.
units.tr: yet it triumphs only under the banner of the cross. See John 16.

units.la: {2}Dei potentia admirabilis, qua hostes frænat, vt inuiti faciant quod nolunt. Tales isti fuerunt, vt videri potuerint metuminem timere. Sed ecce populu timent, cuius clamoribus ante Christum oppresserant, Iob 18. Vt enim mare Deus arena coercet,Ioh 38.ita tyrannos plerunq; medijs ridiculis terret, ne quid possint contra viles & imbelles. Sic olim patriarchas contra Chanan.Psal.105. Gen.34.35. Dauid dem per Philist.1. Sam.25. Denique non semper licet tyrannis quod libet. Tueamur ergo intrepidi stationem nostram, nec dubitemus de Dei prouidentia & cura,2.Tim.2.Ioh.10.Matth.10.Tuetur suos Deus in Ægyp. & Babyl. quoad illi possunt seruire. Vbi cursum absoluimus, ad se vocat,& ne in corpus quidem plus possunt impij,quàm Deus permittit.
units.tr: {2} The power of God is wonderful, by which he restrains enemies so that, though unwilling, they do what they do not want to do. Such were these men, so that they might seem to fear no one; yet look, they fear the people, whose shouting had overwhelmed Christ before (Job 18). For as God restrains the sea with sand (Job 38), so he often terrifies tyrants with trivial things, so that they can do nothing against the weak and unarmed. So once against the patriarchs in Canaan (Ps. 105; Gen. 34, 35); so David among the Philistines (1 Sam. 25). In short, tyrants are not always allowed to do whatever they please. Let us therefore keep our post fearlessly, and let us not doubt God's providence and care (2 Tim. 2; John 10; Matt. 10). God protects his people in Egypt and Babylon, as far as they can serve him. When we have finished our course, he calls us to himself, and the wicked cannot do more to the body than God permits.

units.la: {3}Tyrannorum fortem infelice.Multos timent,qui a multis timentur. Idem ille-fors. Iis accidit quod belluis,quibus multi retia tendunt. Norunt hoc,& ideo fere eos timent, quib.ipsi terrori esse debebat.Hinc exquisitæ illæ custodiæ, & quod peregrinis ferè sese custodiendos traduntDionyf. Mafiniffa. Similia fiunt hodie
units.tr: {3} The unhappy lot of tyrants. They fear many, by whom they are themselves feared. Perhaps the same thing happens to them as to wild beasts, for which many lay nets. They know this, and so they fear almost those by whom they ought to be terrified. Hence those elaborate guards, and the fact that they hand themselves over to foreigners for protection: Dionysius, Masinissa. Similar things happen today.

units.la: Tyrannorum
units.tr: Of tyrants.

units.la: Solentur ista pios. Simul autem magistratus officij admoneant, ne suam dignitatem in effreni potestate putent consiste-re.Hæc enim inuisos facit, & periculis objcit. Meminerint ergo se Dei & populi seruos esse,Rom.13. Pfal.72.Isa.49.Pfal.2. &c. Si officium faciant, etsi habeant infi-diatores,proteguntur tamen à Deo.Vide Dauidem,Iosaphatum, Ezechiam.
units.tr: These things console the godly. At the same time, they should remind magistrates of their office, that they should not think their dignity rests on unbridled power. For this makes them hated and exposes them to dangers. Let them therefore remember that they are servants of God and of the people (Rom. 13; Ps. 72; Isa. 49; Ps. 2, etc.). If they do their duty, even though they have plotters against them, they are nonetheless protected by God. See David, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah.

units.la: II. Quid Apostoli? Renuntiant omnia Ecclesiæ,cum vt omnes excitarent ad prae-ces,tum vt singuli armarentur fidei constantia,& sibi ab insidijs cauerent.
units.tr: II. What did the apostles do? They reported everything to the Church, both to rouse everyone to prayer and so that each might be armed with steadfastness of faith and guard himself against snares.

units.la: Not. §1. Apostolos non sibi dominium vendicasse in Ecclesiam. Singulos iudicarunt dignos, quibus omnia communicarentur.Sic infra 15. Ita Petrus monet, 1.Pet.5. Arguuntur, qui pro suo arbitrio agunt, ab aliis exigunt simpliciter obedientiam. Imo conseruos suos præfe contemnunt. Sunt hi ex eorum numero, de quibus Act.20.Matth.24.
units.tr: Note here, first: the apostles did not claim lordship over the Church. They judged that individuals were worthy to have everything shared with them. So below, chapter 15. Peter likewise admonishes (1 Pet. 5). Those are condemned who act at their own pleasure and demand simple obedience from others; indeed they despise their fellow servants. They belong to the number of those of whom Acts 20 and Matt. 24 speak.

units.la: §2. Licere ministris, vt Ecclesijs indi-cent hostium conatus. Multis hodie hoc superuacaneum videtur, vel etiam sedi-tiosum: vt cum Bullæ pontificum, & Acta Concilij recitantur.At horum iudicio A-poftoli seditiosi fuissent. Atqui speculatores sunt,Ezech.3.33.Debent ergo inten-ti esse ti esse in omnem euentum, Act 20. Imprimis lupos arguere debent: insidias detegere, &c. Ioh. 10. Id vero singuli patienter ferre debent, & admonitionibus locum dare, vt fortes maneant in fide agnita, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: Second: it is lawful for ministers to tell the Churches of the attempts of enemies. Today this seems superfluous to many, or even seditious, as when the papal bulls and the acts of councils are read out. Yet by their judgment the apostles would have been seditious. But they are watchmen (Ezek. 3:33), and so they ought to be alert for every outcome (Acts 20). Above all they ought to expose the wolves and uncover snares, etc. (John 10). Individuals, however, ought to bear this patiently and give room to admonitions, so that they may remain steadfast in the faith they have acknowledged, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXIII.

units.la: 24 Illi vero cum haec audiffent, concorditer sustulerunt vocem ad Deum, dixeruntq;, Domine, tu es Deus ille qui fecisti coelum & terram, mare & omnia quae in eis sunt.
units.tr: 24 When they heard this, they lifted up their voices together to God and said, Lord, you are the God who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them.

units.la: 25 Qui per os Dauid pueri tui dixisti: Cur fremuerunt gentes, et populi meditati sunt inania? &c. vsq; ad haec verba, verjus 31. Et locuti sunt, &c.
units.tr: 25 You who said by the mouth of David your servant: Why did the nations rage, and the peoples devise vain things? etc., down to verse 31, And they spoke, etc.

units.la: EXposuit hucusque Lucas, quid Apostoli fecerint, qui primi propter Christum capti fuerunt: & illis tria tribuit.1. Quòd Christu liberè confessi sint. 2. Quòd negarint se obsequi posse, quando prohibiti sunt praedicare. 3. Quòd dimissi nó faciunt, sed ad suos reuersi Ecclesiae omnia indicarint, nimirum vt omnes sibi cauerent. Ita faciant ministri in persecutionibus. Alijs sint exemplo fidei confessione. Non cedant impiis edictis. Admoneant omnes publicè, ne qui ipsorum ignauia pereant.Ioh.10 ¶ Sequitur quid Ecclesia fecerit,vbi discimus,quid singuli priuatim & publicè faciant in eiusmodi casu.
units.tr: Luke has now set out what the apostles did, who were the first to be seized for Christ's sake, and he ascribes three things to them: (1) that they confessed Christ freely; (2) that when they were forbidden to preach, they said they could not obey; (3) that, once released, they did not act on their own but returned to their own people and reported everything to the Church, namely so that all might take care for themselves. So ministers should act in persecutions. They should be an example to others of confessing the faith. They should not yield to impious edicts. They should publicly warn everyone, lest any perish through their own sloth, John 10. Next comes what the Church did, where we learn what individuals do, both privately and publicly, in such a case.

units.la: Summa,quod vnanimiter Deum precati sunt. Ergo non contemserunt periculum,neque ad humana praesidia,sed ad Deum confugerunt.Est hoc tutissimum asylum,de quo promissiones sunt. Psal.50 If. 65.Matth.18. Ioh.16. Exempla, Exod.14. 17.Item Ioel.2.If.37.Hodie peccatur,quod pericula,dum absunt longius, contemnimus:his autem vrgentibus,ad carnis praesidia fugimus.
units.tr: The sum is that they prayed to God with one accord. Therefore they did not despise the danger, nor flee to human aids, but took refuge in God. This is the safest refuge, and promises have been made concerning it: Ps. 50; Isa. 65; Matt. 18; John 16. Examples: Exod. 14, 17; likewise Joel 2; Isa. 37. Today we sin in that we despise dangers while they are still far off, but when they press upon us, we flee to the aids of the flesh.

units.la: Interim hic veram precandi rationem NOTA ¶ 1. Deum innocant, & quidem solum,non Mosem, &c. Sic iubemur,Gen. 17.Exod 20.Psal.50.Matth.6 Solus etiam nouit omnia, 1.Reg.8. Obseruârunt hoc omnes sancti.Nouum est, quod alii inuocantur ¶ 2.Voce sublata. Atqui Deus gemitus audit,Psal.12 56.Sed facit hoc adfidei confessionem,vt testentur, se non pudere adhuc Dei.Ita Daniel cap.6.Deinde sic alij alios excitent. ¶ 3. Vnanimiter. Eo imprimis opus:quia Christus nos vnum esse vult,Iohan.17.Eph.4.Imprimis in precibus.Matth.5. At hic opus,vt publicae calamitates omnibus cordi sint,Heb.13.Sed videamus partes huius precationis.
units.tr: Meanwhile, here note the true manner of praying. 1. They call upon God, and God alone, not Moses, etc. So we are commanded: Gen. 17; Exod. 20; Ps. 50; Matt. 6. He alone also knows all things, 1 Kings 8. All the saints observed this. It is a novelty that others are invoked. 2. With raised voice. Yet God hears groans, Ps. 12, 56. But they do this as a confession of faith, so that they may testify that they are not still ashamed of God, as Daniel did, ch. 6. Then they stir up one another in this way. 3. Unanimously. This is especially needful, because Christ wills us to be one, John 17; Eph. 4, and especially in prayers, Matt. 5. And it is a work here that public calamities should be dear to all, Heb. 13. But let us look at the parts of this prayer.

units.la: I. Deum describunt, vt testentur, fe verum illum inuocare, qui omnium Creator sit. Ita vero respiciunt eius omnipotentiam & prouidentiam, Psal 113.115 Hinc con solaiio nascebatur, quae omnes hostiu ter rores disciebat, simul fidem confirmabat, si quid grauius accideret. Debet hic etiam nobis esse vsus omnipotentiae & prouidentiae Dei. Si volet, poterit iuuare. Si non vult, tamen videt nos, & nouit ipse quid futurum, 1 Cor.10.
units.tr: I. They describe God so as to testify that they invoke the true God, who is the Creator of all. In this way they look to his omnipotence and providence, Ps. 113, 115. From this there arose a consolation which drives out all the terrors of enemies and at the same time confirms faith, should anything more grievous befall. The use of God's omnipotence and providence should be ours here too. If he wills, he can help; if he does not will it, still he sees us, and knows himself what will come, 1 Cor. 10.

units.la: II. Narrationem contexunt, non quod Deum ignorare putent aliquid, sed vt ipsos leuent, & Dei bonitatem considerent, qui etsi omnia nôrit, nos tamen patientissime audit. Occasionem petunt ex Psal. quasi dicant: Reipsa experimur, quod olim praedictum, &c.
units.tr: II. They weave in the narrative, not because they think God ignores something, but so as to relieve themselves and to consider God's goodness, who, though he knows all things, nevertheless hears us most patiently. They take the occasion from the Psalm, as if they said: In fact we are experiencing what was foretold long ago, etc.

units.la: Ita nos quoque in periculis recurramus ad vetera vaticinia, & minus offendemur. Atqui constat, perpetuas fore inimicitias inter diabolum & Christum, Gen 3. huius membra & mundu. Ioh 15 16. 2. Tim.
units.tr: So we too in dangers should have recourse to the old prophecies, and we will be less offended. Indeed it is certain that there will be perpetual enmity between the devil and Christ, Gen. 3; between his members and the world, John 15, 16; 2 Tim.

units.la: 3 Quid ergo offendimur, quando hodie gentes fremunt, vulgus inania loquitur, Reges conuenerunt, consulant?
units.tr: 3 Why then are we offended when today the nations rage, the crowd speaks vain things, and kings gather and take counsel?

units.la: Soletur potius, quod ista non tam contra nos fiunt, quam contra Deum & vt ista eius. Non enim nostra hęc causa est, sed Christi,quem pater Regem constituit Ps.2.Matt.28.Nihil ergo proficient,quàm quod Deus confestum vult, & dum suas resagunt,Dei consilia promouent.Appa-ret hoc in sacerdotibus, &c. Voluerunt impedire, ne Christus regnum acciperet, Matth 21. Ideo excitant Pilat.milites,vul-gus,occidunt, &c. Sed quid faciunt aliud quàm quod Christus hac ratione fit Ser-uator hominum,& omnes trahit ad se.Io-han.12. Eadem ratio omnium persecutio- num.Vide infra Cap.8.9. Et hodie idem cernimus.Nec ideo excusantur impij. In-terim applicemus hoc nobis in omni ad-uersitate,Iob.1.
units.tr: Rather let us be consoled that these things are done not so much against us as against God and against his anointed. For this is not our cause but Christ's, whom the Father has set up as King, Ps. 2; Matt. 28. Therefore they will accomplish nothing except what God has decided shall be done, and while they carry out their own schemes, they advance God's counsels. This appears in the priests, etc. They wanted to prevent Christ from receiving the kingdom, Matt. 21. So they stir up Pilate, the soldiers and the crowd, and they kill, etc. But what else do they do than what Christ, by this means, becomes the Saviour of men and draws all to himself, John 12? The same reasoning covers all persecutions; see below, chs. 8 and 9. And today we see the same thing. Nor for that reason are the impious excused. Meanwhile let us apply this to ourselves in every adversity, Job 1.

units.la: III. Quid petunt? 1.Inspice in mimas eo-rum,id est,tu vindica. Merito hoc petunt, cùm illius causa esset.Ita solent pij, quan-do ipsis non licet vindicare iniurias, Ps.7. 17.26.Et licet hoc,quando Dei gloria pe-riclitatur. Sic Ezechias, Isa. 37. Nec dubi-um quin exaudiantur. Vide ergo quàm periculosum sit tales affligere? Exod.22. ¶.2.Ne ipsi videantur otiari velle addunt: Da servus tuus,vt cum fidutia verbum tuum loquantur.Necessaria petitio pro ministris qui alioqui facilè terrentur. Agnouit hoc in seipso Paul.Eph.6.Idem singuli sibi ip-sis petant,Lu.17.Imprimis qui magistratū gegerunt.Pf.72. ¶.3.Miracula augeri petunt. quæ doctrinę signilla erant,Mar.16.Ioh.14. Christi verò mentionem faciunt,vt de hu ius gloria se solicitos esse testentur, &c. Obseruandus autem zelus Ecclesiæ. Scie bant Apostolorum prædicatione exacer-baros esse Pontifices.Petunt tamen vt illi adhuc liberius loquantur.
units.tr: III. What do they ask? 1. Look upon their threats, that is, avenge yourself. They rightly ask this, since the cause was his. So the godly are accustomed to do when it is not permitted them to avenge injuries, Ps. 7, 17, 26. And it is permitted when God's glory is in danger, as Hezekiah did, Isa. 37. Nor is there doubt that they are heard. See, then, how dangerous it is to afflict such people, Exod. 22. 2. Lest they seem to want to be idle, they add: Grant to your servants that they may speak your word with confidence. This petition is necessary for ministers, who otherwise are easily terrified; Paul acknowledged this in himself, Eph. 6. Let individuals likewise ask this for themselves, Luke 17; especially those who have held magistracy, Ps. 72. 3. They ask that miracles be increased, which were signs of the doctrine, Mark 16; John 14. But they make mention of Christ so as to testify that they are anxious about his glory, etc. The zeal of the Church is to be noted. They knew that the high priests had been exasperated by the preaching of the apostles, yet they ask that the apostles may still speak more freely.

units.la: Procul ergo abfuerunt à nostri seculi Christianis,qui furori cedendum putant, & ministris irascuntur, fi quem monachu de illis quiritante audiunt.Sed aliter non possunt, qui otiu & mundi pace quærunt, Ioh.5. Tu cogita quod habeturIoh.14.15.
units.tr: So far, then, were they from the Christians of our age, who think one must yield to fury and are angry at ministers if they hear someone complaining of those men. But those who seek peace and quiet with the world cannot do otherwise, John 5. Consider what is to be had, John 14, 15.

units.la: II. Precum effectus.Terræmotus fit.Si-gnum,Deum exaudiuisse, qui simul suam lium exau potentiam declarat.Replentur spiritu san diuntur. ćto,qui nouos animos fecit, vt omnes fer uerent magis quàm antea, vt sequetur.
units.tr: II. The effect of the prayers. An earthquake happens, a sign that God has heard, who at the same time declares his power. They are filled with the Holy Spirit, who made new spirits, so that all were more fervent than before, as follows.

units.la: ¶ Piorum preces non negliguntur à Deo, Psal.34.Imitemur nos primitiuæ Ecclesiæ exemplum. Consultatur vbique contra Christum, & truculenta sunt multorum consilia.Et quid conetur mundus,horren dis exemplis didicimus.Excitent ista om-nes,& vigilent, In primis autem pro mini stris & magistratibus pijs, vt hos Deus confirmet,& suo spiritu regat,hostium au tem consilia disipet,Oremus.
units.tr: The prayers of the godly are not neglected by God, Ps. 34. Let us imitate the example of the primitive Church. Counsel is taken everywhere against Christ, and the plans of many are savage; and what the world attempts we have learned from dreadful examples. Let all be stirred up by these things and keep watch. Especially, however, let them pray for godly ministers and magistrates, that God may strengthen them and rule them by his Spirit, and scatter the counsels of the enemies. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXIV.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXXIV.

units.la: 31 — & loquebantur sermonem Dei cum fiducia.
units.tr: 31 — and they spoke the word of God with boldness.

units.la: 32 Multitudinis autem eorum qui crediderant, erat cor & anima vna: nec quisquam aliquid eorum quae habebat, suum esse dicebat, sed erant eis omnia communia, &c. ad finem Cap.
units.tr: 32 Now the multitude of those who had believed had one heart and one soul; nor did anyone say that any of the things he possessed was his own, but all things were common to them, etc. to the end of the chapter.

units.la: VT primam persecutionem Lucas describit, ita quid tunc pij fecerint, docet. Finis omnium est, vt discamus, quid nobis in simili casu fit agendum. Primo vnanimiter orárunt. Conuertamur ergo nos quoq; ad Deum, non ad carnis praelidia. Petamus autem quae ad gloriam Christi faciunt, non otium priuatum. Sequuntur reliqua, quae docent, illos nihil interm misisse eorum, quae ipsos decebant.
units.tr: As Luke describes the first persecution, so he also teaches what the godly then did. The aim of all this is that we learn what we ought to do in a similar case. First, they prayed with one accord. Let us therefore also turn to God, not to the defences of the flesh. Let us seek what serves the glory of Christ, not private leisure. What follows teaches that they neglected nothing of those things which befitted them.

units.la: I. Loquebantur verba cum fiducia. Id vero de Apostolis, &c. dicitur. Item reddebant testimonium resurrectioni, &c. Fecerunt ergo quod erant, protestati. Nec illos mouit, quod hoc articulo hostes maximè offendebantur: vt qui & illos omnes scelelis conuincebat, & Sadducaeis erat intolerabilis, Matt. 22. Act. 23.
units.tr: I. They spoke the word with boldness. This is said of the apostles, etc. Likewise they bore witness to the resurrection, etc. They therefore did what they were, that is, they testified. Nor was it this article that moved them, though on this point the enemies were most offended: for it convicted them all of wickedness, and was intolerable to the Sadducees. Matt. 22; Acts 23.

units.la: Nota. ¶ In persecutionibus videant ministri, ne propter minas, & pericula sileant
units.tr: Note. ¶ In persecutions let ministers see to it that they do not keep silent because of threats and dangers.

units.la: Apostoli Euangelium constanter tradiderunt. sileant. Tunc enim doctrina & consolatio ne in primis opus est. Et in primis vrgeri debent articuli, quos aduerfar'j maxim é oppugnant. Requirit hoc ministerij fini<, qui est ædificatio Ecclesiæ, Eph.4 1.Cor. 14. Simile rei militaris. Nec audiendi qui prefcribunt,vt olim Ifa.30.Amos 2.2.Tim. 4. Verbi enim ministri lumus, non magi-ftri aut iudices 2.Cor.10.
units.tr: The apostles delivered the Gospel constantly; let them not be silent. For then teaching and consolation are especially needed. And above all the articles which the adversaries attack most strongly ought to be pressed. The purpose of the ministry requires this, which is the building up of the Church: Eph. 4; 1 Cor. 14. It is like military affairs. Nor should those be heard who prescribe, as once in Isaiah 30 and Amos 2; 2 Tim. 4. For we are ministers of the Word, not masters or judges: 2 Cor. 10.

units.la: II. Multitudinis fuit cor vnum, &c.
units.tr: II. The multitude had one heart, etc.

units.la: Id est, vna eademque voluntas, vnum studium, nimirum vt regnum Christi propaga-rent & communem salutem. Qui ad hunc finem tendunt, ij foli consentire possunt, quia non dant locum priuatis affectibus, qui amicitias turbant. Fuit hoc singulare opus Spiritus sancti inter tam multos, Psal.133.
units.tr: That is, one and the same will, one zeal, namely that they might propagate the kingdom of Christ and the common salvation. Only those who aim at this end can agree, because they give no place to private affections, which disturb friendships. This was a singular work of the Holy Spirit among so many: Psal. 133.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Hanc esse propriam notam fi delium, Eph.4. Ioh 13. 17. Exerit autem se in primis, quando pericula instant. Simile parentum & fratrum. Vide quid iudices de nostri seculi Christianis. Audiuntur falsa nomina. Zuing Luther. Si quid periculi oritur, tunc exprobrant, calumniantur, &c. Carnales ergo sunt, 1.Cor.3. Et aliquando consumentur, Gal 5 &c.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ This is the proper mark of the faithful: Eph. 4; John 13:17. It shows itself especially when dangers press. It is like that of parents and brothers. Look at what judges of the Christians of our age: false names are heard: Zwingli, Luther. If any danger arises, then they upbraid, slander, etc. They are therefore carnal, 1 Cor. 3; and sometimes they are consumed, Gal. 5, etc.

units.la: III. Vnanimitatem reipsa testati sunt, ne inanis profesio putareture, beneficia
units.tr: III. They attested the unity in deed, lest a empty profession be thought to be enough, namely by benefits

units.la: nimirum & pauperum fubuentione. Lo<cus dignissimus confideratu, cum propter Anabaptist.tum propter Pseudoeuangeli cos.¶ 1.Summa proponitur: Nemo quicquam dicebat suum esse,&c. Vbi non negatur proprietas,sed animi affectus exprimitur, quod nimirum voluntate omnia habuerint communia. Et hic beneficentiæ fons est: Vt nimirum diuites se bonorû, quæ à Deo acceperunt,dispensatores esse meminerint,Luc.16.Ita fit,vt illis cor non apponant(Ps.62)& cum se non tam multis opus habere videant (1.Tim.6.)in ego nos sint benefici,2.Cor.8. Et hæc vera est communio,quæ nemini suum eripit, & ta men omnia largitur.
units.tr: and by the relief of the poor. This passage is most worthy of consideration, both because of the Anabaptists and because of the pseudo-evangelists. ¶ 1. The sum is set forth: no one said that anything was his own, etc. Where ownership is not denied, but the disposition of the heart is expressed, namely that by their will they held all things in common. And here is the source of beneficence: that the rich, namely, may remember that they are stewards of the goods which they have received from God, Luke 16. Thus it comes about that they do not set their heart upon them (Ps. 62), and when they see that they do not have need of so many things (1 Tim. 6), they may be beneficent to others, 2 Cor. 8. And this is true communion, which takes from no one what is his, and yet bestows all things.

units.la: ¶ 2. Modum indicat. 1.Vendiderunt domos & prædia. Id vero neq; omnes fecerunt, neque lex fuit quæ prohiberet sua retinere. Sunt enim exempla eorum,qui sua feruarunt sibi, Acto.12.Et hoc licuisse, Petrus testabitur,Act.5. Fecit ergo quisq; pro suo arbitrio, & quantum necessitas communis postulabat,&c.Pecuniam depo nebant apud Apostolos.Non ergo in publicum exponebant. 3.Distribuebatur cuiuis, &c.Nulla ergo fuit confusio, nulla alieni vsurpatio.Itaq; finis fuit,vt inopes alerentur:nec dabatur illis,qui seipsos alere poterant, ierant, Ephef.4.2. Theffal.5.1. Timoth.5.
units.tr: ¶ 2. He indicates the manner. 1. They sold houses and lands. Yet neither did all do this, nor was there any law forbidding them to keep their own. For there are examples of those who kept their own for themselves, Acts 12. And that this was lawful, Peter will testify, Acts 5. Each therefore acted according to his own judgment, and as much as common necessity demanded, etc. They deposited the money with the apostles. Therefore they did not put it out for public use. 3. It was distributed to each, etc. Therefore there was no confusion, no appropriation of what belonged to another. And so the aim was that the needy be supported, and it was not given to those who could support themselves: Eph. 4; 2 Thess. 3; 1 Tim. 5.

units.la: ¶ 3. Fructus huius instituti duplex. 1. Non fuit inter eos egens vel mendicus. Implerunt ergo legem, Deut.15. Et hoc illud est; quod impossibile videtur hodie. Sed confutantur hoc exemplo. Isti sub cruce hoc potuerunt, Heb.10. Nos otiamur. Isti ex suis: Nos habemus donationes veteres. Hodie non possumus, quia charitas friget (Matt.24.) & fere opes Ecclesiae rapiunt, qui non egent, aut sua concoxerunt. Et hi deinde Iudam imitantur, Ioh. 12. II. Magna erat gratia super ipsos, id est, gratiosi erant & nondum credentibus. Tanta vis est beneficentiae. Vide quid factum sub Maximino tempore pestis & famis. Eusebius lib.9.cap.7. & 8. Quid ergo mirum hodie, si cum nostro Euangelio exosi fimus?
units.tr: ¶ 3. The fruit of this institution is twofold. 1. There was among them no one in need or a beggar. They therefore fulfilled the law, Deut. 15. And this is that which seems impossible today. But they are put to shame by this example. Those under the cross could do this, Heb. 10; we are at ease. They did it from their own goods; we have old endowments. Today we cannot, because charity has grown cold (Matt. 24), and those who are not in need, or who have digested their own, snatch away almost the wealth of the Church. And these then imitate Judas, John 12. II. There was great grace upon them all, that is, they were gracious and pleasing even to those not yet believing. Such is the power of beneficence. See what was done under Maximinus in the time of plague and famine: Eusebius, book 9, chapters 7 and 8. What wonder then today, if we are hated on account of our Gospel?

units.la: Subijcitur exemplum singulare Iofis, & ita docet Spiritus sanctus, laudem merari eos, qui singulari edunt virtutis specimen. Duo autem dicuntur, quae celebriorem reddunt. 1. Quod Leuita, & tamen conuersus. 2. Quod Cyprius, alienigena. Non habuit ergo personarum respectum. ¶ Praemium recipit, quando memoria eius consecratur (Pfal. 112.) & nomen accipit nobilissimum, & ita remunerat
units.tr: A singular example is set before us in Joses, and the Holy Spirit thus teaches that those who give a singular display of virtue deserve praise. Two things are mentioned that make him more famous: (1) that he was a Levite, and yet converted; (2) that he was a Cypriot, a foreigner. He therefore showed no respect of persons. He receives a reward when his memory is consecrated (Ps. 112), he receives a most noble name, and in this way Christ rewards his own (Matt. 25).

units.la: suos Christus,Matt 25. Vide quid iudices de ijs,qui rapiunt,contristant.
units.tr: Consider what you should judge of those who plunder and distress others.

units.la: Ita hodie imitemur. Sunt tempora dif-ficillima,qualia prædicta Matt.24. Hic er-go fortes sint ministri,nec timeant lupos, Ioh.10.luuet hos Ecclesia precibus & ftu-dio,Gal.4.Eph.6. Studeant omnes vnani-mitati,Ioh.15.Rom. 12. Testentur hanc beneficentiâ in omnes, maximè erga do-mesticos fidei, Gal. 6. Ita non deerit Dei gratia,qui aduersus quosuis tuebitur Mat-thæi 28.Oremus.
units.tr: Let us therefore imitate them today. These are most difficult times, such as were foretold in Matt. 24. Let the ministers, then, be brave and not fear the wolves (John 10). Let the Church help them with prayers and zeal (Gal. 4; Eph. 6). Let all strive for unity (John 15; Rom. 12). Let them bear witness to this by beneficence toward all, and especially toward the household of faith (Gal. 6). Thus the grace of God will not be lacking, for he will defend us against whatever enemies (Matt. 28). Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT V. HOMILIA XXXV.
units.tr: CHAPTER V. HOMILY XXXV.

units.la: Vlr autem quidam nomine Ana-nias, cum Sapphira vxore sua, vendidit possessionem.
units.tr: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession.

units.la: 2 Et interuertit aliquid ex pretio, conscia etiam vxore sua: allatamq; partem aliquam, ad pedes Apostolorum de posuit,&c.ad verf.7.
units.tr: And he kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part and laid it at the feet of the apostles, etc., to verse 7.

units.la: EXposuit Lucas,quæ Ecclesiæ pri-mitiuæ studia fuerint, quando persecutio fuit exorta : vt inde discamus quid nobis faciendum Apostoli intrepide prædicârunt.2.Reli-qui verbo crediderunt & obedierunt. Te statur hoc,quod vnanimes fuerunt,quod quc egenis tam liberaliter prospexerunt. Produxit illic Iosis aut Barnabæ exem- plum. Huic opponit Ananiam auarum & impostorem,qui horribiliter perijt. ¶ V- sus,vt discamus,quid fit fallere sub Dei & Ecclesiæ prætextu. Item ne offendamur, si quid huius hodie etiam fiat. Idem fa- stum Christo adhuc in terris agente,Ioh. 6.12.13. Et semper idem futurum doce- mur,Matth.13. Vigilemus ergo contra ta- les,Phil.3.
units.tr: Luke has set out the zeal the early Church showed when persecution broke out, so that we may learn from it what we ought to do. The apostles preached fearlessly. (2) The rest believed the word and obeyed. Note that they were of one heart, and that they cared so generously for the needy. Here he sets before us the example of Joses or Barnabas. Against this he sets Ananias, greedy and a deceiver, who perished dreadfully. Use: that we may learn what it is to deceive under the pretext of God and the Church; and that we may not be offended if anything of this kind happens even today. The same thing happened while Christ was still on earth, John 6:12-13. And we are taught that it will always be the same, Matt. 13. Let us therefore be watchful against such people, Phil. 3.

units.la: I. Factum Ananiæ narratur simplicisi mè Diligenter tamè examinandum: quia earnis iudicio laude dignus videbitur. Per se licet vendere & emere (1. Cor. 7.) imo absq; fraude. Ita retinere pretium to tum,vel partem tuis vsibus,1.Tim.5. Eph. 4. Nec vult nos depauperari Deus, alios iuuando,2.Cor.8.Et poculum aquæ frigi- dæ,&c.Matth 10.
units.tr: I. The deed of Ananias is told quite simply, but it must be examined carefully, since by human judgment it will seem worthy of praise. In itself it is lawful to sell and to buy (1 Cor. 7), indeed even without fraud. So too it is lawful to keep the whole price, or part of it, for one's own uses, 1 Tim. 5; Eph. 4. Nor does God want us to be impoverished by helping others, 2 Cor. 8. And a cup of cold water, etc., Matt. 10.

units.la: ¶ Animus ergo inspiciatur,& patebit in quo peccârit:hypocrisi nimirum,vel simu latione fidei & charitatis, qua Deo & ho- minibus voluit imponere.Ambitiosus vi- dit Barnaba & vult imitari,& eorū nume ro videri, qui omnia in publicū contule- rant. Interim auarus & diffidens causæ, vult sibi & vxori cōsulere,& interim viue re ex publico. Concurrunt ergo ambitio & auaritia.Accedit diffidentia, nec credit promissioni,Matth.28.6.Luc.12.22. Item Dei contemptus: quasi is nihil videat,Pf. 14.94. Et quod proprium est hypocritarum, putat sibi cum solis hominibus rem esse.Itaque sacrilegium committit in pro pria pecunia,& huius conuincitur.
units.tr: Therefore let the heart be examined, and it will be clear in what he sinned: namely in hypocrisy, or in the pretence of faith and love, by which he wished to deceive both God and men. Ambitious, he saw Barnabas and wants to imitate him, and to seem one of those who had brought everything into the common stock. Meanwhile the covetous man, distrustful of the cause, wants to provide for himself and his wife, and yet to live off the public fund. Ambition and avarice therefore meet. Distrust is added; he does not believe the promise, Matt. 28:6; Luke 12:22. Also contempt for God, as if he saw nothing, Ps. 14; 94. And what is characteristic of hypocrites, he thinks he has to do only with men. And so he commits sacrilege with his own money, and is convicted of it.

units.la: No T. ¶Typum pseudochristianorum. Si videant Christum regnum obtinuisse, de perpetuitate autem dubitant: consentiunt quidem Reformationi, sed cauent ne quid faciant,quod ipsis posit aliquando fraudi esse. Ita vero duobus dominis voluntseruire,&c.Matth.6. Tales hodie multi,qui sapientissimi videri volunt.Sed Ananiae sunt, nec rectum est cor eorum cum Deo. Peiores his, qui cum omnino nihil conferant,tamen ex Ecclesia voluntditescere.Hi fere ex raptoribus hostes fiunt,vt Iudas.Ioh.12.
units.tr: Note. A type of pseudo-Christians. If they see that Christ has obtained the kingdom, but doubt about its permanence, they indeed agree with the Reformation, but take care not to do anything that might one day be to their harm. Thus they wish to serve two masters, etc., Matt. 6. Many such today wish to seem very wise. But they are of the kind of Ananias, and their heart is not right with God. Worse than these are those who, though they contribute nothing at all, nevertheless want to hide within the Church. These mostly become enemies from being plunderers, like Judas, John 12.

units.la: II. Quia vero se multis excusant,audiamus Spiritus S. iudicium, quod per Petrum pronuntiat. Sentit is dolum, nimirum ex spiritus reuelatione. Sic 2. Reg.5. Et semper ratum erit quod dicitur Matt. 10.Nec dissimulat.Debent ergo argui quae cuunq; etiam occulte fiunt contra Eccle siam,&c. Quanto magis manifeste? 1.Tim. 5.2.Tim.4.
units.tr: II. Because they excuse themselves in many ways, let us hear the judgment of the Holy Spirit, which Peter pronounces. He perceives the deceit, namely by a revelation of the Spirit. So 2 Kings 5. And what is said in Matt. 10 will always hold good. Nor does he dissemble. Therefore whatever is done against the Church, even secretly, ought to be rebuked, etc. How much more when it is done openly? 1 Tim. 5; 2 Tim. 4.

units.la: ¶ 1. Fontem mali detegit: Cur impleuit Satan Satan, &c. Ostendit reprobum esse. Ten. tantur etiam sanctì (Luc.22.) sed quia re-sistunt,(1.Pet.5.)non potest diabolus cor totum occupare. Interim vides cuius feruì sint, qui in religione vtuntur dolo diaboli,qui ab initio mendax fuit, &c. Ioh. 8. Gen 3 Ita in Iudam intrauit, Luc.22.Ioh. 13.Nemo igitur talibus fidat.
units.tr: 1. He uncovers the source of the evil: Why has Satan filled your heart, etc.? He shows him to be reprobate. Even the saints are tempted (Luke 22), but because they resist (1 Pet. 5), the devil cannot occupy the whole heart. Meanwhile you see whose servants they are who use deceit in religion: the devil's deceit, who was a liar from the beginning, etc., John 8; Gen. 3. Thus he entered into Judas, Luke 22; John 13. Let no one therefore trust such people.

units.la: ¶ 2. Peccatum definit Vt mentirer is spiritus sancto. Bifariam potest accipi.Nam & ipse Spiritus sancti motum simulauit, & Ecclesiam voluit fallere, cui spiritus semper adest,Iohan.14.16.Impudens audacia. Obseruandum, quales censendi,qui,quod ipsi fatentur Ecclesiæ & pauperibus deberi,in alios vsus transferunt.Præterea mul ta,vt Iudas,Io.12.Sed Spiritui sancto men tiuntur,qui non potest falli,&c.Pfal.139.
units.tr: 2. He defines the sin: That you should lie to the Holy Spirit. It can be understood in two ways. For he both feigned the movement of the Holy Spirit itself, and wished to deceive the Church, in which the Spirit is always present, John 14:16. Shameless audacity. It is to be noted what sort of people are to be judged, who turn to other uses what they themselves confess is owed to the Church and the poor. Besides, many, like Judas, John 12. But they lie to the Holy Spirit, who cannot be deceived, etc., Ps. 139.

units.la: ¶ 3. Excusationem omnem eripit: Annon tibi manebat? &c,Ergo nemo cogeba tur.Quare ergo posuisti in cor,&c. Often dit tam indignum hoc scelus esse, vt ne in mentem quidem venire debuerit. Vult enim Deus animos sibi foli addictos esse, Deut.6. Exod.20. Denique Deo mentitus es. Obseruandum, hæc omnibus dicì, qui sub prætextu fidei & religionis fallut Tales sunt, qui in duas partes claudicant.
units.tr: 3. He takes away every excuse: Did it not remain yours? etc. Therefore no one was being compelled. Why then have you conceived this in your heart, etc.? He shows that this crime is so unworthy that it ought not even to have come into the mind. For God wants minds devoted to him alone, Deut. 6; Exod. 20. Finally, you have lied to God. It is to be noted that these words are said to all who deceive under the pretext of faith and religion. Such are those who limp in two directions.

units.la: L
units.tr: L.

units.la: 1.Reg.18.1.Cor.10.Ieroboamici magistratus, 1.Reg 12 13. Item qui sub Euangelio quærunt peccandi licentiam,Mat 7. Possunt isti omnes fallere homines, 1. Cor.2. Sed Deum non fallent, qui corda scruta-tur,Ier.17.Pf.7.Vide Apoc.21.
units.tr: 1 Kings 18; 1 Cor. 10; Jeroboam's magistrates, 1 Kings 12:13. Likewise those who under the Gospel seek a license to sin, Matt. 7. All these can deceive men, 1 Cor. 2. But they will not deceive God, who searches the hearts, Jer. 17; Ps. 7. See Rev. 21.

units.la: III. Deus confirmat sententiam Petri. Repentè enim cadit mortuus, &c. Vide quid ijs feré fiat, qui per fas & nefas dite-scunt,aut opibus suis luxuriantur.Hi feré omnes præter omnem exspeẗationé pe-reunt,Luc.12.16.
units.tr: III. God confirms Peter's sentence: for he suddenly fell down dead, etc. See what usually happens to those who grow rich by fair means or foul, or revel in their wealth. Almost all of these perish beyond all expectation, Luke 12:16.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Verbum Dei ratum & effi-cax esse, quàmuis per hominem pronun-tietur.Et verbum nô ab hominum autho-ritate pendet, sed per se subsistit, Ifa.40. Debet hoc ad promisiones & minas re-ferri.Vide Matt.16.Iohan.Mar.16.Appli-cent ergo hoc sibijpsis singuli,& cogitent, quid ipsorum peccatis Dei verbũ denun-ciet. Auari,Matth.6.Ephes.4.Ebriosi, Isa. 5.Hab.2.Scortatores & adulteri,Hebr.13. Idololatræ & alij,&c.Coloss.3. 1.ad Corin-thios 6.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The word of God is firm and effective, although it is pronounced through a man. And the word does not depend on human authority but subsists in itself, Isa. 40. This should be applied to the promises and threats. See Matt. 16; John; Mark 16. Let each apply this to himself and consider what God's word denounces against his own sins. The covetous, Matt. 6; Eph. 4. Drunkards, Isa. 5; Hab. 2. Fornicators and adulterers, Heb. 13. Idolaters and others, etc., Col. 3; 1 Cor. 6.

units.la: ¶ 2.Deum initiò Ecclesiam hac potesta-te armauisse,vt noxios mirabiliter possent punire,1.Cor.12.Sic Elymam excæcat Pe-trus,Actor.13.Et huc pertinet,quòd Sata-næ tradebantur aliqui ,1. ad Corinth. 5.
units.tr: 2. That God at the beginning armed the Church with this power, so that it could wonderfully punish the guilty, 1 Cor. 12. Thus Peter blinded Elymas, Acts 13. And to this pertains the fact that some were handed over to Satan, 1 Cor. 5.

units.la: 1.Timot.1.Quod hodie inepte trahitur ad excommunicationem.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 1, which today is foolishly drawn to excommunication.

units.la: Interim ius gladij hic asseritur,Rom.13. Imo officij admonentur magistratus,ne il lud negligant.Si enim per Apostolos potius hoc exequi voluit,quàm vt noxij abirent impunè, quanto magis magistratus debet malum excindere, cui hoc mandatum,Pfalm.71.Leuit.20.Deuter.17.19.&c. Præpostera misericordia est, parcere ijs, quos Deus punitos vult, Prouerb.17.24. Exempla,1.Sam.15.1.Reg.20.In summa disfcant singuli officium facere in sua vocatione,in primis autem in religione fugere hypocrisim,&c Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile the right of the sword is asserted here, Rom. 13. Indeed magistrates are reminded not to neglect it. For if God wished this to be carried out through the apostles rather than that the guilty should go unpunished, how much more should the magistrate cut out evil, to whom this command is given: Ps. 71; Lev. 20; Deut. 17, 19, etc. It is a perverse mercy to spare those whom God wants punished, Prov. 17:24. Examples: 1 Sam. 15; 1 Kings 20. In sum, let each learn to do his duty in his calling, and above all in religion to flee hypocrisy, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXVI.
units.tr: Homily XXXVI.

units.la: 7 Intercesit autem circiter tri um horarum interuallum, quum vxor quoq; ipsius, nesciens quid factum fuerat,ingressa est.
units.tr: 7 About three hours later, his wife, who knew nothing of what had happened, came in.

units.la: 8 Dixit autem ei Petrus: Die mihi, num tanti prædium vendidit? Ipsa vero dixit,Etiam,tanti.
units.tr: 8 Peter said to her, "Tell me, did you sell the land for so much?" And she said, "Yes, for so much."

units.la: 9 Petrus autem dixit ei: Quid est cur conuenerit inter vos,vt tentare tis spiritu domini? ecce pedes eorum, qui sepelierunt virum tuum, ad ostium um adsunt,& efferent te.
units.tr: 9 But Peter said to her, "Why have you agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out too."

units.la: 10. Illico vero cecidit ad pedes eius, & animam efflauit, ingressi autem iuuenes inuenerunt eam mortuam, & elatam sepelierunt iuxta virum suum.
units.tr: 10 At once she fell at his feet and breathed her last. When the young men came in, they found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.

units.la: VT Deus veritas est, & in veritate cu li vult, Ioh.4. Ita mendacio & hypo crisi in primis offenditur. Docent hoc prophetarum sermones, Isa 1.29. Psal 50. lere. 4. & 7. Christus item Matth. 23 24. Quia aliquem sciuit Christus tales semper fore, non fine scandalo voluit in ipso statim principio Ecclesiae exemplum addi, quo docet, quid illos maneat. Ananias Ecclesiae fe coniunxit, & in ea aliis praestare vult. Sed quia fide destituitur, & nihil quam priuatum commodum quaerit, seipsum fallit, &c. Ita fiet semper. Clarius tamen patebunt omnia, si alteram quoque partem vi deamus, quid scilicet actum cum Sapphira.
units.tr: As God is truth, and delights in truth (John 4), so he is offended above all by lying and hypocrisy. The sayings of the prophets teach this (Isa. 1; Ps. 50; Jer. 4 and 7), and so does Christ (Matt. 23, 24). Because Christ knew that such people would always exist, he wished that an example be given at the very beginning of the Church, not without a warning, showing what awaits them. Ananias joined himself to the Church and wanted to stand out among the others in it. But because he lacked faith and sought nothing but private advantage, he deceived himself, and so on. It will always be so. All of this will be clearer, however, if we also look at the other side, namely what happened with Sapphira.

units.la: I. Horis post tribus venit haec omnium ignara. Fere enim postremi rescimus, quae nos scire maxime oportebat. Causa, quod maleuoli traducere malunt, quam in faciem arguere. Alij nolunt nuntiare, quae ingrata sunt, Id hic quoque factum. Sed Nota. Quàm hoc sit noxium. Hoc Sapphiram perdidit. Si quis enim admonuisset, procul dubio non veniret tam confidenter, nec mentira esset. Sed quia rem adhuc occultam putat, pergit. Sunt exempla similia passim. Obserue-mus, nihil retinendum cum proximi per-ni{c} {s}item audiendos patienter eos, qui ad nos pertinentia narrant, Prou. 27.
units.tr: I. Three hours later she came, ignorant of everything. We usually learn last what we most need to know. The cause is that malicious people prefer to slander rather than to rebuke to a person's face, and others are unwilling to report what is unwelcome. That happened here too. Note how harmful this is. It destroyed Sapphira. For if someone had warned her, she would certainly not have come so boldly, and the lie would not have been told. But because she thought the matter still hidden, she went on. There are similar examples everywhere. Let us observe that nothing should be kept back when a neighbour's affairs are at stake, and that we should patiently hear those who report what concerns us (Prov. 27).

units.la: II. Petrus quaestionem instituit. Pote-rat vel ignara omnino, vel à viro coacta vi deri. Quaerit ergo. Sed cuius spiritu duce egerit, Not. Dei morem in puniendo. Sciebat rem omnem, & subito punire po-terat. Sed tempus dat, & arguit, si forte conuertatur. Nec enim tyrannum agit Deus, & vult nos scire, in quo peccaui-mus. Sic Gen. 3. Item in diluuio, Gene 6. 3. Pet. 2. Chananaei, Gen. 15 lof. 2. Experi-mur quotidie. Agnoscamus bonitatem Dei, nec abutamur, Rom. 2. Imitemur ipsi quo-que, in primis magistratus, Pfal. 72.
units.tr: II. Peter raises a question. She could have been entirely ignorant of the matter, or it could be thought that she was forced into it by her husband. So he asks. But note by what Spirit he was acting, and note God's manner of punishing. He knew the whole matter and could have punished her at once. Instead he gives time and argues with her, in case she might perhaps be converted. For God does not act as a tyrant, and he wills that we know what sin we have committed. So Gen. 3. Likewise in the flood, Gen. 6. 2 Pet. 2. The Canaanites, Gen. 15; Josh. 2. We experience this daily. Let us acknowledge God's goodness and not abuse it, Rom. 2. Let us also imitate it ourselves, especially magistrates, Psal. 72.

units.la: III. Sapphira confidenter mentitur, & quidem cum asseueratione. Atqui quae-stio insolita debebat terrere. Sed cum pu-dore timorem Dei excusserat. Vbi Not. Confidentiam hanc hypocritis propri-am est, Iuem enim vereantur, qui putant se posse Deum fallere? Alij icelerati mox
units.tr: III. Sapphira lies confidently, and indeed with asseveration. Yet an unusual question ought to have terrified her. But with shamelessness she had cast off the fear of God. Note that this confidence is peculiar to hypocrites. For whom would they fear, who think they can deceive God? Other wicked people soon

units.la: Petrus Sap-phira im-probitatem arguit.
units.tr: Peter argues against Sapphira's wickedness.

units.la: Sapphira confidenter mentitur.
units.tr: Sapphira lies confidently.

units.la: consternantur Deo audito. At hypocritæ etiam responsant. Cain,Gen.4. Ita hi, de quibus Ifa.58.Mal.3.Pharifæi, Mat.15.Ioh. 8.10.&c.Iudas,Matt.26.Sic Sapphira,que tot exemplis didicerat,Apostolos esse Spi ritu fanêto donatos. At pessimè cessit.Ca ueamus nobis ab hac confidentia,memo-res eius quod dicitur 1.Iohan.3.Itaq; con-uicti faciamus quod Dauid 2.Sam.12.Pfal. 51.Item Luc.18.
units.tr: are dismayed when God is heard. But hypocrites even answer back. Cain, Gen. 4. So do those of whom Isa. 58, Mal. 3; the Pharisees, Matt. 15; John 8, 10, etc.; Judas, Matt. 26. So Sapphira, who had learned from so many examples that the apostles were endowed with the Holy Spirit, did so. But it turned out very badly for her. Let us beware of this confidence, mindful of what is said in 1 John 3. Therefore, when convicted, let us do what David did, 2 Sam. 12; Psal. 51. Likewise Luke 18.

units.la: Sed audiamus Petrum, cuius oratio duabus partibus constat.
units.tr: But let us hear Peter, whose speech consists of two parts.

units.la: 1.Peccatum arguit:Quid hoc? Admira-tione amplificat scelus.Quod verò illud? Confpirâsse, vt tentetis Spiritum sanctum. Nihil grauius poterat dici.Et ipsi interro gati,haud dubiè negassent.Sed non refert vt nos iudicemus de peccatis, Pfa.36.De-um audire oportet. Etenim quia volue-runt Ecclesiam fallere, cui Spiritus per-petuo adest, (Ioh.14.16.) vtiq; Deum ten tarunt non minus quàm Israelitæ, Pfa.78. Num.11.Vide legem Deut.6.Et ne viri no mine fe excuset, consensum in primis vr-get.
units.tr: 1. He rebukes the sin. What is this? He magnifies the crime by his astonishment. And what is that? To have conspired to test the Holy Spirit. Nothing more serious could be said. Even if they had been questioned, they would undoubtedly have denied it. But it is not for us to judge sins as we please (Ps. 36); we must hear God. For because they wished to deceive the Church, to which the Spirit is always present (John 14:16), they certainly tested God no less than the Israelites did (Ps. 78; Num. 11). See the law in Deut. 6. And lest she excuse herself under her husband's name, the passage especially stresses consent.

units.la: Nos. ¶ Nemini nos consentire debe-rein illicitis, & ne ijs quidem, quibus est in nos auhoritas.Vir ius habet in vxorem Gen.2.1.Tim.2.Eph.5.Sed parêre debent, vt in Domino, Col. 3. Peccauit ergo Saph. quòd contra Dominū viro obtemperat. Itaq; quod in Deum peccatur, nullius homīnis authoritate potest excusari, Actor. 4.cap. Obseruent qui sceleratos laudibus vehunt, & patrocinantur, Rom. 1. Qui impedire nequeunt, saltem nō consentiant. Ioseph Arimath. Luc. 23.
units.tr: For us. We ought to consent to nothing unlawful, not even to those who have authority over us. A husband has authority over his wife (Gen. 2; 1 Tim. 2; Eph. 5), but wives ought to obey, as in the Lord (Col. 3). Sapphira therefore sinned in obeying her husband against the Lord. So whatever sin is committed against God cannot be excused by any human authority (Acts 4). Let those who extol the wicked and defend them take note (Rom. 1). Those who cannot prevent it should at least not consent (Joseph of Arimathea, Luke 23).

units.la: 2. Pœnam denuntiat, eandem qua vir punitus. Et mox secuta est eius executio, &c. Vbi NO T. ¶ Deum similia peccata si- milibus pœnis vlcisci. Ierem. 5. 25. Debet hoc extendi ad omnia scelera. Puniuit olim Deus intemperantiam, libidinem & fe curitatem temporibus Noah & Loth. Ge. 6. 7. 19. Ezech. 16. Idem fiet ergo etiam nō uisimis hisce temporibus, Matthæi 24. 1. Theff. 5. Sic oppressionem innocentium, sanguinis effusionem in Ægyptijs, Chananæis, Afsirijs, &c. Erit semper ratum quod habetur Isaiæ 33. Matth. 7. In primis discamus fugere hypocrisin, vt ne quid do lo malo agamus in religione & Ecclesia, Exultant tales interdum, vt Ananias quoque. Sed fit, quod dicitur Iob. 20, Gal. 6. Et sunt exempla pseudoeuangelicorum hodie, quibus illud cessit pessimè. Terrēant ergo nos. Vigilemus & Oremus.
units.tr: 2. He announces the punishment, the same as that which the husband suffered. And immediately its execution followed, and so on. Here NOTE: God punishes similar sins with similar penalties (Jer. 5:25). This ought to be extended to all crimes. God once punished intemperance, lust and security in the times of Noah and Lot (Gen. 6, 7, 19; Ezek. 16). The same will therefore happen also in these last times (Matt. 24; 1 Thess. 5). So too with the oppression of the innocent and the shedding of blood among the Egyptians, Canaanites, Assyrians, and so on. What is said in Isaiah 33 and Matt. 7 will always hold good. Above all let us learn to flee hypocrisy, lest we act deceitfully in religion and in the Church. Such people sometimes exult, as Ananias did too. But what is said in Job 20 and Gal. 6 comes to pass, and there are examples of pseudo-evangelicals today for whom that outcome turned out very badly. Let these things frighten us. Let us watch and pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXVII.

units.la: 11 Et obortus est timor magnus to ti Ecclesiæ, & omnibus qui hæc audiebant.
units.tr: 11 And great fear came upon the whole Church, and upon all who heard these things.

units.la: 12 Per manus autem Apostolorum fiebantur signa & miracula multa in populo: (& erant concorditer omnes in porticu Solomonis:
units.tr: 12 Now by the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people (and they were all with one accord in Solomon's porch;

units.la: 13 Reliquorum autem nemo audebat ipsis adhærere : sed magnificabat eos plebs.
units.tr: 13 But of the rest durst no man join himself to them, but the people magnified them.

units.la: 14 Magis autem accrescebat multitudo credentium Domino, virorum & mulierum:)
units.tr: 14 And believers in the Lord were the more added to them, both men and women.)

units.la: 15 Adeo ut in plateas efferrent ægrotos, & ponerent in lectis ac grabbatis ut venientis Petri vel umbra inumbraret aliquem eorum.
units.tr: 15 Insomuch that they brought the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, so that at least the shadow of Peter as he passed might fall on some of them.

units.la: 16 Conveniebat autem etiam multitudo vicinarum urbium in Hierusalem, adducens ægrotos & vexatos à spiritibus impuris qui sanabantur omnes.
units.tr: 16 There came also a multitude from the neighbouring cities to Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.

units.la: EXposuit Lucas horribile exemplum in Ananiam & vxorem æditum, eò quod fidem simulassent, & Ecclesiam fefellissent, quoad publicas pecunias, &c. Vi dimus Dei seueritate, qui vt falli non potest, ita grauiter punit eos, qui hoc tētant. Deinde primitiuæ Ecclesiæ disciplinam qua cauit, nec qui suis sceleribus fidem Christi infamem aut suspectam facerent. Sequitur præsens locus, qui primo huius exempli fructum: Deinde primitiuæ Ecclesiæ exercitia: Postremo incrementa narrat. Vbi discemus, quibus medijs religio prouehatur, & vera salus, &c.
units.tr: Luke sets out a dreadful example in Ananias and his wife, struck down because they had feigned faith and deceived the Church, namely concerning the public money, and so on. We see the severity of God, who cannot be deceived, and so punishes gravely those who attempt this. Next, he shows the discipline by which the primitive Church guarded itself against anyone who would make the faith of Christ infamous or suspect through their own crimes. The present passage follows: it first narrates the fruit of this example, then the exercises of the primitive Church, and lastly its growth. Here we learn by what means religion is advanced, and true salvation, and so on.

units.la: I. Fructus: Timent omnes tam Christiani quàm exteri. Illi quidem, ne quid doli committerent: hi verò, vt minus audeant contra Ecclesiam. Imò non ausi sunt se coniungere Ecclesiæ, qui sibi malè conscij erant. Interim ab omnibus magnifiebant propter gratiam Dei, quæ in illis relucebat. Notat i. Vsum iudiciorum Dei: vt nimirum ipsum timeamus, & emendemur. Docet hoc Deus ipse, Gen 18. Imò ideo literis mandata sunt. Psal. 78. Sibi ergo applicent singuli quæ fiunt. In eo peccatur hodie, vt prædictum. Mat. 24. Causa præcipua Ebrietas. Isa 5.
units.tr: I. The fruit: all fear, Christians and outsiders alike. The Christians feared lest they commit any deceit; the outsiders, so that they might dare less against the Church. Indeed, those who were conscious of their own wickedness did not dare to join the Church. Meanwhile, they were magnified by all because of the grace of God which shone forth in them. Note first the use of the judgements of God: that we may indeed fear Him and be amended. God Himself teaches this, Gen. 18. Indeed, for this reason they were committed to writing, Ps. 78. Let each therefore apply to himself what happens. Today people sin in the way foretold, Matt. 24. The chief cause is drunkenness, Isa. 5.

units.la: ¶ 2. Vnde Christianis accedat authoritas. Si nimirum respondeant suæ professioni, hypocritas & sceler-
units.tr: ¶ 2. Whence authority accrues to Christians: namely, if they correspond to their profession, restrain hypocrites and wicked men,

units.la: atos coerceant, & Deū & glorificent. Matth. 5. Tunc impletur illud 1. Sam. 2. Exempla sunt vetera vt sub Traiano Plin. testatus est de Christianorum innocentia: Eodem pertinet
units.tr: and glorify God. Matt. 5. Then that saying of 1 Sam. 2 is fulfilled. There are old examples, such as under Trajan, when Pliny bore witness to the innocence of the Christians. To the same point belongs

units.la: Quid ergo mirū, si hodie Euangelium & qui hoc profitentur contempti sint & exosi? Pleriq; sua quaerunt & Ananias aguntur. Alij vero vel vsuris & rapinis dediti sunt, vel morum licentia infames. Fit ergo quod Mal.1.
units.tr: What wonder, then, if today the Gospel and those who profess it are despised and hated? Most seek their own, and act like Ananias. Others are given over either to usury and plunder, or are infamous for licentiousness of manners. Hence what is said in Mal. 1 comes to pass.

units.la: II.Apostoli signa aedunt, & quide solito maiora, quoad vmbra Petri. Impletū quod Christus promisit Ioh.14. Et apparet audi tas fuisse preces Ecclesiae. Aětor.1. Est hic quoq; fructus disciplinae, quod preces audiuntur. Econtra Pf.50. Prou.28. Zach.1.
units.tr: II. The apostles do signs, and greater ones than usual, as with the shadow of Peter. What Christ promised in John 14 is fulfilled, and it is evident that the prayers of the Church were heard, Acts 1. Here too is a fruit of discipline: that prayers are heard. On the contrary, Ps. 50, Prov. 28, Zech. 1.

units.la: Not. ¶ Quod de vmbra Petri dicitur. Abutuntur quidam hoc loco ad superstitiones reliquiarum: Si vmbra sanauit, multo magis vestes, &c. Addunt de Petris sudarijs ex Act. 19. Sed errant in fine istorum signorum. Non enim ideo facta, vt de Petri vel Pauli virtute testarentur, sed vt effent fidei & praedicationis Euangelij sigilla Mar. 16. Ideo in Christi nomine ea fecerunt, non suo. Et constat, illos nihil potuisse virtute & pietate. Act.3. Phil.2.1.Ti.5. Multo minus ergo vestibus. Quid quod neque Christi vestes aliquid potuerunt, &c. Luc.6.&8. Obseruandus ergo verus finis miraculorum, qui est, vt Euang.confirment, & doceant qualis Christus sit, in cuius nomine facta sunt. Quod nimirum medicus dicus sit, qui languores nostros fanat, If.53. Mat.49. Qui lepra animæ emundet. 1 Ioh. 1. Oculos mentis illuminet, Ioh. 1.8 Mal.4. Diabolum vincat, Gen.3.1. Ioh.3. Ex morte eripiat, Ioh.5.11. Rom.14, Huc etiam referri debent quæ ad umbras Martyrum fiunt, ut olim Elisæi 2 Reg.13. Qui alio detor quent, ex veris falsa faciunt, Deut.13.2. Theff.2. Mat.24.
units.tr: Note: what is said of the shadow of Peter. Some abuse this passage for the superstitions of relics: if a shadow healed, how much more garments, and so on. They add the handkerchiefs of Peter from Acts 19. But they err about the purpose of those signs. They were not done so as to bear witness to the power of Peter or Paul, but to be seals of the faith and of the preaching of the Gospel, Mark 16. Therefore they did them in the name of Christ, not their own. And it is certain that they could do nothing by their own power or piety, Acts 3, Phil. 2, 1 Tim. 5. Much less, therefore, by garments. Indeed, not even the garments of Christ could accomplish anything, and so on, Luke 6 and 8. The true end of miracles must therefore be observed: that they confirm the Gospel and teach what Christ is, in whose name they were done. Namely, that He is the physician who heals our infirmities, Isa. 53, Matt. 4 [sic: 9], who cleanses the leprosy of the soul, 1 John 1, who enlightens the eyes of the mind, John 1, Mal. 4, who conquers the devil, Gen. 3, John 3, who snatches us from death, John 5, Rom. 14. To this also must be referred what is done at the shadows of the martyrs, as once at Elisha's, 2 Kings 13. Those who turn them to another purpose make false things out of true, Deut. 13, 2 Thess. 2, Matt. 24.

units.la: III. Quid Ecclesia? Erant vnanimiter om nes, &c. Atqui habuerunt domus. Act 2. Lo quitur ergo hic de sacris cœtibus, quos in publico coegerunt, ut verbū audirent, prae carentur, &c, Not. Duo tribui primiti uæ Eccle. 1 Vnanimitate, ut supra 2.4. Est hic quoq; fructus disciplinæ. Simile ex re domestica 2. Fortitudine, quæ ferè nascitur ex vnanimitate, Eccl. 4. Nouerant minas concilij Act. 4. At nunc liberius agunt, nimirum ut infirmis crescerent animi. Sic Dan.6. Hodie prudentiæ putatur, inter pericula fide dissimulare, cœtus & sacra in termittere, ambiguè loqui vel etiam abnegare, &c. Sed ita aduersarijs animi augentur, & Dei ira prouocatur, qui tepidos nō fert, Apo.3. Iltos ergo imitemur, & Paul. Rom.1. Ita Christus iubet, Mar.9.
units.tr: III. What of the Church? "They were all of one accord," and so on. Yet they had houses, Acts 2. Therefore this passage speaks of the sacred assemblies which they held openly, so that they might hear the Word, be taught, and so on. Note: two things were granted to the primitive Church. 1. Unanimity, as above in 2 and 4. Here too is a fruit of discipline; a similar thing arises from domestic affairs. 2. Fortitude, which is almost born of unanimity, Eccl. 4. They knew the threats of the council, Acts 4, but now they act more freely, namely so that the spirits of the weak might grow. So Dan. 6. Today it is thought prudent, amid dangers, to dissemble one's faith, to give up assemblies and sacred rites, to speak ambiguously or even to deny, and so on. But in this way the spirits of adversaries are increased, and the wrath of God is provoked, who does not bear the lukewarm, Rev. 3. Let us therefore imitate those men, and Paul, Rom. 1. So Christ commands, Mark 9.

units.la: IV. Crescit multitudo credentiū quo tidie. Adeo nihil possunt sacerdotes & seniores in sua vrbe. Imo ex vicinis locis
units.tr: IV. The multitude of believers grows daily. So much can the priests and elders do in their own city, nothing. Indeed, from neighbouring places

units.la: confluunt, qui afferunt aegrotos, & ita fidem discunt. NOTA Quibus medijs regnum Christi propagetur? Peccatur in ea varia prudentibus huius seculi. Alij putant seruiendum esse tempori, & multa eius dissimulanda, donec multorum animi mutentur, de quibus iam dictum. Alij foedera & arma quaerunt. Sed Dei hoc opus est, & non nisi huius spiritu perficitur, Zach.4. Vtitur quidem hominum fortium opera interdum, vt Mach. Constant. Theodosijs,&c.
