Sed tunc quoque res ita moderatur, vt huius opus esse appareat. Nihil ergo violentum tentetur abl q; certa Dei vocatione. Legitima ratio est, vt doctores constanter praedicent simplicem veritatis doctrinam 1.Cor.10 Mich.5. Hanc studiose audiant omnes purgatis animis, Luc. 8. Magistratus disciplinam morum vrgeant. Regnet apud omnes beneficentiae studium. Istis studijs Christus non deerit. Oremus.
units.tr: they flock together, bringing the sick, and so learn the faith. NOTE: By what means is the kingdom of Christ propagated? Here the prudent men of this age go wrong in various ways. Some think one must yield to the times and dissemble many things until the minds of many are changed, of whom we have already spoken. Others seek alliances and arms. But this work is God's, and it is accomplished only by His Spirit, Zech. 4. He indeed sometimes uses the labours of brave men, as the Maccabees, Constantine, Theodosius, and so on. But even then He so governs the matter that it appears to be His work. Nothing violent, therefore, should be attempted without a certain calling of God. The lawful method is that the teachers constantly preach the simple doctrine of the truth, 1 Cor. 10, Mic. 5. Let all hear it earnestly with purged minds, Luke 8. Let the magistrate press the discipline of morals. Let zeal for beneficence reign among all. Christ will not be wanting to these endeavours. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXVIII.

units.la: 17 Exurgens autem Pontifex maximus & omnes qui cum eo erant (quae est secta Sadducaeorum) repleti sunt inuidia.
units.tr: 17 But the high priest rose up, and all who were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees), and they were filled with envy.

units.la: 18 Et iniecerunt manus in Apostolos. stolos, posuerunt eos in custodia publica.
units.tr: 18 And they laid hands on the apostles and put them in the public prison.

units.la: 19 Sed Angelus Domini per nocem aperuit fores carceris: eduxitque illos dixit,
units.tr: 19 But the angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison by night, led them out, and said,

units.la: 20 Ite, et stantes loquimini populo in templo omnia verba vitae huius.
units.tr: 20 Go, and stand and speak to the people in the temple all the words of this life.

units.la: 21 Illi vero cum haec audissent, sub aurora ingressi sunt templum et docebant.
units.tr: 21 When they heard this, they went into the temple at dawn and taught.

units.la: Etsi Christus Rex ille sit gloriae, cui omnis potestas & iudicium datum est (Psal. 2. Matth. 28. Ioh. 5.) ipse tamen fatetur, semper futuros hostes, qui regnum ipsius conentur evertere, Luc. 19. Ioh. 15. 16. Patet hoc in omnibus historiis, maxime tamen in hoc libro, quo Lucas subinde inter se opponit felices regni Christi progressus, & insanos hostium conatus. Vsus, ut nec cruce offendamur, nec nobis perpetuam pacem polliceamur, sed tunc quoque ad crucem praeparemur, quando omnia tuta videntur. Et hoc facit praefens historia. Praemisit statum florentissimum Ecclesiae. Iam subijcit novum certamen, in quo tantum permittitur hostibus, ut Apostoli capiantur, &c. Veruntamen plus consolationis quam terroris etiam hic habet. betur,quando Deus mirificè seruat suos, hostes ludificat,&c.
units.tr: Although Christ is that King of glory, to whom all power and judgment has been given (Ps. 2; Matt. 28; John 5), he himself declares that there will always be enemies who try to overthrow his kingdom (Luke 19; John 15, 16). This is evident in all histories, but most of all in this book, in which Luke repeatedly sets the happy progress of Christ's kingdom against the mad attempts of its enemies. The use of this is that we should be neither offended by the cross nor promise ourselves perpetual peace, but be prepared for the cross even when all seems safe. The present history does exactly this. It first sets out the most flourishing state of the Church; now it adds a new conflict, in which the enemies are permitted only so much that the apostles are seized, etc. Yet even here there is more consolation than terror, when God wonderfully preserves his own, mocks their enemies, etc.

units.la: I Hostes proponuntur,& quid fecerint. Insurgit Pontif.cum suis,qui omnes Sad-ducæi erant. Argumentum extremæ coruptionis, quando religionem damnant, qui præcipuum huius caput negabant,i. Cor.15.No T.1. Qui præcipui sint persecutores veritatis: Qui antistites religionis haberi volunt, sub eo autè prætextu sua modò quærunt. Hi veritatis lucem non possunt ferre.Io.3. & 5.Et tales ferè Sadd. agunt. Nisi enim riderent quæcunque de cœlo & inferis dicuntur, non haberent sa cra venalia. Non corrumperet scripturas. Non grauarent simpliciû conscientias. In terim apparet infelix mundi cæcitas, qui cûm tales videat esse, tamen pro illis pugnat,2 Pet.2.2.Thef.2.¶2.Quid faciunt? Re plentur zelo aut æmulatione: quòd nimirum eos videat in pretio esse, qui ipsorum authoritati derogabant. At non dubiû est, quin Dei zelû prætexuerint,& legis, &c. Ioh.11. Ita hodie fit. Vt tamen detur illis, quòd zelo sancto & bono vtantur, tamen hic quoq; non excusat,Ro.10. Phil.3.Dein de qui scripturis debebant pugnare,inijci unt eis manus,Ita cû Christo actû,Luc.22. Ioh.10. Et hodie hoc ipsum fit multò impudentius
units.tr: I. The enemies are set forth, and what they did. The high priest rises up with his men, who were all Sadducees. This is a sign of extreme corruption, when those who denied the chief head of religion (1 Cor. 15; note on 1 Tim. 1) condemn religion. Who are the chief persecutors of the truth? Those who wish to be thought the leaders of religion, but under that pretext seek their own advantage. Such men cannot bear the light of truth (John 3 and 5), and the Sadducees were mostly of this kind. For if they did not laugh at whatever is said of heaven and hell, they would not have sacred things for sale. They would not corrupt the Scriptures. They would not burden the consciences of simple people. Meanwhile the unhappy blindness of the world appears, which, seeing such men for what they are, nonetheless fights for them (2 Pet. 2; 2 Thess. 2). What do they do? They are filled with zeal or rivalry, namely because they see those esteemed who detracted from their own authority. But there is no doubt that they pretended zeal for God and the law, etc. (John 11). So it happens today. Yet granting that they use a holy and good zeal, still here too it does not excuse them (Rom. 10; Phil. 3). Then those who ought to fight with Scripture laid hands on the apostles, as was done with Christ (Luke 22; John 10). And today this very thing is done far more shamelessly.

units.la: Hostes & persecutores Ecclesiae sacerdotum grege accerrimi veritatis hostes produnt.
units.tr: The enemies and persecutors of the Church, the fiercest enemies of the truth, reveal themselves in a flock of priests.

units.la: Hostium veritatis artes. pudentiús sub prætextu conciliorum,pa-cis publicæ.Fœderum. Vigilemus perpe-tuò, memores cum quibus nobis res fit, Mat.10.26.Psal.116.
units.tr: The arts of the enemies of the truth are more shameless under the pretext of councils, of public peace, and of covenants. Let us watch constantly, mindful of with whom we have to deal (Matt. 10:26; Ps. 116).

units.la: II. Quid Deus, qui videri poterat Ec-clefiam negligere.Sed ostendit verissimū esse quod habetur Psal.121.Vt enim Chri, sto sepulto venit Angelus, qui sepulchrū aperit,&c.Matt.28. Ita hîc angelus carcerem referat,iubet exire,&c.Not.¶1. Ecclesiam Deo curæ esse, & verbū Dei vinciri non posse,2.Tim 2. Imò tunc sæpè agit efficacissimè, quando ministri sunt vin&ti.Vide Paulum Act.16.26.28. Phil.4.Similia hodie fiunt, quando Martyres ducuntur.Ne ergo offendamur.
units.tr: II. What God does, who might seem to neglect the Church. But he shows that what is said in Ps. 121 is most true. For as an angel came when Christ was buried and opened the tomb (Matt. 28), so here the angel leads the apostles out of prison and orders them to go out, etc. Note: the Church is a concern to God, and the word of God cannot be bound (2 Tim. 2). Indeed he often works most effectively when the ministers are bound; see Paul, Acts 16:26–28; Phil. 4. Similar things happen today when martyrs are led away. Let us therefore not be offended.

units.la: ¶2.Modum liberationis.Poterat Deus multis alijs modis carcerem aperire. Sed vult Angeli ministerio vti.Ita docet quan ti suos sciat,quando horum seruitio desti-nat suos famulos.Vide de Angelis Ps.104. Dan.7.At tamen eosdem vult elestis quoque seruiræ,Meb.1. Matt.18.Psal.34.91.Ex sempla passim sunt, Gen.19. 32, 2.Reg.6. Exod.12.Dan.6.Ifa.37. Similia publicè & priuatim experimur. Id soletur,& simul officij admoneat,2.Cor.11.
units.tr: 2. The manner of deliverance. God could have opened the prison by many other means, but he wills to use the ministry of angels. Thus he teaches how much he cares for his people, when he assigns his servants to their service. See on the angels Ps. 104; Dan. 7. Yet he also wills the same angels to serve the elect (Heb. 1; Matt. 18; Ps. 34, 91). Examples are everywhere: Gen. 19; Gen. 32; 2 Kings 6; Exod. 12; Dan. 6; Isa. 37. We experience similar things publicly and privately. This consoles us and at the same time admonishes us of our duty (2 Cor. 11).

units.la: ¶3.Finem liberationis huius,Ite loquimini in templo verba vitæ, &c. Ita dicitur
units.tr: 3. The end of this deliverance: "Go, speak in the temple the words of life," etc. So it is said.

units.la: Euangelium,quia Christi est,qui verba vitæ æternæ habet(Iohan.6.) & quia Christum predicat, in quo vno vita habetur, Ioh.1.4.Act.Ide Cornelio quoq; dicit Angelus, Act.11. Ergo vita seipsos ipoliant, quotquot Euangelium audire dedignantur,Mar.16.Ioh.3.
units.tr: The gospel is so called because it is Christ's, who has the words of eternal life (John 6), and because it preaches Christ, in whom alone life is had (John 1:4; Acts). So the angel also says to Cornelius, Acts 11. Therefore all who disdain to hear the gospel strip themselves of life (Mark 16; John 3).

units.la: Interim hinc generale præceptum petatur. Iubentur Apostoli redire ad suum munus. Idem faciant quicunque Deo opem sentiunt. Vide Psal.50. Peccatur in eo variè.1.Sunt qui putant periculis se ad moneri, vt in posterum abstineant.2.Alij sibijpfis ferias indicunt, & se plus fatis laborare putant. Atqui Deo nos debemus, quoad viuimus,2.Tim.4.3.Luc.9.Matth.24.Vide Paulum, Phil.1.3.Alij sceleribus sese consecrant, quasi farcire velint prius intermissa. Sed cogitent sibi idem dici quod paralitico,Ioh.5.
units.tr: Meanwhile let a general precept be drawn from here. The apostles are ordered to return to their office. Let all who feel God's help do the same (see Ps. 50). Men sin in this in various ways. 1. There are those who think they are warned by dangers to abstain in future. 2. Others declare holidays for themselves and think they labour more than enough. Yet we owe ourselves to God as long as we live (2 Tim. 4:3; Luke 9; Matt. 24); see Paul, Phil. 1 and 3. 3. Others consecrate themselves to crimes, as if they wished to make up for what they had previously left undone. But let them consider that what was said to the paralytic (John 5) is said to them too.

units.la: III.Apostoli obediunt.Atqui multa po terant reuocare. Periculum præsens.Potentia aduersariorum.Publicæ persecutionis periculum,&c. Sed faciunt quod iubentur.
units.tr: III. The apostles obey. And yet they might have objected to many things: the present danger, the power of the adversaries, the peril of public persecution, etc. But they do what they are commanded.

units.la: Not. ¶Exemplum obedientiæ. Non faciamus quod nobis bonû videtur, Numer.15.Deut.28. Ista obseruemus tunc quando omnia videntur diuersum requirere. rere, Sic olim Abraham fecit, & Deo placuit, Gen. 12.22. Hic Euangelij finis, Rom. 1.16. Non fallet nos, qui ipsissima est sapientia & veritas. Oremus.
units.tr: Note: an example of obedience. Let us not do what seems good to us (Num. 15; Deut. 28). Let us observe these things even when everything seems to require the opposite, as Abraham once did, and it pleased God (Gen. 12; 22). Here is the goal of the gospel (Rom. 1:16). He will not deceive us, who is wisdom and truth itself. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXIX.

units.la: 21 Adueniens autem Pontifex maximus, & qui cum eo erant conuocarunt concilium, & vniuersum senatum filiorum Israel: miseruntque in carcerem ministros, a quibus illi adducerentur.
units.tr: But when the high priest arrived, along with those who were with him, they called together the council and the whole senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison for the men to be brought.

units.la: 22 Cum autem venissent ministri, non inuenerunt eos in carcere, quod renuntiauerunt.
units.tr: When the officers came, they did not find them in the prison, and they returned and reported this.

units.la: 23 Dicentes, carcerem quidem inuenimus clausum cum omni diligentia, & custodes foris stantes ad ianuam: quum aperuissemus autem, neminem in tus inuenimus:
units.tr: Saying, "We found the prison shut up with all care, and the guards standing outside at the door; but when we opened it, we found no one inside."

units.la: 24 Ut vero audierunt hos sermones & Pontifex maximus & praefectus templo, principes, & Sacerdotum, ambigebant de illis, quo nam hoc euasurum esset.
units.tr: When the high priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were perplexed about them, wondering what this would come to.

units.la: 25 Adueniens autem quidam nuntiauit eis, Ecce, viri quos coniecerati in carcerem stant in templo, & docent populum.
units.tr: Then someone came and told them, "Look, the men you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people."

units.la: M
units.tr: M

units.la: 26 Tunc prætectus abiens cum mi-nistris, adduxit eos, non tamen per vim (timebant enim populum ne lapidaren-tur.)
units.tr: Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, but not by force, for they feared the people, lest they be stoned.

units.la: DAuid Psal.2 Christi regnum descri-pturus ab hostium conatibus ordi-tur,illis autem Dei consiliu opponit. Di-scamus conatus eiusmodi non modo irri-tos,sed ridiculos quoque, & suis authori-bus pernitisos esse.Exempla sunt passim: inter quæ memorabile est hoc:Capti sunt Apostoli & adhibiti custodes. Mane con-uenitur, vt consultetur de pœna,& hoc i-gne extinguendo. At Deus toti mundo deridendos proponit. Angelus enim libe-rauit Apostolos.Et nunc consilia illorum nulla sunt,Videamus singula.
units.tr: David, in Psalm 2, while describing the kingdom of Christ, begins with the attempts of its enemies, and then sets the counsel of God against them. Let us learn that attempts of this kind are not only futile but also ridiculous, and that they bring ruin on their own authors. There are examples everywhere, and among them this one is memorable: the Apostles were taken and guards were set over them. In the morning they gather to deliberate about punishment and about putting out this fire. But God makes them a laughingstock to the whole world, for an angel freed the Apostles. And now their plans come to nothing. Let us look at each point.

units.la: I. Concilium cogunt. Sunt hic omnia, quæ concilium legitimum referunt. Præ-sidet Pontifex, de quo Deut.17. Adhibet collegas,ne ex affectu priuato agere dica-tur.Seniores item, qui etiam ipsi a Deo in-stituti,Num. 11. Accedit templi præfectus cum ministris publicis. Quis non dicat hos legitimè conuenire? At si finem spe-ctes, conuenerunt in spiritu Satanæ, &c. Et proinde nemo illis debuit obedire.
units.tr: I. They convene a council. Everything here matches a lawful council. The high priest presides, of whom Deut. 17 speaks. He takes colleagues, so that he cannot be said to act from private feeling. Likewise the elders, who were also instituted by God, Num. 11. The captain of the temple comes with the public officers. Who would not say these men met lawfully? But if you look at the end, they met in the spirit of Satan, and so on. Therefore no one ought to have obeyed them.

units.la: Not. ¶ Quid de Concilijs iudican-dum,quæ hodie in omni ore sunt.Optan-dum dum effet,vt legitimum cogeretur, quale fuit Apostolicum, Act.15. Nicaenum, &c. At nihil huius sperandu, quando nolunt Pontifices cedere male vsurpata possessio ne. Ipsi ergo indicunt, praesidi ent, affecti sunt, habent sibi obstrictos. Nec regem vllum admittunt, nisi qui in ipsorum verba iurauit. Finis non alius quam qui hic fuit. Id quod ne in Bullis quidè suis dissimulant. Neminē ergo moueant istorū claares.Beatus, qui non, &c.Pfal.1.Tu maiores fortissimos imitare, qui se se oppo- suerunt Papis. Fuit hoc initium foederis Heluetici. Vtinam Pontificij non dissipent.
units.tr: Note. What should be thought about councils, which are on everyone's lips today? It would be desirable that a lawful one be convened, such as the apostolic council of Acts 15, or the Nicene, and so on. But nothing of this can be hoped for, since the popes refuse to give up a possession wrongly seized. So they themselves appoint the members, preside, act with partisan feeling, and hold the members bound to themselves. Nor do they admit any king unless he has sworn to their terms. Their aim is no other than it was here, and they do not even hide this in their own Bulls. Let not the outcries of these men move anyone. Blessed is he who does not, and so on, Ps. 1. Imitate your greatest and bravest forebears, who set themselves against the Papists. This was the beginning of the Helvetic covenant. Would that the Papists do not scatter us.

units.la: II. Vt Christus illos illuserit. Mittunt, qui Apostolos adducant: Ita nimirum Ec, clesiae toti terrorem incussuri. Sed quid fit? 1. Ministri inueniunt eductos esse. 2. Nuntiant ita, vt Dei opus fateantur. 3. Annuntiantur, quia conscientiae stimuli inuitis quoq; obrepunt. 4. Triftius quid nuntiatur, illos in templo docere. Id quod ambitiosis valde doluit.
units.tr: II. How Christ mocked them. They send men to bring the Apostles, plainly intending to strike terror into the whole Church. But what happens? (1) The ministers find that the Apostles had been led out. (2) They report it in such a way that they confess it to be God's work. (3) They report it because the goads of conscience creep in even on unwilling men. (4) What they report is more distressing: that the Apostles are teaching in the temple. This grieved the ambitious men greatly.

units.la: NOT. Quàm facilè Deus hostium conatus eludat. Idem hic factum, quod Iohan. 7. Nam de miraculo testantur, quorum opera volut veritate opprimere. Sic
units.tr: NOTE. How easily God makes light of the attempts of enemies. The same thing happened here as in John 7. For they bear witness to the miracle, and yet they want to suppress by force the truth whose work it is.

units.la: {a}factum Pharaoni,Exo.2.8.Balaamo,Num.23 Achabo,1.Reg.18.Hamano,Heft.5 6 7. In resurrectione,Matth 27 28. Herodi, Actor.12. Seruiat hoc consolationi, ne impiorum machinationibus terreamur, Pfa. 33.Ifa.40. Simul moneat, nenos temere Dei decretis opponamus. Tales nihil proficiunt,Ifa.14 8. &c.
units.tr: {a} as it happened to Pharaoh, Exod. 2 (8); to Balaam, Num. 23; to Ahab, 1 Kings 18; to Haman, Esther 5, 6, 7. At the resurrection, Matt. 27, 28; to Herod, Acts 12. Let this serve for comfort, that we not be terrified by the machinations of the impious, Ps. 33; Isa. 40. At the same time it should warn us not to oppose God's decrees rashly. Such men accomplish nothing, Isa. 14 (8), and so on.

units.la: III. Quid Sacerdotes? Non contenti stultitiam suam prodidisse, insuper incurabilem quoque contumaciam produnt. Mittunt praefectum templi, qui illos adducat fine vi:non quod iam mitiores sint, sed quod timent populum,cui voluerunt ipsi timore incutere.Ita solent, qui semel coeperunt θεομαχεῖν. Sentiunt Dei mánum,& dolent. Sed quia suam gloriam plu-ris faciunt, quàm gloriam Dei, non pof-sunt credere,vt feruentur,Ioh.5 Itaque conscientiam cum Deo pugnam suscipiunt.Sic Pharao,Exod.8.9.10.Sedechi-as,Ier.37.38.Achab,1.Reg 18.21.22.&c:Hodie multi similes, quoad poenitentiam. Sed ferè est infelix exitus,Ifa.6.
units.tr: III. What of the priests? Not content to have shown their folly, they also show an incurable obstinacy. They send the captain of the temple, who is to bring the Apostles without violence. This is not because they have become milder, but because they fear the people, on whom they had wanted to inflict fear. This is what happens to those who have once begun to fight against God (θεομαχεῖν) [theomachein]. They feel God's hand and are grieved. But because they value their own glory more than the glory of God, they cannot believe so as to be saved, John 5. And so they take up a struggle against God with their own conscience. So it was with Pharaoh, Exod. 8, 9, 10; Zedekiah, Jer. 37, 38; Ahab, 1 Kings 18, 21, 22, and so on. Today many are like them as regards repentance. But generally the end is unhappy, Isa. 6.

units.la: Consoletur autem, quòd impijs non licet quicquid libet. Potest Deus semper licet quòd volunt. Potest Deus arationibus eos terrere, qui ipsum non timent.Ita praefectus iste populum timet. Sic etiam Matth,21.26. Est haec poena di-gna gna tyrannidis & impietatis,&c.
units.tr: Yet it is a comfort that the impious are not allowed to do whatever they please. God can, even though they wish otherwise, always prevent it, and God can terrify by visions those who do not fear him. So this captain fears the people. So also Matt. 21 (26). This punishment is worthy of tyranny and impiety, and so on.

units.la: Sed quaerat aliquis, Cur Deus patiatur Apostolos denuo duci. Num non potuit amplius defendere? Aut num neglexit tam morigeros? Nequaquam, Sed testari voluit, promissionem Euangelij habere conditionem crucis(Mar.10.)& ideo pios per crucem triumphare. Huc facit Ioh.16. Ergo licet iuuemur interdum, semper tamen meminerimus, denuo esse pugnandum.
units.tr: But someone may ask why God allowed the Apostles to be led away again. Could he not defend them more fully? Or has he neglected such obedient servants? By no means. But he wished to testify that the promise of the gospel has the condition of the cross, Mark 10, and therefore that the godly triumph through the cross. John 16 bears on this. So although we are sometimes helped, let us always remember that we must fight again.

units.la: ¶ Obseruarunt hoc Apostoli, & ideo nec murmurant contra Deum, neq; concitant populum. Sciebant Deum iuste & sapienter omnia agere. Regnum Christi non esse de hoc mundo,Iohan.18.Zach.4. Christum ipsis non defuturum, Matt.10. Luc.21.Ioh.14.Itaq; huius curae se commit tunt.Imitemur,Psal.37.55.1. Pet.5.
units.tr: The Apostles observed this, and therefore they neither murmur against God nor stir up the people. They knew that God acts justly and wisely in all things; that Christ's kingdom is not of this world, John 18; Zech. 4; that Christ would not fail them, Matt. 10; Luke 21; John 14. Therefore they committed themselves to his care. Let us imitate them, Ps. 37, 55; 1 Pet. 5.

units.la: Arguuntur hic murmuratores,Item se ditiofi, & qui regnum Christi volunt tumultibus publicis propagare. Punit qui dem Deus tyrannos seditionibus. Sed pij has non concitant,qui nòrunt quod habe tur, Rom.13. Ideo Dauidem imitantur, 1.Sam.24. & 26. Vide D.Ambrosij exemplum.Interim ista non derogant magistra tus officio,Isa.49. Singuli verò suam vocationem sequantur, ferant patienter aduersa,exspectent Dominū, qui suos nunquam deferet,Pf.72.62.lo.14.ro. Oremus.
units.tr: Here murmurers are rebuked, and likewise the proud who wish to spread Christ's kingdom by public tumults. God indeed punishes tyrants by sedition. But the godly do not stir these up, since they know what has been ordained, Rom. 13. Therefore they imitate David, 1 Sam. 24 and 26. See the example of Ambrose. Meanwhile these things do not detract from the office of the magistrate, Isa. 49. Let each follow his own calling, bear adversity patiently, and wait for the Lord, who never forsakes his own, Ps. 72 (62); John 14; Rom. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XL.
units.tr: HOMILY XL.

units.la: 27 Adductos autem eos statuerunt in concilio, & interrogauit eos Pontifex maximus.
units.tr: 27 And when they had brought them, they set them before the council, and the high priest questioned them.

units.la: 28 Dicens, Nonne etiam atq; etiam denuntiauimus vobis,ne docereis in nomine isto? & ecce repleuistis Hierusalem doctrina vestra, & vultis super nos inducere effusum sanguinem hominis istius.
units.tr: 28 Saying, Did we not strictly command you not to teach in this name? And behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring this man's blood upon us.

units.la: 29 Respondens autem Petrus & Apostoli, dixerunt: Obedire oportet Deo potius,quàm hominibus.
units.tr: 29 But Peter and the apostles answered and said: We ought to obey God rather than men.

units.la: 30 Deus patrum nostrorum excitauit Iesum,quem vos interfecistis suspensum in ligno.
units.tr: 30 The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.

units.la: 31 Hunc inquam Deus dextra sua exaltum constituit principem & saluatorem,vt det resipiscentiam Israeli, & remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: 31 Him God, by his right hand, has exalted to be Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.

units.la: 32 Et nos sumus ei testes horum, quæ dicimus: atque etiam Spiritus sancti, quem dedit iis,qui obediunt ipsi.
units.tr: 32 And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.

units.la: ETsi Deus Apostolos per Angelum ex carcere liberârit, eosdem tamen rursus capi & Concilio sisti finit. Ita docet non modò liberare posse, verum etiam
units.tr: Although God freed the apostles from prison through an angel, he nevertheless allowed them to be seized again and brought before the council. Thus he teaches that he can not only deliver but also keep his people safe in dangers.

units.la: Cap.5. etiam in periculis feruare. Ne ergo defpe-remus, si quando noua pericula incidunt, & perpetuis calamitabus exercemur. Fide lis est Deus, 1. Cor. 10. 2. Cor. 1. Pf. 91. Id in praesenti patebit. Nam etiamsi Apostoli accusentur, de vita periclitentur, virgis caedantur, euadunt tamen & triumphat ve-ritas.
units.tr: Chapter 5. So let us not despair if new dangers arise and we are worn down by constant calamities. God is faithful (1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1; Ps. 91). This will be evident in the present case. For even though the apostles are accused, their lives endangered, and they are beaten with rods, they nevertheless escape, and the truth triumphs.

units.la: ¶ Interrogat Pontifex, sed ita vt accu-set, & quasi sceleris conuictos corripiat. Triplex crimen. 1. Contumaciae & inobedientiae contra Concilium. Graue hoc, Deut. 17. Imo similes videri poterant Core, &c. Num. 16. 2. Quod sua doctrina tam vrbe repleuerint. Emphasis in vestra. Ita nouitatis insimulant. Deut. 13. 3. Vultis super nos adducere sanguinem. Seditionis accusant, vt qui populum cupiant concitare. Atqui ipsi hunc sanguinem in se receperant Ioh. 19.
units.tr: The high priest questions them, but in such a way as to accuse them, and to rebuke them as if they were convicted criminals. There is a threefold charge: (1) contumacy and disobedience against the council, which is serious (Deut. 17); indeed they could seem like Korah and his company (Num. 16); (2) that they have filled the city with their teaching, the emphasis being on "your"; thus they charge them with novelty (Deut. 13); (3) "you intend to bring this man's blood upon us." They accuse them of sedition, as men who wish to stir up the people. And yet they themselves had taken this blood upon themselves (John 19).

units.la: In his autem Not. ¶ 1. Insolentiam falsorum antistitum. Vbi semel primatu obtinuerunt, quiduis mandant, & sibi volunt simpliciter obediri. Matt. 23. Imprimis ne quis doceat ipsis inuitis. Ioh. 1. 8. Satis ergo peccarunt Apostoli, quod contra ipsorum edictum praedicarunt. Ita hodie fit. Postquam Pontifices ad se transtulerunt quod Apostolis dicitur Matt. 10. & 16. nihil non cœperunt mandare.Apoc.13. Ad-hæc volunt habere irreprehensibiles. Imo cum videant se agnosci, adhuc pergunt.
units.tr: Here note: (1) the insolence of false prelates. Once they have gained primacy, they command whatever they like and want to be obeyed without question (Matt. 23). Above all, no one may teach against their will (John 1). So the apostles had already sinned enough in preaching against their edict. So it happens today. After the pontiffs transferred to themselves what is said to the apostles (Matt. 10 and 16), they have begun to command nothing short of everything (Rev. 13). Moreover, they want to be beyond reproach; indeed, when they see themselves recognised, they still persist.

units.la: ¶ 2.De quibus ferè accusentur ministri, Idem enim semper est mundi ingenium. Inobedientiæ quod ipsi velint pro suo arbitrio omnia facere. Seductionis & sedi-tionis. Sic accusatus Moses, Exod.5. Helias, 1.Reg.18.21. Micheas. 1.Reg.22. Amos, Cap.7. Ierem.Cap.38.44. Christus ipse, Luc.23.Io.19. Ne ergo offendamur hodie: quin inquiramus diligenter. Sed audiamus Apostolorum responsionem.
units.tr: (2) Of what ministers are usually accused, for the nature of the world is always the same: of disobedience, because they wish to do everything at their own discretion; and of seduction and sedition. Thus Moses was accused (Exod. 5), Elijah (1 Kings 18, 21), Micaiah (1 Kings 22), Amos (ch. 7), Jeremiah (chs. 38, 44), and Christ himself (Luke 23; John 19). So let us not be offended today, but rather inquire diligently. But let us hear the apostles' answer.

units.la: I. Inobedientiæ crimen diluunt. Non negant edictum,sed opponunt Dei authoritatem, vt supra 4.Cap.Sed illic ipsorum iudicio rem permiserant: hic quia obstina-tos vident, simpliciter pronuntiant quid faciendum.
units.tr: I. They refute the charge of disobedience. They do not deny the edict, but set against it the authority of God, as above in chapter 4. But there the apostles had left the matter to the council's judgement; here, since they see the council obstinate, they simply declare what must be done.

units.la: NOTA ¶ Rationem veræ obedientiæ. Euangelium non negat obediendum esse iis, quibus hoc debetur.1.Pet.2.Matth.22. Eph.5 6. At si iubeamur quod Deus prohibet, aut contra: tunc Deo parendum. Vi-de Dan.3.6.Ita fecerunt omnes Martyres.
units.tr: NOTE: the rule of true obedience. The gospel does not deny that obedience is owed to those to whom it is due (1 Pet. 2; Matt. 22; Eph. 5. 6.). But if we are commanded to do what God forbids, or the reverse, then God must be obeyed. See Dan. 3. 6. So all the martyrs have done.

units.la: II.Duo coniungunt : Deus patrum no-strorum, &c. Sensus, Non aliam s prædicamus Seruatorem, quàm quem Deus olim patrib. promisit, & in quo ipsi sperarunt. runt.Neq; nos huius sanguinem vobis im putamus:Sed vos illum occidistis,&c. V- bi Nota. ¶Vt agendum cum hostibus professis veritatis.Ingenuè confitenda ve ritas. Arguendi item ipsi ne fe timeri pu- tent. Quo enim plus timentur, eo magis ferociunt,quia fe putant latere. Conuicti timent.Cain,Gen.4.Achab,1 Regum 21. Hinc illa prophetarum fortitudo. Stulti qui blandiuntur.
units.tr: II. They join two things: "The God of our fathers," and so on. The sense is: we preach no other Saviour than the one whom God long ago promised to our fathers and in whom they hoped. Nor do we impute his blood to you; rather, you killed him, and so on. Here note how one should deal with professed enemies of the truth: the truth must be confessed ingenuously. They must also be argued with, lest they think themselves feared; for the more they are feared, the more fiercely they behave, because they think they lie hidden. The convicted are afraid (Cain, Gen. 4; Ahab, 1 Kings 21). Hence the courage of the prophets. Foolish are those who flatter.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Vt aliqui possint lucrifieri, sum- mam suæ doctrinæ proponunt de Christo salutis ra- & nostra salute. ¶ 1. Christum esse princi- pem salutis à Deo excitatum.Ita inuunt, il lum esse de quo Prophetæ,Pfalm 2.45.72. 89.110.Mich 5.Zach 9.Docent ista,totum Christi negotium in æterno Dei decreto, (1.Pet.1.Ephef.1.) esse fundatum, & illum nos propria virtute feruare, Iohan.10.14. Id nos solatur in omni tentatione, cum conscientiæ tum persecutionum.
units.tr: So that some might be won over, they set out the sum of their doctrine concerning Christ and our salvation. (1) They show that Christ is the Prince of salvation, raised up by God. Thus they intimate that he is the one of whom the prophets spoke (Ps. 2, 45, 72, 89, 110; Mic. 5; Zech. 9). These things teach that the whole business of Christ is founded on God's eternal decree (1 Pet. 1; Eph. 1), and that he saves us by his own power (John 10. 14). This comforts us in every temptation, both of conscience and of persecution.

units.la: ¶ 2. Qualis Seruator? Qui dat pœnitentiam & peccatorum remissionem. Id oppo- nitur nostræ conditioni miserrimæ. Su- mus peccatores & natura peccato delecta mur,Gen.5.Pfalm.36.Rom.7. Deinde ipsi non possumus satisfacere, Pfal.143.130.19. Matth.18. Christus autem largitur pœni- tentiam, dum per Spiritum & Euangelium arguit peccata, illuminat, &c. Iohan. 16. Idem remissionis author est, dum ipse pro nobis peccatum factus, nos patri reconciliat, 2. Cor. 5. 1 Cor. 1. &c. Id vero admonet. 1. Vt vni Christo tribuamus quaecunque ad nostram salutem pertinent, Ifa. 42. Matth 11 Iohan. 14. 2. Vt memores poenitentiae, non quaeramus in illo peccandi licentiam, Mar. 1. Iohannis 13. 1. Iohannis 1. Iac. 1.
units.tr: (2) What kind of Saviour? One who gives repentance and the remission of sins. This is set against our most wretched condition. We are sinners, and by nature delight in sin (Gen. 5; Ps. 36; Rom. 7). Then, we ourselves cannot make satisfaction (Ps. 143, 130, 19; Matt. 18). But Christ bestows repentance, while through the Spirit and the gospel he convicts of sin, enlightens, and so on (John 16). He is also the author of remission, since he himself was made sin for us and reconciles us to the Father (2 Cor. 5; 1 Cor. 1, and so on). This indeed admonishes us: first, to ascribe to Christ alone whatever pertains to our salvation (Isa. 42; Matt. 11; John 14); second, that, mindful of repentance, we should not seek in him a licence to sin (Mar. 1. Iohannis 13. 1. Iohannis 1. Iac. 1.).

units.la: q3. Confirmant: Et nos sumus testes. Non arroganter hoc dicunt, sed ex officio Ioh. 15. Actor. 1. Quia tamen se contemni videbant, addunt. Et Spiritus sanctus. Id referri debet ad donum linguarum, fanationum, regenerationis, &c. Obseruemus, quae debeat esse authoritas doctrinae Apostolicae. Sunt illi Christi testes. Iidem ex Spiritu sancto locuti sunt (Lucae 21.) qui insuper reipsa illis testimonium perhibuit. Qui ergo contradicunt, hi & Christo & Spiritui sancto contradicunt. Act. 7. 1 Ioh. 5. Illi ergo credamus, & in eodem fortes simus & constantes. Oremus.
units.tr: (3) They confirm their words: And we are witnesses. They do not say this arrogantly, but from duty (John 15; Acts 1). Yet because they saw themselves despised, they add: And the Holy Spirit. This must be referred to the gift of tongues, of healings, of regeneration, and so on. Let us observe what the authority of apostolic doctrine ought to be. They are Christ's witnesses. They spoke from the Holy Spirit (Luke 21), who moreover bore witness to them in fact. Therefore whoever contradicts them contradicts both Christ and the Holy Spirit (Acts 7; 1 John 5). Let us therefore believe them, and be strong and constant in the same. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XLI.
units.tr: HOMILY XLI.

units.la: 33 At illi his auditis frendebant, & consilium inibant eos interimendi.
units.tr: 33 But when they heard these things, they were enraged and planned to kill them.

units.la: 34 Surgens autem in concilio quidam dam Pharisæorum, nomine Gamaliel, legis doctor, quem totus populus in pretio habebat, iussit ut paulisper abducerent foras Apostolos.
units.tr: 34 Then a certain man stood up in the council, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, held in high esteem by all the people, and ordered that the apostles be taken outside for a little while.

units.la: 35 Et dixit illis, Viri Israelitæ, attendite vobis ipsis quoad istos homines, quid facturi sitis.
units.tr: 35 And he said to them, "Men of Israel, take care what you intend to do with these men.

units.la: 36 Nam ante hæc tempora exortus est Theudas, dicens se aliquem esse: cui adhæsit numerus virorum circiter quadringentorum, qui interemptus est, & omnes qui assensi sunt ei, dissoluti sunt & ad nihilum redacti.
units.tr: 36 For before these days Theudas arose, claiming to be someone. About four hundred men joined him, but he was killed, and all who had followed him were scattered and brought to nothing.

units.la: 37 Post hunc exortus est Judas ille Galilæus temporibus descriptionis, & avertit populum multum post se: periit & ille, & omnes qui assensi fuerunt ei, dispersi sunt.
units.tr: 37 After him Judas the Galilean arose in the days of the census and drew many people after him. He too perished, and all who had followed him were dispersed.

units.la: 38 Et nunc dico vobis, abstinete ab hominibus istis: & sinite eos, quoniam si ex hominibus consilium sive opus hoc, dissolvetur.
units.tr: 38 And so I tell you: keep away from these men and leave them alone, for if this plan or work is of men, it will come to nothing.

units.la: 39 Si ex Deo est, non poteritis dissolvere, ne quando etiam cum Deo pugnare videamini.
units.tr: 39 But if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow it, lest you be found even fighting against God."

units.la: Exposuit Lucas de quibus accusati in concilio Apostoli, & ut ad ea ipsi responderint. Didicimus, quibus criminibus veritatem & huius ministros infament, & quid tunc his faciendum. 1. Officij ratio habeatur,quo Deo sumus obstristi. 2 For titer agendum, ne impij fiant ferociores. 3.Confessio fidei retineatur,Mar 9.Rom. 1.10. Sequitur vt hanc responsionem illi acceperint: Vbi patebit hostium Christi pertinacia incurabilis, & quàm facilè Deus illorum conatus dissipet.
units.tr: Luke sets out the charges against the apostles in the council and how they answered them. We learn what accusations are used to defame the truth and its ministers, and what must then be done about them. (1) Regard must be had for the duty by which we are bound to God. (2) We must act prudently, lest the impious become more fierce. (3) The confession of faith must be kept; see Mark 9; Rom. 1, 10. It follows that the apostles received this reply. Here it becomes clear how incurable the obstinacy of Christ's enemies is, and how easily God scatters their attempts.

units.la: I. Dissecabantur his auditis praes ira. Dó lebat enim ambitiosis, ficsperni illorum authoritatem. Et volunt occidere, priusquam sententias ex ordine dixerunt. Vnde apparet, illos clamoribus egisse rem.
units.tr: I. When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart with rage. For it grieved the ambitious that their authority was despised. And they want to kill them before they have given their opinions in order. From this it appears that they carried on the matter by shouting.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Eos qui Christi odio indurue-runt,nullis rationibus mitigari.Quia non capiunt Spiritum sanctum,Iohan.14 Verbum quidem audiunt & intelligunt quid dicatur: sed quia suis desiderijs hoc obstare vident,ferociores fiunt. Sic Cain,Gen. 4.Pharao,Exod.5.7.8.9. Achab, 1.Reg.18. 21.22.Iudas,Ioh.12.Mat.26. Discamus non indulgere odio veritatis. ¶ 2. Volunt occidere. Miretur quis tantos viros ita excan-duisse aduersus pauperculos.Sed quia tali-bus nihil magis dolet,quàm cùm verbo Dei arguuntur,se felices putant fore, si à ministris non interturbentur ipsorum stu-dia,Apoc.11.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ 1. Those who have hardened themselves through hatred of Christ are not softened by any reasons, because they do not receive the Holy Spirit (John 14). They hear the word and understand what is said, but because they see that it stands in the way of their desires, they become more fierce. So Cain (Gen. 4), Pharaoh (Exod. 5, 7, 8, 9), Ahab (1 Kings 18, 21, 22), Judas (John 12; Matt. 26). Let us learn not to indulge hatred of the truth. ¶ 2. "They want to kill." One might marvel that such great men should have been so inflamed against poor men. But since nothing grieves such people more than being refuted by the word of God, they think they will be happy if their pursuits are not disturbed by the ministers (Rev. 11).

units.la: Falluntur autem eo, quod se tunc immunes putant & tutos. Atqui non ideo pro talibus agnoscit Deus, cuius iudicium ideo non dormitat, 2 Pet 2. Imo tunc illis accidit, quod malae frugis filio. Vide histo-riam quid his factum, quando Apostoli electi fuerunt, Matth. 21. Luc. 19.
units.tr: But they are deceived in this, because they think they are then immune and safe. Yet God does not for that reason acknowledge such people, whose judgment does not therefore sleep (2 Pet. 2). Indeed, what happens to them is what happened to the prodigal son. See the history of what was done to them when the apostles were chosen (Matt. 21; Luke 19).

units.la: II. Quis vero liberavit Apostolos, cum penes hos esset summa potestas? Exillo-rum coetu surgit vindex Gamaliel. 1. Pharisaeus, ex infensissima secta, Joh. 12. 2. Legis doctor, attentior scilicet aliis, &c. 3. Pretiosus toti populo, quod hic maxime prae-derat, cum sibi a populo timerent, Matth. 26. Not. Quam facile sit Deo suos tue-ri, cum possit ex hostibus vindices dare. Sic factum Nicodemo, Ioh. 7. 19. Sunt & alia exempla. Ruben, Gen. 37. Filia Pharaonis, Exod. 2. Philistaei, 1. Sam 23. Ita hodie quando Turcica bella aut similia turbant Antichristi conatus, Apo. 12. Excitent nos ista, ut non mundo, sed Deo placere studeamus, &c. Sed audiamus orationem Gamalielis, quam Apostolis secedere iusis habuit.
units.tr: II. But who freed the apostles, when supreme power lay with those men? From their assembly rises the defender, Gamaliel: (1) a Pharisee, from the most hostile sect (John 12); (2) a teacher of the law, more attentive than others, of course, etc.; (3) esteemed by the whole people, which he especially excelled in, while they feared the people (Matt. 26). Note: how easily God can protect his own, since he can raise up defenders from among enemies. So it happened for Nicodemus (John 7, 19). There are other examples: Reuben (Gen. 37), Pharaoh's daughter (Exod. 2), the Philistines (1 Sam. 23). So today, when Turkish wars or similar troubles disturb the attempts of Antichrist (Rev. 12), these things should stir us to strive to please God rather than the world, etc. But let us hear the speech of Gamaliel, which he gave when he advised the apostles to withdraw.

units.la: 1. Exordio mitigat furentes: Attendite vobis ipsis, &c. Quasi dicat: Audio vos deliis occidendis cogitare, sed non de illis solis, verum etiam vobis hic agitur, ne irati statuatis aliquid, cuius vos aliquando poæ niteat,&c.
units.tr: 1. He calms the furious at the outset: "Take heed to yourselves," etc. As if to say: "I hear that you are thinking of killing these men, but this concerns not only them but also you, so that in anger you do not decide on something which you may later regret," etc.

units.la: Not. ¶ Generalem doctrinā, ne quid faciamus irati. Est enim ira breuis furor, & proinde pefsimus consultor, Iac.1. In primis ergo hoc obseruent iudices, vt fi-bijpfis attendant,memores ipsorum cau-fam agi in alijs. Iniqua iudicia enim in ip-forum capita recidunt,Pf.82.O fi hoc om-nes expenderent, qui sunt in magistratu.
units.tr: Note. ¶ A general teaching: that we should do nothing in anger. For anger is a brief madness, and therefore the worst counsellor (James 1). Above all, therefore, judges should observe this: that they take heed to themselves, mindful that their own cause is being tried in others. For unjust judgments fall back upon their own heads (Ps. 82). Oh, if all who hold office would weigh this!

units.la: 3 Narrationem contexit,qua docet per exempla, nemini hucufq; impunè fuisse, qui Mefsiæ honorem & nomen vsurpauit falsò,sed eos omnes cum suis perijsse. Vn de postea colliget,idem his quoq; euentu rum. Exempla duo narrat.
units.tr: 3. He weaves in a narrative, by which he teaches through examples that no one until now has gone unpunished who falsely usurped the honour and name of the Messiah, but that all of them have perished with their followers. Therefore he will later conclude that the same will happen to these men too. He relates two examples.

units.la: Nota. ¶ Quid eos maneat, qui Mesfiam verum noluntamplecti? Præda fi-unt impostoribus,qui sua quæruntIoh.5. Ita euenturum prædixit Paulus, 2.Thess. 2. Et hodie experimur. Simus grati & cre-damus Euangelio.
units.tr: Note. ¶ What awaits those who are unwilling to embrace the true Messiah? They become prey to impostors, who seek their own (John 5). Paul foretold that this would happen (2 Thess. 2), and we experience it today. Let us be thankful and believe the gospel.

units.la: 3. Applicat: Abstinete ab istis hominibus. Et Dilemma subijcit,&c.Nota.¶1. Scopum huius consilij.Hunc enim quia multi non obseruant, hinc colligunt, nullius erroribus aut conatibus esse resistendum. Ita verò euertunt omnem disciplinam po-liticam & Ecclesiasticam.Atqui aliud Scri-pturæ pturæ monent, Roman.13. Deuter.13. Leuit.19.20. &c. Ista non ignorauit Gamal. in lege exercitatissimus, Sed quia Apostolos non poterat aliter periculo eripere, & res erat dubia cordatis omnibus, ad hoc consilium delabitur. Nihil ergo hoc ad eos, qui illicitam & apertam ἀταξίαν hoc argumento tuentur. Id verò desperationem arguit. ¶ 2. Oraculi instar sit, huma- na omnia collabi, diuina in æternū cōsistere, Ie.40. Psal.33. Eccl.1. &c. Exépla sunt pas-sim. Dauidem Deus regem populi sui delegerat, 2.Sam.16. Opponit se Saul, & post hunc infiniti alij. Psal.2. Sed nequicquā. Sic factum cum Hierosol. post reditum ex Babylone. Vide Haggæum & Zachariam. In primis ad Christum hoc pertinet. De hoc habemus Dei decretum, 1.Pet.1. Gen.3 49. Psal.8.72.110. Opposuit fe Satan ab origine rerum, & adhuc fe opponit. Sed ratum erit, quod Deus statuit. Vide Mat.16.Ioh. 16. Et infeliciter cesit omnibus tyrannis θεομαχία ista, Zach. 12. Matt. 21. Vide vete ra & hodierna exempla. His oppone gentium superstitiones, quas totus orbis voluit defensas. Sed corruerunt.
units.tr: 3. He applies it: "Keep away from these men." And he adds a dilemma, etc. Note. ¶ 1. The aim of this counsel. Because many do not observe this, they conclude from it that no one's errors or attempts should be resisted. But in this way they overturn all political and ecclesiastical discipline. Yet the Scriptures teach otherwise (Rom. 13; Deut. 13; Lev. 19, 20, etc.). Gamaliel, who was most skilled in the law, was not ignorant of these things, but because he could not otherwise rescue the apostles from danger, and the matter was doubtful to all sensible men, he slipped into this counsel. Nothing in this therefore bears on those who defend unlawful and open anarchy [ἀταξίαν] by this argument. Indeed, this argues despair. ¶ 2. Let it be like an oracle that all human things collapse, while divine things stand forever (Isa. 40; Ps. 33; Eccl. 1, etc.). Examples are everywhere. God had chosen David king of his people (2 Sam. 16); Saul opposed him, and after him countless others (Ps. 2). But in vain. So it happened with Jerusalem after the return from Babylon; see Haggai and Zechariah. Above all, this applies to Christ. We have God's decree concerning him (1 Pet. 1; Gen. 3, 49; Ps. 8, 72, 110). Satan has opposed him from the beginning of things, and still opposes him. But what God has decided will stand. See Matt. 16; John 16. And that fighting against God [θεομαχία] has ended unhappily for all tyrants (Zech. 12; Matt. 21). See ancient and modern examples. Set against these the superstitions of the nations, which the whole world wished to defend. But they have fallen.

units.la: Ista nos moneant, ne quid temere ex nobis instituamus, Iac.4. Interim constan tes simus in ijs defendendis, quæ ex Dei verbo didicimus,Matth.24. Manet hoc aeternum, Isa. 40. Et Christus non deerit, Mat.28. Oremus.
units.tr: Let these things warn us not to undertake anything rashly on our own account (James 4). Meanwhile, let us be steadfast in defending those things which we have learned from the word of God (Matt. 24). This abides forever (Isa. 40), and Christ will not fail (Matt. 28). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XLII.
units.tr: HOMILY XLII.

units.la: 40 Paruerunt autem ei: & cum aduocassent Apostolos, caesis denuntiarunt, ne loquerentur in nomine Iesu & dimiserunt eos.
units.tr: They obeyed him. And when they had called the apostles in and beaten them, they charged them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.

units.la: 41 Ipsi ergo gaudentes profecti sunt a conspectu concilij: quod digni habiti essent, qui pro nomine Iesu contumelia afficerentur.
units.tr: They therefore departed from the presence of the council rejoicing, that they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonour for the name of Jesus.

units.la: 42 Et quotidie in templo & domi non cessabant docere, & Euangelizare Iesum Christum.
units.tr: And daily, in the temple and at home, they did not cease to teach and to preach Jesus Christ.

units.la: Inter ea, quae homines plerosq; remorantur, quo minus ad fidem Christi accedant, praecipuum fere est, quod huius statores perpetuis afflictionibus exerceri vident. Quia enim homo natura sibi bene esse vult, non potest credere eam religionem Deo gratam esse, quae cruci obnoxia est, Matth.13.11. Opus ergo diligenti instructione, quam hic liber exhibet, quo Lucas persecutiones primitiae Ecclesiae & ipsorum Apostolorum describit. Quae ita considerari debent, ut si quid huius accidit, non insolens putemus, neue desperemus mus. Qui olim seruauit, idem faciet,&c. Matt. 28. Argumenta huius consolationis multa vidimus in praesenti historia, cuius exitus modo sequitur.
units.tr: Among the things that hold back most people from coming to faith in Christ, the chief one is that they see its professors constantly harassed by afflictions. For since man by nature wants to be well off, he cannot believe that a religion which is liable to the cross is pleasing to God (Matt. 13.11). There is need, therefore, of the careful instruction which this book provides, in which Luke describes the persecutions of the first Church and of the apostles themselves. These things should be considered in such a way that, if anything of this kind happens to us, we do not think it strange, nor despair. He who once preserved (us) will do so again, etc. (Matt. 28). We have seen many arguments of this consolation in the present history, the outcome of which now follows.

units.la: I. De Senatu dicitur: Paruerunt Gam. vt nimirum non occiderent Apostolos. Interim nō deponunt rabiem, sed cędunt innoxios, & prius edictum renouant. Atqui vtrum q; dissuaserat Gam. Vnde appa ret Oligarchas aliquos fuisse, qui omnia pro suo arbitrio facerent. Sunt hi nocentissimi homines, & fere publicarum calamitatum authores sunt.
units.tr: I. Of the Senate it is said: "They obeyed" (Gamaliel), namely so that they would not kill the apostles. Meanwhile they do not lay down their rage, but beat innocent men and renew the earlier edict. And yet both measures had been advised against by Gamaliel. From this it appears that there were some oligarchs who did everything according to their own will. These are the most harmful men, and they are nearly the authors of public calamities.

units.la: Interim Nota. ¶ Ingenium hostium veritatis. Simulant interdum moderationem aliquam, quasi rationibus cedant: attamen rabiem non deponunt, Iere. 13. Vnde fit, vt nunquam fine ignominia eos dimittant, quos semel coeperunt persequi. Sic Pilatus & Herodes, Luc. 23. Obseruemus hoc, ne aliquid tribuamus illorum consilijs, sed fortes fimus in veritatis defensio ne. Denique caueamus nobis ab hominibus, Mat. 10.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: the nature of the enemies of the truth. Sometimes they feign some moderation, as if they yielded to reasons; yet they do not lay down their rage (Jer. 13). Hence it happens that they never let go of those whom they have once begun to persecute without disgrace. So Pilate and Herod (Luke 23). Let us observe this, so as not to grant anything to their counsels, but to be brave in defending the truth. Finally, let us beware of men (Matt. 10).

units.la: Quoad vero edictum, formulam eius obseruemus: Ne loquantur in nomine Iesu, id est, ne Euangelium Christi praedicent, & in hoc doceant nobis offerri poeniten-tiam & remissionem peccatorum, Luc. 24.
units.tr: As for the edict, let us note its wording: "not to speak in the name of Jesus", that is, not to preach the gospel of Christ; and in this it teaches us that repentance and forgiveness of sins are offered (Luke 24).

units.la: Potest alioqui mundus pœnitentiæ & remissionis doctrinam ferre, & vtramq; genetes quoque tradiderunt. Et inter ludæos Scribæ,Matth 15.23.6.&c. Hodie item in Papatu vtrumq; prædicatur.Sed ea dicuntur,quæ carnis rationi arridēt Pœnitentia tribuitur nostri arbitrij viribus & externis ritibus,Ifa 29 Mar.7.Hos.6.58. Ita remissio in satisfactionibus, quæ doctoribus suis quæstuosæ, aliis autem præstitu faciles sunt.Euangelium autem arguit homînem de peccato,Ioh 16 Gen.5 8. Ps.51. Rom.3 2.Cor 3. Exigit abnegationem nostri,mortificationem carnis, regenerationem,Mat 26.Ioh 3.Col.3 Rom.6. Omnia tamen hæc ex Christo manare docet (2. Cor 5 )vt nos simus inutiles serui,Luc.17 1.Cor.4. Ita quoad satisfactionem, docet corporis exercitia non prodesse (1. Tim. 4.) & traditionibus humanis nō coli Deum,Ifa.29 Mat.15. Ad vnū verò Christum remittit,Act 4 1 Ioh.1.Ioh.14 4.Ifa.42 45. Ista mundo intolerabilia videntur, quia omnes superstitiones damnant, &c. Sed memineris Dei authoritatem omnibus homínibus debere anteponi.
units.tr: Otherwise the world can bear the doctrine of repentance and forgiveness, and the Gentiles too have handed down both. Among the Jews there are the scribes (Matt. 15, 23, 6, etc.). Today likewise both are preached in Papacy. But those things are said which please the reason of the flesh: repentance is attributed to the powers of our own will and to external rites (Isa. 29; Mark 7; Hos. 6). So too forgiveness is attributed to satisfactions, which are profitable to their teachers but easy for others to render. The Gospel, however, convicts man of sin (John 16; Gen. 5, 8; Ps. 51; Rom. 3; 2 Cor. 3). It requires the denial of self, the mortification of the flesh, regeneration (Matt. 26; John 3; Col. 3; Rom. 6). Yet it teaches that all these flow from Christ (2 Cor. 5), so that we are unprofitable servants (Luke 17; 1 Cor. 4). Likewise as to satisfaction, it teaches that bodily exercises do not profit (1 Tim. 4), and that God is not worshipped by human traditions (Isa. 29; Matt. 15). It refers us to Christ alone (Acts 4; 1 John 1; John 14; Isa. 42, 45). These things seem intolerable to the world, because they condemn all superstitions, etc. But remember that God's authority must be placed before the authority of all men.

units.la: II. Quid Apostoli? ¶ 1. Abeunt gaudentes,quod digni, &c. Non fuerunt Stoici, aut qui nullam sui nominis rationem habuerint.
units.tr: II. What did the apostles do? 1. They depart rejoicing, because they were counted worthy, etc. They were not Stoics, nor men who had no regard for their own reputation.

units.la: rint.Gaudent autem, quod propter Christum haec accidissent. Primo enim est hoc ingens beneficiū per fe.Sumus enim peccatores, & supplicijs digni,Rom.3. Psal.13. 143. Magnae ergo gratiae argumentum est, quod Deus nos Filij sui locios facit in crucem, ut per nos suam gloriam afferat, Rom. 8 2.Tim 2 Simile regis & facinorosi.Hoc expenderunt Apostoli,quibus nondū exciderat, quàm turpiter se gesserant, Ioh. 16.Luc.2 Mar.14.1.Cor.15 Deinde recordati sunt promissionum,Matt.5 Iohan.12. Luc.22.eoque magis confirmantur, quod has in Christo impletas viderant, Ioh.14. 16 &c.Ista ad nos transferamus.Et hoc debent considerare,qui quocunq; modo afliguntur : & mox sentient Dei gratiam. Cogita quales hucusq; fuerimus. In religione languidi,& nostra quaerimus.Luxu perditi. Disciplinae impatientes.Quid ergo mirum,si Deus nos punit? At ea gratia dignatur Deus , vt propter suum nomen nos periclitari velit.Simus ergo fortes,[oh 16 Rom.5.&c.
units.tr: They rejoiced, however, that these things had happened on account of Christ. For first, this is in itself a great benefit. We are sinners and deserve punishments (Rom. 3; Ps. 13, 143). It is therefore a proof of great grace that God makes us partners in the cross of his Son, so that through us he may bring forth his glory (Rom. 8; 2 Tim. 2). It is like the case of a king and a criminal. The apostles considered this, having not yet forgotten how shamefully they had behaved (John 16; Luke 22; Mark 14; 1 Cor. 15). Then they recalled the promises (Matt. 5; John 12; Luke 22), and were all the more confirmed because they had seen these fulfilled in Christ (John 14, 16, etc.). Let us apply these things to ourselves. Whoever is afflicted in any way should consider this, and soon they will perceive God's grace. Think what sort of people we have been until now: lukewarm in religion, seeking our own things, ruined by luxury, impatient of discipline. Why then wonder if God punishes us? Yet God deigns to grant such grace that he wills us to be in danger for his name's sake. Let us therefore be brave (Rom. 5, etc.).

units.la: ¶ 2 Non cessárunt docere publicè in tem- plo,& priuatim,&c.Ita faciunt,quod erant protestati,& suo exemplo eos confutant, qui suam ignauiam ed stis principū excu- sant. Deinde eos etiam, qui vbi semel ali-
units.tr: 2. They did not cease to teach publicly in the temple, and privately, etc. They do what they had professed, and by their example they refute those who excuse their cowardice by the edicts of princes. Then also (they refute) those who, once they have suffered something, want to undergo nothing further.

units.la: quid passi sunt,nihil porrò volunt subire. Atqui non est in nostro arbitrio, vt nobis ipsis feriasindicamus. Serui sumus, & ideo nos stare decet succinctos,donec Do minus veniat,Luc.12.Deinde erepti ex pe riculo debemus glorificare Deum. Pf.50. At neutrum faciunt, qui suam stationem deserunt.
units.tr: Yet it is not in our power to declare ourselves released from our duty. We are servants, and so it becomes us to stand with our loins girded until the Lord comes (Luke 12). Then, having been snatched from danger, we ought to glorify God (Ps. 50). But those who desert their post do neither.

units.la: Meditemur ista diligenter. Sunt nouissima tempora. Matthæi 24. Ne communicemus aliorum operibus prauis, 1.Iohan. 2. Apoc.18. Excitet itẽ præmij promissio, Matthæi 25. Et indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: Let us meditate on these things diligently. The last times are at hand (Matt. 24). Let us not share in others' wicked works (1 John 2; Rev. 18). Likewise let the promise of reward stir us (Matt. 25). And let us pray without ceasing.

units.la: CAPVT VI.
units.tr: CAPUT VI.

units.la: HOMILIA XLIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XLIII.

units.la: CAeterum per eos dies, cum multiplicarentur discipuli, ortum est murmur Græcorum aduersus Hebræos, quòd ipsorum viduæ despicerentur in ministerio quotidiano.
units.tr: Now in those days, when the disciples were multiplying, a murmur arose among the Greeks against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily ministry.

units.la: 1 Itaq; duodecim illi, aduocata multitudine discipulorum, dixerunt, Non est æquum nos derelicto sermone Dei, ministrare mensis.
units.tr: 1 Therefore the twelve, calling together the multitude of the disciples, said: "It is not right that we should neglect the word of God and serve tables."

units.la: 3 Despicite ergo fratres, ex vobis viros septem, idoneos testimonio ornatos. tos, plenos spiritu sancto, &c. ad verf. vsque 5.
units.tr: 3 "Look out therefore, brothers, from among you seven men, well attested and full of the Holy Spirit, etc." up to verse 5.

units.la: Vdiuimus primitiuæ Ecclesiæ originem, progressum & formam, vtq; inter perfequutiones omnia secundum Dei verbum optime instituta & administrata fuerint. Sequitur vt in ipsa Ecclesia subito tur ba exorta sit, quæ causam dedit nouæ dispensationis op um Ecclesiæ. Vbi multa traduntur, quæ nos consolari & de Ecclesiæ gubernatione admonere possunt.
units.tr: We have heard of the origin, progress and form of the primitive Church, and how, amid persecutions, everything was most excellently instituted and administered according to the word of God. It follows that a sudden tumult arose within the Church itself, which gave occasion for the new arrangement of the Church's work. Much is set forth here that can console us and admonish us about the government of the Church.

units.la: I. Occasio præmittitur, Cre/cente nume causa pro ro discipulorum, ortum est murmur, &c. Er- go nihil profecerunt suis minis hostes, sed idem factum quod olim Exod. 1. Eftq; hoc perpetuum, &c. Quia autem diuersi confluxerant, non potuerunt diu consentire. Græci enim, id est, qui ex Iudæis inter gentes dispersis nati erant, murmurarunt contra Hebræos, quod ipsorum viduæ (intelligit omnes egenos) negligerentur in quotidiana victus distributione, de qua Act. 4. Factum hoc non malitia, sed quod Apostoli non poterant omnibus sufficere, &c.
units.tr: I. The occasion is set out first: "As the number of the disciples grew, a murmur arose, etc. Therefore the enemies achieved nothing by their threats, but the same thing happened that happened long ago, Exod. 1. And this is perpetual, etc." But because people of different kinds had come together, they could not agree for long. The Greeks, that is, those who had been born of Jews dispersed among the Gentiles, murmured against the Hebrews because their widows (he means all the needy) were neglected in the daily distribution of food, of which we read in Acts 4. This happened not from malice, but because the Apostles could not suffice for everyone, etc.

units.la: Sed Nota. 1. Primitiuam quoque Ecclesiam suis vitijs laborasse, & quidem maximis. 1. Respectu gentis, contra illud,
units.tr: But note: 1. The primitive Church too laboured under its own vices, and indeed the greatest ones. 1. With respect to nation, against that saying,

units.la: Cap 5. Acto.i.Col 3 Gal 3. 2.Factionibus,1.Cor.3 3.Murmur contra Apostolos, qui quotidie pro omnibus laborabant. Non potest ergo Ecclesia sic institui,quin habeat fem per sua vitia. Sumus enim ipsi proclives ad malum, Gen 8. & semper insidiatur Satan,Matth.13 Perpetua ergo cura & studio est opus, Act.20 Ezech.3.2.Tim.4.Arguuntur,qui temere faciunt scisma.
units.tr: Chapter 5 of Acts; Galatians 3; 1 Corinthians 3 (factions); murmuring against the Apostles, who labored daily for all. It is therefore not possible for the Church to be so constituted that it is free of faults on account of its own vices. For we ourselves are prone to evil (Gen. 8), and Satan always lies in wait (Matt. 13). Constant care and diligence are therefore required (Acts 20; Ezek. 3; 2 Tim. 4). Those are rebuked who rashly make a schism.

units.la: 2 Crescente numero hoc factum ita fit, quando nemo potest omnibus satisfacere: & sunt multi natura queruli Sic Mo fi accidit,Exod.5.14 16. Num.11 12.16 &c. Idem nunc Apostoli experiuntur,qui pro culdubio integerrimi fuerunt. Ne mireris ergo, fi hodie murmura audiantur in xenodochijs & tanta mendicantium multitudine.Curent modo omnes, ne ipsi causam iustam praebeant, dum Iudas & Ananias agunt,Ioh.12 Act 5.Periculosa est pecuniae alienae contrectatio.
units.tr: 2. When the number grows, this happens whenever no one can satisfy everyone; and there are many who are naturally querulous. So it happened to Moses, Exod. 5, 14, 16; Num. 11, 12, 16, etc. The Apostles now experience the same thing, though they were without doubt most upright. Do not wonder, then, if today murmurings are heard in the hospices and amid such a great multitude of beggars. Let all only take care that they themselves do not give a just cause, lest they act like Judas and Ananias, John 12; Acts 5. The handling of other people's money is dangerous.

units.la: II.Quid Apostoli.Num obiurgant? num ingratos relinquunt? vel num exfeipsis aliquid instituunt? Aut num dissimulant? Nihil horum: sed coacto coetu consultant publicè,&c.
units.tr: II. What did the Apostles do? Did they rebuke them? Did they abandon the ungrateful? Or did they institute something on their own authority? Or did they dissemble? None of these: but, calling the assembly together, they deliberated publicly, etc.

units.la: Nos. 1 Exemplum omnibus imitandum.1.Ne dissimulétur quae τάξει ordine fiunt, vt hodie,qui ipsem habent in hoc colocatam. locatam. Serpunt mala.2. Non permitten- dum, vt pauci leges condant & dominen tur in Ecclesia,1.Pet. 5. Arguuntur hoc exemplo personati Apostolici. Questus est iam seculis aliquot totus mundus,&c.Ipsi autem negligunt & ridem, aut suas fan- ctiones obtrudunt violenter. Sunt ergo ebriosi œconomi, de quibus Matth.vige- fimo quarto.
units.tr: Our notes: 1. An example to be imitated by all. Things that are done in good order [τάξει] must not be ignored, as today, when those who hold office in this matter... Evils creep in. 2. It must not be allowed that a few men make laws and dominate in the Church, 1 Pet. 5. The masked Apostolics are rebuked by this example. The whole world has now for some centuries complained, etc. But they themselves neglect this and deride it, or they violently force on their own decrees. They are therefore drunken stewards, of whom Matt. 24.

units.la: Sed audiamus Apostolos.
units.tr: But let us hear the Apostles.

units.la: I. Renuntiant officium διακονίας, & ne lites ferant,modeste culpam in fe recipiunt Quasi dicant:Vellemus quidem omnibus seruire,& haftenus fecimus quod potuimus.Sed quia videmus nos non pof fe vtrique satisfacere,necesse est, vt alteri renuntiemus.
units.tr: I. They renounce the office of the ministry [διακονίας], and, so as not to bring on quarrels, they modestly take the blame upon themselves. As if they were saying: "We would indeed wish to serve everyone, and hitherto we have done what we could. But since we see that we cannot satisfy both, it is necessary that we give up the one."

units.la: No T. Dignitatem verbi Dei.Paupe- rum cura sanctissima,Prou 19.Mat.26 25. Et Apostolis maxime cordi fuit, Gal 2. At tamen huic praeferunt verbi ministerium. Maior enim cura habenda animarum quam corporum,Matth.6.Huc faciunt quae habentur Luc.10.1.Corin.1.Examina autem ad hoc exemplum neftros Apostolicos, qui aulas & regna mundi praeferunt verbo Dei,contra illud,Luc.22.
units.tr: Note: the dignity of the Word of God. The care of the poor is most holy, Prov. 19; Matt. 26; 25. It was also especially dear to the Apostles, Gal. 2. Yet they prefer to this the ministry of the Word. For the care of souls must be held greater than that of bodies, Matt. 6. Those things that are found in Luke 10 and 1 Cor. 1 bear on this. Let our Apostolics be examined by this example, who prefer the courts and kingdoms of the world to the Word of God, against that saying, Luke 22.

units.la: 2. Quid fieri debeat? Ordinentur viri fe ptem. Quia hic numerus sufficere videbatur. Et prodest plures eligi,ad cauendam suspicionem,&c.
units.tr: 2. What ought to be done? Let seven men be ordained, since this number seemed sufficient. And it is useful for more to be chosen, to guard against suspicion, etc.

units.la: No T.¶ Quales eligi velint. 1.Ex vobis. Prima ergo ratio fidei habenda. 2.Tc statę probitatis,quibus tuto possit credi. Hue pertinet tota vitæ conuersatio,vt apparet 1.Tim.3.Tit.1.3. Plenos Spiritu sancto,& singularibus donis.4.Sapientes,id est,peritos rerum,&c. Quid hodie? Apud Papi stas inanis titulus restat. Euangelici nolunt habere ex ordine ministrorum. Plerique fidem & Euangelium oderunt,aut saltem odisse incipiunt, & fit quod in Iuda,loh 12. Testatę prodigalitatis.Pleni vino.Inepti & imperiti rationum.Qui tales eligunt,alienis peccatis communicant,1. Tim.5.&c.
units.tr: Note: ¶ What kind of men they wish to be chosen. 1. From among you. The first reason, therefore, is that they must be trusted. 2. Men of established integrity, to whom one may safely entrust things. The whole conduct of life belongs here, as appears from 1 Tim. 3 and Titus 1 and 3. 3. Full of the Holy Spirit, and with extraordinary gifts. 4. Wise, that is, skilled in affairs, etc. What of today? Among the Papists an empty title remains. Evangelicals do not wish to have it from the order of ministers. Many hate the faith and the Gospel, or at least begin to hate it, and it comes to pass as with Judas, John 12. Wasteful of substance. Full of wine. Unskilled and inexperienced in reckoning. Those who choose such men share in others' sins, 1 Tim. 5, etc.

units.la: 2. Repetunt,quid ipsi velint facere, ne videantur otium affectare: Nos incumbemus,&c. Vbi No T.¶ Ministerium Ecclesiæ duobus membris comprehendi.1. Do strina,sub qua & Sacramenta comprehen duntur.His opus,Rom.10 1.Pet.1. Opus studio & vt ritè secetur,1.Tim 4.2.Tim 3.
units.tr: 2. They state again what they themselves wish to do, so that they may not seem to be pursuing leisure: "We will devote ourselves, etc." Here note: ¶ The ministry of the Church is comprised under two heads. 1. Doctrine, under which the sacraments are also included. To this they must give themselves, Rom. 10; 1 Pet. 1. They must give themselves to it with care, and so that it is rightly cut, 1 Tim. 4; 2 Tim. 3.

units.la: 2. Preces, quia nihil proficitur, nisi Deus det incrementum,1 Cor.3. Deinde interceedant pro populo,& stent in ruptura.Sic Moses,Exod.17.32. Num.16.Samuel,1.Samuelis muelis 16 &c. Vide Ezechielis 13. His hodie vacent ministri, & precibus quoque faueat populus, Actorum 4. Ephes. 6. Oremus.
units.tr: 2. Prayers, since nothing is accomplished unless God gives the increase, 1 Cor. 3. Then let them intercede for the people and stand in the breach. So Moses, Exod. 17, 32; Num. 16; Samuel, 1 Sam. 16, etc. See Ezekiel 13. Today let the ministers devote themselves to these things, and let the people also favour them with prayers, Acts 4; Eph. 6. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XLIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XLIV.

units.la: 5 Placuit autem haec oratio toti praesenti multitudini: & elegerunt Stephanum, virum plenum fide & spiritu sancto, & Philippum, & Prochorum, & Nicanorem, & Timonem, & Parmenam & Nicolaum Proselytum Antiochensem.
units.tr: 5 This proposal pleased the whole gathered multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch.

units.la: 6 Quos statuerunt in conspectu Apostolorum : qui cum precati essent, imposuerunt eis manus, & c. ad versum usque 8.
units.tr: 6 These they set before the Apostles, and when they had prayed, they laid their hands upon them, etc., down to verse 8.

units.la: Scriptura non modo virtutes Sanctorum, verumetiam vitia describit, non quidem ut illos infamet, sed ne offendamur si quid simile hodie fit, & ipsi simus cautiores. Debet huc referri quod nuper audiumus de murmure in Ecclesia oborto, vbi multa peccata concurrunt. Apostoli etsi fidelissimi fuerint, peccârunt tamen ignorantia & multitudine negotiorum. Hinc aemulatio & simultas. Sequitur murmur contra optimè meritos. Et hoc inter illos accidit, quorum eadem fuit anima,&c. Nemo igitur offendatur similibus naeuis Ecclesiarum. Interim non dissimulentur hi, sed in tempore occurratur, quod Apostolos fecisse audiuimus. Olten derant in quo erratum,& consulunt quid fieri debeat. Sequitur vt res copofita,&c.
units.tr: Scripture describes not only the virtues of the saints but also their vices. It does not do so to defame them, but so that we will not be offended if something similar happens today, and so that we ourselves may be more cautious. To this belongs what we recently heard about the murmuring that arose in the Church, where many sins came together. The Apostles, although most faithful, nevertheless sinned through ignorance and the multitude of their business. Hence rivalry and enmity. Then comes murmuring against men who deserved very well. And this happened among those whose soul was one, etc. Therefore let no one be offended by similar blemishes in the Churches. Meanwhile these faults should not be ignored, but dealt with in good time, as we hear the Apostles did. They did not know where the error lay, and they consult what ought to be done. Then the matter is settled, etc.

units.la: I. Placuit hic sermo Ecclesiae,&c. Laudandum hoc, quia & iusta erat Petitio,& conueniebat sum Exemplo Christi, Iohannis 12.&13.
units.tr: I. "This proposal pleased the Church," etc. This is to be praised, because the petition was just and agreed with the example of Christ, John 12 and 13.

units.la: NOTA 1. Ecclesiae verae indicium, vt cem pastoris audire(Ioh.10.)nec reluctari Christi exemplo, Pfa.45 Est inexcusabilis contumacia, quando ne videamur erraffe, nihil mutare volumus. Sic Romanenses. Ita Euangelici quidam, qui dum errores receptos tuentur, nouos insuper accumulant. 2. Diaconos a tota Ecclesia electos fuisse. Ergo Ecclesiae totius serui sunt. Imo antiquitus prouehebantur ad altiora,&c. Vide 1. Tim.3. Arguitur nostri seculi mos, quando nulli minus sub Ecclesiae disciplina viuunt.
units.tr: NOTE 1. A mark of the true Church is to hear the voice of the shepherd (John 10), and not to resist the example of Christ, Ps. 45. It is inexcusable obstinacy when, so that we may not seem to have erred, we are unwilling to change anything. So the Romanists. So too some Evangelicals, who, while they defend received errors, pile new ones on top. 2. The deacons were chosen by the whole Church. Therefore they are servants of the whole Church. Indeed, in antiquity they were advanced to higher offices, etc. See 1 Tim. 3. The custom of our age is put to shame, when there are none who live less under the discipline of the Church.

units.la: II. Qui electi Septem. Primus Stephanus plenus fide & Spiritu. Patet quid potissimum fpectarint,&c.
units.tr: II. Who were the seven chosen? First Stephen, full of faith and Spirit. It is clear what they chiefly looked for, etc.

units.la: Sed NOT. Nicolaum quoque nomi nari, qui vxore publicauit, a quo Nicolaitae,
units.tr: But note that Nicolaus too is named, who publicly shared his wife, and from whom come the Nicolaitans,

units.la: 1. Ecclesiae verae indicium: cf. marginal notes. tæ,Apo 2.Poterat hoc offendere,nisi scire mus Ecclesiam Dei proui dentia gubernaö ri,qui patitur improbos obrepere, dum nos dormimus,Mat.13.Sic Iudas inter Apostolos,Ioh 6. Et ita prodest, priori ad Corinthios vndecimo. Discamus: 1. Attenti esse in electone. Si primitiua Ecclesia errauit, quid nobis fit? At qui te merè errat, communicat alienis peccatis, 1. Timoth.5 Obseruandum in ministris, magistratibus, officialibus. 2 Cura opus esse ijs,qui videntur stare,&c. 1.Corinth.10.Prou 24.1.Pet.5 Matth.26.3.Vanam esse gloriationem antecessorum & successionis, ex qua hodie immunitatem captant Romanenses. Sed si valeret argumentum, poterant eo uti Gnostici. Nos non antecessores illorum, sed ipsos accusamus. Et tales fore, olim praedictum, 2. Thess 2.Act 20.2.Pet 2.
units.tr: 1. A mark of the true Church: see the marginal notes. Rev. 2. This could cause offence, unless we knew that the Church of God is governed by providence, which allows the wicked to creep in while we sleep, Matt. 13. So Judas was among the Apostles, John 6. And thus it is of benefit, see 1 Cor. 11. Let us learn: 1. To be attentive in the choice. If the primitive Church erred, what is that to us? But whoever errs alone shares in others' sins, 1 Tim. 5. This is to be observed in ministers, magistrates and officials. 2. There is need of care for those who seem to stand, etc. 1 Cor. 10; Prov. 24; 1 Pet. 5; Matt. 26. 3. The boasting of predecessors and of succession is vain, and the Romanists today seek immunity from it. But if the argument held, the Gnostics could use it too. We accuse not their predecessors but themselves. And that such men would come was foretold long ago: 2 Thess. 2; Acts 20; 2 Pet. 2.

units.la: III. Quomodo inaugurati? Si Stun-tur Apostolis, quorum erat gubernatio Ecclesiae. Ita ergo illis erat agendum, ut possent ratione reddere Apostolis, quorum seueritas eluxerat in Anania, Act 5. Argumentur, qui ministros arcent ab omni insipe ctione bonorum Ecclesiae & pauperum, adeo ut sed ditiosos dicant, &c. At quia ratione possunt hos negligere, quib. tota Ee
units.tr: III. How were they inaugurated? If they were set before the Apostles, whose task was the governance of the Church, then they had to act so that they could give an account to the Apostles, whose severity shone forth in Ananias, Acts 5. They argue, who keep ministers from every concern with the goods of the Church and of the poor, so that they say only the rich ... But for what reason can they neglect those to whom the whole Church

units.la: Diaconi inaugurati tur publi
units.tr: Deacons are installed publicly.

units.la: clefia credita est(lerem.i.Ezech.j. Matth. 24.) cuius præcipua pars sunt pauperes Matth.26. Vide Gal.2.Sed illi Iudam imitantur,Ioh.12.
units.tr: has been entrusted (Jer. 1; Ezek. 3; Matt. 24), the chief part of which are the poor, Matt. 26. See Gal. 2. But they imitate Judas, John 12.

units.la: ¶ 2.Orant pro illis, nimirum vt spiritu donentur & augeantur.Opus hoc in omni ministerio Ecclesiæ, 2.Cor.2.3.Obseruo mus,orandum pro omnibus, qui publica munera obeunt. Vt nofibi solis laborant, ita non sibi foliis peccant. Ante pro Apostolis orârunt,Actor.4. Idem infra,Actor. 12.Et petit hoc Paulus,Eph.6.Ita pro magistratibus,1.Tim.1.Ier.29. Diligens fuit in eo vetus Ecclesia.Tertull.Impij, qui in uident,oderunt.
units.tr: ¶ 2. They pray for them, namely that they may be endowed with the Spirit and increased. This work belongs to every ministry of the Church, 2 Cor. 2 and 3. We observe that one must pray for all who discharge public offices. As they labour not for themselves alone, so they do not sin for themselves alone. The Apostles first prayed for the Apostles, Acts 4. The same below, Acts 12. And Paul asks this, Eph. 6. So too for magistrates, 1 Tim. 1; Jer. 29. The ancient Church was diligent in this. Tertullian: the impious, who envy it, hate it.

units.la: ¶ 3.Manus imponunt. A sacrificijs hoc sumptum, & symbolum erat consecratio-nis & commissionis. Ita certiores fiebant de sua vocatione, & admonebatur se Deo esse sacros. De vtroq; cogitent quicunq; in Ecclesia aut Repub.præsunt, Rom.13.
units.tr: ¶ 3. They lay on hands. This was taken from the sacrifices, and it was a sign of consecration and commission. In this way they were made more certain of their calling, and were reminded that they were holy to God. Let all who preside in the Church or the commonwealth consider both of these, Rom. 13.

units.la: IV. Fructus multiplex. 1 Creuit verbum Dei propagatum scilicet ad alios, & in ijs fructificando qui prius audierant. 2.Hierosolymæ auctus est numerus discipulorum.3.Sacerdotes quoq; accesserunt
units.tr: IV. The fruit is manifold. 1. The word of God grew and spread, namely to others, and bore fruit in those who had heard it before. 2. The number of disciples increased in Jerusalem. 3. Priests also came over.
