units.la: QVoniam Stephanus accusatus fuit, quòd aduersus Mosem, & ab hoc traditum cultum impiè locutus esset, totam Mosis historiam diligenter narrat: partim vt se de illo honorificè sentire ostendat: partim salutem non vllis ceremoniis debere, quando ipsi etiam Mosi omnia obtigerint ex gratia. In hunc finè Mosis natal. educationem: & quàm indignè eum patres reiecerint, expoluit. Sequitur eiusdem vocatio solennis, cuius singulas partes considerabimus, vt euidentius Dei gratia elucescat. Finis omnium, vt Iudæos a cultus Leuitici fiducia ad Christum reuocet.
units.tr: Since Stephen was accused of speaking impiously against Moses and the worship handed down by him, he narrates the whole history of Moses carefully: partly to show that he thinks honourably of him, and partly to show that salvation is owed to no ceremonies, since everything came to Moses himself by grace. To this end he sets out Moses' birth and upbringing, and how unworthily the fathers rejected him. There follows his solemn calling, whose individual parts we will consider, so that the grace of God may shine more clearly. The aim of the whole is to recall the Jews from trust in the Levitical worship to Christ.

units.la: I A tempore & loco orditur. Anno 40. exilij, qui ætatis fuit 89 in deserto apparuit ei Dominus, cùm oues soceri palcebat. Exod. 3. At hoc toto tempore neque templum fuit, neque cultus ille legalis, imò Moses exclusus fuit ab Ifr. Itaque vocatio ista ad solam Dei gratiam referri debet.
units.tr: I. He begins with the time and place. In the fortieth year of the exile, when he was eighty-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him in the desert, while he was tending his father-in-law's sheep. Exod. 3. But during this whole time there was neither the temple nor that legal worship; indeed Moses was excluded from Israel. Therefore this calling must be referred to God's grace alone.

units.la: Interim Not. Mosem, vt primùm populi Dei causam suscepit, exulem, & ex principe ouium pastorem factum fuisse. Vides quid eos maneat, qui relicto mundo, coniungitur Ecclesiæ. Afflictiones inuenient: eo quòd ille luce odit, & separatione hanc ægrè fert. Ioh. 3. & 15. Typ° præ
units.tr: Meanwhile note that Moses, as soon as he took up the cause of God's people, became an exile, and from a prince was made a shepherd of sheep. You see what awaits those who, having left the world, join the Church: they will meet with afflictions, because the world hates that light and bears separation poorly. John 3 and 15. The type

units.la: cessit in Simone Cyre. Mar.15. Et genera le hoc esse, patet Ioh.16. Matt. 26. 2. Tim 3. Act.14. &c. Imo vt Moses etsi a lethrone excipiatur, tamen non est in magno pretio. Ita fere fit exulibus Christi, Mar 10. Iacob, Gen 29.30.31. Quæ tentatio est grauissima. Opus igitur examine diligenti. Luc.24.
units.tr: went before in Simon of Cyrene. Mark 15. That this is the common lot is clear from John 16, Matt. 26, 2 Tim. 3, Acts 14, etc. Indeed, although Moses was received by Jethro, yet he was not held in high esteem. So it generally happens to the exiles of Christ, Mark 10; Jacob, Gen. 29, 30, 31. This is a most grievous temptation. There is need, therefore, of diligent scrutiny. Luke 24.

units.la: ¶ Imitemur autem Mosis modestiam & constantiam, qui tanto tempore ista tulit, haud dubiè var è tentatus. Sed vicit fide, Heb.11. Vincamus & nos fide. 1 Ioh 5. Nec pudeat nos crucis Christi, &c. Phil.2. Erit retributio. Ioh.12. Luc.22. Iohan.14. 2. Tim.2. Isa.64.1. Ioh.3. Phil.3. Ista nos consolentur.
units.tr: Let us imitate, however, the modesty and constancy of Moses, who bore these things for so long, undoubtedly having been tempted. But he conquered by faith, Heb. 11. Let us also conquer by faith, 1 John 5. Let us not be ashamed of the cross of Christ, etc. Phil. 2. There will be a reward: John 12, Luke 22, John 14, 2 Tim. 2, Isa. 64:1, John 3, Phil. 3. Let these things console us.

units.la: II. Quis vocarit? Angelus Domini. Atqui is mox dicet. Ego sum Deus, &c. Item is dicitur, qui fecit prodigia, populum eduxit, &c. Hic vero Christus fuit, 1.Cor. 10. Hunc Steph. angelum dicit, alludens ad Isa. 9 non quod angelos assumpserit (Heb.2.) sed quòda Patre missus, magnum illud consilium Dei de nostra redemptione sit executus, 1.Pet.1. Eph.1.
units.tr: II. Who called him? The angel of the Lord. But he will soon say: I am God, etc. Likewise he is described as the one who performed the wonders and led the people out, etc. Here, however, it was Christ, 1 Cor. 10. Stephen calls him an angel, alluding to Isa. 9; not that he assumed angels (Heb. 2), but that, sent by the Father, he carried out that great counsel of God concerning our redemption, 1 Pet. 1, Eph. 1.

units.la: Quare Not ¶ Christum cum veteribus etiam egisse, nec demum cœpisse, quando ex virgine natus est, Ioh.1. Rom.9. Vidit hunc Abraham, Ioh.8. Daniel. Cap.7. Idem prophetis adfuit, 1. Pet. 1. 2. Pet. 1. Arguit hoc eos, qui veteris testamenti libros reijciunt. Vide Iob 5. Luc 24. 1 Cor. 12. Agnoscamus potius Dei bonitatem, qui ita noft. æ fidei consulit, &c.
units.tr: Therefore note that Christ also dealt with the ancients, and did not only begin when he was born of the virgin, John 1, Rom. 9. Abraham saw him, John 8. Daniel, chap. 7. He was likewise present to the prophets, 1 Pet. 1; 2 Pet. 1. This refutes those who reject the books of the Old Testament. See Job 5, Luke 24, 1 Cor. 12. Let us rather acknowledge God's goodness, who thus cares for our faith, etc.

units.la: II. Modus vocationis: Rubus ardens, qui non consumitur. Voluit sic Mosem atten tumreddere. Interim accommodauit se rei præsenti. Fuit enim hic typus populi, qui ardebat, quasi sub Pharaonis tyranni denon autem consumebatur : quia erat cum illis Filius Dei.
units.tr: II. The manner of the calling: a burning bush, which is not consumed. He wished in this way to make Moses attentive. Meanwhile he accommodated himself to the present situation. For this was a type of the people, who burned, as it were, under the tyranny of Pharaoh, yet were not consumed, because the Son of God was with them.

units.la: No T. ¶ Conditionem Ecclesiæ. Est instar rubi. Imbellis multitudo (Luc. 12. 1. Cor. 1.) sed quam nő facile dissipes, in Christo arctissimè coniunctam, Eph. 4. Ideo ignem subijcit mundus. Permittit Deus. 1. Pet. 1. 3. 4. 1 Cor. 11. Idem tamen eam seruat, &c. Matth. 28. Ioh. 14. Imò consumuntur impij, qui lignorum instar sunt. Vide Zach. 12. Sunt exempla ab exordio rerum, ab inde ab Abelo, Gen. 4. 5. &c. Ista hodie nos consolentur, Ioh. 16.
units.tr: Note. The condition of the Church: it is like the bush. It is an unwarlike multitude (Luke 12; 1 Cor. 1), yet one that you cannot easily scatter, most closely joined to Christ, Eph. 4. Therefore the world sets fire to it, and God permits it: 1 Pet. 1:3–4; 1 Cor. 11. Yet he preserves it, etc. Matt. 28, John 14. Indeed the wicked, who are like the stubble, are consumed. See Zech. 12. There are examples from the beginning of things, from Abel onwards, Gen. 4, 5, etc. These things should console us today, John 16.

units.la: IV. Ipsa vocatio, & huius verba, quibus ista agit. ¶ 1. Seipsum definit, quo minus dubitet Moses. Ego sum Deus Abrahami, &c. Admonet eum fœderis & promissionis, Gen. 17. 12. 13. 15. 22. 26. 28. 35. 46. Docemur ergo, nobis etiam ad veteres promis-
units.tr: IV. The calling itself, and the words by which he acts. 1. He defines himself so that Moses may not doubt: I am the God of Abraham, etc. He reminds him of the covenant and the promise, Gen. 17, 12, 13, 15, 22, 26, 28, 35, 46. We are taught, therefore, that we too must have recourse to the ancient promises.

units.la: Q fiones esse recurrendum. Tam verax enim est, vt ne mortuos quidem negligat, Rom. 8.14. Ita Christus Lazarum dicit suum amicum, Ioh. 11. Quem ergo timeas, quando ne mors quidem nocebit?
units.tr: For he is so faithful that he does not neglect even the dead. Thus Christ calls Lazarus his friend, John 11. Whom, then, should you fear, when not even death will harm you?

units.la: {1}2. Moses cum initio ad spectaculum accedere vellet, & propius intueri, audita Dei voce, territus, vt non poslet attendere, iubetur calceos exuere. Causa, quia locus sanctus sit: nimirum propter Dei praesentiam & vsum. Ita vero ostenditur, Deum & sanctitatem non alligatam esse templo, sed Deum pro sua voluntate se passim manifestare, Ioh. 4. Officij autem nostri esse, vt non simus curiosi res aequo in feruandis Dei mysterijs, sed in eius verbum intenti, affectus pecuinos exuamus, & ipsi nos consecremus totis animis, Ioh. 4,13. Nihil ergo proficiunt, qui Deo gloriantur, indulgent autem sinistris & impuris desiderijs
units.tr: 2. When Moses at first wished to approach the sight and look at it more closely, he was terrified at the voice of God, so that he could not attend, and he is ordered to take off his shoes. The reason is that the place is holy, namely on account of God's presence and use. Thus it is shown that God and holiness are not bound to the temple, but that God manifests himself everywhere at his pleasure, John 4. It is, however, our duty not to be curious beyond measure about the keeping of God's mysteries, but, intent on his Word, to strip off bestial affections and consecrate ourselves with our whole souls, John 4, 13. Those, therefore, who boast of God but indulge their sinister and impure desires accomplish nothing.

units.la: {3}. Testatur se vidisse afflictiones Israelitarum, & ipsum vocat, vt eius opera liberentur. Vidisse se ait, nimirum vt se ostendat ipsis praesentem. Id vero dicit priusquam templum esset, &c.
units.tr: 3. He testifies that he has seen the afflictions of the Israelites, and he calls Moses, so that they may be freed by his work. He says he has seen, namely to show that he is present to them. But he says this before there was a temple, etc.

units.la: Obseruandum Deum non deferere suos, licet ad tempus dissimulet, Psal. 113. 56. 12.145. Sunt exempla passim, Gen. 4. Solentur hæc nos in afflictionibus, 1 Pet. 5. Mat. 6. 10. Luc. 12. Institutioni item seruiant, ne quos affl gamus, qui Deo tam sunt curæ. Exod. 22. Ps 68. Deut. 24, Zach. 2. Oremus
units.tr: It is to be observed that God does not forsake his own, although for a time he may seem to dissemble: Psalm 113; 56; 12; 145. There are examples everywhere, Gen. 4. These things console us in afflictions, 1 Pet. 5, Matt. 6, 10, Luke 12. Likewise they serve as instruction, lest we afflict those who are so dear to God: Exod. 22, Ps. 68, Deut. 24, Zech. 2. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LIII.
units.tr: HOMILY LIII.

units.la: 35 Hunc Mosem, quem abnegauerant, dicentes: Quis te constituit principem & iudicem? hunc inquam Deus principem & redemptorem misit, ductu Angeli, qui visus fuerat ei Rubo.
units.tr: 35 This Moses, whom they had rejected, saying: Who made you ruler and judge? Him, I say, God sent as ruler and redeemer, under the guidance of the angel who had appeared to him in the bush.

units.la: 36 Hic eduxit illos editis miraculis & signis in Aegypto, & in rubro mari, & in deserto, annis quadraginta.
units.tr: 36 This man led them out, performing wonders and signs in Egypt, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness, for forty years.

units.la: 37 Hic est Moses ille, qui dixit filiis Israel, Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus Deus vester, e fratribus vestris, sicut me: eum audite:
units.tr: 37 This is that Moses who said to the sons of Israel: The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, as he raised me; hear him.

units.la: QVamuis Stephanus non aliam tradiderit fidem, quam quæ patribus promissio Seruatore nititur, & quam Moses & Prophetæ prædicarunt, idem tamen, quod ritus externos abolitos diceret, accusatur, quod in Mosem & Patres contumeliosus, fidem nouam doceat. Idem ergo tunc factum, quod hodie, quando similiter qui cum Apostolis unā
units.tr: Although Stephen delivered no other faith than the one that rests on the promised Saviour made to the fathers, and which Moses and the prophets preached, he was nonetheless accused, because he said that the external rites had been abolished, of insulting Moses and the Fathers and teaching a new faith. So what happened then happens today, when those who preach Christ together with the Apostles

units.la: Christum prædicant,&eam fidem, quam Martyres suo sanguine testati sunt, pro hæreticis & Diuorum violatoribus accusantur. Quæ ergo Stephanus pro se dixit,ad nos quoque pertinent, vt disca-mus quibus argumentis ipsi causam no-stram defendamus. Narrat is prolixè,quid Deus cum patrib. egerit,& in primis cum Mose,vt ostendat,se de illo honorificè sen-tire. Deinde docet, ne Mosem quidé sen-se cum ipsis,&c. Et huc facit præsens lo-cus,quo sta tractat.
units.tr: and who defend the faith to which the Martyrs bore witness with their blood are accused of being heretics and violators of the saints. Therefore what Stephen said in his own defence also applies to us, so that we may learn by what arguments we ourselves should defend our cause. He relates at length what God did with the fathers, and above all with Moses, to show that he thought highly of him. Then he teaches that not even Moses thought as they did, etc. And the present passage, which we are now treating, bears on this.

units.la: I. Officium eius denotat, quòd nimi-rum Deus hunc miserit principem & re-demptorem. Fateturautem , quo nihil præstantius dici poterat, & quod vnum poterat ipsum excusare. Ita verò loqui-tur, vt contempti Mosis crimen in ipso-rum patres retorqueat.
units.tr: I. His office is indicated, namely that God sent him as ruler and redeemer. He admits this, and nothing more excellent could be said, and it was the one thing that could excuse him. But he speaks in such a way as to turn the crime of despising Moses back upon their fathers.

units.la: NOT.¶1. De nemine iudicari debere se cundum huius seculi fortuná. Feré enim exaltat eos Deus, quos mundus sastidit Ps.113. Luc.1. Sic Saul.1. Sam.9.10. Dauid, 1.Sam.16 Ps.89 2.Sam 7.Apostoli,1.Cor.1 Matt.4 7.Io.1 7 Soletur hoc abiectos.Hu-mulientur elati,Prou.16.
units.tr: NOTE 1. That no one should be judged by the fortune of this age. For God often exalts those whom the world despises: Ps. 113; Luke 1. So Saul, 1 Sam. 9–10; David, 1 Sam. 16; Ps. 89; 2 Sam. 7; the Apostles, 1 Cor. 1; Matt. 4; 7; John 1. This comforts the abject. The proud are humbled, Prov. 16.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quomodo Moses fuerit redem-ptor? In manu Angeli. Atqui is Christus-fuit,1.Cor.10. Ergo Mosi nihil quàm mini sterium
units.tr: ¶ 2. How was Moses a redeemer? In the hand of the angel. Yet that one was Christ, 1 Cor. 10. Therefore to Moses there is nothing but the ministry.

units.la: ¶ Idem sterium debetur, Christo autem omnis gloria. Agnouerunt hoc omnes sanctiPs. 8. Vide 1.Cor.3.4.15. 2.Cor.5.&c. Obseruandum hoc in omnibus sanctis, &c. Discamus ipsi quoque humiliter de nobis ipsis sentire, nec dicamus, Manus nostra, &c. Dan.4 1.Cor.4.
units.tr: The same ministry is owed; but all glory belongs to Christ. All the saints acknowledged this, Ps. 8. See 1 Cor. 3, 4, 15; 2 Cor. 5, etc. This is to be observed in all the saints, etc. Let us too learn humbly to think of ourselves, and let us not say, "Our hand has done this," etc. Dan. 4; 1 Cor. 4.

units.la: II. Quid fecerit Moses? Eduxit eos edens prodigia, &c. Nihil ergo dissimulat. Ita nos nihil dissimulemus eorum, quæ Deus per suos sanctos agit. Psal.150. ¶ 1. In Aegypto, vbi quædam facta, vt probaret suam vocationem, Exod. 4. Secutæ plagæ, Sanguis, Exod.7. Ranæ. Pediculi. Infecta, Exod.8. Lues pecoris, vlcera, Grando Exod.8. Lo custæ. Tenebræ, Exod.19. Primogenita cæsa, Exod.11.12. Obseruemus, quàm facile sit Deo coercere tyrannos potentissimos. Est Dominus exercituum. Omnia potest armare in hostium perniciem. Phi-list 1.Sam.4 5. Antioch.2. Machab.9. Herod. Act.12.&c.
units.tr: II. What did Moses do? He led them out, performing wonders, etc. He therefore conceals nothing. So let us conceal nothing of what God does through his holy ones. Ps. 150. ¶ 1. In Egypt, where certain things were done so that he might prove his calling, Exod. 4. Then followed the plagues: blood, Exod. 7; frogs; lice; infestation; the murrain of livestock; ulcers; hail, Exod. 8; locusts; darkness, Exod. 10; the firstborn slain, Exod. 11–12. Let us observe how easily God restrains the most powerful tyrants. He is the Lord of hosts. He can arm all things for the destruction of his enemies. The Philistines, 1 Sam. 4–5; 2 Macc. 9; Herod, Acts 12, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. In mari rubro, Exod.14. Psal.115 Potest ergo iuuare per ea, quæ noxia videntur & hostes punire per sua præsidia. Nullis ergo aduersis deijciamur, neque secundis efferamur, quando Deus rerum vices tam facilè mutat.
units.tr: ¶ 2. In the Red Sea, Exod. 14; Ps. 115. He can therefore help through the very things that seem harmful, and punish enemies through their own defences. Let us therefore not be cast down by adversity, nor puffed up by prosperity, since God changes the course of events so easily.

units.la: ¶ 3. In deserto. Manna & coturn. Exo.16
units.tr: ¶ 3. In the wilderness. Manna and quails, Exod. 16.

units.la: Aqua ex petra, Exo.17. Num.20. 1.Cor.10. Amelek, Exod.17. Balaam, Num.22.23. &c. Quibus adde Num.12. 14.16.21. Deutero.
units.tr: Water from the rock, Exod. 17; Num. 20; 1 Cor. 10. Amalek, Exod. 17. Balaam, Num. 22–23, etc. To these add Num. 12, 14, 16, 21; Deut.

units.la: 8. Haec cum omnia Stephanus agnoscat, vtique Mosi nihil derogauit. Ipsi autem erraruntdum non obseruauerunt finem omnium, quae per illum facta sunt. Idem error hodie multos decipit, quoad Diuorum cultum, &c.
units.tr: 8. Since Stephen acknowledges all these things, he certainly took nothing away from Moses. But they erred, because they did not observe the end of all the things that were done through him. The same error deceives many today, regarding the worship of the saints, etc.

units.la: III. Quae Mosis doctrina fuerit? H.dip, se est qui dixit, &c. Deut. 18. Ostendit tam abesse, vt Moses docuerit externis sacris fidere, vt potius relegarit ad Prophetam, &c. Prohibentur illic artes fatidicae, & remittuntur ad verbum Dei. Neue haesitarent, promittit prophetas. Horum quia caput est Christus, rectè de eo locus expo-nitur. Sic Petrus, Act. 3.
units.tr: III. What was Moses' teaching? This is he who said, etc. Deut. 18. He shows that Moses by no means taught that one should trust in external rites, but rather referred the people to the Prophet, etc. Magical arts are forbidden there and the people are referred to the word of God. Lest they hesitate, he promises prophets. Since Christ is their head, this passage is rightly explained of him. So Peter, Acts 3.

units.la: NOT. 1. Christi descriptionem. Efra tribus vestris. Sic promissiones, Gen.22 26 28. Rom.9. Verus ergo homo, potuit causam nostram suscipere. Prophetam verè dicit, quia non modo nos redimere, sed de Patris voluntate edocere debuit, Isaiae 61. Iohan.1. Mar.1. Luc.5. Sicut ME. Vt Moses reliquit opes propter fratres, sic Christus, Phil.2. Vt Moses à suis reiectus, sic Christus, Ioh.1. Vt illius ministerium probatum signis: sic habemus, Isa.35. Ioh.5.20. Vt ille ex Ægypto liberauit: sic hic ex dia
units.tr: NOTE 1. The description of Christ. From among your brothers. So too the promises, Gen. 22, 26, 28; Rom. 9. He was therefore a true man, able to take up our cause. He is rightly called a Prophet, because he had to redeem us and also to teach us the will of the Father, Isa. 61; John 1; Mark 1; Luke 5. "As me." As Moses left his wealth for his brothers, so Christ, Phil. 2. As Moses was rejected by his own, so Christ, John 1. As that man's ministry was confirmed by signs, so ours is, Isa. 35; John 5:20. As Moses freed from Egypt, so this one freed us from the power of the devil, Gen. 3; John 14:16.

units.la: Mosis doctrina. Christi descriptio. boli potestate,Gen.3. Ioh.14.16.Vt Moses turò deduxit, pauit:ita Christus, Ioh.10. 6 4.7. Vt Moses interpres inter Deum & populum:Ita Christus,Ioh.1.15.Vt Moses intercessit, Exod.32. itaChristus, 1.Tim. 12.Ioh.2.Heb.2.4.5.
units.tr: Moses' teaching. Description of Christ. As Moses both led and fed the people, so Christ, John 10; 6:4, 7. As Moses was the interpreter between God and the people, so Christ, John 1:15. As Moses interceded, Exod. 32, so Christ, 1 Tim. 2; John 2; Heb. 2, 4, 5.

units.la: 2.Officium nostrum: Ipsum audite.Ad ditur poena, Deut. 18. Actor.3. Sic patet Matth. 17. Requiritur autem fides & obedientia,Roman.116.2.Corinth.10. Alio- qui non prodest audiuisse. Matth.7. Luc. 8. Ita vero arguit Iudaeorum contumaciam, qui Mosi non obtemperent. Idem de pseudochristianis hodie dici potest, quoad Diuos, quorum cultores dici volunt.De nobis item,qui cum vno Christo gloriemur,eum tamen non audimus.Malachiae 1.Oremus.
units.tr: 2. Our duty: "Hear him." A penalty is added, Deut. 18; Acts 3. This is plain from Matt. 17. Faith and obedience are required, Rom. 1:16; 2 Cor. 10. Otherwise it does no good to have heard, Matt. 7; Luke 8. So indeed he argues against the obstinacy of the Jews, who do not obey Moses. The same can be said today of pseudo-Christians regarding the saints, whose worshippers they wish to be called. It applies also to us, who glory in the one Christ and yet do not hear him. Malachi 1. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LIV.
units.tr: HOMILY LIV.

units.la: 38 Hic ille est, qui fuit in congregatione in deserto, cum Angelo,qui loquebatur ei in monte Sina, & cum patribus nostris, quique excepit viua eloquia,quae nobis traderet,
units.tr: 38 This is he who was in the congregation in the wilderness with the Angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers; who received the living oracles to give to us,

units.la: 39 Cui noluerunt auscultare patres nostri, sed repulerunt eum,& auersi sunt corde suo in Aegyptum,
units.tr: 39 to whom our fathers would not be obedient, but thrust him from them, and turned aside in their hearts to Egypt,

units.la: 40 Dicentes Aharaoni, Fac nobis Deos,qui praecant nobis, Mosi enim illi, qui eduxit nos nos e terra Aegypti, nescimus quid contigerit.
units.tr: 40 saying to Aaron, Make us gods who shall go before us; for as for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we know not what has happened to him.

units.la: 41 Et vitulum fecerunt per illos dies, obtulerunt que sacrificium idolo, & obleCtaverunt se in operibus manuum suarum.
units.tr: 41 And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

units.la: QVoniam Iudaei omnem salutis fiducia in externis ceremonis habebant, & ita patrum religione gloriabantur, impietatis in Deum, Mosem & patres accusabant eos omnes, qui aduersus illas aliquid docebant, & ad vnum Christum relegabant. Sensit hoc Stephanus, qui vt se purgaret, inter alia Mosem magnifice praedicarat, simulque quam indigne a patribus habitus sit docet. Finis, vt Mosis contempti crimen cum in patres, tum in ipsos retorqueat, qui similiter periculo reijciant Christum, &c. Deut. 18. Ex eo sequitur, patres olim ex misericordia gratuita seruatos fuisse propter Christum, & proinde ipsis quoque hanc vnam salutis rationem reliquam esse. Eodem praesens locus facit.
units.tr: Since the Jews placed all their hope of salvation in external ceremonies, and gloried in the religion of their fathers, they accused of impiety towards God, Moses and the fathers all those who taught anything against those ceremonies, and referred everything to Christ alone. Stephen perceived this. In order to clear himself, among other things he had praised Moses magnificently, and at the same time shows how unworthily he was treated by the fathers. His purpose is that the crime of despising Moses should be turned back both upon the fathers and upon themselves, who in the same way were in danger of rejecting Christ, etc. (Deut. 18). From this it follows that the fathers of old were saved by free mercy on account of Christ, and therefore that this is the one remaining way of salvation for them too. The present passage makes the same point.

units.la: I. De legis promulgatione agit, vt Mosem amplius commendet. 1. Fuit in Ecclesia in deserto. Comprehendit historiam 40 annorum, quibus Patrum mores fuistinuit mira patientia. Num. 11. 12. 2. Familiter egit cum Angelo,Christo scilicet:1.Cor. 10. In eo superauit omnes prophetas, Num.12. Vide Exod 10.24.
units.tr: I. He speaks of the promulgation of the law, in order to commend Moses further. (1) He was in the Church in the wilderness. He takes in the history of forty years, during which he endured the manners of the fathers with wonderful patience (Num. 11, 12). (2) He conversed familiarly with the Angel, namely Christ (1 Cor. 10). In this he surpassed all the prophets (Num. 12). See Exod. 10:24.

units.la: 3. Accepit verbum viuum vt nobis, &c. Italoquitur,vt Legem abs fe contemni ne get.Et Legem dicit sermonem viuum:pri mo quia recte viuendi regulâ tradit cum vitæ promissione,Deut.4 6.7. Leuit.1 18. deinde quia ad Christum ducit,in quo vita est,Gal.3.Ioh.1.6.Hinc illa Deut.30.Pf. 1 19 119.&c.Quod alibi dicitur peccati & mortis mysterium(1.Cor 15.2.Cor.3.)Fit per accidens propter nos,Rom 7.8.
units.tr: (3) "He received the living word to give to us," etc. He speaks in this way so that the law may not be despised by them. And he calls the law a living word: first, because it hands down the rule of living rightly together with the promise of life (Deut. 4:6–7; Lev. 18); then because it leads to Christ, in whom is life (Gal. 3; John 1:6). Hence those words of Deuteronomy 30 and Psalm 119, etc. What is said elsewhere, that the law is the mystery of sin and death (1 Cor. 15; 2 Cor. 3), comes about only incidentally because of us (Rom. 7–8).

units.la: Sed Not. ¶ Quod Moses legem accepit,quam nobis traderet. Loquitur enim Stephanus in persona Ecclesiæ & omnium Christianorum. Confutantur ergo, qui hæc ad nos pertinere negant.Vt enim æternus est Deus,ita etiam eius voluntas, Pfal.33. Isa.40.Matth.5.Sunt quidem abrogatæ umbræ, quia neq; in his salus consistebat,(Pf.50.Rom 14 1.Tim.4.) neq; per petuò debebant durare,Hebr.9. Interim firma & rata manent,quæcunq; de fide,de vero vnius Dei cultu,de morum sanctitate traduntur.Confer.In primis quæ ad mores spectant,1.Theff.4.Eph.1.5.1.Cor.5.6. 10. Nemo ergo seipsum fallat vana persuasione,Gal.6.
units.tr: But note: that Moses received the law which he was to give to us. For Stephen speaks in the person of the Church and of all Christians. Those therefore are refuted who deny that these things pertain to us. For as God is eternal, so also is his will (Ps. 33; Isa. 40; Matt. 5). The shadows indeed have been abrogated, because salvation did not consist in them (Ps. 50; Rom. 14; 1 Tim. 4), nor were they to last forever (Heb. 9). Meanwhile, whatever is taught about faith, about the true worship of the one God, and about the holiness of morals, remains firm and valid. Compare especially what pertains to morals (1 Thess. 4; Eph. 1, 5; 1 Cor. 5, 6, 10). Let no one therefore deceive himself with a vain persuasion (Gal. 6).

units.la: II. Opponit patrum contumaciam, qui Mosem & legem indignissime rejecerint. Ex multis vero vituli aurei historiam alle gat Exod.32. Finis, vt intelligant, patres ex misericordia gratuita seruatos fuisse, qua ipsis etiam opus fit, cum illos imitentur.
units.tr: II. He sets against this the obstinacy of the fathers, who rejected Moses and the law most unworthily. From many instances he cites the history of the golden calf (Exod. 32). His purpose is that they may understand that the fathers were saved by free mercy, which they too need, since they are to imitate them.

units.la: Sed totius negotij progressum Noт. 1. Initium mali: Noluerunt obedire, sed cordibus auersi sunt in Aegyptum, id est, ad abominationes, quibus assueuerant. Horrendum, quod & seruitutis & liberationis tam cito obliti sunt. Ita hodie multi quoad papatum. Obseruemus autem omnis malì fontem esse, nolle obedire Deo. Simile filij contumacis. Vide Ieremiae quadragesimo tertio, & quadragesimo quarto. Sic multi hodie.
units.tr: But note the progress of the whole affair. 1. The beginning of evil: they were unwilling to obey, but in their hearts turned aside to Egypt, that is, to the abominations to which they had been accustomed. It is dreadful that they forgot so quickly both their slavery and their deliverance. So today many do with regard to the papacy. Let us observe, moreover, that the source of every evil is to be unwilling to obey God, like a stubborn child. See Jeremiah 43 and 44. So many do today.

units.la: 2. Mosis contemtus. Fatentur beneficium, nesciunt tamen quid ei acciderit. Atqui viderant abeuntem, & habebant commissum, Exodi vigesimo quarto. Ita semper verbi contemptum sequitur contemptus ministrorum, & iniqua de his iudicia. Matthaei vndecimo. Vulgare hodie, vt vt multi protestentur. Sed Dei contemptores sunt.
units.tr: 2. The contempt of Moses. They confess the benefit, yet they do not know what has happened to him. And yet they had seen him going up and had been entrusted with his charge (Exod. 24). Thus contempt for the Word is always followed by contempt for ministers and by unjust judgments about them (Matt. 11). This is common today, even though many protest otherwise. But they are despisers of God.

units.la: 3. Facnobis Deos, &c. Absurda petitio. Sed signum fieri voluntquo de praesenti senti auxilio Dei certiores fiant, & ad quod dirigantur. Et quia semel recefle-runt à Dei verbo, suas intentiones fecu-ti,vitulum faciunt, vt in Ægypto didice-runt. Multiplex scelus. i. Dubitant de Dei præsentia, cuius tot signa viderant. Exo-di duodecimo, decimo tertio,decimo no no,vigesimo quarto, &c. 2. Contra Dei mandatum faciunt idolum, &c. Psal. 106. Hinc vero omnis idololatria, quod non contenti ijs,per quas nobis se Deus reue-lat,noua ex seipsis fingunt. Sic Rom.i.Ita inter Christianos, quando neq; Dei verbo, neque Sacramentis per hunc traditis contenti fuerunt. Dicunt imagines esse libros laicorum, contra id quod Deus nos ex verbo suo vult discere,Hab.2. Deinde Christum habere volunt visibilem, palpabilem & præsentem corporaliter, contra illud Iohannis decimo sexto, &c. Applica Cænæ, ex qua idolum factum contra verum vsum, de quo priori ad Corinthios vndecimo. Itaque nos verbo insistamus, Sacramentis vtamur, prout Deus illa instituit,non fingamus nouos vsus.
units.tr: 3. "Make us gods," etc. An absurd request. They wish for a sign by which they may be more certain of God's present help, and to which they may direct themselves. And because they had once departed from the Word of God, following their own intentions, they make a calf, as they had learned in Egypt. A manifold sin. (i) They doubt the presence of God, whose many signs they had seen (Exod. 12, 13, 19, 24, etc.). (2) Against God's command they make an idol (Ps. 106). Hence comes all idolatry: since men are not content with those means through which God reveals himself to us, they invent new things out of themselves. So Rom. 1. So among Christians, when they were not content either with the Word of God or with the sacraments instituted through it. They say that images are the books of the laity, against what God wills us to learn from his word (Hab. 2). Then they wish to have Christ visible, tangible, and corporeally present, against that saying of John 16, etc. Apply this to the Lord's Supper, from which an idol was made against its true use, of which the earlier passage in the first letter to the Corinthians, chapter 11, speaks. Therefore let us hold to the Word, use the sacraments as God instituted them, and not invent new uses.

units.la: ¶ 4. Immolârunt idolo. Atqui Dei cultu profeisi sunt,Exo.32. Sed quia neq; Deus erat, neque imago Dei, nihil quàm idolum erat. Arguuntur, qui idololatriam
units.tr: ¶ 4. They sacrificed to the idol. And yet they had professed themselves to the worship of God, Exod. 32. But since God was neither present nor an image of God, it was nothing but an idol. Those are rebuked who

units.la: zeli prætextu excusant. In idolis hæretomnis cultus. Imò redundat ad dæmones, 1.Cor.10.
units.tr: excuse idolatry under the pretext of zeal. In idols all worship clings. Indeed it flows back to demons, 1 Cor. 10.

units.la: ¶5. Lætati sunt in operibus manuum suarum. Loquitur primò de fiducia & gaudio, quæ in solo Deo quæri debent. Hinc illæ voces. Isti sunt Dij tui, &c. Deinde de ludis illicitis, qui secuti sunt. Comitantur hi idololatriam, Num. 25. Hof. 4. Hæc si conferas cum Papatu, planè eadem videbis, & eundem progressum, finem, &c. Liberauit nos Deus. Simus ergo grati, & ipsum colamus in spiritu & veritate, Ioh. 4. Oremus.
units.tr: ¶5. They rejoiced in the works of their hands. He speaks first of the trust and joy that must be sought in God alone. Hence those words: These are your gods, etc. Then he speaks of the unlawful games that followed. These accompany idolatry, Num. 25, Hos. 4. If you compare these things with the Papacy, you will see plainly the same, and the same progress and end, etc. God has freed us. Let us therefore be thankful, and worship him in spirit and truth, John 4. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LV.
units.tr: HOMILY LV.

units.la: 42 Auertit autem se Deus, & tradidit eos in seruitutem exercitus cœli, sicut scriptum est in libro Prophetarum: Numquid victimas & hostias obtulistis mihi per annos quadraginta in deserto, domus Israel?
units.tr: 42 But God turned away and delivered them up to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the Prophets: Did you offer victims and sacrifices to me for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?

units.la: QVoniam homo animalis non percipit ea, quæ sunt spiritus Dei, religionem quoque in externis collocat, & Deum ijsdem, quæ nos oblectant, gaudere putat. Hinc multiplex error. 1. Abutitur à Deo institutis ritibus. 2. Noua ex se fingit. 3. Si qui dissentiant, eos odit, & hostes diuini cultus esse clamat. Ista omnia in Iudaeis videmus, in primis vero postremo hoc. Vt enim Christum accusarunt, quasi templum vellet euertere. Ita Stephanus quoque: quem grauarunt insuper patrum authoritate. Vt ergo se excusat, diligenter loquitur de Patriarchis & Mose, qui omnes in vnum Christum respexerint. Deinde docet, quales fuerint patres reliqui post Legem, vt intelligant, hos quoque ex gratuita misericordia fuisse seruatos. Et huc facit historia vituli, Exod. 32. Ne autem dicerent, sihi haec immerito exprobrari, amplius docet, posteros omnes patrum similes fuisse, & olim quoque de eo quesstum fuisse Deum, imo puniuisse. Finis, vt intelligant, quid ipsis sperandum, si pergant, &c. Heb. 10.
units.tr: Since natural man does not perceive the things of the Spirit of God, he also places religion in external things, and thinks that God delights in the same things that delight us. Hence there is a manifold error: (1) he abuses the rites instituted by God; (2) he invents new ones of his own; (3) if anyone disagrees, he hates that person and cries out that he is an enemy of the divine worship. We see all these things in the Jews, and especially the last. For they accused Christ as though he wanted to overthrow the temple, and so did Stephen, whom they further burdened with the authority of the fathers. So, in order to excuse himself, he speaks carefully about the patriarchs and Moses, all of whom, he says, looked to the one Christ. Then he teaches what sort the remaining fathers after the Law were, so that they may understand that these also were preserved by free mercy. The story of the calf (Exod. 32) bears on this. And lest they should say that these charges were unjustly brought against them, he teaches further that all their descendants were like the fathers, and that God had complained of this of old, and indeed punished it. The purpose is that they may understand what they themselves may expect if they persist (Heb. 10).

units.la: I. Progressum idololatriae exponit: Constituitque autem se Deus, &c. Non reijcit in Deum culpam, sed ex praemisis infert. Quia illi tam aperte rebellarunt, & cor-repti non repuerunt, sed idem murmurarunt, Deus quoque iusto iudicio se auertit, & illos suo arbitrio permisit. Itaque coluerunt militiam caeli, & facti sunt gentium similes, qui debebant Dei peculium esse. Vide historiam Baalpeor, Num. 25. Baalim Iudic. 2. Aftaroth, primo Samuelis.
units.tr: I. He sets out the progress of idolatry: "And God turned away," etc. He does not lay the blame on God, but infers it from what has gone before. Because they rebelled so openly, and when corrected did not repent but went on murmuring, God too in his just judgment turned away and left them to their own will. And so they worshipped the host of heaven and became like the nations, though they ought to have been God's own possession. See the history of Baal-peor (Num. 25), Baalim (Judg. 2), Ashtaroth (1 Sam. 7).

units.la: leptimo. Item primo Regum vndecimo, duodecimo,decimo sexto. In Iuda Amasias Dos Idumaeorum,fecundo Paralipo menon vigefimo quinto. Syrorum Achas inuexit, fecundo Paralipomenon vicesimo octauo. Manasses omnem gentilium,fecundo Regum vicesimo primo. A quo tempore non potuit vnquam eradicari,Sophoniae primo, Ieremiae quadragesimo quarto. Post reditum ex Babylone, Philosophiam introduxerunt(primo Machabaeorum primo)accersiuerunt Antiochum,& palam defecerunt. Et licet Stephani tempore non effent idola, tamen templum,& sacra sibi idola fecerunt. Ista omnia hic exprobrat, vt ostendat, non habere eos,quo glorientur,sed gratię Dei opus esse,quod non perierint.
units.tr: Seventh. Likewise 1 Kings 11, 12, 16. In Judah, Amaziah brought in the gods of the Edomites (2 Chron. 25). Ahaz brought in the gods of the Syrians (2 Chron. 28). Manasseh brought in all the practices of the Gentiles (2 Kings 21), from which time it could never be uprooted (Zeph. 1; Jer. 44). After the return from Babylon they introduced philosophy (1 Macc. 1) and summoned Antiochus, and openly fell away. And although in Stephen's time there were no idols, nonetheless they made for themselves the temple and sacred things as idols. He reproaches them with all these things here, to show that they have nothing to boast of, and that it is the work of God's grace that they have not perished.

units.la: NOTA. Quid ijs fiat, qui verbo Dei relicto,suis sensibus indulgent, & hos sapientiae Dei praeferunt. Auertit fe ab illis Deus, & tradit in reprobum sensum. Sic factum gentibus,ad Romanos primo,Pfal mo 115. Inter Christianos, posteriori ad Thessalonicenses secundo. Hinc absurditas idolorum, ἀπολατρεία, peregrinationes, impudens fcortatio,&c. Idem fit, quoad mores, fi qui nolunt Deum audire.Nihil tam turpe,noxium, quod horreant. -ant.Experimur hodie,quoad luxum & ebrietatem. Audiamus Deum nobis loquentem,& in primis cordi sint,quę Christus dicit,Mat.24.Luc.17.21.Isa 5.Eccl.10. Caueamus nos & Oremus.
units.tr: NOTE. Consider what happens to those who, leaving the Word of God, indulge their own senses and prefer these to the wisdom of God. God turns away from them and gives them over to a reprobate mind. This happened to the Gentiles (Rom. 1; Psalm 115), and among Christians it is described in 2 Thessalonians 2. Hence come the absurdity of idols, idolatrous worship [ἀπολατρεία], wanderings, shameless fornication, etc. The same happens in morals to those who are unwilling to hear God: nothing is so shameful or harmful that they shrink from it. We see it today in luxury and drunkenness. Let us hear God speaking to us, and let us take most to heart what Christ says (Matt. 24; Luke 17:21; Isa. 5; Eccl. 10). Let us be on our guard. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LVI.
units.tr: HOMILY LVI.

units.la: 42 — Num quid vitulinas & hostias obtulistis mihi per annos quadraginta in deserto, domus Israel?
units.tr: 42 — Did you offer me slain beasts and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?

units.la: 43 Et bajulastis tabernaculum Moloch, & sydus Dei veștri Remphan, quas figuras fecistis vt eas adoraretis. Itaque transferam vos trans Babylonem.
units.tr: 43 Yea, you carried the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of your god Remphan, the figures which you made in order to worship them. Therefore I will carry you away beyond Babylon.

units.la: INter ea quæ homines remorantur, ne ad veram Christi fidem accedant, præcipuum est,patrum exemplum. Metuunt enim ne hos damnent,si ipsi aliam religionem sequantur. Ideo olim prophetis patres obijciebant. Amos 2. Ezechielis vigesimo. Christo,Iohannis sexto. Et Stephano hoc ipsum fuisse obiectum, ex eius apologia apparet, qua primo de Abraham agit, & hunc non aliter quàm fide iustificatum esse docet,Iohannis 8. Deinde quia patribus, qui legem secuti erant, maximè gloriabantur, hos quoque per legem adeo non seruatos esse ostendit,
units.tr: Among the things that keep men from coming to the true faith of Christ, the chief is the example of the fathers. For they fear that, if they follow another religion, they will condemn their forebears. So in former times the fathers were thrown in the face of the prophets (Amos 2, Ezekiel 20), of Christ (John 6), and of Stephen. That this same objection was made to Stephen is clear from his speech, in which he first speaks of Abraham and teaches that he was justified by faith alone and in no other way (John 8). Then, because the Jews gloried above all in the fathers who had followed the law, he shows that these too were by no means kept by the law,

units.la: vt potiús excidium meruerint. Itaq; hoc etiam ex gratuita misericordia fuisse servatos. Id probat per historiam aurei vitu-li, Exod. 32. Et ne hanc nihil ad se pertinere dicerent, paucis comprehendit quae cunque patres deinceps fecerint, &c. Finis omnium, falsò illos lege gloriari, cum hanc nunquam seruauerint.
units.tr: so that they deserved destruction rather than salvation. Therefore they were saved by free mercy. He proves this from the history of the golden calf (Exod. 32). And lest they should say that this has nothing to do with them, he briefly sums up whatever the fathers afterwards did, and so on. The conclusion is that they were wrongly boasting of the law, since they had never kept it.

units.la: ¶ At ne quid negarent, ipsius Dei testimonio eos convincit, qui de illis olim fit conquestus. Et ex multis locis adducit Amos 5. Accusauit propheta idololatriam & scelera, atq; poenas minatus est. Objicie-bant illi patres & longi temporis praescriptum. Ostendit ergo ista nihil iuuare, eò quòd patres semper fuerint rebelles, & horum ipsos esse imitatores. Tria autem dicit.
units.tr: ¶ But lest they deny anything, he convicts them by the testimony of God himself, who long ago complained about them. He adduces many passages, from Amos 5 in particular. The prophet accused them of idolatry and crimes and threatened punishments. Those fathers also objected the prescription of long time. He shows, therefore, that these things do not help them, because the fathers were always rebels, and they themselves are imitators of them. He says three things.

units.la: I. Negat patres vnquam fuisse veri Dei cultores, ideoq; frustra ipsos his gloriari. Interrogatione vrget, & temporis in de-ferto meminit, vt amplificet scelus. Quasi diceret: Leue esset, si tandem meorum operum immemores peccauissetis: sed ec-ce toto illo tempore 40. annorum in de-ferto, cùm beneficiorum & operum meo-rum memoria recens adhuc esset, fuistis ingratissimi, neq; vnquà mihi sacrificastis.
units.tr: I. He denies that the fathers were ever true worshippers of God, and so he shows that they boast of this in vain. He presses the point with a question and recalls the time in the wilderness in order to magnify the sin. As if he said: It would be a light matter if you had at last forgotten my works; but see, during that whole time of forty years in the wilderness, when the memory of my benefits and works was still fresh, you were most ungrateful and never sacrificed to me.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Vtḣæc debeant accipi Nam constat illos non alium Deum professos fuisse, quàm qui ex Ægypto eduxerat. Exod 32. Ab eodem acceperant sacra, & non tum est illud Pauli 1. Cor. 10. Sed oportet distinguere inter verum vsum sacrorum & hoc quod ipsi faciebant. Quoad illum, adumbrabant Christi & redemptionis no stræ mysteria: & in hæc pij respiciebant. Circumcisio, ad Colossenses 2 Pascha, 1. Corin. 5. Sacrificia, Iohannis 1. Hebr 9 10. &c. At plerique externis intenti, ista negligebant. Itaque lusus erat quod faciebant, & Deus vt nihil ad se pertinens reij cit, &c. Ieremiæ 4. Psalmo 50. Isaiæ 1. Micheæ 6. Isa. 66.
units.tr: NOTE. How these things ought to be understood: it is certain that they professed no other God than the one who had led them out of Egypt (Exod. 32). They had received the sacred rites from the same God, and that saying of Paul (1 Cor. 10) does not apply here. But one must distinguish between the true use of the sacred rites and what they themselves did. As to the former, the rites foreshadowed the mysteries of Christ and our redemption, and the godly looked to these. Circumcision (Col. 2), the Passover (1 Cor. 5), the sacrifices (John 1; Heb. 9, 10), and so on. But most people, intent on externals, neglected these things. Hence what they did was a game, and God rejected it as irrelevant to himself (Jer. 4; Ps. 50; Isa. 1; Micah 6; Isa. 66).

units.la: Obseruemus nullum cultum probari Deo qui non ex fide secundùm ipsius verbum exercetur. Sine fide Deo placere im possibibile est, Hebr. 11. Roman. 14. Hæc autem vno Christo nititur (Matthæi 16. Isaiæ 28. 1. Cor. 3. & verbo regitur, Roman. 10. Sufficit ergo locus hic contra omnes papistarum ceremonias. Nam secundum traditiones hominum fiunt, Isaiæ 29. Matthæi 15. Deinde Christi merito derogant, Rom. 10. 11.
units.tr: Let us observe that no worship is pleasing to God unless it is performed from faith, according to his own word. Without faith it is impossible to please God (Heb. 11; Rom. 14). But this faith rests on Christ alone (Matt. 16; Isa. 28; 1 Cor. 3) and is governed by the word (Rom. 10). This passage therefore suffices against all the ceremonies of the Papists. For those ceremonies are made according to the traditions of men (Isa. 29; Matt. 15), and then they detract from the merit of Christ (Rom. 10, 11).

units.la: II. Quid fecerint? 1. Suscepistis tabernaculum Moloch. Quasi dicat: Ego meum tabernaculum inter vos erexeram, vt me
units.tr: II. What did they do? 1. You took up the tabernacle of Moloch. It is as if he said: I had erected my tabernacle among you, so that I

units.la: vobis cohabitare velle testarer,vosq; meum essetis peculium,Leuit.26.At vos Moloch cultum recepistis. Fuit hic Deus Amonitarum,præfectus genituræ,cui infantes immolabant. Prohibuerat Deus gravissimè,Leuit.20. Sed nequicquam, 2.Regum 21.23. Ieremiæ 32. Horrendum. Sed idem fit hodie in Cœnobijs maiori cum dedecore & cruciatu multorum.
units.tr: might testify that I wished to dwell with you, and that you would be my own people (Lev. 26). But you received the worship of Moloch. This was the god of the Ammonites, the overseer of generation, to whom they sacrificed infants. God had strictly forbidden this (Lev. 20), but in vain (2 Kings 21, 23; Jer. 32). It is horrible. Yet the same thing is done today in monasteries, with greater disgrace and with the torment of many.

units.la: ¶ 2. Sydus Rempham, vnius scilicet ex planetis. Fuit autem apud gentes sydeorum cultus frequentissimus,propter motum,lucem & alia effecta. Sed prohibuerat Deus,Deuter 18.Mich.5.Iere.30. Sed nequicquam,vt apparet 1.Reg.21.23. Iere.44.At hodie illum quoq; Astrologi reducunt,&c.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The figures which you made. He speaks indefinitely, so that the image of God too is included. He also suggests that this worship clung to images alone (1 Cor. 8, 10). This argument is sufficient against our images, for the reason for them is the same as that of the ancient ones. See Psalm 115, etc.

units.la: ¶ 3. Figuras quas fecistis. Indefinitè loquitur, vt Dei quoque imaginem comprehendat. Ita verò innuit, quòd cultus iste in solis imaginibus hæserit, 1. Cor.8.10. Sufficit hoc argumentum contra nostras imagines. Harum enim eadem ratio, quæ olim veterum. Vide Psalmo 115.&c.
units.tr: III. He threatens punishment: I will carry you beyond Babylon. Amos speaks of Damascus, on account of the alliance with Syria (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7). It was first fulfilled by Shalmaneser (2 Kings 13, 10; De 10). Then, because Judah did not repent, it was likewise afflicted by the Assyrians (Isa. 36, 37, 39; 2 Chron. 33). Finally all were carried away to Babylon (2 Chron. 36). Stephen adds this to indicate what they themselves hope for, namely what was foretold (Luke 19).

units.la: III. Pœnam minatur: Transferam vltra Babylonem. Amos Damasum dicit, propter fœdus Syriacum,2.Reg.16.Isaiæ 7.Impletum primò per Salmanazar, 2.Reg.13.10. De10. Deinde quia Iudas non resipuit, hic quoque afflictus ab Assyrijs. Isaiae trigesimo sexto, trigesimo septimo, trigesimo primo, secundo Paralipomenon trigesimo tertio. Tandem abducti omnes in Babylonem, secundo Paralipomenon trigesimo sexto. Istud adijcit Stephanus, vt innuat quid ipsi sperent: Nimirum quod praedictum, Luc. 19.
units.tr: III. He threatens punishment: I will carry you beyond Babylon. Amos says Damascus, on account of the Syrian covenant (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7). It was first fulfilled through Shalmaneser (2 Kings 13.10; De10.). Then, because Judah did not repent, it too was afflicted by the Assyrians (Isa. 36, 37, 38, 39; 2 Chron. 33). At last all were carried away to Babylon (2 Chron. 36). Stephen adds this to hint at what they themselves hope, namely what was foretold (Luke 19).

units.la: ¶ Applicemus haec nostris temporibus. Idololatria regnat passim. Astrorum cultum instaurant multi, qui illis plus tribuunt, quàm olim gentes: contra illud Iere.
units.tr: ¶ Let us apply these things to our own times. Idolatry reigns everywhere. Many restore the worship of the stars, attributing more to them than the nations of old did, contrary to Jeremiah 10.

units.la: 10. Accedunt aliae artes illicitae, Deut. 18. Corripit Deus per verbum. Hoc alij contemnunt, alij persequuntur. Et ex nostris multo auro conducti iuuant persecutores fidei, &c. Exeret ergo Deus scopas Babylon. quae cum idolis enatae sunt. Praeludia multa vidimus, maximè in Budae dedi tione per Solimannum. Caueamus nobis, & Oremus.
units.tr: Other illicit arts are added (Deut. 18). God rebukes through the word. Some despise this, others persecute it. And some of our own people, hired with much gold, help the persecutors of the faith, and so on. God will therefore send out the brooms of Babylon, which have sprung up together with the idols. We have seen many preludes to this, especially in the surrender of Buda to Suleiman. Let us take care, and let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LVII.
units.tr: HOMILY LVII.

units.la: 44 Tabernaculum testimonij fuit patribus nostris in deserto, quemadmodum ordinauerat is, qui cum Mose loquebatur, vt faceret illud secundum formam quam viderat.
units.tr: 44 The tabernacle of testimony was among our fathers in the wilderness, just as he ordained who spoke with Moses, that it should be made according to the pattern he had seen.

units.la: 45 Quod etiam qui successerunt patres nostri, introduxerunt cum Iesu in possessionem.
units.tr: 45 Which also our fathers who succeeded brought in with Jesus into possession.

units.la: Vide Paul. Iouius hist. fui tempo- rum lib. 40. sessionem gentium, quas expulit Deus a facie patrum nostrorum usque ad dies David.
units.tr: See Paul Jovius, Histories of His Own Times, book 40: the possession of the nations, which God drove out from before the face of our fathers, until the days of David.

units.la: 46 Qui fuit in gratia apud Deum, petijt ut mueniret habitaculum Deo Iacob.
units.tr: 46 He who found favour before God asked that he might find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.

units.la: 47 Solomon autem aedificauit illi domum.
units.tr: 47 But Solomon built him a house.

units.la: 48 Sed altissimus ille non in manufactis templis habitat: quemadmodum Propheta dicit: Caelum mihi sedes est, terra vero scabellum pedum meorum. Qualem domum aedificabitis mihi? dicit Dominus: aut qui locus requietionis meae?
units.tr: 48 But the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool. What manner of house will you build for me? says the Lord, or what is the place of my rest?

units.la: 49 Nonne manus mea fecit haec omnia?
units.tr: 49 Did not my hand make all these things?

units.la: Diuus Stephanus de duob. potissimum accusatus fuit: Nimirum quod legem & patrios ritus oppugnet, & templum ipsum destruere conetur. Ad primum hucusque respondit, & de lege disseruit, quod a Deo per Mosem data sit, quod verbum vitae continet, dum vitae bene agendae regula tradit, & Christo adducit, Leuit. 18.26. Gal. 3. Adhaec cotemte legis crime in patres transfert, quib. ipsi gloriabantur: vt sic oftedat, illos ex gratuita misericordia fuisse seruatos. Transit nunc ad alterum Caput, & disputat sputat de templo,cui maximè sidebant, le re.7.Finis omnium, Deum & huius cultum non esse templo alligatum : ideoque non statim in Deum contumeliosos esse, qui illud abolendum fore docent. Ordo hic est.
units.tr: Blessed Stephen was accused chiefly of two things: that he attacked the law and the ancestral customs, and that he tried to destroy the temple itself. To the first charge he has answered so far, and discussed the law, showing that it was given by God through Moses, that it contains the word of life, since it gives the rule of living well and leads to Christ (Lev. 18.26; Gal. 3). Besides, he turns the charge of breaking the law back onto the fathers, in whom they gloried, so as to show that those fathers were saved by free mercy. He now passes to the second charge and disputes about the temple, in which they trusted most (Acts 7). The final point is that God and his worship are not bound to the temple; therefore those who teach that it is to be abolished are not at once insulting God. The order here is this.

units.la: I. De tabernaculo agit, quod ante templum fuit ex tabulis deauratis & cortinis, &c. Exod. 25. 26. Testimonium dicitur, quod eo Deus suam potentia testaretur, & ibidem respondsa daret, Num. 12. 14. 16. Leuit. 26. Deut. 7. 20. 23. &c. At cultu huic non alligatum fuisse probat.
units.tr: I. He deals with the tabernacle, which came before the temple, made of gilded boards and curtains, etc. (Exod. 25, 26). It is called a testimony because by it God bore witness to his power, and gave his responses there (Num. 12, 14, 16; Lev. 26; Deut. 7, 20, 23, etc.). But he proves that it was not bound to this worship.

units.la: ¶ 1. Quia factum secundum formam, quae Mosi in monte exhibita fuerat, Exod. 25. Heb. 8. 9. Ergo typicum fuit. Adumbrabat enim Ecclesia, quae vnica est in Christo, qui nobis est arca gratiae (Col. 2.) mensa & panis (Ioh. 6.) candelabrum (Ioh. 1. 8 9.) ara thymiamatis (Ioh. 16. Matth. 3. 17.) sacrificium deniq; Ioh 1. 2. Cor. 5. Heb. 9. 10. Quia autem haec figurauit, vtique non tabernaculo inhaere re, sed ab hoc mentes in Christum dirigere debuerunt.
units.tr: ¶ 1. Because it was made according to the pattern shown to Moses on the mountain (Exod. 25; Heb. 8, 9). Therefore it was typical. For it foreshadowed the Church, which is one in Christ, who is to us the ark of grace (Col. 2), the table and the bread (John 6), the lampstand (John 1, 8, 9), the altar of incense (John 16; Matt. 3, 17), and finally the sacrifice (John 1; 2 Cor. 5; Heb. 9, 10). But since these things were figures, they ought certainly not to cleave to the tabernacle itself, but to direct minds from it to Christ.

units.la: Quod quia negligebant à prophetis correpti sunt, Psal. 50. Isa. 1. Ier. 4. 7. Mich. 6. Obseruandum hoc in nostris quoq; ritibus, Ioh. 4.
units.tr: Because they neglected this, they were rebuked by the prophets (Ps. 50; Isa. 1; Jer. 4, 7; Mic. 6). This is to be observed also in our rites (John 4).

units.la: ¶ 2. Patres intulerunt illud in possesio nem gentium, prophanam scilicet terram.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The fathers brought it into the possession of the nations, that is, into profane land.

units.la: Quomodo igitur potuit cultus Dei aftrin gi? Imo hoc admonebat, quid futurum,si ipsi essent increduli,Matth.3.21. Interim docemur, Dei institura non pollui ex loco,siquidem praesens,Isa.66.Iere.23. & ipse omnia loca sanctificat,& suos paisim audit,Ioh 4.
units.tr: How then could the worship of God be bound to a place? Indeed, this was a warning of what would come if they themselves were unbelieving (Matt. 3.21). Meanwhile we are taught that God's institutions are not polluted by place, since he is present (Isa. 66; Jer. 23), and he himself sanctifies all places and hears his people everywhere (John 4).

units.la: ¶ 3. Locus fixus sub Dauide demum monstratus, cum hic anxie hunc quaesiuisset,Psal.132.2.Sam.24.1.Par.21.Ante illud tempus sedes habuit varias.In Silo,Iof.18. 1.Sam.1.3. Euersa haec,Psal 78.Iere.7. Sub Saule in Gilgal,& Nob,1.Sam.11.21.22. Da uidis tempore in Gabaon,1.Par.21.2.Par. 1. Tandem Solomon collectum reposuit in templum,1.Regum 8 2.Par.5. Quomodo autem potuit ei cultus alligari?
units.tr: ¶ 3. A fixed place was shown only under David, when he anxiously sought it (Ps. 132; 2 Sam. 24.1; 1 Chr. 21). Before that time it had various seats: at Shiloh (Josh. 18.1; 1 Sam. 1.3), which was overthrown (Ps. 78; Jer. 7). Under Saul it was at Gilgal and Nob (1 Sam. 11.21, 22). In David's time it was at Gibeon (1 Chr. 21.2; 2 Chr. 1). Finally Solomon placed what had been gathered into the temple (1 Kings 8; 2 Chr. 5). How, then, could worship have been bound to it?

units.la: Obseruandum,singulare beneficiu Dei fuisse, quod locus certus templo destinatus fuit. Faciebat hoc ad regni confirmationem. Ideo Dauid de illo tam fuit folici tus,2.Sam.7.Psal.132. Ieroboamus quoq; intellexit,1.Reg.12.Et sane quia salus omnis ex religione dependet, nullum benefi cium in hoc seculo nobis maius obtingit, quam si illa recte constituta fit, & eadem libere ac tuto posit exerceri. Hinc fana vitae institutio. Preces laetae & efficaces, &c.Potuerunt hoc agnoscere Iudaei tem-pore pore exilij. Vide Pfalm. 74.70.80.137. &c. Agnoscunt hodie etiam pij,qui sub tyrannis degunt. Vtinam nos agnoscceremus. Sed meretur nostra ingratitudo poenas, quas resipiscentia sola effugiemus. Vide Pfal.84.
units.tr: It is to be observed that it was a singular benefit of God that a certain place was set apart for the temple. This served to confirm the kingdom; therefore David was so anxious about it (2 Sam. 7; Ps. 132). Jeroboam also understood this (1 Kings 12). And indeed, since all salvation depends on religion, no greater benefit falls to us in this age than when it is rightly established and can be exercised freely and safely. Hence comes a sound ordering of life, joyful and effective prayers, etc. The Jews could recognise this in the time of exile (see Ps. 74, 79, 80, 137, etc.), and pious people who live under tyrants recognise it today. Would that we recognised it! But our ingratitude deserves punishments, which only repentance will let us escape (see Ps. 84).

units.la: II. De templo agit,cuius idem vsus fuit qui Tabernaculorum. Hoc anno ab exitu ex Ægypto 480.extructum fuit, 1. Reg 6. Quia ergo tam diu caruerunt templo,vtique neq; cultus Dei,neq; salus huic alliga ta fuerunt.Quia autem illi mandatum Dei vrgebant, arguit à Dei natura, qui loco non concludatur, & de eo profert ipsius testimonium,Isa.66.Subest duplex argumentum.1. Qui immensus est, non continetur certo loco: Atqui ego omnia compleo,Iere.23.&c. 2. Qui omnium creator est,non opus habet aliorum opificijs:Ego omnia feci,Ergo,&c.
units.tr: II. He deals with the temple, whose use was the same as that of the tabernacles. It was built in the 480th year from the exodus from Egypt (1 Kings 6). Since they went so long without a temple, neither the worship of God nor salvation was bound to it. But since they insisted on God's command concerning it, he argues from the nature of God, who is not confined to a place, and brings forward God's own testimony about it (Isa. 66). There is a twofold argument underlying this: 1. He who is immeasurable is not contained in a certain place; but I fill all things (Jer. 23, etc.). 2. He who is the creator of all has no need of the works of others; I have made all things. Therefore, etc.

units.la: NOT.1 Falli omnes, qui Dei cultum in externis consistere putant, aut huius gratiam certis locis astringunt. Quod enim de templo dicitur,etiam ad sacra pertinet. Vide Psal.50. Mich. 6. Idem Christus docet,Ioh 4.Mat.24.
units.tr: NOTE 1. All are mistaken who think that the worship of God consists in externals, or who bind his grace to certain places. For what is said of the temple also pertains to sacred rites (see Ps. 50; Mic. 6). Christ teaches the same (John 4; Matt. 24).

units.la: 2. Quis ergo externorum vsus? Pof sunt haec omnia comprehendi Tempore, Loco & Ritibus. Tempus & Locus ordini fer tiunt, quo omnino opus est, priori ad Corinthios decimoquarto. Coetus sac i exi-guntur, Deuter.16 Leuit.23. Matth.18. At hi fine tempore certo non possunt cogi. Ideo Sabbatum institutum, Gen.2. Exo i 20. Numeri 15. Opus item loco. Vt ergo illud, ita hic solis sacris debet seruire: Vtque Sabbato non debent fieri opera prophana: ita neque in templis, Marci 11. Interim non probatur superstitio & luxus nimius. ¶ Ritus siue Sacramenta obsignant nobis beneficia Dei & sensibus re praesentant quae verbo traduntur: Deinde admonent officij. De Baptismo vide 1. Pet.3. Ro 6. Mar.1. De Coena, 1. Cor.11.10. Haec erant obseruanda religtis inutilibus rixis & contentionibus. Oremus.
units.tr: 2. What, then, is the use of externals? All of them can be comprehended under time, place and rites. Time and place serve the order which is absolutely necessary (1 Cor. 14). Sacred assemblies are appointed (Deut. 16; Lev. 23; Matt. 18), but these cannot be gathered without a fixed time. Therefore the Sabbath was instituted (Gen. 2; Exod. 20; Num. 15). Work likewise needs a place. As the Sabbath should serve only holy things, so the place should serve only sacred use: just as profane works should not be done on the Sabbath, so neither in temples (Mark 11). Meanwhile, superstition and excessive luxury are not approved. Rites, or sacraments, seal God's benefits to us and present to the senses what is delivered by the word; then they remind us of our duty. On baptism see 1 Pet. 3; Rom. 6; Mark 1. On the Lord's Supper, 1 Cor. 11, 10. These things were to be observed without useless quarrels and contentions. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY 58.

units.la: 51 Duri cervice, & incircumcisi corde & auribus, vos semper spiritui sancto obnitimini: sicut patres vestri: ita et vos:
units.tr: 51 Stiff-necked, and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit: as your fathers did, so do you.

units.la: 52 Quem prophetarum non persecuti sunt patres vestri? & occiderunt eos, qui praenuntiarunt de adventu iusti illius: cuius vos nunc proditores & occisores fuistis:
units.tr: 52 Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who foretold the coming of that Just One, whose betrayers and murderers you have now become.

units.la: 53 Quia accepistis legem per dispositionem Angelorum, nec seruastis.
units.tr: 53 You who received the law by the disposition of angels, and did not keep it.

units.la: 54 Porrò haec audientes, dissecabantur cordibus suis, & stridebant dentibus in eum.
units.tr: 54 Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and gnashed their teeth at him.

units.la: Respondit hucusque Stephanus adversarijs, & multis demonstrauit se nec in Deum nec in legem, neque templum esse contumeliosum, Nam ab Abrahamo exorsus, se veri & unici Dei cultorem esse docet, qui olim cum Patribus egerit. Deinde de Mose & lege disserit, & in hac quoque Christum promissum esse ostendit, Deut. 18. Tandem de Tabernaculo & Templo disseruit, docens Deum & huius gratiam cum culu & salute nostra, his non aliigari, Isa. 66. Ier. 33. Quia autem partim ipse norat, quales essent iudices, partim hi gestibus & voce significabant suam rabiem, &c. graui increpatione sermonem concludit. Finis omnium est, quod laruam Ecclesiae detrahit superbis, ne imperitis vana gloriatione imponant.
units.tr: Up to this point Stephen has answered his adversaries, and has shown that he is no enemy of God, of the law, or of the temple. Beginning from Abraham, he teaches that he is a worshipper of the true and only God, who once dealt with the Fathers. Then he discourses on Moses and the law, and in this too he shows that Christ was promised, Deut. 18. Finally he speaks of the Tabernacle and the Temple, teaching that God and his grace are not bound to these, nor is our worship and salvation, Isa. 66, Jer. 33. But since he partly knew what sort of judges they were, and partly they showed by their gestures and voices their rage, etc., he ends his speech with a severe rebuke. The purpose of the whole is that he strips the mask of the Church from the proud, so that they may not impose on the unlearned with empty boasting.

units.la: Ita agendum cum ijs, apud quos Dei verbo nihil proficitur. Et hodie in primis necessarium. Veritati enim nihil officit magis, quàm quòd hostes habet, qui Ecclesiae titulum & gubernacula iam diu tenent, &c. Tria vero erant, quibus gloriabantur.
units.tr: So one must deal with those among whom nothing is gained by the Word of God. And today this is especially necessary. For nothing harms the truth more than having enemies who have long held the title and the helm of the Church, etc. There were three things in which they gloried.

units.la: I. Circumcisio, cuius fiduciam adimit. Vocat enim, duræ ceruicis & incircumcisos corde. Alludit ad Deut.10. Ierem.4. Quasi dicat: Scio vos in Circumcisione habere fiduciam. Sed hæc vana est, cum spiritualis defit. Voluit quidem Deus sui fœderis symbolum esse Circumcisionem, Gen.17. At idem corda circumcidere iussit, &c. Sed nihil horum facitis. Imò resisti tis Spiritui sancto per prophetas loquenti vobis. Ita verò non vulgaris contumacia, sed insuper perfidiæ accusat.
units.tr: I. Circumcision, whose confidence he takes away. For he calls them stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart, alluding to Deut. 10 and Jer. 4, as if to say: I know you put your confidence in circumcision. But this is vain, since the spiritual reality is lacking. God indeed willed circumcision to be the sign of his covenant, Gen. 17. But he also commanded the heart to be circumcised, etc. Yet you do none of these things. Indeed you resist the Holy Spirit speaking to you through the prophets. So he accuses them not merely of ordinary obstinacy, but of faithlessness besides.

units.la: NOT. 1. Externa symbola non prodesse, nisi ijs studeamus, quæ illis adumbrantur. Quia enim Deus spiritus est, &c. Iohannis 4. Externa propter nos instituit. Hoc si negligatur, Sacramenta perfidiam nostram arguunt. Simile milius, &c. Hinc illæ correptiones, Psalm. 50. Isaiæ 1. 29. 43. Michææ 6. Ieremiæ 4.7. Applicemus nostris Sacramentis, Rom.5. 1.Cor. 11. 10. At si hæc non iuuant absque fide, multò minus hominum traditiones, Isa. 29. Matt.15.
units.tr: NOTE 1. External signs profit nothing unless we strive after the things they foreshadow. For since God is spirit, etc., John 4. He instituted external things on account of us. If this is neglected, the sacraments accuse our faithlessness. The same holds true of ... Hence those rebukes, Ps. 50, Isa. 1, 29, 43, Mic. 6, Jer. 4, 7. Let us apply them to our sacraments, Rom. 5, 1 Cor. 11, 10. But if these do not help without faith, much less do human traditions, Isa. 29, Matt. 15.

units.la: 2. Qui censendi, qui verbo Dei præ dicato se opponunt. Resistunt Spiritui sancto, cum quod hic verbi author est (2.Tim.3.) tum quod idem in animis agit, & obedientiam suadet, 1. Cor.3. Hinc illa, Matt.10.Luc.10.1.Thef.2.2.Cor.13. Qui ita incipiunt, fere ceruicem indurant, vt Pharao. Vide quid de nostris hominibus iudices, qui ex eo laudem quaerunt, quod ministrorum admonitiones, & minas contemnere & scurriliter ridere norunt, 2. Petri 3.
units.tr: 2. Those who set themselves against the Word of God once it is preached are to be judged. They resist the Holy Spirit, both because he is the author of the word (2 Tim. 3) and because he works the same in minds and urges obedience, 1 Cor. 3. Hence those passages, Matt. 10, Luke 10, 1 Thess. 2, 2 Cor. 13. Those who begin in this way usually harden their necks, like Pharaoh. See what you judge of our people, who seek praise from this, that they know how to scorn the admonitions and threats of ministers and to mock them scurrilously, 2 Pet. 3.

units.la: II. Patrum dignitas, quibus inprmis ef-
units.tr: II. The dignity of the Fathers, in which they were especially elated,

units.la: ferebantur, Matt.3.Ioh.8. Sed erant illi in duplici differentia. Boni, vt Abraham, Ifaac, &c. Horum filij (unt, qui credunt Christo, Ioh.8. Rom 9. At his illi non poterant gloriari, Matt.3.Ezech.16. Impii, qui fem-per persecuti fuerant prophetas, &c. 2. Paralip. 36. Horum filios facit, vt Christus Mat.23. Vrget autem Interrogatione &c. Ivstvm vero dicit Christum (vt 1.Ioh. 2) cum quia per fe iustus est If.53.Io.8.tum quia nobis iustitia est factus 1.Cor.1.2.Cor 5. Ierem.23. Huius praenuntios (inquit) occiderunt patres vestri: vos ipsum prodiftis, Ioh. 18. & 19. Itaque mensuram impletis, Imo peiores estis. Sic Matt.23.
units.tr: Matt. 3, John 8. But they were of a twofold kind. Good, like Abraham, Isaac, etc.; their sons are those who believe in Christ, John 8, Rom. 9. But the others could not glory in these, Matt. 3, Ezek. 16. Wicked, who always persecuted the prophets, etc., 2 Chron. 36. He makes them the sons of these, as Christ does, Matt. 23. He presses the point with a question, etc. He calls Christ the Just One (as in 1 John 2), both because he is just in himself, Isa. 53, John 8, and because he was made righteousness for us, 1 Cor. 1, 2 Cor. 5, Jer. 23. Your fathers, he says, killed his forerunners; you yourselves betrayed him, John 18 and 19. Therefore you fill up the measure, indeed you are worse. So Matt. 23.

units.la: NOT. Mundi peruerfitatem. Patrum omnium spes fuit promissum illud femen, Gen 3.17.22. &c. At quando hunc praedicarunt prophetae, iam exacerbati reiecerunt, ipsum vero occiderunt. Ita fit hodie, &c. Gloriatur omnes Christi nomine. At fi
units.tr: NOTE. The perversity of the world. The hope of all the Fathers was that promised seed, Gen. 3, 17, 22, etc. But when the prophets preached him, they, already embittered, rejected him, and in the end killed him. So it happens today, etc. Everyone boasts in the name of Christ. But if

units.la: hic solus prædicetur (secundum illud,Iohan.8.14.Matth.11.&c.Act.4.) mox hæresim clamant.Et hoc in primis faciunt, qui Christi vicarij & Ecclesiæ antistites habere volunt. Cum his ergo agendum, vt hic Stephanus,ne qui horum præstigijs decipiantur. Ita olim Prophetæ fecerunt: & Christus ipse deinceps, Matth.21.23. Lucæ 13.&c.
units.tr: only he is preached (according to John 8:14, Matt. 11, etc., Acts 4), they at once cry heresy. And those especially do this who want to be Christ's vicars and leaders of the Church. So one must deal with them as Stephen did here, lest people be deceived by their tricks. So the prophets once did, and Christ himself afterwards, Matt. 21, 23, Luke 13, etc.

units.la: III.Lex,quæ præcipua erat illorum dignitas,Deut.4.Psalm.147.Fateor(inquit) vos legem accipisse per minissterium angelorum,Exod.19 20. Sed frustra gloriamini,cum eam nunquam seruaueritis.Id vero non de vulgari inobedientia dicit,sed eo potissimum quòd Christus reijcerent, qui legis finis est, & huic satisfecit, Gal.3. Rom.13.
units.tr: III. The law, which was their chief dignity, Deut. 4, Ps. 147. I grant, he says, that you received the law through the ministry of angels, Exod. 19, 20. But you glory in vain, since you never kept it. He says this not of ordinary disobedience, but chiefly because they rejected Christ, who is the end of the law and satisfied it, Gal. 3, Rom. 13.

units.la: ¶ Inanis ergo est verbi Dei gloriatio, nisi ei obtemperemus,Psal 50.Item Matt. 7.Luc.11. Rom.2. Iacob.1. Debet hoc ad politicas quoque leges extendi, quæ ex Dei verbo desumptæ sunt. Alioqui per eas ipsas damnabimur.
units.tr: ¶ Therefore the boasting in the Word of God is empty unless we obey it, Ps. 50; likewise Matt. 7, Luke 11, Rom. 2, James 1. This should be extended to the civil laws as well, which are drawn from the Word of God. Otherwise we shall be condemned by those very laws.

units.la: Vt vero ista acceperunt præsides Concilij: Cordibus dissecti sunt & dentibus striduerunt. Animi dolor notatur,qui illos in rabiem egit. Fuit hoc indecorum isto loco & tempore.
units.tr: But when the presidents of the council heard these things, they were cut to the heart and gnashed their teeth. The pain of their minds is noted, which drove them to rage. This was unseemly in that place and at that time.

units.la: ¶Sed efthoc ingenium impiorum; vt quò magis vrgentur verbo Dei, eò magis exasperentur. Cain, Gen.4. Pharao, Exo. 5.10.11.&c. Hodie multi. Reprimamus ergo hunc affectum initio statim per fidei obedientiam, Rom.1.16.
units.tr: ¶ But this is the nature of the impious: the more they are pressed by the Word of God, the more they are exasperated. Cain, Gen. 4; Pharaoh, Exod. 5, 10, 11, etc. Today many are like this. Let us therefore restrain this feeling at once from the beginning, through obedience of faith, Rom. 1:16.

units.la: Quod si qui nolunt, non tamen ideo parcendum, 2.Tim.4. Non carebit omni fructu Dei verbum, Isa.55. Luc.8. Etsi omnia fallant, animam suam liberabit fidelis minister, Ezech.3.33.&c. Oremus.
units.tr: But if some are unwilling, we must not on that account spare them, 2 Tim. 4. The Word of God will not be wholly without fruit, Isa. 55, Luke 8. Even if all deceive, the faithful minister will save his soul, Ezek. 3, 33, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LIX.
units.tr: HOMILY LIX.

units.la: 55 Quum autem esset plenus spiritu sancto, intentis in coelum oculis vidit gloriam Dei, & Iesvm adstantem ad dextram Dei.
units.tr: 55 But when he was full of the Holy Spirit, he gazed up into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

units.la: 56 Et ait, Ecce conspicio coelos apertos, & Filium hominis adstantem ad dextram Dei.
units.tr: 56 And he said, "Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."

units.la: 57 Exclamantes autem illi voce magna, continuerunt aures suas, & irruerunt concorditer in eum.
units.tr: 57 But they cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, and rushed together upon him with one accord.

units.la: 58 Et eiectum eum ex urbe, lapidabant. Testes autem deposuerunt pallia sua ad pedes adolescentis, qui vocabatur Saulus.
units.tr: 58 They cast him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.

units.la: 59 Et lapidabant Stephanum invocantem & dicentem: Domine Iesus v ,Suscipe Spiritum meum.
units.tr: 59 And they stoned Stephen as he called upon God and said, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."

units.la: 6o Positis autem genibus clamauit voce magna: Domine, ne statuas illis hoc peccatum. Et cum hæc dixisset obdormiuit.
units.tr: 60 Then he knelt down and cried with a loud voice, "Lord, do not lay this sin to their charge." And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

units.la: QVamuis verbum Dei per se salutare & frugiferum sit(Isa.55.) tamen apud eos solos fructificat, qui animis respectè dispositis audiunt, Luc.8.Impijs è contra non prodest, vt eo potius exacerbentur. Quia enim animi illorum intus maris instar æstuant (Isa.48.57.) quò magis vrgentur, eò magis furiunt. Exempla sunt multa. Memorabile autè imprimis quod proponitur in afflictoribus Concilij contra Stephanum coacti. Cum enim hic & suam innocentiam asseruisset, & eorundem malitiam arguisset, tam abest, vt resipiscant, vt potius nouos furores concipiant, & hos oris indecoro habitu prodant. Nec eo contenti, insuper occidunt. Hoc in præsenti Lucas diligenter describit: quia multa hic habentur, quæ institutioni seruiunt, fidem confirmant & solantur.
units.tr: Although the word of God is in itself saving and fruitful (Isa. 55), it bears fruit only among those who hear it with minds rightly disposed (Luke 8). It does not benefit the wicked, but rather makes them more bitter. For their minds seethe within them like the sea (Isa. 48, 57), and the more they are pressed, the more they rage. There are many examples. Especially memorable is what is set before us in the men who were compelled to attack Stephen before the council. For when he had both asserted his innocence and exposed their malice, they were so far from coming to their senses that they conceived fresh fury and betrayed it in their shameful bearing and speech. Not content with this, they also killed him. Luke describes this carefully here, because there is much in it that serves instruction, strengthens faith, and brings comfort.

units.la: I. Vt Deus cum Stephano egerit? Hic se in medio laporum videns in cælum oculos attollit, nimirum Deum inuocans, sicut is iubet. Psalm 50. Sic solent sancti, vt cum Dauide dicant, Psal.121. Et hos imitari dē-
units.tr: I. How did God deal with Stephen? Seeing himself in the midst of troubles, he lifts his eyes to heaven, plainly calling upon God, as the psalm bids (Ps. 50). Thus the saints are accustomed to say with David (Ps. 121), and we ought to imitate them

units.la: Deus Stephanum moriturū consolatur ri debemus, nec fallit Deus,Psal.146. Videt enim suos periclitantes & audit, Psal. 34.56. Et quia Pater est, eorundem miseretur & iuuat, Psal.103 27.
units.tr: God comforts Stephen, who is about to die. and God does not deceive (Ps. 146). For he sees his people in peril and hears them (Ps. 34, 56), and because he is a Father, he has pity on them and helps them (Ps. 103, 27).

units.la: Sed præstat videre,quomodo hic egerit.¶1. Spiritu sanctorepleuit. Præstitit ergo quod promisit, Ioh.14. Luc.21. Matt.10. Et eo in primis est opus propter carnis infirmitatem, Matt.26. Qui hunc recipiunt,omnia possunt vincere,1 Ioh.4. Itaq; oremus vt Dauid,Psalm.51. Matthæi 6. Luc. 11.
units.tr: But it is better to see how he acted here. 1. He was filled with the Holy Spirit. Therefore he did what he had promised (John 14; Luke 21; Matt. 10). And this is especially needed because of the weakness of the flesh (Matt. 26). Those who receive him can overcome all things (1 John 4). So let us pray with David (Ps. 51), as in Matthew 6 and Luke 11.

units.la: ¶2 Quia multa terrebant,visionem ob ijcit,quæ præsenti causa inprimis seruiebat. Videt cœlos appertos, vt de promissione admoneatur, Ioh.14. 17. Christum a dextris Dei sicut prædixerat,Matt.28. Et quidem stantem, vtpote accinctum ad iuuandum, &c.
units.tr: ¶2. Because many things terrified him, he sends a vision, which especially served the present need. He sees the heavens opened, so that he may be reminded of the promise (John 14, 17), and Christ at the right hand of God, as he had foretold (Matt. 28). And indeed standing, as one girded to help, etc.

units.la: Ista primo Martyri obiciuntur, vt reliqui omnes discant, quid ipsis sit sperandum. 1. πολιτευμα nostrum in cœlis esse Phil 3. 2Christum nobis vicisse,Ioh.16. 3. Eundem nos videre, & sibi factum putare, quod suis fit,Mat.15 Zach 2.Act.9. Nemo igitur ex eius manu nos eripiet (Ioh.10. Rom.8.)quo minus in illo nos quoq; vincamus,1 Iohan. 4. His addamus exempla veterum Martyrum,Heb.11.
