units.tr: These things are shown first to the first martyr, so that all the rest may learn what they are to hope for. 1. Our citizenship [πολίτευμα] is in heaven (Phil. 3). 2. Christ has conquered for us (John 16). 3. We see the same Christ, and count as done to himself what is done to his own (Matt. 15; Zech. 2; Acts 9). Therefore no one will snatch us out of his hand (John 10; Rom. 8), so that we too may not conquer in him (1 John 4). To these let us add the examples of the ancient martyrs (Heb. 11).

units.la: ¶ 1.Confirmatur Stephanus ita,vt hæc iudicibus denuntiet, vt quid de ipsis aliquando futurum sit, intelligant. Sic ipse Christus, Matth. 26. Est hæc animositas decet omnes Martyres, &c.
units.tr: ¶1. Stephen is strengthened so as to declare these things to the judges, so that they may understand what will one day become of them. Thus Christ himself (Matt. 26). This courage befits all martyrs, etc.

units.la: II. Quid hostes? ¶ 1. Clamant & aures obturant.
units.tr: II. What of the enemies? ¶1. They cry out and stop their ears.

units.la: Proprium hoc impijs, Pf.58. Ita fastum Christo, Ioh. 18.19. Hodie digni ergo qui ipsi quoque non audiantur, Mich. 3. Zach.1. Imo cogentur olim audire quod nolunt, Matt. 25.
units.tr: This is proper to the wicked (Ps. 58). Thus they scorned Christ (John 18, 19). Today, therefore, they are worthy that they themselves should not be heard (Mic. 3; Zech. 1). Indeed, one day they will be compelled to hear what they do not wish to hear (Matt. 25).

units.la: ¶ 2. Viagunt. Impetu facto eijciunt, lapidant, vt blasphemum & seductorem, Leuit.24. Deut.13.17. His armis ferè pugnatur contra veritatem. Sic cum prophetis actum, Matt.23. Cum Christo, Apostolis, Act.16.18.19.20.21.&c. Hodie ergo non offendamur. Interim arguunt ista eorum tepiditatem, qui apertas blasphemias impunè abire sinunt, imò defendunt.
units.tr: ¶2. They rush at him. Making an assault, they throw him out and stone him, as a blasphemer and seducer (Lev. 24; Deut. 13, 17). Truth is generally fought against with such weapons. So it was done to the prophets (Matt. 23), to Christ and the apostles (Acts 16, 18, 19, 20, 21, etc.). Therefore today let us not be offended. Meanwhile these things expose the lukewarmness of those who let open blasphemies pass with impunity, and even defend them.

units.la: ¶ 3. Iuris tamen speciem seruant, quoad testes, &c. Deut.17. Sed non semper iure sit quod iuris speciem habet, & diligenter omnia expendi debent, Deut.1.2.Paralip. 19.Psalm.72. Interim vides, quousque pro grediatur impietas. Peccarunt falso testimonio, Exod.20. Nec ignorabant quod dicitur Prouerb.6.Deut.19. At non contenti, insuper occidunt, & reos sanguinis se faciunt, nec Dei iudicium verentur, Numer. 35. Disce initijs resistere. Quod de Saule dicitur, parasceuen habet ad lequen tem historiam.
units.tr: ¶3. Yet they keep up an appearance of law, as regards the witnesses, etc. (Deut. 17). But what has the appearance of law is not always lawful, and everything must be weighed carefully (Deut. 1, 2; 2 Chron. 19; Ps. 72). Meanwhile you see how far impiety advances. They sinned by false witness (Exod. 20), nor were they ignorant of what is said in Proverbs 6 and Deuteronomy 19. But not content with this, they also kill him, and make themselves guilty of blood, nor do they fear God's judgement (Num. 35). Learn to resist at the beginning. What is said of Saul has a preparation for the following narrative.

units.la: III. Quid Stephanus? ¶ 1. Invocat Iesum, cui spiritum suum commendat. Fidei argumentum, quam in morte confitetur. Agnoscit Seruatorem, vt latro, Luc. 23. Credit animas in morte seruari, Iohan. 15. Lucae decimosexto. Adeoque moriendo vitam inueniri, Iohannis vndecimo, duodecimo. Imitemur, vt ipsi quoque animas Christo commendemus.
units.tr: III. What of Stephen? ¶1. He calls upon Jesus, to whom he commends his spirit. This is evidence of faith, which he confesses in death. He acknowledges the Saviour, like the thief (Luke 23). He believes that souls are kept safe in death (John 15; Luke 16). And thus by dying, life is found (John 11, 12). Let us imitate him, so that we too may commend our souls to Christ.

units.la: ¶ 2. Orat pro hostibus, vt Christus Lucae 23. Nec fuerunt irritę preces, quando cum multis alijs tandem Saulus quoque conuertitur. Excitet hoc quoque nos ad preces, Matth. 5. Arguit hoc mundi improbitatem, qui fui amantissimos persequitur.
units.tr: ¶2. He prays for his enemies, as Christ did (Luke 23). Nor were his prayers in vain, since in the end Saul too, with many others, was converted. This should also stir us to prayer (Matt. 5). It also exposes the wickedness of the world, which persecutes its most loving friends.

units.la: ¶ 3. Obdormiunt. Ergo non extinctus est, vt hostes volebant. Corpus inuenta requie dormit. Anima viuit in cœlis. Fides adhuc prædicatur. Olim resurget gloriosus. Eadem omnium conditio, qui in Christo moriuntur, Iohan. 5. 11. Apoc. 14. Et hæc semper omnium sanctorum spes fuit Iohan. 11.2. Tim. 4. 1. Thess. 4. priori ad Corinth. decimoquinto. Hac igitur confirmati intrepidè omnia vincamus quæ inci dunt. Vide Matth. 10. Lucæ 12. Oremus.
units.tr: ¶3. He falls asleep. Therefore he was not extinguished, as the enemies wished. The body sleeps, having found rest. The soul lives in heaven. The faith is still preached. One day he will rise up in glory. The same condition belongs to all who die in Christ (John 5, 11; Rev. 14). And this has always been the hope of all the saints (John 11; 2 Tim. 4; 1 Thess. 4; 1 Cor. 15). Strengthened by this, let us therefore conquer all things that befall us without fear. See Matthew 10 and Luke 12. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT IIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: Homilia LX.
units.tr: Sermon LX.

units.la: FActa est autem illo die persecutio magna aduersus Ecclesiam, quæ erat Hierosolymis, & omnes dispersi sunt per regiones Iudææ, & Samariæ, præter Apostolos.
units.tr: On that day a great persecution arose against the Church at Jerusalem, and they were all scattered throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.

units.la: 2 Extulerunt autem vnâ Stephanum viri religiosi, fecerunt{?} planctum magnum super eum.
units.tr: 2 Devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him.

units.la: 3 Saulus vero vastabat Ecclesiam, singulas domus inuadens, trahensque viros & mulieres, tradebat in custodiam.
units.tr: 3 But Saul laid waste the Church, entering every house, and dragging off men and women, he handed them over to prison.

units.la: 4 Illi igitur dispersi peragrârunt regionem euangelizantes verbum Dei.
units.tr: 4 Those who had been scattered therefore went through the country preaching the word of God.

units.la: 5 Vcas ex spiritus sancti suggestione Stephani necem diligentissimè describit, non modò propter ipsum Stephanum, cuius memoria sic seruata est, (Psal. 34. & 112. Prou. 10.) sed maximè propter nos. Discimus enim qua fidei constantia nos quoque omnia pro Christo subire debamus. &c
units.tr: 5 Luke, under the prompting of the Holy Spirit, describes the killing of Stephen most carefully, not only for Stephen's own sake, whose memory is thus preserved (Psal. 34, 112; Prov. 10), but chiefly for our sake. For we learn with what steadfastness of faith we too ought to endure everything for Christ. &c.

units.la: & in ipsum respicere, qui noster vindex est (Iob.19.) & mercedem in cœlis nobis reposuit,Matth.5. Ioh.14.17. Luc.22. Adhæc consolationem habet, quòd Christi regnum sanctorum cædibus non extinguitur,sed propagatur.Factum hoc sæpe, tum etiam in præfenti,vt sequens historia docebit.
units.tr: and to look to him who is our avenger (Job 19), and who has laid up a reward for us in heaven (Matt. 5; John 14:17; Luke 22). Moreover, we have this consolation: the kingdom of Christ is not extinguished by the slaughter of the saints but spread abroad. This has often happened, and also in the present case, as the following history will show.

units.la: I. Vniuersalis persecutio oritur. Ante multa tentata, & Apostoli maximè petiti: at vulgi metus hostes repressit,Actor.3.4. Nunc quia contra Stephanum res successit,nec populus commouetur,vt ferae sanguine gustato sæuiunt. Fit ergo vt Ecclesia dissipetur.
units.tr: I. A general persecution arises. Before this many attempts had been made, and the apostles especially were sought out; but the fear of the common people held the enemies back (Acts 3:4). Now, because things went well against Stephen, and the people are not stirred, the enemies rage like wild beasts that have tasted blood. So it comes about that the Church is scattered.

units.la: NOT. ¶1. Faciem huius Ecclesiæ. Omnia optimè instituta, Actor.4.5.6.Sæpe vi cerunt Apostoli,& auditus fuerat Gamaliel, Act.5. Ergo sperare quis pacem perpetuam. Sed subito omnia turbantur, & vnius Stephani morte ita animantur hostes,&c.Quid ergo nos sperem us, qui neque in doctrina, neque moribus cum his possumus conferri? Vide Luc.23. Simul arguuntur,qui ex euentis huius seculi de fide iudicant. Si enim hos audies, sacerdotum causa iusta, Stephani & Ecclesiæ iniusta fuit.Sunt ergo altius scrutandæ causæ iudiciorum Dei, & apparet bit,iustum esse,&c .1.Pet.4.1.Corinth.11.
units.tr: NOTE 1. The face of this Church. Everything was excellently ordered (Acts 4, 5, 6); the apostles often prevailed, and Gamaliel had been heard (Acts 5). Who, then, could hope for lasting peace? Yet suddenly everything is thrown into turmoil, and by the death of Stephen alone the enemies are so inflamed, &c. What, then, may we hope for, who cannot be compared with these men either in doctrine or in morals? See Luke 23. At the same time, those are refuted who judge of the faith by the outcomes of this age. For if you listen to them, the cause of the priests was just, and that of Stephen and the Church unjust. The causes of God's judgments must therefore be searched out more deeply, and it will appear that it is just, &c. (1 Pet. 4:1; 1 Cor. 11).

units.la: § 2. Alijs dilapsis manent Apostoli. At qui hi priùs præ alijs infestati fuerunt. Nunc ergo miraculosè seruati. Oportebat enim Euangelium quàm diutissimè in ea vrbe prædicari, vt magis eluceret Dei cùm bonitas tum iustitia,&c. Meminerint huius, quibus hodie datur veritatis doctrina frui inter tam graues totius orbis motus, ne quando ipsis conueniat quod habetur Matth. 23. Luc. 19. § Consoletur præterea, quòd videmus impijs Ecclesiæ hostibus suos terminos præscriptos esse, quos non possunt transilire. Licet his aliquid in vulgus credentium, inter quos erant vitia quædam, Actor.6. In Apostolos non item. Ergo impiorum quoq; su-rores Dei prouidentia reguntur, adeoque ipse Satan, Iob.1.2 Mar.5. &c. Semper ergo cogitemus de eo quod habetur Iob. 38. Matt.10.
units.tr: § 2. With the others dispersed, the apostles remain. Yet these were earlier attacked more than the rest, and now they are miraculously preserved. For it was necessary that the Gospel be preached in that city for as long as possible, so that the goodness and the justice of God might shine forth more clearly, &c. Let those remember this who today are granted the enjoyment of the doctrine of truth amid such grave upheavals of the whole world, lest it ever happen to them what is written in Matt. 23 and Luke 19. § Let it further console us that we see the impious enemies of the Church have their set limits, which they cannot pass. Something is allowed them against the common crowd of believers, among whom there were certain faults (Acts 6); but not against the apostles. Therefore the rages of the impious too are governed by the providence of God, and so is Satan himself (Job 1:2; Mark 5, &c.). Let us always then keep in mind what is written in Job 38 and Matt. 10.

units.la: II. Quid cum Stephani corpore factum in his turbis. Num illud neglexerunt? Vel num incluserunt auro & argento? Num consecrârunt aram, diem festum, &c. Nihil huius. Sed duo dicuntur. § 1. Sepulturæ mandârunt. Vetustissimus mos, qui de sententia Dei (Gen.3) & resurrectionis spe nos admonet, 1.Cor.15. Iohannis 12. Simul mul autem hoc facto isti damnârunt Concilij sententiam, vt Iosephus Arimathæus Matth. 27. Luc.23. & suam ergâ Stephaphanum reuerentiam testati fuut. Diffimi les eorum, qui hodie pios ministros turbarum authores esse clamant,
units.tr: II. What was done with Stephen's body amid these tumults? Did they neglect it? Or did they enclose it in gold and silver? Did they consecrate an altar, or a festival day, &c.? None of this. But two things are recorded. § 1. They committed him to burial. This is a most ancient custom, which reminds us of the sentence of God (Gen. 3) and of the hope of resurrection (1 Cor. 15; John 12). At the same time, by this deed they rejected the sentence of the council, as Joseph of Arimathea did (Matt. 27; Luke 23), and they bore witness to their reverence for Stephen. They are unlike those who today cry out that the godly ministers are the authors of the tumults.

units.la: ¶ 2. Fecerunt magnum planctum. Non quidem gentilitio ritu (1. Theffal. 4.) sed dolet eis tantum licuisse impijs, & Ecclesiam tam vtili membro esse spoliatam. Di scimus quid defunctis debeatur. Vt amicorum morte doleamus humanum est, & fecerunt hoc sanctissimi Abrahamus, Genef 23. Iosephus & fratres, Gen. 49. & 50. Dauid, 2 Sam. 1. Christus & sorores Lazari, Ioh. 11. In primis hoc decet, quando bene meriti & præclari Dei serui eripiuntur. Sic Israelitæ lugent Aaronem, Num. 20. Mosem, Deuteronom. 34. Samuelem, 1. Sam. 25. Elisæum Ioas, 2. Regum 13. Iosiam, 2. Paralip. 35. Et damnantur, quibus non cordi est si iusti pereant, Isaiæ 57. Interim seruetur modus, 1. Theffalon. 4. Deinde honestè sepeliantur, vt templa Spiritus sancti, 1. Cor. 6. Graue scelus contumelia afficere mortuos, Amos 2. Absit tamen fastus, quo nihil absurdius. Superstitio ite, aut sacra pro defunctis, quæ Christi merito derogent, Ioh. 5. In lege nihil
units.tr: ¶ 2. They made great lamentation. Not, indeed, in the manner of the Gentiles (1 Thess. 4), but they grieved that this was permitted only to the impious, and that the Church had been stripped of so useful a member. We learn what is owed to the dead. To mourn the death of friends is human, and the most holy men have done it: Abraham (Gen. 23); Joseph and his brothers (Gen. 49 and 50); David (2 Sam. 1); Christ and the sisters of Lazarus (John 11). Especially is this fitting when good men and distinguished servants of God are snatched away. Thus the Israelites mourned Aaron (Num. 20), Moses (Deut. 34), Samuel (1 Sam. 25); Joash mourned Elisha (2 Kings 13); and Josiah was mourned (2 Chron. 35). And those are condemned who have no concern when the righteous perish (Isa. 57). Meanwhile moderation is to be kept (1 Thess. 4). Then they are honourably buried, as temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 6). It is a grievous crime to insult the dead (Amos 2). Yet let pride be absent, than which nothing is more absurd. Superstition, or sacred rites for the dead which detract from the merit of Christ (John 5), are to be avoided. In the law nothing of this

units.la: huius traditum.Imo prohibitum,&c. Leuit.21. Audi Apoc.14.
units.tr: is handed down; rather it is forbidden, &c. (Lev. 21). Hear Rev. 14.

units.la: III. Pedit ad Saulum, in quo sæuissimi persecutoris exemplum proponitur.Primus consensit in necem Stephani, Rom.1. Custodiuit vestes lapidantium. Nunc totam Ecclesiam aggreditur:nec in publico fidem profitentes solum inuadit,sed in domos irruit,& mulieres quoque protrahit: Denique lupum agit,Gen.49. Sequentur grauiorꝯ capite nono,quæ ipse fatetur,Action vigefimo sexto, priori ad Corinthios decimoquinto,Gal.1.
units.tr: III. He turns to Saul, in whom the example of the most savage persecutor is set before us. He first consented to the death of Stephen (Rom. 1); he guarded the garments of those who stoned him. Now he attacks the whole Church: he assaults not only those who profess the faith openly, but breaks into houses and drags off women as well. In short, he acts like a wolf (Gen. 49). What follows, in more serious matters, is in chapter nine, and he himself confesses it (Acts 26; 1 Cor. 15; Gal. 1).

units.la: Obseruemus:1.Bonitatem Dei, qui talem postea conuertit.Hinc ergo consolationem petamus,1.Tim.1.
units.tr: Let us observe: 1. The goodness of God, who afterwards converted such a man. From this let us draw consolation (1 Tim. 1).

units.la: ¶ 2. Irritum conatum. Disperguntur quidem pij,sed ijdem latiùs diuulgant verbum Dei.Ita potest hic suum regnum per ea propagare, quæ videbantur ei obstare. Sic in Euangelio dæmones ad Christum adducunt obsessos, & hunc supplices fatentur, Matth.8. Mar.1. &c. Paulus item captiuus prædicat Agrippæ R. & Romæ, Actor. 26.28. Phil.1.4. Hodie vidimus similia exempla. Nemo igitur persecutionis metu stationem suam deferat. Viuit & regnat Christus, qui suorum hostium conatus dissipat,Pfalm.2.33. Ifa.§. Huic nos fidefideles simus, qui nos non patietur supra vires tentari, 1. Cor. 10. Oremus.
units.tr: ¶ 2. A vain attempt. The godly are indeed scattered, but these same men spread the word of God more widely. Thus he can, through those very things which seemed to hinder him, advance his own kingdom. So in the Gospel demons bring the possessed to Christ and confess him as suppliants (Matt. 8; Mark 1, &c.). Paul too, a captive, preaches before King Agrippa and at Rome (Acts 26, 28; Phil. 1). Today we have seen similar examples. Let no one, therefore, abandon his post through fear of persecution. Christ lives and reigns, who scatters the attempts of his enemies (Psal. 2, 33; Isa.). Let us be faithful to him, who will not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength (1 Cor. 10). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXI.
units.tr: Homily 61.

units.la: 5 Philippus autem cum venisset in vrbem Samariæ, prædicabat eis Christum.
units.tr: 5 But when Philip had come down to the city of Samaria, he preached Christ to them.

units.la: 6 Attendebant autem turbæ concorditer iis, quæ dicebantur a Philippo, cum audirent & viderent signa, quæ faciebat.
units.tr: 6 And the crowds with one accord paid attention to what Philip said, when they heard and saw the signs he performed.

units.la: 7 Nam cum multos spiritus immundi tenerent, clamantes voce magna exibant. Multi item paralytici & claudi sanati sunt.
units.tr: 7 For many who had unclean spirits came out of them, crying with a loud voice. Many paralytics and lame people were also healed.

units.la: VT Christus Apostolos sæpe admonuit de persecutionibus, ita semper promisit ipsos superiores fore, ut regnum suum per orbem propagetur, Ioh. 16. Consentiunt his prophetæ, Psalm. 2. 110. 72. Faciunt ad horum confirmationem, quæ de primitiva Ecclesia & Apostolis traduntur. Habuerunt hostes potentissimos, qui minis, carceribus, flagris egerunt. Tandem lapidatur Stephanus, & sequitur crudelis persecutio. Sed adeo hæc non officiunt regno Christi, ut potius extendatur. Dispersi
units.tr: Just as Christ often warned the apostles about persecutions, so he always promised that they would be superior, so that his kingdom would be spread throughout the world (John 16). The prophets agree with this (Psalms 2, 110, 72). What is handed down about the primitive Church and the apostles also serves to confirm this. They had most powerful enemies, who drove them on with threats, prisons and whips. At last Stephen was stoned, and a cruel persecution followed. But these things did not hinder the kingdom of Christ at all; rather, it was extended. Dispersed

units.la: fi enim prædicant per Iudæam, & ipsa quœ que Samaria conuertitur, vt prædictum olim Isa.11.Ier.31 Act.1.Sunt similia exempla : quorum omnium vsus est, ne offendamur persecutionibus, sed feramus patienter,quicquid incidit:simulque in omnem euentum parati captemus occasiones,&c.
units.tr: (for they went about preaching through Judea), and Samaria itself was also converted, as Isaiah (11) and Jeremiah (31) had foretold long ago, and as Acts 1 shows. There are similar examples, and the use of all of them is that we should not be offended by persecutions, but bear patiently whatever befalls us, and at the same time be ready for any outcome and seize opportunities, and so on.

units.la: 1.Quis conuertit Samariam? Philippus, Diaconus nimirum, de quo Actor 6. Dicuntur de illo duo. ¶ 1. Prædicauit Christum.Infrà. Euangelizauit de regno Dei. Hic solius Christi meminit, cuius nomine totum Euangelium continetur.Partes resipiscentia & remissio peccatorum, Lucæ 14. Vtramq; Christus confert, Act.5. Qui ergo hunc prædicat, is regnum Dei prædicat. Obseruandum, qua nota veri doctores a falsis discerni debeant. Gloriantur omnes Dei regno. Sed quia huius author est vnus Christus,nemo verè prædicat,nisi qui in hoc omnia monstrat.Hinc illud 1.Ioh. 4. Et Apostoli hunc vnum prædicarunt,Actor.4. 1.Corinth.2. Vide Gal. 6 & 1.
units.tr: 1. Who converted Samaria? Philip, the deacon, of course, of whom Acts 6 speaks. Two things are said of him. (1) He preached Christ. Below: he proclaimed the gospel of the kingdom of God. Here he mentions only Christ, in whose name the whole gospel is contained. The parts are repentance and the forgiveness of sins (Luke 14). Christ bestows both (Acts 5). Therefore whoever preaches him preaches the kingdom of God. It should be noted by what mark true teachers are to be distinguished from false ones. All boast of the kingdom of God. But since the author of it is Christ alone, no one preaches truly unless he sets forth everything in him. Hence 1 John 4. The apostles also preached him alone (Acts 4; 1 Corinthians 2). See Galatians 6 and 1.

units.la: ¶ 2. Signa ædidit, vt promissi Mar.16. Opus his olim, vt animi excitarentur, & quæ gentibus insolens erat doctrina confirmaretur. Signa autem non inania fuerunt, runt,sed quæ docebant, quid in Christo sperandum,Gen.3 Ioh.3.15.Phil.4. ¶ Obseruandum, quòd non fine clamore exeunt immundi spiritus. Sic alibi clamant, laniant,Mar.1.3.5 9. Est hoc diaboli ingenium.Perditos vult, Ioh.8.1:Pet.5. Reluctatur igitur Christo,nec cedit, quin turbas det,seditiones,bella,&c.Adhæc expulsus redire cupit, Mat.12.Vtrumq; experimur hodie. Vigilemus ergo, & credamus Euangelio.
units.tr: (2) He performed signs, as Mark 16 promised. These were once needed so that minds might be stirred and a doctrine unusual to the Gentiles might be confirmed. The signs, moreover, were not empty, but taught what was to be hoped for in Christ (Genesis 3; John 3:15; Philippians 4). It should be noted that unclean spirits do not come out without a cry. So elsewhere they cry out and tear (Mark 1, 3, 5, 9). This is the devil's nature. He wants people destroyed (John 8; 1 Peter 5). Therefore he struggles against Christ and does not yield, but stirs up crowds, seditions, wars, and so on. Moreover, once expelled he wishes to return (Matthew 12). We experience both today. Let us therefore be watchful and believe the gospel.

units.la: II. Quid Samaritani? Attendebant vnanimiter his,quæ dicebantur. Ergo amplexi sunt Christum. Mirum & singulare virtutis Dei per Euangelium se exserentis argumentum,Rom.1. Hominis enim ingenium illi reluctatur, 1. Cor.2. Ioh.4. Ioh. 6. Postea baptizati quoque fuerunt, & sic collecta illic fuit Ecclesia, &c.
units.tr: II. What of the Samaritans? They paid attention to what was said with one accord. Therefore they embraced Christ. This is a wonderful and singular proof of the power of God showing itself through the gospel (Romans 1). For the human disposition resists it (1 Corinthians 2; John 4; John 6). Afterwards they were also baptized, and so a congregation was gathered there, and so on.

units.la: NOT.¶ Quo ordine ad salutem perueniatur. Est quidem huius author vnus Deus,Isa.45 Atidem propter nos medijs externis vtitur. Inter hæc primas tenet verbum,quo & voluntatem suam reuelat Deus,& salutem nobis offert, Pf.107.Ioh. 5.Mar.16.Rom.10. Hoc ergo audire oportet. At quia non satis est audisse, animos quoque moueri necesse est. Fit hoc partim externis signis, partim occulta vi spi-
units.tr: NOTE. By what order one comes to salvation. God is indeed the author of it alone (Isaiah 45), yet he uses external means for us. Among these the word holds first place, by which God also reveals his will and offers us salvation (Psalm 107; John 5; Mark 16; Romans 10). It is therefore necessary to hear this. But since it is not enough to have heard, the minds must also be moved. This is done partly by external signs, partly by the hidden power

units.la: ritus sanctì,sine qua nihil proficitur,i Corinth.3.Vide Act.16. Idem procul dubio in præsenti factu. Quando autem ista Deus adhibet, attentione opus est, Leuit.8. Psal.1 &c. Hinc fructus vberrimus.
units.tr: of the Holy Spirit, without whom nothing is achieved (1 Corinthians 3). See Acts 16. Without doubt the same happened in the present case. When God employs these things, attention is required (Leviticus 8; Psalm 1, etc.). Hence the most abundant fruit.

units.la: ¶ Hæc si ad nos transferas,videbis non mirum esse, quod pauci proficiant. Plerique nolunt audire:similes eorum, de quibus Isa.30.Ier.44.Luc.19.Alij prædicribunt quid dici debeat, similes Achabo, 1.Regum 22.Mich.2.Isa,30.Alij negligenter audiunt,vt quidam olim,Ezechielis 33.Quid quod multi conscientiæ dictata improbè explodunt.&c.
units.tr: If you apply these things to ourselves, you will see that it is no wonder that few make progress. Most are unwilling to listen, like those of whom Isaiah 30 and Jeremiah 44 and Luke 19 speak. Others prescribe what ought to be said, like Ahab (1 Kings 22; Micah 2; Isaiah 30). Others listen carelessly, as some did long ago (Ezekiel 33). What of the many who shamefully reject the dictates of conscience, and so on?

units.la: III. Fructus, Factum est gaudium, &c.
units.tr: III. The fruit: "There was great joy," etc.

units.la: Non loquitur de gaudio carnali,sed conscientiæ.Nascitur hoc ex sensu Dei reconciliati.Ira Dei nihil gravius,vt docent exempla desperantium, Genes.4. Matthæi 27. Imo electorum quoque,Psalm.6 38. 39.51.&c.Econtra nihil lætius, quàm si illum nobis placatum esse sentiamus. Similè Regis,Prouerbiorum decimosexto decimo nono. Hinc illud Angeli Lucæ fecundo. Simeon, Luc.2. Zachæus,Luc.19. Carcerarius,Actorum decimosexto. Eunuchus Æthiops, Actorum octavo. Ideo iubet Christianos gaudere perpetuo Phil. 3.4.Rom.5.
units.tr: It does not speak of carnal joy, but of joy of conscience. This arises from the sense of a reconciled God. Nothing is more grievous than the wrath of God, as the examples of the despairing teach (Genesis 4; Matthew 27). Indeed, it is so for the elect too (Psalms 6, 38, 39, 51, etc.). On the contrary, nothing is more joyful than when we perceive that he is appeased toward us. Similar is the king's favour (Proverbs 16, 19). Hence the words of the angel in Luke 2. Simeon (Luke 2), Zacchaeus (Luke 19), the jailer (Acts 16), the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8). Therefore he bids Christians rejoice always (Philippians 3, 4; Romans 5).

units.la: Nota. ¶ Quales censeri debeant, qui Euangelij praedicatione terretur, & hanc turbarum causam esse dicunt. Sentient olim terrores horribiles, Matth. 24. Sap.5. Nos istos imitemur, & vt hoc posse simus, sed ulo Oremus.
units.tr: Note. Of what sort those should be judged to be who are terrified by the preaching of the gospel and say that it is the cause of disturbances. They will one day feel dreadful terrors (Matthew 24; Wisdom 5). Let us imitate them not at all; and so that we may be able to do this, let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXII.
units.tr: Homily 62.

units.la: 9 Vir autem quidam nomine Simon, antea in urbe illa exercuerat artem magicam, et gentem Samariae obstupefecerat, dicens se esse quempiam magnum.
units.tr: 9 But a certain man named Simon had previously practised magic in that city and had amazed the people of Samaria, claiming that he was someone great.

units.la: 10 Quem attendebant omnes a minimo usque ad maximum, dicentes: Ille est virtus illa Dei magna.
units.tr: 10 All of them, from the least to the greatest, paid attention to him, saying: This man is that great power of God.

units.la: 11 Attendebant autem eum propter ea, quod multo tempore magicis artibus eos obstupefecerat.
units.tr: 11 They paid attention to him because for a long time he had amazed them with magic arts.

units.la: ETsi Iesus Christus ex Iudaeis homo natus sit, & his primis praedicari debuerit, idem tamen omnium gentium Seuator est, & ideo Apostolis mandauit, vt Euangelium vbique omnibus praedicent, Mar.16. Matth.28. Actor.1. Id qua occasio nefieri coeperit, Lucas hoc capite narrat: Nimirum quod persecutione exorta pij dispersi exierosolyma, fidem hinc inde docuerint, & Philip. delatus Samariam {C}ap.8. illic prædicârit. Vbi vidimus. ¶ 1. Quæ regni Christi conditio, quodq; persecutioni bus non impediatur, sed propagetur, Pfal. 2.11o. Ioh. 11. ¶ 2. Bonitatem Dei singularem, qui inter gentes primos Samaritanos inuisit, infestissimam gentem, Ioh.4. 8. Nemo igitur desperet, &c.
units.tr: Although Jesus Christ was born a Jew and was first to be preached to Jews, he is nonetheless the Saviour of all nations, and therefore he commanded the Apostles to preach the Gospel everywhere to everyone (Mark 16; Matt. 28; Acts 1). Luke narrates in this chapter how this began: namely, when a persecution broke out, the godly were scattered from Jerusalem and taught the faith wherever they went, and Philip, having gone down to Samaria (Acts 8), preached there. Here we see: (1) the condition of Christ's kingdom, that it is not hindered by persecutions but spread by them (Ps. 2; 110; John 11); (2) the singular goodness of God, who first visited the Samaritans among the nations, a most hostile people (John 4; 8). Let no one therefore despair, etc.

units.la: Vt tamen magis eluceret cum bonitas Dei, tum Euangelij virtus, describit Lucas, quæ prius Samariæ conditio fuerit, & quid factum quando Philippus illic prædicauit, &c.
units.tr: So that both the goodness of God and the power of the Gospel might shine out more clearly, Luke describes what the condition of Samaria was before, and what happened when Philip preached there, etc.

units.la: Fuit illic Simon celebris Magus, qui ar tibus magicis illos dementauit, & sibi ven dicauit Dei honorem. Eufeb. 2. cap 13. Epiphan. Voluit hunc cum Philippo comiti Deus, vt Filij sui virtus effet illustrior, & simul constaret, Apostolos non Magos esse, sed virtute maiori instructos opera miraculosa facere. Idem ergo hic factu, quod in Ægypto, Exod. 7. 8. Et vt illic Magi Pharaonem dementârunt, ita Simon Samaritanos, vt virtutem Dei magnam dicerent, ab ipso vno penderent, &c. Fuit ergo hæc singularis virtus Dei, quæ hanc remoram è medio abstulit, & animos omnium mutauit, &c.
units.tr: There was there a famous magician, Simon, who had bewitched those people with magic arts and claimed the honour of God for himself (Eusebius, bk. 2, ch. 13; Epiphanius). God wished him to be pitted against Philip, so that the power of his Son might be more illustrious and at the same time it might be established that the Apostles were not magicians but, endowed with greater power, performed miraculous works. Here, then, the same thing happened as in Egypt (Exod. 7; 8): just as the magicians there beguiled Pharaoh, so Simon beguiled the Samaritans, so that they called him the great power of God and depended entirely on him, etc. This, then, was the singular power of God, which removed this obstacle from the midst and changed the minds of all, etc.

units.la: ¶ Quia autem quod diabolus tunc fecit, etiam hodie facit, & multorum similis est. €ftleuitas, quædam hic diligentius excu- tienda sunt.
units.tr: Since what the devil did then he also does today, and is like many people, some matters here must be examined more carefully.

units.la: I. Magi ferè dicuntur,quos vulgò <bl>Zauber</bl> & <bl>Hexen</bl> vocamus.Sunt qui cum dia-bolo paciscuntur,cui fe mancipant,vt eius ope miracula faciant,futura & occulta indicent,iuuent aut noceant,<bl>Schwarzkünstler</bl>/&c. Tales olim Ægyptij illi, de quibus Exod.7.8. Balaam, Num.22.23.&c. In Endor.1. Samuel.28. Simon hic. Hodie multi, quos ferè characterè insignit Satan. Et eò deueniunt, vel exegestatis impatientia, vel inuidia,aut vindictæ cupiditate.
units.tr: I. Those are commonly called magicians whom we generally call Zauberer and Hexen (sorcerers and witches). Some make a pact with the devil, to whom they surrender themselves, so that by his help they may work miracles, foretell future and hidden things, help or harm people, and are called Schwarzkünstler (black artists), etc. Such were those Egyptians of whom we read in Exodus 7; 8; Balaam in Numbers 22; 23; the woman at Endor in 1 Samuel 28; and this Simon. Today there are many, whom Satan has marked, almost always, in whom he stamps his character. They come to this either from impatience in seeking their livelihood, or from envy, or from a desire for revenge.

units.la: Vbi Nota. ¶ Vitiositatem humani in genij, & quàm opus sit vigilare aduersus hunc hostè,qui vt in Paradiso coepit (Gen. 3.) ita adhuc pergit,& in Angelum lucis se transformat,1.Pet 5.1.Cor.11.
units.tr: Here note: the wickedness of the human mind, and how necessary it is to be watchful against this enemy, who, as he began in Paradise (Gen. 3), so still continues, and transforms himself into an angel of light (1 Pet. 5; 1 Cor. 11).

units.la: 2. Quæritur,Num aliquid possint Sunt qui negent:sed reipfa conuincuntur. Æ-gyptij multa potuerunt. Endorana. Simon hic.Hi item, de quibus Matthæi 24. Mar.15.2. Theff.2.&c. Et hodie mira faciunt Nigromantici. ¶ Obseruemus autè, nihil vel per fe ipsos, vel virtute verborum effici: sed hæc omnia esse diaboli opus.Ergo ne diabolus potest, quod vult? Minimè: Sed Dei iudiciorum executor est, nec tamen ipse quoque plus potest,
units.tr: 2. It is asked whether they can do anything. Some deny it, but they are refuted by the facts. The Egyptians could do many things; so could the woman at Endor, and this Simon. Likewise those of whom Matthew 24, Mark 13, and 2 Thessalonians 2 speak. And even today the necromancers work wonders. We should observe, however, that nothing is effected either by their own power or by the power of words, but all these things are the work of the devil. Can the devil then do whatever he wishes? By no means: he is the executor of God's judgements, and yet he cannot do more than God permits.

units.la: Magi qui · sint · Sanct. (side notes) quàm Deus permittit. Vide rursum Magos Ægyptiacos, Exod. 7.8. & 9 Iob.1.2. Matth.8.Mar.5. Ergo quicquid per istos nobis infertur, sciamus à Deo proficisci, & consoletur nos,quòd hic diabolû tunc quoq; suo fræno regit,quando videtur to tús furere.
units.tr: Who the magicians are (side note: saints). See again the Egyptian magicians (Exod. 7; 8; 9), Job 1; 2, Matthew 8, Mark 5. Therefore, whatever is inflicted on us through these people, let us know that it comes from God; and let this console us, that the devil is then also restrained by God's bridle, even when he seems to rage completely.

units.la: 2. Quare Deus permittat? 1.Vt suorum fidem probet.Deut.12. Sic in lobo 2. Vt sui verbi contemptum puniat, 2.Thess.2. At lædunt sæpe infantes? Respondeo. 1.Licet Deo quod vult,Rom.9 11.Grauio ra infantes quoque meruere, Rom 5. Et potest remunerari. 2.Parentes punit in liberis(Exod 20)& excitat,vt magis solici ti sint de liberorum institutione, Psal.78. Vt item de seipsis cogitent secundum regulam Christi,Luc.2.
units.tr: 2. Why does God permit it? (1) To prove the faith of his own people (Deut. 12; so in Job 2). (2) To punish the contempt of his Word (2 Thess. 2). But they often harm infants? I answer: (1) God may do what he wills (Rom. 9:11); infants too have deserved graver punishments (Rom. 5), and he can reward them. (2) He punishes parents in their children (Exod. 20) and stirs them up, so that they may be more anxious about the upbringing of their children (Ps. 78), and likewise may think about themselves according to the rule of Christ (Luke 2).

units.la: 4. Quid agendum cum talibus? Non. 1. Philippus exemplum fortitudinis fidei.Non potuit ignorare Simonem. Error vetus.Ipse peregrinus.Odium gentis.Sed illuc abit,ex Dei mandato,Act 1. Imitentur omnes ministri.Sunt Christi ferui,qui venit vt opera diaboli destruat,Gen.3.Iohan.3. Vide quid de plerisque Monachorum & sacrificorum iudices.
units.tr: 4. What is to be done with such people? Nothing. (1) Philip is an example of courage and faith. He could not have failed to know Simon. An old error. He himself was a foreigner. Hatred of the nation. But he went there by God's command (Acts 1). Let all ministers imitate him. They are servants of Christ, who came to destroy the works of the devil (Gen. 3; John 3). See what we judge of most monks and priests.

units.la: 2. Samaritani cedunt piè monenti, & baptizantur,vt Christo nomen dent. Sic Ephe-
units.tr: (2) The Samaritans yield to the pious admonition and are baptized, so as to give their name to Christ. So in

units.la: Ephesij, Act.19.Idem decet veré Christianos,ne dicant, Wenn der teüffel/&c. Christus diabolos vera loquentes reiecit,Mar.1.2. Cur ergo tu audias illum,qui mendacij pater elt (Ioh.8.) & nunquam vera dicit,nisi vt magis noceat? Vel cur salutem speres ex homicida? Ioh.8. Satan semper hoc egit,vt homines à Deo abduceret, & eius verbo. Hinc infinitae species vaticinandi.Hinc illicitae artes medendi per exorcismos,amuleta. &c. Inter horum profeffores primatumferè tenent Magi. Vitanda leuitas,&c.
units.tr: Ephesus (Acts 19). The same is truly fitting for Christians, so that they do not say, "When the devil...," etc. Christ rejected the devils even when they spoke true things (Mark 1; 2). Why then do you listen to him who is the father of lies (John 8), and who never speaks truth except so that he may harm more? Or why do you hope for salvation from a murderer (John 8)? Satan has always aimed to draw people away from God and from his Word. Hence arise infinite kinds of prophesying, hence the illicit arts of healing through exorcisms and amulets, etc. Among the practitioners of these, magicians generally hold first place. Levity must be avoided, etc.

units.la: ¶ 3. Magistratus.Sunt his credita iudicia Dei,Psal.72.Quae sunt illa?Vide Deut.18 Leuit.20.Exo.22. Exempla regum,qui hoc nomine laudantur. In primis Saulis in vtramq; partem,1.Sam.28. 1.Paral.10. Hinc leges Caesareae & Pontificiae. Turpe ergo Christianos homines hodie istis occupari.Non quaerendi dij alieni,Exod.20. 2.Regum 1.Multò minus diabolus,2.Cor. 6. Moueat saltem quod ipse fatetur sibi nihil rei esse cum Christo,Mar.15.Itaq; istos imitemur,vigilemus,Oremus.
units.tr: 3. The magistrate. The judgements of God have been entrusted to such, as in Psalm 72. What are they? See Deut. 18; Lev. 20; Exod. 22. Examples of kings who are praised on this account: above all Saul, in both directions (1 Sam. 28; 1 Chron. 10). Hence the Caesarean and Papal laws. It is shameful, therefore, for Christians today to be occupied with these things. Strange gods are not to be sought (Exod. 20; 2 Kings 1). Much less the devil (2 Cor. 6). Let it at least move us that he himself confesses that he has nothing to do with Christ (Mark 1). Therefore let us imitate them, be watchful, and pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXIII.
units.tr: Homily 63.

units.la: 12 Quum vero credidissent Philippo Euangelizanti, quae ad regnum Dei &c. nomen Iesu Christi pertinent, baptizabantur tum viri tum mulieres.
units.tr: 12 But when they believed Philip preaching the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.

units.la: 13 Simon vero & ipse credidit, & baptizatus perdurabat apud Philippum: & conspiciens signa et virtutes magnas edi, obstupefiebat.
units.tr: 13 Simon himself also believed, and after being baptized he remained with Philip. And seeing the signs and great miracles performed, he was astonished.

units.la: 14 Quum autem audissent Apostoli, qui erant Hierosolymis, quod Samaria recepisset verbum Dei, miserunt ad eos Petrum & Iohannem.
units.tr: 14 When the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.

units.la: 15 Qui quum descendissent, oraverunt pro eis, ut reciperent Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: 15 When they had come down, they prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 16 (Nondum enim in quenquam illorum illapsus fuerat, sed baptizati tantum fuerant in nomine Domini Iesu.)
units.tr: 16 (For he had not yet fallen upon any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)

units.la: 17 Tunc imposuerunt manus super illos, & receperunt Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: 17 Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

units.la: QVoniam regnum Christi per totum orbem extendi debebat, Psa. 2. 72. Zachar. 9. Euangelium quoque passim praedicari oportuit, ut per hoc homines illi adducerentur. Et ita ille iusiit, Mar. 16. Actor. 1. Occasionem huic rei praebuit persecutio Hierosol. Cum enim Apostoli hucusque Hierosolymae modo praedicassent, inde dispersi etiam alibi praedicarunt, & quidem tanto successu,vt Philippus Samariam quoque conuerterit,quam hacte nus Satan non modo superstitione vulgari, verumetiam artibus magicis per Simonem dementauerat. Quia ergo hoc memorabile exemplum est,quo docemur, quanta sit Euangelij vis, & quid conuersos deceat, in præsenti diligenter res tota exponitur.
units.tr: Since the kingdom of Christ had to be extended through the whole world (Ps. 2; 72; Zech. 9), the gospel also had to be preached everywhere, so that people might be brought to him through it. And so he commanded (Mark 16; Acts 1). The persecution at Jerusalem offered an occasion for this. For when the apostles had hitherto preached only at Jerusalem, they were scattered from there and preached elsewhere too, and with such success that Philip also converted Samaria, which Satan until then had deluded not only with common superstition but also with magic arts through Simon. Since this is therefore a memorable example, by which we are taught how great the power of the gospel is and what converts ought to do, the whole matter is set out carefully here.

units.la: I. Vt conuersi & Ecclesia Christi facti sint ⁊ q i. Crediderunt Philippo Euangelizanti de regno Dei & nomine,&c. Contenti ergo miraculis nihil præterea requiruntur.
units.tr: I. How the converts became the Church of Christ, etc. They believed Philip preaching about the kingdom of God and the name, etc. Therefore, content with the miracles, nothing further is required.

units.la: Discimus : 1. Conuersionem veram ex fide manare, & per hanc coalescere Ecclesiam. Intelligé autem fidem,quæ est in nomen Christi, id est, quæ talem agnoscit, qualis nomine suo prædicatur. Vide 1. Iohan 2. Qui ita credunt, hi Christo insiti in vnum corpus Ecclesiæ coalescunt, cuius ille caput est, Ioh. 6,15. 1. Cor. 12. Eph. 5. Vn de sequitur, Ecclesiam Dei non esse, vbi si de in Christum destituuntur homines. Imo illic scismata sunt. Vide Augustinum 1. Ioh. 2. II. Fidem hanc ex Euangelio docet, Rom. 10. Ita ipse Christus monet, Ioh. 5.17. Frustra igitur fide Christiana gloriantur, qui Euangelio audire nolunt, Luc. 10.
units.tr: We learn: 1. That true conversion springs from faith, and that through faith the Church grows together. Understand, however, the faith that is in the name of Christ, that is, the faith that acknowledges him as he is proclaimed by his name (see 1 John 2). Those who believe in this way are grafted into Christ and grow together into one body of the Church, of which he is the head (John 6:15; 1 Cor. 12; Eph. 5). From this it follows that there is no Church of God where men are wholly lacking in faith in Christ. Indeed, there are schisms there. See Augustine on 1 John 2. II. This faith the gospel teaches (Rom. 10). Christ himself so warns (John 5:17). Therefore those who refuse to hear the gospel boast of the Christian faith in vain (Luke 10).

units.la: T
units.tr: T

units.la: ¶2. Baptizati sunt. Facit hoc ad exteram fidei professionem. Vult enim Christus, ne nos ipsius pudeat, vtq; seperati a mundo, ipsi nos totos consecremus, Ioh. 15. Mat. 28. Vide Act. 2.
units.tr: ¶2. They were baptized. This serves as an outward profession of faith. For Christ wills that we should not be ashamed of him, and that, separated from the world, we should wholly consecrate ourselves to him (John 15; Matt. 28). See Acts 2.

units.la: Quod Anabaptistae hinc colligunt, neminem baptizari debere, qui fidem non possit profiteri, conuinci potest ex Matt. 10. 18. 1. Cor. 7. Obseruemus potius, Christianis cauendum esse, ne rursus mundo conformes viuant, neue superstitionibus alienis communicent. Vide Ro. 12. 1. Cor. 10. 2. Cor. 6. Apoc. 18. Smile a re militari.
units.tr: The Anabaptists gather from this that no one ought to be baptized who cannot profess faith. This can be refuted from Matthew 10:18 and 1 Corinthians 7. Rather, let us observe that Christians must take care not to live again conformed to the world, nor to share in alien superstitions (see Rom. 12; 1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 6; Rev. 18). A comparison from military life.

units.la: II. Quid vero Simon? Credidit, & baptizatus adhaesit Philippo. Id vero non praemeditata simulatione fecit, sed quod intra animum suum conuictus sen fit, Philippum diuina virtute instructum esse. In terim quia non Dei gloriam, sed suam quae fuit, non potuit fides ista radices agere, & turpiter defecit, Ioh. 5. 12.
units.tr: II. But what of Simon? He believed, and after being baptized he clung to Philip. He did this not from premeditated pretence, but because in his own mind he was convinced that Philip was endowed with divine power. However, since this faith sought not the glory of God but his own, it could not take root, and it shamefully failed (John 5:12).

units.la: Interim Nota. ¶ 1. Christi potentia, qui tantam remoram tam facile fultulit e medio, & per Philippum triumphat de tanto praestigiatore. Vere ergo is est, qui Satanam deuicit, Genef. 3. 1. Ioh. 3. Huc faciunt quae habentur Matth. 4. 8. Marc. 1. 3. 5. Luc. 10. Ioh. 14. Soletur hoc, & simul officij admoneat.
units.tr: Note meanwhile: ¶1. The power of Christ, who so easily removed such a hindrance from the midst and through Philip triumphs over so great a sorcerer. Truly he is the one who has conquered Satan (Gen. 3; 1 John 3). Relevant here are the passages in Matthew 4:8, Mark 1:3 and 5, Luke 10, John 14. This consoles us, and at the same time admonishes us of our duty.

units.la: ¶ 2. Ne q 2. Ne offendamur, si qui vel falso ani mo ad Euangelium accedant, vel προσκαιροι sint. Est haec fors Euangelij & Ecclesiae, Mat.13. Luc.8. Christus ipse ludam habuit, Ioh.6.13. Philippo ad tempus Simon Magus imponit. Paulo Demas & alij falsi fratres, 2.Tim.4.2.Cor.11. Quid ergo mirum, si nobis idem accidat? Tales suo damno fallunt, 1.Cor.11. Cautos quidem esse oportet, sed interim non praecipites in alijs damnandis, 1.Cor.13.
units.tr: ¶2. Let us not be offended if some approach the gospel with a false mind, or are temporary (πρόσκαιροι [prόskairoi]). This is the lot of the gospel and the Church (Matt. 13; Luke 8). Christ himself had Judas (John 6:13). Simon Magus imposed upon Philip for a time. Demas and other false brethren were with Paul (2 Tim. 4; 2 Cor. 11). Why then is it strange if the same happens to us? Such men deceive to their own harm (1 Cor. 11). We ought indeed to be cautious, but meanwhile not rash in condemning others (1 Cor. 13).

units.la: III. Quid Apostoli? Auditis ijs, quae Samaritanae fiebant, miserunt eo Petrum & Iohannem qui Spiritum sanctum illis conferrent. Vbi nemo putauerit, illos Spiritus omnino fuisse expertes. Fides enim non est abfq; Spiritu sancto, Ioh.6. Matth.11.&16. Eph 2.1 Cor.12. Deinde quia digne acceperant baptismum, non defuerunt, quae obsignarent Christi beneficia: Regeneratio, Mortificatio, peccatorum ablutio, adoptio: quae solius Spiritus effecta sunt, Ioh.3. Act.15. Rom.8. Gal.4.
units.tr: III. What did the apostles do? Having heard what was happening among the Samaritans, they sent Peter and John to them to confer the Holy Spirit upon them. No one should suppose that they were altogether without the Spirit. For faith is not without the Holy Spirit (John 6; Matt. 11 and 16; Eph. 2; 1 Cor. 12). Further, although they had rightly received baptism, the benefits of Christ were not lacking to seal them: regeneration, mortification, washing away of sins, adoption. These are effects of the Spirit alone (John 3; Acts 15; Rom. 8; Gal. 4).

units.la: Agitur ergo hic de singularibus illis donis Spiritus, quibus Ecclesiam primitiuam ornauit Deus, vt apparet Act.10.19. Galat. 3. Ista autem non per quosuis, sed per sos Apostolos conferebantur, quos praero gatiua aliqua excellere oportuit. Hinc il-
units.tr: Therefore this refers to those singular gifts of the Spirit with which God adorned the primitive Church, as appears in Acts 10 and 19 and Galatians 3. These gifts, however, were not conferred by just anyone, but by those apostles who had to excel in some extraordinary grace. Hence

units.la: Cap.8. Iud 1. Cor. 5. Ne ergo credentes Samariae alijs inferiores viderentur,mittuntur isti, &c.
units.tr: Chapter 8. Jude. 1 Cor. 5. Therefore, lest the believers in Samaria seem inferior to others, these men are sent, etc.

units.la: Nota. ¶ 1. Apostolorum zelum & modestiam. Sponte mittunt, ne desintoffi- cio : nimirum memores mandati Christi, Actorum 1. Philippus item non reijcit venientes, licet se nonnihilo inferiorem fore videret. Opus hac animorum coniunctione in Ecclesia & mutuis operib. Vehementer peccant ambitiosi. Hinc illa Luc.22.Ioh.17. In Repub.similiter sic fiat oportet.
units.tr: Note: ¶1. The zeal and modesty of the apostles. They send of their own accord, lest they fail in duty, mindful of Christ's command (Acts 1). Philip likewise does not reject those who come, although he saw that he would be somewhat inferior. This union of minds is needed in the Church and in mutual labours. The ambitious sin grievously. Hence that passage (Luke 22; John 17). In the commonwealth too, it ought to be done in the same way.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quid fecerint Apostoli? Orârunt et manus imposuerunt. Precibus testantur, Spiritum à Deo conferri,nec esse hunc in ipsorum potestate. Manuum impositione,se ministros esse testantur, secundum illud Marci 16. Obseruemus,nobis quoque Spiritu opus esse. Accommodemus igitur nos medijs à Deo institutis.Audiamus verbum, vtamur Sacramentis, & vt Scripturae docent, Psal. 51.Mat.6.Luc.18. indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: ¶2. What did the apostles do? They prayed and laid on hands. By prayers they bear witness that the Spirit is conferred by God, and that this is not in their own power. By the laying on of hands they bear witness that they are ministers, according to Mark 16. Let us observe that we too need the Spirit. Let us therefore apply ourselves to the means instituted by God. Let us hear the Word, use the sacraments, and, as the Scriptures teach (Ps. 51; Matt. 6; Luke 18), pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA LXIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXIIII.

units.la: 18 Quùm autem conspexisset Simon per impositionem manuum Apostolorum lorum dari Spiritum sanctum, obtulit eis pecunias.
units.tr: 18 But when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the Apostles' hands, he offered them money,

units.la: 19 Dicens, Date etiam mihi potestatem istam, ut cuicunque imposuero manus, recipiat Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: 19 saying, "Give me also this power, so that on whomever I lay my hands, he may receive the Holy Spirit."

units.la: 20 Petrus autem dixit ei, Argentum tuum tecum pereat, qui existimaris donum Dei pecunijs acquiri.
units.tr: 20 But Peter said to him, "May your money perish with you, because you thought the gift of God could be acquired with money."

units.la: 21 Non est tibi pars neque sors in hoc negotio: cor enim tuum non est rectum in Dei conspectu.
units.tr: 21 "You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not right before God."

units.la: 22 Resipisce igitur ab ista malitia tua, et roga Deum, si forte remittatur tibi cogitatio cordis tui.
units.tr: 22 "Repent therefore of this wickedness of yours, and pray to God, if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you."

units.la: 23 Video enim te in felle amaritudinis et nexu iniustitiae positum.
units.tr: 23 "For I see that you are caught in the gall of bitterness and the bond of iniquity."

units.la: 24 Respondens autem Simon dixit, Precamini vos pro me apud Dominum, ne quid me imuadat istorum quae dixistis.
units.tr: 24 Simon answered and said, "Pray to the Lord for me, that none of the things you have said may come upon me."

units.la: LVcas non modo felices Ecclesiae progressus & praeclara fidelium exempla narrat, verumetiā pseudochristianorum & hypocritarum quorundam vitia describit, quae illi in Ecclesiam inuexerunt. Ita supra de Anania & murmure, &c. Actor. 5.6. Eadem ratione nunc horribile Simonis exemplum exponit, &c. Vsus omnium, ut intelligamus, semper in Ecclesia hypocritas fore & enormia vitia, nec pro pterea omnes debere damnari, multo mi-nus secessionem fieri,Matt.23. Sed videa-mus praesentis historiae singulas circum-stantias.
units.tr: Luke not only narrates the happy progress of the Church and the notable examples of the faithful, but also describes the vices of certain pseudo-Christians and hypocrites who brought them into the Church. So above he narrated this of Ananias and the murmuring, and so on (Acts 5, 6). For the same reason he now sets out the dreadful example of Simon. The practice of all of them shows that we should understand that there will always be hypocrites and monstrous vices in the Church, and yet for that reason not all should be condemned, much less should secession be made (Matt. 23). But let us look at the individual circumstances of the present history.

units.la: I. Peccatum Simonis narratur. Ante quidem credidit, sed vt hi, qui aliquo Dei timore perculsi, licet nolint carni valedi-cere, nolunt tamen cum Deo contende-re. Simulant ad tempus,tandem erum-punt data occasione.Ita Simon, qui bifa-riam peccat. ¶ 1. Ambitione, quae prius quoq; illum decepit. Vult Apostolorum similis fieri, & quod Dei solius est sibi arrogat.Itavides superbiam in Ecclesia quo que omnis mali causam esse,Eccl.10. Hac elati altiora quaerunt, & hinc contentio-nes nascuntur, cum pij talibus non pof-sint cedere.Core,Num.16.17.Sic Apofto-li,Mat.18.20.Luc.22. Hinc sectae fere om-nes. In Republica quoq; nihil nocentius. Singuli ergo sua forte contenti, & in par-uo fideles sint,Matt.25. ¶ 2.Auaritia, qua quaestum meditatur in donis Spiritus fan cti.Ideo enim emere vult,vt pluris vedat. Est haec prophana cogitatio deDeo,cotra illud Matt.10. Ideo veteres vt quosuis ab hac absterreret, Simoniacos dixerunt eos, qui ad ministerium Ecclesiae largitionibus feintrudunt,& sacra nundinantur. Vnum hoc docet de Papatu iudicare. Venalia sacerdotia, vt apud Iudaeos sub praesidibus. Hinc venalia Sacramenta. Indulgentiae. Dispensationes. Preces. Opera supererogationis, &c. Excogitata Purgatorij alchimia, quae mortuos quoq; vexat. Itaq; impuden tius mercatur quâ Iudei, Ioh. 2. Matt. 21. 22. Sunt ergo nô Petri, sed Simonis successores, & ij omnino, dicte quib. 2. Pet. 2. Zach. 14.
units.tr: I. The sin of Simon is narrated. He had indeed believed before, but like those who, struck by some fear of God, do not wish to bid farewell to the flesh yet do not wish to contend with God, he pretended for a time and finally broke out when the opportunity arose. So Simon sins in two ways. (1) By ambition, which had deceived him before. He wants to become like the Apostles and claims for himself what belongs to God alone. Thus you see that pride is also the cause of every evil in the Church (Eccl. 10). Puffed up by this, people seek higher things, and from this contentions arise, since the godly cannot yield to such people (Korah, Num. 16, 17; so too the Apostles, Matt. 18, 20; Luke 22). From this almost all sects arise. Nothing is more harmful in the commonwealth either. Let each therefore be content with his own lot and let the faithful be faithful in small things (Matt. 25). (2) By avarice, by which he plans a profit from the gifts of the Holy Spirit. For he wants to buy them so that he may sell them for more. This is a profane thought about God, against Matt. 10. Therefore the ancients, to deter anyone from this, called Simoniacs those who push themselves into the ministry of the Church by bribery and trade in holy things. This one thing teaches us how to judge the Papacy. Sacred offices are for sale, as they were among the Jews under the governors. Hence sacraments are for sale: indulgences, dispensations, prayers, works of supererogation, and so on, and the invented alchemy of Purgatory, which vexes even the dead. So they trade more shamelessly than the Jews did (John 2; Matt. 21, 22). They are therefore not the successors of Peter but of Simon, and entirely those of whom 2 Pet. 2 and Zech. 14 speak.

units.la: II. Quid Petrus? Acerrimè corripit.
units.tr: II. What did Peter do? He rebukes most sharply.

units.la: Orditur ab imprecatione, non quidem affectu irae abreptus, sed Spiritu motus, qui per eiusmodi imprecationes impijs suas poenas denuntiat. Sic Psal. 7. 11. 35. 58. 109. &c. Ideo addit, Non est tibi pars, &c. Excludit ab omni communione bonorum coelestium & totius Ecclesiae. Causa: Quia donum Dei, &c. Ex eo enim probat eius cor non esse rectum cum Deo, quando illum auaris mercatorib. similem esse putet.
units.tr: He begins with a curse, not indeed carried away by anger but moved by the Spirit, who through such imprecations announces punishments to the wicked (Ps. 7, 11, 35, 58, 109, etc.). Therefore he adds, "You have no part," and so on. He excludes him from all fellowship in the heavenly goods and the whole Church. The reason is: because the gift of God, and so on. For from this he proves that Simon's heart is not right with God, since he thinks of God as like greedy merchants.

units.la: Notat. Vt agendum cum ijs, qui religionem sibi quaestum faciunt. Non possunt probari Deo, quocunque titulo gloriantur. Vide Iudam, Ioh. 6. 12. Ne ergo noceant, sterio argui debent. Nec enim modestiae & mafuetudinis locus est, vbi Dei gloria periclitatur. Et Petrus recte fecisse, exempla probant. Elisaei, 2. Regum 5. Ipsius
units.tr: Note how one should deal with those who make religion a source of gain. They cannot be approved by God, whatever title they boast. See Judas (John 6, 12). So, lest they do harm, they must be rebuked sharply, for there is no place for modesty and gentleness where the glory of God is in danger. Examples prove that Peter acted rightly: Elisha (2 Kings 5); Christ himself (John 2; Matt. 23, 21; Ps. 69). Those therefore are unjust who take offence at us because we inveigh against monks and sacrifices, for they are more shameless and obstinate than Simon.

units.la: Christi,Iohannis 2.Matthæi 23 21. Psalmo 69 Iniqui ergo sunt, qui nobis indignantur, quod in Monachos & sacrificia inuehamur, qui Simone impudentiores & contumaciores sunt.
units.tr: Those therefore are unjust who take offence at us because we inveigh against monks and sacrifices, for they are more shameless and obstinate than Simon.

units.la: 2. Quod pecuniam quoque execratur. Execrabile ergo est, quicquid eiusmodi hominibus feruit ad suam nundinationem, aut quod hac acquiritur. Ita merces iniquitatis dicitur pecunia Bal.2. Petri 2. Numeror.22. Quid de Iudæ pecunia iudicandum, ipsius exitus docet, & ipsi Sacerdotes fatentur, Actor.1. Matthæi 27. Vide denique Deuteronom.7. Idem cernitur in opibus monasteriorum, quæ Euangelicis fere scandalo sunt. Idem sentiendum de omnibus opibus iniquè partis. Vide Habak 2.
units.tr: 2. Peter also execrates money. Therefore whatever serves such men for their trading, or whatever is acquired by it, is detestable. Thus money is called "the wages of iniquity" (2 Pet. 2; Num. 22). What must be judged of Judas's money his end teaches, and the priests themselves confess it (Acts 1; Matt. 27). Finally see Deut. 7. The same is seen in the wealth of monasteries, which is almost a scandal to the evangelicals. The same must be felt about all wealth unjustly acquired. See Hab. 2.

units.la: III. Hortatur vt resipiscat, & ita veniæ spem facit. Veruntamen multa congerit, quibus eum moueat.1. Cogitationis meminit, vt ostendat tam atrox scelus esse, vt ne in mentem quidem venire debuerit. Vnde apparet, etiam corde peccari, Matt. 5. 2 In fe, &c. Fontes arguit, cor amarum, quod omnia Deo ingrata reddit. Aliudit ad Deut.29. 3. Colligatio iniquitatis. Peccati mancipium esse innuit. Ita verò innuit, scerio resipiscendum.
units.tr: III. He exhorts him to repent, and so holds out hope of pardon. Yet he piles up many things by which he may move him. (1) He mentions the thought, to show that so atrocious a crime is one that ought not even to have come into his mind, from which it appears that sin is committed even in the heart (Matt. 5). (2) He calls the sources of sin a bitter heart, which renders everything displeasing to God (compare Deut. 29). (3) He speaks of the bond of iniquity, hinting that Simon is a slave of sin. In this way he hints that he must repent at once.

units.la: NOTA.
units.tr: NOTE.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Quis finis correptionis in Ecclesia esse debeat, & quo peccatores debe ant remirti? Ad Deum nimirum, vt cum hocin gratiam redeant, & resipiscant, 1. Tim.5. Alioqui maledicentia erit. Hic opus peccati redargutione(2.Tim.4.)quia ex nobis ipsis non agnoscimus. Conuersione ad Deum, & precibus,Psal.51.Ad ista autem omnia opus est fide, qua solaap-prehenditur Christus,qui ista largitur Ac-tor 5.
units.tr: NOTE. What should be the aim of correction in the Church, and to what should sinners be brought back? Surely to God, so that by this means they may return to grace and repent (1 Tim. 5). Otherwise it will be mere slander. Here is the work of the rebuke of sin (2 Tim. 4), because we do not recognise sin from ourselves. Conversion to God and prayers are needed (Ps. 51). For all these things faith is needed, by which alone Christ is apprehended, who bestows them (Acts 5).

units.la: Simon quid? Territus petit vtipsi pro se orent,de se ipso autem nihil dicit: quod diffidentiæ argumentum est, Atqui non iuuant aliorum preces, nisi ipsi redeamus ad Deum. Vide Pharaonem Exod.8.9. Saulem,1.Sam.15.16.Item Ier.15.7.14.Christus item orauit pro crucifigentibus ipsum, Lu. 23. sed hoc conuersis solis proinuit Act.2.
units.tr: What of Simon? Terrified, he asks that they pray for him, but he says nothing about himself, which is a sign of distrust. Yet the prayers of others do not help unless we ourselves return to God. See Pharaoh (Exod. 8, 9), Saul (1 Sam. 15, 16), and likewise Jer. 15, 7, 14. Christ also prayed for those crucifying him (Luke 23), but he promised this only to the converted (Acts 2).

units.la: NOT. ¶ Errare eos, qui precibus meritorijs fidunt,quæ ferè a sacrificulis non intelliguntur, cum ipsi pergant impiè agere. luftus sua fide viuit.Hab.2.Rom.1. Debent quidem alij pro alijs orare,& non sunt inefficaces preces fidelium, Rom.15. Ephes.6. Sed quoad illos, qui etiam ipsi officium faciunt. Discant singuli fugere ambitionem & auaritiam, e contra corde sincero seruiant Deo, &c. Ifaiæ 29. Ore mus.
units.tr: Note that those err who trust in meritorious prayers, which the petty sacrificers scarcely understand, since they continue to act impiously. "The just shall live by his faith" (Hab. 2; Rom. 1). Indeed others ought to pray for others, and the prayers of the faithful are not ineffective (Rom. 15; Eph. 6). But this applies to those who also do their own duty. Let each learn to flee ambition and avarice, and on the contrary serve God with a sincere heart (Isa. 29). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXV.
units.tr: HOMILY LXV.

units.la: 25 Illi igitur testificati & locuti sermonem Dei, reuersi sunt Hierosolymam, & multis vicis Samaritanorum Euangelizarunt.
units.tr: 25 So they, having testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

units.la: 26 Angelus autem Domini locutus est Philippo, dicens: Surge & vade meridiem versus, ad viam, quæ descendit ab Hierusalem ad Gazam, (quæ est deserta.)
units.tr: 26 But the angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying: Arise and go toward the south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza (which is desert).

units.la: OVoniam Deus filium suum Iesum Christum, vniuersalem totius orbis Seruatorem dedit, Euangelium quoque in omnibus gentibus oportuit prædicari. Mar.16. Act 1. Id quomodo fieri cœperit, hoc Capite narratur. Et initiò de Samaria agit Lucas, quam diserte Christus nominarat. Act.1. Venit eò Philippus. Mox mis fi Apostoli, Petrus & Iohannes, qui opus Domini illic confirmârunt. &c. Perminet tamen ad hanc historiam quod prima pars huius loci dicitur.
units.tr: Since God gave his Son Jesus Christ as the universal Saviour of the whole world, the gospel also had to be preached among all nations. Mark 16; Acts 1. How this began to happen is related in this chapter. Luke begins with Samaria, which Christ had expressly named (Acts 1). Philip came there. Soon afterwards the Apostles Peter and John were sent, who confirmed the work of the Lord there, etc. Nevertheless, what is said at the beginning of this passage belongs to this history.

units.la: I. Testificati sunt, nimirum verum esse quod prædicârat Philippus, & ita ipsi Christo testimonium tulerunt, vt iussi erant. Iohannis decimoquinto, Actor. 1. Lo
units.tr: I. They testified, that is, they affirmed that what Philip had preached was true, and so they bore witness to Christ himself, as they had been commanded. John 15; Acts 1.

units.la: Quid por- to Samaritæ fecerint Apostoli. cuti sunt sermonem Dei, non suum, Mat. 28. In reditu pagis quoque Euangelizarunt. Zeli magni argumentum.
units.tr: What the Apostles did in the Samaritan villages. They spoke the word of God, not their own, Matt. 28. On their return they also preached the gospel in the villages. A sign of great zeal.

units.la: Not. Officium ministrorum. i. Meminerint se non vulgares praecones, sed testes esse. Ab his requiritur veritas, Exo. 20. 2. Loquantur non sua commenta, sed Dei verbum. Quid paleae cum tritico? Ierem 23. Ezech. 3 Ierem. 1. 3. Zelo flagrent, nec occasionem vllam negligant. Sic Christus Iohan. 4. 6. Matth. 13. Hoc ipsum faciant etiam qui in magistratu sunt. Singuli item.
units.tr: Note: the duty of ministers. That is, let them remember that they are not ordinary heralds but witnesses. Truth is required of them, Exod. 20. Let them speak not their own inventions but the word of God. What has chaff to do with wheat? Jer. 23; Ezek. 3; Jer. 1. Let them burn with zeal and neglect no opportunity. So Christ, John 4; Matt. 13. Let those also who are in the magistracy do the same. So should each individual.

units.la: II. Historia nova sequitur, vt Euangelium & Christi cognitio ad Aethiopiam vsq; fit propagata. Sicuti praedictum Pf 68 72. 87. If. 60. Estq; vna ex praecipuis huius libri, quia exemplum habet singulare conuersionis perfectae, in quo apparet Dei bonitas erga homines, & quid faciant, qui sua lubriter conuerti volunt.
units.tr: II. The narrative now moves on, to show that the gospel and the knowledge of Christ was propagated as far as Ethiopia, as was foretold: Ps. 68, 72, 87; Isa. 60. It is one of the principal points of this book, because it offers a singular example of a perfect conversion, in which God's goodness toward men appears, and shows what those should do who willingly wish to be converted.

units.la: In praesenti duae personae proponuntur.
units.tr: Two persons are set forth in the present passage.

units.la: Philippus, cuius ministerio hic vsus est Deus. In hoc Not. 1. Vocatione. Angelus loquitur ei, & iubet quid faciat. Ergo nihil fecit ille ex priuato arbitrio, neq; etiam eum vocauit Aethiops. Sed totum hocDei opus fuit, qui hunc voluit saluum fieri. Vnde sequitur, hoc illi contigisse
units.tr: Philip, through whose ministry God here made use. In this part, note 1: the calling. The angel speaks to him and tells him what to do. Therefore he did nothing on his own private judgment, nor did the Ethiopian call him. Rather, this whole thing was the work of God, who wished this man to be saved. Whence it follows that this happened to him

units.la: Aethiopis conuersi hi
units.tr: of the converted Ethiopian.

units.la: Vocatio Philippi specialis
units.tr: The special calling of Philip

units.la: ex gratuita misericordia. Idem de omnibus nobis debet sentiri. Sic vocatus Adam,Gen.3. Arbraham,Gen.12.Iof.23. Petrus,Mat.26.Dauid,2.Sa.11.12.Matthæus, Mat.9.Paul.Act.9.1.Cor.15.Sic Act.16.Ne que hic quicquam tribui debet operibus præparationis: quia hæc quoque ex Deo sunt. Vide Rom.11.Eph.2.Tit.3.
units.tr: from God's free mercy. The same ought to be understood about all of us. Thus Adam was called (Gen. 3), Abraham (Gen. 12), Joshua (Josh. 23), Peter (Matt. 26), David (2 Sam. 11–12), Matthew (Matt. 9), Paul (Acts 9; 1 Cor. 15). Likewise in Acts 16. Nor should anything here be attributed to works of preparation, because these too are from God. See Rom. 11; Eph. 2; Titus 3.

units.la: Interim disciimus. ¶1. Quanti Deus ho minem faciat, quando non contentus omnes creaturas inferiores eius seruitio destinasse,(Psal.89.) insuper Angelos quoq; mittit. Sic de periculis Christus,Matt.18. Similia,Act.10 16.12.27. Rectè ergo Scripturæ,Heb.1.Psal.34.91. Dilige ergo Deum, & hunc solum colito, Apo.19.22.¶2. Euangelij dignitas, quando Angelorum testimonio confirmatur, & eorundem ministerio promouetur. Imò primi prædicârunt Angeli,Lu.1.2 24.Act.1.Adde his Dei Filium & sanctissimos homines veteris & noui Testamenti.Non est ergo commentum humanum, Ioh.7.1.Theff.2. ¶3.Deum in nobis conuertendis vti hominum ad hoc deletorum ministerio. Poterat so lus agere, vt qui solus in corda ius habet. Sed nohis se accommodat, & ministros dat.Sic Act.10.16.Hinc Rom.10.Agnoscamus ergo eius gratiæ signum esse,quando
units.tr: Meanwhile we learn: (1) how highly God esteems man, when, not content to have destined all the lower creatures for his service (Ps. 89), he sends angels as well. So Christ speaks of the dangers, Matt. 18. Similar things are in Acts 10, 16, 12, 27. Rightly therefore Scripture says (Heb. 1; Ps. 34, 91): love God, and worship him alone (Rev. 19, 22). (2) The dignity of the gospel, when it is confirmed by the testimony of angels and advanced by their ministry. Indeed the first preachers were angels (Luke 1, 2, 24; Acts 1). Add to these the Son of God and the most holy men of the Old and New Testaments. It is therefore not a human invention (John 7; 1 Thess. 2). (3) That God, in converting men, uses the ministry of men set apart for this. He could act alone, since he alone has right over hearts. But he accommodates himself to us and gives us ministers. So Acts 10, 16; hence Rom. 10. Let us acknowledge therefore that this is a sign of his grace, when he gives ministers

units.la: ministros dat, Amos 2.Mich.6. Iræ quando aufert, aut falsos finit irrepere,Am.8. 1.Reg.22.Zach.11.Nihil miserius, perinde ac fi Sol eriperetur,Matt.9.¶4.Deum mi nistros præceptis instruere, non suo eos arbitrio permittere.Præcipuum est,vt suum verbum prædicent,de quo supra.Deinde vt fortes sint: & ideo prædicit quid euenturum.Sic Ier.1,Sic Apostolis Matt.10.24.Ioh.15.16. Ex eo igitur petant consolatione,D.quì præuidit,& prędixit non deerit illis,Lu.21.Neq; tentari sinet supra vires,1.Cor.10. 2.Cor.1. Hoc ipsum sibi ap plicent alij quoque. Omnibus enim prædicitur,quòd crux maneat credentes.Mat thæi 16.2.Tim.3.Act.14 Rom.8. Item vide Gen.3.Iob.5.8.&c.
units.tr: (Amos 2; Mic. 6). When he takes them away in anger, or allows false ones to creep in (Amos 8; 1 Kings 22; Zech. 11), nothing is more wretched, just as if the sun were snatched away (Matt. 9). (4) That God instructs ministers with precepts and does not leave them to their own judgment. Chief among these is that they preach his word, of which above. Then that they be brave; and therefore he foretells what will happen. So Jer. 1; so to the Apostles, Matt. 10:24; John 15:16. From this, therefore, let them seek consolation: he who foresaw and foretold will not fail them (Luke 21), nor will he allow them to be tempted beyond their strength (1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1). Let others also apply this to themselves. For it is foretold to all that the cross remains for believers (Matt. 16; 2 Tim. 3; Acts 14; Rom. 8). See also Gen. 3; Job 5, 8, etc.

units.la: ¶2. Obedientiam Philippi. Mox viam ingreditur, & neq; curiosius quærit,quid agendum, neque rationes prætexit, quæ multæ occurrebant, quia peregrinus, solus,in desertum,&c. Sed agnoscit Dei vocem,& ad se pertinere scit,quod habetur Num.15.
units.tr: (2) The obedience of Philip. He immediately enters the road, and neither asks curiously what must be done, nor puts forward the reasons that came to mind in great number: that he was a stranger, alone, going into the desert, and so on. Instead he recognises the voice of God, and knows that what is written in Num. 15 applies to him.

units.la: ¶ Imitemur,vt ipsi quoque simpliciter Deo obediamus,etiam tunc quando suorum mandatorum nullas causas reddit. Tunc enim obedientiâ nostram probare vult. Sic Abraham,Gen.12.22.Sic Aposto-
units.tr: Let us imitate him, so that we too obey God simply, even when he gives no reasons for his commands. For then he wishes to test our obedience. So Abraham (Gen. 12, 22), so the Apostles

units.la: li, Matth. 4 9. Actorum 9 16. Qui cunstantur, eo ipso produnt suam contumaciam. Qui disputant, aut Dei mandata revocant ad carnis rationem, ij sibijpsis remoras injiciunt. Vide Saulem, 1.Samuelis decimoquinto. Meminerimus a nobis fidei obedientiam exigi, 2.Cor.10.Rom.16. In summa bonitatem Dei agnoscamus, qui nostra opera vti dignatur, accommodemus nos eius voluntati, & eidem permittamus eucentum, Psal.55. Interim indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: (Matt. 4, 9; Acts 9, 16). Those who hesitate reveal by that very fact their obstinacy. Those who dispute, or call God's commands back to the reasoning of the flesh, put obstacles in their own way. See Saul, 1 Samuel 15. Let us remember that obedience of faith is demanded of us (2 Cor. 10; Rom. 16). In sum, let us acknowledge the goodness of God, who deigns to use our works; let us accommodate ourselves to his will, and let us leave the outcome to him (Ps. 55). Meanwhile let us pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA LXVI.
units.tr: HOMILIA LXVI.

units.la: 27 Et ecce vir Aethiops eunuchus, dynastes Candacis reginae Athiopum, qui praerat universis illius opibus, veneratque adoraturus in Hierusalem:
units.tr: 27 And behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch, a great officer of Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem to worship:

units.la: 28 Reuertebatur sedens in curru suo, legebatque Esaiam Prophetam.
units.tr: 28 He was returning, sitting in his chariot, and reading the prophet Esaias.

units.la: VT hominis perditio ex eius auersio ne a Deo nascitur: ita salus ex eo dependet, vt a peccatis & superstitionibus ad Deum reuertamur. Ideo hoc omnis Scriptura inculcat. Prophetae, Isa.44 55. Am.5. Ier.3 4 36. Zach.1. Ezech.18 Mal.3 Baptista, Mat.3. Christus, Mat.4. Mar.1i Apostoli Actor.
units.tr: Just as a man's ruin arises from his turning away from God, so his salvation depends on his turning back to God from sins and superstitions. For this reason all Scripture presses this point. The Prophets: Isa. 44; 55. Am. 5. Jer. 3; 4; 36. Zech. 1. Ezek. 18. Mal. 3. The Baptist: Matt. 3. Christ: Matt. 4; Mark 1. The Apostles: Acts 2, etc.

units.la: Act.2 &c. Vt autem doctrina hæc euidentior fit, multis exemplis confirmatur. Inter quæ per quàm memorabile est, quod in Æthiope proponitur. Continet enim omnia: quæ ad veram hominis conuersionem faciunt. Nam primo de Philippo egit Lucas, cuius ministerio vsus est Deus. Vbi didicimus causam nostræ conuersionis esse gratuitam Dei misericordiam. Vt enim Eunucho nihil huius cogitanti, Deus doctorem ei destinat Philippum: ita solet ferè cum hominib.agere, & sic cum gentibus actum fuisse liber hic docet, &c. Sequitur Eunuchi descriptio.
units.tr: But so that this teaching may be clearer, it is confirmed by many examples. Among these, the one set forth in the Ethiopian is most memorable, for it contains everything that contributes to a person's true conversion. For first Luke tells of Philip, through whose ministry God worked. Here we learn that the cause of our conversion is God's free mercy. For just as God, when the eunuch was thinking of nothing of this kind, appointed Philip as his teacher, so he is accustomed to deal with people, and this book teaches that he dealt in this way with the Gentiles, etc. There follows the description of the eunuch.

units.la: I. Genus & Natio. Æthiops. Cœpit er, go impleri, Psalm. 68. 72. 87. Isa. 60. Typus item 1. Reg. 10. Sed Not. ¶ Primum ex gentibus Christianis ex tam remota gente deligi. Ita docemur promissiones gentium vocatione ad omnes extendi, vt ne remotissimi quidem excludantur. Et ita Christus ipse exponit, Matth. 8. Actorum 1. Dulcis consolatio, quòd Deus neminem fastidiat propter gentem aut veteres iniurias. Nouit passim suos, 2. Timoth. 2. Et vt omnes in genere vocat, ita omnes ad se venientes recipit, Matth. 11. Iohan. 6. Seruit autem hoc instituti Fidei, Christum scilicet esse vniuersalem.
units.tr: I. Race and nation: an Ethiopian. What was begun is now being fulfilled: Ps. 68; 72; 87. Isa. 60. Likewise the type in 1 Kings 10. But note: first, that a man from a Gentile people, and from so remote a nation, is chosen. We are taught by this that the promises of the calling of the Gentiles extend to all, so that even the most remote are not excluded. Christ himself explains it this way: Matt. 8; Acts 1. It is a sweet comfort that God despises no one on account of their nation or old wrongs. He knows his own everywhere, 2 Tim. 2. And just as he calls all people in general, so he receives all who come to him, Matt. 11; John 6. This also serves the purpose of the faith, namely that Christ is universal.

units.la: Æthiops Eunuchi descriptio. Genus, Æthiops
units.tr: Description of the eunuch. Race: Ethiopian.

units.la: Seruatorem, ad quem omnes confugere oporteat,qui voluut seruari,Actor.4 Ioh. 4.Errant, qui vnum quenque in sua reli‐gione putant seruari. Officium item erga proximum, ne aliquem faltidiamus propter gentem, &c.
units.tr: He is the Saviour to whom all must flee who wish to be saved: Acts 4; John 4. Those err who think that each person is saved within his own religion. Likewise there is a duty towards our neighbour, that we should not despise anyone on account of their nation, etc.

units.la: II. Conditio. Eunuchus. Sic olim dſti
units.tr: II. Condition. Eunuch. So they were once called.

units.la: Satrapæ,regibus & reginis familiariores. Neue vulgaris putetur,additur† Item præfectus toti gazæ. Potentiæ Christi argumentum, qui potentissimos quoque potest ad se pertrahere,licet multa remorentur. Opes. Matt 19. Honores, Ioh.5 12. Pericula. Si velit omnia obstacula ille tollit, Psal.2 72.Ita Magos adduxit, Matt.2. Hodie idem experimur.
units.tr: Satraps, more intimate with kings and queens. Lest he be thought of ordinary standing, it is added: also prefect over the whole treasury. This is a proof of Christ's power, who can draw even the most powerful to himself, though many things hinder. Wealth: Matt. 19. Honours: John 5; 12. Dangers: if he wills, he removes all obstacles, Ps. 2; 72. So he brought the Magi, Matt. 2. Today we experience the same.

units.la: Nota Magistratus non excludi a Christo & salute. Magistratus enim institutus a Deo, Rom.13. At is nihil instituit, quod salutem impediat,1.Timoth.2.
