Ana‐baptistæ obijciunt exemplum Christi,Iohan.6 Luc.12. Idem quod dixit,Luc.22. At Christus non venerat regni causa, Iohan. 18. Sed vt regnu Dei instauraret, quod omnis loci homines recipit, Galat.3. Colos. 2. Vt igitur olim fuerunt sancti principes. Ita tales erunt in Nouo Testamento, Isa: 49. Tales fuerunt Iosephus Arimathæus, Lucæ 23. Matthæi27. Centuriones Matthæi. thæi 8. Actorum 10. Paulus Sergius, Actorum 13. Eraftus. 1. Corinth. 16. Nec legitur, Apostolos cuiquam mandasse, ut se magistratu abdicaret. Imo seruos habere licuit, 1 Tim. 6. Neminem ergo Anabaptistæ moueant, quorum spiritus, vel hoc argumento sese prodit.
units.tr: Note that magistrates are not excluded from Christ and salvation. For the magistrate is instituted by God, Rom. 13. But he instituted nothing that hinders salvation, 1 Tim. 2. The Anabaptists object the example of Christ, John 6; Luke 12. The same as he said, Luke 22. But Christ had not come for the sake of a kingdom, John 18. Rather, he came to restore the kingdom of God, which receives people of every place, Gal. 3; Col. 2. Just as there were holy princes in the past, so there will be such in the New Testament, Isa. 49. Such were Joseph of Arimathea, Luke 23; Matt. 27; the centurions of Matthew 8; Acts 10; Paul's Sergius Paulus, Acts 13; Erastus, 1 Cor. 16. Nor is it read that the Apostles ordered anyone to give up his magistracy. Indeed, it was permitted to have slaves, 1 Tim. 6. Let the Anabaptists therefore not disturb anyone, whose spirit betrays itself by this very argument.

units.la: III. Studia & mores.
units.tr: III. Pursuits and morals.

units.la: ¶ 1. Venerat Hiero solymam adoraturus. Et hoc fore prædixerat Salomon, 1 Reg. 8. Fuerunt enim in gentibus aliqui vera Dei cognitione præditi ex parte, Rom. 1. 14. Et Regina Saba aliquem gustum suis præbuit, 1. Reg. 10. Iuuit quoque Cyrus, Ezr. 1. Alexander Magnus. Romani item, qui Iudæis αὐτονομίαν concesserunt. Hinc illud Ioh. 12. &c.
units.tr: 1. Here came the Ethiopian to worship in Jerusalem. Solomon had foretold that this would happen, 1 Kings 8. For among the Gentiles there were some who had a partial knowledge of the true God, Rom. 1; 14. And the Queen of Sheba offered some taste of it to her people, 1 Kings 10. Cyrus also helped, Ezra 1. Alexander the Great did so too, and the Romans, who granted the Jews autonomy. Hence that saying in John 12, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Legit Isaiam. Vnde vero hunc habuit Ptolemæus Philadelphus ante Christum natum annis 267. &c. Factum illud singulari prouidentia Dei, qui Euangelij prædicationi sic viam strauit. Nam ex eo tempore gentib. libri sacri non omnino incogniti fuerunt. Vide Act. 17. Non mirum ergo, quòd vir princeps illos habuit, &c.
units.tr: 2. He was reading Isaiah. But how did Ptolemy Philadelphus have it, 267 years before the birth of Christ, etc.? This came about by the singular providence of God, who thus paved the way for the preaching of the Gospel. For from that time the holy books were not wholly unknown to the Gentiles. See Acts 17. It is no wonder, then, that this prince had them, etc.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Quales esse oportet eos, qui conuerti volunt. Non prophani, qui Deum & eius verbum scurriliter contemnant. Tales enim ex mundo sunt, Ioh. 14. Sunt quidé omnes homines naturâ a Deo
units.tr: NOTE 1. What sort of people ought to be those who wish to be converted? Not profane people, who mock God and his Word with buffoonery. For such are of the world, John 14. Indeed all people are by nature

units.la: alieni,neque ëius verbo delectantur,s Corinth.3 Sed Deus irridiat alienorum quoque mentibus aliquas scintillas, quas exci pere,fouere & augere oportet. Id faciunt electi. Aliter Pharao, Exo.5. Quem hodie imitantur qui dicunt: Quis in tanta Deorum multitudine me certū reddet? Quid ad me Prophetas? Annon homines fuerunt? Quis scit an illi haec scripserint? Respondet hoc hominum genus hodie, 2.Pet.3. Ideo pauciores feruantur. Quia autem tales extremè blasphemi sunt, & publicæ sa lutis hostes, publica authoritate coercerī debent.
units.tr: estranged from God, and do not delight in his Word, 1 Cor. 3. But God kindles in the minds even of the estranged some sparks, which we ought to rouse, foster and increase. The elect do this. Pharaoh did otherwise, Exod. 5, whom those imitate today who say: Who will make me sure amid such a multitude of gods? What have I to do with the Prophets? Were they not men? Who knows whether they wrote these things? This kind of people answers today, 2 Pet. 3. Therefore fewer are saved. But because such people are extremely blasphemous and enemies of the public welfare, they ought to be restrained by public authority.

units.la: ¶ 2. Non nouum esse, quod scripturæ in linguas vulgares transferuntur. Quàm erunt item, qui laicos arcent à lectione scripturarū. Aliter Deus instituit, Exo.19 20. Deut.6.2. Tim.3. Pf.1. Est ergo hoc sacrilegium, quo nu lum atrocius potest admitti. Iudæi antistites licet corruptissimi, nihil huius vnquam fecerunt. Solus Antiochus, &c. f. Mach.1. Ex eo igitur apparet, quid iudicandū de nostri seculi tyrannis.
units.tr: 2. It is not new that the Scriptures are translated into the vernacular tongues. How many, again, there are who keep the laity from reading the Scriptures! God has ordained otherwise, Exod. 19; 20; Deut. 6; 2 Tim. 3; Ps. 1. This is therefore sacrilege, and nothing more atrocious can be committed. The Jewish chief priests, though most corrupt, never did anything of this kind. Only Antiochus did, etc., 1 Macc. 1. From this, then, it is clear what ought to be judged of the tyrants of our age.

units.la: ¶ 3. Principes viros decere frequentem lectionem. Vide Deut.17. Exemplum Dauidis, Psal.19 119. 1. Accedat historiæ cognitio, quæ de multis admonet. Memorabile exemplum, Hest. 6. Et constat inter
units.tr: 3. That frequent reading becomes princes especially. See Deut. 17. The example of David, Ps. 19; 119. Let there also be knowledge of history, which warns about many things. A memorable example is in Esther 6. And it is established that among

units.la: gentes vulgò id factum esse. Alexander M. Iulius Cæsar. Stolidi nimis hodie, qui lectionem nihil ad se pertinere putant, interea ludunt, epulantur. Fit ergo quod habetur, Eccl. 10. Dan. 5. Agnoscamus Dei bonitatem & accommodemus nos medijs quæ offert. Legamus, audiamus & indesinenter Oremus
units.tr: the Gentiles this was commonly done. Alexander the Great, Julius Caesar. Today there are too many foolish people who think reading has nothing to do with them, while they play and feast in the meantime. So what is written in Eccl. 10 and Dan. 5 comes to pass. Let us acknowledge God's goodness and accommodate ourselves to the means he offers. Let us read, listen, and pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA LXVI.
units.tr: HOMILIA LXVI.

units.la: 29 Dixit autem spiritus Philippo, Accede, & adiunge te ad currum istum.
units.tr: 29 And the Spirit said to Philip, Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.

units.la: 30 Accurrens autem Philippus, audivit eum legentem Esaiam Prophetam, & dixit: Anne intelligis quæ legis?
units.tr: 30 And Philip ran up, heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and said: Do you really understand what you are reading?

units.la: 31 At ille ait: Qui enim possim, nisi quis mihi præierit? Et precatus est Philippum, ut ascenderet, sederetque secum.
units.tr: 31 But he said: How could I, unless someone guided me? And he begged Philip to come up and sit with him.

units.la: ETsi Deus pro sua bonitate (1. Tim. 2.) peccatores ad se conuerti velit, & ad se conuersis remissionem peccatorum & salutem certam polliceatur, Ezech. 18. Zachariæ 1. Isa. 1. 43. 44. 45.) ea tamen est humani ingenij vitiositas, ut pleriq; conuerti nolint. Causa, quod aut mundo sic deleētantur, ut nolint auelli, aut de Dei gratia diffidunt, &c. Gen. 4. Ideo Scripturæ multa proponunt exempla eorum, qui be ne conuersi sunt, vt his excitemur & confirmemur. Inter hæc præcipuum & præfens hoc,quo omnia continentur, quæ ad salutarem conuersionè faciunt. Primò enim dictum de Philippo,cuius ministerio Deus vtitur. Deind deipso Eunucho,vbi didicimus,nihil obstare saluti eorum, qui volunt conuerti,&c. Sequitur de medio conuersionis, quod non aliud est quàm Euangelij prædicatio, qua peccatoribus offertur Christus, qui & pœnitentiam in nobis efficit,& simul remissionis peccatorum Mediator est, Actor. 5. Narrat ergo Lucas,qua occasione Philippus hunc Eunucho prædicârit: Vbi rursus patebit, nihil hîc absque peculiari prouidentia Dei factum fuisse.
units.tr: Although God, in his goodness (1 Tim. 2), wishes sinners to be converted to himself, and promises forgiveness of sins and certain salvation to those who are converted (Ezek. 18; Zech. 1; Isa. 1, 43, 44, 45), yet such is the perversity of the human mind that most people are unwilling to be converted. The cause is that they either take such delight in the world that they do not want to be torn away from it, or they distrust the grace of God, etc. (Gen. 4). Therefore the Scriptures set before us many examples of those who were truly converted, so that we may be stirred up and strengthened by them. Among these, this present one is outstanding, containing everything that contributes to saving conversion. First, what is said about Philip, through whose ministry God works; then about the Eunuch himself, where we learn that nothing stands in the way of salvation for those who wish to be converted, etc. Next comes the means of conversion, which is nothing other than the preaching of the gospel, by which Christ is offered to sinners; he both works repentance in us and is at the same time the Mediator of the forgiveness of sins (Acts 5). Luke therefore relates on what occasion Philip preached to this Eunuch; here again it will be clear that nothing was done without a special providence of God.

units.la: I. Spiritus aduentante Eunucho iubet Philippum accedere. Loquitur autem Lucas vel de Angelo, qui eum exire iusserat, vel de Spiritu Sancto, quem Christus advocatum discipulis promisit, & qui tunc maximè adfuit eis, quando Euangelium debuerunt prædicare aliquibus, Ioh. 14. 16. Mat. 10. Act. 13. 16. Not. ¶ Exemplum prouidentiæ Dei omnia gubernantis. Diceret quis, fortuitum fuisse, quod duo isti hi hïc sibi occurrunt. Quod item Eunuchus hoc temporis momento legit Ifaiam, & quidem locum, qui præfenti causæ inprimis seruiebat. Sed quia Angeli & Spiritus subinde nominantur, conltat Deum hoc omne pro suo nutu direxisse, Prou.16. Similia exempla sunt in historijs, Iofephi, Gen. 37. 39. &c. Sed nihil fortuitum accidisse, conltat ex Pfal. 105. Et Iofeph hoc agnouit, Gen. 45 50. Idem videmus in Iobi historia, Iob. 1.2. &c. Vtilis doctrina. Itaenim patienter ferimus quæcunque accidunt. Dauid, Pfal. 22. 31. 56. 139. Ideo Christus quoque de hoc Apostolos admonet, Matt. 10. Luc. 12. Et singulos hoc argumento consolatur, Matt. 6. Excitet item hæc consideratio, vt alacriter obediamus Deo & vtamur fortiter occafionib. quas nobis Deus offert. Et huc facit quod sequitur.
units.tr: I. When the Eunuch approaches, the Spirit bids Philip go near. Luke speaks either of an angel, who had ordered him to go out, or of the Holy Spirit, whom Christ promised to the disciples as Advocate, and who was especially present with them whenever they had to preach the gospel to anyone (John 14:16; Matt. 10; Acts 13, 16). Note: an example of the providence of God governing all things. Someone might say that it was by chance that these two men met, and that the Eunuch happened to be reading Isaiah at that very moment, and indeed a passage which especially served the present purpose. But since angels and the Spirit are mentioned here and there, it is clear that God directed all this at his own will (Prov. 16). Similar examples are found in the histories of Joseph (Gen. 37, 39, etc.). But that nothing happens by chance is clear from Psalm 105; and Joseph recognised this (Gen. 45, 50). We see the same in the history of Job (Job 1, 2, etc.). The teaching is useful: for thus we bear patiently whatever happens. David (Ps. 22, 31, 56, 139). Therefore Christ also warns the apostles of this (Matt. 10; Luke 12), and comforts each one with this argument (Matt. 6). This consideration should also stir us to obey God eagerly and to make bold use of the opportunities God offers us. What follows bears on this as well.

units.la: II. Philippus vt prius Angeli mandato paruit, ita nunc occurrit & audit, &c. Vbi Nota. ¶ 1. Deum non deesse in sua vocatione ambulantibus. Iubet pro suo in nos iure, neq; semper ratione reddit suorum præceptorum. At hic cogitemus, illum cefe nostri amantem (Ioh. 3. 1. Iohan. 4.) iustum & ipsissimam sapientiam. Pareamus ergo, & non deerit suis promissionibus, quo minus occasiones rerum præclarè
units.tr: II. Philip, as he had obeyed the angel's command before, so now he runs up and listens, etc. Note here: (1) God is not absent from those who walk in their calling. He commands by his own right over us, and does not always give an account of his precepts; but here let us consider that he is a lover of his own (John 3:1; 1 John 4), and the most just and most perfect wisdom. Let us therefore obey, and he will not fail his promises, so that he does not offer us opportunities of doing noble deeds.

units.la: gerendarum nobis offerat. Et licet quid accidat grauius,dabit euentum,&c.1.Corinth. 10. Sic cum Abrahamo factu, Gen. 12.14.22.Cum Dauide non semel.Cum Elia,Reg 17. 18. ¶ 2 Philippi studium. Non grauatim obtemperat,sed occurrit,neque luti aut pulueris, neq; periculi rationem habens. Imo non pudet illum pedisequi instar currum comitari. Diuersus planè a Pontificum moribus. Item tam propè accedit, vt audiat legentem. Interrogat denique: Ita nimirum occasionem captans. ¶ Officij hic admonentur ministri, vt nimirum occasiones aliquos lucrifaciendi subinde quærant, & oblatas nō negligant. Quia enim piscatores sunt (Matth.4. 13.) hos imitentur.Ita Christus, Iohan. 3.4.6. Matth.13 Imo vide Luc.15. Sic Petrus Actor.16.17. Nemo igitur rusticos aut importunos putet, si quid faciant simile. Idè faciat alij quoq;,iubent primæ petitiones Orationis Dom. At hodie tam abest,vt quæramus occasiones, vt negligamus oblatas.Imo ipsi remoramur Euagelij cursu.
units.tr: And whatever more grievous thing happens, he will give the outcome, etc. (1 Cor. 10). So it was with Abraham (Gen. 12, 14, 22), with David more than once, with Elijah (1 Kings 17, 18). (2) Philip's eagerness. He obeys without reluctance, but runs up, caring neither for mud or dust nor for the danger. Indeed he is not ashamed to accompany the chariot like a servant on foot. This is quite different from the ways of the Papists. Likewise he draws so near that he can hear the reader. Finally he asks a question, thus clearly seizing the opportunity. Here ministers are reminded of their duty: that they should seek out opportunities of winning someone now and then, and not neglect those offered. For since they are fishermen (Matt. 4:13), let them imitate these men. So Christ (John 3, 4, 6; Matt. 13). Indeed see Luke 15. So Peter (Acts 16, 17). Let no one therefore think them rustic or troublesome if they do something similar. The first petitions of the Lord's Prayer likewise bid others to do so. But today we are so far from seeking opportunities that we neglect those offered. Indeed we ourselves hold back the course of the gospel.

units.la: III. Eunuchus amicè respondet: Vbi multa concurrunt obseruatu dignissima. 1.Humanitas in tanto viro. Alius per contemptum respondisset, aut conuitiatus fuisset, vel famulos iussisset illum abripere. re. Hodie certè Abbates nō ferrent talem ignorantiam. Fatetur suam ignorantiam. Rarum hoc in principibus, qui ne ignorantes videantur, qui duis defendunt.Cupit intelligere. Ideo precatur Philippum, vt currum conscendat, & interpretetur.
units.tr: III. The Eunuch answers in a friendly way. Here many things come together that are most worthy of notice. (1) Courtesy in so great a man. Another would have answered with contempt, or railed at him, or ordered his servants to drag him away. Today, certainly, abbots would not tolerate such ignorance. He confesses his ignorance. This is rare among princes, who defend their ignorance so that they may not seem ignorant. He desires to understand. Therefore he begs Philip to mount the chariot and explain it.

units.la: ¶ 1. Vt nos accommodare debeamus medijs quæ Deus offert. Meminerimus nos rerum diuinarum rudes esse, neque pudeat hoc fateri, &c. pudeat eorum, qui possunt docere. Nescicbat hic, quis esset Philippus. Quia tamen ex eius quæstione poterat spem concipere, ad se illum recipit. Hodie contemnuntur etiam notissimi, quos nobis Deus doctores destinauit. Ministros pauci ad se attollunt, sed potius deprimunt. Imo qui in pretio erant, cum Abbates essent, conuersi fastidiuntur.
units.tr: (1) That we ought to accommodate ourselves to the means which God offers. Let us remember that we are unskilled in divine things, and let us not be ashamed to confess this, etc. Let them be ashamed who are able to teach. This man did not know who Philip was; yet because from his question he could hope for something, he takes him in. Today even the most well-known teachers whom God has appointed for us are despised. Few raise up ministers, but rather they press them down. Indeed those who were held in esteem when they were abbots become loathsome once converted.

units.la: ¶ 2. Scripturas interpretatione opus habere, etiam quando in lingua vulgari habentur. Alioqui vel non intelligimus, vel non putamus ad nos pertinere. Vide Dauidem, 2. Sam. 12. Vetus mos, Neh. 8. Lu 4. 24. 1. Cor. 14. Hinc illud Pauli. 2. Tim 2. Errant, qui Scripturas simpliciter recitari volunt. Nimirū quòd applicatio illis dolet. Nec periculū est ab interpretatione,ne quis fallat. Sunt certi indices. Articuli fidei, Oratio Dominica, Decalogus. Fides denique & charitas. Oremus.
units.tr: (2) That the Scriptures need interpretation, even when they are held in the vernacular tongue. Otherwise we either do not understand them, or do not think they pertain to us. See David (2 Sam. 12); the ancient custom (Neh. 8; Luke 4:24; 1 Cor. 14). Hence that saying of Paul (2 Tim. 2). Those err who want the Scriptures simply read aloud, since application is what they dislike. Nor is there danger from interpretation, that someone may be deceived. There are sure guides: the articles of faith, the Lord's Prayer, the Decalogue; and finally faith and charity. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXIIX.
units.tr: HOMILY 68.

units.la: 31 Locus autem quem legebat,hic erat: Vt ouis ad mactationem ductus est:& vt agnus coram suo tonsore mutus,ita non aperuit os suum.
units.tr: The passage he was reading was this: He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he did not open his mouth.

units.la: 33 In ipsius humilitate iudicium eius sublatum est. Generationem vero eius quis enarrabit? quoniam tollitur de terra vita eius.
units.tr: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. But who will declare his generation? For his life is taken from the earth.

units.la: LVcas Aethiopis conuersi historiam fingularidiligentia describit,eo quod eo exemplo docemur,in quo consistat vera conuersio, ex qua omnis salus dependet.Sunt hic consideranda.1.Causam primam ex Deo esse. Quia enim naturâ ab hoc alieni fumus (Rom.3.) nunquam ad eum conuertemur,nisi ille nos prꝫueniat. Thren.4.Cant.1.Videmus hoc in praesenti,& quotidie experimur. 2.Medium esse, verbu Dei,quo nobis Christum offert, in quo refipifcentiam & peccatorum remissio nem habemus,Act.5.Hoc igitur audire,legere & meditari debent, qui conuerti vo lunt. Hoc fecit Æthiops. Etsi innutritus effet fuperftitionib,tamen verùDeũ quaesiuit. siuit. Legit,neq; contempsit occasionem oblatam. Quia autem Dei verbum in Scri pturis late patet,indicatur locus,qui huic causae argumentum praebuit.
units.tr: Luke describes the conversion of the Ethiopian with particular care, because from this example we are taught in what true conversion consists, on which all salvation depends. Three things are to be considered here. (1) The first cause is from God. For since we are by nature alienated from him (Rom. 3), we will never turn to him unless he first comes to us (Lam. 4; Song 1). We see this at present and experience it every day. (2) The means is the Word of God, by which he offers us Christ, and in which we have repentance and the forgiveness of sins (Acts 5). Therefore those who wish to be converted ought to hear, read and meditate on this. The Ethiopian did this. Although he had been brought up in superstition, nevertheless he sought the true God. He read, and did not despise the opportunity offered to him. Because the Word of God is widely spread through the Scriptures, the passage which provided the basis for this cause is indicated.

units.la: ¶ Extat Isa. LIII. Promiserat liberatio- nem. Vt ergo minus dubitarent, ipsum li- beratorem describit. Omnium vero, quae dicuntur, summa his verbis continetur, quae tunc legit Æthiops. Ita vero Deus negotium hoc gubernauit. Obseruemus, huius opus esse, quando nobis obtingunt fidi doctores & monitores. Sed videamus singula.
units.tr: There is Isaiah 53, which had promised deliverance. So that they might doubt less, he describes the deliverer himself. The sum of everything that is said is contained in these words, which the Ethiopian was then reading. God so directed this business. We should observe that this is the work of faithful teachers and admonishers when they come to us. But let us look at the individual points.

units.la: 1. Mactationis meminit, vt ostendat vio lenta morte moriturum. Ideo meminit ex sti tremae ignominiae, dolorum, vulnerum, vi bicum, &c. Praeuidit enim Spiritus san- ctus crucem Christi Iudaeis scandalo fore, 1.Cor.1. Deinde posteris quoque tempo- ribus exorituros, qui illius passionem ne- garent, eo quod carni absurda & impofsi- bilis videatur. Turcae. Ideo hoc iam inde ab initio praedici oportuit. Prima promis- sio, Gen.3. Typi. Isaac, Gen.22. Passa, Exod. 12.1.Cor.5. Sacrificia, Heb.8 9.10. Petra, E- xod.17. Num.20. Dauid, Psalm.22. &c. His quia consentiunt Apostoli, quos testes suos esse voluit (Iohan.15.21.) ne dubite- mus.
units.tr: (1) He mentions the slaughter in order to show that he would die a violent death. He therefore mentions the extreme shame, the pains, the wounds, the scourging and so on. For the Holy Spirit foresaw that the cross of Christ would be a stumbling block to the Jews (1 Cor. 1), and that later generations would arise who would deny his passion, because it seems absurd and impossible to the flesh, as the Turks do. Therefore it was necessary for this to be foretold from the very beginning. The first promise (Gen. 3). Types: Isaac (Gen. 22); the Passover (Exod. 12; 1 Cor. 5); the sacrifices (Heb. 8, 9, 10); the rock (Exod. 17; Num. 20); David (Ps. 22), etc. Since the apostles, whom he wished to be his witnesses (John 15:21), agree with these, let us not doubt.

units.la: Et Not. ¶Propter nos passum & mor tuum esse,quia non aliter fieri poterat hu mani generis redemptio.Docet hoc com munis sensus,&c. Ex eo autem collige : 1. Quanta sit atrocitas peccati,cum non ali-ter expiari potuerit. Vnu hoc sufficiat no bis contra huius blanditias,Ps 6.Etenim impij fuerimus,si hoc non moueat. 2.Va-nas esse omnes peccati expiationes, quæ extra Christum instituuntur,Act.4.1.Ioh. 1.Ro.3 &c.Ideo omnes ad se vocat, Matt. 11.Ioh.7.4.14. Et hoc vno contentos esse decet, vtalió vocantibus respondeamus cum Petro,Ioh.6.
units.tr: And note: that he suffered and died for us, because the redemption of the human race could not come about in any other way. Common sense teaches this, etc. From this, however, gather: (1) how great the atrocity of sin is, since it could not be expiated in any other way. Let this one thing suffice for us against its flatteries (Ps. 6). Indeed, we would be wicked if this did not move us. (2) That all the expiations of sin which are instituted outside Christ are vain (Acts 4; 1 John 1; Rom. 3, etc.). Therefore he calls all to himself (Matt. 11; John 7:37; 14). And we ought to be content with this one thing, so that, when others call us, we may answer with Peter (John 6).

units.la: II. Quomodo mortuus sit? Explicat hoc similibus ouiu & agnorum, eo quod antiquitus hi quotidie immolabantur, Exod.29.Erat autem hic typus Christi,qui a-gnus Dei dicitur Ioh.1. Apoc.13. Hic au-tem innuitur primum mors voluntaria, &c.Ioh.10.18. Deinde patientia perfectis-sima, quæ Pilato quoq; admirationi fuit, Luc.23.Ioh.18.19. Nec obstat, quod quæ-dam grauiter dixit ad montem oliueti,Lu-cæ 23.Caiaphæ,Ioh.18. Nunc vsum No-ţ. ¶ 1.Sua obedientia nostram inobedienti-am expiare voluit.Vide Rom 5. Hinc pe-tenda consolatio in conscientiæ tentatio-nibus. Quia enim dilectus ille Filius est, placuit. Non legible note text beyond the above. placatur in eo Pater,Matt 3.17. Itaq; cum Paulo argumentemur,Rom.8. §2.Vt suo exemplo nobis praeiret,1.Pet.2.Imitemur ergo,Mat.16.Moueat, quod ille innocens propter nos haec tulit,nos quicquid accidit,meruimus,Luc.23. Deinde, quod carnem coerceri necesse est,1.Cor.11. Item quod momento affligimur,2.Cor.4.
units.tr: II. How did he die? He explains this by the likeness of sheep and lambs, because in ancient times these were sacrificed daily (Exod. 29). This was a type of Christ, who is called the Lamb of God (John 1; Rev. 13). Here, however, it is first indicated that his death was voluntary (John 10:18). Then, the most perfect patience, which was a matter of wonder even to Pilate (Luke 23; John 18, 19). Nor does it stand in the way that he spoke certain things severely at the Mount of Olives (Luke 22), to Caiaphas (John 18). Now the use: (1) He willed that his obedience should atone for our disobedience. See Rom. 5. Hence consolation is to be sought in temptations of conscience. For because that beloved Son is pleasing, the Father is appeased in him (Matt. 3:17). Therefore let us argue with Paul (Rom. 8). (2) That he might go before us by his example (1 Pet. 2). Let us therefore imitate him (Matt. 16). Let it move us that this innocent one bore these things for our sake, while we deserved whatever befalls us (Luke 23). Next, that the flesh must necessarily be restrained (1 Cor. 11); likewise that we are afflicted for a moment (2 Cor. 4).

units.la: III. Victoriam & hinc secutam glori- am subijcit: In depressione eius, &c. Id est, per mortem cum depressus & omnino desperatus vi- deretur,Deus causam eius asseruit,& eue xit illum. Sic praedictum, Gen.3. Psal.110. Orat hoc ille Ioh.12.17. Coepit mox fieri. In morte prodigia edita,Matth.27.Iohan.19.Sequuta resurrectio,Mat.28.Vide Hof 13 1 Corinth.15. Gloriosa Ascensio, Psal.68 Ephef 4. Sesio ad dextram Dei, Mat.28 Ps.110.
units.tr: III. He adds the victory and the glory that followed from it: In his humiliation, etc. That is, through death, when he seemed humbled and utterly despaired of, God vindicated his cause and raised him up. So it was foretold (Gen. 3; Ps. 110). He said this himself (John 12:17). It soon began to happen. At his death, prodigies were displayed (Matt. 27; John 19). The resurrection followed (Matt. 28; see Hos. 13; 1 Cor. 15). The glorious ascension (Ps. 68; Eph. 4). The sitting at the right hand of God (Matt. 28; Ps. 110).

units.la: § Consoletur hoc & fidem noštra con firmet, ne vel Christi cruce vel nostra offendamur. Nobis vicit ille, Ioh.16. Ro.8. Ergo etiam nobis regnat, nobis item adest, Mat.28.Ioh.14.Id declarauit in Stephano, Act.7. In aliis Martyribus idem cernitur. Denique ad se transfert, Ioh.14.17. & memoriam suorum in terris feruat,Ps.34.112. Prou.10. Ita in sanctis idem fit, quod de Christo hic dicitur.
units.tr: Let this console us and confirm our faith, so that we are not offended either by the cross of Christ or by our own. He conquered for us (John 16; Rom. 8). Therefore he also reigns for us, and is likewise present with us (Matt. 28; John 14). He declared this in Stephen (Acts 7). The same is seen in the other martyrs. Finally, he transfers them to himself (John 14:17), and preserves the memory of his own on earth (Ps. 34, 112; Prov. 10). Thus what is said here of Christ also happens in the saints.

units.la: Noted: Ioh. 3.
units.tr: Note: John 3.

units.la: Cap 8.
units.tr: Chapter 8.

units.la: IIII. Generationem eius quis enarrabit? Comprehendit personam & regnum tuum. Personæ generatio ineffabilis quoad Deitatem & Humanitatem, loh 1.Mich.5. Psalm.110. Regnum item, quod neque de hoc mundo est(Ioh.18.)neq; huius mundi ratione administratur, cum inter medios hostes durat,Psal.110.2. Vide regna huius seculi, Dan.2.7. Regnum Christi è contra, Luc.1. Similiter subditi sunt filij Dei, qui & ipsi miraculose nascuntur(Ioh. 1.3.1.Pet 1.) & nunquam deficient. Semper Christus suos habebit in terris, vt olim,1.Reg.17.Vide Psalm.89. In cœlis verò ijdem cum illo æternum viuent. ¶ Hæc vt nos consolatur in aduersis,ita vitæ æterne certitudinem asserit,&c.
units.tr: IV. Who will declare his generation? It comprehends his person and his kingdom. The generation of the Person is ineffable as regards both his deity and his humanity (John 1; Mic. 5; Ps. 110). Likewise the kingdom, which is not of this world (John 18), nor is it governed on the principle of this world, since it endures among enemies in the midst (Ps. 110:2). See the kingdoms of this age (Dan. 2, 7). On the other hand, the kingdom of Christ (Luke 1). Similarly, the sons of God are his subjects, who are themselves also born miraculously (John 1, 3; 1 Pet. 1), and will never fail. Christ will always have his own on earth, as of old (1 Kings 17; see Ps. 89). In heaven, indeed, the same will live eternally with him. These things both console us in adversity and assert the certainty of eternal life, etc.

units.la: V. Causa: Quia tollitur e terra vita eius. Ratio absurdissima carni. Sed confirmatur apud Isaiam, quia passus est propter pec cata populi mei. Sunt hæc Dei verba, & sensus est: Etsi totus excilus videatur, tamen nihil proficient hostes: Imo quia hæc ex meo decreto subibit, vt mei populi pec cata expiet, ideo euehetur in summam di gnitatem. Sic Dauid,Psal.110. De torrente in via,&c. Exponitur Phil.2.
units.tr: V. The cause: because his life is taken from the earth. This reason is most absurd to the flesh. But it is confirmed in Isaiah: because he suffered for the sins of my people (Isa. 53:8). These are God's words, and the sense is: although he seems wholly cut off, the enemies will nonetheless accomplish nothing. Indeed, because this will come to pass by my decree, that he may expiate the sins of my people, therefore he will be raised to the highest dignity. So David (Ps. 110). Of the brook by the way, etc. It is explained in Phil. 2.

units.la: ¶ Hæc vt fidem nostram confirmant, & illi vni fidere docent: ita officij admonent, vt illi vni viuamus, qui pro nobis mortu- us est,2.Cor.5. Persequitur nos ideo mun dus,& fumus vt oues mactationis,Rom.8 Pfal 44.Sed ideo viuemus æternum. Vi- ta nostra in Christo abscondita,Col.3. Vi- de2.Tim.2.Luc.22.Matt.16.Oremus.
units.tr: These things both confirm our faith and teach us to trust in him alone; they also admonish us in our duty, so that we live for him alone who died for us (2 Cor. 5). The world therefore persecutes us, and we are like sheep for the slaughter (Rom. 8; Ps. 44). But therefore we shall live forever. Our life is hidden in Christ (Col. 3). See 2 Tim. 2; Luke 22; Matt. 16. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY LXIX.

units.la: 34 Respondens autem Eunuchus Philippo,dixit: Rogo te,de quo Prophe ta hoc dicit? de seipso, an de alio quo- piam.
units.tr: 34 The eunuch answered Philip and said: I beg you, of whom does the prophet say this? Of himself, or of some other man?

units.la: 35 Tum Philippus aperto ore suo, & incipiens à Scriptura ista, euangeli- zauit ei IESVM.
units.tr: 35 Then Philip opened his mouth, began from this Scripture, and preached Jesus to him.

units.la: VT Dominus pasim omnes hor-tatur, vt relictis superstitionibus & huius seculi studijs ad ipsum conuertan- tur: ita ad se conuersis promittit, quòd eos in gratiam recipere velit, quodq; ip- sum inuenturi & salute vera potituri sint, Isa 55 Zach.1.Matth.7.&c. Exempla, qui- bus hoc confirmatur, multa sunt: Inter quæ in primis memorabile est, quod in Æthiope habemus. Hic etsi ex gentibus & in patrijs superstitionibus enutritus es- set, retinuit tamen notitias de Deo gene- rales, &c. Ideo Deum verum quæsiuit, quem Hierosolymis coli audierat, r Reg. 8. Libros sacros in precio habuit, legit, intelligere cupiuit. Non defuit ergo illi Deus, sed ita eum direxit, vt Christi cognitio nem & cum hac salutem veram assecutus, cum gaudio domum rediret. Nam Philippum ei doctorem destinauit, & vtriusque grefus ita gubernauit, vt eo ipso momento, quo ad eum Philippus venit, eum Isaiae locum legeret, qui vaticiniū de Christo clarissimum continet, & Philippus inde haberet cum illo agendi occasionem. Sequitur enim.
units.tr: As the Lord generally exhorts all people to turn to him, leaving behind superstitions and the pursuits of this age, so he promises those who turn to him that he will receive them into grace, and that they will find him and attain true salvation (Isa. 55; Zech. 1; Matt. 7, etc.). There are many examples confirming this, and among them the one we have in the Ethiopian is especially memorable. Although he had been brought up among the Gentiles and in ancestral superstitions, he nonetheless retained general notions of God, etc. Therefore he sought the true God, whom he had heard was worshipped at Jerusalem (1 Kings 8). He held the sacred books in high esteem, read them, and longed to understand them. God therefore was not lacking to him, but guided him so that he obtained the knowledge of Christ and, with it, true salvation, and he returned home with joy. For God appointed Philip as his teacher and so governed the course of both men that at the very moment Philip came to him, he was reading that passage of Isaiah which contains the clearest prophecy about Christ, and Philip thence had an opportunity to engage him. For what follows is this.

units.la: 1. Quod illum rogârit de sensu Prophetae: Nimirum quod sciret à Iudaeis locum istum varie exponi. Ita enim solet Satan il luftriores locos vel obscurare, vel detorquere, vt Matth.16.Ioh.21. Est autem magni zeli argumentum, quod tantus princeps eò vsque se demittit, &c. Vbi Not. ¶ 1. Vt affectos esse oporteat, qui salutariter conuerti volunt? Veritatem quaerant, quae in solis Scripturis inuenitur. At non sufficit, vt scripturas legamus, sed vt intelligamus opus est. Atqui ex nobis id non habemus (1.Cor.2.) quia plerique sibijpsis velum imponuntur, vt Iudaei, 2.Corin.3. Aut non putant de se agi, vt Dauid 2.Sam.12. Ideo interpretatione est opus, &c. & applicatione. Hinc illa 1. Cor. 2. 14. 2. Timot. 2. Neq; hic aliquem moueat sententiarum diuersitas. Quia hæc non noua est, vt patet hic, & Matth. 5. 16. Vt vero ibi Apostolos vult suam sententiam dicere: Ita nos quoq; illos interrogemus, & videamus num quod dicitur conueniat cum religionis Christianæ principijs (Ioh. 17.) Oratione Dominica, Symbolo, Decalogo. Ita non errabimus.
units.tr: 1. That Philip asked him about the sense of the prophet: no doubt because he knew that the Jews explained this passage in various ways. For Satan is accustomed to obscure or distort the more illustrious passages in this way (Matt. 16; John 21). It is, moreover, a sign of great zeal that so great a prince humbles himself so far, etc. Here note: 1. What disposition ought those to have who wish to be converted to salvation? They should seek the truth, which is found in the Scriptures alone. But it is not enough to read the Scriptures; we need to understand them. Yet we do not have this understanding of ourselves (1 Cor. 2), since many have a veil placed over themselves, as the Jews did (2 Cor. 3), or they do not think the matter concerns them, as David did (2 Sam. 12). Therefore interpretation is needed, etc., and application. Hence that saying (1 Cor. 2:14; 2 Tim. 2). Nor should the diversity of opinions disturb anyone here, for this is not new, as is clear here and in Matt. 5:16. But just as there he wishes the Apostles to state their own opinion, so we too should question them and see whether what is said agrees with the principles of the Christian religion (John 17): the Lord's Prayer, the Creed, and the Decalogue. Thus we will not go astray.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quòd tanto studio ardens Æthiops, hucusq; non potuit ista intelligere. Fit hoc frequenter, & suo tempore quoties vocat Deus, Acto. 16. Ita verò proprij ingenij fiduciam deprimit Deus, desideri o accendit, ad preces excitat, & facit attentos. Habes quod respondeas quærentibus: Cur Euangelium tam diu latuerit? Non nouum hoc. Vide Acto. 14. 17. Ro. 16. Sic meruit mundus, vt prædictum 1. Tim. 4. 2. Thess. 2. Tu potius agnosce nunc Dei bonitatem. Oblatam lucem admitte, & vt intelligas ora sedulo, Pf. 25. 119.
units.tr: 2. That the Ethiopian, burning with such zeal, had until then been unable to understand these things. This happens frequently, and at its own time, whenever God calls (Acts 16). God indeed humbles our confidence in our own talent, kindles desire, stirs us to prayer, and makes us attentive. You have an answer for those who ask: why did the Gospel lie hidden for so long? This is nothing new (see Acts 14:17; Rom. 16). Thus the world has deserved what is foretold in 1 Tim. 4 and 2 Thess. 2. Rather, you should now acknowledge the goodness of God. Admit the light offered, and pray diligently that you may understand (Ps. 25; 119).

units.la: II. Philippus mox ore aperto, id est, clarè & liberè (Mat. 5.) ei euangelizauit.
units.tr: II. Philip at once opened his mouth, that is, spoke clearly and freely (Matt. 5), and preached the Gospel to him.

units.la: No. ¶ 1. Facilitate Philippi. Non fast dit, quòd alienigena, aulicus, &c. Neq; remittit ad consensum Ecclesiæ, cui simpliciter credere debeat, & abstrusiora relin quere
units.tr: Note: 1. The affability of Philip. It is not said that the man was a foreigner, a courtier, and so on. Nor does Philip refer him to the consensus of the Church, which he should simply believe, leaving the more abstruse matters to the more learned.

units.la: doctioribus. Ita certè faciunt personati Apostolici hodie. Hinc stolida ignorantia & superstitio. Ministri Philippum imitentur, & requisiti non desint officio. Imò occasiones ipsi captent. Sic Paulus Actorum 20.
units.tr: The pretended apostolic men of today certainly do otherwise, and hence come stupid ignorance and superstition. Ministers should imitate Philip and not be lacking in their duty when asked; indeed they should seek out opportunities themselves. So Paul did (Acts 20).

units.la: ¶ 2. Quid prædicauit? Num primatum Petri, Sacrificium Missæ, Confessionem auriculârem, Purgatorium, Indulgentias, &c. Nihil huius, sed vnum I E S V M. Hunc enim solùm nouerant Apostoli, 1. Cor. 2. Gal. 6. Quia autem huius prædicatione istum conuertit, sequitur veram conuersionem in solius Christi cognitione consistere (1. Pet. 3.) Et hunc vnum prædicari debere. In hoc enim habentur, quæcunque ad salutem sunt necessaria. Ipse nobis datus est sapientia, 1. Cor. 1. Col. 2. Satisfactio, iustitia, & sanctificatio, 1. Cor. 1. 2. Cor. 5. Lux mundi, Ioh. 1. 8. Mal. 4. Via atque veritas, Ioh. 14. Ostium, Ioh. 10. Vitis, &c. Ioh. 15. Pastor Ioh. 10. Luc. 15. Sponsus, Ioh. 3. Rex & Sacerdos, Pfal. 2. 72. 110. In illo denique datur pœnitentia & remissio peccatorum, Act. 5. Hunc ergo solùm prædicârunt Apostoli, neque hodie aliud prædicari debet, Galat. 1. Qui enim hunc agnoscunt, mox omnibus reliftis, ad eum tendunt, neque se auelli patiuntur, Phil. 3. Ioh. 6. Ioh. 9. Idem illi placere studeant, & sanctitatem sectantur, quam tanti constitisse audiunt, Eph. 1. 1. Pet. 1. Heb. 12.
units.tr: 2. What did he preach? Surely not the primacy of Peter, the sacrifice of the Mass, auricular confession, Purgatory, indulgences, and so on. None of these, but one thing: Jesus. For the Apostles knew only this (1 Cor. 2; Gal. 6). Because he converted that man by preaching this, it follows that true conversion consists in the knowledge of Christ alone (1 Pet. 3), and that this one thing ought to be preached. For in him are contained all things necessary to salvation. He was given to us as wisdom (1 Cor. 1; Col. 2), satisfaction, righteousness, and sanctification (1 Cor. 1; 2 Cor. 5). He is the light of the world (John 1; 8; Mal. 4), the way and the truth (John 14), the door (John 10), the vine (John 15), and so on. He is the shepherd (John 10; Luke 15), the bridegroom (John 3), king and priest (Ps. 2; 72; 110). Finally, in him repentance and remission of sins are given (Acts 5). Therefore the Apostles preached him alone, and nothing else ought to be preached today (Gal. 1). Those who acknowledge him at once, forsaking everything, hasten to him and do not allow themselves to be torn away (Phil. 3; John 6; John 9). Let them likewise strive to please him and pursue the holiness which, they hear, cost him so much (Eph. 1; 1 Pet. 1; Heb. 12).

units.la: ¶ Arguuntur nostri seculi Christiani. Plerique in religione nō vno Christo contenti, circa Diuos occupantur, & suorum operum meritis fidunt. Conuenit ergo illis quod habetur Ier. 2. Ifa 55. Rom. 10. Gal. 5. Alij peccatis seruiunt, & Christi nomen prophanant, Malach. 1. Non sunt sti adhuc conuersi, Matth. 7. Christum ergo amplexi in illo vitam nouam viuamus, &c. Rom. 6. 10.
units.tr: Christians of our own age are rebuked. Many, not content with Christ alone in religion, are occupied with the saints and trust in the merits of their own works. What is said in Jer. 2, Isa. 55, Rom. 10 and Gal. 5 applies to them. Others serve their sins and profane the name of Christ (Mal. 1). They are not yet truly converted (Matt. 7). Therefore let us embrace Christ and live a new life in him, etc. (Rom. 6; 10).

units.la: ¶ 3. Quod ex Ifaia prædicauit IESVM. Ergo Euangelium Christi in prophetis quoque traditur, Rom. 1. 1. Pet. 1. 2. Pet. 1. Fatetur hoc ipse, Luc. 4 24. Ioh. 5. Asserit hoc fidei Christianæ vetustatem & certitudinem. Impiè ergo agunt, qui horum libros reijciunt, vt Anabapt. Habent hoc commune cum omnibus hæreticis, maximè Manichæis. Atqui Deus semper sibi constat, neque venit Christus vt legem aboleat, Matth. 5. Eadem item in vtroque Testamento salutis ratio, 1. Cor. 10. Imò non possumus fidei nostræ fundamenta tueri contra Turcas & Iudæos sine veteris Testamenti libris. Ideo hoc mirificè Deus seruauit, & in Græcam omnesque
units.tr: 3. That he preached Jesus from Isaiah. Therefore the Gospel of Christ is also handed down in the prophets (Rom. 1; 1 Pet. 1; 2 Pet. 1). He himself confirms this (Luke 24; John 5). It asserts the antiquity and certainty of the Christian faith. Impiously, therefore, do those act who reject the books of the prophets, as the Anabaptists do. They share this with all heretics, especially the Manichaeans. Yet God is always consistent with himself, and Christ did not come to abolish the law (Matt. 5). Likewise there is the same way of salvation in both Testaments (1 Cor. 10). Indeed we cannot defend the foundations of our faith against the Turks and the Jews without the books of the Old Testament. Therefore God has marvellously preserved them and willed them to be translated into Greek and all other languages.

units.la: X
units.tr: X

units.la: alias linguas transferri voluit. Agnoscamus ergo hanc bonitatem Dei, legamus, audiamus, scrutemur (Ioh 5)& singula ac commodemus institutioni nostræ, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us therefore acknowledge this goodness of God, read, hear and search the Scriptures (John 5), and apply each thing to our instruction, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXX.
units.tr: HOMILY LXX.

units.la: 36 Cum autem pergerent in via, venerunt ad quandam aquam: tum ait Eunuchus, En aqua, quid prohibet, me baptizari.
units.tr: 36 As they went on their way, they came to some water; and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what prevents me from being baptized?

units.la: EXposuit Lucas, vt Philippus Eunuco Æthiopi Euangelium ex Isaia prædicârit, & ita eum ad fidem Christi converterit. Sequitur modo huius concionis effectus, quidq; fecerit Æthiops postquam conuersus fuit. Discimus hic quàm efficax sit verbum Dei. Erat in gentilismo natus & educatus. Dies & authoritatis magnæ. Nec ignorabat, quàm odiosa sit omnis innouatio religionis. Sed nihil horum ipsum terret aut remoratur, &c. Similia exempla, Mat. 9. Luc 19. Infra 10. 16. 13. &c. Ita fit quod est Ioh. 10. Quòd igitur multi hodie cunctantur, argumento est eos verbi semen nondum recte percepisse. Audiamus ergo quid hic fecerit, vt quid conuersos decet, intelligamus.
units.tr: Luke has set out how Philip preached the Gospel to the Ethiopian eunuch from Isaiah, and so converted him to faith in Christ. Now follows the effect of this sermon, and what the Ethiopian did after he was converted. Here we learn how effective the Word of God is. He had been born and brought up in heathenism. He was a man of high rank and great authority, and he was not ignorant of how hateful every change of religion is. Yet none of these things frightens or delays him, and so on. Compare Matt. 9, Luke 19, below 10, 16, 13, etc. Thus what is written in John 10 comes true. That many today hesitate is therefore evidence that they have not yet rightly received the seed of the Word. Let us hear, then, what he did here, so that we may understand what befits converts.

units.la: Summa est, Cum pergerent, &c. Vbi rursus suis elucet Dei prouidentia, qui in deferto ad aquam deducit, quæ occasio fuit ad illam baptizandum. Ita Deus suis nō deest, sed subinde nouas salutis occasiones obijcit. Curemus modo, ne ipsi nobis desimus &c. Luc. 9. Imitemur potius Eunuchum, qui gestiens exclamat, &c. ¶ Vbi dicat aliquis: Atqui nulla hucusque Baptismi mentio facta, &c. Nam Philippus ei Euangelium prædicauit. Huic prædicationi autem Baptismus coniunctus est, Matth. 28. Mar. 16. Deinde aspersionis mentio fit, Ita. 52. Id vero de sanguine Christi dicitur, qui vt olim victimarum sanguis (Exod. 12. 14. Hebr. 9.) nobis aspergitur per Euangelium, vt eo sanctè ficemur, 1. Cor. 6 Signum vero huius est Baptismus. Non dubium ergo est, quin hæc mysteria ei Philippus exposuerit, quod Christus suos à mundo segregatos, sibi autem consecratos esse ve lit. Postulat ergo, vt baptizetur. Vbi ista obseruabis.
units.tr: The summary is: "as they went on," and so on. Here again God's providence shines out, who leads him in the desert to water, which gave the occasion for baptizing him. So God does not fail his own, but from time to time sets before them new opportunities of salvation. Let us only take care that we do not fail ourselves, etc. Luke 9. Let us rather imitate the eunuch, who exclaims eagerly, etc. ¶ Here someone may say: But so far no mention has been made of baptism, etc., for Philip preached the Gospel to him. But baptism is joined to this preaching, Matt. 28, Mark 16. Then mention is made of sprinkling, Isa. 52. This is said of the blood of Christ, which, like the blood of the victims of old (Exod. 12, 14, Heb. 9), is sprinkled upon us through the Gospel, so that we are sanctified by it, 1 Cor. 6. The sign of this is baptism. There is no doubt, then, that Philip explained these mysteries to him, since Christ wills his people to be set apart from the world and consecrated to himself. He therefore asks to be baptized. Here you will observe these things.

units.la: I. Quòd in Ecclesiam adoptari cupit: Non T. ¶ Commune hoc votum esse debere Christianis. Vt enim omnis salus in vno Christo habetur, Act. 4. Ita Deus populum habet peculiare, cui hanc impertit, & quem ab aliis vult esse segregatum. Fatemur hoc in Symbolo. Tales fuerūt ante di-
units.tr: I. That he desires to be adopted into the Church. ¶ That this desire ought to be common to all Christians. For just as all salvation is found in the one Christ (Acts 4), so God has a peculiar people, to whom he imparts this salvation and whom he wills to be set apart from others. We confess this in the Creed. Such were the sons of God before the flood

units.la: luuium filij Dei,Gen.5 No: cum fuis,Ge. 6.9.Ideo euocatusAbraham,cum quo foe dus falutis inftauratum & data circumci‑sio,Gen.12. 15.17.In lege Iudæi ab aliis se‑gregati,Exod.19.Deuter.4. Vnum Taber naculum,vnum altare,&c.Iof.23. Et reges Israelis in eo peccârunt,quod nouis tem‑plis populum diftraxerunt,1.Reg.12 Hof. 4.Amos 5.&c.In Nouo Teftamento fimi‑liter Chriftus fuos feparari vult, & fibi cofecrari per baptifmum, Ioh.15.Matt.28. Actor.2. Obferuent ergo hoc Dei inftitu‑tum quicunque feruari volunt,neque eos Ecclefiæ pudeat. Eft quidé pufillus grex, & vt oues maftationis Luc 12.Rom.8. Pf. 44.At eadem Chrifti grex eft,&c. Act 20. Sponfa item,Eph.5.Imò domus Dei,1.Ti‑mot.3.Et Catholica dicitur,quia vnica eft (Cant. 6.) & ad hanc colligi oportet om‑nes,qui feruari cupiunt.Typus arcæ Noç. Damnantur ergo hic fectæ omnes,etiam hæ quæ cum Chrifti profefsione coniun‑ctæ funt,1 Cor.13.4. In primis autem, qui vnum quenquein fua religione feruari di‑cunt,&c.
units.tr: (Gen. 5), and Noah with his family (Gen. 6, 9). Then Abraham was called, with whom the covenant of salvation was renewed, and circumcision was given (Gen. 12, 15, 17). In the law the Jews were set apart from others (Exod. 19, Deut. 4). One tabernacle, one altar, etc. (Josh. 23). And the kings of Israel sinned in this, that they divided the people with new temples (1 Kings 12, Hos. 4, Amos 5, etc.). In the New Testament likewise Christ wills his people to be separated and consecrated to himself through baptism (John 15, Matt. 28, Acts 2). Let all who wish to be saved therefore observe this institution of God, and let them not be ashamed of the Church. It is indeed a little flock, and like sheep for the slaughter (Luke 12, Rom. 8, Ps. 44). Yet it is the same flock of Christ, etc. (Acts 20). Likewise it is his bride (Eph. 5), indeed the house of God (1 Tim. 3). And it is called catholic because it is one (Cant. 6), and all who wish to be saved must be gathered into it. The ark of Noah is a type of this. All sects are therefore condemned here, even those that are joined to the profession of Christ (1 Cor. 13, 4). Above all, those who say that each man can be saved in his own religion, etc.

units.la: 2. Quòd Baptifmum non faftidit,vt fu‑peruacaneum,quia in Chrifto omnia iam habeat.No 1.¶ Credentes non debere fa‑ftidire externa media falutis,quę funt Prę‑dicatio
units.tr: 2. That he does not despise baptism as superfluous, since he already has everything in Christ. ¶ Believers ought not to despise the external means of salvation, which are the preaching of the Word, prayers, and the sacraments.

units.la: Eunuchus baptismū nō fastidit. dicatio verbi, Preces, Sacramenta. Exprædicatione est fides, Rom. 10. Hæc preces agnit, Psa. 50. 116. Cant. 1. Luc. 16. Sacramenta sigilla sunt iustitiæ fidei, Rom. 8. Et his opus est, ut nos consolentur in periculis & tentationibus, 1. Sam. 14. 27. Qui ergo il la contemnunt, seipsos ignorant, & omnium sanctorum exemplo confutantur. Vide infrà 10. Imò ipsius Christi, Lucæ 2. Matt. 4.
units.tr: The eunuch does not despise baptism. The preaching of the Word: faith comes from preaching (Rom. 10). Prayers are acknowledged (Ps. 50, 116, Cant. 1, Luke 16). Sacraments are seals of the righteousness of faith (Rom. 8), and we need them to comfort us in dangers and temptations (1 Sam. 14, 27). Those, then, who despise these things do not know themselves, and are refuted by the example of all the saints. See below, 10. Indeed, they are refuted by the example of Christ himself (Luke 2, Matt. 4).

units.la: ¶ Obseruemus, non sufficere, si Ecclesiæ coniungamur per baptismum, sed simul vitam requiri, quæ nos mundo mortuos esse doceat. Baptismus enim est signum fœderis, quo Deus testatur, se nos ablutos & renatos, in Christo velle in filios adoptare, ut ei in vitæ novitate seruiamus. De duob. ergo nos admonet: 1. Quid Deus nobis conferat. 2. Quid nos ei debeamus. Vide Tit. 3. Eph. 5. Rom. 6. Gal. 3. Calumniatores ergo sunt, qui fidei doctrina dicunt bona opera prohiberi. Imò illa operum bonorum causa est vera. Meritum solum negatur, quod nullum est, Lucæ 17. Et quia sic Christo derogatur, Gal, 5. ¶ Vide quid de nostri seculi Christianis iudices. Alij superstitiones sectantur, 1. Cor. 10. Alij carnis licentiam. Christus suos è mundo elegit, Ioh. 16. 1. Pet. 2. Eph. 1. At quis tales dixerit, qui cum mundo helluantur contra Christi admonitionem, Matth.24. Luc.17 21. Libidinantur, 1 Cor.6. Vsuras exercent auari, Eph.5. Col 3. Qui fastu & luxu superbiunt contra Christi exemplo, Matth.11 19. Imo contra charitatem, Roman.12. Hebr. 13. Quid vero, qui militant contra eiusdem fidei professores? Vide Deuter.27.1. Corinth.6. Apocal.21. Oremus.
units.tr: ¶ Let us observe that it is not enough to be joined to the Church through baptism, but that a life is also required which teaches us that we are dead to the world. For baptism is a sign of the covenant, by which God testifies that, having washed and reborn us, he wills in Christ to adopt us as sons, so that we may serve him in newness of life. It therefore admonishes us of two things: 1. what God confers on us; 2. what we owe him in return (see Titus 3, Eph. 5, Rom. 6, Gal. 3). They are slanderers, then, who say that good works are forbidden by the doctrine of faith. On the contrary, faith is the true cause of good works. Only merit is denied, since there is none (Luke 17), and because to claim it would detract from Christ (Gal. 5). ¶ See how you judge the Christians of our own age. Some pursue superstitions (1 Cor. 10); others pursue licence of the flesh. Christ chose his people out of the world (John 16, 1 Pet. 2, Eph. 1). But who would call those people his, who revel with the world against the admonition of Christ (Matt. 24, Luke 17, 21), who indulge their lust (1 Cor. 6), whom greedy men who practise usury (Eph. 5, Col. 3), who take pride in arrogance and luxury against the example of Christ (Matt. 11, 19), and indeed against charity (Rom. 12, Heb. 13)? What of those who wage war against the professors of the same faith? See Deut. 27, 1 Cor. 6, Rev. 21. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXI.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXI.

units.la: 37 Dixit vero Philippus, Si credis ex toto corde, licet. Respondens autem ille, dixit, Credo, Filium Dei esse Iesum Christum.
units.tr: 37 Then Philip said, "If you believe with all your heart, you may." And he answered and said, "I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God."

units.la: 38 Iussit quoque stare currum, ac descenderunt ambo in aquam, Philippus et Eunuchus, et baptizavit eum.
units.tr: 38 He also commanded the chariot to stand still, and they both went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

units.la: 39 Cum autem ascendissent ex aqua, spiritus Domini rapuit Philippum, nec vidit eum amplius Eunuchus. Per gebat enim in via sua gaudens.
units.tr: 39 And when they had come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.

units.la: 40 Philippus autem repertus est in Azoti, et per transiens evangelizabat omnibus civitatibus, donec veniret Caesaream.
units.tr: 40 But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through he preached the gospel in all the cities until he came to Caesarea.

units.la: POstquam Aethiops in Christi cognitione institutus & hunc fide veram amplexus plexus est, nihil prius habuit, quam vt in Ecclesiae societatem cooptaretur, ideoque occasione oblata Baptismum petijt. Ita ergo Christum apprehenderat, vt Christianus esse & dici vellet, adeoque Christum omnino referre cuperet. Exigitur hoc ab omnibus, vt Ecclesiae consortium amenet, Psalm 84. Neue Christi eos pudeat & Euangelij. Mar 8. Rom 1. Vt deniq; huic vni v. uanit, quia pro ipsis est mortuus. 2. Corinth 5 lac. 2 Sequitur.
units.tr: After the Ethiopian had been instructed in the knowledge of Christ and had embraced this true faith, he had no greater desire than to be received into the fellowship of the Church. So, when the opportunity arose, he asked for baptism. He had grasped Christ in such a way that he wished to be and be called a Christian, and he wanted altogether to bear Christ's name. This is required of everyone: that they seek the fellowship of the Church (Ps. 84). Let them not be ashamed of Christ and his gospel (Mark 8; Rom. 1). Finally, let them live for him alone, because he died for them (2 Cor. 5; Jas. 2). What follows:

units.la: I. Responsio Philippi. Si credis, &c. Non diu suspendit, neque requirit satisfactio- nes (supe fictiola, ieiunia, peregrinatio- nes &c. Sed fidem examinat, & quid e num ex toto corde, &c.
units.tr: I. The response of Philip: "If you believe," etc. He does not delay long, nor does he demand satisfactions (vain inventions, fasts, pilgrimages, and so on). Rather, he examines the faith, and whether it is held "with the whole heart," etc.

units.la: NOT. Non temere fidendum cuiuis, neq; Sacramenta prophananda alienis à fide. Quia enim Christi & Ecclesiae symbola sunt, non debent communicari cuiuis, Mat. 7 Vide Mar. 16.
units.tr: NOTE. One should not trust just anyone rashly, nor should the sacraments be profaned by those who are alien to the faith. For since they are the symbols of Christ and the Church, they ought not to be shared with just anyone (Matt. 7). See Mark 16.

units.la: Interim non probandi Anabaptistae, qui ex hoc loco colligunt, non baptizandos esse paruulos, quia neq; credere, neq; fidem profiteri possint. Errant, quia non distinguunt inter alienos ab Ecclesia, & in hac natos. Imo Christianorum infantes, in vetéris Testamenti infantes detrudunt. Gen. 17. Obijciunt: Abrahamum habuisse mandatum de infantibus, nos non item, Respondeo: Atqui non semper omnes circumstantiae exprimuntur. In Coena nō iubemur admittere mulieres: admittuntur tamen etiam ab Anabaptistis, quia ex eius institutione patet, eam ad illas quoque pertinere. Eadem est ratio Baptismi. 1. Est signum foederis, quo debent insigniri, qui sunt populus Dei; Matth. 28. Infantes sunt ex populo Dei, Marc. 10. 2. Qui Spiritum sanctum habent, debent baptizari, Act. 10. Infantes habent, Rom. 8. 1. Cor. 7. Ergo, &c. 3. Credentes sunt baptizandi. Infantes pro credentibus Christus habet, Matth. 18. &c. 4. Apostoli debuerunt omnes gentes baptizare, Mat. 28. Atqui gentium pars magna sunt infantes. 5. Baptizatas totas domus, Acto. 10. 16. 1. Cor. 1. 6. Olim baptizati infantes typice, 1. Cor. 10. Ista sufficiant Christianis & non contentiosis, 1. Cor. 14.
units.tr: Yet the Anabaptists are not to be approved, for they gather from this passage that infants should not be baptized, because they can neither believe nor profess faith. They are mistaken, because they do not distinguish between those who are alien to the Church and those born within it. Indeed, they thrust the infants of Christians down among the infants of the Old Testament (Gen. 17). They object that Abraham had a command concerning infants, and we do not. I answer: yet not all the circumstances are always spelled out. In the Supper we are not commanded to admit women, yet even the Anabaptists admit them, because it is clear from its institution that it pertains to them as well. The reason for baptism is the same. (1) It is the sign of the covenant, by which those who are the people of God ought to be marked (Matt. 28). Infants are part of the people of God (Mark 10). (2) Those who have the Holy Spirit ought to be baptized (Acts 10). Infants have the Spirit (Rom. 8; 1 Cor. 7). Therefore, etc. (3) Believers are to be baptized. Christ has infants as those who believe (Matt. 18), etc. (4) The apostles were to baptize all nations (Matt. 28). But a large part of the nations are infants. (5) Entire households were baptized (Acts 10; 16; 1 Cor. 1). (6) Infants were once baptized in type (1 Cor. 10). Let these suffice for Christians who are not contentious (1 Cor. 14).

units.la: II. Confessio Æthiopis. Similis Petri
units.tr: II. The confession of the Ethiopian. Like Peter's.

units.la: Matth. 16. Ioh. 6. Probatur à Christo, ideo que vera & salutaris est confessio secundum illud Ro. 10. &c. Constat autem duabus partibus. ¶ 1. De persona. De Iesu ex Maria nato dicitur, quod sit filius Dei. Ergo Deus & Homo in una persona. Sic Iohan. 1. Rom. 9. Talis autem manet, quia car-
units.tr: Matt. 16; John 6. It is approved by Christ, and therefore it is a true and saving confession, according to Rom. 10, etc. It consists of two parts. (1) Concerning the person. Of Jesus born of Mary it is said that he is the Son of God. Therefore he is God and man in one person (John 1; Rom. 9). Such he remains, since the flesh

units.la: Aethiopi confessio carnem assumptam non depositi Luc.24 Actor.1. Vide insuper Zach.13. Matth.24, Phil.3. Dan 7. §2. De Officio Christus, id est, Rex & Sacerdos, Psalm.2.110. Dic de utroque, & quod utrumque æternum sit. Hæc fides Catholica est, qua omnes electi seruati sunt. In ea igitur simus constantes.
units.tr: which he assumed he did not lay aside (Luke 24; Acts 1). See also Zech. 13; Matt. 24; Phil. 3; Dan. 7. (2) Concerning the office: Christ is King and Priest (Ps. 2; 110). Say of each that each is eternal. This is the Catholic faith, by which all the elect are saved. Let us therefore be steadfast in it.

units.la: III. Quomodo baptizatur? Iubet curnum sisti, ambo descendunt in aquam, &c. Conuenit cum exemplo Baptistæ, Ioh.1. Et cum Christi institutione, Mat.28. Sed Notat. §Baptismi formam veram. In papa tu aqua semel in anno consecratur, adduntur exorcismi, sal, sputum, oleum, &c. Quæ omnia posteris temporibus demum accesserunt, & pepererunt superstitiones. Sifficiat ergo nobis quod Christo satis fuit & Apostolis. Ex Christi institutione omnis aqua consecrata est. Interim nemo hinc temere exemplum sumat. Vbi Ecclesiæ sunt constitutæ, omnia decenter fiant, 1.Cor.14.11.
units.tr: III. How is he baptized? He orders the chariot to stop, and both go down into the water, etc. This agrees with the example of the Baptist (John 1) and with Christ's institution (Matt. 28). But note the true form of baptism. In the papacy, water is consecrated once a year, and exorcisms, salt, spittle, oil, and so on are added. All these things were added in later times, and they gave birth to superstitions. Let what was enough for Christ and the apostles be enough for us. By Christ's institution every water is consecrated. Meanwhile, let no one rashly take this example for himself. Where churches have been established, let all things be done decently (1 Cor. 14:11).

units.la: IV. Quid postea factum narratur. §1. Philippus fit ἀφαντος. Non opus quære, quomodo hoc factum. Sic Christus Luc 24. Voluit Deus testari, nihil sine eius prouidentia factum, & simul Æthiopem monere, vt solo Christo contentus non
units.tr: IV. What is narrated as having happened afterwards. (1) Philip becomes "vanished [ἀφαντος]." Do not seek how this was done. So Christ (Luke 24). God willed to show that nothing is done without his providence, and at the same time to warn the Ethiopian to be content with Christ alone and not to depend on any man.

units.la: pendeat a quoquam hominum. Ita enim Mosem sepeliuit, Deuternom. 34. Et fe é ignorantur prophetarû & Apostolorum tumbæ. Imo virginis Mariæ &c. Stulti, qui Diuorum offa, vestes venerantur & apud salutem quæsunt. Pugnat cum præ-septo Christi, Matt. 24.
units.tr: For thus he buried Moses (Deut. 34). And the tombs of the prophets and apostles are unknown. Indeed, the same holds for the Virgin Mary, and so on. Foolish are those who venerate the bones and garments of the saints and seek salvation from them. This conflicts with Christ's precept (Matt. 24).

units.la: 1. Æthiops restius, qui neque Ieroso-lymam, neque Samariam redit, vt Philippum quærat. Non etiam suspectum habet, vt impostorem, multo minus murmurat, vt Israelitæ, Exod. trigesimo secundo. Sed contentus eo, quod didicerat, gaudens redit per suam viam domum. Sic supra Samaritani gauisi sunt.
units.tr: 1. The Ethiopian returns without hesitation: he goes neither to Jerusalem nor to Samaria to look for Philip. Nor does he regard him with suspicion as an impostor, much less does he murmur like the Israelites (Exod. 32). Instead, content with what he had learned, he returns rejoicing home by his own way. So earlier the Samaritans also rejoiced.

units.la: Est hoc proprium fidei, Ioh. 6. 1. Ioh. 2. Hinc gaudium conscientiæ, Rom. 5. Phil. 4 Intrepidos facit, Roman. 8. Infelices, qui Christi prætextu tumultuantur. Sunt j, de quibus Ioh. 4.
units.tr: This is the proper fruit of faith (John 6; 1 John 2). Hence comes the joy of conscience (Rom. 5; Phil. 4). It makes people fearless (Rom. 8). Unhappy are those who riot under the pretext of Christ. There are some of whom John speaks (John 4).

units.la: 3. Philippus, ne raptus putaretur (Gen. 5. 2. Reg. 2.) inuentus est Azoti. Inde prædicauit maritimis ciuitatibus, & tandem substitit Cæsareæ, Act. 21. Officij admonentur ministri. Multum hucusq; labo rat Philippus, sed nondum cessat. Sic Paulus, Rom. 15. 2. Cor. 11. 1. Cor. 15. Imitatur 2 Cor. 5. &c. Sic magistratus faciat. Singuli, Lu. 9. Mat. 24. Inprimis vide quàm parum
units.tr: 3. Philip, lest he be thought to have been carried off (Gen. 5; 2 Kings 2), was found at Azotus. From there he preached to the maritime cities, and at last settled at Caesarea (Acts 21). Ministers are reminded of their duties. Philip has labored much so far, but he has not yet ceased. So Paul (Rom. 15; 2 Cor. 11; 1 Cor. 15), who imitates (2 Cor. 5, etc.). So should magistrates act. Let each one act likewise (Luke 9; Matt. 24). Above all, see how little

units.la: parùm proficiant persecutionibus hostes Christi. Vnus Philippus, cuius vix mentio facta,cùm Ecclesia otiaretur Hierosolymæ, conuertit Palæstinos,& ad Æthiopiam vsque Euangelium propagat. Ante Samariam subegit.Ita eluduntur tyranno rum conatus, Psal.2 2. &c. Nemo igitur hodie perturbetur. Vide Matth.28.Mar.13.Psal.72.Zach.9. Fidamus Christo, &indesinenter.Oremus.
units.tr: the enemies of Christ advance by persecutions. Philip alone, whose name is scarcely mentioned, while the Church was at rest in Jerusalem, converted the Palestinians and spread the gospel even as far as Ethiopia. Samaria he had already won over earlier. Thus the attempts of tyrants are mocked (Ps. 2). Let no one therefore be disturbed today. See Matt. 28; Mark 13; Ps. 72; Zech. 9. Let us trust Christ, and do so unceasingly. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXII.

units.la: SAulus autem adhuc spirans minas et cædem aduersus discipulos Domini, adijt Pontificem Maximum.
units.tr: Saul, however, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the High Priest.

units.la: 2 Et petijt ab eo epistolas Damascum ad Synagogas, vt si quos inueniret huius sectæ, seu viros seu mulieres, vinctos duceret Hierosolymam.
units.tr: And he asked him for letters to the synagogues at Damascus, so that if he found any of this sect, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

units.la: IESVS Christus Ioh.6 ait. Nemo venit ad me,&c. Item. Non vos me elegistis, Ioh.15. Docet his, salutem & quæ ad hanc fa-ciunt, hominib. ex mera gratia obtingere &c. Est hęc totius Scripturæ doctrina, quæ multis exemplis confirmatur & illustra {a}tur. Inter quæ memorabile est Æthiopis, Quia autem in eo virtutes aliquot præ‑claræ fuerunt, ne quis inde meritum sta‑tueret, subtextitur cómodé Saulus, quem, cùm hostis esset, inuitum Deus non mo‑do traxit, sed coegit etiam intrare, &c. Lu‑cæ 14. Vnde sequitur, hoc omne solius gra‑tiæ opus fuisse, sicuti ipse fatetur, Galat. 1. 1. Cor. 15. 1. Tim. 1. Sunt autem hîc multa alia obseruatu dignissima, maximè quoad Ecclesiæ fata & persecutiones : quare Lucas totam historiam cum omnibus circumstantijs ex ordine describit, & a Saulo orditur, vt Dei bonitas & potentia apertiùs eluceat.
units.tr: Jesus Christ says in John 6: "No one comes to me," etc. Likewise, John 15: "You did not choose me." He teaches that salvation, and whatever pertains to it, comes to men from sheer grace, etc. This is the teaching of all Scripture, and it is confirmed and illustrated by many examples. Among these the conversion of the Ethiopian is memorable. But since there were several outstanding virtues in Saul, lest anyone should on that account attribute merit to him, Luke tactfully adds that Saul, though an enemy, was not only drawn but even compelled by God, against his will, to come in, etc., Luke 14. From this it follows that the whole of this was the work of grace alone, as Saul himself confesses, Gal. 1, 1 Cor. 15, 1 Tim. 1. There are, moreover, many other things here most worthy of notice, especially concerning the fortunes and persecutions of the Church. For this reason Luke describes the whole history in order with all its circumstances, and begins with Saul, so that God's goodness and power may shine out more clearly.

units.la: 1. Quis ei animus fuerit? Spirauit adhuc minas: &c. Emphasim habet particula ad‑hùc, vt innuat, non suisse nouum impetu, sed consulto perseuerauisse in eo quod cœperat, Actor. 7. 8 26. Quia vero se nihil proficere vidit, sed Euangelium magis dif‑fundi, totus in rabiem conuertitur.
units.tr: 1. What was his disposition? "He still breathed threats," etc. The particle still carries emphasis, to show that this was not a sudden fit of passion but a deliberate persistence in what he had begun, Acts 7, 8, 26. But since he saw that he was accomplishing nothing, and that the gospel was spreading all the more, he was turned entirely into rage.

units.la: NOT. 1. Proprium hostium Christi & Ecclesiæ. Quia aduersus Deum insur‑gunt, permittit eos suo arbitrio. Ideo in peius proficiunt, & si semel gustârint pio sanguinem belluarum instar non de‑sinunt, nisi Dei manu potenti coercean‑tur. Ita hic Saulus. Pharao item, Exod. 5. 14. &c.
units.tr: NOTE 1. The mark of the enemies of Christ and of the Church. Because they rise up against God, he allows them to follow their own will. Therefore they advance for the worse, and once they have tasted pious blood they do not stop, like beasts, unless they are restrained by the mighty hand of God. So it was with Saul here, and with Pharaoh likewise, Exod. 5, 14, etc.

units.la: 14. &c. Et hodie exempla sunt eorū, quos nihil movet. ¶ 2. Falluntur ergo vehemen-ter, qui apud tales simulando & diffimu-do putant aliquid profici. Pergunt illi (2 Tim.3 )ipsi autem frigescunt,vt Petrus Matth. 26. Solius Dei est animos rimare, mutare & fraenare, Psalm.7 Ier 17. Hunc ergo oremus, &c. Matth.5. Vt vero nos audiat, ei fideles simus, Iohan. 9. Tepidos non fert, Apo.3.
units.tr: 14, etc. And today there are examples of those whom nothing moves. ¶ 2. They therefore are gravely mistaken who think that anything is gained by pretending and dissembling with such people. They press on (2 Tim. 3), while they themselves grow cold, as Peter did in Matt. 26. It belongs to God alone to search hearts, to change them and to restrain them, Ps. 7, Jer. 17. Let us therefore pray to him, etc. Matt. 5. That he may hear us, let us be faithful to him, John 9. He does not endure the lukewarm, Rev. 3.

units.la: II Arma & vires. Accedit Pontificem, & ab eo accipit literas,&c. Vnde apparet, Romanos praesides causam religionis inter quotidianas controuersias Sacerdotibus commissse, vt se inuidia & molestia liberarent. Fuit autem hoc illis exoptatissimum, & potestate hac crudeliter abusi sunt. Nec dubium est, libenter Saulo dicisse quod petebat, vtpote viro non vulgari, Act.16.22.
units.tr: II. Arms and strength. Saul approaches the High Priest and receives letters from him, etc. From this it appears that the Roman governors had committed questions of religion, amid their daily disputes, to the priests, so that they might free themselves from odium and trouble. This was most welcome to them, and they cruelly abused this power. Nor is there any doubt that he readily granted Saul what he asked, since Saul was no ordinary man, Acts 16:22.

units.la: ¶ Obseruemus fortem piorum. Hostes acerrimos habent Antistites, qui veritatem debebant prouehere, Mal.2. Vt primum enim isti religionis quaestum faciunt & gloriā ex hominibus quaerunt, iam neque credere possunt, neque veritatis lucem ferre, Iohan.5.3. Debebant hos coercere principes, Isa.49. Deut.17. Sed fere nolunt pro religione subire molestiam.
units.tr: Let us observe the lot of the godly. They have the bitterest enemies in their bishops, who ought to have advanced the truth, Mal. 2. For as soon as these men make a trade of religion and seek glory from men, they can no longer either believe or bear the light of truth, John 5:3. The princes ought to restrain them, Isa. 49, Deut. 17. But they are mostly unwilling to undergo trouble for religion.

units.la: Ne tamen illam contemnere putentur ad personatos praesules & Inquisitores rem remittunt: Et ita se extra omnem culpam esse arbitrantur. Sed praeter officium faciunt, Psalmo 2. Esque haec Pilati & Sacerdotum collusio, Lucae 23, Iohannis 19. Idem ergo eis accidit, quod illis olim, &c.
units.tr: Yet, lest they be thought to despise it, they refer the matter to pretended prelates and inquisitors, and so think themselves free of all blame. But they act beyond their office, Psalm 2. And this is the collusion of Pilate and the priests, Luke 23, John 19. So what happened to them of old happens to these men, etc.

units.la: III Finis & institutum: Ut quoscunque inuenerit, &c. Nimirum ut omnes promiscuē tollendo Christi nomen prorsus exstinguere. Si causam quaerās, fuit zelus pro religione patria, Actor 26. Galat. 1. Phil. 3. Apparet ergo hic, quàm nihil ille prosit, nisi Dei verbo regatur. Quo magis iustitiam legis propugnat, eo longius abest a iustitia fidei, quae sola feruat, Gal. 2. Rom. 3. Quo vehementius ardet, eo longius a se iuste recedit. Sic Iudaei Roman. 10 Hodie multi. Errant vehementer, qui nostram intentione sufficere putant. Imo tu hanc suspectam habeto, & per fidei obedientiam te Dei verbo subijce, Numeri decimo quinto.
units.tr: III. The aim and purpose: "that whomever he found," etc. Namely, by removing all people indiscriminately, to extinguish utterly the name of Christ. If you ask the cause, it was zeal for the religion of his fathers, Acts 26, Gal. 1, Phil. 3. It appears here how little he gains unless he is ruled by the word of God. The more he defends the righteousness of the law, the further he is from the righteousness of faith, which alone preserves, Gal. 2, Rom. 3. The more vehemently he burns, the further he withdraws from what is truly just. So did the Jews, Rom. 10. Today many likewise. Those err grievously who think that our own intention is sufficient. Nay, hold it under suspicion, and subject yourself through the obedience of faith to the word of God, Numbers 15.

units.la: Nota. Quantum Deus permittat impijs. Saulus contra discipulos Christi insurgit, quibus hic nihil habet pretiosius. Zach 2. Imo in mulieres. Et quod hic fieri, saepe aliàs fastus, & ita fore praedictum. Matth 10. Ioh 16. 2. Tim 3. Ne ergo offendamur, &c. Heb. 4.
units.tr: Note. How far God permits the wicked. Saul rises against the disciples of Christ, to whom nothing is more precious, Zech. 2. Indeed he rages against women too. That this happens here, and often elsewhere, was foretold: Matt. 10, John 16, 2 Tim. 3. Let us not, therefore, be offended, etc. Heb. 4.

units.la: Interim quidnos decet obseruemus: §1. In fide constanter perseueremus Mat. 24. Lucæ 9. Proderit considerauisse Dei potentiam, quæ hic elucet. Non modò seruat Ecclesiam, & domat Saulum, sed ouem facit, imò pastorem, &c. Isa. 11. Ad de præmij promissiones: Beati qui persecutionem, &c. Matt. 5. Item Luc. 22. Iohan. 14. & 17. Phil. 3. 2. Tim 2.
units.tr: Meanwhile, let us observe what befits us. §1. Let us persevere constantly in faith, Matt. 24, Luke 9. It will profit us to have considered the power of God, which shines forth here. Not only does he preserve the Church and tame Saul, but he makes a sheep, nay a shepherd, etc. Isa. 11. Add the promises of reward: "Blessed are those who suffer persecution," etc. Matt. 5. Likewise Luke 22, John 14 and 17, Phil. 3, 2 Tim. 2.

units.la: § 2. Iuuemus communem causam. Non quidem armis (Iohannis 18) sed pia condolentia, Rom 12. Heb. 13. 2. ad Corinthios 12. Hanc testemur precibus apud Deum, consolatione, beneficentia, &c. Sic olim Christiani, Actorum 4 12. Hoc Paulus petijt, ad Ephesios 6. Hoc ipsi præstitit, Eph 1. &c.
units.tr: §2. Let us help the common cause: not indeed with arms (John 18), but with pious sympathy, Rom. 12, Heb. 13, 2 Cor. 12. Let us bear witness to this by prayers to God, by consolation, by beneficence, etc. So Christians did of old, Acts 4:12. Paul asked this, Eph. 6. He himself rendered this, Eph. 1, etc.

units.la: § 2. Vt preces gratæ sint Deo, serió ad hunc conuertamur, & emendemus mores, ne faciamus quod dicitur Is. 29. Ista agunt nostros mores. In religione nos fri gere patet ex ἀσφορία erga fratres, qui premuntur. Imo an non habet arma nostra coiunximus cum Saulo Damasco eunte. Excusas te egestate. Quæ fronte vero hoc facis, cum luxu, fastu, ebrietate toti fœtea mus, vt de nobis dici possit, quod lere. miæ 3.Isaiæ 1.Hæc emendemus, & Oremus.
units.tr: §2. So that our prayers may be pleasing to God, let us turn to this earnestly and amend our manners, lest we do what is said in Isa. 29. Our conduct drives these things. That we have grown cold in religion is plain from our lack of compassion [ἀσπλαγχνία] towards the brothers who are oppressed. Indeed, have we not joined our arms with Saul on his way to Damascus? You excuse yourself on the ground of poverty. With what face do you do this, when we are steeped in luxury, pride and drunkenness, so that what Jer. 3 and Isa. 1 say can be said of us? Let us amend these things, and pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXIII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXIII.

units.la: 3 Cùm autem iter faceret, factum est, vt appropinquaret Damasco, & repente circumfulsit eum lux de cœlo.
units.tr: 3 As he journeyed, it came about that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven shone round about him.

units.la: 4 Et cùm cecidisset in terram, audiit vocem dicentem sibi, Saul, Saul, quid persequeris me?
units.tr: 4 And he fell to the earth and heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?

units.la: 5 Dixit autem, Quis es Domine? Dominus autem dixit, Ego sum Iesus, quem tu persequeris, durum est tibi contra stimulos calcitrare.
units.tr: 5 And he said, Who are you, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus, whom you persecute. It is hard for you to kick against the goads.

units.la: Ivcas singulari diligentia narrat Sauli conuersi historiam, cùm quod exemplum peculiare continet gratuitæ misericordiæ Dei, qui non solùm vulgaribus vitijs obnoxios, sed hostes quoque respicit, & in gratiam recipit, si vocanti obediant: tum quod hic adumbratur, quæ sit in terris cõditio Ecclesiæ, & quàm facilè sit Deo eam liberare. Id vt clarius appareat, præmisit nuper. 1. Qualis fuerit Saulus, Spirans cædes, &c. 2. Quòd item publica authoritate armatus contenderit Damascũ, instructus nimirum armis, feruis, &c. 3. Finis, vt mulieres & viros vinctos duceret HieHierosolymam, nimirum vt illic vel fidem negarent vel occiderentur, Act. 26.
units.tr: Luke gives the story of Saul's conversion with particular care, since it contains a remarkable example of God's free mercy, who looks upon enemies as well as ordinary sinners and receives them into grace if they obey his call. It also shows what the condition of the Church is on earth and how easily God can deliver her.
