units.la: cæ 12. Rom.8. At Dei peculium, iponfa, domus, hæreditas est, Ioh 1 2 Cor.11. 1 Tim. 3. Matth.21. Et vt in ea sola Deus ve è co- litur, iraın ea sola inuenitur saius. 5 mile Arcæ, Gen.6 7. Ideo omnium vox elt, qu̧ę Dauid. Psalm.84 Et confirmet nos, quod etsi patriam, cognatos, opes possit empere Mundus, tamen a societate Ecclesiæ non potest excludere. Hæc enim nulli loco al- ligata est. Promissiones, Psalm.72 Zach 9. Ioh.4. Et vbique patet accessus per Christum Ioh.10. Imo quando nos ejicit mun- dus, ille nos coll git, Ioh 9.
units.tr: Rom. 8. But God's peculiar possession, his bride, house and inheritance: John 1, 2 Cor. 11, 1 Tim. 3, Matt. 21. And just as God is worshipped in her alone, so salvation is found in her alone, like the ark in Gen. 6–7. Therefore it is the voice of all, which David expresses in Psalm 84: "May he strengthen us." And although the world can buy fatherland, kinsfolk and wealth, yet it cannot exclude anyone from fellowship with the Church, for she is bound to no place. Promises: Psalm 72, Zech. 9, John 4. And access lies open everywhere through Christ, John 10. Indeed, when the world casts us out, he gathers us in, John 9.

units.la: 2. Discipuli timent ab initio, & nolunt eum admittere. Fuit hic non ignauus metus sed iustus & prudens. Vix enim credibile erat, tale tyrannum tam cito conuer sum esse, & iciebant illud Christi, Luc.16.
units.tr: 2. The disciples fear at the start and do not want to admit him. This fear was not cowardly but just and prudent. For it was scarcely credible that such a tyrant had been converted so quickly, and they recalled that saying of Christ, Luke 16.

units.la: Not. 1. Non temere fidendum cuiuis. Omnis homo mendax, Psal.116. Ier.17. Et de fallis fratribus semper quesi sunt pij. Abel a fratre cæsus, Iosephus a fratribus venditus, Gen. 4.37. Moses. Exod 2. Dauid, Psal.41 55. Christus, Ioh 13. Paulus 2 Cor.11. Phil.2. Recte ergo Christus, Mat. 10. Hodie imprimis debet obseruari, Luc æ 18.
units.tr: Note 1. One must not trust anyone rashly. "Every man is a liar," Psalm 116; Jer. 17. And the godly have always complained of false brethren. Abel was slain by his brother, Joseph was sold by his brothers, Gen. 4, 37. Moses, Exod. 2. David, Psalm 41, 55. Christ, John 13. Paul, 2 Cor. 11, Phil. 2. Rightly, therefore, Christ says, Matt. 10. Today above all this ought to be observed, Luke 18.

units.la: 2. Cauendus tamen rigor nimius. Vbi enim iti Barnabam audiuerunt, illum pro fratre agnoscunt. Ita agendum. Qui possunt, testimonium reddant pijs, non augeant suspiciones.Reliqui bene sperent 1.Cor.13.Hodie praepositerè omnia.Opti-mi grauantur suspicionibus.Aperti hostes habentur in precio.
units.tr: 2. Yet excessive rigour must be avoided. For when they heard Barnabas, they acknowledged him as a brother. So it should be done: those who can should bear witness to the godly, not increase suspicions. Others should hope well, 1 Cor. 13. Today everything is turned upside down. The best are burdened with suspicions, while open enemies are held in high esteem.

units.la: 3.De Paulo duo dicuntur. 1.Reiectus non fremit contra pios,non insidiosè sua virtutes praedicat,multò minus ab Ec-clesia resilit, sed patienter hoc omne fert. Memor enim vitae anteactae, agnoscit iudicium Dei, qui ipsum velit humiliare, &c. Imitemur. Hinc enim vera patientia. Dauid,2.Sam.16.Psal.119.peccatur variè.
units.tr: 3. Two things are said of Paul. First, rejected, he does not rage against the godly, does not craftily proclaim his own virtues, and much less leaps away from the Church, but bears all this patiently. For, mindful of his past life, he acknowledges the judgment of God, who wishes to humble him, and so on. Let us imitate him, for here is true patience. David, 2 Sam. 16, Psalm 119. Men sin in many ways.

units.la: ¶ 2. Liberè praedicat, & ita probat se esse verum discipulum. Loquitur aute in nomine I.Christi,in eo nimirū monstrans poenitentiam & peccatorum remissionem Luc.24.In primis autem confutat Hellinistas,de quibus supra 6.Cap.Miscebant hi legem cum Euangelio. His potissimum fuit destinatus Paulus,vt eius Epistolae te stantur. Ita ergo praedicandus Christus, vt contradicentes confutentur,Tit.1.Iniqui,qui hoc nolunt fieri.
units.tr: ¶ 2. He preaches freely, and so proves himself a true disciple. He speaks in the name of Jesus Christ, clearly showing in this repentance and the remission of sins, Luke 24. Above all he confutes the Hellenists, of whom we spoke above in chapter 6. These men mixed the law with the gospel. Paul was especially sent to them, as his Epistles bear witness. So Christ must be preached in such a way that those who contradict are refuted, Titus 1. Wicked are those who do not want this done.

units.la: 4.Rursus insidiae instruuntur.Ita solent hypoctitae iustitiarij. Cum sanctissimi ha beri velint, leue eis est, insontes iugulare, Ioh.18. Rursus aute exerit se discipulorū habet. fides, qui cum vitæ periculo eum deduce-cunt,&c.
units.tr: 4. Again plots are laid. So hypocritical self-righteous men are wont to act: although they wish to be thought most holy, it is easy for them to cut the throats of the innocent, John 18. Again, the faith of the disciples shows itself, who escort him at risk to their own lives, and so on.

units.la: No T.¶ 1. Pauli constantiam, qui etiam si noua indies pericula surgant, non defi-cit tamen. Expendit haud dubiè commu-nem piorum fortem,Pf.34. 2 Tim.3.Matt. 16. Iohan. 15. 16. Cogitat se grauiora me-ruisse,Act.8.26.Itaque agnoscit singulare Dei beneficiū, qui eum non credere mo-do velit in Christum, verumetiam pro-pter eum affligi, 1.Thessal.1.In his simus hodie.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. Consider Paul's constancy: though new dangers arise daily, he does not fail. He doubtless weighs the common lot of the godly, Psalm 34, 2 Tim. 3, Matt. 16, John 15–16. He reflects that he has deserved heavier things, Acts 8:26. Therefore he recognises God's singular benefit, who wills him not only to believe in Christ but also to suffer for him, 1 Thess. 1. Let us be such people today.

units.la: ¶ 2.Recta in patriam contendit,vt huic prædicet.Sic Christus,Luc.4. Commen-datur pietas in patriam. Imitemur Pauli fidem & constantiam: ne deficiamus,quan-do bene cœpimus,Lu.9.Mat.24.Oremus
units.tr: ¶ 2. He makes straight for his homeland, to preach to them. So Christ, Luke 4. Piety is commended towards one's homeland. Let us imitate Paul's faith and constancy, and not fail when we have begun well, Luke 9, Matt. 24. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXI.
units.tr: HOMILIA LXXXI.

units.la: 31 Ecclesiæ igitur per totam Iudæam & Galilæam & Samariam habebant pacem,et ædificabantur, & pergentes in timore Domini, & consolatione sancti spiritus, multiplicabantur.
units.tr: So the churches throughout all Judea, Galilee and Samaria had peace, and were built up; walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, they were multiplied.

units.la: EXposuit hucusque Lucas prima Pauli in apostolatu tyrocinia, plena laboris, & periculi. Bis enim vitæ discrimen subijt, & bis discipulorum opera est libe-ratus.Docent hæc, quid Christi cultores maneat, Matth. 16. 2. Tim. 3. At hic Pauli constantiam imitari oporret, Luc. 9. Matt. 24. Quia autem, quae hucusque narrata sunt, Ecclesiae totius ruinam alatura videri poterant, abrumpit nunc Pauli historiam Lucas vsque ad 13. Cap. & multa narrat, quibus docet, quàm feliciter Ecclesia non modo seruata, verumetiam propagata fit illo tempore. In praesenti in genere huius conditionem describit, hoc ordine.
units.tr: Hitherto Luke has set out Paul's first apprenticeships in the apostleship, full of labour and danger. Twice he underwent peril of life, and twice he was delivered through the efforts of the disciples. These things teach what awaits the worshippers of Christ (Matt. 16; 2 Tim. 3). But here one ought to imitate Paul's constancy (Luke 9; Matt. 24). Since the things narrated so far might seem to portend the ruin of the whole Church, Luke now breaks off the history of Paul until chapter 13, and relates many things by which he shows how happily the Church was not only preserved but also spread abroad at that time. For the present he describes its condition in general, in this order.

units.la: I. Pacem habuerunt Ecclesiae per Iudaeam, Galatiam & Samariam. Mirabile hoc fuit, si repetas id quod Hierosolymis fastum, & quid Aret. tentarit. Sed facillimum hoc est Deo, qui solet aduersa laetis tempore. Simile hyemis, quam sequitur ver, &c. Sic post nubila Phoebus. Post tempestates χαλλων. Sic quoque cum Ecclesia fit: ne prorsus deficiamus, 1. Cor. 10. 2. Corinth. 1. Sunt exempla per totum librum Iudicu. Ita per tota historia: Ecclesiasticam.
units.tr: I. The churches had peace throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria. This would be a marvel if you recall what happened at Jerusalem and what Aretas attempted. But it is very easy for God, who is accustomed to make adversity give way to joy. It is like winter, which is followed by spring, etc. Thus Phoebus shines after clouds; after storms there is something more beautiful [χαλλων]. So it also happens with the Church, so that we may not utterly fail (1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1). There are examples throughout the book of Judges. So it is throughout ecclesiastical history.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Crucem ita pijs imponi, vt tamen haec non perpetua verae Ecclesiae nota sit. Et ideo errare eos, qui clamant Ecclesias, quibus datur in pace agere. Obseruandum hoc propter Anabaptistas, qui hanc quoque aiunt causam esse secessionis suae. Sed cogitarent, vnum quod que vitae genus habere propriam crucem, & quenque diem,&c. Matth.6. At res ipsa probat,tales crucem fugere.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The cross is so laid on the godly that yet this is not a perpetual mark of the true Church. Therefore they err who cry out against churches that are granted to act in peace. This must be observed on account of the Anabaptists, who also say this is the cause of their secession. But let them consider that each way of life has its own cross, and each day, etc. (Matt. 6). Yet the thing itself proves that such men flee the cross.

units.la: ¶2. Ad pacem Ecclesiae non requiri vel dissimulationem,vel abnegationem fidei. Audiuimus enim quid Apostoli,quid Paulus imprimis fecerit. Attamen pax secuta. Fit hoc fere passim. Seruat ingenium suum mundus.Ioh.1.15 Si ergo se timeri putat,ferocit, & piorum indulgentia fit infolentior. At si ijdem constantes sint, incipit timere. Vide supra 5 &c. Quod si qui pergant sequi re, facile eos coercet Dominus,Psal.2.
units.tr: 2. For the peace of the Church neither dissimulation nor the denial of the faith is required. For we have heard what the apostles, and Paul above all, did, and yet peace followed. This happens almost everywhere. The world keeps its own nature (John 1:15). If therefore it thinks itself feared, it becomes proud, and the indulgence of the pious makes it more insolent. But if the same people remain constant, it begins to fear. See above, 5, etc. But if some persist in following these things, the Lord easily restrains them (Ps. 2).

units.la: II. Fructus pacis: Ecclesiae aedificabuntur.
units.tr: II. The fruit of peace: the churches will be built up.

units.la: Potest bifariam exponi: quod vel auctus sit credentium numerus, vel quod singuli profecerint quoad dona spiritus sancti. Sunt ergo vanissimi conatus hostium Christi. Oportet enim huius regnum crescere, Dan.2.Mar.13. Itaque semper fit, quod olim in Aegypto, Exod.1.
units.tr: This can be explained in two ways: either the number of believers increased, or individuals advanced as to the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Therefore the attempts of Christ's enemies are most vain. For his kingdom must grow (Dan. 2; Mark 13). Thus it always happens, as once in Egypt (Exod. 1).

units.la: Interim Nota. ¶Aedificandi verbum. Ratio huius, quod Ecclesia domus Dei, 1.Tim.3. & singuli credentes templa, &c. 1.Cor. 6. Ideo Ecclesia aedificium Dei, & ministri huius architecti dicuntur, 1.Cor. 3.Psa.118. Officij admonet hoc omnes, qui alijs praestant, vt nimirum scopum omnium studiorum sibi proponant, Ecclesiae aedificationem: vt scilicet omnes supra Christum fundamentum vnicum coalescant, & Dei domus fiant, 1 Cor. 3. Minis-tri, Magistratus, If. 49. Parentes, Pf. 78. Ita plus proficies, quàm si marmorea templa erigas. Vici ffim alij se ita extrui patiantur 1 Pet 2. Curent denique, vt in Christo pro ficiant, &c. Eph. 4.
units.tr: Meanwhile note the word "to build." The reason is that the Church is the house of God (1 Tim. 3), and individual believers are temples (1 Cor. 6). Therefore the Church is called God's building, and its ministers are called the workers of this architect (1 Cor. 3; Ps. 118). This admonishes all who excel others of their duty, namely that they set before themselves as the aim of all their studies the building up of the Church: that is, that all, cohering upon Christ the one foundation, may become God's house (1 Cor. 3). Ministers, magistrates (Isa. 49), parents (Ps. 78): so you will accomplish more than if you raised marble temples. Let others allow themselves to be so built up (1 Pet. 2). Finally, let them take care to advance in Christ, etc. (Eph. 4).

units.la: III. Quomodo vsi sunt hac pace? perge, bant in timore Domini. Ita notatur vera religio. Vt enim Deum timeamus, cognitio ne opus est, quae ex verbi praedicatione nascitur, Rom. 10. Haec fidem parit, ex qua Dilectio Dei, Deut. 6. Gal. 5. Timor, 2. Corinth. 4. Obedientia praeceptorum, &c.
units.tr: III. How did they use this peace? They walked in the fear of the Lord. Thus true religion is marked. For that we may fear God, knowledge is needed, which is born of the preaching of the word (Rom. 10). This produces faith, from which comes the love of God (Deut. 6; Gal. 5), fear (2 Cor. 4), obedience to the precepts, etc.

units.la: Notr. Quid eos deceat, qui pace & otio fruuntur. Agnoscant hoc Dei donum esse. Huc facit multum, si cogitent, quid alij patiantur. Deinde huic grati sint: bene vtantur ad Dei gloriam, & aliorum miserijs tangantur, Heb. 13. Si non possunt iuuare, saltem faueant eis: iuuent precibus: non laedant. Peccatur hodie turpiter multis modis, &c.
units.tr: Note what befits those who enjoy peace and leisure. Let them acknowledge this to be a gift of God. It helps greatly if they consider what others suffer. Then let them be thankful for it: use it well to the glory of God, and be moved by the miseries of others (Heb. 13). If they cannot help, let them at least favour those in need; let them help with prayers, and not harm them. Today many sin shamefully in many ways, etc.

units.la: IV. Premium. Replebantur consolatione spiritus sancti.
units.tr: IV. The reward: they were filled with the consolation of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Ita ratae fuerunt promissiones, Iohan. 14. Matth. 25. Interim innuitur, quòd singuli Spiritus consolationem senserunt efficacissimam. Deinde quòd Evangelij praedicatio indies propagata sit. quæ veram consolitione affert,quia Christum tradit, Rom.5.
units.tr: Thus the promises were fulfilled (John 14; Matt. 25). Meanwhile it is hinted that each one felt the consolation of the Spirit to be most effective. Then, that the preaching of the gospel was spread abroad daily, which brings true consolation, because it delivers Christ (Rom. 5).

units.la: ¶Hæc si nobis applicentur, docebunt, quæ causa sit, quod minus proficimus, & quid oporteat emendari, si velimus nobis bene esse. Oremus.
units.tr: If these things are applied to us, they will teach what the cause is that we make less progress, and what ought to be amended if we wish to be well. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXXII.

units.la: 32 Factum est autem, ut Petrus dum illas omnes peragraret, ascenderet etiam ad sanctos qui habitabant Lyddæ.
units.tr: 32 And it came to pass, as Peter passed throughout all quarters, that he went up also to the saints which dwelt at Lydda.

units.la: 33 Reperit autem illic quendam nomine Aeneam ab annis iam octo decumbentem in grabbato, qui erat paralyticus.
units.tr: 33 And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had lain on a bed for eight years, and was paralytic.

units.la: 34 Et dixit ei Petrus, Aenea sanate te Iesus Christus, surge & sterne tibi ipsi. Is autem statim surrexit.
units.tr: 34 And Peter said unto him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately.

units.la: 35 Et viderunt eum omnes, qui incolebant Lyddam & Saronam, qui converterunt ad Dominum.
units.tr: 35 And all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron saw him, and turned to the Lord.

units.la: ETsi Christus suos ad crucem vocet, & in hoc seculo nihil quàm aduersa poiliceatur (Matt.16.Ioh.15. Luc.12.) non debet tamen hoc ita accipi, quasi nulla pax vnquam sperari debeat, aut quasi Christiani non sint, quibus datur pace frui. Quia enim Deus nostri amans est, & nouit qui simus(Psalm.103.) non finit nos supra vires tentari,1.Cor.10.Et ut in rerum natura, sic etiam in Ecclesia ferè solet crucem pacis bono temperare.Vidimus hoc nuper.Cum enim narrasset, quàm difficilis fuerit Ecclesiæ fors iam inde ab initio, & ut Pauli conuersione hostes magis irritati sint, mox ostendit, Ecclesias omnes habuisse pacem,&c. Potest ergo hoc ipsum hodie quoque fieri. ¶ Obseruent mo dò tunc pij,ut isti pace vsi sint. Ambulârunt in timore Dei,id est, fidem non verbis modò profesi sunt, sed ita vixerunt, vt constaret eos vera Dei cognitione illu minatos esse,&c.Ita nobis agendum,vt alij per nos lucrifiant,Iac.2.Matt.5.¶ Quia autem hoc in genere de tota Ecclesia dici tur, sequuntur quædam specialia de Petro, vt ex huius exemplo intelligamus, quid Apostoli omnes fecerint. Fuit enim omnium idem studium,vt regnum Christi propagarent pro virili,&c.Duo autem narrantur.
units.tr: Although Christ calls his people to the cross, and promises them nothing in this age but adversity (Matt. 16, John 15, Luke 12), this should not be taken to mean that no peace can ever be hoped for, or that Christians are not those to whom peace is given to enjoy. For since God is loving towards us and knows what we are (Ps. 103), he does not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength (1 Cor. 10). And as in nature, so also in the Church, he is wont to temper the cross with the good of peace. We saw this recently. For when Luke had related how difficult the Church's lot had been from the beginning, and how the enemies were the more provoked by Paul's conversion, he soon shows that all the churches had peace, etc. So the same thing can happen today too. Let the godly only observe how those men enjoyed peace: they walked in the fear of God, that is, they did not merely profess the faith in words, but lived in such a way that it was plain they had been enlightened by the true knowledge of God, etc. So we must act so that others may be gained through us (James 2, Matt. 5). Since this is said in general of the whole Church, certain particulars follow about Peter, so that from his example we may understand what all the apostles did. For all had the same zeal, to spread the kingdom of Christ as far as they could, etc. Two things are related.

units.la: I. Peragrauit omnes illas Ecclesias:Nimirum vt videret, quid facto opus esset, collapsa instauraret,errores corrigeret, laborantes iuuaret, doceret, consolaretur. Hæc enim fuisse Apostolorum studia,patet ex Act.14.15.Rom.1.2.Cor.11.
units.tr: I. He went through all those churches: namely, to see what needed to be done, to restore what had collapsed, to correct errors, to help the struggling, to teach and to console. That these were the labours of the apostles is evident from Acts 14, 15, Rom. 1, 2 Cor. 11.

units.la: Vbi Noт. ¶Ecclesias non modo constitui oportere, sed insuper multa cura & inspectione opus esse, ne quod partum est dilabatur. Vt enim in aedificio ventis expositò multa pereunt, quae refici oportet: Ita hic, &c. Et vt in agris etiam lolium crescit: sic in agro Domini. Et hoc in primis, quando omnia pacata sunt. Tunc enim securi fiunt homines, & ex eo occasionem Satanas arripit. Matt. 13 12. Cogitent de eo Ministri & Magistratus. Alij vero istorum curam patienter ferant. Quàm enim hac opus sit, res ipsa docet. Quid enim apud nos integrum? Vbi leges & harum vigor? Imò eò deuenimus, vt neque plagis praesentibus, neq; periculis fratrum circumquaq; periclitantium, neq; futurorum malorum praestigijs moueamur.
units.tr: Note: that churches must not only be established, but much care and oversight is also needed, lest what has been gained slip away. For as in a building exposed to the winds many things perish which must be repaired, so here, etc. And as tares grow even in fields, so in the Lord's field; and this especially when all things are peaceful. For then men grow secure, and Satan seizes the opportunity from this (Matt. 13). Let ministers and magistrates consider this, and let others patiently bear their care. How much it is needed the thing itself teaches. For what among us is whole? Where are the laws and their force? Indeed we have come to the point where we are moved neither by present blows, nor by the dangers of brethren on every side in peril, nor by the portents of future evils.

units.la: II. Miracula duo narrantur, quibus Petri ministerium Deus obsignauit, & plures alios excitauit vt crederent. Primum Lyddae, alterum Ioppae editum. In praesenti primum habetur, quo totius negotij Euangelici typus continetur. Talia enim fuerunt Apostolorum miracula, (Mar.16. Mat.10.) non inania & friuola, vt impostorum. Videamus ergo singulas partes.
units.tr: II. Two miracles are related, by which God sealed Peter's ministry and stirred up many others to believe: the first done at Lydda, the other at Joppa. In the present passage the first is found, in which the whole pattern of the gospel enterprise is contained. For the miracles of the apostles were of such a kind (Mark 16, Matt. 10), not empty and frivolous like those of impostors. Let us therefore look at the individual parts.

units.la: 1. Æneas, in quo miraculum editum. Paralyticus ab octo annis. Est paralysis resolutio lutio neruorum ex frigido & crasso humo re,qui membris,in quæ delabitur,sensum motumq; adimit. Vix curatur,licet initio statim medicinam adhibeas. At mora diuturnior omnino incurabilem reddit. Talis hic.
units.tr: 1. Aeneas, in whom the miracle was wrought: paralysed for eight years. Paralysis is a loosening of the nerves caused by a cold and thick humour, which descends into the limbs and takes away sensation and motion. It is scarcely cured, even if you apply medicine at once; but a longer delay makes it altogether incurable. Such was this man.

units.la: ¶ Typus communis omnium nostrûm conditionis. Paralysis enim peccatum adumbrat,qui veré superfluus,crassus & frigidus humor est. Nam accessit ex diaboli suggestione bonæ Dei creaturæ,Gen. 1. 3. Occupatur circa terrena. Extinguit Dei amorem. At in eo omnes concipimur & nascimur,Gen.5. Rom.5 Psal.51. Itaq; terrenis addicti frigemus in diuinis. Imò horum sensu destituimur, & ne cogitare qui dem de illis possumus,1.Cor.2.2.Corin 3. Gen.8.
units.tr: He is a type of the common condition of all of us. For paralysis foreshadows sin, which is truly a superfluous, thick and cold humour. For it arose from the devil's suggestion against God's good creature (Gen. 1, 3). It is occupied with earthly things and extinguishes the love of God. In this we are all conceived and born (Gen. 5, Rom. 5, Ps. 51). And so, given over to earthly things, we grow cold towards divine things. Indeed we are deprived of their sense, and cannot even think about them (1 Cor. 2, 2 Cor. 3, Gen. 8).

units.la: 2. Quis sanat? Petrus quidem proponi tur,sed hic ipse Christum monstrat. Ergo huius fuit opus, neq; propria virtute aliquid potuerunt Apostoli. Ita ipse fatetur supra 3. Sic Paulus infra 14. Et apparet etiam aperte,Phil.2.
units.tr: 2. Who heals? Peter is put forward, but he himself points to Christ. So the work was Christ's, and the apostles could do nothing by their own virtue. Peter himself confesses this above (ch. 3), and Paul likewise below (ch. 14). And it appears plainly also in Phil. 2.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Christum esse medicum nostrû,qui non modò peccata expiauit(Joh. 1) sed qui vitiosæ etiam naturæ medetur. Talem prædixit,Isa 53 35 Talem se profite tur,Matth.9 Regenerat enim nos ex verbi semine.1.Pet.1.Iohan.3. Illuminat, Ioh.
units.tr: Note: that Christ is our physician, who not only expiated sins (John 1), but also heals our vitiated nature. He foretold such a healer (Isa. 53, 35), and professed himself to be one (Matt. 9). For he regenerates us from the seed of the word (1 Pet. 1, 1 John 3), he illuminates (John 1:8, 9),

units.la: 1. 8. 9. Voluntatem mutat & vires largitur, Ioh. 15. Phil. 4. Ad hunc ergo abeamus Matth. 11.
units.tr: he changes the will and bestows strength (John 15, Phil. 4). Let us therefore go to him (Matt. 11).

units.la: 3. Quid mandat? Surge, scilicet in nomine Iesu. Sic supra 2. Item, Sterne tibi ipsi. Id additur, ne quis praestigium fuisse putaret. Ita ipse Christus, Mat. 9. Ioh. 5. In eodem etiam differunt miracula Apostolorum a Magicis. Officij autem admonentur, qui per Christum curati sunt. Non iaceant in stratis peccati, sed his excusis fur gant ad vitae nouitatem. Ita Christus iubet, Ioh. 5. Vide item Rom. 6. 12. Ephes. 4 Col. 3. Qui adhuc sordent & iacent, sed non dum curatos esse produnt.
units.tr: 3. What does he command? "Arise", namely in the name of Jesus; so above, ch. 2. Likewise, "make thy bed." This is added lest anyone think it was a trick; so Christ himself (Matt. 9, John 5). In this also the apostles' miracles differ from magical ones. Those who have been healed through Christ are reminded of their duty: let them not lie on the couch of sin, but, having shaken off these, rise to newness of life. Thus Christ bids (John 5); see also Rom. 6, 12, Eph. 4, Col. 3. Those who still wallow and lie about show that they are not yet healed.

units.la: 4. Fructus miraculi. Viderunt omnes. Vult Deus sua opera innotescere, non celat vt impostores. Et conuertuntur ad Dominum, non ad Petrum, vt Lystrenses. Infra 14. Et hic verus omnium miraculorum finis est & vsus, Mar. 16, Ioh. 20. Impostores sunt, qui illis ad stabiliendum cultum Diuorum abutuntur. Ita ex veris miraculis falsa faciunt, inuitis etiam Sanctis. Vno igitur Christo contenti simus, huic indiuulsè adhaereamus, & vt in eodem vitam viuamus nouam, atque seruemur, indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: 4. The fruit of the miracle: "All saw." God wishes his works to become known; he does not hide them as impostors do. "And turned to the Lord", not to Peter, as the Lystrans did (see ch. 14). Here is the true end and use of all miracles (Mark 16, John 20). Impostors are those who abuse them to establish the worship of saints; so from true miracles they make false ones, even against the will of the saints. Therefore let us be content with Christ alone, cling to him inseparably, and so live a new life in him and be preserved. Let us pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXIII.
units.tr: Homily 83.

units.la: 36 Ioppe autem fuit quaedam discipula nomine Tabitha (quae si interpretetur, dicitur Caprea) Haec erat dives operum bonorum & eleemosynarum, quas praestabat.
units.tr: 36 Now at Joppa there was a certain female disciple named Tabitha (which, when translated, is called Dorcas). She was rich in good works and in the alms she gave.

units.la: 37 Factum est autem per illos dies, ut ex morbo moreretur, quam quum lavissent, posuerunt in coenaculo.
units.tr: 37 And it came to pass in those days that she fell sick and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.

units.la: 38 Quum autem Lydda esset prope Ioppen, discipuli audito, Petrum illic esse, duos viros miserunt ad eum, rogantes, ne cunctaretur usque ad ipsos progredi.
units.tr: 38 Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, asking him not to delay but to come on to them.

units.la: 39 Exurgens igitur Petrus, venit cum eis. Quem, ubi adfuit, duxerunt in coenaculum: ubi adstiterunt ei omnes viduae flentes & ostendentes, &c. ad sinem usque Capitis.
units.tr: 39 So Peter rose and went with them. When he arrived, they brought him into the upper room, where all the widows stood around him weeping and showing him the garments, etc., to the end of the chapter.

units.la: CHristus Apostolos non solum ad Evangelizandum emisit, sed miraculis quoque instruxit, quibus doctrinam suam confirmarent, & adumbrarent quis Christus, & quid is nobis meruerit. Et huc referri debent, quae hic de Petro narrantur. In priori vidimus per Christum collapsas naturae vires restitui, Ioh. 3. 15. Rom. 7. Philip. 4. Sequitur maius, quod mortua reuiuiscit: vt constet, Christum mortis quoq; esse victorem (1.Cor.15.) & ideo hanc non esse timendam,Ioh.5.
units.tr: Christ sent out the apostles not only to preach the Gospel but also equipped them with miracles, by which they might confirm their teaching and foreshadow who Christ is and what he has merited for us. To this should be referred what is narrated here about Peter. In the earlier miracle we saw the fallen powers of nature restored through Christ (John 3:15; Rom. 7; Phil. 4). Now comes something greater: the dead come back to life, so that it is established that Christ is also the conqueror of death (1 Cor. 15), and therefore that death is not to be feared (John 5).

units.la: I. Describitur persona, in qua æditum miraculum. Nomen ponitur ad rei veritatem. Deinde hæc dicuntur. ¶ 1. Discipula fuit, id est, Christiana. Ita initio nominantur, Act.11. Et quamuis mutatum fit nomen, meminerimus tamen, nos Christianos non esse, nisi Christi discipuli simus. Requiritur ergo fides & obedientia, Ro.1 16. 1.Cor.10. Arguuntur sectarij.
units.tr: I. The person in whom the miracle was wrought is described. Her name is given to establish the truth of the matter. Then the following is said. (1) She was a disciple, that is, a Christian. So they are named at the beginning, Acts 11. And although the name has changed, let us remember that we are not Christians unless we are disciples of Christ. Faith and obedience are therefore required (Rom. 1:16; 1 Cor. 10). The sectaries are refuted.

units.la: ¶ 2. Plena bonis operibus. Qualibus? Elee mosyna. Complestitur omnia charitatis of ficia, Matt.25. Ita autem dicuntur, quia per se non probantur, nisi ex misericordia manent, quæ charitatis proprium effectu est, Luc.10. Arguit hoc eos, qui pro bonis operibus vendicant, quæ neq; ex fide neq; charitate fiunt. Dicitur de his idem quod Ifa.1.58.Ier.7. Eos item qui ad ostentationem faciunt, Matth.6.
units.tr: (2) She was full of good works. What kind? Alms. She fulfilled all the offices of charity (Matt. 25). They are so called because they are not approved in themselves unless they flow from mercy, which is the proper effect of charity (Luke 10). This refutes those who claim credit for good works that are done neither from faith nor from charity. The same is said of such people as in Isa. 58 and Jer. 7, and likewise of those who act for display (Matt. 6).

units.la: ¶ 3. Aegrotat & moritur. Sunt ergo sańti quoq; obnoxij communibus miserijs, Act.14. Sed differentia est inter hos & impios, quia illis omnia adiumento sunt ad bonum, Ro.8. Illustratur enim in ipsis gloria Dei, vt de cæco & Lazaro dicitur, Ioh. 9.11. Exercetur eorum patientia & fides. Rom.5. Prosunt exemplo alijs Ista exei-tent,vt aui omnem euentum parati fimus, & simul nos consolentur,&c.
units.tr: (3) She falls ill and dies. So holy people too are subject to the common miseries (Acts 14). But there is a difference between them and the impious, because for the godly all things work together for good (Rom. 8). For the glory of God is revealed in them, as is said of the blind man and of Lazarus (John 9; 11). Their patience and faith are exercised (Rom. 5). They benefit others by their example. These things happen so that we may be ready for every outcome, and at the same time so that they may console us, etc.

units.la: II. Quid fecerunt domestici & reliqui fideles: ¶ 1. Lauerunt & posuerunt in cæ-naculo.Antiquus mos,vt & condiendi aro matibus. Seruiebat resurrectionis myste rio.Et initio potuerunt ista ferri,donec fi des omnium confirmaretur. Hodie non opus,cum in Christo habeamus purifica-tionem,resurrectione,vitam,i.Ioh.i.Ioh.5 ii.&c.Sufficiat ergo,quod honestè condi-antur mortui sepulchris. Vide i.Theff.4.
units.tr: II. What the household and the other faithful did. (1) They washed her and laid her in an upper room. This was an ancient custom, as was also the anointing with spices. It served the mystery of the resurrection, and at first such things could be carried out until the faith of all was confirmed. Today there is no need of them, since in Christ we have purification, resurrection and life (1 John 1; 1 John 5, etc.). It is enough, therefore, that the dead are decently buried in their tombs. See 1 Thess. 4.

units.la: ¶ 2. Miserunt qui vocarent Petrum. Ergo spes illis fuit hanc posse restitui,& hoc in primis cupiunt. Ita vero fidem & charitatem testantur. Huius est mortuos quoque amare.Sic mulieres illæ,de quibus Lucæ 8.23.24. Et est hoc inter pietatis præmia non postremum, quod Deus dat tales, qui mortuorum quoq; curam habeant,& eorum honorem vindicent.
units.tr: (2) They sent for Peter to call him. So they had hope that she could be restored, and this is what they desire above all. Thus they bear witness to their faith and charity. It is the mark of a believer to love even the dead. So did those women of whom Luke 8.23.24 speaks. And among the rewards of piety this is no small one: God gives such people, who take care of the dead as well and vindicate their honour.

units.la: ¶ 3. Cum fletu ostendunt vestes, quas illa fecerat pauperibus. Gratitudinis officium. Pa tet hic,quę vere reliquiæ sanctorum? Non offa,vestes ipsorum,&c. Sed fidei & charitatis monumenta,Apoc.14. Dehis debet exponi quod habetur,Pfalm.34.112. Proverb.10. Arguuntur, qui nihil posteris relinquunt quàm luxus, libidinis, auaritiæ & rapacitatis indicia. Vide Iac. 5. Hab. 2. Quid, qui mortui ista ostentant?
units.tr: (3) With weeping they show the garments that she had made for the poor. This is the duty of gratitude. Here it is plain what are the true relics of the saints: not bones, but their garments, etc. These are monuments of faith and charity (Rev. 14). From these must be explained what is found in Ps. 34; 112; Prov. 10. Those are refuted who leave nothing to posterity but tokens of luxury, lust, avarice and rapacity. See James 5; Hab. 2. What of those who display such things when they are dead?

units.la: III. Quid Petrus? Facilis mox abit Iop pen, vt qui cupiebat omnibus seruire. Ibi hæc fiunt q Omnibus eiectis ipse in genua prouolutus orat. Ita quasi fatetur, opus hoc non esse suarum virium, sed Dei. Deinde accedit, & iubet surgere, nimirum vt Christi Apostolus, & in nomine Christi. Illa aperit oculos, confidet, erigitur, & suis redditur viua.
units.tr: III. What Peter did. He soon leaves for Joppa, as one who was eager to serve all. There, with everyone else put out, he falls on his knees and prays. Thus he, as it were, confesses that this work is not of his own powers but of God's. Then he comes near and bids her rise, of course as an apostle of Christ and in the name of Christ. She opens her eyes, sits up, is raised, and is restored alive to her people.

units.la: q Christus ergo verè Dominus vitæ & mortis, Ioh. 11. Rom. 14. Et habemus hic in fallibile argumentum eius quod dicitur, Ezechiel. 37. Ioh. 5. Matth. 24. Si enim vox Christi in Petro tã efficax, quid fiet olim, quando tuba Dei sonabit, 1. Corinth. 15. 1. Thess. 4.
units.tr: Christ, therefore, is truly the Lord of life and death (John 11; Rom. 14). And we have here an infallible proof of what is said in Ezek. 37, John 5 and Matt. 24. For if the voice of Christ was so effective in Peter, what will happen one day when the trumpet of God sounds (1 Cor. 15; 1 Thess. 4)?

units.la: q Interim officij admonentur, qui in peccatis quasi mortui iacent. Ad Euangelij vocem aperiant oculos mentis. Reside ant erecti. Manum præbente Domino, sub leuari se patiantur. Huc pertinet quod habetur, Eph. 5. At hodie qui Euangelio gloriantur, ferè viuentes mortui sunt, vt viduæ, de quibus 1. Tim. 5. Itaque vt isti dicuntur visohoc signo credidisse : sicnos quoq; credamus Christo, & fidem vita atque factis testemur.
units.tr: Meanwhile, those who lie in sin as if dead are reminded of their duty: at the voice of the Gospel let them open the eyes of their minds, let them sit up and rise, and, with the Lord offering his hand, let them allow themselves to be raised up. To this belongs what is found in Eph. 5. But today those who boast of the Gospel are for the most part living dead, like the widows of whom 1 Tim. 5 speaks. And so, as those others are said to have believed when they saw this sign, let us too believe Christ, and bear witness to our faith by our life and deeds.

units.la: Additur, Petrum diuertisse apud Simonem coriarium: id quod παρασκευὴ ha-bet ad sequentem historiam.
units.tr: It is added that Peter lodged with Simon the tanner, which serves as a preparation [παρασκευή] for the following story.

units.la: Interim ¶ Vide humilem primitiuę Ec-clesiæ faciem. Quales fuerint alij credentes Ioppæ, hinc liquet, quando non alius hospes Petro obtingit. Sed hoc illud est, de quo 1.Cor.1.Matth. 11. E contra vides, Apostolorum frugalitatem. Simile infra 18. Hodie Apostolorum successores vix regalibus palatijs sunt contenti. Agnoscamus Dei bonitatem, imitemur Christum & huius Apostolos, vigilemus & Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile, observe the humble face of the primitive Church. What the other believers at Joppa were like is clear from this, since no other host falls to Peter's lot. This is that of which 1 Cor. 1 and Matt. 11 speak. On the contrary, you see the frugality of the apostles. A similar case occurs below at 18. Today the successors of the apostles are hardly content with royal palaces. Let us acknowledge God's goodness, imitate Christ and his apostles, and watch and pray.

units.la: CAPVT X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXXIV.

units.la: VIR autem quidam erat Cæsareæ nomine Cornelius, Centurio ex cohorte, quæ dicitur Italica.
units.tr: There was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian.

units.la: 2 Pius ac timens Deum cum tota domo sua, faciens eleemosynas multas populo.
units.tr: (2) He was devout and feared God with all his household, giving many alms to the people.

units.la: 3 Qui cum assiduè precaretur Deum, vidit per visum manifestè quasi hora diei nona, Angelum Dei introeuntem, & dicentem ipsi, Corneli.
units.tr: (3) While he was praying constantly to God, he saw clearly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in and saying to him, "Cornelius."

units.la: Cap. 10
units.tr: Chapter 10

units.la: PRIMA huius libri parte narrauit Lucas, vt Apostoli Euangelium Iudæis prædicârint, vtq; hi se gesserint. Crediderunt multi, sed maior pars hostiliter oppugnauit. Erat ergo tempus, vt regnum Dei transferretur ad gentes, Matth.21. Initium fit à Cornelio. Vbi ante omnia obseruabimus: 1. Deum nulli genti esse obstrictum, ideoque ingratos & contumaces reijcere, Ro. 10. Luc.17. Colos 3. 2. Christum gentibus quoque datum 3. Nobis cauendum, nec idem accidat quod Iudæis, Rom. 11. Ioh.15. &c. Quia autem hæc res Iudæis semper impossibilis fuit visa, (Deut.4. Exod.19. Psal.147.) olim prædicta fuit gentium vocatio, Psa.2.72. Zach.9. Isa.2.42.49.60 &c. Et huius initium tale est, vt videas omnia hæc ex Dei consilio fuisse facta.
units.tr: In the first part of this book Luke narrated how the apostles preached the gospel to the Jews, and how they conducted themselves. Many believed, but the greater part attacked them with hostility. There was therefore a time for the kingdom of God to be transferred to the Gentiles (Matt. 21). The beginning is made with Cornelius. Where we first observe: 1. that God is bound to no nation, and therefore rejects the ungrateful and stubborn (Rom. 10; Luke 17; Col. 3). 2. that Christ was given to the Gentiles also. 3. that we must take care that what happened to the Jews does not happen to us (Rom. 11; John 15, etc.). Since this matter always seemed impossible to the Jews (Deut. 4; Exod. 19; Ps. 147), the calling of the Gentiles was foretold long ago (Ps. 2; 72; Zech. 9; Isa. 2; 42; 49; 60, etc.). And the beginning of it is such that you may see all these things were done by the counsel of God.

units.la: I. A descriptione Cornelij orditur, in quo Not. Conditionem Centurio cohortis Italicæ, & proinde Italus, qui Cæsaris erat in prætorio. Ita enim solebant Romani legiones habere dispositas in primis versus Orientem propter Parthos, & vt Iudæi continerentur in officio. Hinc illa Luc.3.7. Vbi obseruemus, quid fiat ijs, qui libertate abutuntur, & factiones foveant. Tales fuerunt Iudæi. Fit ergo, quod Deus minatus fuerat, Deut.28. Similia exempla sunt hodie passim. Cauëamus nos, &c. Interim apparet Dei bonitas.
units.tr: I. The account begins with Cornelius, in which note: his position as centurion of an Italian cohort, and therefore an Italian, who was in Caesar's praetorium. For the Romans were accustomed to station their legions in the first places toward the East, on account of the Parthians, and so that the Jews might be kept in obedience. Hence that saying in Luke 3:7. Here we may observe what happens to those who abuse liberty and foster factions. Such were the Jews. So what God had threatened in Deut. 28 comes to pass. Similar examples are found everywhere today. Let us take care, etc. Meanwhile God's goodness appears.

units.la: ¶ 2. Studia & mores Timens Deum. Er go non coluit multos Deos, neq; idola, vt gentes, Ro. 1. Pręclarum hoc, propter leges & statuta Rom. Act. 16. 17. Tert. Contantur hoc exéplo, qui in religionis causa exspectandam putant summi magistratus authoritatem. Aliter Christus, Mat 22. Daniel & socij, Dan. 3.6. His adde Cornelium & Centurionem, de quo Luc.7.
units.tr: ¶ 2. His studies and manners: fearing God. Therefore he did not worship many gods, nor idols, as the Gentiles did (Rom. 1). This is remarkable, given the laws and statutes of Rome (Acts 16; 17; Tertullian). Those are refuted by this example who think that in matters of religion the authority of the supreme magistrate must be awaited. Christ acted otherwise (Matt. 22). Daniel and his companions (Dan. 3; 6). To these add Cornelius and the centurion of whom Luke 7 speaks.

units.la: ¶ 3. Animi pietatem factis refert.1. Fa-miliam instituit ad pietatem. Propriu pijs, quod suos volunt Dei obseruantes efle. Abraham, Gen. 18. Ita præcipitur Deut.6. Exod.13. Pfal.78. Et patribus imputari pec cata filiorum, Heli exemplum docet, 1. Samuel.2 3.4. Eadem ratio magistratuum.
units.tr: ¶ 3. He shows the piety of his mind by his deeds. 1. He ordered his household to piety. This is proper to the godly, that they want their own to be worshippers of God. Abraham (Gen. 18). So it is commanded in Deut. 6; Exod. 13; Ps. 78. And that the sins of the sons are imputed to the fathers, the example of Eli teaches (1 Sam. 2; 3; 4). The same reasoning applies to magistrates.

units.la: 2. Eleemosynas fecit populo, cui erat præ sectus. Fuit ergo non solum obseruantisi mus regulæ (Luc.3.) sed insuper benefacit omnibus.
units.tr: 2. He gave alms to the people over whom he was set. He therefore not only observed the rule (Luke 3), but moreover did good to all.

units.la: 3. Preces assiduæ, nimirum vt Deus ipsi reuelaret totam salutis rationem.
units.tr: 3. Constant prayers, namely that God would reveal to him the whole plan of salvation.

units.la: Arguunt ista mores militu nostri secu-li. In primis apparet, quales esse oporteat eos, qui volunt in vera salutis cognitione proficere. Arguitur nostra negligentia.
units.tr: These things rebuke the manners of our own age's soldiers. In the first place it appears what sort of people they ought to be who wish to make progress in the true knowledge of salvation. Our negligence is rebuked.

units.la: II. Vocationis initium. Mittitur ad eum Angelus clara luce, qui ingressus ipsum nomine compellat. Deus enim nobiscum perspicuè agit, non tenebras captat, vt Satan. Cornelius miles terretur. Infirmitatis argumentum & simul docet reue rentiá deberi Deo & verbo eius. Sic Saulus, Act. 9.
units.tr: II. The beginning of the calling. An angel is sent to him in clear light, who entering addresses him by name. For God deals with us plainly; he does not seek out darkness, as Satan does. Cornelius the soldier is terrified. This is a sign of weakness, and at the same time teaches that reverence is owed to God and to his word. So with Saul (Acts 9).

units.la: Loquitur ergo ei Angelus, & duo agit. ¶ 1. Solatur, dum Deo docet accepta fuisse, quæ hucusque fecerit: Eleemosynas & preces, &c.
units.tr: The angel therefore speaks to him and does two things. ¶ 1. He comforts him, while showing him by God's word that what he has done so far was accepted: the alms and prayers, etc.

units.la: Abutuntur his verbis Papistæ, vt probent opera præparationis, deinde meritum quoque operum. Sed errant: 1. Quia nisi Deus præueniat, nos neque precari, neque boni quid velle possumus, Zach.12. Isa.65.2. Cor.3. Philip.2.1. Cor.4. Cant.1. 2. Opera nihil merentur: quia non ex nobis fiunt: Quia imperfecta sunt, Isa.64. Lucæ 17. &c. Senssus ergo Deus qui hactenus principia ista decerit, dona sua auctorum, & se totum ipsi reuelare velle. Huc promissio pertinet, Mat.25.
units.tr: The Papists abuse these words to prove works of preparation, and then the merit of works also. But they err: 1. Because unless God goes before, we can neither pray nor desire anything good (Zech. 12; Isa. 65:2; 1 Cor. 3; Phil. 2; 1 Cor. 4; Song 1). 2. Works merit nothing, because they are not done from ourselves, and because they are imperfect (Isa. 64; Luke 17, etc.). The sense therefore is that God, who has hitherto begun these things, wishes to accept his own gifts and to reveal himself wholly to him. The promise pertains to this (Matt. 25).

units.la: ¶ 2. Docet, quid faciat: vt aceerfat Petrum, Magna Dei bonitas, qui Petrum vult ad illum abire. Solet enim ille nos quære re. Sic cum Adamo egit, Ge.3. Abrahamo, Gen.12. Sic Christus de se, Luc.15. Ioh.10.
units.tr: ¶ 2. He teaches what he should do: that he send for Peter. Great is God's goodness, who wills that Peter go to him. For he is accustomed to seek us. So he dealt with Adam (Gen. 3), with Abraham (Gen. 12). So Christ speaks of himself (Luke 15; John 10).

units.la: In primis obseruandum commendari hic verbi ministerium. Poterat Angelus praedicare Cornelio: sed iubet Petrum ac cerfere.Sic supra factum, Act.8.9. Est ergo perpetuum,quod habetur, Rom.10. 2. Cor 5 Impij, qui verbi praedicationem asparnantur & fastidiunt. Poenas dignas ferunt dum ab impostoribus seducuntur. Oremus.
units.tr: In the first place it must be observed that the ministry of the Word is commended here. The angel could have preached to Cornelius, but he orders him to send for Peter. So it was done above (Acts 8; 9). What is found in Rom. 10 is therefore perpetual. 2 Cor. 5. Those unbelievers who spurn and despise the preaching of the Word bring upon themselves deserved punishments, when they are seduced by impostors. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXV.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXXV.

units.la: 3 Cornelius vidit Angelum Dei introeuntē, & dicentē ipsi, Corneli.
units.tr: 3 Cornelius saw an angel of God coming in and saying to him, Cornelius.

units.la: 4 At ille intentis oculis in eum, & expaue factus, dixit: Quid est Domine? Dixit autem ei, Preces tuae & eleemosynae tuae ascenderunt in memoriam coram Deo.
units.tr: 4 And he, fixing his eyes on him and being terrified, said: What is it, Lord? And he said to him, Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial before God.

units.la: 5 Nunc igitur mitte aliquos Joppen, & accerse Simonem qui cognominatur Petrus.
units.tr: 5 Now therefore send men to Joppa and summon Simon, who is surnamed Peter.

units.la: 6 Hic diuersatur apud Simonem quendam coriarium, cui est domus ad mare: hic dicet tibi quid te oporteat facere.
units.tr: 6 He is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea; he will tell you what you ought to do.

units.la: 7 Vt autem discessit Angelus qui loquebatur Cornelio, vocauit duos ex famulis suis, & militem pium ex iis qui cum ipso assidui erant.
units.tr: 7 And when the angel who spoke to Cornelius had departed, he called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among those who were constantly with him.

units.la: 8 Et cum eis expositiffet omnia, misit eos Ioppen.
units.tr: 8 And when he had explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

units.la: ETsi Christus exludæis homo natus est,& secundum veteres promissiones fehis primis perverbum & miracula manifestarit,idem tamen ad gentes quoq; alias pertinet. Docent hoc promissiones, Gen.22.26.28.49. Prophetæ, Isa.2.49.60. Psal.2.72.&c.Et ipse in Euangelio,Matt.8. Ioh.10.Ideoq; iam abituruis iubet Euangelium vbiq; prædicare,Mar.16.Act.1. Quia autem res ista Iudæis iniqua,& quoad gentes impossibilis videbatur,ita eam inchoa-ri oportuit, vt omnibus constaret,hoc Dei decretum & opus esse.Factum hoc in Cornelio cuius historiam hoc sapit.Lucas narrat. Summa,Quòd Cornelius à Deo monitus Petrum accersiuerit, vicisim hic visione cœlesti excitatus ad illum iuerit prædicatum,& conuersum ad fidem baptizârit,nulla præcedente Legis ceremonia.Et hæc ratio postea quoq; fuit obseruanda in aliis.Cœpit à Cornelij descriptione. Sequitur quid cum eo Deus,&c.
units.tr: Although Christ was born a man of the Jews, and according to the old promises manifested himself first to them by the word and by miracles, he nevertheless also belongs to other nations. The promises teach this: Gen. 22.26.28.49; the prophets, Isa. 2.49.60; Ps. 2.72, etc. And he himself in the Gospel, Matt. 8; John 10. Therefore, about to depart, he bids the Gospel be preached everywhere, Mark 16; Acts 1. But because this matter seemed unjust to the Jews and impossible as regards the Gentiles, it had to be begun in such a way that it would be plain to all that this was God's decree and work. This happened in Cornelius, whose history Luke narrates, and which bears this out. The sum is this: Cornelius, warned by God, summoned Peter; in turn, roused here by a heavenly vision, Peter went to him to preach, and having been converted to the faith, he baptized him, with no preceding ceremony of the Law. And this method was afterwards to be observed in other cases as well. The account begins with the description of Cornelius. What God did with him follows, etc.

units.la: I. Mittit Angelum qui clara luce ad eum ingressus nomine cõpellat.Solet Deus perspicuè nobiscum agere,&c.Et NOTA. ¶ 1. Deum ministris suis Angelis vti erga nos quoq; in procuranda salute,cum animarum tum corporum,Heb.1.Psal.34.
units.tr: I. He sends an angel who enters to him in clear light and addresses him by name. God is accustomed to deal with us plainly, etc. And NOTE: ¶ 1. God uses his ministers, the angels, also toward us in procuring salvation, both of souls and of bodies, Heb. 1; Ps. 34.

units.la: 91. Exempla sunt pasim in veteri & nouo Testamento. Sed & ipsi Angeli in eo sunt alacres, vt qui nostra salute gaudent, Luc. 15. q 2. Officij nostri esse, vt hinc consola- tionem petamus in periculis, vt Helisæus, 2. Reg. 6. Et simul studeamus ipsi quoque saluti, Phil. 2. Turpe, si Angelis hanc quæ- rentibus nos eam negligamus. Arguit hoc nostri seculi mores, quando pleriq; occa- siones malas quærunt.
units.tr: 2. Examples are everywhere in the Old and New Testaments. But the angels themselves are eager in this, as those who rejoice in our salvation, Luke 15. It is our duty to seek comfort from this in dangers, as Elisha did, 2 Kings 6; and at the same time to strive for our own salvation, Phil. 2. It is shameful, if we neglect it while the angels seek it for us. The manners of our age show this, when most people seek out evil opportunities.

units.la: II. Cornelius etsi miles sit, terretur. Argumentu humanæ infirmitatis quæ in ele ctis quoque locum habet, Iud. 13. Dan. 10. Mat. 17. Apo. 1. &c. Arguuntur impostores qui visionibus gloriantur. q Officij autem admonet quæstio Cornelij: Quid est Domine? Sic Petrus, Supra 9. Ita nos, quando Deus se nobis exhibet præsentem. Id vero facit per Verbum. Tangamur ergo huius reuerētia, & quæramus sedulo de Dei voluntate. Vide quales censeri debeant, qui Verbum contemnunt, Luc. 10.
units.tr: II. Cornelius, although a soldier, is terrified. This is an argument of human weakness, which has its place even among the elect, Judg. 13; Dan. 10; Matt. 17; Rev. 1, etc. Impostors who boast of visions are refuted. The question of Cornelius, however, reminds us of our duty: What is it, Lord? So Peter, above, chapter 9. So we too, when God shows himself present to us. He does this through the Word. Let us then be moved by reverence for it, and let us diligently inquire into the will of God. See what sort of people must be judged to be those who despise the Word, Luke 10.

units.la: III. Angeli oratio duabus partibus constans. 1. Solatur, dum docet, Deo fuisse accepta quæ hucusque fecerit: Preces tuæ & eleemosynæ, &c. Non debet hoc accipi, quasi meritum nostrorum operum astruant. Prius enim dicitur, Deum timuisse. Hic primo preces nominantur. Atqui neutrum ex nobis possumus. Homo Deum non agnoscit, 1.Cor.2. Ergo eundem neq; timere, neq; invocare potest, Rom. 10. Vnde sequitur, Cornelium fuisse fide generali praeditum, quae fecit, ut verum Deum timeret & invocaret. Atqui fides Dei donum est, Eph.2. Haec item eleemosynam peperit, & alia opera bona. Defuit solum, quod nesciret, quis verus ille Mediator, accedebant controversiae. Ideo orauit, &c. ¶ Idem nos faciamus. Profitemur Dei cognitionem. Hunc timeamus, & ut se plenius reuelet, oremus. Ita dabuntur plura, Matth.25. At hodie qui Cornelio abutuntur, fibijpsis fidunt.
units.tr: III. The angel's speech consists of two parts. 1. He comforts, by teaching that what he has done so far has been accepted by God: Your prayers and your alms, etc. This should not be taken as if they were asserting the merit of our works. For it is said first that he feared God; here the prayers are mentioned first. Yet we can do neither of these of ourselves. Man does not know God, 1 Cor. 2. Therefore he can neither fear nor call upon him, Rom. 10. Hence it follows that Cornelius was endowed with a general faith, which made him fear and call upon the true God. Yet faith is a gift of God, Eph. 2. This likewise produced alms and other good works. Only what he did not know was lacking: who the true Mediator was; controversies were pressing in. Therefore he prayed, etc. ¶ Let us do the same. We profess the knowledge of God. Let us fear him, and pray that he may reveal himself more fully. Thus more will be given, Matt. 25. But today those who abuse Cornelius trust in themselves.

units.la: II. Docet, quid faciat. Accerse Petrum. Is tibi loquetur, &c.
units.tr: II. He teaches what he should do. Send for Peter. He will speak to you, etc.

units.la: Ergo adhuc Christo opus fuit, & non poterat fine hoc seruari Cornel. Confirmatur illud, Luc.17. Ioh.4.
units.tr: Therefore Christ was still needed, and Cornelius could not be saved without him. This is confirmed by Luke 17; John 4.

units.la: Interim NOT. ¶1. Bonitatem Dei. Poterat Cornelius mandare, ut ipse iret, quod aequum fuisset. Sed vult Petro labore m imponere. Ita semper ille quaerit nos. Sic Adamum, Gen.3. Abraham, Gen.12. Israelitas, Exod.3. Ezech.34. Gentes, Isaiae 65. Act.16. Christus eiusmodi pastor, Is.40. Ioh.10. Luc.15. Hodie idem fit, quando ille nobis mittit ministros, & gratis offert Verbum, &c. Sed plerique sunt ingrati.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE: ¶1. The goodness of God. Cornelius could have been ordered to go himself, which would have been fair. But he wishes to lay the labour on Peter. So he always seeks us: thus Adam, Gen. 3; Abraham, Gen. 12; the Israelites, Exod. 3; Ezek. 34; the Gentiles, Isa. 65; Acts 16. Christ is such a shepherd, Isa. 40; John 10; Luke 15. Today the same happens, when he sends us ministers and freely offers the Word, etc. But most are ungrateful.

units.la: ¶2. Commendatur hîc Verbi ministerium. poterat Angelus prædicare Cornelio sed vult Petrum audiat. Sic supra. 8. & 9. Infra 16. Ita enim constituit Deus, noftrę infirmitatis causa, Rom. 1 oErrant, qui ordine Dei neglecto quæsrunt revelationes, &c. Vide Luc. 16.
units.tr: ¶2. The ministry of the Word is commended here. The angel could have preached to Cornelius, but he wills that Peter be heard. So above, chapters 8 and 9; below, 16. For God has so ordained, because of our weakness, Rom. 1. Those err who, neglecting the order of God, seek revelations, etc. See Luke 16.

units.la: IV. Cornelius absque mora obtemperat, &c. Atqui multa poterant impedire. Per se res erat noua & plena periculi proapter leges & statuta Romanorum. Sciebat item homines istos omnibus esse exosos. 1. Cor. 4. Item vir tantus mittitur ad cerdonis officinam. Quis ex ea sperasset aeter næ salutis doctorem? Sed omnia vincit fides. Heb. 11. Imitemur, &c. Simul No T. ¶ Fructum rectæ institutæ familiæ. Habet nunc fidos seruos, quibus tuto potest rem tantam committere. Sic Abraham, Gen. 24. Hodie Reges promissionibus fere a suis produntur. Sed ita luunt poenas suæ impietatis, qui scelerum ministris delectantur, nec suos sinunt Dei fideles esse. Cui ergo fideles essent? Vidit hoc Constantius, Constantini Magni pater. Econtra Neronem vide, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: IV. Cornelius obeys without delay, etc. Yet many things could have hindered him. In itself the matter was new and full of danger, on account of the laws and statutes of the Romans. He also knew that these men were hated by everyone, 1 Cor. 4. Likewise, a man so great is sent to a cobbler's workshop. Who would have expected a teacher of eternal salvation from such a place? But faith overcomes all things, Heb. 11. Let us imitate, etc. At the same time NOTE: ¶ The fruit of a well-ordered household. He now has faithful servants, to whom he can safely entrust so great a matter. So Abraham, Gen. 24. Today kings are almost always betrayed by their own people through promises. But they pay the penalty for their impiety who delight in ministers of crimes and do not allow their own subjects to be faithful to God. To whom then would they be faithful? Constantius, father of Constantine the Great, saw this. On the contrary, see Nero, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXXVI.

units.la: 9 Postridie vero illis iter facientibus & appropinquantibus vrbi ascendit Petrus supra domum vt precaretur circa horam sextam.
units.tr: 9 On the next day, as they were on their journey and drawing near the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour.

units.la: 10 Factum est autem vt valde esuriret, voluitque capere cibum: paratibus autem illis incidit in eum mentis excessus.
units.tr: 10 And it happened that he became very hungry and wanted to eat. While the food was being prepared, he fell into a trance.

units.la: 11 Considexitque cœlum apertum, ac descendens ad se vas quoddam vt linteum magnum quatuor extremis devinctum, quod demitebatur in terram.
units.tr: 11 He saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel coming down to him, like a great linen sheet bound at its four corners, which was let down to the earth.

units.la: 12 In quo erant quadrupedia terræ & ferae ac reptilia & volucres cœli,
units.tr: 12 In it were all kinds of four-footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and birds of the air.

units.la: 13 Et extitit vox ad eum, Surge Petre, macta & vescere.
units.tr: 13 And a voice came to him: Rise, Peter, kill and eat.

units.la: 14 Ait autem Petrus, &c. Ad verf. vsque 17.
units.tr: 14 But Peter said, etc. As far as verse 17.

units.la: VT Deus in Iudæorum electione singulari misericordia vsus est, quam Scriptura passim prædicat: Ita quando his repudiatis gentes adoptauit, iræ & iustitiæ exemplū peculiareædidit, ex quo generalis doctrina peti debet, vt qui ex gentibus oriundi sumus, nobis caueamus. Vide Romanor. 11. Et huc facit, quod in Cornelio, qui primus gentium vocatus est, exemplum proponitur, quo docemur quid eos deceat, qui in Christo seruari voluntate, Fuit is ethnicus, sed seruauit naturales de Deo notitias, quem timuit, inuocauit, &c. Ab Angelis monitus mox paret, &c. Ita nos.
units.tr: As God in His singular mercy dealt with the election of the Jews, which Scripture everywhere proclaims, so, when He rejected them and adopted the Gentiles, He gave a notable example of His wrath and justice. From this a general teaching should be drawn: that we who have sprung from the Gentiles should take care for ourselves. See Romans 11. To this purpose also is the example set before us in Cornelius, who was the first of the Gentiles to be called. From it we are taught what becomes those who wish to be saved in Christ. He was a heathen, but he kept the natural knowledge of God; he feared Him and called upon Him, etc. Warned by an angel, he at once obeys, etc. So far we.

units.la: Caeterum quia vocatio gentium res erat insolens, quam ne Apostoli quidem initio intelligebant, Deus interea Petrum quoque edocet, ne legatos Cornelij reijce ret. Idem ergo fit hic, quod Supra 9. Cap. inter Paulum & Ananiam. Infra item cap. 13. 16. Hodie quoque similia vidimus. Sed singula videamus.
units.tr: But since the calling of the Gentiles was an unfamiliar matter, which even the Apostles did not at first understand, God in the meantime also instructs Peter, so that he should not reject the envoys of Cornelius. So the same thing happens here as in chapter 9 above, between Paul and Ananias; likewise below, in chapters 13 and 16. We have seen similar things today too. But let us look at the particulars.

units.la: I. Petrus tunc, cum legati appropinquant urbi, sub meridiem ieiunus adhuc, dum paratur prandium, ascendit supra tectum ad precandum. Fuerunt enim certae horae precum, Dan. 6. Aetor. 3. Etsi enim hae non astringi debeant superstitiose ad certum tempus, tamen propter occupationes alias opus est ordine, &c. Ita etiam loco, remoto a turbis, Matth. 6. Interim nihil hoc patrocinatur hypocritis, qui ad pulsum campanae astringunt preces, & in publico precantur: non Apostolorum, sed Pharisaeorum similes, Matt. 6.
units.tr: I. Peter then, when the messengers were approaching the city, about noon and still fasting, while the dinner was being prepared, went up onto the roof to pray. For there were set hours of prayer, Dan. 6. Acts 3. Yet these need not be bound superstitiously to a fixed time; nevertheless, because of other occupations there is need of order, etc. So too with the place, away from crowds, Matth. 6. Still, this lends no support to hypocrites, who tie their prayers to the ringing of a bell and pray in public: they are like the Pharisees, not like the Apostles, Matt. 6.

units.la: 2. Excessus mentis. Indicatur hoc, ne quis sensibus aliquid tribuat, qui in diu-nis nihil possunt, 1. Cor. 2. Itaque mentem
units.tr: 2. Ecstasy of mind. This is indicated so that no one should attribute anything to the senses, which can do nothing in divine things, 1. Cor. 2. Therefore the mind

units.la: supra mundum eleuari oportet: quod ita fit, vt Sancti quoque modum ignorent, 2.Cor. 12. Act.22. Apo.1.In praesenti idem patitur Petrus, vt sciret hanc peculiarem Dei reuelationem esse.
units.tr: must be raised above the world; this happens so that even the saints do not know the manner of it (2 Cor. 12; Acts 22; Rev. 1). In the present case Peter suffers the same thing, so that he might know this to be a special revelation of God.

units.la: 3. Visio obijcitur. Videt coelos aperiri, demitti linteum ingens, alligatum a quatuor partibus. Insunt omnis generis animalia, immunda quoque, secundum legem, de quibus Leuit.11.Deut.14. Accedit vox, quae iubet Petrum mactare & edere, &c. ¶ Scopus visionis, sublatu esse discrimen, quod hactenus, quoad Legis ceremonias, fuerit inter Iudaeos & gentes (Eph.2.) & proinde nihil obstare, quo minus gentes quoque recipiantur in Ecclesiae societatem.Id vero mirifice figuratur. Petrus esuriebat Christi gloriam & hominum salutem.Iudaei reluctabantur.Gentes videbantur indigni: & nimirum occurrebant Christi verba,Matt.10.15.Et quod dixerat abiturus(Matth.28.Actor.1.Mar.16.) vidabatur intelligi debere de gentibus circumcidendis,Actor.15.Haerebat ergo dubius, ex quibus deberet colligi Ecclesia.
units.tr: 3. The vision is set before him. He sees the heavens opened and a great sheet let down, tied at four corners, containing animals of every kind, including the unclean ones forbidden by the law (Lev. 11; Deut. 14). A voice comes, bidding Peter to kill and eat, etc. The aim of the vision is that the distinction which until then existed between Jews and Gentiles in respect of the ceremonies of the Law has been removed (Eph. 2), and that therefore nothing stands in the way of the Gentiles also being received into fellowship with the Church. This is wonderfully prefigured. Peter hungered for the glory of Christ and the salvation of men. The Jews resisted, and the Gentiles seemed unworthy. And indeed the words of Christ came to mind (Matt. 10:15), and what he had said at his departure (Matt. 28; Acts 1; Mark 16) seemed to have to be understood of the Gentiles who were to be circumcised (Acts 15). He was therefore uncertain from what people the Church ought to be gathered.

units.la: Docetur ergo: ¶ Quae fit huius conditio: Ex coelo originem habet, licet in terris versetur.Sic Ierusalem, Apo.21. Ratio, quia Dei filios e supernis renasci oportet, Ioh.1.3 1.Pet.1. Eadem quia in mundo colligitur, adiunguntfe multi etiam immundi, vt in sagenæ parabola docemur (Matt. 13.) & zizania sua in Domini agrum afpergitSatan.Hic Petrus nó expellere,sed ma ctare iubetur: Ita ministri non eijcere debent,sed mactare gladio Spiritus, vt Deo fiant grata victima, &c.Rom.15. Obseruemus hoc propter Anabap.qui nisi immundos eijciamus,totas Ecclesias damnant.
units.tr: Therefore it is taught: such is the condition of the Church. It has its origin in heaven, although it dwells on earth. So also the new Jerusalem (Rev. 21). The reason is that the sons of God must be born again from above (John 3; 1 Pet. 1). Because the Church is gathered in the world, many unclean people also join themselves to it, as we are taught in the parable of the net (Matt. 13), and Satan scatters his tares in the Lord's field. Here Peter is not ordered to expel but to slaughter: so ministers ought not to cast out, but to slay with the sword of the Spirit, so that they become a sacrifice acceptable to God (Rom. 15). We should observe this on account of the Anabaptists, who condemn whole churches unless we cast out the unclean.

units.la: 4.Petrus renuit, & Legem respicit.Sed audiuit: Quæ Deus mundauit,&c. Id vero de gentibus dici, exsequentibus patet. Idem ergo sibi dictum putent ministri omnes,ne quem temere excludant, qui fortassis coram Deo mundus censetur,id est, ex electorum numero est. Qui enim hi sint, scire nos non possumus. Interim arguuntur hic, quicunque prohibent quæ Deus concessit. 1.Cibos omnes Deus mundauit,Matt.15.1.Cor.9.1.Tim.4. Minimè ergo audiendi, qui discrimina ciborum constituunt.1.Col. 1.Tim 4. Rom.14. Exemplum Spiridonis. 2. Coniugium licitum & sanctum omnibus,Gen.2.1.Cor.7.Heb. 13. Audacia ergo intolerabilis fuerit, illud damnare cum Syricio,qui abusus est loco Roman.8.
units.tr: 4. Peter refused and held to the Law. But he heard: "What God has cleansed, etc." That this was said of the Gentiles is clear from those who carried it out. Therefore all ministers should take it as said to themselves as well, so that they do not rashly exclude anyone who perhaps is counted clean before God, that is, belongs to the number of the elect. For who these are we cannot know. Meanwhile, here are rebuked all who forbid what God has permitted. (1) God has cleansed all foods (Matt. 15.; 1.Cor.9.; 1.Tim.4.). Least of all, then, are they to be heard who draw distinctions among foods (1.Col. 1.; 1.Tim 4.; Rom.14.). Example of Spyridon. (2) Marriage is lawful and holy for all (Gen.2.; 1.Cor.7.; Heb. 13.). Therefore it would be an intolerable audacity to condemn it with Siricius, who abused the passage of Rom.8.

units.la: ¶ Magistratus a Deo, &c. Roman.13.
units.tr: ¶ The magistrates are from God, etc. Rom. 13.

units.la: Psalm.113.72. Impij,qui negant,&c.
units.tr: Psalm.113.72. The wicked, who deny, &c.

units.la: 5.Tertiò hæc fiunt, vt minus dubitaret Petrus, & tandé vas retrahitur in cœlum, vt sciret huius negotij tractationem cœlestem, & gentibus hucusque immundis, nunc in cœlis locum esse.Et hoc Petrus intellexit. Interim habet hoc consolationem dulcissimam. Dum Ecclesia in terris agit, videtur magna esse in illa confusio variorum animalium, Isa.11.1.Reg.19. Sed tamen ex cœlis dependet eius gubernatio, quá Deus sua manu regit.Et erit tempus, quando ad se illam Christus recipiet. Vide Ioh.14.17.Phil.3.1.Thess.4.Heb.9.Præbeant modò singuli se mactandos gladio spiritus, & eodem ipsimet carnem mortificent,Col.3.Rom.6.12.&c.Oremus.
units.tr: 5. Thirdly, these things happen so that Peter might doubt less. Finally the vessel is drawn back up into heaven, so that he might know that the handling of this business is heavenly, and that there is now a place in heaven for the Gentiles, who until now were unclean. Peter understood this. Meanwhile, this brings the sweetest consolation. While the Church acts on earth, there seems to be great confusion in it, with various animals, Isa.11.1.Reg.19. Yet its governance depends on heaven, and God rules it with his own hand. And there will be a time when Christ will receive it to himself. See Ioh.14.17.Phil.3.1.Thess.4.Heb.9. Let each one now allow himself to be put to death by the sword of the Spirit, and let him mortify the flesh by that same Spirit, Col.3.Rom.6.12.&c. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXVII.
units.tr: HOMILIA LXXXVII.

units.la: 17 Cum autem apud se ambigeret Petrus quod nam esset visum illud quod viderat, ecce, viri qui missi erant a Cornelio, per contati de domo Simonis, supervenerunt ad vestibulum.
units.tr: 17 While Peter was still wondering to himself what the vision he had seen might mean, behold, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, having asked for the house of Simon, arrived at the gate.

units.la: 18 Et evocato quoquam percontati sunt, an Simon, qui cognominatur Petrus, illic diuersaretur.
units.tr: 18 And calling out, they asked whether Simon, who was surnamed Peter, was staying there.

units.la: 19 Petro vero cogitante de visione, dixit ei spiritus, Ecce tres viri quæ runt te. 20 Surgens itaque descende, et nihil ambigens proficisceré cum eis: nam ego eos misi.
units.tr: 19 While Peter was thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him, Behold, three men are seeking you. 20 Arise therefore and go down, and without any doubt go with them, for I have sent them.

units.la: INter opera Dei quibus suam bonitatem daclarauit, feré præcipuum est Vocatio gentium. Patebit hoc, si quales fuerint, expendas: Alieni a republica Israelitica sine Deo & Christo, idololatriæ, scelerum mancipia & filii iræ, Eph. 2. Col. 1. 2. Rom. 1. Quando igitur hos Deus vocauit, perinde hoc fuit, ac si quis heredem capitalem adoptet, &c. Quia autem Iudæis legali iustitia inflatis iniquum videbatur, tales adoptari, sæpe de eo fuerunt præmoniti & ipse Christus prædixerat, Matth. 8. 11. Io. 10. 12. Et ne Apostoli dubitarent, tale initium dedit, ut omnibus constet, hoc omne ex sua prouidentia factum fuisse. Deligitur vir militaris Cornelius. Hunc excitat per Angelum. Deinde Petrum visione instruit, &c. Sequitur negotij progressus.
units.tr: AMONG the works of God by which he has displayed his goodness, the calling of the Gentiles is almost the chief. This will be clear if you consider what kind of people they were: aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, without God and Christ, worshippers of idols, slaves of sins and children of wrath (Eph. 2; Col. 1, 2; Rom. 1). When God called such people, it was just as if someone adopted a chief heir, etc. Since this seemed unjust to the Jews, who were puffed up with legal righteousness, they were often forewarned about it, and Christ himself had foretold it (Matt. 8:11; John 10:12). And so that the Apostles would not be in doubt, he made such a beginning that everyone might agree that all this had come about through his providence. A military man, Cornelius, is chosen. He stirs him up through an angel. Then he instructs Peter by a vision, etc. There follows the progress of the matter.

units.la: I. Petrus dubius hæret, quid hæc uisio portendat. Sciebat procul dubio mysteri um subesse, sed non poterat intelligere. Non tamen eludit, sed cogitat diligenter.
units.tr: Peter hesitates in doubt about what this vision portends. Without doubt he knew that some mystery lay beneath it, but he could not understand it. Yet he does not brush it aside; he thinks about it carefully.

units.la: NOT. Tarditatem ingenij humani in percipiendis Dei misterijs. Petrus hunc in gentij.
units.tr: NOTE. The slowness of the human mind in grasping the mysteries of God, as Peter shows in this matter of the Gentiles.

units.la: tantus Christi discipulus, Matth.17.16.Iohan.6.20.21. &c. Non intelligit hoc, de quo habebat typos & promissiones, Luc.5.Ergo omnino spiritu doctore opus est, 1.Cor.2.Ioh.6.Isa.54. Matth.11.16. Huius memores, non scrutemur curiosius, quae Deus sibi reseruauit, Act.1. Prou.25.Neq; etiam nostro ingenio indnlgeamus, vt faciamus quod nobis bonum videtur, sed Dei voluntatem quaeramus in verbo suo, Num.15.Deut.12.28.Precemur. Ita non fructrabimur, Matt.7.
units.tr: Although he was so great a disciple of Christ (Matt. 17.16; John 6.20-21, etc.), he does not understand this, of which he had types and promises (Luke 5). Therefore we certainly need the Spirit as teacher (1 Cor. 2; John 6; Isa. 54; Matt. 11.16). Mindful of this, let us not inquire too curiously into what God has reserved to himself (Acts 1; Prov. 25). Nor let us indulge our own wit, so as to do what seems good to us, but let us seek the will of God in his word (Num. 15; Deut. 12.28). Let us pray, so that we will not be frustrated (Matt. 7).

units.la: II.Legati eodem tempore articulo sunt ad ostium, & quaerunt, &c.NOT. §1. Pro uidentiam Dei, omnia rerum momenta gubernantem. Exempla similia, Gen.24. Exod.2,1.Sam 9.10.Item Luc.22.&c. Haec prophani fortuita dicunt.At Scriptura ad Deum omnia referre docet, Vide Prou. 16. Vsus, vt occasiones bene agendi amplectamur, vt diuinitus oblatas, nec cunctemur. Deinde in aduersis ex eo petamus consolationem, Matth 6.10.
units.tr: II. At the same time the messengers stand at the door and ask, etc. NOTE §1. God's providence, which governs all the moments of things. Similar examples are Gen. 24; Exod. 2.1; 1 Sam. 9-10, and likewise Luke 22, etc. Profane people call these things chance. But Scripture teaches us to refer all things to God (see Prov. 16). The use of this: let us seize the opportunities for doing good when they are offered to us by God, and not hesitate. Then in adversity let us seek consolation from this, (Matt. 6.10).

units.la: §2.Modestiam istorum. Erant Romani milites, & in praesidio eius regionis. Non tamen irrumpunt in aedes temere, sed euocant aliquem, & quaerunt. Sciebant enim Iudaeos gentium conuersatione horrere, &c. Exemplum disciplinae militaris, & eius quod Baptista admonuit, Lucæ 3. Confert cum his nostri seculi milites, qui licenter omnia agunt, vt qui in præsidijs sunt, nihil ab hostibus differant. Et tamen hæc schola putatur, in quam ablegari debeant iuniores, & qui sua concoxerunt. Ita vero pœnas & exitium nobis accersemus, si aliis sceleribus addatur sanguis, &c. Deuter. 27. Hab. 2. Isa. 33. Apo. 13. Matthæi 7. &c.
units.tr: §2. Their modesty. They were Roman soldiers, and they were stationed in that region as a garrison. Yet they do not rush rashly into the house, but call someone out and ask. For they knew that the Jews shrink from contact with the Gentiles, etc. This is an example of military discipline, and of what the Baptist admonished in Luke 3. Compare the soldiers of our own age, who act licentiously in everything, as if those who are in garrisons differ in no way from the enemy. And yet this is thought to be the school to which younger men ought to be sent, and to which those who have already worked through their own vices should go. Thus we indeed bring punishments and ruin upon ourselves, if blood is added to other crimes, etc. Deut. 27. Hab. 2. Isa. 33. Rev. 13. Matt. 7. etc.

units.la: III. Petrum adhuc cogitantem Spiritus admonet, & iubet, vt cum illis iter ingrediatur absque hesitatione.
units.tr: III. The Spirit admonishes Peter, while he is still deliberating, and bids him go with them on the journey without hesitation.

units.la: Nec aliam rationem adducit, quàm Ego misi eos, &c. Et Petrus mox obtemperat. Atqui de precibus interruptis queri poterat, & causari, quòd homines ignoti sint, &c. Sed sufficit ei mandatum Domini. NOT. ¶ Deo nos simpliciter debere obedire, sepositis omnibus rationibus nostris, quando mandatum Dei habemus. Vt enim in nos ius habet Deus, ita fidei proprium est obedire, 2. Cor. 10. Rom. 1. 16. Admonet de hoc Oratio Dominica, Matth. 6. Ita semper fecerunt Sancti. Abraham, Gen. 12. 22. Hebræorum 11. Idem ergo nobisquoque sufficiat in omnibus actionibus &c. Oremus.
units.tr: He brings forward no other reason than "I have sent them," etc. And Peter at once obeys. Yet he could have complained about the prayers that had been interrupted, and objected that the men are unknown, etc. But the Lord's command is enough for him. NOTE: We ought simply to obey God, setting aside all our own reasons, whenever we have the command of God. For just as God has right over us, so it is proper to faith to obey, 2 Cor. 10, Rom. 1.16. The Lord's Prayer admonishes us of this, Matt. 6. The saints have always done so: Abraham, Gen. 12, 22, Hebrews 11. Let this therefore suffice for us also in all our actions, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY 88.

units.la: 21 Descendens ergo Petrus ad viros,qui ad ipsum missi fuerunt à Cornelio,dixit,Ecce,Ego is sum quem quaeritis: quae causa est propter quam adestis?
units.tr: 21 So Peter went down to the men who had been sent to him from Cornelius and said: "Behold, I am the one you are looking for. What is the reason you have come?"

units.la: 22 Ipsi vero dixerunt, Cornelius centurio,vir iustus & timens Deum,& te stimonio ornatus totius gentis Iudaeorum, diuinitus admonitus est ab Angelo sancto, vt accerseret te domum suam, & abs te quaedam audiret.
units.tr: 22 They said, "Cornelius the centurion, a righteous man who fears God and is well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews, was divinely warned by a holy angel to send for you to his house and to hear words from you."

units.la: 23 Introduxit ergo eos accepit hospitio. Sequenti vero die Petrus abiit cum eis, & quidam ex fratribus Ioppen sibus comitatiti sunt eum.
units.tr: 23 So Peter invited them in and received them as guests. The next day he went off with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went with him.

units.la: 24 Postridie vero introierunt Caesaream: Cornelius autem exspectabat eos,conuocatis cognatis suis & necessarijs amicis.
units.tr: 24 On the following day they entered Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends.

units.la: 25 Vt autem factum est vt introiret Petrus,occurrens ei Cornelius,& accidens ad eius pedes, adorauit.
