units.tr: 25 When Peter came in, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet and worshipped him.

units.la: 26 Petrus vero erexit eum, dicens: Surge:& ego ipse,homo sum.
units.tr: 26 But Peter raised him up, saying, "Stand up; I myself am also only a man."

units.la: Toto hoc libr. nullius conuersio tam diligenter & prolixè describitur, quàm Cornelij Centurionis. Causa est, quòd hic primus fuit, qui ex gentibus à Iudæorú cultu prorsus alienis ad Ghristum conuersus est. Quia enim Iudæi exfœdere (Gen.17.22.26.28.) promissionem & Christum sibi solis vendicabant, ij quoq; qui ad fidem conuertebantur, gentes adhuc fastidiebant,neque admittebant, nisi circumciderentur,Actor.15.Oportuit ergo diligenter demonstrari, Christum non minus ad gentes pertinere: vt & illi odium vetus deponerent, & hi in fide confirmarentur.Id factum in hac historia,quando Angelus ad Cornelium mittitur, qui iubet accersere Petrum, & hic pervifionem docetur,iam adesse tempus, quando discrimen Iudæorum & gentium sublatum sit, ideoque Euangelium gentibus etiam debere prædicari. Et hoc sensu visio ne exponit Spiritus S. qui illo adhuc hæsitante, cum Cornelij legati adessent,illum descendere & cum eis abire iubet. Se quitur vt Petrus obedierit.
units.tr: In this whole book no conversion is described so carefully and at such length as that of Cornelius the centurion. The reason is that he was the first of the Gentiles who was converted to Christ, a people entirely alien to the worship of the Jews. For since the Jews claimed the promise of the covenant (Gen. 17. 22. 26. 28.) and Christ for themselves alone, they despised the Gentiles even when these were converted to the faith, and would not admit them unless they were circumcised (Acts 15). It was therefore necessary to demonstrate carefully that Christ pertains no less to the Gentiles, so that the Jews might put aside their old hatred and the Gentiles might be confirmed in the faith. This was done in this history, when an angel is sent to Cornelius, who orders him to summon Peter, and Peter is taught by a vision that the time has now come when the distinction between Jews and Gentiles has been removed, and that therefore the gospel must also be preached to the Gentiles. And in this sense the Holy Spirit explains the vision, who, while Peter was still hesitating, when Cornelius's envoys were present, bids him go down and leave with them. It follows that Peter obeyed.

units.la: I.Descendit,amicè compellat,se cogno scendum præbet,quærit quid velint, hospitio excipit. No T.¶1.Facilitatem, qua Christum imitatur. Hic enim se omnibus cognoscendum præbuit, & adse omnes inuitauit, Matthæi 9 11. Iohan. 5. 6. 7. 8. &c. Idem neminem vnquam reiecit a se, Iohannis 6. Vide Iohan.3.4 Lucæ 7. 19.
units.tr: I. He goes down, addresses them in a friendly way, offers himself to be known, asks what they want, and receives them as guests. NOTE. 1. The affability by which he imitates Christ. For Christ showed himself to be known by all and invited all to himself (Matt. 9. 11; John 5. 6. 7. 8. etc.). Likewise he never rejected anyone who came to him (John 6). See John 3. 4; Luke 7. 19.

units.la: Petrus mandato Domini sui temperat.
units.tr: Peter moderates himself according to the command of his Lord.

units.la: Matth.9.Luc.23. Ita debent omnes mini-stri affecti esse, adeoque se omnibus ac-commodare, 1.Cor.9. Arguuntur, qui vt magni videantur, omnibus se difficiles præbent. ¶ 2.Hospitalitas erga peregri-nos commendatur. Præcipit hanc Deus passim. Quia enim afflictorum Deus est, peregrinos maximè curat, Deut.22. If.58. Matth.25.Hebr.13. Et constat sanctissimos, quosque hospitalitatis fuisse studiosiss. Vide Genef.18.19. Et Petrus in præsenti etsi ipse peregrinaretur. Imitentur oth-nes, imprimis ministri, 1.Tim.4. Excitet nos exemplum maiorum. Imò Deum no-bis ideo dare, vt pace & otio fruamur.
units.tr: (Matt. 9; Luke 23.) All ministers ought to be disposed in this way, and so accommodate themselves to all (1 Cor. 9). Those are rebuked who, in order to seem great, show themselves difficult to all. 2. Hospitality toward strangers is commended. God prescribes this everywhere. Since he is the God of the afflicted, he especially cares for strangers (Deut. 22; Isa. 58; Matt. 25; Heb. 13). And it is clear that the most holy men were especially zealous in hospitality. See Gen. 18. 19. And Peter in the present case, though he himself was a stranger. Let all imitate this, especially ministers (1 Tim. 4). Let the example of our forebears stir us. Indeed God gives us [peace] for this reason, that we may enjoy peace and leisure.

units.la: 11. Legati fideliter exponunt quod in mandatis habebant. Atqui multa eos po-terant offendere. Vilis Petri aspectus, ho-spitium ignobile, &c. Et insuper herû lau-dant. ¶ Exemplum seruilis fidei, quod imi-tari debet. Generale præceptum est, vt a-lij aliis subijciatur & seruiant. Eph.5.Phil.2.Io.13. Et itaDeus instituit omnes status. Quanto magis ergo hoc faciet, qui ad ser-uiendum sunt peculiariter destinati. Me-minerint ergo hanc suam esse vocatio-nem. Seruiant ergo non ad oculum, &c. Ephel.6.Imò suos heros amant, laudent iuuent,&c.Sic Iofpeph,Gen.29. Necmo, ueat inhumanitas illorū. Deus enim remunerabitur, 1 Pet.2. Pertinet huc promissio,Matth.25.
units.tr: II. The envoys faithfully set out what they had in their instructions. Yet many things could have offended them: Peter's lowly appearance, the humble lodging, and so on. And moreover they praise their master. This is an example of servile faithfulness, which we ought to imitate. There is a general precept that one person should submit to and serve another (Eph. 5; Phil. 2; John 13). And so God has instituted all estates. How much more, then, should those who are especially destined to serve do this? Let them remember that this is their calling. Let them serve therefore not merely to catch the eye, etc. (Eph. 6). Indeed let them love, praise and help their masters, etc. Thus Joseph (Gen. 29). Let no one's inhumanity prevail against them, for God will reward them (1 Pet. 2). To this belongs the promise of Matt. 25.

units.la: III.Quid Cornelius interea? ¶1. Exspe ctat Pertum suis omnibus ad hoc vocatis. Fidei ingenium exprimitur. Nititur haec solius Dei verbo, & ideo hoc anxiè quaerit,Psalm.19. 119. Rursus quia charitatem coniuctam habet, Gal.5. alios quoq; vult in eius communionem venire. Vtrumq; praestat Cornelius neque periculo terretur, quod ex multis conscijs enascipoterat. Sed vincit fides omnia, 1. Iohan.5. Imitemur, neque propter mundum nostram aut aliorum salutem negligamus.
units.tr: III. What about Cornelius meanwhile? 1. He waits for Peter, having called all his people to be present. The nature of faith is expressed here. It rests on the word of God alone, and therefore he seeks it eagerly (Ps. 19; 119). Again, because he has charity joined with faith (Gal. 5), he wishes others too to come into fellowship with it. Cornelius does both, and he is not terrified by the danger that could arise from many consciences. But faith conquers all (1 John 5). Let us imitate him, and not neglect our own salvation or that of others for the sake of the world.

units.la: ¶2. Petro venienti occurrit, procidit & adorat.Indicium animi magnificè de Dei verbo sentientis.Interim nimius est dum plus quiddam quàm humanum eius ministro tribuit.Solet hoc fieri,quando carnis zelum audimus. Sic 1.Cor.1. Hinc cultus Diuorum,reliquiarum,&c.Sed videi Cor.3. & 4.
units.tr: 2. He meets Peter as he comes, falls down and worships him. This is a sign of a mind that thinks magnificently of God's word. Yet he goes too far when he attributes something more than human to his minister. This usually happens when we hear fleshly zeal (1 Cor. 1). Hence come the cult of the saints, of relics, etc. But see 1 Cor. 3 and 4.

units.la: IV.Petrus item, qui errorem Cornelij non dissimulat, sed amicè reprehendit. Quasi diceret: Video te augustius de me sentire,&c. Sed falleris. Etsi enim Christi Apostolus sim, tamen quoad me, homo mortalis, peccator, qui ipse etiam Dei gra tia opus habeo. Sic supra 3. Sic Paulus infra 14. Noluerunt igitur abuti hominum zelo & simplicitate Apostoli: vt quidam hodie. No τ. ¶ Illicitum esse omnem honorem, qui cum aliqua diuinitatis opinione creaturis impenditur. Præcipiuntur quidem ciuilitatis officia, Exod.10. Leuit. 19. Rom.12. 13. At non debet homo honorari, vt Deus. Ne Angeli quidem hoc ferunt, Apocal.19.22. Hinc iudica de Pontifice Romano personato Petri successore. Caligulam & Domitianum imitatur. Nos his omissis Deum vnum colamus & huic seruiamus, &c. Exod.20. Oremus
units.tr: IV. Peter likewise, who does not overlook Cornelius's error but kindly rebukes it, as if to say: "I see that you think more highly of me than you should, etc. But you are mistaken. For even if I am an apostle of Christ, yet as far as I am concerned I am a mortal man, a sinner, who myself also needs the grace of God." So above (Acts 3). So Paul below (Acts 14). The apostles therefore did not wish to abuse the zeal and simplicity of men, as some do today. NOTE. Every honour that is paid to creatures with some notion of divinity is unlawful. Indeed the duties of civility are commanded (Exod. 10; Lev. 19; Rom. 12. 13). But a man should not be honoured as God is. Not even angels accept this (Rev. 19. 22). Hence judge the Roman Pontiff, who plays the part of Peter's successor. He imitates Caligula and Domitian. Setting these aside, let us worship the one God and serve him, etc. (Exod. 20). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXIX
units.tr: HOMILY LXXXIX

units.la: 27 Et colloquens cum eo, ingressus est, inuenitq; multos, qui conuenerant.
units.tr: 27 And as he talked with him, he went in and found many who had come together.

units.la: 28 Dixitq; eis, Vos scitis Iudæo nefas esse conjungi, aut accedere ad alienigenam: sed mihi ostendit Deus, ne quem pollutum aut impurum hominem dicerem.
units.tr: 28 And he said to them, "You know that it is unlawful for a Jew to join himself to, or come near to, a foreigner; but God has shown me that I should not call any man polluted or unclean."

units.la: 29 Quapropter etiam sine contradictione veni accersitus: percontor igitur, quam ob causam me accersierunt.
units.tr: 29 Therefore I came without objection when I was sent for. I ask, then, why you have sent for me.

units.la: 30 Tum Cornelius ait: Nudius quartus vsque ad hanc horam eram je junus, & hora nona precabar domi meae: & ecce, quidam stetit coram me, vestę splendida:
units.tr: 30 Then Cornelius said: "Four days ago, up until this hour, I was fasting, and at the ninth hour I was praying in my house; and behold, a man stood before me in shining clothing,

units.la: 31 Dixitq; Cornelij exaudita sunt preces tuae & eleemosynae tuae commemoratae sunt in conspectu Dei.
units.tr: 31 and said, 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your alms have been remembered in the sight of God.

units.la: 32 Mitte ergo Ioppen, & accerse Simonem, qui cognominatur Petrus: hic diuersatur in aedibus Simonis coriarij apud mare: qui cum adfuerit, loquetur tibi.
units.tr: 32 Send therefore to Joppa and call Simon, who is surnamed Peter. He is staying in the house of Simon the tanner by the sea. When he comes, he will speak to you.'

units.la: 33 Ecce igitur momento misi ad te: & tu bene fecisti qui adueneris. Nunc ergo omnes nos in conspectu Dei adsumus, ut audiamus omnia quae tibi praecepta sunt a Deo.
units.tr: 33 So I sent for you at once, and you have done well to come. Now therefore we are all present before God, to hear all that has been commanded you by God."

units.la: VT D.olim gentes iusto iudicio in tenebris superstitionum & idololatriae errare passus est, Rom. 1. Ita singulare bonitatis exemplum aedidit, quando nihil tale cogitantibus lucem Euangelij accendit, & ad societatem regni sui vocauit. Quia autem hic fundatur salus nostra, Lucas initium huius rei sic describit, vt singulae circumstantiae doceant, nihil hic fortuitum fuisse, &c. Et in Cornelio ostendit, quid eos facere conueniat, qui hodie etiam salute in Christo voluntfrui. Peccauit quidem nimia Petri reuerentia, &c. In eo autem imitandus est, quod Deum timet, de veritate edoceri cupit, neque eum huius pudet, &c. Ideo Petrus eum de errore contentus admonuisse, postquam cum illo aliquantulum collocutus est, domum ingreditur, &c.
units.tr: Just as God once allowed the Gentiles, by his just judgment, to wander in the darkness of superstition and idolatry (Rom. 1), so he has shown a singular example of his goodness, when he kindled the light of the gospel in those who thought nothing of the kind and called them into the fellowship of his kingdom. Since our salvation is founded here, Luke describes the beginning of this matter in such a way that its individual circumstances teach that nothing here happened by chance, etc. And in Cornelius he shows what those ought to do who today also wish to enjoy salvation in Christ. Peter indeed erred through excessive reverence, etc. But in him we must imitate the fact that he feared God, desired to be taught the truth, and was not ashamed to be taught it, etc. Therefore Peter, having admonished him about his error after speaking with him a little, enters the house, etc.

units.la: I. Petrus suum ad gentes ingressum excusat: Idque partim propter Iudaeorum comites: partim ne gentes propter temerè neglectam sui populi consuetudinem leuitatis suspectum haberent. Ordo hic est: 1. Fatetur receptum morem. Videtur petitus ex Lege, Exod. 34. Deut. 7. Iof. 23. At quia necessarijs commercijs multi abutebantur, illa arctius sunt constricta. Et debet hinc peti doctrina generalis, ne consortium habeamus cum alienis a re ligione & sceleratis. Quia natura ad malum procliues sumus, facile inficimur, Eccles. 15. 1. Cor. 15. Deinde poenarum quoq; consortes reddimur. Vide Loth, Gen. 14. 19 2. Pet. 2. Hinc illa, 2. Corinth. 6. Apoc. 18 Act 2. Obseruent haec, qui hodie omnia scelera mundi consuetudine excusant. Au di Christum, Ioh. 15.
units.tr: I. Peter excuses his entering among the Gentiles, and this partly on account of the Jewish companions, and partly so that the Gentiles might not regard him as light-minded because of a custom of his people that had been thoughtlessly neglected. The order here is: 1. He confesses the received custom. It seems to be drawn from the Law (Exod. 34; Deut. 7; Josh. 23). But because many abused necessary dealings, those rules were drawn more tightly. From this a general doctrine should be drawn: that we should not have fellowship with those who are alien from the religion and with the wicked. Since we are naturally prone to evil, we are easily infected (Eccles. 15; 1 Cor. 15). Then we also become partakers of their punishments. See Lot (Gen. 14, 19; 2 Pet. 2). Hence that passage, 2 Cor. 6; Rev. 18; Acts 2. Let those who today excuse all the crimes of the world by custom take note of these things. Hear Christ, John 15.

units.la: 2. Consuetudini receptae allegat oraculum culum Dei receas:Ne quem immundum, id est,Euangelio indignum dicamus. Alio qui,quoad nos, omnes sumus immundi, Psal.51.Gen.8.5.Iob.14.15.25.Isa.64. Quia autem sanguis Christi nos emundat perceptus fide (1 Io.1.Act.15) & hic se omnibus offert,(Gal 3.Col.3.)nos neminem tere debemus excludere.Habes hic regulam omnium commerciorum,&c. Mat.7. 26.In primis obseruemus quòd Deus voluntatem expressam opponit consuetudini receptæ.Sic Num.15.Deut.28. Debent illi cedere quæ bono zelo instituta & diu piè obseruata sunt.Talis fuit Legalis cultus,Heb 9.Quanto magis abusus manifesti,qui non nisi hominum traditionibus niuntur? Isa.29.Mat.15.
units.tr: 2. Against the received custom he sets the oracle of God: that we should not call any man "unclean," that is, unworthy of the Gospel. Otherwise, as far as we are concerned, all of us are unclean (Ps. 51; Gen. 8:21; Job 14:4; 15:14, 25; Isa. 64:6). But since the blood of Christ cleanses us, received by faith (1 John 1; Acts 15), and he offers himself to all (Gal. 3; Col. 3), we ought to exclude no one. Here you have the rule for all dealings, etc. (Matt. 7). First let us observe that God sets his expressed will against received custom, as in Num. 15 and Deut. 28. Those things which have been instituted with good zeal and piously observed for a long time ought to yield to it. Such was the legal worship (Heb. 9). How much more must manifest abuses yield, which rest on nothing but human traditions? (Isa. 29; Matt. 15).

units.la: ¶3. Quærit,cur ipsum vocârint? Atqui ante edoctus erat. Sed vult ex ipsis audire, vt diligentiam & attentionem exciter, Imò ipse etiam magis accendatur, Luc.8.
units.tr: ¶3. He asks why they have summoned him, although he had already been informed. But he wishes to hear it from them, so as to stir up their diligence and attention; indeed, so that he himself may be kindled all the more (Luke 8).

units.la: II. Cornelius simpliciter exponit rem: Nec otiosa est repetitio.
units.tr: II. Cornelius sets out the matter simply, and the repetition is not idle.

units.la: 1.Orditur à causa,cur Petrum vocârit, ne insolentior putetur, qui non ipse ad eum venerit.Summa,Deum ita iusssse &c. Vbi Not. ¶ Quòd ad horam nonam vsq; se ieiunû fuisse & orasse dicit. Exprimunt hæc ardens veritatis studiu, quo propter
units.tr: 1. He begins from the cause for which he sent for Peter, lest he be thought too presumptuous for not having come to him himself. The summary: that God so commanded, etc. Where note: he says that he fasted and prayed until the ninth hour. These words express the ardent zeal for truth with which, on account of the diversity of religion, he burned. So that his prayers might be more effective, he fasted, etc. He was therefore among those who hunger and thirst for righteousness (Matt. 5). If you compare him with the manners of our own age, you will not be surprised that less progress is made today.

units.la: Vbi Not. Quòd ad horam nonam vsque ieiunum fuisse & orasse dicit.
units.tr: Where note: that he says he fasted and prayed until the ninth hour.

units.la: diuersitatem religionis æstuauit. Vt ergo preces efficaciores essent, ieiunauit, &c. Fuit ergo ex ijs, qui esuriunt iustitiá, &c. Matthæi 5. Quod si illum conferas cum nostri seculi moribus,non miraberis hodie minùs proficì.Deus orari vult,Luc.18 11.Matt. 7. Non possunt autem preces ardere, quando carni indulgetur, Matth 9. 1.Cor.7.At hodie paucis res cordi est.Plerique omnes religiones probant, contra illud,Actor.4.Ioh.3.14. Interim regnat Est-brietas apud omnes ordines, Antistites, papisticos & euangelicos,Ifa.56.Magistratus,Eccles.10. Vulgus,Ifa 5 Matthæi 24. & Lucæ 17. Ita pereunt fortia corpora, animæ.
units.tr: God wishes to be prayed to (Luke 18:11; Matt. 7). But prayers cannot burn when the flesh is indulged (Matt. 9; 1 Cor. 7). Yet today few care for the matter. Nearly everyone approves of all religions, contrary to that saying (Acts 4; John 3:14). Meanwhile drunkenness reigns among all orders: bishops, papists and evangelicals (Isa. 56); the magistrates (Eccles. 10); the common people (Isa. 5; Matt. 24 and Luke 17). Thus strong bodies and souls perish.

units.la: 2.Gratias agit qui venerit.Hic enim sensus est locutionis,Benefecisti,&c.Vbi Nota.¶Gratitudinem deberi ministris.Per hos salus offertur,Psal.107.Abd.1.Deinde patrum loco sunt,1.Cor.4.Gal. 4. Adhæc sunt legati Dei, Malach.2.2.Corinth.5.Lucæ 10. Ideo inter summa beneficia, &c. Amos 2. Mich. 6. Ioel.2. Ephef.4. Hodie multi dicunt, Satans der teuffel mit den pfaffen bschissen. Fit ergo, 2 Thessal. 2. 2.
units.tr: 2. He gives thanks that Peter has come. For this is the sense of the phrase, "You have done well," etc. Where note: that gratitude is owed to ministers. Through them salvation is offered (Ps. 107; Obad. 1). Then they stand in the place of fathers (1 Cor. 4; Gal. 4). Moreover, they are the ambassadors of God (Mal. 2:7; 2 Cor. 5; Luke 10). Therefore among the greatest benefits, etc. (Amos 2; Mic. 6; Joel 2; Eph. 4). Today many say, "Satan the devil cheats with the priests." Thus it comes about (2 Thess. 2).

units.la: Tim.4.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 4.

units.la: 3. Offert attentionem, &c. Vbi Nota. ¶ Quales esse deceat auditores? 1.Meminerint se in Dei conspectu agere. Is loquitur in ministris, Iere.1. Matth.10. 2. Corinth.13. Idem coetibus adest, Matth.18. Id simul admonet modestiae, 1. Cor.11. 2. Adsint vt audiant, ne vanis cogitationibus distrahantur, Luc.8. Meminerint sibi opus esse institutione. Orent, Psal.25. 119. 3. Omnia velint audire: non modo quae carni placent. In his hodie peccatur. Plerique veniunt, vt Ezech.33. Imo protestantur, sibi non opus esse doctrina. Deinde praefcri bunt quid velint audire, Isaiae 28. & 30. Mi chea 2. Similes delicatulorum. Cornelius rectius, qui hortatur etiam Petrum, ne quid disimulet. Ita nos hodie oportebat esse affectos. Verumtamen qualiscunque sit mundus, ministri faciant quod iubentur, Ezech.3. Ierem. 3. Matth.10.2. Tim.4. Oremus.
units.tr: 3. He offers attention, etc. Where note: what sort of hearers ought they to be? 1. They should remember that they act in the sight of God. He speaks through the ministers (Jer. 1; Matt. 10; 2 Cor. 13). The same God is present in the assemblies (Matt. 18). This at the same time reminds them of modesty (1 Cor. 11). 2. Let them be present in order to hear, so that they are not distracted by vain thoughts (Luke 8). Let them remember that they need instruction. Let them pray (Ps. 25; 119). 3. Let them wish to hear everything, not only what pleases the flesh. In these things people sin today. Most come as in Ezek. 33. Indeed they protest that they have no need of doctrine. Then they prescribe what they wish to hear (Isa. 28 and 30; Mic. 2), like the pampered. Cornelius is more right, who also urges Peter not to conceal anything. So we too ought to be disposed today. Nevertheless, whatever the world is like, ministers should do what they are commanded (Ezek. 3; Jer. 3; Matt. 10; 2 Tim. 4). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XC.
units.tr: HOMILIA XC.

units.la: 34 Tum aperto ore Petrus dixit, In veritate comperio Deum non accipere personam.
units.tr: 34 Then Peter opened his mouth and said: In truth I perceive that God does not accept persons.

units.la: 35 Sed in quavis gente acceptum ei esse quemvis qui eum timeat, & operetur iustitiam.
units.tr: 35 But in every nation whoever fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.

units.la: 36 Id quod significavit filijs Israel, annuncians pacem per Iesum Christum, qui est omnium Dominus.
units.tr: 36 This is the word he sent to the sons of Israel, announcing peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.

units.la: CHristus Matthæi 7.ait:Petite & dabitur,&c.Consentit his Iacob.1. At quia necesse est nos in fide istarum promissionum confirmari, exempla in Scriptura multa proponuntur:Inter quæ non vulgare est Cornelij.Postquam enim huius animum Deus aperuit, vt veri numinis sensu tangeretur,assiduè orauit, vt de tota salutis ratione edoceretur. Exaudiuit ergo Deus & Petrum submisit, per quem edoceretur: & ita quidem,vt appareat,nihil absque sua prouidentia factum. Idem in sequentibus quoque patebit.Nunc enim Petrum excitat, vt magna cum gratuitate & diligentia concionem instituat.Argumentum est, Sola fide in Christum homines iustificari & seruari.Ordo est: 1. Docet Christum & quam nobis meruit sa lutem ad gentes quoque pertinere: & ita sibi beneuolos reddit. 2.Summam rei pro ponit. 3. Eandem illustrat & confirmat. 4.Modum tradit,quo Christus & salus apprehendatur.
units.tr: Christ says in Matthew 7: Ask, and it will be given you, etc. James 1 agrees with these words. But because we must be confirmed in faith in these promises, many examples are set before us in Scripture, and among them the example of Cornelius is no ordinary one. For after God had opened his mind so that he was moved by a sense of the true God, he prayed constantly that he might be taught the whole way of salvation. God therefore heard him and sent Peter, through whom he might be taught; and so clearly nothing happens without God's providence. This will become plain again in what follows. For now he stirs up Peter to set about the sermon with great readiness and diligence. The argument is that men are justified and saved by faith alone in Christ. The order is: (1) he teaches that Christ, and the salvation he has merited for us, pertains also to the Gentiles, and so makes them well disposed towards him; (2) he sets out the sum of the matter; (3) he illustrates and confirms it; (4) he hands on the manner by which Christ and salvation are laid hold of.

units.la: 1. Ne videretur similis aliorum Iudæorum qui gentes sastidiebant, grauiter pronuntiat:Reipsa comperio, &c. Vbi singuli. Nor.1.Quòd nunc istud comperit. Ignorauit ergo hucusque, & fatetur communem errorem. Ita sanctos interdum aliqua qua latent, etiamsi salutis rationem probè teneant, quæ causa est, vt zelo suo decipiantur. Sic Dauid & Nathan, 2. Sam. 7. Elisa, 2. Reg. 4 Id verò modestiam docet, ne nobis nimium tribuamus, 1. Cor. 1$. Item ne pudeat nosfateri errorem: multo minus eum tueamur.
units.tr: 1. So that he should not seem like those other Jews who despised the Gentiles, he solemnly declares: "In truth I perceive," etc. Note the single words: "now he perceives this." He had therefore been ignorant until now, and he admits the common error. So holy men sometimes are misled by some hidden matters, even when they hold the way of salvation soundly, and this is the cause of their being deceived by their own zeal. Thus David and Nathan (2 Sam. 7), and Elisha (2 Kings 4). This teaches modesty, that we should not attribute too much to ourselves (1 Cor. 13). Likewise, that we should not be ashamed to confess error, much less defend it.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quid comperit? Deum non respice personas: qualis scilicet quis sit gente, conditione, fortitudine, &c. Neq; propter ista regnum suum vel patefacere, vel occultare. Ita Paulus, 1. Timo. 2 Gal. 3. Col. 3. Rom. 1. Id nos soletur in tentationibus. Doceat item, ne quem contemnamus temere: sed imitemur Deum.
units.tr: ¶ 2. What did he perceive? "God does not respect persons": that is, what sort of person someone is by nation, condition, strength, and so on. Nor on account of these things does he either reveal or hide his kingdom. So Paul (1 Tim. 2; Gal. 3; Col. 3; Rom. 1). This consoles us in temptations. It also teaches us not to despise anyone rashly, but to imitate God.

units.la: ¶ r. Ne quis tamen Deum putet absque omni ratione agere, describit eos, quos probet: Sed qui timet, &c. Comprehendit his omnia hominis officia. Timor Dei totam religionem continet. Quia non est sine cognitione, Hab. 3. Deinde parit studium quærendi eius voluntatem, & huic placendi, Prou. 1. Iustitia, suum cuique tribuit, & per omne vitam extenditur ad Deum & homines. Qui his studet, Deo gratus est, qualiscunque sit quoad personam. Et obseruemus Petrum non dicere, In quauis religione. Sed, In quauis gente. Non enim sensit (vt hodie quidam) vnumquenque in sua religione seruari, & salutem ex nostra intentione aut operibus pendere. Sed Deum pro sua bonitate Christum & huius merito paratam salutem omnibus gentibus offerre,&c. Atqui illo non opus eflet,fi salus ex nobis eflet. Imo Christus mendacij argueretur,qui ait, Iohan.14.4. Marc.16.Deus ipse,Matt.3 17.
units.tr: ¶ 1. Lest anyone think, however, that God acts without any reason, he describes those whom he approves: "but he who fears," etc. This comprehends all the duties of man. The fear of God contains the whole of religion, because it is not without knowledge (Hab. 3). Then it produces zeal to seek his will and to please him (Prov. 1). Righteousness gives each his due, and it extends through the whole of life towards God and men. He who studies these things is pleasing to God, whatever his person may be. And let us observe that Peter does not say "in any religion," but "in any nation." For he did not think (as some do today) that each man is saved in his own religion, and that salvation depends on our intention or works. Rather, God, in his goodness, offers to all nations Christ and the salvation prepared through his merit, etc. But there would be no need of that if salvation were from ourselves. Indeed Christ would be convicted of falsehood, who says (John 14; Mark 16). God himself (Matt. 3).

units.la: II. Proponit summam: Sermonem,&c. Sensus: Nolo vos quid nouum & antea in auditum exspectare: Sed hoc prædicabo, quod in omnium ore est, & de quo ipsi quoque audiuistis: Vt nimirum Deus Filium suum miserit Israelitis, & per hunc annunciârit pacem.Hic vero est omnium Dominus & Seruator.
units.tr: II. He sets out the sum: "the word," etc. The sense is: I do not want you to expect anything new or previously unheard; rather I will preach what is on everyone's lips and what you yourselves have heard: namely, that God sent his Son to the Israelites and through him announced peace. And this one is Lord and Saviour of all.

units.la: Vbi NoTA. ¶ Quòd salutem prædicaturus,vnum Christum prædicat,neq; monetur eo,quòd hunc in omniù ore eííe,& de eo diuersa eífe iudicia sciret,Matth.16. Pluris enim fecit Christi dictum,Matt.10. Mar.8. Idem fecerunt omnes Apostoli,Aítor.4. Rom.1.Gal.6.1.Cor.1.2.3. Eadem doctrina ergo etiam hodie inculcetur,non moremur mundi iudicia.
units.tr: Here take note. ¶ That in preaching salvation he preaches Christ alone, and is not moved by the fact that he was on everyone's lips and that he knew opinions about him to be divided (Matt. 16). For he set more store by Christ's saying (Matt. 10; Mark 8). All the apostles did the same (Acts 4; Rom. 1; Gal. 6; 1 Cor. 1, 2, 3). Therefore this same doctrine should be impressed upon us today; let us not linger over the judgments of the world.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quòd Iesum dicit à Deo missum. Fuit enim ab hoc prædestinatus, 1.Pet.1. Ephef.1.Venit autem præfinito tempore, homo factus ex muliere &c.Gal.4. Commendatur Euangelij doctrina & assoritur nostræ salutis certitudo, vt quę in De de creto æterno fundata est, Ro.8 9. Consolatur item contra minas tyrannorum. Vide Actor.5.
units.tr: ¶ 2. That he calls Jesus sent by God. For he was predestined by him (1 Pet. 1; Eph. 1). He came, however, at the appointed time, made man of a woman, etc. (Gal. 4). The doctrine of the gospel is commended, and the certainty of our salvation is asserted, since it is founded in the eternal decree of God (Rom. 8, 9). It also consoles against the threats of tyrants. See Acts 5.

units.la: ¶ 3. Quid confert Christus? Pacem. Lo quitur de pace cum Deo, de qua Philip.4. Prius inimici eramus & filij iræ propter peccatum, Isa 59. Rom.5. At Christus pec- cata tollens nobis pacem acquisiuit, Ioh. 14. Testantur hoc Angeli, Luc.2. Ipse Pater cœlitus, Matth 3 17. Apostoli, Eph.2. Rom.5.
units.tr: ¶ 3. What does Christ bestow? Peace. He speaks of peace with God, of which Phil. 4. We were first enemies and children of wrath because of sin (Isa. 59; Rom. 5). But Christ, taking away sins, obtained peace for us (John 14). The angels testify to this (Luke 2); the Father himself from heaven (Matt. 3); the apostles (Eph. 2; Rom. 5).

units.la: Fructus huius pacis sunt: 1. Salutis certitudo & conscientiæ tranquillitas. 2. Patientia & gaudium in medijs adflictionibus, Roman.5.8. Actor.5. 3. Charitas quæ pacificos facit. Vide Matthæi 5. Iohannis 15. Ex his notis agnoscuntur veri Christiani. Quod hodie propter religionem tumultuatur plerique, hoc ex infelici mundo est, & implentur illa Christi, Lucæ 12. Ioh.3. Interim agnoscamus nos Dei bonitatem & paci quidem studeamus cum omnibus, quantum in nobis est (Rom.12.) potissimum tamen pacis cum Deo habeamus rationem. Vide Ioh.14. Rom.8.
units.tr: The fruits of this peace are: (1) certainty of salvation and tranquillity of conscience; (2) patience and joy in the midst of afflictions (Rom. 5, 8; Acts 5); (3) charity, which makes men peaceable (see Matt. 5; John 15). From these marks true Christians are recognised. That many today are thrown into tumult on account of religion comes from this unhappy world, and those words of Christ are fulfilled (Luke 12; John 3). Meanwhile let us acknowledge the goodness of God, and let us indeed strive for peace with all, as far as lies in us (Rom. 12), but chiefly let us have regard to peace with God (see John 14; Rom. 8).

units.la: Oremus.
units.tr: Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XCI.
units.tr: HOMILY XCI.

units.la: 37 Vos in quam nostis, quod gestum est per totam Iudaeam, incipiens a Galilaea, post baptisma, quod praedicauit Iohannes.
units.tr: 37 You know what took place throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism that John preached.

units.la: 38 Vt Iesum Nazarenum vnxerit Deus Spiritu sancto & potentia: qui ob ambulauit, beneficijs afficiens et sanans omnes, sub diaboli potestatem redactos: quoniam Deus erat cum eo.
units.tr: 38 How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil's power, because God was with him.

units.la: VT Lucas prolixè narrauit, Petrum ab ipso Deo doctorem datum fuisse Cornelio: ita diligenter eiusdem concionem describit, vt discamus quae vbiq; fuerit Apostolorum doctrina, quae hodie etiam in Ecclesijs seruari debeat. Initio autem protestatus est, se non aliud tradere velle quàm Christum, qui omnium Dominus, id est, Seruator fit, ideoque in Mundum missus fit, vt nobis pacis cum Deo author & praeco esset. Quia verò his ostendit, salutem omnem in hoc vno contineri, & proinde hunc vnum praedicari debere: hoc ipsum probat historica narratione, qua docet illum omnia praestitisse, quae secundum Scripturam debebant fieri nostrae redemptionis ergo.
units.tr: As Luke has related at length that God himself gave Peter to Cornelius as his teacher, so he describes that man's sermon so carefully that we may learn what the doctrine of the Apostles was everywhere, and what ought to be preserved in the Churches today. At the outset, however, Peter declared that he wished to deliver nothing other than Christ, who is the Lord of all, that is, who becomes Saviour, and who was therefore sent into the world to be the author and herald of peace with God for us. But since he shows by these words that all salvation is contained in this one, and that therefore this one alone ought to be preached, he proves this very point by a historical narrative, in which he teaches that Christ performed all those things which, according to Scripture, had to be done for our redemption.

units.la: I. Locum indicat, vbi primùm se manifestauit
units.tr: I. The place where he first revealed himself.

units.la: Vbi Christus innote scere caepe-ris. feftauit Christus: Galilæa.Ita vero prædi stum,Matth. 4.Ifa 9.No t. ¶ Non temerè hoc factum. Fuit enim Galilæa totius terræ Iudæorum miserrima, iam inde à Solo monis tempore, 1.Reg 9. Inde dicta Galilæa gentium.Deinde prima vastata per Assyr.2.Regum 15.Ifa 9.Ex Babylon.reuersis quoque miserior.Christo autem iam præsente sub Herode erat. Denique in tenebris sedebat, quoad corpus & animam. Huic tamen primæ assulsit lux in Christo, Ioh. 1. 8. Ita innuitur, Christum maximè pertinere ad afflictos, & proinde talibus non esse desperandum. Imò ex eo consolationem petant,secundum illud,Matt.9. 11.18 1.Tim.1.
units.tr: Where Christ first began to be made known. He was made manifest. Galilee. Thus it was foretold: Matt. 4; Isa. 9. Note. ¶ It was not by chance that this happened. For Galilee was the most wretched part of the whole land of the Jews, from the time of Solomon, 1 Kings 9. Hence Galilee was called "Galilee of the Gentiles." Then it was first laid waste by the Assyrians, 2 Kings 15; Isa. 9, and it was even more wretched after the return from Babylon. When Christ was already present, it was under Herod. Finally, it sat in darkness, both in body and in soul. Yet on this first region light shone forth in Christ, John 1:8. Thus it is hinted that Christ especially belongs to the afflicted, and therefore such people are not to be despaired of. Indeed, let them take consolation from this, according to that saying: Matt. 9; 11; 18; 1 Tim. 1.

units.la: II. Tempus. Post baptismum, quem Iohannes prædicauit,Matt.4. Sic prædictum Ifaiæ 40.Malach.4. No t. ¶ 1.Noui Testamenti & Euangelij initium à Iohanne,&c. Mar.1.qui pœnitentiæ doctrinâ populum Christo præparauit.Sic cautum, ne quis sub huius prætextu peccandi licentiam quæreret. Ideo ipse etiam à pœnitentia cœpit, & sic iussit Apostolos, Matthæi 4. 10. Luc. 24. Obseruent qui hanc partem vellent omitti,vt ij de quibus Ifaiæ 30. Amos 2.Sed vide Iere.1.
units.tr: II. The time. After the baptism that John preached, Matt. 4. So it was foretold in Isa. 40; Mal. 4. Note. ¶ 1. The beginning of the New Testament and of the Gospel was from John, etc., Mark 1, who prepared the people for Christ by the teaching of repentance. This was guarded against so that no one would seek under this pretext a license to sin. Therefore he himself also began from repentance, and so he ordered the Apostles, Matt. 4; 10; Luke 24. Let those who wish this part omitted observe it, so that they may not be those of whom Isa. 30 and Amos 2 speak. But see Jer. 1.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quòd Iohanne capto Christus suc,
units.tr: ¶ 2. That when John was taken, Christ succeeded

units.la: cesfsit,qui eandem doctrinam maiori fuc-cessu prædicauit. Sic olim Eliæ Elizæus,1. Reg.19.2.Reg.2.13. Sic postea,Act.7.8.9.12 27.28. Spirat Dei spiritus, vbi vult, Ioh.3. Imo neq; vinculis neq; morte impeditur. 2 Tim.2 Vide promissionem, Isa.59. Ita contra conatus Mundi nos confirmemur, Psa.2. Vt Christum coacti sunt audire, qui Iohannem spreuerunt: Ita fiet olim, Ioh. 19. Mat 24.25.
units.tr: him, who preached the same doctrine with greater success. Thus of old Elisha succeeded Elijah, 1 Kings 19; 2 Kings 2:13. So too afterwards, Acts 7; 8; 9; 12; 27; 28. The Spirit of God breathes where he wills, John 3. Indeed he is hindered neither by chains nor by death, 2 Tim. 2. See the promise, Isa. 59. Thus let us be strengthened against the attempts of the world, Ps. 2. Just as those who despised John were compelled to hear Christ, so it will happen one day, John 19; Matt. 24; 25.

units.la: III. Vnctum hunc describit. Iesum à Nazareth. Sic nominat, ne quid difsimilet, vel de alio loqui putetur. Neque pudet eum Nazarethi, licet infame haberetur, Ioh.1. Ita nos etiam neq; Christi, neque Euangelij pudeat, &c. Rom.1 Arguuntur, qui reti cent, quæ odium aut contemptum pariunt. 2. Vnctum dicit à Deo spiritu & virtute. Ita docet esse promissum Seruato rem, quem olim Sacerdotes & Reges figurarint. Et vt ab his llum distinguat, vt eum dicit Spiritu sancto & virtute. Ita alludit ad Psal.45. Isa.61.Ioh.1. Scopus,vt ostendat, hunc à Deo nobis datum, vt omnia obeat, quę Sacerdotis & Regis sunt, Psal.2.110.Heb.8.9.10.&c. Vsus, vt nos agnoscamus talem esse, & illo vno contentis et regis fimus.Ioh 6.Act.4.
units.tr: III. He describes this anointed one: Jesus of Nazareth. He names him thus so that nothing is disguised, and so that he may not be thought to speak of someone else. Nor is he ashamed of Nazareth, although it was held to be infamous, John 1. So let us too not be ashamed of Christ or of the Gospel, etc., Rom. 1. Those are rebuked who hold back what produces hatred or contempt. 2. He says that he was anointed by God with the Spirit and power. Thus he teaches that the Saviour was promised, whom priests and kings of old prefigured. And in order to distinguish him from these, he says that he was anointed with the Holy Spirit and power. Thus he alludes to Ps. 45; Isa. 61; John 1. The aim is to show that this one was given to us by God, so that he might perform all that belongs to priest and king, Ps. 2; 110; Heb. 8; 9; 10, etc. The use is that we acknowledge him to be such a one, and be content with him alone and ruled by him, John 6; Acts 4.

units.la: IIII. Quid fecerit? Obambulauit bene faciens.Fidem & industriam exprimit,qua ipse quæsierit quibus benefaceret. Ergo non consedit certo loco, ad quem omnes vocârit,vt personatus eius vicarius, Pontifex Romanus. Sed ipse obambulauit, &c. Vide Matt.4.9. Quid quòd inuitauit, &c.Matt.11.Ioh.7.8. In primis vide Lucæ 15. Id officij admonet, vt nos inueniri patiamur, ne simus ex eorum numero, de quibus Ifa.65. Item ne alio confugiamus, quasi ipse sit rigidior æquo,Matt.12.If.42. Soletur item contra diaboli insidias,1.Petri 5. Adhuc enim pro nobis ille excubat, & nos quærit,Ioh.14.Matth.28. 2. Sanauit à diabolo oppressos. Pertinet hoc in primis ad Regis officium,Psal.72. In primis autem Christus præstitit. In Adamo diabolus genus humanum in suam potestatem redegerat.Hinc communis calami tas,Eph.2.Col.1. Rom.1. At Christus est semen illud mulieris,Gene 3. Fortis ille, Luc.11.Ioh.14.16.
units.tr: IIII. What did he do? He went about doing good. He expresses his faith and diligence, by which he himself sought out those to whom he might do good. Therefore he did not sit in a fixed place to which he summoned everyone, as the Roman Pontiff, his vicar in person, does. But he himself went about, etc. See Matt. 4; 9. What of the fact that he invited people, etc.? Matt. 11; John 7; 8. Above all see Luke 15. This admonishes us of our duty, that we allow ourselves to be found, lest we be among those of whom Isa. 65 speaks. Likewise, lest we flee to another, as if he were more stern than is right, Matt. 12; Isa. 42. It also consoles us against the snares of the devil, 1 Pet. 5. For he still keeps watch for us and seeks us, John 14; Matt. 28. 2. He healed those oppressed by the devil. This pertains above all to the office of a king, Ps. 72. Christ, however, performed this above all. In Adam the devil had reduced the human race under his power. Hence the common calamity, Eph. 2; Col. 1; Rom. 1. But Christ is that seed of the woman, Gen. 3. He is that strong one, Luke 11; John 14; 16.

units.la: 3. Deus erat cum illo.Hoc addit,vt ne videatur ex incantatorum numero fuisse, vt Scribæ calumniabantur, Matth.12. Et res ipsa docet Deum in Christo fuisse (2. Cor.5.) adeoq; eum propria virtute fecit se quæcunq; fecit.
units.tr: 3. God was with him. He adds this so that he might not seem to have been one of the number of enchanters, as the scribes slandered him, Matt. 12. And the fact itself teaches that God was in Christ, 2 Cor. 5; and so he did whatever he did by his own power.

units.la: Vsus omnium, vt hunc nostrû redemptorem agnoscamus,eidem fidamus & ser uiamus. Deinde vt libertatem nostram sedulò tueamur, neue nos rursus regen- dos præbeamus diabolo. Vide Ephes.4.5. Roman.6.12.13.1.Pet.2.&c. Qui hic segne- scunt,peius habent, Matth.12.2.Pet.2.Ita- que sub huius signis militemus contra diabolum, Ephes.6. Vigilemus & Ore- mus.
units.tr: The use of all this is that we acknowledge him as our redeemer, trust in him and serve him. Then that we diligently guard our liberty, and do not offer ourselves to be ruled again by the devil. See Eph. 4:5; Rom. 6:12-13; 1 Pet. 2, etc. Those who grow slack here have it worse, Matt. 12; 2 Pet. 2. Therefore let us fight under his standard against the devil, Eph. 6. Let us watch and pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XCII.
units.tr: HOMILY XCII.

units.la: 39 Et nos sumus testes omnium, quæ & in regione Iudæorum & in Hie- rufalem fecit: quem occiderunt suspen- sum in ligno.
units.tr: 39 And we are witnesses of all the things he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem, whom they killed by hanging him on a tree.

units.la: 40 Hunc Deus excitauit tertio die, fecit vt conspicuus fieret.
units.tr: 40 God raised him up on the third day and caused him to be made visible.

units.la: 41 Non toti populo, sed testibus quos ipse prius designauerat, nimirum nobis, qui comedimus ac bibimus vnà cum eo, posteaquam resurrexit à mor- tuis.
units.tr: 41 Not to the whole people, but to witnesses whom he had chosen beforehand, namely to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

units.la: 42 Præcepit autem nobis vt prædicaremus populo, ac testificaremur eum esse qui definitus sit à Deo iudex viuorum & mortuorum.
units.tr: 42 And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God to be judge of the living and the dead.

units.la: Diuus Petrus Cornelium ita instituit, vt simul generalem salutis doctrinam strinam proponat.Initio autem protesta-tur,se non aliud quàm Christum prædica re velle, vt ostendat, salutem in hoc vno haberi,Act.4.De eo dixit: 1. Quòd Deus illum vnxerit, vt nimirum sui populi Rex & Sacerdos esset,Psalm.2 110.Tenendum hoc,ne eius vili specie offendamur,Pf.118. Matt.21.2. Quòd obâmbulârit, salutem omnibus offerendo,&c. Matt.4.11.Lucę 15. Ingrati ergo,qui fastidiunt. 3. Finis vt saretoppressos à diaholo,vtpotefemen il lud,Gene. 3. Id verò officij admonet nos, ne porrò diabolo seruiamus,sed tueamur nostram libertatem,2.Cor.5.1.Pet.2. Mat. 12.&c. His subijcit pleniorem declaratio-nem , qua modum redemptionis nostræ per illum factæ exponit,&c.
units.tr: Blessed Peter instructs Cornelius in such a way that he sets out at the same time a general doctrine of salvation. At the beginning, however, he declares that he wishes to preach nothing other than Christ, to show that salvation is to be had in this one alone (Acts 4). Of him he says: (1) that God anointed him, that is, to be King and Priest of his people (Ps. 2, 110). This must be held, lest we be offended by his lowly appearance (Ps. 118; Matt. 21). (2) That he went about doing good, offering salvation to all (Matt. 4; Luke 15). Ungrateful, then, are those who scorn it. (3) That he came to free those oppressed by the devil, as the seed promised in Genesis 3. This duty, moreover, reminds us not to serve the devil any longer, but to guard our liberty (2 Cor. 5; 1 Pet. 2; Matt. 12, etc.). To these things he adds a fuller explanation, in which he sets out the manner of our redemption made through him, etc.

units.la: Interserit autem causam,cur ipse & alij Apostoli te Apostoli ista prædicent, vt occurrat ijs, sses Christi qui hoc indignius ferebant. Ita enim solent multi,quando rei veritatem non possunt negare,huius præconibus inuidiam accersere,&c.Dicit ergo: Et nos sumus testes,&c. Quasi diceret.Quòd nos ista prædicamus,nō nouationis studio,aut exambitione fit,sed quia,&c.Respicit ad Ioh.15. Actor.1.
units.tr: He inserts, moreover, the reason why he and the other Apostles preach these things, so as to meet those who bore it more impatiently. For many people, when they cannot deny the truth of a matter, are wont to stir up hatred against its heralds, etc. He therefore says: "And we are witnesses, etc." As if he were saying: that we preach these things is not from a desire for novelty or from ambition, but because, etc. He looks back to John 15 and Acts 1.

units.la: NoT. ¶ Authoritatem doctrinæ Apostolicæ (1.Ioh.1. Apoc.1.) & quàm graue
units.tr: NOTE. The authority of apostolic doctrine (1 John 1; Rev. 1), and how grave a crime it is to deny it.

units.la: Cap.10 scelus fit,hanc negare. Vide i.Ioh.4. Quid vero vulgarius hodie? Punit ergo merito Deus. Quoad vero modum redemptionis nostrae tria dicit.
units.tr: (Chap. 10) See 1 John 4. What, indeed, is more commonplace today? God therefore punishes justly. As for the manner of our redemption, he speaks of three things.

units.la: 1. Occisum ait in ligno. Paucis hoc dicit, quia fatis nota erant, & obiter arguit Iudaeorum ingratitudinem, qui tantum benefactorem tam indigne tractarunt. Meminerimus, ne hodie offendamur similibus, Matth.10. Est hoc mundi ingenium, i. Ioh.5. Ioh.3.
units.tr: 1. He says he was killed on a tree. He says this briefly, because it was well enough known, and in passing he rebukes the ingratitude of the Jews, who treated so great a benefactor so unworthily. Let us remember, lest we be offended today by similar things (Matt. 10). This is the nature of the world (1 John 5; John 3).

units.la: Sed No T. Quod in ligno occisum ait. Innuit sacrificium, ex veteri more, Ge.22. Ita ipse exponit, i. Pet.2. Vide item Ifa.53. Ioh.6. Idq; ad sacerdotium Christi pertinet, Hebr.10. Et hinc oportuit initium fieri redemptionis nostrae, quando propter peccata non poteramus in Dei conspectu apparere, Ifa.59.
units.tr: But note that he says he was killed on a tree. He hints at a sacrifice, after the ancient custom (Gen. 22). He himself explains it so (1 Pet. 2). See also Isa. 53; John 6. And this pertains to the priesthood of Christ (Heb. 10). And hence the beginning of our redemption had to be made, when on account of sins we could not appear in the sight of God (Isa. 59).

units.la: Haec est salutaris Christi mortis consideratio. Hodie quidam fe officium fecife putant, fi imaginem crucifixi erigant. In terim fibijpfis fidunt, & eundem quotidie crucifigunt, &c.
units.tr: This is the saving consideration of Christ's death. Today some think they have done their duty if they set up an image of the crucified. Meanwhile they trust in themselves and crucify him again every day, etc.

units.la: II. Resurrectionem praedicat, & qui dem diligentius, quod in ea consistit nostrae salutis complementum, i.Cor.15. Nec poteramus Christo fidere, nisi mortis vi&orem esse sciremus, quae haftenus domi nabatur.
units.tr: II. He preaches the resurrection, and does so more diligently, because in it lies the completion of our salvation (1 Cor. 15). Nor could we trust Christ unless we knew that he had conquered death, which had hitherto held dominion at home.

units.la: Redemptio humana modum. nabatur, si ea hunc quoq; detinuisset. Ideo hoc saepe ostendit,vt Matth.9.Luc.7. Ioh 11.Matth 27.His accessit, quod seipsum excitauit. Sed quia hoc Sacerdotes negabant (Matth.28.) constanter hoc asserit Petrus. 1.Deus eū excitauit,cui nihil impoísibile, Actor. 26. 2. Exhibuit non quidem toti populo(qui indignissimus erat) sed deleći s testibus, nobis videlicet, &c.Vide 1. Cor.15. 3. Non obiter, sed ita, vt cum eo ederimus,&c. Vide Luc.24.Iohan. 21. Actor. 1. ¶Facilitas Christi magna:quae eorum improbitatem arguit,qui adhuc calumniantur omnia, quae dicuntur de Christi resurrectione. Indigni,qui illa fruantur,Psal.1.
units.tr: Human redemption would have remained under that yoke too, had death also held him. Therefore he often shows this (Matt. 9; Luke 7; John 11; Matt. 27). To this was added that he raised himself. But since the priests denied this (Matt. 28), Peter steadfastly asserts it. 1. God raised him up, to whom nothing is impossible (Acts 26). 2. He showed himself not to the whole people (who were most unworthy), but to chosen witnesses, namely to us, etc. See 1 Cor. 15. 3. Not in passing, but in such a way that we ate with him, etc. See Luke 24; John 21; Acts 1. NOTE: the affability of Christ is great, which argues against those who still cavil at everything said about Christ's resurrection. Unworthy are those who enjoy it (Ps. 1).

units.la: III. Mandauit,vt testemur illum esse iudi{?}em,&c. Addit hoc, vt occurrat scandalo, quod nascebatur, quando videbatur ille suos negligere.
units.tr: III. He commanded that we testify that he is the judge, etc. He adds this to meet the scandal that arose when he seemed to neglect his own.

units.la: Docet ergo illum non defuturū officio licet nunc videatur coniuere, &c. Et obserua, hunc articulum in primis mandatum esse Apostolis, & hodie etiam, adeoque semper debere inculcari inter prædicandum. ¶1. Excitat ad refipiscentiam.Ideo enim perguntmulti in sceleribus quod mortem dicunt esse vltimam lineam rerum, neque præterea
units.tr: He therefore teaches that he will not fail in his office, although for now he may seem to overlook things, etc. And observe that this article was chiefly entrusted to the Apostles, and so today too it ought always to be impressed upon people in preaching. 1. He stirs us to repentance. For many persist in sins because they think death is the final limit of things, and that nothing

units.la: Christus. iudicat vt. uos et mox tuos.
units.tr: Christ judges, that you ... and soon your own.

units.la: aliquid secuturum putant,2.Pet.3. Experimur hoc hodie, quando pleriq; sperant impunitate,&c. & viuunt,vt prædictum, Mat.24.2.Tim.3.1.Theff.5. &c Hinc etiam focordiain ijs qui præsunt. Singuli ergo animo voluant illud Pauli,2. Cor. 5. Vide item Sap.4.5. ¶2. Solatur item contra indignos impiorum successus & afflictiones piorum,Iere.12.Pfal 73. Sed memineris fore vicissitudinem rerum, vt Luc.16. Impij plangent,Matth.24. Zach.1. Pij attollent capita sua,Luc.21. Est hæc magna nostræ fidei gloria:quando hæc sola articulum istum nobis iucundum reddit, 2. Tim.4. Interim discamus in vno Christo haberi, quæcunq; ad nostram salutem spe stant.Hunc ita ampleftamur, vt meminerimus semper nouisimi aduentus, & ad hunc totis animis præparemur.Oremus.
units.tr: further will follow (2 Pet. 3). We experience this today, when most people hope for impunity, etc., and live as has been foretold (Matt. 24; 2 Tim. 3; 1 Thess. 5, etc.). Hence also the carelessness among those who preside. Let each one therefore turn over in mind that saying of Paul (2 Cor. 5). See also Wisdom 4:5. 2. He also consoles against the unworthy success of the wicked and the afflictions of the godly (Jer. 12; Ps. 73). But remember that there will be a reversal of things (Luke 16). The wicked will wail (Matt. 24), and the godly will lift up their heads (Zech. 1; Luke 21). This is the great glory of our faith, when this alone makes that article pleasant to us (2 Tim. 4). Meanwhile let us learn that whatever tends to our salvation is held in Christ alone. Let us so embrace him that we always remember his last coming, and prepare ourselves for it with all our minds. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XCIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XCIII.

units.la: 43 Huic etiam omnes Prophetæ testimonium dant, remissionem peccatorum acceptURUM per nomen eius quem uis qui crediderit in eum.
units.tr: To him all the Prophets bear witness, that through his name everyone who believes in him receives remission of sins.

units.la: Duus Petrus Christum ita prædicat Cornelio, vt breui cocione omnes Symboli articulos comprehendat. 1. Deus misit filiu suu & vnxit,vt nobis pace af-ferret. ferret.In his habemus Trinitatis mysteria, conception.ex Spiritu fan&to,natiuit. ex virgine.2.Suspensum in ligno occiderunt &c.3.Suscitauit tertio die.4. Veniet iudex,&c.Ergo sedet ad dextram Dei, omni potestate accepta,Ioh. 5. Matt.11.&28. In quibus obseruandum quid hodie etiam de Christo prædicari debeat, quoque non audiendæ fabulæ monachorum. Sequitur Conclusio, qua iftorū omniufructum indicat, &simul talem esse probat
units.tr: Peter preaches Christ to Cornelius in such a way that in a brief sermon he takes in all the articles of the Creed. (1) "God sent his Son and anointed him to bring us peace." In these words we have the mysteries of the Trinity, his conception by the Holy Spirit, and his birth from the virgin. (2) "They hanged him on a tree and killed him," etc. (3) "He rose again on the third day." (4) "He will come as judge," etc. "Therefore he sits at the right hand of God, having received all power," John 5; Matt. 11 and 28. In these words one should note what ought to be preached about Christ even today, and that the fables of the monks are not to be listened to. There follows the conclusion, which points out the fruit of all these things and at the same time shows that it is so.

units.la: Huic omnes Prophetæ,&c. Sensus, Deum ideo Filium misisse, eumq; ista omnia fecisse, vt peccatorum remissionem & fa-lutem certam in eo habeant, quotquot ipsum fide apprehendunt.His continetur tota salutis ratio.
units.tr: To him all the Prophets, etc. The sense is this: God therefore sent his Son and had him do all these things so that all who grasp him by faith may have remission of sins and a sure salvation in him. In this is contained the whole method of salvation.

units.la: I.Quod remissionis peccatorum memi nit,qua scilicet omnes opus habeant, etiam qui credunt.|Sunt ergo omnes homines peccatores. Docet hoc omnis Scriptura. Vide Gen.3.5.6.8. Et quia multi hoc non agnoscunt, & sibijpsis placent, speculum Legis Deus dedit, quæ & verbo & ceremonijs arguit,Rom.7. Leuit.12. Et hoc in seipsis sanctissimi quique agnosuerunt.Vide Psal.51.25.130.143.Isa.53. 64. Hæc cognitio salutis initium.Simile ægroti.Ideo ab hoc articulo Christus exordi{a}riiubet,Luc.24. Vide Rom.1.2.5. 1.Ioh.1. Iac.3.Act.2.3. &c. Not. q Necessario igitur salutem extra nos quæri oportere. Ne ergo audiantur, qui vires hominis ex tollunt, opera & horum merita iactant. Sunt hi nocentissimi doctores, & simul tum Christi mysterium euertunt. Vide 2. Cor.3.1.Cor.4.
units.tr: I. He mentions the remission of sins, which all men without exception need, including those who believe. Therefore all men are sinners. All Scripture teaches this; see Gen. 3:5, 6, 8. And since many do not acknowledge this and are pleased with themselves, God gave the mirror of the Law, which convicts by both word and ceremonies, Rom. 7; Lev. 12. And the holiest people have recognised this in themselves; see Ps. 51, 25, 130, 143; Isa. 53, 64. This knowledge is the beginning of salvation, like a sick man's recognition of his illness. Therefore Christ bids the preaching begin from this article, Luke 24. See Rom. 1, 2, 5; 1 John 1; James 3; Acts 2, 3, etc. Note: it is necessary, therefore, that salvation be sought outside ourselves. So let those not be listened to who exalt the powers of man and boast of their works and their merits. They are the most harmful teachers, and at the same time they overthrow the mystery of Christ. See 2 Cor. 3; 1 Cor. 4.

units.la: II. Vbi quærenda remissio & salus? In Christo solo. Hunc Deus misit, vt homo factus causam nostram susciperet, peccata nostra expiaret, & nostra fieret iustitia. 1.Cor.1.2.Cor.5.Ideo ipse omnes ad fe vocat,Matth.11 9.18. Iohan.7.4. Et Apostoli hunc vnum prædicârunt,1.Ioh.1.2. 1.Pet. 1.Rom.3.1.Cor.2.Gal.6.Act.4. Not. q1. Inanes esse omnes alias expiationes, & insuper Christi merito derogare, contra illud, Isa.42. Docet hoc communis sensus. Si enim nos potuissemus satisfacere, non opus erat Christo. q 2. Peccati atrocitatem, quam horribilem esse oportet, cum non aliter expiari potuerit. Obseruemus hoc contra blanditias diaboli & mundi, Psal.36.Cogitemus quod habetur, Ioh.15. 1.Cor.7. III. Vt nos illius participes efficiamur? Nominis eius & fidei in eum meminit. Id vero ipse docet,Ioh.3.5.6.Mar.16. Sic Paulus, lus, Act.13. Rom.3. Apostoli omnes, Act.15 Nec enim alia ratione Christus apprehen ditur.
units.tr: II. Where is remission and salvation to be sought? In Christ alone. God sent him so that, made man, he might take up our cause, expiate our sins, and become our righteousness. 1 Cor. 1; 2 Cor. 5. Therefore he calls all to himself, Matt. 11, 9, 18; John 7, 4. And the Apostles preached him alone, 1 John 1, 2; 1 Pet. 1; Rom. 3; 1 Cor. 2; Gal. 6; Acts 4. Note: (1) that all other expiations are empty, and that to add them detracts from the merit of Christ, contrary to Isa. 42. Common sense teaches this: for if we could have made satisfaction, there would have been no need of Christ. (2) Consider the atrocity of sin, which must be terrible, since it could not be expiated in any other way. Let us observe this against the flatteries of the devil and the world; see Ps. 36. Let us consider what is written in John 15 and 1 Cor. 7. III. How are we made partakers of him? The text speaks of his name and of faith in him. This he himself teaches, John 3, 5, 6; Mark 16. So Paul, Acts 13; Rom. 3; all the Apostles, Acts 15. For Christ is grasped in no other way.

units.la: Sed Not. ¶ Quid sit fides? Non opinio inanis, sed firmus animi assensus, quo Christum talem agnoscamus, qualis nomine suo praedicatur, & qualem Apostoli tradiderunt, Ioh.17.1. Ioh 2. Qui talem agnoscunt, in eo omnem salutis fiduciam collocant, Ioh.6. Gal.6. Ipsi insiti in eo de viuunt, Gal.2.6.2. Cor.5. Propter illum omnia ferunt & vincunt 1. Ioh..5. Ro.8.5. Et haec illa fides est, quam Symbol. profitemur, vbi dicimus, Credo remissionem. Et arguuntur omnes, qui illam bonis operibus inimicam esse aiunt.
units.tr: But note: what is faith? It is not an empty opinion, but a firm assent of the mind, by which we acknowledge Christ as he is named and as the Apostles handed him down, John 17, 1; John 2. Those who acknowledge him thus place all their confidence of salvation in him, John 6; Gal. 6. Ingrafted in him, they live by him, Gal. 2, 6; 2 Cor. 5. For his sake they endure and overcome all things, 1 John 5; Rom. 8. This is that faith which we profess in the Creed, where we say, "I believe the remission [of sins]." And all are condemned who say that it is hostile to good works.

units.la: Interim meminerimus hac frustra eos gloriari, qui operibus eande negant, Iac.5. Vide Ioh.15. Mat.5. Item, Eph.1.4.5.1.Pet. 1.2.3.2.Pet.1.1.Ioh.2.3. &c. At quia hic fegnescimus, propter nos male audit nomen Domini (Mal.1.) & punimur.
units.tr: Meanwhile let us remember that those boast in vain who deny that faith is in works, James 5. See John 15; Matt. 5; likewise Eph. 1, 4, 5; 1 Pet. 1, 2, 3; 2 Pet. 1; 1 John 2, 3, etc. But because we grow slack here, the name of the Lord is ill spoken of on our account (Mal. 1), and we are punished.

units.la: Ne haec doctrina omnino noua & prius incognita putaretur, interfuit Petrus. Huic omnes Prophetae, &c. Similis locus Supra 3. Nec dubium est, illum testimonia adduxisse. Ita enim soliti sunt, vt patet Infra 13.17 Ita ex Christo didicerat Ioh.5. Luc.24. Extant testimonia passim, Moses
units.tr: Lest this doctrine be thought wholly new and previously unknown, Peter brings in the testimony: "To him all the Prophets...". A similar passage occurs above, chapter 3. Nor is there doubt that he adduced testimonies, for that was his custom, as is clear below, chapters 13 and 17. He had learned this from Christ himself, John 5; Luke 24. Testimonies are found everywhere: from Moses

units.la: Gen.3.12.22.26.28.Deut.18.Nathani,2.Samuel,7.Dauidis,Psal.2.22.51.89.72.110.132. 130. &c. Aliorum, quibus hoc commune est, quod consolationis argumenta hinc petunt,Isa.7.6.8.9.35.53.Ierem.23.Mich.4. 5.Amos 9,Ezech.34. Dan.9. Zach.3.4.9. 13.Mal.4.
units.tr: Gen. 3:12, 22, 26, 28; Deut. 18; from Nathan, 2 Sam. 7; from David, Ps. 2, 22, 51, 89, 72, 110, 132, 130, etc.; and from others, for whom this is common, that they seek from here the grounds of consolation: Isa. 7, 6, 8, 9, 35, 53; Jer. 23; Mic. 4, 5; Amos 9; Ezek. 34; Dan. 9; Zech. 3, 4, 9, 13; Mal. 4.

units.la: ¶ Discamus quae omnium vetustissima & catholica fides fit? Vetustissimus omnium scriptorum Moses,idemque fidelis, Num.12. Et hic non suam modo, sed patrum iam inde ab Adamo fidem descripsit.Vide Iohan.8. Apoc.13. Deinde nulla religio tot testibus probata est. Patrum, Heb.11.Prophetarum,1.Pet.1. 2.Pet.1. Apostolorum,Martyrum.Nulla per omnes gentes propagata tam diu durauit, &c. Arguuntur, qui Concilium exspectant, per quod controuersiae decidantur. Atqui nullum Concilium sanctius haberi potest,quàm Prophetarum & Apostolorum, quos omnes constat Spiritu sancto gubernatos fuisse, 1.Pet.1. Ierem.1. Isa.6. 59.Item Iohan.20.Actor.1. &2. Matth.10. Luc.10.
units.tr: Let us learn what the most ancient and catholic faith of all is. The most ancient of all writers is Moses, who is also faithful, Num. 12. And he describes not only his own faith but that of the fathers, from Adam onwards. See John 8; Rev. 13. Then no religion has been approved by so many witnesses: of the fathers, Heb. 11; of the prophets, 1 Pet. 1; 2 Pet. 1; of the Apostles; of the martyrs. No religion, propagated through all nations, has lasted so long, etc. They are condemned who wait for a council by which controversies may be settled. Yet no council can be considered holier than that of the Prophets and Apostles, all of whom it is agreed were governed by the Holy Spirit, 1 Pet. 1; Jer. 1; Isa. 6, 59; likewise John 20; Acts 1 and 2; Matt. 10; Luke 10.

units.la: Hos ergo audiamus, & quia isti omnes vnum Chriftu praedicant, eum amplectamur, & in eius fide fimus constantes. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us therefore hear these, and since all of them preach the one Christ, let us embrace him and be steadfast in his faith. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XCIV.
units.tr: HOMILY XCIV.

units.la: 44 Adhuc loquente Petro verba ista, illapsus est Spiritus sanctus in omnes qui audiebant huius sermonem.
units.tr: 44 While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard the sermon.

units.la: 45 Fideles autem qui erant ex circumsione, & venerant cum Petro, ob stupuerunt quod etiam in gentes effusum esset donum Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: 45 And the faithful of the circumcision who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles too.

units.la: 46 Audiebant enim eos loquentes linguis, ac magnificantes Deum. Tunc respondit Petrus;
units.tr: 46 For they heard them speaking with tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter answered:

units.la: 47 Num quis aquam prohibere potest, quo minus baptizentur isti, qui Spiritum sanctum acceperunt sicut & nos?
units.tr: 47 Can anyone forbid water, so that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?

units.la: 48 Iussitque eos baptizari in nomine Domini. Rogauerunt autem eum ut perseueraret ad dies aliquot.
units.tr: 48 And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. But they asked him to stay on for some days.

units.la: ETsi Deus suum Filium communem omnium gentium Seruatorem fecerit, & hoc per primas promissiones & Prophetas abunde testatus sit (Gen.3.22. 26.28.If.2.49.42 Zach.9) Et ipse Christus iusserit Euangelium omnibus gentibus praedicare, Iudaei tamen [Legis & cultus externi praerogatiua elati, Christum ad se solos pertinere putarunt, & ideo gentes fastidiebant: tamque pertinax fuit hic error, vt ne Apostoli quidem initiò rem intellexerint. Ideo Petrus cum de eo coelitus edoctus effet, concionem suam ad Cornelium sic instituit, vt de illo subinde admoneat. Ab eo enim exorsus est. In consclusione verò hoc ipsum inculcat. Ne quis verò illum aliquid temerè fecisse aut dixisse putet, Deus nunc euentu hoc ipsum probat. Et habet locus hic multiplicem doctrinam.
units.tr: Although God made his Son the common Saviour of all nations, and has attested this abundantly through the first promises and the Prophets (Gen. 3.22; 26.28; Isa. 2; 49; 42; Zech. 9), and Christ himself commanded the Gospel to be preached to all nations, the Jews, however, puffed up with the privilege of the Law and external worship, thought Christ belonged to them alone, and therefore despised the Gentiles. This error was so stubborn that not even the Apostles at first understood the matter. Therefore Peter, when he had been taught about it from heaven, arranged his sermon to Cornelius so that he keeps reminding them of it; for he began from it. In the conclusion he drives this very point home. Lest anyone think he had done or said something rashly, God now confirms this very thing by the outcome. And this passage contains manifold teaching.

units.la: I. Spiritus sanctus cecidit super omnes, et loquuti sunt, etc. Idem ergo hic quod supra 2.8. Fuit hoc tunc commune signum, quod praedicatio fidei in Christum obsignabatur. Hinc illud Gal.3. Et sic fieri oportebat, vt omnibus constaret hoc negotium esse diuinum, &c.
units.tr: I. The Holy Spirit fell on all, and they spoke, etc. This is the same as above, 2.8. This was then a common sign that the preaching of faith in Christ was being sealed. Hence that in Gal. 3: "And so it had to happen, so that it would be clear to all that this business was divine," etc.

units.la: NOT.1. Euangelij dignitatem. Organum est, per quod Deus fidem & Spiritum sanctum nobis largitur, Rom.10.1. Ideo ministerium Spiritus dicitur, 2.Cor.3. Nec obstat, quod non eadem hodie fiunt, quae olim. Nunc enim non opus est, cum fidei doctrina abundè sit confirmata. Interim adhuc datur Spiritus, Rom.8. Et hic adhuc effectus se prodit.
units.tr: NOTE 1. The dignity of the Gospel. It is the instrument through which God bestows faith and the Holy Spirit on us (Rom. 10.1). Therefore it is called the ministry of the Spirit (2 Cor. 3). Nor does it matter that the same things do not happen today that happened formerly. For now there is no need, since the doctrine of faith has been abundantly confirmed. Meanwhile the Spirit is still given (Rom. 8), and here the effect still shows itself.

units.la: ¶2. Quibus adopt. est arrhabo, Rom.8.2.Cor.1.5.Eph.1. Carnem mortificat, & regenerat vt noua fimus Creatura, Ioh.3.
units.tr: ¶2. To those who are adopted it is a pledge (Rom. 8.2; Cor. 1.5; Eph. 1). It mortifies the flesh and regenerates us so that we may be a new creature (John 3).

units.la: 2.Cor.5. Hinc fit, quod nouis linguis loquuntur credentes, Isaiæ 19. Priusnon percipimus quæ sunt Spiritus Dei, & vt pueri sapimus & loquimur, 1.Cor.2. 9. Deinde Deum magnificant, quod sacrificium est ei gratissimum Psa.50.69. Hos. 14. Deniq; sale condiunt sermone Col.4.
units.tr: (2 Cor. 5). Hence it comes about that believers speak in new tongues (Isa. 19). Before, we did not perceive the things of the Spirit of God, and we were wise and spoke like children (1 Cor. 2.9). Then they magnify God, which is a sacrifice most pleasing to him (Ps. 50, 69; Hos. 14). Finally, they season their speech with salt (Col. 4).

units.la: ¶ 3. Arguuntur falsi, qui nihil horum præstant, & absque omni effectu verbum audiunt, vt ij, de quibus Ezech 33. Luc.8. Quales vero, qui Dei gloriam oppugnant? Qui item obscuris verbis simplices offendunt, contra illud Eph.5. Memineris quæ so quid Christus moneat, Matt.12.
units.tr: ¶3. Those are refuted who do none of these things and hear the word with no effect at all, like those of whom Ezekiel 33 and Luke 8 speak. But what of those who oppose God's glory? Likewise those who offend simple people with obscure words, contrary to that in Eph. 5. Remember, I ask, what Christ warns (Matt. 12).

units.la: II. Vt affecti fuerint miraculo spectato res? Perculsi sunt, &c. Adhuc enim fascina-ti erant communi & veteri errore. Ergo in credentibus quoque hærent errores, & vix tolluntur. Vide Apostolos, Actor.1. Imo Pætrum, Gal.4.
units.tr: II. How were they affected by the miracle they had witnessed? They were struck, etc. For they were still bewitched by the common and ancient error. So errors cling even to believers and are scarcely removed. See the Apostles (Acts 1); indeed Peter himself (Gal. 4).

units.la: NOT.¶ Vehementer falli eos, qui non nec esse putant, vt de erroribus & superstitionibus pristinis admoneamur. Hi sepsos ignorant. Sed ex proprio exemplo redarguuntur.
units.tr: NOTE. Those are greatly mistaken who think there is no need to be admonished about former errors and superstitions. They are ignorant of themselves, but they are refuted by their own example.

units.la: III. Petrus intelligit rem: Deum scilicet velle, vt pro Christianis habeantur, & recipiantur in Ecclesiæ sotietatem per baptismum. Argumentu tale:
units.tr: III. Peter understands the matter: namely, that God wills them to be regarded as Christians and received into the fellowship of the Church through baptism. The argument runs thus:

units.la: Baptismus debetur omnibus, qui Spiri-tus sanctı capaces sunt, & eo animantur: At hos tales esse cōstat:Ergo, &c. Et mox baptizantur nemine contradicente.
units.tr: Baptism is owed to all who are capable of the Holy Spirit and are animated by him; but it is clear that these are such; therefore, etc. And straightway they are baptized, no one contradicting.

units.la: NOTA ¶1.Baptismi rationem. Est Sacramentum quo in Ecclesiam recipimur, & quo Christus beneficium regenerationis & ablutionis peccatorum nobis obsignat, Tit.3. Debetur ergo omnibus qui ad Ecclesiam pertinent, & proinde infantibus quoque. Vide Matth,19.18. 1.Cor.7. Sufficiat hoc contra Anabaptistas, qui nou Testamenti gratiam exinaniunt, Genef.17.
units.tr: NOTE ¶1. The reason for baptism. It is the sacrament by which we are received into the Church, and by which Christ seals to us the benefit of regeneration and the washing away of sins (Titus 3). It is owed, therefore, to all who belong to the Church, and so to infants too (see Matt. 19.18; 1 Cor. 7). This is enough against the Anabaptists, who empty the grace of the New Testament (Gen. 17).

units.la: ¶2. Arguı eos, qui Sacramenti vsum vt superuacanum negligunt. Gloriantur fide, sed hanc negant cum inobedientes sint Christo, Matth.28.26. Vetera non licuit negligere, Vide Gen.17. Exod.4. Interim cura fit,ne illis abutamur, sed respondeamus professione,1.Cor.10.11.
units.tr: ¶2. Those are to be refuted who neglect the use of the sacrament as superfluous. They boast of faith, but deny it by being disobedient to Christ (Matt. 28.26). It was not permitted to neglect the old sign (see Gen. 17; Exod. 4). Meanwhile care must be taken not to abuse them, but we must answer with profession (1 Cor. 10.11).

units.la: IV. Cornelius cupit Petrum retinere, vt amplius audiat. Ingenium fidelium NOT.¶1.Etsi instituti sint, non tamen fastidiunt verbum Dei. Imo non possunt satiari voce Patris sui, Ioh.8. Vide Dauidem,Psal.19.119.1. Et quia seipsos probè nôrunt (Ps.51.Rom.7.) sciunt nullāinstitutionem esse superuacaneam. Ideo dura quoque loquentes ferunt, vt Dauid, 2 Sam. 12. 24. Ezechias, Isa. 39. 30. 31. Mich. 3. Iere. 26.
units.tr: IV. Cornelius wishes to keep Peter so that he may hear more. The disposition of believers. NOTE ¶1. Although they have been instructed, yet they do not despise the word of God. Indeed they cannot be satisfied with the voice of their own father (John 8). See David (Ps. 19.119.1). And since they know themselves well (Ps. 51; Rom. 7), they know that no instruction is superfluous. Therefore they also bear harsh words, as David did (2 Sam. 12.24); Hezekiah (Isa. 39.30.31); Micah 3; Jer. 26.

units.la: ¶ 2. Grati sunt erga suos doctores, & ratio ne vtuntur, quam Paulus tradit, 1. Cor. 9. Arguuntur, qui oderunt, auersantur, fugiunt, hostes putant. Talis Achab, 1. Reg. 18. 21. Hodie multi. Sed ad eos pertinet quod minatur Dominus, Matt. 21. Emendemur & Oremus.
units.tr: ¶2. They are grateful toward their teachers and use the reasoning that Paul hands down (1 Cor. 9). Those are refuted who hate, shun, flee from, and regard as enemies their teachers. Such was Ahab (1 Kings 18.21), and many today. But what the Lord threatens applies to them (Matt. 21). Let us be amended. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XI. HOMILIA XCV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI. HOMILY XCV.

units.la: AVdiuerunt autem Apostoli & fratres, qui in Iudæa erant, quòd gentes quoq; recepissent verbum Dei.
units.tr: Now the apostles and brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

units.la: 2 Quùm igitur ascendisset Petrus Hierosolymam, certarunt aduersus eum qui erant ex circumcisione.
units.tr: 2 When therefore Peter had gone up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision contended with him.

units.la: 3 Dicentes: Ad viros præputium habentes introisti, & vna edisti cum eis.
units.tr: 3 Saying: You went in to men having foreskins, and ate with them.

units.la: 4 Exorsus autem Petrus, omnia exposuit eis ordine, dicens;
units.tr: 4 But Peter began and explained everything to them in order, saying:

units.la: 5 Ego eram in ciuitate Ioppe, precans: et visum in mentis excessu vidi, nempe descendens vas quoddam cen linteum magnum, quatuor extremis de vinculo, quod dimittebatur è cœlo: & ad me vsque venit. Ee
units.tr: 5 I was in the city of Joppa, praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain vessel descending, like a great linen sheet, let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.

units.la: 6 In quod cum intendissem oculos, animaduerti & vidi, &c. Adversus 18.
units.tr: 6 Fixing my eyes on it, I noticed and saw, etc. Against 18.

units.la: Tsi Lucas historiam de Cornelij conuersione prolixè describit, eandem tamen hic repetit. Causa, vt omnibus pateat gentes ex Dei decreto per Euangelium vocatas & in Ecclesiæ societate receptas esse. Erat autem hæc demonstratio necessaria, partim propter Iudæos, ne odium suum continuarent: partim vt qui ex gentibus crederent, suæ salutis essent certiores. Itaque non pigeat ea iterum audire, quæ Lucam repetere non piguit. Id verò fecit occasione eius, quod inter Iudæos accidit. Non potuit enim res ista diu latere, cum quod per se esset insolens, tum quòd Cornelius persona esset illustris.
units.tr: Although Luke describes at length the conversion of Cornelius, he nevertheless repeats it here. The purpose is that it be clear to all that the Gentiles were called through the gospel by God's decree and received into fellowship with the Church. This demonstration was necessary, partly on account of the Jews, so that they might not continue in their hatred, and partly so that those who believed from among the Gentiles might be more certain of their salvation. Therefore let us not be reluctant to hear again what Luke was not reluctant to repeat. He did so, however, on the occasion of what happened among the Jews. For the matter could not long remain hidden, both because in itself it was unusual and because Cornelius was a person of distinction.

units.la: Proponuntur autem duo hominum genera.
units.tr: Two kinds of men are set forth.

units.la: I. Apostoli & fratres, id est, verè Christiani. De his simpliciter dicitur, quod audierint gentes recipisse verbum Dei. Nec dicitur, eos aliquid reprehendisse. Licet ergo mysterium non intelligerent, nolunt tamen temerè iudicare de Petro, cuius fides omnibus nota erat. Imitemur, ne zelo nimio peccemus in charitatis legem.
units.tr: I. The apostles and brothers, that is, truly Christian people. Of these it is simply said that they heard the Gentiles had received the word of God. Nor is it said that they found fault with anything. So, although they did not understand the mystery, they were unwilling to judge Peter rashly, whose faith was known to all. Let us imitate them, lest through excessive zeal we sin against the law of charity.

units.la: Huius
units.tr: Of this:

units.la: Vt de Petri facto in dicarit Ec clesia? Huius est bene sperare, 1. Cor. 13. Peccata tegere, Prouerb. 10. 1 Pet. 4. At qui bene facta carpiunt, diaboli ingeniū referunt. Vide Iob. 1 2.
units.tr: How might the Church pass judgment on Peter's deed? It is characteristic of charity to hope well (1 Cor. 13). To cover sins (Prov. 10; 1 Pet. 4). But those who carp at good deeds reproduce the devil's disposition. See Job 1:2.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Locutionem, Gentes recepisse Dei verbum. Poterat dicere Christianos factos esse. Sed vult Christianismi notam exprimere & quomodo Christiani fiant. Verbum Dei enim recipiunt, qui agnoscunt pro Dei verbo, & in hoc transformantur, ut Dei imitatores sint. Vide 1. Thess 2. 1. Gal. 4. Hinc illa, Matt. 5 3. 12. Iac. 2. 1. Ioh. 2. Rom 12. Eph. 4 5. &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note the expression, "the Gentiles had received the word of God." He could have said that they had become Christians. But he wishes to express the mark of Christianity and how Christians are made. For they receive the word of God who acknowledge it as God's word and are transformed by it, so that they become imitators of God. See 1 Thess. 2; Gal. 4. Hence those sayings: Matt. 5:3, 12; Jas. 2:1; John 2; Rom. 12; Eph. 4:5, etc.

units.la: Arguuntur falsi, qui sic viuunt, ut Dei verbum propter ipsos male audiat, Mal. 1. Ideo ipsi quoque inglorij & infelices sunt, 1. Sam. 2.
units.tr: Those are rebuked who live in such a way that God's word is ill spoken of on their account (Mal. 1). Therefore they too become inglorious and unhappy (1 Sam. 2).

units.la: II. Qui erant ex Circumcisione, id est, qui cum Christiani dicerentur, adhuc legi erant addicti. Hi disceptant & accusant quasi scelus admiserit. Nimirum ad traditionem patrum & receptam consuetudinem respicientes. Vide Ioh. 4.
