units.la: 2. Quid illic fecerint? Colletti orabant. Fuerunt similes coetus etiam alibi, & quidem nocturni propter periculum. Hinc manárunt coetus antelucani veterum, qui Matutinas pepererfit.Sedxaxo{ΦαλΦ}ελ est.
units.tr: 2. What did they do there? They prayed, gathered together. Similar assemblies existed elsewhere too, and indeed by night because of the danger. From this sprang the early morning assemblies of the ancients, which gave birth to the Matins. But the Greek here is obscure.

units.la: ¶ Rursus autem obseruemus quae sint vera exercitia Christianorum, maximè quando pericula instant. Quia Christus vnitate gaudet (Iohan.17.) hanc coetibus crebris testentur, in quibus simul audiant verbum & precentur.Hoc Deus praecipit,Leuit.23.Deut.16.Prophetae, Ioel.2. Christus,Mart.18.Apostoli hos diligenter instituunt,1.Cor.11.14.
units.tr: ¶ Again, let us observe what are the true exercises of Christians, especially when dangers press. Since Christ delights in unity (John 17), let them bear witness to it by frequent gatherings, in which they hear the Word together and pray. God commands this (Lev. 23; Deut. 16); the prophets (Joel 2); Christ (Matt. 18); and the apostles diligently establish these (1 Cor. 11; 14).

units.la: Arguit nostri seculi mores, quando vix interdiu conuenimus. Dies vero noctes que inter pocula transigimus,Ifa.5. Si pericula vrgeant,multi execrantur & calumniantur,&c.
units.tr: This rebukes the manners of our age, when we scarcely meet even by day. We spend the days and nights over our cups (Isa. 5). If dangers press, many curse and slander, etc.

units.la: 3.Pulsanti non statim aperiunt,propter periculum. Prudentia opus est, Matt.10. Rhode agnita voce Petri prae gaudio non aperit, sed intus nuntiat. Hic aliqui negant,aliqui dicunt eius Angelum esse,&c. Elucet in his infirmitas sanctorum, & quam procliuis fit lapsus ad superstitiones.Noverant promissionem, Psam.34.91. Hinc error de binis Angelis, qui postea spiritum apparitiones peperit,&c. Quo Apostolos quoque imbutos fuisse patet. hîc & Matthæi 14. Lucæ 24. Discamus ergo ijs contenti esse, quæ Scripturæ tradunt, neque aliquid præterea admittamus.
units.tr: 3. They do not open at once to the one knocking, because of the danger. Prudence is needed (Matt. 10). Rhoda, recognising Peter's voice, is so glad that she does not open but announces it inside. Here some deny it, some say it is his angel, etc. The weakness of the saints shines forth in this, and how prone a fall is into superstitions. They knew the promise (Ps. 34; 91). Hence came the error about two angels, which afterwards gave rise to the notion of spirits appearing, etc. That the apostles too were imbued with this is clear, here and in Matt. 14 and Luke 24. Let us learn, therefore, to be content with what the Scriptures hand down, and to admit nothing beyond it.

units.la: Interim Nota ¶ Deum vota suorum non frustrari, sed plus ferè dare, quàm petant. Isti orant quidem pro Petro, sed vt confirmetur. Liberationem non possunt sperare. Sed illum restituit, vt videant, Deum nolle Ecclesiam suam destituere. Sic olim factum Abrahamo, Gen. 17. 21. 25. Iacob, Gen. 45. 46. Experimur sæpe. Simus ergo constantes, &c. Hab. 2. Si omnia fallant, dabitur tamen quod promissum, Isa. 64. 2. Cor. 4.
units.tr: Meanwhile note: ¶ that God does not frustrate the prayers of his people, but gives almost more than they ask. These men indeed prayed for Peter, but that he might be strengthened; they could not hope for his deliverance. Yet he restored him, so that they might see that God did not wish to abandon his Church. So it was once done for Abraham (Gen. 17; 21; 25), and for Jacob (Gen. 45; 46). We often experience it. Let us therefore be steadfast, etc. (Hab. 2). If all things deceive, yet what has been promised will be given (Isa. 64; 2 Cor. 4).

units.la: IV. Petrus rem omnem narrat, iubet vt nuntient Iacobo & aliis: inde se conferant alió: quod videret, se non posse illic subsistere sine Ecclesiæ totius periculo, neque velle Deum vt iam moreretur.
units.tr: 4. Peter tells the whole matter, bids them report it to James and the others, and then withdraws elsewhere, because he saw that he could not remain there without endangering the whole Church, nor did he wish God to have him die now.

units.la: Nota. ¶ 1. Beneficia Dei vulgari debere. Iubet hoc gratitudo, Psal. 50. 107. Hinc vocata illa Psal. 7. 22. 69. Hos. 14. Charitas item, vt alij quoque confirmentur & discant, Psa. 34. Vt item gaudeant nobis cum, qui propter nos doluerunt. Arguuntur, qui liberati nihil meminerunt ¶ 2. Licere interdum fugere. Sic Christus iubet, Mat. 10. Errant, qui ministros temere periclitari volunt.
units.tr: Note: ¶ 1. Benefits of God ought to be made widely known. Gratitude commands this (Ps. 50; 107). Hence those psalms which are called thanksgivings (Ps. 7; 22; 69; Hos. 14). Charity likewise, so that others too may be confirmed and learn (Ps. 34), and that those who grieved on our account may rejoice with us. Those are rebuked who, once delivered, remember nothing. ¶ 2. It is sometimes lawful to flee. So Christ commands (Matt. 10). They err who wish ministers to expose themselves rashly to danger.

units.la: V. Catastrophe. Milites turbantur,vt qui scirent,quo cum ipsis res esset. Herodes insanit, quaestiones adhibet, sic volente Deo vt miraculi veritas innotescat. Sic Matth.28. Iubet duci & occidi.
units.tr: 5. The outcome. The soldiers are thrown into confusion, as those who knew how matters stood with them. Herod rages, applies examinations, so that, God willing, the truth of the miracle might become known. So in Matt. 28. He orders them to be led away and put to death.

units.la: Ita impij non emendantur Dei operibus, sed irritantur. Pharao, Exod 5.8.9.14. Ita impletur quod habes Isa.6.
units.tr: Thus the wicked are not corrected by the works of God, but are provoked. Pharaoh (Exod. 5; 8; 9; 14). So what you have in Isa. 6 is fulfilled.

units.la: Interim Not. Quid maneat eos, qui tyrannis seruiunt contra Christum & huius seruos. Communicant tyrannidi & peccatis alienis, & ideo puniuntur. Sic Aegyptij cum suo Pharaone, Exodi 14. Coniurati cum Abfolomo, 1. Samuelis 18. Cum Saule item 1. Samuel 31. Quid ergo fiat ijs, qui se mancipant alienigenis? Exempla hodie habemus. Nullum bellum a maioribus nostris tantis cladibus gestum, vt nunc in Gallijs. Moueat nos, ne communices. Si non potes paci consulere, tuer, abstine saltem a Christi Domini, Psal. 105. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile note: what awaits those who serve tyrants against Christ and his servants. They share in the tyranny and in the sins of others, and therefore are punished. So the Egyptians with their Pharaoh (Exod. 14); the conspirators with Absalom (2 Sam. 18); likewise with Saul (1 Sam. 31). What then happens to those who give themselves over to foreigners? We have examples today. No war waged by our forefathers has been carried on with such calamities as now in France. Let it move us not to communicate in it. If you cannot provide for peace, at least keep yourself from the things of Christ the Lord (Ps. 105). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CIII.

units.la: 20 Herodes autem infenso animo erat in Tyrios & Sidonios: at illi concorditer venerunt ad eum, & persuasu Blasto, qui praerat cubiculo Regis, petebant.
units.tr: 20 Now Herod was angry with the Tyrians and Sidonians, but they came to him together and, having won over Blastus, who was in charge of the king's bedchamber, they sought peace, because their country was fed from the king's land.

units.la: Cataftrophe. Fideles iam patientur, impij turbantur. bant pacem: eo quòd aleretur regio ipso-rum ex Regis agro.
units.tr: Catastrophe. The faithful will suffer, the impious are troubled. They sought peace because their region was supplied from the king's territory.

units.la: 21 Statuto autem die, Herodes indutus veste regia, & consedens pro tri-bunali concionabatur ad eos:
units.tr: 21 On an appointed day Herod, clothed in royal robes and seated on the judgement seat, addressed them.

units.la: 22 Populus verò acclamabat, Vox Dei, & non hominis.
units.tr: 22 And the people shouted, "The voice of God, and not of man!"

units.la: 23 Illico verò percussit eum Angelus Domini, eò quòd non dedisset glo-riam Deo, & erosus a vermibus, expi-rauit.
units.tr: 23 Immediately the angel of the Lord struck him, because he had not given glory to God, and he was eaten by worms and breathed his last.

units.la: 24 Sermo autem Domini crescebat ac multiplicabatur.
units.tr: 24 But the word of the Lord grew and multiplied.

units.la: 25 Barnabas autem & Paulus Hierosolyma reuersi sunt Antiochiam, expleto ministerio, simul etiam assum-pto Iohanne, qui cognominabatur Mar-cus.
units.tr: 25 Barnabas and Paul returned from Jerusalem to Antioch, their ministry completed, and they took with them John, who was surnamed Mark.

units.la: VT Deus Ecclesiam persecutionibus exercet: Ita grauiter eos punit, qui hanc impiè oppugnant, Zach.2.12. Psal.2.
units.tr: As God exercises the Church with persecutions, so he severely punishes those who impiously attack it: Zech. 2:12; Ps. 2.

units.la: Exemplum memorabile est in Herode. Is partim scismatis metu, partim vt Iudæis gratificetur, persecutionem instituit: & succedit primus conatus. Iacobum enim tollit, Petrum capit, &c. Sed mox Chri-stus vindicem agit, qui Petrũ miraculo-sè liberat, pœnam transfert in milites, &c. Psalmo 7. Herodem abducit Cæsaream, vbi
units.tr: Herod is a memorable example. Partly from fear of schism, partly to gratify the Jews, he began a persecution, and his first attempt succeeds: he seizes James and arrests Peter, etc. But soon Christ acts as avenger, who miraculously frees Peter, transfers the punishment to the soldiers, etc. (Ps. 7). He takes Herod away to Caesarea, where

units.la: { } vbi eum etiam vlciscitur, & tunc quidem, quando felicisimus videbatur. Videamus singula.
units.tr: where he also takes vengeance on him, and indeed then, when he seemed most fortunate. Let us look at the particulars.

units.la: I. Bellum meditatur Tyrijs & Sido-nijs.Causa fuit haud dubie ambitio & aua ritia, qua Monarchae non possunt ferre liberas ciuitates in vicinia opibus florentes,quales istae fuerunt,Ifaiae 23.Ezech.26 27. 28. Quia autem illis opus erat amicitia Herodis, supplices ei fiunt per Blastum, quem in suas partes pertraxerant, non sine maximis donis.
units.tr: I. He plans war on the Tyrians and Sidonians. The cause was undoubtedly ambition and greed, which monarchs cannot bear: free cities flourishing in wealth nearby, such as these were (Isa. 23; Ezek. 26, 27, 28). But since they needed Herod's friendship, they became suppliants to him through Blastus, whom they had won over to their side, and not without very great gifts.

units.la: Nota. §1. Mores regum. Nunquam suis finibus continenti sunt. Simile auaro-rum, Ifaiae 5. Hinc bella non necessaria. Cumque ipsi omnibus imperare velint, fe re a vilisimis reguntur: qualis hic Blastus fuit. Apud Imper.liberti,&c.Hodie prophani & moriones fere omnia possunt. His deinde oportet omnes fieri supplices: quae causa est,ut omnia sint venalia. Ideo olim Deus dissuasit Regibus, 1. Sam.8.Agnoscamus nos donum Dei, obe diamus bonis legibus & libertatem tuea mur. Vide Pf.118.146. Ne item iuuemus tyrannos.Ingens scelus.
units.tr: Note. §1. The manners of kings. They are never content within their own borders, like misers (Isa. 5). Hence wars that are not necessary. And while they wish to command everyone, they are themselves governed by the lowest men, as this Blastus was. Among the emperors the freedmen... Today profane men and buffoons can do almost everything. Then everyone must become a suppliant to them, and this is why everything is for sale. Therefore God long ago dissuaded kings (1 Sam. 8). Let us acknowledge the gift of God, obey good laws and defend our liberty. See Ps. 118, 146. Likewise, let us not help tyrants. A huge crime.

units.la: §2. Hoc successu vsum Herodem, qui Ecclesiam aggressus Martyrum sanguine se polluerat.Dignus erat,quem Deus per ludium.
units.tr: §2. Herod, who had used this success, having attacked the Church and polluted himself with the blood of martyrs, deserved to be struck down from heaven by God, as Saul was (Acts 9).

units.la: deret coelitus,vt Saul,Act.9. Sed ecce vrbes opulentissimae se eiobmittunt. Hoc est,quod multos offendit, Psal.73. Iere.12. Habac.1. Malach.3. Sed obseruemus impios tunc quoque Dei prouidentia regi, Iob.1.2. Ita vero hic permittit, vt grauius cadant, Prouerb.16. Estque momentanea illorum felicitas, Psalm.37. Isaiae 40. Ne ergo offendamur eorum succesibus qui eis exitio sunt. Quod in praesenti accidit.
units.tr: But behold, the wealthiest cities submit themselves. This is what offends many (Ps. 73; Jer. 12; Hab. 1; Mal. 3). But let us observe that the impious are ruled by God's providence even then (Job 1, 2). Yet here he permits it so that they fall more heavily (Prov. 16), and their happiness is momentary (Ps. 37; Isa. 40). So let us not be offended by the successes of those who are their own ruin, which is what is happening at present.

units.la: II. Ebrius enim fortuna Herodes,diu nos quoque honores affectat. Vide Iosephum 19.Cap.7.
units.tr: II. For Herod, drunk with good fortune, sought honours for himself too. See Josephus, Antiquities 19, ch. 7.

units.la: Not. Vanitatem vulgi, quae docet dignos fuisse hoc principe. Nota erat aui impietas,Matth.2. Patrui libido, Mar.6. Huius praesidia, & quibus artibus venerat ad regnum. Insolentia in vicinos. Attamen ita ei blandiuntur. Fit idem hodie & titulis vanissimis inebriantur spurcissimi tyranni. Abbates item. Digni, qui aliquando illis rursus subijciamur, Apoc.18.
units.tr: Note the vanity of the crowd, which shows that this prince was thought worthy of such flattery. His impiety was known from his grandfather (Matt. 2), the lust of his uncle (Mark 6). Note his guards, and by what arts he came to the kingdom, and his insolence toward his neighbours. Yet they flatter him thus. The same happens today: the most filthy tyrants are intoxicated by the most empty titles, and abbots likewise. We deserve to be made subject to them again at some time (Rev. 18).

units.la: III. Poena. Percusitillum Angelus vi sibiliter: & dolore cruciatus confessus est veritatem. Causa: quod non dedisset gloriam Deo. 1. Regnum Caesari tulit acceptum(contra Psal.113.) cui ludos fecit.2.Ecclesiam persecutus est. 3. Admisit laudes blasphemas.
units.tr: III. Punishment. The angel struck him violently, and, tortured by pain, he confessed the truth. Cause: because he had not given glory to God. (1) He received the kingdom as a gift from Caesar, against Ps. 113, for whom he staged games. (2) He persecuted the Church. (3) He accepted blasphemous praises.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Quid exspectent, qui contra Deum efferuntur. Hunc sibi hostem faciunt, 1. Pet 5. Prouerb. 6. Lucae 1. Is deinde pudefacit eos. Pharao, Exod. 5.14. Philistrates, 1. Sam. 5.6. Sanherib. Isa. 10.36.37. Nabuchodonozor. Dan. 4. Balthazar. Isa. 14. Dan. 5. Hodierna exempla. Singuli ergo intra suos fines sese contineant. Sciant se omnia a Deo habere (1. Cor. 4.) & recte vtantur. ¶ 2. Quam noxij sint adulatores principibus? Natura nobis ipsis placemus, etiam in peccatis, Psalm. 36. Si adulatores accedant, excaecamur prorsus, & veri impatientes efficimur. Itaque reges potentisimi sic pereunt. Vide Achabum, 1. Reg. 21.22. Zedechiam cum suis, &c. Et contra Dauidem, 2. Sam. 12. Ezechiam, Isaiae 39. Discant qui in magistratu sunt, ferre monitores fidos. Alioqui fit, quod habetur Isa. 3.
units.tr: NOTE. §1. What those can expect who exalt themselves against God. They make him their enemy (1 Pet. 5; Prov. 6; Luke 1). He then shames them: Pharaoh (Ex. 5, 14); the Philistine lords (1 Sam. 5, 6); Sennacherib (Isa. 10:36, 37); Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 4); Belshazzar (Isa. 14; Dan. 5). Modern examples likewise. Therefore let each keep within his own bounds, let them know that they have everything from God (1 Cor. 4), and use it rightly. §2. How harmful flatterers are to princes. By nature we please ourselves, even in sins (Ps. 36). If flatterers approach, we are utterly blinded and become impatient of the truth. Thus the most powerful kings perish: see Ahab (1 Kings 21, 22), Zedekiah with his men, etc. Against this, David (2 Sam. 12) and Hezekiah (Isa. 39). Let those in magistracy learn to bear faithful admonishers, otherwise what is said in Isa. 3 comes to pass.

units.la: Redit ad Ecclesiae historiam, vt constet Regni Christi huic per Herodem nihil decessisse. Sermo sti propagat Dei crescebat & propagabatur indies Id in sequentibus exponet, ad quae transitum facit Pauli & Barnabae mentione. Misi Ierosolymam nunc redeunt, &c.
units.tr: He returns to the history of the Church, to show that nothing was taken from Christ's kingdom by Herod: "The word of God grew and spread daily." He will explain this in what follows, to which he passes with the mention of Paul and Barnabas: sent to Jerusalem, they now return, etc.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Ecclesiam tyrannis omnibus esse superstitem. Nascitr ex Dei verbo & eodem regitur, 1. Petri 1. Ioh. 10. At hoc aeternum manet, Isaiae 40. pereuntibus qui huic reluctantur. Docent hoc omnium gentium historiae, quando omnia regna interierunt, vbi ad hunc lapidem impegerunt. Vbi nunc Roma illa aeterna? Idem potest dici de priuatis personis. In summa, Christi regnum aeternum est, Dan. 2. Luc. 1. Psal. 72. 89. 2. 46. &c. Huic ergo adhaereamus constanter. Oremus.
units.tr: NOTE. The Church survives all tyrants. It is born of God's word and is governed by the same (1 Pet. 1; John 10). But this remains eternal (Isa. 40), while those who resist it perish. The histories of all nations teach this, when all kingdoms have perished that dashed themselves against this stone. Where now is that eternal Rome? The same can be said of private persons. In sum, Christ's kingdom is eternal (Dan. 2; Luke 1; Ps. 72, 89, 2, 46, etc.). Let us therefore cling to it constantly. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XIII. HOMILIA CIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII. HOMILY CIV.

units.la: ERant autem quidam in Ecclesia, quae Antiochiae erat, prophetae & doctors, Barnabas & Simon, qui vocabatur Niger, & Lucius Cyrenaeus, & Manaen, qui cum Herode tetrarcha enutritus fuerat, & Saulus.
units.tr: And there were in the Church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers: Barnabas, and Simeon who was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

units.la: 2 Quum autem illi ministrarent Domino & ieiunarent, dixit Spiritus Sanctus. Segregate mihi Barnabam & Saulum in opus ad quod eos vocaui.
units.tr: 2 While they ministered to the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said: Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.

units.la: 3 Tunc igitur quum ieiunassent et precati essent, & impositis eis manus, dimiserunt eos.
units.tr: 3 Then, when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.

units.la: 4 Ipsi igitur emissi a Spiritu San-cto. &o descenderunt Seleuciam, & illinc abnauigarunt Cyprum.
units.tr: 4 So they, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and from there sailed to Cyprus.

units.la: 5 Quumq; peruenissent Salamina, annuntiarunt Sermonem Dei in Synagogis Iudæorum: habebant autem etiam Iohannem ministrum.
units.tr: 5 And when they reached Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; they also had John as their minister.

units.la: DESCRIBITVR hoc & sequenti Capite, vt Euangelium gentibus promiscuè prædicari coeperit. Quia enim Iudæi hucusque soli Dei populus habiti fuerant, ad hos quoque solos Euangelium pertinere videbatur: & quæ in Cornelio & Antiochenis acciderant, priuilegio quodam facta videri poterant. Nunc ergo salutis verbum promiscuè gentibus prædicatur, vt constet Christum esse, de quo olim prædictum, Gen. 49.22. Isa. 2.42.40. Psal. 2.7z. ¶ Ne quis tamen hic aliquid putet priua to consilio factum, diligenter narratur illorum vocatio & missio, quorum opera Deus vti voluit. Singula ergo videamus.
units.tr: This passage, and the one that follows in the chapter, describes how the gospel began to be preached indiscriminately to the Gentiles. For since the Jews had hitherto been regarded as the only people of God, it seemed that the gospel belonged to them alone; and what had happened with Cornelius and the Antiochenes could be seen as a kind of special privilege. Now, therefore, the word of salvation is preached to the Gentiles without distinction, so that it is clear that Christ is the one foretold long ago, Gen. 49.22, Isa. 2.42.40, Psal. 2.7z. ¶ Lest anyone think that this was done on a private plan, the calling and sending of those by whose work God chose to act is narrated carefully. Let us therefore look at each point.

units.la: I. Ecclesia Antiochena describitur, ex qua Barnabas & Paulus prodierunt, vt ex eo constet, hic nihil temere factum esse. Fuerunt illic Prophetæ. Ita dicuntur non modo qui futura prædicunt, sed etiam ido nei Scriptorum veterum interpretes, 1.
units.tr: I. The church of Antioch is described, the church from which Barnabas and Paul went forth, so that it may be clear that nothing here was done rashly. There were prophets there. The name is given not only to those who foretell the future but also to skilled interpreters of the ancient Scriptures, 1 Cor. 14. 11.

units.la: Cor.14. 11. Vtriq; autem illic fuerunt, vt patet, Act.11. Doctores, scilicet ordinarij, siue pastores. Vnde apparet, Antiochiae non modo Ecclesiam vulgarem, sed scholam quoq; fuisse, ex qua doctores emitte-bantur ad alios.
units.tr: Both men were there, as is plain from Acts 11, as teachers, that is, ordinary teachers or pastors. Hence it appears that Antioch was not only a common church but also a school, from which teachers were sent out to others.

units.la: NOTA. Quod ab his Ecclesia Antiochena commendatur, non a potentia, opi-bus, &c. Hoc ergo praecipuum est in Ecclesijs. Per Verbi praecones enim generan-tur, aedificantur & seruantur Ecclesiae, Ro. 10.1. Cor.3.4. Eph.4. Quia autem docendi facultas non omnibus miraculosé contin-git, studio & scholis opus est: quales semper in populo Dei fuerunt. Leuitarum vr-bes, Num.35. Iof.14 Scholae Prophetarum 1. Sam.10.19 2. Reg.2.4 6. Acculantur item illarum corruptores, Amos 2. Iulianus. Vi-derunt hoc pij Reges, qui collegia insti-tuerunt. Et huc pertinet illud, Isa.49.
units.tr: NOTE. The Antiochene church is commended by these men, not by power, wealth, and the like. This, therefore, is the chief thing in churches. For churches are begotten, built up and preserved through the heralds of the Word: Rom. 10. 1; 1 Cor. 3. 4; Eph. 4. Since, however, the ability to teach is not given miraculously to everyone, study and schools are needed, such as have always existed among the people of God: the cities of the Levites, Num. 35; Josh. 14; the schools of the prophets, 1 Sam. 10. 19; 2 Kings 2. 4; 6. Those who corrupt these schools are also accused, Amos 2; and Julian. Godly kings saw this and set up colleges. To this belongs also that passage, Isa. 49.

units.la: § 2. Nomina recensentur, vt constet Deum nosse suos seruos, Lu.10. Inter hos autem fuit Manaes σωτρόφος Herodis, Nobilis nimirum & aulicus. Exemplum bonitatis Dei & liberae electionis. Habet Deus vbiq; suos, quos vocat quando & vbi vult, Ioh.3. Sic Naaman, 2. Reg.5. Da-niel & socij, Dan.2.3. Abdemel, Ierem.3.8. Nicodemus, Ioh.3.7. Ioseph Arimathaeus, Matth.27.Æthyops,Aßo.8.Cæsaris familia,Philip.4. Ita Deus hostes suos ludificat,Psal.2.
units.tr: Let us, moreover, imitate the faith of this Manaen, like that of Moses, Heb. 11, Exod. 2. Those who wish to be saved in Christ ought to do the same. Proof from comparisons, Luke 14, Matt. 16. Those are reproved who wish both to please the world and at the same time to live with Christ, 1 John 5.2, etc., Gal. 1, James 4.

units.la: Imitemur autem nos fidem istius Manaen,similem Mosis,Heb.11.Exod.2.Idem faciant oportet, qui volunt in Christo seruari.Proba à comparatis,Luc.14. Mat 16. Arguuntur,qui & mundo placere volunt, & Christo simul viuere,1.Ioh.5.2.&c.Gal.1.Iac.4.
units.tr: Let us imitate the faith of this Manaen, who was like Moses, Heb. 11; Exod. 2. Those who wish to be saved in Christ ought to do the same. Proof from comparisons: Luke 14; Matt. 16. Those are rebuked who wish both to please the world and at the same time to live with Christ: 1 John 5. 2, etc.; Gal. 1; James 4.

units.la: II. Exponitur vocatio & missio duorum Apostolorum ad gentes: Ministrantibus in publico cœtu,dixit Spiritus: Segregate mihi,&c. Ergo ex Dei iussu hoc factum.
units.tr: II. The calling and sending of the two apostles to the Gentiles is set forth: "While they were ministering in the public assembly, the Spirit said: Separate me," etc. Therefore this was done by God's command.

units.la: No T. 1. Authorem ministerij esse Spiritum sanctum. Sic infrà 20. Non sunt ergo legitimi ministri, nisi qui à Deo vocentur, Rom.10.2.Cor.2.3. Ideo Prophetæ & Apostoli toties suam vocationem indicant. Interim obseruemus, quòd per Ecclesiam eos ordinari voluit Deus, quos ipse iam segregauerat,Act.9.Gal.1.Factum hoc qui dem,vt maior esset horum authoritas. Simul autem docemur, ordine opus esse in Ecclesia,ne qui se intrudant,Heb.5.1.Cor.14. Tales semper Deo displicuerunt, Nu.16.Ier.23.Et historiæ docent,inordinatam ministrorum electionem semper turbas dederunt.
units.tr: Note 1. The Holy Spirit is the author of the ministry. So below, at verse 20. Therefore those are not lawful ministers unless they are called by God: Rom. 10. 2; 2 Cor. 2. 3. For this reason the prophets and apostles so often point out their calling. Meanwhile, let us observe that God wished those whom he had already set apart to be ordained by the Church, Acts 9; Gal. 1. This was done indeed so that their authority might be greater. At the same time we are taught that order is needed in the Church, so that men do not thrust themselves in, Heb. 5. 1; 1 Cor. 14. Such men have always displeased God, Num. 16; Jer. 23. And histories teach that disorderly election of ministers has always brought disturbances.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quomodo ordinârint istos? Ieiu-n ârunt & orârunt. Atqui non poterant sal-li in personis. Sed sciunt spiritus donis o-pus esse in re maximi momenti. Deinde manus imponunt, vt se Deo consecratos scirent. Ita agendum hodie, quoad mini-stros & magistratus.
units.tr: 2. How did they ordain these men? They fasted and prayed. Yet they could not be deceived about the persons, but they knew that in a matter of the greatest moment there was need of the gifts of the Spirit. Then they laid on hands, so that they might know themselves consecrated to God. So it should be done today, both for ministers and for magistrates.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui ista tractant per ludi-brium, & inter pocula. Simile nauigare vo-lentium.
units.tr: Those are rebuked who treat these things as a joke and handle them over cups of wine. It is like the conduct of those who wish to set sail.

units.la: III. Quid illi? ¶ 1. Protinus accinguntur. Argumentū magni zeli. Multa obstabant. Romani Imperij potétia, Philosophi. Vul-gi mores in tuendis patrijs superstitioni-bus, Act 16. 17. Sed nihil horum istos po-test retinere. Sic olim Apostoli alij, Matt. 4. 9. Imitentur omnes in sua vocatione. Deus procrastinatores non fert, Exo. 3 4. Luc. 9.
units.tr: III. What did they do? 1. They immediately girded themselves for the work. This is a sign of great zeal. Many things stood in their way: the power of the Roman empire, the philosophers, and the customs of the common people in defending their ancestral superstitions, Acts 16; 17. But none of these could hold them back. So once did the other apostles, Matt. 4; 9. Let all imitate them in their own calling. God does not tolerate procrastinators, Exod. 3; Luke 9.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quò abierunt? Seleuciam, quæ in vicinia erat. Inde traiecerunt Salaminam in Cyprum, patriam Barnabæ, Act. 4. Insu-la fertilissima & veneri sacra, quæ illic or-ta ferebatur propter luxum, &c. Est ergo hoc diuinæ bonitatis exemplum, quæ pec-catores quærit. Fatetur hoc Christus, Matthæi 9. 11. Luc. 15. Apostolus, 1. Tim. 1. Id nos soletur. Interim officij admoneat, ne deficiamus. Cyprus hodie infelicissima. Idem de illa dici potest, quod de Galilæis vrbibus, Mat. II.
units.tr: ¶ 3. What did they preach? The word of God. The whole reckoning of salvation is contained in this, and this alone ought to be preached even today. For the Church is the house of God, 1 Tim. 3. Therefore only the voice of God should sound in it. So was the command given to the Prophets and Apostles, Ezek. 3, Jer. 1, Matt. 28, Gal. 1. It is an inexcusable impiety to thrust upon others anything else, Jer. 23.

units.la: ¶ 3. Quid prædicârunt? Verbum Dei. Hoc continetur tota salutis ratio. Et hoc vnû prædicari debet etiam hodie. Est enim Ec clefia domus Dei, 1 Timot. 3. Solius ergo Dei vox in illa sonet. Sic mandatum Prophetis & Apostolis, Ezech. 3. Iere. 1. Matt. 28. Gal. 1. Impietas inexcusabilis aliud obtrudere, Iere. 23.
units.tr: 3. What did they preach? The word of God. The whole account of salvation is contained in this, and this alone ought to be preached even today. For the Church is the house of God, 1 Tim. 3. Therefore only the voice of God should sound in it. So was the command given to the prophets and apostles: Ezek. 3; Jer. 1; Matt. 28; Gal. 1. It is inexcusable impiety to thrust anything else upon the people, Jer. 23.

units.la: ¶ 4. Vbi? In Synagoga Iudæorum. Etsi enim missi essent ad gentes, seruari tamen debuit ordo (Act. 1. Rom. 1.) & captanda occasio. In eum finem enim Deus tunc Iudæos voluit dispersos esse per omnes gentes. Vide Theodoretum de Prouidentia, lib. 10. Agnoscamus bonitatem Dei credamus & Oremus.
units.tr: 4. Where? In the synagogue of the Jews. For although they had been sent to the Gentiles, the proper order ought still to be kept (Acts 1; Rom. 1), and the opportunity seized. For to this end God then willed the Jews to be scattered through all nations. See Theodoret, On Providence, book 10. Let us acknowledge the goodness of God, believe, and pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CV.
units.tr: Homily CV.

units.la: 6 Peragrata verò insula Paphum vsque, invenerunt quendam magnum Pseudoprophetam Iudæum, cui nomen erat Bariesus.
units.tr: 6 Having traversed the island as far as Paphos, they found a certain great Jewish false prophet, whose name was Bar-Jesus.

units.la: 7 Qui erat cum Proconsule Sergio Paulo, viro prudente. Hic aduocatis Barnaba & Saulo, efflagitauit audire Sermonem Dei.
units.tr: 7 He was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a prudent man. Summoning Barnabas and Saul, the proconsul desired to hear the word of God.

units.la: 8 Obsistebat autem eis Elymas, id est, magus (ita enim explicatur nomen eius) quaerens auertere proconsulem a fide.
units.tr: 8 But Elymas opposed them, that is, the magician (for so his name is explained), seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

units.la: 9 Saulus autem (qui & Paulus) repletus Spiritu sancto, intentis in eum oculis.
units.tr: 9 But Saul (who is also Paul), filled with the Holy Spirit, fixed his eyes on him.

units.la: 10 Dixit, O plene omni dolo, & omni maleficentia, fili diaboli, hostis omnis iustitiae, non cessabis pervertere vias Domini rectas?
units.tr: 10 He said: "O you who are full of all deceit and all malice, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease to pervert the straight ways of the Lord?"

units.la: 11 Nunc igitur ecce, manus Domini aduersum te: eris, caecus, non videns Solem ad tempus. Illico vero incidit in eum caligo & tenebrae: & circumiens quaerebat qui ipsum manu duceret.
units.tr: 11 "Now therefore, behold, the hand of the Lord is against you: you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time." Immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and going about he sought someone to lead him by the hand.

units.la: 12 Tunc Proconsul quum vidisset quod factum fuerat, credidit, perculsus super doctrina Domini.
units.tr: 12 Then the proconsul, when he saw what had happened, believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

units.la: DAuid de Christo vaticinans, ait: Dominabitur in medio inimicorum, Psal. 110. Innuit regnum quidem habiturum, sed perpetuis assultibus obnoxium: quia durat perpetuo inimicitia: de qua Gen. 3. Exempla huius multa vidimus eorum, qui aperta vi pugnârunt, contra quos Christus victor fuit. Sequitur nouum certamen Magi, qui imposituris agit, cum iam omnia confecta viderentur. Memorabilis historia, quæ docet, qui impostorum artes & mores sint: vt item cum illis sit agendum.
units.tr: David, prophesying of Christ, says: "He will rule in the midst of his enemies" (Ps. 110). He signifies that he would indeed have a kingdom, but one exposed to perpetual assaults, because enmity lasts forever, from which we date it back to Gen. 3. We have seen many examples of those who fought with open force, and against whom Christ was victor. There follows a new contest with a magus, who works by deceit when everything seems already accomplished. It is a memorable history, which teaches what the arts and manners of impostors are, and how one must deal with them likewise.

units.la: I. Occasio. Cùm totam Cypr. impleuisset Euangelio, res ad Proconsulem deferentur. Is Apostolos accersit, vt eos audiat, ipse ethnicus, ergo etsi ethnicus esset, veritatis tamen amans fuit, &c.
units.tr: I. The occasion. When he had filled the whole of Cyprus with the gospel, the matter was reported to the proconsul. He summons the apostles that he may hear them. He himself was a gentile; therefore, even though he was a gentile, he nonetheless loved the truth, etc.

units.la: Nota. 1. Deum in quouis hominum genere habere suos, quos sæpe tunc vocat, quando perijsse videntur. Hic à puero fuit gentilis. Nunc in Magum Iudæorum incidit. Quis ergo eum curæ putaret esse Deo? Sed invenit iam perditum Christus: & omnino facit quod habetur, Luc. 15. Ioh. 16. Discimus nos non debere temere de aliquo desperare.
units.tr: Note. 1. That God has his own in every kind of men, whom he often calls when they seem to have perished. This man was a gentile from boyhood. Now he falls in with a Jewish magus. Who then would think God cared for him? But Christ finds the lost one, and altogether does what is written (Luke 15; John 16). We learn not to despair rashly of anyone.

units.la: 2. Boni & pij magistratus exemplum. Veritatis amans est. Non damnat inaudi-tos, &c. Hunc imitari debebant hodie principes. Sed plerique damnant doctrinam & religionem, quam ignorant. Sed meminerint, ignorantia se non excusari, Psal. 2. Sunt enim ex eorum numero, de quibus Ioh. 3.
units.tr: 2. An example of a good and pious magistrate. He loves the truth. He does not condemn those he has not heard, etc. Rulers today ought to imitate him. But most condemn a doctrine and a religion which they do not know. Yet let them remember that ignorance does not excuse them (Ps. 2). For they belong to the number of those of whom John 3 speaks.

units.la: II. Aduersarius describitur, qui prædicantibus se opponit: nimirum, quod vide quid ret, sibi porro non fore locum. Ideo nihil non fecit, vt Christi causam impediret.
units.tr: II. The adversary is described, who opposes those who preach: namely, as you see, because he thought there would be no place left for himself. Therefore he left nothing undone to hinder the cause of Christ.

units.la: Hic autem mores impostorum obseruerimus. ¶ 1. Nomen vsurpat à Iesu, quasi Filius Seruatoris, adeoq; Seruator fit. Est ergo ex eorum numero, de quibus Matt. 24. Proprium hoc impostoribus, quod Dei nomen praetexunt. Olim Pseudoprophetae, 1. Reg. 22. 1 Ierc. 23. & 28. Mahumet. Antichristus, 2. Thess. 2. Impletur hodie, quando inter multos alios exorti Iesuitae. Vide 2. Cor. 11. In primis 1. Ioh. 4.
units.tr: Here let us observe the manners of impostors. 1. He usurps the name of Jesus, as if he were the Son of the Saviour, and so makes himself a saviour. He is therefore of the number of those of whom Matt. 24 speaks. It is characteristic of impostors that they pretend the name of God. Formerly there were false prophets (1 Kings 22; Jer. 23 and 28); Mahomet and Antichrist (2 Thess. 2). It is fulfilled today, when, among many others, the Jesuits have arisen. See 2 Cor. 11, and especially 1 John 4.

units.la: ¶ 2. Proconsuli indiuulfè adhaeret. Idem impostores omnes quaerunt, vt principibus sint familiares: partim vt tuti sint, partim vt horum exemplo alij trahantur. Sic olim, 1. Reg. 18. 19. 22. Ita creuerunt Pontifices Romani. Et hodie Cardinales in Regum aulis sunt, Monachi diuitum familijs sese insinuant, &c. Tu disce supe&tos habere.
units.tr: ¶ 2. He clings to the proconsul in an underhanded way. All impostors seek the same thing, to be intimate with princes: partly so that they may be safe, partly so that others may be drawn by their example. So it was formerly (1 Kings 18, 19, 22). Thus the Roman pontiffs grew great. And today cardinals are in the courts of kings, monks insinuate themselves into the households of the rich, etc. Learn to hold such men under suspicion.

units.la: ¶ 3. Finis enim illis propositus est, vt à fide auertant, & sibi mancipent, & regnum suum stabiliant. Tu libertatem tuere, quam Christus nobis acquisiuit, Gal. 5. 1. Cor. 7.
units.tr: ¶ 3. For the purpose set before them is to turn people away from the faith, to bind them to themselves, and to establish their own kingdom. You, defend the liberty that Christ won for us (Gal. 5; 1 Cor. 7).

units.la: III. Quid Paulus? Plenus Spiritu sancto. Praemittitur hoc, ne quid affectui demus, & vt sciamus, Dei spiritum talibus resistere. 2. Intentis in illum oculis. Intrepi dè ergo. Et sic oportet, ne se metui arbitrentur, & ideo ferociores fiant. 3. Describbit bit eum qui fit. Plene omni dolo. Veritatis praetextum admit. Et vere Magia nihil nisi dolus est, qui non constat, vbi veritas lucet, Exod 7. 8. Malitia. Quid enim nequius, quàm sub Dei nomine ludere, nec timere eius minas? Exod. 20. Fili diaboli, Opponit hoc eius nomini fictitio. Tales sunt omnes superbi atq; mendaces, Isa. 14. Ioh. 8 Hostis iustitiae omnis: quia extra Christum nulla est iustitia, 1 Cor. 1.2. Cor. 5. Qui ergo hunc nolunt, omnis iustitiae hostes sunt. Non effes. Incurabilis contumacia. Peruertere vias Domini rectas. Sunt haec reſtae, purae, &c. Hos. 14. Psal. 12. 19. 119. Homi num autem vitio fit, vt multis perplexae sint. His infert supplicij comminationem, sic tamen, vt sp em veniae reliquam faciat. Ita solet Deus, Iere. 18.
units.tr: III. What of Paul? Full of the Holy Spirit. This is put first, lest we ascribe anything to feeling, and so that we may know that the Spirit of God resists such men. 2. With eyes fixed on him: be fearless, then. And so it is proper, lest they think they are feared and therefore become fiercer. 3. He describes what sort of man he is: Full of all deceit. He admits a pretext of truth. And indeed magic is nothing but deceit, which cannot stand where the truth shines (Exod. 7, 8). Malice: for what is more wicked than to play with God's name and not to fear his threats? (Exod. 20.) Son of the devil, he opposes this to his feigned name. All the proud and lying are such (Isa. 14; John 8). Enemy of all righteousness: because outside Christ there is no righteousness (1 Cor. 1; 2 Cor. 5). Therefore those who will not have him are enemies of all righteousness. Will you not cease? Incurable obstinacy. Pervert the straight ways of the Lord. These ways are straight, pure, etc. (Hos. 14; Ps. 12, 19, 119). But it happens through men's fault that they become crooked for many. To these he adds a threat of punishment, yet in such a way as to leave the hope of pardon. So God is accustomed to do (Jer. 18).

units.la: In primis Notr. ¶ Vt agendum cum talibus, qui hodie palam regnant, & Dei nomen praetexunt, dolis miris agunt, & euer sa Christi iustitia, viam salutis intricant: deniq; omnia faciunt quę habentur 2. Pet. 2. Vide Apoc. 18.
units.tr: Especially note how one must deal with such people, who today reign openly and pretend the name of God, act with wonderful deceits, entangle the way of salvation and the pure righteousness of Christ, and finally do all the things that are written (2 Pet. 2). See Rev. 18.

units.la: IIII. Effectus. ¶ 1. Mulctatur Magus mox. Sic supra 5. Fuit hoc Apostolicae potestatis opus: de qua 2. Cor. 13. 1. Cor. 5. 1. Tim. 1. Ridiculi qui cum nihil posint, tamen sibi tantum arrogant. Interim obseruandum, quid omnes maneat impostores. Excecantur, si non corpore, certè animo, Isa. 6. Infames facti amittunt brachium carnale, Zachariae 11. Exempla sunt hodie. Sed nostri sunt isto miseriores, qui se caecos efficere non agnoscunt, neque quaerunt ducem, &c.
units.tr: IV. The effect. 1. The magus is at once punished. So also above, in chapter 5. This was a work of apostolic power (2 Cor. 13; 1 Cor. 5; 1 Tim. 1). Ridiculous are those who, though they can do nothing, nevertheless arrogate so much to themselves. Meanwhile it is to be observed what awaits all impostors. They are blinded, if not in body, certainly in mind (Isa. 6). Made infamous, they lose their carnal arm (Zech. 11). There are examples of this today. But our own men are more wretched than these, who do not recognize that they make themselves blind, nor seek a guide, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Proconf. credit atque admiratur vel magni facit doctrinam Christi. Ita filij Dei exemplis iudiciorum Dei emendantur, Psal. 58. Impij econtra, 2. Timoth. 3. Soletur autem, quòd Veritas vincit semper. Idem factum Scribis & Sacerdotibus, Lucae 2. Matth. 21, 22. Philosophis. Imò Imperatoribus & Regibus, sicuti praedictum, Isa. 8. Psalm 2. Omnis caro foenum, &c. Isa. 40. Psal. 33. Simus ergo fortes, & semper meminerimus eorum quae habentur, Rom. 8. Oremus.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The proconsul believes and marvels, or at least sets great store by the teaching of Christ. Thus the sons of God are corrected by the examples of God's judgments (Ps. 58). The wicked, on the contrary (2 Tim. 3). It is consoling, however, that truth always conquers. The same happened to the scribes and priests (Luke 2; Matt. 21, 22), and to philosophers. Indeed, it happened to emperors and kings, as was foretold (Isa. 8; Ps. 2). "All flesh is grass," etc. (Isa. 40; Ps. 33). Let us therefore be strong, and always remember what is written (Rom. 8). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CVI.

units.la: 13 Profecti autem Papho Paulus & qui cum eo erant, venerunt Pergen Pamphyliae urbem. Iohannes vero ascendens ab eis reuersus est Hierosolymam.
units.tr: 13 Now when Paul and those who were with him set sail from Paphos, they came to Perga, a city of Pamphylia. But John, leaving them, returned to Jerusalem.

units.la: 14 At ipsi quum perrexissent Perga, venerunt Antiochiam urbem Pisidiae, & ingressi Synagogam die Sabbathi, sederunt.
units.tr: 14 But they, departing from Perga, came to Antioch, a city of Pisidia, and going into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, they sat down.

units.la: 15 Post lectionem autem Legis & Prophetarum, miserunt Præfecti Synagogæ ad eos, dicentes: Viri fratres, si quis est in vobis sermo exhortationis ad populum, dicite.
units.tr: 15 And after the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying: Men and brethren, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, say on.

units.la: MVltis quidem operibus diuinam suam potentiam declarauit Christus, inter ea autem fere præcipuum est, quòd Apostolorum ministerio intra paucos annos totum orbem subiugauit. Quia enim nullis præsidijs instructi, (1.Cor.1.) res tantas confecerant, apparet hoc diuinæ virtutis opus fuisse, & Christum esse, de quo prædictum, Psalm.2.72.Isa.60.&c. Est hoc præcipuum, quod in Pauli & Barnabæ peregrinatione obseruetur. Emisi, vt Euangelium vbique prædicarent. Obstabant Romani, rerum Domini, Iudæi, 1. Thessal. Philosophi. Sed omnia perrumpunt, & primo statim conatu Cyprum sub iugant, & in Elyma ipsum quoque diabolum vincunt, vt vel inde appareat, Christum esse semen illud, de quo Gen.3. Sequitur quid porro fecerint.
units.tr: Christ declared his divine power by many works, but chief among them is that through the ministry of the Apostles he subdued the whole world within a few years. For although they were furnished with no protection (1 Cor. 1), they accomplished such great things. It is plain that this was a work of divine power, and that Christ is he of whom it was prophesied (Ps. 2, 72; Isa. 60, etc.). This is the chief thing to be observed in the journey of Paul and Barnabas. They were sent out so that they might preach the Gospel everywhere. The Romans, the lords of the world, the Jews (1 Thess. 2) and the philosophers stood in their way. But they break through everything, and at the first attempt they subdue Cyprus, and in Elymas they even overcome the devil himself, so that from this alone it appears that Christ is that Seed of which Genesis 3 speaks. Next follows what they did further.

units.la: I. In Pamphyliam traijciunt, & per mare et terras veniunt Pergen, Vbi haud dubiè etiam prædicarunt.
units.tr: I. They cross over into Pamphylia, and by sea and land they come to Perga, where without doubt they also preached.

units.la: NOT. Quod Cypro victa non cessant quasi officio omni defuncti, sed pergunt ad alia: eoqs plus se debere putant, quo se licius res succederat. Sic alibi Paulus, Ro. 15. Phil. 3. Ita agendum in negotio Christi, ad eius exemplu. Arguuntur, qui vbi vix coeperunt, deficiunt. Sed pergendum, Lucae 9. Matt. 24.
units.tr: NOTE. Having conquered Cyprus, they do not rest as if they had discharged all their duty, but press on to other things, and they think they owe so much more the more freely the matter has succeeded for them. So Paul elsewhere (Rom. 15; Phil. 3). So must we act in the business of Christ, after his example. Those are rebuked who give up as soon as they have scarcely begun. But one must press on (Luke 9; Matt. 24).

units.la: II. Accidit tristis casus, dum alios acquirunt, am ttunt Marcum, qui ipsis relictis redijt Hierosolymam, nimirum pertae sus laborum, &c. Act. 15. Videtur autem praetexuisse matrem, vt quidam, Matth. 8. Luc. 9.
units.tr: II. A sad mishap occurred: while they were gaining others, they lost Mark, who, leaving them, returned to Jerusalem, no doubt wearied of the labours, etc. (Acts 15). He seems to have pretended his mother's illness, as some do (Matt. 8; Luke 9).

units.la: ¶ Obseruemus semper defectores fore, & quo opus Domini interturbent. Nec enim otiatur Satan, (1. Pet. 5.) qui ne ab Apostolis quidem abstinuit, Luc. 22. Mar. 14. Matth. 26. Vide item Ioh. 6. Et Paulo postea cum Demade id accidit, &c. 2. Timo. 4. Nemo igitur in hominibus sperer, (Ps. 116. 146) neque hodie similibus offenda-tur, quando sunt vaticinia, &c. Act. 20. 1. Tim. 4. 2 Timo. 3. Apoc. 7. 8. Tu verbo Dei insiste, 1. Ioh. 2.
units.tr: ¶ Let us always observe that there will be deserters, and that they disturb the work of the Lord. For Satan does not rest (1 Pet. 5), and he did not spare even the Apostles (Luke 22; Mark 14; Matt. 26). See also John 6. Later the same thing happened to Paul with Demas, etc. (2 Tim. 4). Let no one therefore put his hope in men (Ps. 116, 146), nor be offended today by similar things, since these were foretold, etc. (Acts 20; 1 Tim. 4; 2 Tim. 3; Rev. 7, 8). Do you hold fast to the Word of God (1 John 2).

units.la: III. Quid Apostoli? Num ideo opus inceptum relinquunt? Minime. Imo peragratis Pamphyliae locis transeunt in Pisidiam, & veniunt Antiochiam, quae olim Caesarea fuit dicta, Plin. lib. 5. cap. 27. Ibi concionantur fortissimè.
units.tr: III. What did the Apostles do? Did they therefore abandon the work they had begun? By no means. Rather, having traversed the regions of Pamphylia, they pass over into Pisidia and come to Antioch, which was formerly called Caesarea (Pliny, bk. 5, ch. 27). There they preach most boldly.

units.la: NOT.¶ Non cessandum in officio propter alios, qui vel perfidè agunt, vel negligenter. Aliorum vitia nemine excusant. Et quia Domini causa est, poterit eamper nos agere, quicunq; simus. 1.Cor.1. Nes soli sumus, quando ab hominibus deserimur, Ioh.16. Psalm.27. Ioh.14 Matth.27.2. Tim.4. Applicent hoc sibi, qui in Magistra tu versantur. Meminerint se a Deo esse ordinatos, qui ipsis adsit. Rom.13. Psalm. 82. Obseruent exempla Dauidis, Josaphati, Ezechielis, &c. Plus proficient, quàm pos sint sperare.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ One must not give up one's duty because of others who act either treacherously or negligently. The faults of others excuse no one. And since the cause is the Lord's, it can be carried on through us, whoever we are (1 Cor. 1). We are not alone when we are deserted by men (John 16; Ps. 27; John 14; Matt. 27; 2 Tim. 4). Let those who are engaged in the magistracy apply this to themselves. Let them remember that they have been ordained by God, and that he is present to them (Rom. 13; Ps. 82). Let them observe the examples of David, Jehoshaphat, Ezekiel, etc. They will make more progress than they can hope.

units.la: IV. Quid autem factum Antiochiæ? ¶ 1. Sabbatho Synagogam ingrediuntur : nimirum docendi occasionem quærentes. Ita enim Iudæi solebant, &c.. Act.15. Idem soli. ergo prius Salaminæ fecerunt : &postea alibi. Et debent ita agere Veritatis minimè stri, non angulos quærere, &c. Ioh.3. Sicut Christus fecit, Luc.22. Ioh.18:
units.tr: IV. But what was done at Antioch? ¶ 1. On the Sabbath they enter the synagogue, obviously seeking an opportunity to teach. For the Jews were accustomed to do so, etc. (Acts 15). They had done the same before, at Salamis, and afterwards elsewhere. And those who serve the truth ought to act in this way, not to seek out corners, etc. (John 3). As Christ did (Luke 22; John 18).

units.la: Imprimis discimus, in populo Dei debere seruari ordinem quoad sacros cœtus, vt suo tempore & loco cogantur. Ideo Sabbathum institutum, Exo. 20.31. Leuit. 19.23. Numer. 15. Prophani nimis, qui negligunt aut contemnunt.
units.tr: First we learn that order must be kept among the people of God with regard to sacred assemblies, so that they gather at the proper time and place. For this reason the Sabbath was instituted: Exod. 20.31; Lev. 19.23; Num. 15. Those who neglect or despise these assemblies are too profane.

units.la: ¶2. Consederunt, cum aliis nimirum. Modestiæ hoc est, Erant missi a Deo. Non
units.tr: ¶2. They sat down, namely with the others. This is a mark of modesty. "They were sent by God." Not

units.la: Ohne Haus. tamen abutuntur suo priuilegio, vt extra ordinarie prosiliant ad docendum. Ordo enim seruari debet in Ecclesia.1.Corinth. 14.Arguuntur Anabaptistae,
units.tr: Without a house. Yet they do not abuse their privilege by rushing out of order to teach. For order ought to be kept in the Church: 1 Cor. 14. The Anabaptists are refuted here.

units.la: § 3.Antbiocheni quid? Habuerunt pro more lectionem ex Lege & Prophetis. Actor.15.Luc.4.'Accessit haud dubie interpretatio. Tandem Apostolis faciunt dicen di copiam. Discimus, quid in sacris debeat tractari? Dei verbum, quod in Scripturis habetur. Sic Deus instituit per Mosem, Leuit.23. Sic Esdras, Nehem. 8.9. Christus ipse, Luc.4. Et Paulus ministris Scripturam commendat.2.Tim.3:Errant, qui Legendas recitant,&c. Item qui verbum Dei lingua peregrina proponunt, contra illud 1.Cor.14.
units.tr: § 3. What did the Antiochenes do? They had, as usual, a reading from the Law and the Prophets (Acts 15; Luke 4). Without doubt an interpretation was added. Finally they gave the Apostles the opportunity to speak. We learn what ought to be treated in sacred assemblies: the Word of God, which is contained in the Scriptures. So God instituted through Moses (Lev. 23), so Ezra (Neh. 8, 9), Christ himself (Luke 4), and Paul commends Scripture to ministers (2 Tim. 3). Those err who recite legends, etc. Likewise those who set forth the Word of God in a foreign tongue, contrary to 1 Cor. 14.

units.la: § Obseruandum autem quod aiunt: Si quis est vobis Sermo exhortationis. Graeca vox consolationem quoque significat. Ita exprimitur finis, ad quem doctrina referri debet: nimirum, vt omnes aedificentur super verum fundamentum, & in eo constantes perseuerent. Vide 1.Cor.14.Non satis ergo est docuisse, sed istud accedat oportet. Idem obseruent etiam qui in sacris Dei verbum audiunt.
units.tr: § Note also what they say: If there is any word of exhortation among you. The Greek word [παράκλησις] also signifies comfort. In this way the end is expressed to which doctrine must be referred: namely, that all may be built up upon the true foundation and persevere constantly in it. See 1 Cor. 14. It is therefore not enough to have taught; this must be added. Let those also observe this who hear the Word of God in the sacred assemblies.

units.la: Quremus.
units.tr: Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA XCVII.
units.tr: HOMILY XCVII.

units.la: 16 Quum surrexisset igitur Paulus, manu silentio facto, ait, Viri Israelita, et qui timetis Deum, audite.
units.tr: 16 When Paul had risen, and with his hand had asked for silence, he said: Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.

units.la: 17 Deus populi huius Israel elegit patres nostros, et populum extulit, quum esset incola in terra Aegypti, et ex ea eduxit eos elato brachio.
units.tr: 17 The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and raised up the people when they were sojourners in the land of Egypt, and led them out of it with an outstretched arm.

units.la: 18 Et circiter quadraginta annorum tempus mores eorum pertulit in deserto.
units.tr: 18 And for about forty years he bore with their manners in the wilderness.

units.la: 19 Et quum deleuisset septem gentes in terra Chanaan, sorte distribuit eis terram eorum.
units.tr: 19 And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he distributed their land to them by lot.

units.la: 20 Et postea annis circiter quadringentis, quumquam quadraginta dedit iudices usque ad Samuelem Prophetam.
units.tr: 20 And afterwards, for about four hundred years, he gave them judges, until Samuel the prophet.

units.la: 21 Exinde petierunt Regem, dedit eis Deus Saul filium Cis, virum ex tribu Beniamin, annis quadraginta.
units.tr: 21 Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul, son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

units.la: Describet porro Lucas concionem Pauli habitam Antiochiae, estque haec prima, quam Spiritus sanctus literis mandari voluit, quod omnia Christi mysteria comprehendit, adeo ut ex hac de aliis omnibus possimus iudicare: partim quod hac spreta puluerem excusserunt, quod rarissimè factum est.
units.tr: Luke next describes Paul's sermon delivered at Antioch. This is the first sermon that the Holy Spirit wished to be committed to writing, because it embraces all the mysteries of Christ, so that from it we may judge all the others. It is also partly because, when this sermon was despised, they shook off the dust from their feet, which very rarely happened.

units.la: Status concionis, vt Iudæos a legis fiducia ad fidem Christi adducat: quod vt cómodiùs fiat,hoc ordine vtitur. 1. Quia prærogatiuis gloriabantur, nec putabant sibi alia salutis ratione opus esse,docet illos quicquid habeant, ex gratia habere propter Mesiam patribus promissum. Hunc ergo recipi oportere,nisi velint pri uari.2. Decet Iesum esse Seruatorē illum, quem describit, vt totum nostræ redemptionis negotium explicet. 3. Vrget minus veterum Prophetarum.
units.tr: The purpose of the sermon is to lead the Jews from trust in the law to faith in Christ, and to do this more conveniently he uses this order: (1) since they boasted of their privileges and thought they had no need of any other way of salvation, he teaches that whatever they have, they have from grace, on account of the Messiah promised to the fathers; therefore he must be received, unless they wish to be deprived of him; (2) it is fitting that Jesus is the Saviour whom he describes, so that he may explain the whole business of our redemption; (3) he presses the testimony of the ancient prophets.

units.la: Extensa manu silentium petens ordiıtur: Viri Israelitæ, &c. Titulis compellat, quibus & sibi beneuolos reddat, & officij admoneat. Israelitas dicit, quo inprimis gloriabantur,non tam propter Iacobum, quàm propter promissionem. Vide, Gen. 32. Sed addit, Qui timetis Deum, vt innuat tunc demum veros Israelitas fore, Rom.9
units.tr: Stretching out his hand, he asks for silence and begins: Men of Israel, etc. He addresses them with titles by which he both wins their goodwill and reminds them of their duty. He calls them Israelites, the name in which they above all gloried, not so much on account of Jacob as on account of the promise. See Gen. 32. But he adds "who fear God", to suggest that only then will they be true Israelites. Rom. 9.

units.la: NOT. 1. Vsus titulorum in præfatio- nibus, vt constet nos honorifice sentire de ijs, quibus cum agimus, Rom.12. Interim cauendum ne adulatoriè seruiamus ambitioni: sed vt potius officij admonean tur auditores. Hic illa veterum simplicitas, qui officiorum titulis fuerunt contenti. Augustus Cæsar, quid hodie maius dici potest nomine Christiano, fraterno, &c.
units.tr: NOTE 1. The use of titles in prefaces shows that we think honourably of those with whom we deal. Rom. 12. Meanwhile we must take care not to serve ambition by flattery, but rather that the hearers be reminded of their duty. Here is the simplicity of the ancients, who were content with the titles of their offices. Augustus Caesar... what greater name can be given today than the Christian name, brother, and so on?

units.la: ¶ 2. Quales esse oporteat auditores verbi Israeli tæ sint, qui obfirmato in fide promissionum Dei sint animo, If.7. Ne au- temconfidentia pariat securitate, timeant Deum, & contremiscant ad huius verbu. Isa.66. Hinc obedientia nascitur, Rom.1. 16. Tales hodie pauci. Sed fit, quod habe-tur Ezech.33. Luc.8. Non mirum ergo, si absque fructu praedicetur.
units.tr: 2. What kind of hearers of the word of Israel ought to be present: those whose minds are made firm in faith in God's promises, Isa. 7. But lest confidence bring security, let them fear God and tremble at his word, Isa. 66. From this obedience is born, Rom. 1:16. Few such people today. But what is written in Ezek. 33 happens, Luke 8. No wonder, then, if the word is preached without fruit.

units.la: Narrationem contexit historicam, qua absoluitur pars prima. Orditur a patrib. vt testetur se non nouum Deum, aut nouam religionem affere, sed eam, in qua patres seruati sunt. Deinde vt subinde often dat, illis omnia obtigisse propter Messiam, quem ex gratuita misericordia Deus illis promiserit. Ita vero asserit gratiam Dei contra suorum meritorum assertores. Sic Stephanus Act.7.
units.tr: He weaves in a historical narrative, and with this the first part is completed. He begins with the fathers, to bear witness that he is not bringing a new God or a new religion, but the one in which the fathers were saved. Then, as he often does, he shows that all things came to them on account of the Messiah, whom God promised them out of free mercy. In this way he asserts the grace of God against the advocates of their own merits, as Stephen does in Acts 7.

units.la: I. Fontem omnium bonorum indicat, Electionem. Deus populi huius elegit patres nostros. Vocat Deum eius populi, non quod aliorum quoque Deus non sit (Roman 3.) neq; more gentium, &c. sed quod Iudaeis se potissimum obstrinxit, &c. Psal. 76 147. Exod.19. Hic (inquit) elegit patres nostros. Si causam quaeris, respondet Moses, Deut.7 9.4.10.14.32. Id ipsum historia docet, Gen.12. Ioh.24. Et prophetae saepe hoc vrgent contra omnes, qui suis praerogatiuis & opptibus sidebant. Item vt in gratos arguant. Amos 3. Ezech.16.&c.
units.tr: I. He points out the fountain of all good things, which is election: "The God of this people chose our fathers." He calls him the God of this people not because he is not also the God of others (Rom. 3), nor in the manner of the nations, etc., but because he bound himself especially to the Jews. Ps. 76, 147; Exod. 19. "He," he says, "chose our fathers." If you ask the cause, Moses answers: Deut. 7, 9, 4, 10, 14, 32. History itself teaches the same, Gen. 12; John 24. And the prophets often press this against all who relied on their privileges and rites, and likewise to convict them of ingratitude: Amos 3; Ezek. 16, etc.

units.la: Transferamus ad nos, vt discamus, quae causa salutis nostrae. Perieramus omnes in Adamo, Rom.7. Sed Deus, qui praeuidit, elegit ab aeterno in Christo, & hunc praedestinauit, &c. Eph.1. 1. Pet.1. Hinc iudad Psalm 75. Vsus vt non nostris meritis fidamus, 1. Cor.4. Deinde vt gratis mus & electionem atq; vocationem nostram confirmemus, 2. Pet.1. Eph.1.
units.tr: Let us transfer this to ourselves, that we may learn what is the cause of our salvation. We had all perished in Adam, Rom. 7. But God, who foresaw it, chose us from eternity in Christ, and predestined him, etc. Eph. 1; 1 Pet. 1. Hence the judgment of Ps. 75: we are not to trust in our merits, 1 Cor. 4. Then, we confirm freely our election and calling, 2 Pet. 1; Eph. 1.

units.la: II. In altum euexit, cum efflent peregrini. Partim per Iosephum, Gen.41. &c. Psal.5. Partim per literationem miraculis illustrem Exod.7.8.9.12. & 14. Id vero gratiae fuisse patet, quia peregrini etiam a Deo, Ex d.32.&c.
units.tr: II. He lifted them up when they were strangers, partly through Joseph, Gen. 41, etc.; Ps. 105, and partly through a deliverance made illustrious by miracles, Exod. 7, 8, 9, 12, 14. That this was of grace is clear, because even strangers were such by God's choice, Exod. 32, etc.

units.la: Not. Nostrae redemptionis typum. Sumus nos quoque peregrini, Heb.11. Gen.47. 2.Cor.5. Deus tamen nos exaltauit in filiorum dignitatem. Liberauit item brachio forti per suum Filium Isa.53.
units.tr: Note: a type of our redemption. We too are strangers, Heb. 11; Gen. 47; 2 Cor. 5. Yet God has exalted us to the dignity of sons. He also delivered us with a strong arm through his Son, Isa. 53.

units.la: III. Mores eorum pertulit annis 40. Com prehendit quaecunque habentur, Exod.5. 14.15.16. Num.11 14.16.20.21. Exod 32 &c. Indulgentia plus quam paterna. Quis enim filium talem ferret? Experimur simile indulgentiam. Quando enim non peccamus? Sed semper Deus qualis describitur Psa. 103. Mich. 7. Mat. 5. Interim observemus, ita illos tulisse, ut non totos excideret, puniuit autem acriter. Vide Numer. 14. Deuter. 1. 3. Nemo ergo sibi impunitatem perpetuam polliceatur.
units.tr: III. He bore with their manners for forty years. This covers whatever is recorded: Exod. 5, 14, 15, 16; Num. 11, 14, 16, 20, 21; Exod. 32, etc. The indulgence was more than paternal, for who would bear such a son? We experience a similar indulgence, for when do we not sin? But God is always such as he is described in Ps. 103; Mic. 7; Matt. 5. Meanwhile let us observe that he so bore with them that he did not cut them off entirely, yet he punished them sharply. See Num. 14; Deut. 1, 3. Let no one therefore promise himself perpetual impunity.

units.la: IV. Eiectis septem gentibus, terram ipsis dedit tribuit. Vide librum Iosuae. Item Deut. 6. Ne autem Deus iniustus putetur: Ob- seruandum cur illi eiecti? Quod alienae occuparent. Item propter Idololatriam, illicitas artes, libidine, Leuit. 18. 20. Deut. 18. Propter haec Israelitae etiam occisi. Applicemus nobis.
units.tr: IV. Having cast out the seven nations, he gave their land to them as an inheritance. See the book of Joshua, and also Deut. 6. But lest God be thought unjust, we must observe why those nations were cast out: because they occupied what belonged to others, and also on account of idolatry, illicit arts and lust, Lev. 18, 20; Deut. 18. On account of these things the Israelites too were slain. Let us apply this to ourselves.

units.la: V. Rempublicam suam constituit: Iudices per annos 350. quando saepe exitium meruerunt. Et cum ingratissimi peterent Regem, hunc ex fratribus dedit, 1. Sam. 8. 9. 10. &c. Imo illorum temeritate bene visus est, quando surrogavit Dauidem, ut impleri coeperit, Gen. 49.
units.tr: V. He established their commonwealth: judges for 350 years, when they had often deserved destruction. And when, most ungrateful, they asked for a king, he gave them one from among their brothers, 1 Sam. 8, 9, 10, etc. Indeed, by their rashness he was well served, when he set up David, so that what was said in Gen. 49 might begin to be fulfilled.

units.la: NOT. Non temere hoc inter Dei beneficia numerari. Quia enim naturā nolumus coerceri, & litium omnia plena sunt, magnum beneficium est, si sint qui audiant, & iudicent Maius, si ex nobis, & gratis audiant. Maximū, si nō grauent. Habemus nos omnia haec. Sed multi contemnunt.
units.tr: NOTE. This is not rashly counted among God's benefits. For since by nature we do not want to be restrained, and all things are full of lawsuits, it is a great benefit if there are those who hear and judge; a greater one if they hear from among us and freely; and the greatest if they do not burden us. We have all these things, but many despise them.

units.la: Alij ingrati sunt. Multi murmurant, & quæ runtur de bonis legib. maximè sumptua-rijs. Recole quæso quid in Papatu tule-ris. Agnosce Dei beneficium. Studeamus gratitudini, ne fiat quod habetur Hof. 13. Oremus.
units.tr: Others are ungrateful. Many murmur and complain about good laws, especially sumptuary ones. Recall, I beg you, what you endured under the Papacy. Acknowledge God's benefit. Let us strive for gratitude, lest what is written in Hos. 13 happen. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CIIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CIIX.

units.la: 22 Et amoto illo, excitauit eis David regem, cui etiam testimonio dato, dixit, inueni Dauid filium Iesse, virum secundum cor meum, qui exequetur omnes voluntates meas.
units.tr: 22 And when he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king, to whom also he gave testimony, saying: I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who shall fulfil all my wills.

units.la: 23 Huius e semine Deus secundum promissionem excitauit Israeli Seruatorem Iesum.
units.tr: 23 Of this man's seed God, according to his promise, raised up for Israel a Saviour, Jesus.

units.la: 24 Quum ante prædicasset Iohannes coram eo iam aduentante, baptismum refipiscentiæ Israeli.
units.tr: 24 When John had first preached the baptism of repentance to Israel, before the coming of him.

units.la: 25 Quum autem expleret Iohannes cursum, dixit: Quem me suspicamini esse? non is sum ego, sed ecce, venit post me, cuius pedum soleam non sim dignus, qui soluam.
units.tr: 25 And as John was finishing his course, he said: Whom do you suppose me to be? I am not he; but behold, there comes one after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to loose.

units.la: PEtrus tota hac concione in eo est, vt Iudæos ab inani Legis fiducia ad Christi fidem adducat. Quia verò suis prærogatiuis ita efforebantur, vt sibi nullo alio Seruatore opus esse putarent, prima par-te te hanc fiducia oppugnat, docens patres ex mera gratia habuisse, quicquid habuerunt, & quidem propter Mesiam. Vnde colligit, hunc omnino recipi oportere, nisi ab omni gratia & dignitate velint exciderè. Absoluit vero hanc partem narratio ne veterum beneficiorum Dei, qui patres ex gratia elegerat, & excidio dignos seruarit. Et nuper deduxit hanc narrationem ad Saulem usq; ut sic commodius ad Dauidem transfeat, ex quo Mesias debuit nasci, adeo ut vulgo Filius Dauidis diceretur, Matt. 20.22.1. Sequitur ergo.
units.tr: In this whole sermon Peter aims to lead the Jews from vain confidence in the Law to faith in Christ. Since they were so puffed up with their privileges that they thought they had no need of any other Saviour, he first attacks this confidence, teaching that the fathers had received whatever they had from pure grace, and indeed on account of the Messiah. From this he concludes that he must certainly be received, unless they wish to fall away from all grace and dignity. The narrative of God's earlier benefits, by which he chose the fathers out of grace and preserved them when they deserved destruction, completes this part. He has recently brought this narrative down to Saul, so that he may pass more conveniently to David, from whose line the Messiah was to be born, so much so that he was commonly called the son of David (Matt. 20.22.1). Next follows:

units.la: Sublato Saule suscitauit Dauidem, &c. Sensus, Deum tanta gratia illos prosecutum esse, vt cum contra eius voluntatem peterent Regè, & primus turpissimè peccaret, non tamen abiecerit, sed ea occasione bene usus, cum illis suscitarit, ex quo Mesias debuit nasci.
units.tr: When he had removed Saul, he raised up David, etc. The sense is that God showed such great grace to them that, although they asked for a king against his will, and the first king sinned most shamefully, he nevertheless did not cast them off, but made good use of the occasion and raised up for them David, from whose line the Messiah was to be born.

units.la: NOT. 1. Cur Saulem suscitarit? Propter inobedientiam, quæ ex verbi contemptu manauit. 1. Sam. 13.15. Secuta horrenda scelera, 1 Samuel. 18.19.20.22.28. Di scant omnes Dei verbum magni facere, Inprimis Magistratus. Ab illo enim pendet regnorum salus, Pfal. 113. Dan. 4. Pf. 127. Ideo liber Legis commendatus Regi, Deut. 17. Et viderunt hoc Maiores nostri, quoad
units.tr: NOTE 1. Why did he raise up Saul? Because of disobedience, which flowed from contempt of God's word (1 Sam. 13.15). Dreadful crimes followed (1 Sam. 18.19.20.22.28). Let all learn to hold God's word in great esteem, and above all magistrates. For the safety of kingdoms depends on it (Ps. 113; Dan. 4; Ps. 127). Therefore the book of the Law was commended to the king (Deut. 17). Our forefathers saw this as well, as to the transfer of the Jewish kingdom to David.

units.la: Regni Iudaici translatio ad Dauidem.
units.tr: The transfer of the Jewish kingdom to David.

units.la: Saul propter inobedientiam reiectus. iurisjurandi formulam,&c. Hanc ergo sh mentem reuocent sæpe.Populus vero o-bediat piè constitutis ad Romanos 13. Quid fiat rebellibus lofiæ tempora do-cent,Sophon.1 2.3 ¶2.Dauidis encom ũ, ex Psalm.89 1.Samuel.13.Interserit autem quod Isai filius, vt in eo etiam Dei grati-am agnoscant, &ne Dauide quidem su-perbiant,sed meminerint, quid ipse dixe-rit de se, 2. Samuel. 7. Psalm.78. Laudat autem ab obedientia.
units.tr: Saul was rejected because of disobedience. [They used] the formula of the oath, etc. Let them therefore often recall this mind. Let the people obey rulers who are devoutly appointed (Rom. 13). What is to be done with rebels the times of the prophets teach (Zeph. 1, 2, 3). A panegyric on David, from Ps. 89; 1 Sam. 13. He adds that he was the son of Jesse, so that they may also acknowledge God's grace in him, and not be proud even of David, but remember what he himself said of himself (2 Sam. 7; Ps. 78). He praises him, moreover, for his obedience.

units.la: Atqui adulter fuit,Iatro,confidens,&c. 2.Sam.11 24. Sed vicissim obseruandum. 1.Quòd promissiones de Christo fide vera amplexus fuit, Psa.110 2.In eo ergo ipsi placatus Pater, Matth.3.17. 2 Fides hæc genuit virtutes omnis generis:Humilita-tem, & quòd magni fecit Dei beneficia, 2.Sam.7.Studium verbi, Psalm.25 19.119. Patientiam disciplinæ & correptionis, 2. Sam.12.*24.15 16. Seriam pœnitentiam, Ps 51.&c. Cum his si Saulem conferas, longè alium videbis. Dauidem ergo imi-tentur,qui Deo probari volunt.
units.tr: Yet he was an adulterer, a robber, a presumptuous man, etc. (2 Sam. 11.24). But on the other hand we must observe: (1) that he embraced with true faith the promises concerning Christ (Ps. 110); in him therefore the Father was reconciled to him (Matt. 3.17); (2) this faith produced virtues of every kind: humility, and that he esteemed God's benefits highly (2 Sam. 7); zeal for the word (Ps. 25.19; 119); patience under discipline and correction (2 Sam. 12); and serious repentance (Ps. 51, etc.). If you compare Saul with these, you will see a very different man. Let them therefore imitate David, who want to please God.

units.la: Hinc ad secundam partem transit Pe-trus, qua docet IESVM esse promissum Seruatorem,&c. Argumenta sunt hæc.
units.tr: Hence Peter passes to the second part, in which he teaches that Jesus is the promised Saviour, etc. These are the arguments.

units.la: 1.Quòd ex ea stirpe sit natus, vnde se-cundum promissionem nasci debuit. Ar-gumen gumentum eiusmodi. Mefsias ex Dauidis femine nasci debuit. 2. Sam. 7. Pf. 2. 110. 132. Isa. 11. Ierc. 23. Sed ex illo natus Iesus, &c. Ergo &c. Huc refer Matth. 1. Luc. 1. 2. 3.
units.tr: 1. That he was born of that stock from which, according to the promise, he had to be born. The argument runs thus: the Messiah had to be born from the seed of David (2 Sam. 7; Ps. 2, 110, 132; Isa. 11; Jer. 23). But Jesus was born of him, etc. Therefore, etc. Refer here Matt. 1; Luke 1, 2, 3.

units.la: ¶ Obseruandum quod secundum promissionem dicitur excitatus. Ita docet, hoc etiam gratuitae misericordiae donum esse. Patet hoc ex prima promissione, Gen. 3. Agnouit hoc Dauid, 2. Sam 7. Psal. 89. Christus idem docet Ioh. 3. Vide 1. Ioh. 4. Elucet in eo ineffabilis veritas Dei. Qui hic nolluit fallere, cur falleret in aliis. Soletur hoc in tentationibus, If. 40. 14.
units.tr: Note that he is said to have been raised up according to the promise. So he teaches that this too is a gift of free mercy. This is clear from the first promise (Gen. 3). David acknowledged it (2 Sam. 7; Ps. 89). Christ teaches the same (John 3; see 1 John 4). The ineffable truth of God shines forth in this. He who here would not deceive, why would he deceive in others? This consoles us in temptations (Isa. 40.14).

units.la: II. Quod venerit, ut venturum Prophetae praedixerunt: Nimirum praemisso praecursore. Isa. 40. Malach. 4. Fuit is Iohannes Baptista, Luc. 1. 3. Matth. 11. Eodem argumento vtitur Marcus Cap. 1. Vbi rursus Dei bonitas elucet, quinam Messias ignotus veniret, omnes ad eius aduentum excitare voluit.
units.tr: II. That he came as the prophets had foretold he would come, namely with a forerunner sent before him (Isa. 40; Mal. 4). This was John the Baptist (Luke 1, 3; Matt. 11). Mark uses the same argument in chapter 1, where again God's goodness shines forth: that the Messiah was to come unknown, and he wished to rouse everyone to his coming.

units.la: Sed Notr. ¶ Praecursore quali opus fuerit? Eo, qui poenitentia populum praepararet. Arguitur nostrae naturae vitiosi-tas Io. 3. Et simul confutantur, qui Christi praedicatione licentiam inuehi dicunt. At qui mortificari & totos invocari oportet, Col 3. Rom. 6. 12.
units.tr: But note: what kind of forerunner was needed? One who would prepare the people through repentance. The vice of our nature is thereby proved (John 3). At the same time, those are refuted who say that licence is brought in by the preaching of Christ. For we must be mortified and wholly put on Christ (Col. 3; Rom. 6, 12).

units.la: III. Iohannis testimonium adducit non
units.tr: III. He adduces John's testimony, not

units.la: quòd Christi causa hominum testimonij nitatur.(Io.5).sed quòd Iohannis summa esset authoritas inter Iudæos, Mat.21.Facit autem ad pondus testimonij, quòd illud dedit, quando ipsum putabant esse Messiam. Vide Luc.3.Ioh.1.
units.tr: because Christ's cause depends on human testimony (John 5), but because John's authority was very great among the Jews. Moreover, the testimony carries weight because he gave it when they thought he himself was the Messiah. See Luke 3; John 1.

units.la: Not. Quàm bona fide sancti in Christo prædicando utantur. Nonnuntur vulgi stoliditate, vt ipsi sint in pretio, sed vt Christo omnes adducant, studeant. Similia habes, Actor.3 16.14.2.Corinth.11 1.Corinth.2. Sic etiam Angeli, Apoc.19,22. Iniuriam ergo eis faciunt, qui hodie in illos transferunt, quod solius Christi est. Vide Iohan.14.Isa.42. Hinc illa, Act.4 1.Iohan.2. Horum memores, uno Christo contenti simus, & cum Petro dicamus, Domine, quo ibimus, &c. Iohannis 6. Oremus.
units.tr: Note how sincerely the saints ought to be used in preaching Christ: they are not to seek to be prized for themselves, by the foolishness of the crowd, but to bring all to Christ. You have similar passages at Acts 3:16; 14:2; 2 Corinthians 11:1; 1 Corinthians 2. So also the angels, Revelation 19:22. They therefore do wrong to them who now transfer to those men what belongs to Christ alone. See John 14; Isaiah 42. Hence those words in Acts 4:1; John 2. Mindful of these, let us be content with Christ alone, and with Peter let us say, "Lord, to whom shall we go?" etc. (John 6). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CIX.

units.la: 26 Viri fratres, filij generis Abraham, et qui inter vos timent Deum, vobis sermo salutis huius missus est.
units.tr: 26 Brothers, sons of the stock of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, to us has the word of this salvation been sent.

units.la: 27 Qui enim habitabant in Hierusalem et principes eorum, quum ignorarent ipsum, et eo condemnato, vocces Prophetarum quæ per omne Sabbatum leguntur, compleverunt.
units.tr: 27 For those who lived in Jerusalem, and their rulers, not knowing him, and condemning him, fulfilled the voices of the Prophets which are read every Sabbath.

units.la: OMnis Scriptura vnanimi consensu docet, Iesum Christũ esse vnicum Seruatorẽ, in quo vno nobis benedictio, iustitia, vita & salus obtingat. 1.Corinth.1. Actorum 4.&c. Idem tota hac concione Paulus quoque tradit. Quia vero ei res erat cum Iudæis hostibus acerrimis,magno serio rem agit, & post quam ostendit ipsis opus esse Seruatore, hunc docet esse Iesum,&c. 1. Quia natus ex Dauide sicuti promissum 2. Samuelis 7. Psalm.89 Isaiæ 9 Ierem 23 Matthæi 1. 2. Quia venerit, vt venturum prædixerint Prophetæ, nimirum præmisso Iohanne Baptista, Isaiæ 40. Malachiæ 4. 3 Huius testimonium adduxit, vt intelligant, Apostolos non primos esse, qui illum prædicent; sed idem docuit se Iohannem, cuius maxima erat authoritas. Matthæi 11. Ai erant, quæ Iudæos remorabantur, quo minus crederent. Ijs modo occurrit. Ita enim prædicandum, vt obstacula fidei, remoueantur, Ierem.1. Isa.40.
units.tr: All Scripture teaches with one accord that Jesus Christ is the only Saviour, in whom alone blessing, righteousness, life and salvation are obtained for us (1 Cor. 1; Acts 4, etc.). Paul also delivers the same in this whole sermon. But since he had to deal with Jewish enemies who were most bitter, he treats the matter with great earnestness, and after showing them that they need a Saviour, he teaches that this is Jesus, etc. (1) Because he was born of David, as promised (2 Sam. 7; Ps. 89; Isa. 9; Jer. 23; Matt. 1). (2) Because he has come, as the Prophets foretold, John the Baptist having gone before him (Isa. 40; Mal. 4). (3) He brought forward the testimony of John, so that they might understand that the Apostles were not the first to preach him, but that John, whose authority was very great, taught the same (Matt. 11). There were obstacles which held back the Jews, so that they did not believe. He meets these. For preaching must be so done that the hindrances to faith are removed (Jer. 1; Isa. 40).

units.la: 1. Erant, qui putarent controuersiam hanc nihil ad eos pertinere, &c. Quales etiam hodie inueniuntur, qui ex eo pruden-tiæ & modestiæ laudem quærunt. Occurrit ergo Paulus, & vt magis ex ite1, rursus magnificis titulis appellat. 1. Viri fratres.
