units.tr: 1. There were some who thought this controversy did not concern them, etc. Such people are still found today, who seek praise for prudence and moderation from this. Paul therefore meets them, and, that he may move them more, again addresses them with honourable titles: 1. "Brothers."

units.la: Evangelium prædicandum caridebus.
units.tr: The Gospel must be preached to those who lack it.

units.la: Vsitatum hoc, quia omnes ex Iacobo. Et prodest nos admoneri de fraternitate 2. Filij generis Abrahæ. Ita imprimis volebant dici propter fœdus & promissiones. Gen.17.22. Imo hinc sperabant omne salu tem,Mat.3 Iohan.8.Ostendit ergo,se non inuidere eis. 3. Addit autem, qui timetis Deum, vt meminerint, non prodesse generis prærogatiuam, nisi præstent quod in fœdere requiritur. Gen.17. Vobis sermo salutis huius missus, &c. Id est,ad vos impri mis pertinet. Sic Act 9. Ita vero loquuntur Apostoli, non quod gentes exclu serint,sed quod Iudæis primis oportuit prædicari propter fœdus, Matth.10.15. Rom. 1.&15.Actorum 1 &c. Vult ergo hanc Dei bonitatem agnoscant.
units.tr: This is customary, since all are from Jacob; and it helps us to be reminded of brotherhood. 2. "Sons of the stock of Abraham." Chiefly they wished to be so called, because of the covenant and the promises (Gen. 17:22). Indeed, they hoped from this for every salvation (Matt. 3; John 8). He shows, therefore, that he does not begrudge them this. 3. He adds, however, "who fear God," so that they may remember that the privilege of birth profits nothing unless they perform what is required in the covenant (Gen. 17). "To us has the word of this salvation been sent," etc. That is, it pertains first of all to you. So in Acts 9. Yet the Apostles speak thus not because they excluded the Gentiles, but because it was fitting that the Jews should be preached to first, on account of the covenant (Matt. 10:15; Rom. 1 and 15; Acts 1, etc.). He wishes them therefore to acknowledge this goodness of God.

units.la: Interim Not. 1. Euangelium de Christo verbum salutis dici. Ita Roman.1. Sic Angelus Actor.11. Causa quia Christum prædicat,in quo vno salus,&c. Iohan.1.6. Qui ergo hoc contemnunt, propria salutem reijciunt. Ingratitudo, quam Deus non sinet impunitam, Matt 10.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note 1: the gospel of Christ is called the word of salvation. So Rom. 1. So the angel in Acts 11. The reason is that it preaches Christ, in whom alone is salvation (John 1:6). Those therefore who despise this cast away their own salvation. It is an ingratitude which God will not leave unpunished (Matt. 10).

units.la: 2. Ita prædicari debere, vt omnes intelligant ad se pertinere quod dicitur. Nisi id fiat,sit quod est Ezech 33.Luc.8. Obseruemus ergo hoc in salutis doctrina, quoad promissiones de peccator ruem fione,Ifa 1.43. Mich.5. Ezech. 18.1.Ioh.2.1. Matth.11. &c.In praeceptis & minis,Leuit 26.Deuteronom 28. In exemplis veteri-bus,Iere 5 Ita recte secatur Dei verbum 2.Tim.2 4
units.tr: 2. The word must be preached so that all understand that what is said pertains to them. Unless this is done, it is what it is (Ezek. 33; Luke 8). We should observe this therefore in the teaching of salvation: as regards the promises of forgiveness of sins (Isa. 1, 43; Mic. 5; Ezek. 18; 1 John 2; Matt. 11, etc.), in the precepts and threats (Lev. 26; Deut. 28), and in the examples of the ancients (Jer. 5). Thus the word of God is rightly divided (2 Tim. 2:4).

units.la: II. Offendebantur multi cruce & morte Christi,imprimis autem, quod Hierosolymis erat crucifixus. Ibi enim erat sedes cultus (Psal 132) & inde exspectabatur verbum salutis.Psal.110 Isa.2.Mich.4. Videbantur ergo illic non posse errare,& absurdum esse eum recipere, quem sacerdotes & seniores damnassent.Id sic diluit, vt doceat, potius cauendum esse ne similii ingrat tadine peccent.
units.tr: II. Many were offended by the cross and death of Christ, and especially by the fact that he had been crucified at Jerusalem. For there was the seat of worship (Ps. 132), and from there the word of salvation was expected (Ps. 110; Isa. 2; Mic. 4). It seemed, therefore, that they could not err there, and that it was absurd to receive him whom the priests and elders had condemned. He resolves this in such a way as to teach that they should rather take care lest they sin by a similar ingratitude.

units.la: I. Causam indicat, quod ex ignorantia hoc fecerint.Sic 1.Cor.2 Quis vero imite tur ignorantem? Fuit autem crassa & inex cusabilis ignorantia Debebant enim scii re Scripturam Malach.2. Et Christus de eo admonuerat, Iohan. 5. At licet quotidie legerent,non intellexerunt.Causa indicatur 2.Cor.3.
units.tr: I. He indicates the cause: that they did this out of ignorance (so 1 Cor. 2). But who would imitate one who is ignorant? The ignorance was gross and inexcusable. For they ought to have known the Scripture (Mal. 2), and Christ had admonished them about it (John 5). Yet although they read it every day, they did not understand. The cause is indicated in 2 Cor. 3.

units.la: Not. 1. Non semper insistendum esse antistitum exemplis. Si enim isti erraverunt,quid de alijs sperandum? Ps 118. Vide item Exod.32. Ezech.20. Arguuntur, qui nos hodie exemplis vrgent. At debent omnia ad Dei verbum examinari.
units.tr: Note 1: One must not always rest on the examples of the leaders. For if these erred, what can be hoped from others? (Ps. 118.) See also Exod. 32; Ezek. 20. Those are rebuked who today press us with examples. But everything must be tested by the word of God.

units.la: Alioqui excusaretur Adulterium, 2. Sam. 11. Ebrietas, Gen. 9.19.
units.tr: Otherwise adultery would be excused (2 Sam. 11), and drunkenness (Gen. 9:19).

units.la: 2. Scripturas non prodesse, nisi intelligantur Iudaei quia non intelligebant, feceruut quod praedictum Psal. 117.22. &c. Fit hodie idem in Papatu. Legitur & canitur in templis. Interim reijcitur Christus, colitur Antichristus, quem Scriptura cauere iubet, 1. Iohan, 4.2. Theff. 2. 2. Pet. 2. 1. Tim. 4 ad Timoth. 3.4. &c.
units.tr: 2. The Scriptures profit nothing unless they are understood. The Jews, because they did not understand, did what was foretold (Ps. 118:22, etc.). The same happens today in Papacy. It is read and sung in the temples; meanwhile Christ is rejected and Antichrist is worshipped, whom Scripture bids us beware of (1 John 4; 2 Thess. 2; 2 Pet. 2; 1 Tim. 4; 2 Tim. 3, etc.).

units.la: 3. Quid ingratos maneat beneficiorum Dei aestimatores? Vt ea illis exitio sint, quae debebant salutifera esse. Sic istis Christus in ruinam cessit, Luc. 2. Ita hodie Euangelium multis, Mat. 10. 2. Cor. 2. Fit idem quoad externa Dei dona. Experimur hodie.
units.tr: 3. What awaits ungrateful assessors of God's benefits? That those things become their destruction which ought to have been salutary for them. So for these, Christ became a stumbling-block to their ruin (Luke 2). So today the gospel is to many (Matt. 10; 2 Cor. 2). The same happens with regard to the outward gifts of God. We experience this today.

units.la: 2 Non aliud fecere, quam quod praedictum. Nec dubium, quin Scripturas adduxerit, Psal. 118 41.69.22. Isa. 53. Zach. 3.14. Dan. 9. Similis locus, Act. 3.4 2.
units.tr: 2. They did nothing other than what was foretold. Nor is there doubt that he adduced Scriptures (Ps. 118; 41; 69:22; Isa. 53; Zech. 3, 14; Dan. 9). A similar passage is Acts 3 and 4.

units.la: 4. Obseruanda Dei prouidentia & vis eius, quando nihil contra illam possunt impij. Imo tunc Dei decreta exequentur, quando volunt impedire. Id vero non excusat illos. Vide de Iuda Mat. 27. Nos autem consolatur, ne offendamur vllis aduersis, sed dicamus quod Iob cap. primo & secundo. Item 1. Sam. 16. Item ne succumbamus. mus. Nō enim plus poterunt impij quàm velit Deus, qui fidelis est, &c. 1 Cor. 10. Pf. 92. 2. Cor. 1. &c. Oremus.
units.tr: 4. The providence of God and his power must be observed, since the wicked can do nothing against it. Indeed, they will carry out God's decrees precisely when they wish to hinder them. This, however, does not excuse them (see Matt. 27 concerning Judas). It consoles us, so that we are not offended by any adversities, but say what Job says in chapters 1 and 2 (likewise 1 Sam. 16), and so that we do not succumb. For the wicked will not be able to do more than God wills, who is faithful, etc. (1 Cor. 10; Ps. 92; 2 Cor. 1, etc.). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CX.
units.tr: HOMILY CX.

units.la: 28 Et nulla caussa mortis inuenta, petierunt à Pilato, vt necaretur.
units.tr: 28 And though they found no cause of death, they asked Pilate that he should be put to death.

units.la: 29 Quum verò perfecissent omnia, quæ de eo scripta erant, detractum è ligno, posuerunt in monumento.
units.tr: 29 And when they had fulfilled all that was written of him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.

units.la: 30 Deus autem excitauit eum à mortuis,
units.tr: 30 But God raised him from the dead,

units.la: 31 Qui visus est per dies multos ijs, qui simul ascenderant cum eo à Galilæa in Hierusalem, sunt testes eius apud populum.
units.tr: 31 Who was seen for many days by those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses before the people.

units.la: PAulus Iudæis Antiochiæ ita prædicat Christum, vt diligenter omnia amolia-tur, quæ plerosq; illorum in fide impe-diebant. Erat inter illa præcipuum mors indigna & infame Crucis supplicium, 1. Cor. 1. Quia enim Mesiam somniabant victoriis & regni splendore illustrem, nō poterant pro illo agnoscere eum, quem in cruce mori viderant. Et de eo ipse Christus monuerat, Matth. 11. Ideo hoc scandalum multis argumentis remouet Paulus, 1. Quod quicquid fecerint Sacerdotes & Seniores Hierosolymæ, ex ignorantia fecerint.2 Quod ita prædictum olim (Psal. 118) neq; aliud fecerint, quàm quod impleuerint prophetias. Sequuntur al a.
units.tr: PAUL, preaching Christ to the Jews of Antioch, carefully removes everything that hindered many of them in faith. Among these the chief was the unworthy death, the infamous punishment of the Cross, 1 Cor. 1. For since they dreamed of a Messiah renowned for victories and the splendour of a kingdom, they could not recognise as him the one whom they had seen dying on a cross. Christ himself had warned of this, Matt. 11. Paul therefore removes this stumbling-block by several arguments. First, whatever the chief priests and elders of Jerusalem did, they did in ignorance. Second, it had been foretold long ago (Ps. 118), and they did nothing other than fulfil the prophecies. The other points follow.

units.la: I. Quòd innocens fuerit, ideoque non tam mortem quàm huius causam debere respici. Cùm nullam causam inuenissent, &c. Inueniendi verbo innuit illos quæsiuisse.
units.tr: I. That he was innocent, and so it is not so much his death as its cause that should be looked at. "When they had found no cause," etc. By the word "found" he hints that they had searched for one.

units.la: Ex ipsius ore: Ioh. 18.2. Falsis testibus, Matt. 26.14. 3. Coram Pilato, Luc. 23. Herode item. Et haud dubie hæc multis exposuit, vt ostendat, ignominiam hanc in ipsis hærere, qui innocentem nihilominus poftulârint ad crucem. Sic Act. 2. & 3.
units.tr: From his own mouth: John 18. By false witnesses: Matt. 26:14. Before Pilate: Luke 23. Likewise before Herod. Doubtless he set these out at length, to show that this disgrace clings to those who nonetheless demanded that the innocent man be crucified. So Acts 2 and 3.

units.la: Interim NOTA. 1. Vsum innocentiæ Christi. Debebat is victima pro nobis fieri, 1 Cor. 5. Ioh 1. Id verò non poterat, si ipse fuisset peccator. Simile debitoris. Vt er go purus esset, ex Spiritu sancto conceptus & ex virgine natus est, Luc. 1. Deinde innocentissimè vixit, Isa. 53. Ioh 8. Innocentiæ quoq; testimonium ex hominibus habuit, Ioh 19. Mar. 15. Potuit ergo pro nobis satisfacere, 2. Cor. 5. Isa. 53. Et hinc consolatio petenda in tentationibus, Ro. 5. Gal. 4.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE: 1. The use of Christ's innocence. He had to be the victim for us, 1 Cor. 5; John 1. This he could not have been had he himself been a sinner; the case is like that of a debtor. So that he might be pure, he was conceived of the Holy Spirit and born of a virgin, Luke 1. Then he lived most innocently, Isa. 53; John 8. He also had testimony of his innocence from men, John 19; Mark 15. He could therefore make satisfaction for us, 2 Cor. 5; Isa. 53. And from this consolation is to be sought in temptations, Rom. 5; Gal. 4.

units.la: 2. Sortem sanctorum Christi. Sunt quidem illi non abfq; peccato, vt ille Psal. 51. 143. Attamen non sunt sceleratis. Verum tamen sic eos odit mundus, vt nihil non criminis intentet, & omnes quærat occa-siones. Hïc ergo caueant, ne iure accusen tur,1.Pet.4. Quòd si nihilominus tradu-cantur & occidantur pro facinorosis, bea ti sunt,Matt.5 Idem fit eis, quod Prophe-tis & Christo.Impij nihil proficiunt quæ-rendo crimina.Imò seipsos infamát,& vel ipsi vel posteri innocentiæ testes fiunt,Pf. 34 120.Prou.10 Matt.24. Sequetur gloria sempiterna,2.Tim.2 If.64 Ioh 17.Ista cogi temus in nostris & aliorû tormetis.Socra.
units.tr: 2. The lot of Christ's saints. They are indeed not without sin, as in Ps. 51 and 143. Yet they are not wicked. But the world so hates them that it charges them with every crime and seeks every occasion against them. Let them therefore take care that they are not justly accused, 1 Pet. 4. But if they are nonetheless handed over and killed as evildoers, they are blessed, Matt. 5. The same happens to them as happened to the prophets and to Christ. The wicked gain nothing by seeking out crimes; indeed they bring infamy upon themselves, and either they themselves or their descendants become witnesses to innocence, Ps. 34, 120; Prov. 10; Matt. 24. Eternal glory will follow, 2 Tim. 2; Isa. 64; John 17. Let us consider these things in our own torments and in those of others.

units.la: II. Ne quis illum ab aduersarijs superà tum, & proinde alios feruare nō posse pu taret(Matth.27.Luc.23.)docet, illos nihil profecisse suis machinationibus.Perfece-runt quidem omnia, quæ de illo scripta sunt,& tandem sepeliuerunt quoq;: Deus autem illum suscitauit,&c. Loquitur aut quasi à Sacerdotibus sepultus sit, cum hoc fecerint Iofephus & Nicodemus. Ioh. 19. Sed ad hoc respicit quod factum Mat. 27.Et oportuit huius meminisse, quia certitudine resurrectionis asserit contra rumorem,&c.Matt.28. Quid enim profuit? Deus ipse eum excitauit. Imò milites ipsi fuerunt testes,&c. Matth.28 Si quem ergo offendit crux Christi,eundem console tur resurrectio gloriosa.
units.tr: II. Lest anyone think he could not save others because he was overcome by his adversaries (Matt. 27; Luke 23), he teaches that his enemies gained nothing by their schemes. They indeed fulfilled all that was written about him, and at last also buried him; but God raised him up, etc. He speaks as though he had been buried by the priests, although Joseph and Nicodemus did this, John 19. But he refers to what was done in Matt. 27. And it was necessary to recall this, because he asserts the certainty of the resurrection against the rumour, etc., Matt. 28. For what did it profit them? God himself raised him. Indeed the soldiers themselves were witnesses, etc., Matt. 28. If therefore the cross of Christ offends anyone, let the glorious resurrection console that same person.

units.la: Not. I.Irritos esse hostium Christi conatus. Fit item quoad Euangelij cur‑sum, Ioh 3. Mar 13. Regni propagationem, Psal. 2 33. &c. Idem lentiendum de huius corpore, Ecclesia. Visa haec saepe extincta & sepulta. In Aegypto, Exod 1 2 Sed inde erepra, & quidem per mare rubrum, Exo, 14. Sub iudicibus. Sub Regibus, adeo ut Prophetae conquerantur, 1 Reg 19. Ila 8. 24. In Babylone. Sed semper liberata Idé postea sub Imperatoribus. Et hodie vidimus exempla innumera. Ne ergo despere mus, &c. Quin singuli privatim hoc sibi applicent, Matth. 10. Ioh. 10 Rom 8.
units.tr: Note I. That the attempts of Christ's enemies come to nothing. This happens likewise with the course of the Gospel, John 3; Mark 13, and with the spreading of the kingdom, Ps. 2, 33, etc. The same must be thought of his body, the Church. Often it has seemed extinguished and buried. In Egypt, Exod. 1; but it was snatched out of there, and indeed through the Red Sea, Exod. 14. Under the judges. Under the kings, so much so that the prophets complain, 1 Kings 19; Isa. 8, 24. In Babylon. But it was always delivered. Likewise afterwards under the emperors. And today we have seen countless examples. Let us therefore not despair, etc. Indeed let each individual apply this to himself privately, Matt. 10; John 10; Rom. 8.

units.la: ¶ 2. Officij admonemur, vt ipsi quoque non maneamus in morte peccatorum, sed in Christo resurgamus ad vitae nouitatem Rom. 6. Frustra enim gloriabimur Ecclesiae titulo & victoria Christi, si interea Satanae succumbamus, quo cum nobis pugnat est, Eph. 6.
units.tr: ¶ 2. We are admonished of our duty: that we too should not remain in the death of sin, but rise with Christ to newness of life, Rom. 6. For we shall boast in vain of the title of the Church and the victory of Christ if meanwhile we yield to Satan, with whom we have a fight, Eph. 6.

units.la: III. Resurrectionis veritatem diligenter demonstrat, quae h nc Iudaei negant maxime, Act. 4 5. Atqui per illam declaratus fuit Christus Dei Filius, Rom 1. Et in eadem nostrae salutis habetur complementum, 1. Cor. 15 Rom 14.1. Thess. 4. Primos autem producit testes ex Galilaea, quorum magnus fuit numerus, Luc. 24. 10. 1. Cor. 15 Hos praemittit, quia minus suspecta erat sat fides illorum, &c. Postea Apostolorum testimonium subiexet.
units.tr: III. He carefully demonstrates the truth of the resurrection, which the Jews especially deny, Acts 4, 5. Yet through it Christ was declared the Son of God, Rom. 1; and in it is found the completion of our salvation, 1 Cor. 15; Rom. 14; 1 Thess. 4. He first brings forward witnesses from Galilee, whose number was great, Luke 24:10; 1 Cor. 15. He puts these first because their faith was less open to suspicion, etc. Afterwards he sets out the testimony of the apostles.

units.la: Interim NOTA. ¶ Bonitatem Dei, qui nostræ redemptionis & salutis spem tam certam esse voluit. Ne ergo dubitemus, Ioh.5. Imitemur autem istorum fortitudinem qui Christo contra hostes multos & potentes testimonium tulerunt, neq; nos illius pudeat, Rom.1. Ita olim nos pro suis illeagnoscet, &c. Mar.8. Mat.10. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE: the goodness of God, who wished the hope of our redemption and salvation to be so certain. Let us not therefore doubt, John 5. Let us imitate the courage of those who bore witness to Christ against many and powerful enemies, and let us not be ashamed of him, Rom. 1. So in the past he will acknowledge us as his own, etc., Mark 8. Matt. 10. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXI.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXI.

units.la: 32 Nos quoque vobis Euangelizamus eam promissionem, quæ Patribus facta est, Deum expleuisse siliis illorum, id est, nobis excitato Iesu.
units.tr: 32 We too preach to you the promise made to the Fathers, that God has fulfilled it to their children, that is, to us, by raising up Jesus.

units.la: 33 Vt enim in Psalmo secundo scriptum est, Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te.
units.tr: 33 As it is written in the second Psalm: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you."

units.la: 34 Quod autem excitauerit eum à mortuis, non amplius reuersurum in sepulchrum, ita dixit, Dabo vobis firmas illas Dauidis beneficentias.
units.tr: 34 And that he raised him from the dead so that he would never return to the grave, he said thus: "I will give you the sure blessings of David."

units.la: 35 Ideo & alias dicit, Non dabis sanctum tuum sentire corruptionem.
units.tr: 35 Therefore he also says elsewhere: "You will not allow your Holy One to see corruption."

units.la: 36 Nam Dauid quidem quum suo ætate inseruisset, Dei consilio obdormi-uit, & adiunctus est Patribus suis, sen-sit corruptionem.
units.tr: 36 For David, indeed, after he had served his own generation by the counsel of God, fell asleep, was added to his fathers, and saw corruption.

units.la: Secunda huius concionis parte Paulus docet, Iesum esse patribus promissum seruatorem. Et quia ei res erat cum Iudaeis, qui cruce potissimum offendebantur, i. Cor. 1. hoc scandalum diligenter removet. 1 Quod Sacerdotes omnia fecerint ex ignorantia. 2. Quod ita praedictum, &c. 3 Quod innocens. 4. Quod nihil pro fecerint: Idq; docet resurrectio. Quia autem haec praecipuum est Dei atis Christi argumentum, Rom. 1. & ideo habet salutis complementum, multis eam asserit. Et ne soli Apostoli hanc tradere vi derentur, nuper Galilaeos produxit testes 1. Cor. 15. Sequitur.
units.tr: In the second part of this sermon Paul teaches that Jesus is the Saviour promised to the fathers. And since he had to deal with Jews, who were chiefly offended by the cross (1 Cor. 1), he carefully removes this stumbling block: (1) that the priests did everything out of ignorance; (2) that it was so foretold, etc.; (3) that he was innocent; (4) that they did nothing to him. The resurrection proves all this. And because this is the principal proof of the power of Christ (Rom. 1), and so the completion of salvation, he asserts it with many arguments. And lest the Apostles alone seem to hand this down, he recently brought forward the Galileans as witnesses (1 Cor. 15). It follows:

units.la: Apostolorum testimonium, quod magna cum gravitate profert, partim quod Christus ita mandat in genere omnibus Act. 1. partim quod ipse cum Barnab. pecu liarem haberent vocationem. Summa, Deum in Christo praestitisse, quaecunque olim promiserit, 2. Cor. 1. Promisit autem benedictionem, sub qua omnis salus comprehenditur, Gen. 22, 26, 28. In Christo autem habentur omnia, quae ad hanc pertinent, 1. Cor. 1. Vita, Ioh. 5. 6. 14. Adoptio,
units.tr: The testimony of the Apostles, which he presents with great seriousness, partly because Christ commands it to all in general (Acts 1), and partly because they themselves had a special calling with Barnabas. The sum is that God in Christ has performed whatever he promised of old (2 Cor. 1). He promised a blessing, under which all salvation is comprehended (Gen. 22, 26, 28). In Christ, however, are found all the things that pertain to this: life (John 5, 6, 14); adoption

units.la: Ioh.1.Rom.8. Hæreditas regni cœlestis, Luc.22,Ioh.17. Et debet hic obseruari fides Dei infallibilis. Ita enim præstitit, quę promissa vt omnia conueniant. Tempus, Dan 2.9.Gen.49.Isa.11. Virgo mater,Ge. 3. Isa.7 Luc.1 Locus,Mich.5.Miracula,If. 35 &c. Hinc petatur generalis consolatio. Quomodo enim falleret in aliis? vt fame, &c.Matth.6.Pest, Psal.91.
units.tr: (John 1; Rom. 8); the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom (Luke 22; John 17). And here the infallible faithfulness of God must be observed. For he has so performed the promised things that they all agree: the time (Dan. 2, 9; Gen. 49; Isa. 11); the virgin mother (Gen. 3; Isa. 7; Luke 1); the place (Mic. 5); the miracles (Isa. 35), etc. From this a general consolation may be drawn. For how would he deceive in other things, such as hunger, etc. (Matt. 6), or pestilence (Ps. 91)?

units.la: Interim Not. Apostolos non prædi casse nouam doctrinam,sed eam salutis rationem,quæ ipsi Adamo promissa fuit, Gene.3. De qua Moses Ioh.5.Prophetæ,1.Petri 2.Pet.1.Luc.24 Item Act 3 10.Eadem ergo veterum & nostra fides & salus, 1. Cor.10 Discrimen inter nos & veteres. Illi promissionem habuerunt,nos rem ipsam.Illi typos futuræ, nos sigilla partæ salutis Ideo nos illis præferimur, Matth.13. Vide quæ sit fides vetus & catholica.
units.tr: Meanwhile note: the Apostles did not preach a new doctrine, but that way of salvation which was promised to Adam himself (Gen. 3). Of this Moses (John 5), the Prophets (1 Pet. 1), and Peter (2 Pet. 1; Luke 24) spoke; likewise (Acts 3, 10). Therefore the faith and salvation of the ancients and of ours are the same (1 Cor. 10). The difference between us and the ancients: they had the promise, we have the thing itself; they had types of the future, we have the seals of salvation already obtained. Therefore we are preferred to them (Matt. 13). See what the old and catholic faith is.

units.la: Sed ad Paulum redeamus,qui resurrectionem Christi ex Prophetis probat.
units.tr: But let us return to Paul, who proves the resurrection of Christ from the Prophets.

units.la: I. Psal 2.Cuius vnum versum citat,vt totum eis in mentem reuocet. Prædicitur illic Christum habiturum multos & graues hostes,sed tamen fore victorem. Ratio: Quia Dei decretum fit: Filius meus es,&c. Id Paulus applicat resurrectioni, quia per hanc Deus illū Filium suum esse declarauit, quem videbatur d eseruisse,Matt.27. Plus enim hoc fuit,quàm hostes peterent.
units.tr: I. Psalm 2. He cites one verse of it so as to recall the whole to their minds. There it is foretold that Christ will have many and grave enemies, but that he will nevertheless be the victor. The reason: because God's decree is made: "You are my Son," etc. Paul applies this to the resurrection, because through it God declared him to be his Son, whom he seemed to have forsaken (Matt. 27). For this was more than his enemies sought.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Eandem esse ratione m mem brorum Christi. Ex vno enim sunt,qui san ctificat,& qui sanctificantur,Heb.2. Eph 5. Itaq; sumus quidem filij Dei, sed hoc iam non patet omnibus, 1.Iohan.3. Olim vero apparebit, quando Christus veniet. Qui ideo dicitur dies regenerationis,Matthaei 19. Lucæ 21. Tunc fiet, quod habetur 1.Thess.4.Sap.4.5.Simus ergo patientes,Iob.19.
units.tr: NOTE. That the reason is the same for the members of Christ. For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of one (Heb. 2; Eph. 5). So we are indeed sons of God, but this is not yet manifest to all (1 John 3). But it will appear hereafter, when Christ comes. Therefore it is called the day of regeneration (Matt. 19; Luke 21). Then will come to pass what is written in 1 Thess. 4 and Wisd. 4, 5. Let us therefore be patient (Job 19).

units.la: II. Isa.LV.vbi disserit Deus de beneficijs,quæ per Christum conferre velit, & interalia ait:Feriam vobiscum fœdus sempiternum, misericordias Dauidis fideles, id est,præstabo fideliter,quæcunque Dauidi olim promisi ex misericordia gratuita.Id Paulus reddidit ex LXX. per sancta, & intelligit Christum,qui est sanctum sanctorum,& omnium promissionum fundamentum, 2.Cor.1. Ex eo sic argumentatur: DEVS sanciuit cum Dauide fœdus sanctum & æternum,Psal.89. 2.Sam.7.Id autem nititur Christo: ergo hic quoque æternus sit oportet,& per consequens resurrexit, nec amplius in sepulchrum redire,id est,mori debuit.
units.tr: II. Isa. 55, where God discourses about the benefits he wishes to bestow through Christ, and among other things says: "I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the faithful mercies of David," that is, I will faithfully perform whatever I once promised to David out of free mercy. Paul rendered this from the Septuagint by "holy things," and understands Christ, who is the Holy of Holies and the foundation of all the promises (2 Cor. 1). From this he argues thus: God made with David a holy and eternal covenant (Ps. 89; 2 Sam. 7). But this rests on Christ. Therefore he too must be eternal, and consequently he rose again and was not to return to the grave, that is, he was not to die again.

units.la: Nota. Eundem semel oblatum, no-bis meruisse remfsionem, & salutem suffi-cientem, Hebr. 9.10. Ideo etiam dicebat: Consummatum est, Iohannis 19. Contra Missam.
units.tr: Note. That he, once offered, earned for us forgiveness and sufficient salvation (Heb. 9, 10). Therefore he also said: "It is finished" (John 19). Against the Mass.

units.la: III. Psalmo xvi. Probat de Christo de Locu Psa-bere intelligi, vt Petrus Act. 3. qui his plu-ra addit, &c.
units.tr: III. Psalm 16. He proves that this is to be understood of Christ, as Peter does in Acts 3, who adds more on these points, etc.

units.la: Interim Not. 1. Locutionem: Cum Defunctae aetati seruiuisset. Intelligit Dauidem, rn condnio vbi obdormiuit, defunctum fuisse omnibus officijs erga homines. Eadem est conditio omnium hominum. Hac vita defunc-ti, nihil possumus erga alios, neque hi erga nos, &c. Vide Luc.16. Confutatur intercessio Diuorum, Isa 63.1. Ioh.2. Spiritum apparitiones, 2. Sam.28. Exequiae, & sacra pro defunctis, quae Deus nulla instituit. Vide Leuiticum totum: in primis cap.21. Christum, Ioh.5. Luc.23. Apocal 14. Dum tempus est, operemur bonum, Gal.6.
units.tr: Meanwhile note 1. The expression "having served his own generation." He means that David, in the condition in which he fell asleep, had died to all the duties toward men. The condition of all men is the same. Once we have departed from this life, we can do nothing for others, nor they for us, etc. See Luke 16. The intercession of the saints is refuted (Isa. 63; John 2); apparitions of spirits (2 Sam. 28); funerals, and prayers for the dead, which God instituted in no way. See the whole of Leviticus, especially chapter 21; Christ (John 5; Luke 23); Rev. 14. While there is time, let us work good (Gal. 6).

units.la: 2. Mortis conditionem. 1. Ex Dei con filio morimur, in cuius manu sunt tempo ra nostra, Pfal.39.90.91. 31. Nihil possunt homines, Mat.10.
units.tr: 2. The condition of death. 1. We die by the counsel of God, in whose hand are our times (Ps. 39, 90, 91, 31). Men can do nothing (Matt. 10).

units.la: 2. Obdormimus, non perimus. Mors ergo quies est, Apo.14. Nec separamur a Christo, Ioh.11. Rom.8.
units.tr: 2. We fall asleep; we do not perish. Death is therefore rest (Rev. 14). Nor are we separated from Christ (John 11; Rom. 8).

units.la: 3. Colligimus ad patres, Gen.25.35.49.
units.tr: 3. We are gathered to the fathers (Gen. 25, 35, 49).

units.la: Sunt ergo certæ sedes animarum, Ioh.14. Piorum in sinu Abrahami, Luc.16 23. Matthæi 8. Impiorum item, &c. Ezech.32. Isaiæ 14.
units.tr: There are therefore certain abodes of souls (John 14): of the pious in the bosom of Abraham (Luke 16:23; Matt. 8), and likewise of the impious, etc. (Ezek. 32; Isa. 14).

units.la: 4. Caro corrumpitur, secundum illud, Gen.3. Arguit hoc factum sepulchrorum. Obseruemus autem finem: Ut induamur incorruptibilitate, 1.Cor.15 Phil 4. Ergo ne nos quidem æternam videbimus corruptionem. Imo in corruptione ista habemus spem resurrectionis. Simile sementis 1.Cor.15 Ioh.12.
units.tr: 4. The flesh is corrupted, according to that saying (Gen. 3). This fact shows the sepulchres. Let us however observe the end: that we may put on incorruptibility (1 Cor. 15; Phil. 4). Therefore we too shall not see eternal corruption. Indeed, in this corruption we have the hope of resurrection. It is like seed (1 Cor. 15; John 12).

units.la: Hac spe confirmati, Deo constanter seruiamus: simul vigilemus, & sedulo Oremus.
units.tr: Confirmed by this hope, let us serve God constantly; at the same time let us watch and pray diligently.

units.la: HOMILIA CXII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXII.

units.la: 38 Notum igitur sit vobis, fratres, annuntiari vobis remissionem peccatorum per ipsum.
units.tr: 38 Let it be known to you therefore, brothers, that forgiveness of sins is announced to you through him.

units.la: 39 Et ab omnibus, a quibus per Legem Moysis absolvi non potuistis, per hunc omnis qui credat, absolvi.
units.tr: 39 And from all those things from which you could not be absolved through the Law of Moses, through this one everyone who believes is absolved.

units.la: 40 Videte ergo, ne vos innuadat quod dictum est in Prophetis.
units.tr: 40 Take heed therefore, lest what was said in the Prophets come upon you.

units.la: 41 Videte o contemptores, & admiramini, & euanescite: quia opus operor ego diebus vestris, opus quod non credetis, si quis enarrauerit vobis.
units.tr: 41 Look, you despisers, and marvel, and perish: for I am doing a work in your days, a work which you will not believe, if anyone should declare it to you.

units.la: POstquam Paulus diligenter, & proli- xè demonstrauit, Iesum Christum ef- se humani generis redemptorem, qui pro pter nos mortuus, & ex mortuis resusci- tatus sit, subijcit modo concionis hu us conclusionem, qua duo adhuc agit. 1. Sum mam salutis per Christum nobis par- tæ proponit, vt huius commemoratione au- ditores ad huncamplexandum excitet. 2. Minatur Dei graue iudicium, si beneficium tantum aspernentur. Locus ergo est vtilissimus.
units.tr: Having diligently and at length demonstrated that Jesus Christ is the redeemer of the human race, who died for us and was raised from the dead, Paul now adds the conclusion of this sermon, in which he does two things. 1. He sets before them the sum of the salvation obtained for us through Christ, so that by recalling it he may stir his hearers to embrace it. 2. He threatens God's heavy judgment if they despise this benefit. The passage is therefore most useful.

units.la: I. Notum sit, &c. Rursus attentos facit, vt meminerint hæc ad se pertinere. Idem vero nobis dici putabimus. Deus enim nō ignota vult esse, quæ nobis in Christo eon- tulit. Euangelium siquidem pasim praedica- ri & homines charissimos laboribus & pe- riculis exerceri voluit.
units.tr: I. "Let it be known," etc. He again makes them attentive, so that they remember these things pertain to them. Yet we may think the same is said to us as well. For God does not want what he has bestowed on us in Christ to remain unknown. Indeed, he wished the gospel to be preached everywhere and good men to be exercised by labours and dangers.

units.la: Quid vero illud est, quod omnibus no- tum vult esse Paulus? Quod per hunc, &c. Sensus: Dedit quidem Deus patribus le- gem, sed per hanc nemo iustificari & serua- ri potuit, nec adhuc potest Christus vero nobis remissionem peccatorum meruit, quæ per Euangelium prædicatur: cui qui crediderit, is iustificatur. Conuenit cum Baptistæ dicto, Lex per Mosem, &c. Ioh. 1.
units.tr: What, then, is the thing Paul wants known to all? "Through this one, etc." The sense: God indeed gave the law to the fathers, but through it no one could be justified and saved, nor can anyone be yet. Christ, however, has merited for us forgiveness of sins, which is preached through the gospel; whoever believes in him is justified. This agrees with the saying of the Baptist, "The law was given through Moses," etc., John 1.

units.la: Sed obseruanda hic tota salutis ratio.
units.tr: But the whole order of salvation is to be observed here.

units.la: ¶ 1. Quæ omnium nostrūm conditio? Remissionis meminit, quia opus fit. Sunt ergo omnes homines peccatores, & propter peccatum ad mortem damnati, Ro. 6.3 Tanta autem noxa est, vt licet legem dederit Deus, nemo tamen per illam potuerit seruari. Præcepta enim morum, & vitæ nemo potest præstare, Matth. 5. &c. Deut.27. Ceremoniæ per se non prosunt, Psal 50.Heb. 10. Imò hæ quoq; quodammodo nobis exprobrant nostram miseriam, &c. Docet hoc omnis scriptura, Gen. 5 8.Ro.8. Sancti item omnes agnouerunt & confessi sunt, Iob.25. Ps.51.25 32.65 130. 143. Isa.64. Apostoli, Act 15. Rom 3. Arguuntur confidentes illi, qui iustitiam iactant, Luc.18. Tu hoc princi-pium teneto.
units.tr: ¶1. What is the condition of all of us? He mentions forgiveness because there is need of it. Therefore all men are sinners, and condemned to death on account of sin, Rom. 6. The harm is so great that, although God gave the law, no one could be saved by it. For no one can perform the precepts of morals and life, Matt. 5, etc.; Deut. 27. Ceremonies in themselves do not profit, Ps. 50; Heb. 10. Indeed, these too in some way reproach us with our misery, etc. All Scripture teaches this, Gen. 5, 8; Rom. 8. All the saints likewise have acknowledged and confessed it, Job 25; Ps. 51, 25, 32, 65, 130, 143; Isa. 64. So have the apostles, Acts 15; Rom. 3. Those confident ones who boast of their righteousness are refuted, Luke 18. Hold fast to this principle.

units.la: ¶ 2. Vnde ergo salus? Paulus de vno Christo loquitur. Quia autem ille ex gratia datus, (Ioh 3.1 Ioh.4.) salus quoq; gratuita est. Hic pro nobis homo factus, peccata nostra in se transtulit & expiauit, Isa. 53. Et nostra iustitia factus (1.Cor.1. Cor. 5.) nobis patrem placauit, Matth. 3. & 17. In hoc ergo vno omnia salus habetur, Isa. 42. Ioh.4. Act.4. Ioh.6. Euertuntur hic omnes satisfactiones & merita abhominibus confista. Si enim lex non potuit iustificare, ficare, quid facerent hominum traditiones? Isa.29. Matth. 15. Vide Epistolam ad Rom.11.
units.tr: ¶2. Whence, then, is salvation? Paul speaks of the one Christ alone. But since he was given out of grace (John 3; John 4), salvation too is gratuitous. Here he, made man for us, transferred our sins to himself and expiated them, Isa. 53. And, made our righteousness (1 Cor. 1; 1 Cor. 5), he appeased the Father for us, Matt. 3 and 17. In this one alone, therefore, all salvation is found, Isa. 42; John 4; Acts 4; John 6. All satisfactions and merits devised by men are overturned here. For if the law could not justify, what would human traditions accomplish? Isa. 29; Matt. 15. See the Epistle to the Romans 11.

units.la: ¶3. Quomodo salutis participes reddimur. De hoc Paulus duo dicit. 1. Quòd remisio peccatorum praedicetur per Christum. Ita de Euangelio loquitur Luc. 24. Isa.61. 2 Qui credit, iustificatur. Deus ergo Christum nobis offert per Euangelium, nos vero illum recipimus fide. Proprie iustificat Christus, Ioh. 1. 2. Cor.5. 1. Cor 1.1. Ioh.1. Isa.53. Acto. 5. Quia autem hunc fides apprehendit, per hanc iustificari nos docent Apostoli, Acto.15. Rom.3.4. Conuenit huic loco quod ipse loquitur, Ioh.5.15.17. Mar,16. &c.
units.tr: ¶3. How we are made partakers of salvation. On this Paul says two things. 1. That forgiveness of sins is preached through Christ. So he speaks of the gospel in Luke 24; Isa. 61. 2. Whoever believes is justified. God therefore offers Christ to us through the gospel, and we receive him by faith. Christ justifies properly, John 1; 2 Cor. 5; 1 Cor. 1; 1 John 1; Isa. 53; Acts 5. But since faith apprehends him, the apostles teach that we are justified through faith, Acts 15; Rom. 3, 4. What he himself says in John 5, 15, 17; Mark 16, etc., agrees with this passage.

units.la: In eo differt Christiana religio ab aliis. Omnes profitentur vnum summum Deum. Omnes pollicentur peccatorum remissionem & salutem. Sed variant in medio salutis. Euangelium hanc in vno Christo monstrat (Ioh.14.4. Matth 11. Acto.4.) & fidem in hunc praedicat, Gal 2.5. Haec fides catholica & Christiana est.
units.tr: In this the Christian religion differs from others. All profess one supreme God. All promise forgiveness of sins and salvation. But they vary about the means of salvation. The gospel shows this in the one Christ (John 14; Matt. 11; Acts 4) and preaches faith in him, Gal. 2, 5. This faith is catholic and Christian.

units.la: II. Concludit cum comminatione: nimirum quòd videret quales essent pleriique. Adducit autem locum, Hab.1, quem ip sis applicat per comparationem.
units.tr: II. He concludes with a threat, namely because he saw what sort of people most of them were. He adduces a passage, Hab. 1, which he applies to them by way of comparison.

units.la: Nota. ¶1. Verbi contemptum omnia
units.tr: Note. ¶1. Contempt for the Word surpasses all other sins.

units.la: Cap.13. peccata superare. Reliqua infirmitati carnis tribui possunt, Rom.7. Genes 8. Iac. 3. Sed illud diaboli proprium opus est, Ioh. 8 Ideo omnibus seculis punitum grauissime. In primis vide Iudaeos, 2.Par. 36. Luc. 19. At observemus hic peccare non eos modo, qui Christum ex professo reijciunt, vt ij de quibus Psal 2. Luc 19. verum etiam qui huius professionem vita scelerata polluunt. Euangelio enim poenitentia praedicatur, Mar 1. Luc. 24. Finis est obedientia fidei (2.Cor. 10. Rom. 1. 16.) vt sancti simus, & Deus in nobis glorificetur, Eph. 1 Thess. 4. Matth. 5. Qui hoc negligunt, non sunt Christiani.
units.tr: Chap. 13. The remaining sins can be attributed to the weakness of the flesh, Rom. 7; Gen. 8; James 3. But this is the devil's own work, John 8. Therefore it has always been punished most severely. Especially look at the Jews, 2 Chron. 36; Luke 19. But let us observe here that not only those who openly reject Christ sin, such as those of whom Ps. 2 and Luke 19 speak, but also those who pollute his profession by a wicked life. For repentance is preached in the gospel, Mark 1; Luke 24. The end is obedience of faith (2 Cor. 10; Rom. 1:16), that we may be holy and God may be glorified in us, Eph. 1; 1 Thess. 4; Matt. 5. Those who neglect this are not Christians.

units.la: Vt agendum cum talibus. Arguendi liberè, & citandi ad Dei tribunal, vt sciant, quid ipsos maneat. Ita olim iusti Prophetae, Isa 58 1. Ezech 22. Idem Christus fecit, Marth 10.11.21.23 24. Apostoli hic & alibi. Imo contumaciores tradiderunt Satanae, 1.Cor. 5 2.Cor. 12. 13.
units.tr: How we should deal with such people: freely reprove them and summon them to God's tribunal, so that they know what awaits them. Thus of old the righteous prophets did, Isa. 58; Ezek. 22. Christ did the same, Matt. 10, 11, 21, 23, 24. The apostles did so here and elsewhere. Indeed, they handed the more obstinate over to Satan, 1 Cor. 5; 2 Cor. 12, 13.

units.la: Errant, qui illud hodie indignè ferunt & alienum putant ab Euangelica manuetudine. Imo potius alienum ab Euangelio est, seruire mundo & peccatis, Ioh 15.13. 1.Iohan. 2. Roman. 6.12. Galat. 5.1. Cor. 6. Col. 3.
units.tr: They are mistaken who take this badly today and think it foreign to evangelical gentleness. Rather, it is foreign to the gospel to serve the world and sins, John 15:13; 1 John 2; Rom. 6:12; Gal. 5:1; 1 Cor. 6; Col. 3.

units.la: HAEC erant nobis hodie consideranda dida diligentius, qui indies in peius proficimus, & in omnem licentiam effundimur, vt verè de nobis dici posit, quod de Iudaeis, Mal. 1. Ex eo pater, multos non credere (Ioh 6.) sed Nabales esse, Psal. 14. 53. 94. 2. Pet. 3. At meminerimus, Deum esse ignem consumentem, nec rideri, Hebr. 12. Gal. 6. Oremus.
units.tr: These things were to be considered by us today more carefully, who daily grow worse and pour ourselves out into every licence, so that what was said of the Jews, Mal. 1, can truly be said of us. From this it is clear that many do not believe (John 6) but are Nabals, Ps. 14, 53, 94; 2 Pet. 3. But let us remember that God is a consuming fire and is not mocked, Heb. 12; Gal. 6. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXIII.

units.la: 42 Egressus autem eius e Synagoga Iudaeorum, rogarunt Gentes, vt in proxime sequens Sabbathum loquerentur sibi haec verba.
units.tr: 42 As Paul and Barnabas went out of the synagogue of the Jews, the Gentiles begged that these words might be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.

units.la: 43 Soluto autem conuentu, sequuti sunt multi ex Iudaeis & religiosis pro felytis Paulum ac Barnabam, qui alloquentes eos, persuaserunt eis, vt perseuerarent in gratia Dei.
units.tr: 43 When the assembly had broken up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking with them, persuaded them to persevere in the grace of God.

units.la: DEus per Isaiam cap. 55. praeclarè admodum de verbo suo pronuntiat: Vt imber aut nix de caelo descendit, & germinare facit, ita erit verbum meum, quod exit de ore meo: nō redibit ad me vacuū, sed faciet quęcunq; volo & prosperabitur in his, ad quæ misi illud. Licet enim multi sint, quibus frustra prædicatur, habet tamen Deus vbique suos, in quibus fructi-
units.tr: God, through Isaiah, chapter 55, speaks most excellently about his word: "As rain or snow comes down from heaven and makes things grow, so will my word be, which goes out of my mouth; it will not return to me empty, but it will do what I wish and will prosper in the things for which I sent it." For although there are many to whom it is preached in vain, God still has his own people everywhere, in whom it bears fruit.

units.la: Ioh. 6. ; Psal. 14. ; 53. ; 94. ; 2. Pet. 3. ; Hebr. 12. ; Gal. 6. ficat.Idem docet sementis quoq; parabo- la,Matth.13 Luc 8 Exemplum huius memorabile hic proponitur. Post descriptā enim concionem Pauli, effectus indicatur, & duo proponuntur hominum genera, quorum hi quidem imitandi, illi verò fugiendi sunt, si quidem verbum Dei nobis salutare esse volumus.
units.tr: John 6; Psalm 14; 53; 94; 2 Peter 3; Hebrews 12; Galatians 6. The parable of the sower teaches the same, Matthew 13; Luke 8. A memorable example of this is set before us here. After Paul's sermon is described, its effect is shown, and two kinds of people are set before us. The one kind is to be imitated, the other to be avoided, if we want the word of God to be salutary for us.

units.la: I. Iudæi quidem ex synagoga exiuisse dicuntur: nimirum priusquam cœtus dimitteretur. Causa, quòd prædicationem de Christo non possent ferre. Proprium Iudæis. Ita verò impletum, quod præuixe rat Deus, Isa.6. Et hi postea nouum certamen excitarunt. Vbi No TA. ¶ Reprobo- rum ingenium & mores. Qui ex Deo nati sunt, verbū eius audiunt, ita oues vocem sui pastoris agnoscunt, Ioh.8.10. E contra impij & reprobi nihil minus ferre possunt. Et tam abest, vt illud quærant, vt oblatum respuant: aures obturent, & fugiant. Vide Psal.58.
units.tr: I. The Jews are said to have gone out of the synagogue, namely before the assembly was dismissed. The reason was that they could not bear the preaching about Christ. This is characteristic of the Jews, and so what God had foretold in Isaiah 6 was fulfilled. And these men afterwards stirred up a new struggle. NOTE: The disposition and morals of the reprobate. Those who are born of God hear his word; so sheep recognise the voice of their shepherd, John 8 and 10. On the contrary, the godless and reprobate can bear nothing less. Far from seeking it, they reject it when it is offered; they stop their ears and flee. See Psalm 58.

units.la: Disce de illis iudicare, qui similem impatientiam gestibus produnt, è templo in dignabundi exeunt, Ioh.8. Et sunt hæc prę ludia maioris impietatis, 2.Tim.3. Nam si tales vrgeantur fortius, aperti hostes fiunt Sic Pharao, Exo.5.8 9.10. Achab, 1.Re gū 18.21.22. Amazias, Amos 7. Iudæi, Ier.44
units.tr: Learn to judge those who show similar impatience by their gestures, who leave the temple in disdain, John 8. These are the prelude to greater impiety, 2 Timothy 3. For if such people are pressed harder, they become open enemies. So Pharaoh, Exodus 5, 8, 9, 10; Ahab, 1 Kings 18, 21, 22; Amaziah, Amos 7; the Jews, Jeremiah 44.

units.la: Itaque non locum demus carnis fastidio, neipfi quoque in peius proficiamus. Sed imitemur alteros, de quibus sequitur.
units.tr: Therefore let us not give room to the loathing of the flesh, lest we too advance for the worse. Rather, let us imitate the others, of whom the text goes on to speak.

units.la: II. Gentes dicuntur illos rogasse, &c.
units.tr: II. The Gentiles are said to have asked them, etc.

units.la: Mirum hoc. Quem reijciunt domestici, hunc gentes recipiunt. Sed sic prædictû Isa.54. Matth.8.3. Hos.1. Veruntamen coniungunt se aliqui ex Iudæis & proselytis, sicut promissum, Isa.10. Ioel 2. Quid vero de his dicitur? ¶1. Rogant, vt ipsis rursus prædicent. Non ergo eos offendit, quòd alij exierant indignabundi. Quin accensi desiderio verbi, cupiunt amplius audire. Ita nos quoque de verbo Dei non iudicemus ex hominum authoritate, sed illud in se æstimemus. In mundo semper fiet quod habetur 1.Cor.1.2. At pij cum Dauid dicant: Psal.1.19.119. Vide Luc.10.
units.tr: This is remarkable. Those whom their own people reject, the Gentiles receive. Yet this was foretold, Isaiah 54; Matthew 8:3; Hosea 1. Nevertheless, some of the Jews and proselytes join themselves to them, as was promised, Isaiah 10; Joel 2. What is said about these people? (1) They ask that these things be preached to them again. So the offence taken by the others who had gone out in disdain did not put them off. Indeed, kindled with desire for the word, they want to hear more. So we too should not judge the word of God by human authority, but weigh it in itself. In the world what is written, 1 Corinthians 1:2, will always happen. But the godly, with David, say: Psalms 1, 19, 119. See Luke 10.

units.la: ¶2. Sequuntur Apostolos, vt pote veritatis & salutis doctores. Neque pudet eos illorum, qui plerisque exosi & καθάρματα mundi erant, 1.Cor.4. Ergo neque Euangelij eos pudet, sed hoc pluris faciunt quàm mundi amicitiam. Et hoc Christus requirit a suis, Mat.10. Mar.8. Ideo dicebat Paulus, Rom 1. &c. Hos imitemur, neque nos moueant eorum exempla, qui Dei verbum fastidiunt, vt Israelitæ Manna, Num. 11. Qui item mundo placere volunt. Hi enim nō possunt Deo placere, Iac. 4. Gal: 1. Et cupiditatib. indulgendo seipsos perdunt, Num. 11.
units.tr: (2) They follow the apostles, as teachers of truth and salvation. Nor are they ashamed of those men who were hated by most and were the offscouring [καθάρματα] of the world, 1 Corinthians 4. Therefore they are not ashamed of the gospel either, but they value it more than the friendship of the world. Christ requires this of his people, Matthew 10; Mark 8. So Paul said, Romans 1, etc. Let us imitate these people, and let us not be moved by the examples of those who loathe God's word, as the Israelites loathed the manna, Numbers 11, and likewise of those who want to please the world. For these cannot please God, James 4; Galatians 1, and by indulging their lusts they destroy themselves, Numbers 11.

units.la: Quid Apostoli amicè Alloquuntur, non statim rigidi examinant, excommunicant. Hortantur item vt in gratia Dei perseuerent, id est, Euangelio, per quod nobis in Christo gratia Dei offertur, Luc. 2. Ioh. 1. 3. Mat. 5. 17.
units.tr: Note how the apostles speak to them kindly and do not at once examine them harshly or excommunicate them. They also exhort them to persevere in the grace of God, that is, in the gospel, through which the grace of God is offered to us in Christ, Luke 2; John 1; Matthew 5:17.

units.la: Vbi NoT. ¶ 1. Non sufficere, si Christum obiter apprehendimus, sed perseuerantia opus esse, Luc. 9. Matth. 24. Exempla sunt in omnibus hominum studijs & factis. In militia. In literarum studio. In re Medica. Inprimis in salutis æternæ negotio, vbi multa reuocant, impediunt, Matt. 12. 2. Pet 2.
units.tr: NOTE. (1) It is not enough to lay hold of Christ in passing; perseverance is needed, Luke 9; Matthew 24. There are examples of this in all human pursuits and deeds: in warfare, in the study of letters, in medicine, and above all in the business of eternal salvation, where many things call us back and hinder us, Matthew 12; 2 Peter 2.

units.la: ¶ 2. Ne vero perseuerentia in pertinaciam degeneret, certum nobis esse oportet, in quo perseueremus. Vide 1. Ioh. 2.
units.tr: (2) But so that perseverance does not degenerate into obstinacy, we must be sure of what we persevere in. See 1 John 2.

units.la: Loquitur autem de doctrina Apostolorum, cuius est summa. 1. Omnes homines peccatores esse Rom. 3. 1. Ioh. 1.
units.tr: Now he speaks of the doctrine of the apostles, whose sum is this:

units.la: 2. Iustitiam & salutem omnes habere in Christo, 1. Cor. 1. 2. Act. 4.
units.tr: 1. All men are sinners, Romans 3; 1 John 1.

units.la: 3. Hunc apprehendi fide, & idem hac nos iustificari. Act. 13.
units.tr: 2. All have righteousness and salvation in Christ, 1 Corinthians 1; Acts 4.

units.la: 4. Quoad opera, Deum colere in spiritu & veritate, Iohan. 4. Sanctitatem tueri, 1.
units.tr: 3. This is laid hold of by faith, and by it we are justified, Acts 13.

units.la: 1 Thess. 4. Heb. 11. 12 Diligere proximum, Rom. 13. 1. Cor. 13. Haec doctrina simplex & perspicua est & sola debet admitti, Gal. 1. Retineri item, ut cum Petro dicamus, Iohan. 6.
units.tr: 4. As to works, we worship God in spirit and truth, John 4; we keep holiness, 1 Thessalonians 4; Hebrews 11, 12; we love our neighbour, Romans 13; 1 Corinthians 13. This doctrine is simple and plain, and it alone ought to be admitted, Galatians 1. It is likewise to be retained, so that with Peter we may say, John 6.

units.la: § 3. Qui in hac perseuerant, ij perstant in gratia Dei. Exponitur 1. Io. 2. quia in Patre & Filio manent. Ita Christus pollicetur, Ioh. 14. Econtra qui hanc vel non admittunt, vel ab jciunt, super hos manet ira Dei, Ioh. 3. Exempla sunt in Iudaeis, quibus accidit quod praedictum Lu. 19. Mat. 23 24. Videmus hodie quid fiat in illis locis by Euangelium reiectum, & oppugnatum fuit, & adhuc oppugnatur.
units.tr: § 3. Those who persevere in this doctrine persist in the grace of God. This is explained by 1 John 2: because they abide in the Father and the Son. So Christ promises, John 14. On the contrary, those who either do not admit this doctrine or cast it off, on them the wrath of God remains, John 3. Examples are found among the Jews, to whom what was foretold in Luke 19 and Matthew 23 and 24 has happened. We see today what happens in those places where the gospel has been rejected and attacked, and is still attacked.

units.la: Tradidi vobis doctrinam hanc annis 33, bona fide, quantum Dominus dedit. Nunc ita volente Deo, vocatione aliam nactus, vos commendo gratiae Domini, quem rogo ut eum vobis pastorem det, qui in eadem vos seruet bona pace ad nominis sui gloriam & veltram salutem. Oremus.
units.tr: I have delivered this doctrine to you for thirty-three years, in good faith, as far as the Lord has given me the means. Now, as God wills, having obtained another calling, I commend you to the grace of the Lord, whom I beg to give you such a minister as will keep you in the same good peace, to the glory of his name and your salvation. Let us pray.

units.la: Ad quitas. E clefiam juam adhortor.
units.tr: Finally, I exhort your congregation.

units.la: RODOLPHVS SIMLERVS CHRISTIANO Lectori, S.D.
units.tr: RODOLPHUS SIMLERUS, to the Christian reader, greeting.

units.la: QVam modò lustrauimus Homiliam centesimam decimam tertiam, ea illustris et tanquam Cygnæa vox fuit reuerendi senis D. Gualtheri, qua (in D. Ballingeri piæ memoriæ locū a S. P. Q. T. vocatus) Ecclesiæ suæ ad Petrum, cui tringinta tribus annis summa fidei, doctrinæ & pietatis laude præfuit, a. d. 2. Octob. an. 1575 valedixit. De quo te admonendum duxi, Christiane Lectore, vt & Epilogum huius, ac in eo fidei pastoris & de grege suo ad extremum soliciti, exemplum commodius intelligere; at præterea diuersam Homiliarum quæ præcesserunt hactenus, ab iis quæ posthac sequuntur, rationem atque genium melius diiudicare possis, a diuerso, quo vtrææque scriptæ sunt, tempore. Priores enim posterioribus ministerij sui annis consignauit austor; posteriores exprimi eius Tyrocinij schedas schedis hinc inde disiectis, summo labore suos nos collegimus, & non paucis in locis resarciuimus. Tu eodem quo offeruntur animo singula accipe & iudica. Vale.
units.tr: The hundred and thirteenth homily, which we have just gone through, was the illustrious and, as it were, swan-song voice of the venerable old man Mr. Gwalther, with which (after he had been called by the Senate and People of Zurich to the place of the late Mr. Ballinger, of pious memory) he bade farewell to his church at St. Peter's, over which he had presided for thirty-three years with the highest reputation for faith, doctrine and piety, on 2 October 1575. I thought you should be reminded of this, Christian reader, so that you may better understand both the epilogue of this homily and the example in it of a pastor of the faith who was anxious about his flock to the very end; and so that you may be better able to judge the different character and spirit of the homilies that came before, compared with those that follow, from the different times at which each was written. For the author wrote the earlier ones in the later years of his ministry, while we, with great labour, have gathered together the later ones, which are the notes of his early training, scattered here and there among loose papers, and in not a few places have repaired them. Receive and judge each piece in the same spirit in which they are offered. Farewell.

units.la: HOMILIA CXIV.
units.tr: HOMILY CXIV.

units.la: 44 Sequente vero Sabbatho, vrbs prope tota, coacta est ad audiendū sermonem Dei.
units.tr: 44 On the following Sabbath almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.

units.la: 45 Visa autem turba, Iudæi repleti sunt inuidia, & contradicebant iis, quæ a Paulo dicebantur, contradicentes ac blasphemantes.
units.tr: 45 But when the crowd saw this, the Jews were filled with envy and contradicted the things that were said by Paul, opposing and blaspheming.

units.la: 46 Tunc libertate vsi, Paulus ac Barnabas dixerunt: Vobis necesse fuit primum exponi sermone Dei: postquam autem repellitis illud, & indignos vosipsos decernitis æterna vita, ecce conuertimur ad Gentes.
units.tr: 46 Then Paul and Barnabas, speaking boldly, said: "It was necessary that the word of God be declared to you first; but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles."

units.la: 47 Sic enim nobis mandauit Dominus, dicens: Constitui te vt sis lux Gentium, vt sis saluti vsque ad vltimas terras.
units.tr: 47 "For so the Lord has commanded us, saying: I have set you to be a light to the Gentiles, that you may be salvation to the ends of the earth."

units.la: Dominus apud Isaiam Cap. 55. ait: Vt imber aut nix de cœlo descendit, & illuc non redit, sed irrigat terram, & germinare eam facit: Ita erit verbum meum. um, quod exit de ore meo, non redit ad me vacuum, sed faciet quaecunque volo, & prosperabitur in his, ad quae misi illud. Licet enim multi sint, qui illud non rite excipiunt, habet tamen vbique suos Dominus, in quibus fructificat. Matt.13. Luc. 8. Exemplum huius praelens locus in Pauli auditoribus exhibet, in quo duo auditorum genera nobis proposita fuerunt. Primum Reproborum in Iudaeis, qui fallidi- unt verbum, fugiunt, aures obturant. Alterum Electorum in Gentibus, nec non Iudaeis quibusdam & religiosis proselytis, qui pastoris sui vocem agnoscunt, Ioh.10. & verbú Dei amant, quia ex D.nati, Iô 8.
units.tr: The Lord says through Isaiah, chapter 55: "As rain or snow comes down from heaven and does not return there, but waters the earth and makes it bring forth, so shall my word be, which goes out of my mouth. It shall not return to me empty, but it shall do whatever I wish, and it shall prosper in those things for which I sent it." For although many do not receive it rightly, the Lord always has those in whom it bears fruit. Matt. 13; Luke 8. This passage shows us an example of this in the hearers of Paul, in which two kinds of hearers are set before us. The first is the reprobate among the Jews, who reject the word, flee from it, and stop their ears. The second is the elect among the Gentiles, and also certain Jews and devout proselytes, who recognise the voice of their shepherd (John 10) and love the word of God, because they are born of God (John 8).

units.la: Sequitur, Quid vlterius tentarint, Reprobri, ac quibus armis & artibus oppugnarint veritatem: Qua item fiducia ijs ob stiterint Paulus & Barnabas.
units.tr: It follows: what further the reprobate attempted, and with what weapons and arts they assailed the truth; and likewise with what confidence Paul and Barnabas resisted them.

units.la: I. Certamen aduersus nascentem Ecclesiam concitant. Quo docemur eo magis furere impios, quo magis propagatur Evangelium, nec nouum esse, si quid simile eueniat, Lu.2. Sed Notq 1. Occasionem certaminis. Tota ciuitas conuenit, mirum vulgato rumore, alijs bono instituto, alijs ex curiositate concurrentibus. Et parati sunt congregatis praedicare Apostoli.
units.tr: I. They stir up strife against the newly born Church. We are taught that the more the gospel spreads, the more the impious rage; and it is nothing new if something similar happens (Luke 2). Notes: 1. The occasion of the strife. The whole city came together, a great crowd drawn by the spreading rumour, some with a good purpose, others out of curiosity. And the apostles were ready to preach to the assembled people.

units.la: Docemur, studio opus esse in Euangelio lio propagando, nec vllam omitti debere occasionem. Sic Christus, Ioh.4.3.6.&c.
units.tr: We are taught that there must be zeal in spreading the gospel, and that no opportunity should be neglected. So Christ (John 4; 3; 6, etc.).

units.la: ¶ 2. Causa, Iudæi cùm turbas tantas videnr, replentur zelo nimirum, quòd partim inuidia & ambitione moti, suæ gloriæ timerent (Ioh.5.) partim præpostero legis zelo abrepti (Rom.10.) indigne ferunt, sibi æquari gentes. Sic Act.21. Huc refer, quod habuimus Act.11.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The cause. When the Jews saw such great crowds, they were filled with zeal, moved partly by envy and ambition, fearing for their own glory (John 5), and partly carried away by a misguided zeal for the law (Rom. 10), and they took it badly that the Gentiles should be made equal to them. So Acts 21. Here belongs what we had in Acts 11.

units.la: Patet hinc, non quemuis zelum Deo probari. Videndum, ne quis malus affectus concurrat, quod plerunque solet fieri. Deinde inquirenda Dei voluntas, Num. 15. Rom.10.
units.tr: It is clear from this that not every zeal is approved by God. We must take care lest some wicked disposition mingle in, as usually happens. Then the will of God must be sought (Num. 15; Rom. 10).

units.la: ¶ 3. Iudæos, & quid illi faciant, qui ante exiuerant, nec voluerant audire, Contradicunt Paulo. Vbi rationibus nihil proficiunt, ad conuitia conuertuntur. Fit hoc etiam hodie frequenter.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The Jews, and what those do who had gone out before and had not wished to hear, contradict Paul. Where they accomplish nothing by reasoning, they turn to insults. This also happens often today.

units.la: Interim vides, quò perducat nos veritatis odium, si quando illi indulgeamus. Apertos hostes & blasphemos reddit, & calumniatores. Obstandum ergo principijs
units.tr: Meanwhile you see where hatred of the truth leads us, if we ever indulge it. It makes men open enemies, blasphemers and slanderers. Therefore we must resist the beginnings.

units.la: II. Apostoli quid: Sumpta fiducia oppo- nunt sese, non cedunt. Ita instructos esse decet ministros, Tit.1. Huc pertinet Iere. 1. Ita reliqui Prophetæ, 1. Reg.18.21 22. Amoz 7. Ideo Christus prædicit suis pericula, & cótra hæc armat, Luc.10,21. Mat.10.
units.tr: II. What the apostles do: having taken up confidence, they set themselves against them and do not yield. Ministers ought to be equipped in this way (Titus 1). Here belongs Jeremiah 1. So also the other prophets (1 Kings 18:21–22; Amos 7). Therefore Christ foretells dangers to his people and arms them against them (Luke 10:21; Matt. 10).

units.la: Debent singuli sibi accommodare, vt quò magis furiunt impij, eò fortiùs sese opponant. Est hoc veræ fidei ingenii, Pf.72.118.
units.tr: Each should prepare himself, so that the more the impious rage, the more bravely he sets himself against them. This is the nature of true faith (Ps. 72; 118).

units.la: Oratio Pauli ponitur, qua excommunicationis sententiam fert in incurabiles, tandem faciunt, quod mandauit Christus Matt.10, Luc.10. Quid enim sperarent amplius de talibus?
units.tr: Paul's speech is set down, in which he pronounces the sentence of excommunication against the incurable. At last they do what Christ commanded (Matt. 10; Luke 10). For what could they hope for more from such men?

units.la: I. Ingratitudinem exprobrat, Deus vo- bis primis voluit prædicari, propter promissiones, Rom.9. Exod.19. Matt.10. Act.1. Sed vos repellitis, &c.
units.tr: I. He rebukes their ingratitude: God wished the word to be preached to you first, on account of the promises (Rom. 9; Exod. 19; Matt. 10; Acts 1). But you reject it, etc.

units.la: II. Poenam infert: Indigni vita æterna, idque vestro ipsorum iudicio, dum scilicet fastiditis oblatam in Christo salutem. Huc faciunt, quæ de similibus dicuntur, Matt.10.23. Luc.9. &c.
units.tr: II. He inflicts punishment: unworthy of eternal life, and that by your own judgment, since you despise the salvation offered in Christ. Here belong the things said about such people (Matt. 10:23; Luke 9, etc.).

units.la: III. Conuertimur ad gentes. Docet tempus esse, vt impleatur quod est Hos.1. & 2. Matth.21. Ita videmus, regno Christi nihil decedere propter nostram incredulitatem & ingratitudinem. Sic Baptista, Mat.3.
units.tr: III. We turn to the Gentiles. He teaches that the time has come for what is written in Hosea 1 and 2 to be fulfilled (Matt. 21). Thus we see that nothing is lost to the kingdom of Christ because of our unbelief and ingratitude. So the Baptist (Matt. 3).

units.la: IV. Probat id debere fieri per If.49. ne videantur prophanare gratiam Dei Assericur gentiū vocatio, de qua sæpe iam, &c.
units.tr: IV. He proves that this must be done from Isaiah 49, lest they seem to profane the grace of God. The calling of the Gentiles is affirmed, about which we have often spoken already, etc.

units.la: Patet interim hic, quid in Christo nobis datum: Lux & salus. Hæc ex illa sequitur, Ioh.17. Et quidem solus hic illuminat nos Dei cognitione, Ioh.14. Idem vnicus salusalutis author est, Actorum 4. Ambulemus in luce hac, & salutem amplectamur, Ioh. 12. &c. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile it is clear here what has been given us in Christ: light and salvation. The latter follows from the former (John 17). Indeed he alone enlightens us with the knowledge of God (John 14). The same one alone is the author of salvation (Acts 4). Let us walk in this light and embrace salvation (John 12, etc.). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXV.
units.tr: HOMILY CXV.

units.la: 48 Gentes autem hæc audientes, gaudebant quia sunt, & glorificabant sermonem Domini, & crediderunt quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: 48 And the Gentiles, hearing this, rejoiced that they were, and glorified the word of the Lord, and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.

units.la: 49 Perferebatur autem sermo Domini per totam illam regionem.
units.tr: 49 The word of the Lord was spread through all that region.

units.la: 50 Iudæi vero exitimulārunt mulieres religiosas & honestas, & primos urbis, & excitarunt persecutionem in Paulum ac Barnabam, & ejecerunt eos e finibus suis.
units.tr: 50 But the Jews stirred up the devout and honourable women and the leading men of the city, raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their borders.

units.la: 51 At illi excusso pulvere pedum suorum in eos, venerunt Iconium.
units.tr: 51 But they, shaking the dust off their feet against them, came to Iconium.

units.la: 52 Discipuli vero replebantur gaudio & spiritu sancto.
units.tr: 52 And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

units.la: QAmuis Domino nostro Iesu Christo a Deo patre regnum & omnis potestas data sit, eundem tamen suos in mundo aduersarios habituru, passim praedicitur, Psal. 2. 110. Zach. 12. Et de his Christus ipse Apostolos admonet, Matth. 10. Mar. 13. &c. Exemplum vero huius luculentissimum praefens historia continet. Vehit Paulus Antiochiam & docet. Incipit aures praebere tota ciuitas, vt iam conse-ctum v dicatur negotium. Sed mox Iudaei insurgunt, qui maximas turbas dant, quibus tamen fortissime se opponunt Apostoli, & poenam denuntiant, iuxta id quod est Matt 21. Sequitur.
units.tr: Although the kingdom and all power have been given to our Lord Jesus Christ by God the Father, it is nevertheless foretold everywhere that he will have adversaries in the world: Ps. 2, Ps. 110, Zech. 12. Christ himself warns the apostles of this, Matt. 10, Mark 13, etc. The present history contains a most striking example of it. Paul comes to Antioch and teaches. The whole city begins to lend its ears, so that the business is now said to be as good as settled. But soon the Jews rise up, who stir up very great disturbances, against whom the apostles nevertheless oppose themselves most bravely, and they threaten punishment, according to what is said in Matt. 21. It follows:

units.la: I Successus regni Christi in medijs tur bis. Gentes gaudent, non quidem Iudaeorum ru na(Rom.11.)sed quod audirent, sed olim à Deo electos esse. Glorificant verbum Dei & credunt &c. Diuulgatur verbum
units.tr: I. The success of Christ's kingdom in the midst of tumults. The Gentiles rejoice, not indeed at the Jews' ruin, but because they hear that they too were once chosen by God (Rom. 11). They glorify the word of God and believe, etc. The word is spread abroad.

units.la: NOT. Qui ist fuerint de quibus haec dicuntur: Ordinati ad vitam aeternam. Explicitur, unde fit hoc, quod in medijs tur bis credunt homines. Nimirum ex libera & gratuita electione Dei. Si enim homi-nem spectes, id ex semetipso non habet, Ioh 3.6. Matth 11.16. 2 Cor.3. Deus autem suos ab aeterno elegit in Christo, Ephes.1. Eosdem suo tempore vocat & efficaciter trahit, Rom 8. Tales etiam se vocari agnoscunt, & sequuntur, Ioh 10. Quotquot ergo ex horum numero Anthiochiae fuerunt, crediderunt, neque hos impedire potuerunt Iudaei.
units.tr: NOTE. Who were those of whom these things are said: "ordained to eternal life". It is explained whence it comes that men believe in the midst of tumults: namely from the free and gratuitous election of God. For if you look at man, he has this not from himself (John 3:6; Matt. 11:16; 2 Cor. 3). But God chose his own from eternity in Christ (Eph. 1); at their appointed time he calls them and effectually draws them (Rom. 8). Such people also acknowledge that they are called, and they follow (John 10). Therefore, as many of their number at Antioch were there, they believed, and the Jews could not hinder these.

units.la: Seruiunt haec: A.Institutioni. Docent enim vt praedestinatio consideranda debeat. Nimirum in Christo, & vt intelligamus salutem nostram ex mera gratia Dei pen‑dere.Eph.1.Iohan.15.Roman.8.9 B.Con‑solationi in persecutionibus, & simul no‑stræ salutis certitudinem asserunt. Non mutatur Dei ordo,Rom. 11.Insuperabilis quoque est Christus,Mat.16.18. Hinc illa Ioh.10.Mat.24. Qui ergo per fidé in Chri‑sto se inueniunt,non possunt excidere,ad Roman.8.Aliæ quæstiones valeant,Roma‑nor.9.
units.tr: These points serve: A. For instruction. For they teach that predestination ought to be considered in Christ, and that we understand our salvation to depend on the pure grace of God (Eph. 1; John 15; Rom. 8, 9). B. For consolation in persecutions; at the same time they assert the certainty of our salvation. God's order is not changed (Rom. 11). Christ is also invincible (Matt. 16:18). Hence those words of John 10 and Matt. 24. Therefore those who find themselves in Christ through faith cannot fall away (Rom. 8). Other questions may stand aside (Rom. 9).

units.la: ¶2. Quid isti fecerint? Gauisi sunt ver‑bo & gratia Dei.Ita iubemur, Phillip.3.4. &c. Est hic mirabilis effectus verbi, &c. Rom.5.Mat.5. Act.5.
units.tr: ¶2. What did they do? They rejoiced in the word and grace of God. Thus we are commanded (Phil. 3:4, etc.). Here is a wonderful effect of the word (Rom. 5; Matt. 5; Acts 5).

units.la: 2. Glorificauerunt verbu Dei.Gratitudi‑nis hoc fuit.Fit maximè, quando nos per fidem reuerenter subijcimus verbo Dei, & sanctè viuimus, 2.Cor.10. Ideo additur quod crediderint. Arguuntur nostri secu‑limores, & qui electionis doctrina pieta‑tis exercitia euerti clamant.
units.tr: 2. They glorified the word of God. This was an act of gratitude. It happens most of all when we reverently submit ourselves to the word of God through faith and live holily (2 Cor. 10). Therefore it is added that they believed. Our worldly-minded critics are refuted here, and those who cry out that the doctrine of election overthrows the exercises of piety.

units.la: ¶3. Diuulgatur verbum Dei per omnem regionem. Adeo nihil efficitur impiorum conatibus. Sic factum Act.8.11.&c. Spirat Spiritus vbi vult Ioh.3. Isa.55. Quòd ho‑die minùs prosperè succedit,nostræ igna‑uiæ debetur,&c.
units.tr: ¶3. The word of God is spread through every region. So nothing is accomplished by the efforts of the impious. So it was done (Acts 8:11, etc.). The Spirit breathes where he wills (John 3; Isa. 55). That things succeed less prosperously today is owed to our sloth, etc.

units.la: II. Nouus tumultus & aperta persecu‑tio excitatur,cum priori certamine nihil
units.tr: II. A new tumult and open persecution is stirred up, although the enemies had achieved nothing in the earlier struggle.

units.la: profecissent hostes.No t. q 1. Authores Iudaei fuerunt, vt verum videas quod est. 1.Theff.2.Obserua autem in illis Dei iudi-cium,quodqj merito illis acciderint, quae minatur Dominus Luc.19. Matt 23. Idem manet omnes Christi hostes,Zach.12.
units.tr: Note 1. The authors were Jews, so that you may see the truth of what is said (1 Thess. 2). Observe in them God's judgment, and that they deservedly suffered what the Lord threatens (Luke 19; Matt. 23). The same stands for all Christ's enemies (Zech. 12).

units.la: q 2. Instrumenta & socij, quibus pug-nant. A.Mulieres religiofq & honeft q,quq nimirum ex gentibus legem Mosis am-plexae fuerant. Has in suas partes pertra-hunt,quia natura fuperftitiofiores sunt,& ad seducendum idoneae, maxime fi reli-gionis species accedat.Idem in seductori-bus notat Paulus,2.Tim.3.Exempla Gen. 3.Iefabel. Solomon, &c. Admonentur hic mulieres, vt sibi caueant,& ne fucatae re-ligioni confidant.
units.tr: Note 2. The instruments and allies with which they fight. A. Devout and honourable women, who of course had embraced the law of Moses from among the Gentiles. They draw these to their side, because by nature they are more superstitious and suited to seduction, especially if an appearance of religion is added. Paul notes the same of seducers (2 Tim. 3). Examples: Gen. 3, Jezebel, Solomon, etc. Women are admonished here to take care for themselves, and not to trust in a feigned religion.

units.la: B.Proceres quoque extimulant, nimi-rum quasi publicae pacis turbatores.Sic Amasias, Amos 7. &c. Has sunt impio-rum artes, quibus etiam hodie pugnatur. Et arguuntur, qui religiones ex hominum sanctimonia & authoritate aestimant,Mat. 11.1.Cor.1.
units.tr: B. They also stir up the leading men, namely as disturbers of the public peace. So Amaziah (Amos 7), etc. These are the arts of the impious, by which they fight even today. And those are refuted who judge religions by the holiness and authority of men (Matt. 11; 1 Cor. 1).

units.la: q 3.Effectus.Lijciunt suis finibus in exi-lium. Coniuncta huic bonorum amissio. Sic Actor.8.Heb.10.Apoc.2. Frequens hoc die.Non offendamur. Permittit Deus, vt potentiam suam declaret, dum nihilomi-nus nus suos seruat. Vt suos Christo conformes reddat, Roman.8 2.Tim.2.Luc.22. Vt morificet carnem & fidè exploret, 1.Pe. 4. Vt mundum vilescere faciat. Opus hoc. Meditemur ergo promissiones, Mar. 10. Ioh.16. Matt.5.
units.tr: Note 3. The effect. They cast them out of their borders into exile. The loss of goods is joined to this (Acts 8; Heb. 10; Rev. 2). This is frequent today; let us not be offended. God permits it so that he may display his power, while nevertheless he preserves his own. He does it to make his people conformed to Christ (Rom. 8; 2 Tim. 2; Luke 22), to mortify the flesh and test faith (1 Pet. 4), and to make the world grow worthless. This is his work. Let us therefore meditate on the promises (Mark 10; John 16; Matt. 5).

units.la: Interim discamus charitatis officia praestare exulibus Christi, qui ad nos, suis sedibus eiecti, veniunt. Vide Mat.25. Act.20.
units.tr: Meanwhile let us learn to show the duties of charity to the exiles of Christ, who come to us, driven from their homes (see Matt. 25; Acts 20).

units.la: III. Exitus & Catastrophe, laeta pijs, imo pijs tristissima. I. Apostoli excutiunt puluerem, quod symbolum erat execrationis, & testimonium iustae damnationis, vt patet Mat.10. Lu.9. 10. Et ita digressi peruenerunt Iconium.
units.tr: III. The outcome and catastrophe: joyful for the godly, indeed most sad for the godly. 1. The apostles shake off the dust, which was a sign of execration and a testimony of just condemnation, as is clear from Matt. 10 and Luke 9–10. And so, departing, they came to Iconium.

units.la: NOT. 1. Quando discedendi ius habet at minister? Quando desperatae impietatis argumenta videt. Peccant ergo, qui alias ob causas discedunt.
units.tr: NOTE 1. When does a minister have the right to depart? When he sees the proofs of desperate impiety. They sin, therefore, who depart for other reasons.

units.la: 2. Inexcusabiles esse qui verbum Dei, quod ipsis praedicatur, contemnunt. Audiuerunt in testimonium. Excutitur puluis in testimonium aduersus ipsos. Quod si vero puluis contra illos testari poterit, quid iudicandum de ipsis concionibus, laboribus, sanguine ministrorum. Discamus ergo horrere tantum scelus, & simul vitare eos, quo isto sese iam olim polluerunt Apo.18
units.tr: 2. Those who despise the word of God, which is preached to them, are inexcusable. They heard it as a testimony. The dust is shaken out as a testimony against them. But if the dust can bear witness against them, what must be judged of the sermons, labours and blood of the ministers themselves? Let us learn therefore to shudder at so great a crime, and at the same time to avoid those by whom they have long since polluted themselves (Rev. 18).

units.la: II. Discipuli replentur gaudio & Spiritu.
units.tr: II. The disciples are filled with joy and the Spirit,

units.la: tu sancto, id est, omnigenis donis. Est hic verus gustus regni Dei. Rom. 14.
units.tr: that is, with gifts of every kind. Here is a true taste of the kingdom of God (Rom. 14).

units.la: Interim in his No T. §1. Impiorum conatibus aduersus Christum nihil profici, quàm vt latius propagetur huius regnū. Tanta enim Spiritus sancti virtus est, vt omne huius mundi potentia, sapientiam & authoriratem longè superet. Videi. Io. 4. 5. Ioh. 16. Ex his hodie consolationes petatur. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile, in these words, Note 1: nothing is achieved by the efforts of the impious against Christ except that his kingdom is spread more widely. For so great is the power of the Holy Spirit that it far surpasses all the might, wisdom and authority of this world (see John 4, 5; John 16). From these words consolation is to be sought today. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER 14.

units.la: Homilia CXVI.
units.tr: Homily 116.

units.la: FActum est autem Iconij, vt simul ingrederentur Synagogam Iudaeorum, & loquerentur, itavt crederet Iudaeorum simul & Graecorum magna multitudo.
units.tr: It happened at Iconium that they entered the synagogue of the Jews together and spoke, so that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.

units.la: 2 Qui vero incredduli fuerunt Iudaei incitarunt, & male affectos reddiderunt animos Gentium aduersus fratres.
units.tr: 2 But the unbelieving Jews stirred up and poisoned the minds of the Gentiles against the brothers.

units.la: 3 Multum igitur tempus ibi egerunt, libere loquentes freti Domino, qui testimonium dabat sermoni gratiae suae, dabatque, vt signa & miracula ederentur per manus eorum.
units.tr: 3 So they spent a long time there, speaking boldly and relying on the Lord, who bore witness to the word of his grace and granted that signs and miracles were done through their hands.

units.la: 4 Diuisa est autem multitudo vrbis, et alij quidem erant Iudæis, alij vero ab Apostolis.
units.tr: 4 The city was divided: some were with the Jews, and others with the Apostles.

units.la: 5 Cum autem factum esset impetus Gentium ac Iudæorum, vna cum suis principibus, vt contumelijs afficerent et lapidarent eos.
units.tr: 5 When an assault was made by the Gentiles and the Jews, together with their rulers, to insult and stone them,

units.la: 6 Re considerata, perfugerunt Lycaoniæ, Lystram, et Derbem, et ad vicinas regiones.
