units.tr: 6 they took note of it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe, and to the surrounding regions.

units.la: Expositum est præcedenti Cap. Lucas, vt ex spiritus mandato Paulus et Barnabas, vt inter gentes prædicarent, emissi sunt. Conuerte-runt isti breui tempore Cyrum, Pamphyliam et Pisidiam. Antiochiæ autem iterum accepti sunt, vt persecutione per Iudæos ex citata, finibus Pisidiæ eiecti sint, et pedum puluerem excussepint, quod rarissimè factum legimus. Cæterum ne quis illos succubuisse, et regnum Christi labefactarum putaret, sequitur quid porrò factum sit.
units.tr: It was explained in the previous chapter that Paul and Barnabas were sent out by the command of the Spirit to preach among the Gentiles. In a short time they converted Cyprus, Pamphylia and Pisidia. Then they were received again at Antioch, but when persecution was stirred up by the Jews, they were driven out of the borders of Pisidia and shook the dust from their feet, which we read was very rarely done. But lest anyone think they were overcome and the kingdom of Christ was shaken, the text goes on to tell what happened next.

units.la: I. Veniunt Iconium, vbi pro suo more Iudæorum Synagogam ingressi, rursum docent. NOT. 1. Iconium qualis ciuitas. Celeberrima et opulentissima totius Lycaoniæ, sic dicta ab imagine, quam iussu Iouis Prometheus et Minerua post Deucalionis diluuium ibi fecisse ferebatur, quan-quam fuisset animata. Fuit ergo luxu et do lolatr a infamis, vt quæ à Luca depictis imaginibus gloriantur. Elucet hic Dei bonitas, & quod ex gratia salus contingat, cum tales Euangelij splendore illuminare digner-tur. Ideo conditionem gentium albi Paulus diligenter exponit, Rom.1. Eph.2. Col.2. 1.Cor 12. Quid enim tales mereri potuerunt coram Deo?
units.tr: I. They come to Iconium, where, following their custom, they entered the synagogue of the Jews and taught again. NOTE 1. What sort of city Iconium was: the most famous and wealthy city of all Lycaonia, named after the image which Prometheus and Minerva were said to have made there at Jupiter's command after the flood of Deucalion, though it had been given life. It was therefore notorious for luxury and idolatry, since it boasted of painted images. Here God's goodness shines out, and salvation comes from grace, since he deigns to illuminate such people with the splendour of the gospel. So Paul carefully sets out the condition of the Gentiles, Rom. 1, Eph. 2, Col. 2, 1 Cor. 12. For what could such people have deserved before God?

units.la: §2.Apostolos.Denuo docent, Euangelium scilicet in Synagoga Iudæorum. Atqui paulo ante infelicissimè cesserat, nec alios habebant grauiores hostes. A.Constantia magna & fides in commissio mune re.Periclitati fuerant de vita. Ignominiose eiecti. Deinde multa illos iubebant de Iudæorum salute desperare. Nouerant prophetias,Hos.1.2. Matt.21.22. Videbant imminere tempus repudij ob contumaciam Christi odium. Pergunt tamen, ne ipsorum culpa perijsse videantur.Vide Ezech. 3.33. Intentur singuli, nec patiantur se superari hominum malitia,&c. Luc.10.Magistratus Parentes priuati quinque, &c.
units.tr: §2. The Apostles. Again they teach the gospel, namely in the synagogue of the Jews. Yet a little before they had gone away most unhappily, and they had no more serious enemies. A. Great constancy and faith in the task committed to them. They had been in danger of their lives and were ignominiously thrown out. Then many urged them to despair of the salvation of the Jews. They knew the prophecies, Hos. 1, 2; Matt. 21, 22. They saw the time of repudiation approaching because of the obstinacy and hatred of Christ. Still they press on, lest they seem to have perished through their own fault. See Ezek. 3, 33. Each one is urged on, and they do not allow themselves to be overcome by the malice of men, etc. Luke 10. Magistrates, parents, private persons, five, etc.

units.la: B. Charitas erga hostilem gentem, 1. Thess.2. Vident merito perituram. Sed omnia sperat charitas, & rel quias ceu ex naufragio saluare cupiunt. Vide Rom.9. 10 Eodem affectu tangamur, cum eius exemplū in Christo habeamus,Mat 9 Lu.19 Arguuntur,qui propter paucos totá gen- tem oderunt,vel aliorum malis gaudent. Imitemur Deum,qui propter paucos bo- nos etiam malis parcit, Gen.18.19.
units.tr: B. Love towards the hostile nation, 1 Thess. 2. They see that it will rightly perish. But love hopes all things, and they desire to save the rest as from a shipwreck. See Rom. 9, 10. Let us be moved by the same affection, since we have his example in Christ, Matt. 9, Luke 19. Those are rebuked who hate a whole nation because of a few, or rejoice in others' evils. Let us imitate God, who for the sake of a few good men spares even the wicked, Gen. 18, 19.

units.la: ¶ 3 Effectum. Ingens multitudo credit. Nunquam ergo fine fructu prædicatur ver bum,Ifa 55.Luc.8 Nec deest in suo nomi- ne laborantibus Deus,Luc.5. Quod hodie parum proficitur, omnium ordinum ignauiæ tribui debet.
units.tr: ¶ 3 Effect. A huge multitude believes. Therefore the word is never preached without fruit, Isa. 55, Luke 8. Nor does God fail those who labour in his name, Luke 5. That so little progress is made today must be attributed to the sloth of every order.

units.la: Interim patet,irritos esse hostium Christi conatus. His regnum Christi prouehi- tur.Vide Acto 8.11. Idem omnes historiæ docent.Agnoscamus Dei sapientiam, qua hostium suorum consilia eludit, & non desperemus hodie, Psalmo 2.33.no.&c.
units.tr: Meanwhile it is clear that the attempts of Christ's enemies come to nothing. By these the kingdom of Christ is advanced. See Acts 8, 11. All histories teach the same. Let us acknowledge the wisdom of God, by which he frustrates the plans of his enemies, and let us not despair today, Psalm 2, 33, etc.

units.la: II. Rursum persecutio excipit Apostolos, vt verum videas quod Christus præ- dixit,Matth.10.Ioh 15 16. Nota.¶1.Au- thores,qui ijdem fuere, qui etiam Antio- chiæ, nimirum Iudæi incredulì. Dicun- tur exasperauisse gentium animos contra fratres: id quod absque calumnijs non po- tuit fieri,Matth.5.10. Horrendum hoc,si respicias priorem conditionem,Exod.19. Rom 9 Amoz 3 &c.
units.tr: II. Again persecution takes hold of the Apostles, so that you may see the truth of what Christ foretold, Matt. 10, John 15, 16. Note. ¶1. The authors were the same as at Antioch, namely the unbelieving Jews. They are said to have stirred up the minds of the Gentiles against the brothers. This could not be done without slanders, Matt. 5:10. Horrible this is, if you consider their former condition, Exod. 19, Rom. 9, Amos 3, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2.Apostol quid? Pergunt,& fortiter rem gerunt in Domino, qui etiam fideli- terillis adest, dum Euangelio (qui propter Christum sermo gratiæ dicitur, 2.Cor. 5. &c.) testimonium reddit per miracula, &c.
units.tr: ¶2. And what of the Apostles? They press on and act boldly in the Lord, who also stands faithfully by them while he bears witness to the gospel (which on account of Christ is called the word of grace, 2 Cor. 5, etc.) through miracles, etc.

units.la: Pater: A. Officium ministrorum Christi. Non cedant impijs, etiamsi turbas oppressas videant, sed fortiter resistant in Domino, Phil. 4. Nec enim violanda est amicitia Dei propter homines, Matth. 10. Iac. 4. B. Miraculorum vsus. Debent veritati testimonium ferre. In eum finem Christus ædidit, & æ di voluit per Apostolos, Ioh 5 10. Mar. 16. &c. Hodie illis non est opus. Falluntur autem turpissimè, qui miracula contra veritatem allegant, vt in Papatu sit. Primus per verbum Dei probanda erant dogmata. Id cum non possint, signa sunt falsa: qualia Anti-christo tribuuntur, Matt. 24 2. Thess 2 Caute ergo agendum.
units.tr: Father: A. The duty of Christ's ministers. They must not yield to the impious even when they see crowds oppressed, but resist boldly in the Lord, Phil. 4. For the friendship of God must not be violated for the sake of men, Matt. 10, James 4. B. The use of miracles. They ought to bear witness to the truth. To this end Christ performed miracles, and wished them to be performed through the Apostles, John 5, 10, Mark 16, etc. Today there is no need of them. But those are utterly mistaken who allege miracles against the truth, as happens in the Papacy. Doctrines must first be proved by the word of God. Since they cannot do that, the signs are false, such as are attributed to Antichrist, Matt. 24, 2 Thess. 2. Therefore we must act with caution.

units.la: § 3. Scinditur tandem tota ciuitas in partes, sicut prædixit Christus, Matth. 10. Iš vero inobedientibus tribuendum. Vide ergo qui proprie seditionis authores sint. Non qui credunt Euangelio, sed incredduli. Illi enim paci studeant cum omnibus, Matt. 5. Rom. 12. Hi vero lucem ferre nequeunt, Ioh 3. Concitant ergo populū, & ita permittit Deus, &c. Vide 1.Reg. 18. Lucæ 23. Col 3. Non nouum ergo, si quid simile sat hodie. Nec enim aliter fieri poterit.
units.tr: § 3. The whole city is at last split into parties, as Christ foretold, Matt. 10. But this is to be attributed to the disobedient. See, then, who are truly the authors of sedition: not those who believe the gospel, but the unbelievers. For the former strive for peace with all, Matt. 5, Rom. 12. The latter cannot bear the light, John 3. They therefore stir up the people, and God thus permits it, etc. See 1 Kings 18, Luke 23, Col. 3. Nothing new, then, if something similar happens today. For it cannot happen otherwise.

units.la: Cap. 14 teft, cùm impij lucem impugnent, quam pij non possunt negare, Mar. 8. Quare in si mili casu Apostolos imitemur, nec simus Neutrales, de quibus vide Apoc. 3. &c. In Republica dissidente non licet neutralem esse.
units.tr: Chapter 14 shows that when the wicked attack the light, which the godly cannot deny, Mark 8. Therefore in a similar case let us imitate the Apostles, and let us not be neutral, on which see Rev. 3, etc. In a divided commonwealth it is not permitted to be neutral.

units.la: ¶ 4. Fugiunt tandem Apostoli, cùm aperta vi ageretur, nec aliqua esset ipes me lioris fortis. Ita Christus iusit, Matth. 10. Idem ipse fecit, Luc. 4. Ioh. 8. &c. Non ergo omnis fuga vitio dari debet, & improbi calumniatores sunt, qui id faciunt, cùm ex fuga saepe plus boni quàm mali oriatur.
units.tr: ¶ 4. At last the Apostles flee, when force was being used openly and there was no better hope of strength. Christ so commanded, Matt. 10. He himself did the same, Luke 4, John 8, etc. Therefore not every flight should be charged as a fault, and those are wicked slanderers who do so, since from flight often more good than harm arises.

units.la: Interim observa, quid post fugam fecerint. Non otio suo consuluerunt, sed prædicârunt Euangelium alibi. Hoc ergo curandum, ne temerè periculis nos objicientes Deum tentemus, nec ignobili metu deseramus officium. Si qui Dei gloriam ob oculos habent, res, locus & tempus consilium dabunt. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile note what they did after the flight. They did not look to their own ease, but preached the gospel elsewhere. Therefore we must take care not to expose ourselves rashly to dangers and so tempt God, nor abandon our duty from base fear. If people keep the glory of God before their eyes, circumstances, place and time will give them counsel. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXVII.

units.la: 8 Quidam autem vir Lysfris impotens pedibus sedebat, claudus ab utero matris suae, qui nunquam ambulaverat.
units.tr: 8 Now a certain man at Lystra, who was impotent in his feet, sat there, a cripple from his mother's womb, who had never walked.

units.la: 9 Hic audiuit Paulum loquentem, qui cum intendisset in eum oculos, & vt diffet quod fidem haberet, se seruatum sit.
units.tr: 9 This man heard Paul speaking. Paul fixed his eyes on him and, perceiving that he had faith to be made whole,

units.la: 10 Dixit voce magna, Surge in pe des tuos rectus, &c.
units.tr: 10 said in a loud voice, "Stand upright on your feet," etc.

units.la: QVemadmodum Scripturae passim docent multas esse piorum tribulationes, & Christus suos omnes ad crucem inuitat: Sic Apostolos ad Euangelij praedicationem emisurus, de nulla re eos admonuit, &c. Matth. 10, 24. Ioh. 15, 16. Facit hoc, non vt terreat, sed vt praemoniti se arment fortitudine, & in officio fideliter pergant. Ita intellexerunt hoc Paulus & Barnabas, qui emisi inter gentes hoc experti, sed vbiq; constantes fuerunt, &c. In Cypro Elymas. Antiochiae eijciuntur ignominiose, sed Iconij iterum praedicant. Inde eiecti, Lystris & Derbae. Et quidem Euangelium, ne quis propter pericula doctrinae genus mutatum putaret. Docent suo exemplo nihil esse dandum hostibus, vt propter ipsos aliquid mutetur, dissimulatur, &c. Eodem praecepto omnes astringimur, Ezech. 3. Ierem. 1. Matthaei 28. Et Christo indigni sunt, qui mundi gratiam illius mandato praefuerunt.
units.tr: As the Scriptures teach throughout that the godly endure many afflictions, and as Christ invites all his people to the cross, so when he was about to send out the Apostles to preach the Gospel, he warned them of nothing else (Matt. 10:24; John 15:16). He did this not to terrify them, but so that, forewarned, they might arm themselves with courage and persevere faithfully in their office. Paul and Barnabas understood it this way. Sent out among the Gentiles, they experienced this, yet they remained steadfast everywhere. In Cyprus there was Elymas. At Antioch they were shamefully driven out, yet at Iconium they preached again. Cast out from there, they went to Lystra and Derbe. And indeed they preached the Gospel so that no one would think the teaching had been changed because of dangers. By their own example they teach that nothing should be yielded to enemies, that nothing should be altered or dissembled for their sake. All of us are bound by this same command (Ezek. 3; Jer. 1; Matt. 28). Those who have sought the world's favour by departing from his command are unworthy of Christ.

units.la: At quia miraculorum meminerat, quibus testimonium dederit Deus doctrinæ Apostolorum, ex multis vnum describit, & quidem hoc, quod propter euentum in primis dignum erat narratu,&c.
units.tr: But because he recalls the miracles by which God bore witness to the teaching of the Apostles, he describes one of many, and this one especially because its outcome made it worthy of being told in the first place, etc.

units.la: I. Persona eius, in quo ædítum, Ciuis Lystrensis. Facit hoc ad veritatem rei, & suspicionem remouet. Debilis pedibus, i-mò claudus ab vtero, vt is de quo Acto.⁞. Nunquam ambulauerat. Itaq; morbus incurabilis. Facit ad amplificationem miraculi & potentiæ Christi.
units.tr: I. The person in whom the deed was done: a citizen of Lystra. This serves the truth of the matter and removes suspicion. Lame in his feet, or rather lame from his mother's womb, as the one of whom (Acts ...). Had never walked. So the disease was incurable. This serves to magnify the miracle and the power of Christ.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Quòd hunc deligit Deus,pær quem nomen suum illustret,cùm non deessent Lystris nobiles, opulenti, sani, &c. qui Apostolos iuuare poterant. Sed tales ferè eligit Deus, vt ipsius virtus elucear, quæ in alijs non ita apparet.Hinc illa,Ioh. 5. Matth.9.Cæcus natus,Ioh.9.Dæmonia ci,Mar.8.Luc.8.Imò ideo ferè suos incarcerari,&in extrema pericula venire patitur,& facit opus alienum,&c.Isa.28.
units.tr: NOTE. God chose this man through whom to make his name illustrious, although there were noble, wealthy and healthy men at Lystra who could have helped the Apostles. God generally chooses such people so that his power may shine forth, which does not appear so clearly in others. Hence John 5; Matt. 9; the man born blind (John 9); the demoniac (Mark 8; Luke 8). Indeed he often allows his own people to be imprisoned and brought into extreme dangers, and to do work that is not their own, etc. (Isa. 28).

units.la: Discimus: A. Non impatienter ferre quæ Deus immittit, nec putare nos illi i-deo esse exosos.Tam abest,vt potius glo-riæ vasa simus. Vide Psalm. 107. Cogitaanteactam vitam,& inuenies sic oporteresieri. Facit huc petitio,Sanctificetur no-men tuum,&c. B.Non temerè ijs insulta-
units.tr: We learn: A. Not to bear impatiently what God sends, nor to think that we are hateful to him for that reason. Far from it, we are rather vessels of his glory (see Psalm 107). Consider your life before, and you will find that it had to happen this way. The petition "Hallowed be thy name" applies here. B. Not to insult rashly those who are punished more than others for natural defects or other evils.

units.la: {y} Ioan. 3. re, qui præ alijs multantur vitijs naturæ aut alijs malis.Fit hoc varië, corrupto iudicio scurrilitate & leuitate,inuidia. Sed est alienum à sensu humanitatis. Contumelia in Deum redundat,Pro.17.Vide legemLeu.19.Deut.27.Exemplum 2.Reg.2. Obseruent pueri,parentes,&c.
units.tr: John 3. This happens in various ways: through corrupt judgment, through buffoonery and levity, through envy. But it is foreign to the sense of humanity. Insult redounds upon God (Prov. 17). See the law (Lev. 19; Deut. 27). Example: 2 Kings 2. Let children and parents take note, etc.

units.la: II. Quid fecit claudus? Audiuit Paulum, & credidit se saluum fore. Dixit ergo de Christi virtute, quæ miraculis pasim innotuerat. Itaq; credidit, & de corporis etiam salute spem concepit: non fine spiritus suggestione. Ita verò causa salutis ex primitur, fides. Hæc iustificare & seruare dicitur, quia organum est quo Christus apprehenditur. Hinc illa Mat.15.Mar.9.
units.tr: II. What did the lame man do? He heard Paul and believed that he would be saved. He therefore spoke of the power of Christ, which had become widely known through miracles. So he believed, and conceived hope even of the health of his body, not without the prompting of the Spirit. Thus faith is the first cause of salvation. It is said to justify and preserve, because it is the instrument by which Christ is laid hold of. Hence Matt. 15; Mark 9.

units.la: NOTA. Quòd audisse & credidisse di citur. Vides vnde fides obtingat? Est Dei donum, quod nec nostris viribus acquiri tur,nec ab hominibus confertur, Ephe.2. Ioh.6.Matt.11.16. Deus autem per verbū confert, in quo hominibus ministris vtitur. Vide 1.Cor.3.Rom.16.Ideo verbi auditio & fides coniungitur,Ioh.5.Et ita fiat oportet, ne fides incerta fluctuet. Faciunt hæc ad verbi commendationem, ne reuelationes peculiares quæramus,Luc.16.Tales satanæ insidijs se exponunt. Et hæc hæ refium omnium origo. Ideo Deus verbi doctrinam strinam semper extare voluit. Sub Patriarchis, Mose & Leuitis, qui debebant per tribus omnes habitare. Dies festi. His cessantibus dati Prophetæ. In nouo Testamento Christus in docendo asiduus. Apostolos dedit, qui hoc præcipuum putarent, Acto 6. 1. Cor. 1. His se priuatim omnes accommodet. Mag stratus instet, &c. Imperatoriæ leges dedic Dominico. Magnæ occasiones ad salutem.
units.tr: NOTE. That he is said to have heard and believed. Do you see where faith comes from? It is a gift of God, which is acquired neither by our own strength nor conferred by men (Eph. 2; John 6; Matt. 11, 16). God, however, confers it through the word, using human ministers. See 1 Cor. 3; Rom. 16. Therefore hearing the word and faith are joined (John 5), and so it must be, lest faith waver uncertainly. These points commend the word, so that we do not seek peculiar revelations (Luke 16). Those who do so expose themselves to Satan's snares, and this is the origin of all heresies. Therefore God has always willed that the doctrine of the word should stand firm. Under the Patriarchs, and under Moses and the Levites, who were to dwell among all the tribes, there were festival days. When these ceased, prophets were given. In the New Testament Christ was assiduous in teaching, and he gave Apostles who should regard this as their chief task (Acts 6; 1 Cor. 1). Let everyone accommodate himself to this privately; let the magistrate insist, etc. Imperial laws have been issued concerning the Lord's Day. Great opportunities for salvation.

units.la: II. Quid Paulus? Intuetur, & exspiritus suggestione fidem eius videt. Iubet sur gere in nomine Iesu. Nec mora exiit: & ita testimonium fertur de doctrina. Not.
units.tr: II. What did Paul do? He looked at him and, by the prompting of the Spirit, saw his faith. He bids him stand up in the name of Jesus. Without delay the man leapt up, and thus testimony is borne to the doctrine. Note.

units.la: ¶ Salutem misterium simul hic adumbrari. A. Claudus, typus omnium nostrum. De bilēs & corrupti ex natiuitate, Gen. 5. Ro. 5 Hinc illud Psal 51 Rom. 7. Et si vitam examinemus, nunquam ambulauimus, scilicet in vijs Domini, Ifa. 53. 64. Itaq; omnibus pereundum erat, quoad nos. B. Vbi salus? Extra nos, in vno Christo Hunc Pater destinauit huic rei. Is à peccatis liberat, 2. Cor. 5. 1. Cor. 1. 1. Ioh. 1. Regenerat, 1. Pet. 1. Iohan. 1. Vires nouas sufficit, Philipp. 4. Iohannis 15. Et hæc quidem omnia præstat solus, Acto. 4. Ifa. 42. C. Offertur nobis per Euangelium, & sola fide apprehenditur. Iohan. 6. Marc. 16. Actor. 11.
units.tr: NOTE. The mystery of salvation is also shadowed forth here. A. The lame man is a type of all of us: lame and corrupt from birth (Gen. 5; Rom. 5). Hence that statement in Psalm 51 and Rom. 7. And if we examine our life, we have never walked, namely in the ways of the Lord (Isa. 53; 64). So all of us, as far as we are concerned, had to perish. B. Where is salvation? Outside us, in Christ alone. The Father appointed him for this. He frees us from sins (2 Cor. 5; 1 Cor. 1; John 1), regenerates us (1 Pet. 1; 1 John 1), and supplies new strength (Phil. 4; John 15). He alone accomplishes all these things (Acts 4; Isa. 42). C. It is offered to us through the Gospel and is apprehended by faith alone (John 6; Mark 16; Acts 11).

units.la: Humana redemptionis typus & ratio.
units.tr: The type and the reason of human redemption.

units.la: D. Nostrum officium, Audire. Credere. Liberati surgamus ex luto peccatorum, ambulemus in vijs Domini, quęsunt fidesconstans, Innocentia, Charitas, &c. His stud js g'orificemus nomen Domini, &c. Hic ferè peccatur hodie. Autnunquam incipimus, aut aliquo vsqs progressi deficimus. Fit hoc priuatim & publicè. Fient ergo postrema peiora primis, Matthæi 12. Emendemur ergo conuersi ad Dominum, & indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: D. Our duty is to hear and to believe. Freed, let us rise from the mire of sin and walk in the ways of the Lord, which are constant faith, innocence, charity, etc. By these pursuits let us glorify the name of the Lord, etc. Here people sin especially today: either they never begin, or, having advanced to some point, they give up. This happens both privately and publicly. Therefore the last things will become worse than the first (Matt. 12). Let us, then, be amended, converted to the Lord, and pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA CXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXVIII.

units.la: 11 Turba vero quum vidissent quod fecerat Paulus, sustulerunt vocem suam, Lycaonicè dicentes, Dijs assimilati hominibus, descenderunt ad nos.
units.tr: But when the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voices, speaking in the Lycaonian tongue: The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men.

units.la: 12 Vocabant quoque Barnabam Iouem, Paulum verò Mercurium: quoniam ipse erat dux sermonis.
units.tr: They also called Barnabas Jupiter, and Paul Mercury, because he was the chief speaker.

units.la: 13 Sacerdos autem Iouis, collica ti ante illorum vrbem, cum tauros vitta tos adduxisset, & c. ad vers. 16.
units.tr: The priest of Jupiter, whose temple stood before their city, brought oxen and garlands, etc., down to verse 16.

units.la: Quoniam homo animalis non percipit ea, quæ sunt Spiritus Dei, nec modo suis figmentis seipsum seducit, vel sumetriam ijs abutitur, quibus ad veritatis cognitionem institui debebat. Exempla pla sunt in Iudæis & gentibus. Et hodie hoc ipsum frequenter fit. In primis tamen memorabile est quod hîc proponitur,eò quòd simul docet,quid pij in casu eiusmo di faciant. Videamus singulas partes.
units.tr: Because the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, he both deceives himself with his own inventions and misuses for vanity those things by which he ought to have been taught the knowledge of the truth. Examples are plain among both Jews and Gentiles, and today the same thing happens often. Yet what is set out here is especially worth remembering, because at the same time it teaches what the godly do in such a case. Let us look at the individual parts.

units.la: 1. Vt miraculum hoc Lystrenses acce-perint. Longè aliter quàm Paulus vole bat.Hic enim doctrinam suam hoc stabili-re & Christo adducere voluit.Illi à Chri-sto longùs resiliendi occasionem arripi-unt. Nam decepti fabulis Poetarum,putant Deos humana spec e descendisse & nomina Deorum illis partiuntur. Superuenit sacerdos, qui furentes magis insti-gat,&c.
units.tr: 1. How the Lystrians received this miracle: quite differently from what Paul wished. For he wanted to confirm his teaching by it and bring them to Christ. They, on the other hand, seized the chance to turn away from Christ. For, deceived by the fables of the poets, they think the gods have come down in human form, and they assign the names of the gods to the apostles. A priest comes up who stirs the frenzied people even more, etc.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Quàm procliue fit ingeni-um hominis adsuperstiti ones,& quàm difficile fit errores exuere, quibus à teneris assueuimus.Audiuerunt hi concionem de Christo. Viderunt signum in huius nomi-ne ædItum. Manet tamè persuasio de Dijs peregrinantibus,& ex eo ineptiunt, vnde pietatis semina peti debebant. At quantò ineptiores sunt Papistæ. Sciunt hi Apo-stolos,&c.homines fuisse, quorum opera Christus in suo regno propagando sit vsus. Adhuc tamen Deos ex illis faciunt. Partiuntur inter illos officia. In periculis inuocant,vota nuncupant, ijsdem imagi-
units.tr: NOTE. 1. How prone the human mind is to superstition, and how hard it is to cast off errors to which we have been accustomed from childhood. These people heard a sermon about Christ. They saw a sign done in his name. Yet their belief in wandering gods remains, and from this they go astray where they ought to have sought the seeds of piety. But how much more foolish are the Papists! They know that the Apostles were men, whose labour Christ used in spreading his kingdom. Still they make gods of them. They divide up their offices among them. In dangers they invoke them, they make vows to them, they set up images to the same men,

units.la: nes ponunt, sacrificant vt gentes. In soliſ nominibus differentia est. Imo cum eos pro Christo mortuos dicant, huius tamen honorem in illos transferunt, &c.
units.tr: and they sacrifice as the Gentiles did. The only difference lies in the names. Indeed, although they say these men died for Christ, they nonetheless transfer his honour to them, etc.

units.la: § 2. Originé & progressum idololatriæ. A. Fons malignorantia veri Dei, & quòd de Deo ex carnis sensu iudicatur. Hinc multitudo Deorum, intercessio sanctorum, &c. Vbi potius erat cogitandum illud Isa. 55. B. Proxima quæq; arripiunt, quæ alicuius boni causa sunt. Ideo stellas, elementa, homines, animalia, &c. coluerunt gentes. Ita hodie reliquiæ sanctorum, Euangelium Iohan. aqua benedicta, panis Eucharistiæ, sonitus campanarū, &c. C. Sequitur cultus externus. Festi dies, altaria, sacrificia, imagines, peregrinationes, cantus, &c. Et hic se duces præbent antistites, quibus ista honorem & quæstum ferunt. Interim omnes in ore habent Deū & sanctos: cùm nostrorum hominum superstitio detecta bilior fit, quòd sanctorum nomine abutimur. Hæc ergo teneamus, ne leue nobis videatur ad lutum redire & vomitum.
units.tr: § 2. The origin and progress of idolatry. A. The source is ignorance of the true God, and the judging of God by the sense of the flesh. Hence come the multitude of gods, the intercession of the saints, etc. Here one ought rather to have pondered that passage of Isaiah 55. B. People seize whatever is nearest and serves some good purpose. So the Gentiles worshipped stars, elements, men, animals, etc. So today: relics of saints, the Gospel of John, holy water, the bread of the Eucharist, the sound of bells, etc. C. External worship follows: festival days, altars, sacrifices, images, pilgrimages, chants, etc. And here the bishops set themselves forward as leaders, to whom these things bring honour and gain. Meanwhile they all have God and the saints on their lips; yet the superstition of our people is more plainly exposed, since we abuse the name of the saints. Let us therefore hold to these things, lest it seem a small matter to us to return to the mire and to vomit.

units.la: II. Quid Apostoli? Gestibus testantur rei indignitatem. Vestes scindunt, quod fiebat in blasphemijs intolerabilibus, 2. Reg. 5 13. Matth. 26. Insiliunt in turbam non sine periculo. Clamant.
units.tr: II. What did the Apostles do? By their gestures they show the unworthiness of the thing. They tear their garments, as was done in intolerable blasphemies, 2 Reg. 5:13; Matth. 26. They rush into the crowd, not without danger. They cry out.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Ingenium sanctorum, & quo zelo ferantur pro afferenda Dei gloria. In tolerabile ipsis est, Dei gloriam vel ipsis vel aliis creaturis tribuere. Respiciunt enim ad foedus & legem, ubi zelote se prosi tetur Deus. Sic Petrus, Act. 3. 10. Angeli, Apoc. 19. 12. Vide quales censendi, qui diuinos honores sibi vendicant, quales olim fuerunt Herodes, Caligula, Domit. & hodie Pontificij, qui Sanctitas dicuntur, peccata remittunt, impunitate gloriantur. Sunt alienissimi a spiritu Apostolico. Id vero ex oratione eorum magis appare bit, cuius partes excutere oportet.
units.tr: NOTE. The spirit of the saints, and the zeal with which they are carried away in asserting the glory of God. It is intolerable to them to ascribe God's glory either to themselves or to other creatures. For they look to the covenant and the law, where God declares himself a jealous God. So Peter, Acts 3:10; the angels, Rev. 19:12. See what sort of men must be judged those who claim divine honours for themselves, such as Herod, Caligula and Domitian once were, and today the Papists, who are called "Holiness", forgive sins, and glory in impunity. They are most alien from the Apostolic spirit. This will appear more clearly from their speech, whose parts it is right to examine.

units.la: I. Summa est: Non nos, neque vlla alia creatura, sed Deus verus & viuus debet Ap. Itolo. 2 coli & inuocari. Id per interrogationem contradolatriam enuntiant, quae conuenit gestui, & abomi nationem esse testantur, quod hodie sum. ma pietas putatur.
units.tr: I. The sum is: not we, nor any other creature, but the true and living God ought to be worshipped and invoked. They express this by a question that runs against the idea of worship, which fits the gesture, and they testify that what is now thought the highest piety is an abomination.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Idem hodie dici omnibus creaturarum cultoribus. Nec enim Deorum nomina modo abominantur, sed cultum & honores diuinos. Neq; vel Deus suam voluntatem, vel illi suum ingenium in cose lis mutarunt.
units.tr: NOTE. The same can be said today to all worshippers of creatures. For not only are the names of the gods abominated, but also the worship and divine honours given to them. Nor has God changed his will, nor have they changed their nature, in the heavens.

units.la: II. Rationibus confirmant. I. A sua ipso confirmatum persona. Sumus homines, & quidem vobis ὁμοιοπαθεῖς. Fatentur ergo se peccatores quoq; esse.Syllogismus. Sic Paulus suprà.Euertitur hic omnis cultus creaturarum. Si enim non debet coli homo, quantò minùs quæ hoc sunt inferiora. Nec est quòd dicant,Diuos iam malis exemptos esse,& proinde posse coli. Manet enim principium,Exod 20.Deut.6. Dein de rebus nostris Diui non occupantur,If. 63.Quid verò de imaginibus dicemus? If. 40.44.Exod.20.
units.tr: II. They confirm it by reasons. 1. Confirmed from their own person: "We are men, and indeed of like passions with you" [ὁμοιοπαθεῖς]. They therefore confess that they too are sinners. Here is a syllogism, as Paul said above. Every worship of creatures is overturned by this. For if a man ought not to be worshipped, how much less those things which are lower than man. Nor can it be said that the gods are already freed from evils and so may be worshipped. For the principle remains: Exod. 20; Deut. 6. Moreover, the divine ones are not occupied with our affairs: Isa. 63. But what shall we say of images? Isa. 40, 44; Exod. 20.

units.la: HOMILIA CXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CXIX.

units.la: 15 Venimus ad vos, vt à vanis istis rebus conuertamini, ad Deum viuum, qui fecit cœlum & terram, & mare, & omnia quæ in eis sunt.
units.tr: 15 We have come to you, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made heaven and earth, and the sea, and all that is in them.

units.la: 16 Qui praeteritis ætatibus suit omnes gentes ipsarum vijs incedere, &c. adverf.19.
units.tr: 16 Who in past ages suffered all nations to walk in their own ways, etc. (against heresies, book 19)

units.la: PAulus & Barnabas præsenti oratione Lystrenses, qui ipsis sacrificare volebant,à vano creaturarum cultu auocant. Id verò sic faciunt, vt suo exemplo doceant, quo zelo in simili casu omnes ministri vti debeant, & quales censendi sint, qui secus agunt. Primò vestes scindunt, vt intolerabilem impietatem esse doceant.Deinde in turbam insiliunt,quasi publicum malû prohibituri. Clamant, & argumentis vtuntur.1.Homines sumus, vobis bis ὁμοιοπαθεῖς. Ergo stultū est nos pro Dijs & Seruatoribus colere. Valet hoc argumentum adversus omnem cultū creaturarum. Neq; obstat, quod malis omnibus Diui iam exempti sunt.
units.tr: Paul and Barnabas, in this speech, call the Lystrians away from the empty worship of creatures, who wished to sacrifice to them. They do this in such a way that by their own example they teach with what zeal all ministers ought to act in a similar case, and what sort of men are to be judged those who act otherwise. First, they tear their garments, to teach that the impiety is intolerable. Then they leap into the crowd, as if about to prevent a public evil. They cry out and use arguments. (1) We are men, like passions to you. Therefore it is foolish for us to be worshipped as gods and saviours. This argument holds against every worship of creatures. Nor does it matter that the gods have now been freed from all evils.

units.la: Secundum argumentū ab officio suo. Venimus ad vos vt conuertamini, &c. Ergo perfidia esset talia recipere. Simile legati.
units.tr: The second argument is drawn from their office: We have come to you that you may turn, etc. Therefore it would be treachery to receive such things. Compare the envoys.

units.la: Vbi Nota. ¶ 1. Quàm errent qui Diuorum cultores habere volunt. Summa contumelia eosdem afficiunt, dum tales fingunt, qui delectentur hoc cultu, & suum ingenium in cœlis mutârint, & Deos vanos ex ijs faciunt, qui olim gloriæ Dei organa fuerunt.
units.tr: Note here. (1) How wrongly those err who wish to have worshippers of the saints. They inflict the greatest insult on them while they imagine such men as delighting in this worship, and as having changed their nature in heaven, and make them into vain gods out of those who once were instruments of God's glory.

units.la: ¶ 2. Ministrorum esse, ad veri Dei cultum reuocare. Oppugnanda igitur quæ huic repugnant, Iere. 1. Peccant ministri, qui hæc nō faciunt. Peccant item, qui hæc fieri non patiuntur. Vtriq; pœnas dabunt.
units.tr: (2) It belongs to ministers to recall people to the worship of the true God. Therefore those things which oppose this must be assailed, Jer. 1. Ministers who do not do this sin. Those too sin who do not allow these things to be done. Both will pay the penalty.

units.la: Confutat quę obijci poterant. Primum consensus omnium gentiū: Alterum longi temporis præscriptio: Quæ duo hodie etiam obijciuntur: Tot docti, nobiles, potentes, &c. An hi omnes damnati? An hoc passurus fuisset Deus? Sed duplici argumento respondet: 1. Gentes ambulârunt in suis vijs, nō in vijs Dei. Ergo non in exemplum trahi debet quod fecerunt, &c.
units.tr: He refutes objections which might be raised. First, the consensus of all nations; second, the prescription of long time. These two are objected even today: so many learned, noble, powerful men, etc. Are all these condemned? Would God have allowed this to happen? But he answers with a twofold argument: (1) The nations walked in their own ways, not in the ways of God. Therefore what they did ought not to be drawn into example, etc.

units.la: Vbi Not. ¶ In salutis & religionis causa non esse pugnandum humana authoritate. Caeca est hominis ratio & fallitur, 1. Cor. 2. Ro. 1. Diuinitus ergo eam illumina ri & Dei verbo subiici oportet, Ioh. 6. Hoc qui non obseruant, perinde faciunt, ac si quis iudice caecum, surdum & mutu constitueret. Adde qui hic homini nihil licet.
units.tr: Note here. In matters of salvation and religion one must not contend by human authority. Human reason is blind and is deceived, 1 Cor. 2, Rom. 1. Therefore it must be enlightened divinely and made subject to the word of God, John 6. Those who do not observe this act just as if someone were to appoint a blind, deaf and mute man as judge. Add that here nothing is permitted to man.

units.la: II. Permisit hoc fieri Deus, no quod ipsi placeret, sed iusto iudicio, vt puniret hominum curiositatem & audaciam, Rom. 1. Ergo terrere potius debet hoc exemplu.
units.tr: (2) God permitted this to happen, not because it pleased him, but by a just judgement, so that he might punish the curiosity and audacity of men, Rom. 1. Therefore this example ought rather to terrify.

units.la: Vbi Not. ¶ Falli eos quoq;, qui longi temporis praescriptionem, multitudinem & consensum Ecclesiae praetexunt. Primo enim horum sententia, Gentilismus Papa tu esset praestantior. Deinde semper fuit maior eorum numerus, qui de Deo non recte senserunt. Ante diluuium, Gene. 3. 1. Pet. 3. Sub Patriarchis. Prophetarum tempore, Isa 8. Et ijdem reliquiarum subinde meminerunt, Isa. 10. In Euangelio suos Christus pusillum gregem dicit, Luc. 12. Matt. 7. Quoad Ecclesiam saepissime erravit, Exod. 32. Vide Prophetas. Quid deno ui Testamenti Ecclesia futurum, habes, Act. 20. 1. Tim 4, 2. Thess. 2 &c. Qui Rom. Ecclesiam negant errauisse, impudentissime mentiuntur.
units.tr: Note here. Those also are deceived who put forward the prescription of long time, the multitude and the consensus of the Church. For first, by their opinion, Gentilism would be more excellent than the Pope. Then, the number of those who did not think rightly about God was always greater. Before the flood, Gen. 3, 1 Pet. 3. Under the Patriarchs. In the time of the Prophets, Isa. 8. And the same prophets repeatedly mention a remnant, Isa. 10. In the Gospel Christ calls his flock a little flock, Luke 12, Matt. 7. As regards the Church, it has very often erred, Exod. 32. See the Prophets. What is to be expected in the Church of the New Testament you have in Acts 20, 1 Tim. 4, 2 Thess. 2, etc. Those who deny that the Roman Church has erred lie most shamelessly.

units.la: Vsus horum sit, vt reliftis omnibus aliis in solius Dei verbum respiciamus.
units.tr: The use of these things is that, all others set aside, we should look to the word of God alone.

units.la: Occurrit tacitę obiectioni. Ergone Deus author est ignorantiæ, superstitionum & errorum? Minimè. Etsi enim hæc fieri permiserit, nunquam non tamen de se & sua voluntate testatus est, quando per visibilia opera se cognoscendum præbuit, Ro 1. Quia autem hic cum vulgo res erat, quotidiana allegant: Semper dedit pluvias, fructifera tempora, & quæcunq; necessitati & voluptati honestæ seruiunt. Quasi dicat: Nemo tamen in Deo culpam hærere potest. Quis non videat cœlorum influentias, temporum vices, terræ prouentus? Atqui hæc eiusmodi sunt, vt nec fortuito, nec humana inductria fieri possint. Dei ergo virtute fiunt, quam sic manifestauit, & proinde inexcusabiles sunt, qui hanc non agnouerunt.
units.tr: He meets a tacit objection. Is God then the author of ignorance, superstitions and errors? By no means. For although he has permitted these things to happen, he has never failed to bear witness concerning himself and his will, when through visible works he has shown himself to be known, Rom. 1. But since the matter here concerned the common people, they allege everyday things: he always gave rains, fruitful seasons, and whatever serves honest necessity and pleasure. As if to say: Nevertheless no blame can cling to God. Who does not see the influences of the heavens, the changes of the seasons, the produce of the earth? Yet these are of such a kind that they can come about neither by chance nor by human industry. They come about therefore by the power of God, which he has thus made manifest, and therefore those who did not acknowledge it are without excuse.

units.la: Vbi Noт. ¶ Dei prouidentiam non pa trocinari nostris erroribus & peccatis. Iu sto iudicio nos excęcari finit. Ita vero hoc facit, vt semper constet hoc nobis volentibus fieri, & perditionem ex nobis esse.
units.tr: Note here. That God's providence does not shelter our errors and sins. By a just judgement he allows us to be blinded. He does this in such a way that it always stands that this happens with our consent, and that the destruction is from ourselves.

units.la: ¶ 2. Deus qualis agnosci debeat. Prius omnium creatorem dixit. Nunc illi tribuit pluuias, prouentum terræ, &c. Ergo gubernator quoq; est omnium, ex cuius
units.tr: (2) What sort of God ought to be acknowledged. First he named the creator of all things. Now he ascribes to him the rains, the produce of the earth, etc. Therefore he is also the governor of all, at whose nod all things depend

units.la: nutu omnia dependent.Sic omnis Scrip‐tura.Videlob.5.38 Psal.104 147 Amos 5. &3.Eædem regnorum vices illi tribuunt, Dan.2 &c. Confutantur ergo Astrologi, qui nobis gentilſmum instaurant.Papistʋ item cum suis Diuis. Interim officij admonemur, vt donis Dei recte vtamur. Magna de his cogitandi occasio hodie priuatim & publice.
units.tr: on him. So all Scripture. See John 5:38, Ps. 104, 147, Amos 5 and 3. The same God also grants the changes of kingdoms, Dan. 2, etc. Astrologers are therefore refuted, who restore paganism to us; likewise the Papists with their saints. Meanwhile we are reminded of our duty, that we use the gifts of God rightly. Here is a great occasion to think on these things today, both privately and publicly. Let us pray.

units.la: His dictis vix potuerunt compescitur bas, quo minus sacrificarent. Vbi apparet humani ingenij contumacia in retinendis superstitionibus.Cum gratis omnia offert Deus, plerique sumptum & laborem sibi accersunt,Ifa.55.Ierem 2. Et vbi assueuit, non patitur hæc mundus sibi eripi, licet eos sibi aduersari audiat,quos colere vult. Maior tamen nostri seculi contumacia. Isti vna oratione compescuntur. Hodie multorum annorum conciones non suffi-ciunt ijs conuertendis, qui tamen Chri-stiani dici & haberi volunt. Oremus.
units.tr: Having said these things, they could scarcely be restrained from sacrificing. Here appears the obstinacy of the human mind in retaining superstitions. Although God offers all things freely, most men procure expense and labour for themselves, Isa. 55, Jer. 2. And where it has become accustomed, the world does not allow these things to be snatched from it, although it hears that those whom it wishes to worship oppose it. Yet the obstinacy of our age is greater. Those men were restrained by a single speech. Today the sermons of many years do not suffice to convert those who nevertheless wish to be and be held Christians. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXX.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXX.

units.la: 19 Superuenerunt autem quidam Iudæi Antiochia & Iconio, qui illecta turba, Paulum lapidatum traxerunt ex tra vrbem, existimantes eum mortuum esse, & c. ad verf. 21.
units.tr: 19 Now certain Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and having won over the crowd, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing him to be dead, etc., to verse 21.

units.la: VT Christus bonus ille pastor est, qui ouium salutem vnicè quaerit & tue tur: Ita satan totus in hoc incumbit, vt extincta Christi cognitione in hominum animis, omnes à salutis via auocet. Et quàm miris modis hoc agat, hoc Cap. exemplo memorabili docemur. Apostolis enim apud Lystren. praedicantibus primò super stitiosos excitat, qui pro Dijs habent, &c. Ita verò vulgus in errore retinere, Apostolos autem ambitione ab officio revocare volunt, vt Christum, Matth 4. Sed olfaciunt dolum Apostoli, & eo constantius vt rei cognitionem trahunt, vt multi iam credant. Mox ergo alia via rem aggreditur, & per lud. aliunde adductos turbas dat, &c. Vsus historiae, vt satanae & mundi artes agnoscamus, & Apostolorum constantiam imitemur.
units.tr: AS Christ is that good Shepherd who seeks and guards the salvation of the sheep alone, so Satan devotes his whole effort to extinguishing the knowledge of Christ in men's minds and diverting them all from the way of salvation. And this chapter teaches us, by a memorable example, in how wonderful ways he does this. For when the apostles were preaching at Lystra, he first stirs up superstitious people who regard them as gods, etc. Then, indeed, he wants to keep the common people in error and to call the apostles back from their office by ambition, as he did with Christ in Matthew 4. But the apostles smell the trick, and they hold to their knowledge of the matter all the more steadfastly, so that many now believe. Therefore he at once takes up the matter by another route, and by means of a crowd brought in from elsewhere he stirs up tumult, etc. The use of the history is that we may recognise the arts of Satan and of the world, and imitate the constancy of the apostles.

units.la: I. Authores tragediae Iudaei, de quibus 1. Thess. 2. Horrendum, quod tales facti, qui Dei peculium fuerant, Exod. 19. Nemo igitur confidat sibi ipsi, vel ex antea-factis de quouis pronuntiet. NOTA Stratagema diaboli, qui cum Lystris nemi hem inueniat, aliunde adduxit. Curat enim, vt vbique habeat sua organa. Si hic non habet, alibi inuenit, quos submittit. Exempla vetera in haereticis. Hodie, si qui
units.tr: The authors of the tragedy were the Jews, of whom 1 Thess. 2 speaks. It is dreadful that such people, who had been God's own possession (Exod. 19), should have become like this. Let no one therefore trust himself, or pass judgement on anyone from past events. NOTE the stratagem of the devil: when he could not find anyone at Lystra, he brought them in from elsewhere. For he takes care to have his instruments everywhere. If he does not have them in one place, he finds others elsewhere whom he sends in. There are old examples among the heretics.

units.la: benè conueniunt, & Euangelium prosi-cit, excitat legatos à latere. Monachos &c. qui blanditijs, promissis, minis &c. aliquos commouent. Idem fit, si leges bonæ fiant. Vigilemus, & similî studio vtamur, &c.
units.tr: Today, if some agree well and the gospel makes progress, he stirs up envoys from the side. Monks and others, by flatteries, promises, threats and so on, move some people. The same happens if good laws are passed. Let us be watchful and use similar zeal.

units.la: II. Lystren. inconstantiam. Deos puta-runt & voluerunt sacrificare. Nunc per-suasi ab exteris, & quidem Iudæis, lapi-dant. Quid facturi, si præsides Rom. quid iussissent. Nec mouentur recenti beneficio, aut Apostolorum pietate & modestia. Sunt huius generis exempla in historijs multa. Ægyptiorum erga Iosephum, Gen. 41. Exod. 1. Israel. erga Mosem, Exo. 4. 5. 17. Num. 16. &c. Dauidem sub Saule & Abi-lone, Item Roboamo &c. Quotidiana. Sed nemo offendatur, quando idem Christo accidit, Ioh. 6. Mat. 21. Ioh. 19.
units.tr: II. The inconstancy of the Lystrans. They thought Paul and Barnabas were gods and wanted to sacrifice to them. Now, persuaded by outsiders, and indeed by Jews, they stone him. What would they have done if the Roman governors had ordered something? Nor are they moved by his recent benefit, or by the piety and modesty of the apostles. There are many examples of this kind in histories: of the Egyptians towards Joseph (Gen. 41, Exod. 1); of Israel towards Moses (Exod. 4, 5, 17; Num. 16, etc.); of David under Saul and Abishai; likewise of Rehoboam, and so on. These are everyday things. But let no one be offended, since the same happened to Christ (John 6; Matt. 21; John 19).

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Non fidendum aurae populari, qua nihil instabilius, vt singuli proprio exemplo possunt discere. In Deo repositæ sunt virtutis præmia, Matt. 6. &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: we must not trust popular favour, which is nothing more unstable, as each person can learn from his own experience. The rewards of virtue are laid up in God (Matt. 6, etc.).

units.la: III. Deus quid, cuius nutu omnia agun-tur. Permittit vt fideles seruus lapidetur, & quidè ijs authoribus, quibus se totum impendebat, Rom. 10. 9. Non nouum, si quid simile fiat hodie. Idem prophetæ pas-si, Mat. 5. sed tunc argumenta consolationis petamus ex Dei prouidentia, quæ hic egregiè elucet. Lapidatur Paulus, nihil patiente Barnaba: Nimirum quòd infirmi or adhuc essent, Paulus mirificè feruatur inter saxa, ne vulnus læthale accipiat..Restituitur, vt crastino sit sufficiens ad iter.
units.tr: III. God, by whose nod all things are done, indeed permits a faithful servant to be stoned, and at the hands of those very people for whom he was spending himself entirely, Rom. 10. 9. It is nothing new if something similar happens today. The prophets suffered the same, Matt. 5. But here let us seek grounds of comfort in God's providence, which shines out clearly in this passage. Paul is stoned while Barnabas suffers nothing. Clearly, because the others were still weak, Paul is wonderfully preserved amid the stones, so that he does not receive a deadly wound. He is restored so that he is strong enough for the journey the next day.

units.la: NOT. Nemini desperandum interpe ricula.
units.tr: NOTE. No one should despair in dangers.

units.la: Potest Deus in morte seruare, Roman 14.Ioh.11. Quin ad similia præparemur, Hunc vsum Paulus docet, 2.Tim.3. Cogitemus ergo:1. Nihil sine Dei consilio nobis accidere. 2. Deum nemini facere iniuriam. 3.Patrem esse, & tunc maximè tueri, quando hostes omnia posse videntur. Liberat, si ita sit è re nostra. Sin secus, illi videatur, nos qui sumus?
units.tr: God can preserve us even in death, Rom. 14; John 11. Indeed, we should prepare ourselves for similar things. Paul teaches this use, 2 Tim. 3. Let us therefore consider: (1) that nothing happens to us without God's counsel; (2) that God does no wrong to anyone; (3) that he is a Father, and protects us most of all when the enemies seem able to do everything. He sets us free if it is for our good. If otherwise, let it seem good to him; who are we?

units.la: IV.Quid discipuli aut credentes? Num redeunt ad superstitiones? Num pudet il-los Pauli? Minimè. Sed circumdederunt il-lum, iam extractum. Cùm non possent tueri, officium præstant quod possunt, & plangunt, vt Steph.Act.8. Neq; pio officio deest Dominus, qui & ipsos tuetur contra furiosum populum, & Paulum restituit, ac porrò seruat. NOT. Quid debeatur periclitantib. pro Christo.1.Qui possunt iuuare, iuuent. Vbi varia sunt officia, sed nullum sine præmio, Matt.10. Obstetrices, Exo.1. Quanto magis, si fœderibus tenéamur? Qui negligunt,cogitent sibi dici, quod Mardoch.di cebat,&c.Heft.4.
units.tr: IV. What did the disciples or believers do? Did they return to their superstitions? Were they ashamed of Paul? By no means. But the disciples surrounded him, now drawn out. Since they could not protect him, they performed the duty they could and mourned, as at Stephen's death (Acts 8). Nor does the Lord fail in this pious office: he both protects them against the raging people and restores Paul and keeps him safe further on. NOTE what is owed to those in danger for Christ. (1) Those who can help should help. Where duties vary, none goes without reward (Matt. 10). Midwives (Exod. 1). How much more so if we are bound by covenants? Let those who neglect this consider that what Mordecai said is said to them (Esth. 4).

units.la: 2. Qui non possunt iuuare,saltem non consentiant impiorum consilijs,Psal.1.Apologus ciconiæ inter grues.Iosephus Arimath.Mar.15 Felix dissidium,Luc.12.
units.tr: (2) Those who cannot help should at least not consent to the counsels of the impious (Ps. 1). The fable of the stork among the cranes. Joseph of Arimathea (Mark 15). A happy division (Luke 12).

units.la: 3. Afflictos prosequamur pietatis officijs.Suscipe exules,consolare,Matt.25.
units.tr: (3) Let us accompany the afflicted with the offices of piety. Take in exiles, console them (Matt. 25).

units.la: Talibus Dei auxilium ex insperato affulget. Deus enim nec suorum labores frustratur,nec filij sui regnum per impios euerti patitur,Psal.2. Oremus.
units.tr: To such people God's help shines forth unexpectedly. For God neither frustrates the labours of his own, nor allows the kingdom of his Son to be overthrown by the impious (Ps. 2). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXI.
units.tr: HOMILY 121.

units.la: 26 Et postridie abijt Derben cum Barnaba.
units.tr: 26 And on the next day he departed to Derbe with Barnabas.

units.la: 21 Quumque euangelizassent vbi illi, & docuissent multos, reuersi sunt Lystram & Iconium & Antiochiam.
units.tr: 21 And when they had preached the gospel in that city and taught many, they returned to Lystra, Iconium and Antioch.

units.la: 22 Confirmantes animos discipulorum, hortantes vt permanerent in fide, & dicentes, oportere per multas afflictiones nos ingredi in regnum Dei.
units.tr: 22 Confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and saying that we must enter the kingdom of God through many afflictions.

units.la: Dicuus Lucas non modo doctrinam Apostolorum describit, verumetiam narrat quanto studio, labore & periculis hanc inter Gentes promulgarint, in hoc vnum intenti, vt omnes à superstitionibus nibus adChristi fidem adducerent, in qua sola homines seruantur. Vsus omnium est, vt discamus hodie etiam studio & labore opus esse, & vehementer falli eos, qui langui diu agunt. Etsi enim hoc Dei negotium sit, nostro tamen ministerio ille vitatur: vbi nos eius bonitatem agnoscere, & illius organa nos praebere oportet. Facit huc inprimis praesens locus. Postquam enim descripsit Lucas, quid Paulo Lystris acciderit, exponit deinceps, quid porro fecerit. Vbi multa concurrunt, &c.
units.tr: Saint Luke does not merely describe the teaching of the Apostles, but also relates with what zeal, labour and dangers they spread it among the Gentiles, intent on this one aim: to bring all people away from superstitions to faith in Christ, in which alone people are saved. The lesson for all of us is that we too today need zeal and labour, and that those are greatly mistaken who live in idleness for a long time. For although this is God's work, he nevertheless carries it out through our ministry, and we ought to acknowledge his goodness and offer ourselves as his instruments. The present passage bears on this above all. For after Luke has described what happened to Paul at Lystra, he goes on to explain what they did next. Here many points come together, etc.

units.la: I. Postridie Derbam eunt, illic Euangelium praedicant & multos in Christi fide instituunt. Vbi NOT. §1. Exemplū constantiae, quod ne vnum quidem diem officium negligunt, sed ex periculo animosio res facti, maiori zelo ad illud redeunt. Arguuntur, qui si quid passi sunt, iam se omni officio defunctos putant. Ita vero ingratos se praebent Deo liberatori.
units.tr: I. The next day they go to Derbe, preach the gospel there and instruct many in faith in Christ. Note 1. An example of constancy: they do not neglect their duty even for a single day, but, made bolder by danger, return to it with greater zeal. Those are rebuked who, if they have suffered anything, think they have already discharged every duty. In this way they show themselves ungrateful to God, their deliverer.

units.la: §2 Quod rursum solius Euangelij mentio fit. Ergo ne in doctrina quicquam mutarunt. Fidei magnum argumentum, quo simul admonemur, quid in Ecclesia perpetuo debeat praedicari. Damnantur hominum traditiones, &c.
units.tr: §2. Again there is mention only of the gospel. Therefore they changed nothing in the teaching. A great proof of faith, by which we are also reminded what ought always to be preached in the Church. Human traditions are condemned, etc.

units.la: II. Redeunt in 3 vrbes, ex quibus eiecti fuerant, vt nimirum in officio retinerent quos lucrifecerant. Opus hoc in salutis negotio quàm maximè propter satanæ in fidias. Simile rei domesticæ & sementis. Turpiter hodie peccant, qui Ecclesias con stitutas patiuntur corrumpi. Sed Not ¶ Zeli magni argumentum, quòd ad eos redeunt, à quibus ignominiosè erant ejecti. Ergo propter hominum ingratitudinem & iniurias ab officio non est discedendum. Cur enim eum imiteris, quem damnas? Cogita te Dei seruû esse, qui non fallet: à mundo autem gratiam meliorem non rependi. Vide exempla Mosis Dauidis. Christi, Luc. 19. Matt. 23 imitemur sin-guli publicè & priuatim, Rom. 12.
units.tr: II. They return to the three cities from which they had been driven, namely to keep in their duty those whom they had won. This work, in the business of salvation, is especially needful because of Satan's plots. It is like the care of a household and of sowing. Those who today shamefully allow established churches to be corrupted sin disgracefully. But note: a sign of great zeal is that they return to those from whom they had been shamefully expelled. Therefore one must not withdraw from one's office because of human ingratitude and injuries. For why imitate one whom you condemn? Consider that you are a servant of God, who will not deceive you; but from the world you should not expect better thanks. See the examples of Moses, David and Christ: Luke 19, Matt. 23. Let us each imitate them, publicly and privately, Rom. 12.

units.la: III. Quid autem in vrbibus iustis fecerunt Apostoli. 1. Confirmârunt animos discipulorum. Proprie solius Dei hoc opus est, qui fidem quoque solus largitur, & solus in animos ius habet, Iohannis 3. Sed quia verbo externo vtitur, hoc ipsum ministris quoque tribuitur, 1. Cor. 3 Ideo addit, Exhortantes vt perseuerarent, &c. Vbi Not. ¶1. Non sufficere si semel credamus, sed perseuerandum in finem, Matt. 24. Luc. 19. Alioqui fiunt postrema peiora primis. Ob seruandum hoc Ecclesijs bene constitutis. Vide Ephes. & Tyat. Apo. 2. Ministris, vt illi iustent, 2. Tim. 4. Magistratib. Singulis. Sed
units.tr: III. What did the Apostles do in the cities? (1) They strengthened the souls of the disciples. This work belongs properly to God alone, who alone bestows faith and alone has authority over the soul, John 3. But because he uses the outward word, this very work is also attributed to ministers, 1 Cor. 3. Therefore he adds: exhorting them to persevere, etc. Note 1: it is not enough to believe once; we must persevere to the end, Matt. 24, Luke 19. Otherwise the last things become worse than the first. This is to be observed in well-established churches. See Ephesus and Thyatira, Rev. 2. Ministers should exhort, as these did, 2 Tim. 4. Magistrates likewise, and individuals. But

units.la: {¶} Perseuerantia in fide summè necessaria est. lis. Sed ô quám fœde hîc errátur à nobis. {1}2. Fidei doctrinam certam esse & immutabilem. Alioqui non laudem merere tur perseuerantia. Arguuntur qui multa addunt, quæ nō minus necessaria dicunt. Atqui hæc cum fidei doctrina pugnant, admitti non debent Gal. 1.
units.tr: {¶} Perseverance in the faith is most necessary. But oh, how foully we go wrong here! (2) The doctrine of faith is certain and unchangeable. Otherwise perseverance would not deserve praise. Those are rebuked who add many things which they say are no less necessary. But these things conflict with the doctrine of faith and must not be admitted, Gal. 1.

units.la: 2. Offendiculo crucis medentur, quod fieri oportuit, cùm multi offenderentur, quando videbant doctrinam hanc passim explodi. Breui autem sententia vtuntur quæ duas rationes continet. 1. Quòd ita fieri oporteat. Atqui patienter ferri debet quod mutari non potest. Verè autem hoc dici, patet ex vitæ totius cursu, quæ propter peccatum omni malorum genere referta est. Hinc illa, Gen. 47. Matth. 6. Accedunt pijs peculiares ex mundo, qui lucem non ferunt, de quibus admonuit, Matth. 10. Ioh. 15 16 2 Tim. 3 Psal. 34.
units.tr: (2) They heal the offence of the cross, which had to happen, since many were offended when they saw this doctrine being rejected on every side. They use a brief saying which contains two reasons. (1) That it must be so. But what cannot be changed must be borne patiently. That this is truly said is plain from the whole course of life, which because of sin is filled with every kind of evil. Hence that, Gen. 47, Matt. 6. To the godly there are added particular trials from the world, which does not bear the light; of these he warned, Matt. 10, John 15, 16, 2 Tim. 3, Ps. 34.

units.la: Sed NOT. Cur sic fieri oporteat? 1. Vt fides nostra probetur, 1. Pet. 1. 2. Vt ca ro nostra coerceatur, 1. Cor. 11. 3. Vt incendamur desiderio cœlestium, & mundi huius nos taedeat, quem alioqui amamus nimium.
units.tr: But note: why must it be so? (1) That our faith may be proved, 1 Pet. 1. (2) That our flesh may be restrained, 1 Cor. 11. (3) That we may be fired with desire for heavenly things, and grow weary of this world, which otherwise we love too much.

units.la: 11. Finis lætissimus: Regnum Dei. Vbi non putabimus, nos hoc mereri afflictionibus, quod solius Christi merito est quæ tamen. situm.Sed docent,viam hanc Christi sanguine esse consecratam, & promissione confirmatam,Ioh 12 14.17.Luc.22.
units.tr: (3) The most joyful end: the kingdom of God. Here we are not to think that we merit this by afflictions, since it rests on the merit of Christ alone; yet they teach that this way has been consecrated by the blood of Christ and confirmed by promise, John 12, 14, 17, Luke 22.

units.la: Haec meditemur publicè & priuatim. Aliter fieri non potest,etsi mundo seruias mus. Respiciamus in Christi exemplum. Futuram gloriam spectemus. Coniungamus his preces, & indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: Let us meditate on these things, publicly and privately. Otherwise it cannot be done, even though we serve the world. Let us look to the example of Christ. Let us look to the future glory. Let us join prayers to these, and pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXII
units.tr: HOMILIA CXXII

units.la: 23 Quumque ipsi per fufragia eré assent per singulas Ecclesias presbyteros,precatique effent cum jejunijs, commendarunt eos Domino, in quem crediderunt.
units.tr: 23 And when they had appointed elders for them in every church by vote, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord in whom they had believed.

units.la: 24 Peragratáq; Pisidia, venerunt in Pamphyliam, &c. ad ver.29.
units.tr: 24 And after passing through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia, etc., to verse 29.

units.la: QVemadmodum Apostoli per Evangelij prædicationem Christo ex omnibus gentibus discipulos adducere, & Ecclesiam colligere debuerunt,Mat. 28. ita officij illorum fuit, Ecclesias diligenti cura & sedulitate conseruare. Id in præsenti historia fidelissimè præstant Paulus & Barnabas. Postquam enim Ecclesias aliquot Antiochiæ, Iconij & Lystris constituerunt, quas à Iudæis mirificè vexari nouerant,licet indè reiecti essent,redeunt tamen ad illas. Confirmant discipulorum animos, exhortantur ad perseuerantiam: medentur offendiculo crucis, &c. Sequitur quod ad hanc causam pertinet, &c.
units.tr: Just as the Apostles were bound, through the preaching of the Gospel, to bring disciples to Christ from all nations and to gather the Church (Matt. 28), so it was their duty to preserve the churches with careful diligence and zeal. In the present history Paul and Barnabas do this most faithfully. For after they had established several churches at Antioch, Iconium and Lystra, which they knew were being grievously harassed by the Jews, they returned to them even though they had been driven out from there. They strengthen the minds of the disciples and exhort them to perseverance; they heal the offence of the cross, etc. What follows pertains to this matter, etc.

units.la: I. Singulis Ecclesijs presbyteros ordinant. Sunt hi partim doctores siue pastores, partim qui his adsunt, & illos commendant gratiae Dei, &c. No T. ¶ 1 Ad Ecclesia rum conseruationem opus esse ministris, per quos doctrina in continuo vsu seruetur. Postulat hoc carnis infirmitas, & ingenij humani corruptio, quod sic in officio retineri oportet, 2. Tim. 4. Imprimis insidiae diaboli, Matth 13. Luc. 22. 1. Pet. 5. Ideo Christus non modo Apostolos, verum etiam pastores instituit, Eph. 4. 1 Cor. 12. Idé apud Cretenses Paul. obseruauit Tit. 1 gstifte. Arguuntur, qui doctrinam, vt inutilem contemnunt, qui nec seipsos quidem norunt. Qu'n potius huic studeant quàm diligentissimè, quicunq; Ecclesias saluas volunt, &c. ¶ 2. Quo ritu in his creandis vntur? A. Preces & jejunia adhibent, vt Act. 1. & 13. Significatur solennem coetum hoc nomine institutum fuisse. Hic enim mos fuit veterum, si quæ magna necessitas vrgebat, Ioel. 2. 2. Par. 20. Orárunt autem partim vt Deus ipsorum iudicia regeret, cum scirent omnes homines falli pos-
units.tr: I. They ordain elders for each church. These are partly teachers or ministers, and partly those who assist them; and they commend them to the grace of God, etc. Note. ¶ 1. Ministers are needed for the preservation of the churches, through whom doctrine is kept in continual use. The weakness of the flesh and the corruption of human nature require that men be held in office in this way (2 Tim. 4). Above all, there are the snares of the devil (Matt. 13; Luke 22; 1 Pet. 5). For this reason Christ instituted not only apostles but also ministers (Eph. 4; 1 Cor. 12). Paul likewise observed this among the Cretans (Tit. 1). Those are rebuked who despise doctrine as useless, and who do not even know themselves. Should not all who want the churches to be safe devote themselves to this most diligently, etc.? ¶ 2. What rite do they use in creating these men? A. They employ prayers and fasts, as in Acts 1 and 13. This signifies that a solemn assembly was instituted for this purpose. For it was the custom of the ancients, when some great necessity pressed, to do so (Joel 2; 2 Chron. 20). They prayed partly that God would govern their judgments, since they knew all men can err,

units.la: fe:partim vt dignis donis instrueret eos, qui eligebantur. Vt autem feruentiores essent preces, jejunia coniuxerunt, Matt. 9. Hinc colligamus, quantæ molis hoc mu nus sit. 1. Tim. 3. Ier. 1.
units.tr: and partly that he would furnish with worthy gifts those who were being chosen. And to make their prayers more fervent, they joined fasting to them (Matt. 9). From this we gather how great a burden this office is (1 Tim. 3; Jer. 1).

units.la: Βχειροθονία vsi sunt, per quam suffra gia & manuum impositio, quæ erat conse crationis symbolum, poterat intelligi. Nihil ergo fecerunt ex priuato arbitrio. Ob seruemus in his religiosam simplicitatem veteris Ecclesiæ, & quam foeda tyrannide postea Ecclesiæ oppressæ sint. Ad pau cos peruenit eligendi potestas: & fere Simoniacis artibus ministerium patuit, &c. Quæruntur quales Ieroboamus & Herod, quærebant.
units.tr: They used the laying on of hands (χειροθονία), by which the vote and the imposition of hands, which was the symbol of consecration, could be understood. They therefore did nothing from private judgment. Let us observe in these matters the religious simplicity of the ancient Church, and how foul a tyranny the Church was later oppressed by. The power of choosing came to a few, and the ministry was opened almost by Simoniacal arts, etc. Let us ask what sort of men Jeroboam and Herod were, who sought these things.

units.la: ¶ 3. Commendarunt Domino, cui crediderant. Est hoc humanitatis officium, & fidelem Apostolorum cura pro Ecclesijs arguit 1. Co 2. Interim per hæc admonemur. A. In firmitate nostra semper Dei tutela, & gubernatione opus habere. Nam vtipsi ad lapsum proclives sumus, ita satan nō qui- efcit, &c. Hinc illa Christi, Luc. 22. Ioh. 17 Excitet hoc ad religionis studium, & simul consoletur. Constat enim salutem nostram Deo commendatissimam esse, Iohan. 14. 10. Matth. 10. & 28. Romanor. 8. 2. Tim. 2. B. Quid facias, vbi tuo officio functus es. Euentum rei Deo commen-da,cuius prouidentia res reguntur. Qui hoc ignorant, carnis prudentia mirificè torquentur, & sæpe à suo officio recedunt, dum suo consilio res transfigendas putant.Communicant aliorum impietati per consensum,Act 8 Fac ergo officium constanter, & causæ exitu Domino commenda.SicAbraham,Gen.22.Heb.11. Nec enim propter pericula nos officium negligere vult Deus,Mar.10.Lu.10. Io.15.16
units.tr: ¶ 3. They commended them to the Lord in whom they had believed. This is an office of humanity, and the Apostles' faithful care for the churches shows it (2 Cor. 2). Meanwhile we are admonished by these things. A. In our weakness we always need the protection and governance of God. For just as we are prone to fall, so Satan does not rest, etc. Hence those words of Christ (Luke 22; John 17). This should stir us to zeal for religion and at the same time comfort us. For it is certain that our salvation is most entrusted to God (John 14; Matt. 10 and 28; Rom. 8; 2 Tim. 2). B. What you should do when you have discharged your office: commend the outcome of the matter to God, by whose providence affairs are governed. Those who do not know this are wretchedly tormented by the prudence of the flesh, and often withdraw from their office while they think they must carry out matters by their own counsel. They share in the impiety of others through consent (Acts 8). Therefore do your duty constantly, and commit the outcome of the cause to the Lord. So Abraham (Gen. 22; Heb. 11). For God does not wish us to neglect our office on account of dangers (Mark 10; Luke 10; John 15:16).

units.la: II. Reditum parant Antiochiam, & in transitu,Pergā Euangelio illustrant quod nimirum illic offerretur docendi occasio. Fuit autem Perga Dianæ impio cultu maxime infamis.
units.tr: II. They prepare to return to Antioch, and on the way, at Perga, they illustrate the Gospel, since there, no doubt, an opportunity of teaching was offered. Now Perga was most notorious for the impious worship of Diana.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Bonitatem Dei & sedulitatem Apostolorum,qua in euertendo regno vsi sunt. Simili zelo hodie vtendum etiam inuito mundo.Ita Christus.Minimè ergo audiri debent, qui minis & ingratitudine mundi territi, cessandum putant.
units.tr: Note. ¶ The goodness of God and the diligence of the Apostles, which they used in overturning the kingdom. We must use similar zeal today, even though the world is unwilling. So Christ. Those therefore should by no means be heard who, terrified by threats and the ingratitude of the world, think that they should cease.

units.la: III. Exponitur quid Antiochiam reuer sifecerint.I.Acta omnia ad Ecclesiam refe runt, & rerum ab se gestarum rationem reddunt,vt fideles legati,&c.NOT.¶Apostolos non dominatores fidei fuisse, qui absoluta potestate pro suo arbitrio omnia gesserint,vt hodie Rom.Pont.Seruos Christi & Ecclesiæ se esse agnouerunt. Ita omnes decet episcopos.
units.tr: III. It is set out what they did on returning to Antioch. I. They refer all their acts to the Church and render an account of the things they had done, as faithful envoys, etc. Note. ¶ That the Apostles were not lords of the faith, who conducted everything by absolute power at their own pleasure, as the Roman Pontiff does today; they acknowledged themselves to be servants of Christ and of the Church. So all bishops ought to be.

units.la: II. Nihil de se arrogantius prædicant, sed omnia ad Deum authorem referunt. Huc tecum fuisse, & in ipsis operatum esse dicunt. Eun Iem fidei ostium gentibus aperuisse, id et st,gentium corda illumi nauisse & traxisse fatentur, Ioh.6. Magnæ modestiæ argumentum.
units.tr: II. They proclaim nothing arrogant about themselves, but refer everything to God as the author. They say that God was with them and worked in them. They confess that he opened the door of faith to the Gentiles, and that he enlightened and drew the hearts of the Gentiles (John 6). This is a proof of great modesty.

units.la: NoT.¶ Nihil nobis tribui debere.Exigitur à nobis fides & industria. Sed vt euentus Deo permitti debet, ita etiam eidem gloria tribui debet. Ita in verbi mini sterio, 1.Cor.3.Ioh.6.Ifa 54.In magistratu (Dan.4.) & œconomia, Psal. 127. Hoc argumento operum quoque iustitia euerti tur,2.Cor 3.1.Cor.4.Luc.17.
units.tr: Note. ¶ Nothing should be attributed to us. Faith and diligence are required of us. But just as the outcome must be left to God, so also glory must be given to him. So in the ministry of the Word (1 Cor. 3; John 6; Isa. 54), in the magistracy (Dan. 4), and in household management (Ps. 127). By this argument the righteousness of works too is overturned (2 Cor. 3; 1 Cor. 4; Luke 17).

units.la: III. Manserunt ibi longo tempore, nimirum à laboribus & periculis sese recreantes.Est enim hoc licitum, vt qui strenuè laborarunt,honesto vires otio resocillent Vide Mar.6. Interim non putabimus ibi sedisse otiosos,&c. Oremus
units.tr: III. They remained there a long time, no doubt refreshing themselves from labours and dangers. For it is lawful that those who have laboured vigorously should restore their strength with honourable rest. See Mark 6. Meanwhile we shall not think they sat there idle, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXIII.

units.la: ET quidam, qui descenderant à Iudæa, docebant fratres: Nisi circumcidamini... cum circumcidamini secundum ritum Mosis, non potestis salui fieri.
units.tr: And certain men which came down from Judaea taught the brethren, and said: Except ye be circumcised... except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.

units.la: 2 Orta igitur seditione ac disceptatione non exigua Paulo et Barnabae adversus illos, statuerunt ut ascenderent Paulus et Barnabas, et quidam alii ex illis ad Apostolos ac presbyteros Hierosolymam super quaestione hac.
units.tr: 2 When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.

units.la: 3 Illi ergo deducti ab Ecclesia, peragrarunt Phoenicem, et Samariam, narrantes conversionem Gentium: et adferebant gaudium magnum omnibus fratribus.
units.tr: 3 And being brought on their way by the Church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles, and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.

units.la: 4 Quum autem advenissent in Hierusalem, exceperunt eos ab Ecclesia et ab Apostolis ac Presbyteris, et annuntiarunt quaecunque Deus per ipsos fecerat.
units.tr: 4 And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the Church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.

units.la: EXposuit hucusque Lucas, ut primitivam Ecclesiam & Apostoli doctrinam in multis tribulationibus Deus servavit. Sequitur nova historia, qua docetur, ut eadem ad versus falsos fratres & haereses defensa sit. Hactenus enim totis annis 14. Paulus praedicarat, in uno Christo omnem iustitiam et salutem contineri, sicut etiam alii Apostoli (1. Cor. 1. Act. 4. 1. Ioh. 1. 2. &c.) Contra hanc doctrinam aliqui ex Pharisaeis fmo conuersi exurgebant, qui circumcisio-nem & reliquas legis obseruationes ad sa-lutem necessarias esse dicerent. His sese acriter opponit Paulus. Fit publica dif-sensio,quæ eò vsque progreditur,vt Con-cilij Apostolici authoritate eam componi oportuerit. Describitur hoc Capite pri-mum Concilium, & in eo forma propo-nitur, quæ omnibus sæculis obseruetur, & ad quam Concilia omnia examinentur.
units.tr: Luke has thus far set out how God preserved the primitive Church and the doctrine of the apostles amid many tribulations. There follows a new episode, in which it is taught that this same doctrine was defended against false brethren and heresies. For Paul had been preaching for fourteen years that all righteousness and salvation are contained in Christ alone, as the other apostles also taught (1 Cor. 1; Acts 4; 1 John 1; 2, etc.). Against this doctrine some who had recently been converted from the Pharisees rose up, saying that circumcision and the other observances of the law were necessary for salvation. Paul opposes them sharply. A public dissension arises, which goes so far that it had to be settled by the authority of an apostolic council. In this chapter the first council is described, and in it a pattern is set forth which is to be observed in all ages and by which all councils are to be tested.

units.la: Sed singulas historiæ partes excutia-mus.
units.tr: But let us examine the individual parts of the story.

units.la: I. Authores concertationis producun-tur. Iudæi fuerunt,& ex Hierosolyma ve-niebant,quæ Ecclesia vt communis omni-um mater colebatur. Rom.15. Huius no-mine isti abutebantur. NoT.¶ Seducto-res plerunque ex Ecclesia enasci,eos nimi-rum,qui nunquam vera Ecclesia membra fuerunt,1.Io.2. Sic Christus monet, Matt. 7.Paulus,Act.20.Phil.3.&c. Est hæc sata-næ calliditas,qui nisi tegatur,se abomina-bilem esse sentit,2.Cor.11.
units.tr: I. The authors of the dispute are brought forward. They were Jews, and they came from Jerusalem, which was honoured as the common mother of all the Church (Rom. 15). These men abused her name. NOTE: Seducers generally arise from within the Church, namely those who were never true members of the Church (1 John 2). So Christ warns (Matt. 7); Paul too (Acts 20; Phil. 3), etc. This is the cunning of Satan, who, unless he is concealed, feels himself to be detestable (2 Cor. 11).

units.la: Arguuntur hoc loco,qui Ecclesiam ne-gant errare posse, & de externa illa lo-quuntur. Item locum nihil facere ad cau-sæ veritatem.Legati Romani à latere.
units.tr: In this place are rebuked those who deny that the Church can err, and who speak of that outward Church. Likewise, the place has nothing to do with the truth of the cause. Roman legates a latere.

units.la: II. Status concertationis. Gentes nisi circumcidantur,non posse saluari. Habe-bant bant argumenta sua Legem Dei, Genef. 17. Exemplum Hierosol. Ecclesiæ. Item quòd ex circumcisione legis obseruatio pendebat (Galat.5.) quæ illa sublata abrogari, & peccandi licentia impuè videbatur. Alii qui fatebantur Christum & Euangelium.
units.tr: II. The state of the dispute. Unless the Gentiles are circumcised, they cannot be saved. They had their arguments: the law of God (Gen. 17); the example of the church of Jerusalem; also that the observance of the law depended on circumcision (Gal. 5), and that if circumcision were removed, the law would seem to be abrogated and licence to sin would go unpunished. Others, who confessed Christ and the gospel, ...

units.la: Eadem ergo concertatio fuit, quæ hodie nobis cum Papistis est, nisi quòd horum causa minùs plausibilis ob hominum traditiones.
units.tr: Therefore this was the same dispute that we have today with the Papists, except that their cause is less plausible, because of men's traditions.
