units.la: NOT. Ingenij humani peruersitatem. Cùm hominibus salutem Deus gratis offert, illi eam laboribus & sumptibus volunt redimere. Vide Isa 52.
units.tr: NOTE. The perversity of the human mind. When God offers salvation freely to men, they want to buy it back with labours and expenses. See Isa. 52.

units.la: III. Effectus. Seditio oritur in Ecclesia, quæ hucusque pacatissima & commune fidelibus asylum fuerat.
units.tr: III. The effect. Sedition arises in the Church, which until now had been most peaceful and a common refuge for the faithful.

units.la: NOT. Qui Ecclesias turbent. Obijci-tur hoc eis, 1 Reg. 18. Sed ab illis Ecclesiæ turbantur, qui contra simplicem veritatem aliquid obtrudunt. Vide Gal. 1.5. 6. Phil. 3. Habes quo te aduersus pontificios excusés. Faciunt quod est 1. Cor. 1.
units.tr: NOTE. Those who disturb churches. This is charged against them (1 Kings 18). But it is those who push something against the simple truth who disturb the Churches. See Gal. 1, 5, 6; Phil. 3. You have here how to excuse yourself against the Papists. They are doing what is said in 1 Cor. 1.

units.la: § 2. Neminem disseñsionibus offendi debere, vt ideo omnia falsa putet, aut Ecclesias esse neget, &c. Semper enim hæ fuerunt, A. Quia sic probantur homines, & manifesti fiunt qui verè crediderunt, 1. Co rinth.11.Rom.5.8 B. Quia sic ventilantur & examinantur precipui fidei articuli, qui bus alioqui nimis inhaeretur. Sic in Coena hodie factum.
units.tr: § 2. No one should be offended by dissensions, so as to think that everything is false, or to deny that there are Churches, etc. For these have always existed: (A) because thus men are tested, and those who truly believed are made manifest (1 Cor. 11; Rom. 5, 8); (B) because thus the chief articles of faith are sifted and examined, to which otherwise men cling too tightly. So it has been done today in the Supper.

units.la: IV. Quid factum? 1.Paulus & Barnabas fortiter sese opponunt, nec quicquam cedunt, licet alibi infirmis multa det Paulus, & dare iubeat, 1.Cor.8.9.Rom.15. Hic enim fidei iustitia & libertas Christiana evertebatur, Galat.4.5. Corrumpebatur verus legis visus, Gal.3.Rom.10 Obscurabatur Evangelij fulgor & maxima parte impediebatur.
units.tr: IV. What was done? 1. Paul and Barnabas oppose them boldly and yield nothing at all, although elsewhere Paul gives much to the weak and bids others to give too (1 Cor. 8, 9; Rom. 15). For here the righteousness of faith and Christian liberty were being overthrown (Gal. 4, 5). The true view of the law was being corrupted (Gal. 3; Rom. 10). The brightness of the gospel was being obscured and for the most part hindered.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Pacis studio nihil admittendum esse, quod gloriae Christi deroget. Alioqui iudicium Christi incurrimus, Mar. 8 Pax quaerenda in Christo, Iohan.14.16. Ideo Paulus etiam Petro resistit, Gal.2. &c.
units.tr: NOTE. In the pursuit of peace nothing must be admitted which detracts from the glory of Christ. Otherwise we incur the judgement of Christ (Mark 8). Peace is to be sought in Christ (John 14, 16). Therefore Paul also resisted Peter (Gal. 2), etc.

units.la: II. Decernit Ecclesia, ut ad Apostolos Hierosolymam ascendant, & huic decreto acquiescit Paulus, non quod veritatis causam vellet hominum iudicio subijcere, sed quod sciret impostores hoc Apostolorum nomine abuti. Quae causa fuit omnium synodorum.
units.tr: II. The Church decrees that they go up to the apostles at Jerusalem, and Paul acquiesces in this decree, not because he wished to subject the cause of truth to the judgement of men, but because he knew that impostors were abusing the name of the apostles for this purpose. This was the reason for all synods.

units.la: NOT. ¶1. Modestiam Pauli. Constantissimus est, & haud dubie ne Apostolis quide in hac causa cessisset Gal.1.2. Non tamen aspernatur medium pacis, a pijs fratrifratribus inuentum. Idem hodie obser-uandum, &c.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The moderation of Paul. He is most constant, and undoubtedly he would not have yielded even to the apostles in this cause (Gal. 1, 2). Yet he does not scorn a means of peace devised by godly brethren. The same is to be observed today, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quæ ratio sit optima componendo rum dissidiorum in religione. Ad Apostolos alcendamus, quorum doctrina Christi testimonijs confirmata est, Luc. 10. Ioh. 17 Mar. 16. Anxiè enim cauendum, ne ab hac latum vnguem discedamus, 1. Ioh. 2. 2. Timot. 3. &c. Falluntur ergo turpissimè, qui hæc pro suis concilijs allegant, in quibus omnia contra Apostolorum doctrinam & exemplum instituuntur. Concilia pia non sunt, in quibus non sola Apostolorum authoritas valet.
units.tr: § 2. What is the best method of settling disagreements in religion. Let us go up to the apostles, whose doctrine was confirmed by the testimonies of Christ (Luke 10; John 17; Mark 16). For we must take anxious care not to depart from it by a hair's breadth (1 John 2; 2 Tim. 3), etc. Therefore those are shamefully mistaken who cite these things for their own councils, in which everything is set up against the doctrine and example of the apostles. Councils are not godly in which the authority of the apostles alone does not prevail.

units.la: V. Profectio ipsa describitur. 1. Dedu-cuntur ab Ecclesia, quæ comites adduxe-rat, vt videas, hanc ab ipsis steriffe. Not. ¶ Fidos ministros non debere destitui Ec-clesiarum patrocinio, Gal 4. Pro commu-ni enim causa pugnant. Hodie insultamus, quasi priuata Pfafforum causa agatur.
units.tr: V. The departure itself is described. 1. They are brought on their way by the Church, which had provided them with companions, so that you may see that the Church stood by them. NOTE. Faithful ministers ought not to be deprived of the patronage of the Churches (Gal. 4). For they fight for a common cause. Today men mock, as if the cause of the priests were a private matter.

units.la: II. Inter eundum gentium conuersionem pasïm prædicant.
units.tr: II. On their journey they preach the conversion of the Gentiles everywhere.

units.la: Atqui propter hanc omnis lis erat.
units.tr: Yet all the dispute arose because of this.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Non dissimulanda esse Dei opera propter improbos censores. Imò cum mundi improbitate luctandum. Si nos taceamus, lapides clamabunt, Lucæ 19.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ The works of God must not be concealed for fear of wicked critics. Rather we must struggle against the wickedness of the world. If we keep silent, the stones will cry out, Luke 19.

units.la: III. Gaudent fratres, non inuidենt, doli-turi nimirum si secus audiuissent rem suc-cessisse, &c. Nota. ¶ Fidelibus veris maximam gaudij causam ex regni Chri-sti propagatione enasci. Nos hac non gaudere, ex nostra tepiditate patet, &c.
units.tr: III. The brothers rejoice, they do not envy, doubtless they would have grieved had they heard that the matter had turned out otherwise, etc. Note. ¶ The greatest cause of joy for true believers arises from the spread of Christ's kingdom. That we do not rejoice in this is clear from our lukewarmness, etc.

units.la: IIII. Benigné ab Ecclesia suscipiuntur, vt elesta Christi organa. Illi vicifim præ-dicant quid pro illis Dominus gesserit, de quo heri abundè dictum est. Oremus.
units.tr: IIII. They are kindly received by the Church, as chosen instruments of Christ. In turn they preach what the Lord has done through them, about which enough was said yesterday. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXIIII.

units.la: 5 Sed (aiebant) quidam surrexe-runt è secta Pharisæorum, qui crediderunt, dicentes, oportere circumcidere eos, et præcipere vt obseruent legem Mosis.
units.tr: 5 But (they said) certain men rose up from the sect of the Pharisees, who had believed, saying that it was necessary to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses.

units.la: 6 Congregati sunt igitur Apostoli & Presbyteri, vt despicerent de hoc ne gotio.
units.tr: 6 The Apostles and the elders therefore gathered together to consider this matter.

units.la: 7 Quum autem multa disceptatio fuisset, surgens Petrus, dixit eis, Viri fratres, vos scitis, Deum iam pridem in ter nos elegisse me, vt per os meum audi rent gentes verbum Euangelij, & crederent.
units.tr: 7 When there had been much debate, Peter rose and said to them: Men and brethren, you know that God long ago chose among you that through my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the Gospel and believe.

units.la: 8 Et Deus, qui nouit corda, dedit ei testimonium, dato ipsis spiritu sancto, sicut & nobis.
units.tr: 8 And God, who knows the hearts, bore them witness by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us.

units.la: 9 Nihil dissreuit inter nos & illos, fide purgatis cordibus eorum.
units.tr: 9 He made no distinction between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith.

units.la: 10 Nunc ergo, quid tentatis Deum, imposito iugo cervici discipulorum, quod neque patres nostri, neque nos portare potuimus.
units.tr: 10 Now therefore, why do you tempt God by laying a yoke on the necks of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?

units.la: 11 Imo per gratiam Domini Iesu Christi credimus, & c. ad verf. 11.
units.tr: 11 But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we are saved, etc., to verse 11.

units.la: POstquam Euangelium Pauli & Barnabæ ministerio inter gentes propagatum, & hæ in Ecclesiam assumptæ fuerunt, grauis controuersia incidit, eò quòd aliqui gentes circumcidendas & ad legis observationem cogendas esse dicerent. Describitur controuersia hæc diligentissime, quod publicè omnium institutioni seruiat. A: Docet enim non nouum esse, si in rer eiusdem fidei professores lites oboriantur, nec quoquam offendi debere cum publico bono fiat, 1.Cor.11.&c. B. Docemur quid agendum. Fortiter contra quos uis veritas asseri debet. Et Apostoli consulendi, quos Christus nobis doctores dedit, Mar.16. Luc.10. Matth.28 Ioh.17. Sequitur quid coram Apostolis actum.
units.tr: After the Gospel had been spread among the Gentiles through the ministry of Paul and Barnabas, and these had been received into the Church, a serious controversy arose, because some said that the Gentiles must be circumcised and compelled to observe the law. This controversy is described very carefully, because it serves the instruction of all publicly. (A) For it teaches that it is no new thing for disputes to arise among professors of the same faith, and that no one should be offended when it happens for the public good (1 Cor. 11, etc.). (B) We are taught what must be done: the truth must be asserted boldly against those who oppose it; and the Apostles, whom Christ gave us as teachers, must be consulted (Mark 16; Luke 10; Matt. 28; John 17). What was done before the Apostles follows.

units.la: Disceptatio magna oritur. Qui ex Pharisæis crediderat, pertinaciter legis obseruationem vrgent. Habent id adhuc ex ve-
units.tr: A great dispute arises. Those who had believed from among the Pharisees insist stubbornly on the observance of the law. They still have this from the old leaven, as almost all monks do. Others oppose them with similar zeal, etc.

units.la: Disceptatio de iustificatione coram Apostolis. teri fermento,vt feré Monachi.Alij similí feruore se illis opponunt,&c. NOTA ¶. Quòd in sanctissimo coetu summus fidei articulus ita exagitatur, nec statim conuenì potest. Non mirum ergo,si eximij viri nonnunquâ ignorantia & pertinacia peccent. Ita enim Deus propriæ nos infirmitatis admonet,& ad humilitatem exercet, ne altum sapiamus,Rom.12.
units.tr: A dispute about justification before the Apostles. NOTE: that in so holy an assembly the highest article of faith is so vigorously debated, and cannot be settled at once. It is no wonder, then, that distinguished men sometimes err through ignorance and stubbornness. For God thus reminds us of our own weakness and trains us to humility, so that we do not think highly of ourselves (Rom. 12).

units.la: Porrò cùm incaluissent animi, tandem Petrus exurgit,qui hucusq; tacuerat modestè,ne cui præscribere videretur. Tuetur verò eorum sententiam,qui fidem solam sufficere docebant.Exempla duo pro sert,&c.
units.tr: Moreover, when minds had grown heated, at last Peter stood up, who until now had kept modestly silent, lest he seem to prescribe to anyone. He defends the opinion of those who taught that faith alone is sufficient. He brings forward two examples, etc.

units.la: I.Exeplo ipsiusDei docet,gentib.nec circúcisione nec alijs ceremonijs opé esse vbi crediderint. Allegat historiá,Act.10.11.Sed singula verba No.¶ 1. Ipsos testes citat,vt maior dictorum fides sit. Cùm Deus statuisset gentes vocare per me,non aliud decreuit, quàm vt audiret Euangelium & crederent. Ergo duo hæc ad iustificationem & salutem sufficiunt. Mar.16. ¶ 2. Deus qui corda nouit & respicit, nec vlla specie externa sibi imponi patitur, duo hæc suffi cere suo testimonio probauit. Nam Spiritum sanctum dedit illis perinde vt nobis.Actor.2.10. At his impuris & alienis à Deo non datur, sed Dei filijs, Ioh. 14. Roman. 8. &c.
units.tr: First, by the example of God himself he teaches that the Gentiles, when they have believed, have no need of circumcision or other ceremonies. He cites the history (Acts 10, 11). But note the individual words. (1) He cites the witnesses themselves, so that what is said may be more credible. Since God determined to call the Gentiles through me, he decided nothing other than that they should hear the Gospel and believe. Therefore these two things suffice for justification and salvation (Mark 16). (2) God, who knows and looks upon the hearts, and does not allow himself to be bound by any external appearance, has by his testimony proved that these two things suffice. For he gave them the Holy Spirit just as he gave it to us (Acts 2, 10). But this is not given to the impure and those alien from God, but to the sons of God (John 14; Rom. 8, etc.).

units.la: ¶ 3. Nihil inter illos & nos discreuit aliquo signo, cum fide illorum corda purificauisset. In Christo enim sublata maceria, Eph. 2. Huc pertinet locus Ro. 3. An Iudæorum Deus, &c.
units.tr: (3) He made no distinction between them and us by any sign, once he had purified their hearts by their faith. For in Christ the dividing wall has been broken down (Eph. 2). To this belongs the passage Rom. 3: "Is God the God of the Jews only?" etc.

units.la: Obserua: A. Corda purificatione opus habere. Impuri ergo sumus natura. Si enim fons pollutus, quales riui? Vide Ge. 8. Prou. 20. Iere. 17. Matth. 15. Sufficit hoc vnum ad euertendam operum iustitiam.
units.tr: Observe: (A) that hearts need to be purified. We are therefore impure by nature. For if the spring is polluted, what are the streams? See Gen. 8; Prov. 20; Jer. 17; Matt. 15. This one point is enough to overthrow the righteousness of works.

units.la: B. Purificationem fide fieri. Eò quòd hæc Christum apprehendit. Is à peccatis emundat sanguinis sui merito, 1. Ioh. 1. De inde carnis reliquias verbo (Ioh. 15.) & spiritu suo mortificat & tollit.
units.tr: (B) That purification is effected by faith, because faith lays hold of Christ. He cleanses us from sins by the merit of his blood (1 John 1). Then by his word (John 15) and his Spirit he mortifies and removes the remnants of the flesh.

units.la: C. Quòd Deus purificat fide. Ergo is fidei author est, Eph. 2. Ioh. 6. Matth. 11. Ira ad vnum Deum redit nostræ iustificationis gloria, Psal. 51. 32. Rom. 8. Mat. 9. &c.
units.tr: (C) That God purifies by faith. Therefore he is the author of faith (Eph. 2; John 6; Matt. 11). Thus the glory of our justification returns to the one God (Ps. 51, 32; Rom. 8; Matt. 9, etc.).

units.la: II. Exemplo patrum probat, omnem sa lutis rationem euerti, & laqueum iugum que intolerabile conscientijs imponi, si gentes ad legis obseruationem cogantur. Deum tentant, quicunq; sine verbo Dei impossibilia præsumunt, vel ab alijs exigunt: vel qui al js rationibus Dei voluntatem inquirunt, Psal. 78. Num. 11. At lex hu-
units.tr: (II) By the example of the fathers he proves that every way of salvation is overthrown, and an intolerable yoke and snare is laid on consciences, if the Gentiles are compelled to observe the law. They tempt God who presume on or demand of others what is impossible without the word of God, or who seek the will of God by other reasons (Ps. 78; Num. 11). But the law cannot be fulfilled by human strength, nor was it given so that we might obtain salvation by it.

units.la: manis viribus implerinon potest, nec i- deo data, vt per hanc salutem consequa- mur. Imo iugum est intolerabile, quod nec patres necnos ferre potuimus.Est e- nim spiritualis,& totum hominem requi- rit,Rom.7.Deut.6.10. Deinde male dictio ni subijcit,& ira operatur,Deut 27. Ro.7.
units.tr: Indeed, it is an intolerable yoke, which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear. For it is spiritual and requires the whole man (Rom. 7; Deut. 6, 10). Moreover, it subjects us to a curse and works wrath (Deut. 27; Rom. 7).

units.la: No T. 1. Quàm detestabilis illorum error sit,qui operibus homines iustificari docent. Opera enim nulla in Dei iudicio subsistunt, quàm quæ perfectè iuxta legē Dei fiunt. Ateiusmodi homo non habet, Ila.64. Deum ergo sti homines tentant, propriam iustitiam erigendo, Ro.10. &c. Adhęc iugum intolerabile imponunt con scientijs, quod ne sanctissimi quidem pos- tuerunt ferre. Horum enim voces sunt, Psal.51.130.143.1.Reg.8. Rom.7. Iure ergo contendimus.
units.tr: NOTE 1. How detestable is the error of those who teach that men are justified by works. For no works stand in God's judgment except those which are done perfectly according to the law of God. No such man exists (Isa. 64). Therefore men tempt God when they set up their own righteousness (Rom. 10, etc.). Moreover, they impose an intolerable yoke on consciences, which not even the holiest men were able to bear. For these are the voices of such men (Ps. 51, 130, 143; 1 Kings 8; Rom. 7). Rightly, then, we contend this.

units.la: 2. Cur ergo lex data? Vt paedagogus ef set ad Christum ducens,Gal.3. Ducit in peccati cognitionem, & docet salutem a- liunde quærendam,Rom.7. Christū item varie adumbrauit. Præterea docet, qui- bus operibus homines occupari debeant. Sed minimè iustificat.
units.tr: 2. Why then was the law given? That it might be a schoolmaster leading us to Christ (Gal. 3). It leads us into the knowledge of sin and teaches that salvation is to be sought elsewhere (Rom. 7). It also foreshadowed Christ in various ways. Besides, it teaches with what works men ought to be occupied. But it does not justify at all.

units.la: III. Conclusio: Vt Patres per gratiam Christi saluati sunt,&c. No T. 1. Vnam & eandem esse rationem salutis patribus veteris Testamenti & nobis. Ita conciliatur lex & Euangelium, & Iudaeorum offendiculo medetur Petrus, qui nefas putabant a patrum religione & fide discedere.
units.tr: (III) Conclusion: as the fathers were saved through the grace of Christ, etc. NOTE 1. That there is one and the same way of salvation for the fathers of the Old Testament and for us. Thus the law and the Gospel are reconciled, and Peter remedies the stumbling-block of the Jews, who thought it wicked to depart from the religion and faith of the fathers.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quae illa salutis ratio? A.Fudatur in gratia Christi, id est ea quam Christus nobis acquisiuit, patrem nobis reconcilians, 2.Cor.5.Mat.3.17 B.Fide percipitur. Ideo addit, Credimus, Hinc dogma, fide sola iustificari nos, &c. Rom.3.Gal.2. &c.
units.tr: 2. What is that way of salvation? (A) It is founded in the grace of Christ, that is, the grace which Christ acquired for us, reconciling the Father to us (2 Cor. 5; Matt. 3:17). (B) It is received by faith. Therefore he adds, "We believe." Hence the doctrine that we are justified by faith alone, etc. (Rom. 3; Gal. 2, etc.).

units.la: Conticuit tota multitudo, & audiuerunt Barnabam & Paulum, narrantes miracula, &c. Videntur hi ex Petri verbis occasio- nem petijsse, quibus fidem facere voluerunt. Estq; hoc Spiritus sancti euidens argumentum, quod mox cedunt veritati. In hoc minime conueniunt Concilia, quibus veritas oppugnatur, qualia iam seculis aliquot omnia papistica fuerunt.
units.tr: The whole multitude fell silent, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul, relating the miracles, etc. These two seem to have taken the occasion from Peter's words, by which they wished to make their testimony credible. And this is a clear argument of the Holy Spirit, that they soon yield to the truth. In this respect the councils, by which the truth is attacked, do not agree at all, such as nearly all the papistical ones have been for some centuries.

units.la: Interim vides, miraculorum hunc vsum esse, vt Euangelij doctrinae testimonium ferant, Mar.16.Peruertunt, qui his contra Euangelium abutuntur. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile you see that the use of miracles is this: that they bear witness to the doctrine of the Gospel (Mark 16). They pervert it who abuse them against the Gospel. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXV.
units.tr: HOMILY 125.

units.la: 13 Postquam autem conticuissent, respondit Iacobus, dicens, Viri fratres, audite me.
units.tr: 13 And after they had fallen silent, James answered, saying, "Men, brethren, hear me."

units.la: 14 Simeon exposuit, quando primùm Deus respexerit Gentes, vt sume ret ex ipsis populum nomini suo.
units.tr: 14 Simeon has explained when God first looked upon the Gentiles, to take from them a people for his name.

units.la: 15 Et huic rei consonant verba Prophetarum: sicut scriptum est.
units.tr: 15 And the words of the Prophets agree with this matter, as it is written:

units.la: 16 Posthæc reuertar, & restaurabo tabernaculum Dauid collapsum, & ruinas eius restaurabo, & rursus erigam illud.
units.tr: 16 "After this I will return, and will rebuild the fallen tabernacle of David, and I will rebuild its ruins, and I will raise it up again;

units.la: 17 Vt requirant reliqui homines Dominum, et omnes Gentes, super quas invocatum est nomen meum: dicit Dominus, qui facit hæc omnia.
units.tr: 17 so that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles over whom my name has been invoked, says the Lord, who does all these things."

units.la: 18 Nota sunt Deo ab omni ævo omnia opera sua.
units.tr: 18 All his works are known to God from eternity.

units.la: 19 Quamobrem ego censeo non esse obturbandos eos ex Gentibus, qui ad Deum convertuntur.
units.tr: 19 Therefore I judge that those from among the Gentiles who turn to God should not be troubled.

units.la: 20 Sed ad eos scribendum, vt abstineant pollutionibus idolorum, & scortatione, & suffocato, & sanguine.
units.tr: 20 But we should write to them that they abstain from the pollutions of idols, from fornication, from what is strangled, and from blood.

units.la: 21 Moses enim ab ætatibus antiquis in singulis civitatibus habet, qui ipsum prædicent, quum in synagogis per singula Sabbatha legatur.
units.tr: 21 For Moses has had in every city, from ancient times, those who preach him, since he is read in the synagogues every Sabbath.

units.la: Diluus Lucas controuersiam, quæ in primitiua Ecclesia circa iustificationis causam oborta fuit, diligenter describit. Vidimus nuper Petri Apostoli sentensententiam, qui fidem sufficere, nec legis iugo gentes grauan das esse docuit. Probauit. Exemplo Dei, qui hac ratione Cornelium saluarit. Legis conditione quae iugum sit intolerabile, nec a quoquam impleri possit, Rom. 7. 8. Patrum exemplo, qui & ipsi sola gratia salutem sint consecuti, vt patet, Psal. 130. 143. Isa. 64.
units.tr: Luke carefully describes the controversy that arose in the primitive Church concerning the cause of justification. We lately saw the judgement of the Apostle Peter, who taught that faith is sufficient and that the Gentiles should not be burdened with the yoke of the law. He proved it: by the example of God, who in this way saved Cornelius; by the condition of the law, which is an intolerable yoke and cannot be fulfilled by anyone (Rom. 7, 8); and by the example of the Fathers, who also obtained salvation by grace alone, as is evident (Ps. 130, 143; Isa. 64).

units.la: Sequitur Iacobi Apostoli sententia, qui Alphaei filius fuit. Constat duobus membris.
units.tr: Next comes the judgement of the Apostle James, who was the son of Alphaeus. It consists of two parts.

units.la: I. Petri sententiae subscribit, primo qui dem affirmans quod de Cornelij vocato ne ille dixerat. Deinde vero Prophetae oraculum allegat. NOTA. 1. Quod postquam conticuerunt alij, Iacobus demum loquitur, qui tamen inter columnas numeratur, Galat. 2. Hoc argumento patet, illos modestè omnia egisse, nec aliquem fuisse, qui alijs praescriberet temere. Initio Petrus tacet alijs disceptantibus. Tandem ipse etiam reliquis tacentibus sententiam dicit. Inde audiuntur Paulus & Barnabas. Nunc etiam solus loquitur Iacobus, &c. Spiritus ergo propheticus fuit, qui illorum mentes gubernauit, 1. Corint. 14.
units.tr: I. He subscribes to Peter's judgement: first, affirming what Peter had said about the calling of Cornelius; then, he cites the oracle of the Prophet. NOTE: (1) that after the others had fallen silent, James at last speaks, though he is numbered among the pillars (Gal. 2). This argument shows that they all acted modestly, and that there was no one who rashly prescribed to the others. At first Peter keeps silent while the others dispute; at last he himself states his opinion when the rest are silent. Then Paul and Barnabas are heard. Now James alone speaks, etc. Therefore it was a prophetic Spirit who governed their minds (1 Cor. 14).

units.la: Docemur modestiam seruare in actionibus publicis, ne quis solus omnibus præ {Cap. 15} scribat. Confer cum his Papistarum Concilia.
units.tr: We are taught to keep modesty in public actions, so that no one alone prescribes to all. Compare with this the councils of the Papists. {Chapter 15}

units.la: ¶ 2. Quòd non simpliciter sententiam dicit,sed illam scripturis confirmat. Nihil ergo pro imperio egerunt Apostoli, nec sibi permissum putárunt, Ecclesijs quicquam priuata authoritate obtrudere. Habuerunt enim præceptum Domini,quod vide Matth. 28. Ita Prophetæ etiam astrićti fuerunt,vt videre est,lere.1.Ezech.3.33. Arguitur his Pontificum impudentia,qui sibi quiduis statuendi ius esse dicunt. Minimè audiendi,Ioh.10.
units.tr: ¶ 2. He does not simply state his opinion, but confirms it from the Scriptures. The Apostles therefore did nothing by way of command, nor did they think it permitted to impose anything on the Churches by private authority. For they had the command of the Lord, which see at Matt. 28. Likewise the Prophets were bound, as may be seen in Jer. 1, Ezek. 3, 33. Here the impudence of the Papists is refuted, who say that they have the right to decree whatever they please. They are by no means to be heard (John 10).

units.la: ¶ 3.Testimonium Prophetæ, quod exat Amos 9. Prædixerat Iudæis excidium propter peccata. Sed quia sic collabi vide bantur promissiones de Mefsia, consolatur,& fe tabernaculum Dauidis,id est, regnum Christi reftituturū promittit.Tunc (inquit) reliquiæ Iudæorum (vbi nimirum refecti fuerint alij,iuxta Isa.10.1.) & omnes alij populi requirent Dominum, super quem invocatum est,&c. Expone locutionem ex Gen.48 Isa.4. Argumentum tale est. Deus tam Iudæos quàm Gentes suo nomine censeri vult: ergo vna eademq; vtriusque populi dignitas,&c.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The testimony of the Prophet, which is found in Amos 9. He had foretold to the Jews destruction because of their sins. But since the promises concerning the Messiah seemed to fall in ruins, he consoles them and promises that he will restore the tabernacle of David, that is, the kingdom of Christ. "Then," he says, "the remnant of the Jews (where indeed others have been restored, according to Isa. 10.1) and all other peoples will seek the Lord, over whom my name has been invoked," etc. Explain the expression from Gen. 48 and Isa. 4. The argument is this: God wishes both the Jews and the Gentiles to be named by his name; therefore the dignity of each people is one and the same, etc.

units.la: Interim obserua.A. Quòd dirutum Tabernaculum reædificare vult. Non igitur nostro excidio Dei promissiones interci-dunt, Rom. 5. Imo solet Deus ex ruinis ex citare Ecclesiam. Vide Matth. 5. B. Quod fit officium eorum, qui in Dei populo cen seri volunt? Requirant Dominum, Isa. 55. Amos 5. Fit hoc fide, quia spiritus est, Ioh. Vide item Matt. 24.
units.tr: Meanwhile observe: A. That he wishes to rebuild the ruined tabernacle. Therefore God's promises do not perish by our downfall (Rom. 5). Indeed God is accustomed to raise up the Church out of ruins. See Matt. 5. B. What is the duty of those who wish to be counted among God's people? They should seek the Lord (Isa. 55; Amos 5). This is done by faith, because it is spiritual (John ...). See also Matt. 24.

units.la: ¶ 4. Occurrit ijs, quibus nouum & insolens videbatur, gentes subito Iudæis æquari: Nota sunt Deo omnia opera sua. Non est ergo, quod illa accusemus. Nemo ergo Dei opera pro humani ingenij modulo metiri, sed religiose admirari & venerari debet, Rom. 11.
units.tr: ¶ 4. He meets those to whom it seemed new and strange that the Gentiles should suddenly be made equal to the Jews: "All his works are known to God." There is therefore no reason for us to find fault with them. No one should measure God's works by the measure of human understanding, but should religiously admire and revere them (Rom. 11).

units.la: II. Consulit quid ad concordiam fouen dam sibi vtilissimum videatur. Et quidem non vult obturbari gentes lege, tanquam necessaria ad salutem, interim illis frenum inijcit, ne abusu libertatis Iudæos offendant. Quatuor vero nominat, quorum duo per se illicita sunt, duo autem reliqua, media sunt & indifferentia, &c.
units.tr: II. He considers what seems most useful to himself for fostering concord. And indeed he does not wish the Gentiles to be troubled by the law as if it were necessary for salvation; meanwhile he puts a bridle on them, so that by abusing their liberty they do not offend the Jews. He names four things, of which two are unlawful in themselves, while the other two are indifferent and matters of choice, etc.

units.la: 1. Abstineant ab inquinamentis simulachrorum & scortatione. In duobus his maximè peccabant gentes. Putabant licitum inter esse gentilitijs sacris, vt patet 1. Cor. 8. Vocat ergo inquinamenta, vt se pollui sciant iuxta illud Deut. 7. De scortatione gentium historiæ & scripta testatur, quàm efrænis fuerit, &c.
units.tr: 1. They should abstain from the defilements of images and from fornication. The Gentiles sinned most of all in these two things. They thought it lawful to take part in pagan sacrifices, as is clear from 1 Cor. 8. He therefore calls them defilements, so that they know they are polluted, according to that passage in Deut. 7. The histories and writings of the Gentiles bear witness concerning fornication, how unbridled it was, etc.

units.la: In his autem Not. ¶Perpetuum hoc esse præceptum, vt Christiani sese Christo puros seruet per omnia. In religione, ne alienis sacris communicent. Quia totos nos sibi vendicat Deus. Deut.6. Vide 1.Reg.18.1. Cor.10. In vitæ conuersatione corpora sua Deo consecrent, cuius templa sunt, 1.Cor.6.1. Thess.4. Turpiter falluntur, qui scortationem licitam putant. Vide Deut.22; 22. Heb 13. &c.
units.tr: In these matters note: this is a perpetual precept, that Christians keep themselves pure for Christ in all things. In religion, they should not join in alien rites, because God claims us wholly for himself (Deut. 6; see 1 Kings 18; 1 Cor. 10). In the conduct of life they should consecrate their bodies to God, whose temples they are (1 Cor. 6; 1 Thess. 4). Those who think fornication lawful are shamefully deceived. See Deut. 22, 22; Heb. 13, etc.

units.la: II. Abstineant à sanguine & suffocato.
units.tr: II. They are to abstain from blood and from what is strangled.

units.la: Fuit de his antiquissima lex, toti mundo præscripta, Gen.9. Repetita Leu. 19 & 17. Allegoria prohibebat violentiam, oppressionem & sanguinis studium. Licet verò hanc cum reliquis cæremoniis abrogauit set Christus, quia tamen gentium libertate offendebantur lucæ, vult hoc charitati dari Iacobus, ne licentius libertate sua gentes abutantur. Vide expositionem Pauli, Rom.14.1. Cor.9.
units.tr: There was an ancient law concerning these things, prescribed for the whole world, in Genesis 9, and repeated in Leviticus 17 and 19. Its figurative meaning forbade violence, oppression and the pursuit of blood. Although Christ abrogated it along with the other ceremonies, James nevertheless wishes this to be granted to charity, because the Gentile liberty offended the Jews; so that the Gentiles might not abuse their freedom too recklessly. See Paul's exposition, Romans 14 and 1 Corinthians 8 and 9.

units.la: NOTA.¶Non patrocinari ijs hunc lo-cum, qui tra ditionibus suis conscientias grauant. Contra hos dicta sunt, quæ habentur Matt.15. Col.2. Act.10. Rom.14. Interim in externis his prima semper charitatis ratio habeti debet.
units.tr: NOTE. This passage does not lend support to those who burden consciences with their own traditions. Against such people are the words found in Matthew 15, Colossians 2, Acts 10 and Romans 14. Meanwhile, in these external matters the first consideration must always be the regard for charity.

units.la: Rationem subijcit, qua docet fieri non posse, vt aliter concilientur duo isti populi. li, cum Moses passim antiquo more legatur, & magna sit eius authoritas. Dandum ergo hoc tempori.
units.tr: He gives a reason, by which he teaches that these two peoples cannot otherwise be reconciled: namely, because Moses is read everywhere according to the ancient custom, and his authority is great. This time must therefore be granted.

units.la: Interim obserua veterem hunc morem esse, vt populus Dei sese diebus festis legis & Scripturæ sacræ studio exerceat. Teneamus ergo hûc nos quoq; &c. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile, observe that this was the ancient custom of the people of God, that on festival days they occupied themselves with the study of the law and of Holy Scripture. Let us therefore hold to this ourselves too, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXVI.

units.la: 22 Tunc visum est Apostolis & senioribus cum tota Ecclesia, delectos ex sese viros mittere Antiochiam cum Paulo & Barnaba: nempe Iudam qui cognominatur Barsabas, & Silam viros primarios inter fratres.
units.tr: 22 Then it seemed good to the apostles and elders, with the whole Church, to send chosen men from among themselves to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: namely Judas, who was surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, leading men among the brethren.

units.la: 23 Et ista per manus eorum mittenda scribere, Apostoli et presbyteri & fratres: ijs qui sunt Antiochiæ & in Syria, & in Cilicia fratribus qui sunt ex Gentibus, salutem.
units.tr: 23 They wrote these things to be carried by their hands: The apostles, the elders and the brethren, to the brethren who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia: greeting.

units.la: 24 Quoniam quosdam è vobis egressos audiuimus vos turbasse, verbis labefactantes animas vestras, iubentes vos circumcidi, & seruare legem, quibus hoc non præceperamus.
units.tr: 24 Since we have heard that certain of you who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, telling you to be circumcised and to keep the law, to whom we gave no such command.

units.la: 25 Visum est nobis concorditer conuenientibus electos viros mittere ad vos cum dilectis nostris Barnaba & Paulo.
units.tr: 25 It seemed good to us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul.

units.la: 26 Hominibus qui exposuerunt animas suas pro nomine Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: 26 Men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: 27 Misimus ergo Iudam et Silam, qui et ipsi vobis, et c.ad verf.30.
units.tr: 27 We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who themselves also shall tell you the same things by word of mouth, etc., to verse 30.

units.la: Oboniam Christo omnis potestas data est, regnum suum non modo defendit & seruat, sed ita moderatur omnia, vt quae contra hoc satan molitur, ad illius propagationem faciant. Exemplum huius praesens historia exhibet. Voluit satan intestinis dissensionibus Ecclesiam scindere, & per has suspectam reddere omne Euangelij doctrinam, &c. Sed adeo nihil proficit, vt potius hac occasione illustretur veritas, & vnanimi consensu iustitia fidei afferatur contra Pharisaeos. Vidimus id in Petri, Pauli & Barnabae, demum etiam Iacobi orationibus. Sequitur exitus totius negotij.
units.tr: Since all power has been given to Christ, he not only defends and preserves his kingdom but so governs all things that whatever Satan plots against it serves to advance it. The present history provides an example of this. Satan wanted to split the Church with internal dissensions and through them make the whole doctrine of the Gospel suspect, etc. But he achieves so little that rather, on this occasion, the truth is made clearer, and by unanimous agreement the justification of faith is asserted against the Pharisees. We have seen this in the speeches of Peter, Paul and Barnabas, and finally also of James. The outcome of the whole affair follows.

units.la: Consentit tota Ecclesia, nec aliquis restat, qui vel ambitionis vel vano contendendi studio veritati contradicat. Consensus hic nos hodie moueat. Decernunt itaq; legationem & literas mittere Antiochiam, &c. Prudentiae hoc est, quia nouerant Paulum & Barnabam suspectos esse, & ne nouis calumnijs peterentur, quasi malis artibus literas has emendicassent.
units.tr: The whole Church agrees, and no one remains who contradicts the truth out of ambition or from a vain zeal for contention. Let this agreement move us today. They therefore decide to send a delegation and letters to Antioch, etc. This was prudence, because they knew that Paul and Barnabas were under suspicion, and lest they be attacked with new slanders, as if they had obtained these letters by bad arts.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Ordinem obseruatum in veteri Ecclesia. Apostoli nihil pro imperio vel priuata authoritate egerunt: sed in publicis causis populum totum adhibuerunt, ne dominium affectare viderentur. 1.Pet.5. Rursum populus veritati cedit, nec quicquam geritur tumultuose. Idem vidimus, Act.1.6.13. Ordinem hunc, tyrannis Pontificiorum euertit, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note the order observed in the ancient Church. The apostles did nothing by command or private authority, but in public matters they brought in the whole people, so that they would not seem to be claiming lordship. 1 Pet. 5. Again, the people yield to the truth, and nothing is done tumultuously. We saw the same in Acts 1:6, 13. This order the tyranny of the Papists has overturned, etc.

units.la: Sed literas Synodales videamus, breues in re maxima & simplices. Quia veritas verborum fuco non opus habet.
units.tr: But let us look at the synodal letter, brief and plain in a most important matter, because the truth has no need of the paint of words.

units.la: Partes totius Epistolae ferè sunt tres aut quatuor.
units.tr: The parts of the whole letter are roughly three or four.

units.la: I. Inscriptio authores notat & eos, ad quos scribitur. Nihil ambitiosum hic, sed ordo tamen seruatur. Primus locus Apostolis tribuitur, idq; propter officium & dignitatem à Christo concessam, Matt.5. 19.28. Deinde Seniores nominantur. Inde tota Ecclesia.
units.tr: I. The address indicates the authors and those to whom it is written. Nothing ambitious here, yet the order is kept. The first place is given to the apostles, and that on account of the office and dignity granted by Christ, Matt. 5:19; 19:28. Then the elders are named. Then the whole Church.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Quòd fratres se inuicem vocant. Fuit hoc vetustissimum nomen inter Christianos. Sic dicti partim Christi re spectu, qui pro fratribus agnoscit in se credentes, Psal.22 Mat.28. Heb.2. partim nostri respectu, quia vnus omnium pater, vna & eadem omnium hereditas, Rom.8. 4.Mat.6.
units.tr: NOTE. That they call one another brethren. This was the most ancient name among Christians. They were so called partly with respect to Christ, who acknowledges as brethren those who believe in him, Ps. 22; Matt. 28; Heb. 2; partly with respect to ourselves, because there is one Father of all, one and the same inheritance for all, Rom. 8; 4 Matt. 6.

units.la: Seruit hoc cófolationi in adserfis,quia Christus fratres non deferet.Deinde infti-tutioni ad concordiam Vide Eph.4 Nul-lum nationis discrimen,Gal.3.Col.3.Vide præsentem inscriptionem.
units.tr: This serves for comfort in adversity, because Christ will not desert his brethren. Then for instruction toward concord. See Eph. 4. No distinction of nation: Gal. 3; Col. 3. See the present address.

units.la: II. Impostores perstringunt egregiè & diligenter. I. Egressi ex nobis, sed nos nihil tale mandauimus. Opponunt hoc vanisi-mæ illorum gloriationi. Et ita veritati patrocinantur,vt nec sibijpsis parcant.
units.tr: II. They sharply and carefully expose the impostors. 1. They went out from us, but we commanded nothing of the sort. They set this against their most vain boasting, and so they defend the truth in such a way that they spare not even themselves.

units.la: Nota. Ex ipsa Ecclesia ferè prodire seductores,1.Ioh.2.Act 20.Mat.8 2 Thess. 2.Non sufficit ergo posse titulos iactare & successionem.
units.tr: Note. Seducers almost always come forth from the Church itself: 1 John 2; Acts 20; Matt. 8; 2 Thess. 2. It is not enough, therefore, to be able to boast of titles and succession.

units.la: II. Turbârunt vos verbis & labefactâ-runt,&c.Huc videtur Paulus respicere ad Gal 1.&c.
units.tr: 2. They troubled you with words and unsettled you, etc. Paul seems to refer here to Gal. 1, etc.

units.la: Interim Nota. Effectum falsæ doctrinæ, quæ non vno Christo omnia tribuit.Primò turbat & salutis incertos reddit, dum omnem fidem euertit, Rom.4. Gal.3.Ioh.4.Deinde etiam externas turbas mouet,dum scismata serit,1.Corint.1. 3.Vtrumq; in papatu expe rti.
units.tr: Meanwhile note the effect of false doctrine, which does not attribute all things to Christ alone. First, it disturbs and makes men uncertain of salvation, while it overturns all faith: Rom. 4; Gal. 3; John 4. Then it also stirs up external tumults, while it sows schisms: 1 Cor. 1; 3. We have experienced both in the papacy.

units.la: III. Quibus nihil mandauimus. Nihil ergo Apostolis commune cum illis, qui operibus iustificationem tribuunt,&c.
units.tr: III. To whom we gave no command. Therefore the apostles have nothing in common with those who ascribe justification to works, etc.

units.la: Not.Mendaces esse omnes,qui Apostolicam authoritatem suis traditionibus præteprætexunt, Mat.15. Isa.29. Quotquot itEm legati à latere, diuersa ab Apostolis docent.
units.tr: Note. All those are liars who cover up their own traditions with apostolic authority: Matt. 15; Isa. 29. Whoever are legates a latere teach things different from the apostles.

units.la: III. Paulus & Barnabas laudantur, quibus impostores omnem authoritatē adimebant, Gal.1. & 2. Notandum. {1} Asseri debere famam benè meritorum. Ita Christus laudat Ioh.Bapt. Matth.11. Apostolos aliquos præ aliis ornat, Mar.3. Matt.16. Paulus Titum & Lucam & Epipha. celebrat, 2.Cor.9. Phil 2. Inprimis hoc in Rebus publicis obseruandum, &c.
units.tr: III. Paul and Barnabas are praised, whom the impostors stripped of all authority: Gal. 1 and 2. Note: {1} that the fame of those who have deserved well ought to be asserted. So Christ praises John the Baptist: Matt. 11. He honours some apostles above others: Mark 3; Matt. 16. Paul commends Titus and Luke and Epaphroditus: 2 Cor. 8; Phil. 2. Especially this must be observed in public affairs, etc.

units.la: {2} Quæ vera ministri laus sit: Animam ponere pro nomine Christi, nimirum vbi necessitas exigit. Alioqui non vult temerarios & vitæ prodigos Christus, vt patet Matth.10. Sed animi promptitudo & voluntas parata exigitur, qualis in Paulo cernitur, Act 20. & 21. Phil 1. Interim idem omnium Christianorum est, Mar.8. Luc.14.
units.tr: {2} What is the true praise of a minister: to lay down his life for the name of Christ, certainly where necessity demands it. Otherwise Christ does not want rash men who waste their lives, as is clear from Matt. 10. But readiness of mind and a prepared will are required, such as is seen in Paul: Acts 20 and 21; Phil. 1. Meanwhile this is the same for all Christians: Mark 8; Luke 14.

units.la: IV. Decretum synodi exponunt, in quo repetuntur & connectuntur Petri & Iacobi sententiæ. Sed singulas partes NOTA {1} Authorem: Visum est spiritu S. & nobis. Se adiunguntur vt seruos, per quos spiritus suam sententiam declarârit. Sic populus Mosi credidisse dicitur, Exo.14. Eodem sensu dicitur: Qui vos audit, &c. Luc.10. Vere autem hoc ab Apostolis di-
units.tr: IV. They explain the decree of the synod, in which the opinions of Peter and James are repeated and connected. But note the parts one by one. {1} The author: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us. They join themselves as servants, through whom the Spirit declared his judgment. So the people are said to have believed Moses, Exod. 14. In the same sense it is said: He who hears you, etc., Luke 10. Indeed that this was said by the apostles

units.la: dici,omnis scriptura probat,&c. Sine spiritu S. nulla Conciliorum authoritas.
units.tr: is proved by all Scripture, etc. Without the Holy Spirit there is no authority of councils.

units.la: § 2. Ipsum decretum. Ne quid oneris imponeremus quàm necessariahæc, &c. Mar. 7. Apoc. 2. Quoad scortationem, necesse est ut per se caueatur, 1. Cor. 6. Heb. 13. Quoad reliqua, necessaria dicuntur per accidens, & eius seculi ratione: quia charitas monet, ne offendamus quenquam, Ro. 14. 1. Cor. 8.
units.tr: § 2. The decree itself. That we should not lay upon you any burden beyond these necessary things, etc. Mark 7; Rev. 2. As for fornication, it must be avoided of necessity in itself: 1 Cor. 6; Heb. 13. As for the rest, they are called necessary by accident, and in view of that age: because charity warns us not to offend anyone, Rom. 14; 1 Cor. 8.

units.la: Arguuntur Papistæ, qui absolutam necessitatem statuunt observandi ipsorum decreta. At si hic huius locifenfus, quomo do conueniet cum 1. Cor. 10. Matth. 19. 1. Tim. 4. &c.
units.tr: The Papists are refuted, who lay down an absolute necessity of observing their decrees. But if this is the sense of this passage, how will it agree with 1 Cor. 10; Matt. 19; 1 Tim. 4, etc.?

units.la: § 3. Fructum & vtilitatem adijciunt, Benefacietis, & cedet in bonum. Quia sic & vosipsos impollutos seruabitis, & nemini eritis offendiculo. Nulli anathematismi.
units.tr: § 3. They add the fruit and usefulness: You will do well, and it will turn to good. Because thus you will also keep yourselves undefiled and will be a stumbling block to no one. No anathemas.

units.la: Hic scopus omnib. nobis propositus esse debet, 1. Cor. 10. Phil. 1. Mat. 18. Oremus.
units.tr: This aim ought to be set before all of us: 1 Cor. 10; Phil. 1; Matt. 18. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY 127.

units.la: 30 Illi ergo dimissi, venerunt Antiochiam, & coacta multitudine, reddiderunt Epistolam.
units.tr: 30 So they were sent off, came down to Antioch, gathered the multitude together, and delivered the letter.

units.la: 31 Quam cum legissent, gauisi sunt super exhortatione,
units.tr: 31 When they had read it, they rejoiced at the encouragement it gave.

units.la: 32 Iudas quoq; & Silas, quum essent sent et ipsi Prophetæ, multo sermone ad hortati sunt fratres, et confirmarunt:
units.tr: 32 Judas also and Silas, since they were themselves prophets, encouraged the brothers with many words and strengthened them.

units.la: 33 Et cum egissent illic aliquanto diu emisisfunt, etc. ad ver. 35.
units.tr: 33 And when they had spent some time there, they were sent away in peace (etc.) to verse 35.

units.la: EXposuit Lucas, vt primitiua Ecclesia controuersiam de iustificatione fidei & operum publici & Apostolici Concilij authoritate composuerit. Quo exemplo docemur, quibus rationibus omnes controuersiæ in Ecclesia componi & veritas inuestigari debeat. 1. Positis affectibus omnes vnius veritatis studium & pacem in Christo sibi proponant. 2. Patienter fe inuicem audiant, ne quis sibi ius omne vendicet. Alioqui qui cotentiofiores sunt queruntur. 3. Scripturæ audiantur, & ex illis dicantur sententiæ, Ioh. 5. Hunc ordinem hic obseruatum fuisse vidimus. Quia vero dictum fuit, legatos destinatos fuisse cum literis, qui Ecclesijs hæc renuntiarent, & passim curarent obseruari, pergit Lucas, & vt hi suum officium fecerint docet, quæque fuerit Concilij totius executio.
units.tr: Luke sets out how the primitive Church settled the controversy about justification by faith and by works, by the authority of a public apostolic council. From this example we are taught by what means all controversies ought to be settled in the Church and the truth sought out. (1) With their feelings set aside, let all men keep before themselves the pursuit of the one truth and peace in Christ. (2) Let them hear one another patiently, so that no one claims every right for himself; otherwise the more contentious are the ones who complain. (3) Let the Scriptures be heard, and opinions be drawn from them, John 5. We have seen this order observed here. Because it was said that envoys were sent with letters to report these things to the churches and to see that they were observed everywhere, Luke goes on to show that these men did their duty, and what the full execution of the council's decision was.

units.la: Vbi Notª Non sufficere, si quid bene statuatur nisi suam habeat executionem, & ratum maneat. Prius hoc omnes ferè possunt, in posteriori autem elucet homi-
units.tr: Here note: it is not enough for something to be well decided unless it has its own execution and remains in force. Almost anyone can do the first; but the diligence of men and their welfare rest on the second.

units.la: num industria & salus consistit. Est hoc vi dere in œconomia In Repub.vbi fine exe cutione leges & iura non prosunt. Hinc nomophyl. ephori censores. Qui quàm necessarij sint, nostro exemplo discimus. Sic in Ecclesia. Ideo isti legatos ordinâ-runt executores, & illis adhibuerunt te-stes.
units.tr: This can be seen in the government of the commonwealth, where laws and rights are of no use without execution. Hence the nomophylakes [νομοφύλακες], the ephors, and the censors. We learn from our example how necessary these are. So it is in the Church. Therefore these men appointed envoys as executors and brought in witnesses for them.

units.la: Vbi simul obseruemus,quàm alieni sint ab Apostolorum moribus,qui fuorü Con ciliorum executores faciunt Reges, quos ferro & igne armant.
units.tr: Here we should also observe how far removed from the manners of the apostles are those who make kings the executors of their councils, and arm them with iron and fire.

units.la: At videamus in præsenti, quid isti fecerint.
units.tr: But let us see now what these men did.

units.la: I. Dicuntur venisse Antioch.neque aliacuius rei interea fit mentio. Ergò recta illuc cótenderunt omnibus alijs rebus post habitis. Est hoc fidelis industriæ argumentum. Qui lua quærunt,nec publica cura tanguntur, initiò moras nectunt, deinde ad quamuis occasionem subsistunt, aut alio deflectunt. Ita Respub & Ecclesiæ inanibus impensis grauantur. Aliter hi, quos imitari debent, quicunque publicas causas agunt.
units.tr: I. They are said to have come to Antioch, and meanwhile no other matter is mentioned. So they made straight for it, setting aside all other concerns. This is a sign of faithful diligence. Those who seek their own interests and are not moved by public concern first put off the journey, then stop for any pretext, or turn aside elsewhere. So commonwealths and churches are burdened with empty expenses. It is otherwise with those whom they ought to imitate, all who conduct public business.

units.la: II. Congregant totam Ecclesiam, exhibent literas, quæ mox coram omnibus recitantur. Non ergo agunt cum pauculis & delectis. Pertinebat enim causa hæc ad totam tam Ecclesiam, & literæ omnibus erant in scriptæ.
units.tr: II. They gather the whole Church and present the letters, which are at once read aloud before everyone. So they did not deal with a few select people, for this matter concerned the whole Church, and the letters were addressed to everyone.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Morem veteris Ecclesiæ, quæ publicè tractauit ea, quæ ex æquo ad omnes pertinebant. Requirit hoc publica salus, & vnitatis Ecclesiasticæ ratio. Aliter postea Episcopi laruati, qui pro suo arbitrio (contra illud 1. Pet. 5.) proponut quæ volut, reliqua celant. Imò laicos à scriptu rarum lectione violenter arcent. Pugnat hoc cum Dei instituto, qui, quæcunque scripta sunt, omnibus communia vult esse. Promissiones. Historia liberationis Ægyptia ¢, Exo. 13. Legis promulgatio, Exo. 19. &c. Prophetæ, Ier. 1. Imò vulgari lingua olim vsus est, & sic in nouo testamento voluit fieri. Ptolomæus Philad. Act 1. 1. Cor. 14. Et constat, sacros libros in omnium manibus fuisse. Vide orationem Iacobi & Berrh. Act. 16. Item 2. Tim. 3. Obijciunt, Errores hinc enasci & scismata. R. Imò ex scripturæ ignorantia. Ideo interpretes sint, & faciant ipsi officium.
units.tr: NOTE: This was the custom of the ancient Church, which dealt publicly with those things that pertained equally to all. Public welfare and the principle of ecclesiastical unity require this. Later, masked bishops, who (contrary to 1 Peter 5) propose whatever they wish according to their own judgment, hid the rest. Indeed they violently keep laymen away from reading the Scriptures. This conflicts with God's institution, who wills that whatever has been written should be common to all. See the promises, the history of the liberation from Egypt, Exodus 13; the promulgation of the law, Exodus 19, etc.; the prophets, Jeremiah 1. Indeed the people once used the vernacular, and so in the New Testament it was meant to be done. Ptolemy Philadelphus; Acts 1; 1 Corinthians 14. And it is clear that the holy books were in the hands of all. See James's speech and Berrhoea, Acts 16; likewise 2 Timothy 3. They object that errors and schisms arise from this. Answer: rather they arise from ignorance of Scripture. Therefore let them be interpreters and do the work themselves.

units.la: III. Excipiunt Iudas & Silas: & quia Prophetæ erant, proponunt quod ipsis erat mandatum, hortanturque & confirmant, &c.
units.tr: III. Judas and Silas then take up the matter. Because they were prophets, they set out what had been entrusted to them, and they exhort and confirm the brethren, etc.

units.la: NOTA ¶ Ecclesiam assiduis hortationibus opus habere, Antiochena Eccle-
units.tr: NOTE: The Church has constant need of frequent exhortations. The Church of Antioch

units.la: sia doctores & dona habuit Act.13.Tamen bos quoque audit, & quidem diutius secum manentes.Nulla æmulatio.Arguuntur. A. Qui doctrinam & hortationes putant superuacaneas esse. Ratio, quia omnia satis norint,&c.At seipsos ignorant,neque respiciunt exempla sanctorum, Psal. 25.119.1.Apostolos.Timotheum, 2.Tim.3. 1.Tim.4. B. Qui indigne ferunt peregrinos monitores. At non obseruant, quisquis quid doceat. Et quia singulorum est, publica salutis causam tueri, imprimis ad ministros hæc cura pertinet. Vt verbum vbiq; feruetur,& fructum ferat.Vide Paulum,2.Cor.11. Idem magistratum quoque decet. Constantinus.
units.tr: had teachers and gifts (Acts 13). Yet it listened to these men too, and indeed they stayed with them for a considerable time. There was no rivalry. Those are refuted (A) who think doctrine and exhortations superfluous, on the ground that people already know everything. But they do not know themselves, and they do not look to the examples of the saints: Ps. 25; Ps. 119; the Apostles; Timothy (2 Tim. 3; 1 Tim. 4). (B) Those who take it badly when outside admonishers come. But they do not consider who it is that teaches what. Since it is the business of individuals to defend the public cause of salvation, this care belongs especially to the ministers, so that the word is kept everywhere and bears fruit. See Paul, 2 Cor. 11. The magistrate too ought to be concerned with this. Constantine.

units.la: IV.Quid Ecclesia.1.Gaudent omnes.Fuerunt ergo amanter,& honorifice excepti. Prius turbati fuerunt,quod de præcipuo Capite conuerteretur: pax scissa effet, Apostoli duo pessimè tractarentur. Gaudent ergo patefacta veritate ob pacem & Apostolos suos liberatos.
units.tr: IV. What the Church did. 1. All rejoice. They were therefore received lovingly and honourably. Before, they had been troubled, because the matter concerned the chief article and the peace was torn apart, and two apostles were being treated very badly. So now, with the truth revealed, they rejoice over the peace and over the liberation of their apostles.

units.la: No t. Quomodo pij afficiantur ergaveritatis doctrinam & doctores. Vide Galatas & Theffalon.Arguuntur, qui tur bis gaudent, ministros laniant,&c.
units.tr: NOTE: How the godly are affected towards the doctrine of truth and its teachers. See Galatians and Thessalonians. Those are rebuked who rejoice in tumults and tear the ministers to pieces, etc.

units.la: II. Dimittunt in pace,&c.Finis ergo concionis fuit pax publica Ecclesiarum. Etsi enim perexerint aliqui,tamen plerique in his acquieuerunt.
units.tr: II. They dismiss them in peace, etc. The end of the sermon, then, was public peace among the churches. For even if some went on, most of them rested content with this.

units.la: NOT.¶ Quo argumento discamus,Concilia in spiritu sancto conuenisse? Si similem habeant exitum. Confer cum his pastica ab annis 800. videbis omnia turbas dedisse.Anno 730.Concilia habita propter imagines. Secutu scisma Orient. & Occident.quod Turcis via aperuit.Anno 1051 Concilium contra Berengarium.Finis Cruciatae & persecutio publica.An. 1095. Claromont. Secutu bellu sacrum. Heinrichi. IIII.Historia. Anno 1416..Bella Bohemica.Basilien.1431.Armeniaci.Trident. 1546.bellum Germanicu. Si praefens hoc felicius cedat,principes in causa erunt, & orandus eritDominus,vt omnium corda ad pacem inclinet.
units.tr: NOTE: By what argument shall we learn that councils have met in the Holy Spirit? If they have a similar outcome. Compare with these things the events of the eight hundred years since: you will see that everything caused disturbances. In 730 councils were held concerning images, followed by the schism of East and West, which opened the way for the Turks. In 1051 a council against Berengarius. The end of the crusade and public persecution. In 1095 Clermont, followed by the holy war. The history of Henry IV. In 1416 the Bohemian wars. Basel 1431. The Armenians. Trent 1546. The German war. If the present council turns out more happily, the princes will be responsible for it, and the Lord must be prayed to, that He may incline the hearts of all to peace.

units.la: V.Syla cum posset redire ad suos,mansit, partim ob Pauli consortium, partim quod Ecclesiam videret sua opera adhuc egere. Semper ergo maior habenda ratio Ecclesiae quam nostrarum rerum. Oremus.
units.tr: V. Silas, though he could have returned to his own people, stayed, partly because of his companionship with Paul, and partly because he saw that the Church still needed his work. So the regard due to the Church must always be greater than regard for our own affairs. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXVIII
units.tr: HOMILY CXXVIII

units.la: 35 Paulus autem & Barnabas quoque egerunt Antiochiae,docentes et euangelizantes cum aliis etiam multis sermonem Domini.
units.tr: Paul and Barnabas also remained at Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord together with many others.

units.la: 36 Post aliquot autem dies, dixit Barnabæ Paulus, Reuerti insuper fratres nostros per omnes ciuitates, in quibus annuntiauimus sermonem Domini cognituri, quomodo habeant.
units.tr: After some days Paul said to Barnabas: "Let us go back and visit our brothers in every city where we have proclaimed the word of the Lord, to learn how they are doing."

units.la: 37 Barnabas autem consuluit, vt assumerent secum Iohannem, qui vocabatur Marcus.
units.tr: Barnabas advised that they take with them John, who was called Mark.

units.la: 38 Paulus autem censebat eum non assumere, qui abscesserat ab ipsis ex Pamphylia, nec eorum comes in illo opere fuisset, &c. vsque ad versum 24.
units.tr: Paul, however, thought that he should not be taken, since he had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them in that work, and so on down to verse 24.

units.la: SPiritus sanctus non modò felices Euangelij in primatiua Ecclesia progressus describit, verumetiam contentiones & scandala quæ satan excitauit, partim ne similibus offendamur, partim vt discamus, quomodo ea amoueri possint, & quid nos tunc deceat. Facit huc imprimis hoc Cap. cuius prima pars publicum dissidium in doctrina & fidei negotio obortum continet, quod Concilij authoritate fuit compositum. Didicimus, quæ optima componendorum difficilium ratio. Secunda parte narratur, quid fecerint pij dum stores pace iam restituta. Vbi rursus conincidit Barnabæ & Pauli. &c. Discemus, quàm diligenti cura opus sit, & quid sin-
units.tr: The Holy Spirit describes not only the happy progress of the gospel in the primitive Church, but also the contentions and scandals that Satan stirred up, partly so that we may not be offended by similar things, and partly so that we may learn how they can be removed and what is then fitting for us. This chapter bears especially on the matter: its first part contains the public dissension that arose over doctrine and the affairs of faith, which was settled by the authority of the Council. We have learned what is the best method of settling difficult matters. The second part relates what the godly did once peace had been restored, where again Barnabas and Paul are in agreement. We shall learn with how diligent a care it is necessary to act, and what each one ought to do

units.la: gglos gulos deceat facere inter doctorū dissidia
units.tr: amid the dissensions of teachers.

units.la: I. De Syla dictum. Nunc additur, Paulum & Barnabam quoq; mansisse, docuisse atque Euangelizasse cum multis aliis Ergo non securi fuerunt parta victoria, neque superbè insultārunt aduersarijs, qui causa ceciderant, vt Constantinus, PP. qui MO nothelitis damnatis patrum imagines in porticu Sancti Petri pingi voluit. Est hoc argumentum modestiæ, & quod veritate contenti, in reliquis cōcordiæ studuerūt.
units.tr: I. We have spoken of Silas. Now it is added that Paul and Barnabas also remained, taught, and preached the gospel with many others. Therefore they were not careless about the victory won, nor did they proudly insult their adversaries who had fallen in the cause, as Constantine the pope did, who, after the Monothelites had been condemned, wanted the images of the fathers painted in the portico of St Peter's. This is an argument of modesty: content with the truth, they strove for concord in other matters.

units.la: Sed NOT. ¶ Quid in Ecclesia præcipuè fieri debeat? Apostoli toto hoc libro non circa ceremonias occupantur, sed vbique docent, & quidem Euangeliū. Hoc enim sibi iniunctum sciebant, Mar.16. 1. Cor.1. Idem hoc salutis nuntium esse nouerant, quo mundus hic debellatur, & Christo subijcitur, 2.Cor.10. Rom.10. Habebant Christi exemplum, qui nihil fecit frequen tius, Mar.1. Luc.4. Typum veterem, Exo-di 28.
units.tr: But note: what ought chiefly to be done in the Church? Throughout this whole book the apostles are not occupied with ceremonies, but everywhere teach, and indeed teach the gospel. For they knew this was enjoined on them (Mark 16; 1 Cor. 1). They knew this to be the message of salvation by which this world is subdued and made subject to Christ (2 Cor. 10; Rom. 10). They had the example of Christ, who did nothing more often (Mark 1; Luke 4). The old type: Exod. 28.

units.la: Arguuntur his Episcopi, qui aut inuti les ceremonias inuehunt, aut nouis tradi-tionibus Ecclesias grauant. Imprimis, qui à nulla re magis quàm a docendi officio abhorrent, & libentius canes, equos, &c. quàm oues Christi pa scunt. Ita verbum incontemptum adducunt.
units.tr: These words are an argument against bishops who either introduce useless ceremonies or burden the churches with new traditions. Above all, they shrink from nothing so much as the duty of teaching, and they more willingly feed dogs, horses, and so on, than Christ's sheep. Thus they bring the word into contempt.

units.la: II. Paulus de Ecclesijs antea collectis consilium init', & de hoc Barnabam quoque admonet. Sic Act.14. Magni zeli argumentum, quod labores nouos quaerit, 2. Cor.12. Non sufficere, vt Christo adducantur aliqui, &c, Ecclesiae bene constituantur, sed curandum, vt quae bene constituta sunt seruentur. Opus hoc propter diaboli insidias, Matth.12.1.Pet.5. Deinde propter ouium stoliditatem, cuius hodie exempla multa videmus, &c. Hic ergo boni patres familias imitandi & imperatores. Maximè fi hirci sint aliqui. Arguuntur ignaui pastores, Imprimis diffipatores Ecclesiarum.
units.tr: II. Paul takes counsel about the churches gathered earlier, and admonishes Barnabas about this too (Acts 14). It is a sign of great zeal that he seeks new labours (2 Cor. 12). It is not enough that some are brought to Christ and the churches are well founded; care must be taken that what has been well established is preserved. This work is needed because of the snares of the devil (Matt. 12; 1 Pet. 5), and then because of the stupidity of the sheep, of which we see many examples today. Here, therefore, good heads of households and commanders are to be imitated, especially where there are some he-goats. Idle ministers are rebuked, above all those who scatter churches.

units.la: III. Dissidium oritur inter Paulum & Barnabam, multis nominibus memorabile. Coniunxerat hoc Spiritus sanctus, Act.13. Multa simul subierant. Senserant gratiam Dei mirificè. In dissidio de iustificatione consenserant. Nunc subito dissociantur causa fuit Marcus, de quo Act.15. Hunc recipi vult Barnabas, & habuit rationes. Exemplum Dei, Ezech.18. Christi, Ioh.21. Pietas matris, Act. 12. Paulus opponit se. Permisit haud dubie vt Christianus habere retur, (imo postea secum habuit. Col.4.) sed nunc ministerij societum non vult habere, secundum illud Luc.9. Videtur Ecclesia illi cosensisse. Nam huius solenni be hedicione dmittitur, cum Barnabas indignabundus insalutatis omnibus abijfe videbatur.
units.tr: III. A dissension arises between Paul and Barnabas, memorable for many reasons. The Holy Spirit had joined them (Acts 13). They had undergone many things together; they had wonderfully experienced the grace of God; they had agreed about justification. Now they suddenly part company. The cause was Mark, of whom Acts 15. Barnabas wishes him to be received and had his reasons: the example of God (Ezek. 18), of Christ (John 21), and the piety of a mother (Acts 12). Paul sets himself against this. Undoubtedly he allowed that Mark be regarded as a Christian (indeed afterwards he had him with him, Col. 4), but now he does not wish to have him as a companion in the ministry, according to Luke 9. The Church seems to have agreed with Paul, for Paul is dismissed with its solemn blessing, while Barnabas seemed to depart in indignation, without greeting anyone.

units.la: NOT.¶ In ministris eligendis circumspectè agendum esse. Non neganda quidem venia lapsis. Sed ad ministerium non temerè admittendi, qui scandali authores fuerunt, & quorum fides suspecta est. 1. Tim. 3. Hodie quia nimium faciles sumus, vilescit ministerium. Imò quidam Herodem imitantur.
units.tr: Note: in choosing ministers we must proceed with caution. Indeed, pardon is not to be denied to the lapsed; but those who were the authors of scandal, and whose faith is suspect, are not to be admitted to the ministry rashly (1 Tim. 3). Today, because we are far too easy-going, the ministry becomes cheap. Indeed, some even imitate Herod.

units.la: ¶ 2. Cur hoc passus est Deus, & cur horum errore conscribi voluit? (Scripturæ fides asseritur.) A. Docemur sanctos etiam homines fuisse, affectibus obnoxios, & proinde gratia Dei opus habuisse. Fate tur hoc Paulus, Act. 14. 2. Cor. 12. Rom. 7. Ergo ad Deũ authorem referamus quicquid egregiè fecerunt.
units.tr: 2. Why did God allow this, and why did he want their error written down? (The trustworthiness of Scripture is affirmed.) A. We are taught that even holy men were subject to passions and therefore had need of the grace of God. Paul confesses this (Acts 14; 2 Cor. 12; Rom. 7). Therefore let us ascribe to God, as author, whatever they did nobly.

units.la: B. Excitamur ad Dei timore & ardens salutis studium, Phil 2. 1. Cor. 10. Si enim tam præclaris organis Dei hæc acciderut, quid de nobis fiat?
units.tr: B. We are stirred up to the fear of God and to an ardent zeal for salvation (Phil. 2; 1 Cor. 10). For if these things happened to such excellent instruments of God, what will become of us?

units.la: C. Propter ministrorum dissidia non dubitandum de veritatis doctrina. Hæc enim non ab hominibus pendet, sed semper sibi constat, If. 40. Frustra tripudiant hostes, quia hæc verit. illustrandæ seruiut.
units.tr: C. Because of the dissensions of ministers, we should not doubt the doctrine of truth. For this does not depend on men, but always agrees with itself (Isa. 40). The enemies exult in vain, because these things serve to illustrate the truth.

units.la: IV. Virius profectio. Licet eunim dif sideant, neuter tamen officium suum negligit, quin exequantur consilium. Barnabas Cyprum, Paulus in Syriam & Ciciliam abit, & vterque patriae imprimis consulit. Exemplum. Discant item omnes, ne se superari sinant cotendendi libidine, vt propter hominum improbitatem officium deserant.
units.tr: IV. Their departure took place separately. For although they disagreed, neither neglected his duty, but each carried out the plan. Barnabas sails to Cyprus, Paul goes into Syria and Cilicia, and each especially looks after his homeland. This is an example. Let all likewise learn not to let themselves be overcome by the lust of contending, so as to abandon their office because of the wickedness of men.

units.la: Bonitatem & sapientiam Dei, qui electorum erroribus bene vtitur. Discipulos ... sociantur isti, sed ea occasione plures inuisuntur & confirmantur in doctrina. Sic peccatis imporu ad sui nominis illustrationem bene vti potest. Iosephi venditio Gen. 45. & 50. Psal. 105. Iudas, Caiphas &c. Non tamen ideo illi excusantur. Peccant enim & irae vasa fieri merentur. Quod bonus inde fructus enascitur, ei sapientiae tribui debet. Oremus Deum, vt nos in suis vijs dirigat, & si peccamus, nostris quoque delictis vtatur ad suam gloriam & multorum salutem.
units.tr: The goodness and wisdom of God, who makes good use of the errors of the elect. ... join themselves to these men, but on that occasion more are gathered and confirmed in doctrine. So God can make good use of sins for the illustration of his name: the sale of Joseph (Gen. 45 and 50; Psalm 105), Judas, Caiaphas, and so on. Yet these men are not thereby excused, for they sin and deserve to become vessels of wrath. That good fruit springs from it must be attributed to his wisdom. Let us pray God to direct us in his ways, and, if we sin, to use even our offences for his own glory and the salvation of many.

units.la: CAPVT XVI.
units.tr: Chapter 16.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXIX.
units.tr: Homily 129.

units.la: Peruenit autem Derben & Lystram: & ecce discipulus quidam erat illic, nomine Timotheus, filius cuiusdam mulieris, Iudaeae fidelis, caterum patre Graeco. 2 Huic dabant testimonium fra‐tres,qui Lystris erant & Iconij.
units.tr: Then he came to Derbe and to Lystra. And behold, a certain disciple was there named Timothy, the son of a certain woman who was a believing Jewess, but his father was a Greek. Brethren who were at Lystra and Iconium gave him a good report.

units.la: 3 Eum itaque voluit Paulus se‐cum proficisci: & assumptum eum cir‐cumcidit,&c.ad ver.6.
units.tr: Paul therefore wanted him to set out with him; and taking him, he circumcised him, etc., to verse 6.

units.la: Iuus Paulus Ecclesias,quas Euangelij prædicatione college rat,inuisere & confirmare insti tuit,ne vel securitate, vel sata‐næ oonis circumuenti, vel persecutioni‐nibus territi deficiant.Id sic facit,vt simul vbicunque occasio sese offert, nouas Ec‐clefias lucrifacere studeat.Eam historiam in sequentibus describit Lucas, qui Pauli comes & omnium oculatus testis fuit. Dictum nuper, quod Syriam & Ciliciam lustrauerit.Sequitur vt in Lycaonia transierit,cuius Ecclesiæ cum primis consola tione opus habebant, eo quod præ alijs infestarentur.In præsenti 2.cösiderabimus I, Comitem & laborum socium assumit Timotheum. Nouerat enim sine idoneis ministris regnum Christi & fidem propa‐gari non posse,Rom.10.Vt ergo reges vn‐dique bonos milites conquirunt,ita Pau‐lus curat vt multos fideles verbi mini‐stros habeat Ecclesia, Tit.1.Hoc studium imitentur quicunque Ecclesias saluas vo‐lunt.Hic finis & vsus scholarum fuit olim.
units.tr: Paul, having decided to visit and strengthen the churches he had gathered by preaching the Gospel, so that they should not fail through complacency, be deceived by the snares of Satan, or be terrified by persecutions, does this in such a way that wherever an opportunity presents itself he also strives to win new churches. Luke, who was Paul's companion and an eyewitness of everything, describes that history in what follows. It was said just now that Paul traversed Syria and Cilicia. It follows that he passed into Lycaonia, whose churches especially needed consolation, because they were harassed more than the others. In the present passage we shall consider two things: first, he takes Timothy as his companion and fellow labourer. For he knew that the kingdom of Christ and the faith cannot be spread without fit ministers (Rom. 10). Therefore, just as kings everywhere seek good soldiers, so Paul takes care that the Church has many faithful ministers of the Word (Titus 1). Let all who wish their churches to be safe imitate this zeal. This was once the aim and use of the schools.

units.la: Thimothei vocatio.
units.tr: The calling of Timothy.

units.la: Hic tamen NOT.¶1. Qualem deligat? Timotheum, qui matre Iudæa oriundus fuit, eaque fideli, patre autem gentili. Discipulus tamen fuit, id est, Christianus, & omnium fratrum testimonio commendatus, Vide 2. Tim 3 Phil.2. &c. Discis quales eligi debeant? A. Qui discipuli sint, id est, Christiani, non alieni à religione, nec etiam neophyti & proinde incerti rerum, 1. Tim.3.&c. Tales enim & ipsi religionem pro lusu habent, & eandem aliorum ludibrijs exponunt. B Studiosi sint & inscripturis exercitati, 2.Tim.3.1 Tim.4. Ex his enim doctrina peti debet, Ezech.3. Mal.2. Et quomodo docebit, qui non antea didicit? Cæcus dux, Matth.15. Ideo Christus Apostolos non nisi instructissimos misit, Ioh.14. Actor.1.&2.&c. Mal.2. 1 Tim.4.C. Probatæ vitæ sint, ne propter ipsos Evangelii contemnatur, 1. Tim.3. Tit.1.&c. Huc refer exempla filiorum Heli, 1.Sam. 3.4. Mal.1.2.
units.tr: Here, however, note 1. What sort of man does he choose? Timothy, who was born of a Jewish mother, and she a believer, but of a Gentile father. Yet he was a disciple, that is, a Christian, and commended by the testimony of all the brethren (see 2 Tim. 3; Phil. 2, etc.). Do you learn what sort of men ought to be chosen? A. Those who are disciples, that is, Christians, not strangers to religion, nor yet neophytes, and therefore uncertain of matters (1 Tim. 3, etc.). For such men treat religion as a game and expose it to the mockery of others. B. Let them be diligent and trained in the Scriptures (2 Tim. 3; 1 Tim. 4). For teaching ought to be sought from these (Ezek. 3; Mal. 2). And how will he teach who has not first learned? A blind guide (Matt. 15). Therefore Christ sent only the most thoroughly instructed Apostles (John 14; Acts 1 and 2, etc.; Mal. 2; 1 Tim. 4, etc.). C. Let them be men of proven life, lest the Gospel itself be despised on their account (1 Tim. 3; Titus 1, etc.). Refer here the examples of the sons of Eli (1 Sam. 2–4; Mal. 1–2).

units.la: ¶2. Quomodo cum Timotheo agat? Circumcidit eum, cum vellet secum circumducere. Et quia hoc mirum videri poterat, causa indicatur: Propter Iudæos, qui in illis locis erant. Hi enim incircicusum abominati fuissent. Act.10.11. Et Paulum ut prophanatorem religionis reiecisset, ut pateret patet Act 21. Circumcidit ergo Timotheum, ut ipsi aditus pateret ad Iudaeos, & sic paulatim aboleatur circumcisio: no quod hanc ad salutem putarit necessariam. Nam quid de hac senserit, habes Galat. 5. Imo cum liberati quidam insidiarentur, Titum circumcidere noluit. Vide Gal. 2.
units.tr: ¶2. How does he deal with Timothy? He circumcised him, though he wished to take him along with him. And because this might seem strange, the reason is given: on account of the Jews who were in those places. For they would have abhorred an uncircumcised man. (Acts 16:1-3.) And so that he might not reject Paul as a profaner of the religion, as is clear from Acts 21. Paul therefore circumcised Timothy, so that access to the Jews would be open to him, and so that circumcision might gradually be done away with; not because he thought it necessary to salvation. For what he thought about it you have in Galatians 5. Indeed, when some false brethren plotted against him, he refused to circumcise Titus. See Galatians 2.

units.la: Obserua igitur: A. Vt in externis difpen sare liceat? Nimirum ex charitate, quatenus aedificationi seruit, 1. Cor. 9. Vt primum vero cultus alligatur & meriti fiducia, vel libertati insidiae struuntur, minime ferenda. Haec si obseruies, videbis Pauli ex emplum non patrocinari Papistis. Non in statuta a Deo. Cultum & salute allegant, libertatem euertunt. Character bestiae.
units.tr: Observe therefore: A. Whether it is lawful to dispense with external matters? Surely out of charity, insofar as it serves edification (1 Cor. 9). But when worship is bound to them and trust is placed in merit, or snares are laid for liberty, they are in no way to be tolerated. If you observe this, you will see that the example of Paul does not support the Papists, who do not hold to the statutes of God, who insist on these things as worship and as the means of salvation, and who overthrow liberty. The mark of the beast.

units.la: B. Quid mali eximpari coniugio? Euni ca & Lois fideles fuerunt, 2. Tim. 1. Sed ha stenus filium non potuerunt Deo conse- crare, &c. Hinc iste leges, Deut. 7. Iof. 23. 2. Cor. 6. Memorabile tamen, quod sacris literis illu instituerunt, vt patet ex 2. Tim. 3. Imitemur hoc quae infidelium maritorum iugo diuexantur. Vide 1. Cor. 7. &c. Impij qui liberos turpiter negligunt.
units.tr: B. What harm is there in mixed marriage? Eunice and Lois were believers (2 Tim. 1). Yet until now they could not consecrate their son to God, etc. Hence those laws (Deut. 7; Josh. 23; 2 Cor. 6). It is worth remembering, however, that they had him instructed in the sacred letters, as is clear from 2 Tim. 3. Let those imitate this who are harassed by the yoke of unbelieving husbands (see 1 Cor. 7, etc.). Those are impious who shamefully neglect their children.

units.la: II. Quid docuerunt, dum lustrant Ec- clesias? Quae ab Apostolis erant statuta in Synodo; (Papistae tradit, suas hinc colli,
