units.tr: II. What did they teach while they visited the churches? What had been decreed by the Apostles in the Synod (the Papists hand down that their own [traditions] are gathered from this

units.la: gunt )Nimirum sola Dei gratia per fidem iustificari credentes,Rom.3.Eph.2.&c. In terim studendum sanctitati, & charitatis rationem habendam esse,ne libertate abutamur cum offendiculo. Hæc inculcauit Paulus vbique pacis studio. Interim vbi nullum fuit scandali periculum, libertatem candide asseruit,1.Cor.10.&c.
units.tr: ), namely that believers are justified by the grace of God alone through faith (Rom. 3; Eph. 2, etc.). Meanwhile, we must strive for holiness and have regard for charity, lest we abuse liberty to the stumbling of others. Paul inculcated this everywhere, with zeal for peace. Yet where there was no danger of offence, he candidly asserted liberty (1 Cor. 10, etc.).

units.la: Interim in Pauli exemplo Not.¶ Non sufficere si bonæ leges condantur,sed eas dem vrgeri & retineri oportere. Executio legum neruus & anima est. Quæ si absit iuxta Anacharsis dictum aranearum tela similes erunt, quas cuiusuis audacia perrumpit. Facit huc multum consensus legislatorum.Vide Pfal.72.82.Rom.13.
units.tr: Meanwhile, from Paul's example, note that it is not enough for good laws to be enacted; they must also be enforced and maintained. The execution of laws is the sinew and soul of them. If this is lacking, then, in the words of Anacharsis, they will be like spiders' webs, which the boldness of anyone breaks through. Much agreement of legislators bears on this (see Ps. 72 and 82; Rom. 13).

units.la: III. Fructus studij Apostolici. Ecclesia confirmantur in fide. Non ergo ad ceremonias, sed ad Christum relegârunt, 1. Cor 2.Gal. 6. Crescunt quotidie numero Sunt hi effectus verbi,Isa.55 Luc.7.&c.
units.tr: III. The fruit of the Apostolic labour: the churches were strengthened in the faith. They did not therefore refer them to ceremonies, but to Christ (1 Cor. 2; Gal. 6). They grow daily in number. These are the effects of the Word (Isa. 55; Luke 7, etc.).

units.la: Not. ¶ Quibus armis Ecclesiæ Christo adduci simul etiam conseruari possint. Verbi sedula prædicatione. Vbi hoc negligitur, fides intermoritur, si non cogantur ad manifestam impietatem, interim verbo destituuntur.Oremus.
units.tr: Note. By what arms the churches can be brought to Christ and at the same time preserved: by diligent preaching of the Word. Where this is neglected, faith dies out; and if people are not driven into open impiety, they are nevertheless deprived of the Word. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXX.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXX.

units.la: 6 Phrygia autem peragrata et Galatica regione, prohibiti à spiritu sancto loqui sermonem in Asia.
units.tr: 6 And when they had gone through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to preach the word in Asia.

units.la: 7 Quum venissent in Mysiam, tentabant ire in Bithyniam, sed non siuit eos spiritus.
units.tr: 7 When they had come to Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit did not allow them.

units.la: 8 Praeterita autem Mysia, descenderunt Troada.
units.tr: 8 And passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.

units.la: 9 Et visum per noctem apparuit Paulo: Vir Macedo quidam, aderat stans, et rogans eum, et dicens: Transi in Macedoniam, et succurre nobis.
units.tr: 9 And a vision appeared to Paul in the night: a certain man of Macedonia was standing there, begging him and saying, "Come over into Macedonia and help us."

units.la: 10 Ut autem visum vidit, statim studuimus abire in Macedoniam, collatis argumentis colligentes vocasse nos Dominum, ut eis Euangelizaremus.
units.tr: 10 And when he had seen the vision, we immediately sought to go into Macedonia, concluding from the evidence that the Lord had called us to preach the gospel to them.

units.la: 11 Proiecti igitur Troade, rectum cursum tenuimus Samothracen, et sequenti die Neapolim.
units.tr: 11 Therefore, setting sail from Troas, we ran a straight course to Samothrace, and the next day to Neapolis.

units.la: 12 Et illinc Philippos, quae est prima partis Macedoniae urbs, colonia.
units.tr: 12 And from there to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, a colony.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus Apostolorum peregrinationes, et quidem Pauli in primis, diligentissime describit, eo quod nostrae institutioni plurimum seruiunt. Primo enim elucet hic magna Dei bonitas, qui
units.tr: The Holy Spirit describes the journeys of the apostles with great care, and especially those of Paul, because they serve our instruction very much. For first, here shines forth the great goodness of God, who wished the whole world to be converted so quickly in a most corrupt age.

units.la: totum orbem corruptissimo seculo tam cito conuerti voluit. Qualis enim huius facies fuerit,historię docent,tum etiá Paulus,Rom.1.Eph.2.Tit.3.&c. Deinde patet hic, quibus armis & medijs Christi regnū propagetur simul & conseruetur: nimirū verbi prædicatione. Per hoc enim spirat Deus etiam inuito mundo,Ioh.3. In eo autem Pauli diligentiam & zelum imitari oportet. Conuertit is antea multas provin cias,Act.13.14. Nunc easdem denuò inuisit,& prædicando confirmat,docens, fem per vigilandum esse aduersus satanam, 1. Pet.5. Simul verò in hoc incumbit,vt nouas quoque Ecclesias colligat. Et de hoc in præsenti agitur.
units.tr: What the condition of that age was, the histories teach, and Paul too (Rom. 1; Eph. 2; Tit. 3, etc.). Next, it is plain here by what means and instruments the kingdom of Christ is spread and at the same time preserved, namely by the preaching of the word. For through this God breathes even on an unwilling world (John 3). In this we ought to imitate Paul's diligence and zeal. He had earlier converted many provinces (Acts 13, 14); now he visits the same again and strengthens them by preaching, teaching that one must always be watchful against Satan (1 Pet. 5). At the same time he applies himself to gathering new churches also. And it is of this that the present passage speaks.

units.la: I. Peragrauerunt totam Phrygiam & Galatiá:quas regiones conuersas ad Christum fuisse ex Pauli epistolis patet.Ex quibus etiá colligi potest, quid prædicârint. Sed hic peculiare quiddam accidit, quòd à spiritu prohibentur in Asia & Bithynia prædicare Euangelium.
units.tr: I. They travelled through all of Phrygia and Galatia; that these regions had been converted to Christ is clear from Paul's epistles. From these one can also gather what they preached. But here something peculiar happens: they are forbidden by the Spirit to preach the gospel in Asia and Bithynia.

units.la: NOTA.¶1. Apostolos non temerè circumcurrisse per orbe,sed spiritu Dei duce omnia fecisse. Promiserat hunc Christus,Ioh.14.16.Actor.1.Hunc acceperunt, Act.2.Sed simul acceflerunt peculiares relationes,si quando opus fuit. Exempla similiia habuimus, Act. 8. 10. 18 &c. Facit hoc ad commendationem doctrinae ipsorum, nec illam vt humanam aspernemur, sed Christi verba agnoscamus, Mat. 10. Lucae 10. Ioh. 13.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The apostles did not run about the world at random, but did everything with the Spirit of God as their guide. Christ had promised him (John 14:16; Acts 1), they received him (Acts 2), but at the same time particular revelations came whenever there was need. We have similar examples (Acts 8, 10, 18, etc.). This serves to commend their doctrine, so that we do not scorn it as human, but recognise the words of Christ (Matt. 10; Luke 10; John 13).

units.la: 2. Cur alibi permisi sint docere, alii cubi non? Quidam ad praescientiam Dei confugiunt, qui praeuiderit qui digni, qui non. Sed quoad homines, perequè omnes indigni sunt, Rom 1.3. Nec quisquam ideo neus auditor est, nisi quem Deus talem fecerit, Ioh. 6. Isa. 54. 1. Cor 3. Ita dictum, Act. 14. Idem mox in Lydia parebit. Non aliam ergo causam allegare possumus, quàm liberam & gratuitam Dei electionem, qui quorum vult miseretur, &c. Rom. 9. Exo. 33. Et in electis quidem suam bonitatem in reprobis iustitiam declarat, &c. Ro. 9. 11.
units.tr: 2. Why were they allowed to teach in one place but not in another? Some take refuge in God's foreknowledge, who foresaw who were worthy and who were not. But as far as men are concerned, all are equally unworthy (Rom. 1, 3), and no one is a better hearer for that reason, unless God has made him such (John 6; Isa. 54:1; 1 Cor. 3). So it is said in Acts 14, and soon the same will appear in Lydia. We can therefore assign no other cause than God's free and gratuitous election, who has mercy on whom he wills, etc. (Rom. 9; Exod. 33). And in the elect he declares his goodness, and in the reprobate his justice, etc. (Rom. 9, 11).

units.la: Et huius doctrinae vsus est. A Confirmat fidem in tentationibus. Est enim haec firmissima consolatio, quòd scimus salutem nostram à Dei gratia dependere, & in vno Christo esse fundatam. Quis enim illam euerteret? Rom. 8. Vide Ioh. 10. 17.
units.tr: And this doctrine has its use. A. It strengthens faith in temptations. For this is the firmest consolation, that we know our salvation depends on the grace of God and is founded in Christ alone. For who could overturn it? (Rom. 8; see John 10:17.)

units.la: B. Officij nos admonet. Est hoc Deum timere & vereri. Vocanti obedire. Gratos nos praebere, quando prae alijs illius boni tatem experimur. Vt enim bonitatem non meritis offert, ita si ingrati simus.
units.tr: B. It reminds us of our duty. To fear and revere God is this: to obey the one who calls, to show ourselves grateful when we experience his goodness above others. For as he offers goodness not on account of merits, so if we are ungrateful...

units.la: feuerisimè punit,Mat. 10. Vide Iudæos, Matth. 11.21.23.24. Lucæ 10.19. Has ipsas Ecclesias,de quibus hic agitur. Vtinam di ligentiùs hoc meditaremur!
units.tr: ...he punishes most severely (Matt. 10). See the Jews (Matt. 11:21, 23, 24; Luke 10:13, 15). These very churches of which this passage speaks. Would that we pondered this more diligently!

units.la: II. Paulus licet alicubi prohibeatur,nō tamen officium negligit, sed Mysiam transit, & tandem venit Troadem, nimirum vndiq; docendi occasionem captans. Illic ergo per visionem ab angelo admonetur, vt in Macedoniam abeat,&c.
units.tr: II. Although Paul is somewhere forbidden, he nevertheless does not neglect his office, but passes through Mysia and at last comes to Troas, plainly seizing every opportunity of teaching. There, therefore, he is admonished by an angel in a vision to go over into Macedonia, etc.

units.la: ¶ In his Notr. ¶1. Non turpiter cessan dum,etiamsi in bona causa primus & alter conatus non successerint. Sæpe hoc Prophetis & Apostolis accidit. Mosi item,vt videre est,Exod.5.6.7.&c. Pergamus modò nos,nec deerit Dominus,qui suo tempore occasionem dabit & successum.
units.tr: ¶ On these matters, note: 1. One must not cease shamefully, even if the first and second attempts in a good cause do not succeed. This has often happened to the prophets and apostles. Likewise to Moses, as can be seen (Exod. 5, 6, 7, etc.). Let us only press on, and the Lord, who will give opportunity and success in his own time, will not be lacking.

units.la: ¶2. Bonitas Dei magna, qui etiam nescientibus nobis salutem nostram operatur. Quis enim apud Macedones cogitavit de Paulo? Sic impletur quod est Is.65. Rom.10. Sic elegit ante mundi creationem,Eph.1.Adam,Gen.3. Quotidie in ijs quæ corpori seruiunt, similia experimur, iuxta illud,Psal.34.91. Excitet hoc ad gratitudinem & soletur.
units.tr: ¶2. The goodness of God is great, who works our salvation even when we do not know it. For who among the Macedonians thought of Paul? So what is said in Isa. 65 and Rom. 10 is fulfilled. So he chose us before the creation of the world (Eph. 1); Adam (Gen. 3). Daily we experience similar things in those things that serve the body, according to that saying (Ps. 34; 91). Let this stir us to gratitude and comfort us.

units.la: ¶3. Ministerij Euangelici dignitas commendatur bifariam. A. Per Angelum & divino oraculo vocatur & ducitur Paulus. Sic Petrus, Act. 10. Philippus, Act. 8. Non ergo est, quòd Angelos doctores quæramus, quando hi ad homines relegant, Gal. 1. B. Succurre nobis. Hoc solius Dei est. Ministris vero tribuitur propter verbum Euangelij quod est potentia Dei, &c. Ro. 1. Hinc illæ locutiones, Pf. 107. Abd. 1. Confutantur, qui ex Euangelio interitus gentium enasci clamant. Imò gens & regnum, quod non seruierit Christo peribit, If. 60. Psalm. 2.
units.tr: ¶3. The dignity of the evangelical ministry is commended in two ways. A. Paul is called and led by an angel and by a divine oracle. So Peter (Acts 10), Philip (Acts 8). It is not necessary, therefore, that we seek teachers among angels, since these send us back to men (Gal. 1). B. Help us. This belongs to God alone. But it is attributed to the ministers on account of the word of the gospel, which is the power of God, etc. (Rom. 1). Hence those expressions (Ps. 107; Obad. 1). They are refuted who cry out that the destruction of the nations is born from the gospel. Indeed, the nation and kingdom that does not serve Christ will perish (Isa. 60; Ps. 2).

units.la: III. Paulus mox surgit & obtemperat, quemadmodum Petrus Act. 10. Et felicis fines in Matter eò peruenit. Not. Vt Dei vocatio exspectāda est, ita vbi de hac certi sumus, non procrastinandum, Luc. 9. Vide Apostolos, Mat. 4. Zachæum, Luc. 19. Discipulos, Luc. 10. Econtrà Ionam, cap. 1.
units.tr: III. Paul immediately rises and obeys, just as Peter did (Acts 10), and by a happy course he came thence to the borders of Macedonia. Note: as the call of God is to be awaited, so when we are certain of it, we must not delay (Luke 9). See the apostles (Matt. 4); Zacchaeus (Luke 19); the disciples (Luke 10). On the contrary, Jonah (ch. 1).

units.la: Hin patet, vnde læti rerum successus proficiscantur. Nimirum si in Dei vocatione homines respiciant, & hanc bona fide sequantur. Qui suis consilijs nituntur, & in vanitatem respiciunt, succumbunt, Psalm. 66. &c. Oremus.
units.tr: From this it is plain whence the happy outcomes of affairs proceed: namely, if men look to God's calling and follow it in good faith. Those who rely on their own counsels and look to vanity succumb (Ps. 66, etc.). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXXI.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXXI.

units.la: 12 Egimus autem Philippi aliquot dies.
units.tr: 12 Now we stayed in Philippi for some days.

units.la: 13 Et die Sabbathi egressi sumus ex vrbe ad flumen, vbi solebat esse precatio: vbi quum consedissemus, alloquuti sumus mulieres, quæ conuenerant.
units.tr: 13 And on the Sabbath day we went out of the city by the river, where prayer was customarily made; and when we had sat down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.

units.la: 14 Quædam autem mulier nomine Lydia, quæ purpuram vendebat in vrbe Tyriorum, Deum colens, nos audiuit, cuius Dominus adaperuit cor, vt attenderet ea, quæ dicebantur à Paulo.
units.tr: 14 And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who worshipped God, heard us; the Lord opened her heart to attend to the things that were said by Paul.

units.la: 15 Quum vero baptizata esset, & domus eius, rogauit nos, dicens, Si iudicastis me fidelem esse Domino, ingressi domum meam, manete. Et adegit nos.
units.tr: 15 And when she and her household were baptized, she begged us, saying, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay." And she persuaded us.

units.la: Dvuus Paulus visione & diuino oraculo vocatur, vt in Macedoniam Euangelium prædicet. Quo exemplo partim Euangelij dignitas asseritur, partim docetur salutem nobis ex mera gratia ob tigere. Nam si Macedones inspicias, eadem illorum, quæ & aliarum gentium futit conditio, Rom. 1. Eph 2. Tit. 3. Et de salute vera ne cogitarunt quidem, quando illis Paulum doctorem destinauit Deus. Se quitur quid Philippis in Macedonia gestum sit.
units.tr: Paul is called by a vision and a divine oracle to preach the gospel in Macedonia. By this example the dignity of the gospel is asserted, and partly it is taught that salvation comes to us from pure grace. For if you look at the Macedonians, their condition was the same as that of the other nations, Rom. 1; Eph. 2; Tit. 3. They did not even think about true salvation when God appointed Paul as their teacher. There follows what was done at Philippi in Macedonia.

units.la: I. Manent diebus aliquot Philippis: ni mirum quòd nusquam se offerret prædicandi & propagandi regni Christi occasio.
units.tr: I. They remain in Philippi for some days: clearly because no opportunity for preaching and spreading the kingdom of Christ presented itself anywhere.

units.la: Interea diebus festis extra vrbem eorum coetus ingrediebantur, qui apud flumen ad publicas preces confluebant. Et ibi mu lieribus praedicant.
units.tr: Meanwhile, on the festival days, their assembly went outside the city, to the river, where they gathered for public prayers. And there they preach to the women.

units.la: Vt Deus suorum fidem & constantiam exercere soleat. Vocatus fuit Paulus per Angelum. Putaret aliquis omnes illi obuiam venturos, &c. Sed adeo fallit haec spes, vt in vrbe ne vnus quidem sese offerat ad verbi praedicationem. Extra vrbem solae mulieres audiunt, ex quibus vix vnam tandem conuertunt. Quare videri poterat lusoria fuisse haec vocatio. Ita Mosi accidit, Exod. 2. 4. 5. 14. &c. Similia exempla alibi inueniuntur.
units.tr: So God is accustomed to exercise the faith and constancy of his people. Paul was called through an angel. One might suppose that all would come to meet him, etc. But this hope is so disappointed that in the city not even one person presents himself for the preaching of the Word. Outside the city only women listen, and from them they at last convert scarcely one. Wherefore this calling might seem to have been a joke. So it happened to Moses, Exod. 2, 4, 5, 14, etc. Similar examples are found elsewhere.

units.la: ¶2. Officium nostrum in simili casu. Imitemur Apostolorum constantiam & sedulitatem. Illi omnem occasionem vsenan tur, etiam extra vrbem progressi. Praeterea ne mulierculas quidem fastidiunt, nimirum Christi exemplum secuti, Io. 4. Luc. 7. 8. 10. &c.
units.tr: ¶2. Our duty in a similar case. Let us imitate the constancy and diligence of the Apostles. They seize every opportunity, even when they go out of the city. Moreover, they do not despise even the little women, clearly following the example of Christ, John 4; Luke 7, 8, 10, etc.

units.la: II. Lydiae conuersio, in qua singulas par Lydia con tes Nota. ¶1. Persona eius describitur. Mulier fuit, ex eo nimirum sexu, per quem peccatum in mundum introiuit, 1. Tim. 2. Conditione, purpurarum venditrix. Mercaturam ergo exercuit, & talem quidem, quae fastui & superbiae potius quam necessaCap. 16. sitati inseruiret. Preterea aliena fuit, Thyatirensis nimirum.
units.tr: II. The conversion of Lydia, in which we note the individual circumstances. ¶1. Her person is described. She was a woman, of that sex, namely, through which sin entered the world, 1 Tim. 2. Her condition: a seller of purple. She therefore practised trade, and indeed of a kind that served pomp and pride rather than necessity. Besides, she was a foreigner, namely from Thyatira.

units.la: Hinc ergo docemur: A. Deum nullius ordinis aut conditionis homines asperna ri,1. Tim.2. Ita alibi meretrices & publicani vocantur, Iohan.4 Matth 9 1. Luc.7. 19. Milites, Matth 27. Actor. 10. Pharisaei quoque & principes, Ioh.3.12. Nemo ergo desperet.
units.tr: From this, therefore, we are taught: A. That God does not despise men of any rank or condition, 1 Tim. 2. Thus elsewhere harlots and tax collectors are called, John 4; Matt. 9; Luke 7, 19. Soldiers, Matt. 27; Acts 10. Pharisees also and rulers, John 3, 12. Let no one therefore despair.

units.la: B. Dei consilium, qui sui filij regnum paruis initijs prouehit. Lydia primitiae fuit eius Ecclesiae, quàm Paulus postea tantoperè commendat. Vult autem Deus Christi regnum in hoc mundo humilitatem crucis sapere, vt constet illud non esse de hoc mundo, & ipsi omnem gloriam esse tribuenda, 1. Cor.1. Habes item quod illis opponas, qui Euangelij fide propter viles & ignobiles sectatores contemnunt Matt.11.
units.tr: B. The counsel of God, who advances the kingdom of his Son from small beginnings. Lydia was the firstfruits of that Church, which Paul afterwards commends so highly. God wills, however, that the kingdom of Christ in this world should savour of the humility of the cross, so that it may be established that it is not of this world, and that all glory is to be ascribed to him, 1 Cor. 1. You have also here what to set against those who despise the faith of the gospel on account of its base and ignoble followers, Matt. 11.

units.la: ¶ 2. Modus & ordo conuersionis diligenter describitur. A. Religiosa fuit, nimirum vt Cornelius. Atqui hoc non profuisset, nisi accessisset vera illuminatio, vt exempla docent, Act.13. Gal.1. Phil.3. &c. Interim oportet ante omnia terram bonam esse, Luc.8. Id autem solius Dei donum est. Quale enim hominis ingenium sit, scriptura docet, & ipsi experimur quotidie, Gc.6.8. Ro.7.2. Cor.3. B. Att-
units.tr: ¶2. The manner and order of the conversion is carefully described. A. She was religious, like Cornelius. But this would not have profited her, unless true enlightenment had been added, as examples teach, Acts 13; Gal. 1; Phil. 3, etc. Meanwhile, it is necessary above all that the soil be good, Luke 8. But this is the gift of God alone. For what kind of disposition man has, Scripture teaches, and we ourselves experience daily, Jas. 6, 8; Rom. 7, 2; Cor. 3. B. Att-

units.la: B. Audit verbum. Hoc organum est legitimum, quo fides datur. Rom. 10. Lu. 10. Ioh. 6. Falluntur, qui θεοπνευστος fomai ant & externum verbum reijciunt. Tales fere satanae praeda fiunt, &c.
units.tr: B. She hears the Word. This is the lawful instrument by which faith is given, Rom. 10; Luke 10; John 6. They are mistaken who call the Scripture inspired by God [θεόπνευστος] and reject the external Word. Such people are almost always made the prey of Satan, etc.

units.la: C. Dominus aperuit cor. Hoc nisi fiat, frustra docent ministri. 1. Cor. 3. Hinc illa, Ioh. 6. Matt. 11. 16. Luc. 10. Qui interrogant, cur non aliorum quoque corda aperuerit Deus, nimis temerarii sunt. Respondetur illis Rom. 9. 11.
units.tr: C. The Lord opened her heart. Unless this happens, ministers teach in vain, 1 Cor. 3. Hence those sayings, John 6; Matt. 11, 16; Luke 10. Those who ask why God did not also open the hearts of others are too rash. An answer is given to them in Rom. 9, 11.

units.la: ¶ 3. Effectus fidei huius. 1. Baptizatur, conversionis. Habet hoc confessionem fidei, qua cupit fidei vera censeri inter membra Ecclesiae, Rom. 10. effectum. Et simul patet sanctos non contemnere sacramenta. Vide Act. 8 10. &c.
units.tr: ¶3. The effects of this faith. 1. She is baptized, the sign of conversion. She has this effect by a confession of faith, by which she desires to be counted a true believer among the members of the Church, Rom. 10. At the same time it is clear that the saints do not despise the sacraments. See Acts 8, 10, etc.

units.la: 2. Baptizatur tota domus. Cupiunt enim sancti omnes suos eiusdem salutis consortes habere. Et praecipit Deus patribus, ut suos quoque ipsi adducant. Genef. 17 18. Deut. 6. Psal. 78. Eadem ratione magistratus superstitiones exterminare, & inter suos fidem veram plantare debent.
units.tr: 2. Her whole household is baptized. For all the saints desire to have their own household partakers of the same salvation. And God commands the fathers that they also bring their own children, Gen. 17, 18; Deut. 6; Ps. 78. For the same reason magistrates ought to root out superstitions and plant the true faith among their subjects.

units.la: 3. Inuitat Apostolos domum suam. Gratitudinis hoc est, & intrepidi animi indicium. Sumptuosum erat tam multos alere. Sed cogitat quod est, 1. Cor. 9. Non carebat periculo, maxime cum alienigena esset. Hi effectus sunt verae fidei, ex quibus teipfum æstimare debes.
units.tr: 3. She invites the Apostles to her house. This is a sign of gratitude and of a fearless spirit. It was costly to feed so many. But she considers what is fitting, 1 Cor. 9. She was not free from danger, especially since she was a foreigner. These effects are the marks of true faith, by which you ought to judge yourself.

units.la: ¶ 4. Paulus & comites primò reluctan- tur, partim ne mulierculas pecunijs in sidiari viderentur, quod impostores solent,2.Tim.3. partim quòd neminem velle nt grauare,1.Cor.9.2.Cor.3.2.Thessal.3. Interim licet aliorum beneficentia frui, Luc.8.Ioh.12.13.Oremus.
units.tr: ¶4. Paul and his companions at first resist, partly lest they should seem to be ensnaring the little women with money, which impostors are wont to do, 2 Tim. 3; partly because they did not wish to burden anyone, 1 Cor. 9; 2 Cor. 3; 1 Thess. 3. Meanwhile it is lawful to enjoy the beneficence of others, Luke 8; John 12, 13. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXXII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXXII.

units.la: 16 Factum est autem, proficiscen tibus nobis ad precationem, vt ancillula quædam habens spiritum Pythonis, occurreret nobis, quæ quæstum magnum præbebat Dominis suis, vaticinando.
units.tr: 16 And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, that a certain slave girl possessed with a spirit of Python met us, who brought her masters great gain by fortune-telling.

units.la: 17 Hæc subsequuta Paulum ac nos, clamabat dicens, Isti homines servi sunt Dei illius summi, qui annuntiant vobis viam salutis.
units.tr: 17 She followed Paul and us, crying out and saying, "These men are servants of the most high God, who proclaim to you the way of salvation."

units.la: 18 Hoc autē fecit ad multos dies, sed molestè ferens Paulus, & conuersus, spiritu dixit, Præcipio tibi per nomen Iesu Christi, vt exeas ab ea. Exijt igitur eodem illo momento.
units.tr: 18 She did this for many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her." And it came out the same hour.

units.la: QVemadmodum Dei Filius, Iesus Christus in mundum venit, vt homines saluos faceret, nec quicquam eorum rum intermisit, quæ ad nostram salutem spectant: Ita vicissim satan totus in hoc est, ut homines à salute revocet & perdat 1.Pet. 5. Ideo Christi regnum indesinenter oppugnat. Exemplum huius in præsenti historia proponitur. Postquam enim Philippos venit Paulus, conuersa ad fidem fuit Lydia, & fidem egregijs operibus declarauit. Gratitudinem enim exercet erga Apostolos, & non sine periculo illos domum suam inuitat. Interea pergunt illi decendo, & ut in fine Cap. patebit, coepit illorum ministerio Ecclesia colligi. Hoc ferre non potest satan, & mox opponit se, primo quidem blanditijs & malis dolis, dein de etiam aperta vi. In præsenti primus describitur congressus, qui hoc ordine confi derandus erit.
units.tr: Just as the Son of God, Jesus Christ, came into the world to save men, and omitted nothing that pertains to our salvation, so in turn Satan is wholly intent on calling men away from salvation and destroying them (1 Pet. 5). Therefore he attacks the kingdom of Christ without ceasing. An example of this is set before us in the present history. For after Paul came to Philippi, Lydia was converted to the faith and showed her faith by excellent works. For she exercises gratitude towards the Apostles and, not without danger, invites them into her house. Meanwhile they go on their way, and as will be clear at the end of the chapter, the Church began to be gathered through their ministry. Satan cannot bear this, and at once he sets himself against it, first indeed with flatteries and wicked tricks, and then also with open force. In the present passage the first encounter is described, which will be considered in the following order.

units.la: 1. Orditur à persona descriptione, per quam satan egit. Fuit puella, spiritu Pythonis præditâ, quæ quæstu magnu præstabat, &c.
units.tr: 1. He begins with a description of the person through whom Satan acted: There was a girl endowed with a spirit of Python, who brought her masters great gain, etc.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Quibus artibus & armis satan inter homines regnum affectet. Mendacijs nimirum (Gen.3.) & curiosis fiue validicis artibus quibus prophetiæ spiritu imitatur, & homines à verbo Dei revocat. Talis in Ægypto habuit, 2.Tim.3.Exo. 7.8. Talis Balaam fuit, Nu.22.23. Tales multi alij, augures, aruspices, somniorum interpretes, vates omnis generis, à quorum oraculis Regum consilia pendebant.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ 1. By what arts and weapons Satan seeks dominion among men: certainly by lies (Gen. 3) and by curious or magical arts, by which he imitates the spirit of prophecy and calls men away from the Word of God. Such a one was in Egypt (2 Tim. 3; Exod. 7–8). Balaam was such (Num. 22–23). Many others were such: augurs, haruspices, interpreters of dreams, soothsayers of every kind, on whose oracles the counsels of kings depended.

units.la: ¶ 2. Cur id permiserit Deus olim, & ho die etiam permittat? Propter hominum leuitatem, qui non contenti ijs, quæ Deus reuelat, ex seipsis volunt sapere, Rom 1. Item quòd veritatem fastidiunt, 2 Thef. 2. Vide hos Philippen. Vtrumq; hodie nimis vulgare est.
units.tr: ¶ 2. Why did God permit this formerly, and why does he still permit it today? On account of human levity, since men, not content with what God reveals, want to be wise from themselves (Rom. 1); also because they loathe the truth (2 Thess. 2). See these at Philippi. Both are all too common today.

units.la: Interim discamus cauere huius generis artes, & ab vnoDei verbo pendere. Leuit. 20. Deuter. 18. Isa. 8. Quàm infeliciter cedant, Saulis exemplum docet, 1. Samuel. 28. Manasses 2. Par. 33. Croesus, Pirasus, Iulianus.
units.tr: Meanwhile let us learn to beware of this kind of art and to depend on the one Word of God (Lev. 20; Deut. 18; Isa. 8). How unhappily such things turn out the example of Saul teaches (1 Sam. 28); also Manasseh (2 Chron. 33), Croesus, Pyrrhus, Julian.

units.la: II. Quid per puellam hanc Satan egerit, docetur. Sequitur Apostolos ad preca tionem ex more euntes. Clamat, & honorifice illos commendat: Isti homines serui Dei excelsissimi sunt, &c. Id verò facit primum, vt Apostolorum doctrinam apud cordatos suspectam reddat. Cordati ex gentibus ista damnârunt, &c. Deinde vt nullum inter hanc & sua ludibria discrimen relinquat, adeoq; se cum illa misceat. Postremò vt vana gloriae cupiditate Apostolos titillet. Hoc proposito alibi Christo quoq; fert testimonium, Mar. 1. Luc. 4.
units.tr: II. What Satan did through this girl is taught. She follows the Apostles, as they went to prayer as usual. She cries out and commends them with honour: "These men are servants of the most high God," etc. He does this first so that he makes the Apostles' teaching suspect to the discerning; the discerning among the Gentiles condemned such things, etc. Then, so that he leaves no difference between this and his own mockeries, and so mixes himself with her. Finally, so that by a desire for empty glory he tickles the Apostles. With this same purpose elsewhere he also bears witness to Christ (Mark 1; Luke 4).

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Ingenium satanae, qui cum opus pus est veritatis odium dissimulare, & in angelu lucis fe transformare nouit,2.Cor. 11. Non ergo temere credendum ijs, qui etiam sacra verba tonant magnifice. Sed animi propositum & finis ante omnia inspici debent.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ The nature of Satan, who knows how to hide his hatred of the truth when need arises and to transform himself into an angel of light (2 Cor. 11). Therefore one should not rashly believe those who loudly thunder even sacred words. But the intention and purpose of the mind must be examined before all else.

units.la: Arguuntur ergo:A. Qui papatum excu fant,quod lectiones sacras habeat, & Christum agnoscat,&c. Atqui ita de hoc praedictum,Dan.7.11.2.Theff.2.Mat.24. Item, Non omnis qui dicit mihi,&c.Mat.7. Lingua peregrina.Confirmantur superstitiosa operum merita,&c.
units.tr: They are therefore refuted: A. Those who excuse the papacy because it has the reading of sacred texts and acknowledges Christ, etc. But this was foretold in this way (Dan. 7:11; 2 Thess. 2; Matt. 24). Likewise: "Not everyone who says to me," etc. (Matt. 7). A foreign tongue. Superstitious merits of works are confirmed, etc.

units.la: B. Qui exorcismis hoc praetextu patro cinantur,quod non nisi sacris verbis constent,suos habeant effectus,&c.At eo graviùs peccatur,quod nomine Dei abutuntur,Exod.20.Quoad effectus, tentat nos Deus,&c.Deut.13.
units.tr: B. Those who are puffed up with exorcisms on this pretext, that they consist of sacred words alone and have their effects, etc. But the sin is the greater because they abuse the name of God (Exod. 20). As to the effects, God tests us, etc. (Deut. 13).

units.la: III. Quid Paulus? Fert quidem aliquan diu,nimirum spiritus suggestionem exspe ctans. Tandem zelo plenus, & sancta indignatione, spiritum increpat, & in nomine Iesu Christi eijcit.
units.tr: III. What did Paul do? He indeed bears it for some time, namely waiting for the spirit's suggestion. At last, full of zeal and holy indignation, he rebukes the spirit and casts it out in the name of Jesus Christ.

units.la: NOT. 1. Verbi ministros non modo veritatem docere, verumetiam impostu- ras oppugnare debere,nec quicquam ferre,quod veritati deroget,etiamsi cum ipsorum laude coniunctum sit. Ita Christus
units.tr: NOTE 1. Ministers of the Word ought not only to teach the truth but also to attack impostures, and to bear nothing that detracts from the truth, even if it is joined with their own praise. Thus Christ did not permit Satan to speak (Luke 4).

units.la: satanæ non permisit loqui, Luc.4. Blandi-tijs enim falcinare studet, quos alioqui in uictos nouit. Arguuntur, qui iuratos veri-tatis hostes ferendos esse censent.
units.tr: For he seeks to ensnare with flatteries those whom otherwise he knows to be conquered. Here are refuted those who think that sworn enemies of the truth should be tolerated.

units.la: ¶2. Quod ad nomen Christi mox cedit satan. Patet hic. A. Potentia Christi insupe-rabilis. Inuictus putatur satan, vt qui totū mundū subegerat. Omnes gentes sub po-testate tenebrarum, Col.1. Sed potentior Christus, qui tam facile illum deuicit, Ioh. 12.16. Luc.21. Vide dæmoniacos. Et in Apo-stolis quoq; tam efficaciter operatur. Imo obtinete religione Christiana oracula cef-farunt, vt prædictum Soph.2. Mich.5. Præ-stigiæ. Imo vbicunq; Christus regnare in-cipit, regnum satanæ corruit, iuxta primā promisionem, Gen.3. Venit enim Chri-stus, vt opera satanæ destruat, 1.Ioh 3. &c. Seruiat hoc consolationi in tentationi-bus, ne illum timeamus, 1.Ioh.4 5.&c.
units.tr: ¶ 2. That Satan immediately yields at the name of Christ. This is plain here. A. The power of Christ is insuperable. Satan is thought unconquerable, as one who had subdued the whole world: all nations lie under the power of darkness (Col. 1). But Christ is more powerful, who so easily overcomes him (John 12:16; Luke 21). See the demoniacs. And he works so effectively also in the Apostles. Indeed, once the Christian religion prevailed, the oracles ceased, as was foretold (Zeph. 2; Mic. 5). Illusions. Indeed, wherever Christ begins to reign, the kingdom of Satan falls, according to the first promise (Gen. 3). For Christ came to destroy the works of Satan (1 John 3), etc. Let this serve for consolation in temptations, that we need not fear him (1 John 4:5), etc.

units.la: B. Nihil commune esse Christo & Euangelio cum satana. Contra Iudæos, Ioh.8, Ab hoc enim non recipit testimonium.
units.tr: B. That Christ and the Gospel have nothing in common with Satan. Against the Jews (John 8): for he does not receive testimony from him.

units.la: C. Christianis quoque nihil cum diabo-lo commune esse debere, 2.Cor.6. Fugiant ergo vatidicas artes, quibus ille seducit. Scriptura & Christum audiant. Illum auxiliatorem abominentur, vt qui Christum saluatorem agnoscant vnicum. Exo. to. Horreant peccati tyrannidem, qui nobis imperat, Roman. 6. Denique vigilent, & resistant illi constantes in vera fide, 1. Pet. 5. Luc. 22. Eph. 6.
units.tr: C. Christians too ought to have nothing in common with the devil (2 Cor. 6). Let them therefore flee the divinatory arts by which he seduces. Let them hear Scripture and Christ. Let them abhor him as a helper, since they acknowledge Christ as the one Saviour (Exod. 20). Let them shudder at the tyranny of sin, which rules over us (Rom. 6). Finally, let them watch and resist him, steadfast in the true faith (1 Pet. 5; Luke 22; Eph. 6).

units.la: Haec qui facere negligunt, facile illius dolis circumueniuntur. Quare indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: Those who neglect to do these things are easily caught in his snares. Wherefore let us pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXXIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXXXIII.

units.la: 19 Videntes autem Domini abiisse ipsem quaestus sui, prehensum Paulum & Silam, traxerunt in forum ad magistratus.
units.tr: 19 And when her masters saw that their hope of gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the forum before the magistrates.

units.la: 20 Et offerentes eos praefectis dixerunt, Homines isti conturbant civitatem nostram, quum sint Iudaei,
units.tr: 20 And presenting them to the praetors, they said: "These men are throwing our city into confusion, since they are Jews,

units.la: 21 Et annuntiant ritus, quos non licet nobis suscipere, neque vsurpare, quum simus Romani.
units.tr: 21 and they preach customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or practise, since we are Romans."

units.la: 22 Vnà autem insurrexit turba adversus eos, & praefecti diruptis eorum vestibus, iusserunt eos virgis caedi.
units.tr: 22 Then the crowd rose up together against them, and the praetors, tearing off their garments, ordered them to be beaten with rods.

units.la: 24 Quumq; multas plagas eis im posuissent, &c. ad verf. 25.
units.tr: 24 And when they had laid many stripes upon them, etc., to verse 25.

units.la: QVemadmodum Christo in terris agenti, & Euangelium praedicanti, Satan iste partim blanditiis & dolis, partim aperta vi oppositi: ita ijsdem armis aduersus Christi Apostolos, omnesq; veritatis ministros vtitur. Exemplum huius praesens historia exhibet. Paulo enim apud Philippenses docenti, primum blandi- tur, vt ita doctrina illius suspectam reddat, & sibi locum paret. Sed animaduertit Paulus dolum, & eijcit illum: docens, partim Christum diaboli victorem esse, partim Christianis nihil cum hoc commune esse debere, 2. Cor. 6. Quia vero primus conatus non successit satanae, nunc in furorem versus, per puellae dominos apertas inimicitias exercet: in hoc totus in cumbens, vt Apostolos vrbe eijciat. Videamus singula.
units.tr: As Satan dealt with Christ on earth, while he was preaching the gospel, so he used partly flattery and trickery, and partly open force against him, so he uses the same weapons against the apostles of Christ and all the ministers of the truth. The present history sets out an example of this. For when Paul was teaching at Philippi, first Satan flatters him, so that by this means he may render his teaching suspect and prepare a place for himself. But Paul perceives the trick and casts it out, teaching partly that Christ is the conqueror of the devil, and partly that Christians ought to have nothing in common with him (2 Cor. 6). But because Satan's first attempt did not succeed, he now turns to rage and, through the masters of the slave-girl, carries on open enmity, bending all his efforts to this: to drive the apostles out of the city. Let us look at the particulars.

units.la: I. Exponit causam, quae hos contra Apostolos extimulauit: Videntes ipsum quaestus sui abijfe. Auaritia ergo hos exacerbauit, vt non modo veritatem non agnoscerent, verumetiam hostiliter persequerentur.
units.tr: I. He sets out the cause which stirred these men up against the apostles: "when they saw that their hope of gain had gone." Avarice, then, inflamed them, so that they not only refused to acknowledge the truth but even persecuted it with hostility.

units.la: NOT. Quanta auaritia pestis sit. Paulus radicem omnium malorum vocat, 1. Tim. 6. Auaro item nihil scelestius dicitur, Ecclesiast. 10. Apparet hoc in multis rebus priuatim & publice. Sed id nusquam clarius quam in religione cernitur. 1. Animum a Deo auocat, & per se manifesta est idololatria, Matth. 6. Ita nominatur Col. 3. Eph. 5. &c.
units.tr: NOTE. How great a plague avarice is. Paul calls it the root of all evils (1 Tim. 6). Likewise nothing is called more wicked than the covetous man (Ecclesiasticus 10). This appears in many matters, privately and publicly, but nowhere is it seen more clearly than in religion. 1. It draws the mind away from God, and idolatry is plainly its effect (Matt. 6). So it is named in Col. 3 and Eph. 5, etc.

units.la: 2 Religionem facit quæstum, & omnia reddit venalia. Vide Iudæos, Ioh. 2. Matt. 21.12. Ita Petrus nouissimo tempore euen turum prædixit, 2. Pet. 2. &c. Impletur hodie passim in Papatu.
units.tr: 2. It makes religion a source of gain and renders everything saleable. See the Jews (John 2; Matt. 21:12). So Peter foretold that in the last times this would happen (2 Pet. 2, etc.). It is fulfilled today everywhere in Papistry.

units.la: 3. Veritatis impatientes, adeo q; hostes reddit. Furit enim auarus, vt primum quæ stus materiam subtrahis. Hinc proueniunt cofultationes impiæ, proditiones, tur bæ, persecutiones contra veritatem. Exempla in sacerdotibus, Ioh. 11. In Iuda, Io. 12. In præsenti loco, & postea in Demetrio, Act. 19. &c.
units.tr: 3. It makes men impatient of the truth, and indeed makes them its enemies. For the covetous man rages as soon as the material of his gain is taken away. Hence come impious consultations, betrayals, tumults, and persecutions against the truth. Examples are found among the priests (John 11), in Judas (John 12), in the present passage, and afterwards in Demetrius (Acts 19), etc.

units.la: Hodie non alia causa exagitat monachos, episcopos, principes, nobiles, plebeios, milites, &c.
units.tr: Today no other cause stirs up monks, bishops, princes, nobles, commoners, soldiers, etc.

units.la: Imo ipsi euangelici hîc maximè impingunt. Quærunt, quod Ananias & Simon. Actor 5.8. Correpti insaniunt, &c. Cauea-mus eos, & pestem hanc, & eos qui hac moti, ex priuata causa publicam faciunt.
units.tr: Indeed the evangelicals themselves here very often stumble. They seek what Ananias and Sapphira did (Acts 5:8). Seized by madness, etc. Let us beware of them, and of this plague, and of those who, moved by a private cause, make it a public one.

units.la: II. Quid faciunt? Comprehendunt Paulum & Silam. Trahunt in forum & magistratibus offerunt. Accusant amarulenter simul & artificiose: nimirum quòd turbatores sint, & nouarum religionum authores, quas Romanæ leges non ferant. Tertull: Interim personarum circumstantijs causam amplificant, dum se Romanos, il-
units.tr: II. What do they do? They seize Paul and Silas. They drag them into the forum and offer them to the magistrates. They accuse them bitterly and cunningly at once: namely, that they are disturbers and authors of new religions, which Roman laws do not allow. Tertullian: Meanwhile they magnify the case by the circumstances of the persons, while they call themselves Romans and those men Jews.

units.la: los vero Iudeos vocant.Erat enim Iudæo rum nomen inuisum omnibus,vt patebit, Act.18. Et mox totus populus concurrit.
units.tr: For the name of Jews was hateful to all, as will be shown in Acts 18. And soon the whole people runs together.

units.la: NOTA. ¶1.Artes hostium veritatis. Priuatis commodis publicum prætexunt. Sic Caiaphas,Ioh.11.Hodie nil vulgarius. Habent hoc ex suo capite,diabolo,qui pri mam tentationem hoc prætextu velauit, Gen.3. Sic cum Christo agit,Matt.4. Ne- mo se falli patiatur.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The arts of the enemies of the truth. They pretend public grounds for private advantages. So Caiaphas (John 11). Nothing is more commonplace today. They have this from their head, the devil, who in the first temptation veiled it with this pretext (Gen. 3). So he deals with Christ (Matt. 4). Let no one allow himself to be deceived.

units.la: ¶2. Quorum criminum feré accusetur veritas? Seditionis & seductionis. Sic olim Exod.5.1 Reg.18. Amos 7.Iere. 44.37. Ita Christus accusatus, Ioh 18.19 Luc.23. Hodie eadem nobis obijciuntur.
units.tr: 2. With what crimes is the truth usually charged? Sedition and seduction. So of old (Exod. 5; 1 Kings 18; Amos 7; Jer. 44; 37). So Christ was accused (John 18:19; Luke 23). Today the same things are thrown in our faces.

units.la: Patet hic mundi improbitas,quæ in no ftris eo maior est,quod Christiani haberi volunt. Interim seditiosam & seducto-riâ doctrinam dicunt, quæ vnum Christum tradit & in hoc vno omnem salutis ratio-nem monstrat,sicut ipse Christus & Apo-stoli tradiderunt Ioh.14.10.Matth.11.Act. 4.1.Cor.2. &c. Quæ item vitæ innocenti-am & charitatem tradit. Quæ magistrati-bus sua iura permittit,Rom 13. &c. Hor-reamus quæsò tam horribilem calumniam,&c. Agnoscamus autem mundi cœci-tatem,nec moveamur istis calumniis.
units.tr: Here the wickedness of the world is plain, which in our time is greater because men wish to be called Christians. Meanwhile they call the doctrine seditious and seductive which sets forth Christ alone and in him alone shows the whole method of salvation, as Christ himself and the apostles taught (John 14:10; Matt. 11; Acts 4:12; 1 Cor. 2, etc.). It likewise teaches innocence of life and charity. It leaves to the magistrates their rights (Rom. 13, etc.). Let us, I beg you, shudder at so horrible a calumny, etc. But let us acknowledge the blindness of the world, and let us not be moved by these calumnies.

units.la: III.Quid coram magistratibus factum?
units.tr: III. What was done before the magistrates?

units.la: Apostoli ca ut incarce-rantur.
units.tr: The apostles are cast into prison.

units.la: Moxindicta causa virgis cædunrur inno, centiffimi homines. Inde in carcerem conijciuntur, & quidem vt facinorofiffimi singulari cura custodiuntur, donec nimirum causa ipsorum plenius cognoscatur.
units.tr: Soon, the case being decided, the most innocent men are beaten with rods. Then they are thrown into prison, and indeed they are guarded with special care as the most wicked criminals, until, of course, their cause is more fully examined.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Iniustitiæ exemplum in magistratibus his proponitur. Peccant, qui excusandi copiam negant. At isti cum peregrinis & ignotis indignißimè & iniquißimè agunt, nimirum calumnijs & ira seducti. Obseruent ergo omnes magistratus Videant officium suum, Rom. 13. Binè autres. Alexander Magnus. Meminerint Deum esse iudiciorum prasidem, Pfal. 82. 72. 2. Par. 19. Iram ergo moderentur, & nihil aliquo affectu consultore faciant.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. An example of injustice is set forth in these magistrates. They sin who deny the opportunity of defence. But these men treated strangers and unknown men most unworthily and unjustly, no doubt led astray by calumnies and anger. Let all magistrates therefore take note: let them see their duty (Rom. 13). Alexander the Great. Let them remember that God is the president of judgments (Ps. 82; 2 Chr. 19:6-7). Let them therefore moderate their anger and do nothing under the guidance of any passion.

units.la: ¶ 2. Sortem piorum in hoc mundo Peßimis hominibus tuto in hoc viuere licet. Soli pij persecutionem sustinent. Et cum omnibus benefaciant, malefaciant nemini, hanc gratiâ referunt. Applica praesenti exemplo, Sed ita prædictum est, Ioh. 15.16 Marth. 5.16. Ita Paulus 2 Tim. 2. Act. 14. Non offendamur. Oremus.
units.tr: 2. The lot of the godly in this world. Wicked men may live safely in this world. Only the godly endure persecution. And though they do good to all and harm no one, they receive this in return for their kindness. Apply this to the present example. But so it was foretold (John 15:16; Matt. 5:16). So Paul (2 Tim. 2; Acts 14). Let us not be offended. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXXIV.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXXXIV.

units.la: 25 Media autem nocte precantes Paulus & Silas, hymnos canebant: & qui vinčti erant, exaudiebant eos.
units.tr: 25 But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns, and those who were in chains were listening to them.

units.la: 26 Repente vero terræmotus ma gnus extitit, &c.
units.tr: 26 Suddenly, however, a great earthquake arose, etc.

units.la: OVemadmodum scriptura passim de persecutionibus ferendis pios Dei cultores admonet, ita ijsdem opem divinam abunde pollicetur, Psal.34. 145. 146. Matth 5. & 10. Iohan.16. If.65. Exempla vero passim extant, quæ promissiones has verissimas esse docent: qualia habuimus, Act.5.12. &c. Eodem referri debet, quod modo recitari audiuit C. V. quod cum primis memorabile est, eò quod non modò è carcere liberantur Apostoli, verumetiam custos carceris, homo crudelis, & immanissimi sceleris paulò ante mi nister, ad Christum conuertitur. Videamus singula ordine.
units.tr: Just as Scripture everywhere admonishes the pious worshippers of God to bear persecutions, so it also abundantly promises them divine help: Psalm 34, 145, 146; Matthew 5 and 10; John 16; Isaiah 65. Examples too are everywhere present which teach that these promises are most true, such as we had in Acts 5:12 etc. To the same point should be referred what the honourable audience has just heard read, which is especially memorable because the apostles are not only freed from prison, but the jailer also, a cruel man and until a little before a minister of the most savage crime, is converted to Christ. Let us look at the individual points in order.

units.la: I. Docetur quid Apostoli fecerint, post quam indignissimè tractati, & tandem in cippum fuerunt coniecti. Media nocte orauerunt, & laudauerunt Deum, idq; tam alta voce, vt ab reliquis captiuis audiretur. Est hoc constantis fidei argumentum, & lætæ conscientiæ testimonium, qua soli pij in aduersis gaudent, Rom.5. Causam vi dimus Act.5. Gaudent, & Deum laudant, quod digni habiti sint, qui Christi nomine patiantur. Respiciunt in promissiones, Matt.5. Ioh.12.14. Luc.22.2. Tim.2.
units.tr: I. We are taught what the apostles did after they had been most shamefully treated and at last thrown into the stocks. At midnight they prayed and praised God, and that with a voice so loud that it was heard by the other prisoners. This is a proof of steadfast faith and a witness of a joyful conscience, in which only the pious rejoice in adversity, Romans 5. We saw the cause in Acts 5: they rejoice and praise God because they were judged worthy to suffer in the name of Christ. They look to the promises: Matthew 5; John 12, 14; Luke 22; 2 Timothy 2.

units.la: Sed Not. §1. Quod Apostoli orant, qui spiritum sanctum habuerunt, & fide præditi, sciuerunt omnia per Dei prouidentiam geri. Matth.6.10. Hæc ergo non tollit preces, vt quidam argutè ratiocinantur. Nec enim vt ignoranti recitamus nostra, sed fidem nostram fouemus. Sciunt item hoc quoq; perpetuum Dei prouidentiæ decretum esse, vt qui hunc in ad uersis inuocant, exaudiantur, Psalm.34. 50.145. Matt.7. Luc.11.18.
units.tr: But note §1. That the apostles, who had the Holy Spirit and were endowed with faith, knew that all things are governed by the providence of God, Matthew 6:10. Therefore this does not abolish prayers, as some subtly argue. For we do not recite our petitions as if to one who is ignorant, but we nourish our faith. They know likewise that it is a perpetual decree of God's providence that those who call upon him in adversities are heard: Psalm 34, 50, 145; Matthew 7; Luke 11, 18.

units.la: §2. Quid nos in aduersis agere conue-niat. Vnum Deum inuocare. Item non modo orare pro liberatione, verumetiam gratias agere & laudare, &c. Est enim hoc argumentum paterni fauoris, Prou.13. Heb.12. Deinde diuinæ consolationis vis nusquam efficacior est, quàm in aduersis, Psalm 94.2. Cor.1. Ideo Petrus etiam hnc orditur, 1.Pet.1. Peccant murmuratores, 1.Cor.10.
units.tr: §2. What it becomes us to do in adversities: to call upon the one God; likewise not only to pray for deliverance but also to give thanks and praise, etc. For this is a sign of a father's favour, Proverbs 13; Hebrews 12. Next, the power of divine consolation is nowhere more effective than in adversity: Psalm 94; 2 Corinthians 1. Therefore Peter also begins here, 1 Peter 1. Murmurers sin, 1 Corinthians 10.

units.la: II. Quid Deus? Terræmotus carceris fundamenta concutit, & omnium vinculà soluit. Fuit hoc Dei opus. Impletur Psal.50.107.
units.tr: II. What God does: the earthquake shakes the foundations of the prison and loosens the chains of all. This was God's work. It is fulfilled in Psalm 50, 107.

units.la: Not. §Vim fidelis precationis. A. Nubes penetrat & ascendit in Dei consperum, qui non negligit, Eccles.35. Psal.12. 34.56. Est hæc magna consolatio. B. Effi-cit, quæ humanis viribus impossibilia sunt
units.tr: Note §. The power of faithful prayer: A. It penetrates the clouds and ascends into the presence of God, who does not neglect it, Ecclesiasticus 35; Psalm 12, 34, 56. This is a great consolation. B. It effects what is impossible to human powers

units.la: Iac.5. Nam rerum natura cedere cogitur Deo, suorum precibus expugnato. Vide Exod.14.1.Reg 18. Ian 3. Simile habuimus Act.12.Nemo igitur desperet, quando hæc arma nemo potest eripere & eædem tanto fortiores sunt, quanto grauius premimur.Nemo etiam affligat innocentes, quorum preces & clamores tantæ apud Deum authoritatis sunt, Exod.22. Gen.4.&c.Oremus.
units.tr: James 5. For the nature of things is compelled to yield to God, when his people's prayers have overcome it. See Exodus 14; 1 Kings 18; Jonah 3. We had a similar case in Acts 12. Let no one therefore despair, since no one can snatch these weapons away, and they are all the stronger the more heavily we are oppressed. Let no one also afflict the innocent, whose prayers and cries have such authority with God: Exodus 22; Genesis 4, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXXV.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXXV.

units.la: 27 Expergefactus autem Commentariensis, quum videret fores carceris apertas, educto gladio, erat seipsum interempturus existimans vinctos effugisse:
units.tr: 27 And the jailer, awaking, when he saw the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners had escaped.

units.la: 28 Clamauit autem Paulus voce magna, dicens: Ne quid feceris tibi ipsi mali, omnes enim hic sumus.
units.tr: 28 But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying: Do not harm yourself, for we are all here.

units.la: 29 Is vero petito lumine irrupit, & tremefactus accidit Paulo & Silæ ad pedes.
units.tr: 29 Then he called for a light, sprang in, and fell trembling at the feet of Paul and Silas.

units.la: 30 Et productis ipsis foras, ait, Domini, quid me oportet facere, ut seruer? &c. ad verf. 33.
units.tr: 30 And bringing them out, he said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? etc., to verse 33.

units.la: ETsi Deus credentes variè tentari & exerceri sinat, idem tamen suarum propromissionum memor, non illos modo eripit & seruat, sed fere ipsorum afflictioni bus ad sui regni propagationem vtitur, quando ea occasione veritatem discunt, qui prius alieni & hostes erant. Exempla sunt palsim, vt Act. 8.9, &c. In primis tamen memorabile est, quod hoc Cap. describitur. Audiuimus enim Apostolos Philippi s caesos & in carcerem coniectos fuisse, & quidem eiusmodi homini commissos fuisse, qui & ipsos oderat, & ab omni humanitate alienus erat. Liberantur tamen & quidem sic, vt ipse custos reti Euangelij captus Christo adducatur. Describit autem tem huius conuersionem Lucas diligenter, partim vt Dei gratiam agnoscamus, qui hostes quoque recipit, partim vt hinc petamus veras conuersionis exemplum.
units.tr: Although God allows believers to be tried and exercised in various ways, he nevertheless, mindful of his promises, not only rescues and preserves them but often uses their very afflictions to spread his kingdom, when those who were formerly strangers and enemies learn the truth from such an occasion. Examples are found everywhere, as in Acts 8 and 9, etc. Yet the most memorable is that described in this chapter. For we have heard that the apostles of Philippi were beaten and thrown into prison, and indeed committed to a man who hated them and was a stranger to all kindness. Yet they are freed, and in such a way that the jailer himself is taken captive and brought to Christ. Luke describes his conversion carefully, partly so that we may acknowledge the grace of God, who receives even enemies, and partly so that we may seek from it a true example of conversion.

units.la: 1. Occasio inspicienda, vbi repetendum quod dictum est de terræmotu. Expergefactus ergo custos, videt fores apertas, & quia captiuos aufugisse putat, seipsum vult occidere. Causa, legum seueritas, cuius exemplum Act. 12.
units.tr: 1. The occasion is to be considered, where what was said about the earthquake must be repeated. So the jailer, awakened, sees the doors open, and because he thinks the captives have fled, he wants to kill himself. The cause is the severity of the laws, of which an example is Acts 12.

units.la: Quæ etsi non probari, arguit tamen Christianos, qui sanctas leges sinunt collabi, & ipsi dimittunt quos tolli præstat. Quoad verò hunc, vult maiore infamiam vitare communi errore deceptus, quo hoc fortitudo putabatur.
units.tr: Although this cannot be approved, it nevertheless shows up Christians who allow holy laws to collapse and themselves let go those whom it would be better to keep. As for him, he wishes to avoid greater infamy, deceived by a common error by which this was thought to be courage.

units.la: Sic gentes dementârat diabolus. Sed reuera est ignauia coniuncta cum inobedientia, Ezech.18. & desperatione. In solis reprobis exempla habes, vt Saule, Iuda, &c. Itaque cauendæ diaboli suggestiones Ioh.8. Et Paulus hunc recte reuocat.
units.tr: Thus the devil had driven the nations mad. But in truth it is cowardice joined with disobedience, Ezek. 18, and despair. In the reprobate alone you have examples, such as Saul, Judas, etc. Therefore the suggestions of the devil must be guarded against, John 8. And Paul rightly recalls him.

units.la: NOT. Sortem eorum, qui seruiunt impijs, & consentiunt. Periclitantur corpore & anima. Perierat hic, &c. Vide Psal.1.
units.tr: NOTE. The lot of those who serve the impious and consent: they are in danger in body and soul. He had perished here, etc. See Psalm 1.

units.la: § 2. Charitatis Christianæ exemplum: qua Paulus tam amicè consulit ei, qui ipsum tam iniquè tractuerat, Sic iubemur Matth.5. Arguuntur, qui non lacessiti oderunt, inuident, gaudent item aliorum perditione, &c.
units.tr: § 2. An example of Christian charity: Paul so kindly counsels him who had treated him so unjustly. Thus we are commanded, Matt. 5. Those are reproved who, though not provoked, hate, envy, and rejoice also in the ruin of others, etc.

units.la: II. Quid carcerarius? Expendit miraculum. Confert eum eo Apostolorum fortitudinem & ingenuitatem. Ideo colligit, quàm grauiter peccârit, & sensu numinis tactus irruit, procidit, quærit quid faciat?
units.tr: II. What of the jailer? He weighs the miracle. He compares with it the courage and frankness of the apostles. Therefore he infers how gravely he had sinned, and, touched by a sense of the divine power, he rushes in, falls down, and asks what he should do.

units.la: NOT. § Quid in simili casu fieri debeat. Non leuiter negligantur ea, quibus nos excitat Deus, siue signa sint, siue verbum. Hoc Pharaoni nocuit & multis hodie. 2. Descendamus in nosipsos, & compungamur, 3. Quæramus. Sic Act.2.
units.tr: NOTE. § What ought to be done in a like case. The things by which God stirs us, whether signs or the word, are not lightly neglected. This harmed Pharaoh and many today. 2. Let us descend into ourselves and be pricked. 3. Let us seek. So Acts 2.

units.la: III Apostoli paucis agunt. Primo summam salutis proponunt, & hanc in Christo monstrant. Dei gde, quia hoc non potest rat sufficere rudi & Barbaro, prædicârunt illi & familiæ Euangeliũ, quo docuerunt, quis Iesus ille sit, & quid in eo nobis datum.
units.tr: III. The apostles act briefly. First they set out the sum of salvation and show it in Christ. Since this could not suffice for a rude and barbarous man, they preached the gospel to him and his household, teaching who that Jesus is and what has been given us in him.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Quòd vnam fidė in Christum docent Hæc ergo sufficit, quia Christum apprehendit, qui nobis factus est, &c. 1. Cor. 1. Actor. 4. Obseruabis autem, quòd hanc prædicârunt ex verbo Dei. Ergo non est imaginaria persuasio, sed ex Dei verbo dependet, Ioh. 6. Discamus ipsi etiam vno Christo niti, ne quicquam admittere Euangelio contrarium, Gal. 1.
units.tr: NOTE. That they teach faith in Christ alone. This therefore suffices, because he lays hold of Christ, who was made for us, etc., 1 Cor. 1, Acts 4. You will observe also that they preached this from the word of God. Therefore it is not an imaginary persuasion, but depends on the word of God, John 6. Let us also learn to rest on Christ alone, lest we admit anything contrary to the gospel, Gal. 1.

units.la: 1. Opera carcerarij, quibus fidem testatur. 1 Eduxit ex carcere & abluit, &c. Fit hoc contra magistratus mandatum. Imo qui prius sese occidere voluit, nunc spontē hoc periculum subit. NOT. ¶ Effectus fidei primus, quòd Deo obedientes & animosos reddit in eius præceptis, licet mundus diuersum velit. Idem omnes fidelēs sentiunt quod Petrus, Act. 4. 5.
units.tr: 1. The jailer's works, by which he testifies his faith. First, he led them out of the prison and washed them, etc. This was done against the command of the magistrate. Indeed, he who had first wished to kill himself now willingly undertakes this danger. NOTE. The first effect of faith is that it makes men obedient to God and courageous in his precepts, although the world wills otherwise. All believers feel what Peter felt, Acts 4, 5.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui torpent, & magistratuū iura, leges, mundi amicitias, &c. allegant.
units.tr: Those are reproved who grow sluggish and allege the rights of magistrates, laws, and the friendships of the world, etc.

units.la: II. Baptizatur cum tota domo. Quòd nihil ex Euangelio didicit, Mat. 28. Non ergo contemnit sacramenta, nec ex præmissa fidei doctrina paralogizat, &c.
units.tr: II. He is baptized with his whole household. He had learned nothing from the gospel in vain, Matt. 28. He therefore does not despise the sacraments, nor reason fallaciously from the preceding doctrine of faith, etc.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Zelum verè credentium, qui
units.tr: NOTE. The zeal of truly believing men, who

units.la: {a}Cap. 16 suos quoque Deo consecratos voluntas Sic Lydia.Abraham,Gen.18.Requirit hoc Deus Gen.17.Deut.6. Pfalm.78.Matt.19. Arguuntur tam Anabaptistae quàm qui su os liberos plane negligunt,vel etiam corrumpunt.
units.tr: {a} Chap. 16. They also consecrate their own to God, as Lydia did. Abraham, Gen. 18. God requires this, Gen. 17, Deut. 6, Psalm 78, Matt. 19. Those are reproved who are Anabaptists, as well as those who plainly neglect or even corrupt their children.

units.la: III. Apponit eis mensam, nimirum quod miserè vel omnino non coenatos esse scia ret.Nota. Fidei coniunctam esse charitatem. Quia enim Deo nititur, hunc non potest non amare. At qui Deum amat, proximum quoq; amabit, quem illi adeo curae esse nouit, 1.Ioh.4. Hinc illa, Ioh.15. Obseruent vsurarij,inuidi,ofores,&c.
units.tr: III. He sets a table before them, doubtless because he knew they had eaten miserably or not at all. Note that charity is joined to faith. For because he rests on God, he cannot but love him. And he who loves God will also love his neighbour, whom he knows to be so dear to God, 1 John 4. Hence that saying, John 15. Let usurers, the envious, and oppressors take note.

units.la: IV. Exultat cum tota domo,eò quòd credidisset & se ad Ecclesiam pertinere sci ret. Atqui imminebat ei periculum grauissimum. Sed vt fides facit obedientiam, ita etiam omnia vincit, vt nulla tentatio coelestis gaudij sensum possit eripere, Philipp.3.4.Rom.5.
units.tr: IV. He rejoices with his whole household, because he had believed and knew that he belonged to the Church. Yet the most grievous danger was hanging over him. But as faith produces obedience, so it also conquers all things, so that no temptation can take away the sense of heavenly joy, Phil. 3, 4, Rom. 5.

units.la: Interim Nota. Fidem mihi me esse o tiosam. Quid enim bonorum operum hic desiderauerit? Emendat iniurias factas Apostolis.Deo praestat obedientiam cum praesenti periculo. Sacramentis rite vtitur.Suos etiam curat, vt Ecclesiae conse crentur. Charitatem & beneficentiam exercet. Adhaec inter pericula gaudet. Atqui
units.tr: Meanwhile note that faith is never idle. For what good works did he lack here? He makes amends for the injuries done to the apostles, renders obedience to God in the face of present danger, uses the sacraments rightly, cares also that his own be consecrated to the Church, exercises charity and beneficence, and besides rejoices amid dangers. Yet

units.la: {a} Fides nunquam est otiosa. qui solam fidem praeceperant Apostoli. Ergo haec fructus tantos protulit.
units.tr: {a} Faith is never idle. The apostles had taught faith alone. Therefore it brought forth such great fruits.

units.la: Confutantur, qui fidei doctrinam bonis operibus inimicam dicunt. Item qui sub fidei praetextu carni indulgent. His Apostolus loquitur, Iac. 2. Rom. 6. Baptista item, Matth. 3. In horum ergo considera-tione versamur, & indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: Those are refuted who say the doctrine of faith is hostile to good works, and likewise those who under the pretext of faith indulge the flesh. The Apostle speaks to these, James 2, Rom. 6. The Baptist likewise, Matt. 3. In considering these things we are occupied, and let us pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXXVI.

units.la: 35 Die autem exorto praefecti miserunt viatores qui dicerent, Dimitte homines illos.
units.tr: 35 When day came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: "Let those men go."

units.la: 36 Annuntiavit autem commentariensis hos sermones Paulo, Miserunt, inquit, praefecti ut dimittamini, nunc igitur egressi ite in pace.
units.tr: 36 The jailer reported these words to Paul: "The magistrates have sent orders that you are to be released. Now, then, go out and go in peace."

units.la: 37 Paulus autem dixit eis, Caesos nos publice, indicta causa, quum cives Romani, conjecerunt in carcerem, et nunc clam nos ejiciunt? non profecto: sed veniant ipsi, et nos educant.
units.tr: 37 But Paul said to them: "They beat us publicly, without a trial, though we are Roman citizens, and threw us into prison. Are they now releasing us in secret? Certainly not! Let them come themselves and lead us out."

units.la: 38 Renuntiaverunt autem praefecti viatores verba ista: timueruntque audito eos Romanos esse.
units.tr: 38 The officers reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that the men were Romans.

units.la: 39 Et venientes precati sunt eos, et eductos rogarunt ut egrederentur ex urbe.
units.tr: 39 They came and begged them, and after leading them out, asked them to leave the city.

units.la: 40 Egressi autem e carcere, intro ierunt ad Lydiam : & visis fratribus consolati junt eos, & egressi sunt.
units.tr: 40 Then, leaving the prison, they went to Lydia's house, and when they had seen the brothers, they comforted them and departed.

units.la: QVoniam Deus veritas est, nemi‐nem falsis persuasionibus & imagi‐nationibus ludit, (sed quæcunque pollicetur, reipsa præstat. Videre est hoc in præ‐senti exemplo. Dei promissio est, quod su‐os in tribulationibus exaudire & iuuare velit, Psal. 50. & 34. Isa. 65. &c. His quia se accommodant Paulus & Silas, mirabili‐ter liberantur, imo accerrimum hostem vident amicu factu esse. Sed nihil adhuc effectum videri poterat, sed Carcerarius quoq; in periculu adductus esse videtur.
units.tr: Since God is truth, he mocks no one with false persuasions and fancies, but what he promises he actually performs. This can be seen in the present example. It is God's promise that he wishes to hear and help his people in their tribulations (Ps. 50, 34; Isa. 65, etc.). Because Paul and Silas trusted this promise, they are wonderfully freed, and indeed they see their bitterest enemy made their friend. But it could still seem that nothing had been achieved, and the jailer himself seems to have been brought into danger.

units.la: Sequitur ergo quod cœptum liberatio nis beneficium absoluit, nimirum quod magistratus authoritas liberos dimittit. Mirifice tamen exagitantur impij illi, vt ipsis inuitis Deus seruos suos extorserit. Videamus singula.
units.tr: It follows, then, that the benefit of liberation that had begun is completed, namely in that the authority of the magistrate dismisses them free. Yet those impious men are wonderfully harassed, so that God wrested his servants from them against their will. Let us look at the particulars.

units.la: I. Magistratus mittunt apparitores, qui Apostolos dimittere iubeant, nimirum clam (vt Pauli verba innuunt) & sic vt simul vt be eijciantur. Agnouerunt ergo tum iuam iniustitiam, tum illorum innocentiam. Cæterum qua occasione id fecerint, non ex-primitur. Iniustitiam certè & leuitatem simul produnt. Interim communi impio- rum more dolo agunt, & scelus suum frau- dulenter tegere volunt. Apostolos enim in suspicione venire volunt, quasi illi male fidi ebscij, carceribus effractis fugerunt. Sceleris ergo illos pudet quidem, sed non vere poenitet, quin suae tantummodo famae metuunt.
units.tr: I. The magistrates send officers to order that the apostles be dismissed, clearly in secret (as Paul's words imply), and so that they are thrust out at the same time. They acknowledged, then, both their own injustice and the innocence of those men. Yet the occasion for their action is not stated. Certainly they reveal both injustice and fickleness at once. Meanwhile they act with the common deceit of the impious and want to conceal their crime by fraud. For they want the apostles to come under suspicion, as if those faithless men had fled after breaking out of the prison. So their crime shames them, certainly, but they do not truly repent; they fear only for their reputation.

units.la: NOT. 1. Qualis sit fere impiorum poenitentia? Propter homines aliquando illos pudet suae nequitiae, sed non poenitent examino. Sic Saul, 1 Sam. 15. Id vero nil iuuat, quia interea Dei verbum oderunt, Io. 3. Discamus nos peccatum agnoscere, de illo dolere, nec tegere cum aliorum in familia, imo illud publicare ad aliorum emen-dationem. Vide Dauidem, 2. Sam. 11. 12. Psalm. 51. Sic Paulus 1. Cor. 15. 1. Timoth. 2. Gal. 1.
units.tr: NOTE 1. What is the repentance of the impious like? Sometimes they are ashamed of their wickedness for the sake of men, but they do not repent before the judge. So Saul, 1 Sam. 15. This, however, does them no good, because meanwhile they hate the word of God, John 3. Let us learn to recognize sin, to grieve over it, and not to cover it up, whether in our own household or another's; indeed to make it public for the correction of others. See David, 2 Sam. 11, 12; Ps. 51. So Paul, 1 Cor. 15; 1 Tim. 2; Gal. 1.

units.la: 2. Quàm facilè sibi ipsis grauissima dele-ctâ ignoscant impij magistratus. Quid ab his indignius fieri poterat? Nunc suf-ficere existimant, si non maiori iniuria afficiant. De emendatione & satisfactione verbum nullum. Frequens hoc hodie, si quando pauperum & contemptorum causae agantur, &c. Item cultorum Christi, &c.
units.tr: 2. How easily the impious magistrates pardon themselves for the gravest crimes! What could be more shameful than this? Now they think it enough if they do not inflict a greater injury. There is no word of amendment or satisfaction. This is common today, when the causes of the poor and the despised are heard, etc., and likewise those of the worshippers of Christ, etc.

units.la: Sed cogitent iudices, sed a Deo constitu-
units.tr: But let the judges consider that they have been appointed by God,

units.la: tos esse, cuius iudicium est, & cui ipsi ra- tionem reddituri sint, Rom. 14. Deut. 11. 2. Par. 19. Pf. 82. Pretiosu ergo ducantPf. 72
units.tr: whose judgment it is, and to whom they themselves must render an account (Rom. 14; Deut. 11; 2 Chron. 19; Ps. 82). Let them therefore count it precious (Ps. 72).

units.la: ¶ 3. Dei potentiam, qui impijs suos extorquere potest, licet illi in impietate sua perseuerent. Sic in Aegypto factum, vt cogerent Aegyptij exire Israelé, & simul auro & argento onerarent, &c. Exod. 12. Ita Saul Dauidem absoluit, cum moxad ingenium redeat, 2. Sam. 24. 26. Sic factum Actor. 4 5.
units.tr: 3. The power of God, who can wrest his people from the impious even when they persist in their impiety. So it was in Egypt, where the Egyptians were compelled to let Israel go, and were laden with gold and silver, etc. (Exod. 12). So Saul absolved David, though soon he returned to his former disposition (1 Sam. 24, 26). So it happened in Acts 4. 5.

units.la: Consoletur hoc nos, ne incurabili impiorum malitia terreamur. Pergant illi vt libet, attamen vasa Dei sunt, qui ipsis etiam pro suo arbitrio vtitur, Rom. 9 &c.
units.tr: Let this console us, so that we are not terrified by the incurable malice of the impious. Let them carry on as they please; nevertheless they are vessels of God, who uses even them according to his own will (Rom. 9, etc.).

units.la: ¶ I. Custos laetus hoc renuntiat, nimirum non intelligens fraudem, quae est simplicitas filiorum lucis, Luc. 16. Ita hodie multi bene rem gestam putant, si qui viui dimittantur, quorum vita periclitabatur. Interim non vident praeiudicio grauari causam totam, & Euangelio ostium claudi.
units.tr: I. The jailer reports this joyfully, not understanding the deceit, which is the simplicity of the sons of light (Luke 16). So today many think the matter well handled if those whose lives were in danger are released alive. Meanwhile they do not see that the whole cause is burdened by prejudice, and the door of the gospel is closed.

units.la: Rectius ergo Paulus, qui hanc gratiam respuit fortissimè. Conqueritur de illata iniuria. Allegat Rom. ciuitatis priuilegiu, vt etiam Act. 22. Praeterea honorificè vult deduci. Nec fastuosus est vel impatiens, sed habet causas fui facti graues: A. Non vult Euangelium mala suspicione grauari. Id enim teneros adhuc in fide offendit. set, & impijs calumniandi occasionem dedisset. B. Timorem inoutit ferocibus illis, vt posthac manus cohibeant, in Christi sidellibus vexandis.
units.tr: Paul therefore acts more rightly, for he most stoutly rejects this kind of grace. He complains of the injury done to him and appeals to the privilege of Roman citizenship, as also in Acts 22. Moreover, he wishes to be escorted out with honour. Nor is he haughty or impatient, but he has grave reasons for his action: A. He does not want the gospel burdened with a bad suspicion, for this would offend those still weak in the faith and would have given the impious an occasion to slander. B. He strikes fear into those fierce men, so that afterwards they restrain their hands from harassing the faithful of Christ.

units.la: No T. 1. Non eam esse Christianae patientiae rationem, vt quiduis impune permittatur impijs. Imo arguendi sunt & coercendi quando possumus. Asserenda tum Dei gloria, tum nostra innocentia &c. Vide Luc. 22. Ioh. 18. Act. 25.
units.tr: NOTE 1. This is not the rule of Christian patience, that anything should be allowed to the impious with impunity. Rather, they must be reproved and restrained whenever we can. Both the glory of God and our innocence must be asserted, etc. See Luke 22; John 18; Acts 25.

units.la: 2. Licere pijs, legibus & priuilegijs politicis uti ad sui defensionem & propagationem gloriae Dei. Hinc est, quod alibi prouocat Paulus & armato praesidio vtitur. Act. 25. Contra Anabaptistas,
units.tr: 2. It is lawful for the pious to use legal and political privileges for their own defence and for the spreading of God's glory. Hence it is that Paul elsewhere appeals to Caesar and uses an armed guard (Acts 25). Against the Anabaptists.

units.la: III. Timent nunc etiam iudices, quos ante pudebat tantum. Sciebant enim quae esset Romanorum in suo iure vindicando seueritas. Cic. in Verr. Est hic neruus rerumpub. Veniunt ergo, deprecantur culpam, honorificè educunt.
units.tr: III. Now the judges also fear, whom before they were ashamed of only. For they knew how severe the Romans were in vindicating their rights (Cicero against Verres). This is the sinew of the commonwealth. So they come, beg pardon for the fault, and lead them out with honour.

units.la: No T. Impiorum ingenium. Non timent Deum, sed homines tantum: apud quos, si impunitas detur, quiduis audent. Causa est, quod non credunt Deum esse, Ps. 14. 53. 94. Longè aliter pij. Vides ergo legibus & executione opus esse, &c.
units.tr: NOTE. The nature of the impious: they do not fear God but only men, among whom, if impunity is granted, they dare anything. The cause is that they do not believe God exists (Ps. 14; 53; 94). The pious are quite otherwise. You see, therefore, that laws and their execution are needed, etc.

units.la: 2. Quorsum exeant temeraria iudicia magistratuū, &c. Pudorem & consusio nem,deinde etiam pericula afferunt. Exempla sunt,&c. Discant iudices fraenare affectus & deliberare &c. Interim elucet hic innocentiae vis,quae impios, quamuis potentissimos confundit. Vide 2. Sam. 24. 26. &c. Ita pij de hostibus suis triumphant
units.tr: 2. Where rash judgments of magistrates lead, etc. They bring shame and confusion, and then also dangers. There are examples, etc. Let judges learn to restrain their passions and to deliberate, etc. Meanwhile the power of innocence shines forth here, which confounds the impious, however powerful they are (see 2 Sam. 24, 26, etc.). So the pious triumph over their enemies.

units.la: IV. Apostoli non ita discedunt, ut simul Ecclesiam negligant, sed apud Lydiā collectos fratres inuisunt, &c. Postea Epistolam scribit Paulus, quae docet quam felici ter haec Ecclesia profecerit, cuius tam tri ste fuit initium
units.tr: IV. The apostles do not depart in such a way as to neglect the Church at the same time, but visit the brothers gathered at Lydia's house, etc. Afterwards Paul writes an Epistle, which shows how happily this Church has progressed, though its beginning was so sad.

units.la: Patet hic, nullis impiorum conatibus Euangelij cursum impediri, Iod. 3. 2. Tim. 2. Pelluntur aliquando ministri. Sed illis tacentibus lapides clamant, Luc. 19. Oremus.
units.tr: It is clear here that the course of the gospel is impeded by no attempts of the impious (John 3; 2 Tim. 2). Ministers are sometimes driven out, but while they are silent, the stones cry out (Luke 19). Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XVII. HOMILIA CXXXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVII. HOMILY CXXXVII.

units.la: QVum autem iter fecissent per Amphibolim & Apollonium, venerunt Thessalonicam, vbi erat Synagoga Iudaeorum.
units.tr: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.

units.la: 2 Paulus autem sicut consueuerat introiuit ad eos, & per Sabbatha tria disseruit cum eis ex Scripturis.
units.tr: And Paul, as was his custom, went in to them, and for three sabbaths reasoned with them from the Scriptures.
