units.la: ¶ 3. Quomodo iudicabit? In iustitia. Non ergo valebit vllus praetextus, Eph.6 Rom.2. Secundum id quod fecerunt homines, sententia feretur, 2. Cor.5. Obserua contra peccati blanditias & mundi fastu, Pfal.3.6.Mat.16.
units.tr: ¶ 3. How will he judge? "In righteousness." Therefore no pretext will avail (Eph. 6; Rom. 2). Sentence will be pronounced according to what men have done (2 Cor. 5). Observe against the flatteries of sin and the pride of the world (Ps. 3, 6; Matt. 16).

units.la: ¶ 4. Quis iudex? Vir quem præfinuit, Ita Christum nominat propter humanam naturam, vt Petrus, Act 2.Zach.13. Rationem habet rudium.
units.tr: ¶ 4. Who is the judge? "The man whom he has appointed." Christ is so named because of his human nature, as Peter does (Acts 2; Zech. 13). He takes account of the unlearned.

units.la: Seruit: A.Consolationi fidelium. Idem iudex erit, qui modo noster aduocatus est & fidelis Pontifex, 1.Ioh.2 Heb.2.4. Vindex, Iob.19. Nulla ergo damnatio illis m« tuenda erit, Ioh.5 Rom.8.
units.tr: It serves: A. For the comfort of believers. He will be the same judge who is now our advocate and faithful high priest (1 John 2; Heb. 2, 4). He is the avenger (Job 19). Therefore no condemnation is to be feared by them (John 5; Rom. 8).

units.la: B. Terrori impijs. Hi videbunt in què pupugerunt, Zach.12.Ioh.19.Cogentur iu dicem ferre, quem noluerunt saluatorem agnoscere, Pf.2.110.Ioh.5.
units.tr: B. For the terror of the impious. They will see him whom they pierced (Zech. 12; John 19). They will be compelled to bear judgment from him whom they would not acknowledge as Saviour (Ps. 2, 110; John 5).

units.la: III. Occasione hac ad Christi causam delabitur, quam haud dubie multis expli- cuit. Lucas capita duntaxat annotat, & qui dem tria potisima. 1. Quod præfinitus à Deo ad hoc negotium. Sic 1.Pet.1.Ephes.1. Promissiones, Gen.3.22.Pfal 2 &c. Not. ¶ Salutem esse ex gratia, id quod Paulus colligit, Eph.1.Ioh.1.Certam item Ro 8.
units.tr: III. On this occasion he moves to the cause of Christ, which he doubtless explained at length to many. Luke only notes the chief points, and three in particular. 1. That he was appointed by God for this work. So 1 Pet. 1; Eph. 1. The promises (Gen. 3:22; Ps. 2, etc.). Note: that salvation is by grace, which Paul also infers (Eph. 1; John 1). Likewise certain also in Rom. 8.

units.la: II. Fidem omnibus præstitit, id est, In illo & per illum impleuit omnes promissiones, typos, prophetias, &c. Hinc illa, Ioh. 19.Consummatum est. Item Luc.24. Vide etiam Eph.4.&c.
units.tr: II. "He has given assurance to all," that is, in him and through him he has fulfilled all promises, types, prophecies, etc. Hence those words: John 19, "It is finished." Likewise Luke 24. See also Eph. 4, etc.

units.la: NOTA. ¶¶ Impiè falli, qui alias extra Christum salutis rationes mostrant. Quid enim aliud, quàm Deum & Christum mendacij arguunt? 1. Ioh. 5.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶¶ Those who show other grounds of salvation apart from Christ are impiously mistaken. For what else do they do but accuse God and Christ of lying? (1 John 5.)

units.la: III. Resuscitatus ex mortuis. Et per hoc declaratus est Deus & iudex esse, Rom. 1. Resurrectione autem & mortem & totum redemptionis negotium complexus est, Rom. 4. Deuicta mors & peccatum, 1. Cor. 15. Rom. 4. 10. &c.
units.tr: III. "Raised from the dead." And by this God was declared to be the judge (Rom. 1). By the resurrection, moreover, he has embraced both death and the whole business of redemption (Rom. 4). Death and sin are overcome (1 Cor. 15; Rom. 4, 10, etc.).

units.la: Effectus prædicationis Pauliniæ. Aliqui rident audita resurrectione, nimirum Epicuræi, quorum sunt hodie socij multi. Alij denuo audire cupiunt, quod argumentum, illos aliquem gustum percepisse, & proinde meliores primis. Quidá crediunt & adhærent illi palàm. Impletur 2 Cor. 2. Nominatur Dionysius Areopagita iudex, & mulier Damaris.
units.tr: The effect of Paul's preaching. Some mocked when they heard of the resurrection, namely the Epicureans, of whom there are many companions today. Others desired to hear again, which is a sign that they had tasted something and were therefore better than the first. Some believed and openly adhered to him. It is fulfilled (2 Cor. 2). Dionysius the Areopagite is named as a judge, and a woman, Damaris.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Nunquam sine fructu prædicari Euangelium: Licet pauci credant initio, mox tamen crescit Ecclesia, quod & hic factum est. Simile fermenti & synapis, Matth. 13. Non offendamur credentium pauc̈itate, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ The gospel is never preached without fruit. Although few believe at first, the Church soon grows, which also happened here. It is like leaven and mustard seed (Matt. 13). Let us not be offended by the small number of believers, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XVIII. HOMILIA CXLIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII. HOMILY CXLIV.

units.la: POstea Paulus discedens Athenis venit Corinthum.
units.tr: After these things Paul, departing from Athens, came to Corinth.

units.la: 2 Et reperto quodam Iudæo, nomine Aquila, Pontico natione, quinuper venerat ex Italia & Priscilla vxore eius (eo quod edixisset Claudius vt omnes Iudæi Roma excederent) venit ad eos:
units.tr: And having found a certain Jew named Aquila, a Pontic by nation, who had lately come from Italy with Priscilla his wife (because Claudius had issued an edict that all Jews should leave Rome), he came to them.

units.la: 3 Et quia eiusdem erat artificij, mansit apud eos, & operabatur: erat enim ars illorum conficere tabernacula.
units.tr: And because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked, for their craft was making tents.

units.la: 4 Disserebat autem in Synagoga omnibus Sabbathis, & illiciebat tum Iudæos, tum Græcos.
units.tr: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuaded both Jews and Greeks.

units.la: 5 Venerunt autem è Macedonia Silas & Timotheus, constringebatur spiritu Paulus testificans Iudæis Christum Iesum.
units.tr: And when Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

units.la: Escripsit Lucas in præcedenti Capite conuersionem Athenarum, vrbis tum sapientiæ tum religionis fama celeberrimæ. Huic commodè subijcitur Corinthi, vrbis corruptissimæ conuersio, in qua spiritus Christi & Euangelij virtus tam clarè emicuit, vt hanc Paulus sui Apostolatus sigillum dicat, 1.Cor. 9. Fuit enim ciuitas clarissima emporio propter situm, & proinde opulenta, adeoq; lumen Græciæ. Ex diuitijs autem & mercatorum confluentia cor-
units.tr: Luke wrote in the preceding chapter of the conversion of Athens, a city famed both for wisdom and for religion. Fitly joined to this is the conversion of Corinth, a most corrupt city, in which the Spirit of Christ and the power of the Gospel shone out so clearly that Paul calls this the seal of his apostleship, 1 Cor. 9. For the city was very famous as a trading centre because of its site, and therefore wealthy, and indeed the light of Greece. But from its riches and the crowding of merchants it was steeped in corrupt morals of such a kind that it gave rise to proverbs, etc. Above all it was notorious for fornication, as also appears in 1 Cor. 6 and 5. Paul came into this city not without the divine will, as will become clear. There was a great people for the Lord, etc.

units.la: Corinthus
units.tr: Corinth

units.la: qualis corruptissimis moribus imbuta, prouerbijs locum fecit, &c. In primis fcortatione nobilitata, vt apparet etiam, 1. Cor. 6. & 5. In hanc vrbem Paulus venit, non fine numine, vt patebit. Multus populus Domino erat, &c.
units.tr: What a city it was, steeped in most corrupt morals, which gave rise to proverbs, and so on. In particular, it was notorious for fornication, as is also evident from 1 Cor. 6 and 5. Paul came into this city not without the divine will, as will become clear. There was a large people for the Lord, and so on.

units.la: Exemplum insigne proponitur tum bonitatis Dei erga peccatores (1. Timot. 1. 2.) tum virtutis Euangelij. Confer enim virtutis splendorem, opes & corruptione cum Pauli ignobili conditione, & ridiculus vi-debitur ipsius conatus. Attamen intra fe-quiannum reformationem inuehit, quam nullus legislator persuadere potuisset. Videres quantum possit ferium studium. Obseruent ministri & magistratus. Non teme re ergo fit, quod tam diligenter narrantur singula.
units.tr: Here is a notable example both of the goodness of God towards sinners (1 Tim. 1, 2) and of the power of the Gospel. For compare the splendour of its power, its wealth and its corruption with Paul's humble condition, and his undertaking will seem ridiculous. Yet within a year and a half he brought in a reformation which no lawgiver could have persuaded them to accept. You would see how much earnest zeal can achieve. Let ministers and magistrates take note. It is therefore no accident that each detail is related so carefully.

units.la: I. Hospitium Pauli describitur, quod haud dubie se dignum quaesiuit, iuxta Christi praeceptum, Mat. 10. Luc. 10. Fuit hoc apud Aquilam Pontium, qui Roma paulo ante pulsus erat, ideoque bis exul. Erant tunc Iudaei miserrimi. Christi sanguine pollutos sequebatur vltio. Natura seditio & deinde fames (Act. 13.) potuit causa esse edicti. Ad hunc diuertit, quia fidelis erat, vt opera restantur. Quia exul potuit peregrinis condolere, iuxta illud, Exo. 22.
units.tr: I. Paul's lodging is described, which he surely sought as one worthy of it, in keeping with Christ's precept, Matt. 10, Luke 10. He lodged with Aquila the Pontic, who had been expelled from Rome shortly before, and was therefore doubly an exile. The Jews at that time were most wretched; the vengeance of Christ's blood pursued them. Their natural sedition and then the famine (Acts 13) may have been the cause of the edict. Paul turned aside to him because he was faithful, as the works attest. Because an exile could sympathise with strangers, in keeping with that text, Exod. 22.

units.la: Cap.18. Quia eiusdem artificij: apud illos ergo operatur.
units.tr: Chap. 18. Because of the same trade: therefore he works with them.

units.la: Not 1. Aquilam insigne fidei & charitatis exemplum. Homo mechanicus, & proinde non omnino dives. Adhaec exul. Recipit tamen ad se Christi ministrum, magna cum diuitum Corinthiorum infamia. Imo Ecclesiam quoq; habet domesticam, 1 Cor.15.16. Rom.16.
units.tr: Note 1. Aquila is a notable example of faith and charity. He was a craftsman, and therefore not altogether rich; moreover he was an exile. Yet he received into his home a minister of Christ, to the great disgrace of the wealthy Corinthians. Indeed he also had a church in his house, 1 Cor. 16, Rom. 16.

units.la: Arguuntur hoc exemplo, qui cum opus lenti in pace degunt, tamen Christi fideli-bus officium negant. Memineris non temere ad te venire exules, quos alio Deus deducere poterat. Vult te exemplo illorum docere & probare fidem tuam. Memineris item promissionum, Matt.10 25. Act.20.Heb.11. Aquila hinc factus celebrimus, &c.
units.tr: By this example are rebuked those who, living at ease in peace while their work is slight, nevertheless deny the duty owed to Christ's faithful. Remember that exiles who come to you are not come by chance, whom God could have led elsewhere. He wishes by their example to teach you and to prove your faith. Remember likewise the promises, Matt. 10:25, Acts 20, Heb. 11. Aquila, from this point on, became most famous, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Paulum, in quo praeclarae virtutes lucent. A. Fides firma, qua instructus non offenditur, quando se tam sordide excipi videt. Noverat quod scribit, 1. Corin. 1. Simile exemplum in Macedonia praebuit, Actor.16.
units.tr: ¶ 2. Paul, in whom outstanding virtues shine. A. Firm faith, by which, being strengthened, he is not offended when he sees himself received so meanly. He knew what he wrote, 1 Cor. 1. He gave a similar example in Macedonia, Acts 16.

units.la: B. Aequitas charitati coniuncta. Non abutitur horum bonitate, sed laborat: tum ne ipsis onerosus sit, 2. Cor. 11. tum ne Apostolis falsis, qui hoc nomine obrepebat, ef-set inferior, 1. Cor. 9. Alioqui non generale dole dogma hinc concludendum, &c. Vide 1.Cor.9.Mat. 10. Adhæc quod ab aliis accepit Paulus,2.Cor.11 Phil.4.
units.tr: B. Fairness joined with charity. He does not abuse their kindness, but labours, both lest he be burdensome to them, 2 Cor. 11, and lest he be inferior to the false apostles who crept in under this pretence, 1 Cor. 9. Otherwise one should not conclude from this a general dogma of ..., etc. See 1 Cor. 9, Matt. 10. Moreover, what Paul received from others, 2 Cor. 11, Phil. 4.

units.la: Interim arguuntur laruati Episcopi, qui cum opes Ecclesiæ vsurpent, Ecclesijs tamen non seruiunt. Item Euangelici ventres, qui nihil nisi lucrum quærunt, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile are rebuked the masked bishops, who, while they seize the revenues of the Church, nevertheless do not serve the churches. Likewise the Gospel-bellies, who seek nothing but gain, etc.

units.la: II. Vt in Christi regno propagando se gesserit, docetur. 2. Disputabat per omnia sabbatha in Synagoga. Obseruat religionem sabbathi & sacrorum cœtuum.
units.tr: II. How he conducted himself in propagating Christ's kingdom is taught. 2. He disputed in the synagogue on every Sabbath. He observes the religion of the Sabbath and of the sacred assemblies.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Ab omni religione alienissimos esse, qui aspernantur & negligunt quæ Deus religionis exercendæ causa instituit. Christum vide.
units.tr: NOTE. Those are most alien from all religion who scorn and neglect what God has instituted for the exercise of religion. Look to Christ.

units.la: II. Suadebat Iudæis & Græcis Senses est illum moderatione vsum esse, ac prudenti ordine tradidisse salutis mysteria. Hærebant in lege. Docuit ergo omnes nos peccatores esse, nec legem posse exequi & proinde per hanc neminem iustificari,Rom 7.8. &c. Inde ostendit alio nobis iustificatore opus esse,&c.Laete aluit, 1.Cor.3.
units.tr: II. He persuaded Jews and Greeks. The sense is that he used moderation and delivered the mysteries of salvation in a prudent order. They clung to the law. He therefore taught that all of us are sinners, that no one can keep the law, and that therefore no one is justified through it, Rom. 7, 8, etc. Then he showed that we need another justifier, etc. He nourished them gently, 1 Cor. 3.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Prudentia & moderatione opus esse ministris, ne per æpostero aut con fato ordine animos turbent, Matth 24.2. Tim.2.
units.tr: NOTE. Ministers need prudence and moderation, lest by an untimely or confused order they disturb minds, Matt. 24:2, 2 Tim. 2.

units.la: III. Cum venirent Silas & Timotheus, coarctari coepit spiritum, Vel quod audiret foelicem successum Euangelij apud Macedones: vel quod afficeretur miseria caecutientis populi, vt Christus Matth.9. Certe feruentiorem spiritus motum sensit, qui fecit vt acrius instaret, & apertius testaretur, Iesum esse Christum, id est, Salvatorem, &c.
units.tr: III. When Silas and Timothy came, his spirit began to be pressed; either because he heard of the happy success of the Gospel among the Macedonians, or because he was moved by the misery of a people going blind, as Christ was, Matt. 9. Certainly he felt a more fervent motion of spirit, which made him press harder and testify more openly that Jesus is the Christ, that is, the Saviour, etc.

units.la: NOTA. Praecipuum Apostolicae doctrinae caput esse Christum. In hunc finem enim deléfti fuerunt, vt de hoc testentur, Actor.1.Iohan.15. Hunc ergo Petrus vrget, Actor.4.10. Non alium Paulus nouit, 1.Cor.2.Gal.6. Hic scripturae scopus, Gal.4. Ioh.20. Eodem nos quoque contentos esse decet. Nefas plus scire quàm Apostoli.
units.tr: NOTE. The chief head of apostolic doctrine is Christ. For to this end they were chosen, that they might bear witness to this, Acts 1, John 15. Peter therefore presses this, Acts 4:10. Paul knew no other, 1 Cor. 2, Gal. 6. This is the aim of Scripture, Gal. 4, John 20. We too ought to be content with the same. It is wrong to know more than the Apostles.

units.la: Agnoscamus hunc sacerdotem nostrum, Psal.110. Hebr.2. 4.8.9.&c. Regem & asserto rem, Psal.2. Zach.9. Ioh.19. Ita fiet, vt in illum credentes vitam consequamur aeternam, Ioh.20. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us acknowledge this our priest, Ps. 110, Heb. 2, 4, 8, 9, etc. The king and the one asserted, Ps. 2, Zech. 9, John 19. So it will come about that believing in him we obtain eternal life, John 20. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXLV.
units.tr: HOMILY CXLV.

units.la: 6 Illis autem sese opponentibus ac blasphemantibus, excussis pedibus dixit eis, Sanguis vester super caput vestrum: strum: purus ego, ab hoc tempore ad Gentes proficiscar.
units.tr: 6 But when they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his garments and said to them, "Your blood be upon your own heads. I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."

units.la: 7 Et digressus illinc introiuit domum cuiusdam nomine Iusti, colentis Deum, cuius domus contigua erat Synagogæ.
units.tr: 7 And he departed from there and entered the house of a certain man named Justus, a worshipper of God, whose house adjoined the synagogue.

units.la: 8 Crispus autem præfectus Synagogæ credidit Domino cum tota domo sua: multique Corinthiorum audientes credebant et baptizabantur.
units.tr: 8 Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his household. And many of the Corinthians, hearing, believed and were baptized.

units.la: Dicuus Paulus, 1. Tim. 1. ait: Christus Iesus in mundum venit peccatores saluos facere. Probatur id primum ipsius Christi exemplo, qui peccatoribus hoc nominis familiarissimum exhibuit, ut videre est, Mat. 9. Luc. 19. 7. Deinde per ea, que Apostoli ex spiritu Christi fecerunt. Nam ipsi quoque maximè peccatoribus prædicâ runt verbum gratiæ, & pœnitentes salutis lucrifecerunt, Actor. 2. 3. &c. Est euidens cum primis in Corinthi conuersione. Fuit enim vrbs illa corruptissima vt patet, 1. Cor. 5. 6. &c. Ad hanc tamen Paulus mittitur, vt prædicet. Et quidem Iudæis primùm prædicat, qui præ aliis digni erant, vt à Deo negligerentur. Sequitur, vt illi Euangelium exceperint, vtq; illud in medijs turbis vicerit, &c.
units.tr: The apostle Paul says, 1 Tim. 1: "Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners." This is proved first by Christ's own example, who showed himself most familiar with this name of sinners, as may be seen in Matt. 9 and Luke 19, 7. Next, by what the apostles did from the Spirit of Christ. For they too preached the word of grace chiefly to sinners and gained the penitent for salvation, Acts 2, 3, etc. This is especially evident in the conversion at Corinth. For that city was most corrupt, as is clear from 1 Cor. 5, 6, etc. Yet Paul is sent to this city to preach. And indeed he preaches first to the Jews, who were more worthy than others to be neglected by God. It follows that they received the gospel, and that it prevailed in the midst of the crowds, etc.

units.la: Vu
units.tr: Vu

units.la: I. Iudaei contradicunt & conuiciantur. Perpetuum hoc illis, i Thes. 2. Est hęc horalim fuerint, Exo. 4. 19. Rom. 9. Amos 3. Dura rat etiam hodie. Arguuntur qui religionem suam ex successione & patribus probant, Roma.
units.tr: I. The Jews contradict and revile. This is constant with them, 1 Thess. 2. It was so in the time of Exod. 4:19 and Rom. 9, Amos 3, and it persists even today. Those are rebuked who prove their religion by succession and by the fathers, Rom.

units.la: Interim NOTA. ¶ 1. Quod nunc demum contradicunt, quando de Christo Paulus diserte testari coepit. Antea de lege & aliis articulis differentem tulerunt. Idem hodie fit. Feruntur vtcunq; qui manifestos abusus & corruptos mores reprehendunt. Sed vt primum Christus vrgetur, nemo ferre poterit. Causa est, quia huius praedicatio ad viuum vsq; omnem corruptionem resecat, & intolerabiles sunt consequentiae. Tolluntur omnes alij Dii. Augustinus de Socrate. Ruit nundina & quaestus sacrorum, Ioh. 2. Acto. 8. Meritorum & proprię iustitię fiducia, Rom. 11. Arguitur vitę licentia, & nouus homo requiritur, Iohannis 3. Prodit ergo sic hic mundi licentiosa corruptio, & quod reuera Dei hostes sint, quicunque huic studeunt. Licet enim id pauci fateantur, negare tamen non possunt, cum Dei filium nolint amplecti, neque eius verbo subiici. Ioh. 3 12.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE. (1) They only now contradict, when Paul begins to testify plainly about Christ. Before this, they put up with him discussing the law and other articles. The same happens today: those who rebuke manifest abuses and corrupt morals are somehow tolerated. But as soon as Christ himself is pressed, no one will be able to bear it. The reason is that his preaching cuts out every corruption to the quick, and the consequences are intolerable. All other gods are removed. Augustine on Socrates. The market and the profit from sacred things collapse, John 2, Acts 8. Confidence in merits and one's own righteousness falls, Rom. 11. The license of life is challenged, and a new man is required, John 3. Thus the licentious corruption of the world is exposed here, and it is clear that those who strive against this are in truth enemies of God. For although few admit it, they cannot deny it, since they refuse to embrace the Son of God or submit to his word, John 3:12.

units.la: ¶ 2. Lq. q 2. Locutionis ordinem. Primo contradicunt, nimirum ex prauo affectu. Deinde cum Paulus non cedit, ad conuitia vertuntur. Qualia illa fuerint, collige ex Act. 6.7.16.17.22.
units.tr: ¶ 2. Note the order of their behaviour. First they contradict, out of a perverse disposition. Then, when Paul does not yield, they turn to reviling. Gather from Acts 6, 7, 16, 17, 22 what such reviling was like.

units.la: Docemur horum exemplo, quo tandem delabantur, qui fibijpfis permittunt aduersus veritatem aliquid dicere. Fit idem quod in alijs litibus. Contentione irritati conuitiantur quoq;. Imo tandem in manifestam vim erumpunt. Exempla habes, 1. Reg. 22. Amos 7. Hodie nimis multa sunt. Est hic primus gradus ad peccatum in spiritum sanctum, Mat. 12. 1. Io. 5. Discamus ergo veritati cedere.
units.tr: We are taught by their example where those finally end up who allow themselves to say anything against the truth. The same happens as in other quarrels: provoked by contention, they also revile, and in the end they break out into open violence. You have examples in 1 Kings 22 and Amos 7. Today there are far too many. This is the first step towards the sin against the Holy Spirit, Matt. 12, 1 John 5. Let us learn, therefore, to yield to the truth.

units.la: II. Quid Paulus? 1. Vefles exeuntit, iuxta Christi præceptum, Matth. 10. Luc. 9. 10. Fecit idem Antiochiæ, Act. 13. Erat hoc solenne execrationis symbolum, quosigni-ficabatur, instar pulueris disijciendos, Deoq; tam abominabiles esse, ut ne pulue-ri quidem ipsorum communicare tutum sit. Et voluit Christus cum publica prote-statione Apostolos discedere ab impijs verbijs contemptoribus, vt ignorantiæ præ-textus adimeretur.
units.tr: II. What did Paul do? 1. He shook out his garments, in keeping with Christ's precept, Matt. 10, Luke 9, 10. He did the same at Antioch, Acts 13. This was a solemn symbol of execration, signifying that such people were to be cast off like dust, and were so abominable to God that it is not even safe to share in their dust. And Christ willed that the apostles depart from impious words and contemners with a public protest, so that the pretext of ignorance might be taken away.

units.la: Sed NoT. Quàm graue sceleus sit vetbi & Christi Iesu contemptus. Quia hoc omnium malorum remedium est, & per
units.tr: But NOTE how grave a crime is the contempt of the word and of Christ Jesus. For this is the remedy for all evils, and through

units.la: Vu 2
units.tr: Vu 2

units.la: solum hunc patri conciliamur,nó possunt non à Deo abijci, quicunqj illud &hunc abijciunt,1.Sam.15. Vide Matth.10. Nec est quod fe excusari posse sperent, quan- do puluis solus ipsis conuincendis suffi- cit. Quid ergo putandum de concioni- bus,&c.Vide Ioh.12. Item Ioh.15. Difca- mus nos quoque talium consortia fugere, Apoc.18.
units.tr: only this one are we reconciled to the Father. Those who cast off this word and this one cannot but be cast off by God, 1 Sam. 15. See Matt. 10. Nor have they any reason to hope they can excuse themselves, since the dust alone suffices to convict them. What then must be thought of the sermons, etc.? See John 12, and likewise John 15. Let us learn to flee the company of such people too, Rev. 18.

units.la: II. Pœnam denuntiat: Sanguis vester super eos, &c. Ego mundus, &c. Alludit ad verba Ezech. 3.33. Sensus est: Ego meo officio functus sum. Quia autem vos Dei gratiam reijcitis, ad gentes transferetur illius regnum, sicut Christus prænunciauit, Mat.21. In vobis autem hæret omnis vestræ perditionis culpa. Hoc ipsum omnes contem ptores ad se transferant.
units.tr: II. He announces punishment: "Your blood be upon them," etc. "I am clean," etc. He alludes to the words of Ezek. 3:33. The sense is: I have discharged my office. But since you reject God's grace, his kingdom will be transferred to the Gentiles, as Christ foretold, Matt. 21. The whole blame for your destruction, however, clings to you. Let all contemners apply this to themselves.

units.la: Sed Nota. Tunc demum extra culpam esse ministros, si officio suo erga peccatores satisfaciant. Quód si canes muti sint(Isaiæ 56.) ab ipsis sanguis populi exigetur, Ezech.3.33. Matth.24. Hinc illæ zelus Prophetarum & Apostolorum, Amos 3. 1.Cor.9.
units.tr: But NOTE. Ministers are free from guilt only if they satisfy their duty towards sinners. But if they are dumb dogs (Isa. 56), the blood of the people will be required of them, Ezek. 3:33, Matt. 24. Hence the zeal of the prophets and apostles, Amos 3, 1 Cor. 9.

units.la: III. Diuertit ad Iustum, qui gentilis haud dubiè fuit, non quód Aquilam odis- set, sed vt protestationi suæ pondus acce- deret, & hunc minùs grauaret odio. Inte-
units.tr: III. He turns to Justus, who was undoubtedly a Gentile, not because he hated Aquila, but so that his protest might carry more weight and so that he might burden him less with hatred. Meanwhile

units.la: rim adhuc occasionem captat Iudaeos lu- crifaciendi, cum aedes Synagogae proxi- mas deligat. Non enim potuit suam gen- tem odisse, Rom 9.10.
units.tr: he still seeks an occasion to gain the Jews, since he chooses a house next to the synagogue. For he could not hate his own nation, Rom. 9, 10.

units.la: Hic autem No r. Quo affectu mini- stri debeant praediti esse. Pastores & patres dicuntur, Ezech.34 Zacha.11. Ioh.10. 1.Cor.4. Horum ergo affectum induant. Sic Christus, Luc.19. Matt.9. Idem magistratus ad se transferat, Dauid.
units.tr: Here note what disposition ministers ought to have. Pastors and fathers they are called, Ezek. 34, Zech. 11, John 10, 1 Cor. 4. Let them therefore put on their disposition. So Christ, Luke 19, Matt. 9. Let the magistrate likewise make this his own, David.

units.la: III, Fructus studij Apostolici. Credit Crispus vir primarius, de quo 1.Cor.1. Simul etiam multi ex Corinthijs, qui & baptizantur. Non ergo incrementum deest strenue laborantibus, Luc.8. Isa.55. Nec aliquorum rebellio Dei veritati quicquam derogare potest, Rom.2 Excitet hoc mini stros, magistratus, singulos, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: III. The fruit of apostolic labour. Crispus, a leading man, of whom 1 Cor. 1, believes. At the same time many of the Corinthians also believe, and are baptized. So no increase is lacking to those who labour earnestly, Luke 8, Isa. 55. Nor can the rebellion of some detract anything from the truth of God, Rom. 2. Let this stir up ministers, magistrates, each individual, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXLVI.
units.tr: Homily 146.

units.la: 9 Dixit autem Dominus nocte per visionem Paulo, Ne time, sed loquere, & ne tacueris:
units.tr: 9 And the Lord said to Paul in a vision by night: Do not be afraid, but speak, and do not keep silent,

units.la: 10 Nam ego sum tecum, & nemo te muadet ut tibi malefaciat: quoniam populus est mihi multus in hac urbe.
units.tr: 10 for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, because I have a great people in this city.

units.la: 11 Commoratus est itaque illic annum & sex menses, docens eos sermonem Dei.
units.tr: 11 So he stayed there a year and six months, teaching them the word of God.

units.la: DOminus noster Iesus Christus, Ioh. 16. ait: In mundo afflictionem habebitis, sed bono animo sitis, ego vici mundum. Docent haec, Christi regnum persecutionibus non euerti, sed propagari. Exempla huius multa hucusque vidimus. Et praeclarum est quod Corinthi euenit. Docuit illic Paulus primum absque persecutione. Sed nullius q crediderit, fit metio. Mox autem, vt Iudaei insurgunt, fructus Euangelij emicat. Credit Crispus, vir primarius, & multi alij ex Corinthijs. Nemi nem ergo turbae persecutionum offendant.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ says in John 16: "In the world you will have tribulation, but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world." These words teach that the kingdom of Christ is not overthrown by persecutions but spread by them. We have seen many examples of this up to now, and what happened at Corinth is a notable one. Paul taught there first without persecution, but no mention is made of anyone who believed. Soon, however, when the Jews rose up, the fruit of the Gospel shone forth: Crispus, a leading man, believed, and many other Corinthians too. Let no one therefore be disheartened by the storms of persecution.

units.la: Sequitur autem insignis locus de Pauli consolatione, quam illi Deus adhibuit, & qua inter pericula confortatus est. Eum ordine per singulas circumstantias considerabimus.
units.tr: Next comes a remarkable passage about the comfort with which God consoled Paul and by which he was strengthened amid his dangers. We shall consider it in order, through its separate circumstances.

units.la: I. Paulus inspiciendus, quem humani aliquid passum esse, & timuisse, ex Dei consolatione patet. Et sane multa illum terre repuerunt. Cognita Iudaeorum rabies. Vrbis corruptio. Priora pericula. Falsi fratres. Quid quod ipse fatetur, se inter ipsos versatum esse cum multo timore, 1. Corinth. 2. &c. Videtur voluisse discedere.
units.tr: I. Paul is to be considered, who, as God's consolation makes clear, suffered and feared like a human being. Indeed many things troubled him: the known rage of the Jews, the corruption of the city, the earlier dangers, the false brothers. Note also what he himself confesses, that he was among them in great fear (1 Cor. 2, etc.). It seems he wished to leave.

units.la: Not. Sanctos etiam obnoxios esse affectibus maxime timori. Abraham, Gen. 12.20. I2 2o.Iacob,Gene.32.Moses,Exod.2.4 Io-iuę,Cap.7.Dauid,1 Sam.21.Helias,1.Reg. 18.19. Petrus,Mat.14 26.
units.tr: Note: that even the saints are liable to the emotions, above all to fear. Abraham, Gen. 12:20; Jacob, Gen. 32; Moses, Exod. 2, 4; Joshua, ch. 7; David, 1 Sam. 21; Elijah, 1 Kings 18, 19; Peter, Matt. 14:26.

units.la: Seruit hoc institutioni,partim vt agnita nostra infirmitate non fimus confidentes,vt Petrus, Luc.32.partim vt non teme rè damnemus alioqui bene meritos, fi quid ta'e patiantur. Vult Deus in illis agnosci suam gratiam.Ora potiùs pro illis, vt Christus feeit,Luc.22.Iohan.17. Idem Paulus cupit,Eph 6.
units.tr: This serves our instruction: partly so that, recognising our weakness, we do not become overconfident, as Peter did (Luke 22); partly so that we do not rashly condemn those who are otherwise well deserving if they suffer something of this kind. God wills that his grace be recognised in them. Pray rather for them, as Christ did (Luke 22; John 17). Paul himself desires the same (Eph. 6).

units.la: II. Deum,qui æstuantem mox solatur, licet nulla mentio fiat inuocationis. Deus enim gemitus quoq; audit:Quod vt fi-atopus est,Rom.8.Sic cum Moise agit,Exod 14.Implerur promissio,Ifa.65. Elucet magna Dei bonitas & paterna prouidentia.Nouit quibus nobis opus fit, Mat. 6. Immittit tentationes, vt admoneat & excitet, sed pro illarum ratione consolatur,Pfal.34.94.1.Cor.10.2.Cor.1.12.Nemo igitur desperet, cum multa habeat media Deus,quibus solatur & iuuet.
units.tr: II. God, who soon consoles the one who is troubled, although no mention is made of invocation. For God also hears groaning, which is what the need requires (Rom. 8). So he deals with Moses (Exod. 14). The promise is fulfilled (Isa. 65). The great goodness and fatherly providence of God shines forth. He knows what we need (Matt. 6). He sends temptations to warn and stir us, but he consoles according to the measure of them (Ps. 34; 94; 1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1). Let no one therefore despair, since God has many means by which he comforts and helps.

units.la: Hic visione vtitur, cum adhortatione in primis necessaria, cuius partes sunt: 1. Occurrit fonti omnis inobedietię,& eius effectui, quo maximè Paulus tentabatur: Ne timeas.Sic Mosi dicitur,Deut.5 Iofuæ Cap.10.Iere.1.Apostolis,Matth.10.
units.tr: Here he uses a vision, together with an exhortation that is especially necessary. Its parts are: 1. It meets the source of all disobedience and its effect, by which Paul was above all tempted: "Do not be afraid." So it is said to Moses (Deut. 5), to Joshua (ch. 10), to Jeremiah (1), to the apostles (Matt. 10).

units.la: Vu 4
units.tr: Vu 4

units.la: Not. ¶ Causam huius præcepti. Quia nihil efficacius ad reprahendum ab officio, quàm timor. Rationem impedit primo, & consiliorum incertos facit. Si præualeat, pudorem quoque aufert. Fit vt pericula maiora accersamus. Obseruent Magistratus & Antistites. Ideo fortes deligi iubentur, Exod. 18.
units.tr: Note: the reason for this command. Because nothing is more effective in turning us from our duty than fear. First it hinders reason and makes our counsels uncertain. If it prevails, it also takes away shame. Thus we bring greater dangers upon ourselves. Magistrates and church leaders should take note. For this reason brave men are ordered to be chosen (Exod. 18).

units.la: II Præcipit quid faciat: Loquere & ne taceas. Coniungit duo hæc, quia multi loquuntur simul & tacent. Sensus est, vt diserté totum Euangelium prædicet, &c.
units.tr: II. He instructs what he is to do: "Speak and do not keep silent." He joins these two because many people speak and keep silent at the same time. The meaning is that he should preach the whole Gospel plainly, and so on.

units.la: Nota. ¶ Non sufficere, si ministri obiter proponant verbum Dei, interim multa dissimulent. Diserté agenda & applicanda singulis doctrina, vt de feagi intelligant. Simile legati, Ierem. 1. Ezech. 3. 2 Tim. 2. &c.
units.tr: Note: it is not enough for ministers to set forth the word of God in passing while meanwhile concealing much. The teaching must be carried out plainly and applied to each hearer, so that they understand it as it is meant. Compare the envoy (Jer. 1; Ezek. 3; 2 Tim. 2, etc.).

units.la: III. Rationes adhibet grauissimas. A. Ego tecum sum. Hæc vna sufficere debet aduersus quoquis periucula. Est enim Deus omnipotens. Quid ergo creaturæ faciant? Psal. 115. Dan. 7. Hinc illa Dauidis, Psal. 23. 27. 118. 1. Sam. 18. Asa, 2. Par. 14. 16. Generalis promissio (Genes. 17. Exod. 20.) omnibus in Dei vocatione ambulantibus seruiens.
units.tr: III. He brings forward the weightiest reasons. A. "I am with you." This one alone ought to suffice against any dangers whatever. For God is omnipotent. What, then, can creatures do? (Ps. 115; Dan. 7). Hence David's words (Ps. 23; 27; 118), and 1 Sam. 18, and Asa (2 Chron. 14, 16). It is a general promise (Gen. 17; Exod. 20), serving all who walk in God's calling.

units.la: B. Nemo insurget contra te, vt noceat. Tentabunt quidem, sed non proficient.
units.tr: B. "No one shall rise against you to harm you." They will indeed try, but they will not prevail.

units.la: Est haec specialis promissio, quae non semper locum habet. Paulus alibi vexatur. Plerique enim sunt multae tribulationes, &c. Psalm 34. Ioh. 16. Nihilominus pergendum spe promissionis.
units.tr: This is a special promise, which does not always hold good. Paul is troubled elsewhere; for many are the tribulations of the righteous (Ps. 34; John 16, etc.). Nevertheless one must press on in the hope of the promise.

units.la: C. Est mihi populus multus, &c. Loquitur de electis, & ostendit laborem non fore ritum, &c.
units.tr: C. "I have a great people," etc. He speaks of the elect, and shows that the labour will not be in vain, etc.

units.la: NOT. 1. Quod in urbe corruptissima multos habet Deus, & plures quidem quàm Athenis. Peccatores ergo manifesti magis capaces sunt regni coelorum, quàm iustitiarij. Idem fit quod in morbis. Matth. 22. 9. Luc. 18. Ideo à redargutione peccatorum incipit Euangelij praedicatio, Luc 24. Simul consoletur hoc nos &c. Vide 1. Reg. 19.
units.tr: NOTE 1. That God has many people in a most corrupt city, and indeed more than at Athens. Manifest sinners are therefore more receptive of the kingdom of heaven than the self-righteous. The same happens as in sicknesses (Matt. 22:9; Luke 18). Therefore the preaching of the Gospel begins with the rebuke of sins (Luke 24). At the same time this consoles us, etc. See 1 Kings 19.

units.la: 2. Quod suos vocat, qui adhuc errabant. Erant enim scripti in libro vitae, Exo. 32. Ita suas oues vocat Christus, Ioh. 10. Affirmatur hic certitudo praedestinationis & electionis, 2. Tim. 2. Rom. 11. Consoletur, Rom 8. Ne peccatis quidem impediri potest electio Dei, Rom. 11.
units.tr: 2. That he calls his own, who were still erring. For they were written in the book of life (Exod. 32). So Christ calls his sheep (John 10). The certainty of predestination and election is affirmed here (2 Tim. 2; Rom. 11). It consoles (Rom. 8). The election of God cannot be impeded even by sins (Rom. 11).

units.la: III. Paulus manet Corinthi annum et menses.
units.tr: III. Paul remains at Corinth a year and some months.

units.la: Effectus divinae consolationis, in quo NOT. 1. Dei fidem & potentiam, qui seruum suum in urbe corruptissima seruauit. Sic Daniel in Babylone, in Aegypto Moses. Soletur.
units.tr: The effect of divine consolation, in which we note: 1. God's faithfulness and power, who preserved his servant in a most corrupt city. So Daniel in Babylon, and Moses in Egypt. Let him be consoled.

units.la: Vu 5
units.tr: Vu 5

units.la: 2. Patientiam Pauli, qui inter superbos & ingratissimos tam diu traxit moram. Nam quales fuerint erga ipsum concjce ex 1.Corinth 3 4.5 9 10. posteriori ad Corinthios 10 & 11. Arguuntur, qui Ecclesias temere deserunt, vt primum non omnia pro voto succedunt. Atqui Apostolus erat paulus,&c.
units.tr: 2. Paul's patience, who spent so long a delay among the proud and most ungrateful. For you may gather what sort they were towards him from 1 Corinthians 3, 4, 5, 9, 10, and the later letter to the Corinthians, chapters 10 and 11. Those are rebuked who rashly desert churches, since at first not everything succeeds as they wish. And yet the Apostle was Paul, etc.

units.la: 3. Quanti laboris res sit, Ecclesiam constituere. Nemo melior artifex Paulo, Actorum 18. Hic tamen tam diu laborat in fundamentis unius Ecclesiae. Nam se tantummodo plantauisse testatur, priori ad Corinthios tertio & quarto Opus postea multa cura, posteriori ad Corinthios vndecimo.
units.tr: 3. How great a labour it is to establish a church. No craftsman was better than Paul (Acts 18), yet here he labours so long over the foundations of a single church. For he testifies that he only planted, in the first letter to the Corinthians, chapters 3 and 4; that afterwards he laboured with much care, in the later letter, chapter 11.

units.la: Arguuntur socordes ministri, & qui ze lum ardentiorem ministrorum superuacaneum putant. Oremus.
units.tr: Lazy ministers are rebuked, and those who think the more ardent zeal of ministers superfluous. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXVII.

units.la: 12 Quum autem Gallio esset Proconsul Achaiae, insurrexerunt concorditer Iudaei in Paulum, & adduxerunt eum ad tribunal.
units.tr: 12 When Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up together against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

units.la: 13 Dicentes, Iste persuadet homines colere Deum contra Legem. 14 Paulo verò iam os aperturo, dixit Gallio Iudæis, Si qua iniuria esset, aut facinus malum ô Iudæi, quatenus æquum esset, vos tolerarem.
units.tr: 13 Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law. 14 And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you.

units.la: 15. Sin verò quæstio est de sermone et nominib. & Lege vestrate, ipsi vide ritu: Iudex enim ego istarum rerum esse nolo.
units.tr: 15 But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.

units.la: 16 Et abegit eos à tribunali.
units.tr: 16 And he drave them from the judgment seat.

units.la: 17 Omnes autem Græci Sosthenem praefectu Synagogæ apprehensum verberabant ante tribunal: neque quicquam eorum Gallioni curæ erat.
units.tr: 17 Then all the Greeks laid hold on Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.

units.la: QVamuis Christus ministros suos emittit in medios lupos, eosdem tamen tueri & protegere consueuit. Mat. 10 Experitur hoc Paulus, quando Corinthi inter maxima pericula cum magno timore & tremore versatur, 1.Cor.2. Timentem enim & de deserenda urbe cogitantem, Deus consolatione sua præsuenit, & suam illi gratiam ac opem pollicetur. Quod autem pollicitus est, orto tumultu & periculo ingruente fideliter præstitit, ut præsens locus docet. Sed singulas circunstantias ordine videamus.
units.tr: Although Christ sends his ministers out into the midst of wolves, he is nonetheless accustomed to defend and protect them. Matt. 10. Paul experiences this when at Corinth he lives among the greatest dangers, with great fear and trembling, 1 Cor. 2. For when he was afraid and was thinking of leaving the city, God anticipated him with his consolation and promised him his grace and help. What he promised, he faithfully performed when a tumult arose and danger pressed in, as the present place shows. But let us look at the individual circumstances in order.

units.la: I. Authores tumultus producuntur.
units.tr: I. The authors of the tumult are brought forward.

units.la: Fuerunt Iudæi, de quibus iam sæpe di-
units.tr: These were the Jews, of whom we have already often spoken.

units.la: Iudæi turbarum authores contra Paulum. stū Hi cum nouus venisset Procons. Gallio, vnanim ter contra Paulum insurgunt, illumque in forum trahunt,&c.
units.tr: The Jews, the authors of the disturbances against Paul. When the new proconsul Gallio had arrived, they rise up unanimously against Paul and drag him into the forum, etc.

units.la: NOT.1.Dei promissiones non ita debere accipi, quasi in vniuersum omni crucé liberent. Vult enim suos exerceri Deus: Interim fideliter liberat, dum non suprà vires tentari sinit,Psalm.34. 1 Cor.10. 2.Cor.1. Vide Abrahamum, Gen.12. 17.14. 20.&c. Iacobum,Gen.28.32. Mosem, Exo. 3.4.5.10,14. Ieremiam.Cap.1.20. &c. Faluntur ergo qui promissiones Euangelij sic exponunt,vt statim mendacij arguant, vt primum crux incidit. Vide Mar.10. Mat 16.
units.tr: NOTE 1. The promises of God are not to be understood as if they free us from every cross in general. For God wills that his people be exercised; yet meanwhile he faithfully delivers them, while not allowing them to be tempted beyond their strength, Ps. 34; 1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1. See Abraham, Gen. 12, 17, 14, 20, etc.; Jacob, Gen. 28, 32; Moses, Exod. 3, 4, 5, 10, 14; Jeremiah, chap. 1, 20, etc. They are therefore mistaken who expound the promises of the Gospel in such a way that they charge them with falsehood as soon as the cross falls. See Mark 10; Matt. 16.

units.la: 2. Hostium veritatis studia & mores. A. Occasionem astutè vænantur, & hac oblata prosiliunt, etsi omnino sopiti videantur. Isti ferè sefquianno cessârunt. Sed noue Procof.dato infurgüt,vel quòd suis conatibus idoneum sperarent,vtpote à religione & iustitıtia aljenissimum. Vel quòd nunc commodè res nouas tentari posse putarent. Impletur quod est Luc. 16 Exciter hoc ad vigilantiam, & circumspectisimus.Vide Mat.10.
units.tr: 2. The studies and manners of the enemies of the truth. A. They hunt eagerly for an opportunity, and when it is offered they leap forth, even if they seem entirely dormant. These men had kept quiet for about a year and a half. But with the arrival of the new proconsul they rose up, either because they hoped the situation suited their attempts, being most alien from religion and justice, or because they thought new schemes could now conveniently be tried. What is written in Luke 16 is fulfilled. This should stir us to vigilance and the greatest circumspection. See Matt. 10.

units.la: B Coniungunt animos & studia. Nunquam recté consentiunt impij in externis. In solo Christo oppugnando conueniunt. Similia habes, Matt. 22. Luc. 22. 23. &c. Non ergo in hostium dissensione sed Christo habemus spem positam.
units.tr: B. They join their minds and efforts. The impious never agree rightly in external matters; they unite only in assailing Christ. You have similar examples, Matt. 22; Luke 22, 23, etc. Therefore our hope is not placed in the dissension of enemies but in Christ.

units.la: II. Accusationis caput ponitur, quòd cultus nouos inuehat contra legem. Erat autem Rom. exosa omnis religionis innouatio. Amplificârunt haud dubiè verbis, vt Act. 6. 16. 17. Sed salsissimum erat, cum Christum docceret, qui legis finis est Rom. 10. Ioh. 5. Luc. 24. Ipsi vero legem corruperent traditionibus.
units.tr: II. The head of the accusation is set forth: that he introduces new forms of worship contrary to the law. Now every innovation in religion was hateful to the Romans, and they doubtless amplified the charge with words, as in Acts 6, 16, 17. But it was most absurd, since he was teaching Christ, who is the end of the law, Rom. 10; John 5; Luke 24. Indeed, they themselves were corrupting the law with traditions.

units.la: Not. Hoc crimine potissimum accusari pios, quòd religionem prophanent. Et hic mirè religionem simulare possunt, qui ab omni religione sunt alieni simi. Faciunt hoc, qui Diuos, imagines, &c. tonant.
units.tr: Note. The pious are especially accused of this crime, that they profane religion. And those who are most alien from all religion can most wonderfully feign religion. They do this who thunder against the saints, images, etc.

units.la: III. Quid Gallio? Paulum, qui Apolo-giam parabat, non audit. Deinde palam te statur, huius causae cognitionem nihil ad se pertinere. Vbi contemptissimè loquitur de Iudaeorum religione, eò quòd ipsi hanc λογομαχίας & γενεαλογίας vrgen-do contemptâ & inuisam facerent: quod ipsum Papistę hodie faciunt. Tandem abs se illos relegat.
units.tr: III. What does Gallio do? He does not hear Paul, who was preparing his defence. Then he openly declares that the investigation of this cause does not concern him. Here he speaks most contemptuously of the Jews' religion, because they, by pressing wrangling over words and genealogies [λογομαχίας & γενεαλογίας], made it despised and hated; which the Papists themselves do today. At last he sends them away from himself.

units.la: Not. 1. Probandum quod religio-nem sibi ignoram non vult iudicare. Mo-destior multis Christianis magistratibus,
units.tr: Note 1. It must be shown that he who does not wish to judge a religion unknown to him is more modest than many Christian magistrates,

units.la: qui cum nec Papistica nec Euangelicam religionem intelligant, tame omnem huius causae cognitione sibi solis vendicant. Causa maximorum malorum.
units.tr: who, since they understand neither the Papist nor the Evangelical religion, nevertheless claim for themselves alone all knowledge of this cause. This is the cause of the greatest evils.

units.la: § 2. Improbandum quod a religione alienus, illam nec curat nec discit. Non enim tales vult esse magistratus Deus, Dei tronom. 17. 13. Exempla sanctorum regum.
units.tr: § 2. It must be condemned that he who is alien to religion neither cares for it nor learns it. For God does not wish magistrates to be such, Deut. 17. 13. Examples of holy kings.

units.la: Arguuntur: A. Qui religionis causam ad ciuiles magistratus pertinere negant, & nolunt inquiri. Id vero faciunt, ut sibi vi an: fernant figmenta suaquibusque obtru dendi. At illi Galliones esse volunt magistratus.
units.tr: They are condemned: A. Those who deny that the cause of religion pertains to civil magistrates and are unwilling that it be examined. They do this so that they may freely impose their own fabrications on whomever they wish. Yet they want such men to be Gallios as magistrates.

units.la: B. Qui cum Christiani principes habe-ri velint, omnem religionis causam vt nihil ad se pertinentem, indoctis Monachis & auaris Episcopis comendant. Quae maxima persecutionum fax est. Putant se excusatos, sed ex illorum manu requiretur populus, & ipso facto conuincentur.
units.tr: B. Those who, while they want to be considered Christian princes, commit every cause of religion, as if it had nothing to do with them, to unlearned monks and greedy bishops. This is the greatest torch of persecutions. They think themselves excused, but the people will be required at their hand, and they will be convicted by the very deed.

units.la: IV. Exitus Tragoediae describitur. Graeci Softhenem arripiunt & verberant, nimirum Iudaeis authoribus. Nam Paulicol lega fuit, vt patet, 1. Cor. 1. Gallio nihil horum curat.
units.tr: IV. The outcome of the tragedy is described. The Greeks seize Sosthenes and beat him, no doubt at the instigation of the Jews. For Sosthenes was, as is clear from 1 Cor. 1, a colleague of Paul. Gallio cares nothing for these things.

units.la: NOT. 1. Quod Paulus nihil mali patitur, licet ad manus veniat res. At non auditae fuit Apologia. Non defendit illum pro-
units.tr: NOTE 1. Paul suffers no harm, although the matter comes to blows. Yet his defence was not heard; Gallio did not defend him

units.la: pro officio Gallio. Nemo alius patronus. Solius ergo Dei protectione feruatur, idque mirabiliter. Elucet fides promissionis Dei, Psal. 105. Similia exempla habes, &c.
units.tr: in the discharge of his office. Paul had no other advocate. He is therefore preserved by the protection of God alone, and that wonderfully. The faith of God's promise shines forth, Ps. 105. You have similar examples, etc.

units.la: 18. Non timeamus.
units.tr: 18. Let us not fear.

units.la: ¶ 2. Mores impiorum magistratuum. Profitentur se ciuilium legū vindices; vt Gallio antea fecit. Cur ergo nunc non de fendit Softhenę. Frequens id hodie. Nec speres aliud ab illis, quicunq; religionem semel abiecerunt. Vide Psalm. 82. Quanto peiores, qui ipsi pios tradunt excruciandos?
units.tr: ¶ 2. The manners of ungodly magistrates. They profess themselves avengers of the civil laws, as Gallio did before. Why, then, does he now not defend Sosthenes? This is frequent today. Nor should you hope for anything else from those who have once cast off religion. See Psalm 82. How much worse are those who hand the pious over to be tortured!

units.la: ¶ 3. Conditionem eorum, qui amissa libertate alienis seruiunt. Tales Iudæi rant, propter peccata, Leuit. 26. Tales Corinthij à Mummio deuicti, ante annos fere 200. Iam Iudæi passim dispersi & omnibus inuisi sunt cum sua religione. Corinthij eiusmodi Procof. reguntur, qui apertas iniurias non vindicat.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The condition of those who, having lost their liberty, serve foreigners. Such were the Jews, on account of their sins, Lev. 26. Such were the Corinthians, conquered by Mummius about 200 years ago. Now the Jews are scattered everywhere and hated by all for their religion. The Corinthians are ruled by such proconsuls as do not avenge open injuries.

units.la: Meditemur nos hodie. Vide quid faciant, &c. Tueamur libertate pacis studio. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us consider this today. See what they do, etc. Let us defend our liberty with zeal for peace. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXLIIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CXLVIII.

units.la: 18 Paulus vero quum adhuc illic permansisset dies multos, valedicto fratribus enavigauit in Syriam, et cum eo Priscilla & Aquila, quum totondissęt caput Cenchreis: habebat enim votum.
units.tr: 18 Paul, when he had stayed there yet many days, took his leave of the brothers and sailed for Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; at Cenchreae he had his head shorn, for he was under a vow.

units.la: 19 Peruenit autem Ephesum, & eosibi reliquit: ipse vero ingressus Synagogam disserunt cum Iudæis.
units.tr: 19 He came to Ephesus and left them there, but he himself entered the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

units.la: 20 Rogantibus autem ipsis, vt diu eius apud ipsos maneret, non annuit.
units.tr: 20 When they asked him to stay with them for a longer time, he did not consent.

units.la: 21 Sed valedixit eis, dicens, Oportet omnino me festum quod instat agere Hierosolymis: sed iterum reuertar ad vos, Deo volente. Et profectus est Epheso.
units.tr: 21 But he bade them farewell, saying: "I must by all means keep the feast that is coming up at Jerusalem; but I will return to you again, God willing." And he sailed from Ephesus.

units.la: 22 Quumque descendisset Cæsaream ascendisset que Hierosolymam, ac salutasset Ecclesiam, descendit Antiochiam.
units.tr: 22 And when he had landed at Caesarea and gone up and greeted the church, he went down to Antioch.

units.la: 23 Et quum peregisset illic aliquantum temporis, abiit, peragrans ordine Galaticam regionem, confirmans omnes discipulos.
units.tr: 23 And after he had spent some time there, he departed and travelled in order through the region of Galatia, strengthening all the disciples.

units.la: QVemadmodum Diuus Paulus Corinthi propter hostes acerrimos maximo terrore & timore tentatus est: Ita vix alibi magis praesentem Deum sensit. Primo enim illi apparens opem promisit. Deinde promissa tam fideliter praestitit, vt captum & omni praesidio destitutum, mirabiliter liberarit, licet iam ad manus nus res deuenisset, & percuteretur Sost-henes. Porrò vsus omnium horum est, vt communi piorum consolationi seruiant. Poterit enim hos similiter eripere Deus. Et quia verax est, non deerit suis promis-sionibus, Iohan.16.Mat. 10. Sequitur quid porrò actum, &c.
units.tr: Just as holy Paul at Corinth was tried by most fierce enemies with the greatest terror and fear, so he scarcely ever felt God more present anywhere else. For first, appearing to him, He promised help; then He kept the promises so faithfully that, when Paul was taken and destitute of all protection, He marvellously freed him, although the matter had already come to hand-to-hand blows and Sosthenes was being beaten. Moreover, the use of all these things is that they serve the common comfort of the pious. For God can likewise snatch such men away, and because He is true, He will not fail His promises: John 16, Matt. 10. The text goes on to what was done next, etc.

units.la: I. Paulus post tantas turbas Corinthi a-liquandiu manet. Inde cum Aquila disce-dens, in Syria tendit, raso priùs capite, &c.
units.tr: I. Paul, after such great tumults at Corinth, remains there for some time. Then, departing with Aquila, he heads for Syria, having first had his head shaved, etc.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Paulum eiusque in commis-so officio constantiam, qua post tantos ter-rores sub ignauo proconsule Corinthi ad huc manet, nimirum propter rudes & in-firmos, qui confortatione indigebant. Nec illis insalutatis discedit. Est pastor bo-nus, Ioh.10.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. Consider Paul and his constancy in the office committed to him, by which, after such great terrors, he still remains at Corinth under a slothful proconsul, no doubt on account of the simple and weak, who needed encouragement. Nor does he depart without bidding them farewell. He is a good shepherd, John 10.

units.la: Interim omnium est, vt Dei opem ex-pertí, in sua vocatione confirmentur, non deficiant, vt quidam praepostere sapien-tes facere consueuerunt.
units.tr: Meanwhile it is for all who have experienced God's help to be strengthened in their calling and not to fail, as certain men who are foolishly wise have been accustomed to do.

units.la: ¶ 2. Aquilam & Priscillam. Comitantur Paulum etiam ante exilium experti, quod non carebat periculo. Vide Ro.16.Sed im mortale gloriam sibi pepererunt. Excitet hoc ad similia, quando vniuersales promis-siones extant de praemio, Mat.10.
units.tr: 2. Aquila and Priscilla. They accompany Paul, having shared his dangers even before his exile, which was not without peril. See Rom. 16. But they won for themselves immortal glory. Let this stir us to similar deeds, since universal promises of reward stand, Matt. 10.

units.la: Obseruemus idem erga indignos & ex-sules, quos peculiariter Christus comen-
units.tr: Let us observe the same toward the unworthy and the exiles, whom Christ especially

units.la: Xx dat,Matth.26.25. Nec nobis onerosos putemus, quando Dei gratiam conciliant virtutibus. Ob vnum Lothum liberantur Sodomæ, Gen.14. Et postea felices fuisse, si plures habuissent, Gen.18. Sunt & alia exempla.
units.tr: embraces, Matt. 26:25. Nor let us think them burdensome when they win God's grace for us by their virtues. For the sake of Lot alone Sodom was spared, Gen. 14; and they would have been happier had they had more such men, Gen. 18. There are other examples too.

units.la: § 3. Quod de capitis tonsione & voto Pauli dicitur. Fuit haud dubie Nazaræi votum, de quo Num.6. Eo ad seruitus viuendi genus adstringebantur, qui diuinis rebus ardentius volebant vacare. Liberi vero vnicuique erat votum hoc. Abstinebant vino, funerib voluptatibus quoque licitis. Nutriebantur comam, quia non fuit iuris erant, 1.Cor.11. Euoluto voti tempore, tondebantur solenniter. Tale votum propter Iudæos in se transtulit Paulus, vt illos iudicaret, 1.Cor.9. Act.15. Alioqui non ignorabat, libertatem Christianam nullis ceremoniis debere violari Col.3.Rom.14.
units.tr: § 3. As to what is said of Paul's shaving of the head and his vow: it was without doubt the Nazirite vow, of which Num. 6. By it, those who wished to devote themselves more ardently to divine things were bound to a kind of servile life. But the vow was free for each person. They abstained from wine and from even lawful pleasures. They let their hair grow, since it was not lawful to cut it, 1 Cor. 11. When the time of the vow was complete, they were shaved solemnly. Paul took such a vow upon himself for the sake of the Jews, so that he might win them, 1 Cor. 9; Acts 15. Otherwise he did not forget that Christian liberty must not be violated by any ceremonies, Col. 3; Rom. 14.

units.la: At qui hinc votis Monasticis patroci-nantur, errant: 1. Iudæi legem habebant, quæ cum honore debebat sepeliri. Deinde Deo vouebant. Leuit.27.Pf.76. Illi homines traditiones sequuntur & creaturis vota nuncupantes sectas, & scismata inuenerunt contra Christi legem, Matt.23.1.Corinth.1.3.&7.
units.tr: But those who from this defend monastic vows are wrong. 1. The Jews had the law, which was to be buried with honour. Then they vowed to God (Lev. 27; Ps. 76). Those men follow traditions, and by making vows to creatures they have invented sects and schisms against the law of Christ (Matt. 23; 1 Cor. 1, 3 and 7).

units.la: 2. Votum Nazaræi non mutat ac vitæ
units.tr: 2. The vow of the Nazarite did not change the manner of life,

units.la: genus, cultui Dei seruiebat, nō scindebat vnitatem, & possibile erat praestitu. Deinde nemini onerosos reddebat. Illorum vero genus vitae mutant, Dei cultui repugnant. Isa. 29. Mat. 15. Sectas inuehunt. Partim impossibilia sunt, vt castigatis, Mat. 19. 1. Cor. 7. Gen. 2. Partim alios grauant, vt paupertatis. Nazaraei non tollebant domi nicam obedientiam. At monachi ab hac se eximunt.
units.tr: but served the worship of God, did not break the unity, and was possible to perform. Moreover, it did not burden anyone. But the monks change their manner of life and oppose the worship of God (Isa. 29; Matt. 15) and introduce sects. Some of their vows are impossible, such as chastity (Matt. 19; 1 Cor. 7; Gen. 2), and others weigh heavily on people, such as poverty. The Nazarites did not take away domestic obedience, but the monks exempt themselves from it.

units.la: 3. Huic nō tribuebatur meritū. Imò fatebantur se peccatores, bonū omne per gratiarum actione ad Deū referebant, Nu. 6. Illi suam iustitiā stabiliunt, &c. Rom. 10. 11.
units.tr: II. He comes to Ephesus. NOTE. He enters the synagogue and disputes. His love for his own nation breaks out again, Rom. 10:9. And yet he had already shaken off the dust twice, Acts 13:18. So the wrath of God and punishment are to be set before the impious, so that for the converted the hope of pardon always remains whole, Ezek. 18. Besides, one must press on and be watchful, if perhaps some can still be won, etc.

units.la: II. Venit Ephesum: Vbi NoT. ¶ In- greditur synagogam & disputat. Eluect denuo amor erga suam gentem, Rom. 10. 9. Atqui iam bis puluerem excusit. Act. 13 18. Sic ergo ira Dei & poena impijs propo nenda, vt conuersis integra semper maneat veniae spes, Ezech. 18. Adhaec instandum & vigilandum, si qui forte lucrifieri adhuc possint, &c.
units.tr: 2. The Ephesians desire him to stay with them for a long time. The argument: they had profited greatly. Those who hate ministers have not yet tasted the Gospel at all.

units.la: ¶ 2. Ephesij illum diu apud se manere cupiunt. Argumentum, illos multum pro faciffe. Quicunqi ministros odio habent, Euangelij gustu nondū habent aliquem.
units.tr: 3. Paul cannot remain, because it was necessary for him to be at the feast in Jerusalem.

units.la: ¶ 3. Paulus manere non potest. Quia necesse erat, illū in sosto Hierosolymis ef-
units.tr: ¶ 3. Paul could not stay, because it was necessary for him to be at the feast in Jerusalem.

units.la: Paulus Ephesi docet Iudaeos.
units.tr: Paul teaches the Jews at Ephesus.

units.la: fe. Id vero instigante spiritu sensit, qui illi rerum agendarum dux fuit, vt vidimus Act. 16. Non quidem festi religio ipsum traxit, sed in conuentu frequenti plures conuenti potuerunt. Est autem memorabile quod ab illis diuellitur, de quibus tanta magni profectus spes affulgebat. Sed ita ratio-nem Dei arbitrio subijci debere, discimus.
units.tr: ...to be there. He felt this under the prompting of the Spirit, who was the leader of his actions, as we saw in Acts 16. It was not the religious observance of the feast that drew him, but in a crowded assembly more people could be gathered. It is memorable that he is torn away from those in whom great hope of progress was shining. But from this we learn that reason must be subject to the will of God.

units.la: ¶ 4. Quomodo discedit? Valedicit, quod gratitudinis est. Relinquit illis Aqui-la, ne omnino destituerentur. Pollicetur reditum, si ita velit Dominus. Argumenta haec sunt praeclari in illos studij. Interim imitanda modestia & religio, qui nil teme-re praesumit, quamuis refancta. Quae er-go temeritas, in prophanis tibi aliquid trium buere? Vide Iacob. 4. Luc. 12. &c.
units.tr: ¶ 4. How does he depart? He bids farewell, which belongs to gratitude. He leaves Aquila behind for them, so that they should not be utterly left destitute. He promises to return, if the Lord so wills. These are the arguments of his excellent zeal for them. Meanwhile we must imitate his modesty and piety, for he presumes nothing rashly, however much he is pressed. What rashness, then, has ever been granted to you in worldly matters? See James 4; Luke 12, etc.

units.la: III. Epheso abit Caesaream. Inde Hiero-solymam & salutata Ecclesia venit Antio-chiam. Hinc Galatas & Phryges perambu-lat, vbique confirmans fratres in fide. Non enim ignorabat Satanae artes, 2. Cor. 11. Ita alibi ipsum fecisse vidimus, Actorum 14. & 16.
units.tr: III. He goes from Ephesus to Caesarea. From there he went up to Jerusalem, greeted the Church, and came down to Antioch. From there he travels through Galatia and Phrygia, everywhere strengthening the brothers in the faith. For he was not ignorant of Satan's arts (2 Cor. 11). We have seen him do the same elsewhere, in Acts 14 and 16.

units.la: Not. ¶ Laboriosam Pauli industriam. Pudeat nos socordiae nostrae. Obseruent etiam laruati Episcopi, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: Note. Consider the laborious diligence of Paul. Let us be ashamed of our sloth. Let the masked bishops also take note, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA . CXLIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CXLIX.

units.la: 24 Iudæis autem quidam Apol‑los nomine, Alexandrinus natione, vir eloquens, peruenit Ephesum, potens in Scripturis.
units.tr: 24 Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus, mighty in the Scriptures.

units.la: 25 Hic erat initiatus in via Domini: & feruens spiritu, loquebatur & docebat diligenter ea quæ sunt Domini, sciens tantùm baptisma Iohannis.
units.tr: 25 This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.

units.la: 26 Cœpitque libere loqui in Synagoga. Quem quum audissent Aquila & Priscilla, assumpserunt eum & exquisitius ei expósuerunt viam Dei.
units.tr: 26 And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Aquila and Priscilla had heard him, they took him aside and expounded to him the way of God more accurately.

units.la: 27 Quum autem vellet transire in Achaiam, fratres eum adhortati scripserunt discipulis vt exciperent eum: qui cum aduenisset, multum contulit iis qui crediderant per gratiam,
units.tr: 27 And when he wished to pass over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples that they should receive him; and when he had arrived, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace.

units.la: 28 Magna enim contentione Iudæos magis ac magis redarguebat publice, ostendens per Scripturas IESVM esse Christum illum.
units.tr: 28 For with great vehemence he publicly refuted the Jews more and more, showing from the Scriptures that Jesus is that Christ.

units.la: Postquam Lucas res Pauli apud Corinthios & Ephesos gestas expósuit, commodè narrationem de Apollo interse rit: partim quòd hęc ijs seruit, quę de Corintho dicta sunt, eò quòd illuc profectus
units.tr: After Luke had set out Paul's affairs among the Corinthians and Ephesians, he fittingly inserts the narrative about Apollos: partly because it serves what was said about Corinth, since Apollos went there.

units.la: {Cap.18} Apollo rigauit quæ à Paulo plantata erant, 1.Cor.1.3. Partim quòd Dei prouidentia elucet, quia is suæ Ecclesiæ prospicit. Audiuimus enim Paulum ab Ephesijs, ipsum manere volentibus, auulsum fuisse. Ne quis ergo illos indignè à Christo neglectos putaret, Apollo surrogatur. Nec enim suos negligit Dominus Eph.4. Quia verò absolutissimum fidelis ministri exemplum fuit Apollo hic, singula quæ ad hunc spectant diligentissimè narrantur, quæ ordine eo, quo proponuntur, considerabimus.
units.tr: {Chap. 18} Apollos watered what Paul had planted, 1 Cor. 1.3. Partly because God's providence shines forth, since he watches over his Church. For we have heard that Paul was torn away from the Ephesians, though they wished him to remain. So that no one should think they had been unworthily neglected by Christ, Apollos is put in his place. For the Lord does not neglect his own, Eph. 4. Because Apollos was a most perfect example of a faithful minister, everything pertaining to him is narrated most carefully; we shall consider these things in the order in which they are set forth.

units.la: I. Describitur persona eius. Iudæus, vt & Dei bonitas eluceat, & minùs excusabi lis fit eius gentis rebellio. Alexandrinus. Eloquens. Potens in scripturis, vtpote quas non tantùm ostentationis gratia didicerat. Institutus in via Domini Christi, vbi tamen aliquid illi defuit. Nam nouerat tantummodo baptisma, Iohan. 1. prima tantum tenebat rudimenta Christianismi, vt à Iohanne tradita fuerant. Baptismus enim pro tota doctrina sumitur, vt Matt.20. Iohannes enim præcursor Christi tantùm fuit, medius inter hunc & prophetas, Isa. 40. Mal.3.4. Luc.1. Iohan.1.3. Docuit quidem Christum, sed mysteria mortis eius, resurrectionis & ascensionis nusquam plenè tradidit, vt quæ nondum debebant re uelari. Imo etiam Apostolis anteaccepta spiritum fuerunt incognita, Mar.9. Luc.9.
units.tr: I. His person is described. He was a Jew, so that God's goodness may shine forth and the rebellion of that nation may be less excusable. He was an Alexandrian. He was eloquent. He was mighty in the Scriptures, as one who had learned them not merely for show. He was instructed in the way of the Lord Christ, though something was still lacking to him. For he knew only the baptism, John 1; he held only the first rudiments of Christianity, as they had been handed down by John. For baptism is taken for the whole doctrine, as in Matt. 20. John was indeed only the forerunner of Christ, standing midway between him and the prophets, Isa. 40, Mal. 3.4, Luke 1, John 1.3. He did indeed teach Christ, but he nowhere fully delivered the mysteries of his death, resurrection and ascension, since these were not yet to be revealed. Indeed, even the Apostles before they received the Spirit did not understand them, Mark 9, Luke 9.

units.la: Sed No T. §1. Ordinem & concathena tionem donorum huius viri Eloquentiane ceffarium donum in Ecclesia & Republi-ca versaturis, sed ex spiritu est, non natura 1. Cor.12. Scripturae cognitio. Sine hac elo quentiae nulla dignitas, vtpote quae circa res bonas tantum versabitur, Laconis di-ctum. Institutus in via Domini. Est hic omnium bonorum Colophon. Docemur, quis omnium donorum finis esse debeat, Vt Christu teneamus, & hunc tantum sectemur. In hunc finem scripturae scrutandae, Ioh. 5. Qui hunc ignorant, horum studia vaniffima sunt. Recte ergo Paulus, Phil.3.4. Cor.1. & 3. Obleruent scholae.
units.tr: But note §1. The order and chain of this man's gifts. Eloquence is a necessary gift for those who will be engaged in the Church and the commonwealth, but it is from the Spirit, not from nature, 1 Cor. 12. Knowledge of Scripture is needed. Without this, eloquence has no dignity, since it is concerned only with good things, as the saying of the Laconian has it. "Instructed in the way of the Lord": this is the summit of all good things. We are taught what the end of all gifts ought to be: that we hold fast to Christ and pursue him alone. To this end the Scriptures are to be searched, John 5. Those who do not know him, their studies are most vain. Rightly, therefore, Paul, Phil. 3.4, 1 Cor. 1 and 3. Let the schools take note.

units.la: §2. Quod tanto viro adhuc deest aliquid. Sunt ergo incrementa donorum. Imo semper aliquid adijci poterit. 1. Cor.13. Nunquam ergo nobis quiescendum est, quin semper foeneremur. Mat.25.
units.tr: §2. That something is still lacking to so great a man. So there are increases of gifts; indeed, something can always be added. 1 Cor. 13. We must therefore never rest, but always put our money out at interest, Matt. 25.

units.la: Arguuntur otiosi & praesumptuosi, qui quasi omnia assecuti sint, nihil vltra discere volunt. Hi nec seipsos bene norunt.
units.tr: Those are rebuked who are idle and presumptuous, who, as if they had attained everything, want to learn nothing further. These do not even know themselves well.

units.la: II. Quid fecerit, & vt donis his vsus sit, narratur. Ferventis spiritu tocquebatur, & quidem diligenter, & liberein Synagoga docebat ea, quae sunt Domini. No T. §1. Vsum
units.tr: II. What he did, and how he used these gifts, is narrated. Being fervent in spirit he spoke, and indeed diligently and freely, in the synagogue he taught the things of the Lord. §1. The use of God's true gifts: they should serve to illustrate the glory of him from whom they were given. The law of nature requires this. See Matt. 25.

units.la: verum donorum Dei Vt huius gloriæ ilI-lustrandæ seruiant, à quo data sunt, Exigit Lex naturæ. Vide Matth.25. Peccant otio si. Multò magis autem, qui etiam contra Dominum illis abutuntur, quod vulgò fit in spiritualibus & corporalibus.
units.tr: Those who are idle sin. Much more do those sin who even abuse them against the Lord, which commonly happens with spiritual and bodily gifts alike.

units.la: §2. Vt doceri debeat in Ecclesia. A Fer uor & Zelus adsit, vt constet ex animo rem geri. Sic Christus, Matth.7. 9. Ioh.2. Alioqui ostentationi seruitur, 1.Cor 2. Ioh an.5. Mat.23.
units.tr: §2. That he ought to teach in the Church. Fervour and zeal must be present, so that the matter is done from the heart. So Christ, Matt. 7, 9, John 2. Otherwise one serves display, 1 Cor. 2, John 5, Matt. 23.

units.la: B. Diligentia adhibeatur. Opus hac propter ingenij humani tarditatem, 1.Corinth.2. Naturæ corrupt. Rom 7 Satanæ insidias, 2.Cor.11. Matt.12. Hinc illa Pauli sunt, 1.Tim.4.2.Tim.3.4. Act 20.
units.tr: B. Diligence must be applied. The work requires this, on account of the slowness of the human intellect, 1 Cor. 2; of corrupted nature, Rom. 7; and of Satan's snares, 2 Cor. 11, Matt. 12. Hence those words of Paul, 1 Tim. 4, 2 Tim. 3.4, Acts 20.

units.la: C. Libertas, ne quid dissimuletur, Ier.1. Ezech.3.33, Gal.1. Ita agendum in omnibus aliis officijs.
units.tr: C. Freedom, so that nothing is concealed, Jer. 1, Ezek. 3.33, Gal. 1. So must one act in all other offices.

units.la: III. Aquila & Priscilla audiunt, & quia aliquid deesse vident, assumptum exactius instituunt. Ita impletur Mat.25. Habenti dabitur & abundabit. Extendendum ad omnia.
units.tr: III. Aquila and Priscilla hear him, and because they see that something is lacking, they take him aside and instruct him more exactly. Thus Matt. 25 is fulfilled: to him who has, more will be given, and he will abound. This is to be extended to everything.

units.la: Interim hic Notr. §1. Aquilæ fidem & inductiam cum charitate. Ipsi instructissimi audiunt eum docentem. Vident hunc posse multum prodesse. Non inuident ergo, imò prouehūt nec priuatā, sed Christi gloriam {a}gloriam & multorum salutem quærunt. Imitandum omnibus. In hoc autem peccant summi Theologi.
units.tr: Meanwhile note here §1. The faith and kindness of Aquila, joined with charity. They, most well instructed themselves, hear him teaching. They see that he can greatly benefit others. They therefore do not envy him but rather advance him, and they seek not their own glory but Christ's glory and the salvation of many. This is to be imitated by all. But in this the highest theologians sin.

units.la: ¶ 2. Apolli modestiam & tractabilitas. Vir doctissimus & bene meritus ab opifice & muliere doceri vult. Arguitur illorum insolentia, qui ne à Symmistis quidem edoceri & admoneri volunt. Olim talium ferocia Ecclesijs incommodauit, & hodie incommodat plurimum. Aliter Paulus 1. Cor.14.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The modesty and teachability of Apollos. A most learned man, well deserving, is willing to be taught by a craftsman and a woman. Here is rebuked the insolence of those who will not be taught or admonished even by their fellow-students. Such ferocity has long harmed the Churches, and today it harms them greatly. Paul was otherwise, 1 Cor. 14.

units.la: IV. Apollo instructus iam Corinthum abit, nimirum quòd illam Ecclesiam sua opera opus habere videret. Nouum zeli argumentum. Simile militum. Vbi hæc NOTA. ¶ 1. Fratres hortantur & commendant ipsum Corinthijs, Doctori enim bono testimonio opus est, 1. Tim. 3. Nec id negandum bene meritis. Interim cura ne indignos commendes, 1. Tim. 5. Idem in alijs quoq; obseruandum.
units.tr: IV. Apollos, now instructed, departs for Corinth, evidently because he saw that that Church had need of his work. This is a new proof of his zeal, like that of soldiers. Here note: ¶ 1. The brothers exhort and commend him to the Corinthians, for a good teacher needs good testimony, 1 Tim. 3. Nor is this to be denied to those who deserve it. Yet take care not to commend the unworthy, 1 Tim. 5. The same is to be observed in other cases too.

units.la: ¶ 2. Industria eius narratur, qui testimonio fratrum satisfecit, Multum contulit ijs, qui crediderant per gratiam. Interseritur hoc, ne quid humanæ industriæ tribuatur, 1. Cor. 3. Ioh. 6. Matt. 11. 16. Probandum in Apollo, quòd bono fratrum testimonio respondere studet, ne pudefiant.
units.tr: ¶ 2. His diligence is narrated: he satisfied the testimony of the brothers. He greatly helped those who had believed through grace. This is inserted so that nothing is attributed to human diligence, 1 Cor. 3, John 6, Matt. 11, 16. In Apollos this is to be approved: that he strives to answer the good testimony of the brothers, lest they be put to shame.

units.la: ¶ 3. Quomodo profuerit? Conuincen-
units.tr: ¶ 3. How did he profit? By convincing

units.la: do Iudæos publicè. Afferendo Christum ex scripturis. Docemur: A In Ecclesia non institutione modo, verum etiam aduersa-riorum confutatione opus esse, Tit. 1. 2. Tim 3. Vide Ier. 1. &c.
units.tr: the Jews publicly, by setting forth Christ from the Scriptures. We are taught: A. The Church needs not only instruction but also the refutation of adversaries, Titus 1, 2; 2 Tim. 3. See Jer. 1, etc.

units.la: B. Quibus armis pugnandum? Scripturis. Ergo non determinatione Concilio rum. Elucet harum dignitas.
units.tr: B. With what weapons is one to fight? With the Scriptures. Therefore not with the determinations of councils. The dignity of the Scriptures is evident here.

units.la: C. Finis Euangelicæ doctrinæ, Iesum esse Christum, Ioh 20. &c. Oremus.
units.tr: C. The end of evangelical doctrine is that Jesus is the Christ, John 20, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: HOMILIA CL.
units.tr: HOMILY 150.

units.la: FActum est autem interim dum Apollos esset Corinthi, ut Paulus peragratis superioribus partibus veniret Ephesum: vbi quum discipulos inuenisset,
units.tr: Now it came to pass, while Apollos was at Corinth, that Paul, having travelled through the upper coasts, came to Ephesus; and when he had found certain disciples there,

units.la: 2 Dixit eis: Num Spiritum sanctum accepistis postea quam credidistis? At illi dixerunt ei, Imo ne hoc quidem audimus an sit Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: 2 He said to them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" But they said to him, "No, we have not even heard whether there is a Holy Spirit."

units.la: 3 Tunc dixit eis, In quid ergo baptizati estis? At illi dixerunt, In Iohannis baptisma.
units.tr: 3 Then he said to them, "Into what, then, were you baptized?" They said, "Into John's baptism."

units.la: 4 Dixit autem Paulus, Iohannes quidem baptizauit baptismo respipiscentiæ, tia, dicens populo, vt in eum, qui venturus erat post ipsum crederent, hoc est, le sum, &c. ad Verf. 7.
units.tr: 4 Paul said, "John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, telling the people that they should believe in him who was to come after him, that is, Jesus, etc. (see verse 7)."

units.la: DEscribitur hoc Cap. vt Paulus Ephesum reuersus, sicut promiserat, Ecclesiam illic inchoatam absoluerit. Vt vero magis elucescat Dei gratia & Euangelij vis, Ephesus inspici debet. Celeberrima vrbium Asiae propter situm fertilem & emporijs aptissimam & religionem, quę plurimos attrahebat. Illic enim templum Dianae erat, à tota Asia per annos 220. conditum.
