Regnabat ergo illic superstitio, magia, luxus, &c. sic vt diceretur lumen Asiae. Hanc tamen intra biennium Paulus conuertit, vt Ecclesia ibi fuerit celeberrima, Apo. 2. Ob seruanda nobis partim gratia Dei (Eph. 2) partim vis Euangelici ministerij, quam olim Prophetae praedixerant, Isa. 19. &c. Soletur in conscientiae terroribus & conatibus hostium, 2. Cor. 10. Narratur autē ante omnia, vt quosdam fide gloriantes, nondum tamen plenè instituto s, Paulus absoluerit, & Spiritus sancti donis Ecclesiam illam nobilitârit. Locus obseruatu dignus, tum quòd olim hoc quidam abusi sunt, & hodie Anabaptistae, Ordo hic est.
units.tr: This chapter describes how Paul, returning to Ephesus as he had promised, completed the Church that had been begun there. So that the grace of God and the power of the gospel may shine more clearly, Ephesus must be examined. It was the most famous of the cities of Asia, on account of its fertile site, its very suitable markets, and its religion, which drew very many people. For there stood the temple of Diana, founded over 220 years by all of Asia. Superstition, magic, luxury and the like therefore reigned there, so that it was called the light of Asia. Yet Paul converted this city within two years, so that the Church there became most famous (Rev. 2). This was recorded partly to keep before us the grace of God (Eph. 2), and partly the power of the evangelical ministry, which the prophets had foretold long ago (Isa. 19, etc.), and to comfort us in the terrors of conscience and the attempts of enemies (2 Cor. 10). It is related, above all, so that we may see that Paul completed what some had boasted of in faith but had not yet fully established, and that he ennobled that Church with the gifts of the Holy Spirit. This passage is worth noting, both because some abused it in former times and because the Anabaptists do so today. The order is as follows.

units.la: Ephesi com. ditto.
units.tr: Ephesus, as before.

units.la: I. Ephesum delatus Paulus (vbi iam plures erant credentes, Cap.18.) inuenit duodecim discipulos, quorum examen in stituit. Causa fuit, quòd Christianæ fidei minùs responderent. Verisimile enim est, idem Ephesi contigisse, quod hodie fit, quando veritas primùm prædicatur, nondum verò Ecclesiæ disciplina constituitur. Tunc enim multi odio potiùs prioris conditionis, cuius absurditatem & gravamina sentiunt, quàm veritatis amore Euangelicos se profitentur, Matth.13. terra petricosa. Tales quia hos videbat Paulus, ut in viam vocet, quærit num spiritum sanctum acceperint? Intelligit autem miraculosa illa dona, quæ illo tempore credentibus conferebantur iuxta promissiones, Ioel.2. Vide Act.2.8.10. Gal.3.
units.tr: I. Paul, brought to Ephesus (where many were already believing, ch. 18), found twelve disciples, whose examination he undertook. The reason was that they responded poorly to the Christian faith. For it is likely that what happened at Ephesus happens today, when the truth is first preached but church discipline is not yet established. Then many profess themselves evangelical, not out of love of the truth, but rather from hatred of their former condition, whose absurdity and burdens they feel (Matt. 13, stony ground). Because Paul saw such people, he asks, in order to call them to the right way, whether they have received the Holy Spirit. He means those miraculous gifts which were then conferred on believers according to the promises of Joel 2. See Acts 2, 8, 10; Gal. 3.

units.la: Interim No T. Quo iudicio veri Christiani agnoscantur? Si spiritum Christi habeant, Rom.8. Licet enim miraculosæ operationes cessarint, manet tamen promissio Christi, Ioh.14.16. Et necessariæ sunt reliqui spiritus effectus, ut Morti vicatio veteris hominis, Col.3. Rom 6. Regeneratio & innovatio, Ioh.3. Tit.3. Sanctificatio, 1.Cor.5.6. &c. Si qui istis omnino carent, hos Christo & fide falsò gloriari certum est, 1.Corin.4. Matth.7. Iohan.3. 1. Petri 1. &c. Seruit illis hæc eadem quæ-stio.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: by what judgment are true Christians recognized? If they have the Spirit of Christ (Rom. 8). For although miraculous operations have ceased, the promise of Christ remains (John 14:16). And the other effects of the Spirit are necessary: the mortification of the old man (Col. 3; Rom. 6), regeneration and renewal (John 3; Titus 3), sanctification (1 Cor. 5, 6), etc. If some wholly lack these, it is certain that they falsely boast of Christ and of faith (1 Cor. 4; Matt. 7; John 3; 1 Pet. 1, etc.). This same question serves them.

units.la: II. Respondent illi & crassimam ignorantiam fatentur. Imo, nec an ht Spiritus sanctus audiuimus. Atqui non poterant ignorare loca scripturæ, cum Iudæi essent, Gen. 1. Psal. 33. Isa. 61. &c. Num. 11. Sed de effectibus Spiritus loquuntur, &c. Nos contenti ijs quæ didicimus, altiora non curamus, &c.
units.tr: II. They reply, and confess the grossest ignorance: No, we have not even heard whether there is a Holy Spirit. Yet they could not have been ignorant of the passages of Scripture, since they were Jews (Gen. 1; Ps. 33; Isa. 61, etc.; Num. 11). But they are speaking of the effects of the Spirit, etc. We, content with what we have learned, do not care about higher things, etc.

units.la: NOTA. Typum carnalium, qui cum Euangelio glorientur, vim eius plane ignorant, imo si rogentur, plane negat hanc ad se pertinere, 2. Tim. 3. Tit. 1, &c. Ingens horum numerus nostro seculo, qui mortificatione ad solos Pharisæos remittunt. Et hi fere sunt, propter quos Euangelium male audit. Arguendi ergo, &c.
units.tr: NOTE. Those carnal men who boast of the gospel while plainly ignoring its power, and who, if they are questioned, flatly deny that it pertains to them (2 Tim. 3; Titus 1, etc.). Their number is great in our age, those who reduce mortification to the Pharisees alone. And these are for the most part the ones on whose account the gospel is ill spoken of. They must therefore be refuted, etc.

units.la: III. Paulus illos propius vrget, vt ex ipsorum ore illos conuincat. In quid ergo baptizati estis? Id est, Quid professi estis, cum Ecclesiæ vos adiunxistis? Respondent. In Iohannis baptismo. id est, Iohannis doctrinam & religionem profesi sumus. Hanc tenemus, & illa putamus sufficere.
units.tr: III. Paul presses them more closely, so that he may convict them from their own mouths. Into what, then, were you baptized? That is, what did you profess when you joined yourselves to the Church? They reply: Into John's baptism, that is, we have professed John's doctrine and religion. We hold to this, and think it is sufficient.

units.la: Docet ergo Paulus, ipsos Iohannis Baptisma & doctrinam non intelligere, eo quo ipse Iohannes plus quiddam à suis requisierit.
units.tr: Paul therefore teaches that they did not understand John's baptism and teaching, in that John himself required something more from his followers.

units.la: A. Iohannes pœnitentiæ studio conse-crauit suos, & hanc magno ferio requisi-uitab omnibus ordinibus,Mar.1.Luc.3.
units.tr: A. John consecrated his people to the pursuit of repentance, and required this with great zeal from all orders (Mark 1; Luke 3).

units.la: B.Locutus est de Christo,ad hunc suos relegans, vtpote in quo solo inueniatur, quod externus Baptismus figurat,Matth. 3.Ioh. 1.3. Inde colligit, illis annitendum esse,vt Christo infiniti, illius spiritu animen-tur. Alioqui baptismum Iohannis non profuturum.
units.tr: B. He spoke of Christ, sending his followers to him, since in him alone is found what the external baptism signifies (Matt. 3; John 1, 3). From this he infers that they must strive to be initiated into Christ and to be quickened by his Spirit. Otherwise John's baptism would not profit them.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Errorem turpissimum illo-rum,qui ex hoc loco euincunt non eun-dem esse externum baptismum Iohannis & Christi.Gloriam baptismo omnem eri-piunt,quæ est,quod Christus eo tingi vo-luit. Imo hoc nos relegari ad Christum Paulus docet. Interim commune dogma hic stabilitur, Minimè ferendum esse,vt hominum authoritati inhæreant & horum regulis insistant, qui Christo consecrati esse debent,1.Cor.1.3.7.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ Those most shameful errors of those who from this passage argue that the external baptism of John and that of Christ are not the same. They snatch from baptism all its glory, which is that Christ willed to be washed in it. Indeed, Paul teaches that we are sent back to Christ by this passage. Meanwhile, the common doctrine is established here: that it must by no means be tolerated that men cling to the authority of men and follow the rules of those who ought to be consecrated to Christ (1 Cor. 1, 3, 7).

units.la: IV. Credunt illi,et baptizantur in nomine Iesu,&c.Quod non ita accipi debet,quasi baptismum externum iterarint. Ita enim sequeretur,Iohannis Baptismo verum & sanctum fuisse. Atqui ab illo ipse Christus baptizatus est,Matth.3. Nec vspiam rebaptizatos fuisse legimus, quos ille baptizauit. Intelligendus ergo locus de bap-tifptifmo ignis(Matt.3.) id est, donis Spiri-tus sancti, qui ignis figurà conferri solebat,Act.2. Ita baptizandi verbo Iohannes & ipse Christus vtuntur,Mar.3.Act.1. Sic Petrus,Act.10.& 11.
units.tr: IV. They believe, and are baptized in the name of Jesus, etc. This must not be understood as if they repeated the external baptism. For then it would follow that John's baptism was true and holy. Yet Christ himself was baptized by John (Matt. 3). Nor do we read anywhere that those whom John baptized were rebaptized. The passage must therefore be understood of the baptism of fire (Matt. 3), that is, of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, which were usually conferred under the figure of fire (Acts 2). Thus John and Christ himself use the word "baptize" (Mark 3; Acts 1). So Peter (Acts 10 and 11).

units.la: Et in praesenti hoc sensu exponitur per sequentia : Et cùm imposuisset illis manus Paulus, venit Spiritus sanctus super eos, & loquebantur linguis,&c. Ergo manuum impositione toti Christo consecrati sunt.
units.tr: And in the present passage this sense is explained by what follows: And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke with tongues, etc. Therefore by the laying on of hands they were wholly consecrated to Christ.

units.la: Quare Nota. 1. Abusos fuisse veteres hoc loco, qui ab haereticis baptizatos putauerunt rebaptizandos esse. Fefellit eos, quòd Iohannis baptismû à Christi diuersum esse putauerunt. Simili ratione Anabaptistae falluntur,cum de aquae baptismo exponunt, quod de Igne,id est,Spiritus sancti & donorum ipsius collatione intelligi debet,&c.
units.tr: Wherefore note: 1. The ancients abused this passage, who thought that those baptized by heretics had to be rebaptized. They were deceived because they thought John's baptism was different from Christ's. By a similar reasoning the Anabaptists are deceived when they interpret of water baptism what must be understood of fire, that is, of the bestowal of the Holy Spirit and his gifts, etc.

units.la: 2. Fine & vsum miraculi. Voluit hoc modo Deus Euangelij authoritate inter gentes confirmare & nobilitare, Mar.16. Ioel.2.Sic factum Samariae,Act.8.Sic apud Cornelium,Act.10.&c. Deinde ijs occurrere, qui carnis licentiam quaeruntur,Iacob.2.
units.tr: 2. The purpose and use of the miracle. By this means God willed to confirm and ennoble the authority of the gospel among the nations (Mark 16; Joel 2). So it was done in Samaria (Acts 8), and with Cornelius (Acts 10), etc. Then, to meet those who seek licence for the flesh (James 2).

units.la: Credamus ergo Euangelio tam probè confirmato & profesioni fidei vitâ respondeamus. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us therefore believe the gospel so well confirmed, and let our life correspond to our profession of faith. Let us pray.

units.la: {†}Ipse porrò ingressus Synagogam, liberè loquebatur ad tres menses, disputans et suadens, quae ad regnum Dei pertinent.
units.tr: Moreover, entering the synagogue, he spoke boldly for three months, disputing and persuading concerning the things that pertain to the kingdom of God.

units.la: 8 Quum autem quidam indurarentur et parere nollent, malè loquentes de via Domini apud multitudinem, abscedens ab illis separavit discipulos, quotidie disputans in schola Tyranni cuiusdam.
units.tr: 8 But when some were hardened and would not obey, speaking evil of the way of the Lord before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of a certain Tyrannus.

units.la: 9 Hoc autem factum est per biennium: ita ut omnes qui habitabant in Asia, tum Iudaei tum Graeci, audirent sermonem Domini Iesu.
units.tr: 9 And this went on for two years, so that all who lived in Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the word of the Lord Jesus.

units.la: 10 Virtutes autem non vulgares faciebat Deus per manus Pauli:
units.tr: 10 And God worked no ordinary miracles by the hands of Paul,

units.la: 11 Ita ut etiam ad aegrotos deferrentur a corpore eius sudaria seu semicinctia, et discederent ab eis morbi, et spiritus mali ab eis exirent.
units.tr: 11 so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried from his body to the sick, and diseases left them, and evil spirits went out of them.

units.la: POstquam Diuus Lucas exposuit, ut duodecim viros Christiani nominis professioni non plenè respondentes Paulus instituerit, deinceps narrat, ut eiusdem Pauli ministerio regnum Dei apud Ephesios propagatum fit. Summa omnium praesenti loco habetur, cuius singulae partes tes infpicien dæ sunt, eó quód multa fingu lis insint, quæ ædificatiuni seruire poi- sunt, &c.
units.tr: AFTER holy Luke has set out how Paul instituted the twelve men who did not fully respond to their profession of the Christian name, he next relates how, through the ministry of the same Paul, the kingdom of God was spread among the Ephesians. The summary of the whole is given in this place, and its individual parts must be examined, because many things are contained in each that can serve for edification, etc.

units.la: I. De doctrina Pauli agitur. Synagogam ingressus Iudæis maximè prædicat, de quo iam aliquoties dictum. Elucet partim ve- ritas & bonitas Dei erga illam gentem, partim charitatis affectus in Paulo, qui tot tamque atrocibus iniurijs non potuit extingui, Rom. 9. 10. Sic Prophetæ & Christus. Imitemur.
units.tr: I. The teaching of Paul is treated. Entering the synagogue, he preached chiefly to the Jews, about which we have already spoken several times. It shines forth partly in the truth and goodness of God towards that nation, and partly in the affection of charity in Paul, which could not be quenched by so many and such atrocious injuries (Rom. 9, 10). So the prophets and Christ. Let us imitate them.

units.la: Interim NOTA. ¶ 1. Vbi docuerit? In Synagoga, vt semper alias licet non ignoraret Iudæorum mores, qui illic dominantur. Certus ergo doctrinæ locus esse debet, qui etiam non temerè deferendus est. Facit hoc ad retinendam faniorem do ctrinam & cohercendos impostores, 1 Timot. 4. Ideo Christus quoq; locos publicos frequentauit, Ioh. 18.
units.tr: Meanwhile, NOTE. ¶ 1. Where did he teach? In the synagogue, as he always did elsewhere, although he was not unaware of the customs of the Jews, who hold sway there. A fixed place for teaching ought therefore to exist, and it should not be lightly abandoned. This serves to keep sounder doctrine and to restrain impostors, 1 Tim. 4. For this reason Christ also frequented public places, John 18.

units.la: Arguuntur exemplis his Anabaptistæ, qui cœtus publicos horrent, & non nisi in angulis spargunt sua dogmata.
units.tr: Anabaptists are refuted by these examples, since they shun public assemblies and scatter their teachings only in corners.

units.la: ¶ 2. Modum. Libere egit, primo quidem disputans, confutando nimirum errores Iudæorum. Deinde suasit, & hortatus est vt veritati cederent.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The manner. He acted freely, first indeed by disputing, that is, by refuting the errors of the Jews. Then he persuaded and exhorted them to yield to the truth.

units.la: Patet hic quis optimus sit docendi modus. Confutantur impij & quicquid veritati obstat, Tit.1. Simile agriculturae. Deinde vrgeantur homines ad amplectendam veritatem, 2. Tim. 4. Luc 14. Errant turpiter simé qui nudam scripturae tractationem sufficere dicunt.
units.tr: Here it is clear what the best method of teaching is. The impious are refuted, and whatever stands in the way of the truth, Titus 1. It is like farming. Then people are pressed to embrace the truth, 2 Tim. 4, Luke 14. Those men err shamefully who say that the bare handling of Scripture is enough.

units.la: §3. Materiam & argumentum: Regnum Dei. Intelligitur salutis mysterium, cuius executor & administrator Christus fuit. De hoc carnales opiniones habebant Iudaei, vt patet, Matth. 20. Luc. 24. Act. 1. Alij vero cerimonijs considebant. Exposuit ergo huius veritatem Paulus. Quod non terrenum, sed spirituale sit, Ioh. 18. Quod non externis cerimonijs, sed fide constet, Rom. 14. 1. Cor. 5. 6. 10. Ioh. 4. &c.
units.tr: §3. The matter and subject: the kingdom of God. It is understood to be the mystery of salvation, whose executor and administrator was Christ. The Jews had carnal opinions about this, as is plain from Matt. 20, Luke 24, Acts 1. Others, however, relied on ceremonies. Paul therefore expounded the truth of this. That it is not earthly but spiritual, John 18. That it consists not in external ceremonies but in faith, Rom. 14, 1 Cor. 5, 6, 10, John 4, etc.

units.la: Interim obserua salutis negotiu, Dei regnū dici. Exprimitur finis redemptionis, qui est vt pulso diabolo Deus suum in nobis regnum & ius obtineat. Pro hoc oramus, Matth. 6. Sunt ergo Pseudochristiani, qui sub Christi titulo sese diabolo regendos praebent. Christiani non sunt, nisi qui sub Christi regno sunt. Vide Ro. 6. 2. Cor. 6. Tit. 2. 3. Veste nuptiali opus est Matth. 22. &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile observe that the work of salvation is called the kingdom of God. The purpose of redemption is expressed: that, with the devil driven out, God may obtain his own kingdom and right in us. We pray for this, Matt. 6. There are therefore pseudo-Christians, who, under the name of Christ, offer themselves to be ruled by the devil. Those are not Christians who are not under the kingdom of Christ. See Rom. 6, 2 Cor. 6, Titus 2, 3. A wedding garment is needed, Matt. 22, etc.

units.la: II. Quid cum reprobis egerit, quales passim & semper inueniuntur, Luc 2. Vbi Not. §1. Quid illi fecerint? A. Indurantur. Proprium hoc impijs, vt quo magis vrgentur verbo Dei, eo magis durefcant. Non enim habent in fe femen Dei,&c. Simile luti & Solis.Cain,Gen.4. Pharao,Exod.9 Saul,&c.Vide vnde agnoscas,&c.
units.tr: II. What he did with the reprobate, who are found everywhere and always, Luke 2. Note here. §1. What did they do? A. They are hardened. This is characteristic of the impious: the more they are pressed by the Word of God, the harder they become. For they do not have the seed of God in themselves, etc. Like clay and the sun. Cain, Gen. 4; Pharaoh, Exod. 9; Saul, etc. See by what sign you may recognise them, etc.

units.la: B. Nolunt credere. Abijciunt ergo verbum Dei & eludunt,quasi vanum & nihil ad fe pertinens,&c.
units.tr: B. They are unwilling to believe. They therefore cast away the Word of God and mock it, as if it were empty and had nothing to do with them, etc.

units.la: C. Male loquuntur de via Domini coram vulgo, vt exosam & inuisam reddant. Eo quod diaboli ingenium secuti impietatis socios habere cupiunt.
units.tr: C. They speak evil of the way of the Lord before the common people, so as to make it hateful and odious. Because they follow the nature of the devil, they want to have companions in impiety.

units.la: His gradibus progreditur impietas,do nec ad summum peruenit, vnde ad interitum ruit.Discimus primum cauendu esse ab ijs,qui nolunt toti perire,&c.
units.tr: Impiety advances by these steps, and does not reach its height until it rushes to destruction. We learn first that we must beware of those who do not want to perish altogether, etc.

units.la: ¶ 1. Quid Paulus? 1. Discedit ab illis, iuxta Christi præceptum,Luc 9.10, Mat. 10.7. Noluit ipsos inflammare magis, nec rixis inutilibus occasionem præbere.
units.tr: ¶ 1. What did Paul do? 1. He departed from them, following the precept of Christ, Luke 9, 10, Matt. 10. He did not want to inflame them further, nor to offer an occasion for useless quarrels.

units.la: 2. Segregat discipulos quoq;, nimirum ne inficerentur. Est hoc boni pastoris, non schismatici,&c.Imo vitari conuenit impio rum commercia,cum his & ipsi indurentur,& pij corrumpantur,Act 2.Apoc.18.
units.tr: 2. He also separated the disciples, namely so that they would not be infected. This is the mark of a good shepherd, not of a schismatic, etc. Indeed, it is fitting to avoid the company of the impious, since by them the godly are corrupted and themselves become hardened, Acts 2, Rev. 18.

units.la: ¶ 4. Quotidie docet in schola Tyranni cuiusdam, loco nimirum publico & commodo. Ita non cessandum ab officio, etiamsi multi mali sint. Aliunde captida occasio. Simul vides quæ vera sint Ecclesiæ exercitia, nimirum doctrinæ & verbi Dei studium, Psalm 1. Luc. 4.10. In Papatu minimè curatur, &c.
units.tr: ¶ 4. He taught daily in the school of a certain tyrant, that is, in a public and convenient place. Thus one must not cease from one's duty, even though many are wicked. Meanwhile an occasion is given elsewhere. At the same time you see what the true exercises of the Church are: namely, the study of doctrine and of the Word of God, Psalm 1, Luke 4, 10. Under the Papacy this is by no means cared for, etc.

units.la: III. Fructus, quem triplicem NOTA. Estque hæc peculiaris Dei gratia, quod fama monentur hominum animi, apud quos non sonat ministri vox. Solent autem primarium civitatum exempla latisime spargi. Interim admonentur civitates primariæ quàm diligens apud illas esse debeat pietatis & disciplinæ ratio, ne mali exempli authores sint.
units.tr: III. The fruit, which is threefold, NOTE. And this is a peculiar grace of God: that the minds of men are moved by report, among whom the voice of the minister does not sound. Moreover, the examples of the chief cities are usually spread very widely. Meanwhile the chief cities are reminded how careful the regard for piety and discipline ought to be among them, lest they become the authors of a bad example.

units.la: 2. Dominus cooperatur Paulo, & doctrinæ ipsius testimonium fert per miracula stupenda. Sic de umbra Petri dictum, Actor. 5. Impletur illud Christi, Iohan. 14.
units.tr: 2. The Lord works together with Paul and bears witness to his teaching by astounding miracles. So it was said of the shadow of Peter, Acts 5. That saying of Christ is fulfilled, John 14.

units.la: Ridiculi sunt, qui ista ad reliquiarum superstitiosum cultum transferunt. Plus tribuunt his, quàm tunicæ Christi debeatur, Mar. 5. Deus author fuisse dicitur, Paulo solum ministerium tribuitur. Finis, ut doctrinæ crederetur, Mar. 16.
units.tr: Those are ridiculous who transfer these things to the superstitious worship of relics. They attribute more to them than is owed to the garment of Christ, Mark 5. God is said to have been the author, while only the ministry is attributed to Paul. The end was that the teaching might be believed, Mark 16.

units.la: 3. Sanantur ægroti & liberantur daemonici. Euangelio salus animarum offertur, & diaboli regnum destruitur, Act. 11. 16. Luc. 11 Gen. 3.
units.tr: 3. The sick are healed and the demon-possessed are freed. Salvation of souls is offered by the gospel, and the kingdom of the devil is destroyed, Acts 11, 16, Luke 11, Gen. 3.

units.la: Discamus Christo fidem habere, cuius virtuvirtute hæc omnia facta sunt, non Pauli sudariorum sanctitate, &c. Mar. 5. Lucæ 8. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us learn to have faith in Christ, by whose power all these things were done, not in the holiness of Paul's handkerchiefs, etc. Mark 5, Luke 8. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLII.
units.tr: HOMILY CLII.

units.la: 12 Aggressi sunt vero quidam ex circulatoribus Iudæis exorcistæ nomine suppe eos qui habebant spiritus malos, nomen Domini Iesu, dicentes, Adiuramus vos per Iesum, quem Paulus prædicat.
units.tr: 12 Then some of the wandering Jewish exorcists undertook to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, "We adjure you by Jesus, whom Paul preaches."

units.la: 13 Erant autem quidam filii Sceuæ Iudæi principis facere dotum septem, qui hoc faciebant.
units.tr: 13 Now there were certain sons of Sceva, a Jew and chief priest, seven in number, who did this.

units.la: 14 Respondens vero spiritus malus dixit, Iesum novi et Paulum scio: vos autem qui estis?
units.tr: 14 But the evil spirit answered and said, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?"

units.la: 15 Et insiliit in eos homo in quo erat spiritus malus, et superatis illis invaluit contra eos, ita ut nudi et vulnerati effugerent ex domo illa.
units.tr: 15 And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped upon them, overpowered them and prevailed against them, so that they fled naked and wounded out of that house.

units.la: IEsus Christus non præcipit modo Apostolis, ut Euangelium in toto orbe prædicent, verumetiam spiritu suum illis polliceatur, qui eos ducturus sit, ut hoc officio feliciter defungi possint. Promissione vero istam signis confirmat, quæ per illos acdita sunt. Inter hæc in primis memorabile est, quod Ephesi accidit. Quia enim ea ci-
units.tr: Jesus Christ not only commanded the apostles to preach the gospel throughout the whole world, but also promised them his Spirit, who would lead them so that they might discharge this office successfully. He confirmed the promise with signs, which were performed through them. Among these, the one that happened at Ephesus is especially memorable, for since that city

units.la: uitas præ aliis dedita erat superstitionibus, signis quoque singularibus opus fuit. Ideo factum vt etiam sudarijs Pauli dęmo-nes & morbi cesserint. At hic finis istorum obseruandus, ne in eorum superstitiones incidamus, qui reliquijs sanctorum vim diuinam tribuunt, & his exemplis abutun-tur variè. Sed conuincuntur: 1. Huius lo-ci authoritate qui Deo hoc omne tribuit. 2. Fine & vsu signorum, qui est vt doctri-nam obsignent, Mar. 16. At hæc ad vnum Christum remittit, Iohannis 20. 3. Exem-plis Apostolorum, qui ne sibi quidem vo-luerunt ista tribui, Actor. 3.14. His accedit præsens historia, quæ memorabile exem-plum habet diuinę seueritatis contra eos, qui verbis conceptis & nomine Christi su-perstitiose abusi sunt.
units.tr: was given over to superstitions more than others, singular signs were also needed. Hence it came about that even by Paul's handkerchiefs demons and diseases departed. But the limit of these must be observed, lest we fall into the superstitions of those who ascribe divine power to the relics of saints and abuse these examples in various ways. But they are refuted: (1) by the authority of this passage, which ascribes all this to God; (2) by the end and use of signs, which is to confirm doctrine (Mark 16), but this refers everything to Christ alone (John 20); (3) by the examples of the apostles, who did not wish these things to be ascribed even to themselves (Acts 3.14). To this is added the present history, which contains a memorable example of divine severity against those who superstitiously misused the set words and the name of Christ.

units.la: Docemur, Deum nunquam passurum, vt quæ illi debetur gloria in creaturas qualescunq; transferatur. Affuturum præ-terea suis contra omnes, qui præstant gijs suis fidei & veritatis doctrinam reddunt suspectam.
units.tr: We are taught that God will never allow the glory due to him to be transferred to creatures of whatever kind. Moreover, he will be present with his own against all who, by their trickery, make the faith and the doctrine of truth suspect.

units.la: 1. Describuntur personæ, & quid sece-rint. Iudæi fuerunt, & quidem summi sacerdotis filij. Deinde Exorcistæ, qui oberran-tes adiurationibus spirituum quaestum faciebant. Quia ergo Paulu videbant Chri-sti nofti nomine dæmonibus præcipere, & signa facere non vulgaria, nouam exorcismi for-mam finxerunt.
units.tr: 1. The persons are described, and what they did. They were Jews, and indeed sons of the high priest. Then they were exorcists, who wandered about and made profit from adjurations of spirits. Because they saw Paul commanding demons in the name of Christ and performing signs that were not ordinary, they devised a new form of exorcism.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ 1. Vnde primum exorcistæ apud Iudæos Moses nufpiam ho-rum meminit. Humanum ergo inuentum fuerunt. Initium habuerunt ex fabula de Solomone, Iof. antiq. 8. cap. 2. Ita satan pro phetis fide derogare voluit. Tandem Exorcismi instituti, quibus hodie adhuc v-tuntur Iudæi, & Christi quoque miracula his tribuunt. In præsenti magnum argu-mentum corruptionis, quod sacerdotis filij hæc exercuerunt.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. First, whence did exorcists among the Jews come? Moses nowhere mentions them. They were therefore a human invention. They had their origin in the fable about Solomon (Josephus, Antiquities 8, ch. 2). Thus Satan wished to detract from faith in the prophets. Finally, exorcisms were instituted, which the Jews still use today, and they ascribe Christ's miracles to them as well. In the present case, a great argument for corruption is that the sons of a priest practised these things.

units.la: Vides, vt nullus errorum finis sit, quàm primum à Dei verbo discedit. Idem fa-ctum in Papatu etiam, vbi Exorcistæ insti-tuti qui Baptismum & omnia sacra con-spurcarunt. Spiritus & animas adiurà-runt. Secuta Magia & Nigromantia, cui in primis studuerunt Monachi & Pontifices Romani.
units.tr: You see how there is no end to errors as soon as one departs from the word of God. The same happened in the Papacy too, where exorcists were instituted who defiled baptism and all the sacred rites. They adjured spirits and souls. Magic and necromancy followed, to which the monks and Roman pontiffs especially devoted themselves.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quales censendi, qui hodie verbis conceptis vim diuinam tribuunt contra spiritus, morbos, &c. Est hæc Iudæorum superstitio, à gentium quoq; sapientibus improbata. Pericles. 1. Contra primum præceptum salus tribuitur sono verbo-rum, characteribus. 2. Auocantur homi-
units.tr: 2. What sort of people are to be judged those who today ascribe divine power to set words against spirits, diseases, and so on? This is a Jewish superstition, also condemned by the wise men of the Gentiles (Pericles, 1). Against the first commandment, salvation is ascribed to the sound of words and to characters. 2. Men are drawn away from the invocation of God to impious arts,

units.la: Hodierni Exorcistæ quales cum fendi.
units.tr: What sort of exorcists today are to be judged.

units.la: Cap. 19. nes ab inuocatione Dei ad impias artes,& his illum quasi cogere volunt. 3. Abusus nominis Dei. 4. Deniq; non alia re diabo li regnum magis stabilitur. Ideo semper damnatae hae artes legibus Imperat. & etiam iure Pontificio.
units.tr: Chapter 19. and they wish to compel him by these. 3. Abuse of the name of God. 4. Finally, the kingdom of the devil is established by nothing more than this. Therefore these arts have always been condemned by the laws of the emperors, and also by papal law.

units.la: Nec iuuant obiectiones. 1. Qui dolent, iuuari cupiunt, nec ideo credunt diabolo. Non enim vult, vt illicitis medijs salutem quaeramus, Deus: nec iuuantur vere qui hoc faciunt. Deinde creditur in diabo- lum.
units.tr: Nor do the objections help. 1. Those who suffer wish to be helped, and so they do not believe the devil. For God does not wish us to seek salvation by illicit means, nor are those who do this truly helped. Then, they do believe in the devil.

units.la: II. Atqui magna faciunt? Verum, sed ex permissione Dei, qui vel efficaci illusione punit incredulos, 2. Theff. 2. vel fidem no- stram probat, Deuter. 13. Hic ergo simus constantes.
units.tr: II. But do they accomplish great things? True, but by the permission of God, who either punishes unbelievers with effective delusion (2 Thess. 2) or tests our faith (Deut. 13). Here, therefore, let us be steadfast.

units.la: III. Verba sancta & diuina sunt. Atqui eo deteritabilior abusus est. Et idem potestate praetexere qui iurant & execrantur. Imo quid hic desideres quoad formam. Adiurant quod etiam sancti faciunt, 2. Tim. 4. Nomen Iesu adhibent, & quidem definiunt diserte. Attamen impij censentur, & puniuntur.
units.tr: III. The words are holy and divine. But for that very reason the abuse is more detestable. And the same pretext serves those who swear and curse. Indeed, what would you want here as to the form? They adjure, which even the saints do (2 Tim. 4). They use the name of Jesus, and indeed define it clearly. Yet the impious are judged and punished.

units.la: II. Euentus rei. Spiritus malus Iesu & Paulo testimonium fert, sed ipsos impro- bat. Deinde irruit & pesimè mulctat. Quod haud dubie inuitus fecit, sed Christi vir-
units.tr: II. The outcome of the matter. The evil spirit bears witness to Jesus and Paul, but condemns those very men. Then it rushes upon them and mauls them severely. This it doubtless did unwillingly, but it is compelled by the power of Christ, who wished to avenge the abuse of his name.

units.la: Euentus Exorcista- rum funesti. sti virtute cogitur, qui sui nominis absum vlcisci voluit.
units.tr: The fatal outcome for the exorcists.

units.la: Interim No T.¶1. Verbis & sono nullam inesse vim, qua vel morbi vel dæmones pellantur. Alius usus,ut doceant & sciant uiant inuocationi. Quod aliquando quid fit,ex singulari permissione fit.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE. 1. That there is no power in words and sound by which either diseases or demons are driven out. Their other use is that they teach and make people aware of the way of invocation. That this sometimes happens is by a singular permission.

units.la: ¶2. Quid eos maneat, qui Christi nomine & mysterijs ad suum quæstum abutun-tur. Fit hoc non modo ab incantatoribus, verum etiam in religione multiuariam. 1. In Missa Christum fingunt Iouem Elici-um. Verborum recitatione tribuunt transubstantiandi vim. Deinde pane illo adva-riā abutuntur. Denique hinc quæstum fecerunt ex viuis & mortuis. 2. In clauium potestate & absolutione. Hic per confessionem penetrârunt in corda & arcana homi-num. Verbis absolutionis tribuerunt remissionem peccatorū. Instituerunt nouas expiationes. Licet non subito puniat Deus, non tamen dormitat vindicta, 2. Petri 2.
units.tr: 2. What awaits those who abuse the name and mysteries of Christ for their own gain. This happens not only among enchanters but also, in many ways, in religion. 1. In the Mass they fashion Christ as a Jupiter Elicius. They attribute to the recitation of words the power of transubstantiation. Then they abuse that bread in various ways. Finally, from this they made profit out of the living and the dead. 2. In the power of the keys and absolution. Here, through confession, they penetrated into the hearts and secrets of men. They ascribed the remission of sins to the words of absolution and instituted new expiations. Although God does not punish at once, the vengeance does not sleep (2 Pet. 2).

units.la: ¶3. Christi potentiam, qui diabolo eti-am inuito vtitur ad sui regni propagatio-nem. Cogitur hic ipsi testimonium ferre, & suis seruis nocere. Sic factum in Balaam, Num. 22.23.24. In Euangelio multa hu-ius generis extant.
units.tr: 3. The power of Christ, who even against the will of the devil uses him to propagate his kingdom. Here he is compelled to bear witness to him and to harm his own servants. So it happened with Balaam (Num. 22, 23, 24). Many things of this kind exist in the Gospel.

units.la: Quid ergo Satanam & mundum timea mus? Vicit hunc Christus, Gen 3. Ioh 12. & 16. Huic ergo fidamus, huic seruiamus, & semper Oremus.
units.tr: Why, then, should we fear Satan and the world? Christ conquered them (Gen. 3; John 12 and 16). Let us therefore trust in him, serve him, and always pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA CLIII.

units.la: Id vero innotuit omnibus tum Iudaeis tum Graecis qui habitabant Ephesi: & incidit timor in eos omnes, & magnificabatur nomen Domini Iesu.
units.tr: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

units.la: Et multi eorum qui crediderant veniebant confitentes & indicantes facta sua.
units.tr: Many of those who had believed came, confessing and declaring their deeds.

units.la: Multi vero ex ijs qui curiosas artes exercuerant, comportatos libros exusserunt in omnium conspectu: quorum supputatis pretijs, repererunt denariorum quinquaginta millia.
units.tr: Many of those who had practised curious arts brought their books together and burned them in full view of everyone. When the price was reckoned up, they found it came to fifty thousand denarii.

units.la: Ita fortiter crescebat sermo Domini, & invalescebat.
units.tr: So the word of the Lord grew mightily and prevailed.

units.la: His autem expletis, proposuit Paulus per spiritum, peragrata Macedonia & Achaia, proficisci in Hierusalem, dicens, Postquam fuero illic oportet me etiam Romam videre.
units.tr: When these things were finished, Paul resolved in the Spirit, after travelling through Macedonia and Achaia, to go on to Jerusalem, saying, "After I have been there, I must also see Rome."

units.la: Misis ante in Macedoniam duo bus ex ijs qui ipsi ministrabant, videlicet licet, Timotheo & Erasto, ipse subsitit ad tempus in Asia.
units.tr: Sending ahead into Macedonia two of those who ministered to him, namely Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a time.

units.la: QVemadmodum Dominus noster Iesus Christus Apostolos miracu-lis instruxit, vt maior esset Euangelij per ipsos praedicati authoritas: Ita eorundem miracula aduersus Magicas praestigias & incantationes fidelissimè asseruit, ne scilicet Euangelij veritas his suspecta redderetur. Exempla habuimus in Simone Mago, Bariesu & puella Pithonissa, Act.8.13.16.&c.Cum primis tamè memorabile est, quod de filijs Scenæ praecessit. Docet illud quanta sit veritate Deus sui nominis & verbi abusum vindicet, iuxta illud,Exod. 20. Item quàm nihil tribui debeat Magorum carminibus & conceptorum verborum virtuti, &c. Sequitur in praesenti, quod ad huius historiae exitum pertinet.
units.tr: Just as our Lord Jesus Christ equipped the Apostles with miracles, so that the authority of the gospel preached through them would be greater, so he also most faithfully vindicated their miracles against magical tricks and incantations, lest the truth of the gospel be made suspect by these. We have examples in Simon the Magician, Bar-Jesus, and the fortune-telling slave girl (Acts 8.13, 16, etc.). Yet what happened to the sons of Sceva is most memorable of all. It teaches how truly God avenges the abuse of his name and word, according to that saying in Exodus 20. Likewise, how little credit should be given to the songs of magicians and the power of spoken formulas, etc. What follows in the present passage pertains to the outcome of this story.

units.la: 1 Fructus totius negotij multiplex.1.Omnibus innotuit factum hoc, & Dei timorem incussit, quando illum tam seuerum sui nominis vindice viderunt, &c. N o. Vsum verum iudiciorum Dei. Timore incutere debent, & vitae emendationi seruire.
units.tr: 1. The fruit of the whole affair is manifold. (1) This deed became known to all, and it struck fear of God into them, when they saw him to be so severe an avenger of his name, etc. NOTE: the true use of God's judgments: they ought to strike fear and serve the amendment of life.

units.la: Am.5.Hunc obseruat sanctì,Dauid 2 Sam. 24.Act.2.&c. Arguitur stupor nostri secu-li, quando nec peccatorū atrocitatem agnoscimus, nec mouemur exemplis, quæ
units.tr: Amos 5. Holy men observed this, as in 2 Samuel 24 and Acts 2, etc. The stupor of our age is condemned, when we neither recognise the enormity of sins nor are moved by the examples which God

units.la: quotidie in blasphemos, ebrios, sanguina- rios Deus aedit. Vide Isa. 9.
units.tr: daily makes of blasphemers, drunkards and murderers. See Isaiah 9.

units.la: II. Multi veniunt, & sponte confitentur suafacta, id est, pristinos errores & scelera. Est hoc euidens mortificatae carnis argumentum. Huius enim ingenium est suae existimationi consulere, & proinde errores contegere. Sed praeualet studium veritatis & gloriae Dei, &c. Dauid, Psa. 51. Paulus, 1. Tim. 1.
units.tr: II. Many come and freely confess their deeds, that is, their former errors and crimes. This is clear evidence of a mortified flesh. For it is the nature of the flesh to look after its own reputation and therefore to cover its errors. But the zeal for truth and for the glory of God prevails, etc. David, Psalm 51; Paul, 1 Timothy 1.

units.la: NOT. Qualis exigatur peccatorum confessio: Publica, quae gloriae Dei & mul- torum emendationi seruiat, &c. Ridiculi nimis sunt, qui hoc exemplo auricularem confessionem stabiliunt, cum nihil infit fi- mile. Hi quid ante fidem receptam passi sint publice fatentur, vt grati sint Deo. Hic omnium & singulorum, imo occultorum, enumeratio exigitur in aurem sacrificuli. Hi semel tantum &c. Item non omnes, nec coacti, sed multi & sponte, &c. Vide 1. Ioh. 1. Psal. 32. &c.
units.tr: NOTE: What sort of confession of sins is required: a public one, which serves the glory of God and the amendment of many, etc. Those are far too ridiculous who establish auricular confession by this example, since nothing like it is there. These people publicly confess what they suffered before receiving the faith, in order to be pleasing to God. Here the enumeration of all and each, even secret sins, is demanded into the ear of the little priest. These confessed only once, etc. Likewise not all, nor under compulsion, but many and of their own accord, etc. See 1 John 1; Psalm 32, etc.

units.la: III. Factis testantur poenitentiam. Congerunt enim libros publice & exurunt. Indicatur pretium flore. 6666. Fuerunt non Magici modo, sed quotquot inanibus potius & offendiculi plenis quam necessarijs studijs seruiunt: vt Astrologici, Geomantici, Aruspices, &c. Causa, quod partim scelerum
units.tr: III. They testify to repentance by their deeds: for they gather their books together publicly and burn them. The price is indicated as 6666. There were not only magicians but all who devoted themselves to empty studies, full of stumbling-blocks rather than useful ones: such as astrologers, geomancers, diviners, and so on. The reason was partly that they hated the instruments of their sins,

units.la: lerum instrumenta odiunt,partim quod peccandi ansam praefcindunt.
units.tr: partly that they cut off the occasion of sinning.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Pœnitentiæ veræ proprium. Peccatum sic odisse, vt nec instrumenta nec memoriam ferre possis. Similia Pfal. 51. Matth 26. Hinc fit, quod verè pœnitentes pretiosissimarum rerum iacturam leuem ducunt. Vnde simul constat,eos non verè pœnitere, imò ne peccata quidem adhuc agnoscere, quicunque superstitionis & scelerum organa studiosè retinent, vel etiam horum memoriâ oblectantur. Imagines,libri impuri,vestes,&c. Quanto minus,qui scelerum comemnratione delectantur.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ A mark of true repentance: to hate sin so that you can bear neither its instruments nor its memory. Similar things in Psalm 51; Matthew 26. Hence it follows that those who truly repent count the loss of most precious things a trifle. From this it is also clear that those who keep carefully the instruments of superstition and of crimes, or even take pleasure in remembering them, do not truly repent, and indeed do not yet recognise their sins. (Images, impure books, garments, etc.) How much less those who delight in recalling their crimes.

units.la: IV. Verbum Dei potenter credit, aucto nimirum discipulorum numero. Deinde confirmatum est, in animis scilicet credentium, ita vt quotidianos in fide progressus facerent. NOT. ¶ Effectum prioris pœnitentiæ. Sublatis impietatis organis pro ficere potest verbum Domini. Simile agriculturæ. Vbi vero illa reliquuntur, & tu ta omnia sibi promittunt homines, redit Satan, Matth. 12. Luc. 11. Ideo officinas impietatis deleuerunt pij reges, vt Iehu, 2. Reg. 9. 10. Ezechias, 2. Reg. 18. Iosias, 2. Reg. 22. 23. In hoc multum hodie peccant Euangelici, quod aliquibus pessimè cessi- fe vidimus.
units.tr: IV. The word of God grew powerfully, the number of disciples of course increasing. Then it was strengthened, namely in the minds of believers, so that they made daily progress in faith. NOTE. ¶ The effect of the earlier repentance: once the instruments of impiety are removed, the word of the Lord can make progress. Similar to agriculture. But where those instruments are left, and men promise themselves everything safe, Satan returns (Matthew 12; Luke 11). Therefore godly kings destroyed the workshops of impiety, as Jehu (2 Kings 9, 10), Hezekiah (2 Kings 18), and Josiah (2 Kings 22, 23). In this respect the evangelicals sin greatly today, in that we have seen it turn out very badly for some.

units.la: Effectus pœnitentiæ.
units.tr: The effect of repentance.

units.la: II. Nouum Pauli consilium subijcitur, quod ex spiritus suggestione cepit, de qua iam saepe diximus. Erat illi commissa Ecclesiarum cura. Voluit ergo redire in Macedoniam & Achaiam, nimirum vt Ecclesias ante constitutas confirmaret, & vt illic colleftam eleemosynam Hierosolymas deferret, vt videre est 1 Cor.16. 2.Cor.8 9 Inde Romam concedere statuit, Rom. 1. Ne quid tamen in confulto ageret, premit tit Timotheum & Eraftum, qui nimirum explorent & praeparent, &c.
units.tr: II. Paul's new plan is set out, which he undertook at the prompting of the Spirit, of which we have often spoken already. The care of the churches had been committed to him. He therefore wished to return to Macedonia and Achaia, namely to strengthen the churches already founded, and to carry the collected alms there to Jerusalem, as may be seen in 1 Corinthians 16 and 2 Corinthians 8, 9. From there he decided to go on to Rome (Romans 1). Yet, lest he act without deliberation, he sends ahead Timothy and Erastus, who were to spy things out and prepare the way, etc.

units.la: NOT. 1. Quanta cura opus fit in ferendis Ecclesijs, quando exercitatissimus Apostolus, cui tot agenda restabant, ties inuisit, &c. Act.14.15. 2 Cor.11. Noue- rat Satanae artes & humani ingenij lubricitatem, 2.Cor.11.
units.tr: NOTE 1. How great a care is needed in governing the churches, when the most practised Apostle, who still had so much to do, visited them so often, etc. (Acts 14, 15; 2 Corinthians 11). He knew the arts of Satan and the slipperiness of human nature (2 Corinthians 11).

units.la: Arguuntur, qui omne huius generis studium inutile & superuacaneum esse clamant. Hi seipsos non norunt.
units.tr: They are condemned who cry out that all study of this kind is useless and superfluous. These do not know themselves.

units.la: 2.Fidei virtus ingenium elucet. Non iners & otiosa, sed industrios reddit in sua vocatione. Ardet enim studio gloriae Dei, & proximi amore, Gal.5.Paulum vide, qui nec laborib. nec periculis fatigatur. Transferant ad fe omnium ordinum homines, & sic factis fidem testentur, Iac.2. Interim circumspecta quoque est fides, non temeraria. Vtebatur spiritu duce, praemittit tamen sibi fidos. Vbi quid de expressum Dei verbum habet, iussa capessit, nihil disputans. At vbi specialia incidunt, de quibus certum Dei praeceptum nō habetur, prudenter agit, Matt. 10. Magna hodie necessitas.
units.tr: 2. The virtue of faith shows in one's character. It is not idle and lazy, but makes men diligent in their calling. For it burns with zeal for the glory of God and with love of neighbour (Galatians 5). Look at Paul, who is wearied neither by labours nor by dangers. Let men of every rank apply this to themselves, and so bear witness to their faith by their deeds (James 2). Meanwhile faith is also circumspect, not rash. Paul was guided by the Spirit, yet he sends trusty men ahead of himself. Where the matter is expressly contained in the word of God, he takes up the commands without disputing. But where particular matters arise, about which there is no certain command of God, he acts prudently (Matthew 10). There is great need of this today.

units.la: Hanc regulam secuti officia nostra constanter obeamus, & in ijsdem indesinenter Oremus.
units.tr: Following this rule, let us faithfully perform our duties, and in them pray without ceasing.

units.la: HOMILIA CLIV.
units.tr: HOMILY CLIV.

units.la: 22 Ortus est autem illo tempore tumultus non parvus ob viam Domini
units.tr: 22 A great stir arose at that time concerning the Way of the Lord.

units.la: 23 Nam quidam nomine Demetrius, signator argenti, qui faciebat templa Dianae argentea, praebebat artificibus non parvum quaestum.
units.tr: 23 For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Diana, provided no small profit to the craftsmen.

units.la: 24 Quibus congregatis, & ijs qui similium rerum erant opifices dixit, Viri, scitis ex hoc opificio nostras esse facultates.
units.tr: 24 He gathered them together, with the workmen of like trades, and said, Men, you know that our wealth comes from this trade.

units.la: 25 Et spectatis & auditis Paulum non solum Ephesinam, sed prope totius Asiae multam turbam persuadendo auertisse, quod dicat deos illos non esse, qui manibus fiant
units.tr: 25 And you have seen and heard that Paul has turned away not only Ephesus but nearly all of Asia, by persuading a great crowd that those gods are not gods which are made with hands.

units.la: 26 Periculum est autem non solum nobis pars ista, sed per ipsum confutata pereat, sed etiam ne magnae deae Dianae templum pro nihilo putetur, futurumque sit vt etiam destruatur maiestas eius, quam tota Asia & orbis colit.
units.tr: 26 There is danger not only that this part of our trade will perish, refuted through him, but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana will be thought of as nothing, and that her majesty, which all Asia and the world worships, will be destroyed.

units.la: QVamuis Paulus Apostolus ab Ephesijs summa animi promptitudine exceptus fuerit, & illic per biennium tanto cum fructu docuerit, vt non modo multi ex vulgo, verùmetiam ex Asiae principibus crediderint, vt postea paterent: tandem tamen hoc ipsum, quod alibi, experitur, turbas nimirum & seditionem publicam qua iniquissimè exagitatur, & periculum subit grauissimum, 1. Cor.15. Describit hanc in praesenti Lucas mira diligentia, eo quod historia haec hostium veritatis ingenium, artes & arma evidentissimè ob oculos ponit, simulque docet, vt Deus suos & veritatis causam fideliter deliberare afferere soleat, &c. Ordo hic est.
units.tr: Although the apostle Paul was received by the Ephesians with the greatest eagerness, and taught there for two years with such fruit that not only many of the common people but also some of the leaders of Asia believed, so that they later stood firm, nevertheless in the end he experienced the very thing he had met elsewhere: namely, tumults and public sedition, by which he was most unjustly harassed, and he incurred the gravest danger (1 Cor. 15). Luke describes this here with remarkable care, because this story sets out most clearly the character, the tricks and the weapons of the enemies of the truth, and at the same time teaches how God is accustomed to deliver his own and to defend the cause of the truth faithfully, etc. The order is this.

units.la: I. Proponit summam. Ingens tumultus ortus est propter viam, id est, fidem & religionem Christianam. Et quidem illo tempore, quando Paulus, quasi in tuto collocatus Ephesiorum rebus alio proficisci statuerat, iamque duos ex suis praemiserat, qui omnia pararent, &c.
units.tr: I. He states the summary: a great tumult arose about the Way, that is, the Christian faith and religion. And indeed it arose at that time, when Paul, as if settled in safety, had decided to set out elsewhere, and had already sent two of his companions ahead to make all the preparations, etc.

units.la: NOTA. Vigilandum nobis esse, maximè mè quidem, quando omnia probè conse-cta putantur. Non quiescit enim satan ex pulsus,sed reditum quaerit, Mat.12. 1.Pet. 5.2.Cor. 11. Fit publicè post reformationes.Exempla veteris Testamenti. Iulianus.Priuatim item. Et habentur exempla eorū, qui subita cruce offensi sunt Mat.13.
units.tr: NOTE. We must be watchful, especially I myself, when all things are thought to be well ordered. For Satan, though driven out, does not rest, but seeks to return (Matt. 12; 1 Pet. 5; 2 Cor. 11). It happens publicly after reformations. Examples from the Old Testament. Julian. Likewise in private. And there are examples of those who took offence at the sudden cross (Matt. 13).

units.la: Consoletur tamen nos, quod vtut furiat satan, nihil tamen in Christum iuris habet Ioh 14. Imo iam deiectus,Ioh.12.16. Luc.11.Mat.12.Nihil ergo timeamus,Mat. 16 Rom.8.&c.
units.tr: Yet let this console us: however furiously Satan rages, he has no right over Christ (John 14). Indeed he has already been cast down (John 12; Luke 11; Matt. 12). Therefore let us fear nothing (Matt. 16; Rom. 8, etc.).

units.la: II. Author seditionis & eiusdem mini stri fiue adiutores describuntur. Fuit quidam Demetrius argentarius, homo diues, qui delubra,id est, aediculas & reliqua ad cultum Dianae pertinentia parabat,& magnum quaestum praestabat opificibus diuersi generis.
units.tr: II. The author of the sedition and his ministers or helpers are described. There was a certain Demetrius, a silversmith, a wealthy man, who made shrines, that is, small temples and other things pertaining to the worship of Diana, and provided great profit to workmen of various kinds.

units.la: Fuit enim Ephesi Dianae templum in toto orbe celeberrimum. Colebatur sub πολυμαστῳ siue Multimammiae nomine, ceu omniū animantium nutrix. Ad hanc peregrinationes fiebant. Emebantur imagines templi,&c. Non possunt ergo Pauli doctrinam,superstitioni aduersam, ferre, qui ex hac quaestum habebant.
units.tr: For at Ephesus the temple of Diana was the most famous in the whole world. She was worshipped under the name of Polymastos, or Multimammia, as the nurse of all living things. Pilgrimages were made to her, and images of the temple were bought, etc. Therefore those who made profit from it could not bear Paul's teaching, which was opposed to superstition.

units.la: NOTA 1.Euangelium per se seditionum non esse. Nam vt Deus vnit homines
units.tr: NOTE 1. The gospel is not in itself a cause of sedition. For just as God unites men

units.la: Cap. 19. (Ioh.17.) Ita charitatem & pacem quàm maximè commendat, Matth. 5. Ioh. 13. 15. Rom.12. &c. Et hic diserte Demetrius pro ducitur seditionis author, non Paulus. Ex empla similia sunt in prophetarum & Christi historia, Luc.23. Item Act.13.14 16.17.18 Non ergo temere ijs credendum, qui seditionis accusant Euangelij praecones, sed indaganda veritas.
units.tr: Chap. 19 (John 17). So it commends love and peace most highly (Matt. 5; John 13, 15; Rom. 12, etc.). And here Demetrius is plainly presented as the author of the sedition, not Paul. Similar examples are found in the history of the prophets and of Christ (Luke 23); likewise Acts 13, 14, 16, 17, 18. Therefore we should not lightly believe those who accuse the heralds of the gospel of sedition, but the truth must be sought out.

units.la: 2. Qui veri seditionum contra Euangelium authores sint? Quotquot ex rebus a Deo prohibitis viuunt & voluptuantur.
units.tr: 2. Who are the true authors of sedition against the gospel? All those who live by, and take their pleasure in, things forbidden by God.

units.la: A. Papa cum suis creaturis. Is Demetrij instar maximum quaestum habet. Deinde Episcopis & sacrificulis, Monachis item prospicit varie, ius dans emendi & vendendi, Apoc.13. Isti omnes ferre non possunt Euangelium, quia haec euertit, Zach. 14. Ioh.2. Mat.21. Act.8.
units.tr: A. The Pope with his creatures. He, like Demetrius, has the greatest profit. Then he provides in various ways for bishops and little priests, and likewise for monks, giving them the right to buy and sell (Rev. 13). All of these cannot bear the gospel, because it overturns these things (Zech. 14; John 2; Matt. 21; Acts 8).

units.la: B. Principes & nobiles, qui Ecclesiasticis bonis liberorum multitudini prospiciunt. Indignum putant suos ad operas regari.
units.tr: B. Princes and nobles, who provide for the large numbers of their children from ecclesiastical goods. They think it unworthy that their own sons should be made to work.

units.la: C. Sordidiores ex vulgo, qui ex Monachis & sacrificulis in de viuunt. Hi ventris gratia quiduis persuaderi sibi patiuntur.
units.tr: C. The baser sort of the common people, who live off the monks and little priests. These, for the sake of their belly, allow themselves to be persuaded of anything.

units.la: D. Qui sceleribus vel voluptatem vel quaestum venantur. Viurarij. Militès. Scorratores. Ebrij &c. Hi omnes sua facta arguì nolùt Io.3. Deu.27. Hab.2.1. Go.5.6. Heb.13
units.tr: D. Those who hunt after pleasure or profit through crimes: usurers, soldiers, plunderers, drunkards, etc. All of these refuse to have their deeds rebuked (John 3; Deut. 27; Hab. 2; Gal. 5, 6; Heb. 13).

units.la: III. Oratio Demetrij ponitur. Caput est, non ferendum esse Paulum, qui sua doctri na abducat a veteri religione homines. Ratio tiones habet. 1. Ab vtili. Interuertitur non ster quæstus, & vobis erit fame moriendu, si Pauli sententia vbique præualuerit.
units.tr: III. The speech of Demetrius is set out. Its main point is that Paul, who turns people away from the old religion by his teaching, must not be tolerated. He has reasons. 1. From the useful: our trade is being diverted, and we shall have to die of hunger if Paul's view prevails everywhere.

units.la: 2. A necessario. Totam enim Asiam ferè persuasit, quare amplius res dissimulari non potest.
units.tr: 2. From the necessary: he has persuaded almost all of Asia, so the matter can no longer be ignored.

units.la: 3. Ab honesto. Non de quæstu nostro tantum modo agitur, sed Dianæ nostræ maiestas in periculum venit, quam tota Asia colit, cuiusque cultus tot iam seculis in orbe durauit. Quasi diceret. Quàm turpe si hanc domi perire patiamur?
units.tr: 3. From the honourable: it is not only our gain that is at stake, but the majesty of our Diana is in danger, which all Asia worships, and whose worship has lasted for so many centuries throughout the world. As if he said: how shameful it would be if we allowed her to perish at home!

units.la: Interim hic NOT. ¶ 1. Artes impiorum & mores. Solius privati commodi cupidi tate extimulantur. Interim religionem & rempublicam quoq; prætexunt. Sic Caiaphas, Ioh. 11. Sic hodie Monachi & qui Patum falsum vellent. Sed pauci tam inge nui reperiuntur, vt Demetrius hic. Discè diligenter obseruare quò tendant, nec illorum clamoribus citò crede, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile here note: 1. The arts and manners of the wicked. They are spurred on only by the desire for private advantage. Yet they also put forward religion and the commonwealth as pretexts. So Caiaphas (John 11). So today the monks, and those who wish to defend the false Fathers. But few are found as ingenious as this Demetrius. Learn diligently to observe where they are heading, and do not quickly believe their outcries, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quibus argumentis ferè superstitionem tueantur impij Multitudinis con sensu, regum & principum authoritate. Sic Amoz 7. Externæ religionis splendore, Temporis diuturnitate. Priuato com-
units.tr: 2. By what arguments the impious defend superstition: by the agreement of the multitude, by the authority of kings and princes (so Amos 7); by the splendour of an external religion; by the long duration of time; by private

units.la: modo,& hæc quidem ratio maximè plau-sibilis. Vulgaria hæc hodie. Sed turpe est, Christianos homines Ethnicorum argu-mentis vti. Ex scripturis causa hæc dijudi-cari debet,& his firmiter insistendum,Io-han.5.2.Tim.3.
units.tr: advantage. This last argument is by far the most plausible. These commonplaces are heard today. But it is shameful for Christians to use the arguments of the heathen. This cause must be judged from the Scriptures, and we must stand firmly on them (John 5; 2 Tim. 3).

units.la: ¶3. Euangelij finis & vis. Paulus do-cens non esse Deos qui manibus fiunt, & intra biennium Dianæ cultum & templum vile fecit,quod per an.220.extructum fue-rat,& cui olim Persæ pepercerant. Dein-de populum auertit à superstitione. Vbi hæc fiunt, veré profecerunt homines in Euangelio.
units.tr: 3. The aim and power of the gospel. Paul, teaching that the gods made by hands are not gods, and within two years made the worship and temple of Diana worthless, which had been built over 220 years earlier and which the Persians had once spared, turned the people away from superstition. Where these things happen, people have truly made progress in the gospel.

units.la: Examina te ad horum exemplum, & vi-de num verè credideris. Oremus
units.tr: Examine yourself by the example of these things, and see whether you have truly believed. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLV.
units.tr: HOMILY CLV.

units.la: 27 His autem auditis pleni excan-descentia clamauerunt dicentes, Ma-gna Diana est Ephesiorum.
units.tr: 27 When they heard this they were filled with anger and cried out, saying, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians."

units.la: 28 Et impleta est ciuitas tota con-fusione: & irruerunt cocorditer in thea-trum,correpto Caio & Aristarcho Ma-cedonibus,socijs peregrinationis Pauli.
units.tr: 28 And the whole city was filled with confusion. They rushed together into the theatre, seizing Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, companions of Paul's travels.

units.la: 29 Paulo vero volente prodire ad populum, non siuerunt eum prodire discipuli.
units.tr: 29 When Paul wanted to go out to the people, the disciples would not let him go out.

units.la: 30 Sed & quidam ex Asiæ pri-mori• moribus, quum essent ei amici, rogarunt ne se daret in theatrum.
units.tr: 30 But some of the chief men of Asia, since they were his friends, begged him not to give himself up to the theatre.

units.la: 31 Alij igitur aliud clamabant: erat enim concio confusa, & plerique nesciebant cuius rei causa convenissent
units.tr: 31 Some therefore cried out one thing, others another, for the assembly was confused, and most did not know why they had come together.

units.la: 32 Ex turba vero quidam produxerunt Alexandrum, propellentibus eum Iudaeis. Alexander igitur quum manu silentium fecisset, volebat causam dicere re ad populum.
units.tr: 32 Some of the crowd then drew Alexander forward, the Jews pushing him on. Alexander, therefore, when he had made silence with his hand, wanted to make a defence before the people.

units.la: 33 Quem vt cognouerunt Iudaeum esse, vox extitit vna omnium, quasi ad horas duas clamantium, Magna Dia na Ephesiorum.
units.tr: 33 When they knew he was a Jew, one voice arose from them all, as they cried out for about two hours, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians."

units.la: Iuinus Lucas hoc libro ex spiritus sancti suggestione non modo persecutiones a Magistratibus legitime institutas contra Apostolos, verum etiam in sanas vulgi seditiones, quibus exagitati sunt, commemorat. Arguunt hanc mundi ingratitudinem, & hanc merito puniri docent. Vide Act. 13.14.16.17.18.&c. Praecipua autem praefens est, cuius visus est duplex. A. Ministrorum institutioni seruit, ne his tanquam re insolita offendantur, nec harum metu officium negligant, Cogitent Ecclesiam nauì similē esse, quae ventis agitatur (Mar.4.Mat.8.14.) nec vitari posse seditiones, cum tot sint, qui Enangelium ferre non possunt. Matth. 10. Sufficiat ijs, si ipsi nullam his causam praebeant. Si alii excitent, euentum Deo per mittant, & perstent in officio. Ambrosius lib. 5. Epistola 33. &c.
units.tr: Luke, in this book, by the prompting of the Holy Spirit, records not only the persecutions lawfully instituted by the magistrates against the apostles, but also the groundless uprisings of the common people by which they were harassed. They point out this ingratitude of the world and teach that it is rightly punished. See Acts 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, etc. The principal use of this passage is twofold. A. It serves to instruct ministers, so that they are not offended by these things as if they were unusual, nor neglect their duty out of fear of them. Let them consider that the Church is like a ship tossed by the winds (Mark 4; Matt. 8:14), and that seditions cannot be avoided, since there are so many who cannot bear the gospel. Matt. 10. It is enough for them if they themselves give no cause for these. If others stir them up, let them commit the outcome to God and persist in their duty. Ambrose, book 5, letter 33, etc.

units.la: B. Omnium instituunt, feruit, neminiftros & Euangelium seditionū causam putent, sed penitius inspiciant rem, & eos authores deprehendent, qui Euangelio coercere nolunt. Talis fuit in praefenti Demetrius, cuius imitatores sunt, quicunque hodie contra Euangelium tumultuantur. Sed uideamus reliqua, &c.
units.tr: B. It instructs everyone that they should not think ministers and the gospel the cause of sedition, but should look more deeply into the matter and detect those authors who are unwilling to be restrained by the gospel. Such was Demetrius in the present case, and his imitators are all who today make tumult against the gospel. But let us see the rest, etc.

units.la: I. Descriptio seditionis, In qua Not. ¶1.
units.tr: I. Description of the sedition, in which Note 1.

units.la: Causam. Replentur ira, quae consultor est peffimus, nec quicquam recti operatur. Iac. 1. Concitauit hanc periculum sui quae ftus, quod imminere Demetrius praedixerat, & forte iam sentiebant, nec enim quicquam est, quod indignius ferat mundus, &c. Haec ipsa causa est tumultuum nostri seculi. Irascuntur Pontifices, Episcopi, Sacrificuli, Principes, Nobiles, Vulgus, &c. Ita frementes concurrunt, Psalm. 2. Quid ergo boni ex illorum Comitijs speres?
units.tr: Cause. They are filled with anger, which is the worst counsellor and accomplishes nothing right. James 1. This was stirred up by the danger to their livelihood, which Demetrius had predicted, and perhaps they already felt it; for there is nothing the world bears more indignantly, etc. This very cause is the source of the tumults of our age. Pontiffs, bishops, sacrificers, princes, nobles, the common people, etc. are angry; thus raging they come together, Psalm 2. What good, then, can you hope for from their assemblies?

units.la: ¶2. Clamant: Magna Diana Ephesiorum. Ita testantur se huius cultu etiam sanguine asserturos esse. Sicque religione quaestui praetexunt. Patet hostium veritatis aestutia, quam sufficiam improbitatem tegunt. Ita hodie Dianas & Mariam tonant. Impudentius vero quàm Ephesij. Dianam enim reuera oppugnauit Paulus. Quis autem hos impugnat, aut debitû honorem negat? Fatemur omnia, quae scripturae his tribuunt.
units.tr: ¶2. They shout, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians." In this way they declare that they will defend her worship even with blood, and so they cloak their profit with religion. The cunning of the enemies of the truth is plain, which they cover with a pretence of worship however wicked. So today they thunder for Dianas and for Mary. But more shamelessly than the Ephesians. For Paul really did attack Diana. But who attacks these women, or denies them their due honour? We grant all that the Scriptures attribute to them.

units.la: ¶ 3. Tota cuntas impletur confusione. Id vanus Demetrius facere potuit. Vide quid sit pauculos seditiosos ferre. Vna scintilla ingens incendium excitat. Sic Corah cum suis, Nu.16. Abiolon, 2.Sam.15 16.17. Saeba 2.Sam.20. Sic Catilina apud Saluftium,
units.tr: ¶3. The whole city is filled with confusion. Demetrius alone could do this. See what it is to tolerate a few seditious people. One spark kindles a huge fire. So Korah with his men, Num. 16; Absalom, 2 Sam. 15, 16, 17; Sheba, 2 Sam. 20. So Catiline in Sallust,

units.la: Discant magistratus initiô illis obstare, quos aliquando seditiosos fore credibile est. Plurimum hic potest morum disciplina, maximè si luxus bonis legibus coerceatur.
units.tr: Magistrates should learn to resist at the outset those whom it is credible will someday be seditious. The discipline of morals has great power here, especially if luxury is restrained by good laws.

units.la: ¶ 4. Impetu in theatrum facto, publicû locum vi occupant, & ibi innoxios rapiunt, non audita causa. Improbi semper in seditionibus praevalent. Stultissimi ergo sunt, qui ex his aliquid boni sperant. In in nocentium capita tandem furor omnis effunditur. Obstent ergo his pro virili, quicunque Respub. & Ecclesias saluas volunt.
units.tr: ¶4. With the rush made into the theatre, they seize the public place by force and carry off the innocent there without hearing the case. The wicked always prevail in seditions. Therefore those are most foolish who hope for any good from them. At last all their fury is poured out on the heads of the innocent. Let those, then, who want the commonwealth and the churches safe resist them with all their strength.

units.la: II. Quid verò Paulus? Voluit se medium inferre: nimirû vt furentes mitigaret & ne quid mali paterentur sui comites.
units.tr: II. But what did Paul do? He wanted to go in among them, certainly to calm the raging and so that his companions would suffer no harm.

units.la: {y} Quid Paulus in seditione fecerit?
units.tr: {y} What did Paul do in the sedition?

units.la: Cap.19. Sed non permittunt amici, imprimis magnates, qui populi ingenium magis perspectum habebant, &c.
units.tr: Chap. 19. But his friends do not allow it, especially the great men, who knew the temper of the people better, etc.

units.la: NOT.1 i.Pauli insignes virtutes.A.Fides eximia erga suos, quos non vult desere in periculo. Haec demum vera est amicitia, quae rarissime confspicitur hodie. Quod si vero duos comites tanti fecit, quanto pluris fieri debent Ecclesiae totae? 2.Cor.11 Act.20.
units.tr: NOTE 1. Paul's remarkable virtues. A. Exceptional fidelity toward his own, whom he does not want to desert in danger. This is true friendship, which is very rarely seen today. But if he held two companions in such regard, how much more should he hold the whole churches? 2 Cor. 11; Acts 20.

units.la: B.Constantia admirabilis, quod furentibus se vult credere. Quid hoc aliud quam si quis insano mari aut incendio se committat? At Christi promissionem & suum officiū respiciebat, Io.17 Mat.10
units.tr: B. Admirable steadfastness, in that he is willing to entrust himself to raging men. What is this but if someone committed himself to a raging sea or a fire? But he looked to Christ's promise and his own office. John 17; Matt. 10.

units.la: C.Modestia eximia, qua sanioribus con filijs cedit, nec est captiosus. Imitemur, quando maxima ingenia in periculis interdum fallantur.
units.tr: C. Remarkable modesty, by which he yields to wiser counsel and is not captious. Let us imitate this, since the greatest minds are sometimes deceived in dangers.

units.la: 2. Quod ex principibus habet amicos. Effectus Euangelij. Sic Christus Ioh,12. 3.7.Matth.27.Mar.15. Anabaptistae confutantur, qui tales Christianos esse negant. Imo nulli idonei, nisi Christiani,Exod.18. Isa.49.Psal.2.
units.tr: 2. That he has friends among the princes is the effect of the gospel. So Christ, John 12; 3, 7; Matt. 27; Mark 15. The Anabaptists are refuted, who deny that such men are Christians. Indeed, none are fit for this unless they are Christians. Exod. 18; Isa. 49; Ps. 2.

units.la: Interim vides quam vana sint praesidia huius mundi, quando isti non potuerunt obstare, quo minus seditio haec oriretur. Faciunt tamen quod possunt. Imitentur omnes pmnes Magistratus. Interim nos vni Deo fidamus, non carni, Psal. 118.146. Ierem. 17. Hunc vsum exempli huius ipse Paulus indicat, 2. Cor 1.
units.tr: Meanwhile you see how vain are the protections of this world, since these men could not prevent this sedition from arising. Still they do what they can, and let all magistrates imitate them. Meanwhile let us trust in God alone, not in flesh. Ps. 118, 146; Jer. 17. Paul himself points out this use of the example, 2 Cor. 1.

units.la: III. Redit ad seditionem 1. Alij aliud clamant, & plerique cur conuenerint, ignorant. Proprium hoc seditionibus Ceutor rente boni quoq; viri abripiuntur, simul & rudes, qui quidab improbis authoribus quæratur, plane ignorant.
units.tr: III. He returns to the sedition. 1. Some shout one thing, others another, and most do not know why they have come together. This is characteristic of seditions: even good men are carried away along with the simple, who plainly do not know what cause is being pursued by the wicked authors.

units.la: NOT. Seditiones consilio potiùs & ratione, quàm vi reprimi debere. Si enim hæc adhibeatur, fere innoxius sanguis fundi-tur. Meminerint Magistratus eius quod dicitur, Ps. 7. Vtinam cogitasset German.
units.tr: NOTE. Seditions should be restrained by counsel and reason rather than by force. For if force is applied, innocent blood is almost always shed. Let magistrates remember what is said in Ps. 7. Would that German had considered this.

units.la: II. Tandem propellentibus Iudæi Alexandrum rapiunt, nimirum Pauli fautoré. Qui cum rationem reddere vellet, denuò ad clamores conuertuntur, nihil qnàm Dianam suam in ore habentes per duas horas.
units.tr: II. At last, with those pushing him, the Jews seize Alexander, certainly a supporter of Paul. When he wants to give an account, they are turned again to shouting, having nothing in their mouths but their Diana for two hours.

units.la: NOTA. Surdos esse fere, qui ventris causa tumultuantur, & veritate plerunq; clamoribus opprimi. Sic ipse Christus Io. 18. 19. Sed tales fere seditionibus pereunt.
units.tr: NOTE. Those who make tumult for the sake of their bellies are almost deaf, and are overwhelmed by shouting rather than by the truth. Thus Christ himself, John 18, 19. But such people for the most part perish in seditions.

units.la: Interim noster languor arguitur, qui in veritatis confessione tam tepemus, cum pij superstitiones suas tanto serio tucan-tur. Vide Ps. 116. Mar. 8. Rom. 10. &c. Ore.
units.tr: Meanwhile our sluggishness is condemned, which is so lukewarm in confessing the truth, while the godly defend their superstitions with such seriousness. See Ps. 116; Mark 8; Rom. 10, etc. Ore.

units.la: HOMILIA CLVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CLVI.

units.la: 34 Tum scriba quum repreßissTet turbam, dixit, Viri Ephesij, quis enim est hominum qui nesciat Ephesiorum vrbem ædituam esse magnæ Deæ Diæ næ, & à Ioue delapsi simulachri?
units.tr: 34 Then the town clerk, when he had quieted the crowd, said: "Men of Ephesus, who is there among men who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is the temple-keeper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image that fell down from Jupiter?"

units.la: 35 Quum igitur istis non posset eos tradici, oportet vos sedatos esse, nec quic quam præceps facere.
units.tr: 35 Since these things cannot be denied, you ought to be calm and do nothing rash.

units.la: 36 Adduxistis enim homines istos, neque sacrilegos, neque contumeliosos in Deam vestram.
units.tr: 36 For you have brought these men here, who are neither sacrilegious nor blasphemers of your goddess.

units.la: 37 Quod si Demetrius & qui cum eo sunt artifices, negotium habent cum aliquo, agitur forum, & Proconsules sunt, alij alios in ius vocent.
units.tr: 37 But if Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a grievance against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls; let them bring suit against one another.

units.la: 38 Si quid autem de rebus alijs re quiritis, in legitima concione explica-bitur.
units.tr: 38 If you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in a lawful assembly.

units.la: 39 Nam periculum est ne posside-mur seditionis propter diem hodiernū, quum nulla subsit causa ob quam possi-mus reddere rationem concursus istius. Et quum hæc dixisset, dimisit concio-nem.
units.tr: 39 For there is a danger that we may be called to account for the sedition of this day, since there is no cause by which we could give an account of this gathering. And when he had said these things, he dismissed the assembly.

units.la: Vidimus nuper seditionem grauissi-mam, quæ authore Demetrio con-tra Paulum excitata fuit. In illa præter vulgi tumultuantis ingenium, Paulus ma ximè spectandus est. Constans animi ac in trepidus populi coetum vult ingredi, & rationem reddere. Id quia non licet, continet se, nimirum Deo euentum omnem permittens, nihil tamen à veritate declinans, nec quicquam dissimulans, &c. Disci mus quales nos in similí casu esse oportet at. Parati simus ad reddendam rationem, 1. Pet. 3. Quòd si id nō licet, contineamus nos, nec temerè periculis immergamus, Matth. 10 4. Interim constantes simus in veritatis agnitione, & Dominum exspe- ctemus, Psal. 27. 62. 66. Et facilè sedabit tur bas Deus, qui maximas tempestates vno verbo tranquillare potest. Vide Mar. 4. Matth. 8. 14. Exemplum huius in praesenti loco habemus: vbi Scribae opera vtitur Deus, & per hunc suos liberat, licet à reli gione alienior esset. Magna Dei potentia, qui reprobis quoque vtitur pro suo arbi- trio. Sic per Philistinos liberatur Dauid, &c. Orationis partes sunt hae:
units.tr: We recently saw a very grave sedition, which was stirred up against Paul at the instigation of Demetrius. In that affair, apart from the nature of the raging crowd, Paul is especially worth observing. Steadfast in spirit and unafraid of the people, he wishes to go in to the gathering and give an account. Since this is not permitted, he restrains himself, namely leaving every outcome to God, yet never departing from the truth nor dissembling anything, etc. We learn how we ought to be in a similar case: let us be ready to give an account, 1 Pet. 3. But if this is not permitted, let us restrain ourselves and not rashly throw ourselves into dangers, Matt. 10. Meanwhile let us remain steadfast in the knowledge of the truth and wait for the Lord, Ps. 27, 62, 66. God will easily calm the tumults, he who can still the greatest storms with a single word. See Mark 4, Matt. 8, 14. We have an example of this in the present passage, where God uses the scribe's work and through him frees his people, although he was rather alien to their religion. Great is the power of God, who uses even the reprobate at his own will. So David is delivered through the Philistines, etc. The parts of the oration are these:

units.la: I. Orditur ab eo remouendo, quod se- ditiosos maximè exasperabat. Dianae su- timebant, & ob hanc vociferabantur. At negat hanc sufficientem causam tumultu- andi esse. Quia omnes nõrunt vbe veltrà Dianae cultui esse deditam, nec quisquam
units.tr: I. He begins by removing that which especially exasperated the seditious. They were zealous for Diana and cried out on her account. But he denies that this is a sufficient cause for tumult. Because all know that your city is devoted to the worship of Diana, and no one

units.la: prohibet,quo minus hanc colatis. Decet ergo vos quietos esse,&c. Atqui non poterat ignorare Paulu secus docuisse. Sed quia frustrà disputauisset, ciuili prudentia hoc etiam dissimulat, & illi satis erat seditiosos copescere, interim de ipsa causa non valde solicitus, vt multi hodie.
units.tr: forbids you from worshipping her. Therefore it is fitting that you be quiet, etc. And yet he could not have been ignorant that Paul had taught otherwise.
