But because Paul's disputing would have been in vain, the scribe, with civil prudence, also passes this over, and it was enough for him to check the seditious; meanwhile he was not greatly concerned about the cause itself, as many are today.

units.la: Sed No T.¶ Quod Dianae imago a Ioue delapsa dicitur. Ita credebat Ephesij,& multa huius generis diabolus gentib. per suasit.Palladiu.Ancyle,&c.Nec dissimilia his in Papatu credita sunt. Maria Laureta na trans mare allata creditur.Quaedam sacella ab ipsoDeo & angelis cofecrata. Imagines aliquae a Luca pictae. Quaedam immobiles,quaedam sponte loco motę sunt. Quaedam fleuerunt, miracula ædiderunt.
units.tr: But note: that the image of Diana is said to have fallen from Jupiter. The Ephesians so believed, and the devil persuaded the peoples of many such things, the Palladium, the ancile, etc. Nothing unlike these has been believed in Papistry. The Loreto Mary is believed to have been carried across the sea. Certain shrines are believed to have been consecrated by God himself and by angels. Some images were painted by Luke. Some are immovable, some have moved from their place of their own accord. Some have wept and performed miracles.

units.la: Patet hinc quàm fœcunda sit circa imagines errorum seges,Hab.2. Lactan. Vide ad Roman.1. Quàm item contumaces & sequos faciant. Non sufficit his,quod ipsis licet credere & facere quod volunt, &c. Ita hodie. Non ergo temerè tam ferio oppugnantur à verbo Dei,Exo.20. Deut. 4.5.27.Isa.40.41.44. Habac.2.Baruch 5.1.
units.tr: From this it is evident how fruitful a seedbed of errors is in regard to images, Hab. 2; Lactantius; see on Rom. 1. Likewise how stubborn and unjust they make men. It is not enough for these people that they are permitted to believe and do what they will, etc. So it is today. Therefore they are not rashly attacked so seriously by the Word of God, Exod. 20; Deut. 4, 5, 27; Isa. 40, 41, 44; Hab. 2; Baruch 5.

units.la: loh.3.&c.
units.tr: John 3, etc.

units.la: II. Reprehendit temeritatę,quod Caio & Ariftarcho manus iniecerint. Adduxi-stis hos,neq; sacrilegos neq; contumelio-sos, fos,&c. Locum hoc habet,quia ipsi fortaf sis non docuerant. In Paulo non habuisset locu, qui diserte pasim oppugnabat idolatriam, vt vidimus Act. 17. Nec disimulasset, si praesens affuisset.
units.tr: II. He rebukes the rashness of laying hands on Gaius and Aristarchus. "You have brought these men here, who are neither sacrilegious nor blasphemers," etc. This applies here because perhaps they themselves had not taught such things. It would have had no place in the case of Paul, who openly and everywhere attacked idolatry, as we saw in Acts 17. Nor would he have dissembled had he been present.

units.la: NOTA. Quibus criminibus graue tur veritatis ministri. Sacrilegi dicuntur & blasphemi in Deos & Diuos. Hodie nil vulgarius. At si causam ipsam excutias, vtrum q; falsum est. A Sacrilegi sunt, qui opes Deo & Ecclesiae sacras rapiunt & in alios vsus couertunt. Id nemo impudentius facit quàm Episcopi, Monachi, Sacrificuli, Papa, &c. Imo propter hoc maximè indignatur, quod Christo & Ecclesiae vendicamus. Viderint tamen magistratus diligenter. B. Blasphemi in Deum & Diuos sunt, qui Dei & Christi nomine abutuntur, & Diuis debitum honorem eripiunt. Hoc ipsi faciunt, nos minimè, &c. Ipsi Dei verbo abutuntur, Dei honorem in creaturas transferunt, Diuorum fidem haereseos accusant. Habent hi patronum. Hodie nemo innocentes tuetur.
units.tr: NOTE. With what charges the ministers of the truth are burdened. They are called sacrilegious and blasphemous against the gods and the divinities. Nothing is more common today. But if you examine the cause itself, both charges are false. A: those are sacrilegious who seize the wealth consecrated to God and the Church and turn it to other uses. No one does this more shamelessly than the bishops, monks, little priests, the Pope, etc. Indeed he is most indignant about this, because we claim it for Christ and the Church. Yet let the magistrates look to this carefully. B: those are blasphemers against God and the divinities who abuse the name of God and Christ, and snatch away the honour due to the divinities. They themselves do this, we by no means, etc. They abuse the Word of God, transfer the honour of God to creatures, and accuse the faith of the saints of heresy. These men have a patron. Today no one defends the innocent.

units.la: § 2. Quod tales negat scriba, vt pote poena dignos dicturus si tales essent, Exo. 20. Iof. 7. Arguitur Christianorum languor, qui sacrilegos & blasphemos facilè ferunt, &c.
units.tr: § 2. That the scribe denies such people are guilty, as he would have said they deserved punishment if they were such. Exod. 20; Josh. 7. The languor of Christians is rebuked, who bear sacrilegious and blasphemous men with ease, etc.

units.la: III. Docet modum & rationem, qua procedant: 1. Si Demetrius & sui habent aliquam priuatam causam, agant ipsi, cùm non desint iudices & forum. Quid verò opus est, vt simul omnes implicemur causæ non ad omnes simul pertinenti? Iniqui tatis accusat Demetrius. II. Si quę vero est publica causa ad omnes pertinens, dirima tur in legitima concione, non per tumul- tum Periculum quoq; proponit.
units.tr: III. He teaches the manner and method by which they should proceed: 1. If Demetrius and his fellows have some private cause, let them pursue it themselves, since there are judges and a court. But what need is there for us all to be entangled together in a cause that does not pertain to everyone at once? Demetrius is accused of injustice. II. If there is a public cause that pertains to all, let it be settled in a lawful assembly, not by tumult. He also sets out the danger.

units.la: NOT. Formam Reipub. sub Rom. Magistratus erant certi. Agebantur forensi conuentus. Nemo nisi dicta causa & contumacus damnabatur. Publicæ autem causæ legitimis conuentibus dirimebantur, nec cuiuis permittebatur, vt vel bono zelo pu blicos cœtus conuocaret. Quia ex talibus fere seditiosis occasio offertur tumultuan di, & seditiones nihil vnquam boni pariunt. Hæc optima Rerumpub. forma, qualem ipse Deus præscripsit. Sint certi iudices, Exod. 18. Deut. 1 Rom. 13. Audiant cau sas omnes, Deut. 1. 2. Par. 19. Iuste iudicent ex Deo, Exod. 23. Leuit. 19. Psal. 72. 82. &c. Graue est hic peccare. Nil agatur seditiose. Parum Christiani sunt, qui illas nō hor rent. Vide Rom. 13. 1. Pet. 2.
units.tr: NOTE. The form of the commonwealth under the Roman magistrates was fixed. Cases were heard in the courts of law. No one was condemned unless the case had been heard and he was contumacious. Public causes, however, were settled in lawful assemblies, nor was it permitted to anyone to call together public gatherings, even from good zeal. For such matters very often offer an occasion for tumult to the seditious, and seditions never produce any good. This is the best form of a commonwealth, such as God himself prescribed. Let there be fixed judges, Exod. 18; Deut. 1; Rom. 13. Let them hear all causes, Deut. 1; 2 Chron. 19. Let them judge justly from God, Exod. 23; Lev. 19; Ps. 72, 82, etc. It is grave to sin here. Let nothing be done seditiously. Few are the Christians who do not shudder at these things. See Rom. 13; 1 Pet. 2.

units.la: His dictis, dimittitur concio & sedantur omnia, Vt enim facile commouetur vulgus.
units.tr: With these words said, the assembly is dismissed and all things are calmed, for the common people are easily stirred.

units.la: Seditiones facile cum penuntur.
units.tr: Seditions are easily checked.

units.la: vulgus,ita facilè cicuratur,si rationem potius quàm vim adhibeas. Obseruent magistratus.
units.tr: The common people are as easily tamed, if you apply reason rather than force. Let the magistrates observe this.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Dei paternam curam pro suis.Eidem difficile est nihil, Iob.38. 39.&c.Huic ergo fidamus.Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile note: God's fatherly care for his own. Nothing is difficult for him, Job 38, 39, etc. Let us therefore trust in him. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XX.
units.tr: Chapter 20.

units.la: HOMILIA CLVII.
units.tr: Homily 157.

units.la: Postquam autem cessauit tumultus, quum aduocasset Paulus discipulos,& complexus esset, abijt profecturus in Macedoniam.
units.tr: But after the uproar had ceased, Paul summoned the disciples, embraced them, and set out to go into Macedonia.

units.la: 2 Quum autem illas partes peragrasset, & hortatus illos fuisset multo sermone, venit in Graeciam.
units.tr: 2 When he had travelled through those parts and encouraged the believers with much speech, he came into Greece.

units.la: 3 Et ibi peractis mensibus tribus, quum ei in Syriam pronehendo fatlae fuissent à Iudaeis insidiae, censuit reuertendum per Macedoniam.
units.tr: 3 And after he had spent three months there, since the Jews had laid plots against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he resolved to return through Macedonia.

units.la: 4 Comitabatur autem eum vsque in Asiam Sopater Beroeensis, Thessalonicenses vero, Aristarchus & Secundus,& Gaius Derbaeus, & Timotheus: Asiani vero, Tychicus et Trophimus.
units.tr: 4 Sopater of Beroea accompanied him as far as Asia; of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; also Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of the Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.

units.la: 5 Qui cum praeuiffent, exspectarunt nos Troade.
units.tr: 5 These went on ahead and waited for us at Troas.

units.la: 6 Nos vero enauigauimus Philip-
units.tr: 6 But we sailed from Philip-

units.la: Cap.20. pis post dies Azymorum, & venimus ad eos Troadem intra dies quinq, vbi egimus dies septem.
units.tr: Chapter 20. ...after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas within five days, where we stayed seven days.

units.la: OVoniam Paulum electum suum organum Christus vocauit (Act. 9) non temerè Lucas res per illum gestas tanta diligentia describit. Ita enim testimonij Iesu Christi veritate asserit, & exemplum generale proponit, quod omnes imitentur, qui Christi organa esse volunt. Eo autem ordine procedit Lucas, vt interdum totas historias commemoret, in quarum singulis partibus scilicet multa memorabilia incidunt: interdum vero multa simul comprehendit, vt clarius eluceat, quanta ipsius fides & industria: quanti item eius labores fuerint. Vtrumq; fit hoc Capite. Primò enim summatim narrat profectionem Pauli in Macedoniam & Achaiam, de cuius consilio dictum Capite 19. Deinde peculiaria recensset, vt miraculum Troadis aeditum & Synodum Miletanam, &c.
units.tr: Since Christ called Paul his chosen instrument (Acts 9), Luke does not describe the things done through him with such care without reason. In this way he confirms the truth of the testimony of Jesus Christ and sets forth a general example that all who wish to be Christ's instruments should imitate. Luke proceeds in such an order that sometimes he recounts whole histories, in each part of which many memorable things occur, and sometimes he gathers many things together at once, so that it may shine more clearly how great Paul's faith and diligence were, and likewise how great his labours were. Both are done in this chapter. For first he briefly narrates Paul's journey into Macedonia and Achaia, whose plan was mentioned in chapter 19. Then he recounts particular events, such as the miracle wrought at Troas and the synod at Miletus, etc.

units.la: I. Profectio ipsa describitur, in qua Notatur. Quomodo ab Ephesijs discedat. Sedato demum tumultu, convocat discipulos, & publicè valedicit. Elucet insignis charitas & fides erga Ecclesiam. Non defe rit.
units.tr: I. The departure itself is described, and in it we note: how he leaves the Ephesians. Once the tumult was at last calmed, he calls the disciples together and bids them farewell publicly. A remarkable love and faith towards the Church shines forth. He does not desert it when the danger is seen, but stays with it until all things are set in order.

units.la: Argumentum capitis XX. rit hanc conspecto periculo, sed adest illi donec omnia componantur. Bonus ergo pastor, Ioh.10. Deinde valedicit, nimirum de singulis prius admonens, &c. quod vt animi sibi bene conscij argumentum est, ita docet ipsum ne absentem quidem huius Ecclesiæ fore immemore, Eph.1.2.Cor. 11. Imitentur exemplum hoc, quibufcunq; vel Ecclesiæ vel Refpub. commendatæ sunt, ne sibi modo consulant in periculis, & ne leuiter negligant suos.
units.tr: The argument of chapter 20: he does not desert this Church when danger is seen, but stays with it until all things are settled. Therefore he is a good shepherd, John 10. Then he bids farewell, first admonishing each one individually, etc. This is a sign of a conscience well aware of itself, and it also teaches that he will not be forgetful of this Church even when absent (Eph. 1:2; 2 Cor. 11). Let those to whom either a church or a commonwealth has been entrusted imitate this example, so that they do not look only to their own interests in dangers, and do not lightly neglect their own people.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quo abit? In Macedoniam & in Graeciam, per menses tres hinc inde Ecclesias inuisens. Idem facit Act.14.15. &c. Fuit hic mos Apostolis, &c. Imitatur bonos patres familias, qui non modo acquirunt, sed acquisita feruare student. Sic boni agrico læ. Ideo nullis laboribus parcit.
units.tr: 2. Where does he go? Into Macedonia and Greece, visiting the churches here and there for three months. He does the same at Acts 14:15, etc. This was the custom of the apostles, etc. He imitates good heads of households, who not only acquire but also take care to keep what they have acquired. So do good farmers. Therefore he spares no labours.

units.la: Discimus non securos nos esse debere, fi quando Ecclesiæ & Refpub. bene constitutæ sunt. Vigilandum ne quid mali aspergat satan, Matth.13. Curat hoc fieri in Ecclesijs quoad religionem, 2. Cor.11. In Repub. quoad leges bonas, quas subinde oppugnat, vt suum regnum stabiliat, nec semper successu caret, quia pauci labores & pericula subire volunt.
units.tr: We learn that we ought not to be secure when churches and commonwealths are well established. We must watch lest Satan sow something bad (Matt. 13). He takes care to do this in the churches as regards religion (2 Cor. 11), and in commonwealths as regards good laws, which he attacks from time to time in order to establish his kingdom. Nor does he always lack success, because few are willing to undergo labours and dangers.

units.la: ¶ 3. Quid egit, Exhortatus est sermone multo, nimirum ad perseuerantiā, fine qua nemo saluatur, Luc. 9.21 Mat.24.2. Tim.2. Opus autem exhortatione, quia ad lapsum natura proclives sumus, Gen 8 Psal. 51 &c. Quia non dormitat satan, 1.Pet.5. Ioh.8.Stulti, qui curam hanc superuacaneam dicunt. Se pfos non satis nouerunt, &c. Interim vides Ecclesiam nihil praestantius habere verbo Dei, Luc.10. Matth.13. Hoc maxime vrserant Apostoli, 1. Cor. 9. Act.6. Arguuntur qui hoc neglecto circa ceremonias occupantur.
units.tr: 3. What did he do? He exhorted them with much speech, namely to perseverance, without which no one is saved (Luke 9:21; Matt. 24:13; 2 Tim. 2). The exhortation is needed because we are by nature prone to fall (Gen. 8; Ps. 51, etc.), and because Satan does not sleep (1 Pet. 5; John 8). Fools who say this care is superfluous do not know themselves well enough, etc. Meanwhile you see that the Church has nothing more excellent than the Word of God (Luke 10; Matt. 13). The apostles especially strove for this (1 Cor. 9; Acts 6). Those are rebuked who, neglecting this, busy themselves with ceremonies.

units.la: 2. Quid in hac profectione Paulus pafus? Stuntur insidiae a Iudaeis in mari. Plenius omnia, 2.Tim.1.2.Corinth.11. Sed prudenter periculum declinat mutato consilio.
units.tr: 2. What did Paul suffer on this journey? Ambushes were laid for him by the Jews at sea. See everything more fully in 2 Tim. 1 and 2 Cor. 11. But he prudently avoids the danger by changing his plan.

units.la: NOTA. 1. Quae gratia veritatis minis-tris referatur? Perdios voluntij, quorum saluti maxime inuigilant. Vide Pauli animum erga Iudaeos, Rom.9.&10. Sed non alij sunt hostes infensiores. Idem Moses expertus est, Exod.31.Heb.11.Act.7. Prophetae Christus item, Matt.9.23, Lucae 19. Vide gentes. Non offendamur. Nam haec mundi natura est, vt bene meritis pefsimam gratiam referat, & se quietum fore non putet, nisi pijs sublatis. Cainum vide Gen.4. Iosephi fratres, Gen.37. Sacerdotes, Ioh.11. At turpissime falluntur, quia tunc demum infœlices sunt, &c. Suis intercessoribus priuantur, & pœnas accelerant, Gen. 19.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. To whom is the grace of the truth referred, by the ministers? To the stubborn, whose salvation they watch over most of all. See Paul's attitude towards the Jews, Rom. 9 and 10. Yet no enemies are more hostile than these. Moses experienced the same (Exod. 31; Heb. 11; Acts 7), and Christ likewise, and the prophets (Matt. 9:23; Luke 19). Look at the Gentiles. Let us not be offended. For this is the nature of the world: it repays the best deserving with the worst ingratitude, and does not think itself at peace unless the godly are removed. See Cain, Gen. 4; Joseph's brothers, Gen. 37; the priests, John 11. But they are most shamefully deceived, for then at last they are unhappy, etc. They are deprived of their intercessors and hasten their own punishments (Gen. 19).

units.la: ¶ 2. Quod officiu̅ in simili ẹ̈su: Paulum imitentur, de quo duo nobis proponuntur: A. Pergit in suavocatione. Non deserenda haec propter improbitatem mundi. Vide Luc. 6. &c. Cur enim mundum imitemur? B. Prudenter declinat periculu̅. Non temere nos immergamus, quasi Dei am tentaturi, Mat. 10.
units.tr: 2. What duty in a similar case? We should imitate Paul, from whom two things are set before us. A. He persists in his calling. This is not to be abandoned because of the wickedness of the world. See Luke 6, etc. For why should we imitate the world? B. He prudently avoids danger. We should not rashly throw ourselves in, as if we were about to tempt God (Matt. 10).

units.la: III. Vt Deus se gesterit? Ille comites ad iungit Paulo, praestantissimos ex diuersis Ecclesijs viros. Septem nominantur, octo uus fuit Lucas. Hi partim praecedunt, ut exploreunt & praeparent, partim comitantur, ut adsint & subleuent. Conueniunt Troadę.
units.tr: III. How did God act? He joins companions to Paul, men most excellent from different churches. Seven are named, and Luke makes eight. Some go ahead to explore and make preparations, others accompany him to be present and to support him. They gather at Troas.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Dei fidem, qui suis nunquam deest, nec supra vires finit tentari, 1. Cor. 10. Audetibus aliquid pro suo nomine ad dit fidos laborum socios. Sic Iosepho Nicodemus iungitur, Ioh. 19. Hodie de aliis querimur, ipsi interim desides nimis, &c. Faciamus officium & alij accedent ¶ 2. Fidei & pietatis exemplum in Pauli comitibus. Laboriosum erat hunc comitari, sum ptuosum item & plenu̅ periculi, cum toti haberet hostes, & passim seditiosus haberetur. Sed maioris faciunt fidei donu̅, quod per illum acceperant, Gal.4.Ideo laudantur,&c.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. God's faithfulness: he never fails his own, nor allows them to be tempted beyond their strength (1 Cor. 10). He gives faithful companions in labour to those who dare something in his name. So Nicodemus is joined to Joseph (John 19). Today we complain about others, while we ourselves are too idle, etc. Let us do our duty, and others will come. 2. An example of faith and piety in Paul's companions. It was laborious to accompany him, costly too, and full of danger, since he had enemies on every side and was regarded everywhere as a seditious man. But they valued more highly the gift of faith which they had received through him (Gal. 4). Therefore they are praised, etc.

units.la: Imitentur hoc qui fide gloriantur. Sed o tempora! A.Symmyftis lacerantur,quorum fide & labore salutis cognitio nobis illuxit. Sed soletur nos Dei ndes,qui remunerator est,&c.Heb.11.Dan. 11. Orem.
units.tr: Let those who boast of their faith imitate this. But oh, the times! Our fellow-initiates are torn apart, through whose faith and labour the knowledge of salvation has dawned upon us. But let God, who is the rewarder, console us, etc. (Heb. 11; Dan. 11). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CLVIII.

units.la: 7 Primo autem die hebdomadis co actis discipulis ad frangendum panem Paulus differebat, abiturus postridie: perduxitq; sermonem vsque in mediam noctem.
units.tr: 7 On the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul, who was to leave the next day, preached to them and prolonged his speech until midnight.

units.la: 8 Erant porro lucernæ multæ in cœnaculo vbi erant congregati.
units.tr: 8 There were also many lamps in the upper room where they were gathered.

units.la: 9 Et sedens quidam adolescens nomine Eutychus in fenestra, deiciente cum somno profundo,quum diutius disseret Paulus, præ somno ruens, decidit ex tertia contignatione deorsum, & sublatus est mortuus.
units.tr: 9 And a young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window and sinking into a deep sleep as Paul went on talking at length, was overcome by sleep, fell from the third storey to the ground, and was picked up dead.

units.la: 10 Quum descendisset autem Paulus, ruit in eum, & complexus dixit, Ne tumultuemini: anima enim eius in ipso est.
units.tr: 10 But Paul went down, fell upon him, embraced him and said, "Do not be troubled, for his life is in him."

units.la: POstquam D. Paulus Ephesi omnia ea confecit,quæ ad Ecclesiæ illius constitutionem faciebant, peregrinationem inftiinstituit, qua Macedoniæ & Græciæ Ecclesias inuisit, & in fide confirmauit. Elucet in ea fides Pauli & induftris, qui tot la boribus & periculis Ecclesias & acquisiuit & seruauit. Imitanda hæc omnibus, quorum curæ vel Ecclesiæ vel Respub. creditæ sunt. Sequitur rerum Troadis gerum historia, vbi duo cumprimis obseruanda narrantur.
units.tr: After St Paul had completed at Ephesus everything that pertained to the constitution of that church, he undertook a journey in which he visited the churches of Macedonia and Greece and strengthened them in the faith. Paul's faith and diligence shine forth here, for by so many labours and dangers he both gained and preserved the churches. All who have been entrusted with the care of churches or of the commonwealth should imitate this. There follows the account of what was done at Troas, where two things especially are narrated for our observation.

units.la: I. Disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ & sacri cœtus exemplum: in quo No. ¶ 1. Tempus. Fuit dies sabbathi, qui tunc propter veterem morem adhuc celebrior erat. Postea proximus à Sabbatho rebus sacris destinatus est, propter resurrectionem Christi & Dominicus diētus, Mar. 16. Apoc. 1. Interim docemur necessariam esse dierū à Domino traditorum obseruatione. Opus his tum propter externum cultum, tum propter internum, qui meditatione diuinorum excitatur, Exo. 20. Grauis culpa, hos vel negligere vel prophanare. Ingratitudo in Deum, & animi prophani indicium, Num. 15. Numeratur inter maximas scelera à prophetis, Ierem. 17. Ezech. 20. 22. 13. Hinc illa Neh. 23. Christi, Matth. 12. Luc. 6. 13. 14.
units.tr: I. An example of church discipline and of the holy assembly, in which note: ¶ 1. Time. It was the day of the Sabbath, which at that time was still more widely observed because of the old custom. Afterwards the day next after the Sabbath was set apart for sacred use, on account of Christ's resurrection, and was called the Lord's day (Mark 16; Rev. 1). Meanwhile we are taught that the observance of the days handed down by the Lord is necessary. It is needed both for outward worship and for inward worship, which is stirred up by meditation on divine things (Exod. 20). It is a grave fault either to neglect these days or to profane them; it is a sign of ingratitude toward God and of a profane mind (Num. 15). It is counted among the greatest sins by the prophets (Jer. 17; Ezek. 20, 22, 13). Hence that (Neh. 23.); Christ's (Matt. 12; Luke 6, 13, 14).

units.la: ¶ 2. Locus. Fuit cœnaculum in domo aliqua priuata, quia à templis idolorum
units.tr: ¶ 2. Place. It was an upper room in some private house, because they shrank from the temples of idols,

units.la: abhorrebant, & ipsis publicum templum non concedebatur. Sors Christi & Euangelij. Illustratur lucernis, quia nox erat, ne qua oriatur turpitudinis suspicio. Inepti, qui has ad cultum facere putant, & eas hoc exemplo & Mosaico ritu defendunt. Hic nox fuit. Alia fuit candelabri ratio in lege, Exod. 25.37. Typus Christi erat per verbum & Apostolos illuminantis Ecclesiam, Ioh. 1 8 Matth. 5. Patet interim, exteriori cultui & coetibus sacris certo loco opus esse. In veteri populo Templum & Synagogae. In veteri Ecclesia Oratoria. In his autem honestati omnia serviant. Absit prophanatio & superstitio.
units.tr: and the public temple was not granted to them. The lot of Christ and of the Gospel. It is lit by lamps, because it was night, lest any suspicion of shameful conduct should arise. Foolish are those who think these are made for worship and defend them by this example and by the Mosaic rite. Here it was night. The candelabrum had a different purpose in the law (Exod. 25, 37). It was a type of Christ, who by the word and the apostles illuminates the Church (John 1; Matt. 5). It is clear meanwhile that outward worship and sacred assemblies need a fixed place. Among the old people there were the Temple and the synagogues; in the old Church, oratories. But in all these, decency should serve everything. Far be profanation and superstition.

units.la: ¶ 3. Causa conuentus: Vt panem gerant. Intelligitur Cœna Domini, vt Act. 2.4. Quis enim comessatos putet? Ita nominatur propter singulare fractionis mysterium, quae & nos de peccato arguit, & Christi meritum in nos distribui docet, Ioh. 6. simulq; vnitatis in Christo admonet, 1.Cor. 10. Obserua autem ritum & ordine. Paulus primum concionatur. Inde demum celebratur Cœna, nimirum ritu à Christo tradito, vt patet 1 Cor. 11. Ita Christus doctrinam & praedicationem de sua morte praemisit, & nihil tradidit super stitiosum, Luc. 22. Ioh. 13.14. &c. Iubet hoc ipsum Paulus, 1.Cor. 11. Arguntur Missæ inuentores. Nulla in hac prædicatio. Lingua peregrina. Frigidæ gesticulationes. Meritum ei tribuitur. Christo negatur, fides euertitur. Optimus ritus, quem Dominus tradidit, & quem tanto studio vetus Ecclesia diutisi mè retinuit.
units.tr: ¶ 3. Cause of the gathering: to break bread. This is understood as the Lord's Supper, as in Acts 2:42. For who would think they were drunk? It is so named because of the singular mystery of the breaking, which both convicts us of sin and teaches that Christ's merit is distributed to us (John 6), and at the same time reminds us of unity in Christ (1 Cor. 10). Notice also the rite and order. Paul first preaches; only then is the Supper celebrated, namely by the rite handed down by Christ, as is clear from 1 Cor. 11. So Christ placed doctrine and preaching about his death first, and handed down nothing superstitious (Luke 22; John 13, 14, etc.). Paul himself commands this in 1 Cor. 11. The inventors of the Mass are refuted: there is no preaching in it, the language is foreign, the gestures are frigid, merit is ascribed to it, Christ is denied, and faith is overturned. The best rite is the one the Lord handed down, and which the old Church so zealously and so long retained.

units.la: ¶ 4. Concionandi modus. Extempore colligitur. Protraxit enim sermonem vsq; ad mediam nostem. Inde ad diluculû vsq;. Non ergo perfunctoriè, sed magna diligentia & zelo docuit. Quæ recte udicauit de ministerio suo, 1 Cor 5 13. Et hæc ipsa cau sa fuit, quod auditores tá attenti fuerunt. Vide 1. Thess. 2. Gal. 4.
units.tr: ¶ 4. The manner of preaching. It is gathered that he spoke extempore, for he prolonged the discourse until midnight, and then on until daybreak. Therefore he taught not perfunctorily but with great diligence and zeal. He rightly judged about his ministry (1 Cor. 5:13). This very thing was also why his hearers were so attentive. See 1 Thess. 2; Gal. 4.

units.la: Arguitur nostri temporis væcordia In ministris negligentia cernitur, & inanium rerum studium, Ifa 56. Populus audiendi impatiens, non recte iudicat, Ezech 33. Omnem moram nimiû putat. Semper habet quod causetur: Metuendum ne fiat quod est Amos 7. &c.
units.tr: Our own age's heedlessness is refuted. Negligence is seen in ministers and a zeal for empty things (Isa. 56). A people impatient of hearing does not judge rightly (Ezek. 33). It thinks every delay too long; it always has something to complain of. We must fear lest what is written in Amos 7 should happen, etc.

units.la: II. Miraculum, quo Deus Pauli ministe rium approbare, simulq; omnes ad Apostolicæ doctrinæ considerationem excita re voluit. Sed de hoc in sequenti.
units.tr: II. A miracle, by which God willed to approve Paul's ministry and at the same time to rouse everyone to consider the apostolic doctrine. But of this in what follows.

units.la: Nos ad exemplum primitiuæ Ecclesiæ discamus cætus sacros piè frequentare, sacramenta religiosè celebrare, & vs
units.tr: Let us, after the example of the primitive Church, learn to attend sacred assemblies devoutly, to celebrate the sacraments reverently, and ...

units.la: Deus incrementum fidei nobis quotidie largiatur assidué Oremus.
units.tr: May God grant us an increase of faith daily. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CLIX.

units.la: 9 Et sedens quidam adolescens, nomine Eutyches in fenestra, deijciente eú somno profundo, ruens decidit ex tertia contignatione deorsum, & sublatus est mortuus.
units.tr: 9 And a certain young man named Eutychus, sitting in a window and overcome by a deep sleep, fell headlong from the third floor and was taken up dead.

units.la: 10 Quum descendisset autem Paulus, ruit in eum, & complexus dixit, Ne tumultuamini, anima enim eius in ipso est.
units.tr: 10 But Paul went down, threw himself upon him, embraced him and said, "Do not be troubled, for his life is in him."

units.la: 11 Quum ergo ascendisset, fregisset panem, ac gustasset, diu colloquutus usque ad diluculum, ita demum profectus est.
units.tr: 11 When he had gone back up, broken the bread and eaten, he talked with them a long time, until daybreak, and then at last he set out.

units.la: 12 Adduxerunt autem puerum vivum, & recreati sunt non mediocriter.
units.tr: 12 They brought the boy home alive, and were not a little comforted.

units.la: 13 Nos autem progressi ad navem, proueetifimus Assòn, illinc recepturi Paulum: sic enim constituerat, pedibus ipse iter facturus.
units.tr: 13 But we went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for so he had arranged, since he meant to make the journey on foot himself.

units.la: 14 Vt autem congressus est nobiscum ad Assòn, recepto eo venimus Mytilenen.
units.tr: 14 When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.

units.la: 15 Et cum illinc abnaugassemus, sequenti die peruenimus contra Chium: postridie vero appulimus Samum: & et quum diuersati essemus Trogylii, se-quenti die venimus Miletum.
units.tr: 15 Sailing from there, the next day we came opposite Chios; the day after that we put in at Samos; and when we had stayed at Trogyllium, on the following day we came to Miletus.

units.la: 16 Decreuerat enim Paulus præternauigare Ephesum, ne contingeret tempus terere in Asia. Festinabat enim si fieri posset, vt die Pentecostes esset Hierosolymis.
units.tr: 16 For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he would not have to spend time in Asia. For he was hurrying, if it were possible, to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

units.la: DEscripsit Lucas cœtum piorû, qui Troadis conuenerunt, vt Paulum audirent & Cœnâ Dom. sumerent. Didici mus cœtus eiusmodi necessarios esse: quia ad fidei confession faciunt, charitatem fo uent, & promissionibus commendantur. Matt. 18. Deinde quomodo haberi debeant. Conuenerunt quidem hi noctu, sed lu cernas habuerunt. Docuit Paulus tota no cte illi audiuerunt &c. Studeatur honesta ti 1. Cor. 14. 11. Primas teneat Dei verbum, non inanes Ceremoniæ. Non pigeat nos vllius studij aut temporis. Ingens peccatum hic negligentem esse. Ezech. 33. Docet hoc sequens historia, quasimul Deus Pauli ministerium commendare, & omnes ad doctrinæ Apostolicæ considerationem excitare voluit, &c. Videamus singula.
units.tr: Luke describes the gathering of the godly who came together at Troas to hear Paul and to receive the Lord's Supper. We learn that such gatherings are necessary, because they foster the confession of faith, cherish charity, and are commended by promises (Matt. 18). Next, we learn how they ought to be held. These people met at night, but they had lights. Paul taught through the whole night, and they listened. Let honest study be pursued (1 Cor. 14). Let the Word of God hold the first place, not empty ceremonies. Let us not grudge any effort or time. It is a great sin to be negligent here (Ezek. 33). The following story teaches this, and at the same time God wished both to commend Paul's ministry and to rouse everyone to consider the Apostolic doctrine. Let us look at the parts one by one.

units.la: I. Occasionem. Eutychus sedit in fenestra, vel propter multitudinem, vel iuueni li temeritate, aut vt somnum vitaret, sed huic succumbit, decidit & moritur.
units.tr: I. The occasion. Eutychus sat in the window, either because of the crowd, or from the rashness of youth, or to keep off sleep; but he succumbed to it, fell, and died.

units.la: Vbi No. ¶ 1. Quid eos maneat, qui verbum negligenter audiunt. Vt qui circa alias cogitationes occupantur: A fomnu se componunt: Superbiæ aut libidini student. Hi & propriæ salutis negligentes sunt, & Dei maiestatem contemnunt. Ergo verbum eis cedit ad mortem.
units.tr: Here note: 1. What awaits those who hear the Word carelessly, such as those who are occupied with other thoughts, who give themselves over to sleep, who pursue pride or lust. These are negligent of their own salvation and despise the majesty of God. Therefore the Word turns to death for them.

units.la: ¶ 2. Deum interdum tristes casus immittere suis, dum crica res sanctissimas occupantur: non quod displiceat, sed ut negligentiores excitet, fidem exerceat, & habeat occasionem, qua suam potentiam declaret. Abraham, Genef. 12. &c. Ita hic, quid potuerat accidere, quod Pauli doctrinam magis suspectam redderet? Aut ei inuidiam accerseret maiorem? Sed pijs omnia cooperantur in bonum Rom. 8. Ideo hic quoq; lætus est exitus, & confirmando Euangelio seruit, quod huic aduersum videbatur. Discimus iudicare de affli&ionibus piorum. Examinemus nos ipsos, & videbimus nobis non fieri iniuriam. Patienter feramus. Perseueremus in veritate agnita, & lætissimus erit exitus, &c.
units.tr: 2. God sometimes sends sad accidents upon his people while they are busy with the most holy things, not because he is displeased, but to rouse the more negligent, to exercise faith, and to have an occasion to show his power (Abraham, Gen. 12, etc.). So here, what could have happened that would make Paul's teaching more suspect, or bring him greater odium? But all things work together for good for the godly (Rom. 8). Therefore here too the outcome is happy, and it served to confirm the Gospel, which had seemed to be harmed by it. We learn to judge the afflictions of the godly. Let us examine ourselves, and we will see that no injury is done to us. Let us bear it patiently. Let us persevere in the truth we have acknowledged, and the outcome will be most joyful, etc.

units.la: II. Miraculum, in quo No. ¶ 1. Paulus
units.tr: II. The miracle, in which, No. 1. Paul

units.la: mox descendit, non causatus vel Sabbathi vel Coenæ religionem. Hæc enim propter hominem, &c. Mar. 2. 3. Arguitur eorum supersuperstitiio, qui hominū traditiones violari nolunt in tali necessitate, vt Missam, regulas monasticas, &c.
units.tr: went down at once, not pleading the sabbath or the observance of the Supper. For "the sabbath was made for man" and so on (Mark 2. 3). Here is refuted the superstition of those who will not have human traditions violated in such a necessity, such as the Mass, monastic rules, and so on.

units.la: ¶ 2. Incumbit puero. Sic 1. Reg. 17. 2. Reg. 4. Non autem suo contactu sanauit, sed Christi virtute, cuius erat minister 2. Cor. 5. Salutis mysterium. Ex Adamo mortem hausimus. In Christo vita offertur per Evangelium. Huic nos vniri oportet fide.
units.tr: 2. He lay upon the boy. So did Elijah (1 Kings 17) and Elisha (2 Kings 4). Yet he did not heal by his own touch, but by the power of Christ, whose minister he was (2 Cor. 5). This is the mystery of salvation. From Adam we drew death; in Christ life is offered through the Gospel. We must be united to this by faith.

units.la: ¶ 3. Consolatur & modestissimè loquitur. Ne turbemini. Timebat enim nealiquorum fides nutaret. Anima eius in ipso est. Non negat miraculum, sed arroganti-um vitat, ne quid sibi tribuatur, vt Aposto-rū. 3. Inde redit ad officium, Coenam peragit, docet vsq; ad auroram, & tunc iter ingreditur. Commendatur nobis sedulitas Apostolica. Post tantum signū redit ad officium. Imo abiturus crastino tamen non stem non quiescit. Ne pigeat nos laboris in resancta: nec putemus nos omni officio defunctos, si quid magni per nos factū
units.tr: 3. He consoles and speaks most modestly: Do not be troubled. For he feared that the faith of some might waver. His life is in him. He does not deny the miracle, but avoids arrogance, lest anything be attributed to himself, as the Apostles also did (Acts 3). Then he returns to his duty: he completes the Supper, teaches until dawn, and then sets out on his journey. The Apostolic diligence is commended to us. After so great a sign he returns to his work; indeed, although he was to depart the next day, he does not rest. Let us not grudge labour in holy things, nor think ourselves released from every duty if something great has been done through us.

units.la: ¶ 4. Fructus omnium. Adduxerunt vi-um puerum, & refocillati sunt, non ob hoc modò, sed quòd gratiæ Dei specimen vi-derunt.
units.tr: 4. The fruit of all. They brought the boy home alive, and were comforted, not only because of this, but because they saw a sample of God's grace.

units.la: Sunt hi Euangelij & fidei fructus: 1. Vita restituitur damnatis ad morte. Et ijdem resuscitantur ad vitæ nouitatem Rom. 6.
units.tr: These are the fruits of the Gospel and of faith: 1. Life is restored to those condemned to death, and the same people are raised to newness of life (Rom. 6).

units.la: Cap.20. 2. Gaudium oritur afflictis conscientijs. Rom.5.Phil.5.4.
units.tr: Chap. 20. 2. Joy arises for troubled consciences (Rom. 5; Phil. 4).

units.la: Arguuntur,qui in peccatis pergunt, & intra se tumultuantur.
units.tr: Those are refuted who persist in their sins and stir up tumult within themselves.

units.la: III. Redit ad Pauli profectionem. Praemittit suos nauigio,ipse per terras profecturus,nimirum vt Ecclesias in transitu vi deret.Interim suos labore leuat,nec illorum opera superbè abutitur. Inde Ephesum praeteruectus venit Miletum, vbi Synodum collegit.Ephesum autem reliquit, ne tempus consumeret in Asia,sed Pentecosten agere posset Ierosolymis, ob homi num frequentiam.
units.tr: III. He returns to Paul's journey. He sends his companions ahead by ship, while he himself was going to travel by land, namely so that he might visit the churches on the way. Meanwhile he lightens their labour and does not arrogantly abuse their service. From there he sailed past Ephesus and came to Miletus, where he gathered a synod. He left Ephesus, however, so as not to spend time in Asia, and so that he might keep Pentecost at Jerusalem because of the crowd of people.

units.la: NOT. ¶1. Labores & molestias Pauli, item pericula 2. Cor.11. Vide quàm ardua res sit seruire Deo. Nec enim otiosos vult cultores. Vide Abrahamum,Iacobum,Genef.47. Mosem. Prophetas. Ipsum Christum. Non offendamur similibus, nec ipsi nobis otium quaeramus, Ioh.13.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The labours and troubles of Paul, likewise his dangers (2 Cor. 11). See how hard a thing it is to serve God, for he does not want idle worshippers. See Abraham, Jacob (Gen. 47), Moses, the Prophets, and Christ himself. Let us not be offended by similar things, nor seek idleness for ourselves (John 13).

units.la: ¶. Magna sit apud nos Euangelij authoritas. Chara sunt quae magno constant. At quid preciosius Euangelio? Tot sudoribus & sanguine propagatum. Propter hoc laborârunt omnes Apostoli. Ante hos prophetae, 1. Petri 1. Christus, qui se huius gratia venisset ait Mar.1.Luc.4. Execrabilis ignauia,si nos nihil ferre aut facere ve-
units.tr: 2. Let the authority of the Gospel be great among us. Dear are the things that cost much. But what is more precious than the Gospel? It was spread with so much sweat and blood; for this all the Apostles laboured, and before them the prophets (1 Pet. 1). Christ himself, who said he had come for this purpose (Mark 1; Luke 4). It is a detestable laziness if we are unwilling to bear or do anything.

units.la: Pauli pericula et labores plena. ve velimus, vel etiam insidiosis compositionibus nosipsos aut alios circumscribi patimur. Quin potius pro hoc thesauro & margarita impendamus nostra omniaMatthaei 13. Oremus.
units.tr: Paul's dangers and labours are full of lessons. Whether we wish it or not, we also allow ourselves to be cheated by deceitful agreements. Rather, let us spend all our possessions for this treasure and pearl (Matt. 13). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLX.
units.tr: HOMILY CLX.

units.la: 17 Miss autem Mileto nuntijs Ephesum, accersiuit Presbyteros Ecclesiae.
units.tr: 17 Now from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and summoned the elders of the church.

units.la: 18 Qui cum ad ipsum venissent, dixit eis, Vos scitis, a primo die quo ingressus sum Asiam, quomodo vobiscum per omne tempus fuerim:
units.tr: 18 And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,

units.la: 19 Seruiens Domino cum omni modestia & multis lachrymis ac tentationibus, quae mihi euenerunt in insidiis Iudaeorum:
units.tr: 19 Serving the Lord with all humility, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:

units.la: 20 Vt nihil subterfugerim eorum quae vobis conducerent, quo minus ea vobis annuntiarem, & docere vos publice & per singulas domos.
units.tr: 20 And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house,

units.la: 21 Testificans Iudaeis & Graecis conuersionem ad Deum, & fidem in Dominum nostrum Iesum.
units.tr: 21 Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus Apostolorum & Pauli imprimis res gestas diligentissime commemorat: partim quidem, ut exemplar habeant omnes ministri quod imitentur: partim vero vt omnes intelligant, quanta sit Euangelij authorit. & certitudo, quod illi nobis tanta diligentia tradiderunt. Et huc maximè praefens actio referri debet. Licet tempus noluerit in Asia terere Paulus, & Herosolymam feftinarit, nihil tamen eorum omittit, quae ad Ecclesiarum salutem faciebant. Conuocat enim ad fe haerum seniores, id est, pastores & ministros & in generali synodo de rebus maximis & necessarijs cum illis agit.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit records the deeds of the Apostles, and of Paul above all, with the greatest care: partly so that all ministers may have an example to imitate, and partly so that everyone may understand how great is the authority and certainty of the Gospel, which they have handed down to us with such diligence. And to this the present action should above all be referred. Although Paul was unwilling to spend time in Asia, and hastened to Jerusalem, he nonetheless omits nothing that served the salvation of the churches. For he calls to himself the elders of this church, that is, the pastors and ministers, and in a general synod deals with them on matters of the greatest importance and necessity.

units.la: Sed NOTA 1. Paulum, qui synodum indicit de regraui actu-rus. Ita factum Act. 15. Vnde patet necessarios esse ministro-rum coetus, in quibus communibus omnium suffragijs res Ecclesiae tractentur. Faciunt ad retinendam disciplinam inter ministros. Ad coercendam ambitionem. Ad consensum in vera doctrina, & haereses re-primendas. Ideo his ita studuit Constantinus, & ijsdem tam infensus fuit Ecclesiae persecutor Licinius. Et Papa omnem syno-di potestatem ad se rapuit. Iusiurandum episcoporum.
units.tr: But NOTE 1. Paul, who convenes the synod, is about to deal with a weighty matter. So it was done in Acts 15. Hence it is evident that assemblies of ministers are necessary, in which the affairs of the Church are handled by the common vote of all. They serve to keep discipline among the ministers, to restrain ambition, to secure agreement in true doctrine, and to suppress heresies. Therefore Constantine took such pains over these things, and the persecutor of the Church, Licinius, was so hostile to them. And the Pope seized for himself all the power of the synod. The oath of bishops.

units.la: 2. Seniores Asiae, qui ad Pauli vocationem comparent, nec superbè imperium detrectant. Agnoscunt in Paulo gratiam Dei, & fidem. Modestiae exemplum.
units.tr: 2. The elders of Asia, who come together at Paul's summons, do not proudly refuse his authority. They acknowledge the grace of God and the faith in Paul. An example of modesty.

units.la: Licet
units.tr: Although

units.la: Euseb. lib. 1. de vita Constant. Licet enim eadem dignitas sit omnium, ordo tamen necessarius: & proinde humi litate & obedientia mutua inuicem certa re debent, 1. Pet. 5.
units.tr: Eusebius, book 1, On the Life of Constantine. For although all have the same dignity, the order is nonetheless necessary; and therefore they ought to be bound to one another by humility and mutual obedience, 1 Pet. 5.

units.la: Porro orationem Pauli videamus, quę causas conuocat synodi continet. Est ve hemeas ac grauis hortatio, vt quando ip- sum non amplius visuri sint, exemplū ip- sius imitentur, & abse traditam doctri- nam constanter seruent: pro Ecclesiarum salute sedulò inuigilent, & hæreticis sese fortiter opponant, &c. Et in præsenti qui- dem de vita & doctrina sua agit.
units.tr: Next let us consider Paul's speech, which contains the reasons for convening the synod. It is a vehement and serious exhortation: that, since they were not going to see him again, they should imitate his example, constantly keep the doctrine delivered to them, watch diligently over the salvation of the churches, and oppose heretics boldly, and so on. And in the present passage he speaks of his life and of his teaching.

units.la: I. Vitæ suæ exemplum proponit, vt ma ior esset adhortationis authoritas. Liberi ūs autem de se ipso loquitur: quia cum il lis agebat, quibus omnia erant notissima. Scitis quomodo vobiscum egerim à pri- mo die, & vt Domino seruierim in meo ministerio, &c. Totum tempus allegat, nec aliquandiu simulasse putetur. Humilis. Cum multis lachrymis, quas vestræ salu- tis studium extorsit. Tentationibus, in qui- bus minim. è succubui, &c. Cæterum No- ta Quales esse deceat ministros verbi? A. Humiles sint, ne sibi vendicent diuina, quod Antichristi est 2. Thes. 2. Dan. 7. Mat. 24 Deinde ne quem præ se fastidiant, nec Symmystis superbè dominentur 1. Petri 5.Huc pertinent,Matt.11.18.&20. Luc. 22.Ioh.13.
units.tr: I. He sets before them the example of his life, so that the authority of his exhortation might be greater. He speaks of himself freely, because he was dealing with those to whom everything was very well known. "You know how I have conducted myself among you from the first day, and how I have served the Lord in my ministry," and so on. He appeals to the whole period, so that no one may think he was pretending for some time. Humble. With many tears, which the zeal for your salvation drew from him. In temptations, under which I did not in the least give way, and so on. Moreover, note: What sort of people ought ministers of the Word to be? A. They should be humble, so that they do not claim for themselves what belongs to God, which is the mark of Antichrist, 2 Thess. 2, Dan. 7, Matt. 24. Then, they should not despise anyone, nor lord it proudly over their fellow ministers, 1 Pet. 5. To this belong Matt. 11:18, 20; Luke 22; John 13.

units.la: B. Salutem Ecclesiarum studiosè quærant,etiá cum lachrymis. Sic Moses, Exo. 32 33.Samuel.1.Sa.15.16.Ier.5. Ita Christus Matt 9.23 Luc.19. Sunt enim patrum instar: quare paterno debe ff etu esse præ diti 1.Cor.4 Gal.4.&c. C In tentationib. non succumbant, vt propter has velint Ecclesias deserere. Imò tunc demum se pa stores esse probent,non mercenarios Ioh, 10. Cum his confer pontificum & episcoporum mores, & patebit,cuius successores sint. Transferant hæc ad se magistratus,&c.
units.tr: B. They should seek the salvation of the churches zealously, even with tears. So Moses, Exod. 32:33; 1 Sam. 15, 16; Jer. 5. So Christ, Matt. 9, 23; Luke 19. For they are in the place of fathers; therefore they ought to be endowed with a fatherly disposition, 1 Cor. 4; Gal. 4, etc. C. In temptations they should not give way, so that on account of these they will not wish to forsake the churches. Rather, then at last they prove themselves to be shepherds, not hirelings, John 10. Compare with these the manners of the popes and bishops, and it will be plain whose successors they are. Let magistrates apply these things to themselves, etc.

units.la: II. De doctrina agit: vbi hæc NoT. Nihil suffugi, vel cælaui, quod esset in rem vestram. Ministrorum est omnia tradere, nec quicquam celare in mundi gratiam. Imò quò magis illi fuit, eò magis clamandum. Isa.58. &c. Arguuntur, qui in hosti um gratiam putant tacendum, ne feros ciant.
units.tr: II. He treats of doctrine, where this is to be noted: he kept nothing back, or concealed anything that would be for your good. It is the task of ministers to hand everything down, and to conceal nothing for the sake of the world's favour. Rather, the more hostile the world is, the more loudly must they cry out, Isa. 58, etc. Those are rebuked who think that silence should be kept to please enemies, lest they stir them to fury.

units.la: Simul patet, Euangelij doctrinam, ab Apostolis traditam, perfectam esse, Christus enim hos nihil cælauit, Ioh.15. Deinde spiritum promisit & dedit, qui omnia suggereret,Ioh.14.16.Act.2.Rursus ijdem omnia tradiderunt Ecclesijs. Quid ergo addidamentis opus. Iniuriam Christo & Apostolis faciunt aduersarij, &c.
units.tr: At the same time it is plain that the doctrine of the Gospel, handed down by the Apostles, is perfect: for Christ concealed nothing from them, John 15. Then he promised and gave the Spirit, who would bring all things to their remembrance, John 14, 16; Acts 2. Again, the same men handed everything down to the Churches. Why, then, is there need of additions? Our adversaries do injury to Christ and the Apostles, etc.

units.la: ¶2. Modū docendi Publicé & priuatim per domos singulas. Indefeßum studium Apostoli. In genere ergo & publicè tradenda, quæ ad salutem faciunt. Deinde quia omnes sponte obtemperát, priuatim quo que monendi; quorum peccata nondum publicè offendunt. Debent hoc Christiani singuli. Mat. 18. Quanto magis ministri? Ezech. 33. Præterea testificandū est, id est, diserté, liberè, & serió agendum. (Testis off. Prouerbior. 6.) idque cum omnibus, Mar. 6.
units.tr: ¶2. The manner of teaching: publicly and privately, from house to house. The tireless zeal of the Apostle. Therefore what serves salvation is to be delivered in general and publicly. Then, since all do not obey willingly, they must also be admonished privately, whose sins have not yet offended publicly. Individual Christians ought to do this, Matt. 18. How much more ministers? Ezek. 33. Moreover, one must testify, that is, act plainly, freely, and seriously (Testis off. Prov. 6), and that with everyone, Mark 6.

units.la: Vides quantum iuris sit ministro in suas oues. Vnde simul constat, non oues, sed vrsos esse, qui nec publicè nec priuatim admoneri volunt, &c.
units.tr: You see how great the right of a minister is over his sheep. Hence it is also clear that those who wish to be admonished neither publicly nor privately are not sheep but bears, etc.

units.la: ¶3. Summam doctrinæ proponit, cuius partes sunt eædem, quas Christus constituit, Luc. 24. Ergo verum prædicauit Euangelium. A. Pœnitentia, id est, conuersio ad Deum, &c. Hinc ordiendum; quia omnes deflexímus, & natura corrupti sumus, If. 53. Continet regulam piè viuendi, mortificationem & nostri abnegationem, & veræ obedientiæ studium. De hac Baptista, Matt. 3. Luc. 3.
units.tr: ¶3. He sets out the sum of the doctrine, whose parts are the same as those Christ laid down, Luke 24. Therefore he preached the true Gospel. A. Repentance, that is, conversion to God, etc. We must begin here, because we have all gone astray and are corrupted by nature, Isa. 53. It contains the rule of godly living: mortification, self-denial, and the zeal for true obedience. John the Baptist spoke of this, Matt. 3; Luke 3.

units.la: B. Fides in Iesum Christum. Hæc coniungenda, quia Deum fugimus natura, nec nisi fide per Christum regeniti, conuertemur, & cum Deo reconciliabimur, Ioh.14 Ita coniunxit Christus, Luc.24.
units.tr: B. Faith in Jesus Christ. These are to be joined together, because by nature we flee from God, and unless we are born again through faith in Christ, we shall not be converted and reconciled to God, John 14. So Christ joined them, Luke 24.

units.la: Errant qui poenitentiam abfq; fide docent. Vel fide gloriantur abfq; poenitentia &c. Imo ex his regulam sumeomnes dostrinas iudicandi, 1.Ioh.4. &c Oremus
units.tr: They err who teach repentance without faith, or who boast of faith without repentance, etc. Indeed, from these take the rule for judging all doctrines, 1 John 4, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXI.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXI.

units.la: 22 Et nunc ecce, ego vnctus spiritu proficiscor in Hierusalem, ignorans, quae in ea mihi occurrent.
units.tr: 22 And now, behold, bound in the Spirit, I go to Jerusalem, not knowing what will befall me there.

units.la: 23 Nisi quod spiritus sanctus per singulas urbes testificatur, dicens vincula & afflictiones me manere.
units.tr: 23 Except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.

units.la: 24 Sed nihil mihi cura est, neque vita mea mihi ipsi cara est, vt peragam cursum meum cum gaudio, & ministerium, quod accepi a Domino Iesu, ad testificandum Euangelium gratiae Dei.
units.tr: 24 But I count nothing of account, nor is my life dear to me, so that I may finish my course with joy and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God.

units.la: QVemadmodum Dominus noster Iesus Christus suum erga Ecclesiam amorem iam discessurus maximè declarauit, quod illius admonitiones testantur, Ioh 13.14 15.16. Actor. 1. &c. Ita Paulus iuxta huius exemplum discessurus, imò ahsens absfens quoque Ecclesias cum primis turavit. Exemplum huius praefens actio con tinet. Nouerat fe non ampl us rediturum ad Asia Ecclasi s. Nouerat orituros lupos, qui Ecclesias mirifi è turbarent. Conuocatis ergo omnibus ministris, illos fidelissime admonet, & suum exemplum illis imitandum proponit, de quo in prima ora tionis parte egit, suae vitae simul & doctrinae rationem reddens. Sequitur.
units.tr: As our Lord Jesus Christ most clearly showed his love for the Church when he was about to depart, as his admonitions testify (John 13, 14, 15, 16; Acts 1, etc.), so Paul, about to depart, and though absent still, cared above all for the Churches in the same way. The present action contains an example of this. He knew that he would not return again to the Churches of Asia. He knew that wolves would arise who would wonderfully disturb the Churches. So, having called together all the ministers, he admonishes them most faithfully and sets his own example before them to be imitated, which he dealt with in the first part of his speech, giving an account of his life and teaching at the same time. There follows:

units.la: I. Rationem reddit, cur ita suum exemplum vrgeat: Quia discessurus, nec post hac ad illos reditur ussit. Inde colligitur, ipsos fui dodoris exemplum sequi, & Ecclesiae curam summo studio suscipere debere, ne quod ille tot acquisiuit laboribus, sua negligentia perdant.
units.tr: I. He gives the reason why he presses his example so: because, being about to depart, he would not return to them afterwards. From this it is gathered that they ought to follow the example of their teacher and take up the care of the Church with the greatest zeal, lest they lose through their negligence what he gained with so many labours.

units.la: Interim verba Not. ¶ 1. Ego alligatus spiritu profic scor, &c Intelligit occultum spiritus motum, qui illi semper dux fuit, vt vidimus Act. 16. 19. Licet autem volens parere, se tamen alligatum dicit ne leuis aut temerarius vel Deum tentare putare, tur, ostendens se, nisi Deo velit rebellare, aliter facere non posse.
units.tr: Meanwhile, the note on "Now I go bound in the Spirit, etc.": he understands the hidden motion of the Spirit, which was always his guide, as we saw in Acts 16 and 19. Yet he says he is bound, although he is willing to obey, lest anyone think him light or rash or one who tempts God, showing that unless he wishes to rebel against God he cannot act otherwise.

units.la: Interim vides, quo loco apud nos esse occultae spiritus suggestiones, & a- perta eius oracula. Vinculorum instar sint, quibus reluctantem carnem in obedi-
units.tr: Meanwhile you see where among us the hidden promptings of the Spirit and his open oracles are. They are like chains by which the reluctant flesh is drawn into obedience,

units.la: Argumenta huius loci.
units.tr: Arguments of this passage.

units.la: Paulus spiritu dixte Hierosolymam abiit.
units.tr: Paul went to Jerusalem at the Spirit's prompting.

units.la: Occultae ipsius suggestiones quae Ioh. 16. 20. ut obediant.
units.tr: The hidden promptings of the Spirit (John 16, 20) so that we obey.

units.la: entiam trahamus, & sp onte quidem, ne malo nostro cogamur. Qui noluntid face re, vel inuiti trahentur. Obseruemus in officijs ad quæ vocamur. Vide Mosem, E-xod.4. Item Ier.1.Ioh.1.1.Cor.9.In ijs quæ ad mores spectant, vbi sæpe multa fugge-rit spiritus.
units.tr: and drawn willingly indeed, lest we be compelled to our hurt. Those who are unwilling will be drawn even against their will. Let us observe this in the duties to which we are called. See Moses, Exod. 4; likewise Jer. 1; John 1; 1 Cor. 9. In those things which concern morals, the Spirit has often suggested much.

units.la: {q}2. Ignorans quæ mihi eueniunt sint, nisi quód &c. Obserua: Fidele Dei curam pro suis electis. Extremè diligit hos, Zac.2. Isa. 49. In tempore ergo admonet de omnibus, quæ eueniunt. Cur enim hos negligeret, cum impios de futuris malis fidelissimè admoneat? Amos 3. Gen. 6.13. 19.41.2.Par.36.
units.tr: 2. "Not knowing what will befall me, except that, etc." Observe: God's faithful care for his own. He loves his elect exceedingly (Zech. 2; Isa. 49). In time, therefore, he warns them about all that is going to happen. For why would he neglect these, when he most faithfully warns the impious about coming evils? (Amos 3; Gen. 6, 13, 19, 41; 2 Chron. 36.)

units.la: B. Vt suos admoneat Deus. Paulus sibi afflictiones paratas audit, quales autem sint, & quis exitus futurus ignorat adhuc. Postea certius omnia indicantur, Act. 21.
units.tr: B. That God may admonish his own. Paul hears that afflictions are prepared for him, but what they will be and what the outcome will be he does not yet know. Later everything is made clearer (Acts 21).

units.la: Non quidem spiritualiter semper reuelat omnia, sed ingenere quantum illis opus est, vt præparentur, uentum autem Deo per mittamus. Sic Ier.1.Ita nos quoque generales prædictiones habemus, Ioh.15. & 16. Matth.6.Act.14.2.Tim.3.Ad has præparemur, euentum omne Deo permittentes.
units.tr: God does not always reveal everything spiritually, but in general as much as is needful for them to be prepared; the outcome, however, we commit to God. So Jer. 1. Thus we too have general predictions (John 15 and 16; Matt. 6; Acts 14; 2 Tim. 3). Let us be prepared for these, committing every outcome to God.

units.la: C. Mirabile Dei consilium, quo suorum res administrat. Antea Paulus sæpe admonitus fugit, & insidias declinat. Act.9.17.19 Nunc admonetur quidem, sed tamen spiritu sibi pergendū esse intelligit. Ita Christus Luc. 4. Ioh. 8. 11. 12. 18. &c. Unde colligimus, pericula non semper sufficientem fugae causam esse. Quando Dei vocatio vrget, non ignes, non mare (Exod. 14.) nos impedient.
units.tr: C. The wonderful counsel of God, by which he manages the affairs of his people. Previously Paul, often warned, fled and avoided plots (Acts 9, 17, 19). Now he is indeed warned, yet understands that he must go on by the Spirit. So Christ (Luke 4; John 8, 11, 12, 18, etc.). Whence we gather that dangers are not always a sufficient reason for flight. When God's call urges, neither fires nor the sea (Exod. 14) will hinder us.

units.la: II. Consolationem adhibet, ne nimis consternarentur. Nihil mihi curae est. No. lo vos discruciari, &c. Causa: Quia vita mea non est mihi pretiosa, id est, non maioris hanc facio, quam meā vocationem. Imo gaudeo meum cursum absoluere, & ministerio mihi commisso defungi, &c. Non debent ergo vincula & pericula terrere.
units.tr: II. He offers consolation, so that they may not be too dismayed. "I count nothing of account." I do not want you to be tormented, etc. The reason: because my life is not precious to me, that is, I do not hold it of greater value than my calling. Indeed I rejoice to complete my course and to discharge the ministry committed to me, etc. Therefore chains and dangers ought not to terrify.

units.la: NOT. 1. Quomodo se sanctì in pericu lis gerant. A. Nō curent illa, sic nimirum, vt aliquid se indignū faciant. Alioqui non vult nos ἀπαθεῖς Deus, sed ne maiorem nostri quàm suae voluntatis rationem &c. In his vero nihil efficacius, quàm prouidentiae consideratio, Matt. 10. Psalm. 65. B. Vitam temporariam non praeferant aeternae. Causas potiùs vitae cōsiderent, quae sunt, vt Deo viuamus, & eidem, cum opus est, moriamur, &c. Rom. 14. Et cùm semel moriendum sit, felicius mori non possumus, quàm in Dei vocatione. Tunc locum habet Psalm. 116. Quòd si vero vita non preferenda, quanto minus opes, honores, voluptates. Vide Matth. 16 Luc 9. Psalmo 3.
units.tr: NOTE 1. How the saints conduct themselves in dangers. A. Let them not care about these things, in such a way that they do anything unworthy of themselves. Otherwise God does not want us impassible [ἀπαθεῖς], but that we not set our own judgment above his will, etc. In these matters nothing is more effective than the consideration of providence (Matt. 10; Ps. 65). B. Let them not prefer temporal life to eternal life. Let them consider rather the purposes of life, which are that we live to God and, when need be, die for him, etc. (Rom. 14). And since we must die once, we cannot die more happily than in God's calling. Then Psalm 116 has its place. But if life is not to be preferred, how much less wealth, honours and pleasures? See Matt. 16; Luke 9; Ps. 3.

units.la: C In hoc sint toti, vt cursum suum cum gaudio absoluant. Meta est cœlestis corona. 2 Tim. 4. Perseuerantia autem opus est Matt. 24 Luc 9. 2. Tim. 2. Cogita vitam stadium esse. Ad huius metam mo te feltna mus, 2 Tim 4. &c.
units.tr: C. Let them be wholly intent on finishing their course with joy. The goal is the heavenly crown (2 Tim. 4). But perseverance is needed (Matt. 24; Luke 9; 2 Tim. 2). Consider life a race-course. Let us press on toward its goal (2 Tim. 4, etc.).

units.la: ¶ 2. Euangelium gratiæ vocat: idque ab effectu: quia Dei gratiam & salutem nobis in Christo offert. Vide Matth 3. 17 Luc. 2. Vnde patet quanta sit improbitas eorum, qui illud contemnunt & fastidiunt. Simi les sunt seditiosis, qui sponte oblatá principis sui gratiam aspernantur. Defecerarmus enim omnes nos, Isa. 53. &c.
units.tr: 2. He calls it the gospel of grace, and does so from its effect, because it offers us God's grace and salvation in Christ. See Matt. 3, 17; Luke 2. Whence it is plain how great is the wickedness of those who scorn and loathe it. They are like seditious men who spurn the grace of their prince when it is freely offered. For we have all gone astray (Isa. 53, etc.).

units.la: ¶ 3. Quomodo versandum in Euangelio: Paulus teft sicari vult. Intelligitur libera & feria prædicatio. Officium testis. Est enim testimonium de Christo Apo. 17. Et Apostoli sunt. Ioh. 15. Act. 1 Ingenuè ergo testati sunt ore & verbis, Actor. 3 4. 5. &c. Factis item, & tandem morte. Qui huic contradicunt, Deum falsi insimulant, 1. Ioh. 5.
units.tr: 3. How one should conduct oneself in the gospel: Paul wishes to be a witness. A free and open preaching is meant. This is the office of a witness. For it is testimony about Christ (Rev. 17), and the apostles are such (John 15; Acts 1). Ingenuously, therefore, they bore witness with mouth and words (Acts 3, 4, 5, etc.), likewise by deeds, and finally by death. Those who contradict this make God a liar (1 John 5).

units.la: Hoc ipsum interim ab omnibus nobis requiritur. Non enim tales cultores vult Christus, quos sui pudeat. Vide Matth. 10. Mar. 8 Rom. 1. 10. &c. Testemur ore, vita moribus. Oremus
units.tr: This very thing is in the meantime required of all of us. For Christ does not want worshippers of whom he would be ashamed. See Matt. 10; Mark 8; Rom. 1, 10, etc. Let us bear witness by our mouth and by the morals of our lives. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXII.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXII.

units.la: 25 Et nunc ecce, ego scio non amplius visuros faciem meam vllos ex vobis omnib. per quos transfiui, prædicans regnum Dei.
units.tr: 25 And now, behold, I know that you will see my face no more, all of you among whom I have passed, preaching the kingdom of God.

units.la: 26 Ideo teflor vobis hodierno die me purum esse à sanguine omnium.
units.tr: 26 Therefore I testify to you this day that I am pure from the blood of all men.

units.la: 27 Non enim subterfugi, quo minus annuntiarem vobis omne Dei, consilium.
units.tr: 27 For I have not shrunk from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.

units.la: Vemadmodum Paulus Apostolus in constituendis Ecclesijs omnem curam adhibuit: ita ab ijsdem discessurus, de omnibus illarum pastores admonet, quæ ad ipsas coferuandas faciebat. Docet exemplum hoc, non sufficere, si semel recte constituantur Ecclesiæ & respub. sed iugi cura in illis seruandis opus esse, tum quod ad lapsum homines procli ues sunt, tu quod semper insidiatur satan, 1. Pet. 5. 2. Cor. 1. Porro vt maior esset adhortationis huius authoritas, suum exemplum allegauit, vt ostendat sibi aliquod in eos ius esse: similiq; de discessu suo admonuit, vt intelligant posthac omne curam ipsis incumbere. Sequitur breuis omnium quæ dixit recapitulatio, quæ nobis ordine consideranda venit.
units.tr: As the Apostle Paul took every care in founding the churches, so, about to leave them, he admonishes their ministers concerning everything that serves to preserve them. This passage teaches that it is not enough for churches and commonwealths to be rightly established once; there must be constant care in keeping them, both because men are prone to fall and because Satan always lies in wait (1 Pet. 5; 2 Cor. 1). Moreover, so that his exhortation might carry greater authority, Paul cited his own example, to show that he had some right over them. Likewise he warned them of his departure, so that they might understand that the whole care of them now rests upon themselves. There follows a brief summary of all that he said, which we must now consider in order.

units.la: I. Et nunc ecce ego scio, &c. Apertius suum discessum simul, & quòd nunquam rediturus sit, exprimit. Imitatur patres moituros, qui similia allegant, dum filios admonent.
units.tr: I. "And now, behold, I know," etc. He states more plainly both his departure and that he will never return. He imitates dying fathers, who make similar appeals when they admonish their sons.

units.la: Sed Notᵀ. Inuistum Pauli animum. Scit se hos amplius visurum non esse, nec aliud quàm mortem ob oculos habet. Attamen nullum vel metus, vel nimiæ tristitiæ signum ædit: quin potius de sola aliorum salute solicitus est. Verè electum organum, Aêto. 9. Imitentur ministri, magistratus. Exempla.
units.tr: But note the unconquered spirit of Paul. He knows that he will not see them again, and he has nothing before his eyes but death. Yet he shows no sign either of fear or of excessive sorrow; rather, he is anxious only for the salvation of others. Truly a chosen vessel (Acts 9). Let ministers and magistrates imitate him. Examples.

units.la: Docemur, vt ipsi quoq; mortem consideremus. Ne ploremus, quasi solis nobis hoc accidat. Nec amicos deploremus, quasi nemo sit reliquus. Est enim mors via vniuersæ terræ, Ios. 24. 1. Reg 2. Cur ergo non subiremus communem omnium sortem? Deinde amicos non amittimus, sed vel illi nos, vel nos ipsos præcedimus, & tandem in cœlis denuò omnes congregamur, Matth 8. Ibi enim communis patria, & locus omnibus paratus est, Ioh. 14 Phil. 3. Sic Dauid, 2. Sam. 12. Interea eorū, quos hic relinquimus, tutor & pater Deus est, cui qui commendari debent, Psalm. 68. Nos constanter viam ingrediamur, qua in coelos venitur.
units.tr: We are taught to consider death for ourselves as well. We should not weep as though this happened to us alone, nor lament our friends as though none were left. For death is the way of all the earth (Josh. 24; 1 Kings 2). Why then should we not undergo the common lot of all? Moreover, we do not lose our friends; either they go before us, or we go before them, and at last we shall all be gathered together again in heaven (Matt. 8). For there is our common homeland, and a place prepared for all (John 14; Phil. 3). So David (2 Sam. 12). Meanwhile, God is the guardian and father of those whom we leave here, and those who ought to be commended to him (Ps. 68). Let us walk steadfastly along the way by which one comes to heaven.

units.la: II. Contestatione subijcit grauissimam, qua omnem perditionis culpam in ipsorum capita reijcit, si Ecclesias suae fidei commissas à fide deficere patiantur. Ego mundus, ab omni sanguine. Respicit ad Ezech. 3. & 33. Causa: Quia non sunt superfugi, quo minus annuntiarem vobis omne consilium Dei Sic Moses, Deut. 30. Iosuae item Cap. 24.
units.tr: II. He adds a most solemn declaration, by which he throws all the guilt of ruin upon the heads of those who allow the churches committed to their trust to fall away from the faith. "I am clean, from all blood." He looks back to Ezek. 3 and 33. The reason: because I have not shrunk from declaring to you the whole counsel of God. So Moses (Deut. 30), and likewise Joshua in chapter 24.

units.la: Sed NOT. 1. Coram Deo excusatos esse qui suum officium faciunt, licet nihil proficiant apud homines. In ijs enim culpa haeret, qui incurabiles non obediunt. Pertinet ad omnes ordines. Ministros ver bi, Ezech. 3. 33. Luc. 9. 10. Vide Actor. 13. 18. Magistratus. Iosiam vide, sub quo multi impij, quorum tamen impietas illi nō frau di fuit, Reg. 22. 23. Soph. 1. 2. &c. Parentes. Fit vt pij impios habeant liberos, & tamen extra culpam sint: vt Abraham Ismaelem, Gen. 16. 21. 18. Iacob, Gen. 34. 35. 37. Dauid, 2. Sam. 13. 15. 16. At non extra culpam sunt, qui officiū negligunt, vt Heli, 1. Sam. 2. 3. 4. Arguuntur, quicunque cessandum putant, eo quod nihil proficias. Objcitur hoc ministris & magistratibus. Hoc ipso si bi patrocinantur ignaui parentes. Sed vi-
units.tr: But note, first, that those who do their duty are excused before God, even if they accomplish nothing among men. For the blame rests on those who do not obey, though they are beyond cure. This applies to all orders: ministers of the Word (Ezek. 3, 33; Luke 9, 10; see Acts 13, 18); magistrates. Consider Josiah, under whom many were impious, yet his impiety was not imputed to him as a fault (2 Kings 22, 23; Zeph. 1, 2, etc.); parents. It happens that the godly have ungodly children and yet are free from blame, as Abraham with Ishmael (Gen. 16, 21), Jacob (Gen. 34, 35, 37), David (2 Sam. 13, 15, 16). But those who neglect their duty are not free from blame, as Eli (1 Sam. 2, 3, 4). Whoever thinks that one should cease because nothing is achieved is condemned. This objection is made to ministers and magistrates; and idle parents plead the same excuse for themselves. But see

units.la: Deo. de vt tuam animam liberes, & non frustra laboraueris.
units.tr: ...to God, that you may free your soul and not have labored in vain.

units.la: § 2. Infelice eorum fortem, qui cum of ficio suo probè functi sunt antecessores, ipsi vel ignaui relabuntur, vel etiam malitia corrumpunt bene constituta. Sunt il li inexcusabiles coram Deo, & in ipsis haec culpa interitus.
units.tr: § 2. Unhappy is the lot of those who, though their predecessors discharged their office well, themselves either slip back through sloth or even corrupt by wickedness what was well established. Such men are inexcusable before God, and this fault is their ruin.

units.la: Obseruemus ergo: A. In Ecclesia, quoad doctrinam & religionem. Tradita sunt recte omnia. Summis laboribus & pericu lis introducta reformatio. Sed fit quod Iud. 2. Quae erit autem excusatio, si relabamur? Solus puluis sufficiens aduersus nos testis. Quid ergo facient tot labores, &c.
units.tr: Let us therefore observe: A. In the Church, as regards doctrine and religion. All things were rightly handed down; the reformation was introduced with great labors and dangers. But what happens is what is said in Judges 2. What excuse will there be if we fall back? The dust alone will be a sufficient witness against us. What then will so many labors avail, etc.?

units.la: B. In Repub. Maiorum sanguine parta libertas. Per Euangelium conditae bonae leges, disciplina, &c. Si ignaui haec nobis eripi patiamur, aut ipsi d fciplinae i npatientia euertamus, inexcusabiles fumus.
units.tr: B. In the commonwealth. Liberty was won by the blood of our forefathers; good laws and discipline were established through the Gospel, etc. If through sloth we allow these to be taken from us, or by impatience with discipline overthrow them ourselves, we are inexcusable.

units.la: § 3. Omne Dei consilium annuntiauit Paulus: nimirum quoad nostrae salutis & redemptionis negotium attinet. Aliquid multa sunt in prouidentia Dei, quae scrutari nos non decet, Eccl. 3. Prou 25. Mar. 13. Act. 1.2. Cor. 12. At quoad salutem nostra, nihil omisit. Tradidit causas salutis, & eiusdem rationē, Eph. 1.2. &c. Item saluatorum rum officia diligentissimè. Apostolorum ergo doctrina perfecta est. Vide Ioh. 15. 14 16. Continetur in scriptu ris, de quibus 2. Tim. 3. Vanissimi ergo sunt, qui traditiones Ecclesijs obtrudunt. Pugnant hæ maximæ expar e cum Apostolis, qui vnum Christum nobis tradiderunt, Actor. 4. 1. Cor. 2 Gal 6. 1. Ioh 1. 2. &c. Quapropter non possunt eundem habere authorem, Spiritum Christi.
units.tr: § 3. Paul declared the whole counsel of God, namely as far as concerns the business of our salvation and redemption. Many things in God's providence we ought not to pry into (Eccl. 3; Prov. 25; Mark 13; Acts 1; 2 Cor. 12). But as regards our salvation he omitted nothing. He handed down the causes of salvation and their rationale (Eph. 1, 2, etc.), and likewise the duties of the saved most diligently. The teaching of the apostles is therefore complete (see John 15, 14, 16). It is contained in the Scriptures, of which 2 Tim. 3 speaks. Therefore they are most vain who thrust traditions upon the churches. These great inventions clash with the apostles, who delivered to us one Christ alone (Acts 4; 1 Cor. 2; Gal. 6; 1 John 1, 2, etc.). Therefore they cannot have the same author, the Spirit of Christ.

units.la: ¶ 4. Quod li et omnia coràm tradidis-set Paulus, tamen postea ad illos epistolam scribit, qua eadem repetuntur. Patet hinc, quanta salutis hominum ratio habe-ri debeat, & quàm parùm Apostolici sint, qui Ecclesias tam facilè negligunt, &c. Nos Dei consilium in Christo revelatum & impletum ampleciamur. Oremus.
units.tr: ¶ 4. Although Paul had already delivered everything in person, he nevertheless wrote an epistle to them afterwards, in which the same things are repeated. From this it is clear how great a concern for men's salvation ought to be had, and how little they are apostolic who so easily neglect the churches, etc. Let us embrace the counsel of God revealed and fulfilled in Christ. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXIV.
units.tr: HOMILY 164.

units.la: 28 Attendite igitur vosipsos, & totum gregem, in quo vos spiritus sanctus constituit Episcopos, ad pascendam Ecclesiam Dei, quam proprio sanguine acquisivit.
units.tr: 28 Take heed therefore to yourselves, and to all the flock, over which the Holy Spirit has made you bishops, to feed the Church of God, which he purchased with his own blood.

units.la: QVamuis omnes homines Ecclesiæ conseruationi diligenter studere debeant, eò quòd Deo nihil illa præstantius tius & charius sit: cumprimis tamen ad ministros huius cura pertinet, quos pecu liariter huius gubernationi Deus destina uit, & à quibus olim rationem exiget, Lucæ 16. Est hæc causa, propter quam Paulus Asiam relicturus, Ecclesiarum minifiros conuocauit, & tam ferió cum illis omnia tractauit, quæ ad Ecclesiarum salutem & ministerium illorum spectant. Ante omnia vero suum exemplum illis proposuit, & de suo discessu cum graui protestatione diferuit, vt scirent, sibi posthac solis omnem curam incumbere, &c. Nunc ergo officij illos admonere incipit, & rationibus vrget.
units.tr: Although all men ought diligently to strive for the preservation of the Church, since nothing is more excellent and dear to God than it, the care of it pertains especially to the ministers, whom God has appointed in a peculiar way to this governance, and from whom he will one day require an account, Luke 16. This is the reason why Paul, about to leave Asia, called together the ministers of the Churches and dealt earnestly with them about everything that concerns the salvation of the Churches and their ministry. Above all, he set his own example before them, and he spoke of his departure with solemn protestation, so that they might know that from now on all care rested on them alone, etc. Now he begins to admonish them of their duty and urges it with reasons.

units.la: I. Proponit quid faciant in suo munere. Attendendi verbo summum studium requirit, &c. Vbi duo Not. ¶1. Attendite vobis ipsis. Hinc orditur, ne se exemptos putarent, sed intelligerent suam ipsorum quoque salutem periclitari. Nec enim periculo carere potest in alto coftitutus aut ambitione peccant, aut offenduntur ingratitudine. Nec credibile est, aliorum fa-lutem curaturum eum, qui suæ negligens fuerit. Hoc autem obseruent quicunq; in eminentia constituti sunt.
units.tr: I. He sets out what they should do in their office. He requires the greatest zeal in attending to the word, etc. Here two points are to be noted. ¶1. "Take heed to yourselves." He begins here so that they would not think themselves exempt, but understand that their own salvation is also in peril.
