For one set in a high place cannot be free from danger, whether he sins through ambition or is offended by ingratitude. Nor is it credible that he will care for the salvation of others who has been negligent of his own. Those who are placed in eminence should observe this.

units.la: Minister autem duo curet. A. Doctrinam, vt hæc vera fit. Fetat hac ex ore Dei, &c. & proinde lectioni sedulò incumbat, E. zech.3.1.Tim.4.2.Tim.3.Eandem rectè se cet,& prudenter agat omnia, 2.Timot.2. Matth.24.
units.tr: A minister, moreover, should attend to two things. A. Doctrine, that it be true. It comes from the mouth of God, etc., and therefore he should apply himself diligently to reading, E. Zech. 3.1; 1 Tim. 4.2; 2 Tim. 3. He should handle the same rightly and act prudently in all things, 2 Tim. 2; Matt. 24.

units.la: B. Vitam, quæ irreprehensibilis esse de bet,ne malo exèplo offendat, ne propter illū doctrina & religio vilescat,vt olim,1. Sam.2.Mal.1.2. Pertinet huc familiæ cura,1.Tim.3.Tit.1.
units.tr: B. Life, which ought to be blameless, lest he offend by a bad example, and lest through him doctrine and religion become contemptible, as once happened, 1 Sam. 2; Mal. 1–2. To this pertains the care of his household, 1 Tim. 3; Titus 1.

units.la: ¶ 2. Vniuersum gregem. Adijcit hoc, ne sibi ipsis attendentes,hunc negligant. Ita vero Ecclesiam vocat,iuxta illa Ezech.34. Ioh.10.21. Commendat Dei bonitatem. Comprehendititem omnes ordines,vt alibi sub domus & familiæ nomine, Ezec. 3.33.Mar.24.Expònitur Ier.1.
units.tr: ¶ 2. "The whole flock." He adds this lest, attending only to themselves, they neglect the rest. The Church is so called according to those passages, Ezek. 34; John 10.21. He commends God's goodness. It comprehends all orders, as elsewhere under the name of house and family, Ezek. 3.33; Mark 24. It is explained at Jer. 1.

units.la: Docemur:A. Omnium hominum curā ad ministros pertinere, nec illis licere, vt negligant aliquem. Cogitent in magna domo varia vasa esse ; quæ omnia curari vult paterfamiliās,nec esse personarum re spectum,2.Tim.2.Col.3.Gal.3.
units.tr: We are taught: A. The care of all men pertains to ministers, and it is not lawful for them to neglect anyone. Let them consider that in a great house there are various vessels, all of which the father of the household wants to be cared for, and that there is no respect of persons, 2 Tim. 2; Col. 3; Gal. 3.

units.la: B. Omnes ordines verbi ministerio & disciplinæ subijci debere, nec aliquem ex eis immunem,Iere.1.Pfal.2.119. Vide Prophetas & Baptistam. Christum & Apostolos,&c.
units.tr: B. All orders ought to be subject to the ministry of the word and to discipline, and none of them is exempt, Jer. 1; Ps. 2; 119. See the Prophets and the Baptist, Christ and the Apostles, etc.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui impatientes disciplinæ, res suas ad Pfaffum pertinere negant.
units.tr: Those are rebuked who, impatient of discipline, deny that their affairs belong to the priests.

units.la: II. Rationes adhibet, quibus persuadet, at. 1. Spiritus sanctus vos constituit. Docet, ipsos non esse sui iuris, sed a Deo ordinatos, cui rationem sint reddituri. Vide Matth. 25. Luc. 16. Spiritus autem expressè monuit, quia per hunc Ecclesia maximè administratur, Ioh. 14. 16. Act. 1. 2. Est haec ratio gravissima, si cogites, Deum nihil latere. Simul solatur.
units.tr: II. He gives reasons by which he persuades. 1. The Holy Spirit has made you overseers. He teaches that they are not their own masters, but ordained by God, to whom they will render an account. See Matt. 25; Luke 16. The Spirit expressly warned them, because through the Spirit the Church is chiefly governed, John 14.16; Acts 1.2. This reason is most weighty if you consider that nothing is hidden from God. At the same time it consoles.

units.la: Sed Not. Eadem ratione omnes quo que alio vrgeri, qui in officijs a Deo instituti versantur. Magistratus, Rom. 13. Psal. 82. Heb. Eph. 6. Parentes, Exod. 20. Eph. 6. Deut. 6. Coniuges, Eph. 5. Heb. 13. &c. Servi ac subditi quoniam, 1. Petri 2. Roman. 13. Cogitent se olim Deo rationem reddituros.
units.tr: But note: by the same reasoning, all others also are urged who are engaged in offices instituted by God: magistrates, Rom. 13; Ps. 82; Heb.; Eph. 6. Parents, Exod. 20; Eph. 6; Deut. 6. Spouses, Eph. 5; Heb. 13, etc. Servants and subjects likewise, 1 Pet. 2; Rom. 13. Let them consider that they too will one day render an account to God.

units.la: II. Officium ipsorum, & huius finem indicat. Pofiutvos episcopos ad pascendum Ecclesiam Dei. Alludit ad Ezech. 3. 33. Zac. 11. Ioh. 10. 21. Duo coniungit, ne quoquam ipsatores sint. Finis, ut pascatis. Facite ergo pastoris officium, quod habes, Ezech. 34. Ioh. 10. Huius partes sunt, deducere in laeta pascua verbi Dei. Praeire vitae exemplo. Perditas quaerere, Luc. 15. Propulsatam vi & tyrannide reducere. Contritam conscientiam obligare. Infirmam roborare. Pinguem & ferocientem coercere pedo,i.Cor.4.2.Cor.12.13.Lupos arcere, Io. Omnia facere cum iudicio,1 Pet.5.
units.tr: II. He indicates their office and its end. "He has set you as bishops to feed the Church of God." He alludes to Ezek. 3.33; Zech. 11; John 10.21. He joins two things, lest they be mere hirelings. The end is that you feed. Do the duty of the shepherd that you have, Ezek. 34; John 10. Its parts are: to lead into the pleasant pastures of God's word; to go before with the example of life; to seek the lost, Luke 15; to bring back those driven off by force and tyranny; to bind up the contrite conscience; to strengthen the weak; to restrain the fat and frisky with discipline, 1 Cor. 4.21; 2 Cor. 12.13; to keep off wolves; to do all things with judgment, 1 Pet. 5.

units.la: NOT Episcoporum nostri seculi insolentiam. Quid illi horum faciunt? Quin potius quae albi rej rehendit Deus, faciunt,Ezec.34.Zach 11.56 Et contra Christi mandatum repugnant,Matthae 20 Lucae 22. Poenam vide Zach.11.Malach 2.Magistratus.
units.tr: NOTE the insolence of the bishops of our age. What of these things do they do? Rather, they do what God rebukes in the shepherds, Ezek. 34; Zech. 11; and they resist Christ's command, Matt. 20; Luke 22. For the punishment see Zech. 11; Mal. 2. Magistrates.

units.la: III. A Dignitate Ecclesiae: Quam Deus Ecclesiam acquisivit sanguine suo, 1.Pet.1. Eph.1. Est gnitas ergo ei clarissima, & qui hanc negligunt, prophanatores sanguinis Christi sunt, cuius fructum abolent. Sic loquitur propter unitatem Deitatis.
units.tr: III. From the dignity of the Church, which God acquired with his own blood, 1 Pet. 1; Eph. 1. Its dignity is therefore most clear, and those who neglect it are profaners of the blood of Christ, whose fruit they destroy. He speaks thus on account of the unity of the Godhead.

units.la: NOTA.1. Ecclesiam Dei esse, qui illam acquisivit, & sibi despondit, non alicui hominis, Ephes. 5. Iohan. 3. Ezech. 16. Huic ergo consecrati esse debent, qui huius membra censeri volunt. Qui alios sequuntur, fornicantur, Ezech. 16. Adhaec nemo sibi dominium debet vendicare, 1. Pet 5.
units.tr: NOTE 1. The Church is God's, since he acquired it and betrothed it to himself, not to any man, Eph. 5; John 3; Ezek. 16. Therefore those who wish to be counted among its members ought to be consecrated to him. Those who follow others commit fornication, Ezek. 16. Moreover, no one ought to claim lordship for himself, 1 Pet. 5.

units.la: Interim consolationi servit. Quia non negligit tanto pretio acquisitam Deus, Is. 49. Mat.28 &c. Petant hinc singuli consolationem in privatis malis.
units.tr: Meanwhile it serves for consolation, because God does not neglect what was acquired at so great a price, Is. 49; Matt. 28, etc. Let individuals seek consolation from this in their private troubles.

units.la: 2. Eandem rationem etiam erga quosque privatos valere. Ad Dei imaginem proximus tuus creatus,& Christi sanguine redemptus est. Cur ergo conuiciatis, laedis,offendis,&c? Vide 1.Cor.8. Ro.14. Oremus.
units.tr: 2. The same reasoning holds also for each private person. Your neighbour was created in God's image and redeemed by Christ's blood. Why then do you revile, harm, and offend him, etc.? See 1 Cor. 8; Rom. 14. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXIV.
units.tr: HOMILIA CLXIV.

units.la: 29 Ego enim hoc nouipoft difcef-sum meum lupos graues, non parcentes gregi,ingressuros esse in vos.
units.tr: 29 For I know that after my departure grievous wolves, not sparing the flock, will come in among you.

units.la: 30 Et ex vobis ipsis exorituros,qui loquantur peruersa, vt discipulos post fe abstrahant.
units.tr: 30 And from among yourselves there will arise men speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.

units.la: 31 Ideo vigilate,memores, me per triennium noäte & die non ceffaffe cum lachrymis monere vnumquemq;.
units.tr: 31 Therefore watch, remembering that for three years I did not cease to warn each one of you night and day with tears.

units.la: 32 Et nunc quoq; fratres commen-do vos Deo & sermoni gratiæ ipsius: qui quidem Deus potens est superstrue re, et dare vobis hæreditatem interfan ctificatos omnes.
units.tr: 32 And now, brothers, I commend you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and to give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.

units.la: QVamuis Paulus in omni sua doctrina zelo sancto totus ardeat,pe cuiaris tamen spiritus vis in hac oratione elucet, qua Asiae ministros instituit. Causa huius est,quòd à ministris non minima ex parte Ecclesiarum salus depen-det,cùm horum negligentia ouibus damnosa fit. Quare non obiter modò officij illos admonet, veram etiam grauissimis rationibus illos vrget. 1. Authorem ministerij Deum, proposuit,cui rationem sint reddituři, Matth.25. Ezech.3. 2. Finem officij indicauit,qui noninani speculatione, sed pascendo versatur,Ioh.10 21. Ezec.34. 3. Dignitatem Ecclesiae allegat, quam filij sanguine Deus acquisiuit. Sequuntur reliquae.
units.tr: Although Paul burns with holy zeal throughout all his teaching, the force of his spirit shines out especially in this speech, in which he instructs the ministers of Asia. The reason is that the salvation of the churches depends in no small part on the ministers, since their negligence is harmful to the sheep. So he does not merely remind them of their duty in passing but presses it upon them with the most weighty reasons: (1) he sets before them God as the author of the ministry, to whom they must give account (Matt. 25; Ezek. 3); (2) he points out the purpose of the office, which concerns not empty speculation but feeding the flock (John 21; Ezek. 34); (3) he appeals to the dignity of the Church, which God acquired with the blood of his Son. The rest follows.

units.la: I. A necessitate argumentatur quarto loco Necesse est, vt imminentibus lupis, pastores officium faciant,Ioh.10. At ego noui graues lupos venturos, & quidem ex vobisipsis orituroc. Ergo,&c. Ita verò falsos doctores vocat iuxta,Christi exemplum,Matth.7. Hos venturos nouerat,nimirum peculiari spiritus reuelatione, vt patet,1.Tim.4.
units.tr: I. He argues from necessity in the fourth place: it is necessary that ministers perform their duty when wolves are at hand (John 10). But I know that grievous wolves will come, and indeed from among you yourselves. Therefore, etc. He calls false teachers wolves after the example of Christ (Matt. 7). He knew they would come, namely by a special revelation of the Spirit, as is clear from 1 Tim. 4.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ 1. Fidem & curam Dei, qua is suae Ecclesiae prospicit. Versatur haec ceu in medio luporum,Matt.10. Sed Dei us non de praesentibus modo, verumetiam futuris periculis admonet. Vide Dan. 7.11.12. Zach.11. Item Matt.7.24. 1.Ioh.2.4. 2.Pet.2.2.Thess.2.1, Tim.4.2.Tim.3.4.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ 1. The faith and care of God, by which he watches over his Church. She dwells as it were in the midst of wolves (Matt. 10). But God warns not only of present dangers but also of future ones. See Dan. 7:11-12; Zech. 11; likewise Matt. 7:24; 1 John 2:4; 2 Pet. 2:2; 2 Thess. 2:1; 1 Tim. 4:2; 2 Tim. 3:4.

units.la: Arguuntur hic,qui veritatem simplicicer praedicari volunt, at de periculis aliibus Ecclesias admonēri & lupos arguino' lunt, vt qui magis irritentur. Ergo canes
units.tr: Here are rebuked those who want the truth preached plainly but do not want the churches warned of other dangers and the wolves exposed, lest they be provoked the more. Therefore they want dumb dogs (Isa. 56), and the wolf is not tamed.

units.la: Ccc
units.tr: Ccc

units.la: mutos volunt,If 56.Et lupi nö cicuratur. ¶ 2. Quód post suum discessum ventu-ros dicit. Solent enim vigilantia fidelium ministrorum cura tales coerceri. Hanc quia indignè mundus aest mat,lupos submittit Deus. Discis quanti in Ecclesia simul & Repub.pij antistites fieri debeant. Horum obitus feré grauisimorum malorum sunt prasagia,If 57.
units.tr: ¶ 2. That he says they will come after his departure. For the watchfulness of faithful ministers usually restrains such men. Because the world is unworthy of this, God sends wolves. Learn how much the godly leaders of the Church and of the commonwealth ought to be prized. The deaths of these men are almost always the omens of the gravest evils (Isa. 57).

units.la: ¶ 3. Quæ falsorum doctorum ratio? A. Lupi dicuntur: Quia naturali odio omium laborant, & insatiabili voracitate vel aua-ritia totum gregem defœdant. Ideo grauues vocat. Vide Mat.7. Obseruemus hoc, ne blanditijs decipiamur.
units.tr: ¶ 3. What is the nature of false teachers? A. They are called wolves because they suffer from a natural hatred of all, and by insatiable greed or avarice they foul the whole flock. Therefore he calls them grievous. See Matt. 7. Let us observe this, lest we be deceived by flattery.

units.la: B. Vnde emergunt? Ex vobis ipsis, 1.Ioh. 2 4 2.Theff. 2. Sic Iudas vnus ex duodecim. Obseruemus contra offendiculum. Interim confutatur stolida Rom.Pontifi-cum de continua succesione gloriatio, quæ illos prohibeat errare
units.tr: B. Whence do they arise? From among yourselves (1 John 2:4; 2 Thess. 2). Thus Judas was one of the twelve. Let us observe this against stumbling. Meanwhile the foolish boast of the Roman Pontiffs about continuous succession is refuted, which supposedly prevents them from erring.

units.la: C. Doctrina. Loquentur peruersa. Veritas simplex est. Hanc illi peruertunt & corrumpunt suis figmentis, & incerta reddunt, quæ alio quin certa, simplicia & plena sunt.
units.tr: C. Their teaching: they will speak perverse things. The truth is simple. They pervert and corrupt it with their inventions, and make uncertain what otherwise is certain, simple and full.

units.la: D.Finis, Abducent post se discipulos. Ambitione ergo exagitati, sectas inuchunt,2. Pet.2.Facta hæc statim post Pauli obitu, vt quoq; prædictum 1.Tim.4.Huc pertinent hæretici. Adde his quæ hodie fiunt. Nobis non minus necessaria hæc admonitio.
units.tr: D. Their aim: they will draw away disciples after them. Driven by ambition, they therefore introduce sects (2 Pet. 2). These things happened immediately after Paul's death, as was also foretold in 1 Tim. 4. To this belong the heretics. Add to these what happens today. This warning is no less necessary for us.

units.la: II. Exemplum suum denuo infert, quin tæ rationis loco. Sed simul adhortatione mem adijcit: Vigilate ergo, &c Triennj minit, ne fatigentur eito. Quasi dicat: Turpe foret, vos tam cito defatigari, cum tam diu ego laborârim. Turpe item est ea dissipare, quæ aliorum laboribus parta sunt.
units.tr: II. He again brings forward his own example in the place of a second reason. But at the same time he adds an exhortation: Therefore watch, etc. He reminds them of the three years, so that they do not grow weary quickly. As if he said: It would be shameful for you to grow weary so soon, when I laboured so long. It is also shameful to squander what has been gained by the labours of others.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Quorsum nobis sanctorum virtutes seruire posint. Exemplorum loco sint, quæ imitemur. Sic 1.Cor.11. Phil. 3.2. Theff. 3. Abutuntur, qui ideo invocandos & colendos putant. Deum authorem omnis boni in ipsis agnoscamus, 1.Cor.15.3.Act.3 14.&c.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ How the virtues of the saints can serve us. Let them be for us examples to imitate. So 1 Cor. 11; Phil. 3:2; 2 Thess. 3. They abuse them who think that the saints ought therefore to be invoked and worshipped. Let us acknowledge God as the author of all good in them (1 Cor. 15:3; Acts 3:14, etc.).

units.la: III. Concludit argumenta Deo illos commendans, vt partim illis occurrat, qui difficultate munens & periculis terreba tur, partim ne quid sibijpsis tribuant. Vt verò magis pathetica sit oratio, sub forma precationis proponit. A. Commendo vos Deo, & sermoni gratiæ eius, qui potens est, &c. Quasi dicat. Scio arduum hoc esse. Non putetis autem hæc vestris viribus confecturos. Dei agricolatio & opus est 1.Corinth.3. Ille cœpit & fundamentum iecit. Poterit ergo superstruere, nec imperfectum reliquit opus, Psal. 136. Phil. 1. Aderit is suo spiritu & verbo gratiae, Hebr. 4.
units.tr: III. He concludes his arguments by commending them to God, partly to meet those who are terrified by the difficulty and the dangers, and partly lest they attribute anything to themselves. So that his speech may be more moving, he sets it out in the form of a prayer. A. I commend you to God and to the word of his grace, who is able, etc. As if he said: I know this is a hard task. But do not think that you will accomplish these things by your own strength. The tilling and building is God's (1 Cor. 3). He began and laid the foundation; therefore he will be able to build upon it, and he has not left the work unfinished (Ps. 136; Phil. 1). He will be present with his Spirit and the word of grace (Heb. 4).

units.la: B Ille ipse remunerator erit fidelis, & haec hereditatem dabit inter sanctificatos. Admonet promissionum, Dan. 12. Mat. 5. Ioh. 14. 17.
units.tr: B. He himself will be a faithful rewarder, and will give this inheritance among the sanctified. He reminds them of the promises (Dan. 12; Matt. 5; John 14, 17).

units.la: NOTA. Quibus armis pugnare & confidere debeant ministri. De his armis Paulus, 2. Corin. 10. Gratia Dei & verbo Dei. Non deest illis Deus, Ioh. 14. 16. Mat. 28. Verbum vero est penetrantior quovis gladio, Heb. 4. Eph. 6. Apoc. 1. Quem ergo timeamus? Rom. 8. Falluntur qui adcarnem respiciunt, foedera, &c.
units.tr: NOTE. With what weapons ministers ought to fight and trust. Paul speaks of these weapons in 2 Cor. 10: the grace of God and the word of God. God is not lacking to them (John 14:16; Matt. 28). The word is more piercing than any sword (Heb. 4; Eph. 6; Rev. 1). Whom then should we fear? (Rom. 8.) Those are deceived who look to flesh, covenants, etc.

units.la: 2. Ad quos pertineat regni caelorum hereditas? Ad sanctificatos. Sunt hi quorum corda fides mundavit, quosque sibi consecravit Christus, Act. 15. 1. Cor. 5. 6. Ijdem suo officio funguntur.
units.tr: 2. To whom does the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven belong? To the sanctified. These are the ones whose hearts faith has cleansed, and whom Christ has consecrated to himself (Acts 15; 1 Cor. 5, 6). The same people perform their office.

units.la: Haec spes nos sustineat, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: May this hope sustain us, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXV.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXV.

units.la: 33 Argentum & aurum aut vestem nullius concupivi:
units.tr: "I have coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing."

units.la: 34 Imo ipsi nostris, vestibus meis, & iis, qui mecum sunt, manus istas miniistrasse.
units.tr: "Yes, you yourselves know that these hands have ministered to my own needs and to those who were with me."

units.la: 35 In omnibus ostendi vobis oportere tere sic laborando suscipere infirmos, et memimisse verborum Iesu, ipsum videli cet dixit: Beatius est dare potius quam accipere.
units.tr: "In all things I have shown you that by labouring in this way you must support the weak, and remember the words of Jesus, which he himself said: It is more blessed to give than to receive."

units.la: 36 Et quum haec dixisset, positis genibus suis, orauit cum illis omnibus.
units.tr: And when he had said these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

units.la: 37 Magnus autem fletus omnium ortus est, et ruentes in collum Pauli, deosculabantur eum.
units.tr: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck and kissed him.

units.la: 38 Cruciati maxime ob sermonem, quem dixerat, ipsos non esse amplius visuros faciem eius conspecturos: et deduxerunt eum ad navem.
units.tr: Sorrowing most of all for the words he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. And they brought him to the ship.

units.la: Diuus Paulus monuit nuper post sum dum discessum graues lupos orituros, qui Ecclesiam turbent & disipent: & hos quidem ex illis ipsis proditu-ros dixit, vt ad vigilantiam magis excitaret Asi ministros. Ita vero ista proponit, vt often dat quae tanti mali causae futurae sint, quo facilius sibi caueant. Primam fecit ambi-tionem, quo nimirum discipuli post se ad-ducturi, & priuatam gloriam quaesituri sint, contra illud Christi, Matth 28. Fuit haec olim praecipua haeresum causa, & hodie eadem sectas inducit & fouet. Obser-uent ergo hanc priuatim singuli, vt lupos agnoscere possint. Alteram nunc subiji-
units.tr: The divine Paul recently warned, after his departure, that grievous wolves would arise who would trouble and scatter the Church, and he said that some of them would come from among the ministers themselves, in order to stir the ministers of Asia more to vigilance. He sets this out so that he may give in advance the causes of such great evil, so that they may guard themselves more easily. First he names ambition, by which disciples will draw others after themselves and seek private glory, against that saying of Christ, Matt. 28. This was long the chief cause of heresies, and today the same thing brings sects into being and fosters them. Let each person therefore observe this in private, so that he may recognise wolves. Next I now add

units.la: citauaritiam nimirum,quæ vt omnis ma-li radix est,ita fi apud Antistites obtineat, omnia corrumpit. Ex religione quæstum facit. Venalia sacra. Doctrinam vitiat. Con temptum religionis inuehit, quæ publica licentiæ causa est. Exemplo sunt sacerdo-tes Iudæorum, Ioh.2. Matth.15.23.21. Et in papatu hinc omnis corruptio enata. Ideo contra hanc graviter monet, 1.Tim.3.Tit. 2. In præsenti vero rursus vt antea, suo exemplo illos vrget.
units.tr: avarice, namely, which, as it is the root of every evil, so, if it holds sway among the leaders, corrupts everything. It makes a profit out of religion; sacred things are put up for sale; it vitiates doctrine; it brings in contempt for religion, which is a public licence for wrongdoing. The priests of the Jews are examples: John 2; Matt. 15, 23, 21. And from this source all corruption has sprung up in the papacy. Therefore he warns strongly against this, 1 Tim. 3; Tit. 2. In the present passage, as before, he urges them by his own example.

units.la: I. Qualis fuerit? Aurum, &c. id est. Non ex vobisditescere volui, sed vos ditare in Deo. Imo ne necessar. a quidem à vobis accepi. Unde ergo victus? Manus hæ, &c. Vide Actorum 18. Ita Samuel, 1. Samuel. 12.
units.tr: I. What was he like? "Gold, etc." That is: I did not want to grow rich from you, but to enrich you in God. Nay, I did not even receive from you what was necessary. Whence then did he support himself? "These hands, etc." See Acts 18. So Samuel, 1 Sam. 12.

units.la: Notes. Modestiam Apostolorum, qui à licitis quoq; abstinuerunt, ne cui essent onerosi. Idem singuli debent.
units.tr: Notes. The modesty of the apostles, who abstained even from lawful things, lest they be burdensome to anyone. Each individual ought to do the same.

units.la: Arguuntur qui Ecclesias expilant, vt in papatu fit. Qui easdem ob stipendium de feruant. Item qui in Repub. prædones agunt, & ex egentium sudore voluptuan-tur. Qui item priuatim onerosi sunt alijs vsura & lucro immodico, vel etiam impu-denter mendicando, &c.
units.tr: Those are condemned who plunder the churches, as happens in the papacy, and who keep them for the sake of their stipend. Likewise those who act as robbers in the commonwealth and grow fat on the sweat of the needy. Likewise those who are burdensome to others privately through usury and immoderate gain, or even through shameless begging, etc.

units.la: II. Causam indicat duplicem. 1. Offendi sic oportere suscipere infirmos, id est, rudi-um. um infirmitati aliquid concedere, &c. Fu-ius hoc exponit, 1. Corinth. 9. & 2. Co-rinth. 11. Ne inferior esseт Pseudoapostolis, &c.
units.tr: II. He indicates a double cause. 1. It is necessary thus to support the weak, that is, to concede something to the infirmity of the untrained, etc. He explains this more fully in 1 Cor. 9 and 2 Cor. 11, lest he be inferior to the false apostles, etc.

units.la: Quare Not. ¶ Non statui hic legem generalem. Ita enim damnaretur Christi statutum Matthaei 10. Deinde ipse Paulus probat multis, licere ut ministri ex Ecclesijs viuant, 1. Cor. 9. Allegat Deuter. 25. Item parabola rei pastoritiæ, rusticæ, &c. Num. 18. Et ipse ab aliis accepit, 2. Corint. 11. Phil. 4. Quod si licuit ab absentibus accipere, quanto magis, &c. Nemo igitur ab utatur.
units.tr: Wherefore note: I do not lay down a general law here. For in that case Christ's statute in Matthew 10 would be condemned. Then Paul himself proves by many arguments that it is lawful for ministers to live from the churches, 1 Cor. 9. He cites Deut. 25; likewise the parable of the work of the shepherd and the farmer, Num. 18. And he himself received from others, 2 Cor. 11; Phil. 4. If it was lawful to receive from those who were absent, how much more from those who are present. Let no one therefore abuse this.

units.la: II. Christi dictum allegat, Beatus, &c. Non extat hoc in forma, sed potest colligi ex Luc. 6. 14. & 16. Nota. ¶ Quæ huius dicti ratio? Non ciuili sensu accipiendum, quod qui accipiunt obstringuntur aliis, &c. Sed altius quid spectat spiritus san-ctus. 1. Quod tales sunt fidi œconomi Dei, qui inæqualitatem hanc instituit, ut bene ficentia locum haberet, & pauperes graui-ter commendauit, Mat. 26. 25 &c.
units.tr: II. He cites a saying of Christ: "Blessed, etc." It is not found in this form, but it can be gathered from Luke 6:14 and 16. Note. What is the reason for this saying? It is not to be understood in a civil sense, that those who receive are bound to others, etc. Rather the Holy Spirit looks at something higher. 1. Because such people are faithful stewards of God, who established this inequality so that beneficence would have a place, and who commended the poor very earnestly, Matt. 26:25, etc.

units.la: 2. Quia fœnerantur Domino (Prouer. 19.) qui fidelis est remunerator. Præstabit ergo promissiones, Psal. 112. Luc. 16. Matth. 25.
units.tr: 2. Because they lend to the Lord (Prov. 19), who is a faithful rewarder. He will therefore fulfil his promises, Ps. 112; Luke 16; Matt. 25.

units.la: 3. Ad Dei naturam proximè accedunt, quæ summa est felicitas. Nihil tam diu- num quàm plurimis benefacere.
units.tr: 3. They draw nearest to the nature of God, which is supreme happiness. Nothing is so godlike as doing good to very many.

units.la: Obseruare debebant Monachi, qui religionem in accipiendo constituunt, & prætextu voluntariæ paupertatis abutuntur.Item qui Mendici charitatem ab omnibus flagitant,ipsi eius immemores. Vide Eph.4 2.Theff.3.
units.tr: Monks ought to observe this, who place religion in receiving and abuse the pretext of voluntary poverty; likewise beggars who demand charity from everyone while themselves forgetting it. See Eph. 4; 2 Thess. 3.

units.la: III. Claudit orationem precibus Scie- bat à solo Deo dari incrementum, 1.Cor. 3.Et hinc illemos Ecclesiæ Prophani sunt qui se proripiunt, nec publicis precibus intersunt. Testantur,se verbum quoq; non magni facere,Ezech.33.
units.tr: III. He closes the discourse with prayers, knowing that increase comes from God alone, 1 Cor. 3. Hence those profane men in the Church who slip away and do not take part in public prayers. By this they testify that they do not value even the Word, Ezek. 33.

units.la: Not. ¶ Quòd positis gentibus orant. Oratio quidem fit corde. Sed pij gestus quoq;adhibent,partim vt membra omnia exerceant ad pietatem, partim vt seipsos & alios excitent ad deuotionem. Capitis apertio numinis reuerentiam suadet. Genuum flexio humilitatis admonet. Manuum elevatio fidem & accipiendi desiderium exprimit. Sed curandum, vt animus respondeat. Alioqui in nos quadrat,If.29.1.
units.tr: Note. That they pray kneeling. Prayer is indeed made in the heart, but pious gestures are also employed, partly so that all the members may be exercised in piety, and partly to stir up both themselves and others to devotion. Uncovering the head suggests reverence for the divine majesty. Bending the knees reminds us of humility. Raising the hands expresses faith and the desire to receive. But care must be taken that the mind answers to the gesture; otherwise Isa. 29 applies to us.

units.la: Discessus Pauli describitur, qui duo habet.1.Oritur fletus,ruunt in collu,&c.Quòd audirent se priuari tanto organo. Argumentum magni amoris, quamuis illos nō obscurè perstrinxisset.
units.tr: The departure of Paul is described, and it has two parts. 1. Weeping breaks out; they rush upon his neck, etc., because they heard that they would be deprived of so great an instrument. This is an argument of great love, although he had not obscurely hinted at it to them.

units.la: Notæ. Quo affectu subditi in suos præsides esse debent. Amauit hos Paulus. Amatur vicissim, vt pater. Ita mutuum sementum ministri, magistratus, populus. Hinc omnia prosperera. Vbi odijs certatur, ibi omnia infeliciter cedunt. Arguit exemplū hoc etiam ἀσόργως Stoicos. Affectus per se non malj, accedat saltem moderatio.
units.tr: Notes. With what affection subjects ought to be toward their rulers. Paul loved these men, and he is loved in return, as a father is. Thus there is mutual concord between ministers, magistrates and people, and hence all things prosper. Where contention and hatred prevail, all things turn out unhappily. This example also refutes the Stoics, who were without affection [ἀστόργως]. Affections are not evil in themselves; let moderation at least be added.

units.la: II. Deducunt ad nauim honoris gratia, etiam ex charitate. Not. ¶ 1. Honore dignos esse, quicunque in suo officio sunt diligentes, Roman. 13. Impij, qui omnes contemnunt.
units.tr: II. They escort him to the ship out of respect, and also out of charity. Note. 1. Those who are diligent in their office are worthy of honour, Rom. 13. Impious men, who despise everyone, are not.

units.la: ¶ 2. Deum honore eos cumulare, qui ipsum honorant, 1 Sam. 2. Exempla sunt, quæ docent tales malcuolis quoque esse terrori. Obseruent ministri, magistratus, patres familiâs. Qui suam functionem in contemptum adducunt, contemni merentur. Oremus.
units.tr: 2. God heaps honour upon those who honour him, 1 Sam. 2. There are examples which teach that such men are also a terror to the ill-disposed. Ministers, magistrates and heads of households should observe this. Those who bring their function into contempt deserve to be despised. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXI.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXVI.

units.la: VT autem proueētī sumus aliquando ab eis recto cursu venimus Coum: & sequenti die Rhodum, & illinc Patara.
units.tr: When we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

units.la: 2 Et inuenta naui,quæ traÿcie-bat in Phœnicem, ea conscensa, proue-cti fumus.
units.tr: And finding a ship that was crossing over to Phoenicia, we went on board and set sail.

units.la: 3 Quum autem cœpisset nobis ap-parere Cyprus, ea adsinistram relicta, nauigauimus in Syriam, & deuecti su-mus Tyrum : illic enim nauis erat suum onus expositura.
units.tr: When Cyprus came into view, we left it on our left and sailed to Syria, and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload its cargo.

units.la: 4 Permansimus autem ibidem di-es septem,inuentis discipulis, qui Paulo dicebant perspiritu, ne ascenderet Hie-rusalem.
units.tr: We stayed there seven days, having found disciples, who told Paul through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.

units.la: 5 Sed peractis illis diebus,abimus omnibus deducentibus nos cum vxori-bus & liberis, donec vrbe exiuissemus, & positis genibus in littore, precati su-mus.
units.tr: But when those days were over, we departed, and all of them escorted us, with their wives and children, until we were out of the city. Kneeling on the shore, we prayed.

units.la: 6 Et alij alios complexi,confcen-dimus nauim, illi aut.m reuersi sunt ad suos.
units.tr: Embracing one another, we went on board the ship, and they returned to their homes.

units.la: 7 Nos vero nauigatione perfecta, peruenimus Tyro Ptolemaida,& salu-tatis fratribus , mansimus diem vnum apud eos.
units.tr: And we completed the voyage, came from Tyre to Ptolemais, greeted the brothers, and stayed one day with them.

units.la: Piritus S. Apostolorm pere-grinationes laboris & pericu-li plenas , magna diligentia commemorat.Causa est,vt ex his Dei bonitatem agnosca-mus, mus, qui electos suos & fideles cultores nostrae salutis ergo tot laboribus & periculis diuexari voluit, & vt Euangelium, quod sanctorum sanguine propagatu est, maiori studio completamur, Matth. 13. Huc referri debet, quae hoc capite audiemus. Describit enim Lucas, vt Paulus molestissima navigatione tandem in Syriam, & inde Hierosolymam peruenerit, vt illic a fratribus amice exceptus, tandem vero a seditiosis quibusdam proditus & captus fit. In praesenti haec habentur.
units.tr: The Spirit of the holy Apostles records their journeys, full of toil and danger, with great care. The reason is that we may acknowledge from these the goodness of God, who willed that his chosen and faithful worshippers should be harassed by so many labours and dangers for the sake of our salvation, and that we should be engaged all the more eagerly in the gospel, which was spread by the blood of the saints, Matt. 13. To this should be referred what we hear in this chapter. For Luke describes how Paul, after a most troublesome voyage, at last came to Syria and thence to Jerusalem, where he was received kindly by the brothers, but at last was betrayed and seized by certain seditious men. At present the following points are contained:

units.la: I. Quo animo Paulus cum suis ab Asia discesserit. Anulfi ab eis. Eodem verbo vti-tur, quo de Christo loquens, Luc. 22. Exprimitur animi dolor, quo non immerito angebantur. Diu conuixerant. Senserant se ab illis amari. Nunquam redituri audiuerant pericula ex lupis oritura. Dolent ergo parentum instar, qui morituri liberos tenuiores adhuc relinquunt &c. Supe rat tamen dolorem, &c.
units.tr: I. With what spirit Paul departed from Asia with his people. "Tore himself away from them": the same word is used of Christ speaking, Luke 22. The sorrow of soul is expressed, by which they were not undeservedly distressed. They had lived together a long time. They had felt that they were loved by them. Having heard that they would never return, and that dangers would arise from wolves, they grieve like parents who leave behind younger children when they are about to die, etc. Yet he overcomes the grief, etc.

units.la: No. ¶ Dei vocationem omnibus asse-ctibus anteponi debere Manent quidem affectus etiam in pijs. Sed subiugandi sunt per fidem, 2. Corinth. 10. Vide Luc. 9. Mat. 8. Abraham. Genef. 12. 22. Transferamus ad omnes casus, etiam ad mortem. Auellimur hac inuiti, summo dolore. Sed
units.tr: No. ¶ God's calling ought to be preferred to all affections. Affections indeed remain even in the godly, but they must be subdued through faith, 2 Cor. 10. See Luke 9, Matt. 8, Abraham, Gen. 12, 22. Let us apply this to all circumstances, even to death. We are torn away from this unwillingly, with the greatest grief. But

units.la: Deo vocanti parendum. Vide 1. Sam. 12. Ioh. 12. 14. 17.
units.tr: One must obey God when he calls. See 1 Sam. 12, John 12:14, 17.

units.la: II. Nauigatio describitur longa, & haud dubie periculi plena. Et tot locis autem praeternauigatis, festinandi studium colligitur, Act. 20. Notq. Constantiam & fidem Pauli in committo sibi munere, vt & reliquorum Apostolorum. Poterant in mundo quieti & praeclari viuere. Sciebant quid futurum, si Christo nomen darent, Ioh. 15. 16. Matth. 19. 16. 2 Timoth. 3. Hoc ta men vitae genus eligunt. Vide Paulum, Phil. 4. Respexit ad coronam, 2 Tim. 2. 4.
units.tr: II. The voyage is described as long, and undoubtedly full of danger. From the many places passed by, the eagerness to hasten is gathered, Acts 20. Note also the constancy and faith of Paul in the office committed to him, as also of the other Apostles. They could have lived quiet and distinguished lives in the world. They knew what would follow if they gave their name to Christ, John 15, 16, Matt. 19:16, 2 Tim. 3. Yet they chose this kind of life. See Paul, Phil. 4. He looked to the crown, 2 Tim. 2:4.

units.la: Imitemur nos omnes, ne laboribus fran gamur, aut illecebris cedamus. Infelix coe citas, mundi conditione foelicitatem aeflimare. Quid in hoc stabile? Ecclesia 1 2. &c. Quid quod animum satiet? Solus Deus est Schaddai, Gen. 17. &c. Ioh. 4.
units.tr: Let us all imitate them, so as not to be broken by labours or to yield to allurements. Unhappy blindness, to judge happiness by the condition of the world! What is stable in this? Ecclesiastes 1, 2, etc. What satisfies the soul? God alone is Shaddai, Gen. 17, etc. John 4.

units.la: III. Tyrum appellunt, vbi haec euene-runt. 1. Repetiunt ibi discipulos Christianos: & tales, quidem, qui fidei charitatis officijs hucusq; omnes superauerunt. Mirum hoc, si Tyri conditionem inspicias, Isa. 73. Ezech. 27. 28. Matth. 11. Attamen illic Ecclesiam constituit Deus, sic promiserat, Isa 23. Psal. 45.
units.tr: III. They land at Tyre, where these things happened. 1. There they find Christian disciples, and such as have hitherto surpassed all others in the offices of faith and charity. This is wonderful if you look at the condition of Tyre, Isa. 73, Ezek. 27, 28, Matt. 11. Yet God established a Church there, as he had promised, Isa. 23, Ps. 45.

units.la: Notq. Dei bonitatem & veritatem ergo conuersos peccatores, Ezech. 18. Exempla empla huius generis multa extant. Vide I.Tim. 1. Non ergo vel de nobis vel de aliis facile desperemus.
units.tr: Note God's goodness and truth in converting sinners, Ezek. 18. Many examples of this kind exist. See 1 Tim. 1. Therefore let us not easily despair either of ourselves or of others.

units.la: II. Discipuli ex spiritu monent Paulum, ne Hierosolymam ascendat. Synechdoche est. Ex spiritu enim praedicunt vincula. Consilium autem de suo addunt, non ex spiritu, qui Paulo volebat ascendere, neque sibi poterit esse contrarius, Act.21.
units.tr: II. The disciples warn Paul through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem. This is a synecdoche, for through the Spirit they foretell chains. But they add counsel of their own, not from the Spirit, who wished Paul to go up, nor can the Spirit be contrary to himself, Acts 21.

units.la: NOT. Tentationem Pauli multiplicem. Admonet illum passim Deus de vinculis, nunc prophetae dehortantur. Fit hoc, non ut abstterreat, sed partim ut praeteratur longa meditatione, partim ut illa strior effet eius constantia. Sequamur hanc, ne spiritu gloriantes audiamus contra Deum. I Reg.13. Iudica de spirituum appa-rationibus.
units.tr: NOTE. Paul's temptation was manifold. God warns him everywhere about chains; now the prophets dissuade him. This happens not so as to terrify him, but partly so that it might be overcome by long meditation, and partly so that his constancy might be the stronger. Let us follow this, lest, boasting in the Spirit, we hear [something] against God. 1 Kings 13. Judge the appearances of spirits.

units.la: III. Deducunt illum cum uxoribus et liberis extra urbem. Argumentum magni amoris, et patet quam facile sibi ipsi consere potuisset Paulus, nisi Dei gloriam oculos habuisset. Interim praestat Christus promissionem Mar.10.
units.tr: III. They escort him outside the city with his wives and children. This is a sign of great love, and it is plain how easily Paul could have been turned aside by them, had he not kept the glory of God before his eyes. Meanwhile Christ fulfils his promise, Mark 10.

units.la: NOT. Christianos omnia sua ad Dei cultum destinare debere, curare item ut omnis ipsorum familia pia erga pios officia fit. In viduis hoc commendatur. I Timoth.5. Vide quam peccent, qui liberos?
units.tr: NOTE. Christians ought to direct all their possessions to the worship of God, and also take care that their whole household be pious in its pious duties. This is commended in widows, 1 Tim. 5. See how greatly they sin who, [as regards] their children,

units.la: ita instituuent, vt vexentur ab his peregri-ni, &c. 2 Reg. 2.
units.tr: bring them up so that strangers are harassed by them, etc. 2 Kings 2.

units.la: IV. Orant in littore, & quidem positis genibus. Comendantur preces, vt supra. Publicè hoc factum, & nimirum multis spectantibus.
units.tr: IV. They pray on the shore, and indeed kneeling. Prayers are commended, as above. This was done publicly, and surely with many looking on.

units.la: Interim NOT. ¶ Non debere nos pude dere nostræ fidei & religionis coràm hominibus. Mar. 8. Rom. 1. Miseri, qui quid-uis simulant & dissimulant in hominum gratiam.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE. ¶ We ought not to be ashamed of our faith and religion before men. Mark 8, Rom. 1. Wretched are those who pretend and dissemble anything to win men's favour.

units.la: IV. Ptolomaidem veniunt, vbi rursus diem vnum terunt cum fratribus. NOT. ¶ Intra tam breue tempus tot Ecclesias paf sim constitutas. Circa 2½ annum conuer-fionis Pauli hæc facta. Obserua veritatem Dei, & quàm fœliciter cedant quæ hoc auspice fiunt. Pfalm 2 19. Rom 10. Actor. 1. Ioh. 3. Quid ergo homines timemus hodie? Oremus.
units.tr: IV. They come to Ptolemais, where again they spend one day with the brothers. NOTE. ¶ Within so brief a time, so many Churches were established everywhere. These things were done about two and a half years after Paul's conversion. Observe the truth of God, and how happily those things turn out which are done under his auspices. Ps. 2, 19. Rom. 10. Acts 1. John 3. Why then do we fear men today? Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXVII.

units.la: 8 Postridie vero egressi Paulus et nos qui cum eo erant, venimus Cæsaream: & ingressi domum Philippi Euangelistæ (qui erat vnus ex illis septem) mansimus apud eum.
units.tr: The next day Paul and we who were with him set out and came to Caesarea, and entering the house of Philip the Evangelist (who was one of the seven), we stayed with him.

units.la: 9 Huic autem erant quatuor filiæ virgines prophetantes.
units.tr: He had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

units.la: 10 Et cum illic permansissemus de scenæ scendit ex Iudæa quidā Propheta nomine Agabus.
units.tr: While we were staying there for some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

units.la: 11 Qui cū venisset ad nos sumpsit zonam Pauli, & vinctus sibi pedibus ac manibus dixit, Hæc dicit spiritus sanctus, Virum cuius est hæc zona, ita vincient in Hierusalem Iudæi, tradentque in manus Gentium.
units.tr: He came to us, took Paul's girdle, bound his own feet and hands with it, and said, "Thus says the Holy Spirit: the man whose girdle this is, so will the Jews bind in Jerusalem, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles."

units.la: 12 Vt verò ista audiinimus, rogabamus & nos, & qui in eo loco erant, ne ascenderet in Hierusalem.
units.tr: When we heard this, both we and the others who were in that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

units.la: 13 Tunc respondit Paulus, Quid facitis flentes & comminuentes cor meum? Nam ego non solum vincîri, sed et mori paratus sum in Hierusalem pro nomine Domini Iesu.
units.tr: Then Paul answered, "What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."

units.la: 14 Quum igitur non assentiretur acquiescimus, dicentes: Fiat Domini voluntas.
units.tr: Since he would not be persuaded, we desisted, saying, "The will of the Lord be done."

units.la: QVemadmodum Deus Euangelium per Pauli vincula illustrare voluit (Phil.1) Ita per Lucam diligenter descripsit, ut ad vincula Paulus festinârit, nobis nimirum fidelis obedientiæ & constantiæ exemplum relinquens. Exposuit enim hucusque, ut per terras & maria Hierosolymam contenderit, vbi se capien-dū esse nouerat, vtq; nullis vel prædictionibus vel etiam dehortationib. fratrum sa abducipassus sit, Luc.9. In praesenti duo sequuntur.
units.tr: Just as God willed to illustrate the Gospel through Paul's chains (Phil. 1), so Luke has described with care how Paul hastened to his chains, leaving us, no doubt, an example of faithful obedience and steadfastness. For he has related so far how Paul pressed on through lands and seas toward Jerusalem, where he knew he would be seized, and how he suffered himself not to be turned aside either by predictions or even by the dissuasions of the brethren (Luke 9). Two things follow in the present passage.

units.la: 1. Vt Caesaream venerit, & quid ibi gestum. Not T. ¶1. Philippi hospitis descriptionem. Fuit is, de quo Act.6. Eiectus venit Samariam. Act.8. Videtur Ecclesiae Caesarensis antistes fuisse. Paulus enim hospitem habet quem olim eicerat urbe, Actor.8. Est autem typus boni & veri Episcopi, qualis describitur, 1.Ti.11.3. Tit.A Euangelista. Ergo ευαγγελιστής. Fuerunt medij inter Apostolos & pastores, Eph.4. Nomine autem hoc officicij admoneban tur, quod erat, Euangelium praedicare. Id praecipuum est in pastore. Nec liberum est quiduis tradere. Matth 28. Mar,16. Vbi simul continetur, vt ad docendum aptus sit, 1. Tim.3. &c.
units.tr: 1. That he came to Caesarea, and what was done there. Note: ¶1. The description of Philip the host. This is the man of whom Acts 6 speaks, who went down to Samaria, Acts 8. He seems to have been the bishop of the church at Caesarea, for Paul has as his host a man whom he had once expelled from the city (Acts 8). He is moreover a type of the good and true bishop, such as is described in 1 Tim. 3, Tit. 1. An evangelist: Greek euangelistes. These stood between the Apostles and the pastors (Eph. 4). The name of the office reminds them what their task is, namely to preach the Gospel. This is especially the chief duty of a pastor, nor is it lawful for him to deliver whatever he likes (Matt. 28; Mark 16), where it is also implied that he be apt to teach (1 Tim. 3), etc.

units.la: B. Domum habuit propriam, & hospitalis fuit. Excipit enim Paulum cum numeroso comitatu. Confutantur, qui minis tros omnes erronum instar esse volunt. Non distinguunt illi inter Apostolos & pastores, quos esse oportet. Tit.1.
units.tr: B. He had a house of his own and was hospitable, for he received Paul with a large retinue. Those are refuted who want all ministers to be like wandering vagabonds. Such men do not distinguish between Apostles and pastors, which they ought to be (Tit. 1).

units.la: C. Filias habuit. Ergo & vxorem, nisi scortatorem potius (quod vel cogitatu nefas est.) dicere velimus. Ita Petrus, Mat. 8. Et Apostoli vxores circumduxerunt se cum, 1.Cor.9. Diabolicum est, ministris ma-
units.tr: C. He had daughters. Therefore he also had a wife, unless we would rather say he was a fornicator, which even to think of is wicked. So Peter (Matt. 8), and the Apostles led about wives with them (1 Cor. 9). It is diabolical to forbid marriage to ministers.

units.la: Philippus Euangelista typus pastoris.
units.tr: Philip the Evangelist is a type of the pastor.

units.la: Hospitalitas.
units.tr: Hospitality.

units.la: Vxorati. matrimonio interdicere, 1. Tit. 4. Heb. 13.
units.tr: Married men: marriage is not to be forbidden (1 Tim. 4; Heb. 13).

units.la: D. Quales filiæ? Prophetantes. Sumitur interdum pro studio verbi Dei, vt 1. Cor. 11. 14. Sed quia singulare quid vulj narrare Lucas, Spiritu sancto donatæ fuerunt, cuius instinctu vaticinati sunt. Fuit enim hoc singulare donum primitiuæ Ecclesiæ, Ioel 2 Act. 2. Vsus, vt magis excitarentur homines, & Messiam missum esse constaret. Et mulieribus datum (Ioel. 2.) ne de salute dubitarent, 1. Tim. 2. Interim obseruent ministri, quales liberos habere debeant, 1. Tim. 3. Diuersa exempla extant 1. Sam. 2 3. 8.
units.tr: D. What kind of daughters? Prophesying. The word is sometimes taken for the study of God's Word, as in 1 Cor. 11:14. But since Luke wishes to narrate something singular, they were endowed with the Holy Spirit, at whose impulse they prophesied. For this was a singular gift of the primitive Church (Joel 2; Acts 2). Its purpose was that men might be more stirred up, and that it might be established that the Messiah had been sent. It was also given to women (Joel 2) so that they might not doubt about salvation (1 Tim. 2). Meanwhile let ministers note what sort of children they ought to have (1 Tim. 3). Diverse examples exist: 1 Sam. 2, 3, 8.

units.la: 2. Agabus aduenit, per quem rursus de vinculis Paulus admonetur. Chriam fi mul adhibet, more veterum Prophetarum vt magis excitet animos. Sic Ier. 13. 18. 24. 27. 28. 32. &c. Ita vero Paulû præparari De us voluit, nos quoque docere, ne semper pericula iustam fugæ causam putemus.
units.tr: 2. Agabus arrives, through whom Paul is again warned about his chains. He also adds a pointed short saying (chria) in the manner of the old prophets, so as to stir their minds more: so Jer. 13, 18, 24, 27, 28, 32, etc. Thus God willed that Paul be prepared, and also that we be taught not to think that dangers are always a just cause for flight.

units.la: 3. Quid in certo periculo vtrinque fa factum? A. Comites & amici flent, & multum rogant, ne ascendat. Habuerunt mul tas rationes etiam verbo Dei velatas. Videbatur Deum tentare, Matt. 4. Deut. 6. Videbatur longè aliud poscere Ecclesiarum salus. Sed est zelus nō secundum scientiam, qualis in Petro fuit, Mat. 16. Lau-
units.tr: 3. What was done on both sides in a certain danger? A. The companions and friends weep and beg earnestly that he not go up. They had many reasons, even if veiled in the Word of God. They seemed to be tempting God (Matt. 4; Deut. 6). The welfare of the churches seemed to demand something quite different. But this is zeal not according to knowledge, such as was in Peter (Matt. 16). Praise

units.la: Ddd dem tamen meratur pietas, & arguuntur, qui ministros temerè periculis obijciunt, vt mundi pacem redimant.
units.tr: Nevertheless piety deserves praise, and those are rebuked who rashly expose ministers to dangers in order to buy the peace of the world.

units.la: B Paulus acriter contradicit illis, & que ritur illos cor sibi affl gere. Fatetur fe non minus dolore tangi, nec ferreum esse. Ingenuè autem vocationem Dei corpore & vita sua potiorem se habere testatur. Imitentur exemplum hoc ministri, imo omnes Christiani. Qui non ita animum induxerunt, nihil proficient, 2.Tim.3. Luc.14. Matt.10.&c. Neque hoc graue est pijs, Roman.14.&c.
units.tr: B. Paul sharply contradicts them and rebukes them, so that they do not bind his heart to themselves. He confesses that he is touched by grief no less than they, and that he is not made of iron. Yet he frankly testifies that the calling of God is dearer to him than his body and life. Let ministers imitate this example, and indeed all Christians. Those who have not so resolved in their minds accomplish nothing (2 Tim. 3; Luke 14; Matt. 10), etc. Nor is this burdensome to the godly (Rom. 14), etc.

units.la: C. Cedunt tandem ipsi quoque diuinae voluntati, cui se totos committunt. Ita iubemur orare, Mat.6. Ita Christus, Luc.22. &c. Est haec sacra anchora, quae sola animos aestuantes sustinere potest. Ad hanc confugiamus, maximè cum Dei voluntas sit optima, priore ad Corinthios 10. Oremus.
units.tr: C. At last they too yield to the divine will, to which they entrust themselves wholly. So we are commanded to pray (Matt. 6), and so Christ (Luke 22), etc. This is the sacred anchor, which alone can steady restless minds. Let us flee to it, especially since the will of God is best (1 Cor. 10). Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXIIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXVIII.

units.la: 15 Porro post dies istos collectis sar cinis ascendimus in Hierusalem.
units.tr: 15 After these days we packed up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.

units.la: 16 Venerunt autem simul etiam quidam ex discipulis Caesareae nobiscum, adducentes secum apud quem hospitaremur, Mnasone quendam Cyprium antiantiquum discipulum.
units.tr: 16 Some of the disciples from Caesarea also came with us, bringing with them Mnason, a Cypriot, an old disciple, with whom we were to stay.

units.la: 17 Quum igitur peruenissemus Hierosolymam, libenter exceperunt nos fratres.
units.tr: 17 When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.

units.la: 18 Sequenti autem die introijt Paulus nobiscum ad Iacobum, & omnes Presbyteri adfuerunt.
units.tr: 18 On the following day Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders were present.

units.la: 19 Quos complexus expositi sigil latim quæ Deus fecisset inter Gentes per ipsius ministerium.
units.tr: 19 Greeting them, he related in detail what God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

units.la: 20 At illi his auditis glorificarunt Dominum.
units.tr: 20 When they heard this, they glorified the Lord.

units.la: INter multas Pauli actiones, quibus fidei suæ constantiam & se electum Dei organum esse probauit, non postremum est, quod tanto studio Ierosolymam contendit, quamuis sciret sibi illic vincula parata esse, deque imminenti periculo passim a fratribus admoneretur. Voluit hoc prolixè describi Spiritus S. vt non modò eius fides nobis elucear, verumetiam exemplū hoc nostrę seruiat institutioni. 1. Facit ad doctrinæ Apostolicę commendationem. Quomodo enim falsi nobis suspecti esse possunt, qui suam fidē tot argumentis probārunt? 2. Excitat constantiam, ne doctrinam tot sanctorum periculis & laboribus propagatam nobis eripi patiamur.
units.tr: AMONG the many actions of Paul by which he proved the constancy of his faith and that he was a chosen instrument of God, no small one is that he hastened to Jerusalem with such zeal, although he knew that chains were prepared for him there, and although he was warned on every side by the brothers of the danger that threatened. The Holy Spirit wished this to be described at length, so that not only his faith might shine forth for us, but that this example might also serve our instruction. (1) It serves to commend the apostolic teaching: for how could those be suspected of falsehood who have confirmed their teaching by so many proofs? (2) It stirs up constancy, so that we do not allow the doctrine spread abroad by the labours and perils of so many saints to be snatched from us.

units.la: 3.Docet de periculis iudicare,& quid fieri in his debeat. Sunt qui his visis,putant fe iustas deficiendi causas habere. Sed aliud docet Pauli exemplum,Prima ergo vocationis nostræ ratio habeatur. Hancfequamur,& quia futura nos latent, euentum omnem Deo permittamus. 1.Cor.10. Sequitur Pauli in vrbem aduentus.
units.tr: 3. It teaches us how to judge dangers and what ought to be done in them. There are those who, when they see such dangers, think they have just reasons for giving up. But the example of Paul teaches otherwise: the first reason of our calling is to be taken into account. Let us follow this, and since the future is hidden from us, let us leave every outcome to God. 1 Cor. 10. Next comes Paul's arrival in the city.

units.la: 1.Qui ipsum deduxerint? Hi qui hafte-nus ei comites fuerunt,Act. 10. Accedunt his noui amici ex Cæsarea.Not.1. Non deesse socios laborum & periculorum ijs, qui pro Christo aliquid audent. Sic lofe-pho additur Nicodemus,Ioh.19. Obseruandum hoc illis, qui fe solos esse querun tur,& ipsi faciunt quod in alijs accusant. Fac tu officium prior. Singuli item memi nerint dicti Mardochaici Heft 4.
units.tr: 1. Who escorted him? Those who had been his companions up to this point, Acts 10. To these are added new friends from Caesarea. Note 1. Those who dare something for Christ are not without companions in their labours and dangers. So Nicodemus is added to Joseph, John 19. Those who complain that they are alone should observe this, for they themselves do what they accuse others of. Do your duty first. Likewise, let each one remember the words of Mordecai, Esther 4.

units.la: §2.Exemplum fidei & constantiæ magnæ.Sciebant quid euenturum. Et magnę erant causæ,vt & sibi timerent. Non defe-runt tamen , quem sciebant Christi causam agere,sed in promissionem respiciunt Matt.19.
units.tr: §2. An example of great faith and constancy. They knew what would happen, and the reasons for fearing for themselves were great. Yet they did not desert the one whom they knew to be pleading Christ's cause, but looked to the promise, Matt. 19.

units.la: Obseruandum hoc in alijs etiam officijs charitatis , vt in peste. Nescis quid futurum de te. Scis autem quid proximo debeas,&c.Pfal.40.Matt.25. Qui hoc negligunt,ollæ amici sunt, & simul testantur se Deum adhuc ignorare. Matth. 6 10. Lu cæ 12.
units.tr: This should be observed also in the other duties of charity, as in a plague: You do not know what will become of you, but you know what you owe your neighbour, etc. Ps. 40; Matt. 25. Those who neglect this are friends of the pot, and at the same time testify that they still do not know God. Matt. 6:10; Luke 12.

units.la: II. Ad quem diuerterint? Ad Mnasonem quendam Cyprium, discipulum veterem, quem secum adduxerunt. Curarunt igi-tur vt tuto & commodè ageret.
units.tr: II. With whom did they lodge? With Mnason, a Cypriot, an old disciple, whom they had brought with them. They therefore took care that he should act safely and conveniently.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Prudentiam adhuc locu habere, etsi nos à Dei prouidentia totos pen dere scimus, & quiduis ferre aut facere in statuimus. Matt. 10. Qui omnia temerè faciunt, Deum tentant. Matt 4.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ 1. Prudence still has its place, although we know that we depend entirely on God's providence, and we resolve to bear or do whatever. Matt. 10. Those who do everything rashly tempt God. Matt. 4.

units.la: ¶ 2. Exemplum Mnasonis. Vetus discipulus. Ergo in fide perseuerauit, & quidé Hierosolymis, vbi fames, persecutio. Nunc Paulum cum tam multis excipit, & ita fidem testatur charitatis operib. Gal. 5. Est que hæc eò luculentior, quòd sumtuosum & periculosum, ipse verò peregrinus erat. Imitentur omnes. Arguuntur, qui in lauta fortuna quosuis negligunt. Item qui pe grinos oderunt, cum etiam ipsi sint peregrini.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The example of Mnason, an old disciple. He therefore persevered in the faith, and indeed at Jerusalem, where there was famine and persecution. Now he receives Paul with so many others, and so bears witness to his faith by the works of charity. Gal. 5. This is all the more striking because it was costly and dangerous, and he himself was a stranger. Let all imitate him. Those are rebuked who neglect guests when their fortune is lavish. Likewise those who hate foreigners, though they themselves are foreigners.

units.la: III. Quomodo acceptus à fratribus? Libenter & humaniter. Atqui rumores fini. stri iam de illo spa si erant. Sed nolut dam nare inauditum. Obseruandum hoc maximè quoad ministros & in quouis officio constitutos, quia multorum odijsfubiacent. Vide 1. Tim. 5. Et sunt selecta Dia-
units.tr: III. How was he received by the brothers? Gladly and kindly. And yet rumours about him had already reached them, but they were unwilling to judge without a hearing. This should be observed especially with regard to ministers and those placed in any office, since they are exposed to the hatred of many. See 1 Tim. 5. And they are chosen instruments of the Devil, who trouble whole churches with slanders.

units.la: boli organa, calumnijs totas Ecclesias tur bant. Idem priuatim singuli curent. Impri mis Magistratus, quorum est partem v* tramque audire. Alexander Magnus.
units.tr: Individuals should take care of this in private too. Above all the magistrates, whose duty it is to hear both sides. Alexander the Great.

units.la: IV. Quid fecerit Paulus? Accedit Iaco- bum & eius loci seniores, & priusquam a- liquid tentet, ministerij fui & rerum abs fe gestarum rationem reddit.
units.tr: IV. What did Paul do? He went to James and the elders of that place, and before he attempted anything, he gave an account of his ministry and of the things he had done.

units.la: Vbi NOT. ¶ 1. Ordinem in Ecclesia fer uari debere, ne quid cuiuis liceat. Erat e- lectum organum, & plus alijs laborauit,i. Corinth.15 Nihil tamen agit arrogantius in peregrina Ecclesia. Sufficit hoc exemplum contra Romanos Pontifices,qui sibi in Ecclesias omnes ius vendicant,con tra Christi regulam, Luc.22. Item Anabaptistae, qui Ecclesias quidem nullas plan- tant, sed aliorum labore plantatas turbant, atq; ministris odio & inuidiam conciliant.
units.tr: Here, note 1. Order ought to be preserved in the Church, so that no one is permitted to do whatever he likes. He was a chosen instrument, and laboured more than the others, 1 Cor. 15. Yet he undertakes nothing arrogantly in a church that is not his own. This example is enough against the Roman Pontiffs, who claim for themselves the right over all churches, against the rule of Christ, Luke 22. Likewise the Anabaptists, who indeed plant no churches, but disturb those planted by the labour of others, and win hatred and envy for the ministers.

units.la: ¶ 2. Modestia Pauli, qui ita res suas narrat, vt omnium authorem faciat Deum, fi- bi foli minifteriu referuet. Obseruat quod scripsit 1. Cor. 3. Sic 1. Cor. 15. Imitemur in omni vocatione. In œconomia, Pfal. 127. In studijs, &c. In Repub. Pfal. 127. Humiliter sentiamus de nobis ipsis, ne cum Sanc- rib & Nabuchodonofore peccemus, Ifa. 10. Dan. 4. Intenti vero fimus in ardentes preces. &c.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The modesty of Paul, who so relates his affairs that he makes God the author of all, and reserves the ministry to himself alone. Observe what he wrote, 1 Cor. 3. So 1 Cor. 15. Let us imitate him in every calling: in household management, Ps. 127; in studies, etc.; in the commonwealth, Ps. 127. Let us think humbly of ourselves, lest we sin with Sennacherib and Nebuchadnezzar, Isa. 10; Dan. 4. Let us be intent indeed on fervent prayers, etc.

units.la: ¶ 3. Seniores glorificant Deum. Charitatis hoc est, quod non inuident alienis successibus vt fere ambitiosi solent. Interim non adulatorie illum celebrant, sed ipsi quoque glorificant Deum.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The elders glorify God. It is a mark of charity that they do not envy the successes of others, as ambitious men usually do. Meanwhile they do not praise him flatteringly, but glorify God themselves as well.

units.la: Docent nos iudicare de sanctorum laboribus & gestis. Homines fuerunt, Act. 14. Si quid ergo fecerut plus puam huma num,hoc Dei opus est, qui ex gratia illorum ministerio vti voluit. Gratulemur illis hanc felicitatem, obedientiam imitemur, laudem omnem tribuamus Deo. Ita & illos honorabimus, & Deo suus honor integer manebit. Denique quaeramus vnius Dei gloriam, & huic soli seruiamus. Oremus.
units.tr: They teach us to judge the labours and deeds of the saints. They were men, Acts 14. If therefore they did anything beyond ordinary human power, this is the work of God, who chose to use their ministry out of his grace. Let us rejoice with them in this good fortune, imitate their obedience, and give all praise to God. So we shall also honour them, and God's honour will remain whole. Finally, let us seek the glory of the one God alone, and serve him alone. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXIX.

units.la: 20 Et seniores dixerunt ei, Conspicua frater, quot sint millia Iudæorum, qui crediderunt: sunt omnes accensi zelo legis.
units.tr: 20 And the elders said to him, "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are who have believed; they are all zealous for the law."

units.la: 21 Audierunt autem de te ex alio rumfermone, te defectionem a Mose docere omnes qui inter gentes sunt Iudæos, & dicere, eos non debere circumcidere filios, neque secundum ritus ambulare.
units.tr: 21 "But they have heard about you, from a report of others, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to fall away from Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their sons, nor walk according to the customs."

units.la: 22 Quid est ergo? Omnino oportet conuenire multitudinem: audient enim te venisse.
units.tr: 22 "What then is to be done? The multitude must certainly come together, for they will hear that you have come."

units.la: 23 Hoc igitur fac quod tibi dicimus. Sunt nobis viri quatuor voto obnoxij.
units.tr: 23 "Therefore do this that we tell you. We have four men who are bound by a vow."

units.la: 24 His assumptis sanctificator cum eis, & adde ad eorum sumptus, vt raadant capita, & norint omnes nihil esse eorum, quae de te fama acceperunt, sed te quoque ita incedere, vt Legem obseruues.
units.tr: 24 "Take these men with you, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses, so that they may shave their heads; and everyone will know that there is nothing in the things they have heard about you, but that you yourself also walk in observance of the Law."

units.la: 25 De iis autem qui crediderunt Gentibus, nos scripsimus, & decreuimus, ne quid huiusmodi obseruent, nisi vt caueant ab iis, quae sunt immolata simulachris, & a sanguine & suffocatis, & fortatione.
units.tr: 25 "But as for those Gentiles who have believed, we have written and decided that they should observe nothing of that kind, except that they abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols, from blood, from what is strangled, and from fornication."

units.la: QVemadmodum Lucas hucusque diligenter exposuit, quanto studio Paulus contenderit Ierosolymam ire festinabat, vt in eo facto discamus, quàm nos ferventes esse deceat in Dei negotijs: Itanò minori diligentia narrat, quid cum eo actu fuerit quando eò venit: eò quod haec etiam pars multa habet quae ad nostram institutionem faciunt. Inter quod primum est quod nuper audiuimus, beneficium exceptum fuisse, licet sinistri rumores essent, spargi: illud priusquam aliquid tentaret
units.tr: Just as Luke has carefully described how eagerly Paul strove and hastened to go to Jerusalem, so that from that deed we may learn how fervent we ought to be in the affairs of God, so he now relates with less care what happened with him when he came there, because this part also contains much that pertains to our instruction. Among these things the first is that we have just heard that he was well received, although unfavourable rumours were spreading; and that before he attempted anything, he gave an account of his ministry, while the elders glorified God.

units.la: rct set, ministerij fui rationem reddidisse: seniores vero Deum glorificaffe.Didicimus non temere damnandos esse fratres ex ru moribus,maxime qui alijs præsunt. Item neminem debere sibi imperium vendicare in Ecclesia. Adhæc laudem omnem ad vnum Deum debere referri.
units.tr: We have learned that brothers are not to be condemned rashly on the basis of rumours, especially those who preside over others. Likewise, that no one should claim authority for himself in the Church. Moreover, that all praise is to be referred to the one God alone.

units.la: Sequitur nunc actio memorabilis, vt Seniores Paulo authores fuerint facti, quod impijs tumultuandi occasione præbuit, & ipsum adduxit in extremum periculum.
units.tr: Now follows a memorable action: the elders became the authors of Paul's course, which gave the impious an occasion to riot and brought him into extreme danger.

units.la: Discemus, sanctos quoque interdum decipi suis rationibus, & proinde non omnia eorum in exemplum trahi debere, sed constanter in ijs perseuerandum esse, quæ Dei verbo traduntur, Pfalm. 119.2 Ti motheo. 3. Vt autem rem omnem recte intelligamus, ante omnia inspici debent.
units.tr: Let us learn that even holy men are sometimes deceived by their own reasonings, and that therefore not all of their actions are to be taken as examples; rather, we must persevere steadfastly in those things which are delivered in the word of God (Ps. 119; 2 Tim. 3). But that we may understand the whole matter correctly, the following must first be considered.

units.la: Occasio,quam Pauli doctrina præbuit: Docebat is (vt reliqui Apostoli) hominem sola fide in Christum iustificari, Act. 15. At quia ei cum illis lis erat, qui gentes ad legis obseruationem cogere nitebantur, de eius visu diligentius differebat: Quod nimirum peccatum arguat, damnet, & instar pædagogi ad Christum deducat, Ro. 7. Gal. 4. Imo Christum euacuari dicebat
units.tr: The occasion which Paul's teaching provided: he taught (as did the other apostles) that a man is justified by faith in Christ alone (Acts 15). But because he was in dispute with those who strove to compel the Gentiles to observe the law, he discussed its purpose more carefully: namely, that it convicts sin, condemns it, and, like a tutor, leads us to Christ (Rom. 7; Gal. 4). Indeed, he said that Christ is made void by those who want to be justified by the works of the law (Gal. 5).

units.la: ab ijs, qui per legis opera iustificari vo- lunt, Gal.5. Hinc occasionem sumebant ca- lumniatores, quòd legem simpliciter dam- naret, & omniu odia aduersus ipsum con- citabant.
units.tr: From this the slanderers took their occasion, because he seemed simply to condemn the law, and they stirred up hatred against him on all sides.

units.la: Vbi No T.¶ Non nouum esse, fi hodie similibus calumnijs traducantur Euange- lij ministri. Accidit hoc ipsi Christo, Matt. 15.11. Paulo & posteris illius. Sunt vanifi mi, qui hic offenduntur, & non potius sta- tum controuersiæ inspiciunt. Interim cau- ti fimus, & eò studeamus diligentius mo- rum innocentiam tueri.
units.tr: Note. It is no new thing if the ministers of the Gospel are today traduced by similar slanders. This happened to Christ himself (Matt. 15:11), and to Paul and his successors. Those who are offended here are vain men, who do not rather look at the state of the controversy. Meanwhile, let us be cautious, and let us study more diligently to guard the innocence of our conduct.

units.la: Quoad veró seniores, illi bono zelo consulunt Paulo, & orationis partes sunt hæc.
units.tr: As for the elders, they act with good zeal for Paul, and the parts of their speech are these.

units.la: I. Indicant ipsum male audire, quasi le- gem simpliciter damnet, & defectionem à Mose doceat. Est hoc probandum quòd nihil dissimulant, &c. NOTA.¶ Liberè & ingenuè agendum esse cum fratribus, vt fi quid peccarunt, illud emendent, aut sal- fa crimina possint excusare. Peccant gra- uiter, qui absentes traducunt: præfentibus adulantur. Qui item fratres traduci patia- ntur, neque monent, à quibus sibi ca- ueant.
units.tr: I. They point out that he is ill spoken of, as though he simply condemned the law and taught a falling away from Moses. This must be shown to be false, since they conceal nothing, etc. Note: one must deal freely and openly with brothers, so that if they have sinned, they may amend it, or may be able to excuse false charges. Those who slander the absent sin gravely; those who flatter the present do likewise. Those too who allow brothers to be slandered, and do not warn them against those from whom they should guard themselves, also sin.

units.la: II. Consulunt vt fe purget, & rationes adducunt. 1. Sunt multa millia, qui hanc de te suspicionem conceperunt : & quia credunt,non debent negligi. Plurimum hoc potuit apud Paulum , qui gentis suæ erat studiosissimus. Errant, qui non curant aliorum defe iudicia. 2. Necesse est hoc fieri, quia res non potest dissimulari. Oportet enim conuenire multitudine:& quia in suspicione inueterata nihil profici tur verbis,publico aliquo facto opus erit.
units.tr: II. They advise that he purify himself, and they give reasons. 1. There are many thousands who have conceived this suspicion about you, and because they believe it, it must not be neglected. This weighed very much with Paul, who was most zealous for his own nation. They err who do not care about the judgments of others. 2. This must be done, because the matter cannot be concealed. For the multitude must come together, and since nothing is gained by words against a long-standing suspicion, some public deed will be necessary.

units.la: Nota. ¶ Modestiam seniorum in ve-teri Eeclefia , qui in rebus grauibus nihil ex priuato arbitrio statuerunt. Sic Act.15. Vide quid de Pontificibus Romanenfi-bus iudices,&c.
units.tr: Note. The modesty of the elders in the ancient Church, who in weighty matters decided nothing by private judgment. So in Acts 15. See what you judge concerning the Roman pontiffs, etc.

units.la: III. Exponunt consilium. Sunt nobis quatuor viri, qui votum fecerunt, nimi-rum Nazaræi: de quo Act.18 His te con-iunge,& communibus impensis purifica-tor cum ipsis. Ita videbunt omnes, te non docere defectionem à lege, neq; eam sim pliciter damnare,&c.
units.tr: III. They explain the plan. We have four men who have made a vow, namely Nazirites, concerning which see Acts 18. Join yourself to these, and purify yourself with them at common expense. Thus all will see that you do not teach a falling away from the law, nor simply condemn it, etc.

units.la: Videtur hoc tolerabile,& idem cum eo quod in Cenchris fecerat: sed longè alia est hic ratio. 1.Illic infirmis hoc dederat, & nihil quàm rasit caput: hîc sacrificium accedit, quod excusari non potest: quia abolita erant,Ioh.19.Heb.8.9.10. 2.Illic ni hil factum in confirmationem legalium rituum : sed hîc vnum illud agitur, vt
units.tr: This seems tolerable, and it is the same as what he did at Cenchreae; but here the reasoning is quite different. 1. There he had done this for the weak, and shaved his head only; here a sacrifice is added, which cannot be excused, because those things had been abolished (John 19; Heb. 8, 9, 10). 2. There nothing was done to confirm the legal rites; but here the one thing is being done, namely, to prove by his own example the observance of these things.

units.la: suo exemplo probet horum obseruato-res. 3. Non debebat tam diu ferri fuperfti-tioforum contumacia. Exitus docet, con-filium fuisse non bonum, & Deus nō mul tò post templum euertit, cùm illi nollent finem facere.
units.tr: 3. The stubbornness of these superstitious people ought not to have been indulged for so long. The outcome shows that the counsel was not good, and God overthrew the temple not long afterwards, since they were unwilling to make an end.

units.la: Nota. ¶ 1. Quàm noxium fit ea ser-uare, quæ abolita esse debebant, & rationi bus humanis vti in causa Dei. Sic olim pec catum quoad excelsa. Hodie multa sic re-tinentur, & excusantur astutè hoc exem-plo, & ijs quæ dicuntur, 1 Cor 9. Atqui hæc locum habent in ἀδιάφοροις. Sed v-bi Christiana libertas, & fidei profesio pe riclitatur, fortiter agendum. ¶ 2. Obser-uandum idem in externis alijs, ne in alicu ius gratiam quid fiat verbo Dei contrari-um, & ne foueantur errores nimia indul-gentia. Dic de peste,
units.tr: Note. 1. How harmful it is to keep those things which ought to have been abolished, and to use human reasons in the cause of God. So formerly sin was tolerated regarding the high places. Today many things are retained and excused in this way, cunningly by this example, and by those things that are said in 1 Cor. 9. Yet these things have a place in matters indifferent (adiaphora). But where Christian liberty and the profession of faith are endangered, we must act boldly. 2. The same is to be observed in other external matters: nothing contrary to the word of God should be done out of favour to anyone, and errors should not be fostered by excessive indulgence. Speak of the plague.

units.la: IV. Præoccupant quod de gentibus obijci potarat: Quasi dicerent: Non est pe riculum de his, ne tuum factum illis præ-iudicet. Iam pridem enim has liberaui-mus, & tantum monuimus, ne libertate abu tantur, & vt charitatis rationem habeant. Regula perpetua.
units.tr: IV. They anticipate what might be objected concerning the Gentiles, as if they said: There is no danger concerning these, lest your action prejudice them. For we have already long since freed them, and have only admonished them that they not abuse their liberty and that they have regard for the rule of charity. A perpetual rule.

units.la: Nota. ¶ Peruicaciam Iudæorum, & quàm parum prærogatiuæ habeat mundi huius dignitas in religione, quando non alibi maior infirmitas fuit quam in Ierofo lymitana Ecclesia, ex qua lex Christi prodierat, Isa.2 Stulti, qui loco alligant spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: Note. The obstinacy of the Jews, and how little prerogative the dignity of this world has in religion, since nowhere was there greater weakness than in the Church of Jerusalem, from which the law of Christ had gone forth (Isa. 2). Foolish are those who bind the Holy Spirit to a place.

units.la: Discant singuli omissis suis rationibus, in solius Dei verbum respicere: & non errabunt. Oremus.
units.tr: Let each one, having set aside his own reasonings, look only to the word of the one God, and he will not go astray. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXX.
units.tr: HOMILY 170.

units.la: 26 Tum Paulus assumptis viris il lis, sequenti die cum eis sanctificatus, in gressus est in templum, denuntians expletionem dierum sanctificationis, vsque dum oblata fuit pro vnoquoque eorum oblatio.
units.tr: 26 Then Paul, taking those men, the next day purified himself with them and went into the temple, announcing the completion of the days of purification, until the offering was made for each one of them.

units.la: 27 Quum autem septem illi dies iam essent explendi, quidam Iudaei ex Asia, eum conspicati in templo, concitarunt totam turbam, et iniecerunt manus in eum.
units.tr: 27 When the seven days were almost completed, some Jews from Asia saw him in the temple, stirred up the whole crowd, and laid hands on him.

units.la: 28 Clamantes, Viri Israelitae, huc currite: hic est homo ille, qui aduersus populum et legem et locum hunc omnes ubique docet: atque adeo Graecos introduxit in templum, et polluit sanctum locum istum.
units.tr: 28 Crying out, "Men of Israel, come here! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against the people, the law and this place. Moreover, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place."

units.la: 29 Viderant enim antea Trophimum Ephesium in urbe cum eo, quem existimabant fuisse a Paulo introductum in templum.
units.tr: 29 For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they supposed Paul had brought into the temple.

units.la: 36 Commota est igitur vrbs tota, & factus est concursus populi, & prehensam Paulum trahebant è templo, statim clausæ sunt fores.
units.tr: 30 So the whole city was stirred, and a crowd of people gathered. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the doors were shut.

units.la: 31 Studentibus autem ipsis eum tri cidare, peruenit fama ad Tribunum cohortis, totam Hierusalem conturbatam esse:
units.tr: 31 While they were trying to kill him, word reached the tribune of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion.
