units.la: 10 Respondit autem Paulus, quum innuisset ei praeses vt loqueretur: Quia te à multis annis iuli geti praefuisse scio, meliore animo in rebus meis defensione vtar.
units.tr: Paul answered, when the governor had nodded to him to speak: "Since I know that you have for many years been judge over this nation, I shall make my defence with the better heart."

units.la: 11 Quum tu possis noscere non plures exactos esse dies quam duodecim, ex quo ascendi adoraturus in Hierusalem. &c. vsq; ad vers. 17.
units.tr: "Since you can ascertain that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem," etc., as far as verse 17.

units.la: AVdiuimus accusationis contra Paulum institutae capita: quae ex Tertulli ore diligentissime conscribi voluit Spiritus S. non modo vt Apostolicae historiae veritas nobis minus suspecta esset, verumetiam quo minus offendamur, si quando nobis hodie similia obiiciuntur. Sequitur, vt Paulus Felicis permissione omnia diluerit. Vbi priusquam verba videamus, quo nobis obseruanda veniunt.
units.tr: We have heard the heads of the accusation brought against Paul, which the Holy Spirit wished to have written down most carefully from the mouth of Tertullus, not only so that the truth of the apostolic history might be less open to suspicion, but also so that we may be less offended if similar charges are brought against us today. Next, Paul clears himself entirely by the permission of Felix. Before we look at his words, let us consider what we must observe here.

units.la: A. In iudicijs vtramq; partem audiri debere. Quia nisi id fiat, iudex partialis erit, & Verum nunquam cognoscet, Deut.1.
units.tr: A. In judicial hearings both sides ought to be heard. For unless this is done, the judge will be partial and will never come to know the truth (Deut. 1).

units.la: B. Pios in iudicijs modestiam decere. Paulus calumnijs intolerabilibus petitur. Non tamen impudenter prorumpit, sed copiam sibi fieri exspectat. Inde prudenter & fortiter causam agit.
units.tr: B. Modesty befits the godly in judicial matters. Paul is attacked with intolerable slanders, yet he does not burst out shamelessly, but waits for an opportunity to be given him. Hence he pleads his cause wisely and bravely.

units.la: I. Exordio beneuolentiam captat, sine turpi adulatione tamen, & simul aduersarios obiter perstringit, quod & ipsi fecerant. Eo libentius apud te causam dico, quod te multis annis praefuisse huic genti sciam. Quasi diceret: Scis ergo quam turbulenti sint, & proinde illorum calumnijs non illico credis. Respicit autem ad communem morem, quo multum prodest iudicem habere, qui rerum gnarus sit.
units.tr: I. In his opening he wins goodwill, yet without shameful flattery, and at the same time touches lightly on his opponents, as they themselves had done. "I answer the more willingly, because I know that you have for many years presided over this nation." As if he were saying: "You know therefore how turbulent they are, and so you do not readily believe their slanders." He is referring to common custom, by which it greatly helps to have a judge who knows the affairs of the people.

units.la: Sed Not. 2. Magistratibus opus esse diligentia, ne ignorantia peccent. Haec enim illos non excusat, si crassa fuerit, &c. 1.Reg.3. Obseruent ergo populi commissi mores, ingenia, causarum circumstantias. Vide 2.Par.19. Item Psal.82. 72.&c. In primis non ferant caussidicos impostores.
units.tr: But note (2): magistrates need diligence, lest they sin through ignorance. For this does not excuse them if their ignorance is gross (1 Kings 3). Let the peoples committed to them therefore observe their customs, their characters and the circumstances of their causes. See 2 Chron. 19. Likewise Psalm 82 and Psalm 72, etc. Above all, let them not tolerate impostor advocates.

units.la: Haec obseruent, qui hodie honorum titulis & imperandi dulcedine ebrij, otio sese dedunt, comessationibus, choreis, &c. Vide Eccl.10.
units.tr: Let those observe these things who today, drunk with the titles of honour and the sweetness of commanding, give themselves over to idleness, to revelries, to dances, etc. See Eccles. 10.

units.la: 2. Quod Felicem, tyrannum turpissimum mam in suo peculio tot annis Deus praefe voluit. Sed ita merebatur illorum ingrati tudo. Dederat ante optimos pastores & prophetas, Mich. 6. Amos 2. Hos asperna-ti sunt. Imo ne Christum quidem audire voluerunt. Patiuntur ergo quod saepe prae dictum fuerat, Vide Isa. 5. Psal. 74. 80. Mat. 23. Luc. 19. Possunt haec docere, quid nobis sperandum sit, qui simili ingratitudine & improbitate Libertatis donum asperna mur, &c.
units.tr: 2. God allowed Felix, a most shameful tyrant, to rule over his own people for so many years. But the ingratitude of that people deserved it. God had earlier given them excellent ministers and prophets (Mic. 6; Amos 2), yet they rejected them. Indeed, they did not even wish to hear Christ. They therefore suffer what had often been foretold. See Isaiah 5, Psalm 74, Psalm 80, Matt. 23, Luke 19. These things can teach us what we ought to expect, since we likewise reject the gift of liberty with similar ingratitude and wickedness, etc.

units.la: II. Diluit obiecta crimina 1. Seditionis crimen multis depellit. 1. Tempus non fert. Quia duodecimus demum dies agitur, ex quo veni. Mox captus & huc missus sum. 2. Non eo nomine veni, sed vt ado rarem, & eleemosynis iuuarem egenos. Vbi obiter violati templi crime amolitur 3. Non inuenerunt me quicquam tale mo lientem, &c. 4. Nō possunt probare quod dicunt, &c. Grauiter dictum, quia falsi testimonij insimulat. Sed ita permissum pijs, ne veritas fiat suspecta, aut Dei gloria periclitetur.
units.tr: II. He refutes the charges brought against him. 1. He drives away the charge of sedition by many arguments. (1) The time does not allow it: it is only the twelfth day since I came. I was soon seized and sent here. (2) I did not come for that purpose, but to worship and to help the poor with alms. Here he also briefly removes the charge of violating the temple. (3) "They did not find me doing anything of the kind." (4) "They cannot prove what they say." It is a weighty statement, since it accuses them of false witness. But the godly are allowed to speak thus, so that the truth may not become suspect or the glory of God be endangered.

units.la: Sed Nota. Quod seditionis crimen tam multis depellit. Debent igitur ab hoc abhorrere ministri, eo quod nihil exitiali-us reipub. & concordiam & vnitate Deus maxime probat, Psalm. 133. Ioh. 17. At si ob
units.tr: But note: that he so readily drives away the charge of sedition. Ministers ought therefore to shrink from this, since God above all approves nothing less destructive to the commonwealth than discord, and commends concord and unity (Psalm 133; John 17). But if, on account of the gospel preached, they are stirred up by the impious,

units.la: Euangelium prædicatū excitentur ab im-pijs, ea culpa ministris imputari non de-bet,&c.
units.tr: that fault ought not to be imputed to the ministers, etc.

units.la: II. Hæreseos crimen diluit.Fatetur in-genuè se ex illa secta esse.Interim fidei suæ articulos recenset,vt ostendat, se hæreti-cum tamen non esse,&c.
units.tr: II. He refutes the charge of heresy. He frankly confesses that he belongs to that sect. Meanwhile he recounts the articles of his faith, so as to show that he is nevertheless not a heretic, etc.

units.la: Vbi No t. ¶1.Quòd fidem ob quam ac cusatur,ingenuè fatetur,etiam coràm Ethnico. Nō sufficit ergo,si corde credas,&c. Non vult cultores Dominus, quos sui pu deat.Vide Luc.12.Mat.10.Mar.8.Rom.10. Obseruent hæc frigidi tergiuersatores.
units.tr: Here note (1): that he openly confesses the faith for which he is accused, even before a Gentile. It is not enough, therefore, if you believe in your heart, etc. The Lord does not want worshippers whom he would be ashamed of. See Luke 12, Matt. 10, Mark 8, Rom. 10. Let the cold shufflers and evaders observe these things.

units.la: ¶2. Quæ fides Pauli fuerit.Quatuor ar ticulis comprehenditur: A.Colo Deum patrium,id est,quem patres coluerunt.Er go non sum hæreticus. Est hic primus fi-dei articulus,vt verum Deum credamus colamusque,non nouos aut alienos, Exo. 20. Est is, qui cum patribus egit, filium promisit,&in hoc salutem,Ioh.8.7. Hunc neque Iudæi nec Turcæ agnoscunt,Ioh.5.
units.tr: (2) What was Paul's faith? It is comprised in four articles. A. "I worship the God of my fathers," that is, whom the fathers worshipped. "Therefore I am not a heretic." This is the first article of faith, that we believe and worship the true God, not new or foreign gods (Exod. 20). This is he who made covenant with the fathers, promised a Son, and in him salvation (John 8). Neither the Jews nor the Turks acknowledge him (John 5).

units.la: B.Formam &modum cultus illius ex-primit. Credo omnibus quæ in Lege & Prophetis, &c. Athorum omnium finis Christus est,Rom.10.Luc.24.Ioh.5.Ergo fide in Christum Paulus Deum coluit. Continentur omnes articuli, Ioh.17. In-terim vides Deum iuxta scripturas coli oportere,non humanis traditionibus,Isa. 29.Mat.15.
units.tr: B. He sets out the form and manner of that worship: "I believe all things which are in the Law and the Prophets," etc. The end of all of them is Christ (Rom. 10; Luke 24; John 5). Therefore Paul worshipped God by faith in Christ. All the articles are contained in this (John 17). Meanwhile you see that God ought to be worshipped according to the Scriptures, not by human traditions (Isa. 29; Matt. 15).

units.la: G. Spem habeo fore resurrectionem, &c. Hunc articulum nominatim allegat, quia in hoc omnes alij fundantur, 1.Cor. 15. Iob.19. Obserua autemquod vniuersa-lem facit resurrectionem,vt Christus Iob. 5.Matt.25.Sic 2.Cor.5. Arguuntur qui ad pios solos restringunt.
units.tr: C. "I have hope that there will be a resurrection," etc. He cites this article by name, because all the others rest upon it (1 Cor. 15; Job 19). Observe, moreover, that he makes the resurrection universal, as Christ does (John 5; Matt. 25). So also 2 Cor. 5. Those are refuted who restrict it to the godly alone.

units.la: D. Hinc fit,quod conscientiae puritati studeo erga Deum & homines. Est hic vere fidei genuinus effectus, 1.Ioh. 3.Rom. 6.Iac 2.&c.Parit hunc Christi cognitio & resurrectionis meditatio.
units.tr: D. Hence it follows that I strive for purity of conscience towards God and men. This is truly the genuine effect of faith (1 John 3; Rom. 6; James 2, etc.). The knowledge of Christ and the meditation on the resurrection bring this forth.

units.la: ¶ 3.Ex his patet, quae Pauli & omnium Apostolorum fides fuerit olim,& qui Christiani veri sint hodie.Examinent se ad hoc singuli. Ista si habeas,non est,quod impio rum & Antichristianorum iudicia moreris.Oremus.
units.tr: (3) From these things it is clear what the faith of Paul and of all the apostles was in former times, and who are true Christians today. Let each examine himself on this point. If you have these things, there is no reason for you to be troubled by the judgements of the impious and the Antichristians. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXXXV.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXXXV.

units.la: 17 Pluribus autem annis interie-ctis veni eleemosynas exhibiturus gentimea,& oblationes.
units.tr: 17 "After many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings."

units.la: 18 Quo tempore inuenerunt mesan-ctificatum in templo, non tamen cum turba,neq; cum tumultu,quidam ex Asia Iudaei.&c.vsq; ad ver.24.
units.tr: 18 "While they were purifying themselves in the temple, not with a crowd and not with a tumult, certain Jews from Asia..." to verse 24.

units.la: OVemadmodum accusationis contra Paulum institutæ capita Spiri tus sanctus diligentissimè describi voluit, vt inde disceremus, de quibus mundus hic Christi ministros semper accusaturus sit: Ita non minori diligentia Pauli responsio describitur, qua docemur, vt nos in simili casu geramus. Et primò quidem seditionis crimen constantissimè à se depel lit, suo exemplo docens, Christianos ab hoc alienissimos esse debere. Porrò quoad fidem, hanc ingenuè fatetur, ac eius rationem reddit. Discimus ergo, non dissimulandam esse fidem, cùm pericula vrgent, Mar. 8 Luc. 12. Rom. 10. Adhæc fidem veram esse, quæ vnum Deum colit iuxta scripturas per Iesum Christū, & spe futuræ resurrectionis conscientiæ purita-tem custodit. Hanc ergo teneamus, & hæ-retici non erimus. Sequitur.
units.tr: Just as the Holy Spirit wished the charges brought against Paul to be described with the greatest care, so that we might learn what the world will always accuse Christ's ministers of, so too Paul's reply is described with no less care, teaching us how to behave in a similar case. First, he most firmly rejects the charge of sedition from himself, teaching by his own example that Christians ought to be utterly far from it. Next, as to faith, he frankly confesses it and gives its reason. We learn, then, that faith must not be concealed when dangers press (Mark 8; Luke 12; Rom. 10). Moreover, that faith is true which worships the one God according to the Scriptures through Jesus Christ, and which, with hope of the future resurrection, keeps the conscience pure. Let us hold to this, and we shall not be heretics. It follows:

units.la: I. Violati templi excusatio, in qua mirè diligens est, cùm tamè non ignoraret, tem-pli vsum & maiestatem Christi aduentu abolitam esse. Sed ad veram rationé tem-plorum respicit. Licet enim nec Deus his includatur (1. Reg. 8. Isa. 66. Act. 7.) nec ijs-dem cultus alligari debeat, Ioh. 4. externa tamen religio certû locum postulat. Propter hanc ergo illa ab omni prophanatio-ne neferuari decet. Vide Mar. ii. Quæ causa est, quòd Paulus etiam in hoc diligentissimè versatur: & arguuntur, qui hodie prophanis rebus polluunt.
units.tr: I. The excuse for violating the temple. Here he is wonderfully careful, although he did not ignore that the use and majesty of the temple had been abolished by the coming of Christ. But he looks to the true reason for temples. For although God is contained neither in these (1 Kings 8; Isa. 66; Acts 7), nor ought worship be bound to them (John 4), external religion still requires a fixed place. For this reason it is fitting that such a place be preserved from all profanation. See Mark 11. This is why Paul also takes such care in this matter, and those are reproved who today defile the temples with profane things.

units.la: Sunt autem argumenta: i. A tempore. Multis annis abfui, quibus nimirum hinc inde Euangelium prædicaui. Ergo contra templum nihil moliri potui.
units.tr: The arguments are these. (1) From the time: "I was absent for many years," during which, of course, I was preaching the gospel here and there. Therefore I could have undertaken nothing against the temple.

units.la: II. Veni, non templi gratia, sed vt egenis in hac gente eleemosynam afferrem, inter gentes collectam. Vide Actor. ii. i. Corin. 16. 2 Corint. 8. 9. Hic verò illos obiter inhumanitatis & ingratitudinis accusat, &c.
units.tr: II. "I came not for the sake of the temple, but to bring alms to this nation for the needy, collected among the Gentiles." See Acts 11; 1 Cor. 16; 2 Cor. 8–9. Here, however, he incidentally accuses them of inhumanity and ingratitude, etc.

units.la: Sed No T. §1. Quanta inter Christianos beneficentiæ ratio esse debeat, quando veteres procul abs fe dissitos, sibi tam commendatos habuerunt. Sciuerunt hoc requirere Christianam communionem, i. Cor. 12. Rom. 12. Deinde hoc esse sacrificium Deo gratissimum, Hof. 6. Matth. 15. Phil. 4. Heb. 13. &c. Arguimur nos, qui domestcos fidei negligimus.
units.tr: But note (§1): how great the practice of beneficence among Christians ought to be, when the ancients held in such esteem those who were far off and strangers to them! They knew that Christian fellowship requires this (1 Cor. 12; Rom. 12). Then, that this is a sacrifice most pleasing to God (Hos. 6; Matt. 15; Phil. 4; Heb. 13, etc.). We are reproved, who neglect the members of the faith.

units.la: §2. Ingratitudinem mundi erga Christi ministros benè meritos. Perditos vult, qui illius salutem quærunt, eò quòd hanc non magni facit. Vide Lothum, Ge. 14. 19. Mosem, Exod. 2. 3. 14. 15. 16. Num. 11. 14. 16. Heb. 11. Actorum 7. Prophetas. Christum,
units.tr: §2. The ingratitude of the world towards Christ's ministers who have deserved well. He holds those to be lost who seek their salvation, because they do not value it highly. See Lot (Gen. 14, 19); Moses (Exod. 2, 3, 14, 15, 16; Num. 11, 14, 16; Heb. 11); Acts 7; the Prophets; Christ;

units.la: Ioh 5 8.10.Paulum in primis.Sed non offendamur hodie.
units.tr: John 5, 8, 10; and Paul above all. But let us not be offended today.

units.la: III.Purificatum inuenerunt in templo, sine turba,&c. Quomodo igitur prophanare volui,&c.Nota.¶ Templa non prophanari à purificatis.Tales vero fuit,quos Christus sanctificauit,1.Cor.5. 6. Cur ergo hodie accusamur? Vide hinc longé alios hodie templorum prophanatores esse,quàm nos simus,&c. Nundinatores sacrorum,idololatras.
units.tr: III. "They found me purified in the temple, without a crowd," etc. How then did I wish to profane it, etc.? Note: the temples are not profaned by the purified. Such were those whom Christ sanctified (1 Cor. 5, 6). Why then are we accused today? See from this that far others today are profaners of temples, rather than we are: sellers of sacred things, idolaters.

units.la: IV. In Asiaticos crimen transfert,quos abesse conqueritur.Vide Act.21.&c.Nota.¶ Seditiosorum mores.Turbas dant, quibus periculum struunt insontibus. Quo exorto, ipsi subducunt se. Sed non effugient Dominum. Interim tu tales caueto.
units.tr: IV. He shifts the crime onto the Asians, whose absence he complains of. See Acts 21, etc. Note: the manners of seditious men. They stir up tumults, by which they lay dangers for the innocent. When these break out, they themselves slip away. But they will not escape the Lord. Meanwhile, beware of such men.

units.la: II. Prouocat aduersarios confidenter. Si isti volunt Asiaticorum causam suscipere,dicant quid in me deprehenderint. Scio illos nihil habere,nisi forte me accusare velint propter resurrectionis confessionem, quae ipsos inter se commisit,&c. At quomodo in me accusabunt quod ipsi fatetur.
units.tr: II. He confidently challenges his adversaries. "If these men want to take up the cause of the Asians, let them say what they have found in me. I know they have nothing, unless perhaps they wish to accuse me on account of my confession of the resurrection, which has set them at odds among themselves," etc. But how will they accuse me of what they themselves confess?

units.la: Nota.¶ Qua fiducia & integritate mi nistri agere debeant? Vt nimirum similiter certi sint, se obso à veritate accusari. Sic Christus Ioh.8.19.Ita monemur 1.Pet.
units.tr: Note: with what confidence and integrity ministers ought to act: namely, that they may be equally certain that, when they are falsely accused, it is not the truth that is being accused. So Christ (John 8:19). So we are warned (1 Pet.

units.la: 3.& 4. Hoc demum vere intrepidos facit Exitus notatur. Felix differt causam: tum quod nolTet controuersiam fidei & Iudaeorum mores: tum quod Lyfiam ex<note side="right">Paulus et cafatorum manum eius fugit.</note>fpeftare voluit, quem illi produxerant tem. Interim mitius cum Paulo agi curat, & relaxari iubet. NOT. 1. Felicem qui suo exemplo docet, non praecipitanda esse iudicia in hominum gratiam. Meminerint magistratus & populum & iudicium Dei esse, i Par.19. Pfal.82. Dei ergo exemplum imitentur, Exo.34. Gen.18. Interim in captivos humanitatis officia exerceant etiam facinorosos, &c.
units.tr: 3 and 4. Here at last the outcome is noted, which truly makes them fearless. Felix postpones the case, partly because he did not want to settle the controversy over faith and the customs of the Jews, and partly because he wished to await Lysias, whom they had produced as a witness. Meanwhile he takes care that Paul be treated more gently, and orders that he be released. (Paul escapes the hand of his accusers.) Note 1: happy is the one who by his own example teaches that judgments must not be rushed in order to gain men's favour. Let magistrates and people remember that judgment belongs to God (1 Chron. 19; Ps. 82). Let them therefore imitate God's example (Exod. 34; Gen. 18). Meanwhile let them perform the offices of humanity towards captives, even towards criminals, etc.

units.la: 2. Familiares Pauli, quorum hic fit men tio. Fuit ex his Lucas quoque. Non deserendi martyres Christi cum periclitantur. Quia sibi factum putat Dominus, quod il lis fit. Matt. 25. 10. Heb. 13.
units.tr: 2. Paul's companions, whom he here mentions. Luke was one of them too. The martyrs of Christ must not be deserted when they are in danger, since the Lord counts as done to himself whatever is done to them (Matt. 25, 10; Heb. 13).

units.la: 3. Dei fidem ergo suos, & potentiam in hostes. Dat suis gratiam apud homines, vt dictum Cap.23. Deinde efferas men tes mollire potest. Huic ergo nos approba re studeamus, non autem timeamus homines, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, the faithfulness of God towards his own, and his power against their enemies. He gives his people grace in the sight of men, as was said in chapter 23, and then he can soften fierce minds. Let us therefore strive to please him, and not fear men, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXXXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXXXVI.

units.la: 34 Aliquot autem post diebus, quum adesset Fel: cum Drusyla uxore sua, quæ erat Iudæa, accersiuit Paulum, & audiuit eum de fide quæ est in Christo.
units.tr: 34 Some days later, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith that is in Christ.

units.la: 25 Differente autem ipso de iustitia & continentia, & iudicio futuro, ex pauefactus Felix respondit, Nunc quidem abi: Ceterum opportunitatem nactus accersam te.
units.tr: 25 As Paul discoursed about righteousness, self-control and the future judgment, Felix was alarmed and replied, "Go away for now; but when I find a convenient time I will send for you."

units.la: 26 Simul & illud sperans, fore vt pecunia ipsi daretur à Paulo, vt eum vinculis exoluéret: quamobrem etiam frequentius eum accersens colloquebatur cum eo, &c. ad ver. 18.
units.tr: 26 At the same time he hoped that money would be given him by Paul, so that he might release him from his chains; for this reason he also sent for him more often and talked with him, etc., to verse 18.

units.la: NArrat hoc loco Diuus Luc. vt Paulus in vinculis nō modo diuina opē ieruatus fit, verùmetiam concionandi occasionem inuenerit coram Felice Præside & Drufylla, cuius concionis capita recen-sentur. Finis omnium est, vt discamus Dei verbum non vinciri, licet huius ministri vinciantur. 2. Tim. 2. Ioh. 3. Exempla huius multa passim extant, & similia fiunt hodie inter suplicia martyrum. Sed ordine videamus singula
units.tr: Here St. Luke relates that Paul in chains was not only preserved by divine help but also found an opportunity to preach before the governor Felix and Drusilla, whose sermon's main heads are listed. The aim of all is that we learn that the word of God is not bound, although its ministers are bound. 2 Tim. 2; John 3. Many examples of this exist everywhere, and similar things happen today among the sufferings of the martyrs. But let us look at the individual points in order.

units.la: I. Præmittitur concionis occasio, & simul auditores producuntur. Felix Cæsareæ relisto Paulo, aliquandiu abfuit. Redijt tamen cum Drufylla, quæ præcipua videtur
units.tr: I. The occasion of the sermon is introduced, and at the same time the hearers are brought forward. Felix, having left Paul at Caesarea, was absent for some time. He returned, however, with Drusilla, who seems to have been the chief cause of this sermon.

units.la: Paulo audi tores. videtur concionis huius causa fuisse. Fuit enim Iudæa, filia Herodis Agrippæ, de quo Act. 12 Delponsata primum Antiocho Epiphani, Comagen Regis filio. Deinde Aziazo Amazorum Regi. Ab hoc per Cyprium Magnum abducta, Felici nupsit contra legem. Attamen veri simile est, mansisse aliquem veræ religionis sensum, quæ causa fuit, quòd Paulum, qui in omnium ore erat, audire voluit.
units.tr: Drusilla was the daughter of Herod Agrippa, of whom Acts 12. She was first betrothed to Antiochus Epiphanes, son of King Comagenus, then to Azizus, king of the Amazons. Taken from him by Cyprian the Magician, she married Felix contrary to the law. Nevertheless it is likely that some sense of the true religion remained in her, and this was the reason she wished to hear Paul, who was on everyone's lips.

units.la: Nota. §1. Quid ferè imparia coniugia maneant? Excutiunt initio omnem religionis sensum. Morsus autè conscientiæ redit, & fames religionis aliquando ob libidinem & opes negatæ. Non temerè ergo diuinitus prohibentur, Deut. 7. Iof. 23 in no uo Testamento, 2. Cor. 6.
units.tr: Note. §1. What usually becomes of unequal marriages? At first they extinguish all sense of religion. But the sting of conscience returns, and the hunger for religion sometimes returns when lust and wealth are denied. Therefore they are not rashly forbidden by God: Deut. 7; Josh. 23; in the New Testament, 2 Cor. 6.

units.la: §2. Bonitatem Dei magnam, qui tam fœdis hominibus salutis verbum offerre voluit. Verè ergo est, qualis describitur, 2. Tim. 2. Ezech. 18. Huc pertinent exempla, Matth. 9. 18. Luc. 7. 19. 15. Consoletur & officij admoneat. Et obserua, inexcusabiles fieri eos, qui non emendantur, Matt. 10. Ioh. 15. &c.
units.tr: §2. The great goodness of God, who wished to offer the word of salvation to such foul people. It is truly as described in 2 Tim. 2; Ezek. 18. To this belong the examples in Matt. 9:18; Luke 7:19; 15. It consoles and admonishes us of our duty. And observe that those who are not amended become inexcusable: Matt. 10; John 15, etc.

units.la: II. Concio Pauli proponitur, non verbotim quidem, sed per capita, ex quibus liquet, quid dixerit. 1. Disseruit de fide in Christum eadem nimirum quæ alibi, cum
units.tr: II. Paul's sermon is set forth, not word for word, but by its heads, from which it is clear what he said. 1. He discoursed on faith in Christ, certainly the same as elsewhere, since

units.la: Christus sibi ipsi semper constet, Heb. 13. Vide ergo conciones, Actor. 13.14. 17. &c. Item Rom. 1.2.3.4.5. &c. Gal. 2 3 4.
units.tr: Christ always remains the same, Heb. 13. See therefore the sermons in Acts 13, 14, 17, etc. Likewise Rom. 1–5, etc.; Gal. 2, 3, 4.

units.la: NOT. Fide non modo in angulis esse praedicandam, sed etiam ubi periculum instare videtur. Arguitur, qui confessione huius inter ἀσιάρχας numerant. Damnant hi martyres omnes. Vide Luc. 12. Mar. 8 Ro. 10. Item Anabaptistae, qui sapti ad nul las quaestiones respondent, 1 Pet. 3.
units.tr: NOTE. Faith must be preached not only in corners but also where danger seems to threaten. Refuted are those who number the confessors of this among the Asiarchs [ἀσιάρχας]. All these martyrs condemn them. See Luke 12; Mark 8; Rom. 10. Likewise the Anabaptists, who, as if clever, answer no questions: 1 Pet. 3.

units.la: II. De iustitia & temperantia. Compre hendutur sub his fidei iustifiantis fructus. 1. Ioh. 3. Iustitia suum cuique tribuit, Mat 22. Rom. 13. Haec fugit illicita vota & voluptates. 1. Cor. 6. 1. Thess. 4. Et de his quidem dicendum necessario, ne quis sub fidei praetextu carnis licentiam quaerat. Vide Rom. 6. 1. Ioh. 1. 2. 3. Eph. 1. 4. 5. Tit. 2. 9. 3.
units.tr: II. On righteousness and temperance. These are included under the fruits of justifying faith. 1 John 3. Righteousness gives to each his due: Matt. 22; Rom. 13. It flees illicit vows and pleasures: 1 Cor. 6; 1 Thess. 4. And these things must indeed necessarily be spoken of, lest anyone seek licence for the flesh under the pretext of faith. See Rom. 6; 1 John 1, 2, 3; Eph. 1, 4, 5; Tit. 2. 9. 3.

units.la: Sed NOT. Quod de ijs virtutibus maxime disseruit, quae in auditoribus imprimis requirebantur. Felix auarus magis quam iustus erat. Drusylla impudica & ad ultera. Vides quid praedicandum & quomodo. Vellent multi solam fidem & gratiam Dei praedicari. Isa. 30. Sed aliud postulat mundi nequitia. Arguenda haec, ne gratiam ijs praedicemus, qui se illa non putant opus habere, Io. 16. 2. Ti. 4. Vide prophetas, Christum, Apostolos.
units.tr: But NOTE. That he discoursed chiefly on those virtues which were especially required in the hearers. Felix was more greedy than just; Drusilla was unchaste and adulterous. You see what should be preached and how. Many would want only faith and the grace of God to be preached (Isa. 30). But the wickedness of the world demands otherwise. These things must be rebuked, lest we preach grace to those who do not think they need it (John 16; 2 Tim. 4). See the prophets, Christ, and the Apostles.

units.la: III. De iudicio futuro. Confutat ergo errore, qui gentes seduxit maximè, quòd mundum æternum putarent. Securos igitur terret, ne priora friuola putarent.
units.tr: III. On the future judgment. He therefore refutes the error which above all led the nations astray, namely that they thought the world eternal. Thus he terrifies the secure, lest they think former things were trivial.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Iudicij extremi articulum in fidei negotio semper inculcari debere. Primo enim ijs medetur, quos mundi facies offendit. Psal. 7). Erit enim illis dies redemptionis, Luc. 21. Deinde nulla alia efficacior ratio est admonendi homines, vt officium faciant, & à peccatis abstineant. Eccle. 7. 2. Tim. 4.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ The article of the last judgment must always be inculcated in the matter of faith. For first it heals those whom the appearance of the world offends (Psal. 7). For the day of redemption will be theirs (Luke 21). Then no other reason is more effective for admonishing men to do their duty and abstain from sins (Eccl. 7; 2 Tim. 4).

units.la: III. Effectus concionis, planè irritus quo ad Felicem. 1. Terretur quidem, sed non cogitat de emendatione, quin ablegat, qua si non commodum illi fit diutiùs audire.
units.tr: III. The effect of the sermon was entirely fruitless so far as Felix was concerned. He is indeed terrified, but does not think about amendment; rather he dismisses Paul, as if it were not convenient for him to hear more.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Impiorum mores. Audiunt ex curiositate. Afficiuntur etiam aliquando & terrentur, vt diaboli, Iac. 2. Sed non mutantur. Imò dedignantur audire, cùm verbum illorum votis non respondet. Sic Achab, 1 Reg. 21. & 22. &c.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ 1. The manners of the impious. They listen out of curiosity. They are sometimes moved and terrified, like the devils (James 2), but they are not changed. Indeed they disdain to listen when the word does not match their wishes. So Ahab, 1 Kings 21 and 22, etc.

units.la: II. Pecuniam captat à Paulo. &c. Proprium hoc fuit Romanis, vtpote luporum alumnis, &c. Mithrydates. Perdit hoc tandem Rempub. omnibusque inuisos fecit.
units.tr: II. He seeks money from Paul, etc. This was characteristic of the Romans, as nurslings of wolves, etc. Mithridates. This at last ruined the commonwealth and made them hated by all.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Munerum corruptelam maximè iudicibus cauendam esse, Exod. 23. Deut. 16. Perdit florentissimas Respub. Nec dubium est, ideo non dedisse Paulum, ne mali exempli author esset, &c. Quid hodie inter nos possint munera, notitius est, quàm ut laudem aliquam mereatur.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ The corruption of bribes is to be guarded against especially by judges: Exod. 23; Deut. 16. It destroys the most flourishing commonwealths. Nor is there doubt that Paul did not give a bribe for this reason, lest he himself become the author of a bad example, etc. What gifts can do among us today is too well known for them to earn any praise.

units.la: III. Successore misso Paulum in vincu-lis relinquit, apud Iudæos gratiam initu-rus, quos sæpe offenderat.
units.tr: III. Having sent a successor, he leaves Paul in chains, about to win favour with the Jews, whom he had often offended.

units.la: No T. ¶ Piorum sortem. Semper mate-ria sunt impijs, qua sibi inuicem gratificen-tur. Idem Christo euenit, Luc. 23. Ioh. 18, 19. Iohanni Baptistæ. Sic Petrus capitur in Iudæorum gratiam, Act. 12. Fit idem in politia. Triumuiri Aug. Ant. Lipid. At nō inueniunt impij semper quod volunt.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ The lot of the pious. They are always material for the impious, who gratify one another. The same happened to Christ (Luke 23; John 18, 19) and to John the Baptist. So Peter is taken to win the favour of the Jews (Acts 12). The same happens in politics: the triumvirs Augustus, Antony, and Lepidus. But the impious do not always find what they want.

units.la: Discamus non offendi hodie, & Pauli exemplo patienter feramus omnia, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: Let us learn not to be offended today, and following Paul's example let us patiently bear all things, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XXV. HOMILIA CLXXXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXV. HOMILY CLXXXVII.

units.la: Festus ergo ingressus provinciam, triduo ascendit Hierosolymam, ab urbe Cæsarea.
units.tr: Festus therefore entered the province and went up to Jerusalem three days after arriving from the city of Caesarea.

units.la: 2 Indicârunt autem ei Pontifex maximus, & primarij ex Iudæis de Paulo, & eum rogârunt:
units.tr: 2 Then the high priest and the chief men of the Jews informed him about Paul, and they petitioned him,

units.la: 3 Petentes gratiam aduersus eum, ut accusarent eum in Hierusalem fa-
units.tr: 3 asking for favour against him, that he would summon Paul to Jerusalem,

units.la: ctis Eius insidijs, vt eum in via interimerent.
units.tr: and they laid a plot to kill him on the way.

units.la: 4 Festus autem respondit, seruari Paulum Cæsareæ, se vero cito illuc profecturum.
units.tr: 4 But Festus replied that Paul was being kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would soon set out for there.

units.la: 5 Qui ergo inter vos, inquit, possunt, vna descendant, & si qua est in hoc viro improbitas, accusent eum.
units.tr: 5 "Let those among you who are able, he said, go down with me, and if there is any wickedness in this man, let them accuse him."

units.la: 6 Et facta inter eos diebus non pluribus quam decem, quum descendisset Cæsaream, postero die sedit pro tribunali, iussit Paulum adduci.
units.tr: 6 And after he had stayed among them not more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and the next day he sat on the judgement seat and ordered Paul to be brought in.

units.la: 7 Qui cum venissent, circumstetterunt eum, qui Hierosolymis descenderant Iudæi, multas et graues criminationes aduersus Paulum adferentes, quas non poterant demonstrare.
units.tr: 7 When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges against Paul, which they could not prove.

units.la: 8 Quum ipse exciperet se neque in Legem Iudæorum, neque in templum, neque in Cæsarem quicquam peccasse.
units.tr: 8 Paul answered that he had committed no offence either against the law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against Caesar.

units.la: Escribitur hoc & sequenti capite duæ grauissimæ actiones Pauli Apostoli, quarum altera coram nouo præside Festo, altera coram Aggrippa Rege fidei causam dixit. Priorem vero ingens periculum præcessit, quod ipsi à Iudæis structum fuit. Liberatus tamen iuxta promissionem, Act.23. Finis omnium, ut discamus, Deum suorum curam habere, & permitte re quidem, ut variè tententur, sed eosdem ex tentationibus afferre, Psal.34.94,1.Corinth.10.2.Cor.1.Istis ergo fidem cofirme mus. Præstat autem singula ordine videre, &c.
units.tr: In this chapter and the next, two very weighty proceedings of the apostle Paul are described: in the first he pleaded his cause of faith before the new governor Festus, in the second before King Agrippa. A great danger had gone before the first, which the Jews had prepared for him. Nevertheless he was freed, according to the promise (Acts 23). The purpose of it all is that we learn that God takes care of his people, and that he permits them indeed to be tempted in various ways, but brings them out of their temptations (Ps. 34; 94; 1 Cor. 10; 2 Cor. 1). Let us therefore confirm ourselves in faith by these examples. It is better to look at each thing in order, etc.

units.la: I. Nouus Iudæorum conatus narratur. Festus venit Hierosolymam, nimirum ut in fidem illos recipiat. Mox adsunt Sacerdotes & primores, & Paulum ipsorum iudicio sisti petunt. Interim illum in viam occidere statuunt. Ingens hoc fuit periculum.
units.tr: I. The new attempt of the Jews is related. Festus came to Jerusalem, no doubt to win them over to his favour. Soon the priests and leading men are present and ask that Paul be brought to stand trial before their judgement. Meanwhile they resolve to kill him on the way. This was a great danger.

units.la: Not. 1. Irrequietos impiorum animos, vbi semel veritatis odio exarserunt, Isa.48.57. Quia enim veritas illos arguere nunquam definit, ipsi quoque non defi-nunt illam odisse, Ioh.3.7. Fremunt ut male-ric, Isa.48. Et tantum est illud odium, ut post habeant interdum sua commoda, modo veritatis ministri tollantur, qui illos excru-ciant, ut est Apoc.11. Vtrumq; hic cerni-tur. Biennij tempore non mitigati sunt isti &c. Deinde primas preces contra Paulum insumunt, quas Reipub. debebant. Nimirum ut præses publicum hostem puter, &c. Sic Herodias, Mat.14. Mar.6. Hodi similia passim extant.
units.tr: Note 1. The restless minds of the wicked, once they have flared up in hatred of the truth (Isa. 48; 57). For since the truth never ceases to convict them, they too never cease to hate it (John 3). They rage at what is good (Isa. 48). And this hatred is so great that sometimes they set aside their own advantages, provided that the ministers of the truth, who torment them, are removed (as in Rev. 11). Both are seen here. Those men were not softened by the lapse of two years, etc. Then they put forward first their requests against Paul, which they ought to have directed to the commonwealth: namely, that the governor should consider him a public enemy, etc. So Herodias (Matt. 14; Mark 6). Similar things are found everywhere today.

units.la: Discipulis Discimus non fidendum esse talibus. Prauum cor hominis, &c. Ier.17. Interdum simulant sibi satis fastum, &c. Vide Matth æi 10.
units.tr: Lesson for disciples: we learn that we must not trust such men. "The heart of man is deceitful," etc. (Jer. 17). Sometimes they pretend to have enough zeal, etc. See Matthew 10.

units.la: ¶2. Impiorum arma. Primo iuris speciem simulant. Petunt illum Hierololymis sisti quod æquissimâ videbatur, tum quòd illic turba primùm exorta esset, tum quòd ipsos plures laboribus & sumptibus propter vnum grauari, indignum videretur. Interim hoc prætextu parant occultam vim & latrocinium, vt etiam Act.23. Quid de illis iudicandum, qui hodie similia faciunt. Est hæc Antichristiani potestas, 2. Thess.2. Ita verò diabolo seruiunt, qui ab initio mendax & homicida est, Ioh.8. Luc. 22. Eiusdem igitur cum illo præmij consortes erunt.
units.tr: ¶2. The weapons of the wicked. First they put on a show of legality. They asked that he be summoned to stand trial at Jerusalem, which seemed most fair, both because the uproar had first arisen there, and because it seemed unworthy that many should be burdened with labour and expense on account of one man. Meanwhile under this pretext they prepare secret violence and robbery, as also in Acts 23. What should we judge of those who do similar things today? This is the power of Antichrist (2 Thess. 2). Truly they serve the devil, who was a liar and a murderer from the beginning (John 8; Luke 22). Therefore they will share the same reward with him.

units.la: II. Festus non consentit, & leges Romanas allegat, vt cras patebit. Interim iure agendi copiam facit. No T.¶1. Iudicis officium, vt nihil faciat in hominum gratiam, sed leges sequatur. Multa Festum mouere poterant, vt consentiret. Præiudicium ingens, quod Felix vinctum reliquerat. Authoritas Sacerdotum, quos proderat amicos habere. Primæ preces. Paulus vilis & contemptus. Sed omnia ista non mouent. Ita iubentur magistratus, Exod.23. Deute-
units.tr: II. Festus does not consent, and appeals to Roman law, as will appear tomorrow. Meanwhile he gives them the opportunity of pleading their case by law. Note 1. It is the duty of a judge to do nothing to win men's favour, but to follow the laws. Many things could have moved Festus to consent. There was a great prejudice, since Felix had left him in chains. There was the authority of the priests, whom it was useful to have as friends. There were the first requests. Paul was cheap and despised. But none of these things moves him. So magistrates are commanded (Exod. 23; Deut.

units.la: Iudicü est aiure non desistere propter homines. Kkk
units.tr: It is the office of a judge not to desist from the law because of men.

units.la: ronom.i.i.Paral.19. Psalmo 72.8z.
Arguütur Christiani reges, qui in Pontificum gratiam inauditos damnant, imò illis omnem in Christi fideles potestatem permittunt. Vindicabit suos Christus.
units.tr: Christian kings are rebuked who condemn unheard-of things to win the favour of the priests, and indeed grant them all power against the faithful of Christ. Christ will vindicate his own.

units.la: {1}2. Deum omnium horum authorem fuisse, qui promissa præstare voluit, Act.21. Contra hunc nullum confiliu valet, Proverb.21. If.8. Is hunc animum Fecto indidit, vt ex eo patet, quod postea Iudæis gratifi cari voluit. Sed tunc rursum Deus obstat alio medio. In corda enim ius habet, Proverb.21.
units.tr: 2. God was the author of all these things, since he willed to fulfil his promises (Acts 21). Against him no counsel prevails (Prov. 21; Isa. 8). He put this disposition into Festus, as is clear from the fact that afterwards he wished to gratify the Jews. But then again God hinders by another means. For he has power over hearts (Prov. 21).

units.la: Seruiat consolationi, quod impios quoque Dei imperio subiectos esse videmus. Nec in illorum arbitrio est, quid velint & possint. Quid ergo timemus? Luc.12.
units.tr: Let us take comfort from this, that we see even the wicked subject to the command of God. Nor is it in their power what they wish or what they can do. Why then do we fear? (Luke 12).

units.la: III. Ipsa actio sequitur, in qua Nota.1. Actores Iudæos. Circumstant, nimirum vt ipsa specie terreant, & authoritate Feltum moueant. Deinde proferunt vetera crimina, vt ex Pauli refponfione patet, quæ tamen probare non possunt. Maximè tamen vrgent seditionis crimen, quasi in Cæsaris maiestatem paccârit. Quanta fit impiorum impudentia patet. Denuo prose-runt, quæ prius abundè confutata erant, idque fine argumentis. Interim suam authoritatem valere voluit, vt etiam Iohan.
units.tr: III. The action itself follows, in which note: 1. The Jewish accusers. They surround him, no doubt to frighten him by their very appearance and to move Festus by their authority. Then they bring forward the old charges, as is clear from Paul's reply, which however they cannot prove. Yet they press most of all the charge of sedition, as if he had conspired against the majesty of Caesar. How great the impudence of the wicked is, is clear. Again they repeat what had already been fully refuted before, and that without arguments. Meanwhile they wished their own authority to prevail, as also in John

units.la: 18. Discimus, impijs non posse satis fieri vllis apologijs, &c. Nec pudet hos aliquius apud homines, quos nō pudet coram Deo.
units.tr: 18. We learn that it is impossible to make sufficient satisfaction to the wicked by any apologies, etc. Nor are they ashamed before men, who are not ashamed before God.

units.la: 2. Paulū Excusat se, vt supra. In primis de eo quod nihil in Cæsarem peccârit. At qui aliam à Cæsare fidem docebat, quod non licebat per leges Rom. Tertull. Sed religionis causa non ita subiacet Cæsari, vt illi quod lubet statuere liceat. Ad Deum enim pertinet. Quin tenenda est Christi regula, Matth. 22. Non ergo in magistratum peccat, qui absque tumultuandi studio Dei cultum asserit. &c. Magistratus talis suos fines egreditur, &c. Vide Actor.
units.tr: 2. Paul makes his defence, as above. First, as to the fact that he has committed no offence against Caesar. But he taught a faith other than Caesar's, which was not lawful by the laws of Rome. Tertullian: But religion is not so subject to Caesar that it is permitted to him to decree what he pleases. For it pertains to God. Indeed the rule of Christ must be kept (Matt. 22). Therefore he does not sin against the magistrate who maintains the worship of God without any intent to stir up tumult, etc. A magistrate of this kind goes beyond his limits, etc. See Acts.

units.la: 4. & 5. Vide quid nostris obiicias, qui nos contra magistratuum edicta seditiose pere gere dicunt. Hi non nos modo, sed prophetas, Christum, Apostolos & omnes martyres accusant. Non moremur ergo eiusmodi calumnias. Oremus.
units.tr: 4 and 5. See what is thrown at us, who are said to act seditiously against the edicts of the magistrates. These accuse not only us, but the prophets, Christ, the apostles and all the martyrs. Let us not dwell on calumnies of this kind. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXXXIIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXXXVIII.

units.la: 9 Sed Festus volens gratiam inire à Iudæis, respondens Paulo dixit, Vis Hierosolymam ascendere, et illic de his judicari apud me?
units.tr: But Festus, wishing to win the favour of the Jews, answered Paul and said: Do you want to go up to Jerusalem and be judged there before me on these charges?

units.la: 10 Dixit autem Paulus, Ad tribunal Cæsaris sto, vbi me oportet iudicari. cari, Iudæis nulla in re iniuriam feci, sicut & tu pulchrè nosti.
units.tr: Paul said: I stand before Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews in anything, as you yourself know very well.

units.la: II Nam si quam iniuriam, ac dignum morte aliquid feci, non recuso mori: sin vero nihil est eorum, quorum illi me accusant, nemo potest me illis condonare. Cæsarem appello.
units.tr: For if I have done some wrong or anything deserving of death, I do not refuse to die. But if none of the things of which they accuse me is true, no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar.

units.la: 21 Tunc Festus cum Concilio colloquutus, respondit: Cæsarē appellasti? ad Cæsarem proficisceris.
units.tr: Then Festus, after conferring with the council, answered: You have appealed to Caesar? To Caesar you shall go.

units.la: PAulus Apostolus de suis afflictionib. loquens, sepe spectaculum fuisse ait mundo, angelis & hominibus, 1. Cor. 4. Patet hoc clarissimè ex ijs, quæ illi in hac sua captivitate acciderunt. Iam enim quarto capitis causam agit. Primum enim hoc fecit coram toto populo, per Tribunum ereptus, cap. 22. Deinde coār Concilio, cap. 23. Tertiò coră Felice cap. 42. Nunc coram Festo novo præside. Interim variis periculis fuit tentatus, quæ tamen omnia euasit. Finis omnium est, ut videamus, quantum malis in suos electos permittat Deus, quos tamen semper asserit. Psal. 34. Non ergo hodie offendamur. Et hunc maximè præsens locus facit, quo docetur, ut periculum nō uum, ab ipso præside sibi structum euasē rit: ut eò clarius Dei fides & bonitas pateret, neue præsidum fauore defensus esse videatur. Videamus singula.
units.tr: Paul the Apostle, speaking of his afflictions, says that he has often been a spectacle to the world, to angels and to men (1 Cor. 4). This is shown most clearly by what befell him in this captivity. For now he is pleading his cause for the fourth time. First he did so before the whole people, rescued by the tribune (ch. 22). Then before the council (ch. 23). Thirdly before Felix (ch. 24). Now before Festus, the new governor. Meanwhile he was assailed by various dangers, all of which he escaped. The purpose of all this is that we may see how far God permits his elect to be troubled by evils, whom nevertheless he always declares to be his own (Ps. 34). Let us therefore not be offended today. This present passage especially shows it, in which we are taught that he escaped a new danger set for him by the governor himself, so that God's faithfulness and goodness might appear all the more clearly, and lest he seem to have been defended by the favour of governors. Let us look at the parts one by one.

units.la: I. Festus vult iam gratificari Iudæis. Videtur ab his corruptus fuisse. Siue vero in tellexerit aliquid de insidijs, seu minùs, ini quissimè agit. Quia vero non audet inuitum ablegare, ne ius Rom. violasse dicatur, astutè num Hierosolymam ascendere velit, rogat, & se iudicem fore respondet.
units.tr: I. Festus now wants to gratify the Jews. He seems to have been corrupted by them. Whether he understood something of the plots or not, he acts most wickedly. But because he does not dare to send Paul away against his will, lest he be said to have violated Roman law, he cunningly asks whether Paul is willing to go up to Jerusalem, and answers that he himself will be the judge.

units.la: Not. 1. Facilè corrumpi eos, qui Dei cognitione & timore carent. Quia enim natura ad malum procliues sumus, quauis occasione impellimur, nisi Dei timor cohibeat. Id in Festo cernitur. Discimus non fidendum esse talibus, licet aliquando de se præbeant virtutis specimen. Mox enim ad ingenium redeunt. Pharao, Exod. 6.7.8.9.&c. Saul, 1. Sam.19.24.26. Achab. 1.Reg.18 21. Cauti ergo simus.
units.tr: Note 1. Those who lack the knowledge and fear of God are easily corrupted. For since we are by nature prone to evil, we are driven by any occasion unless the fear of God restrains us. This is seen in Festus. We learn not to trust such men, although at times they show some sample of virtue, for soon they return to their nature. Pharaoh (Exod. 6, 7, 8, 9, etc.), Saul (1 Sam. 19, 24, 26), Ahab (1 Kings 18, 21). Let us therefore be cautious.

units.la: 2. Quanta iudiciorum pestis sit perso narum respectus, quo gratiam apud homines venamur. Hoc Festo omnem priorem laudem obscurat, & ex iusto iudice quasi latro efficitur. Frequens hoc. Ideo tam grauiter cauetur lege Dei, Exo.23 Leu.19. Deut.1.16. Prou.24. Perdidit vitium hoc multas florentissimas Respub.
units.tr: 2. How great a plague to judgments is respect of persons, by which we seek favour with men. By this Festus obscures all his earlier praise, and from a just judge becomes almost a robber. This is common. Therefore the law of God guards against it so severely (Exod. 23; Lev. 19; Deut. 1:16; Prov. 24). This vice has ruined many most flourishing commonwealths.

units.la: Meminerint ergo magistratus, se Dei vices obire, 2.Par.19.Psal.82. Rom.13. Hunc ergo imitentur,qui personas non respicit Act.10 Rom.2 Eph.6. Et quod bene prō-nuntiârunt,non mutent. Hinc lites infini-tæ,& licentia nimia.
units.tr: Let magistrates therefore remember that they discharge the office of God (2 Chron. 19; Ps. 82; Rom. 13). Let them imitate him who does not regard persons (Acts 10; Rom. 2; Eph. 6), and not change what they have rightly pronounced. Hence come endless lawsuits and excessive licence.

units.la: II. OlfacitPaulus, quorsum res exitura sit,nimirum ex spiritus reuelatione,quem suis aduocatum Christus promisit,Ioh.14. Luc.13.21:Mar.13.Ideo liberè agit,& quidē rationib. A. Ad Cæsaris tribunal sto. Ibi ergo iud cari debeo. Innuit aūte ad Cæsare redundaturam iniuriam,si aliis iudicibus, & quidem Iudæis,subijciatur. Iudæu nullam s ci miuitam. Huius testem citatipsum Festum. Ergo non est,quod secundum eo rum leges iudicer.C. Dilemmate pugnat. Si mortem merui, non recuso mori. Sin mi-nus,nemo me illis donare potest iure.His præmissis rationibus tandem ad Cæsarem prouocat eo quod apud Festum nulla iu-stitiæ spes erat reliqua.Tum quod oracu-lum habuit Act.23.
units.tr: II. Paul smells out where the matter will end, namely by the revelation of the Spirit, whom Christ promised to his people as advocate (John 14; Luke 12; 21; Mark 13). Therefore he acts freely, and for good reasons. A. I stand before Caesar's judgment seat. There I ought to be judged. He hints that an injury would redound upon Caesar if he were subjected to other judges, and indeed to Jews. He has done no wrong to the Jews, and he cites Festus himself as witness. Therefore it is not right that he be judged by their laws. B. He argues by a dilemma: if I have deserved death, I do not refuse to die; but if not, no one can rightly hand me over to them. Having set down these reasons, he at last appeals to Caesar, because there was no hope of justice left with Festus, and also because he had an oracle (Acts 23).

units.la: Not.¶ 1.Pios non cogi patientiæ legi-bus,vt fe temerè impiorum libidini subij-ciant. Imo l cet declinare pericula, quan-do id fieri potest, vt nec fidem negemus, nec vocationem nostram negligamus. Vi-de Mat.10 Sæpe fugerunt Apostoli Nunc iudicium iniquū Paulus detrectat. Ita A-thanaf. Tyrum, Mediol. Ariminū horruit. Ambrof. Mediolani iudicari voluit. Arguuntur, qui abusi loco 1 Pet. 3. verbi ministros Papisticis Concilijs obijcere volunt, vt ibi fidei rationem reddant, vbi nulla ratio admittitur.
units.tr: Note 1. The godly are not compelled by the laws of patience to submit themselves rashly to the lust of the impious. Indeed, it is lawful to avoid dangers when this can be done without denying the faith or neglecting our calling. See Matt. 10. The Apostles often fled. Now Paul refuses an unjust judgment. Thus Athanasius shunned Tyre and Milan, and he dreaded Ariminum; Ambrose wished to be judged at Milan. They are refuted who, abusing 1 Pet. 3, want the ministers of the Word to be summoned before Papistical councils to give an account of their faith, where no reasoning is admitted.

units.la: 2. Quòd ita declinat periculum, vt interim innocentiam suam fortiter asserat. Huius potissimum raticnem ministros habere decet, ne propter ipsos Euangelij do strina male audiat. Huc refer, Matt 5.
units.tr: 2. That he so avoids danger as in the meantime to assert his innocence boldly. Ministers especially ought to heed this reason, lest the doctrine of the gospel be badly spoken of because of them. Refer here to Matt. 5.

units.la: 3. Licere Christianis legum praesidio & legitimis iudicijs vti. Sunt enim bonae Dei ordinationes Rom. 13. Deut 1 Ita fecit Actor. 16 & 23 Nunc pronocat, quod nunquam fit abfq; iudicis quoque contumelia, nedum partis aduersariae. Abutuntur locis, Matt 5 1. Cor. 6. Priuata vindicta & litigandi libido prohibetur.
units.tr: 3. That Christians may lawfully use the protection of the laws and lawful judgments. For these are good ordinances of God (Rom. 13; Deut. 1). So he acted in Acts 16 and 23. Now he appeals, which is never done without insult to the judge, let alone the opposing party. They abuse Matt. 5 and 1 Cor. 6. Private revenge and the lust for litigation are forbidden.

units.la: 4. Neminii ius esse, innocentem donare aliorum libidini. Dei enim ministri sunt iudices, vt innocentes tueantur, Rom. 13. Idem de fortunis iudicandum. Qui aliter faciunt in hominum gratiam, peccant. Herodes, Mar. 6 Pilatus, Ioh. 18. 19. &c.
units.tr: 4. No one has the right to deliver an innocent person to the lust of others. For ministers of God are judges so that they may protect the innocent (Rom. 13). The same should be judged concerning property. Those who act otherwise to gain the favour of men sin: Herod (Mark 6), Pilate (John 18, 19), etc.

units.la: III. Festus attonitus confert cum asse foribus, & videt se captum. Salse ergo respondet. Ita impij indigne ferunt se nota ri. Melior tamen nostris, qui Christianos nullis priuilegijs gaudere patiuntur, imo ne jure quidem.
units.tr: III. Festus, astonished, compares Paul with the hinges of a door and sees that he is caught. So he answers sharply. Thus the impious bear it with indignation when they are marked. Our own people, however, are better, who do not allow Christians to enjoy any privileges, indeed not even the right of law.

units.la: Festum pro nocatione admittit, quamuis inuitus.
units.tr: Festus admits the appeal, although unwillingly.

units.la: Interim patet, qua seueritate ius inter gentes administrârint Romani, quando in vilissimum hominem nihil licet Festo post prouocationem. Hic neruus diu seruauit Rempub. Ita hodie coercendi præsides, ne se rerum Dominos esse arbitrentur. Sic minus inuidiæ haberent principes, & innocentia floreret. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile it is clear with what severity the Romans administered justice among the nations, when after the appeal nothing is permitted to Festus against this most worthless of men. This sinew long preserved the commonwealth. So today governors should be restrained, lest they think themselves masters of affairs. Thus princes would have less hatred and innocence would flourish. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXXXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXXXIX.

units.la: 13 Diebus autem aliquot exactis, Agrippa Rex & Bernice venerunt Cæsaream, salutaturi Festum.
units.tr: 13 Some days later, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.

units.la: 14 Et quum dies complures illic versatifuissent, Festus Regi exposuit, quæ ad Paulum spectabant, dicens: Vir quidam est relictus à Felice vinctus, vsque ad ver. 25.
units.tr: 14 And when they had stayed there for many days, Festus laid Paul's case before the king, saying: "There is a certain man left in custody by Felix, to ver. 25.

units.la: OVemadmodû suos varijs afflictionibus exercet Deus: Ita easdem ad ipsorum salutem & sui nominis gloriam dirigit. Docet hoc præsens Pauli historia. Ex quo enim Hierosolymis captus fuit, indies nouam habuit prædicandi occasionem. Primùm coram populo, quod alioqui non licuisset. Deinde apud sacerdotes in Concilio, qui alioqui non dignati fuissent audire. Tertiò coram Felice, qui illum sæpissimè piffimè accersiuit. Tandem apud Festum. Ita verò causam suam egit, vt milites quoque & præsides viderent innocentem esse: quod ad Euangelij propagationem multum fecit. Manserunt femina in multorum animis. Et huc sequentia quoq; pertinent, quibus narrabitur, vt coram Agrippa & gentis illius nobilitate prædicandi occasio data fit. Videamus singula.
units.tr: As God exercises his people with various afflictions, so he directs them to their own salvation and to the glory of his name. Paul's history here teaches this. From the time he was seized at Jerusalem, he had a fresh opportunity to preach every day. First before the people, which otherwise would not have been allowed. Then before the priests in the council, who otherwise would not have deigned to hear him. Third, before Felix, who summoned him very often. Finally before Festus. He so pleaded his cause that the soldiers and the governors also saw that he was innocent, which greatly helped the spread of the gospel. His words remained in the minds of many. The following passages also belong here, in which it is told how he was given an opportunity to preach before Agrippa and the nobility of that nation. Let us look at the particulars.

units.la: I. Occasio totius negotij præmittitur. Agrippa cum Bernice descendit, vt Festum salutaret. Fuit hic iunior, Prisci filius, de quo Act. 12. Bernice soror fuit, sulpe‑ta vt quæ cum fratre stupri consuetudinem haberet. Quare vitandæ suspicionis causa Polemoni nupsit, Regi Lyriæ. Mox autem facto diuortio, ad fratre redijt. Non mirum autem quod ad Festum veniunt, cum non nisi precario regnarent.
units.tr: I. The occasion of the whole matter is set out first. Agrippa came down with Bernice to greet Festus. He was the younger, son of Priscus, of whom we read in Acts 12. Bernice was his sister, suspected of having an incestuous relationship with her brother. Therefore, to avoid suspicion, she married Polemon, king of Lyria. Soon, however, after a divorce, she returned to her brother. It is not surprising that they came to Festus, since they reigned only by sufferance.

units.la: Nota. Exemplum diuinæ bonitatis, qui ex nefaria familia ortus, & incœstu pol-lutis, gratiam suam per Euangelij prædi-cationem offert. Proauus enim fuit Hero des magnus, qui infantes occidit, Matth. 2. Aui frater Antippas, qui Iohannem Bapti-stam sustulit & Christo illusit, Mar. 6. Luc. 3. & 23. Pater, Agrippa Priscus, Iacobum necauit, & Petrum cepit, &c. Act. 12. Docent hæc, Deum non ita vindictæ cupidu esse,
units.tr: Note: an example of divine goodness, which offers its grace through the preaching of the gospel to one born of a wicked family, polluted by incest. For their great-grandfather was Herod the Great, who slew the infants, Matt. 2. Their great-uncle Antipas beheaded John the Baptist and mocked Christ, Mark 6, Luke 3 and 23. Their father, Agrippa Priscus, killed James and seized Peter, etc., Acts 12. These things teach that God is not so eager for vengeance

units.la: vt patrū scelera filij luere cogantur. Imo illius gratiam omnibus patere, Ezech.18. Sic illis Christus mittitur,quorum patres Prophetas occiderunt,Matth 23 Luc 11. &c.Postea prædicatur ijs,qui ipsum occi- derant,Act.2.
units.tr: that the sons are forced to pay for their fathers' crimes. Rather, his grace is open to all, Ezek. 18. So Christ is sent to those whose fathers killed the prophets, Matt. 23, Luke 11, etc. Afterwards he is preached to those who had killed him, Acts 2.

units.la: Seruiat consolationi, tum etiam institutioni,ne aliquē temerè damnemus pro pter maiores suos. Vide Christi genealogiam, in qua infames multi numerantur, Matt.1.Luc.3.&c.Ita testari voluit, fe pec catorum maximè gratia venisse,Mat.9.18. Luc.15.1.Tim.1.&c.
units.tr: Let this serve for comfort, and also for instruction, that we should not rashly condemn anyone on account of his ancestors. See Christ's genealogy, in which many infamous persons are numbered, Matt. 1, Luke 3, etc. Thus he wished to testify that he came chiefly for the grace of sinners, Matt. 9, 18, Luke 15, 1 Tim. 1, etc.

units.la: II.Post multos dies,nimirum in delitijs transactos,Festus in Pauli mentionem incidit. Talibus enim captiui nön multùm curæ sunt.Et quia Agrippæ consilio fe iuuari posse putabat, rem narrat:subdolè tamen & mala fide.Nam iniquitatem suam, qua in illum vsus erat,pulchrè dissimulat, &c.Orationis partes sunt hæ.
units.tr: II. After many days, namely spent in pleasures, Festus came to mention Paul. For captives are of little concern to such men. And because he thought he could be helped by Agrippa's counsel, he tells the matter, yet deceitfully and in bad faith. For he skilfully conceals the injustice by which he had dealt with Paul, etc. The parts of his speech are these.

units.la: I. Proponit quis Paulus, quid in eius causa poftulârint Iudæi, & quid ipse reffponfi dederit initiò relictus à Felice.Priæ mittit hoc,ne abs fe captum putaret. Iudæi poftulârunt contra illum mortis sententiam. Sed negaui,Romanam consuetudinem allegans.
units.tr: I. He sets out who Paul is, what the Jews demanded in his case, and what answer he himself gave, having been left in custody by Felix. He mentions this first, so that Agrippa would not think he had been taken captive. The Jews demanded a sentence of death against him. But I refused, citing the Roman custom.

units.la: No T.qi.A iudicijs omnem gratiam re mouendam esse, quæ cum iure & legibus pugnat. Licet enim magna sit humanitatis laus, iudicibus tamen prima debet iusti tiæ ratio esse, Exod.23. Leu.19. Deut.1.16. Prou.17. Hoc Ethnici viderunt in nostri confusionem. Hodie in impiorum gratiam pij vexantur, deseruntur, occiduntur.
units.tr: Note on the courts: all favour must be removed from judgments when it conflicts with right and with the laws. For although humanity is great praise, yet for judges the first consideration ought to be justice, Exod. 23, Lev. 19, Deut. 1:16, Prov. 17. The heathen saw this to our shame. Today the godly are harassed, abandoned and killed for the favour of the wicked.

units.la: Obseruent Magistratus Romanam consuetudinem: A.Præsentes sint accusatores, ne locus detur obtrectatoribus, per quos sæpe pericula structa sunt innocentibus, i. Sam.21.22. Hest.3. &c. B. Locus detur defensioni. Cogitet iudex, sibi binas esse aures, ne ex eorum sit numero, quos Appelles pinxit. C. Nihil fiat in alicuius gratiam vel odium. Magistratus commune personam sustinet.
units.tr: Let magistrates observe the Roman custom: (a) the accusers should be present, so that no opportunity is given to slanderers, through whom dangers have often been laid for the innocent, 1 Sam. 21, 22, Esth. 3, etc. (b) Opportunity should be given for the defence. The judge should consider that he has two ears, lest he be one of those whom Apelles painted. (c) Nothing should be done for the favour or hatred of anyone. The magistrate bears a public person.

units.la: ¶ 2. Impudentiam Sacerdotum. Audent postulare quod Ethnicus videt esse iniquum. Interim sanctissimi & primi in populo Dei habesi volunt. Ita gentibus faci unt sese suspectos. Similia hodie fiunt ab Episcopis, Monachis, Sacrificulis, &c.
units.tr: ¶ 2. The shamelessness of the priests. They dare to demand what even a heathen sees to be unjust. Meanwhile they want to be held most holy and foremost among the people of God. Thus they make themselves suspect to the Gentiles. Similar things are done today by bishops, monks, little sacrificers, etc.

units.la: II. Quomodo causam egerit, & quid coram pererit. Absque dilatione audiui. Compe ri innocentem. Nihil enim afferebant eorum, quæ putabat sed quæstiones, &c. Con temtissimè loquitur, nimirum vt homo pro phanus, qui non magni fecerat Pauli ver.
units.tr: II. How he pleaded the case and what he achieved before the court. "I heard him without delay. I found him innocent. For they brought no charge of the sort I supposed, but questions, etc." He speaks most contemptuously, namely as a profane man who did not value Paul at all.

units.la: Romanorum mos laudabilis in iudicijs exercendis.
units.tr: The commendable custom of the Romans in conducting judgments.

units.la: Festum Pan innocentiae testimonium fert. ba. Exemplum omnium, qui verbo Dei mysteria, in primis resurrectionem commemorunt. Nec mirum, si hodie nihil prosi-ciamus docendo, cum in hoc Paulus nihil profecerit.
units.tr: Festus also bears witness to Paul's innocence. Example of all who proclaim the mysteries of God's Word, especially the resurrection. Nor is it surprising if today we make no progress in teaching, since Paul made no progress in this.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ 1. Absq; dilatione procedendum in iudicijs. Procrastinationibus enim sæpe innocentissimi grauantur. Hoc nimis vulgare, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: (1) In judgments one must proceed without delay. For the most innocent are often burdened by procrastinations. This is too common, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Pauli innocentia multipli hostium testimonio probatur: vt Lysiæ, Felicis, Festi. Mox etiam Agrippæ. Accusatores nihil probant. Eadem ratio aliorum quoq; Apostolorum, Act. 4.5. Christi item, Ioh. 8. 10. Mar. 14. Ioh. 18.19. Imò hodie inter Turcas bene audiunt. Magna fidei dignitas. Ethnicis peiores, qui calumniantur.
units.tr: ¶ (2) Paul's innocence is proved by the testimony of many enemies: that of Lysias, Felix and Festus, and afterwards also Agrippa. The accusers prove nothing. The same reasoning applies to the other apostles, Acts 4, 5, and likewise to Christ, John 8, 10, Mark 14, John 18, 19. Indeed today among the Turks they are well spoken of. Great is the dignity of faith. The accusers are worse than the heathen.

units.la: ¶ 3. Infelix Iudæorum fors, quando omnis religionis contemptor inter ipsos iudex sedet, & quidem in religionis causa. Sed hoc impijs sacerdotibus & suæ ingratitudini debebant. Matt. 23. Luc. 19. Idem nonnullis hodie sub Turcis euenit. Resi-pifcamus.
units.tr: ¶ (3) The unhappy lot of the Jews, when a despiser of all religion sits among them as judge, and indeed in a matter of religion. But they owed this to their impious priests and to their own ingratitude, Matt. 23, Luke 19. The same thing happens today to some under the Turks. Let us repent.

units.la: III. Quraduc in vinculis detineat innocentem, docet. Astutè dissimulat suum scelus, attamen seipsum prodit, qui hoc facere coegerit. Exemplum eorum, qui hodie etiam splendidis verbis suam iniustitiam tiam pailiare solent. Vsitatum hoc principibus.
units.tr: III. He shows why he keeps the innocent man in chains. He cunningly conceals his own wrong, yet betrays himself, since he was compelled to do this. This is the example of those who today too are accustomed to cover their injustice with fine words. This is common among princes.

units.la: III. Agrippa cupit audire Paulum, & hac occasione producitur. Obserua Dei providentiam. Quae minime putares, illius regnum prouehunt. Quid ergo anxij tumultuamur? In Deum respiciamus, & huic committamus rem, ipsi faciamus officium. Oremus.
units.tr: III. Agrippa wishes to hear Paul, and by this occasion Paul is brought forward. Observe God's providence. Things you would least expect advance his kingdom. Why then do we anxiously stir ourselves? Let us look to God, commit the matter to him, and do our own duty. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXC.
units.tr: HOMILY CXC.

units.la: 23 Postero autem die quum venisset Agrippa & Bernice cum multa ostentatione, & introitu in auditorium cum tribunis & eminentibus eius viris ciuibus, iubente Festo, adductus est Paulus.
units.tr: 23 On the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp and entered the hall with the tribunes and the leading men of the city, Paul was brought in at Festus's command.

units.la: 24 Tum Festus, Agrippa Rex, inquit, & omnes qui simul adestis nobiscum, conspicitis istum, de quo omnis multitudo Iudaeorum compellauit me, & Hierosolymis & hic, vociferantes non oportere eum viuere amplius, &c. ad verf. 28.
units.tr: 24 Then Festus said: King Agrippa, and all you who are present with us, you see this man, about whom the whole multitude of the Jews has petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying out that he ought no longer to live, etc., to verse 28.

units.la: QVamuis homines nihil praestantius & salutarius habeat verbo Dei, quo gratiam suam & veram salutis rationem ille nobis offert: ea tamen est mundi peruerfitas, vt nihil illi perinde inuisum & exosum fit. Quae causa est,quod varijs afflictionibus huius ministri exercentur, & quasi καθάρματα mundi sunt, 1. Cor. 4. Porro neiftis offenderemur hoc nouis fimo seculo, Spiritus S.partim praedixit haec euentura,Zach.12.Mich.7.Psal.2.Ioh. 15.16.Matt.10.&c. partim exempla propo nit,quibus docetur, semper hanc verbi & ministrorum eius fortem in hoc mundo fuisse, nec tamen illud vnquam potuisse extingui. Nam & manet in aeternum, & nunquam caret suo legitimo fructu, Ifaiae 40.55.Exemplum huius in praesenti quoque Lucas propon't in Paulo qui vinctus & prouocare coactus,coram illustrissimis in gente Iudaica sic concionatur,vt innocentia sua omnibus pateat, &c. & aculeos relinquat in multorum animis. Videamus singula.
units.tr: Although men have nothing more excellent and healthful than the Word of God, by which he offers us his grace and the true way of salvation, such is the perversity of the world that nothing is equally hated and detested by it. The reason is that this minister is exercised by various afflictions and is like the refuse [καθάρματα] of the world (1 Cor. 4). Moreover, lest we be offended by this in these latest times, the Holy Spirit partly foretold that these things would happen (Zech. 12; Mic. 7; Ps. 2; John 15:16; Matt. 10, etc.) and partly set forth examples by which we are taught that this lot of the Word and of its ministers has always existed in this world, yet it could never be extinguished. For it remains forever and never lacks its proper fruit (Isa. 40; 55). Luke sets forth an example of this now too in Paul, who, bound and compelled to appeal, preaches before the most illustrious men of the Jewish nation in such a way that his innocence is made plain to all, etc., and leaves goads in the minds of many. Let us look at the particulars.

units.la: I. Auditores describuntur Primus Agrippa est cum Bernice. Veniunt cum magnifico apparatu,vt reges solent,1.Sam.8. Simul adsunt Tribuni & proceres vrbis. Voluit nimirum hos interesse Festus, vt quocunque res exiret, inuidiam facilius subterfugeret.
units.tr: I. The hearers are described. First comes Agrippa with Bernice. They arrive with magnificent display, as kings are wont to do (1 Sam. 8). The tribunes and the leading men of the city are present too. Festus no doubt wanted these men to be present so that, whatever the outcome, he could more easily escape odium.

units.la: Interim Nota. Agrippam. Cupiuit audire Paulum,sed ex curiositate,vtHero des Antipas, Mar. 6. Luc. 23. Huius indicium est, quod non vt discipulus venit, nec aliquid remittit ex fastu regio, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile note Agrippa. He desired to hear Paul, but out of curiosity, like Herod Antipas (Mark 6; Luke 23). The evidence for this is that he does not come as a disciple, nor does he lay aside anything of his royal pride, etc.

units.la: Docemur, vt mundus hic erga Dei verbum afficiatur. A. Odit illud natura, eo quod non vult argui, Ioh. 3. Vel certè non magni facit, terrena præferens.
units.tr: We are taught how this world is disposed toward the Word of God. A. Nature hates it, because it does not want to be reproved (John 3), or at least does not value it highly, preferring earthly things.

units.la: B. Interim fit, vt quidam carnis affectibus ducti accedant, vt curiositate, sque quæ stus, odio discipulinæ Papisticæ, vel etiam ex consuetudine, ne ἀθεοι videantur.
units.tr: B. Sometimes it happens that certain people, led by fleshly affections, come to it: out of curiosity, for gain, from hatred of Papist discipline, or even from habit, so as not to seem to be atheists.

units.la: C. Hi nihil proficiunt. Afferunt enim sua præiudicia, & vt censores veniunt. Tales hodie multi. Vel vt specatores, &c. Vide Ezech 33. Humiliemur ergo, & cogitemus ante omnia fidei obedientiam requiri, Rom. 1 16.2. Cor. 10. Luc. 8.
units.tr: C. These gain nothing. For they bring their own prejudices and come as critics. Many such today, or as mere spectators, etc. See Ezek. 33. Let us therefore be humbled and consider that, above all, obedience of faith is required (Rom. 1:16; 2 Cor. 10; Luke 8).

units.la: ¶ 2. Quales sint, qui fastum & luxu tem plis inferunt. Agrippæ similes. Ingens pecatum. Lœuitas magna, nõ cogitare quod lutum es, & quæ vestium origo, Gen 3. Of fendis multos, vel libidine, vel exemplo, vel impatientiæ occasione, & ita incurris sententiam, quæ habetur, Matt. 18. Peruer sitas magna, quod in Dei conspectum affers, vbi te humiliari oportebat, 1. Pet. 5. Si mile supplicis coram rege. Vide quæ de vestium necessariarum cura dicuntur, Luc. 12. Mat. 6. Item quæ habes If 3.
units.tr: 2. What sort of people bring pride and luxury into the temples? Those like Agrippa. It is a huge sin. There is great levity in not considering that you are dust, and where clothing comes from (Gen. 3). You offend many, either by lust, or by example, or by giving occasion for impatience, and so incur the sentence found in Matt. 18. There is great perversity in bringing this into God's sight, where you ought to be humbled (1 Pet. 5). It is like a suppliant before a king. See what is said about care for necessary clothing (Luke 12; Matt. 6), and likewise what you have in Isa. 3.

units.la: II. Paulus iubente Festo producitur, catenis vinctus, vt ex ipsius sermone patebit, non tamen vt reus ad iudices, sed vt dominus Ecclesiastes, &c. Hic vero Nota.
units.tr: II. Paul is brought at Festus's command, bound in chains, as will be clear from his own speech; yet he is not brought as a defendant before judges, but as a minister of the Church, etc. Here note:

units.la: ¶ 1. Mirum Dei consilium, quo fit, vt auro & ostro redimiti Paulum vinctum exspectent, & audire cupiant. Imo eidem in vinculis occasionem offert fortiter pro suo nomine agendi, Act. 9.
units.tr: 1. A wonderful counsel of God, by which men adorned with gold and purple await Paul in chains and long to hear him. Indeed, God offers him in his chains an opportunity to act boldly for his name (Acts 9).

units.la: Vides quàm nihil proficiant impij contra filijs suis. Iudaei hoc vnum quaerebant, vt Pauli doctrinam extinguerent. Id vero adeo non assequuntur, vt sua opera Paulo auditores adducant, qui nunquam alias audituri fuissent. Impletur quod est Psal. 2.33. Non timeamus ergo. Eadem adhuc Dei potentia. Fiet similiter, quod praedictum Mar. 13. Matt. 28. Rom. 11.
units.tr: See how little the ungodly accomplish against his sons. The Jews sought only this, to extinguish Paul's teaching. But they fail so completely that by their own efforts they bring hearers to Paul who would never otherwise have heard him. What is written in Ps. 2:3 is fulfilled. Let us not fear. The same power of God is still at work. What was foretold in Mark 13, Matt. 28 and Rom. 11 will likewise come to pass.

units.la: ¶ 2. Paulum. Qualem se gesserit, oratio docet. Non mouetur aspectu Regis & procerum. Deinde intrepidus causam agit, sic vt ipse vinctus terrorem incutiat auditoribus, adeoq; ipsi Agrippae. Ita supra cum Felice agit, Act 24.
units.tr: 2. Paul. His speech shows how he conducted himself. He is not moved by the sight of the King and the nobles. Then he pleads his cause fearlessly, so that he himself, though bound, strikes terror into his hearers, and so into Agrippa himself. In the same way he dealt with Felix above (Acts 24).

units.la: Obseruabis hic: A. Verbum Dei non vincitur ciri, licet ministri vinciantur, 2. Tim. 2. Iohan. 3. Nec enim ex hominibus eius authoritas & effectus dependet. Ioh. 3. Quid ergo vinculis & persecutionibus offendimur? B. Quid nobis in simili casu agendum? dum Intrepidi fimus. Causa bona & gratuis est, ex qua salus nostrae dependet. Non nostra, sed Dei. Agit hanc ipse per nos suo spiritu, Matth. 10. Luc. 12. 21. Mar. 13. Hosti-um potentia nulla, Luc. 12. His animemur, &c.
units.tr: Observe here: A. The Word of God is not bound, even though ministers are bound (2 Tim. 2; John 3). For its authority and effect do not depend on men. Why, then, are we offended by chains and persecutions? B. What must we do in a similar case? Let us be fearless while we are steadfast. The cause is good and free, and our salvation depends on it. It is not ours but God's. He carries it on through us by his Spirit (Matt. 10; Luke 12, 21; Mark 13). The power of enemies is nothing (Luke 12). Let us be encouraged by these things.

units.la: III. Oratio Festi, qua Paulum quasi il-lis sist t, adeo q; illi attentionem conciliat. NOTA. 1. Nouum innocentiae Pauli testimoniū. Opus hoc propter doctrinam, Asserit suorum innocentiam Deus, Psal. 34. Interim elucet insuperabilis Judaeorum equitia, qui talem ad mortem postu lārunt. Sic Ioh. 18. 19. Merito igitur excisi, vt praedictum fuerat, Mat. 23. 24. 21. Luc. 19.
units.tr: III. Festus's speech, by which he presents Paul to them, as it were, and so wins their attention. NOTE: 1. A new testimony to Paul's innocence. This happens because of the doctrine. God asserts the innocence of his people (Ps. 34). Meanwhile the unconquerable injustice of the Jews shines forth, for they demanded such a man's death. So John 18–19. Rightly, then, they were cut off, as had been foretold (Matt. 23, 24, 21; Luke 19).

units.la: ¶ 2. Cum captiuis sic agendum, vt omnium ratio nobis constet. Non ludendum in hominis vita. Si hoc Ethnicus vidit, quid nos decet, qui scimus in his Christo benefieri, Matt 25. Vtinam hodie Papistae Festum sequerentur! Licet vero nobisCU durius agatur, non tamen offendamur, Christum vide, &c. Oremus.
