units.tr: 2. One must deal with captives so that the reason for everything is clear to us. Human life is not to be trifled with. If a heathen saw this, how much more should we do so, who know that in such people Christ is benefited (Matt. 25)! Would that the Papists today would follow Festus! Although we may be treated more harshly, let us not be offended; look to Christ, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XXVI. HOMILIA CXCI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVI. HOMILY CXCI.

units.la: A Grippa vero ad Paulum ait: Per mittitur tibi pro te ipso dicere.
units.tr: Then Agrippa said to Paul: "You are permitted to speak in your own defence."

units.la: Tunc Paulus extenta manu, hac defen-sione vsus est.
units.tr: Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defence.

units.la: 2 Super omnibus, de quibus postu-lor à Iudaeis, Rex Agrippa, beatum me duco, quòd sim hodie causam apud te di-cturus:
units.tr: 2 "King Agrippa, I count myself happy that I am to make my defence before you today concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews,

units.la: 3 Maxime quod te gnarum esse sci-am omnium, quae apud Iudaeos sunt & rituum & quaestionum. Ideo rogo te, ut patienter me audias.
units.tr: 3 especially because I know you to be expert in all the customs and questions that are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.

units.la: 4 Itaque vitam meam a iuuen-tute, quae a principio fuit in gente mea Hierosolymis, sciunt omnes Iudaei, etc. ad verf. 6.
units.tr: 4 My manner of life from my youth, which from the beginning was spent among my own nation at Jerusalem, is known to all the Jews, etc. to verse 6."

units.la: Dominus noster Iesus Christus de Paulo loquens inter alia in-quit: Organum electum est mihi, ut portet nomen meum coram gentibus & regib. ac filijs Israel. Quae verba, ut Pauli ministerium commendant, ita nos excitare debent ad diligentè confi-derationem actionum Pauli, cùm conster, nihil illi sine Dei prouidentia accidisse. Et hoc quidè cumprimis in praesenti hac ob-seruemus, quia coram Agrippa & tota gen-tis huius nobilitate fidè & doctrinam suam ea constantia defendit, ut non officij mo-do admoneamur omnes, verùmetiâ difca-mus, quàm efficax verbi Dei & verae fidei effectus sit. Singula ergo ordine videam9.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ, speaking of Paul, said among other things: "He is a chosen vessel to me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, kings and the children of Israel." These words commend Paul's ministry, and they ought to stir us to a careful consideration of Paul's actions, since it is certain that nothing happened to him without God's providence. We should observe this especially now, because before Agrippa and the whole nobility of this nation he defends his faith and teaching with such constancy that we are reminded not only of our duty but also learn how effective the Word of God and the true faith are. Let us therefore look at each point in order.

units.la: I. Agrippa liberam facit dicendi copiam. Quod Dei prouidentia factum fuisse constat, qui hac occasione Euangelium iis hominibus praedicari voluit. Quia enim vult nos omnes saluos fieri (1. Tim. 2.) salutis quoq; verbum omnibus reuelari vult, Mar.13. & 16. Matt.28. Act. 1. Quod eius consilium adeo firmum est, ut nemo obstare possit, Ioh.3. Act.2. Pfal.2.
units.tr: I. Agrippa gives him free liberty to speak. That this came about by God's providence is clear, since by this occasion he willed the Gospel to be preached to these men. For since he wills all of us to be saved (1 Tim. 2), he also wills the word of salvation to be revealed to all (Mark 13 and 16, Matt. 28, Acts 1). This counsel of his is so firm that no one can oppose it (John 3, Acts 2, Ps. 2).

units.la: Seruiat hoc consolationi. Interim Nota. Æquitatis & iustitiae exemplu. Audiuerat Paulum a tota gente Iudaeorum pe ti ad mortem. Nihil ex illo poterat spera re. Non tamen illo praeiudicio mouetur, sed ipsum quoq; audiendum esse censet. Ita faciant Iudaei. Quo plures vident ali cuius hostes, & quo importunius illi agat, co maiori diligentia sibi opus esse intelli gant, ne sua negligentia aliorum improbitatem iuuent. Huc pertinet Deut.1. Patet hic infelix fidelium nostri seculi fors, quando ab episcopis, &c. accusati, defendendi se copiam non habent.
units.tr: Let this serve for comfort. Meanwhile, note an example of fairness and justice. Paul had heard that the whole nation of the Jews sought his death. Nothing could be hoped for from them. Yet Agrippa is not moved by that prejudice, but judges that he too ought to be heard. Let the Jews act so. The more enemies someone has, and the more insistently they press, the more diligence they understand they need, lest by their own negligence they help the wickedness of others. To this belongs Deut. 1. Here is seen the unhappy lot of the faithful in our age, when they are accused by bishops, etc., and do not have the opportunity to defend themselves.

units.la: II. Paulus mox dicere orditur praesentia & alacri animo, cuius indicium est, quod manu protendit p more veteri. No. Ve ritate & effectu promissionum Christi. Habuit Paulus generales promissiones, Mat.10
units.tr: II. Paul at once begins to speak with a present and cheerful mind, the sign of which is that he stretches out his hand in the old manner. Note: the truth and effect of Christ's promises. Paul had general promises (Matt. 10,

units.la: Mar.13. Luc.12.21. Deinde particularem: Act 9. H s quia credidit,in omni periculo stat inperterritus. Vide Act. 21.22.23.&c. Discamus ipsi quoq; non terreri,quia pro missiones hæ etiam noftrę sunt,Ioh 14.16.
units.tr: Mark 13, Luke 12:21). Then a particular one (Acts 9): "He who believes stands undaunted in every danger." See Acts 21, 22, 23, etc. Let us also learn not to be terrified, since these promises are ours too (John 14, 16).

units.la: Porrò quoad orationem Pauli, narratione argumentosa coftat,ad fui defensionem accommodata.Narrat enim vt vixerit ab initio,quomodo ad Christi fide per uenerit,quomodo fe gesserit in sua vocatione,quod nihil noui docuerit, & proinde immerito hoc odium sustineat,&c.
units.tr: Moreover, as to Paul's speech, it is a narrative full of arguments, fitted to his own defence. For he tells how he lived from the beginning, how he came to faith in Christ, how he conducted himself in his calling, and that he taught nothing new, and therefore bears this hatred undeservedly, etc.

units.la: I. Exordio commodissimo beneuolen tiam captat à regis persona,dum fe beatu putat in eo,quod coram ipso causam hanc agere debeat,qui & ritus & quæstiones Iudæorum intelligat.Frustra enim apud ignaros rerum disputatur.
units.tr: I. In a most suitable opening he wins goodwill from the king's person, while he counts himself happy that he must plead this cause before one who understands both the customs and the questions of the Jews. For it is vain to dispute before those ignorant of the matters.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Magistratus non iusti tiæ modo studiosos,sed prudentia, & vsu rerum debere instrui. Ipsos decere,vt religionis causam probè intelligant: imò etiam tueantur. Sunt enim à Deo ordinati, & huius vicarij,Rom.13.Pfal 82.72. Huius ergo honore cumprimis afferere debent, & obstare ijs,quæ hanc obscurant. Hinc illud Deut.17.&c. Exempla sunt in sanctissimis regibus. Hodie eo nomine sibi pietatis titulum vendicant Reges,quod religionis
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: magistrates ought to be instructed not only in zeal for justice but also in prudence and experience of affairs. It becomes them to understand the cause of religion properly, and indeed also to defend it. For they are ordained by God and are his vicars (Rom. 13; Ps. 82, 72). Therefore, above all, they ought to assert the honour of this, and to oppose those who obscure it. Hence that passage of Deut. 17, etc. There are examples in the most holy kings. Today kings claim the title of piety for themselves on this ground, that they think the cause of religion has nothing to do with them, etc.

units.la: gionis ligionis causam nihil ad fe pertinere putent,&c. Debetur hoc pontificum tyrannidi, qui in regum ignorantia suam potentiam consistere vident.
units.tr: ...ion, the cause of religion. This is owed to the tyranny of the popes, who see their power resting on the ignorance of kings.

units.la: II. Narratione ab anteaſtæ vitæ primor Pauli pue- ritu & e- dit,ipsos Iudæos testes citans, iuxta illud, ducatio. Inter hos vixi à pueris,non obfcu-rus,sed Hierosolymis, vbi schola,&c. Vitæ genus, laudatiffima Pharifæorum festam secutus. Præfertur hæc aliis: tum quod de scripturis sanctius sentirent,tum quod honestius etiam viuerent. Interim in eo impingebant, quòd operum iustitiam & meritum statuebant, Luc.18. Matth.6.23. Finis & fcopus Pauli est,fe nihil vel impio vel leui animi proposito fecisse, nec teme-ré accusari debere,&c.
units.tr: II. From the narrative of his earlier life, Paul relates his childhood and upbringing, citing the Jews themselves as witnesses, according to that: "I lived among them from boyhood, not in obscurity, but at Jerusalem, where the school..." The manner of life of the most praised sect of the Pharisees he followed. This is preferred to the others, both because they thought more soundly about the Scriptures and because they lived more honourably. Yet in this they stumbled, that they set up the righteousness and merit of works (Luke 18; Matt. 6, 23). The aim and purpose of Paul is to show that he has done nothing with an impious or frivolous intention, and that he ought not to be rashly accused, etc.

units.la: No T. ¶ 1. In publicis personis multùm referre, qualis quis à pueris fuerit. Licet enim non reijci debeant,qui ferió conuer-tuntur,præferendi tamen alteris illi. Con-ftantius agunt,& minus sunt expositi calumnijs. In alteris verò illis iuuentutis vitia feré tenacius hærent, & authoritatem adimunt, dum mali habent quod expro-brent. Imò bonis,etiam suspecta sunt illorum consilia,dum metuunt,ne quid ex leuitate faciant. Magna ergo educationis ratio haberi debet in talibus.
units.tr: Note 1. In public persons it matters greatly what sort of person someone was from boyhood. For although those who are converted late should not be rejected, yet the others are to be preferred. They act more steadily and are less exposed to slanders. But in the others the vices of youth cling more tenaciously and take away their authority, since wicked men have something to reproach them with. Indeed, even to good men their counsels are suspect, since they fear that something may be done out of levity. Great account, therefore, must be taken of education in such people.

units.la: {q}Quid obseruandum maximè in educatione liberorum? Paulus de seipso duo potissimum dicit. A Quòd in sua gente locatus sit, & quidem Hierosolymis, vbi religio patria maximè florebat. Cauendum ergo, ne inter alienos à religione educentur iuniores. Hodie fere diuites suos inter Papistas, aut etiam in castris educare solent, &c.
units.tr: Question: what is to be especially observed in the education of children? Paul says two main things about himself. (A) That he was placed among his own nation, and indeed at Jerusalem, where the religion of the fathers flourished most. Care must therefore be taken lest young people be brought up among those alienated from religion. Today the rich usually educate their sons among the Papists, or even in camps, etc.

units.la: B. Optimum vitæ genus deligant ab initio, in quo minima vitiorum occasio. Per se enim iuuentus ad peccandum procliuis est. At nostri fere solius quæstus rationem habent. Hinc enascuntur homines, penes quos nulla religio, nulla denique constantia, & qui patriam venalem habent, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: (B) Let them choose the best way of life from the beginning, one in which there is least occasion for vices. For youth is by itself prone to sin. But our people mostly consider only the reckoning of profit. From this spring men with no religion and in the end no constancy, who have their country for sale, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXCII.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXCII.

units.la: 6 Nunc vero ob spem promissionis factæ patribus nostris à Deo, sto in iudicium vocatus.
units.tr: 6 But now I stand here on trial, for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers.

units.la: 7 Ad quam duodecim tribus nostræ, Deo noctu & die perpetuò seruien tes, sperant se peruenturas: de qua spe po stulor, Rex Agrippa, à Iudæis.
units.tr: 7 To this hope our twelve tribes, serving God night and day, hope to attain; and it is concerning this hope, King Agrippa, that I am accused by the Jews.

units.la: 8 Quid? incredibile iudicatur apud vos quòd Deus mortuos excitet?
units.tr: 8 Why is it judged incredible among you that God should raise the dead?

units.la: Paulus Apostolus fidei & doctrinæ suæ rationem reddituros, in hoc maximè incumbit, vt offendat, nihil absque temerè aut impiè factum esse. Et in hunc finem, quæ ipsius educatio & institutio à pueris fuerit, docuit. Vbi simul didicimus, ita in religione nobis versandum esse, vt ab ipsa pueritia huius rationem reddere possimus. Vt enim omnis ætatis tutor est Deus, ab ipso vtero matris (Psal.22.10. Ier.1. &c.) Ita omnem quoq; ætatem huic concessam & addictam esse conuenit. Vide Deut.6. Exod.13.
units.tr: The Apostle Paul, knowing that he must render an account of his faith and doctrine, labours chiefly to show that nothing has been done rashly or impiously. To this end he teaches what his upbringing and training were from boyhood. From this we learn at the same time that we ought to live in religion in such a way that we can give an account of it from our very childhood. For just as God is the guardian of every age, from the very womb of the mother (Ps. 22.10; Jer. 1, etc.), so it is fitting that every age is granted to this and committed to it. See Deut. 6; Exod. 13.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui religionis causam ita intricatam esse putant, vt eius tractatio non pertineat ad laicos. Atqui nihil ita ex æquo ad omnes homines pertinet.
units.tr: Those are rebuked who think the cause of religion so entangled that its discussion does not belong to laymen. Yet nothing pertains equally to all men as this does.

units.la: Sequitur status totius causæ. Dicit ei sacrifari de spe promissionis patribus facta, & in quam tota gens Israelis respexerit. Idem repetit. Habet autem propositio speciem quandam indignationis. Quasi dicat: Quis non videat, quàm iniqui sint mei aduersarij &c. Porrò spes illa, de qua loquitur, Christus est, in quo patribus salus & vita promissa fuit. Quia verò Christi tum diuina potentia, tum officium in resurrectione potissimum elucet, (Ro. 1.) huius præ aliis meminit. Cùm enim
units.tr: Next comes the state of the whole case. He says that he was called to account for the hope of the promise made to the fathers, the hope on which the whole nation of Israel had fixed its gaze. He repeats the same point. The statement carries a certain air of indignation, as if he were saying: "Who does not see how unjust my adversaries are?" etc. Moreover, that hope of which he speaks is Christ, in whom life and salvation were promised to the fathers. But since the divine power of Christ, and above all his office, shine forth in the resurrection (Ro. 1.), he mentions this above the rest.

units.la: seipsum ex morte asseruerit, ipsum Dei Filium: adhæc vitæ & salutis esse authorem omnibus constare potest, Iohan. 11.6. 1. Corinth. 15. Nec dubium est pluribus hæc tractata fuisse. Interim obseruemus.
units.tr: For when he has asserted that he himself rose from death, and that he is God's Son, it can be agreed by all that he is also the author of life and salvation (John 11.6; 1 Cor. 15.). Nor is there doubt that many have treated these matters. Meanwhile let us observe the following.

units.la: I. Quæ omnium sanctorum, adeoque veræ Ecclesiæ fides & spes semper fuerit. Ea nimirum, quæ Christo nititur, & in uno hoc vitam & salutem sitam esse credit. Docet hoc ipse Christus, Iohan. 5.8. Lucæ 24. Paulus item 1. Cor. 10. 2. Cor. 1. Euidenter vero hoc ipsum patet, si patres simul & promissiones Dei in spicias ab ipsa mundi origine. Adam, Genes. 3. Semen mulieris. Credidit Adam, & ideo He ua dixit, &c. Abel, Henoch, Noe, &c. Hebr. 11. Abraham. Credidit, &c. Roman. 4. Quid vero credidit? Vide Genes. 12. 22. Iohan. 8. Galat. 3. Isaac, Genes. 26. Iacob, Gen. 28. & 29. Mosem, Iohan. 5. Deuter. 18. Actor. 7. Typos legales. Agnus paschalis, Exod. 12. Ioh. 1.1. Cor. 5. Manna, Exod. 16. Iohan. 6. Petra fonte scaturiens, Exod. 17. 1. Cor. 10. Serpens, Num. 21. Ioh. 3. Totus cultus Leuiticus, Hebr. 7.8. 9.10. Prophetæ omnes & Psalmi, &c. Luc. 24. 2. Pet. 1. Recte ergo Paulus hic pronunciat, &c. Vides quæ sit fides vetustissima.
units.tr: I. That the faith and hope of all the saints, and so of the true Church, has always been the same: the faith that rests on Christ and believes that life and salvation are found in him alone. Christ himself teaches this (John 5.8; Luke 24.), and Paul likewise (1 Cor. 10.; 2 Cor. 1.). This is plainly evident if we look into the fathers and God's promises from the very beginning of the world. Adam: the seed of the woman (Gen. 3.). Adam believed, and therefore Eve called her name..., etc. Abel, Enoch, Noah, etc. (Heb. 11.). Abraham believed, etc. (Rom. 4.). But what did he believe? See Gen. 12.; 22.; John 8.; Gal. 3. Isaac (Gen. 26.); Jacob (Gen. 28. and 29.); Moses (John 5.; Deut. 18.; Acts 7.). The legal types: the paschal lamb (Exod. 12.; John 1.; 1 Cor. 5.); the manna (Exod. 16.; John 6.); the rock gushing with water (Exod. 17.; 1 Cor. 10.); the serpent (Num. 21.; John 3.); the whole Levitical worship (Heb. 7.; 8.; 9.; 10.). All the prophets and Psalms, etc. (Luke 24.; 2 Pet. 1.). Rightly, therefore, does Paul here declare, etc. You see what the most ancient faith is.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Quòd de hac ipsa fide, se accusari queritur; & quidè apud Iudæos. Docet hoc, quæ veritatis & fidei fors sit in hoc mundo. Non modò ab apertis hostibus petitur, verùmetiam ijs, qui huius ie&atores haberi volunt. Sic factum tempore prophetarum. 1. Reg. 18. &c. Item vide Mat. 23. Sic Christo euenisse dicitur, Ioh. 1.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: that he complains of being accused over this very faith, and indeed by the Jews. This teaches what the lot of truth and faith is in this world. It is attacked not only by open enemies, but also by those who wish to be counted among its champions. So it happened in the time of the prophets (1 Kings 18., etc.). See also Matt. 23. So it is said to have happened to Christ (John 1.).

units.la: Hodie hoc ipsum fit. Gloriamur Christi nomine, & propter hunc Virginè matrem, Diuos, imò res inanimatas, colimus. Interim si quis vni Christo redemptionis nostræ gloriam vendicet, iuxta illud Isa. 42. Act. 4. Gal. 6. 1. Tim. 1. 2. 1. Ioh. 1. 2. &c. mox hæreticos accusatur. Deploranda improbitas & coecitas. Sed non offendamur, Luc. 2. Ioh. 15. &c.
units.tr: Today this very thing is happening. We boast in the name of Christ, and yet on account of this Virgin mother we worship saints and even inanimate things. Meanwhile, if anyone claims the glory of our redemption for Christ alone, according to that word of Isaiah 42., Acts 4., Gal. 6., 1 Tim. 1., 1 John 1., 2., etc., he is at once accused of heresy. This is a deplorable wickedness and blindness. But let us not be offended (Luke 2.; John 15., etc.).

units.la: II. Quomodo fidem & doctrinam suam Paulus afferat. Primò promissiones adeo que verbum Dei allegat. Deinde demum duodecim tribus, id est, totius Ecclesiæ consensum, non solos sacerdotes, &c. NOTA ¶ Quæ optima fit afferendæ fidei ratio: Verbum Dei ante omnia obseruetur, quia nulla est humanarum traditionum authoritas, Isa. 29. Matt. 15. Hoc fundamento iacto, Ecclesia quoque obseruetur, in qua non pauci quidam, sed totus grex & ordo
units.tr: II. How Paul sets forth his faith and doctrine. First he appeals to the promises and the word of God; then, finally, to the twelve tribes, that is, to the consent of the whole Church, and not merely to the priests, etc. NOTE: The best method of setting forth the faith is this: the Word of God must be observed before all else, because human traditions have no authority (Isa. 29.; Matt. 15.). With this foundation laid, the Church too is to be observed, in which not a few, but the whole flock and order...

units.la: Cap. 26. populi Dei censeri debet ab origine rerū. Arguuntur Papistæ, qui ordine præpostero procedunt. Primò enim de Ecclesia loquuntur, & hanc ex coniuratis modo constituunt, saruis nimirum. His deinde verbum Dei subiciunt, qui non sunt Ecclesiæ membra. Vide notas Ecclesiæ, 1. Petri 1. Psal. 45. Ioh. 10. Eph. 5. 2. Cor. 11.
units.tr: But note that in the present place he appeals to God's power alone. He does this on account of the weakness of our senses, which thinks nothing can happen except what it sees the reason for itself. He therefore teaches us to look to the power of God (Phil. 3).

units.la: III. Quod resurrectionem præalijs artis culis adducit, & quidem non sine indigna tionis specie. Opus hoc; quia Sadducæi & Epicuræi obtinuerant, qui hac doctrina maximè terrentur. Felix Act. 24. Quasi dicat: Mirum est, de hac aliquem dubitare, cum tot huius extent argumenta. Requirit hanc Dei iustitia, quæ alioqui non posset subsistere. Exempla sunt passim. In plantis arboribus, ipsa terra. In primi hominis creatione, Gen. 1. 2. In ijs, qui miraculosè reuixerunt, 1. Reg. 17. 2. Reg. 4. Mat. 9. Luc. 7. Ioh. 11. &c.
units.tr: III. That he brings up the resurrection along with other arguments, and indeed not without an air of indignation. This was necessary because the Sadducees and Epicureans had gained the upper hand, and it is especially this doctrine that terrifies them (Felix, Acts 24.). As if he were saying: it is strange that anyone should doubt this, when so many proofs of it exist. God's justice requires it, which otherwise could not stand. Examples are everywhere: in plants and trees, in the earth itself. In the creation of the first man (Gen. 1.; 2.). In those who were miraculously restored to life (1 Kings 17.; 2 Kings 4.; Matt. 9.; Luke 7.; John 11., etc.).

units.la: Sed NoT. Quod in præsenti solam Dei potentiam allegat. Facit hoc propter nostri sensus imbecillitatem, qui nihil fieri putat, quàm cuius rationem ipse videt. Docet ergo ad Dei potentiam respicere, vt Phil. 3.
units.tr: But note: that here he appeals only to the power of God. He does this because of the weakness of our senses, which think that nothing can happen unless they themselves see its reason. He therefore teaches us to look to the power of God (Phil. 3.).

units.la: Obseruandum hoc in alijs quoq; vt intellestum carnis fidei obedientiæ subijciamus,2.Cor.10.Interim non audiendi, qui hoc praetextu noua dogmata obtrudunt, &c. Nos constantes simus in spe patrum, &c.Oremus.
units.tr: This is to be observed in other matters too: that we bring the understanding of the flesh under the obedience of faith (2 Cor. 10.). Meanwhile, those who push new dogmas on us under this pretext are not to be heard, etc. Let us stand firm in the hope of the fathers, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXCIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXCIII.

units.la: 9 Equidem statueram mihi aduersus nomen Iesu Nazareni multa con traria facienda.
units.tr: 9 I had indeed resolved to do many things hostile to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

units.la: 10 Quod etiam feci Hierosol. et multos sanctorum ego carceribus inclu si, a principibus sacerdotum potestate accepta, quum ab eis interimeretur, tuli suffragium. et c. adver. vfq; 16.
units.tr: 10 And this I also did at Jerusalem: I shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received the power from the chief priests, and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them. And so on, down to verse 16.

units.la: PAulus Apostolus totius controuer- siae, quae sibi cum Iudaeis intercedat, statum in hesternis exposuit, nimirum de humanae salutis ratione lite ipsis esse. Probauit autem se non aliud docere vel credere, quam quod olim Deus patribus promiserit, & in quo omnis Israeliticae Ecclesiae spes sita fit. Didicimus eo loco Christia nam fidem omnium vetustissimam, adeoque vnicam esse, per quam patres omnes saluati sint. Deinde controuersias de fide ex Dei verbo dirimi debere, in quo sancti omnes omnibus seculis consenserint. Porro, quia initio se a pueris Pharisaeum fuisse dixerat, commodè nunc ad rerum suarum narrationem redit, conuersio {Cap. 26.} nis suæ historiam exponens. Scopus om-nium est, ut leuitatis crimen excuset, quan-do se diuinitus vocatum, imò coactu suis- se probat.
units.tr: The Apostle Paul, having set out the state of the whole controversy that lies between him and the Jews, explained yesterday that the matter at issue is the manner of human salvation. He showed that he teaches and believes nothing other than what God long ago promised the fathers, and in which the whole hope of the Israelite Church rests. We learned in that place that the Christian faith is the most ancient of all and therefore the only one, through which all the fathers were saved. Next, that controversies about faith ought to be settled by the Word of God, in which all the saints have agreed in every age. Moreover, since he had said at the beginning that he had been a Pharisee from boyhood, he now fitly returns to the narration of his own affairs, setting out the history of his conversion {Chap. 26.}. The aim of the whole is to excuse the charge of levity, since he proves that he was called by God, or rather compelled.

units.la: 1. Exponit quomodo erga Christum & fidem Christianam affectus fuerit, & qui-dem multis. 1. Causam omnium præmittit: Putabat me oportere multa facere contra Chri-stum. Vnde hoc? Primùm ex eo quòd se vi-deret in authoritate esse: Deinde ex zelo carnis, quem alibi Iudæis omnibus tribuit Rom. 10. Duo hæc hodie multos decipi-unt. Ita nobis imponit diabolus, Ioh. 16. In terim hic zelus non excusat persecutores. Nam alibi se grauiter peccauisse testatur, 1. Tim. 1. 1. Cor. 15. Quanto minus excusan-tur ergo, qui prauis affectibus abrepti, per sequuntur, &c.
units.tr: 1. He sets out how he was disposed towards Christ and the Christian faith, and that in many ways. 1. He sends ahead the cause of all: "I thought I ought to do many things contrary to Christ." Whence this? First, from the fact that he saw himself to be in authority; then, from the zeal of the flesh, which he elsewhere attributes to all the Jews (Rom. 10). These two things deceive many today. Thus the devil imposes upon us (John 16). Meanwhile this zeal does not excuse the persecutors. For elsewhere he testifies that he had sinned grievously (1 Tim. 1; 1 Cor. 15). How much less, then, are those excused who, carried away by perverse affections, persist, etc.

units.la: Notr. ¶ Hostium Ecclesiæ conatus me-ram opinionem esse, & vanos carnis con-ceptus, qui nunquam finem suum attin-gunt, vtut videantur procedere, Psa. 7. Ri-det enim huiusmodi conatus Deus. & qua si per ludibrium exertit. Psal. 2. 3. Exem-pla habes in tyrannis, Achabo, Pharaone, Romanis Imperatoribus. Hodie. Ne ergo his offendamur Id occultè innuit, vt quid ipsis exspectandum sit, intelligant.
units.tr: Note. The attempts of the enemies of the Church are mere opinion, and the vain conceptions of the flesh, which never reach their end, however much they seem to advance (Ps. 7). For God laughs at such attempts, and as it were mocks them (Ps. 2). You have examples in tyrants: Ahab, Pharaoh, the Roman emperors. Today likewise. So that we may not be offended by these things, he hints at this obscurely, that they may understand what is to be expected for themselves.

units.la: II. Facta quoq; commemorat, ne quis Thra-
units.tr: II. He also recounts his deeds, lest anyone think he was a braggart

units.la: Thrasonem fuisse putaret. Multos sanctorum, id est, Christianorum (1. Cor. 5. 6. Ephes. 5. &c.) inclusi carceribus, potestate nimirum a sacerdotibus acceptâ, quâ non dedi-sent, nisi serió vidissent agere. Deinde cùm occiderentur detuli sententiam Act. 8. In synagogis per tormenta excruciaui, & coegi blasphemare, abnegando scilicet & recantando. Ergo primitiua quoq; Ecclesia suas habuit quisquilias. Et vt plus satis insani-rem, in exteras quoque ciuitates contendi, Act. 9. &c.
units.tr: a braggart. "I shut up many of the saints," that is, of the Christians (1 Cor. 5, 6; Eph. 5, etc.), "in prisons, having received the power, namely, from the priests," which they would not have given unless they had seen that he was acting in earnest. "Then, when they were being put to death, I gave my sentence" (Acts 8). "In the synagogues I punished them with torments and compelled them to blaspheme," that is, by denying and recanting. Therefore the primitive Church too had its trifles. And that I might be utterly mad enough, "I pressed on even into foreign cities" (Acts 9, etc.).

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Imaginem persecutorum, & quid pios ferè maneat. Odio sunt summis, ijs maximè, qui religionis titulum sibi vendicantes, interim priuatae gloriae & quaestui studentes, Ioh. 5. 2. Matt. 21. Hi deinde idoneos habent scelerum ministros, qui non dormitant, vt etiam apparet Luc. 22. Sequuntur ergo carceres, condemnationes, blasphemiae &c. Adhaec praeparemur, Matt. 10. Ioh. 15. 16.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. The picture of persecutors, and what remains for the pious. They are hateful to the highest, especially to those who, claiming the title of religion for themselves, meanwhile seek private glory and gain (John 5; Matt. 21). These then have fit ministers of crimes, who do not sleep, as is also apparent from Luke 22. Thus there follow prisons, condemnations, blasphemies, etc. Let us prepare ourselves for these things (Matt. 10; John 15, 16).

units.la: ¶ 2. Quid faciunt persecutores, qui fidem Christi extinctam volunt? Blasphemare cogunt, dum nimirum vrgent homines, vt reclamante conscientia Christi fidem abnegent, feque erraiffe profitentur. Blasphemia est, quia Deum falsi arguunt, & scripturas negant, Dei honorem in
units.tr: 2. What do persecutors do who wish the faith of Christ extinguished? They compel blasphemy, while they press people, so that, with conscience protesting, they deny Christ and profess that they have erred. It is blasphemy, because they charge God with falsehood and deny the Scriptures, transferring the honour of God to creatures.

units.la: Pauli contra Ecclesiam tyrannum.
units.tr: Paul against the tyrant of the Church.

units.la: Ecclesia cunctis.
units.tr: The Church against all.

units.la: Persecutores blasphemare cogunt. creaturas transferunt.Est hæc species pec cati in Spiritum,sanctum vt patet ex Luc. 12. Sequitur ferè, vt tales aperti quoque hostes fiant,& tandem desperent. In hoc ergo authores proprie quadrat, quod de scandalo dicitur, Matt.18. Vtinam ista quidam expeaderent,qui autipfi cogunt, aut conniuent vel consentiunt,Pfal.1.
units.tr: Persecutors compel to blaspheme. This is a kind of sin against the Holy Spirit, as is clear from Luke 12. It almost follows that such men become open enemies as well, and at last despair. In this, therefore, what is said of scandal in Matthew 18 fits the authors properly. Would that certain men would consider these things, who either compel these things themselves or connive at them or consent (Ps. 1).

units.la: ¶3.Quod dedecus suum tam multis tam que aperte Paulus exponit. Num vt hoc glorietur more impiorum? Pfal.52. Mini, mè. Sed quia hoc ad Dei gloriam cedere nouerat.Præter illud enim quod suum mi nifterium sic asserit,etiam Dei bonitatem commendat erga peccatores. Sic ipse exponit,1.Tim.10. Ideo frequenter horum meminit, vt etiam Act.22 Gal.1. Phil.3. 1. Cor.15.Ita solent sancti,Pfal.51.&c.
units.tr: 3. Paul sets out his own disgrace so openly and so fully. Is it that he might boast of this in the manner of the impious? (Ps. 52). Far from it. But because he knew this would redound to the glory of God. For besides asserting thus his own ministry, he also commends the goodness of God towards sinners. He himself explains this (1 Tim. 1). Therefore he often mentions these things, as also in Acts 22, Gal. 1, Phil. 3, 1 Cor. 15. So the saints are accustomed to do (Ps. 51, etc.).

units.la: Arguitur illorum ambitio , qui vt suæ modo gloriæ consulant, errores suos nun quam fatentur aut saltem extenuant.
units.tr: Here is censured the ambition of those who, in order to look after their own glory after a fashion, never confess their errors, or at least minimise them.

units.la: II. Conuersione subijcit per ἀντίθεσιν vt ostendat fe contra animi fui voluntas tem fuisse mutatum diuina virtute.Ne ve- ro quis inani spectro delusum putaret,cir cumftantias omnes comemorat. Locum felicet,Tempus,Colloquium Christi,co- mitum quoq; testimonium, &c. Vbi non opus est repetere,quæ de conuersione ad
units.tr: II. He subjoins the conversion by antithesis, to show that he was changed against the will of his own mind by divine power. Lest anyone think he had been deluded by an empty phantom, he recounts all the circumstances: the place, the time, the conversation with Christ, the testimony of his companions, etc. Where there is no need to repeat what has been said elsewhere about conversion to God and the duty of converts.

units.la: Deum & conuersorum officio alibi dicta sunt. Finem & scopum præsentis narratio-nis videamus, qui est, vt vocationem suam asserat. Simul quoque ad illum pertinet, quòd Christi de suo facinore sententiam diligenter repetit, nimirum vt omnibus fidei Christianæ persecutoribus terrorem incutiat, &c.
units.tr: Let us look at the end and aim of the present narration, which is to assert his calling. At the same time it also pertains to this, that he carefully repeats the sentence of Christ upon his crime, namely, so that he may strike terror into all the persecutors of the Christian faith, etc.

units.la: Quare Not. ¶ Quæ horum sors sit & conditio? A. Christum Dei Filium perse-quuntur. Quid atrocius dicitur, propter communionem, quæ nobis cum illo est, Eph.5. Hoc idem alibi pronuntiat ipse Matthæi 25. Zach.2.
units.tr: Hence the note: What is the lot and condition of these men? A. They persecute the Son of God Christ. What more atrocious can be said, on account of the communion which we have with him (Eph. 5)? He himself declares the same thing elsewhere (Matt. 25; Zech. 2).

units.la: B. Durum ipsis est, adeoque noxium. Nam contra stimulum calcitrant. Vide Zachriæ 12. Exempla sunt passim obuia. Vide exempla Imperatorum. Terreantur hi impij, & inde consolationem percipiant. Oremus.
units.tr: B. It is hard for them, and therefore hurtful. For they kick against the goad. See Zechariah 12. Examples are everywhere at hand. See the examples of the emperors. Let these impious men be terrified, and let them thence receive consolation. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXCIV.
units.tr: Homily 194.

units.la: 16 Sed exurge, & sta in pedes tuos: idcirco enim apparui tibi, vt designarem te ministrum ac testem, tum eorum quæ vidisti, tum eorum, in quibus apparebo tibi.
units.tr: 16 But rise up and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a minister and a witness both of the things you have seen and of the things in which I will appear to you.

units.la: 17 Eruens te ex hoc populo, & gentibus, in quas nunc te mitto.
units.tr: 17 Rescuing you from this people and from the Gentiles, to whom I now send you.

units.la: 18 Vt aperias oculos eorum, vt se conuertant a tenebris ad lucem, & a potestate Satanae ad Deum, vt remissionem peccatorum, &c.
units.tr: 18 To open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins, etc.

units.la: Quoniam Paulus se à Iudæis de duobus potissimum accusari noue-rat, quòd nimirum à Iudaismo ad Christi fidem transfuisset, & quod Euangelium gentibus prædicando, has Iudæis æquaret: luæ conuersionis historiam diligentissimè narrat, qua vtrumque crimen clariss ime diluebatur: Ad primum enim pertinent quæ hucusque dicta sunt, quibus probauit, se nō animi leuitate, sed Deo vocante præter animi voluntatem ad Christum transfiuisse. Secundum in præsenti diluitur, vbi ex ipsius Christi verbis totius ministerij sui rationem reddit. Continent haec & ministerij & salutis nostræ rationem plenissimam. Videamus ergo singula ordine.
units.tr: Since Paul knew that the Jews chiefly accused him of two things, namely that he had passed from Judaism to the faith of Christ, and that by preaching the Gospel to the Gentiles he was placing them on a level with the Jews, Luke carefully narrates the history of his conversion, by which both charges are most clearly refuted. For what has been said so far pertains to the first charge, showing that he went over to Christ not from levity of mind but by God's calling, against his own inclination. The second is refuted here, where he gives an account of the whole of his ministry from the words of Christ himself. These words contain the most complete account both of the ministry and of our salvation. Let us therefore consider each point in order.

units.la: I. Christus Paulum, quem ante prostrauerat, surgere iubet. Suppplendum verò ex Act. 9. quòd de Domini voluntate supplex quodammodo quæsiuit.
units.tr: I. Christ bids Paul, whom he had previously struck down, to rise. One must supply from Acts 9 that he sought the Lord's will in a kind of supplication.

units.la: Nota. Deum etiam in ira sua bonitatis non obliuisci. Vult enim saluos fieri homines 1. Tim. 2. Docet ergo primum per verbum & monet, Quòd si nihil proficiat, virvirgam profert, non alio tamen animo, quàm vt saluet ad se conuersos. Vide Amoz 4.5. Isa.9. Et vt primum humiliati, de ipsius voluntate quaerimus, rursum erigit, nec in perpetuum irascitur, Psal.103. Exempla publica & priuata. Haec ad omnes afflictiones transferamus, vt nobis consolationi sint, Heb 12.
units.tr: Note: that God, even in his anger, does not forget his goodness. For he wills that men be saved (1 Tim. 2). He therefore first teaches through the word and admonishes; but if this accomplishes nothing, he brings forth the rod, yet with no other intention than to save those who are converted to him. See Amos 4 and 5; Isa. 9. And when we, having been humbled, seek his will, he raises us up again, and he does not remain angry forever (Ps. 103). Examples, public and private. Let us apply this to all afflictions, so that they may be a consolation to us (Heb. 12).

units.la: II. Maximo muneri illu destinat, & quo nullum honorificentius, apostolatui nimi rum: quod singulare fuit gratiae argumentum, vt ipse fatetur, 1. Cor.15. 1.Tim.1. &c. Definit autem munus hoc, in quo omnium ministrorum officium NOT. ¶ 1. Mi- nistri sunt. Ita passim nominantur, & tales quidem qui toti Ecclesiae seruiant, vt œco nomi,&c. Vide Matth.24. Luc.12. 1.Cor.4. Ideo ipse postea se omnibus debitorem ef se dicit, Roman.1.1.Corinth.9. &c. Excluditur his dominandi libido, quam passim prohibet Christus, vt Matt.18.20. Luc.22. Ioh.13.
units.tr: II. He appoints him to that office, the greatest of all and the most honourable, namely the apostleship, which, as he himself confesses, was a singular proof of grace (1 Cor. 15; 1 Tim. 1, etc.). This office defines the duty of all ministers. Note: ¶ 1. They are ministers. They are called this everywhere, and indeed those who serve the whole Church, as the Greek word implies, etc. See Matt. 24; Luke 12; 1 Cor. 4. Therefore he later calls himself a debtor to all (Rom. 1; 1 Cor. 9, etc.). By this the lust of domination is excluded, which Christ forbids everywhere (Matt. 18; 20; Luke 22; John 13).

units.la: 2. Testes sunt, Act.1. Hoc ad pleniorem ministerij explicationem facit. Nam simul docet de quibus nam testificari debeat. Ijs nimirum quae vidisti. Viderat autem Christum viuere, esse vindicem suorum, redemptorem & Deum verum &c. De his ergo testificari debuit. Sic Apostolis dicitur,
units.tr: 2. They are witnesses (Acts 1). This serves to explain the ministry more fully, for at the same time it teaches what they must testify to: namely, the things you have seen. Paul had seen that Christ lives, that he is the avenger of his own, the Redeemer and true God, etc. Of these things, therefore, he ought to testify. So it is said to the Apostles (Acts 26; John 15; Acts 1).

units.la: Cap. 26. Ioh. 15. Act. 1. Apostoli non erronesfue-runt, sed testes, ab ipso Christo producti. Discimus. A. Quanta Apostolicae doctrinae certitudo sit. Viderunt omnia corām, Ioh. 1. 21. Act 19. 1. Ioh. 1. Miraculis instructi. Consentit Patris testimonium, Matth 3. 17. Vide quid sit contradicere? 1. Ioh. 5.
units.tr: The Apostles were not wanderers but witnesses, produced by Christ himself. We learn: A. How great is the certainty of apostolic doctrine. They saw everything with their own eyes (John 1; 21; Acts 19; 1 John 1). They were furnished with miracles. The Father's testimony agrees (Matt. 3). See what it is to contradict (1 John 5).

units.la: B. Restringi libidinem ministrorum, ne pro suo arbitrio noua dogmata proferat. Testis est comperta loqui, non ficta, nisi falsi accusari velit, &c. Gal. 1.
units.tr: B. The licence of ministers is restrained, lest they put forward new doctrines at their own discretion. A witness speaks of what he has known, not of what he has invented, unless he wishes to be accused of falsehood (Gal. 1).

units.la: III. Quia ex anteactis munus hoc horrere poterat, consolationem subijcit, qua auxilium promittit. Hic vero obiter interfertur mandatum de gentibus quoque vocandis per Euangelium, vt etiam Act. 22. &c.
units.tr: III. Because from what has gone before this office might cause dread, he adds a consolation, in which he promises help. Here, in passing, the command to call the Gentiles also through the Gospel is interposed (see also Acts 22, etc.).

units.la: Sed Notr. 1. Sortem ministrorum, dum omnium salutem student. Omnium oculi expositi crucem subinde sentiunt, a deo vt nullo alio quàm Dei auxilio sustentur. Ita praedixit Christus. Matth. 10. 16. Ioh. 15, 16 21. 2. Tim. 3. Miserē falluntur, qui felicitatem terrenam somniant, & hanc in ministerio quaerunt.
units.tr: But note: 1. The lot of ministers, while they strive for the salvation of all. The eyes of all who are exposed sometimes feel the cross, so that they are sustained by nothing but God's help. Christ foretold this (Matt. 10:16; John 15:16; 21; 2 Tim. 3). Those are sadly mistaken who dream of earthly happiness and seek it in the ministry.

units.la: 2. Deum non deserere suos. Sunt pa-sim promissiones. Psal 34. Ioh. 14. Matt. 28. Hac autem non sic intelligenda, quasi ex omnibus aduersis liberatos otio donet, aut semper liberet. Nam post obtrunca-tur Paulus. Sed quatenus opus est in praesenti, liberat. Dat spiritum, os, sapientiam, &c. Matth. 10. Luc. 12. Mar. 13. Act 4 5 &c. Constantiam in cruce & morte Roman. 5. Transfert in regnum suum. Memoriam quoque tuetur, Psal. 34.
units.tr: 2. God does not forsake his own. There are promises everywhere (Ps. 34; John 14; Matt. 28). These must not be understood as though he grants those freed from all adversities leisure, or always frees them. For Paul was afterwards beheaded. But he frees them as far as is needful for the present: he gives the Spirit, speech, wisdom, etc. (Matt. 10; Luke 12; Mark 13; Acts 4; 5, etc.). He gives constancy in the cross and in death (Rom. 5). He transfers them into his kingdom. He also preserves the memory (Ps. 34).

units.la: IV. Finem totius ministerij exponit, Ut aperias oculos caecorum, &c. Quae ita dicuntur, ut simul omnem redemptionis rationem comprehendant.
units.tr: IV. He sets out the end of the whole ministry: That you may open the eyes of the blind, etc. These words are so spoken that together they comprehend the whole account of redemption.

units.la: In qua Nota. ¶ 1. Ut de hominibus pro huntiet. A. Caeci sumus natura, 1. Cor. 2. Exempla philosophorum. B. Accedunt tenebrae, quas mundus & satan offundut. Erramus ergo in superstitionibus, moribus, &c. C. Sub potestate diaboli, Col. 1. Is in nos potestatem obtinuit per peccatum. Vide gentes. Item omnes qui huic seruiunt, ut a daemoniacis nihil differant.
units.tr: Note in this: ¶ 1. How he speaks of men. A. We are blind by nature (1 Cor. 2). Examples from the philosophers. B. Added to this are the darknesses which the world and Satan cast over us. We therefore err in superstitions, morals, etc. C. We are under the power of the devil (Col. 1). He has obtained power over us through sin. See the Gentiles. Likewise all who serve him, so that they differ in nothing from demoniacs.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quis liberat? Si proprie loquamur, solus Christus, qui lux est, Ioh. 1. 8. 9. Fortis ille Heros, Luc. 11. Gen. 8. Et qui unus nos Patri conciliat, ut vides Matth. 3. 17. Hic autem Paulo ista tribuuntur ratione ministerij Euangelici, quo Christus nobis offertur. Est ergo probe distinguendum in eiusmodi locutionibus, 1. Cor. 3. & 4.
units.tr: ¶ 2. Who frees us? Speaking properly, Christ alone, who is the light (John 1; 8; 9). He is that strong Hero (Luke 11; Gen. 8), and he alone reconciles us to the Father, as you see in Matt. 3. Here, however, these things are attributed to Paul by reason of the Gospel ministry, through which Christ is offered to us. In such expressions one must therefore distinguish carefully (1 Cor. 3 and 4).

units.la: ¶ 5. Medium, quo ista percipiuntur: Fides in Christum.Hæc illi insitos bonorum eius omniū participes reddit. Itaq; sanctificamur fide hac in Christo, & proinde hæ reditatem in sanctis promissam adimus. Symbolum Apostolorum.
units.tr: ¶ 3. The means by which these things are received: faith in Christ. This, being implanted in them, makes them partakers of all his goods. Thus we are sanctified by this faith in Christ, and so we attain the inheritance promised among the saints. The Apostles' Creed.

units.la: ¶ 4. Officium nostrum, vt nos testemur illuminatos esse, opera lucis faciamus, dia bolo renuntiemus, & vni Christo viua- mus, Ephes. 1. Elucet hic mundi ingratitudo, qui in hanc salutis rationem fastidit conuiciatur & perlequitur. Spoliant tales se bonis tantis, & sentiunt quod est Iohan. 5. 2. Thess. 2. Nos constantes simus, & Oremus.
units.tr: ¶ 4. Our duty is that we, testifying that we have been enlightened, do the works of light, renounce the devil, and live to Christ alone (Eph. 1). Here the ingratitude of the world shines forth, which scorns this way of salvation, reviles it and persecutes it. Such men deprive themselves of such great goods, and they feel what is written in John 5 and 2 Thess. 2. Let us be steadfast. And let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXCV.
units.tr: Homily 195.

units.la: 19 Vnde, Rex Agrippa, non fui rebellis cœlesti visioni:
units.tr: 19 Whereupon, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.

units.la: 20 Sed iis, qui sunt Damasci primum, & Hierosolymis, & per omnem regionem Iudeæ, deinde & Gentibus, annuntiaui, vt resipiscerent, & conuertant se ad Deum, opera facientes digna iis, qui resipuissent.
units.tr: 20 But I declared first to those at Damascus and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of those who have repented.

units.la: 21 Horum causa Iudæi me in tem- plo comprehensum tentarunt interfi- cere. &c. Vide ad ver. 24.
units.tr: 21 For these reasons the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me. &c. See on verse 24.

units.la: Dluus Paulus suae conuersionis histo- riam diligenter exposuit, eo quod per illam probare poterat,se nec animi leuitate ad Christum transfuisse, nec temerario ausu Euangelium praedicauisse, sed omnium, quae abs se facta fuerint, authorem esse Deum: qui & longe aliud meditantem conuerterit, & gentibus quoque praedicare iusserit. His vero praemissis, nunc quid postea fecerit, quidue sibi euenerit, narrat.
units.tr: Saint Paul set out the history of his conversion carefully, because by it he could prove that he had not gone over to Christ out of levity of mind, nor preached the gospel by rash daring, but that God is the author of all that has been done by him: God, who both turned him from a quite different purpose and ordered him to preach to the Gentiles too. Having said these things beforehand, he now tells what he did afterwards and what happened to him.

units.la: I. Vt visioni & vocationi diuinae cesse-rit, docet. Vbi Nota T. 1. Quod diserte fatetur, se Deo obediuisse. Atqui aliud dixerunt & iusserant patres Hierosolymae. Act 3.4.5.8.9. &c. Docet ergo Paulus suo exemplo, Deo potius quam hominibus obediendum esse. Imo absque mora cedere debemus, vt primum nobis de Dei voluntate constat. Sic Petrus, Act.4.5. Sic Psal. 95. Heb.4. Obseruemus in omnibus.
units.tr: I. He teaches that he yielded to the vision and the divine calling. Note here, first, that he expressly confesses he obeyed God. Yet the fathers at Jerusalem had said and commanded otherwise: Acts 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, etc. Paul therefore teaches by his own example that God must be obeyed rather than men. Indeed we ought to yield without delay as soon as the will of God is clear to us. So Peter, Acts 4 and 5; so Psalm 95, Heb. 4. Let us observe this in all things.

units.la: 2. Quomodo obedierit? Sicut Domi-nus iusserat. Sunt enim qui obediunt qui-dem, sed ex parte, & quatenus ipsis com-modum est. Ita Saul.1.Sam.13. &15. Pro-pheta.1.Reg.13. Sed plena obedientia exi-gitur. Deut.4.12.Num.15. 2.Cor.10.Id Pau-lus praestitit, quod ex ijs patet, quae se sta-tim accepto Dei mandato fecisse ait. Prae-dicauit enim omnib. vt iussus erat, & quod iussus erat.
units.tr: 2. How did he obey? As the Lord had commanded. For there are those who obey indeed, but only in part, and so far as it suits them. So Saul, 1 Sam. 13 and 15; the prophet, 1 Kings 13. But full obedience is required: Deut. 4:12; Num. 15; 2 Cor. 10. Paul performed this, as is clear from what he says he did at once on receiving God's command. For he preached to all as he had been commanded, and what he had been commanded.

units.la: Vides interim, quid Euangelio debeat prædicari. A. Vt homines resipiscant. Hinc initium fiat: quia omnes peccatores sunt. Gen 8. Isa. 53. Psal. 14. Rom. 1. 2. Hinc Baptista cœpit, Matth. 3. Luc. 3. Christus, Matth. 4. Apostoli, hoc iubente. Matt. 10 Luc. 24. Errant, qui hoc principium hodie vellent omitti, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile you see what ought to be preached in the gospel. A. That men repent. Let the beginning be made here, because all are sinners: Gen. 8; Isa. 53; Ps. 14; Rom. 1 and 2. From here the Baptist began, Matt. 3, Luke 3; Christ began, Matt. 4; the apostles, at his command, Matt. 10, Luke 24. They err who would wish this beginning to be omitted today, etc.

units.la: B Vt conuertantur ad Deum. Expositio prioris. Vt enim auersi à Deo, peccamus & perimus: ita in hoc consistit resipiscentia & salus, vt ad illum reuersi, ipsi reconciliemur. Id vero per solum Christum fit, qui & pœnitentiæ spiritum largitur, & peccatis deletis nos patri reconciliat. Act. 5. Matt. 3. 17.
units.tr: B. That they be converted to God. This explains the former point. For as we sin and perish when turned away from God, so repentance and salvation consist in this: that, returning to him, we ourselves are reconciled. This, however, happens through Christ alone, who both bestows the spirit of repentance and, our sins being blotted out, reconciles us to the Father: Acts 5; Matt. 3; 17.

units.la: III. Arguuntur, qui absque Christo pœnitentiam prædicant. C. Vt facerent opera digna pœnitentiæ. Sic Baptista. Matt 3. Opera ribus ergo probandum, nos conuersos esse. Debent hæc diuersa esse à pristinis. ad Tit. 3. Hinc vero patet, opera à nobis exigi vt debita: non vt meriti loco sint. Luc 17. &c.
units.tr: III. Those are refuted who preach repentance without Christ. C. That they should do works worthy of repentance. So the Baptist, Matt. 3. The works must therefore be the proof that we have been converted, and they ought to be different from our former ones: Tit. 3. Hence it is plain that works are required of us as duties, not that they should take the place of merit: Luke 17, etc.

units.la: II. Causam exponit suæ captiuitatis, sic vt ex præmissis cuincat, iniquissimè secum agi. Horum causa, quòd nimirum Deo obedire voluit, Iudæi me in templo captum occidere voluerunt, &c. Amplificationi seruiunt.
units.tr: II. He sets out the cause of his imprisonment, so that from what has been said he proves he has been treated most unjustly. The cause of these things was, namely, that he wished to obey God; the Jews wished to kill me when I had been seized in the temple, etc. These things serve for amplification.

units.la: Paulum eo quod Deo obedit, ca. pitur, &c. unt omnia, &c. ¶ Veritatis & obedientiæ studium, quam Deo præstant sancti, esse persecutionum causam. Sic phrophetis euenit. Amoz 3 7. &c. Sic Apostolis, Act 1. 4.5. Hodie quid aliud faciunt, quos Reges persequuntur? Eò maiorautem est rei indignitas, quòd salutem ex Dei mandato hominibus offerunt, qui tam malam gratiam reportant. Sed soletur nos, quòd Paulus auxilio Dei se liberatum testatur. Generale hoc, Psal 34.
units.tr: Paul is seized because he obeys God, etc. The zeal for truth and obedience which the saints show to God is the cause of persecutions. So it happened to the prophets: Amos 3:7, etc. So to the apostles: Acts 1, 4, 5. What else do those do today whom kings persecute? The unworthiness of the matter is all the greater, because they offer men salvation by God's command, and yet receive such a bad return. But Paul's testimony that he was freed by God's help comforts us. This is a general truth: Ps. 34.

units.la: III. His absolutis, ad præsentes audito-res conuersus, illis liberius concionari incipit, &c.
units.tr: III. Having finished these matters, he turns to the present hearers and begins to preach to them more freely, etc.

units.la: NOT. ¶ 1. Cur pergat in eo munere, quòd iam toties illi malum conflauerat. Quia Dei auxilium naetus sit: ideo se suo officio non debere deesse. Loquitur autem de liberatione per tribunum, quam vni Deo tribuit, Psalm 107. Discimus, eos qui Dei opem senserunt, accendidebere: non negligentiores fieri, vt quidam solent. Nam præter id, quod Deo aliàs debemus, nouum officium gratitudo requirit, &c.
units.tr: NOTE. 1. Why he persists in that office, since they had already so often stirred up evil against him. Because he has obtained God's help, he ought therefore not to fail in his duty. He speaks of the deliverance through the tribune, which he ascribes to God alone: Psalm 107. We learn that those who have felt God's help ought to be kindled to more zeal, not to become more careless, as some are wont to do. For besides what we owe to God on other grounds, gratitude requires a new duty, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Quibus prædicet, Testificor, tum magno tum parvo. Agnoscit ergo se omnibus hominibes debitorem esse. Romanor. 1. Euangelium ergo ad omnes homines
units.tr: 2. To whom he preaches: "I testify, both to small and great." He acknowledges, therefore, that he is a debtor to all men: Rom. 1. The gospel therefore

units.la: pertinet:nec est personarum respectus apud Deum, qui omnes vult saluos fieri, 1. Tim 2. Col.3. Actor.10. Galat.3. Ideo toti fa mil q dantur œconomi isti, Luc.12. Nemo ergo fib jpsi discipulos eligat profuo arbi trio. Simul meminerint omnes fe Euange lio debere subijci, fi quidem Dei filij esse velint. Ioh.8.
units.tr: pertains to all men; there is no respect of persons with God, who wills all to be saved: 1 Tim. 2; Col. 3; Acts 10; Gal. 3. Therefore these stewards are given to the whole household: Luke 12. Let no one, therefore, choose disciples for himself by his own free judgment. At the same time let all remember that they must submit to the gospel, if indeed they wish to be sons of God: John 8.

units.la: ¶3. Quid dezeat? Non alia, quàm quæ prophetæ & Moses prædixerunt. Distinguit vero in certa capita, & ea quidé,quæ tunc maximè controuertebantur. Primùm docet Christum debuisse pati & mori. Hoc cùm primis absurdum Iudæis videbatur, 7.12 1.1 Cor.1. At facilè demonstrari pote- rat typis legalibus,Exod.12.Num.21. Item ex Ifa.53.
units.tr: 3. What does he teach? Nothing other than what the prophets and Moses foretold. He divides it under certain heads, and those indeed which were then most disputed. First, he teaches that Christ ought to have suffered and died. When this was first proposed, it seemed utterly absurd to the Jews: 1 Cor. 1. Yet it could easily be demonstrated from the legal types: Exod. 12; Num. 21. Likewise from Isa. 53.

units.la: Deinde quòd ex mortuis resurgere debuerit primus, propria nimirum virtute, &c. Id probatur, Act.2.&13.ex Pfal 16.
units.tr: Next, that he ought to rise from the dead first, by his own proper power, etc. This is proved in Acts 2 and 13 from Ps. 16.

units.la: Tertiò, quòd gentes quoq; debuerit illuminare. De hoc diserte habes, If.42.49. Eòdem debent referri quæcunq; de genti um vocatione habentur.Ifa.2.Pfalm.2.45. 72.&c.
units.tr: Thirdly, that he ought to enlighten the Gentiles too. You have this expressly in Isa. 42 and 49. To the same must be referred whatever is said about the calling of the nations: Isa. 2; Ps. 2, 45, 72, etc.

units.la: Atqui hæc scripturis probauisse Paulu, Festi exclamatio docebit. Ita verò rursum patet Euangelij doctrinam, & fidem nō esse nuperam. Simul docemur hic,fcri pturis omnia ea contineri, quæ ad credendum necessaria sunt. Ex his enim Paulus omnia probauit, Christi & fidei Christianæ mysteria. Atqui constat, ipsum omnia perfectè tradidisse, Gal.1. Fac ergo quod iuberis, 2.Tim.3. Oremus.
units.tr: That Paul proved these things from the Scriptures, Festus' exclamation will show. Thus again it is clear that the doctrine of the gospel and the faith are not new. At the same time we are taught here that all things necessary for believing are contained in the Scriptures. For from these Paul proved everything, the mysteries of Christ and of the Christian faith. And it is certain that he delivered everything perfectly: Gal. 1. So do what you are commanded: 2 Tim. 3. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CXCVI.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXCVI.

units.la: 24 Hæc autem ipso prosè excipien te, Festus magna voce ait, Insanis Paule: multæ literæ te ad insaniam adigunt.
units.tr: 24 But while he was making his defence in this way, Festus shouted in a loud voice: You are mad, Paul; much learning is driving you to madness.

units.la: 25 Tunc ille, Non insanio, inquit, præstantissime Feste, sed vera ac sobria verba loquor. &c. Vsque ad verf. 33.
units.tr: 25 But he replied: I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but I speak true and sober words. &c. Down to verse 33.

units.la: DEI verbum per se salutare & efficax est, vt per quod ille suam gratiam & salutem nobis offert: at non idem eius apud omnes effectus est. Alij enim omnino contemnunt: alij leuiter & ad tempus mouentur: multi, quando videntur fructum daturi, subito deficiunt. Pauculi ex eo meliores fiunt. Id autem non verbi, sed hominum vitio fit, qui animos minus idoneos afferunt. Explicat hoc Christus sementis parabolâ, Luc.8. Et exempla huius generis pasim occurrunt, quæ obseruari debent, vt discamus quid caueri, quid
units.tr: The word of God is in itself saving and effective, since through it God offers us his grace and salvation; yet its effect is not the same on everyone. Some despise it altogether; others are moved slightly and for a time; many, just when they seem about to bear fruit, suddenly fail; a few become better because of it. This happens not through fault of the word but through the fault of the men who bring minds unfit for it. Christ explains this by the parable of the sower, Luke 8. Examples of this kind occur everywhere, and they must be observed so that we may learn what to beware of and what ought to be done.

units.la: Cap. 26. fieri debeat. Facit huc in primis hic locus, quo describitur effectus concionis Paulinæ, & duo hominum genera producuntur, quibus frustrà prædicatur.
units.tr: Chapter 26. In particular this passage bears on the matter, in which the effect of Paul's sermon is described, and two kinds of men are presented to whom preaching is in vain.

units.la: I. Genus Festi præsidis est, qui propha norum & eorum typus est, qui rerum diuinarum omnino rudes sunt. Audiuit is Paulû dicentê de visionibus, & sua confirmantem scripturis, de quibus nihil audiuerat hucusq;, vtpote homo militaris. Putat ergo illû præ nimio studio alienatum à mente, vt phrenetici sunt. Ideo interpellat eum importunissimè.
units.tr: I. The first kind is Festus the governor, who is a figure and type of those who are wholly untrained in divine things. He heard Paul speaking about visions and confirming what he said from the Scriptures, of which he had heard nothing until then, being a military man. So he thinks Paul has been turned out of his mind by excessive study, as the frenzied are. Therefore he interrupts him most rudely.

units.la: No T. ¶ Similes huius esse, qui carnis ratione ducuntur. Quæcunq; enim non intelligunt, pro ludibrio habent. At nihil minus capiunt, quà quæ sunt spiritus Dei, 1.Cor.2. Ideo Christi prædicatio illis stultitia est, 1.Cor.1. Accidit hoc olim Prophetis, 2.Reg.9. Baptistæ, Matth.11. Christo, Ioh.18. Paulo, Acto.17. Hodie passim. Imò optimiferè sunt, qui sic iudicant. Nam sunt, qui improbè conuitiantur, vt Achab &c. Sed non offendamur, sunt enim qui se men in viam excipiunt.
units.tr: Note. Those are like him who are led by the reasoning of the flesh. For they treat as a joke whatever they do not understand; yet they grasp nothing of what belongs to the Spirit of God, 1 Cor. 2. Hence the preaching of Christ is foolishness to them, 1 Cor. 1. This happened once to the prophets, 2 Kings 9; to the Baptist, Matt. 11; to Christ, John 18; to Paul, Acts 17; and today it happens everywhere. Indeed, those who judge in this way are most often the best sort; for there are some who abuse us shamefully, as Ahab did, etc. But let us not be offended, for there are those who receive the seed on the good road.

units.la: Quid Paulus? Respondet grauiter, vt Euangelij authoritatem afferat: Modestè tamen, ne contumeliosus sit in Magistratum, qui ex ignorantia peccabat. Alia ratio eorum, qui Christiani dici volunt. Non insanio, sed veritatem, &c. Probat 1. Regis testimonium. Nouit is, quia nihil in obscuro gestum. Et mox ad hunc conuersus vrget eum. Sciebat enim in corruptissima gente suam adhuc constare scripturis authoritatem. Et videtur ex sequentibus hic pluribus egisse.
units.tr: What does Paul do? He answers gravely, so as to lend authority to the gospel; yet modestly, lest he be insulting to the magistrate, who was sinning through ignorance. This is the other sort of those who wish to be called Christians. I am not mad, but speak the truth, etc. He proves it by the testimony of the king. He knew that nothing had been done in a corner, and soon turned to him and presses him. For he knew that in a most corrupt nation the authority of the Scriptures still held firm; and it seems from what follows that he dealt with it more fully here.

units.la: NOT. 1. Optimam docendi rationem. Ante omnia veritati studendum, quae solo Dei verbo continetur. Ingens scelus mentiri sub Dei praetextu, Ier. 23. Vide Christum, Io. 7. Item quid Apostolis mandarit, Matt. 28. Ioh. 17. Deinde sobrie & modeste omnia tractentur, ne rudiores quaestionibus curiosis inuoluantur. Ne ergo velimus inquirere, quae Deus non reuelauit.
units.tr: NOTE 1. The best method of teaching. Before all things we must aim at the truth, which is contained in the word of God alone. It is a great crime to lie under the pretext of God's name, Jer. 23. See Christ, John 7; likewise what he commanded the apostles, Matt. 28; John 17. Then let all things be handled soberly and modestly, lest the simpler sort be entangled in curious questions. Let us therefore not wish to inquire into what God has not revealed.

units.la: 2. Salutis & religionis Christianae ne gotium certum esse & nihil habere obscuri aut suspecti. Vt enim Christus aperte omnia egit, ita aperte olim actum cum Patribus. Patriarchę clari & illustres fuerunt. Nota omnibus liberatio ex Aegypto, promulgatio legis, &c. Deinde omnibus monarchijs cum hac gente & religione negotium fuit, &c. Christus ipse non in angulis docuit, Ioh. 18. Apostoli doctrina & miraculis totum orbem peruaserunt.
units.tr: 2. The business of salvation and of the Christian religion is certain and has nothing hidden or suspicious about it. For just as Christ acted openly in all things, so openly was dealing carried on with the Fathers of old. The patriarchs were famous and illustrious. The deliverance from Egypt, the promulgation of the law, etc., are known to all. Then all monarchies had dealings with this people and religion, etc. Christ himself taught not in corners, John 18. The apostles' teaching and miracles spread through the whole world.

units.la: Est & hoc singulare, quod sola Biblia &
units.tr: This too is singular: the Bible alone

units.la: in hunc vsque diem seruata sunt,& in omnibus linguis leguntur. Nimis ergo impudentes, qui hodie in dubium vocant religionem & fidei doctrinam.
units.tr: has been preserved down to this day and is read in all languages. Therefore those are far too shameless who today call religion and the doctrine of faith into doubt.

units.la: II. Genus Agrippæ est,qui eorû typum gerit, qui semen verbi studio huius mundi patiuntur suffocari. Non audet negare scripturas, neq; vt nihil ad se pertinentes reijcere. Videt his conuenire quæ à Paulo dicebantur. Sentit animi motus, quibus solicitabatur,& id fatetur. Quid ergo obstat? Infelix mundi studium, quo deterrentus non putat ad eos transeundum esse, qui omnibus exosi erant,& multis insanire videbantur. Tales sunt hodie multi,qui Euangelij testimonium ferunt, Antichristum abominantur: Manent tamen cum illo,ne honoribus, diuitijs, voluptatibus excidant,Matt.19. Interim apparet in his magna vis veritatis.
units.tr: II. The second kind is Agrippa, who bears the type of those who suffer the seed of the word to be choked by the zeal for this world. He does not dare to deny the Scriptures, nor to reject them as having nothing to do with him. He sees that what Paul was saying applies to him; he feels the stirrings of mind by which he was troubled, and he confesses it. What then stands in the way? The unhappy zeal for the world, by which, being deterred, he does not think he must cross over to those who were hated by all and seemed to many to be mad. Many today are like this: they bear witness to the gospel and abominate Antichrist, yet they remain with him, lest they fall from honours, riches and pleasures, Matt. 19. Meanwhile there is evident in them a great power of truth.

units.la: Quid vero hic Paulus? Votum opponit verè Christianum. Nec dubium, quin ex animo hoc dixerit,Rom.9.10.
units.tr: But what does Paul here? He sets against him the wish of one truly Christian. There is no doubt he spoke this from his heart, Rom. 9, 10.

units.la: Vbi Nota. Non sufficere,vt ex parte credamus,sed requiri incrementa fidei, Eph.4. Arguuntur, qui vnum & alterum articulū apprehendunt. Atqui totus Christus manducandus,&c.
units.tr: Note here: it is not enough to believe in part, but increases of faith are required, Eph. 4. Those are reproved who lay hold of one or another article. Yet all of Christ must be eaten, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2.Ministris non esse potestatem in animos nimos hominum. Alioqui his opus non fuisset.Imo vide If.53. Item 1.Cor.3.Nemo ergo nobis imputet quod pauci credunt. Christum audi,Ioh.6.
units.tr: ¶ 2. Ministers have no power over the minds of men. Otherwise there would have been no need of them. Indeed see Isaiah 53. Likewise 1 Cor. 3. Therefore let no one impute to us that few believe. Hear Christ, John 6.

units.la: ¶3. Quòd vincula excipit.Etsi hæc ipsi non essent molesta, imò in his glorietur alibi, non tamen inuidet aliorum otio & paci. Ita nos nostram crucem patienter serramus, aliorum commodis autem cupiamus consultum.
units.tr: ¶ 3. That he accepts the chains. Even if these were not troublesome to him himself, indeed he glories in them elsewhere, he does not envy others their ease and peace. So let us patiently bear our own cross, but desire that the advantage of others be consulted.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui omnes vellent secum periclitari, & non Christianos dicunt eos, qui commodius viuunt.
units.tr: Those are reproved who would wish all to be imperilled with themselves, and who call those Christians who live more comfortably not Christians.

units.la: Finis omnium, Exurgunt & secedunt ni hilo meliores facti. Conferunt tamen inter se, & vnanimi consensu Paulum innocentem pronuntiant, non autem dimittunt, sed prouocationem eius abutuntur, &c. Vides quàm paucum cordi sit impijs conditio piorum, quando cum horum sanguine quasi ludunt.
units.tr: The end of all: they rise up and withdraw, yet they have become no better. Still they confer among themselves and with one voice pronounce Paul innocent, but they do not release him; they abuse his appeal, etc. You see how little the condition of the pious matters to the impious, when they toy, as it were, with the blood of these men.

units.la: Notr. ¶ Dignitatem fidei Christianæ. Arguuntur, qui seditiosam dicunt. Atqui acerrimus huius doctor sub Ethnicis iudicibus absoluitur iam toties. Non ergo mouemur impiorum calumnijs, sed constantes simus, & Deo seruiamus sancti, qui suos non deserit.
units.tr: Note. The dignity of the Christian faith. Those are reproved who call it seditious. Yet its most zealous teacher has already so often been acquitted before heathen judges. Therefore let us not be moved by the calumnies of the impious, but let us be steadfast and serve God as holy men, who does not desert his own.

units.la: Oremus.
units.tr: Let us pray.

units.la: CAPVT XXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVII.

units.la: HOMILIA CXCVII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXCVII.

units.la: POstquam autem decretum est, vt non nauigaremus in Italiam, tradi derunt & Paulum et quosdam alios vin-ctos Centurioni nomine Iulio, cohortis Augusta.
units.tr: When it was decided that we should not sail to Italy, they handed over Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.

units.la: 2 Conscenso igitur nauigio Adra-mytteno, nauigaturi secundum Asiae re-giones, proueЯi sumus, & nobiscum eat Aristarchus Macedo Thessaloni-censis. &c. vsque ad ver. 9.
units.tr: (2) So, going on board an Adramyttian ship, which was about to sail along the coasts of Asia, we put out to sea, and with us was Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica. And so on, down to verse 9.

units.la: Efcribitur hoc Capite mole-sta, & plena periculi nauigatio, qua Paulus Romā delatus est, vt illic Cæsari sisteretur, ad quē prouocauerat. Et videtur quidem primo intuitu sterilis omnino esse descriptio, sed si penitius inspiciatur, multa habet cogni-tu vtilissima. Docet enim, quæ fidelium Christi sors sit in hoc mundo. Adhæc con-stantiæ & patientiæ exempla proponit. Præterea inuistam esse probat promissio-num Dei veritatem, vt quæ nullis aduer-sis impediri possit. Quàmuis enim ipsa na-tura Paulo sese opponere videatur, venit tamen Romam, sicut promissum fuerat, Acto.23. Insunt & alia multa, quæ tum institutioni, tum consolationi nostræ serviunt: de quibus omnibus suo loco dicetur.
units.tr: This chapter describes a voyage full of trouble and danger, by which Paul was carried to Rome so that he might be presented there to Caesar, to whom he had appealed. At first glance the account seems altogether barren, but if it is examined more closely it contains many things most worth knowing. For it teaches what the lot of Christ's faithful is in this world. It also sets before us examples of steadfastness and patience. Moreover, it proves that the truth of God's promises is invincible, since nothing adverse can hinder it. For although nature itself seems to oppose Paul, he nevertheless came to Rome, as had been promised (Acts 23). There are also many other things which serve both our instruction and our comfort; all of these will be discussed in their proper place.

units.la: I. Quomodo ammandatus fit, narratur. Traditus cuidam Centurioni Iulio, vnà cum aliis captiuis, qui haud dubiè facinorosi erant. Illis ergo Paulus adiungitur. NOT. ¶ Romanorum diligentia in iure administrando. Huius enim euidens argumentū est, quòd vinctos suos, qui vel ip si prouocauerant, vel alias digni videbantur, tantis sumptibus & laboribus Romá deduci curauerunt. Elucet hęc ipsa in multis aliis exemplis. Valer. lib. 6. Cap. 5 Ideo imperio sunt au&ti, diuq; tenuerunt.
units.tr: I. It is related how he was sent off. He was handed over to a certain centurion, Julius, together with other captives, who were doubtless criminals. Paul is therefore joined to them. NOTE: the diligence of the Romans in administering justice. For this is clear evidence that they took care, at such great expense and labour, to have their prisoners, who had either appealed themselves or seemed otherwise deserving, brought to Rome. This appears in many other examples as well (Valerius, book 6, chapter 5): "for this reason they were increased in power and held it for a long time."

units.la: Vides quæ optima sit imperia acquirendi & seruandi ratio. Exprimitur hæc ipsa, Psal. 72. Exempla sunt in Nabuchodonosore, Ezech. 29. Promittitur Ægyptijs in mercedem. Cyro, Isa. 45. Rursum vbi iusti tia publica violatur, respublicæ interciduntque, Leuit. 26. Isa. 1. &c. Coniunge his domesticta exempla, vt inde discas, quid nobis sperandum sit hodie.
units.tr: You see what the best method is for acquiring and preserving empire. This very thing is expressed in Psalm 72. There are examples in Nebuchadnezzar (Ezek. 29), a reward promised to the Egyptians; in Cyrus (Isa. 45). Again, where public justice is violated, commonwealths perish (Lev. 26; Isa. 1, etc.). Join to these domestic examples, that you may learn from them what we ought to hope for today.

units.la: ¶ 2. Sortem piorum. Paulus facinorosis coniungitur. Ita Christus, Isa. 53. Lucæ 22. &c. Frequenter hoc ipsum martyribus accidit, & hodie etiá crebro fit. Non offendamur. Interim elucet diuinæ bonitatis spectimen, quæ miseris hisce tantum consolatorem & consultorem adiunxit: per quem postea seruati sunt. Et Paulus bene agendi occasionem habuit. Possent & alia huius rei exempla adduci.
units.tr: 2. The lot of the pious. Paul is joined with criminals. So Christ was (Isa. 53; Luke 22, etc.). This very thing has often happened to martyrs, and it still happens frequently today. Let us not be offended. Meanwhile there shines forth a sign of divine goodness, which gave these wretched men such a comforter and counsellor, through whom they were afterwards saved. And Paul had an opportunity of doing good. Other examples of this matter could be adduced.

units.la: II. Vt Pauli quoque curam Deus habuerit? Duo huc pertinent. I. Comites ad iunxit illi, quorum præsentia & ministerio subleuaretur. Fuit inter hos ipse Lucas. Deinde Aristarchus, vir haud dubié diues, qui sumptibus tam diuturnis potuit sufficere. Ita vero Deus suis nunquam deeste solet, 2. Cor. 1. i. Cor. 10. Pfal. 94. Et si nemo hominum adsit, ipse præsens est, Ioh. 16. Matt. 28. Luc. 12. 21.
units.tr: II. Whether God also took care of Paul. Two points pertain to this. First, he joined companions to him, by whose presence and service he was sustained; among these was Luke himself. Then Aristarchus, a man doubtless wealthy, who could meet such lengthy expenses. Indeed, God is accustomed never to fail his own (2 Cor. 1; 1 Cor. 10; Ps. 94). And if no man is present, he himself is present (John 16; Matt. 28; Luke 12:21).

units.la: Sed Nota. Aristarchum insigne charitatis & patientiæ exemplum. Accedens cum Paulo ex Græcia, Act. 20. Vbi captum videt, non deserit, sed biennio toto apud ipsum manet. Nunc Romam vsque sequitur. Arguuntur huius exemplo mol. Iculi, qui nihil ferre volunt, & quos martyrum Christi pudet. Quin retributionem spectat, Pfal. 41. Mat. 25. Sensit hanc in præsenti etiam Aristarchus. Immortalis enim est eius gloria.
units.tr: But note: Aristarchus is a remarkable example of love and patience. Having come with Paul from Greece (Acts 20), when he sees him taken, he does not desert him, but remains with him for two whole years. Now he follows him even to Rome. By his example are rebuked the soft-hearted, who want to bear nothing, and who are ashamed of the martyrs of Christ. Moreover, he looks to the reward (Ps. 41; Matt. 25). Aristarchus also felt this even in the present; for his glory is immortal.

units.la: II. Centurionis quoque animum flectit,
units.tr: II. He also bends the mind of the centurion,

units.la: vt humaniter Paulum tractet, & Sidonis copiam illi faciat inuisendi amicos, vt illis curetur. Ita supra tribunum Lysiam & Felicem illi deuinxit. Sic Ieremias habet, qui ipsum foueant, Ier. 38. Eodem Abdias pertinet, 1. Reg. 18. Consulentur nos ista, ne tyrannorum minis cedamus, & vt vni Deo approbemus nos, &c.
units.tr: so that he treats Paul kindly and grants him the opportunity to visit his friends at Sidon, that he might be cared for by them. So he had won over the tribune Lysias and Felix as well. So Jeremiah had those who cherished him (Jer. 38). To the same point belongs Obadiah (1 Kings 18). These things console us, that we may not yield to the threats of tyrants, and that we may approve ourselves to the one God, etc.

units.la: Interim Nota. Paulum, qui cum effugij occasionem haberet, non tamen illa vtitur. Causae sunt, partim quod Centurio optime merito de se periculum conflauisset: partim quod oraculo admonitus nouerat se Romam debere proficisci. Discimus, ne quis illicitis medijs sibijpsi consulat.
units.tr: Meanwhile note: Paul, who had an opportunity of escape, did not use it. The reasons were partly that the centurion had deserved very well of him and had brought himself into danger on his account, and partly that, admonished by an oracle, he knew he ought to set out for Rome. We learn that no one should provide for himself by unlawful means.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui quiduis arripiut. Quod si nullum offertur medium licitum, certo scias, Deum peculiare quiddam de te cogitare. Huius ergo voluntati credas te, ne corpori consulturus animae iacturam facias, Iok 12. Luc. 22.
units.tr: Those are rebuked who seize upon anything at all. But if no lawful means is offered, know for certain that God has some particular purpose concerning you. Therefore trust yourself to his will, lest, while seeking to provide for the body, you suffer loss of the soul (John 12; Luke 22).

units.la: III. Navigatio prolixè describitur, & sic quidem, vt aduersam fuisse constet. Atqui longè aliter poterat rem instituere Deus: qui & mari & ventis imperat, vt vides Exod. 14. Psal. 107. Matth. 8. 14. Sed ita exeri voluit.
units.tr: III. The voyage is described at length, and in such a way that it is clear it was adverse. Yet God could have ordered the matter quite differently, he who commands both sea and winds, as you see in Exodus 14, Psalm 107, Matthew 8 and 14. But he chose to have it so.

units.la: Nota. Quae vita nostra sit in hoc mundo do Perse ærumnosa est, & mari simillima Pfa.90.Gen.47.Imprimis autem piorum 2.Tim.3.Christum vide.Item quæ suis præ-dixit cuentura,Ioh.15.16. Mar.13. Paulus vix elapsus,mari committitur,2.Cor.11.Vi-dere est in martyribus omnibus.
units.tr: Note: what our life is in this world is wretched, and most like the sea (Ps. 90; Gen. 47). Above all, the life of the pious (2 Tim. 3). Look to Christ, who foretold that these things would befall his own (John 15–16; Mark 13). Paul, scarcely escaped, is committed to the sea (2 Cor. 11). This may be seen in all the martyrs.

units.la: Non ergo offendamur hodie. Portus quietis in cœlo est. Itaq; Pauli constanti-am imitemur,& indesinenter Oremus.
