units.la: ideo talium preces non exaudiuntur, Pro uerb.21. Olim vero sentient, quod Christus minatur Matt.25. Quòd si vero peregrinis debetur fides & beneficentia, multo magis socijs & conciuibus, quos & vetus amicitia, & publicæ salutis necessitas nobis commendant.
units.tr: therefore the prayers of such people are not heard (Proverbs 21). But in time they will feel what Christ threatens (Matthew 25). If faith and beneficence are owed to strangers, much more are they owed to companions and fellow citizens, whom both old friendship and the necessity of public welfare commend to us.

units.la: II. Remunerat Deus hospitalitate isto- rum, & quidem per Paulum captiuum & assi&ctissimum. Nemo igitur tam vilis & miser, qui non posit aliquando nos iuuare. Exempla. Neque perit illorum mercès, qui Dei feruis benefaciunt, Matth 10. Hic duo fiunt. I. Publij pater ex incurabili morbo restituitur. Ingens bonum, si corpus modo spectes, vt nihil dicamus de occasione veræ fidei.
units.tr: II. God rewards the hospitality of these people, and indeed through Paul, a captive and most afflicted man. Therefore no one is so lowly and wretched that he cannot sometimes help us. Examples. Nor does the reward of those perish who do good to God's servants (Matthew 10). Two things happen here. I. The father of Publius is restored from an incurable disease. This is a great good, if you look only at the body, to say nothing of the opportunity for true faith.

units.la: Sed Not. ¶ Paulum feruasse ordinem à Christo præscriptum, Mar.16. Ergo non Pauli, sed Christi virtute fuit æditum. Apparuit hoc in aliis quoque. Et ipsi hoc fatentur, Act.3. Ergo propter miracula non in sanctis hærere, sed ad Deum, & finem omnium miraculorum respicere debemus. Mar.16.
units.tr: But note: Paul kept the order prescribed by Christ (Mark 16). Therefore the healing was accomplished not by Paul's power but by Christ's. This appeared in others also, and they themselves confess it (Acts 3). Therefore, on account of miracles, we ought not to cling to the saints, but to look to God and to the end of all miracles (Mark 16).

units.la: II. Huius signi fama excitati venerunt multi alij, qui & ipsi curati sunt, ficq; quod ab uno coeperat beneficium, ad multos est extensum. Et voluit occasione hac Deus illis æternam salutem offerre, qui Paulum cum suis amicè exceperunt. Sic magistratus pietas populo salutaris est. Obseruent hoc omnes, vt patienter ferant peregrinos, & quosuis, quibus magistratus beneficium cupit.
units.tr: II. Roused by the report of this sign, many others came, who were also cured, and so the benefit that had begun with one man was extended to many. And by this occasion God wished to offer eternal salvation to those who had received Paul and his companions kindly. So the piety of the magistrate is salutary to the people. Let everyone take note of this, so that they patiently bear strangers and whoever else the magistrate wishes to benefit.

units.la: Interim Nota. Christum esse medicum, qui ab infirmitate omni nos liberat, Isaiæ 53. Matth. 9. 1. Ad hunc ergo omnes contendant, Matth. 11. Ioh. 4. 7. Lere. 2. Relinquant item morbida vitæ prioris studia, & huic vniuersi ruant, Mat. 8.
units.tr: Meanwhile, note: Christ is the physician who frees us from every infirmity (Isaiah 53; Matthew 9). Let all therefore hasten to him (Matthew 11; John 4; 7; Luke 2). Likewise let them abandon the sickly pursuits of their former life and rush headlong to him (Matthew 8).

units.la: III. Gratitudo Melitensium, qui non quæstum priuatum quæsiuerunt. Honorarium maxime. Discessuris dederunt necessaria. Vbi Nota. 1. Gratitudinem decere eos, qui beneficium accepe-runt. Requirit hanc Lex naturæ. Deinde vinculum est beneficentiæ. Indigni homines nomine, qui ab aliis modo beneficia ac cipiunt, ipsi vero nihil rependunt.
units.tr: III. The gratitude of the Maltese, who did not seek private gain. They showed honour above all, and to those about to depart they gave what was necessary. Here note: (1) that those who have received a benefit ought to show gratitude; the law of nature requires this, and it is also the bond of beneficence. Men are rightly called unworthy who only receive benefits from others and repay nothing.

units.la: In primis docemur, quid debeatur iis, per quos nobis Christus innotescit. A. Honor, non diuinus, sed qualem homo potest accipere ab homine. Huc pertinet Lex, Exod. 20. Vide 1. Timoth 5. Idem obseruandum quoque quo ad magistratum, 1. Petri 2. B. Victus & debita mercedes, &c.
units.tr: In the first place we are taught what is owed to those through whom Christ is made known to us. (A) Honour, not divine honour, but such as one man can render to another. The law pertains to this (Exodus 20; see 1 Timothy 5). The same must be observed with regard to the magistrate (1 Peter 2). (B) Food and the wages that are due, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2 Quòd Paulus ista accepit.Ergo nō statim ventris præcones sunt, qui ex mini sterio viuunt. Sic olim ordinauit Deus, Num.18. Christus item, qui suo exemplo præiuit,Matth.10. Luc.8. Et hoc obser-uarunt passim Apostoli. Vide 1.Corint. 9.2.Corint 11.Philip 4 &c. Studeant omnes humanitati,& pietatem colant ex animo,& ita non facilè à scopo aberrabunt. Oremus.
units.tr: (2) That Paul received these things. Therefore those who live from the ministry are not at once heralds of their bellies. So God ordained of old (Numbers 18), and Christ too, who went before with his example (Matthew 10; Luke 8). The apostles everywhere observed this (see 1 Corinthians 9; 2 Corinthians 11; Philippians 4, etc.). Let all strive for humanity and cultivate piety from the heart, and so they will not easily stray from the mark. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CCVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CCVI.

units.la: 11 Tribus itaque post mensibus de-uectii sumus in naui Alexandrina, quæ in insula hyemauerat, cui erat insigne castor & Pollux.
units.tr: 11 After three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship, which had wintered at the island, whose figurehead was Castor and Pollux.

units.la: 12 Et deuecti Syracusas, illic man-simus triduum.
units.tr: 12 And landing at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

units.la: 13 Ibidem circumlegentes deueni-mus Rhegium, & altero post die quum superuenijset Auster, secundo die veni-mus Puteolos.
units.tr: 13 From there we sailed round and reached Rhegium, and after one day, when the south wind had risen, on the second day we came to Puteoli.

units.la: 14 Vbi repertis fratribus, rogati sumus manere apud eos dies septem, & ita contendimus Romam.
units.tr: 14 There we found brethren, and were asked to stay with them seven days; and so we went on to Rome.

units.la: 15 Vnde quum audissent fratres de rebus nostris, prodierunt nobis in occur-sum vsq; ad Appij forum & tres taber-nas, quos cum vidisset Paulus, gratijs a-ctis {ß}is Deo, sumpsit fiduciam.
units.tr: 15 When the brethren heard about us, they came out to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he gave thanks to God and took courage.

units.la: 16 Quum autem venissemus Romam, Centurio tradidit vinctos praefecto exercituum, sed permissum est Paulo, ut habitaret sibi cum milite, qui ipsum custodiret.
units.tr: 16 And when we came to Rome, the centurion handed the prisoners over to the prefect of the army; but Paul was permitted to live by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

units.la: Inter Pauli actiones, & quę cum illo gesta sunt, nihil memorabilius est, quàm quod ex Iudæis Romam vsque tanto apparatu ductus est, ut Cæsari sisteretur. Eluce t hoc, si Pauli personam vilem & exosam cum Cæsaris & imperij Romani maiestate conferas. Nec enim vel præsides tantum pro uno homine laborare, vel Cæsar Nero tale audire voluisset, nisi Deus hoc negotium gubernauisset. Ideo nauigatio nem hanc tam diligenter describit Lucas, ut hinc constet, quàm multa acciderint, quæ Dei consilium impeditura viderentur, & ut hic ferui sui authoritatem inter medios hostes & homines barbaros mirifice defenderit. Sed & miraculis illustrem fecit, ut horum fama praecurrens Romanos ad illum videndum & audiendum excitaret. Quod ut factum sit hic narratur, &c.
units.tr: Among Paul's actions and the events that befell him, nothing is more worth remarking than that he was led from the Jews all the way to Rome, with such an escort, so that he might be presented to Caesar. You will see this clearly if you set the lowly and hated person of Paul beside the majesty of Caesar and the Roman empire. For neither would the governors have laboured so much on behalf of one man, nor would Caesar Nero have wished to hear such a case, unless God had directed this business. Therefore Luke describes this voyage so carefully, so that it is clear how many things happened which seemed likely to hinder God's purpose, and how wonderfully he defended the authority of his servant among hostile men and barbarians. But he also made him famous by miracles, so that the report of these would run ahead and stir the Romans to come and see and hear him. That this came about is what is narrated here, etc.

units.la: 1. Post menses tres conscenca naui Alexand. post longum ambitum veniunt Puteolos,&c. Quod naui ido​lolatrica vehitur. Hoc enim exemplo non nulli idololatriam faciunt indifferentem. Sed obseruemus quod captiuus non potuit pro suo arbitrio agere. Deinde, quod nihil dissimulauit, neque illum Christi puduit, Rom.1. Longe alia eorum ratio, quia nihil quam sua quaerunt, &c.
units.tr: 1. After three months they embarked in an Alexandrian ship; after a long detour they come to Puteoli, etc. That they travelled in a ship dedicated to idolatry. Some people use this example to make idolatry a matter of indifference. But let us note that the prisoner could not act at his own discretion. Next, that he concealed nothing, and was not ashamed of Christ (Rom. 1). Their attitude is quite different, since they seek nothing but their own interests, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Inueniunt fratres, qui exceptos detinent septem dies. Hospitalitatis exemplum simul & fidei constantis, &c. Deinde elucet rursum maiestas Christi in cruce sanctorum. Paulus captiuus vbique amicos inuenit. Adhaec Centurione & mi​litibus ad nutum ceu feruis vtitur. Sic Actorum decimosexto. Simus ergo constantes.
units.tr: ¶ 2. They find brethren, who keep them for seven days. An example of hospitality and at the same time of steadfast faith, etc. Next, the majesty of Christ shines out again in the cross of the saints. Paul, though a prisoner, finds friends everywhere. Moreover, he uses the centurion and soldiers at his nod, as if they were servants. So in Acts 16. Let us therefore be steadfast.

units.la: II. Fratres Roma procedunt illis obuiam
units.tr: II. The brethren come out from Rome to meet them

units.la: vsq; ad Foroappium, &c. Quibus visis gratias egit Deo & confirmatus est. Etsi enim fortissimus erat, homo tamen erat & non alienus a tentationibus, & fortasis metuebat se nihil proficere posse apud Romanos. Ergo hanc curam illi eximit Deus, &c. Sic Act. 18.
units.tr: as far as the Forum of Appius, etc. When he saw them he gave thanks to God and was strengthened. For although he was most courageous, he was nevertheless a man, and not immune to temptations, and perhaps he feared he could accomplish nothing with the Romans. Therefore God removes this anxiety from him, etc. So Acts 18.

units.la: Sed Nota.¶ Fratres Romanos. Scripserat ad illos, & omne suum studium vna cum suo aduentu promiserat, ad Romanos manos I .15. Sunt ergo grati, quamuis multa essent quae offendere possent. Vinctus cum facinorosis ducebatur. Quem ergo non puderet eius? Deinde periculosum erat Christi fidem profiteri, sub Tybrio damnatam. Tertullianus. Item commune periculum timeri poterat. Sed nolunt decesse pro communi causa laborant Discimus cum periculo quoque defendi deberi Christi ministros, qui pro illo quiduis ferre & facere paratisunt. Ita Christi sto seruitur. Arguitur nostri seculi languor, quando qui tuto possent, nihil audendum putant, imo suos Monachis obijciunt, & his alieno sanguine gratificantur. ¶ 2. Paulus Deo gratias egit. Non quidem fratres neglexit. Sed in primis respexit in Deum, cuius spiritu & virtute hos excitatos esse videbat, & huius consideratione totus confirmatur. Imitemur, ut quicquid nobis boni accidit, ad authorem Deum referamus. Ita & hominibus recte grati erimus, & eorundem inconstantia minus offenduntur. III. Traditur praefecto exercitus cum aliis vinctis, sed dispari conditione. Conceditur enim ei domus priuata, & vnus modo miles additur, qui ipsum custodiat. Fuit ergo haud dubie commendatus a Paulus in domo conductitia asseruatur Romae.
units.tr: But note. The Roman brethren. He had written to them and had promised all his zeal together with his coming, to the Romans in chapter 1 (Rom. 1:15). They are therefore grateful, although there were many things that could have offended them. He was led along with criminals as a prisoner; who therefore would not be ashamed of him? Moreover, it was dangerous to profess faith in Christ, which had been condemned under Tiberius (Tertullian). Likewise a common danger could be feared. But they do not wish to depart; they labour for a common cause. We learn that the ministers of Christ must also be defended even at risk, and that they are ready to endure or do anything for him. Thus Christ is served with sincerity. The sluggishness of our age is condemned, when those who could act safely think that nothing should be risked; indeed they throw their own people to the monks and gratify themselves with the blood of others. ¶ 2. Paul gave thanks to God. He did not indeed neglect the brethren, but first he looked to God, by whose Spirit and power he saw that these men had been stirred up, and from considering this he is wholly strengthened. Let us imitate him, so that whatever good befalls us we refer to God as its author. In this way we shall also be rightly grateful to men, and we shall be less offended by their inconstancy. III. He is handed over to the prefect of the army with other prisoners, but on a different footing. For a private house is granted to him, and only one soldier is added to guard him. He was therefore without doubt commended by Paul... he is kept in a rented house at Rome.

units.la: Centurione, &c. Inprimis tamen Deus spectandus, qui Praefecti quoque animum ei deuinxit, vt prius Lysiae, Felicis, Agryppæ & aliorum militum.
units.tr: Centurion, etc. Yet above all God is to be regarded, who bound the heart of the prefect to him, as he had earlier bound that of Lysias, Felix, Agrippa and other soldiers.

units.la: Interim Nor. Sortem sanctorum in mundo, cum iniquis reputantur, vt Christus Isa 53. Et cum mundus quosuis ferat, foli pij videntur coercendi, vt qui omnium turbarum authores sint. Sic olim accidit, Reg. 18. Ier. 36 37.38. Nemo ergo offendatur hodie.
units.tr: Meanwhile note: the lot of the saints in the world is that they are counted with the wicked, as Christ was (Isa. 53). And since the world tolerates whoever it likes, the godly alone seem to be restrained, as though they were the authors of all the disturbances. This happened of old (1 Kings 18; Jer. 36, 37, 38). Let no one therefore be offended today.

units.la: Interim obseruemus Dei fidem & potentiam, qui suos tunc quoque seruat, & omnia moderatur in suam gloriam. Miles hic Pauli seruus & defensor fuit contra quosuis. Deinde liber aceessus omnibus patuit ad illum, quos docuit, & sic ad se collegit Ecclesiam. Scripsit praeterea ad exteras Ecclesias, &c. Verè ergo ait, verbum Dei non esse vinctum, posteriori ad Timotheum secundo. Sunt similia exempla passim. Et hodie multi Euangelium ex carceribus & ad supplicium ducti propagant. Ista nos consolentur & in officio contineant, ne desera mus nostram statio- nem. Ore- mus.
units.tr: Meanwhile let us observe the faithfulness and power of God, who then also preserves his people and governs all things to his own glory. This soldier was Paul's servant and defender against all comers. Then free access was open to him for all whom he taught, and so he gathered a church to himself. Moreover he wrote to the churches abroad, etc. Truly, then, he says that the word of God is not bound (2 Tim. 2). There are similar examples everywhere, and today many spread the gospel from prisons and from those led to punishment. Let these things console us and keep us in our duty, so that we do not desert our post. Let us pray.

units.la: Hoc.
units.tr: This.

units.la: HOMILIA CCVII.
units.tr: HOMILIA CCVII.

units.la: 17 Factum est autem, ut tertio post die conuocaret Paulus Iudæorum primos, qui vbi conuenissent dixit eis, Ego viri fratres, quum nihil fecerim ad uersus populum aut ritus patrios, vinctus traditus sum Hierosolymis in manus Romanorum.
units.tr: 17 And it came to pass that on the third day after, Paul called together the chief of the Jews; and when they were come together, he said to them: Men and brethren, though I have done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, I was delivered prisoner at Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

units.la: 18 Qui quæstione de me habita, volebant me dimittere, quod nullum sit in me crimen capitale.
units.tr: 18 They, having examined me, would have released me, because there was no capital crime in me.

units.la: 19 Sed contradicentibus Iudæis coactus sum appellare Cæsarem, non tamen quod habeam, de quo gentem meam accusem.
units.tr: 19 But when the Jews contradicted, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not as though I had anything whereof to accuse my nation.

units.la: 20 Ob hanc igitur causam vos aduocaui, quos viderem et alloquerer: nam propter spem Israelis circumdatus sum hac catena.
units.tr: 20 For this cause therefore I have called you, whom I might see and speak with; for because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

units.la: 21 Illi vero dixerunt ei, Nos neque literas accepimus de te ex Iudæa, neque aduenienes quisquam fratrum annuntiauit aut loquutus est aliquid male de te.
units.tr: 21 But they said to him: We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brethren who came hither report or speak anything evil of you.

units.la: 22 Velimus autem ex te audire quid sentias: nam de secta ista notum est nobis, vbique ei contradici.
units.tr: 22 But we would hear from you what you think; for as to this sect, we know that it is everywhere spoken against.

units.la: Diuus
units.tr: The divine

units.la: Diluus Paulus ad Romanos scribens, fe dies & noctes pro Iudaeis Deum precari testatur, adeoque pro illis anathema fieri optat, Rom 10. 9. At hoc illi non ficto animo excidisse, tum ex aliis locis, tum ex praesenti colligi poterit. Licet enim vbique terrarum acerrimos hostes inuenerit Iudaeos (1. Thess. 2.) semper tamen illis primis Euangelium praedicat. Et nunc cum illorum opera effectum esset, vt Romam captiuus duceretur, mox primos ex illis conuocat, & illis non a quoquam requisitus, rerum suarum omnium rationem redere dignatur.
units.tr: Divus Paul, writing to the Romans, testifies that he prays to God day and night for the Jews, and even wishes to be made anathema for them (Rom. 9.2–3; printed 10.9). That this came from no feigned heart can be gathered both from other passages and from the present one. For although he found the Jews the bitterest enemies everywhere on earth (1 Thess. 2), he still always preaches the gospel to them first. And now, since by their doing it had come about that he was led away captive to Rome, he soon summons the leaders among them, and, though no one has asked him, deigns to give an account of all his affairs.

units.la: Quo exemplo docemur, vt iuxta Christi praeceptu inimicos diligere debeamus. Matth. 5. Non vt ad illorum scelera conniueamus, sed vt salutl illorum studeamus per omnia. Porro videamus praesentem locum ordine.
units.tr: From this example we are taught that, according to Christ's precept, we ought to love our enemies (Matt. 5), not so as to wink at their wickedness, but so as to labour for their salvation in every way. Let us now look at the present passage in order.

units.la: I. Paulus, cum illi conuenissent, apologiam instituit, cuius capita sunt haec: I. Medetur prauis suspicionibus. Videbatur publicam pacem populi Iudaici turbare noua doctrina. Deinde violatae patrum religionis accusabatur. Act. 21. 25. Sed verumque negat. Unde colligimus, Christiano licere, vt causam suam & famam tueatur, ne videlicet Euangelium male audiat.
units.tr: I. When they had assembled, Paul set out his defence, whose heads are these: 1. He meets their wrong suspicions. The new teaching seemed to disturb the public peace of the Jewish people; then he was accused of violating the religion of the fathers (Acts 21:25). But he denies both. From this we gather that a Christian may defend his cause and his reputation, lest the gospel be ill spoken of.

units.la: Sed Not. ¶ Christi ministros nec in publicam pacem,nec in patrum religionem peccare, quando scelera & superstitiones oppugnant. Accusantur quidem de vtroque, sed falso. Pax enim non reprehensione scelerum legitima, sed ipsis celeribus solet turbari. Reg. 18. 2. Sam. 12. Hic primi sunt vsurarij, monopolae, &c. Deinde Christi fides & religio vetustissima omnium est, 1. Pet. 1. 2. Pet. 1. Heb. 11. Moriturus hac praeitur.
units.tr: But note: Christ's ministers do not sin against the public peace or against the religion of the fathers when they attack crimes and superstitions. They are indeed accused of both, but falsely. For peace is not lawfully disturbed by the rebuke of crimes; it is usually disturbed by the crimes themselves (1 Kings 18; 2 Sam. 12). Here the first offenders are usurers, monopolists, etc. Then, Christ's faith and religion is the most ancient of all (1 Pet. 1; 2 Pet. 1; Heb. 11). In dying, he goes before in this faith.

units.la: II. Prouocationis rationem reddit, quae Iudeis odiosissima erat. Partim enim gentis liberati derogare videbantur, qui prouocabant: partim per se ignominiosum, & cum iudicis contumelia coniunctum putatur. Ergo coactum id fecisse dicit, non vt apud Caesarem accuset, sed vt se liberet.
units.tr: II. He gives an account of his appeal, which was most hateful to the Jews. For those who appealed seemed partly to disparage their nation, and partly the act was thought disgraceful in itself and joined with an insult to the judge. Therefore he says he did it under compulsion, not in order to accuse his nation before Caesar, but to free himself.

units.la: Not. ¶ Defensionem ciuilem & legitimam Christianis minimè prohibitā esse. Iuliani sunt, qui in eum finem abutuntur loco Matth. 5. Ad vindictam priuatam pertinet: de qua Deut. 32.
units.tr: Note: a civil and lawful defence is by no means forbidden to Christians. There are some who abuse Matt. 5 to this end. That passage pertains to private vengeance, concerning which see Deut. 32.

units.la: III. Statum totius causae proponit. Pro-pter ipsum Israelis vinctus sum. Christum in intelligit, in quo omnes Iudaei regnum & libertatem sperabant, Luc. 2. Fallebantur autem in eo, quod illum non agnoscerent, vt adhuc hodie, &c.
units.tr: III. He sets out the state of the whole case: "For the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain." He means Christ, in whom all the Jews hoped for a kingdom and liberty (Luke 2). But they were deceived in this, that they did not acknowledge him, as even today, etc.

units.la: Cap. 28. Nor. ¶ Cæcitatem mundi in salutis negotio. Frequens hodie, vt qui Christo gloriantur, oblatum respuunt. Maximè, quando vel quæstu suo derogari, vel carni frænum iniici sentiunt.
units.tr: Chapter 28. Note: the blindness of the world in the matter of salvation. It is common today for those who boast of Christ to reject him when he is offered, especially when they feel that their gain is diminished or a bridle is put on the flesh.

units.la: Interim obserua, non aliam salutis spem esse, quàm quæ Christo nititur. In hoc enim promissionibus datæ, 2. Cor. 1. Hunc vnum Patres nouerunt, Ioh. 8. Gen. 49. Moses & Prophetæ Ioh. 5. 1. Pet. Apostoli Act. quarto, priori ad Corinthios secundo, Ioan. 6. In hoc firmiter ipsi quoque sperem us, & bene erit.
units.tr: Meanwhile observe that there is no other hope of salvation than that which rests on Christ. For in him the promises were given (2 Cor. 1). The Fathers knew this one alone (John 8; Gen. 49). Moses and the Prophets (John 5); Peter and the Apostles (Acts 4); the first letter to the Corinthians, chapter 2; John 6. In him let us also hope firmly, and it will be well.

units.la: II. Respondent Iudæi. 1. Testimonium innocentiæ ferunt Paulo. Nemo de te scripsit. Nam sacerdotes iam securi, nihil sibi amplius ab illo timendum putabant. Deinde nemo venit, &c.
units.tr: II. The Jews reply. 1. They bear witness to Paul's innocence: "No one has written anything about you." For the priests, now secure, thought they had nothing more to fear from him. Then: "No one came," etc.

units.la: Nor. ¶ Sortem sanctorum. Quamuis illorum innocentia omnibus comperta sit, hostes tamen habent, quibus authoribus vel incarcerantur, vel in exilium relegantur. Vtrum verò fiat, hostes securi illorum causam negligunt, nec quisquam est, qui horum curam ad se pertinere putet. Elias, Ieremias. Tandem ferè è medio tolluntur, &c. Exempla hodie multa sunt passim.
units.tr: Note: the lot of the saints. Although their innocence is known to all, they have enemies, at whose instigation they are either imprisoned or banished. Whether this happens, the enemies, being secure, neglect their cause, and no one thinks the care of these people is his concern. (Elijah, Jeremiah.) At last they are for the most part removed from the midst, etc. There are many examples of this today, everywhere.

units.la: II. Cupiunt audire Pauli sententiam de fide & religione, quamuis vbique contradicatur.
units.tr: II. They desire to hear Paul's opinion on faith and religion, although everywhere it is contradicted.

units.la: Nota. ¶ 1 Laude dignum, quòd non ex cæcati sunt præiudicio, ita vt audire dignentur. Faciunt hoc multi hodie, qui sibijpsis oft um regni cælorum præclu- dunt, &c. Serpentum instar sunt. Pudeat autem illos, quòd Iudæis excæcatiores sunt, &c.
units.tr: Note. 1. It is worthy of praise that they are not blinded by prejudice, so as to deign to hear him. Many today do the opposite, who shut the kingdom of heaven against themselves, etc. They are like serpents. But they should be ashamed that they are more blinded than the Jews, etc.

units.la: ¶ 2. Euangelij fortem, cui ab initio contradictum fuit. Ita prædictam Pfal.2. Luc. 2. Non potest hoc ferre diabolus, mundi princeps, 1. Iohan. 3. Non flagitiosi, Iohannis tertio. Non iustitiarij hypocritæ, ad Roman 10.9. Non mundo dediti, &c. Arguitur magna mundi corruptio, & eiusdem damnatio iusta Ioh. 3. Præparemur ad certamen.
units.tr: 2. The lot of the gospel, which was contradicted from the beginning. So it was foretold (Ps. 2; Luke 2). The devil, the prince of the world, cannot bear this (1 John 3). Nor can the licentious (John 3), nor the self-righteous hypocrites (Rom. 10), nor those given over to the world, etc. The great corruption of the world is shown, and its just condemnation (John 3). Let us prepare for the struggle.

units.la: Interim vides inuictam & proinde diuinam esse Euangelij potentiam. Alias religiones nemo oppugnauit armata manu, & tamen corruerunt. Huic semper contradictum, imo contra hanc pugnatum. Durat tamen. Quid ergo offendimur? Iohan. 15. Vide Isa. 40. Oremus.
units.tr: Meanwhile you see that the power of the gospel is invincible and therefore divine. No one has attacked other religions with armed hand, and yet they have fallen. This one has always been contradicted, indeed fought against, yet it endures. Why then are we offended? (John 15). See Isa. 40. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CCIIX.
units.tr: HOMILY 208.

units.la: 23 Quum igitur constituissent diem, venerunt ad eum in hospitium
units.tr: "And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God,

units.la: complures, quibus cum testificatione ex ponebat regnum Dei, studens eis persuadere, quae de Iesu Christo sunt, ex Lege Mosis et Prophetis, a mane usque ad vesperam.
units.tr: persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening."

units.la: 24 Et alii quidem assentiebantur iis, quae dicebantur, quidam vero non credebant.
units.tr: "And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not."

units.la: QVamuis Iesu Christi & Euangelij ipsius ministri varijs persequutionibus exerceantur, & saepe vincula & carceres sustineant, Dei verbum tamen vinci non potest, cum spiritus ille spiret ubi vult, 2. Tim. 2. Ioh. 3. Imo vt Christi morte latius propagatum fuit, sicuti ille praedixerat, Ioh. 12. Ita ministrorum quoque afflictionibus augescit. Exemplum huius in Paulo habemus. Praedicauit quidem hucusque per totum orbem, Rom. 15. Sed magis ostium illi iam capto aperitur. Iam enim Romae praedicat liberè omnibus, sic vt in Caesaris quoque familiam doctrina haec penetret, Phil. 4. 1. Id quomodo factum sit, Lucas diligenter describit, & qui dem ex multis concionibus vnam deligit, ex qua alias omnes iudicemus. Videamus singula.
units.tr: Although the ministers of Jesus Christ and of the Gospel itself are harassed by various persecutions, and often endure chains and prisons, the word of God cannot be conquered, since that Spirit blows where it wills (2 Tim. 2; John 3). Indeed, just as Christ's death spread the Gospel more widely, as he had foretold (John 12), so it grows through the afflictions of its ministers as well. We have an example of this in Paul. He had indeed preached until now throughout the whole world (Rom. 15), but now a door is opened wider to him. For now at Rome he preaches freely to all, so that this teaching even penetrates into the household of Caesar (Phil. 4; 1). Luke describes carefully how this came about, and he selects one sermon out of many, by which we may judge all the others. Let us look at the details.

units.la: I. Locus notatur & tempus. Conueni-unt
units.tr: I. The place and the time are noted. They assemble

units.la: unt constituto die in hospitiu Pauli. Non-dum enim templa habebant Christiani, nec si habuissent Romae, liberum fuisset Paulo, in illa exire. Ideo in privatis domibus concionati sunt. Vide Actorum 1 2 4. 12.20.
units.tr: on an appointed day at Paul's lodging. For Christians did not yet have churches, and even if they had had them at Rome, it would not have been lawful for Paul to go out to them. So they preached in private houses. See Acts 1, 2, 4, 12, 20.

units.la: NOTA Cultum Dei & doctrinam non debere ita alligari loco, quasi ille alij quid ad salutem faciat. Nam Dei verbum ex seipso authoritatem habet. Preces vero ubique locorum exaudiuntur, i ad Timoth 2 Psalm. 34. In necessitate ergo cuiuis locus & quoduis tempus sufficiet. Probatur hoc multis sanctorum exemplis. Interim vbi pace fruimur, & permagistratus licet, ordo feruetur, qui & locum & tempus certum requirit, i ad Corinthios decimoquarto. Vnde colligimus primitiuae Eccl. fiae exemplum minime patrocinari Anabaptistis, &c.
units.tr: NOTE: The worship of God and doctrine ought not to be tied so closely to a place, as if one place contributed something to salvation. For God's word has authority from itself. Prayers, however, are heard in every place (1 Tim. 2; Ps. 34). In necessity, therefore, any place and any time will suffice for anyone. This is proved by many examples of the saints. Meanwhile, where we enjoy peace and the magistrate permits it, order must be kept, which also requires a fixed place and time (1 Cor. 14). Hence we gather that the example of the primitive Church by no means favours the Anabaptists, etc.

units.la: II. Argumentum concionis Paulinae ex primitur. Differunt de regno Dei. Euangelium sic dicitur, & quae hoc continentur mysteria. Ita vero confutauit Iudaeorum errores, qui ex prophetijs male intellectis regnum Messiae terrenum imaginabantur.
units.tr: He therefore taught that the kingdom of God is spiritual, its beginning in this age being the new life, but its future being eternal happiness, etc. Because they did not know the author of this kingdom, he taught that it is Christ, and urged them to embrace him.

units.la: Docuit ergo spirituale esse regnum Dei, cuius initium in hoc seculo fit vitae nouae. tas,in futuro autem æterna felicitas, &c. Quia verò huius regni authorem ignorabant, hunc docuit esse Christū, & ad hunc amplexandum hortatus est.
units.tr: But note: the Gospel is called the kingdom of God (Matt. 3; 4; 13; 21; Mark 1; Luke 13; Acts 8; 19). It is so named from its effect and its end. For it offers us the kingdom of God and happiness, and at the same time subjects us to be governed by God (2 Cor. 10; Rom. 1:16).

units.la: Sed Not. ¶ Euangelium dici regnum Dei. Matth.tertio, quarto, decimotertio, vigesimo primo, Marci primo, Lucæ decimotertio, Actorum octauo, decimonono. Ab effectu & fine sic dicitur. Offert enim nobis regnum Dei & felicitatem, simulque Deo nos gubernandos subijcit, 2.Cor. 10. Rom.1.16.
units.tr: Hence it is clear what the duty of those who hold the Gospel is: that they take care that God reigns in them, not the devil, whose kingdom is destroyed by Christ (1 John 3; Gen. 3). The whole man is required. We pray for this kingdom (Matt. 6). Would that the pseudo-evangelicals would weigh these things, etc. Meanwhile, ministers are also reminded of their office.

units.la: Vnde patet quod sit officium Euangelicorum: Curent vt Deus in ipsis regnet, non diabolus, cuius regnum à Christo destruitur, priore Iohannis 3. Genef.3.Requiritur totus homo. Pro hoc regno oramus, Matth. 6. Hæc vtinam expenderent pfeudoeuangelici, &c. Interim ministri sui officij quoque admonentur.
units.tr: III. The source of this doctrine is indicated: he drew it from Moses and the prophets, showing that what they foretold about the Messiah has been fulfilled in Christ. So Christ (Luke 24; John 5).

units.la: III. Fons doctrinæ huius indicatur, Sumpsit ex Mose & prophetis, ostendens in Christo impleta esse, quæ illi de Messia prædixerunt. Sic Christus Lucæ 24. Iohan.5.
units.tr: Note 1. What ought to be taught in the Church? Not the inventions of men, but the word of God. For it is the house of God (1 Tim. 3). Hence all ministers are bound by this command (Jer. 3; Ezek. 3; 33; Matt. 28). Thus both ministers who preach the doctrine of others are rebuked (Jer. 33), and the Church, which hears another voice (Ps. 45; John 10).

units.la: Not. ¶ 1. Quid in Ecclesia doceri debeat? Non hominum figmenta, sed Dei verbum. Est enim domus Dei, prioread Timoth 3. Hinc est, quod huic mandato omnes ministri astringuntur, Ier.3. Ezech. 3,33. Matth.28. Arguuntur itaque tum ministri, qui aliorum doctrinam praedicant, Ier.33. tum Ecclesiae, quae aliam vocem audiunt, Psal.45. Ioh.10.
units.tr: Note 1. What ought to be taught in the Church? Not human inventions, but God's word. For it is the house of God (1 Tim. 3). Hence all ministers are bound by this command (Jer. 3; Ezek. 3, 33; Matt. 28). Thus both ministers are condemned who preach the teaching of others (Jer. 33), and churches are condemned which hear another voice (Ps. 45; John 10).

units.la: § 2. Consensum veteris & noui testamenti. Vtrinque vnus Christus & eadem salutis ratio. In illo praedictum, quicquid in hoc impletum esse scribitur, priore Petri 1. posteriore Pet. 1. Patet hinc omnium vetustissimam esse fide in Christo, vt quae ab ipsa mundi origine fuit patribus tradita. Refer huc primas promissiones, Gen. 3. vigesimo secundo, quadragesimo nono, Ioh. 8. &c.
units.tr: § 2. The agreement of the Old and New Testaments. In both there is one Christ and the same way of salvation. What is written as fulfilled in the one was foretold in the other (1 Pet. 1; 2 Pet. 1). It is clear from this that faith in Christ is the most ancient of all, since it was handed down to the fathers from the very origin of the world. Refer here the first promises (Gen. 3, 22, 49; John 8), etc.

units.la: IV. Quamdiu praedicârit Paulus? Ama navsq; ad vesperam.
units.tr: IV. How long did Paul preach? From morning until evening.

units.la: Vnde disputationem to die de fuisse patet. No 1. § Studium ardens tum Pauli, tum auditorum. Simile exemplum habes Act.20.
units.tr: From this it is clear that the disputation lasted a whole day. Note 1. § The ardent zeal both of Paul and of the hearers. A similar example you have in Acts 20.

units.la: Arguitur nostra ignauia & fastidium, quo & ministri quidam, & multi ex audi-toribus hodie laborant. Idem fit vtrinque, quod est, Isa.28 56. Ezech.33. Nisi vtrinque corrigamur, cueniet quod Deus minatur Amoz 7.
units.tr: Our sloth and weariness are rebuked, which today afflicts both some ministers and many of the hearers. The same thing happens on both sides, which is in Isa. 28; 56; Ezek. 33. Unless we are corrected on both sides, what God threatens in Amos 7 will come to pass.

units.la: V. Effectus. Alij credunt, alij non. Imo
units.tr: V. The effect. Some believed, others did not. Indeed,

units.la: multa vtrinque exoritur disceptatio: vt fe quentia docebunt. &c. NOT. {q}Euangelij fortem in hoc mundo. Christus enim lapis est, alijs in ruinam positus, alijs in resurrectionem Luc. 2.
units.tr: a great dispute arises on both sides, as the following will show, etc. Note the lot of the Gospel in this world. For Christ is a stone, laid for the fall of some and for the resurrection of others (Luke 2).

units.la: Consolentur hæc ministros, quando fe frustra prædicare vident, Ioh.15 Simul offendiculo medeantur, quod hodie expau citate credentium oritur. Hic ex voluntate rijs auditoribus tam pauci credunt, &c. Oremus.
units.tr: These things console ministers when they see that they preach in vain (John 15). At the same time they remedy the stumbling block which arises today from the timidity of believers. Here, from the will of God, so few of the hearers believe, etc. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CCIX.
units.tr: HOMILIA CCIX.

units.la: 25 Quum autem inter fe discordes effent, difceffierunt, quum Paulus hoc verbum dixisset: Recte sane locutus est Spiritus sanctus per Efaiam Prophetam patribus nostris:
units.tr: 25 When, however, they were disagreeing among themselves, they departed, after Paul had spoken this word: Rightly did the Holy Spirit speak through the prophet Isaiah to our fathers,

units.la: 26 Dicens, Vade ad populum istum, & dic: Auditu audietis, & non intelligetis, & videntes videbitis, & non cernetis.
units.tr: 26 saying, Go to this people and say: By hearing you will hear, and will not understand; and seeing you will see, and will not perceive.

units.la: 27 Pinguefactum enim est cor populi hujus, & auribus graviter audiunt, & oculos suos conniuerunt, ne cernant oculis, & auribus audiant, & corde intelligant, et convertantur, et sanem eos. 28 Notum ergo sit vobis, missam esse Gentibus hanc Dei salutem, & ipsos audituros.
units.tr: 27 For the heart of this people has grown fat, and they hear heavily with their ears, and they have closed their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I heal them. 28 Let it be known therefore to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will hear it.

units.la: 29 Quum ergo haec dixissent, exierunt Iudaei, multam habentes inter se disceptationem.
units.tr: 29 When he had said these things, the Jews went out, having much disputation among themselves.

units.la: QVamuis Euangelij doctrina veritatis lucem, ipsamque salutem nobis offerat, plerumque tamen illam mundus hic aspernari solet. Quia vero hoc multos in fide infirmos offendit, frequenter de eo scripturae admonent: & simul veteres exempla proponit spiritus sanctus, ut hanc mundi peruersitatem non nouam esse agnoscamus. Inter haec memorabile est praesens hoc. Paulus enim toto die ex scripturis de Christo disseruit, & quidem apud peritos scripturae, & voluntarios auditores. Attamen non omnes conuertere poterit. Imo plerique reclamant.
units.tr: Although the doctrine of the Gospel offers us the light of truth and salvation itself, the world here is accustomed for the most part to despise it. Because this offends many who are weak in faith, the Scriptures often warn us about it, and at the same time the Holy Spirit sets before us examples from the past, so that we may recognise that this perversity of the world is not new. Among these, the present passage is worth remembering. For Paul reasoned from the Scriptures about Christ all day long, and that among those skilled in the Scripture and willing listeners. Yet he could not convert all of them. Indeed, many objected.

units.la: Sequitur ergo quid cum illis porro actum sit.&c.
units.tr: What then followed with them is told next, etc.

units.la: I. Arguit illorum contumaciam Paulus, & Dei horrendum iudicium illis denuntiat. Ita enim cum contumacibus agendum est iuxta Christi exemplum, Matt. 15.21.25. Luc.11.&c. Allegat autem (ne quid exaffeƈtu dicere videatur) oraculum ex Isa.6. vt per hoc impios terreat, infirmis vero medeatur.Quasi diceret : Non nouum est, hos ita reluctari. Tales olim fuerunt, & tales fore reuelato Christi regno, olim praedictum,Ioh. 12. Isa.53. Sed sententi ent tande magno suo malo quid fecerint.
units.tr: I. Paul rebukes their obstinacy and announces to them God's dreadful judgment. For so ought one to deal with the obstinate, following the example of Christ, Matt. 15.21.25; Luke 11, etc. He cites, however (lest he seem to speak out of personal feeling), an oracle from Isaiah 6, so that by it he might terrify the wicked and heal the weak. As if he were saying: It is nothing new that these men resist in this way. Such men there were in former times, and such there will be when the kingdom of Christ is revealed; this was foretold long ago, John 12, Isaiah 53. But let them at last feel, to their great harm, what they have done.

units.la: Porrò quoad oraculum cumprimis me morabile est, & sexies citatur, Matth. 13. Mar.4.Luc.8.Ioh.12.Rom.10.&c.
units.tr: Moreover, as to the oracle, it is especially noteworthy, and it is cited six times: Matt. 13; Mark 4; Luke 8; John 12; Rom. 10; etc.

units.la: Tria continet. 1.Peccatum Iudaeorum de incredulitas volutamaridi scribitur, quòd nimirum scientes & volentes caecutiant, & agnitam veritatis lucem aspernentur. Id vero explicat similibus eorum, qui se caecos & surdos esse simulant.Intellexerunt ergo, sed ne sic qui dem crediderunt. Vide Iohan.3.5.7.8.10. Matt.22. Frequens hoc malum hodie.
units.tr: It contains three things. 1. The sin of the Jews and their unbelief are described, namely that knowingly and willingly they make themselves blind and despise the light of truth once recognised. This he explains by comparison with those who pretend to be blind and deaf. They understood, therefore, but not even so did they believe. See John 3, 5, 7, 8, 10; Matt. 22. This evil is frequent today.

units.la: Interim Not. ¶ Perspicuitatem verbi Dei. Vident,audiunt,intelligūt homines: nec id negare possunt. Est enim lux Psal. 119.Gladius item,qui inuitis illis cordapenetrat. Quòd vero non creditur illi,nec obeditur,ex hominibus est, qui quod vident,nolunt videre & intelligere,&c. Vide 2.Cor.4.
units.tr: Meanwhile note the clarity of the Word of God. Men see, hear and understand; nor can they deny it. For it is light, Psalm 119. And also a sword, which penetrates their unwilling hearts. But that it is not believed or obeyed comes from men who, though they see what they see, are unwilling to see and understand, etc. See 2 Cor. 4.

units.la: II. Causa huius incredulitatis: Corinthiorum: nimirum prauis affectibus, quando illos do illos præualere patiuntur homines, fe que totos illis mancipant. Explicat Christas elegantiparabolaLuc.14. Videre est hoc in ludæis,sacerdotibus simul & populo. Suis commodis & honori studuerunt, Ioh 5 12 Populus suis præsulibus gratifica ri voluit,& non nisi carnalia quæsiuit, Iohan 6.In noltris etiam hodie cernitur.
units.tr: II. The cause of this unbelief: the depravity of the heart, namely evil affections, when men allow them to prevail over them and wholly surrender themselves to them. Christ explains this with an elegant parable, Luke 14. It may be seen in the Jews, the priests and the people alike. They sought their own advantage and honour; the people wished to please their leaders and sought only carnal things, John 6. It is seen in our own times as well.

units.la: NOT. Homines ipsos sibi malorum authores esse.Mittit enim veritatis lucem Deus.Sed hanc ingenita peruerfitate hominesafpernantur,Ioh.1. Vide Ioh.3 ita de nouissimis temporibus Paulus vaticinatur, 2.Tim.4. Id vero videmus impleri iuxta literam. Quid quod multi publicè testantur, fe docentes meliora nolle fere,&c.
units.tr: NOTE. That men themselves are the authors of their own evils. For God sends the light of truth. But by their inborn perversity men reject it, John 1. See John 3. Thus Paul prophesies about the last times, 2 Tim. 4. Indeed we see this fulfilled according to the letter. What of the fact that many publicly testify that, while teaching, they hardly wish for better things, etc.

units.la: III. Pœna talium denuntiatur: & quidem duplex.
units.tr: III. The punishment of such people is announced, and indeed it is twofold.

units.la: In prophetatertia quoque adijcitur.Primum ipsi non conuertuntur, vt fanari possint.Negatur omnis spes Quia verbum respuunt, quo ad conuersionem inuitantur, Isa.65. Amoz 2. Pereunt ergo in peccatis suis,iuxta illud Christi, Iohan nis 8. Deinde salus transfertur ad gentes.Ita minatur Deus, Deuter. 32. Matth. 21.Crebrò hoc denuntiatur propter confidentem perfuasionem. Id verò sic eue
units.tr: In the third part of the prophecy this is also added. First, they themselves are not converted, so that they could be healed. All hope is denied, because they spurn the Word by which they are invited to conversion, Isa. 65; Amos 2. They therefore perish in their sins, according to that saying of Christ, John 8. Then salvation is transferred to the Gentiles. Thus God threatens, Deut. 32; Matt. 21. This is often announced on account of their confident persuasion.

units.la: Incredulitatis pœna.
units.tr: The punishment of unbelief.

units.la: nisse constat Rom.10.11 Tandem secutum excidium, quod praedictum fuit, similiter Isa.6 Item Mat.23.24. Luc 13.19. Tunc vero hoc factum, quando regnum Dei ablatum. Pella.
units.tr: It is agreed that this came to pass, Rom. 10, 11. Finally there followed the destruction that had been foretold, likewise Isa. 6; also Matt. 23, 24; Luke 13, 19. And this happened then, when the kingdom of God was taken away. Pella.

units.la: NOT. Quid hodie spectandum, si similia faciamus. Constat enim sibi psi Deus semper, Ier.3. Nec est, quod nobis repulsis Dei regnū collapsurum putemus. Eadem persuasio olim Iudaeos seduxit. Mat. 3. Ioh.8. Quin cogitemus quod nobis dicitur, Rom.11 Lactantij oraculum.
units.tr: NOTE. What we should consider today if we do similar things. For God is always consistent with himself, Jer. 3. Nor is there reason for us to think that the kingdom of God will fall when we are rejected. The same persuasion once led the Jews astray, Matt. 3; John 8. Rather let us consider what is said to us, Rom. 11. The oracle of Lactantius.

units.la: II. Effectus omnium narratur. Exeunt multam inter se habentes disceptationem. Ita fieri solet, quando Euangelium mundo praedicatur, sicuti Christus praedixit, Luc.12. Matt.10. Fit hoc non Euangelij sed impiorum vitio. Quo enim propius vrgentur impij verbo Dei, eo magis insaniunt. Sic Cain, Ge 4. Pharao, Achab, Zedechias &c. Hodie multi qui sibi dedecori esse putant, si arguantur. At qua his pij non possunt cedere, exardescunt contentiones.
units.tr: II. The effect of all this is recounted. They departed, having much disputation among themselves. So it usually happens when the Gospel is preached to the world, just as Christ foretold, Luke 12; Matt. 10. This comes about not through the fault of the Gospel but of the wicked. For the more the wicked are pressed by the Word of God, the more they rage. So Cain, Gen. 4; Pharaoh, Ahab, Zedekiah, etc. Today many think it a disgrace to them if they are rebuked. But since the godly cannot yield to these, contentions blaze up.

units.la: Interim NOT. Non omnino nihil apud illos profecisse Paulum, quando non defuerunt, qui se impijs illis Christi hostibus opponerent. A. Discimus, nunquam sine omni fructu praedicari verbum Dei. Vt enim per fe frugiferum est, ita vbique suos habet Christus, qui illud rite suscipiunt. Huc pertinent, quae habemus, Isa. 55. Matth. 13. Luc. 8.
units.tr: Meanwhile NOTE. That Paul had accomplished something among them, not at all nothing, since there were not lacking those who opposed themselves to those wicked enemies of Christ. A. We learn that the Word of God is never preached without some fruit. For as it is fruitful in itself, so Christ has his own everywhere who receive it rightly. To this pertain the passages we have, Isa. 55; Matt. 13; Luke 8.

units.la: B. Piorum & vere credentium esse, vt sese impijs opponant, nec ad illorum contradictiones & scommata conniueant. Non enim tepidos probat Deus, Apoc. 3. Arguuntur qui quiduis audire & referre possunt, &c. Sunt impij, stulti, miseri. Oremus.
units.tr: B. It belongs to the pious and truly believing to set themselves against the wicked, and not to connive at their contradictions and mockeries. For God does not approve of the lukewarm, Rev. 3. Those are rebuked who can hear and repeat anything whatever, etc. They are wicked, foolish, miserable. Let us pray.

units.la: HOMILIA CCX.
units.tr: HOMILY CCX.

units.la: 30 Mansit autem Paulus bien nium totum in proprio conductio: & exc piebat omnes, qui ad ipsum mi- grediebantur.
units.tr: 30 And Paul remained two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who came in to him.

units.la: 31 Praedicans regnum Dei, ac docens quae sunt de Domino Iesu Christo, cum omni libertate, nemine prohibente.
units.tr: 31 Preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, with all freedom, no one forbidding him.

units.la: DOminus noster Iesus Christus, Iohan. 14. ait: Non relinquam vos orphanos, &c. Item, Ego vobiscum sum vsque ad consummationem seculi, Matth. 28. Quarum promissionum veritas maxi-
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ says in John 14: "I will not leave you orphans," etc. Likewise, "I am with you always, even to the end of the age," Matt. 28. The truth of these promises shines most clearly in adversity, when Christ uses even these things for the advancement of our salvation and his own glory.

units.la: mè in aduersis elucet, quando ijs etiam Christus ad nostræ salutis & suæ gloriæ propagationem vtitur.Exemplum huius in Pauli captiuitate habemus. Licet enim hæc initiò totum Euangelij cursum impe ditura videretur,plus tamé ad propagan-dum quàm impediendū valuit. Nam hac occasione factum est,vt Paulus coram Ro-manis præsidibus, & tandem etiam Ro-mæ, adeoque in ipso prætorio prædican-di occasionem habuerit, ad Philippen. 1. Restant adhuc explicanda hæc.
units.tr: We have an example of this in Paul's captivity. For although at first this seemed likely to hinder the whole course of the Gospel, it nevertheless did more to advance it than to impede it. For through this occasion it came about that Paul had the opportunity to preach before the Roman governors, and finally at Rome itself, and so even in the praetorium, Phil. 1. These matters still remain to be explained.

units.la: Tempus captiuitatis Pauli. Mansit toto biennio,&c. Antea etiam toto biennio Hierosolymis detentus fuit, Act 24. Inter-cessit nauigatio, &c. Hic tamen illud com-modi fuit, quòd non in carcere, sed in con-ducto suo hospitio agere potest.
units.tr: The time of Paul's captivity. He remained two whole years, etc. Previously too he was held at Jerusalem for two whole years, Acts 24. A voyage intervened, etc. Here, however, this was the advantage: he could live not in a prison but in his own rented lodging.

units.la: NOTA. ¶ Sortem sanctorum in hoc mundo. Quàm multi enim facinorosi inte-ra liberè grassati sunt. At Paulus pro fa-cinorosissimo tam diu detinetur. Sic cum Iohanne sub Herode factum, Lucæ 3 Mar. 6. Sic dimiso Barnaba Christus crucifigi tur, Iohan. 18. Lucæ 23. Vsus horum est, ne similibus offendamur, Matthæi 5. Non est magistro maior discipulus, Mat. 10. De inde tribulationum diuturnitas æterni-tate tate prænij compensatur,ad Rom.8. 2.ad Timotheum 2.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ The lot of the saints in this world. For how many criminals have gone about freely all their lives! Yet Paul is detained so long, as though he were the most notorious criminal. So it happened with John under Herod, Luke 3; Mark 6. So Christ, with Barabbas released, is crucified, John 18; Luke 23. The purpose of these examples is that we not be offended by similar things, Matt. 5. "The disciple is not above his master," Matt. 10. Moreover, the long duration of tribulations is compensated by the eternity of the reward, Rom. 8; 2 Tim. 2.

units.la: ¶ 2. Bonitas Dei magna,qui propter electos suos Paulū tam diu custodiunt Romæ,& quidem in libera custodia, sub Nerone crudelissimo tyranno. Quis enim hoc sperauisset? Consoletur hoc omnes, qui in Dei vocatione ambulant. Quoad enim Deo vsui erimus,& nostræ salutis ratio exigit,Deus nos tuebitur.Noe,Moses, Ionas,&c. Idem vbi tempus postulauerit, nos in filij sui regnum transferet.
units.tr: ¶ 2. God's goodness is great, who for the sake of his elect keeps Paul so long at Rome, and indeed in free custody, under Nero, the most cruel tyrant. For who would have hoped for this? Let this console all who walk in God's calling. For as long as we shall be useful to God, and the reason of our salvation requires it, God will protect us. Noah, Moses, Jonah, etc. The same God, when the time requires it, will transfer us into the kingdom of his Son.

units.la: II. Quid toto hoc biennio fecerit Paulus. Suscepit omnes ad se venientes. Item prædicauit ingenuè cum fiducia. Idem ergo fecit quòd cùm liber esset. Adhæc Epistolas scripsit, quibus Ecclesias hinc inde docuit simul & consolatus est: nimirum ad Ephesios,Philippens.Colossenses, posteriorem ad Timotheum, ad Philemonem,Hebræos, &c. Itaque plus profuit, quàm antea. Atqui multa absterrere potè rant. Captiuus propter doctrinam hanc. Iudæos iam contumaces & hostes sensè-rat. Quid solus facere? Seditiosum,ex vinculis scribere? Periculum ne arctius as seruetur.Sed officium facit.
units.tr: II. What Paul did during these two years. He received all who came to him. Likewise he preached openly and with confidence. So he did the same as when he was free. Besides, he wrote Epistles by which he taught and at the same time comforted the churches here and there: namely to the Ephesians, the Philippians, the Colossians, the later one to Timothy, to Philemon, to the Hebrews, etc. Thus he profited more than before. And yet many things could have frightened him: a captive on account of this doctrine; the Jews, already obstinate, had become his enemies. What could he do alone? Write seditiously from his chains? Would the danger not be pressed more tightly? But he performs his duty.

units.la: NOT. ¶1. Quid Deo debeamus, quando illum beneficum & protectorem expe- rimur. Vtamur omnibus ad gloriam ipsi- us,nec propter pericula,vel praeterita vel futura,officium negligamus.
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ 1. What we owe God, when we experience him as benefactor and protector. Let us use everything for his glory, and let us not neglect our duty on account of dangers, whether past or future.

units.la: Arguuntur, qui hodie propter hostes vndique imminentes & omnis generis pe- ricula silendum putant. Quin eo fortius agendum,vt Deo nos gratos praebeamus, cuius fidem & opem in tantis periculis experimur.
units.tr: Rebuked are those who today think one should keep silent because of enemies threatening on every side and dangers of every kind. Rather we must act all the more boldly, so that we may show ourselves pleasing to God, whose faith and help we experience in such great perils.

units.la: 2. Quid praedicauit? Regnum Dei. Dictum de hoc antea. Sed additur per ex- positionem: Docens quae sunt de Domino Iesu. Tum ergo praedicatur Dei regnum, cum Christus praedicatur. Vnde colligi- tur, non aliam esse rationem perueniendi ad regnum Dei, nisi per Christum, Iohan. 14. Actor. 4. Vnus enim hic mediator est, in quo pater placatus, 1. Timot. 2. Matth. 3. 17 Vnus item, qui regnum diaboli euer- tit, Gen. 3. 1. Ioh. 3. Arguuntur omnes aliae religiones.
units.tr: 2. What did he preach? The kingdom of God. This was mentioned before. But it is added by way of explanation: teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus. Thus the kingdom of God is preached when Christ is preached. From this it is gathered that there is no other way of reaching the kingdom of God except through Christ, John 14; Acts 4. For there is one mediator, in whom the Father is appeased, 1 Tim. 2; Matt. 3:17. There is also one who overthrows the kingdom of the devil, Gen. 3; 1 John 3. All other religions are refuted.

units.la: 3. Quomodo praedicauit? Cum fidu- cia. Id est, liberè & ingenuè. Non puduit illum Euangelij, nec aduersa timuit, Rom. 1. 8. Vides quales ministros Dominus re- quirat. Nihil dandum mundo aut carnis sapientiae, quae sub modestiae praetextu fidei abnegationem introducit. Quin potius Christum audiamus, Marci 8. Lucæ 12.
units.tr: 3. How did he preach? With confidence. That is, freely and openly. He was not ashamed of the Gospel, nor did he fear adversity, Rom. 1:8. You see what kind of ministers the Lord requires. Nothing is to be yielded to the world or to the wisdom of the flesh, which under the pretext of modesty introduces the denial of the faith. Rather let us hear Christ, Mark 8; Luke 12.

units.la: ¶ 4. Successus.Nemine prohibente.Mirum hoc : si Neronem & Romam infpi-cias. Alibi semper fuerunt, qui se illi opponerent. Romæ non item, vbi diabolus regnare videbatur.Ita vbi & quando mini mè speres,fructum fert Euangelium. Sic Dan.4 &c.Sunt enim in Dei manu corda hominum,qui illa vt maris fluctus frænare nouit,Iob.38. Huius auxilium sperent, quicunq; in illo fortes sunt.
units.tr: ¶ 4. The outcome. No one forbidding. Remarkable this is, if you look at Nero and Rome. Elsewhere there were always those who opposed him; at Rome there were none, where the devil seemed to reign. Thus where and when you least expect it, the Gospel bears fruit. So Dan. 4, etc. For the hearts of men are in God's hand, and he knows how to bridle them as the waves of the sea, Job 38. Let those who are strong in him hope for his help.

units.la: III. Quid euoluto biennio egerit?Lucas non scripsit,quia non opus fuit Ecclesiam grauari pluribus. Nihil enim præter noua locorum & personarum nomina habemus.Bonitas Dei. Interim conseruat. Reditum in Græciam & Syriam promittit,Philip 2. Philem.1. Hebr.13. Deinde profectionem per Italiam meditatur in Hispanias,nondum visas,Rom.15. Vnde verisimile est, primo in Orientem abiuisse, deinde in Hispanias,vt veteres pleriqué tradunt. Tandem Romæ truncatus anno 37.conuersionis.
units.tr: III. What did he do after the two years had rolled by? Luke did not write of it, because there was no need to burden the Church with more. For we have nothing beyond new names of places and persons. God's goodness: meanwhile he preserves him. He promises a return to Greece and Syria, Phil. 2; Philem. 1; Heb. 13. Then he plans a journey through Italy into Spain, not yet seen, Rom. 15. Hence it is likely that he first went to the East and then to Spain, as most of the ancients relate. At last he was beheaded at Rome in the thirty-seventh year after his conversion.

units.la: NOT. ¶ Pauli indefessum studium pro gloria & Ecclesia Christi,2. Cor.11.&c.Si-
units.tr: NOTE. ¶ Paul's tireless zeal for the glory and Church of Christ, 2 Cor. 11, etc. Likewise

units.la: nnul vero exitum indignum, quoad mundum, vides. Sic Petrus, Iohan. 21. Sed ita seruos suos sibi conformes facit Christus, 1. Tim. 2. Rom 8. &c.
units.tr: you see an end unworthy as far as the world is concerned. So Peter, John 21. But thus Christ makes his servants conformed to himself, 1 Tim. 2; Rom. 8, etc.

units.la: VIDIMVS hucusque librum hunc. Veteris Ecclesiae formam, fidem & doctrinam continet. Docet item, Ecclesiam in hoc mundo exerceri, sed per Christum defendi fidelissimè, Matth 28. Ioh. 10. In hoc ergo nobis hodie fiendum, qui non deerit.
units.tr: WE HAVE HITHERTO surveyed this book. It contains the form, faith and doctrine of the early Church. It also teaches that the Church is exercised in this world, but is most faithfully defended by Christ, Matt. 28; John 10. Therefore in this we must today do what will not be wanting.

units.la: Oremus.
units.tr: Let us pray.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.
